prs.title: fix(cli): keep pasted @ text and fuzzy @ matches from attaching secrets
prs.body:
Fixes #26730

## Summary

A pasted shell transcript could make Gemini CLI attach an SSH private key to the model request without asking. This PR closes both halves of that path:

- **Pasted text is inert by default.** `ui.escapePastedAtSymbols` now defaults to `true`, so `@` in pasted text is stored as `\@` and is not treated as a file reference. The escape is removed before the text reaches the model or a `!` shell command.
- **The fuzzy fallback never picks secrets.** When an `@name` reference does not resolve, the recursive glob fallback skips matches that look like credentials and uses the next match instead.

This builds on #29458 by @MartinCajiao, which flipped the default but was closed by the bot before review. The default change, its description text, and the paste and schema tests are adapted from that PR.

## Root cause

1. `ui.escapePastedAtSymbols` (#21239) was opt-in, so pasted text such as `[dave@webserver ~]$ ssh-add -l` kept a bare `@webserver`.
2. `webserver` is not in the workspace root, so `resolveFilePaths` ran `**/*webserver*` in every workspace directory (dotfiles included) and attached the first match. Started from `$HOME`, that match can be `~/.ssh/webserver`.

The existing escape feature also had a gap: when no `@` reference resolved, the escaped text reached the model with the backslashes still in it (`dave\@webserver`), and shell commands received them too. That had to be fixed before the setting could default to on.

## Changes

- `settingsSchema.ts`: `ui.escapePastedAtSymbols` defaults to `true` (docs and JSON schema regenerated).
- `atCommandProcessor.ts`: glob-fallback matches are skipped when they are inside `.ssh`, `.gnupg`, `.aws`, `.azure` or `.kube`; when the name looks like a private key (`id_rsa`, `id_dsa`, `id_ecdsa`, `id_ed25519` and variants, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.ppk`) or an env file (`.env`, `.env.*`, `*.env`); when the file is owner-only (for example 0600); or when it cannot be stat'ed. The early return for queries without resolvable references now unescapes `\@`.
- `useGeminiStream.ts`: plain prompts and `!` shell commands receive the unescaped text.
- `docs/reference/commands.md`: documents paste escaping and the fuzzy-match exclusions.

Explicit paths are unchanged: `@.ssh/webserver` still attaches the file, because typing the exact path is a deliberate request.

## Trade-offs

- **Skip instead of confirm.** The issue suggests a confirmation prompt. A dialog inside `@` processing needs new async UI plumbing. Skipping is smaller, fails closed, and leaves a clear way to include the file on purpose: type its exact path.
- **Filter instead of exact-match-only.** Accepting only exact basename matches would not have stopped this leak (the key was named after the host) and would break lookups like `@README` → `README.md`.
- **Heuristics can over-match**, but only in the fuzzy fallback: Keynote `.key` files, `.env.example`, repositories with an `.aws/` folder, or every file of a user with umask 077. An exact `@path` still works for all of them. The permission check has no effect on Windows.
- **Visible `\@`.** Pasted `@` now shows as `\@` in the input box, as it already did for users who enabled the setting.

## Not in this PR

- Ignoring `user@host` in the parser (issue item 3).
- Pasted text in slash-command arguments and model-steering hints still keeps `\@`, as it does today with the setting on.
- Terminals without bracketed paste cannot be detected; the secret filter still applies there.

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/cli
```

prs.title: fix(core): apply local subagents' generateContentConfig for every model
prs.body:
Fixes #30168

## Summary

Local subagents now send the generation settings they declare in `modelConfig.generateContentConfig` (temperature, topP, topK, thinkingConfig) for every model value: `auto`, aliases such as `flash` and `pro`, and concrete model names. Before this change, only `auto` agents got them, and they lost them after `refreshAuth()` or `/clear`, which in `gemini -p` means before the first prompt.

## Details

- **Root cause.** Since #16043, `LocalAgentExecutor.callModel` sends GeminiChat the model name rather than the agent's model config alias, and GeminiChat looks the config up again by the concrete model id. The agent's settings only travelled through an override scoped to the agent, and #16043 registered that override for `auto` models only. #27315 later added `clearRuntimeOverrides()`, which deletes those overrides along with the quota-fallback ones.
- **Fix.** A new `ModelConfigService.registerRuntimeScopeOverride(scope, modelConfig)`, which `AgentRegistry` now uses for every local agent. It is stored per scope, so re-registering on a model change replaces the previous entry. `clearRuntimeOverrides()` does not remove it. It is applied before configured overrides, so `modelConfigs.overrides` and `customOverrides` that target the agent's scope (as `docs/core/subagents.md` describes) still win.
- **Thinking settings.** The API rejects a request that sets both `thinkingLevel` and `thinkingBudget`. `ModelConfigService.merge` now lets the one an override sets replace the inherited one. Without this, `cli_help`'s `thinkingBudget` would be merged with Gemini 3's default `thinkingLevel: HIGH` and every request would fail. No default model config sets both, so the main chat is unchanged.
- **Behaviour changes.** `codebase_investigator`, `cli_help`, `browser_agent`, and markdown agents with a non-`auto` model now send their declared temperature and thinking settings. `generalist`, the skill extraction agent and the main chat are unchanged. For `auto` agents, user overrides that target the agent's scope now beat the agent's defaults; before, the defaults silently won.
- **Interplay with #29257.** `cli_help` declares `thinkingBudget: -1` (dynamic thinking, no cap), which is never sent today. With this PR, the −1 takes effect. The #29257 fix (a separate PR) caps it at `DEFAULT_THINKING_MODE` and adds a per-turn timeout; that cap only reaches the API once this PR lands. The two PRs touch different files and can merge in either order.

## Related Issues

Related to #29257.

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/agents/registry.test.ts src/services/modelConfigService.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
```

The "generation config sent by the agent" tests fail on `main` for `flash`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, `cli_help` and the cleared-overrides case, and pass with this change.

prs.body:
Fixes #27114

## Summary

In an untrusted folder, the CLI never read the user's own `~/.gemini/.env`. Workspace-account users who keep `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` there got an endless login loop outside trusted folders. This PR lets untrusted folders read `~/.gemini/.env` again, with the same allowlist and sanitization that untrusted folders already apply to other `.env` files.

## Details

- `findEnvFile()` (`packages/cli/src/config/settings.ts`): #25814 gated both `.gemini/.env` checks on workspace trust. That also skipped the user's `~/.gemini/.env`, both when the upward walk reaches the home directory and in the home fallback. The walk now also checks `.gemini/.env` when the current directory is the home directory, and the home fallback is no longer gated.
- Nothing else changes. A project's `.gemini/.env` is still skipped in untrusted folders. The plain `.env` lookup, `advanced.ignoreLocalEnv` / `--ignore-env`, and `loadEnvironment()` (allowlist plus `sanitizeEnvVar()` for untrusted folders) are untouched. Trusted folders behave exactly as before.
- Precedence is unchanged: a project `.env` found while walking up still beats `~/.gemini/.env` ("first file found, not merged"). Users who want their home file instead can use `advanced.ignoreLocalEnv` / `--ignore-env` (#26445), which with this fix also works in untrusted folders.
- `docs/cli/trusted-folders.md` now says which variables an untrusted folder loads and from where. The old sentence said no project `.env` file is loaded, which hasn't been accurate since #17806/#25814.

## How to Validate

```bash
npm run build
cd packages/cli
npx vitest run src/config/settings-env-isolation.test.ts src/config/settings.test.ts src/config/trustedFolders.test.ts
```

New cases cover an untrusted folder with only `~/.gemini/.env` (cwd under home and outside home), `~/.gemini/.env` winning over `~/.env`, a project `.env` still winning when untrusted, a project `.gemini/.env` never being loaded when untrusted, and trusted folders unchanged. prs.title: fix(core): keep one result per tool call ID in session records and live history
prs.body:
Fixes #28004

## Summary

Each tool-call ID now has exactly one result in saved sessions and in the requests sent to the model. The `--resume` duplication from #28004 was fixed when reading sessions by #29618. This PR removes the two places that still produced extra results per call ID.

## Details

- **Session records** (`chatRecordingService.ts`): the masking sync in `updateMessagesFromHistory` copied the whole tool-response turn into every matching `toolCalls[].result`, so with parallel calls each record held every sibling's response (the second half of #29365). It now stores only the call's own parts: its `functionResponse` plus the sibling parts that follow it, such as `inlineData`. Parts before the first response stay with the first call, so behavior for single calls does not change. Sessions written by earlier versions are repaired the next time they are resumed.
- **Live tool loop** (`turn.ts`): when the provider omits `functionCall.id`, `Turn` builds `${name}_${Date.now()}_${counter}`. A new `Turn` is created for every model request and the counter belonged to the instance, so two rounds in the same millisecond produced the same ID. The counter is now shared by all turns. The ID format is unchanged.
- There is no new dedupe at send time, and `convertSessionToClientHistory` is unchanged.

Thanks to @N0zoM1z0 for the deterministic reproducer, and to @xanister for the version bisection (0.42.0 to 0.45.0), which pointed to #26939 as the origin.

## Related Issues

Fixes #28004. Related to #29365 and #29618.

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/core/turn.test.ts src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts
```

These new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change:
- `turn.test.ts`: should not reuse a synthesized call ID across turns in the same millisecond
- `chatRecordingService.test.ts`: should store only each call's own parts when parallel calls share a response turn

prs.title: fix(core): stop local subagents from waiting out their deadline on a stalled model call
prs.body:
Fixes #29257

## Summary

When a single model call stalled, `cli_help` waited out its whole 3-minute `maxTimeMinutes`, then up to 60 s more on a recovery turn, before reporting `Agent timed out after 3 minutes.` This PR adds an optional per-turn limit on the model response to the local agent executor and enables it for `cli_help` (1 minute), so a stalled call fails fast with a clear error.

## Root cause

- `LocalAgentExecutor` bounds a model call only by the agent's overall deadline. Inside one call, `GeminiChat` can retry for minutes without yielding a stream event (connection retries with 5–30 s backoff on 429/503/timeouts, retries of empty or thought-only responses). When the deadline fires, the executor sends a recovery turn to the same model and waits up to `GRACE_PERIOD_MS` (60 s) again.
- The `thinkingBudget: -1` called out in the issue is not what the API receives. `callModel` sends the bare model name (`flash`) to `GeminiChat`, which resolves that model's default chat config. `AgentRegistry.registerModelConfigs` only registers the agent's `generateContentConfig` as a scope override for `auto` models. With a mocked content generator, the request goes to `gemini-3.5-flash` with `temperature: 1` and `thinkingLevel: HIGH`, so capping the budget alone does not change the request. This affects every local agent with a non-`auto` model; I left it for a separate issue because fixing it changes generation settings for those agents.

## Changes

- `RunConfig.maxTurnTimeMinutes` (optional): the maximum time to wait for the model's response in a single turn. Tool execution is not counted. On expiry the turn stops with `ERROR` and `Agent stopped: the model did not respond within N seconds.` The recovery turn is skipped because it would wait on the same model. Agents that don't set the field are unchanged.
- `cli_help`: sets `maxTurnTimeMinutes: 1` and replaces `thinkingBudget: -1` with `DEFAULT_THINKING_MODE` (8192), the cap other configs use.

@saikat709 proposed a capped budget and a per-turn timeout earlier in the issue. This PR implements the timeout in the shared executor and explains why the cap by itself would not change the request.

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/agents
```

- `local-executor.test.ts`, new `run (Turn Timeout)` suite (mocked streams, fake timers): a stalled stream that ends, or throws `AbortError`, stops with `ERROR` after the limit, with one model call and no recovery turn; tool execution time is not counted, and the timer is cleared; after an empty model turn, the recovery turn is bounded by the turn limit instead of the 60 s grace period; the real `cli_help` definition fails after 60 s instead of waiting out 3 minutes. Against the previous executor, the four stall tests hang until the vitest timeout.
- `cli-help-agent.test.ts`: the budget is capped and `maxTurnTimeMinutes` is below `maxTimeMinutes`.

prs.title: fix(core): respect active YOLO mode in taint and build file checks
prs.body:
## Summary

Respect active, trusted YOLO mode (`--approval-mode=yolo` / `-y`) in shell taint/build-file risk checks and `PolicyEngine` build file protection so autonomous interactive and headless YOLO runs are no longer interrupted by confirmation prompts or hard-denied (`POLICY_VIOLATION`) when editing build configuration files or running commands referencing external context.

All indirect prompt-injection protections remain fully enforced in `default` and `auto_edit` modes, in untrusted folders (`!isTrustedFolder()`), when YOLO mode is administratively disabled (`disableYoloMode` / `isYoloModeDisabled()`), and when higher-tier user/admin policy rules explicitly require `ask_user` or `deny`.

## Details

1. **`ShellToolInvocation` (`packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`)**:
   - Added `isActiveYoloMode()` verifying both `ApprovalMode.YOLO` and `!isYoloModeDisabled()`.
   - Updated `shouldConfirmExecute()` to skip forcing confirmation for `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` when active YOLO mode is enabled (unless `forcedDecision === 'ask_user'` from an explicit policy rule or hook).
   - Updated `isCommandSubstitutionAllowed()` so active YOLO mode delegates command substitution checks to `PolicyEngine` (`yolo.toml` sets `allowCommandSubstitution = true`) rather than unconditionally blocking on `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()`.
   - Preserved the `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` guard in `getPolicyUpdateOptions()` so tainted commands never persist permanent `"Always allow"` rules.
2. **`Scheduler` (`packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts`)**:
   - Skipped escalating `PolicyDecision.ALLOW` to `ASK_USER` (interactive) or `DENY` (non-interactive/headless) for `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` when active YOLO mode (`!isYoloModeDisabled()`) is enabled.
3. **`PolicyEngine` (`packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts`)**:
   - Skipped the hardcoded `Build File Protection` downgrade (`ASK_USER` / `DENY` on `package.json`, `Makefile`, `BUILD.bazel`, etc.) when running in trusted YOLO mode (`this.approvalMode === ApprovalMode.YOLO && this.isTrustedFolder()`). `auto_edit` mode, `default` mode, untrusted workspaces, and explicit user/admin rules remain protected.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29682
Fixes #29680
Related to #29687
Related to #30004

## How to Validate

1. Run targeted unit test suites:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/tools/shell.test.ts src/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts
   ```

prs.title: fix(cli): detect local git clone installation from CLI executable path
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes an issue where running Gemini CLI from a source checkout outside of the clone directory causes `getInstallationInfo` to misclassify the installation as a global npm install, triggering an unintended background `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli@latest` during auto-update.

Fixes #30209

## Details
In `packages/cli/src/utils/installationInfo.ts`, local git clone detection previously relied on:
```ts
isGitRepository(process.cwd()) &&
realPath.startsWith(normalizedProjectRoot) &&
!realPath.includes('/node_modules/')
```
Because `projectRoot` comes from `config.getProjectRoot()` (which is the current target directory / `process.cwd()`), running the CLI from any other directory caused `realPath.startsWith(normalizedProjectRoot)` or `isGitRepository(process.cwd())` to fail. As a result, detection fell through to the default branch (`PackageManager.NPM`, `isGlobal: true`), spawning `npm install -g` in the background.

This fix:
- Updates the detection to check `!realPath.includes('/node_modules/') && isGitRepository(path.dirname(realPath))`, inspecting where the CLI executable itself is located rather than the user's working directory.
- Preserves the `node_modules` exclusion so package-manager installations (npx, npm, pnpm, yarn, bun) remain unaffected.
- Updates existing tests and adds unit test coverage in `installationInfo.test.ts` for running a local clone from an unrelated working directory.

## Related Issues
Fixes #30209

## How to Validate
Run the unit tests in `packages/cli`:
```bash
npx vitest run src/utils/installationInfo.test.ts --coverage false
```
Expected: All 22 tests pass, including the test asserting that running from an unrelated working directory is correctly identified as a local git clone.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve trimmed function-call name in history to prevent 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT (#30256)
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #30256.

When the model produces a function call whose name contains leading or trailing whitespace (e.g. `" update_topic"`), `Turn.handlePendingFunctionCall` trims the name to dispatch tool execution and constructs the `functionResponse` under that trimmed name (`"update_topic"`). However, the in-place mutation of the function call object in history updated `fnCall.id = callId` but omitted updating `fnCall.name = name`.

On subsequent conversational turns, the paired `functionCall` (`" update_topic"`) and `functionResponse` (`"update_topic"`) carried mismatched names under the same `id`, causing the Gemini API to reject the request with `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

This PR ensures `fnCall.name = name` is consistently written alongside `fnCall.id = callId` during function call handling in `Turn` and stream consolidation in `GeminiChat`.

## Details

1. In `packages/core/src/core/turn.ts`:
   - Updated `Turn.handlePendingFunctionCall` to assign `fnCall.name = name` alongside `fnCall.id = callId`.
2. In `packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts`:
   - Updated stream processing loops (both context-management enabled and fallback modes) to set `fnCall.name = name`.
3. In `packages/core/src/core/turn.test.ts` & `packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.test.ts`:
   - Added unit tests verifying that padded function call names are trimmed and recorded consistently in history turns.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30256

## How to Validate

Run unit tests in `packages/core`:
```bash
npm test src/core/turn.test.ts src/core/geminiChat.test.ts
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
```
All pass with 0 errors.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): improve permission denial detection and unsupported environment handling (#29338)
prs.body:
## Description
Fixes #29338.

This PR addresses sandbox compatibility and permission error handling across containerized and restricted execution environments in `@google/gemini-cli-core`.

### Issues Addressed
1. **Permission Denials Unrecognized**: POSIX sandbox denial detection previously missed common tool-level permission errors (`mkdir: cannot create directory`, `touch: cannot touch`, `chmod: changing permissions of`, `scandir`, `access`, and Python `[Errno 13]`). This prevented the CLI from identifying file permission denials and offering dynamic permission resolution.
2. **Unhandled Crash on Unsupported Environments**: When tool sandboxing was requested in environments without supported sandbox managers, `LocalSandboxManager` threw an untyped generic error rather than the canonical `FatalSandboxError` (exit code 44), causing an unhandled crash rather than graceful user diagnostic exit.

### Changes Made
- `packages/core/src/sandbox/utils/sandboxDenialUtils.ts`:
  - Extended `isFileDenial` keyword detection for `cannot create directory`, `cannot touch`, `changing permissions of`, and `errno 13`.
  - Added dedicated extraction regexes for `mkdir`, `touch`, `chmod`, `scandir`, `access`, Python `[Errno 13]`, and shell permission denied errors.
- `packages/core/src/services/sandboxManager.ts`:
  - Updated `LocalSandboxManager.prepareCommand()` to throw `FatalSandboxError` with actionable remediation guidance.
- `packages/core/src/sandbox/utils/sandboxDenialUtils.test.ts`:
  - Added 8 regression test cases covering all new permission denial formats and `FatalSandboxError` verification.

## How Was This Tested?
- Added regression tests in `sandboxDenialUtils.test.ts` for all permission error formats.
- Verified `LocalSandboxManager` throws `FatalSandboxError` with exit code 44 (`ExitCodes.FATAL_SANDBOX_ERROR`).

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows the style guidelines of this project.
- [x] Unit tests have been added to verify changes.
- [x] No breaking changes introduced.

prs.title: fix(core): unify exit codes mapping and fatal error hierarchy
prs.body:
## Description
This PR centralizes and unifies CLI process exit codes across `@google/gemini-cli-core`.

Previously, `ExitCodes` in `exitCodes.ts` was missing several fatal error codes that were hardcoded as raw numeric literals in `errors.ts` (`FatalSandboxError`, `FatalTurnLimitedError`, `FatalToolExecutionError`, and `FatalUntrustedWorkspaceError`). Furthermore, `FatalError` subclasses in `errors.ts` used raw magic numbers rather than referencing the canonical `ExitCodes` constant.

This change:
1. Adds the missing fatal exit codes (`44`, `53`, `54`, `55`) to `ExitCodes`.
2. Exports the strongly-typed `ExitCode` union for autocomplete and compile-time validation.
3. Refactors all `FatalError` subclasses to reference `ExitCodes.*`.
4. Adds a comprehensive unit test suite in `exitCodes.test.ts` to ensure 100% test coverage and prevent future regressions.

## Changes Made
- `packages/core/src/utils/exitCodes.ts`:
  - Added `FATAL_SANDBOX_ERROR: 44`
  - Added `FATAL_TURN_LIMITED_ERROR: 53`
  - Added `FATAL_TOOL_EXECUTION_ERROR: 54`
  - Added `FATAL_UNTRUSTED_WORKSPACE_ERROR: 55`
  - Exported `type ExitCode = (typeof ExitCodes)[keyof typeof ExitCodes]`
- `packages/core/src/utils/errors.ts`:
  - Imported `ExitCodes` from `./exitCodes.js`
  - Replaced all magic numbers in `FatalError` subclasses with `ExitCodes.FATAL_*`
- `packages/core/src/utils/exitCodes.test.ts`:
  - Added unit test suite validating canonical exit code values, type constraints, subclass alignments, and custom exit code overrides.

## How Was This Tested?
- Added unit tests in `packages/core/src/utils/exitCodes.test.ts` covering:
  - Canonical numeric exit code mappings.
  - Subclass instantiation exit codes for all `FatalError` subclasses.
  - Custom exit code overriding in `FatalCancellationError`.
- Verified 100% backward compatibility (zero breaking changes to numeric exit code values).

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows the style guidelines of this project.
- [x] Unit tests have been added to verify changes.
- [x] No breaking API changes introduced.

prs.title: fix(cli): resolve reference ambiguity during extension checkout
prs.body:
## Summary

Improve the robustness of the extension clone and checkout implementation by resolving references to their concrete commit SHAs and verifying checkout integrity.

## Details

During extension installation or update from a Git repository, the CLI clones the source and fetches the requested reference, which writes the target commit SHA to the `.git/FETCH_HEAD` pseudo-ref. Previously, the code performed `git checkout FETCH_HEAD`.

However, if a repository's default branch is literally named `FETCH_HEAD`, Git's reference resolution during a `checkout` command prioritizes the local branch over the pseudo-ref. This can cause the checkout to stay on the local branch instead of switching to the fetched commit.

This PR refactors the checkout process to resolve the reference name unambiguously:
- Resolves the target pseudo-ref (`FETCH_HEAD`) to its absolute, unambiguous commit SHA using `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` (as `rev-parse` prioritizes the `.git/` pseudo-refs).
- Performs the checkout directly using the absolute commit SHA (e.g., `git checkout <sha>`), forcing an unambiguous detached HEAD state on the correct target commit.
- Asserts that the checked-out commit SHA (`git rev-parse HEAD`) matches the resolved target SHA to ensure checkout integrity.
- Adds an explicit SHA verification check: if a full 40-character (SHA-1) or 64-character (SHA-256) commit pin was requested, the checked-out commit SHA is verified to match the requested pin. This avoids false positives with short named branches or tags (e.g. ticket numbers) consisting entirely of hex characters.

## Related Issues

None.

## How to Validate

Run the unit tests targeting the modified git extension code:
```bash
npx vitest run packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.test.ts
```

Verify build and lint compliance:
```bash
npm run typecheck -w @google/gemini-cli
npm run lint -w @google/gemini-cli
```

prs.title: fix(core): quote IDE CLI command path on Windows for cmd.exe
prs.body:
## Summary

Quotes the resolved IDE CLI path on Windows when installing companion extensions. This resolves an issue where `/ide install` fails when VS Code (or Positron / Antigravity) is located in default folders containing spaces (such as `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Microsoft VS Code` or `%ProgramFiles%\Microsoft VS Code`).

## Details

On Windows, `ide-installer.ts` invokes `child_process.spawnSync` with `shell: true` to execute `.cmd` files. When `shell: true` is enabled, Node.js formats arguments for `cmd.exe /d /s /c "<command>"`. Because `cmd.exe` strips the outer quotes when `/s` is present, any unquoted path containing spaces is split at the first whitespace character (e.g. `C:\Program` or `C:\Users\...\Microsoft`), causing execution to fail with exit status 1.

This PR wraps the resolved `commandPath` with `quoteCmdArg` from `packages/core/src/utils/editor.ts` across `VsCodeInstaller`, `PositronInstaller`, and `AntigravityInstaller` on `win32`. Paths without spaces remain unquoted, and non-Windows platforms remain completely unaffected.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30245

## How to Validate

1. Run unit tests verifying path quoting across all IDEs and platforms:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/ide/ide-installer.test.ts
   ```
2. Verify linting and typechecking pass:
   ```bash
   npm run lint && npm run typecheck
   ```
3. On Windows with VS Code installed in the default location (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\bin\code.cmd`), run `/ide install` inside Gemini CLI and verify that the companion extension installs successfully.

prs.title: fix(cli): resume most recently active session instead of most recently started
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where `gemini --resume` (and `--resume latest`) reopens the most recently started session instead of the most recently used/active session.

## Details

When resolving `RESUME_LATEST`, `SessionSelector.resolveSession` previously sorted available sessions by `startTime` ascending and selected the last element. Consequently, in workflows involving a long-lived primary session and a newer temporary spike session, returning to and chatting in the primary session updated its `lastUpdated` timestamp, but running `gemini --resume` subsequently reopened the stale spike session.

This change:
- Updates `resolveSession` for `RESUME_LATEST` to sort sessions by `lastUpdated` ascending (so the most recently active session is selected).
- Uses `startTime` ascending as a deterministic tiebreaker if `lastUpdated` timestamps are identical.
- Preserves `startTime` sorting for numeric index resolution (`--resume 1`, `--resume 2`) to ensure stable chronological numbering matching `--list-sessions`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29410

## How to Validate

1. Run unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/sessionUtils.test.ts
   ```
2. Manual verification:
   - Start Session A, send a message, and exit.
   - Start Session B, send a message, and exit.
   - Resume Session A explicitly (`gemini --resume 1`), send another message, and exit.
   - Run bare `gemini --resume` (or `gemini --resume latest`).
   - Verify that Session A is resumed rather than Session B.

prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes path resolution for Windows home-relative paths using native backslashes (`~\...`). Previously, `resolvePath()` only expanded `~` or `~/...`, leaving `~\...` with an unexpanded literal `~` on Windows, which caused policy paths, extension registries, and include directories to point at incorrect locations under the current working directory.

## Details

- In `packages/cli/src/utils/resolvePath.ts`:
  - Added support for `(process.platform === 'win32' && p.startsWith('~\\'))` to expand `~` using `homedir()`.
  - Normalized paths using `process.platform === 'win32' ? path.win32 : path` to ensure correct platform separator normalization.
  - On POSIX platforms, literal backslashes after `~` (e.g. `~\policies\custom.toml`) are preserved unchanged, since backslash is a valid filename character and not a path separator on POSIX systems.
- In `packages/cli/src/utils/resolvePath.test.ts`:
  - Added comprehensive test suites for both Windows and POSIX environments covering exact matches, subpaths, normalization, environment variable variants, and unexpanded literals.

Fixes #29916

prs.title: fix(core): handle nested .gitignore negations under dir/** patterns
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where `GitIgnoreParser` incorrectly ignored files that were re-included by a nested `.gitignore` file located under a directory matching a wildcard pattern (e.g., `logs/**` in root `.gitignore` and `!keep.txt` in `logs/.gitignore`).

## Details

- **Problem:** PR #29582 added subtree pruning by using `expandWildcardDirectoryPatterns` to convert wildcard patterns like `dir/**` into directory-level ignore patterns like `/dir/`. When evaluating `computeRelDirState(relDir)`, `GitIgnoreParser` checked `parentState.combinedIg.ignores('dir/')`, which evaluated to `true` due to the synthetic pattern. This caused `GitIgnoreParser` to immediately prune the directory without loading `<dir>/.gitignore`, ignoring any negation rules (`!`) inside it.
- **Solution:** 
  1. Updated `expandWildcardDirectoryPatterns` in `packages/core/src/utils/ignorePathUtils.ts` to accept an optional `hasNestedNegation?: (dir: string) => boolean` callback.
  2. In `GitIgnoreParser.processPatterns`, passed `hasNestedNegation` to inspect whether `<dir>/.gitignore` exists on disk and contains any un-escaped negation rule (`!`). If a negation rule exists, the synthetic `/dir/` directory pattern is not added, allowing GitIgnoreParser to traverse into the directory and parse its nested rules.
  3. Preserved subtree pruning optimization for all wildcard patterns where child ignore files do not contain negations (e.g. `node_modules/**`, `build/**`).
- **Tests:** Added comprehensive test coverage in `ignorePathUtils.test.ts`, `gitIgnoreParser.test.ts`, and `fileDiscoveryService.test.ts`.

## Related Issues

- Fixes #29826

## How to Validate

1. Run core unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/gitIgnoreParser.test.ts src/utils/ignorePathUtils.test.ts src/services/fileDiscoveryService.test.ts
   ```
2. Verify all checks pass:
   ```bash
   npm run lint && npm run typecheck
   ```
3. Manual verification:
   Create a git repo with:
   - `.gitignore`: `logs/**`
   - `logs/.gitignore`: `!keep.txt`
   - `logs/keep.txt`: `payload`
   - `logs/a.txt`: `discard`
   Verify that `logs/keep.txt` is not ignored and `logs/a.txt` is ignored.

prs.title: fix(cli): show executing subagent tool calls in UI state
prs.body:
Fixes #22589

The filter for non-root schedulers in `useToolScheduler` only kept tool calls that were awaiting approval or already present in state. Subagent calls that never need approval (reads, searches, and similar) go straight to `Executing` on their first update, so they were dropped before reaching state. With nothing in state, the task tree has no call to attach them to and the subagent's work stays invisible.

This adds `Executing` to the filter. Calls that have not started yet (`Scheduled`/`Validating`) are still hidden, so transient subagent work doesn't start flickering in the UI.

Testing:
- Updated the two existing tests that expected executing subagent calls to be dropped, and added a regression test that first-seen `Scheduled`/`Validating` calls remain hidden
- `useToolScheduler.test.ts`: 14/14 passing locally
- Neighbouring suites (`AppContainer`, `useGeminiStream`, `useTurnActivityMonitor`): 226/226 passing
- Pre-commit lint and format checks pass

prs.title: fix(core): fallback to system ripgrep and trust Termux paths on Android
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where Gemini CLI fails with an unhandled `spawn ... ENOENT` error on Android/Termux during `grep_search`. It skips bundled glibc Linux binaries that lack the required ELF dynamic linker in Android's Bionic libc environment, and allows `isTrustedSystemPath()` to recognize Termux system paths so system-installed `rg` (`$PREFIX/bin/rg`) is trusted.

## Details

- **Binary Resolution (`packages/core/src/tools/ripGrep.ts`)**:
  - Skipped bundled Linux glibc binaries when running on Android or when `TERMUX_VERSION` is detected (`platform === 'android' || !!process.env['TERMUX_VERSION']`).
  - Directly falls back to resolving system `rg` via `resolveExecutable('rg')`.
  - If system `rg` is not installed on Termux, `resolveRipgrepPath()` returns `null`, allowing `packages/core/src/config/config.ts` to cleanly fall back to `GrepTool` without throwing an uncaught `spawn ENOENT` error.
- **Trusted Paths (`packages/core/src/utils/paths.ts`)**:
  - Extended `isTrustedSystemPath()` to trust `/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin`, `/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/applets`, and `${process.env['PREFIX']}/bin` when on Android or in a Termux environment.
- **Unit Tests**:
  - Added test coverage in `packages/core/src/utils/paths.test.ts` verifying Termux system paths are trusted on Android/Termux and rejected on desktop platforms.
  - Added test coverage in `packages/core/src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts` verifying `resolveRipgrepPath()` skips bundled binaries on Android and resolves Termux system ripgrep.

## Related Issues

Fixes #21836

## How to Validate

1. Run the targeted Vitest test suites:
   ```bash
   npx vitest run packages/core/src/utils/paths.test.ts
   npx vitest run packages/core/src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts
   ```

issues.title: Agent ran `rsync -a --delete <dir>/ /` in WSL (empty variable after quoting failure) and irrecoverably wiped a user drive

labels.name: triage:needs-human
labels.description: Auto-triage could not classify this issue confidently. Remove the label to re-queue it.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

While working on an unrelated task (preparing an upstream PR), the agent wanted to run Go tests in WSL. It passed a multi-line bash script inline from PowerShell:

```
wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- bash -lc $s   # $s = multi-line here-string
```

The line breaks/quoting were mangled on the way through PowerShell -> wsl.exe, so the line `D=~/src/rs-pr` never took effect and `$D` was empty. The next line therefore ran as:

```
rsync -a --delete --exclude .git /mnt/c/Users/<user>/Code/<repo>/ /
```

i.e. "make / look like the repo, delete everything else". It ran ~7 minutes as the normal WSL user before the agent noticed (the tool output was 34 MB of rsync errors) and stopped it.

**Damage:** all user-deletable files on the Windows data drive D: (mounted at /mnt/d) were deleted, ~10 GB incl. a Thunderbird profile (mail) and games. D: is an SSD, so TRIM made the data unrecoverable (verified by raw MFT/cluster analysis: deleted files' clusters now return random data). C: survived only because rsync deletes in reverse alphabetical order and hit C:\Windows (permission denied) before C:\Users. The user had no backup of D:.

### Affected version

- Copilot SDK-based agent in VS Code 1.147.0 (8a14f0cc1b08d531eb83255ea3764ae22aa932b5, x64)
- Model: claude-opus-5.5, reasoning effort medium (verified from session usage log)
- OS: Windows 11 (NT 10.0.26300) + WSL Ubuntu 24.04
- Date: 2026-11-20

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Agent session on Windows with PowerShell tool and WSL installed (Windows drives auto-mounted under /mnt).
2. Agent builds a multi-line bash script in a PowerShell here-string that sets a variable and then uses it as a destructive target, e.g.
   `D=~/src/x; mkdir -p $D; rsync -a --delete src/ $D/`
3. Agent runs it via `wsl -- bash -lc $script`.
4. Quoting breaks, the assignment is lost, `$D` is empty -> `rsync --delete src/ /` runs and deletes user files on all mounted drives.

### Expected behavior

- The agent must never run a command with `--delete`, `rm -rf`, `find -delete` etc. whose target is built from a variable without guarding it (`set -euo pipefail`, `${D:?}`) and without checking the resolved path is not `/` or a mount root.
- Destructive commands outside the workspace should require explicit user confirmation; none was requested.
- Multi-line scripts for WSL should be written to a file and executed, not passed through PowerShell -> wsl.exe argument quoting.
- When the first output shows clear signs of a broken command (bash "not a valid identifier" errors, rsync touching /mnt/c/Windows), the run should be aborted immediately.

### Additional context

- The agent's `initial_wait` was 400 s, so the destructive command ran unobserved for that long.
- Root filesystem / and /mnt/c/Windows were protected only by permissions; any drive where the user has delete rights (/mnt/d) was wiped.
- Filed by the affected user, with the summary written by the agent itself at the user's request.

issues.title: Supabase OAuth status probe fails with missing Mcp-Session-Id (HTTP 400) while normal App tool calls succeed

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Summary

The separate OAuth/authorization status check for an existing Supabase MCP connection fails with HTTP 400, while a normal GitHub Copilot App session can successfully invoke `get_project_url` through that connection.

The server's actual response body identifies a missing MCP session header:

```json
{"message":"Mcp-Session-Id header is required for non-initialization requests"}
```

Related: #5014 describes the same session-initialization failure pattern for another provider; #5039 describes a different possible cause of a similar HTTP-400 probe error. This report adds a Supabase-specific reproduction and the actual response body; I am not claiming that protocol-version rejection is the cause here.

### Environment

- macOS
- GitHub Copilot App 1.4.3 (in-app updater reported up to date)
- Copilot Business
- Existing project-scoped HTTP MCP server: Supabase hosted MCP
- Passive diagnostic used the SDK bundled with the App and the installed CLI runtime with `--no-auto-update`; no model prompt was sent during that diagnostic.

### Configuration (sanitized example)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "supabase": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=REDACTED&features=docs%2Caccount%2Cdatabase%2Cdebugging%2Cdevelopment%2Cfunctions%2Cbranching",
      "tools": ["*"]
    }
  }
}
```

`REDACTED` is a placeholder, not a real project reference. There are no static Authorization headers.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure one existing project-scoped Supabase MCP server and complete its normal OAuth connection.
2. Verify that a new local Copilot App session can call `get_project_url` successfully. This was observed in the actual App transcript.
3. Open Customize > Installed and the existing Supabase server's configuration/actions UI.
4. Observe the separate authorization check report:

```text
Could not check authorization
WsCommandError: invalid argument: MCP server probe returned HTTP 400 Bad Request
```

The server row can still report `Connected. Enabled.` afterward.

### Passive diagnostic evidence (sanitized)

```json
{
  "probe_status": "failed",
  "http_status": 400,
  "server_response": {
    "message": "Mcp-Session-Id header is required for non-initialization requests"
  },
  "anonymous_checks": {
    "ping_2026-07-28": 401,
    "initialize_2026-07-28": 401,
    "ping_2025-03-26": 401,
    "initialize_2025-03-26": 401
  },
  "normal_app_tool": "get_project_url succeeded in a separate actual Copilot App session",
  "new_login_during_diagnostic": false
}
```

The passive `session.mcp.oauth.probe` result exposed HTTP 400 and the response body above. No stored token was read, exported, or manually inserted into a request. No reauthentication was started for this diagnostic.

The anonymous checks only establish that those unauthenticated requests receive an expected 401. They do not prove which protocol versions are accepted after authentication.

Limitation: a separate attempt to compare `tools/list` in the explicitly created SDK diagnostic session required authentication in that isolated context, so I did not reauthenticate it. The successful normal tool call is independently evidenced by the actual Copilot App session, not by that SDK session. The successful project URL and all private identifiers are intentionally omitted here.

### Expected behavior

The authorization probe should establish an MCP session correctly before issuing non-initialization requests, or otherwise use a protocol-compliant status check. It should not present a missing-session protocol error as a reason to reauthenticate a working OAuth connection.

Please preserve the response detail in the UI and distinguish a protocol/session failure from rejected credentials. A blanket rule treating every HTTP 400 as authenticated would not be appropriate.

### Current safe workaround

Keep the existing OAuth connection and use normal Copilot App sessions. Avoid unnecessary login resets triggered only by this configuration-dialog probe error. This preserves the functioning connection but does not fix the faulty probe itself.

### Privacy

No credentials, account/organization names, real project reference or URL, local paths, database contents, or raw logs are included. Configuration and connection were preserved during diagnosis.

issues.title: Permission UX: persistent user-level read access without per-repository duplication or complex policy rules

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
## Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

The permission UX is too complex for a human to configure confidently. I want one simple, permanent rule:

> Always allow reading files in or below three directories in my home directory, across sessions and repositories. Continue asking before writes, execution, or access elsewhere.

Instead, I have to understand multiple configuration files, per-location scoping, separate path and tool permission gates, different matching syntaxes, session-only versus persistent approvals, and differences between terminal CLI and SDK/IDE-hosted sessions. Selecting an approval that sounds permanent does not necessarily cover the next repository or session.

This is not just a request for another setting. It is a complaint about the complexity and discoverability of the permission rules themselves. A security model that users cannot understand or maintain encourages them to select "Allow all" simply to get work done. Repeated low-value confirmations cause approval fatigue rather than meaningful informed consent.

## Proposed solution

- Provide a documented, user-level recursive read allow-list, effective across repositories and sessions. No administrator privileges, machine-wide policy, hooks, or shell aliases should be necessary for permissions limited to my own home-directory trees.
- Support read-only grants separately from write/execute grants. Do not require granting broader access just to stop read prompts.
- Define clear approval scopes: once, this session, this repository, and all my sessions. Show the scope and persistence explicitly in the approval UI.
- Avoid duplicating identical grants for every repository. New clones and worktrees should inherit the user's directory-tree rule automatically.
- Use consistent, understandable path matching and configuration validation. Report unsupported keys rather than leaving users guessing whether a rule worked.
- Show why a request still needs confirmation and which configuration controls it, including any separate path/tool gate or host-specific restriction.
- Clearly document and expose which rules and defaults are honored in CLI versus SDK/IDE-hosted sessions. An "always" choice must not hide a narrower scope.

Illustrative desired user rule, not a claim about supported syntax:

```text
Allow Read recursively below:
  ~/repos
  ~/tmp/worktrees
  ~/.config/agents
Ask for writes, execution, and reads elsewhere.
Scope: all my sessions and repositories; persistent.
```

## Example prompts or workflows

1. Start in repository A and read shared documentation in another allowed directory without an approval prompt.
2. Start a new session in repository B and read the same documentation without repeating the approval.
3. Clone a new repository below an allowed directory, or create a linked worktree, and retain the same read permissions without editing configuration.
4. Attempt a write, command execution, or read outside the allowed trees and still receive a meaningful approval prompt unless separately authorized.

## Additional context

Observed with Copilot CLI 1.0.101 on Linux, 2026-11-20.

As a workaround, identical `allowed_directories` lists were inserted for 179 locations in `permissions-config.json`. The resulting file grew to 1,387 lines for what should be three user-level directory rules. Existing tool approvals were preserved. A terminal CLI read from an allowed location succeeded; the same read from a location without the grant was denied. The workaround requires rerunning a script after new clones and does not establish whether SDK/IDE hosts use the same grants.

I know assisted permissions exists. It is useful, but a probabilistic assessment is not a replacement for a simple deterministic read-only directory grant, and the documented `defaultPermissionMode` default does not apply to all hosting/resume modes. In my experience, Claude Code's auto mode prompts much less often and the prompts are more meaningful. Copilot should offer a usable middle ground between repeated confirmations and "Allow all".

Please simplify both the UX and the underlying permission configuration, rather than requiring customers to become experts in the schema.

issues.title: Browser extension: approval flow for Chromium browsers without a native toolbar (e.g. Vivaldi)

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

The GitHub Copilot Browser extension and Browser Use plugin are documented for Chrome and Edge 127+, and I understand other browsers are not officially supported. I'm filing this as a feature request, not a bug.

I installed the extension from the Chrome Web Store in Vivaldi (Chromium-based). The connection works and tabs can be opened, driven and screenshotted once a site is allowed. But the interactive approval prompt never appears, so any origin that is not pre-allowed fails with `APPROVAL_UNAVAILABLE` ("Browser approval is unavailable").

Cause, from the extension's service worker console:

```
[copilot-browser] Approval presentation failed Error: Browser window has no toolbar.
```

The approval flow focuses the window and calls `chrome.action.openPopup()`. Vivaldi replaces Chromium's toolbar with its own UI, so the call throws and the approval is abandoned. The browser comes to the front but nothing is shown.

### Proposed solution

When `chrome.action.openPopup()` fails, fall back to another way to ask:
- open the approval UI in a small extension page in a new tab or window (for example `toolbarPopup.html` loaded as a tab), or
- show a clear "this browser can't show approval prompts; add an allow rule in the extension settings" message instead of the generic `APPROVAL_UNAVAILABLE`.

This would help users of other Chromium browsers (Vivaldi, Brave, Arc, Opera) without changing behavior on Chrome and Edge.

### Example prompts or workflows

- "Open google.com in my browser and take a screenshot" on a site with no allow rule.
- "Open this page, fill the form and show me the result", approving the origin once.
- Approving a new origin on demand while running a longer browsing task.

### Additional context

- Workaround today: add per-origin "allow" rules on the extension settings page, or set the default permission to allow. This avoids prompts but loses per-site approval.
- Environment: Windows 11, Vivaldi (Chromium), extension 0.2.2, Browser Host and plugin 0.1.0.
- `/browser-use:doctor` reports the runtime as connected and compatible; the only warning is that the extension install can't be verified, because Vivaldi's profile isn't one it checks.
- Seen alongside the error above: `Tab cleanup failed: group not found` at finalize, which looks like a side effect of the failed approval.

issues.title: Remote control fails on GitHub Mobile and github.com: relay connect failed — "sealed value must bind this connection's challenge"

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Remote control of a local Copilot CLI session fails on every client: GitHub Mobile (Android) and github.com. The session is listed and synced, and you can read it, but you cannot control it.

- **GitHub Mobile 1.284.0 (Android):** opening the session shows only "Something went wrong". A second attempt shows "This session is no longer available".
- **github.com (`/copilot/tasks/<id>`):** the page stays on "Opening previous chat…" or "Loading session history…", then shows "We couldn't reconnect". The browser console logs:

```
[ahp-relay] relay connect failed (terminal): RPC error -32602: invalid params: sealed value must bind this connection's challenge in ctx.connection ({ challenge, nonce, issuedAt }); read the challenge from the handshake result's _meta and seal again
```

On the CLI side, nothing fails visibly, even with `--log-level all`. The log shows `client initialized` (protocol_version 1.0.0) and the host sending one AHP frame back through AWPS, then nothing else. It looks like the web and mobile relay clients are not sealing the handshake challenge that the host now requires. The error says the client should "read the challenge from the handshake result's _meta and seal again".

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.112. The same error occurs with 1.0.110, started with `--no-auto-update`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Enable remote control: `"remoteSessions": true` in `~/.copilot/settings.json`. The enterprise policy "Store local sessions in the Cloud" is set to "View and control from cloud".
2. Start `copilot` interactively and send a message. The CLI prints `Remote access enabled - registered as "Copilot CLI on <host>"`.
3. Run `/remote on`. The CLI prints `Sharing this session through Mission Control environment <id>`, with `Local listener: disabled (WPS-only)`.
4. Open the session from GitHub Mobile, or from the Copilot sessions list on github.com.
5. Mobile shows "Something went wrong". The web shows "We couldn't reconnect", and the console shows the `sealed value must bind this connection's challenge` error above.

### Expected behavior

The remote client completes the relay handshake and can control the session: send prompts and approve tools.

### Additional context

- OS: Linux x86_64 (WSL2, Ubuntu), bash. Native standalone CLI install.
- Account: Copilot Business seat assigned directly by an enterprise. The user is not a member of any organization. `GET /copilot_internal/user` returns `cli_remote_control_enabled: true`.
- Working directory is a git repository hosted outside GitHub, so the session shows under "No repository". It fails the same way in new sessions.
- The CLI log also shows `Mission Control rejected the session id; retrying with a Mission Control minted id` at each session start, and `device managed settings updated {"remote_control":false}`. No MDM or managed policy is present: `device MDM: no policy present on this device`, `server policy: none for this account (404)`.
- Viewing works. The session transcript renders on github.com for the export entry, with the message "Continue this session where it was started". Only the control (relay) connection fails.

issues.title: Sessions become unrevivable: a stale `inuse.<pid>.lock` from a crashed host is never reclaimed on open

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Several saved sessions became impossible to reopen ("crashed out / unrevivable"). On investigation the **session data was not corrupt** — the append-only `events.jsonl` replayed cleanly and the engine logged a successful resume. The sessions were blocked by **runtime/lifecycle issues**, not data loss.

The primary cause is **stale lock handling**. Each live session writes `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/inuse.<pid>.lock`. When the owning `copilot --server` process exits uncleanly (crash, force-quit, OS kill), the lock file is left behind. On the next open, the session is treated as in-use / unrevivable instead of checking whether that PID is still alive.

Scanning one local store, **14 of 184 sessions (~8%)** carried a fault signature; **8 held an `inuse.<pid>.lock` whose PID was dead**. Deleting the stale lock made each session openable again, and the app then spawned a fresh host and resumed normally — confirming the data was fine and only the lock blocked recovery.

Three related lifecycle defects compound the impact (details under Additional context):
1. **Orphaned engine host after a failed UI attach** — the engine resumes but no session host registers, leaving a live server holding the lock (which then becomes defect #1 on the next attempt).
2. **MCP OAuth timeouts block session readiness** — resume stalls ~5 minutes on `OAuth callback timeout` before the session is interactive, so users abort.
3. **Unbounded `events.jsonl`** makes replay hang on large/old sessions (appears to overlap #4251).

### Affected version

`1.0.83` (`copilot --server --stdio --no-auto-update`)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Primary defect (stale lock not reclaimed):

1. Open a session, then hard-kill its `copilot --server` process to simulate a crash / force-quit (`kill -9 <pid>`).
2. Confirm `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/inuse.<pid>.lock` remains, now pointing at a dead PID.
3. Try to reopen the session → it does not revive.
4. `rm` the stale lock file → the session reopens and resumes cleanly (a fresh host is spawned and `events.jsonl` replays without error).

### Expected behavior

On open, if the lock's PID is dead or a zombie, the app should **reclaim the session automatically** rather than treating it as in-use. A liveness check combined with a PID start-time comparison avoids the classic PID-reuse race. Recoverable work should never be gated behind a leftover lock file that only manual filesystem surgery can clear.

### Additional context

- **OS:** macOS · **shell:** zsh

**Defect 2 — orphaned engine host after a failed UI attach.** Engine log from a single resume: the host never registers, yet the engine reports the session resumed, so the process lingers as an orphan holding the lock:
```
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::pending_request_flow] pending-request event was not delivered to the session host
          {"error":"GenericFailure, no session host is registered for session <id>"}
...
[INFO]  Resumed session: <id>        (logged repeatedly)
```
Suggested fix: tie the engine host's lifetime to successful UI host registration; if registration fails/times out, tear the host down and release the lock.

**Defect 3 — MCP OAuth timeouts block resume (~5 min).** With several MCP servers configured, resume stalls until interactive OAuth flows time out. MCP init begins at `20:27`, first hard failures at `20:32`:
```
[ERROR] [rust:mcp_engine::session_authorizer] OAuth login failed after returning its authorization URL
        {"server_name":"...","error":"OAuth callback timeout"}
```
During that window the session looks hung and users abort — observed as sessions whose only recent events were `resume → abort (user_initiated) → shutdown`, twice in a row. Suggested fix: make MCP init lazy / non-blocking; never gate session interactivity on MCP OAuth.

**Defect 4 — unbounded `events.jsonl`.** The append-only log grows without bound; worst local session reached **38.6 MB / ~13k events with 42 compaction cycles** (173 re-injected `system.message` events ≈ 10.7 MB). Reopening replays the whole log, so large sessions hang on open even though nothing is corrupt. This looks like the same root cause as #4251; noting here for linkage. Suggested fix: snapshot-and-truncate the event log at compaction so replay cost stays bounded.

**Possibly related:** #4020 (session falsely "already in use by another client"), #4098 (truncated/concatenated events on resume), #4138 (resume compaction hangs), #4251 (large-session resume OOM/hang).

All four are addressable without changing the on-disk event format. Defects 1–2 turn recoverable work into apparent data loss; 3–4 make large/older sessions feel dead on open.

issues.title: ACP: support an ask_user / ask_question style extension method
issues.body:
## Summary

Please consider adding ACP support for an `ask_user` / `ask_question` style extension method so custom ACP clients can surface clarifying questions and return structured answers to Copilot CLI.

Today ACP support in Copilot CLI includes `session/request_permission`, but that only covers allow/deny tool approvals.

## Why this would help

Custom ACP frontends can already render streaming messages, plans, tool calls, and permission prompts. The missing piece is a first-class way for the agent to ask the human a question and wait for a reply.

That makes it hard to support workflows that depend on interactive clarification, even though GitHub Copilot itself supports this kind of host-side interaction in some environments.

A small extension method would make custom ACP frontends much more capable without requiring each client to invent incompatible workarounds.

## Suggestion

A Copilot-specific ACP extension would already be helpful, for example something like:

- request method: `copilot/ask_user` (or similar)
- params:
  - `sessionId`
  - `question`
  - optional `choices: string[]`
  - optional `allowFreeform` / `allow_freeform: boolean`
- result:
  - `{ outcome: "answered", answer: string }`
  - or `{ outcome: "cancelled" }`

Cursor has `cursor/ask_question` Source: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/acp#cursor-extension-methods

issues.title: Option for 1-hour prompt cache TTL for Claude models (5-minute cache expires during normal interactive use)

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Claude prompt caching in Copilot CLI appears to use Anthropic's default **5-minute** cache TTL. In normal interactive use (read the answer, think, write the next prompt) gaps of more than 5 minutes are common, so the full conversation gets re-written to cache on almost every turn instead of being read from cache.

I measured this with `copilot -p` / `--resume` in fresh sessions (~35k-token context), sending a follow-up after different idle gaps, and reading `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_write_tokens` from the local session usage data. Two independent runs gave identical results:

| Idle gap | Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 | GPT-6.1-sol / GPT-6-sol / GPT-5.6-sol |
|---|---|---|
| 2 min | ~95% cache read | ~95% cache read |
| 11 min | **0% cache read** (~100% cache write) | ~95% cache read |
| ~85 min | 0% | 0% |

My broader session history (Claude 5.x, CLI) shows the same pattern: 98% cache read for gaps < 4 min vs ~1% for gaps of 6–60 min.

Anthropic supports a 1-hour TTL (`cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}`). VS Code Copilot Chat already has experimental settings for this (`github.copilot.chat.anthropic.promptCaching.extendedTtl` / `extendedTtlMessages`), though they currently miss Claude 5.x models (microsoft/vscode#340830, fix in microsoft/vscode#340831). Copilot CLI has no equivalent option.

### Proposed solution

Add an option in Copilot CLI (config setting and/or env var) to use the 1-hour cache TTL for Claude models, covering the Claude 5.x family. Consider making it the default for interactive sessions, since the higher write cost (2x vs 1.25x) is usually recovered after one or two follow-up turns with a pause longer than 5 minutes.

### Example prompts or workflows

Any interactive session with a large context where the user pauses longer than 5 minutes between prompts (reviewing diffs, testing changes, meetings).

### Additional context

- Related: #3808 (prompt caching for Claude), #4724 (auto-compact on idle aligned to cache TTL)
- Triggered by this discussion: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1xauf3s/anthropic_caching_is_this_a_bad_joke/
- Tested with Copilot CLI 1.0.102-1 on Windows.

issues.title: Agent Plugins 1.0: `.instructions.md` files and `applyTo` frontmatter in `com.github.copilot/rules/` are silently ignored

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When packaging a plugin using the **Agent Plugins 1.0.0** format (`"$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json"`), Copilot CLI loads skills (`skills/`), MCP servers (`mcp.json`), custom agents (`com.github.copilot/agents/`), hooks (`com.github.copilot/hooks/hooks.json`), and LSP servers (`com.github.copilot/lsp.json`), **but silently ignores standard GitHub Copilot `.instructions.md` files placed in `com.github.copilot/rules/`**.

According to the [CLI plugin reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference#components) and the [VS Code Agent plugin authoring reference](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/agent-plugin-reference), `com.github.copilot/rules/` is the Copilot-specific extension directory for plugin rules/instructions. Across the Copilot ecosystem (`.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`, `~/.copilot/instructions/*.instructions.md`, and VS Code Agent Plugins), the standard Copilot rule format is `*.instructions.md` with YAML frontmatter (`description`, `applyTo`).

Through black-box testing on Copilot CLI `1.0.109`, two cumulative issues prevent `.instructions.md` plugin rules from working across VS Code and Copilot CLI:

1. **`.instructions.md` (and `.md`) files in `com.github.copilot/rules/` are completely ignored.**
   Copilot CLI only discovers files ending in `.mdc` inside `com.github.copilot/rules/`. Files ending in `.instructions.md` or `.md` do not appear in `/env`, `/instructions`, or `copilot instruction list`, are never injected into the prompt, and produce no warning even with `--log-level debug`. Meanwhile, VS Code loads `.instructions.md` from the exact same `com.github.copilot/rules/` folder.
2. **Copilot frontmatter (`applyTo`) is ignored in plugin rules, and `alwaysApply` semantics are inverted for glob-scoped rules.**
   Even after renaming a file from `.instructions.md` to `.mdc`:
   - `applyTo` is ignored; Copilot CLI only parses `globs` (and requires a non-empty `description`), whereas VS Code parses `applyTo` and ignores `globs`.
   - Omitting `alwaysApply` or setting `alwaysApply: false` on a glob-scoped rule (e.g., `globs: ["**/*.yaml"]`) causes `copilot instruction list --json` to report `"defaultDisabled": true` (`0/1 enabled` in `/instructions`). As a result, **glob-scoped rules with `alwaysApply: false` (or omitted) never fire out of the box** when matching files are read unless the user manually enables them in `/instructions` in every session.
   - Counter-intuitively, a rule must set **both** `alwaysApply: true` **and** `globs: [...]` to be enabled by default (`"defaultDisabled": false`) while still scoping activation to matching files rather than injecting globally at startup.


Also, it seems there is another issue with instructions on command like :  **`copilot --plugin-dir <dir> instruction list` ignores `--plugin-dir`.**
   Unlike `copilot --plugin-dir <dir> skill list` (and interactive `/env` / `/instructions`), the `instruction list` subcommand ignores `--plugin-dir` and always prints `No instruction sources found.` unless the plugin is installed into `$COPILOT_HOME`.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.109

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Run the following self-contained reproduction script in an isolated `COPILOT_HOME`:

```bash
rm -rf /tmp/repro-plugin /tmp/repro-copilot-home
mkdir -p /tmp/repro-plugin/com.github.copilot/rules /tmp/repro-copilot-home

cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/repro-plugin/plugin.json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json",
  "name": "repro-plugin",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Minimal reproducer for plugin instructions"
}
EOF

# 1. Standard Copilot .instructions.md file -> SILENTLY IGNORED
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/repro-plugin/com.github.copilot/rules/standard-copilot.instructions.md
---
name: "Standard Copilot Rule"
description: "Standard Copilot instruction file using applyTo"
applyTo: "**/*.yaml"
---
Follow standard YAML conventions.
EOF

# 2. .mdc with globs and alwaysApply: false -> DISCOVERED, BUT DISABLED BY DEFAULT
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/repro-plugin/com.github.copilot/rules/mdc-glob-disabled.mdc
---
description: "MDC rule with globs and alwaysApply false"
globs: ["**/*.yaml"]
alwaysApply: false
---
Follow MDC YAML conventions (disabled by default).
EOF

# 3. .mdc with globs and alwaysApply: true -> ENABLED BY DEFAULT & SCOPED TO GLOBS
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/repro-plugin/com.github.copilot/rules/mdc-glob-enabled.mdc
---
description: "MDC rule with globs and alwaysApply true"
globs: ["**/*.yaml"]
alwaysApply: true
---
Follow MDC YAML conventions (enabled).
EOF
```

#### Step A — Test `instruction list` with `--plugin-dir` (Bug 4)

```bash
COPILOT_HOME=/tmp/repro-copilot-home copilot --plugin-dir /tmp/repro-plugin instruction list
```

Actual output:
```text
No instruction sources found.
```
*(Whereas launching interactively with `copilot --plugin-dir /tmp/repro-plugin` and running `/env` or `/instructions` **does** find the `.mdc` files, and `copilot --plugin-dir <dir> skill list` honors `--plugin-dir`.)*

#### Step B — Install the plugin and inspect `copilot instruction list --json` (Bugs 1 & 2)

```bash
COPILOT_HOME=/tmp/repro-copilot-home copilot plugin install /tmp/repro-plugin
COPILOT_HOME=/tmp/repro-copilot-home copilot instruction list --json
```

Actual output:
```json
[
  {
    "id": "plugin-rule/repro-plugin:mdc-glob-disabled",
    "label": "repro-plugin: mdc-glob-disabled",
    "description": "MDC rule with globs and alwaysApply false",
    "location": "plugin",
    "type": "plugin",
    "sourcePath": "/tmp/repro-copilot-home/installed-plugins/_direct/repro-plugin-xxxx/com.github.copilot/rules/mdc-glob-disabled.mdc",
    "defaultDisabled": true,
    "applyTo": [
      "**/*.yaml"
    ]
  },
  {
    "id": "plugin-rule/repro-plugin:mdc-glob-enabled",
    "label": "repro-plugin: mdc-glob-enabled",
    "description": "MDC rule with globs and alwaysApply true",
    "location": "plugin",
    "type": "plugin",
    "sourcePath": "/tmp/repro-copilot-home/installed-plugins/_direct/repro-plugin-xxxx/com.github.copilot/rules/mdc-glob-enabled.mdc",
    "defaultDisabled": false,
    "applyTo": [
      "**/*.yaml"
    ]
  }
]
```

Notice that:
- `standard-copilot.instructions.md` is completely missing from the discovered sources.
- `mdc-glob-disabled.mdc` has `"defaultDisabled": true`, so in a session (`/instructions`) it starts unchecked (`•`) and does not trigger when reading a `.yaml` file.
- `mdc-glob-enabled.mdc` has `"defaultDisabled": false` and `"applyTo": ["**/*.yaml"]` (mapped from `globs`, while an actual `applyTo` key in frontmatter is ignored).

### Summary of observed behavior matrix

| File in `com.github.copilot/rules/` | Frontmatter | VS Code behavior | Copilot CLI `1.0.109` behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rule.instructions.md` | `description` + `applyTo: "**"` | Loaded (global) | **Silently ignored** |
| `rule.instructions.md` | `description` + `applyTo: "**/*.yaml"` | Loaded (glob-scoped) | **Silently ignored** |
| `rule.mdc` | `description` + `applyTo: "**/*.yaml"` | Loaded (glob-scoped) | Discovered, **`applyTo` ignored**, disabled by default (`defaultDisabled: true`) |
| `rule.mdc` | `description` + `globs: ["**/*.yaml"]` + `alwaysApply: false` (or omitted) | Loaded, **`globs` ignored** | Discovered, **disabled by default** (`0/1 enabled` in `/instructions`; never triggers unless manually toggled per session) |

### Expected behavior

1. **Support `.instructions.md` natively in `com.github.copilot/rules/`**: Since `com.github.copilot/` is GitHub Copilot's own client extension namespace in Agent Plugins 1.0, Copilot CLI should discover `*.instructions.md` files alongside `*.mdc` (matching `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`, `~/.copilot/instructions/*.instructions.md`, and VS Code's plugin loader).
2. **Support Copilot frontmatter (`applyTo`) and intuitive activation defaults**:
   - Accept `applyTo` (string or array) in addition to `globs` so a single `.instructions.md` file works identically in both VS Code and Copilot CLI without duplicating metadata.
   - Treat glob-scoped rules (`applyTo` / `globs` without `alwaysApply: false`) as enabled for pattern-matching by default, rather than disabled for the whole session unless `alwaysApply: true` is also set. When `applyTo` is `"**"` or `"*"`, treat the rule as session-wide.
3. **Honor `--plugin-dir` in `copilot instruction list`**: Match `copilot skill list` and interactive sessions so plugin authors can validate `com.github.copilot/rules/` during local development without reinstalling the plugin on every edit.
4. **Document the `com.github.copilot/rules/` file format and frontmatter contract** in the [CLI plugin reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference#components).

### Additional context

- **OS:** Linux (`x86_64`, Ubuntu / WSL2)
- **Shell:** `bash`
- **Impact & current workaround:** As VS Code deprecates its legacy Local harness in favor of the shared Copilot harness, organizations migrating shared engineering harnesses to **Agent Plugins 1.0** need a single plugin package to deliver skills, MCP servers, agents, hooks, LSPs, and `.instructions.md` rules across both VS Code and Copilot CLI. Currently, the only way to avoid duplicating every rule file in `com.github.copilot/rules/` is to include both `applyTo` and `globs` + `alwaysApply: true` in each `.instructions.md` frontmatter and commit relative `<name>.mdc -> <name>.instructions.md` symlinks alongside them (which breaks on Windows checkouts when `core.symlinks=false`).

issues.title: CIMD declares callback port 33418 but Copilot CLI uses an ephemeral port

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Copilot CLI’s Client ID Metadata Document declares a fixed loopback callback port, but the CLI sends a different ephemeral port in the OAuth authorization request.

Client metadata: https://github.com/copilot/cli/client-metadata.json

   ```json
   {
     "client_id": "https://github.com/copilot/cli/client-metadata.json",
     "application_type": "native",
     "redirect_uris": [
       "http://127.0.0.1:33418/"
     ]
   }
```

The authorization request generated by Copilot CLI instead contains a callback such as:

 ```text
   redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:60005/
 ```

My authorization server rejects the request with:

 ```text
   unauthorized_client: Callback URL mismatch.
   http://127.0.0.1:60005/ is not in the list of allowed callback URLs
 ```

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.83

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

 1. Configure a remote MCP server protected by an Auth0 authorization server.
 2. Register Copilot CLI in Auth0 using: https://github.com/copilot/cli/client-metadata.json
 3. Add the remote MCP server to Copilot CLI.
 4. Start authentication.
 5. Inspect the generated /authorize request.

 The request uses an ephemeral loopback port rather than the 33418 port declared in the metadata document.

### Expected behavior

The redirect URI used by Copilot CLI should be compatible with its published metadata.

 Either:

 1. Copilot CLI should bind to the declared callback:

    ```text
      http://127.0.0.1:33418/
    ```

 2. The metadata should declare a portless loopback callback compatible with ephemeral ports:

    ```json
      "redirect_uris": [
        "http://127.0.0.1/"
      ]
    ```

There should not be a requirement for every MCP server operator or Copilot user to configure a callback-port override.

### Additional context

- Operating system: macOS 26.5.1
- MCP transport: Streamable HTTP
- Authorization server: Auth0
- Client registration: Client ID Metadata Document

For reference, Claude Code also uses an ephemeral loopback but its metadata document declares port-less loopback callbacks:

 ```json
   "redirect_uris": [
     "http://localhost/callback",
     "http://127.0.0.1/callback"
   ]
 ```

The same Auth0 authorization server accepts Claude Code’s runtime callback while rejecting Copilot CLI’s callback because Copilot’s metadata explicitly pins port 33418.

Claude's metadata: https://claude.ai/oauth/claude-code-client-metadata

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Summary

WorkIQ authentication fails when GitHub Copilot CLI runs inside WSL2.

The same WorkIQ authentication flow succeeds when GitHub Copilot CLI runs natively on Windows. The failure occurs only when Copilot CLI runs inside WSL2.

After completing Microsoft Entra sign-in, the loopback callback includes valid `code` and `state` parameters but returns `404 Not Found`.

## Environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI: `1.0.80`
- WorkIQ plugin: `2.0.0`
- WSL: `2.7.1.11`
- Kernel: `6.1.18.3-2`
- Windows: `10.0.26200.9106`
- Ubuntu: `26.04`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `copilot` inside WSL.
2. Enable the WorkIQ plugin.
3. Trigger a WorkIQ tool call, causing authentication to start.
4. Open the Microsoft Entra authorization URL displayed by Copilot and complete sign-in.
5. The browser redirects to:

   ```text http://127.0.0.1:12798/?code=...&state=...```

**Actual behavior**

The callback URL returns:

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: text/plain

Not Found

Additional observations:

• The callback includes both  code  and  state .
• The callback is reachable from Windows and WSL.
•  ss -ltnp 'sport = :12798'  shows that  copilot  itself owns  127.0.0.1:12798 .
• Calling the complete callback URL from WSL with  curl  also returns  404 Not Found .
• Restarting Copilot and shutting down WSL do not resolve the issue.
• Clearing the persisted WorkIQ OAuth configuration/cache does not change the behavior.

Expected behavior

When running under WSL2, Copilot CLI should handle the WorkIQ OAuth callback as it does when running natively on Windows: associate the valid  code  and  state  with the pending OAuth transaction and exchange the authorization code successfully.

Related context

This may be related to WSL support in  microsoft/work-iq#15 , but differs from callback-reachability issues: here the loopback callback is reachable and handled by the Copilot process itself, which returns  404 .

2. Enable the WorkIQ plugin.
3. Trigger a WorkIQ tool call, causing authentication to start.
4. Open the Microsoft Entra authorization URL displayed by Copilot and complete sign-in.
5. The browser redirects to:

   ```text http://127.0.0.1:12798/?code=...&state=...````

Actual behavior

The callback URL returns:

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: text/plain

Not Found

### Expected behavior

When running under WSL2, Copilot CLI should handle the WorkIQ OAuth callback as it does when running natively on Windows: associate the valid  code  and  state  with the pending OAuth transaction and exchange the authorization code successfully.

labels.name: area:platform-windows
