issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When I try to uninstall the installed `workiq` plugin on Windows, the uninstall fails with an access-denied error.

The UI reports:

```text
Uninstalling plugin "workiq"...
Failed to uninstall plugin: Request plugins.uninstall failed with message: Failed to uninstall plugin: 拒绝访问。 (os error 5)
```

`拒绝访问` means "Access is denied". I asked the agent to inspect which processes were keeping the plugin resources in use. It found that Copilot CLI itself still had the plugin's MCP server running and holding those resources, preventing the uninstall.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI `1.0.96-2`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Observed:
1. Have the `workiq` plugin installed on Windows.
2. Request plugin uninstall through the Copilot plugin UI (`plugins.uninstall`).
3. The operation fails with `Access is denied (os error 5)`.

After the failure, I asked the agent to check process usage. It identified the CLI's own running MCP server for the plugin as the resource holder.

### Expected behavior

Uninstall should complete without requiring the user to terminate the CLI manually. If the CLI owns an active MCP server or other resources for the plugin, it should stop/dispose those resources and release relevant handles before removing the plugin files.

If another process prevents removal, report the affected path and actionable recovery guidance rather than only the generic OS error. A failed uninstall should not leave inconsistent plugin registration or partially deleted files.

### Additional context

- Operating system: Windows.
- Plugin: `workiq`.
- Operation: `plugins.uninstall`.
- Process inspection by the agent identified Copilot CLI's own running plugin MCP server as keeping the plugin resources in use.
- Related reports: #4095 and #4570 describe similar access-denied failures involving plugin directory handles on Windows. This report records the uninstall failure and asks that CLI-owned MCP server teardown also be checked; the failures may share a root cause.

issues.title: MCP OAuth login fails with HTTP 400 when server rejects MCP-Protocol-Version (no fallback to older version)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary

Logging in to a remote HTTP MCP server fails with:

```
Authentication failed
jira: RPC error -32603: Request session.mcp.oauth.login failed with message: MCP request failed: MCP server probe returned HTTP 400 Bad Request
```

The server rejects the client's protocol version with HTTP 400. The normal connection path handles this by retrying with legacy `initialize`, but the OAuth login probe does not retry. So the browser OAuth flow never starts and the user cannot log in at all.

## Environment

- GitHub Copilot app 1.1.26 (commit 5ab79c8), Windows x86_64
- Copilot CLI runtime 1.0.90-0
- Started after the app updated to 1.1.26. Login against the same server worked on the previous version.
- MCP server config (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`):
  ```json
  { "jira": { "type": "http", "url": "https://jira.mcp.spiris.ai/mcp/p/common" } }
  ```

## Server behavior (reproduced with curl)

The server only accepts `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-03-26`, or no header at all:

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| POST/GET, no `MCP-Protocol-Version` header | `401` + valid `WWW-Authenticate` with `resource_metadata` |
| `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-03-26` | `401` + valid `WWW-Authenticate` |
| `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18` | `400 {"error":"unsupported_protocol_version","message":"Unsupported MCP protocol version: 2025-06-18"}` |
| `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28` | `400 {"error":"unsupported_protocol_version","message":"Unsupported MCP protocol version: 2026-07-28"}` |

The OAuth metadata is otherwise correct. `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/...` and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` both return 200. Dynamic client registration also succeeds.

## Logs

The connection path falls back as expected:

```
[WARNING] [rust:mcp::client] server/discover failed; retrying with legacy initialize {"error":"unexpected server response: HTTP 400 Bad Request: {\"error\":\"unsupported_protocol_version\",\"message\":\"Unsupported MCP protocol version: 2026-07-28\"}"}
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::mcp::agent_host] HTTP 401 challenge (WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="jirast-mcp", resource_metadata="https://jira.mcp.spiris.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/p/common", ...) {"server":"jira"}
[WARNING] [rust:mcp_engine::session_authorizer] MCP OAuth authorization failed; reporting the server as needing auth {"server":"jira","error":"Browser-based OAuth required for https://jira.mcp.spiris.ai/mcp/p/common"}
```

When the user then starts the login (`session.mcp.oauth.login`), the probe gets the 400 and the login aborts with no fallback.

## Expected

The OAuth login probe should handle a 400 `unsupported_protocol_version` the same way the connection path does. It should retry with an older or legacy protocol version, or without the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header. That retry gets the 401 challenge, and browser OAuth can then start.

## Actual

The login fails right away with `MCP server probe returned HTTP 400 Bad Request`. There's no workaround on the client side: clearing `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config` and restarting doesn't help.

## Side note

Before the reset, `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config` had collected 167 orphaned `<hash>.tokens.json` files. They had no matching client config and no refresh token, and they covered about a month of sessions, all for one server. Possibly a separate token-cache cleanup issue.

issues.title: /mcp <server-name> fails due to case sensitive matching

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

`/mcp <server-name>` finds a server name only with an exact-case match. For a server with the name `MyServer`, `/mcp myserver` and `/mcp myServer` fail with `Server "myserver" not found. Use /mcp to open the MCP server list.`

### Proposed solution

Make the server-name lookup case-insensitive for the `/mcp` slash commands (`/mcp <name>`, `/mcp edit`, `/mcp enable`, `/mcp disable`) and for `--disable-mcp-server`.

1. Try the exact-case match first.
2. If no exact match exists, use the one server whose name matches without case.
3. If two or more servers match without case, show the error with the list of matching names.

This change helps users who do not remember the exact case of a server name. Brand names with mixed case cause this error frequently.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. A plugin declares the server `MyServer`. The user types `/mcp myserver` to sign in again. Today the command fails. With this change, it opens the detail view for `MyServer`.
2. A user starts `copilot --disable-mcp-server myserver`. Today the CLI does not disable the `MyServer` server. With this change, it disables that server.
3. A user types `/mcp disable MYSERVER`. With this change, the CLI disables `MyServer`.

### Additional context

- Version: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.91 on Windows.
- Workaround: run `/mcp` with no name, then select the server from the list.
- Related: #1062. That fix made `/mcp enable` and `/mcp disable` reject unknown names. Thus a name with the wrong case now gets the "not found" error.

issues.title: Stricter exit code when MCP servers fail to start (CI / agent use)

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

The CLI exits 0 in CI even when the agent had zero tools available at startup or terminated before producing any output. In Actions / CI consumers (Agentic Workflows in our case) the exit code is the contract; a green exit on a no-tools run looks like success and downstream `if: success()` jobs run as if the agent worked.

### Proposed solution

Make `copilot` exit non-zero in this failure mode so CI consumers can trust the exit code. Two shapes work for us, pick whichever fits the CLI's design:

- `CI=true`-conditional behavior: when `CI=true`, exit non-zero if any configured MCP server fails to start. Matches the convention `npm`, `yarn`, `jest` already follow for stricter machine-readable defaults; preserves the interactive UX.
- Explicit flag (e.g. `--strict-mcp-start`): clearer opt-in, easier to roll out without changing existing behavior.

Either way, the benefit is that any CI consumer (not just AW) can rely on the exit code as the primary signal instead of parsing logs after the fact.


### Example prompts or workflows

1. **MCP allowlist enforcement fails closed in a sandboxed runner.** v1.0.22 enabled enforcement that calls `https://api.github.com/copilot/mcp_registry` directly at startup. In Agentic Workflows the agent container has no auth token (all `api.github.com` access flows through an api-proxy sidecar) and `api.github.com` isn't on the egress allowlist, so the request is blocked, the CLI fails closed on every MCP server, and the agent runs with an empty tool surface. v1.0.22 still exited 0, the Actions job came back green, and we didn't detect the regression — a customer did ([gh-aw#25550](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/25550), [gh-aw#25680](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/25680)).
2. **Broader shape of the same ask:** any configured MCP server failing to start (config error, network blip, server-side outage, partial allowlist mismatch). We haven't been bitten by a partial-MCP-failure scenario yet, but losing one MCP server can degrade the agent's tool surface in subtle ways, and we'd rather have a non-zero exit than silently run with fewer tools.


### Additional context

- Customer reports from the v1.0.22 incident: [gh-aw#25550](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/25550), [gh-aw#25680](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/25680)
- Customer-facing run showing the silent-success pattern: [`devantler-tech/ksail` run 24270819213](https://github.com/devantler-tech/ksail/actions/runs/24270819213)
- Kusto fingerprint we used after the fact: skipped `detection` jobs in AW (whose `if:` checks the agent job's result) jumped from a baseline of 8 to 40 per day to 2,569 on 04-10. Distinct repos jumped from 10 to 20 per day to ~438. That signal was only visible in our telemetry, not in the exit code.

### Describe the bug

On macOS, a secret configured for a stdio MCP server using Copilot CLI's `${secret:...}` placeholder does not appear to reach the spawned server process.

The same server works when the credential is provided as a normal process environment variable. When launched by Copilot CLI using the secret placeholder, authentication fails because the server behaves as if the environment variable is unset.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.88.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

_No response_

### Expected behavior

1. Store a test credential using Copilot CLI's MCP secret mechanism.
2. Configure a stdio MCP server with an environment entry like `"API_TOKEN": "${secret:example-mcp/env/API_TOKEN/v}"`.
3. Start the MCP server through Copilot CLI and call a tool that checks whether `API_TOKEN` is set.
4. Start the same server outside Copilot CLI with `API_TOKEN` set directly in its process environment.

## Actual behaviour

The server launched by Copilot CLI behaves as if `API_TOKEN` is missing. The same server works when `API_TOKEN` is set directly in the process environment.

### Additional context

- OS: macOS 26.5 (25F71)
- Server transport: stdio
- The secret was present in the configured secret store.
- The issue persisted after refreshing the secret and restarting Copilot CLI.
- The report intentionally excludes the server implementation, service
  endpoints, secret values, and internal configuration paths.

labels.name: area:terminal-rendering
labels.description: Display and rendering: flickering, scrolling, line wrapping, output formatting

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When I use `/ask` or its `/btw` alias, answer text appears and then disappears without me pressing Escape or otherwise dismissing the response. The answer box stays open but becomes blank.

This is different from the expected disappearance after explicitly closing the temporary answer panel.

### Affected version

`1.0.83-5`

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Run Copilot CLI in the VS Code integrated terminal on Windows.
2. In an existing conversation, submit `/ask <a short text-only question>` or `/btw <a short text-only question>`.
3. Allow the answer to render and leave the panel open without dismissing it.
4. Observe that the answer text can disappear while the panel remains open.

This has happened repeatedly in this environment, but a deterministic minimal reproduction has not yet been isolated. It is not established whether a resumed conversation or a concurrently running main task is required.

### Expected behavior

Once answer text is displayed, it should remain readable in the open panel until I explicitly dismiss it. Finishing the response should not erase already displayed text.

### Additional context

- OS/architecture: Windows, x64.
- Terminal: VS Code integrated terminal.
- Related closed report: github/copilot-cli#3759 describes blank `/ask` responses on resumed chats in version `1.0.61`. Linking as possibly related, not as a confirmed duplicate or regression.

**Suspected cause, not confirmed:** Completion handling may replace an already streamed answer with an empty value when the final answer payload is empty or missing. A component-level simulation reproduces that failure mode, but the final payload from an actual failing live query has not been captured.

**Local workaround status:** The symptom was observed before modifying the installation. A temporary local UI workaround was subsequently applied to retain displayed and buffered streamed text when the final answer is empty or missing, while still using a nonempty final answer when provided. Its effectiveness against the original live symptom has not yet been confirmed; it is not an upstream fix or proof of the suspected cause.

issues.title: Windows: /upgrade on a winget install replaces the WinGet\Links alias and leaves winget/Add-Remove Programs on the old version

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:installation
labels.description: Installing, updating, versioning, PATH setup, and binary distribution

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows, when Copilot CLI is installed with winget (`GitHub.Copilot`) and then updated with the built-in updater (`/upgrade`), the update bypasses winget. The new binary is written over winget's command alias instead of the winget package, so the install record is never updated:

- `winget list` and Add/Remove Programs keep reporting the old version, and winget offers an "upgrade" to the version that is already running.
- Software inventory tooling that relies on install records (Uninstall registry keys / winget) reports the wrong version.
- The winget package folder and the binary that actually runs are out of sync.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.91 (updated from 1.0.89 via `/upgrade`)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Install with winget: `winget install --id GitHub.Copilot -e` (here this installed 1.0.89).
2. Run `copilot` and use `/upgrade`.
3. `copilot --version` reports `1.0.91`.
4. `winget list --id GitHub.Copilot` still shows the old version, with the running version offered as an update:
   ```
   Name        Id             Version Available Source
   Copilot CLI GitHub.Copilot v1.0.89 v1.0.91   winget
   ```
5. The Uninstall entry `HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\GitHub.Copilot_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe` still has `DisplayVersion = v1.0.89`.
6. Compare the two binaries:
   ```powershell
   $links = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\WinGet\Links\copilot.exe"
   $pkg   = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\GitHub.Copilot_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe\copilot.exe"
   (Get-Item $links).LinkType                      # empty: no longer a symlink
   (Get-Item $links).VersionInfo.ProductVersion    # 1.0.91
   (Get-Item $pkg).VersionInfo.ProductVersion      # 1.0.89 (unchanged)
   ```
   The other winget portable packages in `WinGet\Links` are still symbolic links into `WinGet\Packages`; for Copilot CLI the link has been replaced by a regular file containing the new version.

### Expected behavior

Either of:

- The updater detects a winget-managed install and defers to the package manager (for example: "Copilot CLI was installed with winget; run `winget upgrade GitHub.Copilot`"), or
- The update is applied in a way that keeps the winget install consistent (package folder, `WinGet\Links` alias and install record reflect the running version).

The same question likely applies to other package-manager installs (Homebrew, npm) where a self-update can diverge from what the package manager reports.

### Additional context

- OS: Windows 11, x64
- Shell: PowerShell 7
- Install method: winget (portable package, user scope)
- The old 1.0.89 binary remains in the winget package folder; only the `WinGet\Links\copilot.exe` alias was replaced.

- Installing a plugin that contains a link to a device such as /dev/zero or to a named pipe no longer hangs; the install fails right away and names the file
- SDK clients connected through --ui-server can resume a session the CLI has not loaded, instead of waiting forever and blocking later session loads
- MCP sign-in completes when you manually open the authorization URL if the CLI cannot launch a browser
- Deleting or pruning a session now removes the MCP OAuth access tokens it saved in the system keychain or token files, instead of leaving one item per session and server behind
- Single-setting writes now refuse to overwrite malformed settings.json files and report when changes are not saved.
- The /subagents table highlights the correct agent when switching between sessions in the same folder
- Rewinding to a prompt whose image or file attachment was moved or deleted no longer re-attaches it silently: the attachment is left out and a warning names the missing file.
- MCP servers that provide only prompts or resources stay connected and appear without errors in /mcp
- grep and rg commands no longer request path access for search patterns passed with option values
- A URL approved for the rest of the session is no longer asked for again after /cd when another CLI process has saved a new allowed URL in the meantime
- A sessionStart prompt hook or -i prompt is no longer silently skipped when sign-in finishes while a repository startup prompt is running
- /session prune says it has started before it deletes, and a second prune run while the first is still deleting no longer reports the first one's sessions as its own
- The MCP tool cache now removes entries older than 14 days when it writes, so sessions started in many different working directories no longer grow it without limit
- /user switch completes account selection after switching sessions while the account picker is open
- Startup and resume avoid premature MCP tool and organization plugin-check warnings, and organization settings initialization notices no longer repeat or replay from history
- Pasting followed by three Escape presses in Vim mode clears an idle draft even when rendering or paste preparation is slow.

**Removed**
- Remove the AUTO_APPROVAL feature flag: only managed policy can disable Assisted Permissions, and a leftover AUTO_APPROVAL=false is ignored with a deprecation warning

issues.title: [FEATURE]: TUI plugin API for inline prompt suggestions

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/plugins
labels.description: Plugins, skills, custom agents

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

TUI plugins have no supported way to show an inline suggestion in the prompt. [opencode-autosuggestions](https://github.com/fedeya/opencode-autosuggestions) already completes drafts while typing and suggests follow-ups after each turn, but it finds the prompt textarea through renderer internals and draws the ghost text in an absolutely positioned overlay at the cursor's screen coordinates. Its source notes that an OpenCode update can break this.

Proposal: add a suggestion API to `context.ui.prompt`, next to the draft access requested in #51209.

```ts
context.ui.prompt.suggest({ sessionID, text }): () => void
```

- The host draws `text` as muted ghost text right after the cursor, in an empty or non-empty draft, and handles wrapping.
- Tab accepts the whole suggestion, Ctrl+Right accepts the next word, and Escape dismisses it. All three are configurable keybinds. Accepting inserts text into the draft and never submits.
- When the user types characters that match the start of the suggestion, the host trims it. Any other edit, cursor move or session switch clears it.
- Suggestions are ignored in shell mode, while autocomplete or a dialog is open, and when the cursor is not at the end of the draft.
- Plugins also need to read the draft and cursor (#51209) and get a change event, so they can debounce their own requests.

This covers what #54197 did for the empty composer and extends it to drafts in progress. Model calls stay in plugins, so core sends no extra model requests.

I plan to implement this in a single PR and test it against opencode-autosuggestions.

### Description

### Observed Behavior

Tokscale reports significantly worse prompt-cache efficiency using Opus 5.5 through the new Claude Agent provider.

issues.title: v2: no credential path for custom provider IDs breaks adding custom providers from GUI clients
issues.body:
### Description

Custom providers seem to have no working credential path on the v2 integration API, which breaks adding them from GUI clients:

- `Integration.connection.key` (packages/core/src/integration.ts) dies with `Key method not found: <id>` unless an integration with that exact ID is registered.
- Key methods are only registered for providers present in the models.dev catalog (packages/core/src/plugin/models-dev.ts) plus plugin-defined ones — so a *custom* provider ID can never get a key through `integration.connect.key`.

Concretely: OpenChamber's custom-provider form routes the API key through this endpoint and always fails with "Integration not found: <id>" for any custom ID (filed as openchamber/openchamber#4038). The official desktop dialog works around this by using the legacy `auth.set` (packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/control.ts) + config write instead.

Separately: a user on the stable OpenCode Desktop reports being unable to add custom providers/models from the UI — can you confirm which desktop release ships the custom-provider dialog (packages/app/src/components/dialog-custom-provider.tsx), and whether it is expected to work against the bundled server?

**Question:** is `auth.set` the intended long-term path for custom-provider credentials, or should `integration.connect.key` also accept arbitrary provider IDs? Right now any third-party GUI following the integration API cannot add custom providers.

### OpenCode version

Source analysis of dev branch (2026-09-27); stable desktop 1.2.x

### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

### What do you want to change / add?

In OpenCode Desktop v2.3.2, when the projects-first sidebar layout is enabled (Interface layout = **Side tabs**, Organize vertical sidebar = **Projects**), the Home screen is no longer reachable, and the only discoverable **Add Project** entry point is buried inside **Settings**. The two visible "New Session" buttons (text + `+`) only create sessions inside the currently open project folder; neither offers a folder/project picker. Adding a second project becomes effectively undiscoverable unless you already know to look in Settings.

Please surface **Add Project** as a first-class, visible action in this layout — e.g. an "Add Project" item on the Projects sidebar section header, next to the two New Session buttons, or in the new-session/project picker. Also keep a route back to Home, or preserve Home's Add Project affordance somewhere in the new layout.

### Benefit

Project management is a primary workflow action, not a setting. Making it visible removes the dead-end where a user in the projects-first layout cannot see how to add another folder, and reduces confusion / support requests.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Settings → General → Interface layout → **Side tabs**.
2. Settings → Experimental → Organize vertical sidebar → **Projects**.
3. Home screen is gone; there is no navigation back to Home from the sidebar.
4. Only two "New Session" buttons are visible (text + `+`).
5. Both only create sessions in the current project folder; no folder picker appears.
6. The only working way to add a project is "Add Project" inside Settings.

### Expected behavior

Adding a project should be a visible action in the projects-first layout (Projects section header or new-session picker), and Home should remain reachable.

### Actual behavior

- Home disappears entirely in this layout, with no way back from the sidebar.
- Both New Session buttons stay inside the current project.
- "Add Project" is only discoverable inside Settings.
- Changelog entry points (#57962, #59607, #56952) were not visible or discoverable in this layout — the Settings entry was the only one found.

### Additional context

- Discoverability / UX report, reproducible on every launch with this layout.
- Current workaround: add the project from inside Settings.
- Related issues: #48882, #55446, #60241, #58188, #56903.
- `gh` CLI not installed, so drafted but not submitted automatically.
- No secrets, tokens, or private URLs included.

issues.title: desktop: hiding the thinking timeline category also silences the Thinking status

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/desktop
labels.description: Desktop app

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/macos
labels.description: macOS

issues.body:
## Description

Two symptoms from the same coupling, which together leave no usable middle ground for the thinking category:

1. **Hidden thinking kills the status signal.** With 思考 = 隐藏, the status line under a working turn can only read 工作中 ("Working"). The Thinking state becomes unreachable, so there is no way to tell "the model is streaming reasoning" from "the request is stalled waiting on the provider".
2. **Grouped thinking gives one row per reasoning part.** With 思考 = 分组 + 折叠, a stretch of reasoning parts with no tool call in between renders as N separate 「思考 N 秒」 rows (16 in a row in my session). There is no option to merge them.

Source (dev branch):

- `packages/session-ui/src/timeline-next/rules.ts:190` — `liveThinkingShows()` is just `detail.thinking.placement !== "hidden"`, and it gates the whole signal
- `packages/session-ui/src/timeline/turn-phase-machine.ts:60` — a turn only enters the `thinking` phase when `reasoning.placement !== "hidden"`, otherwise it falls through to `WORKING_TURN_PHASE`
- `packages/app/src/session/timeline/message-timeline.tsx:469-470` — "Thinking" is not a status-line string at all; the streaming thought row *replaces* the status lane
- `packages/session-ui/src/timeline-next/tools/context-group.tsx:64,151-168` — a group containing only reasoning parts (`thoughtsOnly`) skips the group wrapper and emits one `ThoughtRow` per part, so the collapse switch has nothing to act on
- the projection already collects adjacent reasoning parts into a single context group (`projection.ts:730`, `:905-935`); only the renderer splits them back out

Suggested fixes, in order of how much they would help:

1. Decouple the status signal from the display setting — allow the `thinking` phase and a "Thinking" status line even when thinking rows are hidden.
2. Merge consecutive grouped reasoning parts into one row, e.g. 「思考 3 条 · 共 21 秒」.
3. Optional: show elapsed time in the status line ("Working 1:23"). The data already exists — the sidebar inbox renders `sidebar.inbox.status.workingFor`.

## OpenCode version

2.3.2 — desktop on macOS, New timeline experiment enabled (`general.newTimeline = true`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Settings → General → Timeline → 高级, set 思考 = 隐藏
2. Run any turn that emits reasoning. The status line reads 工作中 for the entire turn, including while reasoning is actively streaming.
3. Set 思考 = 分组 + 折叠
4. A stretch of reasoning parts with no tool call between them renders one row each

## Plugins

none

## Operating System

macOS (desktop app)

## Terminal

n/a — desktop app

## Screenshot

16 consecutive 「思考 N 秒」 rows. Can attach if useful.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Better execution permissions and sandboxing
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

OpenCode's current execution controls could be improved in three areas:

## 1. Make permission mode easier to access

The current permission settings are relatively hidden.

It would be useful to show the active permission mode directly in the conversation UI and allow quick switching during a session.

## 2. Add sandboxed execution

OpenCode has permission controls such as `allow`, `ask`, and `deny`, but lacks a built-in sandbox comparable to a restricted execution environment.

A sandbox could limit filesystem, network, and process access even when an action is approved.

## 3. Add optional model-assisted approval

For `ask` mode, an optional reviewer model could evaluate requested actions and decide whether to:

* auto-approve
* ask the user
* deny

Ideally, the reviewer model could be configured separately from the main agent, so a small and inexpensive model can handle approval checks.

These three features would make OpenCode safer and more convenient for autonomous execution.

issues.body:
## Summary

An OpenAI-compatible provider that emits a streaming error chunk with `"error"` as a plain string (e.g. `{"error": "some message"}`) causes the entire session to abort with `SchemaError: Expected object | null | undefined at ["error"]`. The standard OpenAI error format is `{"error": {"message": "...", "type": "..."}}`, but vLLM-based providers sometimes emit string errors mid-stream during transient server issues.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.2
- OS: Darwin 27.2.0 (arm64)
- Terminal: xterm-256color
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest (macOS app)
- Active plugins: None

## Reproduction

1. Configure an OpenAI-compatible provider whose upstream emits string error chunks mid-stream. We used Spuric AI → `spur-glm-5-3`, a vLLM-served Z.AI GLM-5.3 model:
   ```jsonc
   {
     "spuric-glm": {
       "name": "Spuric GLM 5.3",
       "env": ["SPURIC_GLM_API_KEY"],
       "package": "@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible",
       "settings": { "baseURL": "https://ai.spuric.com/v1" },
       "models": { "glm-5-3": { "name": "GLM 5.3", "modelID": "spur-glm-5-3" } }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Start a session that includes tool calls with a large prompt context.
3. When the upstream hiccups mid-stream (intermittent), it emits a chunk containing `"error": "some string"` instead of the standard `"error": {"message": "...", "type": "..."}`.
4. The session drain aborts.

Error is intermittent — normal requests succeed, but transient server errors trigger it. Also confirmed with `spur-auto` (routing to `spur-deepseek-v4`) on a separate API key.

## Expected Behavior

A non-standard `error` field (string instead of object) should either:
- Be coerced to `{"message": "the string"}`, or
- Surfaced as a recoverable provider error without aborting the entire session

## Actual Behavior

The entire session drain aborts with:

```
AI.Error: Invalid spuric-glm/openai-compatible-chat stream event
  [cause]: AI.Error.InvalidProviderOutput: Invalid spuric-glm/openai-compatible-chat stream event {
    [cause]: SchemaError: Expected object | null | undefined
      at ["error"]
  }
```

## Additional Context

- Related but not duplicate: #60760 covers `error` objects missing a `message` key; #50314 covered `data: null` payloads (fixed). This is the remaining case: `error` as a bare string.
- The same failure path (`packages/llm/src/route/protocol.ts` Schema validation) affects all SSE-based routes (openai-chat, openai-compatible-chat, anthropic-messages, gemini).
- Same behavior confirmed across two different provider configs and two different API keys hitting the same upstream endpoint.
- The error is intermittent — the provider works correctly for many turns, then fails this way during what appears to be transient upstream hiccups.

issues.title: Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here

issues.body:
This is the **main issue for free tier problems**. If you see any of these, you're in the right place:

- `Free usage exceeded, subscribe to Go`
- `Free usage limit reached`
- `You've used today's free messages. They reset at ...` and the reset never happens
- `This version of OpenCode Desktop no longer supports free models`
- `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`
- `OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer is required to use the free tier`

**Please comment here instead of opening a new issue.** We're closing duplicates and pointing them here so everything is in one place.

## 1. Make sure you're on the latest OpenCode v2

Most free tier reports come from **OpenCode v1** (versions `0.x` and `1.x`, for example Desktop or CLI `1.19.5`). v1 no longer supports free models and only gets fixes for critical bugs. Updating to v2 has fixed this for many people.

Check your version:

- **Terminal:** `opencode --version`
- **Desktop:** Settings → About

The latest v2 release is **2.2.1**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The v1 Desktop app's built-in updater keeps you on `1.x`. Download v2 manually from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**.

### Desktop

Download v2 Desktop for macOS, Windows or Linux from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**, or on macOS:

```sh
brew install --cask opencode-desktop
```

### Terminal (TUI / CLI)

All install options are listed at **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**. The quickest on macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

Or use a package manager:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode/cli
bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
paru -S opencode-beta
```

v1 and v2 both use the `opencode` command. If you installed v1 with a package manager, remove it first, for example `npm uninstall -g opencode-ai`. Windows package managers (Chocolatey, Scoop) don't support v2. On Windows, use the Desktop app, npm, or a [standalone binary](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/).

### Useful docs

- [Install OpenCode v2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)
- [Migrate from v1](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/)
- [Free models, limits and privacy](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/models/#free-models)
- [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/)
- [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting/)

## 2. Other things to check

- **Free models only work inside OpenCode.** Other clients, proxies and direct API calls can't use them. Use a paid model or [Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/) there instead.
- **Subscribed to Go but still seeing free limits?** Run `/connect`, sign in with **OpenCode Console** in your browser (make sure you authorize the workspace with your Go subscription, or choose **OpenCode Go** if you use a Go API key), then pick a Go model (`opencode-go/...`) with `/models` rather than a free model (`opencode/...-free`).
- **Hit the real daily limit?** Wait for the reset time shown, subscribe to [Go](https://opencode.ai/go), or connect another provider with `/connect`.

## 3. Still broken on the latest v2? Comment with:

- OpenCode version, and whether you use Desktop, TUI, CLI or web
- Operating system
- The free model you used
- The exact error message (a screenshot is fine)
- When it started and the reset time you were shown
- Whether you have Go or Console credits

> [!WARNING]
> Don't post email addresses, payment details or other account information here. This issue is public.

## 4. Still don't know what's going on?

If you're on the latest v2 and none of the above helps, or the problem is about your account, billing or Go subscription, email **help@anoma.ly** with the details from step 3. Billing and account issues can't be fixed in GitHub issues.

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.description: Agent loop, tools and config

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
### Description

In the OpenCode TUI, the parent committed its changes and sent a final “done” report while a native subagent was still working. The subagent later sent its first `<subagent state="completed">` report, which woke the parent and resulted in a second assistant reply without another user prompt.

In the latest case, the parent assigned one new `code-fixer` session a test file and a syntax check. The parent owned implementation and final integration testing. They shared the workspace, so the parent could see the test file, run the full integration suite successfully, and commit before the child reported back. The child was still trying its own database test when the parent declared the work complete. Code edits were disjoint. Syntax checks and execution of the new cases overlapped.

I expect the parent to be able to yield while a required child runs, then review its report before committing or declaring the task complete. A pending-work state or a native wait/join option would make this reliable without polling and would still allow independent parent work in parallel.

### Plugins

Oh My OpenCode Slim was disabled for this occurrence. The server config declares `plugins: []`. Local plugin files are present for Herdr agent state, Magpie model integration, and RTK. The CLI config enables the Herdr plugin. A run with all local plugins disabled is still pending.

### OpenCode version

`opencode v2.3.2` (V2 CLI/TUI). Parent model route `magpie/auto/gpt-6.2-sol`. Configured child route `magpie/group/auto-deepseek-flash#high`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a global `AGENTS.md` that delegates bounded work to native subagents, assigns non-overlapping files, and makes the parent responsible for reviewing results and final verification. My configuration defines `code-fixer`, `designer`, `fast-generic`, `oracle`, and `repo-scout`. The affected turn used only `code-fixer` in a fresh child session. My rules call for fresh sessions for independent tasks and reuse only for follow-ups to the same task.
2. Ask the parent to finish a change. Have it delegate a regression test and syntax check to the child while implementing the production change itself. The child writes its file and continues checking it.
3. Let the parent run integration checks after the child's file appears. In the observed turn, the parent then committed and reported completion before the native child report arrived.
4. Leave the session open without sending another prompt. Observe the late child report and the additional parent reply. Similar premature “done” reports have occurred repeatedly in my workflow. These steps describe the observed case, and I have not established a deterministic minimal reproduction.

### Related reports

My earlier Slim report documented repeated replays of previously delivered results. The latest occurrence involved one late first delivery from the native tool. I would like to understand whether OpenCode can support waiting for required child results before a parent finalizes. This may involve model behavior as well as the native tool lifecycle. [OMO Slim #1940](https://github.com/alvinunreal/oh-my-opencode-slim/issues/1940) · [OpenCode #63785](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/63785) · [OpenCode #64073](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/64073)

### Operating System

macOS 13.3 (Darwin 22.4.0, x86_64).

### Terminal

OpenCode TUI in Herdr, `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`, `/bin/zsh`.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Settings to customize the text color of delivered and pending user messages
issues.body:
### Description

**Current behavior**

In the desktop app my own messages are styled with the generic theme tokens only (`packages/session-ui/src/components/message-part.css`):

- delivered: `color: var(--v2-text-text-base)` / `background: var(--v2-background-bg-layer-02)`
- not delivered yet, `[data-pending]`: `color: var(--v2-text-text-muted)` / `background: var(--v2-background-bg-layer-01)`

**Why it's a problem**

Because those are the same tokens the assistant's text uses:

1. My own message is not distinguishable from the answer by color at all.
2. The step between `text.base` and `text.muted` is very small, so "still waiting" vs. "already sent" is hard to see at normal zoom. Before the 2.2.0 UI refresh delivered messages had their own color and the send state was obvious at a glance.

I checked whether this is configurable today: there is no setting for message colors, and themes can't express it either — a theme only remaps `text.base` / `text.muted`, so changing those changes the assistant's text as well. There is also no way to add a custom theme in the desktop app; the theme list is limited to the built-in ones.

**What I'd like**

Options under Settings -> Appearance to set the color of user messages per delivery state, e.g.:

- User message text color (delivered)
- User message text color (pending)

Two dedicated tokens that currently fall back to `text.base` / `text.muted` would be enough as a base, with the settings UI exposing overrides for them. Then the default appearance stays exactly as it is now, built-in themes don't have to change, and a theme can adopt the new tokens later if it wants to.

**Benefit**

- The delivery state becomes readable at a glance again, instead of relying on a nearly invisible color difference.
- Users who need higher contrast can raise the contrast of their own messages without changing the whole theme.
- Nothing changes for users who never touch the new setting.

Environment: desktop app 2.2.1, Windows 11.

Related: #49340 asks for color customization per chat role in general — this is the narrower, delivery-state part of it. #52028 discussed the previous user bubble styling.

### Description
After updating OpenCode Desktop to v2.3.2 on Windows, the app repeatedly defaults to opening `%USERPROFILE%` (`C:\Users\<username>`) instead of the selected project folder. This appears to be the same issue previously reported in #62635 (closed as not planned on v2.2.6.0), and it still occurs after updating to v2.3.2.

### Environment
- **OpenCode Version:** 2.3.2 (Desktop)
- **OS:** Windows 11

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Update OpenCode Desktop to v2.3.2 on a Windows machine with existing local OpenCode data.
2. Launch OpenCode Desktop.
3. Attempt to open a specific project folder.

### Expected Behavior
OpenCode opens and switches context to the selected project folder.

### Actual Behavior
OpenCode ignores the selected folder and remains locked on `%USERPROFILE%` (`C:\Users\<username>`).

### Workaround / Root Cause Clues
Fully exiting OpenCode and resetting the local data and desktop cache folders resolves the issue:
- `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode`
- `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opentui`
- `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop`

issues.title: app: keybinds match the produced character, so Ctrl+F and other letter shortcuts fail on non-Latin layouts
issues.body:
### Description

App keybinds are matched against `event.key` (the character produced by the active
layout) and only fall back to the physical `event.code` when **Alt** is held. On
non-Latin layouts (e.g. Russian) `event.key` is Cyrillic, so letter and punctuation
shortcuts silently do nothing unless Alt is involved.

Example: the session find bar added in #48470 is bound to `mod+f`. On an English
layout `Ctrl+F` opens it; on a Russian layout it does nothing. `session.search` is
registered with `hidden: true`, so the command palette cannot reach it either — the
shortcut is the only entry point, and on a Cyrillic layout it never fires.

Root cause — `packages/app/src/shell/commands/command.tsx`:

```ts
export function keyFromKeyboardEvent(event: KeyboardEvent) {
  const key = normalizeKey(event.key)

  if (!event.altKey || /^[a-z0-9]$/.test(key)) return key

  if (!event.code.startsWith("Key") || event.code.length !== 4) return key

  return event.code.slice(3).toLowerCase()
}
```

`matchKeybind` compares the configured key (`"f"`) with `keyFromKeyboardEvent(event)`.
With a Russian layout, `Ctrl+F` arrives as `event.key === "а"`, `event.code === "KeyF"`,
`event.altKey === false`, so the function returns `"а"` and `"f" !== "а"` — no match.
`Alt+F` *does* match, so the `event.code` fallback exists but is gated on Alt (it was
added for macOS Option). Ctrl/Meta/Shift on a non-Latin layout are not covered.

The same applies to `mod+p`, `mod+t`, `mod+w`, `mod+u`, `mod+shift+a/e/l/o/r/s/t/x`,
`mod+shift+d`, and the punctuation binds `mod+comma`, `mod+.`, `mod+;`, `mod+'`,
`mod+[`, `mod+]`, `mod+\\`. Digit binds (`mod+1..9`) are fine because the digit row
matches across these layouts.

Suggested fix: remove the `!event.altKey` gate so the physical-key fallback applies to
every modifier (this keeps the macOS Option behavior), and additionally map `event.code`
for the punctuation keys used in keybinds (`Comma`, `Period`, `Semicolon`, `Quote`,
`BracketLeft`, `BracketRight`, `Backslash`, …).

Related, but not the same:

- #40048 — "Keybind Ctrl + . does not work with non-US keyboard layouts (e.g., Russian)"
  — identical root cause, auto-closed by the stale bot, not fixed.
- #6364 — "Hotkeys don't work if the keyboard layout isn't english" — same, auto-closed.
- #54708 — handles `Dead`/`Unidentified` keys; here `event.key` is a valid character, so
  that fallback does not trigger.
- #55371 — open, but the TUI (terminal input / Kitty protocol); the app path is separate.

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

2.0.29 (desktop app)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the desktop app on Windows and switch the keyboard layout to Russian (ЙЦУКЕН).
2. Open a session and press `Ctrl+F` on the physical F key. → Nothing happens.
3. Switch to the English layout and press the same physical keys. → The find bar opens.
4. Still in the Russian layout, `Alt+F` matches while `Ctrl+F` does not.

### Screenshot and/or share link

N/A

### Operating System

Windows 11 (10.0.22631)

### Terminal

N/A — desktop app

issues.title: tui: window returns to the start screen after the computer sleeps and wakes
issues.body:
## Summary

After the computer sleeps and wakes, an open TUI window can lose the session it was showing and go back to the start screen. The session keeps running and its history stays intact. The window just stops showing it, so a long unattended run looks lost.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.1
- OS: macOS, Darwin 27.0.0 (arm64)
- Terminal: iTerm.app (TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: @weaveio/weave-adapter-opencode2@0.2.0

## Reproduction

1. Start a long-running session in the TUI, for example with `/goal`.
2. Leave the window open and let the Mac go to sleep, with the usual short maintenance wakes overnight.
3. Wake the Mac and look at the same TUI window.

## Expected Behavior

The window still shows the session it was showing before sleep, with any messages added since.

## Actual Behavior

The window shows the start screen, as if `opencode` had just been launched. The session still exists and had finished successfully. The first attempt to reopen it with `/sessions` failed with an error; the second attempt worked.

## Additional Context

- The session's last model request was at 23:09 UTC, and the run finished successfully seconds later. The Mac went to sleep about 18 minutes after that.
- Overnight, the log shows the TUI's event stream dropping and reconnecting at every wake, about every 10 to 20 minutes:

  > `level=INFO message="event stream disconnected" component=client attempt=1 error="Event stream stalled" role=cli`
  > `level=INFO message="event stream connecting" component=client attempt=1 role=cli`
  > `level=INFO message="event stream connected" component=client role=cli`

- The server process stayed up the whole time, with the same run ID before and after sleep.
- The log does not show what the TUI displayed, so the link between a reconnect and the reset is inferred, not proven.
- The failed `/sessions` attempt left no ERROR or WARN entry in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`.
- I've seen this once so far.
- Possibly related: #54181, where a service stall loses sessions. Here the server did not restart, so the cause seems to be on the TUI side.

prs.title: feat(core): accept machine links over iroh
prs.body:
**A machine on another network can now reach a home that has no public address.**
The server accepts the machine link over Iroh (QUIC, dial by public key) next to the WebSocket route. Same handshake, same frames; only the carrier is new.

🚦 **Flag:** `machines`. With the flag off, or on with no machines and no invitation made, the binding is never loaded, nothing is bound and nothing is contacted.

🐛 **Before → after**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Home on a laptop behind a home router, worker elsewhere | Only through the public tunnel, which exposes the whole server | The worker dials the home's key; direct when the networks allow, relayed otherwise |
| Join string | `reach: [{ type: "url", … }]` | One more entry, `{ type: "iroh" }`: "dial this join string's `home` key". No new address: the key is the address |
| The link | Noise handshake and frames over a WebSocket | Unchanged, over one QUIC stream, each message a 2-byte length and its bytes |

```text
worker ══ Iroh: direct, or through a relay ══ server ── Link.serve → machines.connect
                                              (the path the WebSocket route already uses)
```

```ts
// packages/core/src/machine/iroh.ts
endpoint = bind({ secretKey: home identity seed, alpn: "opencode-link/1" })   // endpoint id == home key
for each incoming stream:  Link.serve(carrier(stream))  →  machines.connect(machine, connection)
```

📊 **Proof**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Two networks, no tunnel, no VPN: a cloud Linux VM joined a home on a laptop behind a home router, join string with no public address | ✅ paired in about 4 s; path relayed at 0.5 s, direct at 0.8 s |
| A model ran a command and read a file on that machine; 2 MB of command output arrived intact | ✅ |
| Home restarted | ✅ worker back and direct in about 8 s |
| Offline test in `bun test`: a second endpoint dials the home on loopback with relays off, completes the handshake, exchanges a frame; a refusal closes with 1008 | ✅ `machine-iroh.test.ts`, ×5 |
| Binding loads: 0 with the flag off, 0 after a list, 1 after an add | ✅ counted in the test |
| The compiled CLI (`build.ts --single`), run from an empty directory | ✅ binds Iroh; its join string carries the `iroh` entry |
| Binding throughput under Bun, 64 KiB chunks | 77 to 110 MB/s; worst event-loop gap 8 ms during a 50 MiB transfer |
| Packed workerd SDK | ✅ `packed SDK consumer OK`; the native module is not pulled in |

One independent review found three problems (a handshake finishing after its deadline was never closed; quadratic copying when many small messages arrive in one read; the startup check read the machine list before the flag). All fixed, with tests for the first two. The review bot then found that the Iroh path did not re-read the flag per connection as the WebSocket route does; fixed, with a test.

**Worth knowing** (accepted for now, since all of this sits behind the experimental flag)

- **A native dependency.** `@number0/iroh` 1.2.0 is optional; its seven platform packages are listed in `packages/core` the way the file watcher's are, so the build can embed the right one per target. That is about 11 MB per platform on install and in the binary.
- **No Intel Mac build.** There the server logs one line and join strings carry URLs only.
- **Third parties.** The default preset uses n0's public relays and address lookup: once machines are in use, the home's endpoint id (its public key) and addresses are published there. Their public relays are rate-limited and meant for development. A real release wants our own relay (the relay is open source and stateless) or their hosted plan. It is one line in `iroh.ts`.
- **One key, two uses.** The home's Ed25519 identity key is also its Iroh key, which is what lets the join string say only `{ type: "iroh" }`. If that is unwelcome, a second key costs one field in the join string.

**Left out**

- A failed Iroh start stays failed until the server restarts.
- Iroh's cap of 32 handshakes at once is counted separately from the WebSocket route's.
- Idle timeout is Iroh's default (keep-alive every 5 s, 30 s idle); the binding has no setting for it.

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/machine/iroh.ts` (126 lines: `listen`, `serve`, `carrier`), then `makeMachine` in `packages/server/src/handlers/machine.ts` (where it is bound, lazily), then `irohBindingPlugin` in `packages/cli/script/build.ts`.

<sub>Follows #65259 · the worker that dials this is kept outside the repo for now</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`, `packages/server`, `packages/cli`; `typecheck:tsc` in core and server
- Core machine tests, `machine-iroh.test.ts` and routes tests, new ones with `--rerun-each 5`
- `bun run test` in `packages/client`: 267 pass; `bun run verify:package` in `packages/sdk`
- oxlint and prettier

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): machine commands accept --server
prs.body:
**`opencode machine add|list|remove` now take `--server`, like the other commands that talk to a server.**
Before, they could only reach the managed background service, so anyone running the server themselves could not use them.

🚦 **Flag:** none of its own. The machine commands are already behind `machines`.

🐛 **Before → after**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode machine list --server http://127.0.0.1:4096` | `Unrecognized flag: --server` | Lists that server's machines |
| `opencode machine list` (no flag) | The managed service, started if needed | Unchanged |
| `opencode machine add gpu --standalone` | `Unrecognized flag` | Refused in plain words: a private server exits with the command, so its join string would point at nothing |

```ts
// handlers/machine/common.ts
before   Service.ensure(ServiceConfig.options())      // always the managed service
after    ServerConnection.resolve()                   // --server if given, else the managed service
```

`machine add` builds the join string from the addresses the server reports for itself, so with `--server` pointing at a loopback-only server the join string lists loopback only; `--url` still overrides.

📊 **Proof**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `--server` accepted before the group, after it, and after the subcommand; absent means none | ✅ new test, fails on `dev` with "Unrecognized flag" |
| `bun typecheck` in `packages/cli` | ✅ |
| `packages/cli/test/machine.test.ts` | ✅ 6 pass |

No independent review: this wires an existing global flag into one command group (8 production lines).

👀 **Read:** `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/machine/common.ts`, `ensureMachineClient`.

prs.title: fix(browser): copy sign-ins to a remote server's pages without stalling the app
prs.body:
### What a person saw

- With **Share sign-ins with remote servers** on, opening a session on a remote server froze the whole app for seconds to minutes.
- The remote browser pane attached late or attached again and again, and each new attempt made the freeze longer.
- Quitting waited until every copy finished.

### Cause

- **One read fetched the whole store.** `link.ts:19-24` read a single cookie with `cookies.get({ domain, path, name })`. Electron answers a `get` that has no `url` by fetching every cookie the store holds and filtering in the main process (`Cookies::Get` → `GetAllCookies` in `electron_api_cookies.cc`, Electron 44.9.1).
- **The first copy made that read 4 times per cookie.** `link.ts:84-94` reconciled each cookie by itself: 2 reads per cookie, then 2 more for the echo of each write. That is 4N reads of N cookies. At N = 3,000: 12,000 reads, 36 million cookie objects built in the main process.
- **The attachment waited for the copy, and nothing could stop it.** `pane.ts:310` awaited `profile.link` (`profile/index.ts:673`) inside an uninterruptible `acquireRelease`. The 15 s registration timer (`pane-machine.ts:8`) fired, the window registered again, and a second partition started a second copy beside the first. `runtime.dispose()` waited for all of them at quit.

| One read of the profile's store (Electron 44.9.1, Windows) | 500 cookies | 3,000 cookies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get({ domain, path, name })` (dev) | 4.1 ms | 30.5 ms |
| `get({ url, name })` (this PR) | 0.13 ms | 0.21 ms |
| `get({})` (whole list) | 5 ms | 42.8 ms |

### Fix

- **First copy, O(N):** each store's list is read once, the two are compared in memory through the same `reconcileCookie` rule (`planCopy`), and only the differences are written, 16 at a time with a turn of the event loop between batches.
- **A change, O(1):** a change that reports what both stores already agreed on (the echo of the mirror's own write) costs no read. Any other change asks each store for one site's cookies, `get({ url: "https://host/path", name })`, then matches domain and path exactly as before. The whole-store read remains only for a path that no address can name (a space, `?`, `#`).
- **Cancellable:** unlink, dispose and quit stop the copy at its next batch and drop the reconciles that wait.
- **Attach no longer waits:** `profile.link` returns at once. Only a page that is about to load waits for the copy (`signedIn`), through the hook that already holds a load for content filters. No timer is involved, and a registration that ends takes its copy along.
- **State:** a small machine in `link-machine.ts`: `copying` → `following` → `stopped`.
- **No flag:** this is a fix; the setting, the partition a remote session uses and the direction cookies flow are unchanged.

Before:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant W as Window
  participant P as Pane (main)
  participant M as Mirror
  participant S as Remote server
  W->>P: register
  P->>M: link, awaited
  Note over M: 4N whole-store reads
  Note over P: 15 s timer fires
  P-->>W: registration closed
  W->>P: register again
  P->>M: link, second copy beside the first
  M-->>P: copy done
  P->>S: attach
```

After:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant W as Window
  participant P as Pane (main)
  participant M as Mirror
  participant S as Remote server
  W->>P: register
  P->>M: link, returns at once
  P->>S: attach
  S-->>P: attached
  P-->>W: registered
  W->>P: load restored tab
  P->>M: signedIn(signal)
  Note over M: 2 list reads, N writes in batches of 16
  M-->>P: copy ended
  Note over P: page loads signed in
```

### Measurements

Pinned Electron 44.9.1 on Windows, through `electron-run.ts`, hidden windows, made-up cookies (6 per host: domain, host-only, plain-http on a path), empty remote partitions. "Stall" is the longest time the main process's event loop did not turn.

| Cookies | Mirrors | dev: copy finished | dev: main CPU / stall | PR: copy finished | PR: main CPU / stall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 500 | 1 | 3,156 ms | 1,751 / 1,490 ms | 42 ms | 16 / 0 ms |
| 500 | 5 | 16,384 ms | 8,687 / 5,126 ms | 176 ms | 297 / 24 ms |
| 1,500 | 1 | 26,737 ms | 15,359 / 14,113 ms | 131 ms | 141 / 10 ms |
| 1,500 | 5 | over 55 s | no result | 444 ms | 484 / 50 ms |
| 3,000 | 1 | over 55 s | no result | 232 ms | 282 / 29 ms |
| 3,000 | 5 | not run | not run | 897 ms | 1,078 / 83 ms |
| 3,291 | 1 | not run | not run | 236 ms | 250 / 31 ms |
| 3,291 | 5 | not run | not run | 982 ms | 999 / 123 ms |

- **"over 55 s":** the harness ends a fixture at 55 s; the main process was too busy to print a result at its own 30 s cap.
- **3,291:** 6,000 cookies were seeded. Chromium keeps at most about 3,300 per store, so that is the largest store there is.

| | dev | PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quit with a copy under way: `runtime.dispose()` | 22,872 ms (1,500 cookies) | 1 ms (3,000 cookies) |
| Stop a mirror during its copy: until both stores answer again | 14,917 ms (1,500 cookies) | 1 ms (3,000 cookies, 80 written) |
| 50 page writes of one cookie reach the partition (500 cookies, 1 mirror) | 200 ms | 36 ms |
| The same at 3,000 cookies, 5 mirrors | not run | 48 ms |

### Log

Main log; every field is a number or a string, and none names a cookie or a site.

```
info browser sign-in copy started    { copy }
info browser sign-in copy finished   { copy, profile, remote, toRemote, toProfile, refused, ms }   (warn, with cause, when refused > 0)
info browser sign-in copy cancelled  { copy, written, ms }
warn browser sign-in copy failed     { copy, cause, ms }
warn browser sign-in change was not copied     { copy, failures, cause }   (1st, 10th, 100th failure)
warn browser shared sign-ins were not removed  { copy, kept, cause }
```

### Tests

- `profile/link.test.ts`: counting stores. 3,000 cookies on both sides → 2 list reads, 0 per-cookie reads, 0 writes. 3,000 on one side → 3,000 writes, 0 per-cookie reads, echoes included. One change → 1 scoped read per store at 10 and at 3,000 cookies. Cancel, failure, and what a link waits for. The mirror cases fail on `dev`.
- `profile/electron-link.test.ts`: the same counts and the copied cookies on the pinned Electron's own stores, for domain, host-only, secure, plain, path-scoped and session cookies and two cookies of one name under one host.
- `electron-sign-in-copy.test.ts`: the real pane against a stand-in remote server with a copy held open. The attachment completes, the restored tab loads signed in after the copy, a registration that is replaced has its copy cancelled, and quit does not wait.

### Limits

- **One list read holds the main process about 30 ms at 3,000 cookies.** Five mirrors that start together read five lists: one stall of 83 to 123 ms.
- **A write a store refused is not retried by a later no-change event.** `dev` reread the key on every event, and for such a key would then remove the cookie from the profile.
- **A page waits for the copy without a deadline.** The person can stop the load; the copy ends when both list reads answer or fail.
- **Partitioned cookies:** the scoped read returns them as the unscoped one did (measured). Electron's `cookies.set` cannot write a partition key, as before.
- **Not in this PR:** a partition is left behind per registration; there is one mirror per attachment, not per server; the mirror is two-way.

prs.title: fix(app): handle prompt delivery during undo
prs.body: ### Issue for this PR Fixes #64648 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix ### What does this PR do? Undo can race prompt delivery. Inbox cancel returns 204 either way, so the app now checks whether the prompt reached session history. If delivery already happened, Queue Undo clears the stale queue row, leaves the draft intact, and tells the user the prompt was already sent. `/undo` rewinds the delivered turn before restoring its prompt. ### How did you verify your code works? Both browser regressions fail on upstream base `b83ea513658eed65291d218d2363fc91c09a2141`. The review regression also fails on the original PR head `00dde43a8362ffe4fc2df38cdcf8c936fc83dcfa`, where the app shows “Request failed”. At `39cf7a3c64128c0bce7bc6378488a3e72ed65b80`, the built app says “This prompt was already sent” and passed all 50 queue cases in Brave. All 69 focused tests and `bun run check` passed. The real source server replay with a loopback model kept one prompt and one reply after rewind and resend. A separate Vite dev-server run timed out on two cases, both of which passed against the built app. The local Strobe run ran out of disk. In hosted check mode, both revisions encoded the large draft 26 times per typing run and both recalled prompt history. For cursor moves, the upstream base varied between 5 and 6 encodes, so Strobe could make no exact comparison. Timing remains unverified. [Hosted Strobe run](https://github.com/archit15singh/autonomous-delivery-loop/actions/runs/44869930492/job/136741952701). [Replay commands and logs](https://github.com/archit15singh/autonomous-delivery-loop/tree/a2cd92e2052dc03c18c1ab396955daa7fd217bdd/docs/evidence/opencode-64648) ### Screenshots / recordings | Before · Undone text is appended | After · Original draft is preserved | | --- | --- | | | | ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Related: #54150

prs.body:
### Screenshots

The app's own taskbar button, cropped at 3x. Captured on a taskbar docked at the left edge, where Windows draws progress as a pill on the button's edge; on the default bottom taskbar the same states appear as the usual bar under the icon. The app shows as "Electron" with Electron's icon because it is an unpackaged dev build.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Idle | ![Before: idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6303a7c-e10b-485c-ad71-af8165da295c) | ![After: idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/579039ca-6e67-46e6-8a37-3b533dc829aa) |
| Working (clip) | ![Before: working](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b242bcc4-7992-40c8-a33e-210af0c8c9dc) | ![After: working, animated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/061c802c-cb3e-4a2d-8ceb-819c0958e934) |
| Waiting on a permission | ![Before: waiting on a permission](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e541c06c-2a24-4cb9-ae20-d8a9bc5631a0) | ![After: waiting on a permission](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/346f2a93-b18e-4835-92ec-ccf9d4199379) |
| Waiting on a question | ![Before: waiting on a question](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04788bee-1760-49b1-af31-c7b9079a818c) | ![After: waiting on a question](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9047d2a2-c494-40cd-baf9-92c8c2bc324e) |
| A failed run, not viewed yet | ![Before: failed, not viewed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df3742fd-b8fb-40e4-a2f1-45e238603b98) | ![After: failed, not viewed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc9f84fd-2275-4dc0-9c9d-aa383005368c) |
| The failed run viewed (window focused, so the button is highlighted) | ![Before: failed run viewed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a910a6c3-610b-42f8-be5c-662f2d974537) | ![After: failed run viewed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ef14632-2763-4ec6-9905-7ea092cbc171) |
| One session working, another waiting | ![Before: working and waiting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd816573-6856-4e4d-837e-17b4424977b8) | ![After: working and waiting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a222e8b-4d64-421d-99d8-5b04fb496d38) |
| Permission answered, the other still working | ![Before: answered, still working](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1850f476-581e-4113-9ff5-b98c76388d5c) | ![After: answered, still working](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75a1ae8a-a192-4df2-86f1-90d5eb6b0c39) |
| Two windows: one waiting, one working | ![Before: two windows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/884e2d11-c683-4533-adc7-3856e552215f) | ![After: two windows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d74c6ddf-eaa3-453c-883f-90d8f274cb33) |

What sets each state: a session in one of the window's tabs running (animated); a permission or question waiting (yellow); a run that failed and hasn't been viewed (red). Waiting wins over a failure, and a failure over running. Viewing the failed session or answering the request clears it.

### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Ported from the native Rune desktop build (`anomalyco/rune-desktop`, `apps/desktop/src/workspace/windows/taskbar.rs`).

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Shows each window's open-tab session status on its Windows taskbar button using Electron's `BrowserWindow.setProgressBar`, with no feature flag (Windows-only shell integration):

- **Amber (`paused`, progress `1`)** while any unmuted tab waits on a permission or question.
- **Red (`error`, progress `1`)** when an unmuted tab finished with an unseen failure.
- **Indeterminate (`indeterminate`, progress `2`)** while a session in the window is running.
- **Cleared (`none`, progress `-1`)** once all sessions are idle and read.

Main remembers the last mode each window applied (a `WeakMap`), so an idle launch makes no `setProgressBar` call and a repeated mode makes no extra shell call.

macOS and Linux behaviour is unchanged: the main-process handler exits immediately unless `process.platform === "win32"`, and the renderer effect is gated on `platform.os === "windows"`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test src/main/windows/taskbar-progress.test.ts` (7 pass): the priority order (`paused` > `error` > `indeterminate` > `none`), no call on an idle launch, repeats skipped, and no call on `darwin` or `linux`.
- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/desktop`; `bun typecheck` in `packages/app`.
- `bun run lint:changed origin/dev`: 0 problems across the changed files.
- Checked on a real Windows taskbar, before and after, for every state in the table above.

### Checklist

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR
