prs.title: feat(app): bundle OpenMono as the default mono font
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

OpenMono becomes the app's bundled default font for code and for the terminal. It replaces IBM Plex Mono (code) and JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono (terminal). OpenMono is built on [Iosevka](https://github.com/be5invis/Iosevka); its terminal icons come from [Nerd Fonts](https://github.com/ryanoasis/nerd-fonts).

- `monoDefault` and `terminalDefault` are `"OpenMono"`. A stored font choice does not change: an empty value follows the new default, and a typed name (the old defaults included) still goes first, with OpenMono as its fallback.
- The files come from the final OpenMono 1.000 build, in its app form: no ligatures, every character one cell wide, in Regular, Bold and Italic. Regular covers weights 100 to 599 and Bold covers 600 to 900.
- The app's `@font-face` rules take the name ahead of an installed OpenMono, which has ligatures.
- The `@font-face` rules state the font's typographic line metrics (ascender 965, descender 285, no gap). Without them macOS reads the files' `hhea` table (descender 220), and inline code backgrounds and terminal rows become 17px instead of 18px. The overrides can go if the font's `hhea` table ever matches its typographic metrics.
- Settings › About › Third-party notices lists OpenMono and every icon set in the icons file, with each set's copyright line and its license file from its own repository at the version the Nerd Fonts patcher lists. Each text names the commit it came from.
- Bold Italic is not bundled. The app's own code never asks for it; a terminal program that does gets the Italic file made bold, as it got a slanted Bold before.

**How the files load**

Each style's text is split into three files by `unicode-range`, the way the websites split the same font: `latin` (Latin, punctuation, arrows, shapes, box drawing, the six shortcut keys `⌃ ⌘ ⌥ ⌫ ⎋ ⏎` and 27 common symbols such as `✓ ✗ ⚠ ≠ ≤ ∞`), `cyrillic`, and `rest` (every other character). The nine files are byte-identical to the websites' files, and their rules have the websites' `unicode-range` values. The icons are the same in every style, so all styles share one icons file. Each of the 3,552 text characters and 10,876 icon characters is in the range of its own file's rule; only the two stress marks U+0300 and U+0301 are in two files, on purpose. A browser asks the last rule that has a character first, so the order of the rules is latin, rest, cyrillic, icons: a stressed Russian word loads only the Cyrillic file, and the four icon code points that the `rest` range runs across (U+23FB to U+23FE) load only the icons file.

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "OpenMono";
  src: url("./assets/fonts/OpenMono-Regular-latin.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 100 599;
  unicode-range: U+0020-007E, U+00A0-017F, /* … */ U+FFFD;
}

/* The same for -rest and -cyrillic, then one icons rule for each style, all with the same file. */
@font-face {
  font-family: "OpenMono";
  src: url("./assets/fonts/OpenMono-icons.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 100 599;
  unicode-range: U+23FB-23FE, U+2630, /* … */ U+F0001-F1AF0;
}
```

What CSS selects is not all that is downloaded:

| When | What is downloaded | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The app starts | Regular latin, 29 KB | The app loads the code font with the shell, as it did before. |
| Italic or bold code is drawn | Italic or Bold latin, 33 KB or 29 KB | `unicode-range` and the style select the file. |
| A Cyrillic letter is drawn | cyrillic, 18 KB to 22 KB | `unicode-range` selects the file. |
| Another character is drawn, such as `λ` or `π` | rest, 122 KB to 140 KB | `unicode-range` selects the file. |
| An icon character is drawn, or a terminal opens | Icons, 1.06 MB, one request for all styles | The emulator asks for two Powerline characters when it opens, so the file loads even if the session never draws an icon. The old terminal font loaded the same way. |
| The web app's service worker installs | All ten files, 1,594 KB, in the background | The worker precaches the build, as it did the old fonts (2,252 KB). I kept every file in the precache so that an offline terminal has them. |

The files are in `src/assets/fonts`, so the bundler puts a content hash in each URL. The web server lets a browser keep every file except the page for a year. The old code font also went through the bundler; the old terminal font and Inter have fixed names in `public/assets`, so they already had this risk, and Inter still has it.

**Why the split, measured**

The final build's text file is 202 KB for Regular. I measured it whole and split, against `dev`, on a Mac: 24 cold and 24 warm loads each, in the web build with the e2e mock server, and the font files alone in Electron through a handler like the desktop app's.

| | `dev` | Final build, one file per style | This PR: split |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First paint, cold / warm | 164 ms / 108 ms | same within noise | 164 ms / 108 ms |
| First session view, cold / warm | 374 ms / 212 ms | same within noise | 369 ms / 210 ms |
| Code font: fetch and decode in Electron | 1.7 ms | 4.1 ms | 1.0 ms |
| Code font downloaded at startup | 46 KB | 202 KB | 29 KB |
| Downloaded by the first session view with italic code | 98 KB | 429 KB | 62 KB |

- Desktop startup does not change: the differences are smaller than the run-to-run spread (4 ms to 13 ms).
- The split matters for the web UI over a network. On a 1.6 Mbps link the single file added about 0.8 s to the first session view.
- No load showed a reflow of code text: the code block and inline code had their final width when they first appeared.
- The times were measured before the keys and symbols moved into the Latin files, which made each about 2 KB larger. The sizes are those of the files in this PR.

**Terminal redraw**

The icons, and the characters outside Latin, are now files of their own, so a character that the terminal draws before its file arrives stays a fallback glyph, because the canvas only redraws rows that change. The terminal now renders every row again when a file of one of its own font families finishes loading: a render pass only, with no theme or emulator configuration change, and nothing for other fonts.

`draws terminal characters whose font files arrive after the first paint` in `e2e/regression/terminal.spec.ts` holds the icons file and the `rest` file until the terminal has painted, then compares the first row with the same text drawn on another row after the files loaded. It fails when only the listener is removed.

**File sizes**

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code font that loads with the app | 46 KB | 29 KB |
| Font that loads when a terminal opens | 1,061 KB | 1,060 KB |
| Mono font files in the build | 2,252 KB | 1,594 KB |

- Added to `packages/app/src/assets/fonts`, in the order Regular, Bold, Italic: latin 29,416 / 29,060 / 32,884 bytes; cyrillic 18,412 / 17,952 / 21,968; rest 122,432 / 121,880 / 139,804; and `OpenMono-icons.woff2`, 1,059,872. Added to `packages/app/public/assets`: `OpenMono-OFL.txt` (5 KB).
- Removed: the two JetBrainsMono Nerd Font files (1,061 KB and 1,047 KB), the three IBM Plex Mono files the build took from `@ibm/plex` (145 KB), and the `@ibm/plex` dependency of `packages/app`.
- The build's mono fonts are 658 KB smaller than on `dev`.

**Feature flag**

**Open question for the maintainer: may this change ship without a flag?** `AGENTS.md` asks for a flag on new user-visible behavior, and a new default font is that. I ask for an exception, for these reasons:

1. A flag cannot gate a font without both font sets in the build, which keeps the 2.25 MB this change removes.
2. The app does not read the flag registry, and the client must not depend on Core, so the gate would need new plumbing for one default.
3. The change is a default, not a behavior: a user types another font name in Settings › Appearance, and the earlier default-font change (#44876) shipped without a flag.

If the answer is no, I will add the gate before this leaves draft.

**How to rebuild the font files**

```sh
cd packages/app
uvx --from 'fonttools[woff]==4.60.1' python script/openmono.py <app-nerd build folder>
```

The script splits each style's text file with the websites' rules (`services/site/script/openmono.py`): the same Latin and Cyrillic blocks, the same keys and symbols in the Latin file, the stress marks in the Cyrillic file too, and the same subsetting options. Both scripts make the same files, byte for byte, and the same input gives the same bytes. The text rules in `src/index.css` have the `unicode-range` values of the websites' `openmono.json`.

It reads every input first, builds in a temporary folder, and replaces the checkout's files only when all checks pass. It writes nothing and says why when:

- a text file, an icons file or the license is missing;
- the icons files of the build's styles differ in code points, outlines or horizontal metrics;
- a character of a file is outside the `unicode-range` of that file's own `@font-face` rule, or a rule's range takes a character that only another file of the same style has, unless that file's rule comes later;
- a copyright line of the build's license is not in the third-party notices.

**Known limits**

- The subset files keep only the layout features for accents, as the websites' files do. The app sets no font features for code, so nothing visible changes, but `zero`, `frac` and `cv01` to `cv04` are not in the files.
- OpenMono has all but 12 of the code points the old terminal font had (among them `⟵ ⟶ ⟷ ⟅ ⟆` and two fullwidth braces) and all but 6 of the old code font's (control and format characters, the ideographic space and two private-use code points). Those draw from the system fallback font.
- Safari ignores the three metric overrides. In the web app there, inline code backgrounds are 17px tall instead of 18px.
- A bold italic terminal cell uses the Italic file made bold by the browser.

**Not in this PR**

- `Inter.ttf` is 875 KB with no `font-display`, and is the largest font cost at startup. Converting it to WOFF2 (about 349 KB) is a separate change.

### How did you verify your code works?

- The DevTools protocol reports the rendered font of code blocks, inline code, diffs and shell output as `OpenMonoNerd-*` from the app's `@font-face` rules. prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. This follows the release of OpenMono 1.000.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The data site (`packages/data/app`), its Open Graph cards and the shared nav menus set their text in OpenMono, Anomaly's typeface, built on Iosevka by Belleve Invis (SIL OFL 1.1). The files are the website's subsets of the OpenMono 1.000 build, so both sites serve the same bytes.

- **Family name.** `"OpenMono"` in `src/routes/index.css`, with the stand-ins renamed to `"OpenMono Menlo"`, `"OpenMono Consolas"` and `"OpenMono Courier"`.
- **Layout does not move.** The metrics are identical (advance 600 of 1000, ascender 965, descender 285, x-height 520, cap height 690). Only C, c, G and the letters built on them changed shape, by 0.002 em.
- **Weights.** Unchanged: the Regular file serves 100 to 599 and the Bold file 600 to 900, so the page's 500 text stays Regular and its 600 and 900 text stays Bold.
- **Ligatures.** Off, as before: the files have none.
- **Cyrillic.** The language menu lists Русский and Українська, which OpenMono can now draw. They are in a `cyrillic` file of their own (18 kB, with the two stress marks), so a page fetches that and not the `rest` file, which is 122 kB now that the font has Greek, Vietnamese, Armenian and more. The `cyrillic` rule comes after the `rest` rule, which has the stress marks too, so a stressed word such as `ру́сский` fetches the Cyrillic file only (checked in Chromium).
- **Open Graph cards.** The OG Worker's font modules are renamed to `openmono-{regular,bold}-{latin,rest}.bin`, in the build and in the pinned deploy targets. The deploy compares the two, so they change together. A card whose text is in the Latin file and has no C, c or G is pixel-identical.
- **Characters outside the Latin file now draw.** Satori keeps one face per family name and weight, so with both files named alike the `rest` file was never used and `⚠`, `✓` or `⥈` drew as the empty box. This was so before the rename. Each file now has a family name of its own (`OpenMono`, `OpenMono Rest`) and the card names both, which costs no bytes. A new test renders `α`, `⥈` and a character no file has, and fails if any two come out alike. With the final build the two `rest` modules are 414 kB and 407 kB (they were 90 kB each), and the OG Worker's files are 5.8 MB, 2.2 MB gzipped.
- **Common symbols in the Latin file.** The site's Latin files now also have 27 common symbols (`✓ ✗ ✕ ✖ ⚠ ∙ ⋅ ≈ ≠ ≤ ≥ ∞ √ ∑ ⋯ �` and the numbers `⁰ ⁴ ⁵ ⁶ ⁷ ⁸ ⁹ ₀ ₁ σ Σ`), so a page or a card that shows one does not need the `rest` file. The Latin file grows by 1.5 kB.
- **This PR edits `.github/release/targets/data/`** (`dev/og.json` and `production/og.json`: the four font module names, nothing else). That path needs a review from its code owner, `@thdxr`.
- **Card cache.** `cardVersion` goes from 2 to 3, so every page links a new image URL and the card is drawn with the new font the first time that URL is asked for. It does not purge the old URLs: a preview that a site has already unfurled stays as it is until that site fetches the page again, and an old URL can be served from the edge for up to 7 days, then one more day while it revalidates.
- **Nav menus.** The fallback family in `packages/nav-menus` becomes `"OpenMono"`. A host that does not set `--nav-menu-mono` gets that fallback, so it must load OpenMono or set the token. Hosts of the package:
  - `packages/data/app` (this PR): uses the fallback, and loads OpenMono here.
  - `services/site`: sets `--nav-menu-mono`, so it is not affected.
  - The Console repository's synced copy, used by its site and its status page (`packages/status/public/nav-menus.css`): neither sets the token on its `dev`. **The Console must merge anomalyco/opencode-console#8139, which sets it in both, before it next syncs `packages/nav-menus`**; otherwise its lockup and menus fall to the system monospace font.
  - A code search of the organisation finds no other copy.

| Font bytes | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular Latin (preloaded) | 19,084 | 29,416 |
| Bold Latin | 18,700 | 29,060 |
| All served files | 91,380 (4 files) | 339,152 (6 files) |
| Of those, the two `rest` files | 53,596 | 244,312 |

**Feature flag.** None. The data site reads no flags, and the pinned OG module names cannot be switched at run time. The gate was the font's release, and OpenMono 1.000 is out.

**Refresh the fonts** after the website's files change, from `packages/data/app`:

```sh
bun script/openmono.ts ../../../services/site/src/asset/fonts
```

It reads every file and checks each `@font-face` rule in `index.css` against the range of its own file before it writes anything, so a missing file or one stale rule leaves the app's fonts untouched. Until the website's PR is merged, give it that branch's folder.

Companion: #64796 (the website and docs). This PR can merge before or after it: it carries its own font files, and the website sets `--nav-menu-mono` and never uses the fallback family.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun run check` at the root (lint, and typecheck of every package), which the pre-push hook also ran. `bun typecheck` and `bun test` in `packages/data/app` (37 pass, including the OG Worker build and the new render test) and in `packages/nav-menus` (11 pass), and `bun typecheck` in `services/data`.
- The OG Worker build lists exactly the modules in both pinned targets.
- The new render test fails with the two files under one family name and passes with their own names.
- The copy script with a source file missing, and with the Regular rules right and a Bold rule stale: each stops with "Nothing was written", names the file, and the app's fonts keep their hashes.
- A model card and a lab card rendered from `dev` and from this branch: the letters change and the layout does not, and their `?v=` values change.
- `/data/compare` on the development server in Chromium, light and dark: the browser reports `OpenMonoNerd-Regular` and `-Bold` from the bundled files for all mono text, and the open nav menu resolves to OpenMono.
- The main page needs the stats database, which was not available. It was checked as the deployed dev page with this branch's built stylesheets and fonts in place of the deployed ones: same 6,403 glyphs, all drawn by the bundled files, 0.009% of pixels differ.
- Not checked: the deployed OG Worker, Safari, Firefox, Windows and Linux fallbacks, and phones.

### Screenshots / recordings

| --- | --- | --- |
| Main page | ![Data main page before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24f7aedf-a440-4670-a4c1-7ca55b7b378d) | ![Data main page after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f662295-5e46-4a00-9da9-7b63843fa71d) |

The main page is the deployed dev page; the after shots use this branch's stylesheets and fonts. Only the C, c and G change.

### Issue for this PR

No issue. This follows the release of OpenMono 1.000.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The website and the docs (`services/site`) set their mono text in OpenMono, Anomaly's typeface, built on Iosevka by Belleve Invis (SIL OFL 1.1). The files come from the OpenMono 1.000 build.

- **Family name.** `"OpenMono"` in CSS, with the metric-matched stand-ins renamed to `"OpenMono Menlo"`, `"OpenMono Consolas"` and `"OpenMono Courier"`. The previous family name is gone from the service, and `test/fonts.test.ts` now fails if it comes back.
- **Same letters as Desktop.** `src/docs/assets/fonts/OpenMono-{Regular,Bold,Italic,BoldItalic}.woff2` are the text files of the final app build (1.000, build 2026-11-19; no ligatures, every character one cell). `script/openmono.py` splits each into three files by the rules OpenCode Desktop's script uses: no character is left out, every style has a Cyrillic file, and the ranges around the Powerline characters are exact. The Latin file also has the six keys that shortcuts name (`⌃ ⌘ ⌥ ⌫ ⎋ ⏎`) and 27 common symbols (below). With the same two lists, both scripts make the same files.
- **Layout does not move.** Units per em, advance (600), ascender, descender, line gap, x-height and cap height are identical, so every size, weight, tracking, line height and the fallback overrides stay as they are. Of the 1,320 characters the site served before, the upright styles change the shape of C, c, G and the letters built on them (29 characters, terminals 0.002 em longer). The italics slant 11.8° where they slanted 12°, and their C, c and G terminals move 0.02 em. `⥈` and `⬰` are now one cell wide.
- **Weights.** Unchanged: Regular draws 100 to 500 and Bold draws 600 to 900. Section titles keep their 0.2 px stroke as the stand-in for Medium.
- **Ligatures.** Off, as before: the source has none and the subsets keep only `ccmp`, `locl`, `mark` and `mkmk`.
- **Cyrillic.** OpenMono has Cyrillic, so the Russian and Ukrainian pages now set mono text in OpenMono and not in the system font. It is a file of its own (`cyrillic`, in every style) so those pages fetch 18 kB and not the whole `rest` file. That file also has the two stress marks (U+0300 and U+0301), so a stressed letter such as `у́` sets in OpenMono; a browser takes a letter and its mark from one file or falls back for both. The `rest` file has those marks too, so each style's `cyrillic` rule comes after its `rest` rule: a browser asks the last rule that has a character first, and `ру́сский` then fetches the Latin and Cyrillic files only (checked in Chromium; with the other order it also fetched the 123 kB `rest` file). A Latin letter that has no code point of its own with its mark, such as `x́`, still falls back, as on `dev`.
- **Every character the font has.** The final build adds Greek, Vietnamese, Armenian and more, which are in the `rest` file (122 kB in Regular). `⇧` is in the Latin range again. The search box on every docs page shows `⌘K`, which the font now has: from the `rest` file that one character would cost 122 kB a page, so the shortcut keys are in the Latin file and a docs page still fetches only the two Latin files.
- **Common symbols in the Latin file.** For the same reason, 27 symbols that a terminal prints or that a page sets in mono are in the Latin file, which grows by 1.5 kB (Regular: 27,876 to 29,416 bytes): the status marks `✓ ✗ ✕ ✖ ⚠`; the dots `∙ ⋅` of terminal recordings; the math signs `≈ ≠ ≤ ≥ ∞ √ ∑`; `⋯` and `�`, which a changelog page has in code; and `⁰ ⁴ ⁵ ⁶ ⁷ ⁸ ⁹ ₀ ₁ σ Σ`, the numbers on `/font` (the page sets its `σ` in capitals). The list comes from a scan of the rendered mono text of every page of the site and the docs in Chromium, each page in a browser context of its own. Before, `/font` and `/changelog/v2.3.1` fetched the `rest` file; now no page does.
- **Docs stylesheet budget.** 30,665 of 30,720 gzipped bytes (`dev` is at 30,492). In blocks where the font lacks only unassigned or rare code points (Greek, Armenian, phonetic letters, superscripts, currency, letterlike and technical symbols, Latin Extended-D to G, double-struck letters, legacy computing symbols) a `unicode-range` runs on across the gaps, up to a character another file has. The only cost is that a page using one of the lacking characters fetches the `rest` file before it falls back.
- **Settings.** `monoFontRevision` goes to 3, so a mono font saved on the development server resets to OpenMono once.
- **Credits.** `humans.txt` credits OpenMono, Iosevka by Belleve Invis, and the licence. `src/asset/fonts/OpenMono-OFL.txt` carries the copyright lines of the build.
- **Link cards.** `script/og.ts` renders its four cards (`/product/browse`, the changelog release card, and the two legal documents) with the new files. Each font file now has a family name of its own there: Satori keeps one face per family name and weight, so under one name only the Latin file was ever used. The four cards are English and render the same bytes as before that fix. `src/asset/og/release.jpg` is captured again from this branch; inside the card's crop it differs from the old still only by the font. The two legal stills stay: those pages have changed since the stills were made, so a new capture changes more than the font.
- **Brand rules for agents** (`/brand.md`). One new rule: turn OpenMono's code ligatures off, because the released family has them on and OpenCode shows none.
- **Terminal captures.** `script/capture-assets.ts` records the Terminal screenshots and product video cuts with VHS and an installed font. Its default is now OpenMono Nerd, the terminal family: the status marks come from the font, and arrows and the ellipsis are one cell wide. VHS draws each cell on its own, so neither family shows ligatures.
- **Badges.** The 160 `-mono` badge files are not redrawn. Their text is outlines, and only the C of OpenCode differs, by 0.002 em: 0.02 px on the 20 px badge and 0.05 px on the 44 px one.

| Font bytes | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular Latin (preloaded on every page) | 19,084 | 29,416 |
| Bold Latin | 18,700 | 29,060 |
| All served files | 193,076 (8 files) | 728,284 (12 files) |
| Of those, the four `rest` files | 113,372 | 523,972 |
| Source files in the repo | 250,508 | 856,072 |

The Latin files are larger because the build stores accented letters as full outlines, not as components. The `rest` files are larger because the font has 3,552 characters where it had 1,321; a page fetches one only when it uses one of those characters. First load of mono fonts: 29,416 bytes on the home page, 58,476 on a docs page (Regular and Bold Latin), 47,828 on the Russian home page.

**Feature flag.** None. The site reads no flags, and a typeface cannot be half on: both families would have to ship. The gate was the font's release, and OpenMono 1.000 is out.

**Refresh the fonts** after a font build, from `services/site`:

```sh
uvx --from 'fonttools[woff]==4.60.1' python script/openmono.py path/to/app-nerd
```

It reads and checks every input and builds every file in a temporary folder before it replaces anything, so a missing source, a file that is not the one-cell build, or styles whose characters differ leave the checkout untouched. With the same ranges, no other file changes.

**Follow-ups**, after this merges:

- Export the 13 OG Studio cards again, with their 13 videos and 153 locale cards (`src/asset/og-studio/manifest.json`). They are made by hand in OG Studio and are not part of this PR.
- Redraw the 160 `-mono` badge files in `public/brand/badges`. They were drawn with the earlier build of the same letters, so the copy that calls them OpenMono is right to within 0.002 em in one letter, the C of OpenCode.
- Capture `src/asset/og/privacy-policy.jpg` and `terms-of-service.jpg` again, as a change of their own.
- Capture `public/brand/screenshots/opencode-terminal-{dark,light}.png` (and `.webp`) again with `script/capture-assets.ts`.
- Record the Terminal and SDK product videos and posters again.
- When the OpenMono repository is public, link it from the Type rules in `/brand.md` and from `humans.txt`.

Companion: #64798 (the data app). The two can merge in either order.

`packages/nav-menus` is not in this PR. The site sets `--nav-menu-mono` itself, so the menus follow `--font-mono` and never use the package's fallback family. Until #64798 merges, that fallback still carries the old family name into the site's compiled stylesheet as a dead value; the guard test scans `services/site`, not that package.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun run check` at the root (lint, and typecheck of every package), which the pre-push hook also ran. `bun typecheck` and `bun test` in `services/site` (242 pass).
- `bun run build -- --mode dev` on the current `dev`, which includes the docs build and its budget. Then the home page, product, Brand, legal, changelog, the font page and three docs pages in Chromium, light and dark. On each page the browser reports the drawn mono font as `OpenMonoNerd-Regular` or `-Bold` from the bundled files, no element still names the old family, and on the English pages under 0.03% of pixels differ from `dev` (the C, c and G shapes). With the final build, checked again on the home page, the Russian home page, the changelog, the font page and three docs pages: no mono text is drawn by a system font. With the common symbols in the Latin file, a scan of all 265 site pages and 666 docs pages finds none that fetches a `rest` file.

- The refresh script against a folder with a source missing, with a two-cell font, and with one style short of characters: each stops with "Nothing was written" and the checkout's files keep their hashes.
- `ру́` in a browser with the old and the new Cyrillic file: the stressed letters were Menlo and are now OpenMono.
- The four link cards from `script/og.ts` build and are byte-identical before and after the family names. A test line with `⥈ ⚠ ✓` and Cyrillic drew empty boxes under one family name and the glyphs under separate names. The new release still was compared with the old one and with a capture of `dev`.

prs.title: test(browser): wait for the menu's first row before End
prs.body:
## The flake

- `browser-pane.spec.ts`, "restores the full pane when the toolbar closes and keeps the selected device on reopen", fails at `expect(moreDevices).toBeFocused()` after `End`: focus is on the first row, "Responsive".
- It fails alone, so no earlier test or shared worker state is involved.

## Cause

- A menu opened from the keyboard shows its rows before it takes the keyboard. Kobalte defers the menu's autofocus (`deferAutoFocus`) until its items are mounted.
- The test pressed `End` once the rows were visible. When that came before the first row had focus, the key went to the trigger, which ignores it, and focus then landed on the first row.

Measured from the opening `ArrowDown`, 30 runs per row (ms, min / median / max):

| | Rows visible | First row focused |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal speed | 12 / 14 / 21 | 21 / 33 / 38 |
| 4× CPU throttling | 101 / 121–141 / 222 | 169 / 194–227 / 348 |

Events from an instrumented run (ms since page load):

| | Failing run | Passing run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ArrowDown` on the trigger | 517 | 5194 |
| menu rows in the page | 531 | 5207 |
| `End` | 547 on the **trigger**, ignored | 5227 on "Responsive" |
| focus | 569 "Responsive" | 5222 "Responsive", 5230 "More devices" |

## Fix

```ts
await expect(option("Responsive")).toBeFocused()
await page.keyboard.press("End")
await expect(moreDevices).toBeFocused()
```

- The test waits for the menu's first row to be focused, which is the menu's own signal that it has the keyboard.
- No timeout, retry or product change.

## Counts (Windows, 2 workers, retries off)

| Run | `dev` | With the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The test alone | 5 of 40 failed (an instrumented copy: 9 of 40) | 0 of 80 |
| Whole file | 2 of 10 runs failed | 0 of 20 |

- `browser-pane*` and `plugin-host` specs, cold story server: 148 passed, no dependency re-optimization.
- Three other tests press a key on a menu right after it opens: `browser-pane-restore.spec.ts:328` and `:360`, and `browser-pane.spec.ts:2021`. They focus the menu item they press, so the key cannot go to the trigger, and each passed 40 of 40. They are unchanged.

## Limits

- On a slow or busy machine (4× CPU throttling: 170–350 ms) a fast ArrowDown-then-End can lose the End in any dropdown menu, because the shared menu focuses its first row after it shows it. This PR does not change that.

Feature flag: none needed. Test only.

prs.title: fix(tui): retry session reads after reconnect instead of returning to start screen
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60839. Related: #59543, #53497.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

After sleep or a shared-service restart, the TUI re-reads the session it is showing on every event-stream reconnect. If that read fails once (ECONNRESET, a brief 503), the view currently toasts and goes to the start screen, even though the session and its rows are still cached. Long-running panes therefore look lost and need `opencode -s <id>` to recover.

This ports the approach from #59543 by @x0c (thanks!) onto current `dev`:

- `retry()` takes an abort signal and exports `isTransientError`.
- A small `retrySessionSync()` retries transient transport errors and 408/429/5xx responses (5 attempts), cancelled when the route or connection changes.
- Session metadata and initial history reads use it. After retries run out, a temporary error only shows a toast and keeps the cached session visible; the view leaves only when the session is actually missing. Older-page failures stay best-effort.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/util`: 160 tests pass. `packages/tui`: 1744 pass, 2 skip; the 2 failing `dialog-shell-output` 5s timeouts reproduce on pristine `dev` here and are unrelated. `tsc -b` and Prettier pass. The bot's #60839 reproduction script keeps the session here and ends on the start screen on base.

prs.title: test(browser): wait for the menu to return focus before submitting the page note
prs.body:
## The flake

- `browser-pane.spec.ts`, "keeps a page note editable beside a tiny viewport and attaches it to the session", fails at the last assertion: the note is not attached.
- The next test, "adds the whole page to the session and keeps the draft when the button is pressed again", has the same steps and fails the same way.
- It started with #63002 (`cd0d037d68`), which moved "Add page to session" into the Browser options menu.

## Cause

- A menu returns focus to its button one task after it closes (Kobalte's `setTimeout(0)` in its focus scope, then `DropdownMenuContent.onCloseAutoFocus`).
- The tests pick "Add page to session" a second time and then call `editor.press("Enter")`, which focuses the editor first. When that focus lands in the one task between the menu's removal and its focus restore, the button takes focus back and Enter opens the menu again.

Focus and key events from an instrumented run (ms since page load):

| | Failing run | Passing run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| menu item pressed | 927 | 6083 |
| menu removed | 941 | 6096 |
| focus | 942 editor, then 942 **Browser options** | 6098 Browser options, then 6100 editor |
| Enter | 944 on **Browser options**, menu opens | 6101 on the editor, note attached |

- This is a test race, not a product bug. A person cannot focus the editor inside that task.
- The first "Add page to session" is not affected: in 120 of 120 instrumented runs (60 of them with 4× CPU throttling) the editor took focus before the menu was removed, and kept it.

## Fix

```ts
await addPage(page, root)
await expect(root.getByRole("button", { name: "Browser options", exact: true })).toBeFocused()
await expect(editor).toHaveValue("Check the header layout")
await editor.press("Enter")
```

- Both tests wait for the menu's button to have focus, which is the app's own signal that the menu finished closing.
- No timeout, retry or product change.

## Counts (Windows, 2 workers, retries off)

| Run | `dev` | With the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "keeps a page note editable…" alone | 9 of 60 failed | 0 of 120 |
| "adds the whole page…" alone | 8 of 60 failed | 0 of 120 |
| Both, whole file | 0 of 10 each | 0 of 20 each |

- The whole-file runs on `dev` did not reproduce the failure in 10 runs, so the before and after evidence is the runs of each test alone.
- `browser-pane*` and `plugin-host` specs, cold story server: 148 passed, no dependency re-optimization.

## Not in this change

- The whole-file runs showed another flaky test in the same file, with and without this change: "restores the full pane when the toolbar closes and keeps the selected device on reopen" failed 2 of 10 on `dev` and 3 of 20 with the fix, at `await expect(moreDevices).toBeFocused()` after `End`. It is not investigated here.

With edits set to expanded, a file diff in the timeline has no height limit, so a 300-line write takes over 7,000px. These blocks were capped at 420px (240px for writes) with inner scrolling until aaf8317c82 removed the caps when it added the expand setting. Now an opened file diff shows at most 420px. prs.title: fix(desktop): open projects and new sessions from opencode:// links again
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. The routing was lost in #40947 (`a1b4843a33`, "refactor(app): remove legacy layout", Aug 7): `handleDeepLinks` lived only in the legacy layout (`packages/app/src/pages/layout.tsx`), which listened for `opencode:deep-link`. The new layout never had a listener, so links already did nothing there. #43789 (`9be3aa92b5`) then deleted the unused parser (`pages/layout/deep-links.ts`).

Since then the desktop still receives the link, delivers it to a window and focuses that window, and nothing opens.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Restores the two links from #10072 and #15322, with the same URLs:

- `opencode://open-project?directory=<folder>` adds the folder as a project on the app's own server and opens a new session in it.
- `opencode://new-session?directory=<folder>&prompt=<text>` does the same with the prompt typed into the composer. The prompt is not sent.

How it works:

- **App:** a small state machine (`src/shell/deep-links/machine.ts`) parses the links and holds them until the app's own server is connected and has its project list. Then it opens them in order. A folder the server can't open shows the server's error, as Open project does. The shell runs it through a new optional `platform.onDeepLinks`. The web platform doesn't define it, so the web app is unchanged.
- **Desktop renderer:** links that reach the window before the app listens wait in `startup/deep-links.ts` and go to the first listener. That replaces the unused `window.__OPENCODE__.deepLinks` array and `opencode:deep-link` event.
- **Desktop main, cold start:** the entry module now keeps the links the app was **started** with and hands them to the `DeepLinks` router once it exists. Until now these were never read:
  - On Windows and Linux they are on the command line (`process.argv`), which nothing read; only `second-instance` argv was read.
  - On macOS they arrive as `open-url` while the app finishes launching. The router's listener is installed only after the main bundle loads, so the link could arrive before it.

**Platforms:** this fixes every platform where the scheme is registered, which is all three desktop platforms:

- **Windows:** `app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient("opencode")` at startup writes the per-user registration.
- **macOS:** the bundle's `CFBundleURLTypes`, from electron-builder's `protocols`.
- **Linux:** the same `protocols` entry in the package's desktop file, plus `setAsDefaultProtocolClient` at startup.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test src/shell/deep-links` in `packages/app` with its usual preloads (12 pass, new):
  - parsing: Windows and POSIX folders, an optional prompt, missing or control-character folders, other hosts and schemes, a malformed URL;
  - a link that started the app waits for the server, then all open in order;
  - a link opens at once while the server is ready and waits again after it drops;
  - links the app doesn't open change nothing.
- `bun test src/renderer/startup/deep-links.test.ts src/main/deep-links` in `packages/desktop` (9 pass). The new case checks that links that came before the app listened reach its first listener once, and that later links reach the current listeners.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/app`, `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/desktop`, `bun run lint:changed origin/dev` clean.
- Not tested: clicking a real `opencode://` link with the app running or closed, on any platform. That needs an installed build that owns the scheme.

### Checklist

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(desktop): drag files from the file tree into other Windows apps
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Ported from the native Rune desktop build (`anomalyco/rune-desktop`, `features/open-in/src/lib.rs` `drag_item`, and Rune's `crates/rune/src/drag_out/windows.rs`).

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

On Windows, a file or folder dragged from the file tree now drops into other apps as the file itself: File Explorer copies it, a browser uploads it, a chat app attaches it. Today the drag carries only text, so other apps get nothing or a `file:` string.

A drop back into the composer still adds an `@` mention, as it does today.

How it works:

- The tree sets its drag data as before, then calls a new built-in host API, `desktop.dragOut(event, path)`, with the row's absolute path. The tree calls it only for a session on a local server (the same check as Open in).
- On Windows desktop the host cancels the page's drag and asks main for a system drag (`FilesStartDrag`). Main checks that the path is absolute and exists, then calls `webContents.startDrag` with the file's shell icon.
- The host keeps the page drag's `text/plain` until main answers that the drag ended. A drop into the composer whose single file is that path reads as that text, so it becomes the same mention. While the drag is out, the composer shows its mention drop state, not the attachment one.

Only Windows changes. The desktop platform defines `startFileDrag` only when `os === "windows"`, and main's `startDrag` returns false unless `process.platform === "win32"`. Elsewhere `dragOut` returns false and the tree's own drag goes on, so macOS, Linux and the web are unchanged.

`dragOut` is on `BuiltinDesktop` (`@opencode/plugin/gui/builtin`), not the public SDK.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `src/runtime/platform/drag-out.test.ts` in `packages/app` (2 pass, new):
  - with a system drag, `dragstart` is cancelled, and only a drop of that one file reads as the row's text, until the drag ends;
  - without one, the row keeps its own drag.
- `src/composer/attachments` in `packages/app` (6 pass), `bun test src/file` in `packages/gui-plugins` (195 pass).
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/plugin`, `packages/app` and `packages/gui-plugins`, `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/desktop`, `bun script/sdk-docs.ts` and `bun run lint:changed origin/dev` clean.
- Not tested: a real drag to File Explorer, a browser or back into the composer. That needs a mouse on a visible desktop. The mention on a drop back relies on Windows' `startDrag` returning only after the drop, which is how Electron's Windows implementation reads. If it returned sooner, such a drop would add the file as an attachment instead.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not captured: needs a visible desktop.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(app): keep an open session's side tabs when old sessions are forgotten
prs.body:
A person switches back to a session whose shell tab was open the whole time, and its side panel is empty: its file, review, terminal and browser tabs are gone. Nobody closed them. #65322 is the browser's half; this is the host's, for every tab kind.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The open session's side panel, empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1504a852-7679-41fa-804d-ae48feed12cd) | ![The open session's file tab, kept](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e886d784-d6c5-480b-8e27-c1657449959e) |

The app's e2e build, with 52 stored side strips: 51 closed sessions and one session open in a background shell tab. The pictures show that session's side panel after the person switches to it.

## Cause

- **The cap ignored open sessions.** The layout stores the side-panel state of 50 sessions (`layout.tsx:383`, `prune` at `:428`). `pruneSessionKeys` (`helpers.ts:21`) ranked them only by `used` (`layout.tsx:386`), the time each was last on screen in this run. Once 50 others were used, a session still open in a shell tab went.
- **The ranking does not outlive a restart.** `used` starts empty, so every session not used yet ranks equal, and `.slice(input.max)` (`helpers.ts:42`) dropped the keys stored last: the newest sessions, open or not.

## The rule

- **A session open in a shell tab is never forgotten.** The shell tabs are mounted above the layout (`TabsProvider` in `app.tsx`, `LayoutProvider` in `routes.tsx`). `AppLayout`, which has both, hands the layout the fact, so the layout does not import the tabs:

```tsx
const open = () => (tabs.restoreReady() ? (key: string) => sessionKeyOpen(key, tabs.store, servers.scope) : undefined)

<LayoutProvider open={open}>
```

- **Nothing is forgotten for want of knowledge.** `open` is undefined until the saved shell tabs have loaded. The first prune waits for it, and a later one returns at once without it.
- **After a restart the keys stored first go first**, so the newest sessions stay.

## What the cap still drops

For a session that is **not** open in a shell tab and falls outside the 50, the layout still forgets (`dropSessionState`, `layout.tsx:407`, and `prune`):

- its file, review, terminal and browser tabs, the selection, and the split and bottom placement;
- side-tab scroll offsets and the recently closed list;
- **the unsent prompt draft**, the file-view state, and every plugin's session store.

Not changed here.

## Tests

All fail on `dev`.

- `e2e/regression/side-panels.spec.ts`: the real app with 52 stored strips. At startup the two oldest closed sessions go and the open one, stored last, stays. A file scrolled in the session on screen prunes again and drops the next oldest. The background session then shows its file tab. On `dev` the startup prune drops the open session.
- `layout.test.ts`: `pruneSessionKeys` keeps open sessions, also when they outnumber the cap, and drops the keys stored first in a new run; `sessionKeyOpen` matches a tab's shown or routed session on the same server.

## Limits

- **Ranking after a restart is by stored order**, not by last use: `used` is still not stored.
- **More open sessions than the cap** are all kept, so the stored layout can exceed 50.
- **A saved server that never appears** keeps the shell tabs from loading, and nothing is pruned in that run.
- `createSessionKeyReader` changes one line (`typeof` to `Predicate.isString`): `lint:changed` fails on `anti-slop/no-runtime-typeof` there once the file is touched.
- **Not run:** the desktop app, whose storage loads asynchronously; macOS and Linux.

No feature flag: a fix.

prs.title: feat(desktop): answer permission requests from Windows toast buttons
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Ported from the native Rune desktop build (`anomalyco/rune-desktop`, `features/notifications/src/actions.rs`, and Rune's `crates/rune-notify/src/windows.rs`).

Stacked on #65325, which adds the toast tags this uses. Its base is that branch, so the diff here is only this change.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

On Windows, a permission request's toast now has **Allow once**, **Allow always** and **Deny**, the same answers and labels as the permission dock. A button answers the request where you are, without bringing the app forward. A click on the toast's body still opens the session.

How it works:

- The renderer asks main to post the toast (`WindowShowToast`). Main builds it with `toastXml`: the body and each button open an `opencode://toast/<token>?action=<id>` link (`activationType="protocol"`).
- Windows runs the app with that link, and the running app gets it on `second-instance`. Main looks up the token, then sends `ToastActivated` to the window that posted the toast. That window replies through `data.session.permission.reply`, as the dock does. A reply that fails opens the session.
- The token is a random UUID per toast, held only in main's memory. A link from a web page, another program or a toast from an earlier run names no live toast, so it answers nothing and only brings the app forward.
- When the toast can't have working buttons, main says so and the renderer posts today's plain toast. That happens when `opencode://` opens another install (`app.isDefaultProtocolClient`) or notifications aren't supported.
- Answering in the app, or from another client, takes the toast back through #65325's `dismissNotification`, which now also closes main's toast.

Which notifications fire, and when, is unchanged: the Permissions notification setting and the cross-window claim still decide. No new setting. Questions keep their plain toast.

macOS, Linux and the web are unchanged. The renderer only asks main for a toast with buttons when `os === "windows"`. Main posts one, and treats `opencode://toast/...` links as toast links, only when `process.platform === "win32"`. Other platforms' `opencode://` links go to `DeepLinks` as before.

Possible follow-up, not in this PR:

- Register a COM toast activator at install (NSIS `CustomActivator` and `LocalServer32`, called through `ffi-rs`).

prs.title: fix(browser): keep every open tab in the strip
prs.body:
A person comes back to a session and its browser tabs are gone from the right pane: all but the one the agent worked in last, or the next one to open. Nobody closed any, and the desktop still held every one.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![One tab left of three](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba2f9042-d88d-4ecf-95b4-d4504b6c1f15) | ![All three tabs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/728fb598-17fa-42f4-8718-ec6286f51e2c) |

Three tabs are open. The person uses fifty other sessions, the agent works in Pricing, and the person comes back. Pictures are from the pane's component fixture: the real side region, pane and model, the host's own `pruneSessionKeys` choosing the strip to forget, main's events through the Ipc schema, made-up pages.

## Cause

| Path | On `dev` | What happened |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The host forgets a strip | `layout.tsx:428` `prune`, `helpers.ts:21` | The layout stores the strips of the 50 sessions used last. A session open in a shell tab is not excluded, and the whole strip goes with no plugin told. |
| A session returns in another directory | `host-apis.tsx:690-698` | Its strip is copied to the new key only while the session is listed. |
| The window only added new tabs | `machine.ts:1311`, `:467` | `ids.filter((id) => !mirrored.includes(id))`: a tab the desktop had already was never added again, and the panel lists only inventory tabs the strip stores. The next `focus-strip-tab` then stored one tab, alone. |
| A registration replaced main's tabs | `pane-machine.ts:567` | A new binding started from the inventory the window last heard. A tab opened since (its report on the way, or not sent yet) left the desktop, the saved tabs and the strip. |

## The rule: the strip shows main's inventory

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[main reports an inventory] --> M
  B[the person comes to the session] --> M
  C[main asks to show one tab] --> M
  M["machine.ts: lost = tabs the inventory had before, that the strip no longer stores, minus the ones the person is closing"]
  M --> S["sync-strip { open, placed }"]
  S --> H["layout.open(key, session, { tab: 'append', after })"]
```

- **Every tab main holds comes back**, each once, after the tab before it in main's order.
- **A tab the person closes stays out.** The machine keeps its close (`closing`) until the desktop answers. A close no binding could take is kept and sent with the next inventory, instead of being dropped.
- **A registration merges.** The new binding lists the window's inventory and every tab main still holds: the tabs of the binding it replaces, else the saved ones.

```ts
const listed = (held.length > 0 ? held : saved).reduce<readonly Browser.Tab[]>((tabs, tab, index, own) => {
  if (tabs.some((item) => item.id === tab.id)) return tabs
  const before = tabs.findIndex((item) => item.id === own[index - 1]?.id)

  return before === -1 ? [...tabs, tab] : [...tabs.slice(0, before + 1), tab, ...tabs.slice(before + 1)]
}, restore.tabs)
```

## Unchanged

- A tab the strip stores never moves. A new tab lands where it did (#65126), and a restored strip draws once in its saved order (#65067).
- No host code, no plugin API (public or built-in) and no stored shape changed.

## Tests

All fail on `dev`.

- `machine.test.ts`, "the strip shows the desktop's inventory": a lost strip gets every tab back with the next report, when the person returns, and before the agent's tab is selected; only lost tabs are placed; a tab the person closes stays out until the desktop answers; a close made while no binding could take it reaches the desktop.
- `pane-machine.test.ts`, "a registration keeps the tabs the window had not heard of": a tab opened in the binding being replaced, reported or not, and a tab main saved after the window's last report.
- `electron-open.test.ts`: the real pane in Electron registers again with an inventory of its first two tabs; the new binding lists every tab the pane held, in order.
- `browser-pane-restore.spec.ts`: three tabs, fifty other sessions used, the agent works in one tab, the person returns. On `dev` one tab is left. Now all three are drawn as before, with the same widths, and a tab the agent opens meanwhile joins them at the end.

## Limits

- **The other tabs of a forgotten strip are still lost**: files, review, terminals, the selection and the pane placement. That is the host's `prune`, which also drops an open session. Not changed here.
- **Selection**: only a tab main asks to show is selected again. Otherwise the pane shows the host's fallback.
- **Order**: a lost tab that was first in main's order goes to the end when the strip still stores later ones. The host can place a tab only after another.
- **Not run**: the host's `prune` inside the real layout provider (the story calls `pruneSessionKeys` itself), a session that moves while its shell tab is closed, the installed app, macOS and Linux.

No feature flag: a fix.

### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Ported from the native Rune desktop build, which reads the Windows contrast theme's colours for its window chrome (`anomalyco/rune`, `crates/rune/src/platform/preferences.rs`).

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

With a Windows contrast theme on (Settings › Accessibility › Contrast themes), Chromium repaints the page in the theme's system colours, but the native caption buttons drawn by `titleBarOverlay` keep the app theme's `white` or `black`. macOS and Linux are unchanged: both the colour choice and the listener run only when `process.platform === "win32"`, and macOS has no `titleBarOverlay`.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Ported from the native Rune desktop build (`anomalyco/rune-desktop`, `crates/opencode-runtime/src/window/placement.rs` and Rune's `platform/win32/placement.rs`).

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Fixes three ways a window reopens in the wrong place on Windows:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A window snapped to a display's edge (Win+Left, or dragged to the edge) reopens at the default size on the primary display. Windows counts the invisible resize borders in the window's bounds, so a left-half snap starts at `x = -7` and fails the "fits on a display" check by a few pixels. | Bounds may hang up to 16px past a display's edges and still count as fitting. |
| A maximized window moved to another display with Win+Shift+Arrow keeps the restored frame it had on the first display, because bounds are only read while the window is restored. On restore it is centred on the new display instead of where Windows put it. | While maximized, the saved frame comes from `getNormalBounds()`, the frame Windows keeps for a maximized window and moves with it. |
| Closing a minimized window (from the taskbar, or at sign-out) saves it as not maximized, with its display taken from the `-32000, -32000` frame Windows gives minimized windows. A maximized window then reopens restored. | A minimized window's state isn't updated, so it reopens as it was shown before it was minimized. |

Each change applies only when `process.platform === "win32"`; macOS and Linux keep today's behaviour. `manageWindowState` now takes the subset of `BrowserWindow` it uses, so the test can drive it.

- `bun test src/main/windows/window-state.test.ts` (11 pass): new cases for the snapped window (kept on `win32`, reset on `linux`), the maximized window's restore frame, and the minimized window, the last two through the real `close` and `closed` events and the state file written. prs.title: feat(desktop): open in Windows Terminal and list only installed apps on Windows
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Ported from the native Rune desktop build (`anomalyco/rune-desktop`, `features/open-in/src/windows.rs`).

### Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Two changes to the file panel's **Open in** menu on Windows.

**Windows Terminal is listed.** It opens a new Windows Terminal window in the file's folder (`wt -w new -d .`, with the folder as the working directory), never a tab in a window the user already has open. The folder is never put on `wt`'s command line, because Windows Terminal splits its arguments on `;` even inside quotes, so a repository named `a;b` would start a second command. The entry has its own drawn mark (`windows-terminal.svg`) and the English label `Windows Terminal`; other locales fall back to it until translated.

**Only installed apps are listed.** `checkAppExists` answered `true` for every app on Windows, so VS Code, Cursor, Zed and Sublime Text showed up on machines without them, and picking one failed. It now asks `resolveAppPath`, which runs the `where` lookup it already had, and when `where` finds nothing it also looks in the folder each installer uses (for example `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe`, `%ProgramFiles%\Sublime Text\sublime_text.exe`, or Windows Terminal's Store alias in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps`). An app found that way also opens, since `openPath` resolves the same path.

PowerShell 7 gets no entry of its own: the existing PowerShell entry already opens `pwsh` when it is installed.

macOS and Linux are unchanged: the Windows Terminal entry is only in `WINDOWS_OPEN_APPS`, and the new launch and detection code runs only when `process.platform === "win32"`. In `app-icon.tsx`, `typeof document !== "object"` became `!("document" in globalThis)` (same result) because the file was touched and `lint:changed` flags the old check.

- `bun test src/main/files/apps.test.ts` on Windows, with an empty `PATH` and scratch `LOCALAPPDATA` and `ProgramFiles`: Windows Terminal's alias is found in its installer's folder, and Sublime Text and VS Code are reported missing. prs.title: fix(desktop): resync server event streams after Windows resumes from sleep
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Ported from the native Rune desktop build (`anomalyco/rune-desktop`, `apps/desktop/src/workspace/lifecycle/launch/network.rs`), which wakes every server stream on resume.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

When a Windows laptop wakes from sleep with the app window still visible, each server's event stream can still read as connected while its socket died during sleep. Nothing replaces it until the stream's idle watchdog fires: the renderer's `pageLifecycle` handlers only react to `online` (which does not fire when Chromium never saw the network drop) and to a hidden page becoming visible again.

Main now listens for `powerMonitor`'s `resume` and sends every app window a `SystemResumed` event. Each server connection then calls its existing `connection.internal.resync(...)`, the same path that "Network connection restored" uses. A stream that is not connected ignores it, as it does today.

The listener is installed only when `process.platform === "win32"`, so macOS and Linux are unchanged. The same wiring would help on macOS too; that is left for a separate change. The web platform has no `onSystemResume`, so the app's code path is a no-op there.

prs.title: fix(browser): keep the pane's tabs unless the person or the agent closes them
prs.body:
A person clicks a link in the conversation. Its page opens in a new tab of the right pane and shows. About 15 seconds later, while they type a prompt, the tab closes by itself. A link to an address that does not answer opens a tab that closes at once. Nobody closed either, and the window says nothing.

- **Now:** a tab that showed a page stays until the person, the agent's close tool or the page itself closes it.
- **Since:** #63002 (19 Nov). Release 2.3.2 does not have this code.

| | The strip after the link's tab opened and the person typed |
|---|---|
| Before | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ae67b89-5b14-4a9c-9538-89619e5b6ab3) |
| After | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fce4fdca-f0cd-4891-8d33-63286fd5051e) |

![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd6a5eee-7a19-466a-bd0f-cc43f3460e92)

## Cause

`tabs.open` makes the tab, then runs its first navigation, and undoes the tab when that navigation rejects (`pane.ts:1181`, `:1192` on `dev`; the agent's file preview does the same at `:1120`).

```ts
opening.defer(() => { if (page(binding, tabID) === opened) dispatchBinding(binding, { type: "tab.closed", tabID }) })
await opened.execute({ action: { type: "navigate", tabID, url: action.url }, files: [] }, signal, origin)
```

- **A page still loading:** the navigation rejects when the page has not fired `load` within 15 s (`navigation-deadline.ts:13`, around `loadURL` at `chromium.ts:1334`). A page with slow ads or one hanging request has shown long before that.
- **A page that fails to load:** `loadURL` rejects with Chromium's error.
- **Silent:** the window's command swallows both, because "the tab itself reports" them (`pane.ts:580`). By then the tab is gone.

## What removes a tab

| Path | Who | |
|---|---|---|
| `tabs.close`: strip button, shortcut, menu, "Leave site?", the agent's tool | person, agent | kept |
| `window.close()`, a pop-up whose first address is refused | the page | kept |
| A plugin closing the tab it opened, an extension's `chrome.tabs.remove` | the person's plugin or extension | kept |
| Session deleted: main forgets its saved tabs | person | kept |
| `tabs.open` undone when its first load rejects | **nobody** | **fixed** |
| The agent's file preview undone the same way | **nobody** | **fixed** for a page still loading |
| A binding that closes (session switch, reconnect, idle eviction, reload): pages are released, the tabs come back unloaded | no removal since #63002 | unchanged |
| A registration that lands before a new tab's first report restores without it | **nobody**, a window of milliseconds | listed |
| Host: the layout keeps 50 session strips and drops the rest, whole (`layout.tsx` `prune`) | **nobody** | listed, host |
| Host: a strip key removed without the plugin is not added again in that run, since the window only appends tabs new to the inventory | **nobody** | listed |

## Fix

- **One rule** (`keepsOpenedTab` in `errors.ts`) decides what an open leaves behind when its first load rejects:

  | The first load | The person's tab | A plugin's tab (`experimental.open`) | The agent's tab |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | still under way at the deadline | stays, loading; the command settles | stays; the call resolves with the handle | stays, reported and shown as a tab that loaded; the agent's error names the tab |
  | failed by Chromium | stays, with the page that says why and offers Reload | stays; the call resolves with the handle | undone; the agent gets the failure |
  | committed no page (cancelled, became a download), or the pane could not open it | undone | undone; the call rejects | undone |

- **A tab that stays is an ordinary tab.** One path (`firstLoad` in `pane.ts`) serves the tab that loaded and the tab that stays: its state is refreshed, it is announced and shown per the same options (`focus: false` keeps it in the background, a file preview takes the pane), and its opener holds it. No tab exists whose opener has neither a handle nor an undo.
- **The agent's error names its tab**, in the message only (no tool schema changed): `browser.tabs.open failed. The browser page did not finish starting or navigating. Reload the tab and inspect it before retrying. The tab stays open as tab_…: use that tabID with browser.wait, browser.reload or browser.tabs.close, and do not open the address again.`
- **`experimental.open`** documented a rejection only for an unavailable pane or a session not on screen. Its TSDoc and the guide now say that it resolves once the tab exists, also while the page loads or after the load failed, and rejects when the address opened no page.

- **Deadline as an input:** the pane and its pages take `navigationDeadlineMs` for a `navigate` command's load. Production passes nothing and gets `NAVIGATION_DEADLINE_MS`, the same 15 s. Page start-up keeps the constant.
- **Log:** main writes `browser tab closed: its open failed` when it undoes a tab, and `browser pane closed` with the reason when a binding closes. The desktop log had no line about either. The window's `[browser] unmapped failure` line now carries the failure's code and the action as text; it passed them as an object, which the desktop log wrote as `[object Object]`. No unmapped failure removes the pane or a tab that existed: the only removal behind one is an open undone as in the table, which main logs.

## Unchanged

- Every close the person or the agent asks for, a page that closes itself, a deleted session.
- The agent's open of an address that fails to load still leaves no tab.
- No window behaviour and no stored shape changed, so the strip's order, widths and selection are untouched. The only window change is the text of one log line.

## Tested

| | On `dev` | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `electron-open.test.ts`: the real pane in Electron, attached to a stand-in server, opening tabs as a conversation link, a plugin and the agent do | fails: both tabs are gone from the inventory | **Person:** two tabs open, then a link to a page that shows and keeps loading past the deadline, and a link to a page that fails to load. Every tab is still reported, in order; the commands do not fail. **Plugin:** both of those opens resolve with a handle and `closeTab` on it closes the tab; an address that opens no page rejects and leaves no tab. **Agent:** a tab kept at the deadline is announced in front, in the background with `focus: false`, and a file preview takes the pane; each error names the tab. The fixture gives the pane a 300 ms deadline, so a run takes about 3.5 s |
| `browser-pane-model.test.ts` | fails: the log call gets an object | the unmapped-failure line holds the code and the action as text |
| `errors.test.ts` | new rule | each row of the table above, for the person and the agent |
| `navigation-deadline.test.ts` | passes | the default is still 15 s, to the millisecond |

## Limits

- **Release 2.3.2 loses tabs another way** (#64734): a window that left a session closed its binding as `client.closed`, and main forgot the saved tabs. `dev` fixed that in #63002: the window's close keeps them, and `pane-machine.test.ts` "only explicit deletion forgets the saved tabs" guards it. #64742 targets the old code; on `dev` it would keep a deleted session's tabs.
- **"All tabs but one"**, as reported on 2.3.2, is not reproduced here. That build was not run.
- The pictures are the component fixture's strip, fed what main reported in the Electron run on each head.
- The `[browser] unmapped failure [object Object]` line in the owner's log of 21 Nov cannot be decoded: its fields were not written.
- The agent's open of an address that fails to load is still undone, and its tab is drawn in the strip meanwhile as an unselected "New tab".

No feature flag: a fix.

prs.title: fix: fix Windows MCP pool and review toggle CI failures
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Fixes the two dev CI failures left after https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65302, which fixed the core typecheck. One commit each.

**1. `unit (windows)`: `MCP pool > fails a pooled server that can't be spawned after one attempt`** (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/44843747161, https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/44842940962). Since https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65282, a stdio server that exits during the auto probe gets respawned once for a plain `initialize`, for legacy servers that quit on the unknown request. On Windows a missing command spawns through the shell and only shows up as that same exit, so the private connection now spawns twice. That's the intended fallback, so the test's Windows count goes from 1 to 2. Linux and macOS still fail at spawn, with no private attempt.

**2. `e2e (*, app-1)`: `review toggle stays at the header edge`**, plus intermittent `session header groups controls...` failures. These began with https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65213 and have failed in most app-affected dev runs since (e.g. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/44828483743, https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/44843747161). That PR renders a second copy of the review toggle in the panel's strip, shown once the panel settles open, and hides the header's copy. This broke the tests in two ways:

- The pixel check hides `.session-review-v2-tabs-bar` and compares. Once the panel settles, the toggle being measured is the strip's copy, so hiding the bar hides the toggle itself and the screenshots never match.
- Playwright keeps acting on the element it first resolved. A click that starts on the header's copy while the panel is still moving waits until the test times out, because that copy stays hidden after the swap.

The tests now wait for the strip's copy before acting on the settled panel. The pixel check hides everything in the strip except the toggle.

Waiting for the settled panel exposed a real regression that the race had been hiding. Pressing Enter on the strip's toggle closed the panel and moved focus to the composer instead of keeping it on the toggle. `giveBackFocus` treats any focus inside `#review-panel` as "the reader was in the panel" and sends it back to where it was before opening. The strip's toggle belongs to the session, as `closed-tabs.ts` already assumes, so `giveBackFocus` now skips it. `guardClosingFocus` then hands focus to the header's copy, as the existing `toBeFocused()` assertion expects:

```diff
  open the panel, let it settle, Tab to the strip's toggle, press Enter
- focus: composer
+ focus: header's Toggle review
```

This is the only product change: `packages/app/src/runtime/plugin/panels.tsx`.

Not addressed: `summary overlays the view and submenus follow` (session-summary.spec.ts) sometimes fails on Windows. It was already flaky before https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65213 (flaky in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/44769478490), and I couldn't reproduce it locally, even with CPU throttling.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun run check` at the root passes
- `packages/core`: `bun test test/mcp.test.ts -t "MCP pool"` passes. The Windows count is inferred from the CI log (2 spawns received) and the new fallback; I couldn't run it on Windows locally.
- `packages/app`, built mode: on `dev`, `review toggle stays at the header edge` failed 3 of 8 runs. With the settle wait but without the `panels.tsx` fix, it failed 12 of 12 at `expect(toggle).toBeFocused()`. With both, it passed 6 of 6 and the session-header case passed 6 of 6 (`--repeat-each --retries=0`).
- I ran every spec that uses the review toggle (review, session-header, session-summary, side-panels, tabs, terminal, panel-edges, session-panel-scrollbar, subagent-child-navigation). The 9 local failures also fail on unchanged `dev` on macOS: shortcut and modifier tests that the e2e guide says only pass on CI's Windows UA.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(app): keep the background pill's rows in place
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR No issue. Reported by Luke: with many subagents running, the rows in the background work menu keep changing places. ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? - **Cause:** subagent rows took the order of `data.session.list()`, which sorts every loaded session by `time.updated`, newest first. The app reads a session's info again when its run starts or ends, when it is opened, and when its tab is selected again. Each read moved that row to the top. - **Fix:** `createSessionBackground` orders each group by when its work was created, then by id. That time never changes, so a row keeps its place until a row above it leaves. - **Keys:** subagents use the session's `time.created`. Shells and scripts use their start time, because their lists can also come back in another order after a reconnect. - **Unchanged:** the groups still read subagents, scripts, shells. A subagent that goes idle and resumes returns to the same place. - **Cost:** one sort of the open session's descendants, shells and jobs, inside memos that already walk those lists. No strobe benchmark was run. ```mermaid flowchart LR E["run starts or ends
row opened
tab selected"] --> R[app re-reads session info] R --> U[time.updated changes] U --> L["data.session.list() re-sorts"] L -->|before| J[row jumps to the top] L -->|after| K["no effect: rows sort by time.created"] ``` ```ts // packages/app/src/session/requests/background.ts function oldestFirst(items: readonly T[], created: (item: T) => number) { return items.toSorted((a, b) => created(a) - created(b) || (a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0)) } ``` ### How did you verify your code works? - New case in `test-browser/session-background.test.ts`: it reorders the session, shell and job lists and expects the same rows. It fails on `dev`, where the rows follow the lists. - Ran `createSessionBackground` from `dev` and from this branch on the same reordered input: `dev` moved the rows, this branch did not. The test suite runs in CI. ### Screenshots / recordings A simulation of both rules on the same 40 events, not the app. Each number is the order in which the subagent was created. | Before: `time.updated`, newest first | After: `time.created`, oldest first | | --- | --- | | ![Before: rows in mixed order, 114 row jumps](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e66e62aa-12a3-42a6-ae92-8668e3985ef9) | ![After: rows in creation order, 0 row jumps](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d903cbd7-3d3f-4b4a-8283-d4feb92f0a4e) | ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: test(core): expect the legacy respawn when a pooled server exits during the handshake
prs.body:
## What failed
`check-test / unit (windows)`: `MCP pool > fails a pooled server that can't be spawned after one attempt` has failed on every Windows unit run since #65282 landed, except run 10747. I couldn't download that run's logs, so I can't confirm why it passed; my guess is that it didn't run the core tests, since its commit only touched the app. This is a real regression, not flakiness.

## Root cause
#65282 (`bda12b51d`, "feat(mcp): negotiate the newest protocol by default") made `auto` the default protocol. It also made `McpClient.connect` respawn a local server with `legacy` when the server closes during the `server/discover` probe (`ConnectionClosed` / `EraNegotiationFailed`), for legacy servers that exit when they get the probe.

On Windows, cross-spawn runs a missing command through `cmd.exe`, so the spawn succeeds and the missing command only shows up as an exit during the handshake. The pool counts that as the server answering but refusing, so the location opens its own connection. That connection keeps the configured protocol, as the pool intends ("a refusal proves nothing about the protocol"): it probes, sees the exit and respawns for `legacy`. So the location now spawns twice on Windows, while the test still expected 1. On Linux the spawn fails with ENOENT, which the pool treats as final, so the location never spawns and the count is 0.

## Fix
- Expect 2 location spawns on Windows (0 elsewhere, unchanged) and update the comment to explain why.
- Add a test that runs on every platform, `connects on its own, probe then legacy, when a pooled server exits during the handshake`. It uses a server that exits immediately (`process.execPath -e "process.exit(1)"`) to reproduce the Windows behaviour, and checks the status is failed, there is 1 pool attempt and there are 2 location spawns. Linux CI now covers this path.

No product code changed. If you'd rather have the pool send the location straight to `legacy` when the shared attempt closed during the probe (saving a spawn for real legacy servers too), that goes against the pool's current design and would need a separate change.

## Verification
- Reproduced on Linux before the fix: with the exiting server, asserting 1 location spawn failed with `Expected length: 1, Received length: 2`.
- `cd packages/core && bun test test/mcp.test.ts -t "MCP pool"`: 23 pass, 0 fail, three runs in a row.
- `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/core` is clean.
- The Windows test itself couldn't be run in this sandbox.

---

**CI failure:** `check-test / unit (windows) / MCP pool > fails a pooled server that can't be spawned after one attempt` failed 3 runs in a row on `dev`.
- Failing run: [run 10758](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/44850378877) at `09bfa60` (first failing: [run 10749](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/44849368967))
- Last green run: [run 10747](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/44849335911) at `80f41d7`
- Culprit: [`bda12b5`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/bda12b51d7f32c5876f6d79366feb9b6637f5eb9)

Opened by the CI fix job: it does not merge or push to `dev`.
