prs.title: fix(coding-agent): pass Windows bash commands in an environment variable
prs.body:
Closes #12340

## Problem

On Windows, Git Bash (and MSYS2/Cygwin bash) parse their command line with the Cygwin runtime. For a process started by a non-Cygwin parent such as Node, that runtime:

- silently cuts any quoted argument to 8,186 characters, and
- splits unquoted arguments at newlines (Node quotes only arguments with a space, tab or `"`).

`bash -c <command>` therefore runs only part of the command and exits 0:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `printf 'START\n'; # <8,300 x a>` `\nprintf 'DONE\n'` | prints `START`, exit 0 |
| `true\nfalse` | runs `true` with `$0=false`, exit 0 |

Measured with `spawnSync(bash, ["-c", 'printf %s "${#1}"', "_", value])`: an unquoted 20,000-character value arrives intact, a quoted one arrives as 8,186 characters. `dash.exe` from Git behaves the same, so it is not bash, RPC, or the 32,767-character Windows command-line limit.

## Fix

On Windows, a shell named `bash.exe`/`bash` that is not a WSL launcher (System32/Sysnative, which keep stdin, or the `WindowsApps` alias, which keeps argv) gets a new `"env"` command transport:

```sh
bash -c '__pi_command=${PI_BASH_COMMAND?pi: ...}; unset PI_BASH_COMMAND; eval "$__pi_command"'
```

- The environment arrives whole or the spawn fails, so no partial delivery (also no 32 KB cap; 200K-character commands work).
- stdin stays ignored, so `rg` without a path, `BASH_ENV` files and `SHELLOPTS=errexit` behave as before.
- The variable is unset before the command runs, so children do not inherit it.
- A caller that still appends the command to `args` fails with an error instead of running nothing.

The bash tool, `!command` config values and durable's `NodeExecutionEnv` set the variable. Other shells, Linux and macOS are unchanged.

### Alternatives rejected

- `bash -s` over stdin (as for legacy WSL): a command that reads stdin consumes the rest of the script.
- Stdin with a reader script: `rg` sees a pipe and searches stdin, timeouts can run a half-written command, `errexit` and stdin-reading `BASH_ENV` files break it.
- `MSYS=noglob`: Cygwin then stops handling quotes, breaking short commands too.
- Splitting into several sub-8 KB arguments: newline splitting still corrupts space-free chunks, and the 32 KB cap stays.

### Remaining differences on Windows bash

- Syntax errors say `eval: line N` instead of `-c: line N`.
- `xtrace` shows the command as the argument to `eval`.
- With `set -a` from a startup file, `__pi_command` would be exported.

`getShellConfig()` is public: extensions spawning the shell themselves must handle `commandTransport: "env"` (noted in the changelog).

## Testing

- `test/windows-shell-config.test.ts`: which shells get which transport, plus runs through the real executor (`createLocalShellOperations`) for a long command, the newline split, `$?`/stdin/exit, the hidden variable, and a caller appending to `args`.
- Issue repro over RPC on the built CLI (Windows 11, Git for Windows): 8 KB and 200 KB commands print `START`/`DONE`; `true\nfalse` exits 1.
- `resolve-config-value`, `bash-execution`, durable `env-node` pass. `tools.test.ts` has 4 Windows failures that also fail on `main`.

prs.title: fix(ai): Gemini 3+ detection for prefixed Google model IDs, add compat.supportsStrictMode
prs.body:
Closes #12321

Google adapters decided Gemini 3+ behavior from model IDs starting with `gemini-N`. Gemini models served under prefixed IDs, such as `randomprefix-gemini-4-argon`, were treated as older Gemini: no strict tools (`strict: "prefer"` fell back, `strict: "require"` failed), no tool-call IDs, and tool-result images in a separate user turn. The thinking-level check (`usesGoogleThinkingLevel`) already matched `gemini-N` anywhere in the ID, so the same model got Gemini 3+ thinking but pre-3 tool handling.

Two changes:

1. `getGeminiMajorVersion` matches `gemini-N` anywhere in the ID, like `usesGoogleThinkingLevel`. Prefixed Gemini 3+ IDs get strict tools, tool-call IDs, and multimodal function responses without configuration. No built-in catalog model changes behavior (all built-in Google IDs start with `gemini-`).
2. `compat.supportsStrictMode` for the `google-generative-ai` and `google-vertex` APIs, following the OpenAI, Mistral, and Bedrock adapters, for IDs that carry no version at all. When set, it decides; when unset, the ID detection applies (as in `openai-completions`).

```json
"compat": { "supportsStrictMode": true }
```

- `google-shared.ts`: unanchored version match; `supportsGoogleStrictToolSampling(model)` reads the override
- `compat-schema.ts`: `GoogleCompatSchema`, registered for both Google APIs and in the provider-level schema

prs.title: fix(ai): resolve Bedrock SSO credentials through HTTPS_PROXY
prs.body:
With `HTTPS_PROXY` set, the Bedrock runtime client gets a proxy-aware `NodeHttpHandler`, but credentials still come from the AWS SDK's default chain. For SSO profiles that chain creates its own `SSOClient` (GetRoleCredentials) and `SSOOIDCClient` (token refresh). Both are built only from the credential provider's `clientConfig` and do not inherit the Bedrock client's request handler. So these requests go direct, and on networks that only allow traffic through a proxy the run hangs until it times out.

When a proxy is in use, pi now sets the client's `credentialDefaultProvider` hook to `(init) => defaultProvider({ ...init, clientConfig: { ...init.clientConfig, requestHandler } })` with the same proxy handler. The SDK calls this hook only when `credentials` is unset, with its usual chain input, so it builds the same default chain as before and the SSO and SSO OIDC requests go through the proxy.

Other credential sources keep their behavior:
- Env keys, `AWS_BEDROCK_SKIP_AUTH` and bearer tokens don't reach this branch.
- STS assume-role already inherited the handler.
- Container, IMDS and `credential_process` credentials ignore `clientConfig`.
- A configured profile still wins over ambient env keys.

`@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node` was already installed as a dependency of `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime`. It is now a direct dependency of `pi-ai`, pinned to the same version, and the lockfiles and install lock are updated.

Not changed: the proxy is still chosen for the Bedrock host only. If the Bedrock endpoint matches `NO_PROXY` but the SSO portal needs the proxy (or the reverse), SSO requests follow the Bedrock decision. This is an edge case that didn't seem worth a per-host handler here.

Testing:
- Added `test/bedrock-proxy-credentials.test.ts`. It runs a local CONNECT proxy and a temporary SSO profile with a cached token, and points `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_SSO` at `sso.invalid` so nothing reaches the network. It checks that the SSO request reaches the proxy. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `test/bedrock-credentials.test.ts` checks that explicit access keys still win when a proxy is set.
- I also checked the `sso_session` token-refresh path (SSO OIDC `CreateToken`) with a temporary variant of the test. It reaches the proxy with the fix and does not without it. That variant is not committed.
- Ran `npm run check` and all `test/bedrock-*.test.ts` plus `test/node-http-proxy.test.ts`. I also ran the two credential test files with `HTTPS_PROXY` and lowercase `https_proxy` set in the environment.
- Manual run with a logging proxy and a fake SSO profile: `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8888 AWS_PROFILE=my-profile pi -ne --provider amazon-bedrock ... -p ok`.
  - Before: the proxy saw nothing and the SSO call went straight to AWS.
  - After: the proxy logs `CONNECT portal.sso.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com:443`.

Fixes #12353

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): tree navigation no longer re-adds prompts to history
prs.body:
Closes #12279.

**Problem.** Both tree navigation paths (the `/tree` selector and the extension `navigateTree` action) re-render the chat with `renderInitialMessages()`, which renders with `populateHistory: true`. Every navigation therefore adds the prompts of the branch it lands on to Up-arrow history again. `Editor.addToHistory` only skips a repeat of the latest entry, so with prompts p1..p5:

- before: `p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`
- after going back to p4: `p3 p2 p1 p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`
- after going back to p3: `p2 p1 p3 p2 p1 p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`

History is capped at 100, so the repeats also push older entries out.

**Fix.** `renderInitialMessages()` takes `{ populateHistory?: boolean }` (default `true`), and both tree navigation paths pass `false`. Startup and session switches still fill history from the session. This matches the rebuild after compaction (`rebuildChatFromMessages`), which already re-renders without populating history.

One consequence: navigating to a branch whose prompts were never rendered in this process (one written by an earlier run and not on the branch pi started on) no longer adds those prompts to history. History is otherwise filled only from submitted prompts and the startup branch, so this follows the existing rule.

**Validation** on main `05fd3fbda0`:

- New tests in `test/interactive-mode-tree-navigation.test.ts`: tree navigation re-renders with `populateHistory: false`, and `renderInitialMessages()` populates history by default and not with `false`. Both fail without the fix.
- In tmux, with an empty agent dir and a session of five prompts, rewinding twice with double Esc: before, history grows to the lists above; after, it stays `p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`.
- `npm run check` passes. In `./test.sh` the only failures are unrelated to this change:
  - The find tool tests fail because fd is not installed here and `PI_OFFLINE=1` prevents downloading it.
  - The pi-env tests need cargo, which is not installed here.
  - One `auth-storage` test also fails on main; chord's `state-fuzz` timed out under load and passes on its own.

prs.title: fix(tui): move repeated prompts to the front of editor history instead of duplicating them
prs.body:
Fixes #12279. Alternative to #12280.

**Problem.** Tree navigation re-renders the branch with `populateHistory: true`, which calls `Editor.addToHistory` for every prompt on the branch. `addToHistory` only skipped a repeat of the most recent entry, so each navigation duplicated the branch's prompts. With prompts p1..p5, going back to p4 turned history `p5 p4 p3 p2 p1` into `p3 p2 p1 p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`, and the duplicates push older entries out of the 100-entry cap.

**Fix.** `addToHistory` now moves a prompt that is already in history to the most recent position instead of adding it again (like zsh `HIST_IGNORE_ALL_DUPS`).

Why here and not in the callers (#12280 stops tree navigation from filling history):
- Navigating to a branch from an earlier run that pi did not start on still adds its prompts to Up-arrow history, once. With #12280 those prompts never reach history.
- `/fork`, `/clone` and `/resume` back to a session also re-add prompts; this covers them without changes in coding-agent.

Behavior change: a prompt submitted several times is stored once, at its latest position. The old test "allows non-consecutive duplicates in history" was replaced.

**Validation.**
- New editor test for #12279; it and the updated duplicate test fail on the old code.
- tmux, session with prompts p1..p5, going back with `/tree`: history is `p3 p2 p1 p5 p4` after going back to p4, then `p2 p1 p3 p5 p4` after going back to p3. Before: 8, then 10 entries.
- `npm run check` passes.

prs.title: fix(durable): list only reachable code-mode namespaces
prs.body:
## Problem

When a conversation's `AgentDoc.tools` is an exact allowlist, code mode's prompt section still lists every selected extension's namespace and description while all of that namespace's tools are disabled for the agent. The model reads a manual for tools it cannot call: `await tools.example_list({})` is `undefined`, and `describeNamespace("example")` returns `{ ..., tools: [] }`.

## Root cause

- `packages/durable/src/codemode/describe.ts`: `declaredNamespaces()` collects every selected extension's namespace and `codemodeSection()` prints each heading, without checking whether any of the namespace's tools survived `resolveAgent()`'s filter (`callers` plus the agent's `tools` allowlist).
- `packages/durable/src/codemode/codemode.ts`: `start.namespaces` is built from the same list, so `describeNamespace()` answers for an unreachable namespace too.
- `namespacesOf()` attributed a duplicate tool name to the first extension declaring it, while `resolveAgent()` composes tools last-wins; with duplicate names the heading can describe a different extension than the tool that runs.

## Fix

- Add `listableNamespaces(extensions, callable)`: a namespace is listed when at least one of its declared tools is in the agent's script-callable set, or when its extensions declare no tools yet (a server not connected, kept for prompt-cache stability as its deferred tools appear). A namespace whose declared tools are all unreachable is not listed; `start.namespaces` uses the same predicate, so `describeNamespace()` returns `undefined`.
- The decision uses only static metadata: the extensions' tool declarations and `agent.callable` (deferred tools included). It does not depend on connection state, `deferred`, or what was offered to the model, so the section text is unchanged before and after an extension's deferred tools appear.
- `namespacesOf()` now follows the winning registration (last), matching `resolveAgent()`.

## Tests

Ran in the PR branch: `packages/durable/test/codemode-describe.test.ts`, `packages/durable/test/codemode.test.ts`, `packages/durable/test/harness-callers.test.ts` — 56 passed. New cases: callers-only and allowlist-filtered namespaces are hidden, a zero-tool namespace stays listed, deferred appearance keeps the section identical, `describeNamespace()` returns `undefined` for a model-only namespace, and duplicate tool names follow the last extension.

Closes #12362.

AI assistance was used to prepare and validate this change.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): load sessions with very many entries after the last compaction
prs.body:
`buildContextEntries` in `session-manager.ts` appended the entries after the last compaction with `contextEntries.push(...path.slice(compactionIdx + 1))`. That spread passes every entry as a separate function argument. When a branch had about 120k or more entries after its last compaction, it threw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. Most such entries are extension custom or `context_edit` entries. After that, every context rebuild failed, as did `ctx.getContextUsage()` and opening the session with `--session`.

The change appends those entries with a plain loop instead. The result is unchanged: same entries, same order.

I found no other spread in session loading or context building whose size grows with session length. `getTree` still has `stack.push(...node.children)`, which would only overflow if a single entry had on the order of 100k direct children. I left it unchanged because it is not on the load or context path. Spreads in `packages/durable` add one storage page at a time, so their size is bounded.

## Testing
- Added a test in `test/session-manager/build-context.test.ts`: a compaction followed by 200,000 custom entries and a user message. Without the fix it fails with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. With the fix it passes and the context has the expected messages.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Reproduction from the issue: I generated a session with 150k custom entries after a compaction.
  - Before the fix, `SessionManager.open(file).buildSessionContext()` and `pi -ne --session big.jsonl -p hi` threw the RangeError.
  - After the fix, the context builds, and the CLI loads the session and only stops at the missing API key.

Fixes #12154

prs.title: fix(ai): report OpenAI Decisions cache read and write tokens
prs.body:
The OpenAI Decisions API (`gpt-6-luna` classifier) returns `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`. Like in the Responses API, both are already included in `input_tokens`. `parseClassifierUsage()` ignored them and always reported `cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0`, so every input token was counted as uncached input.

What this change does:

- `parseClassifierUsage()` (`packages/ai/src/api/classifier-shared.ts`) now reads both counts, reports them as `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite`, and subtracts them from `input`. `totalTokens` is unchanged. Bad counts are clamped: non-finite or negative values become 0, and cache counts are capped at `input_tokens`, so `input` cannot go negative.
- The catalog entry for the classifier (`packages/ai/catalog/providers/openai.ts`) had cache prices of 0. With the split usage, cached tokens would then have cost nothing. They are now priced at the input rate (0.1, and 0.2 above 272K), which matches the existing catalog note that the Decisions API bills input tokens only. The cost estimate stays exactly what it was; only the token breakdown changes.

**Pricing still to check:** the issue says the GA Decisions docs discount cache reads and charge cache writes, but I could not verify the actual GA rates. If they differ, change the two cache numbers in the catalog entry. The parser change does not depend on them.

**Shared parser:** `parseClassifierUsage()` is also used by the System One classifiers (`system-one-shared.ts`). Their responses carry no `input_tokens_details`, so their usage is unchanged. If one of them ever sent cache counts, those tokens would be priced at that model's cache rates, which are 0 today.

**Testing:**

- Added a test in `test/openai-decisions.test.ts`. It uses the built-in `gpt-6-luna` catalog model with the usage from the issue (2000 input, 1600 cached, 100 cache write) and expects `input: 300, cacheRead: 1600, cacheWrite: 100, totalTokens: 2000` and a cost of `$0.0002`. It fails without the parser change.
- Before the change, the same reproduction through `classify()` with a stubbed `fetch` gave `input: 2000, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0`. After it, it gives `input: 300, cacheRead: 1600, cacheWrite: 100`, same total cost.
- Ran `npm run check`, plus the `openai-decisions`, `classifier-models` and System One classifier tests in `packages/ai`.

Fixes #12264

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): show the end of an over-long line followed by a blank line in bash output
prs.body:
When a command's output ended with a line over 50KB followed by a blank line (output ending in `\n\n` or `\r\n\r\n`), the bash tool returned `(no output)`. Once the output passed about 200KB, it returned only newlines. The full log file was correct, but the model saw nothing. #12092 fixed the single-trailing-newline case and left this one out.

There were two causes:
- **`truncateTail()`** counts back from the end of the output. It kept the trailing blank line first. When it reached the long line, the byte limit was hit, and the partial-line path only ran when nothing had been kept yet.
- **`OutputAccumulator.snapshot()`**: after trimming its rolling buffer, the clipped tail was `"\n"`. That is truthy, so the `|| this.tailText` fallback from #12092 was skipped.

What the change does:
- **`truncateTail`:** when a line exceeds the byte limit and only blank lines come after it, it takes the end of that line, sized to fit the remaining budget, and keeps the trailing blank lines. Blank means empty or whitespace-only, so `\r` from CRLF counts. Short lines, whitespace-only content and line-limit truncation behave as before.
- **`OutputAccumulator.snapshot`:** it falls back to the unclipped tail when the clipped text is only whitespace, not only when it is empty.
- **Bash tool notice:** it now names the line that is actually partial (`startLine`). It used to name the last line, which is the blank one in this case. When the partial line is the only output line, the two are the same.

Not changed: the notice still says `(line is 0B)` when the long line ends with a newline. That is #10015, a separate cause in `getLastLineBytes()`.

**Testing**
- Added a parameterized test to `test/tools.test.ts`. It streams `first line` plus a long line and a blank line through the bash tool, in 8KB chunks, for three inputs:
  - 60KB with `\n`
  - 219KB with `\n`
  - 219KB with `\r\n`

  Each case checks that the end of the long line is shown and that the notice says `of line 2`. All three fail without the fix and pass with it.
- `node ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/tools.test.ts`: 117 passed. The truncate, bash and output tests also pass.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Reproduction through `createBashTool().execute()` with `python3` printing `first line\n` + 60000 or 219000 `y` + `END\n\n`:
  - Before: `(no output)\n\n[Showing lines 3-3 of 3 (50.0KB limit)…]` for 60000, and only newlines for 219000.
  - After: `…yyyEND\n\n\n[Showing last 50.0KB of line 2 …]` for both.

Fixes #12350

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): exit nonzero in JSON mode when the final response fails
prs.body:
`pi --mode json` exited 0 even when the final assistant message had stopReason `error` or `aborted`. Text print mode exits 1 for the same failure. The cause is in `runPrintMode` (`print-mode.ts`): the whole final-message check ran only inside `if (mode === "text")`.

What the change does:
- The check now runs in both modes.
- For `error` and `aborted`, both modes write the error message to stderr and return exit code 1.
- For `length` (output token limit reached), both modes write a truncation warning to stderr and return exit code 1.
- Only text mode writes the final assistant text to stdout. In JSON mode that message is already in the JSONL stream, and stdout stays pure JSONL.

**Behavior change to note:** `docs/cli-integration.md` described the old behavior on purpose ("A failed or aborted assistant response ... does not by itself produce a nonzero exit status"). This PR changes that contract and updates that paragraph. Scripts that relied on exit code 0 after a failed, aborted, or truncated JSON-mode run will now see exit code 1. If the old contract should stay, this PR should not be merged.

I found no other copy of this print/JSON exit logic in the repository.

Testing:
- Added a test in `test/print-mode.test.ts`: in JSON mode, an assistant error now returns exit code 1 and writes the error to stderr. The test fails without the change.
- The real CLI with a request that fails: `OPENAI_API_KEY=invalid pi --no-session --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini --mode json -p "Say hello" </dev/null`. The final `message_end` event has `stopReason: "error"`. Before the change it exits 0. After, it exits 1, with the error on stderr and the event stream unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ai): retry gateway provider-unavailable and partial-response errors
prs.body:
Some OpenRouter-style gateways send a mid-stream SSE `event: error` frame with no HTTP status. Examples:

- `The provider is temporarily unavailable. Retry shortly.`
- `The provider ended the response before it was complete.`
- `The connection to the provider was reset. Retry shortly.`
- `The provider reported a failure while generating the response.`

`isRetryableAssistantError` matched none of these. Auto-retry never started, and the agent run ended with the error. The existing pattern from #10965 only accepted "service … unavailable".

This change adds four patterns to `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN`:

- `provider.?(?:is.?)?temporarily.?unavailable`. "temporarily" is required here: a bare "provider unavailable" is often a lasting routing or region error, so it stays non-retryable.
- `ended the response before it was complete`
- `connection to the provider was reset`
- `reported a failure while generating the response`

The non-retryable quota and billing list is checked first, as before.

I did not add "Upstream response did not include complete usage data", also quoted in the issue. That error may repeat on every attempt for a given route, and retrying it would repeat full paid requests.

No other copy of the classifier needs the change. AgentSession and the durable harness both call `isRetryableAssistantError`.

**Testing**
- `packages/ai/test/retry.test.ts` has a new case that checks all five gateway messages from the issue are retryable. A second new case checks that "provider unavailable" without "temporarily" is not retried. The test file passes (56 tests).
- `npm run check` passes.
- Before the change, calling `isRetryableAssistantError` on the issue's messages returned `false` for all of them. After it, the five transient messages return `true`. The usage-data message still returns `false`.

Fixes #12227

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): repaint editor after extension pasteToEditor and setEditorText
prs.body:
Extensions can call `ctx.ui.pasteToEditor()` or `ctx.ui.setEditorText()` outside terminal input handling, for example after an `await` or in a timer inside a command handler. In that case the editor's text changed but nothing repainted, so the new text stayed invisible until the next key press. Neither the editor's `setText` nor its paste path requests a render. In the input loop, the TUI's normal render after each key hid this.

Both methods in the interactive extension UI context now call `this.ui.requestRender()` after changing the editor. When they are called during input handling, the extra call merges with the render that is already pending, so it costs nothing.

I checked the other interactive `ExtensionUIContext` methods and the internal `editor.setText` calls that run after an `await` (fork, tree navigation, external editor). All of them already request a render, so none needed the same fix. RPC mode forwards these calls to the client and is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ai): remove abort listeners after retry backoff
prs.body: *Completed retry backoffs now release their abort listeners, preventing caller-owned signals from accumulating stale retry state.* ## Context `retryAssistantCall()` attaches an abort listener while waiting between attempts. The listener uses `{ once: true }`, but that removes it only when the signal aborts. When the timer completes normally, the listener remains attached. As a result, three completed backoffs leave three listeners on the caller’s signal even when the subsequent attempt succeeds. Repeated retries can retain additional listeners and their closures for the lifetime of that signal. ## Implementation The backoff now uses a named abort handler. When the timer completes, it removes that handler before resolving. If the signal aborts first, the existing behavior remains unchanged: the timer is cleared, the listener removes itself after firing, and the retry returns an aborted assistant message. The retry regression exercises three transient failures followed by a successful response and verifies that no abort listeners remain on the caller-owned signal. ## Validation We created a temporary TUI hook which ran eleven timer-backed retry waits against one signal and displayed the listener count after every completed backoff. Node’s standard diagnostic was piped to a log file for review. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | On `origin/main`, each completed backoff retained another listener. The final count was 11 and Node emitted a `MaxListenersExceededWarning` whose stack pointed to `sleep()` in `retry.ts`. After this change, the listener count remained zero after every completed backoff. The final count was zero and the redirected warning log remained empty. Closes #10506

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep tool preview text readable across terminal themes
prs.body: *Tool previews now apply Pi’s theme foreground to unscoped highlighted text, keeping code readable when Pi and the terminal use contrasting color themes.* ## Context The shared syntax highlighter assigned colors to recognized tokens such as keywords and numbers, but emitted unscoped text without a foreground color. Identifiers, operators, spaces, and punctuation therefore inherited the terminal’s default foreground instead of Pi’s theme. This made ordinary code text nearly invisible on tool cards when the terminal and Pi used contrasting themes. A dark terminal with Pi’s light theme produced pale text on a pale card, while a light terminal with Pi’s dark theme produced dark text on a dark card. ## Implementation The CLI highlighting theme now uses Pi’s `text` color as its default formatter. Recognized syntax scopes continue to use their existing keyword, number, string, and other syntax colors. Regression coverage verifies that a fully unscoped identifier receives the theme foreground and that the foreground is restored for ordinary text after a syntax-colored keyword. ## Validation Reopened the same session with extension discovery disabled using `./pi-test.sh -ne --use-theme --session ` and verified that ordinary tokens use Pi’s foreground while syntax colors remain unchanged. | Theme combination | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Light Pi / Dark terminal | | | | Dark Pi / Light terminal | | | Closes #11092

prs.title: fix(ai,coding-agent): make system the default instruction role in openai-completions
prs.body:
TLDR:
On chat-completions api, change the default instruction role from developer to system.

Inspired by: #12101 by @qoli

---
The trigger was #10741: Groq's qwen/qwen3.8-27b failed on the first message:
`400: minijinja: rendering failed: raise_exception: Unexpected message role.`

Problem: openai-completions sent the system messages of every reasoning model with the `developer` role unless the catalog turned it off. `developer` is OpenAI's role; many other hosts' chat templates reject it, as Groq's Qwen template does.

Every new OpenAI-compatible provider or reasoning model hit the same bug until someone added `supportsDeveloperRole: false` to the catalog; about 20 provider files carried that line. Nothing in models.dev says which role a model accepts, so the catalog could not get this right on its own.

Solution: detectCompat() now defaults supportsDeveloperRole to true only for api.openai.com. Every other host gets `system`. This applies to the initial system prompt and to mid-conversation system messages.

Built-in models whose role changes from developer to system:
- groq: 5 (gpt-oss and Qwen)
- xiaomi, xiaomi-token-plan-*: 9 MiMo models
- openrouter: 89 openai/* and anthropic/* models; 12 of them (newer GPT models) also support mid-conversation system messages (supportsMidConvoSystemMessages), which change role too All other built-in Chat Completions models already sent `system`.

Why the default is only api.openai.com:
- api.openai.com keeps `developer` because OpenAI documents it as the role for its reasoning models. In practice this rarely matters: the built-in OpenAI models all use the Responses API, so it only affects custom models that call OpenAI through openai-completions.
- Azure is excluded. Its built-in OpenAI models also use the Responses API; its only built-in Chat Completions model is DeepSeek, which needs `system`.
- OpenRouter is excluded: its Chat Completions reference accepts `system` ("System message for setting behavior") and `developer` with the same fields, and gives no reason to prefer `developer` for any model (https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/chat/create-a-chat-completion). The openai/* and anthropic/* exception came in with #5309 without a reported need.
- compat.supportsDeveloperRole still overrides the default.
- The Responses API has its own setting and is unchanged.

The now-redundant `supportsDeveloperRole: false` lines are removed from the catalog and the llama extension.

How we checked it is safe: live requests to the affected hosts, each model given the same instruction once as `developer` and once as `system`:
- Groq qwen/qwen3.8-27b: developer 400, system OK. Groq gpt-oss-20b: both OK.
- Xiaomi mimo-v2.6-pro and mimo-v2.6-flash: both roles OK.
- OpenRouter openai/gpt-5-mini, openai/gpt-oss-20b, anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, moonshotai/kimi-k2.6, qwen/qwen3.6-plus, deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro: both roles OK.
- OpenRouter openai/gpt-5.4-mini and openai/gpt-5.5 with an instruction added mid-conversation: both roles OK.

Released clients: they fetch new catalogs from pi.dev and still default supportsDeveloperRole to true, so the removed `false` lines would make them send `developer` to hosts that reject it. MINIMUM_PI_VERSION is raised to 1.5.3 so they keep the last catalog published for them.

closes #10741 #12101

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): tree navigation no longer re-adds prompts to history
prs.body:
Closes #12279.

## Problem

Both tree navigation paths (the `/tree` selector and the extension `navigateTree` action) re-render the chat with `renderInitialMessages()`, which renders with `populateHistory: true`. Every navigation therefore adds the prompts of the branch it lands on to Up-arrow history again. `Editor.addToHistory` only skips a repeat of the latest entry, so with prompts p1..p5:

- before: `p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`
- after going back to p4: `p3 p2 p1 p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`
- after going back to p3: `p2 p1 p5 p4 p3 p2 p1` (plus any intermediate resends)

History is capped at 100, so the repeats also push older entries out.

## Fix

`renderInitialMessages()` takes `{ populateHistory?: boolean }` (default `true`), and both tree navigation paths pass `false`. Startup and session switches still fill history from the session. This matches the rebuild after compaction (`rebuildChatFromMessages`), which already re-renders without populating history.

One consequence: navigating to a branch whose prompts were never rendered in this process (one written by an earlier run and not on the branch pi started on) no longer adds those prompts to history. History is otherwise filled only from submitted prompts and the startup branch, so this follows the existing rule.

## Validation

- New tests in `test/interactive-mode-tree-navigation.test.ts`: tree navigation re-renders with `populateHistory: false`, and `renderInitialMessages()` populates history by default and not with `false`. Both fail without the fix.
- `npm run check` passes (biome, pinned-deps, runtime-deps, ts-imports, entry-graphs, install-lock, tsc, browser-smoke).
- Full suite `./test.sh` passes except for unrelated environment failures (fd not installed, cargo not installed, pre-existing auth-storage test failure, chord state-fuzz timeout under load).

releases.name: v1.6.0
releases.body:
### New Features

- **GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol**: both models are available on the `openai`, `azure`, and `openai-codex` providers, and GPT-6.2 Sol is now the default model for all three. See [Providers](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.6.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/providers.md).

### Breaking Changes

- Extension components: `render()` now returns `readonly string[]`, and `Container` returns the same cached array while its children are unchanged. Extensions that modify render output in place, including `super.render()` in a `Container` subclass or an embedded component's output, must copy it first ([#9549](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9549))

### Added

- Added GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol to the `openai`, `azure`, and `openai-codex` providers. Both reject reasoning effort `none` and `minimal`, so thinking level `off` is unavailable. Azure serves them with a 1.05M context window; Codex serves GPT-6.2 Sol with 500K and GPT-6.2 Astra with 272K
- Added `qwen4-max-preview` to the Qwen Token Plan Individual providers ([#12259](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12259))
- Added `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` to the Qwen Token Plan Individual providers, and per-plan key variables `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_TEAM_API_KEY`, `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_TEAM_CN_API_KEY`, `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_INDIVIDUAL_API_KEY`, and `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_INDIVIDUAL_CN_API_KEY`; the shared `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY` and `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_CN_API_KEY` still work ([#11773](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11773))
- Added a transcript notice when OpenAI drops reasoning items from a request, such as `OpenAI dropped 2 reasoning items: prefix_mismatch (details in session)` after compaction on GPT-6.2. Like the Anthropic thinking notice, it is shown when `showCacheMissNotices` is on and only when more items are dropped than in the previous response. Both notices now name the reasons

### Changed

- Qwen Token Plan providers now use the current gateways (`token-plan.maas.qwencloudapi.com` international, `token-plan.maas.qianwenaiapi.com` China), and `qwen-token-plan` and `qwen-token-plan-cn` are named "Qwen Token Plan Team" and "Qwen Token Plan Team CN". Provider IDs are unchanged, and the old `aliyuncs.com` hosts still work ([#11773](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11773))
- Updated `undici` to 8.12.4 for security advisories GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32, GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg, GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954, GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f, GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2, and GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc ([#12200](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12200))
- The default model for the `openai`, `azure`, and `openai-codex` providers is now GPT-6.2 Sol (`gpt-6.2-sol`) instead of GPT-6.1 Sol, at the same price
- The find tool's path patterns are now relative to the search directory, like grep's `glob`: `src/*.ts` finds `src/a.ts` but no longer `pkg/src/a.ts`; use `**/src/*.ts` to match at any depth. Patterns without `/` still match file names at any depth ([#12066](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12066))
- The llama.cpp extension now connects to `http://127.0.0.1:9931` by default, the current llama-server default port, instead of port 8080 ([#12001](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12001) by [@julien-c](https://github.com/julien-c))
- Anthropic message threads are now on by default for any provider whose baseUrl is on api.anthropic.com, not only the `anthropic` provider ([#11987](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11987))
- The resume command printed on exit is now on its own line after `To resume this session:`, so it can be selected with a triple-click ([#12237](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12237))

### Fixed

- Fixed `read` storing a note that the current model does not support images, which was replayed to the model as stale text after switching to a vision model. The image is still replaced with a placeholder per request for models without image input, and the read result now shows the warning in the TUI only, also when collapsed ([#12131](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12131))
- Fixed MCP tools loaded by `tool_search` being dropped on resume and `/reload` when an extension deactivates only its own tool at `session_start`, as pi-web-access and pi-subagents do in `toolActivation: "auto"` mode ([#11996](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11996))
- Fixed the standalone binary failing to resolve extension npm dependencies whose entry point is declared in `package.json` `main` or `exports` (for example `shiki`, `yaml`, `graceful-fs`), including imports made from inside other dependencies ([#12012](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12012))
- Fixed the find tool returning no results for patterns starting with `./`, such as `./src/*.ts` ([#12020](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12020))
- Fixed pi exiting with an uncaught `AbortError` when a `read` tool call is cancelled while the file is being opened ([#11956](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11956))
- Fixed pi exiting with an uncaught `AbortError` when the session picker cancels loading after skipping a `.jsonl` file that is not a session, and fixed such files staying open ([#11956](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11956))
- Fixed `/share` crashing pi when the GitHub CLI fails to start
- Fixed `pi update` on Windows managed installs failing with "Could not verify managed Pi" when an older system Node.js comes before the installer's standalone Node.js on PATH ([#12048](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12048))
- Fixed `/export` HTML showing raw terminal hyperlink escape codes around links in custom tool output; links are now clickable ([#12003](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12003))
- Fixed the bash tool returning no output, with a footer like `[Showing lines 3-2 of 2]`, when the output ends in one line longer than about 100KB, such as a `grep` match in a minified file; it now shows the end of that line ([#12062](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12062))
- Fixed provider errors reading "Connection closed." not triggering automatic retries ([#12064](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12064))
- Fixed `/resume` sometimes selecting an unrelated session while the list reloads after deleting or renaming a session ([#12106](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12106))
- Fixed Groq Qwen models failing with `400 Unexpected message role`; OpenAI-compatible providers other than OpenAI now receive system messages (the system prompt and mid-conversation system messages) with the `system` role ([#10741](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10741))
- Fixed `enabledModels`/`--models` warnings such as `No models match pattern "github-copilot/nope"` being written over the interactive TUI on every `/new`, `/resume` and `/fork`, which left stale lines in fullscreen mode. The warnings are now shown once at startup, in the chat in interactive mode and on stderr in other modes; RPC mode no longer repeats them on stderr for each `new_session`, `switch_session` or `fork` ([#11264](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11264))
- Fixed the find tool matching path patterns through folders above the search path: with the project in `~/src/app`, `src/**/*.ts` returned every `.ts` file in the project ([#12066](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12066))
- Fixed pi crashing with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` when rendering a very large edit diff, for example after editing a file with a multi-megabyte line, and again on every resume of that session ([#8036](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8036))
- Fixed pressing Esc during a batch of tool calls leaving the calls that had not started yet without a result in the session; they now get an "Operation aborted" result ([#9986](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9986))
- Fixed an unreadable `CHANGELOG.md` (pi's own or an extension package's) printing `Warning: Could not parse changelog` over the interactive TUI; it now shows no changelog notes ([#11264](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11264))
- Fixed problems found when replacing the session with `/new`, `/resume`, `/fork` or RPC `new_session`, `switch_session` and `fork` never being shown, for example a project extension that fails to load after `/resume` into another project, or an `enabledModels` pattern that matches nothing after a settings change. Interactive mode now shows them in the chat and print, JSON and RPC modes write them to stderr; a problem already reported is not repeated. SDK hosts can call the new `AgentSessionRuntime.takeUnreportedDiagnostics()` at startup and after each replacement to get each diagnostic once
- Fixed RPC `new_session`, `switch_session`, `fork` and `clone` running extension `session_start` and `resources_discover` handlers twice for the new session. RPC clients now also receive events emitted by `session_start` handlers, such as `entry_appended` for entries they append ([#10470](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10470))
- Fixed an exception thrown by an extension's `pi.events` handler being printed with `console.error` over the interactive TUI. It is now reported like other extension errors: in the chat in interactive mode, as `extension_error` in RPC mode and as `Extension error (...)` in print mode. Errors from a handler that fails after its session was replaced are dropped ([#11264](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11264))
- Fixed `AgentSession.reload()` not emitting `session_start` to extensions when the SDK host bound them with `bindExtensions({})`, after it had already emitted `session_shutdown`. Extensions that start work in `session_start`, such as the MCP extension connecting its servers, stayed stopped after a reload
- Fixed `--mode json` dropping events emitted by extension `session_start` handlers, such as `entry_appended` for entries they append, at startup and after an extension replaces the session
- Fixed `Could not restore model <provider>/<model>. Using <fallback>` being shown only at interactive startup. Resuming or forking into a session whose model no longer exists or has no login switched to another model without notice, and print, JSON and RPC modes never showed it. It is now reported in every mode, at startup and after `/resume`, `/fork` and RPC `switch_session` or `fork`
- Fixed git and npm output, such as `Cloning into ...` or `added 12 packages`, being drawn over the interactive TUI when pi installed or refreshed packages during `/reload`, `/new`, `/resume` and `/fork`, including temporary `-e git:` and `-e npm:` packages. In interactive mode their output is now captured, and a failed install reports the end of it. Until the TUI starts, each install is announced as `Installing <source>...` on stderr instead of showing git and npm output. git and ssh can no longer prompt in interactive mode: a package that needs a typed password or passphrase fails with a hint to set up a credential helper or ssh agent, or to run `pi install <source>` once from the shell. `pi install` and `pi update` keep live output ([#11264](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11264))
- Fixed fullscreen scrolling in long sessions saturating a CPU core by re-rendering the whole transcript on every wheel event ([#9549](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9549))
- Fixed search in `/login`, `/logout`, `/scoped-models` and `/resume` keeping the highlight on the row scrolled to before typing, so Enter picked whichever entry landed there instead of the best match; a query now highlights the top match, as `/model` does ([#12245](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12245), [#12246](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12246) by [@acmerfight](https://github.com/acmerfight))
- Fixed exiting pi, `pi config` and the `--resume` and other startup pickers dropping terminal output still queued in stdout, such as the resets that turn off mouse tracking and Kitty keyboard reporting; the shell could then print mouse and key reports as text. pi now waits up to one second for queued output before exiting or continuing ([#12133](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12133))
- Fixed moving the cursor in a search field with Left, Right, Home or End moving the highlight back to the first entry in `/login`, `/logout`, `/model`, `/scoped-models`, `/resume`, `/settings`, the per-model settings model picker and `pi config` ([#12245](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12245))
- Fixed llama.cpp decision classifiers ignoring the image input that llama.cpp reports, such as Clef with its `mmproj`; `models.classify()` now sends their images to `/v1/systemone` ([#12282](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12282))
- Fixed `kill -TSTP` from outside pi stopping it without restoring the terminal, which left mouse tracking and the Kitty keyboard protocol on at the shell prompt and turned mouse movement into garbage input. pi now suspends as with Ctrl+Z and redraws on `fg` ([#12283](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12283) by [@haoqixu](https://github.com/haoqixu))
- Fixed changing the thinking level on the `openai-codex` provider invalidating the prompt cache on GPT-6 models ([#12269](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12269))
- Fixed unscoped syntax-highlighted text inheriting the terminal foreground and becoming unreadable on contrasting tool cards ([#11092](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11092))
- Fixed `/copy` saying "No agent messages to copy yet." after Esc during a tool call or after a provider error; it now copies the previous answer. RPC `get_last_assistant_text` skips the same messages ([#12119](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12119), [#12121](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12121) by [@acmerfight](https://github.com/acmerfight))
- Fixed `pi.exec` reporting exit code 0 for commands ended by a signal, such as a timeout, an abort or a crash; it now reports 128 + the signal number, like a shell (143 for SIGTERM, 137 for SIGKILL) ([#12088](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12088), [#12089](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12089) by [@acmerfight](https://github.com/acmerfight))
- Fixed GitHub Copilot Gemini and Kimi models (`gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-4-carbon`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `kimi-k3`) ignoring the thinking level, and Copilot usage always reporting 0 reasoning tokens ([#12110](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12110) by [@DenielC1](https://github.com/DenielC1))
- Fixed provider errors that report only a Node socket error code, such as `read ECONNRESET`, `write EPIPE`, or `connect ETIMEDOUT`, not triggering automatic retries ([#12128](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12128))
- Fixed OpenAI rejecting requests with a 400 error when a tool's schema contains a node without a `type` (such as `items: {}` or `Type.Unknown()`); such tools are now sent in non-strict mode ([#12049](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12049))
- Fixed Mistral Large 4 tool calls stalling for minutes; Mistral models no longer receive strict tools unless `compat.supportsStrictMode` is set ([#12148](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12148))
- Fixed non-strict Anthropic tool schemas not telling the model that extra arguments are forbidden ([#12067](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12067))
- Fixed GitHub Copilot models on the Responses API (GPT, Grok, MAI-Code) filling omitted optional tool arguments with empty strings or invented values ([#12286](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12286))
- Fixed the OpenAI Codex WebSocket 60-minute connection limit failing the turn when it hit mid-stream, for example during long thinking; the request is now retried on a fresh connection ([#12124](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12124))
- Fixed the `openai-codex` provider getting almost no prompt cache hits for the system prompt on GPT-6.2 models ([#12273](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12273))
- Fixed the `openai-codex` provider ignoring a model's `maxTokens`
- Fixed fullscreen Kitty images disappearing after a full redraw such as a window resize ([#12010](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12010))
- Fixed text after a multi-row inline image in Markdown drawing over the image ([#12017](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12017))
- Fixed Kitty and iTerm2 images covering overlays drawn over them ([#11584](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11584))
- Fixed Enter on a Tab path menu for an absolute path (`look at /tmp/fi`) or a slash command argument menu (`/open /tm`) submitting the prompt instead of accepting the completion ([#12309](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12309), [#12312](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12312) by [@acmerfight](https://github.com/acmerfight))

### Removed

- Removed the retired `deepseek-v3.2` and `deepseek-v4-flash` from the Qwen Token Plan Team providers; use `deepseek-v4-flash-0731` or `deepseek-v4.1-flash` ([#11773](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11773))

issues.title: serve: read listener-slot occupancy offline (discovery record / daemon status) — #17479 A.4 follow-up

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: category/cli
labels.description: Command line interface and interaction

labels.name: type/enhancement
labels.description: Non-bug improvement or optimization

issues.body:
## Context

#17479 measured a production outage where long-lived SSE streams exhausted the HTTP listener pool and locked out `/health`. Proposal **A.4** in that issue asked for occupancy to be readable **without spending a connection slot from the exhausted pool** — e.g. an active-SSE field in offline `daemon status` alongside the existing cap. A.4 was deferred by maintainer decision when #17904 was scoped to B.2/B.3; #17904 has now merged (`0b310181ca`), so this issue tracks the deferred item.

The rest of the incident is covered elsewhere: defect A by #17502 / #17662 (admission cap, writer-stall reaper, keepalive), the cross-surface occupancy unification by #17554 (closed), B.2/B.3 by #17904, and B.1 by #17534 (open).

## Current state (verified at main `b62d4ab7fa`)

- The offline discovery record (`DaemonDiscoveryRecord`, `packages/cli/src/serve/daemon-discovery.ts`) carries pid/port/url/auth/logPath/pidNamespace — **no occupancy field, and no cap field either**.
- Live occupancy (`StreamOccupancySnapshot`, `sse-occupancy.ts`) is consumed only by HTTP surfaces: `/daemon/status` (`routes/daemon-status.ts` → `daemon-status.ts`, `transport.streamOccupancy`) and `/health?deep=1` (`routes/health.ts`). Nothing persists it to disk.
- `limits.maxSseConnections` / `maxSseConnectionsPerListener` expose the **caps** in the status payload, not the live occupancy.

## Gap

When the listener pool is exhausted — exactly the incident condition — reading occupancy over HTTP requires a connection slot from the exhausted pool, and offline `qwen daemon status` (discovery-record based) cannot show it. An operator diagnosing a saturated daemon has no connection-free way to see how many slots are held and by which surface.

## Proposal

Make live listener-slot occupancy readable offline, additively:

1. An occupancy field (total + per-surface breakdown, mirroring `StreamOccupancySnapshot`) in a periodically refreshed on-disk surface — either the discovery record or a companion status file — so `qwen daemon status` can render it without an HTTP round-trip.
2. Keep the existing HTTP surfaces unchanged; the offline view is a diagnostic complement, not a replacement. Staleness of the on-disk snapshot should be visible (e.g. an `asOf` timestamp).

## Out of scope

- Admission enforcement, reaper, keepalive — landed via #17502 / #17662 / #17554.
- B.1 (explicit `--port` fail-fast) — #17534.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

## 背景

#17479 实测了一次生产事故：长活 SSE 流耗尽 HTTP 监听池并锁死 `/health`。该 issue 的提案 **A.4** 要求占用量可以**不消耗已耗尽池中的连接槽**就能读取——例如离线 `daemon status` 在既有上限字段旁带上 active-SSE 字段。#17904 定范围只做 B.2/B.3 时，A.4 经维护者决定延期；#17904 现已合入（`0b310181ca`），本 issue 跟踪该延期项。

事故其余部分已有归宿：缺陷 A 由 #17502 / #17662 修复（准入上限、写停滞回收、keepalive），跨表面占用统一由 #17554 覆盖（已关闭），B.2/B.3 由 #17904 修复，B.1 在 #17534（开放）。

## 现状（在 main `b62d4ab7fa` 核实）

- 离线发现记录（`DaemonDiscoveryRecord`，`packages/cli/src/serve/daemon-discovery.ts`）携带 pid/port/url/auth/logPath/pidNamespace——**没有占用字段，也没有上限字段**。
- 活占用（`StreamOccupancySnapshot`，`sse-occupancy.ts`）只被 HTTP 表面消费：`/daemon/status`（`transport.streamOccupancy`）与 `/health?deep=1`。没有任何落盘路径。
- `limits.maxSseConnections` / `maxSseConnectionsPerListener` 暴露的是**上限**，不是活占用。

## 缺口

监听池耗尽时——正是事故条件——经 HTTP 读占用需要从已耗尽的池里拿连接槽，而基于发现记录的离线 `qwen daemon status` 显示不了占用。运维诊断饱和 daemon 时没有免连接的方式看到槽位被谁占了多少。

## 提案

以增量方式让活占用可离线读取：

1. 在周期性刷新的落盘表面（发现记录或伴生状态文件）带上占用字段（总量 + 分表面明细，镜像 `StreamOccupancySnapshot`），使 `qwen daemon status` 无需 HTTP 往返即可渲染。
2. 既有 HTTP 表面不变；离线视图是诊断补充而非替代。落盘快照的陈旧度应可见（如 `asOf` 时间戳）。

## 范围外

- 准入执行、回收器、keepalive——已随 #17502 / #17662 / #17554 落地。
- B.1（显式 `--port` fail-fast）——#17534。

</details>

issues.title: bug(serve): SSE can exhaust the listener cap and lock out /health; explicit --port silently duplicates daemons

labels.name: priority/P1
labels.description: High priority issue

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/cli
labels.description: Command line interface and interaction

issues.body:
## What happened?

Two defects in `qwen serve` compound into a daemon that is alive but completely unreachable. Both were measured on a long-running deployment (Linux x86_64, Node v26.12.1, qwen 0.27.3), and all code references below were verified against `main` @ `27681123f719`.

Host paths and addresses are redacted.

### A. Long-lived SSE connections exhaust the listener cap, and the cap also locks out `/health`

After ~46 hours of uptime the daemon stopped answering **every** route, including `/health` and the static Web Shell index. `curl -v` shows the TCP connection being accepted and then immediately closed, with no HTTP response at all:

```text
* Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 4170
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
* Closing connection
curl: (52) Empty reply from server            # code 000
```

The process was healthy by every other measure: `STAT=Ssl`, 11 threads, `kill -TERM` still worked and released the port, its log kept growing, and disk / memory / fd counts were all normal.

The cause is the listener-level cap:

```ts
// packages/cli/src/serve/run-qwen-serve.ts:9843
const cap = opts.maxConnections ?? 256;
if (cap > 0 && Number.isFinite(cap)) {
  server.maxConnections = cap;
}
```

Once `server.maxConnections` is reached, Node closes new sockets at accept time, so no request reaches the router — not even a health check. The rejection is silent: no `503`, no log line, no metric.

**The decisive measurement.** `SSE stream opened` minus `SSE stream closed` in the daemon log is the number of live SSE streams, because both are emitted from the same `finalize()` path:

```ts
// packages/cli/src/serve/routes/sse-events.ts
:579  res.prependOnceListener('finish', finalize);
:580  res.prependOnceListener('close', finalize);
:581  activeSseCount++;
:587  daemonLog?.info('SSE stream opened', { … });
:539  daemonLog?.info('SSE stream closed', { … });   // inside finalize()
:561  activeSseCount--;                              // inside finalize()
```

| state | opened | closed | live SSE | `ss -tn state established '( sport = :4170 )'` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| healthy | 11 | 0 | **11** | **11** |
| unreachable | 1396 | 1140 | **256** | **256** |

256 is exactly the default `--max-connections`. The two counters agree with the kernel's own socket count in both states.

This log covers a **single process lifetime**, so the difference is not an artifact of summing across restarts: the file contains exactly one `qwen serve listening on http://0.0.0.0:4170` line, and its last entry (`10:17:00.392Z`) predates the first duplicate daemon described in section B (`10:17:24Z`).

Three gaps let the count reach the cap and stay there:

1. **Writer-idle reclamation is off by default.**

   ```ts
   // packages/cli/src/serve/routes/sse-events.ts:650
   const trackWriterIdle =
     writerIdleTimeoutMs !== undefined && writerIdleTimeoutMs > 0;
   let lastWriteAt = trackWriterIdle ? Date.now() : 0;   // :652
   ```

   The surrounding comment states that "a writer that stalls indefinitely on `drain` will never refresh this stamp, so the timer fires and forces cleanup" — but that timer only exists when the flag is set. With the flag unset (the default), a stalled writer is never reclaimed. The default is off to avoid a per-chunk `Date.now()`.

2. **No TCP keepalive.** `git grep setKeepAlive -- packages/cli/src/serve` returns **0 matches**, so half-open peers are never probed by the kernel.

3. **The observation endpoint shares the exhausted quota.** `/health?deep=1` already reports the live count (plain `/health` returns only `{"status":"ok"}`; the fields below are on the deep-probe branch):

   ```ts
   // packages/cli/src/serve/routes/health.ts:136
   connectedClients: getActiveSseCount(),
   ```

   ```console
   $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'http://127.0.0.1:4170/health?deep=1'
   {"status":"ok","workspaceCount":22,"sessions":6,"pendingPermissions":0,
    "activePrompts":3,"activeWork":true,"activeWorkReporting":"full",
    "activeWorkStaleMs":6837,"connectedClients":7,"channelAlive":true, …}
   ```

   This is the sharpest part of the failure: the data needed to diagnose the outage is already exposed, but reading it requires a connection slot from the very pool that is full. The operator's only remaining tool is subtracting two log counters by hand.

   Offline `daemon status` does not close the gap either — it carries the cap but not the occupancy (`listenerMaxConnections` at `daemon-status.ts:205`, `:1010`, `:1707`; there is no active-SSE field).

The cap's own comment describes its purpose as bounding fds against an attacker who "opens *connections* that never finish their headers, never reach the bus". Legitimate long-lived SSE streams are not that threat, yet they consume the same budget, and `DEFAULT_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS` (`packages/acp-bridge/src/eventBus.ts:243`, value 64) is per-session, so it cannot bound the listener-wide total.

#### A second production observation: the same accumulation, measured without the log

After the outage was cleared, the daemon was restarted with the same defaults. 20.9 hours later it is accumulating again — and this time the measurement does not depend on subtracting log counters at all:

```console
$ ss -lntp | grep ':4170 '
LISTEN 0 511 0.0.0.0:4170 0.0.0.0:* users:(("node-MainThread",pid=3699681,fd=21))

$ ps -p 3699681 -o lstart,etimes
Mon Nov 16 23:05:01 2026   75284        # 20.9 h, single process lifetime

$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'http://127.0.0.1:4170/health?deep=1'
{… "sessions":16, "activePrompts":2, "connectedClients":146 …}

$ ss -tn state established '( sport = :4170 )' | tail -n +2 | wc -l
146
```

Three consecutive samples returned `connectedClients=146` and `ss_established=146` — **the daemon's own SSE counter and the kernel's socket count agree exactly**, on a port-scoped measurement that no other daemon can contaminate. So 146 of the 256 listener slots (**57%**) are held by SSE streams, with 16 sessions and only 2 active prompts.

This is the pre-outage state of the same defect, not a second outage. A naive linear extrapolation of 146 slots over 20.9 h (~7 slots/h) reaches the cap in roughly another 15–16 h; that estimate is only indicative, since the rate depends on client churn rather than being a constant.

Note that the log-subtraction method used for the first measurement is **not** usable here, for the reason given in section B: a duplicate daemon is still writing to the same file. Verified directly —

```console
$ ls -l /proc/3699681/fd/1   # intended daemon, port 4170
… -> /home/<user>/qwen-serve.log
$ ls -l /proc/1976105/fd/1   # duplicate, port 4176
… -> /home/<user>/qwen-serve.log
```

Two daemons, one log sink, and no `pid`/`port` on the lines. `/health?deep=1` plus `ss` is the only attribution-safe measurement available, which is itself an argument for fix (4) below.

### B. With an explicit `--port`, port fallback silently multiplies daemons

Port fallback itself is intended behaviour (added in #6513; #7500 fixed the `--open` side of it). The problem is the case where the port is held by **another `qwen serve`**, which is exactly what happens when an operator retries a start while recovering an unresponsive daemon.

```ts
// packages/cli/src/serve/run-qwen-serve.ts
:570    const MAX_PORT_ATTEMPTS = 10;

// the retry branch, :11859–11868
} else if (
  err.code === 'EADDRINUSE' &&
  opts.port !== 0 &&
  nextPort <= 65535 &&
  attempt < MAX_PORT_ATTEMPTS - 1
) {
  writeStderrLine(`qwen serve: port ${attemptPort} is in use, trying ${nextPort}...`);
  tryListen(nextPort, attempt + 1);   // :11867
  return;
}
```

Note that `--profile hosted-harness` already opts out of this retry (`:11854`), because "the control plane names the Hosted Harness by its exact port, so a moved Harness would start while no Session could reach it". The same reasoning applies to an operator who named an explicit port.

Nine successive start attempts against a busy 4170 each **succeeded** on the next port. The result was ten complete daemons, exactly filling the `MAX_PORT_ATTEMPTS` window:

```text
0.0.0.0:4170  pid=3699681     <- the one the operator believes exists
0.0.0.0:4171  pid=1972303
0.0.0.0:4172  pid=1974504
0.0.0.0:4173  pid=1975503
0.0.0.0:4174  pid=1975635
0.0.0.0:4175  pid=1975889
0.0.0.0:4176  pid=1976105
0.0.0.0:4177  pid=1976531
0.0.0.0:4178  pid=1976817
0.0.0.0:4179  pid=1977369
```

Each wrote its own `~/.qwen/daemon/daemon-<port>.json`, so no single record reveals the siblings.

Five hours later, `/health?deep=1` on each port shows that **eight of the nine duplicates had never served anything at all**, yet all nine were still resident:

| port | sessions | activePrompts | connectedClients | channelAlive | lastActivityAt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4170 | 6 | 3 | 7 | true | recent (the intended daemon) |
| 4171 | 0 | 0 | 0 | false | `null` |
| 4172 | 0 | 0 | 0 | false | `null` |
| 4173 | 0 | 0 | 0 | false | `null` |
| 4174 | 0 | 0 | 0 | false | `null` |
| 4175 | 0 | 0 | 0 | false | `null` |
| 4176 | 1 | 1 | 1 | true | recent |
| 4177 | 0 | 0 | 0 | false | `null` |
| 4178 | 0 | 0 | 0 | false | `null` |
| 4179 | 0 | 0 | 0 | false | `null` |

`lastActivityAt: null` means the duplicate never had any activity in its lifetime. Note that 4176 *did* pick up real work — an active prompt on a different workspace — so these duplicates are not inert: work can land on any of them, and an operator who believes there is one daemon cannot tell which one holds a given session.

Consequences measured on the host:

- **Resident memory cost.** The nine duplicates held **2121 MB** themselves, plus **706 MB** in 7 child processes — **2827 MB** of permanent background weight that the operator never asked for.
- **They keep doing side-effecting work.** Duplicate pid 1976105 still had a channel worker and an ACP child, and was observed spawning `gh pr list --state all --limit 500 --json number,url,headRefName,state` hours later. So duplicates repeat channel polling and outbound API calls.
- **They are all reachable on the same public interface.** Every duplicate inherited `--hostname 0.0.0.0`, so nine extra authenticated endpoints were exposed, not just the intended one.
- **They share one stdout log, and log lines carry no `pid`/`port` field.** Counter-based diagnosis like the `opened − closed` subtraction in section A becomes unattributable once duplicates exist. (In this incident the section-A log predates all duplicates, which is why that measurement is still sound.)

A channel single-instance guard does exist and does produce a conflict error:

```ts
// packages/cli/src/serve/run-qwen-serve.ts:2117
`Channel service is already running under ${owner} (PID ${info.pid}). Stop it before enabling daemon-managed channels.`
```

but when the channel selection came from settings rather than an explicit flag, the conflict is **downgraded instead of fatal**:

```ts
// packages/cli/src/serve/run-qwen-serve.ts:9787
reserveChannelServicePidfile(opts.channelSelection);
} catch (error) {
  if (!channelSelectionFromSettings) throw error;
  removeCurrentServePidfile();
  opts.channelSelection = undefined;
  reportConfiguredChannelStartupFailure(error);
}
```

Startup continues. Which exact path then re-admits the channel worker (a workspace-level restore is logged at `:4503`, `restoring channels from workspace serve.channels`) still needs to be pinned down — the observation above is that duplicates demonstrably ran channel children, not that this specific line is proven to be the one that admitted them.

### How the two defects combined into an outage

The 2827 MB of duplicate-daemon weight was permanent background load on a 125 GB host that also runs test workloads. A burst of ~319 concurrent `git pack-objects` processes (230–360 MB each, spawned by local clones against one large source repository) then exhausted memory, and the kernel OOM killer took the intended daemon — which was only ~700 MB — along with two larger test processes:

```text
Out of memory: Killed process 3683453 (node) anon-rss:2142196kB
Out of memory: Killed process 3683755 (node) anon-rss:2148900kB
Out of memory: Killed process 3650951 (node-MainThread) anon-rss:704688kB   <- the daemon
```

Section A and section B are independent defects with different fixes; they are reported together because B both amplified A's blast radius and polluted the evidence needed to diagnose it.

## What did you expect to happen?

**A.**
1. Long-lived SSE streams should not be able to consume the entire listener budget. A separate SSE quota (e.g. 80% of the cap) with slots reserved for `/health` and static assets would keep the daemon diagnosable when the SSE quota is full.
2. Exceeding the SSE quota should be an explicit, logged `503` with `Retry-After`, not a silent socket close at accept time.
3. Stalled writers should be reclaimed by default. This can stay zero-overhead on the hot path: stamp `lastWriteAt` only in the backpressure branch (`res.write()` returned `false`, near `sse-events.ts:688`), leaving the normal path untouched while still covering the dangerous "stalled on `drain`" case the existing comment describes.
4. Occupancy should be readable without spending a connection slot from the exhausted pool — e.g. an active-SSE field in offline `daemon status` alongside the existing `listenerMaxConnections`.
5. Optionally, `socket.setKeepAlive(true, 30_000)` so the kernel probes half-open peers. Its responsibility should be stated relative to (3): keepalive detects dead peers, idle reclamation detects live-but-not-reading ones.

**B.**
1. When an explicit `--port` is held by another `qwen serve` (as opposed to an unrelated process), starting a second daemon should not silently succeed on a neighbouring port. Failing fast with the holder's pid and port — or requiring an opt-in flag for fallback — matches what the operator asked for. #6513's intent (start despite an unrelated squatter) can be preserved by distinguishing the two cases.
2. A settings-derived channel selection should not turn a single-instance conflict into a silent downgrade that leaves a duplicate daemon running side-effecting work.
3. Daemon log lines should carry `pid` and `port` so that any counter-based diagnosis remains attributable when more than one daemon writes to the same sink.

## Client information

```console
Qwen Code v0.27.3
Platform: Linux x86_64 (Alibaba Cloud Linux 3, kernel 5.10.134)
Node.js: v26.12.1
Verified code references: main @ 27681123f719
```

Daemon invocation (token redacted):

```bash
qwen serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4170 --require-auth \
  --max-sessions 64 --workspace <workspace>
```

`--max-connections` and `--writer-idle-timeout-ms` were both left unset, i.e. the defaults described above.

## Login information

Bearer token via `QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN` with `--require-auth`; no model credentials are involved in reproducing either defect.

## Anything else we need to know?

**Reproduction for A** does not need a 46-hour wait: open 256 concurrent `GET /session/:id/events` streams against a daemon started with default `--max-connections`, then request `/health`. Expected observation: the 257th stream and `/health` both connect and close with no HTTP response, while `opened − closed` and the kernel's ESTABLISHED count both read 256. Running the same load with `--writer-idle-timeout-ms 60000` is the A/B that tests whether missing idle reclamation is what lets the count accumulate.

**Reproduction for B**: start one daemon on port P, then start a second with the same explicit `--port P`. The second reports `port P is in use, trying P+1...` and becomes a fully functional duplicate.

**Existing issues checked.** #5706 (closed) is about fractional `--max-connections` limits; #7500 (closed) is about `--open` using a stale port after fallback; #12277 (closed) is Local Control EADDRINUSE; #3803 (open) is the daemon proposal. None covers either defect above.

**A measurement caveat worth recording.** On this host `dmesg -T` timestamps ran ~1–2 minutes early: it labelled the daemon's OOM kill `23:02:11` while a `ps` sample at `23:03:06` still showed that pid alive. OOM timing should be cross-checked against live process sampling rather than read from `dmesg -T` alone.

Only a transition between two known, different epochs resets the cursor. A daemon that never supplied an epoch retains the legacy behavior. Event acknowledgement timing within one stream is unchanged.

issues.body:
<!-- ecs-fleet-update-failure -->

[`Update ECS Runner Qwen`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43336836312) failed, so at least one ECS pool is still running an older `qwen` than the release it was asked to install.

- Target version: `0.27.3`
- Pools left stale: ecs-update-hk-5, ecs-update-hz-2, ecs-update-hk-4, ecs-update-hz-1, ecs-update-hk-2, ecs-update-hk-1, ecs-update-hz-3, ecs-update-hz-6
- Run: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43336836312

Nothing else surfaces this. The review and triage workflows install `qwen` only when `command -v qwen` finds nothing, which on a self-hosted runner is never, so a stale pool keeps reviewing PRs on the old CLI until someone reads a version string.

To repair: re-run **Update ECS Runner Qwen** through `workflow_dispatch` (an empty version means latest), then read the `Verify version` step of every pool.

prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds the PkgDiet dependency guardrail skill to Qwen Code as an **opt-in, user-invoked** skill (`/pkgdiet`). When activated, it registers the PkgDiet MCP server and gates npm package installs through explicit security checks before the user confirms each installation.

## Why it's needed

As AI coding agents become more autonomous, there is a risk of them hallucinating malicious packages or installing deprecated, bloated dependencies (like `request` or `moment.js`). This skill provides a user-controlled guardrail using the PkgDiet MCP server.

**This skill is NOT automatic.** It only activates when the user explicitly runs `/pkgdiet` and confirms the consent prompt. It makes no network calls and costs nothing until then.

## Disclosure

The `pkgdiet@2.0.0` npm package used by this skill is published by the same author as this PR (`om-tajne`). This is disclosed here and in the skill's SKILL.md itself, so maintainers can make an informed decision about bundling.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run `/pkgdiet` in Qwen Code to trigger the skill.
2. Confirm the consent prompt to register the MCP server.
3. The server is registered via: `qwen mcp add --scope user pkgdiet npx -y pkgdiet@2.0.0 mcp`
4. Ask Qwen Code to "Install the `request` package to handle HTTP calls."
5. Observe the agent checking the package via the MCP server and blocking the install while suggesting `axios` or native `fetch`.
