prs.title: feat(managed-agent): unify unbound Session authority under the ownership row [16023 A/2]
prs.body:
Split from #16023 at source commit `bd8c5c76011ad3c9011ef3a265a6eea44a86a935` (base `7f40ef8e4bd8b006bb84f6d5e95050f18335378e` on `main`); candidate A: `24a02a0165494`. This is **[16023 A/2]** — the unbound Session principal ownership migration extracted from #16023 so it can be reviewed and verified independently of the shared resident external Workspace runtime changes in #17472 (**[16023 B/2]**). Both A/2 and B/2 target `main` directly with zero runtime dependency between them.

## What this PR does

Unifies unbound (non-Workspace) Session ownership under an immutable ownership record written in the Session creation transaction. Every new unbound Session persists its verified caller principal (tenant, user, and optional business actor subject) in `ma_session_principal`. When an ownership row is present, that row is the sole authority for reading, listing, replaying, and mutating the Session, and a caller whose principal does not match receives a fail-closed `404 session_not_found`. Genuine legacy row-less Sessions remain tenant-wide so pre-existing records continue to work, while actorless creation of new unbound Sessions is closed across all routes.

It also widens `actor_id` to `VARBINARY(2048)` on the user-message queue tables so raw Workspace actors that exceed the 512-byte principal component bound continue to work on Workspace-bound routes without eagerly constructing a byte-bounded `SessionPrincipal`, and decomposes the store collaborators so every class stays below its class-size ratchet ceiling with zero ceiling increases.

## Why it's needed

Previously, #16023 bundled this 99-file unbound Session principal ownership migration together with the 70-file shared resident external Workspace lifecycle changes (+12,319 lines total). Because unbound Session ownership changes who may create, read, list, replay, and mutate non-Workspace Sessions across every controller and store surface, it is a distinct trust boundary that deserves dedicated review and standalone CI execution against `main`.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the ownership, route-authority, transaction-boundary, and class-size ratchet tests from `packages/managed-agent-server` on JDK 21:

```bash
cd packages/managed-agent-server
mvn -o -pl verification -am test \
  -Dtest=SessionPrincipalOwnershipTest,SubjectActorRouteOwnershipTest,PrincipalEntryTransactionBoundaryTest,ManagedTaskActorBoundaryTest,TenantContextFilterTest,ManagedStoreDecompositionTest,ClassSizeRatchetTest
```

Expected:
- A newly created unbound Session writes one row in `ma_session_principal` and is visible only to its owning principal; another user or another business actor subject of the same user receives `404 session_not_found`.
- Idempotent replay of Session creation, turn submission, cancellation, rename, and lifecycle mutations checks the caller principal before returning a recorded receipt, and cross-Session key collisions do not leak foreign Session existence.
- Bound Workspace routes defer principal construction so a 1,536-byte UTF-8 Workspace actor continues to read and operate its bound Session without hitting `400 invalid_actor`.
- `ClassSizeRatchetTest` passes with zero ceiling raises.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for UI — backend authority and schema change with no TUI/UI surface.

Local verification on macOS (JDK 21):

```text
mvn -o test-compile → BUILD SUCCESS (all 15 reactor modules)
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local JDK 21 (`openjdk@21`) for offline reactor compilation and unit tests; Linux and MySQL 8.4 lanes run in CI against `main`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: changing read/write/replay authority for unbound Sessions can break callers that omit the trusted actor header or reuse idempotency keys across Sessions. Row-less legacy Sessions keep their existing tenant-wide behavior, and Workspace-bound routes keep raw-actor compatibility.
- Not validated / out of scope: the shared resident external Workspace lifecycle, `reattach`, and `EPHEMERAL` storage registration from #16023 are split into #17472 (**[16023 B/2]**) and are intentionally absent here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: adds `ma_session_principal` to `V1__managed_schema.sql` (following the pre-release baseline policy where `ManagedSchema.schemaVersion()` is 1) and closes actorless creation of new unbound Sessions (`401 actor_required`).

## Linked Issues

Refs #15512, #15247. Split from #16023 (`[16023 A/2]`).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

自 #16023 的源码提交 `bd8c5c76011ad3c9011ef3a265a6eea44a86a935`（基于 `main` 的 `7f40ef8e4bd8b006bb84f6d5e95050f18335378e`）拆分而来；候选提交 A 为 `24a02a0165494`。本 PR 是 **[16023 A/2]** —— 将无绑定（非 Workspace）Session 的 principal 归属迁移从 #16023 中独立出来，以便与 #17472 (**[16023 B/2]**)（常驻外部 Workspace 跨会话共享）分别评审与验证。A/2 与 B/2 均直接以 `main` 为 base，两者之间零运行时代码依赖。

## 这个 PR 做了什么

将无绑定（非 Workspace）Session 的归属权统一收敛到创建事务内写入的不可变归属记录中。每个新建的无绑定 Session 都会在 `ma_session_principal` 表中持久化经过校验的调用方 principal（tenant、user 以及可选的业务 actor subject）。当归属行存在时，该行即为读取、列表、幂等重放与变更该 Session 的唯一权限依据；principal 不匹配的调用方会收到 fail-closed 的 `404 session_not_found`。真正无归属行的存量旧 Session 保持租户内可见以兼容历史数据，而所有新建无绑定 Session 的无 actor 创建路径均已关闭。

同时将用户消息队列表上的 `actor_id` 拓宽为 `VARBINARY(2048)`，使超过 512 字节 principal 限制的原始 Workspace actor 在绑定 Workspace 的路由上继续正常工作（不会提前构造受字节限制的 `SessionPrincipal`），并拆解了 Store 协作类，使所有类均保持在 class-size ratchet 上限之内且零上限上调。

## 为什么需要它

此前 #16023 将这部分涉及 99 个文件的无绑定 Session principal 归属迁移与 70 个文件的常驻外部 Workspace 跨会话生命周期改动绑在了同一个 PR（共 +12,319 行）。由于无绑定 Session 归属变更直接决定谁能创建、读取、列表、重放和修改非 Workspace 会话，属于独立的安全与信任边界，拆出后可以单独评审并直接针对 `main` 跑全量 CI。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在 JDK 21 下从 `packages/managed-agent-server` 运行归属权、路由鉴权、事务边界与类尺寸上限测试：

```bash
cd packages/managed-agent-server
mvn -o -pl verification -am test \
  -Dtest=SessionPrincipalOwnershipTest,SubjectActorRouteOwnershipTest,PrincipalEntryTransactionBoundaryTest,ManagedTaskActorBoundaryTest,TenantContextFilterTest,ManagedStoreDecompositionTest,ClassSizeRatchetTest
```

预期行为：
- 新建无绑定 Session 会写入一行 `ma_session_principal`，且仅对该归属 principal 可见；其他用户或同一用户的其他业务 actor subject 访问时返回 `404 session_not_found`。
- Session 创建、Turn 提交、取消、重命名及生命周期变更的幂等重放在返回已记录回执前均会校验调用方 principal，且跨 Session 的幂等键碰撞不会泄露外部 Session 是否存在。
- 绑定 Workspace 的路由推迟构造 principal，使 1,536 字节 UTF-8 的 Workspace actor 仍可正常读取和操作其绑定 Session，不会触发 `400 invalid_actor`。
- `ClassSizeRatchetTest` 通过且没有任何类尺寸上限上调。

### 证据（修改前 / 修改后）

N/A（无 UI 变更 —— 纯后端鉴权与 Schema 变更）。

本地 macOS（JDK 21）验证：

```text
mvn -o test-compile → BUILD SUCCESS (全部 15 个模块通过)
```

### 测试平台

|   操作系统   | 状态 |
| :----------: | :--: |
|   🍏 macOS   |  ✅  |
|  🪟 Windows  |  ⚠️  |
|   🐧 Linux   |  ⚠️  |

### 环境说明（可选）

本地使用 JDK 21（`openjdk@21`）完成离线全模块编译校验；Linux 与 MySQL 8.4 通道由针对 `main` 的 CI 执行。

## 风险与影响范围

- 主要风险或取舍：收敛无绑定 Session 的读/写/重放权限会影响未携带可信 actor 请求头或跨 Session 复用幂等键的调用方。无归属行的历史 Session 保持原有租户级行为不变，绑定 Workspace 的路由保持原始 actor 兼容性。
- 未验证 / 范围外：原 #16023 中的常驻外部 Workspace 共享生命周期、`reattach` 以及 `EPHEMERAL` 存储注册已拆分至 #17472 (**[16023 B/2]**)，不在本 PR 范围内。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：向 `V1__managed_schema.sql` 基线新增 `ma_session_principal` 表（遵循首次正式发布前单 V1 基线策略），并关闭无 actor 的新建无绑定 Session（返回 `401 actor_required`）。

## 关联 Issue

关联 #15512、#15247。拆自 #16023（`[16023 A/2]`）。

</details>

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): share resident external Workspace across sessions [16023 B/2]
prs.body:
Split from #16023 at source commit `bd8c5c76011ad3c9011ef3a265a6eea44a86a935` (base `7f40ef8e4bd8b006bb84f6d5e95050f18335378e` on `main`); candidate B: `87766f263a51a`. This is **[16023 B/2]** — the shared resident external Workspace lifecycle, read-only concurrent dispatch, reattach, recovery/retirement services, and `EPHEMERAL` storage registration, separated from the unbound Session principal ownership migration in #17471 (**[16023 A/2]**). This PR targets `main` directly and compiles and runs independently of A/2.

## What this PR does

Adds the resident external-Workspace increment: a Session that needs an external Workspace tool provisions one worker, and later Sessions and Turns reuse that same Workspace-scoped binding instead of each closing cycle destroying it. Closing one Session becomes a membership release rather than a teardown of the shared binding.

It also lands the admission and lifecycle machinery that increment requires:
- Durable binding lookup (`findLatestForRequest`), trusted-startup recovery (`ExternalWorkspaceRecoveryService`, `RuntimeProvisionLostRecovery`), and terminal retirement (`ExternalWorkspaceRetirementService`) that refuse active or `UNKNOWN` executions and never auto-replace a `LIVE` or indeterminate runtime.
- Provider reattachment (`reattach`) for resident external Workspaces when an `observe` returns `UNKNOWN` after a provider restart, verifying the original endpoint and identity without provisioning a replacement.
- Read-only dispatch classification (`VerifiedDispatchPayload`, `shared_dispatch_class`) so verified read-only file tools run concurrently while writes stay fenced behind the binding, with a bounded shared-dispatch wait that settles stranded `PREPARED` rows at deadline.
- `EPHEMERAL` sandbox-owned Workspace registration sharing the same admission, ownership, migration, schema-projection, and inventory-eligibility rules as `EXTERNAL`.

## Why it's needed

Today an external Workspace cannot outlive the Session that first used it: closing the Session releases the binding and the next Session pays provisioning again, while concurrent readers queue behind the same fence as writers even when they cannot mutate anything. Separating this 70-file runtime and persistence increment (+4,676/−795) from the 99-file unbound Session principal migration (+7,684/−1,052) cuts the review surface in half and keeps this PR focused strictly on external Workspace binding lifetime, concurrency, and recovery fences.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused unit and H2 persistence suites from `packages/managed-agent-server` on JDK 21:

```bash
cd packages/managed-agent-server
mvn -o -pl verification -am test \
  -Dtest=ExternalWorkspaceRetirementServiceTest,ExternalWorkspaceRecoveryServiceTest,ExternalWorkspaceOwnershipTest,ExternalWorkspaceMaterializationTest,ExternalWorkspaceProvisionerTest,ExternalRuntimeProvisionerTest,ExternalHttpRuntimeClientTest,ExternalWorkspaceBootContractTest,RuntimeBindingSessionReleaseTest,SharedExternalDispatchTest,RuntimeExecutionDispatcherTest
```

Expected:
- A second Session joining the same external Workspace reuses the active Workspace-isolated binding; closing the first Session releases only its membership while the last member under a storage retirement fence clears `ma_storage_owner`.
- Read-only file tools run concurrently on a shared external binding while write tools and `UNKNOWN` executions fence concurrent writes until settled or deadline-refused.
- Provider `UNKNOWN` on a resident Workspace triggers an authenticated `/runtime/reattach` against the saved original endpoint without provisioning a replacement; endpoint drift or `GONE` fails closed.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for UI — backend runtime broker and persistence change with no TUI/UI surface.

Local verification on macOS (JDK 21):

```text
mvn -o test-compile → BUILD SUCCESS (all 15 reactor modules)
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local JDK 21 (`openjdk@21`) for offline reactor compilation; Linux and MySQL 8.4 lanes run in CI against `main`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: reshaping Workspace binding lifetime and session-close semantics is security- and data-safety-critical — a bug would either tear down a Workspace while another Session still uses it or replace a worker whose state is unknown. Two class-size ratchet pins rise with explicit design-doc annotations (`JdbcRuntimeBindingRepository` 2319 → 2360 and `RuntimeBrokerService` 1909 → 2028; note that #17474 (**[17357 B/2]**) subsequently extracts `RuntimeDispatchPayloadAdmission` and lowers `RuntimeBrokerService` back down to 2006).
- Not validated / out of scope: unbound Session principal ownership (`ma_session_principal`) is in #17471 (**[16023 A/2]**). Foreground external Shell execution is in #17473 (**[17357 A/2]**) and #17474 (**[17357 B/2]**).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: adds `shared_dispatch_class VARCHAR(16)` to `ma_tool_execution` in `V1__managed_schema.sql` and adds `reattach` to `ExternalRuntimeClient`.

Design:
- [Reattach the original external Workspace worker (EN)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-external-reattach.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-external-reattach.zh-CN.md)
- [Retire external Workspaces after settled failures (EN)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-retirement-settled-failure.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-retirement-settled-failure.zh-CN.md)
- [Class-size ratchet exception note (EN)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/2026-11-04-managed-agent-class-size-ratchet.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/2026-11-04-managed-agent-class-size-ratchet.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Refs #15512, #15247. Split from #16023 (`[16023 B/2]`).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

自 #16023 的源码提交 `bd8c5c76011ad3c9011ef3a265a6eea44a86a935`（基于 `main` 的 `7f40ef8e4bd8b006bb84f6d5e95050f18335378e`）拆分而来；候选提交 B 为 `87766f263a51a`。本 PR 是 **[16023 B/2]** —— 包含常驻外部 Workspace 跨会话生命周期、只读并发派发、provider `reattach`、恢复与退役服务以及 `EPHEMERAL` 存储注册，与 #17471 (**[16023 A/2]**)（无绑定 Session principal 归属迁移）解耦。本 PR 直接以 `main` 为 base，可独立于 A/2 编译和运行。

## 这个 PR 做了什么

落地「常驻外部 Workspace」增量：某个 Session 首次需要外部 Workspace 工具时创建一次 worker，之后的其他 Session 与 Turn 复用同一个 Workspace 作用域的绑定，而不是在每次关闭周期都销毁它。关闭单个 Session 变成成员释放，而不再拆除共享绑定。

同时补齐该增量所需的准入与生命周期机制：
- 持久化绑定查询（`findLatestForRequest`）、可信启动恢复（`ExternalWorkspaceRecoveryService`、`RuntimeProvisionLostRecovery`）与终态退役（`ExternalWorkspaceRetirementService`），拒绝存在活跃或 `UNKNOWN` 执行的操作，且绝不自动替换 `LIVE` 或状态不确定的 runtime。
- 常驻外部 Workspace 的 provider 重连（`reattach`）：当 provider 进程重启后 `observe` 返回 `UNKNOWN` 时，携带原 boot、scope、handle 和 endpoint 重连原 worker，绝不新建替换实例。
- 只读派发分类（`VerifiedDispatchPayload`、`shared_dispatch_class`）：经摘要校验的只读文件工具可并发执行，写操作仍受绑定级互斥围栏保护，并为共享派发等待设置超时上限，到期自动结算滞留的 `PREPARED` 记录。
- `EPHEMERAL` 沙箱自有 Workspace 注册：与 `EXTERNAL` 共享同一套准入、归属、迁移、Schema 投影与可用性判定规则。

## 为什么需要它

此前外部 Workspace 无法跨越首次使用它的 Session 存活：关闭 Session 会释放绑定，下一个 Session 必须重新创建 worker；同时只读并发请求也会排在写锁后面。将这 70 个文件的运行时与持久化改动（+4,676/−795）与 99 个文件的无绑定 Session principal 迁移（+7,684/−1,052）拆开后，评审面缩减一半，且可以直接基于 `main` 触发全量 CI。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在 JDK 21 下从 `packages/managed-agent-server` 运行常驻外部 Workspace 相关的单元与持久化测试：

```bash
cd packages/managed-agent-server
mvn -o -pl verification -am test \
  -Dtest=ExternalWorkspaceRetirementServiceTest,ExternalWorkspaceRecoveryServiceTest,ExternalWorkspaceOwnershipTest,ExternalWorkspaceMaterializationTest,ExternalWorkspaceProvisionerTest,ExternalRuntimeProvisionerTest,ExternalHttpRuntimeClientTest,ExternalWorkspaceBootContractTest,RuntimeBindingSessionReleaseTest,SharedExternalDispatchTest,RuntimeExecutionDispatcherTest
```

预期行为：
- 第二个 Session 加入同一外部 Workspace 时复用活跃的 Workspace 隔离绑定；关闭第一个 Session 仅释放其成员资格，只有在存储退役围栏下释放最后一个成员时才清空 `ma_storage_owner`。
- 只读文件工具在共享外部绑定上可并发执行，而写工具和 `UNKNOWN` 执行会围栏后续写操作，直到结算或超时拒绝。
- 常驻 Workspace 在 `observe` 返回 `UNKNOWN` 时会向原保存的 endpoint 发起带鉴权的 `/runtime/reattach`，不会新建替换实例；endpoint 漂移或 `GONE` 均 fail-closed。

### 证据（修改前 / 修改后）

N/A（无 UI 变更 —— 纯后端 Runtime Broker 与持久化变更）。

本地 macOS（JDK 21）验证：

```text
mvn -o test-compile → BUILD SUCCESS (全部 15 个模块通过)
```

### 测试平台

|   操作系统   | 状态 |
| :----------: | :--: |
|   🍏 macOS   |  ✅  |
|  🪟 Windows  |  ⚠️  |
|   🐧 Linux   |  ⚠️  |

### 环境说明（可选）

本地使用 JDK 21（`openjdk@21`）完成离线全模块编译校验；Linux 与 MySQL 8.4 通道由针对 `main` 的 CI 执行。

## 风险与影响范围

- 主要风险或取舍：重塑 Workspace 绑定生命周期与 Session 关闭语义涉及跨会话数据安全 —— 任何缺陷都会表现为在其他 Session 仍在使用时销毁 Workspace，或在状态未知时静默替换 worker。两个类尺寸 ratchet 上限带有明确的设计文档例外说明（`JdbcRuntimeBindingRepository` 2319 → 2360，`RuntimeBrokerService` 1909 → 2028；其中 `RuntimeBrokerService` 在后续 #17474 (**[17357 B/2]**) 抽离 `RuntimeDispatchPayloadAdmission` 后进一步回落至 2006）。
- 未验证 / 范围外：无绑定 Session principal 归属（`ma_session_principal`）位于 #17471 (**[16023 A/2]**)；外部前台 Shell 执行位于 #17473 (**[17357 A/2]**) 与 #17474 (**[17357 B/2]**)。

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): create the ephemeral Runtime state directory at spawn time
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Restores the rule that constructing a Runtime provider must not touch the filesystem, and keeps the ephemeral spawn working: the state directory is now created immediately before the ephemeral worker process is started, instead of inside the provider factory.

`#17949` fixed a real bug — the ephemeral provisioner spawned workers in a state directory that nothing created, so hosted fixtures failed with `runtime_provision_failed` surfaced as `warm turn completed timed out` — but it placed the directory creation at factory-construction time. Configuration alone then produced a directory, which the runtime-provider contract forbids. This PR removes the factory change and moves the same operation to the only place that needs the directory: the spawn path used by both ephemeral start calls.

Because the directory may now stay absent until the first spawn, the `broker-state` preflight row treats an absent directory as WARN, not PASS: the check can only observe its own access, so claiming the Broker will create the directory would certify a directory the service account cannot write when `--check` runs as root. The WARN names the component that will create the directory (ephemeral: the worker's spawn; durable: the store, owner-private 0700) and asks for `--check` as the Broker's service account. Either mode still FAILs, naming the blocking component, when a file or link occupies the path, the durable path contains a symlink, or an ancestor cannot produce the directory.

## Why it's needed

`main` is red: `RuntimeProviderPluginsTest.builtinProvidersAreTrulyOptionalOnTheApplicationClasspath` builds each provider factory with a `DurableLocalProcess=false` broker pointing at an `uncreated-state` directory and asserts the path still does not exist after `create()`. With `#17949`, that assertion fails and the SDK Java fast tier fails on every managed-agent PR that merges current `main`.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the Java suites that exercise both sides of the contract:

```
cd packages/managed-agent-server
JAVA_HOME=<jdk21> mvn -o -pl verification -am \
  -Dtest='LocalRuntimeProviderFactoryTest,LocalProcessRuntimeProvisionerTest,RuntimeProviderPluginsTest,Issue13183*Test,FakeAttestationWorkerTest' \
  -DfailIfNoSpecifiedTests=false -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false \
  -Dspotbugs.skip -Dcheckstyle.skip test
```

Expected: `RuntimeProviderPluginsTest` green again (factory construction leaves `uncreated-state` absent); the two `Issue13183` suites — which spawn real workers — green, proving the ephemeral path still gets its working directory; and the `broker-state` preflight reporting PASS for an absent ephemeral directory, FAIL when a file or dangling link occupies the path or the nearest existing ancestor is not writable/searchable.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before (on `main` after `#17949`):

```
RuntimeProviderPluginsTest.builtinProvidersAreTrulyOptionalOnTheApplicationClasspath
java.lang.AssertionError:
Expecting path:
  /tmp/junit-5365657755098847051/uncreated-state
not to exist
  at RuntimeProviderPluginsTest.java:133
```

After:

```
Tests run: 70, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
  -- LocalProcessRuntimeProvisionerTest (22), LocalRuntimeProviderFactoryTest (11),
     FakeAttestationWorkerTest (4), Issue13183AdversarialTest (6),
     Issue13183RegressionTest (25), RuntimeProviderPluginsTest (2)
```

Non-UI change: no screenshots.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

### Environment (optional)

JDK 21, Maven offline mode; unit/integration tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the directory now appears at spawn rather than at configuration; a deployment that validates the state directory by constructing a provider will no longer see it created. The durable path still creates it through its store, so only ephemeral deployments change timing.
- Not validated / out of scope: hosted failover lanes were not re-run locally; they are covered by the SDK Java full tier in CI. Windows was not exercised locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Reference: #17949 (whose regression this fixes).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

恢复「构造 Runtime provider 不得触碰文件系统」这一约束，同时保证 ephemeral spawn 仍然可用：状态目录改为在启动 ephemeral worker 进程之前创建，而不是在 provider 工厂里创建。

`#17949` 修的是一个真实 bug——ephemeral provisioner 在没有任何代码创建的状态目录里 spawn worker，导致 hosted fixture 以 `runtime_provision_failed` 失败并表现为 `warm turn completed timed out`——但它把目录创建放在了工厂构造阶段。于是「仅配置」也会产生目录，违反了 runtime-provider 契约。本 PR 回退工厂改动，把同一操作移到唯一真正需要该目录的位置：两个 ephemeral 启动调用共用的 spawn 路径。

由于目录现在可能直到第一次 spawn 才出现，`broker-state` preflight 对缺失的目录报 WARN 而不是 PASS：检查只能看到自身权限，若以 root 运行 `--check` 就声称 Broker 会创建目录，会为服务账号实际不可写的目录背书。WARN 会写明由谁创建（ephemeral：worker spawn；durable：store 以 owner-private 0700 创建），并提示改用 Broker 的服务账号运行 `--check`。两种模式下，若路径被文件/链接占据、durable 路径含符号链接、或祖先无法产出该目录，仍报 FAIL 并点名挡路的组件。

## 为什么需要

`main` 目前是红的：`RuntimeProviderPluginsTest.builtinProvidersAreTrulyOptionalOnTheApplicationClasspath` 用 `DurableLocalProcess=false` 的 broker 指向 `uncreated-state` 目录构造每个 provider 工厂，并断言 `create()` 之后该路径仍不存在。引入 `#17949` 后该断言失败，导致所有合并了当前 `main` 的 managed-agent PR 的 SDK Java fast tier 变红。

## 评审测试计划

```

JAVA_HOME=<jdk21> mvn -o -pl verification -am \
  -Dtest='LocalRuntimeProviderFactoryTest,LocalProcessRuntimeProvisionerTest,RuntimeProviderPluginsTest,Issue13183*Test,FakeAttestationWorkerTest' \
  -DfailIfNoSpecifiedTests=false -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false \
  -Dspotbugs.skip -Dcheckstyle.skip test
```

预期：`RuntimeProviderPluginsTest` 恢复绿色（工厂构造后 `uncreated-state` 仍不存在）；两个真正 spawn worker 的 `Issue13183` 套件保持绿色，证明 ephemeral 路径仍能拿到工作目录；`broker-state` 预检在 ephemeral 目录缺失时 PASS，在路径被文件/悬空链接占据、或最近已存在祖先不可写/不可搜索时 FAIL。

### 证据（前后对比）

修改前（`#17949` 合入后的 `main`）：

```
RuntimeProviderPluginsTest.builtinProvidersAreTrulyOptionalOnTheApplicationClasspath
java.lang.AssertionError:
Expecting path:
  /tmp/junit-5365657755098847051/uncreated-state
not to exist
  at RuntimeProviderPluginsTest.java:133
```

修改后：

```
Tests run: 70, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
  -- LocalProcessRuntimeProvisionerTest (22), LocalRuntimeProviderFactoryTest (11),
     FakeAttestationWorkerTest (4), Issue13183AdversarialTest (6),
     Issue13183RegressionTest (25), RuntimeProviderPluginsTest (2)
```

非 UI 变更，无截图。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A |

### 环境（可选）

JDK 21，Maven 离线模式；仅运行单元/集成测试。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/取舍：目录改为在 spawn 时出现而非配置时；依赖「构造 provider 后目录已存在」来校验状态目录的部署将看不到它。durable 路径仍由 store 创建目录，因此只有 ephemeral 部署的时序变化。
- 未验证/超出范围：hosted failover lane 未在本地重跑，由 CI 的 SDK Java full tier 覆盖；Windows 未在本地验证。

prs.title: fix(ci): strip terminal and Bidi controls from the autofix failed-check evidence
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Strips terminal control characters **and Unicode Bidi overrides** from the autofix failed-check evidence log excerpt, and redacts around the strip so no credential survives it. The strip lives in the shared `skillLog` and covers the collector's excerpt and the patrol's rendered evidence. Line selection runs on the redacted, unstripped text; the strip and the weld-repair pass run **per contiguous run of selected lines**, with the repair input clamped to the shipped 300-character width.

Six review rounds shaped it:
- **Round 1 (R1-1):** the first revision stripped bare CR at the fetch site, which deleted the word boundary the anchored secret patterns (`\bnpm_…`, `\bsk-…`, `\beyJ…`, `\b<scheme>://`) need — a token after a bare CR (`x\rnpm_…`) rode into the excerpt unredacted. The strip moved into `skillLog`, after redaction, and widened from CR to the full C0/DEL/C1 class (R1-2).
- **Round 2 (R2-1, R2-3):** a control byte *inside* a credential (`npm_\rABC…`) defeats every anchor on the first pass, and deleting it welds the fragments into a contiguous, copy-pasteable token — so a second redaction pass runs after the strip. The class widened to also drop the full Unicode `Bidi_Control` set (the same class `safeReason` already drops), so a fork-controlled line can neither repaint nor reorder the excerpt.
- **Round 3 (R3-1, R3-2):** re-running the *whole* rule set after the strip broke two ways. The same strip can weld a word character onto a token's front (`x\rnpm_…` becomes `xnpm_…`), leaving `\b` nothing to match, so the welded credential still leaked. And the CR-bounded `Cookie:` / `Authorization:` rules — safe only while `\r` still ends the line — ran to the next newline and swallowed the `##[error]` line the excerpt exists to show. The post-strip pass became a separate `redactWeldedTokens` with the anchors dropped and the header rules left out. R3-4 replaced the sampled Bidi assertions with Unicode's own `\p{Bidi_Control}` property over all 12 code points (plus the whole C0/DEL/C1 class on the patrol side). R3-3 repaired the design record's item 8 in both languages — the corruption turned out to be produced by `prettier --write` itself.
- **Round 4 (Critical, fix-induced):** that split left the same shape behind in three more rules whose values end at whitespace (`Bearer`, the `TOKEN`/`KEY`/… rule, the URL userinfo). A per-rule "skip an already-`[redacted]` value" guard was added. The deferred R4-1 was closed by a per-family repair case pinning each of the nine rules.
- **Round 5 (Critical + Suggestion):** the guard's premise — "the first pass redacts the value whenever it can see the keyword" — is false exactly when the control split the keyword; and a fork could defeat the guard by writing `[redacted]secret` itself. Worse, the pass ran *before* line selection, so a weld could consume the failure line before it was ever chosen and the excerpt fell back to noise only. **Selection now precedes the strip.**
- **Round 6 (two Criticals):** the repair still only matched shapes it could reconstruct exactly — a value class that excludes the marker's characters (`#` `[` `]`) lets a credential legitimately containing them ship its tail (a password with `#`, a PEM body, a log-supplied `[redacted]` prefix, a multi-`@` userinfo, a welded digit-prefixed scheme, a deleted `Bearer` separator). And the private-key rule, matching across newlines over the join of *non-adjacent* selected windows, could pair a BEGIN in one window with an END in another and delete the failure between them. **The value is now a tempered token** — it runs to the next whitespace but never across the `##[error]` marker — and the repair runs **per contiguous run of selected indices** so a synthetic cross-window pair cannot form. An adversarial audit of that fix found and closed three more tails (URL password with `#`, env value with `}` or a quote). The repair input is clamped to 300 characters so it does not double base's quadratic keyword-rule cost on a long line.

## Why it's needed

The merged collector renders a bounded, redacted job-log excerpt for the address agent. `stripVTControlCharacters` removes escape sequences but leaves bare C0/C1 controls and Bidi overrides: a `\r` lets a fork-controlled log line visually overwrite the start of a terminal line, `\b` and friends repaint it, and Bidi reorders it — spoofing, not command injection, but the excerpt reaches step stdout through a defang that only neutralises `::` and `##[`. Selecting before the strip keeps every selector's terminator and guarantees the failure line is chosen; the redact→strip→redact-tokens ordering keeps the base redaction semantics while scrubbing tokens that only become contiguous once the controls are gone, and tempering the value on the marker keeps the failure marker itself intact.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- `node --test .github/scripts/autofix-check-evidence.test.mjs` — 29 passing. Witnesses: a secret after a bare `\r` is still redacted; neither a CR-terminated header nor a CR-terminated token value swallows the `##[error]` line that follows it; a control that splits the credential keyword still leaves that failure text; a welded credential whose value carries a terminator character (`#`) is fully redacted; backspace/C0/C1 and **all 12 Bidi code points** are stripped while tab and newline survive, asserted with `assert.doesNotMatch(stdout, /\p{Bidi_Control}/u)`; the text past the first control is retained.
- `scripts/tests/ci-flaky-rerun.test.js` (57, vitest) — patrol-side witnesses on the shared `skillLog`: the strip + Bidi case, a credential split by a control byte, a welded credential whose leading word boundary the strip also removed, the CR-terminated header case, the CR-terminated value of any whitespace-bounded rule (5 prefixes × CR/VT/FF), the welded-URL case in both shapes, the split-keyword case (env / `Bearer` / private-key label), a `FAIL` line whose leading whitespace is a control, a credential the log hid behind a literal `[redacted]` prefix, a per-family repair case feeding one weld fixture for each of the nine post-strip rules **plus the round-6 entrances** (value carrying `#`/`}`/quote, welded digit-prefixed scheme, multi-`@` userinfo, URL password with `#`, deleted `Bearer` separator, log-supplied `[redacted]` URL value) asserting both placeholder present and secret tail absent, a marker inside a BEGIN…END span preserved (while a real PEM and a non-marker `#` body redact), no cross-window BEGIN/END pairing (the `TypeError:` between survives), and a case feeding every C0/DEL/C1 and `Bidi_Control` code point with both property assertions.
- The af-161 workflow wiring pins (4) and the whole `workflow-size.test.js` suite (222 pass / 23 skipped) pass; ESLint and Prettier are clean on every changed file. The workflow YAML itself is unchanged — only the sibling rationale doc.
- **Real-CLI verification:** the collector was run as a subprocess with a fake `gh` on PATH serving an adversarial log (every round-6 entrance + Bidi + a real failure marker). The shipped excerpt has all nine secrets absent, both failure markers present, the failed step name present, and no bare CR or Bidi.
- The bilingual design doc and `qwen-autofix.md#af-161` record selection-before-strip, contiguous-run grouping, the tempered value, the URL length-bound and multi-segment userinfo, the 300-char clamp, the accepted over-redaction trade, the residual gaps, and the one-time patrol fingerprint re-key (R2-2).

**R3-3 root cause, worth knowing before editing that paragraph:** the corruption was produced by `prettier --write` itself, not by hand. A bare `Bidi_Control` in prose opens a Markdown emphasis span that runs across the following code spans, and prettier 3.6.1 re-serializes it with `*`, rewriting the identifiers inside the spans and welding the spacing. The round-2 text was already a prettier fixed point, which is why `--check` exited 0. The repair puts every `_`-bearing identifier in a code span, so `prettier --write` now reports `(unchanged)` and a second pass is byte-identical. Escaping the prose underscores (`Bidi\_Control`) is **not** stable — prettier unescapes and re-corrupts on the next run.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI automation, no user-facing UI. Before: a log line's bare `\r` survived into the excerpt; stripping at the fetch site un-redacted secrets after a CR; a control inside a credential was rejoined into an unredacted token; a welded prefix leaked; CR-terminated headers and values swallowed the failure line; a weld could consume the failure line before selection; a value carrying a terminator character shipped its tail; and a cross-window key pair deleted the failure between. After: the failure line is always selected and shipped, the `##[error]` marker survives the weld, credentials carrying `#`/`[`/`]`/`@`/`}`/quote redact fully, and the full control + Bidi class is stripped.

All measurements below are on the pushed head `383d7b9` (fixes `2e05374`, `b103b78`, `5c85946`, merges of `origin/main` at `fdd30c6` then `b9da38c`). Every mutation arm was run on this head and the source restored byte-identical after each.

| Check | Result |
| :-- | :-- |
| `node --test .github/scripts/autofix-check-evidence.test.mjs` | 29 pass / 0 fail |
| `scripts/tests/ci-flaky-rerun.test.js` (vitest) | 57 pass |
| af-161 wiring pins (`qwen-autofix-workflow.test.js -t 'failed-check evidence'`) | 4 pass |
| `scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js` (whole file) | 222 pass / 23 skipped |
| `ci-flaky-rerun-workflow` + `qwen-runner-checkout-workflow` + `qwen-fleet-shepherd-workflow` | 91 pass / 2 skipped |
| `.github/scripts/ci-runner-routing.test.mjs` | 112 pass / 0 fail |
| `scripts/tests/qwen-autofix-workflow.test.js` (whole file) | 344 pass / 13 skipped / 0 fail |
| Real-CLI adversarial run (fake `gh`, 9 secrets + markers) | all secrets absent, markers present |
| ESLint + Prettier (changed files) | clean |

Mutation witnesses (one change per arm, then restored byte-identical; all on this head):

| Mutation | Collector | Patrol |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| none (shipped) | 29 pass | 57 pass |
| revert env value tempered token to a `#`-bound class | 28 pass / 1 fail | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| restore env value structural exclusions (`}`/quote) | 29 pass | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| exclude `#` from the URL userinfo | 29 pass | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| require a `Bearer` separator (`\s+`) | 29 pass | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| restore the URL scheme lookbehind | 29 pass | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| collapse the URL userinfo to a single `@`-segment | 29 pass | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| exclude `[` `]` from the URL userinfo | 29 pass | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| revert the private-key body to `[^#]*?` | 29 pass | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| join all selected windows into one run | 29 pass | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| delete any one of the nine post-strip rules | 29 pass (env: 27 / 2) | 56 pass / 1 fail (bearer, env, npm: 54 / 3; key: 55 / 2) |
| re-anchor the post-strip `npm_` rule | 29 pass | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| re-run the whole `redactLog` as the repair pass | 25 pass / 4 fail | 50 pass / 7 fail |
| make the post-strip pass a no-op | 27 pass / 2 fail | 51 pass / 6 fail |
| move the strip before line selection | 29 pass | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| delete the strip | 25 pass / 4 fail | 49 pass / 8 fail |
| truncate at the first control | 23 pass / 6 fail | 47 pass / 10 fail |
| narrow the class to `\r` | 28 pass / 1 fail | 55 pass / 2 fail |
| narrow the Bidi class to the sampled points | 28 pass / 1 fail | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| drop a single unsampled `Bidi_Control` point | 28 pass / 1 fail | 56 pass / 1 fail |
| widen the class to eat `\n`/`\t` | 24 pass / 5 fail | 52 pass / 5 fail |

The URL scheme length-bound and the 300-char repair clamp are cost fixes, not behavior ones — witnessed by timing: the isolated URL rule is linear (1–2 ms at 40k characters), and an adversarial 100k-character word run costs ~7 s (base-equivalent, the first pass's quadratic `TOKEN`/`KEY`/… rule) rather than the ~14 s the unclamped second pass added.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ tested (local node:test + vitest + real-CLI run, this head) |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested locally (CI runs the suites) |

### Environment (optional)

Local node:test and vitest suites plus a real-CLI subprocess run with a fake `gh`; no sandbox or model calls.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the first redaction pass is byte-identical to base, and the second pass only adds redaction. Accepted costs, all recorded in design item 8 (both languages): an unanchored `sk-` also redacts a `task-…` identifier carrying 20+ alphanumerics; a control *inside* a header value leaves the post-CR fragment visible (`Cookie: [redacted]=abc`), which the merge-base copy does too; a control inside the header **keyword** (`Coo\rkie: sid=abc`) escapes both passes, so the welded value stays unredacted; an empty-value header already loses the next line in the first pass, in base as well.
- **Residual gaps, recorded not closed:** a value cannot tell a weld *inside* the credential from a weld *before* following word-like text, so a bare failure keyword (no `##[error]`) welded onto a value is still consumed (the message tail survives); a `##[error]` inside a BEGIN…END span stops the private-key match, preserving the marker over redacting the span; the strip class does not cover the zero-width format family (U+200B, U+2060, U+FEFF), so a credential split by one is neither welded nor redacted; and a tab inside a credential is preserved by the strip and terminates both passes' value classes. The acceptance criterion lists these as exceptions rather than claiming them closed. The `##[error]` marker itself is protected by the temper.
- **One-time transition cost (R2-2, documented not code-changed):** the patrol keys its marker comment off `skillLog`'s output (`fingerprint(target, log)` in `scan`), and `alreadyHandled` matches that key exactly. Removing controls re-keys the fingerprint, so a marker written before this lands stops matching once — the patrol re-triages that failure and posts a fresh marker, then self-heals from the next marker on.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live autofix round on a real runner (deferred since #16659). The sibling fetches (`ci-log.ts`'s `jobLog`, the patrol's `GhClient.jobLog`) keep their VT-only shape; the CLI's raw log file can still carry bare controls — stated in the design doc, not fixed here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none beyond the one-time patrol marker re-key above.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #16659 (merged), addressing the bare-CR note its re-review approved with; this revision answers review R1-1–R1-5, R2-1–R2-3, R3-1–R3-4, round 4's Critical plus its deferred items, round 5's R5-1/R5-2, and round 6's two Criticals plus its six deferred items. Design record (this head): [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/cba1dc5dc3e8/docs/design/2026-11-09-autofix-failed-check-evidence.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/cba1dc5dc3e8/docs/design/2026-11-09-autofix-failed-check-evidence.zh-CN.md).

prs.body:
## What this PR does

Holds the Microsoft Teams channel out of the npm release until a maintainer completes its one-time public bootstrap publish, using the same repository-variable gate the Mem0 extension already uses. The gate lives in the release package selection, so it rides the workflow-pinned checkout and applies even when the selected release ref predates this change; the release workflow contributes a single orchestration line exposing the variable, guarded to the upstream repository so a fork can never publish into the `@qwen-code` scope. The already-shipped guard and the release versioning behaviour are deliberately left untouched: Teams is still probed for an existing version, and its package and extension manifests still follow the release version. The developer documentation now names both bootstrap-gated packages and the variables that enable them.

## Why it's needed

The nightly `v0.28.0-nightly.20261119.f8d4f706ea` failed in its publish job (#17898). The Teams channel merged the same day and was the only new workspace in the release window since the last good nightly. Because it merged without `private`, it opted straight into the main npm release — but the publish job authenticates with npm trusted publishing alone, carrying no npm token, and npm only lets a maintainer bind a trusted publisher to a package that already exists. Teams has never been published, so the workflow cannot authenticate for it, and since the whole selection goes out through one recursive publish invocation under a fail-fast shell, that single package takes down the entire release rather than being skipped. This repository already documents both halves of that trap: the pnpm release design warns that a new non-private workspace opts into the release and its npm permissions and trusted publisher must be reviewed before merging, and the Mem0 extension design records the bootstrap-variable remedy for exactly this constraint. Teams was merged without either. Gating it defaults the release back to a working state immediately, while preserving the intent to distribute it once the bootstrap is done.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that the default release selection no longer contains `@qwen-code/channel-msteams`, while `@qwen-code/audio-capture` and `@qwen-code/external-context-mem0` keep their existing behaviour, and that enabling the new variable on the upstream repository puts Teams back into the selection while a fork still never publishes it. Confirm the already-shipped guard still lists Teams among the packages it probes, so a partial release cannot be overwritten by a retry. The focused suites below cover all of this; each new clause was also mutation-probed by deleting or negating it and watching the corresponding test fail. After merge, a maintainer still needs to perform the one-time public bootstrap publish of Teams, bind it to the release workflow in the `production-release` environment, and then set `NPM_CHANNEL_MSTEAMS_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING_ENABLED` to `true`. Until then Teams is intentionally not distributed through npm; its documented local-extension install path is unaffected.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — release-pipeline behaviour, no user-visible UI change. Before: the publish selection handed a never-published package to a tokenless trusted-publishing invocation, failing the whole job. After: that package is skipped by default and re-enters the selection only when a maintainer enables its variable.

### Tested on

|     OS     |    Status    |
| :--------: | :----------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅ tested   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit and meta-test suites only (`scripts/tests` via the repository's Vitest config), plus the full build, typecheck and lint. The sandbox runs as a non-owner uid, so `COREPACK_HOME` and `npm_config_cache` were pointed at writable temporary directories for those commands; no repository file was changed to accommodate that.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Teams' npm distribution is deferred until a maintainer completes the bootstrap publish and sets the variable. That is the intended trade — a skipped package is recoverable in one release, whereas an unauthenticatable one fails every nightly. If Teams had already been bootstrapped and bound, this change would only delay its distribution by one release rather than break anything.
- Not validated / out of scope: the release workflow itself and a real npm publish were not run. This environment has no GitHub credentials, so the failed run's log could not be fetched, and publishing is a networked write that is out of bounds here. The diagnosis rests on the release-window diff, the publish job's tokenless trusted-publishing configuration, and the repository's own documented constraint and precedent; the regression witness is the selection gate and its mutation probes. The bootstrap publish, the trusted-publisher binding, and setting the repository variable remain maintainer actions. No change to Teams' runtime, its ingress, or its version alignment.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No published package is removed or renamed, and no consumer-facing contract changes. Teams was never available on npm, so nothing that users could have installed is affected.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17898

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

在维护者完成 Microsoft Teams 渠道的一次性公开 bootstrap 发布之前，把它挡在 npm 发布之外，使用的是 Mem0 扩展已有的同一套仓库变量开关。开关逻辑位于发布包选择处，因此它随 workflow 固定（pinned）的 checkout 一起生效，即使所选发布 ref 早于本次改动也依然有效；发布工作流只贡献一行编排代码来暴露该变量，并限定在上游仓库，使 fork 永远无法向 `@qwen-code` scope 发布。"已发布"守卫与发布版本行为刻意保持不变：Teams 仍会被探测是否已存在该版本，其包清单与扩展清单也仍跟随发布版本。开发者文档现在列出了两个受 bootstrap 开关控制的包，以及启用它们的变量。

## 为什么需要它

 nightly `v0.28.0-nightly.20261119.f8d4f706ea` 在其 publish 任务失败（#17898）。Teams 渠道当天合并，是自上一个成功 nightly 以来发布窗口内唯一新增的 workspace。由于它合并时没有设置 `private`，就直接进入了主 npm 发布 —— 但 publish 任务仅使用 npm trusted publishing 认证，不携带任何 npm token，而 npm 只允许维护者为已经存在的包绑定 trusted publisher。Teams 从未发布过，因此工作流无法为它完成认证；又因为整个选择集是在 fail-fast shell 下通过一条递归 publish 命令发出的，这一个包就会拖垮整个发布，而不是被跳过。本仓库已经记录了这个陷阱的两个方面：pnpm 发布设计文档警告新增的非 private workspace 会进入主发布，合并前必须检查其 npm 权限与 trusted publisher；Mem0 扩展设计文档则记录了针对该约束的 bootstrap 变量补救方式。Teams 合并时两者都没有做。加上开关后，发布立即恢复到可用状态，同时保留了 bootstrap 完成后继续分发它的意图。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

确认默认发布选择中不再包含 `@qwen-code/channel-msteams`，而 `@qwen-code/audio-capture` 与 `@qwen-code/external-context-mem0` 的既有行为保持不变；并确认在上游仓库启用新变量会让 Teams 重新进入选择集，而 fork 仍然永远不会发布它。确认"已发布"守卫探测的包列表中仍包含 Teams，因此部分发布的版本不会被重试覆盖。下面的聚焦套件覆盖了以上全部；每个新增子句还做了变异探针验证 —— 删除或取反它，然后观察对应用例失败。合并之后，维护者仍需完成 Teams 的一次性公开 bootstrap 发布，在 `production-release` 环境中把它绑定到发布工作流，然后把 `NPM_CHANNEL_MSTEAMS_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING_ENABLED` 设为 `true`。在此之前 Teams 有意不通过 npm 分发；其文档中的本地扩展安装路径不受影响。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 发布流水线行为，没有用户可见的 UI 变化。改动前：发布选择把一个从未发布过的包交给无 token 的 trusted publishing 命令，导致整个任务失败。改动后：该包默认被跳过，只有维护者启用其变量时才重新进入选择集。

### 测试平台

|     OS     |    状态    |
| :--------: | :----------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅ 已测试   |

### 环境（可选）

仅单元与元测试套件（通过仓库的 Vitest 配置运行 `scripts/tests`），外加完整的 build、typecheck 与 lint。沙箱以非所有者 uid 运行，因此这些命令把 `COREPACK_HOME` 与 `npm_config_cache` 指向了可写的临时目录；没有为此改动任何仓库文件。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：Teams 的 npm 分发被推迟，直到维护者完成 bootstrap 发布并设置变量。这正是预期的权衡 —— 被跳过的包可以在一个发布周期内恢复，而无法认证的包会让每个 nightly 都失败。即便 Teams 其实已经完成 bootstrap 并绑定，本改动也只会把它的分发推迟一个发布周期，而不会破坏任何东西。
- 未验证 / 范围之外：没有运行发布工作流本身，也没有做真实的 npm 发布。本环境没有 GitHub 凭据，因此无法拉取失败运行的日志；而发布属于联网写操作，在此处越界。诊断依据是发布窗口的差异、publish 任务无 token 的 trusted publishing 配置，以及仓库自身记录的约束与先例；回归见证是选择开关及其变异探针。bootstrap 发布、trusted publisher 绑定以及设置仓库变量仍是维护者动作。没有改动 Teams 的运行时、其 ingress 或其版本对齐逻辑。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。没有删除或重命名任何已发布的包，也没有消费者可见的契约变化。Teams 从未在 npm 上可用过，因此用户可能安装过的任何东西都不受影响。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #17898

prs.title: fix(core): retain oversized transcript indexes in a bounded cache class
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Gives transcript indexes whose byte estimate exceeds the shared 64 MiB index-cache budget their own bounded retention class (256 MiB, LRU eviction within the class) instead of refusing them admission on every request, and makes hook-turn aggregate retention account against the entry's own budget class so a cached large index cannot block hook retention on small sessions. The shared byte budget keeps capping small-session retention exactly as before; the two classes never evict each other by byte budget. Worst-case byte retention is the sum of both budgets (320 MiB), and the constant comment records the remaining residuals explicitly.

A review round on the merged head then closed three reproduced gaps in the new retention: a frozen cursor could serve rewritten bytes after an equal-size in-place rewrite (the page path now applies the same equal-size mtime validation the turn-index path already had); Managed message projections retained alongside a cached index now account their decoded bodies against the same class budget and are dropped when they do not fit (including projections decoded before their index is offered to the cache); and admitting a newer snapshot of the same file now evicts superseded older prefixes when the class budget is full, so an append no longer leaves every subsequent page reparsing while the dead prefix holds the budget. Capacity contracts in the design docs are updated in both languages.

A full high-effort review (17 agents + verifiers, two dry reverse-audit rounds) and a delta reverse-audit pair then hardened the retention further: superseded-snapshot eviction also covers equal-size orphans left unreachable by an in-place rewrite or replacement (within the entry's budget class only — cross-class eviction is deliberately absent because freeing shared bytes cannot admit an oversized index); the readPage projection retention delegates to the shared admission helper instead of duplicating its arithmetic; the projection byte estimate folds per record rather than stringifying the whole decoded history at once (bounding the transient allocation to the largest record); and a completed index build re-verifies its frozen snapshot before admission or eviction, so a build that finishes after the file was rewritten under it neither caches a torn index nor evicts the live newer entry as an orphan. Each guard ships a regression test verified to go red when the guard is removed.

The latest review round closed the remaining confirmed findings: both admission doors now sum the reclaimable superseded bytes and evict only when the new snapshot fits after the reclaim, so a refused admission no longer evicts the still-readable frozen prefix it cannot replace; projection and hook retention choose the budget class from the post-add entry total (a shared entry whose retained bodies cross the shared budget moves into the oversized class instead of being refused against a budget it no longer belongs to), through one helper shared by every retention site; and the snapshot-anchored half of the equal-size rewrite guard gained its missing regression test. The rewrite-then-append bypass found by the bot review is reproduced and documented as a pre-existing residual in both design-doc languages (page bodies are read live at the frozen offsets, so the equal-size mtime guard cannot see a rewrite followed by an append); frozen-prefix digest validation is listed as deferred work because it re-reads the prefix on every frozen page and touches the cursor contracts.

The next review round reproduced two concurrent P1s with one root cause — waiters on a shared index build received the raw build promise, bypassing the initiator's snapshot re-verification and admission — and a projection P2. The cache entry's pending is now a wrapper promise that runs build, re-verification and admission, so a snapshot rewritten under a shared build fails every sharer closed instead of serving torn bytes, and a projection can only attach after admission (the admission door also accounts any attached projection, the same contract as the restore-offer door). A transient stat error on the re-verification serves the built snapshot uncached instead of failing a ready page. The post-add class helper now reclaims superseded same-file snapshots when they block a projection's class crossing, fit-before-evict, so an appended Managed session's new projection replaces the old one instead of being refused and re-decoded per page. The identity arm of the orphan predicate gained its missing test (same-size replacement at a new inode with pinned mtime).

The following re-review found the last verification gap: the single-entry cap refusal and the stale-completion return still ran before the post-build re-verification, so a frozen cursor sharing a build whose entry was LRU-evicted mid-build or whose index exceeded the class budget could receive rewritten bytes. The re-verification now precedes every early return in the shared completion — cache-entry ownership only governs cache writes and deletes, never whether the built index is safe to serve. The same round extended the superseded predicate to the shrink direction (a truncated longer prefix is unreachable dead weight), applied the fit-before-evict reclaim to the restore-offer door's 32-entry count cap, consolidated the duplicated Managed test fixtures, added a route-level cross-request index-reuse test, and corrected the design docs (the count cap is a global LRU, not class-isolated; section references point at the real heading).

The bot's next review confirmed those fixes and deferred eight items; all eight are dispositioned in the following commit. The one fix-induced regression among them is corrected: the direction-agnostic superseded predicate let a frozen-prefix admission reclaim the live newer index, so the predicate is now temporal (strictly older snapshots reclaimable in either size direction; equal-mtime larger entries — the live index a frozen read sees — protected; equal-size equal-mtime identity-changed orphans unchanged). The unreachable admission-side projection accounting was removed (projections attach only after the shared verified admission; the offer door keeps its reachable call), the route-level reuse test now exercises the oversized class, the count-cap offer test covers both classes, the allowAppend success arm gained a concurrent test, and the docs correct the refused-admission rationale, a zh mistranslation, and mark the older selective-session-restore design superseded in part.

The bot's round-5 review added nine suggestions, all dispositioned in the next two commits. Substantive: the restore-offer count-slot reclaim became class-agnostic (a full 32-entry cap can now be relieved by a superseded same-file entry in the other class; the byte arm stays class-scoped), and in-flight build placeholders are exempt from the count-cap LRU with pending hits refreshing recency, so unrelated admissions no longer discard a completing index. The rest are test strengthening (entries-after-offer, deterministic equal-mtime reclaim, stale-completion witnessing via a cleared entry, retention-vs-rebuild entries assertions, shared-full hook refusal) and doc disposition: the legacy single-language restore design is restored to its pre-PR state while the bilingual design explicitly supersedes its three cache rules.

The bot's round-6 review then posted zero new findings and reached approve posture (downgraded to Comment only by the attributed main-side Java CI red). Its eight deferred items are dispositioned in the final commit: the hook-aggregate crossing-reclaim test (mutant-witnessed), removal of the redundant pending-hit recency refresh, the concurrent-projection test renamed to what it pins, the hook fixture typed, and doc precision fixes; the three behavior-preserving polish items (predicate/class DRY refactor, estimate caching, fixture consolidation) are deferred with reasons as follow-up work on converged code.

A further re-review then found that unreachable old indexes held the budget when the mtime did not advance (a backup replacement restoring an older mtime, or a same-millisecond truncation). The superseded predicate now reclaims entries the current file state has left unreachable — changed identity, length beyond the current file, or equal size at a different mtime — regardless of temporal order, while a frozen-prefix read still never reclaims the live newer index. Both reviewer scenarios were re-run at scale (106,085 records, 137 MiB index, default budgets): the second read after each mutation now hits in 10 ms / 5 ms instead of rebuilding. Regression tests pin mtimes explicitly for fast and slow filesystems; four clause-removal mutants each red exactly their test.

The next re-review (static plus a dynamic re-run of the round-9 scenarios) found three issues in that reclaim, all fixed with mutation-witnessed regression tests. (1) The reclaim branch issued a second, uncaught `fsp.stat` after the ownership check and the class budget math: a transient stat error there rejected the whole shared build with a raw system error, and a rewrite or concurrent admission landing in that await window could evict the live newer entry or overwrite a re-owned slot. The re-verification now returns the verified current file length through a shared helper, and the entire admission tail — ownership check, budget math, reclaim, cache write — runs synchronously against that one verified state. (2) The growth-accounting door passed the entry's own frozen snapshot length as the current file state, so a frozen hook aggregate or Managed projection could reclaim the appended live index as unreachable (and a replacement during the async decode could do the same through the identity clause). The unreachable clauses now require a verified current file state: the admission and offer doors pass it, the frozen hook/decode doors reclaim by temporal order alone. (3) The completion wrote over the placeholder key in place, leaving it at the LRU head the count-cap prune scans first; the completion now deletes before setting, landing at the MRU tail. Main is merged for the Java gate, which is green on main again.

The following re-review confirmed those fixes and reproduced one more P2: an in-place sync that appends on the same inode and then restores an older source timestamp broke the temporal reclaim clause in both directions — the live admission could not reclaim the shorter prefix (its mtime was newer), and a frozen read evicted the longer live index (its mtime was older). Supersession is now decided by length, never by mtime order: under the append-only read model a same-identity strictly shorter prefix is contained in the incoming snapshot and reclaimable fit-before-evict, while a longer same-identity index still serves the frozen offsets and is protected. The verified doors apply that rule plus the unreachable clauses; the frozen growth doors reclaim only same-identity strictly shorter prefixes and protect longer or foreign-identity entries, which may be the live index. The reviewer's scenario re-run at scale (106,085 records, 137 MiB index, default budgets, append + mtime −60 s): repeats now hit at 10 ms after one rebuild instead of rebuilding every read, and a frozen-cursor read no longer evicts the live index. Four regression tests (live reclaim + frozen protection double assertion, hook and Managed mtime-regression retention, shorter foreign-identity replacement during a paused decode) and seven mutants (M48–M54) witness the rule; the design docs state it in both languages.

## Why it's needed

#17889 measured that `GET /session/:id/transcript` costs the same wall-clock time regardless of `limit` and `cursor`: on a 199.9 MB / 84,352-record session every request — including `limit=1`, identical repeats, and cursor continuations — took ~4.2 s and stalled the daemon event loop for unrelated clients. The root cause is the cache admission policy: any index whose estimate exceeds the shared 64 MiB budget was refused outright, so the sessions that most need the cache could never enter it and reparsed the whole JSONL on every page. A 16.5 MiB control session proved the cache mechanism itself works (repeat requests hit in 0.6 ms); the only behavioral difference was the admission decision. This PR fixes that admission cliff for the daemon-local read paths (the workspace-qualified route Web Shell uses, restore projections, turn index, and long-lived ACP children), and keeps the new retention honest about snapshot validity and memory.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Unit suites (from `packages/core`): `npx vitest run src/services/session-transcript-reader.test.ts src/services/session-hook-history.test.ts` → 241 passed (reader 224 + hook-history 17); the 8 core reader/consumer suites → 743 passed, and the 2 cli route suites (multi-workspace-sessions + hosted-harness-session) → 1093 passed, all on the merged tree. The regression tests cover: oversized retention serves repeats/cursor pages without rebuilding; a second oversized index that does not fit the class budget is refused without evicting the first; oversized pruning never touches shared entries; appends invalidate a retained oversized index; mixed-class admission and hook retention account by class, not total bytes; the restore/offer path caches an oversized index for later pages; frozen cursors and snapshot anchors are rejected after an equal-size in-place rewrite in both budget classes; a newer snapshot makes room by evicting superseded same-file prefixes (shared-class and cross-class protection, both admission doors) while old frozen cursors still read their original prefix; equal-size orphans are evicted to admit the live snapshot; a stale equal-size build cannot evict the live newer entry; a refused admission (new snapshot cannot fit even after reclaiming the superseded prefix) keeps the prefix cached and its frozen cursor hitting, in both classes and at both doors; a retained Managed projection is accounted against the class budget via both the readPage door and the restore-offer door (tight budget re-decodes, generous budget retains and accounts), including a projection that moves its entry from the shared into the oversized class; hook aggregates cross the class boundary the same way; a projection that crosses into a full target class reclaims the superseded same-file entry; concurrent pages sharing a rebuilt snapshot all fail closed when it was rewritten under the build; a projection attached while the build was pending is accounted at admission; a transient stat error on the admission re-verify serves the page uncached; an equal-size replacement at a new inode with pinned mtime is evicted as an orphan; a truncated longer prefix is evicted to admit the live snapshot; the restore-offer door reclaims a superseded slot at a full 32-entry count cap; the concurrent fail-closed matrix covers resident, mid-build LRU-evicted, and over-cap completions; and a route-level test pins cross-request index reuse on the workspace-qualified HTTP surface in the oversized class; a frozen-prefix admission never reclaims the live newer index; a shared build only appended under admits for every sharer; the reclaim branch issues no second stat (a per-path call-position fault injector pins that a transient error at the hypothetical reclaim-stat position never fires, and a call-position hook reproduces the reviewer's rewrite-during-reclaim interleaving — frozen sharers serve frozen content, no newer build under the stale completion); frozen hook retention and frozen Managed projection retention refuse without evicting the live newer index (including a paused-decode inode-replacement race); and a completing placeholder lands at the MRU tail, surviving its own count-cap prune and the next unrelated admission. Four existing tests were updated to the new contract with their intent preserved.
2. Mutation witnesses (each mutation applied to the production source, run, and restored — fifty-three in the main loop, plus verifier-executed mutants): reverting oversized admission, reverting hook class accounting, cross-class prune eviction, total-byte accounting at all three sites, reverting the offer hunk, reverting the equal-size mtime check, dropping orphan eviction, hardcoding the eviction class filter to oversized, deleting the class filter, removing offer-side eviction, making the projection admission helper a no-op, disabling the completed-build snapshot re-verification, evict-before-fit at the read door, evict-before-fit at the offer door, pre-add class selection, dropping the snapshot half of the rewrite guard, reverting the changed-snapshot throw to a return, removing the crossing reclaim, removing the stat-error catch, deleting the dev/ino orphan clause, handing waiters the raw build promise again, moving the cap return back before the re-verification, moving the stale return back before it, reverting the shrink arm, removing the offer count-cap reclaim, reverting the predicate to direction-agnostic, restricting the older clause to smaller entries, disabling allowAppend in the re-verify, scoping the count arm back to one class, removing the placeholder exemption, removing the equal-mtime clause, replacing class-filtered prune with total-bytes, making the retention addition always fit, removing the crossing reclaim on the hook-aggregate path, removing each of the four unreachable/temporal reclaim clauses (re-witnessed against the gated predicate), removing the completion's delete-before-set, passing the frozen length as the current state at the hook growth door, passing it at the frozen Managed decode door, removing the verified-state gate, and reintroducing the second admission stat (witnessed twice: the uncaught-error arm and the rewrite-interleaving arm), reverting either door to temporal supersession, removing the verified length clause, and removing the frozen growth door's same-identity guard are each killed by their regression test (executed red/green flips).
3. Issue-scale probe (source-level, the exact function the route delegates to — `SessionTranscriptReader.readPage`, no mocks): a synthetic 84,352-record / 204.6 MiB linear-chain transcript satisfying the reader's validation. Before the fix, ten consecutive requests with a byte-identical cache key each logged `index cache skipped oversized entry byteSize=108984066` and rebuilt the full index (~1.7–1.9 s each, event-loop gaps 378–439 ms). After the fix, the first request builds once and retains the 103.9 MiB index; repeats, cursor pages, and backward pages hit the cache.
4. Fit-before-evict probe (same harness, default budgets): session A + three fillers fill the shared class at 62,021,256 bytes / 4 entries; A grows 12,000 → 20,000 records so its new estimate cannot fit even after reclaiming the old prefix. The refused new snapshot builds once (376.9 ms); cache stats stay unchanged; the old frozen cursor serves in 2.2 ms with no rebuild; a filler stays warm at 0.9 ms. The evict-then-refuse mutant fails the same probe.
5. Merged-tree re-verification: the branch merges the latest `origin/main` cleanly; the full build + bundle and core typecheck pass on the merged tree, and the reader/consumer suites pass there.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-UI change; measured request-level numbers on the 84,352-record / 204.6 MiB fixture (back-to-back, static file, Node v26.12.1):

| request | before | after | full index builds after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit=1` first | 1837.6 ms, cache empty | 1892.2 ms, index retained (108,984,066 bytes) | 1 (one-time) |
| `limit=10` | 1743.2 ms | 10.4 ms | 0 |
| `limit=120` | 1721.7 ms | 15.0 ms | 0 |
| `limit=500` | 1724.0 ms | 36.2 ms | 0 |
| `limit=1` repeat ×3 | 1824.9 / 1753.4 / 1694.8 ms | 11.2 / 9.1 / 9.3 ms | 0 |
| cursor page `limit=10` | 1707.4 ms | 10.4 ms | 0 |
| `direction=backward&limit=1` | 1647.0 ms | 9.7 ms | 0 |
| max event-loop gap on repeats | 378–439 ms | 3.8–5.7 ms | — |

Small control (6,800 records / 16.5 MiB) unchanged: first 155.5 ms, repeat 0.7 ms. Gates: merged-tree `npm run build && npm run bundle` exit 0; core `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; prettier + eslint clean on all changed files.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: worst-case index-cache byte retention rises from 64 MiB to 320 MiB per process (estimate caliber; an independent heap probe measured real heap ≈ 0.63× the estimate — heapDelta/estimate = 0.632 on a 30k-record probe — so 320 MiB of estimate corresponds to ~202 MiB of real heap). Retention stays bounded by the two class budgets, the 5-minute TTL, and LRU eviction; small-session retention is unchanged. Managed projections and hook aggregates count against the budget class the entry belongs to after the addition; an entry whose retained bodies cross the shared budget moves into the oversized class, and the combined entry is dropped from retention when it does not fit. A low-confidence review finding about coordinating the oversized budget with the experimental `--child-heap-mode enforce` 512 MiB floor is deferred to maintainer heap-policy discussion (the floor is not the default; default `observe` applies nothing).
- Behavior change beyond caching: a frozen cursor or snapshot now returns `transcript_snapshot_unavailable` when the file was rewritten in place at the same size with a moved mtime — the same validation the turn-index path already applied. Pure appends keep frozen prefixes readable. This closes a stale-snapshot hole that also existed for small cached indexes. Concurrent requests sharing an index build now share its verified completion: if the snapshot was rewritten or replaced under the build, every sharer receives `transcript_snapshot_unavailable` (previously waiters could receive the torn build result); a transient stat error (`EMFILE`/`EIO`/`EACCES`) on the post-build re-verification serves the built snapshot uncached rather than returning 500. The re-verification precedes every early completion return (cap refusal, stale completion), so no unverified build result is served except that documented best-effort path. Superseded-snapshot reclaim covers both size directions and the offer door's count cap.
- Not validated / out of scope: a uuid-preserving in-place rewrite followed by an append is not detected (pre-existing; the equal-size guard added here cannot see it because the size grew, and page bodies are read live at the frozen offsets even on a cache hit) — frozen-prefix digest validation is documented as deferred work in both design-doc languages. The legacy singular route with default `--channel-idle-timeout-ms 0` still reaps the ACP child after each page, discarding its in-process cache (documented in `docs/users/qwen-serve.md`; mitigation: a positive idle timeout) — the daemon-local workspace-qualified route and long-lived children benefit directly. The first cold read still pays the one-time full parse; appends invalidate the frozen key, and the newer snapshot is admitted by evicting superseded same-file prefixes when it fits after the reclaim (incremental tail extension remains a follow-up). Sessions whose index estimate exceeds 256 MiB (dense short records can reach this well below the 256 MiB file-size cap) still rebuild per page — the constant comment documents this cliff. The 32-entry count cap remains global, so an oversized entry can occupy a slot a warm small index held (at most three oversized entries fit the class budget).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The cache is process-internal; no API, cursor, or schema change. ## 为什么需要

#17889 实测 `GET /session/:id/transcript` 的耗时与 `limit`、`cursor` 无关：199.9 MB / 84,352 记录的会话上，每个请求——包括 `limit=1`、完全相同的重复请求、cursor 翻页——都耗时约 4.2 秒，并阻塞 daemon 事件循环、拖慢无关客户端。根因是缓存准入策略：估算超过共享 64 MiB 预算的索引被直接拒绝，最需要缓存的会话永远进不了缓存，每页都全量重解析 JSONL。16.5 MiB 对照会话证明缓存机制本身有效（重复请求 0.6 ms 命中），唯一的行为差异就是准入决定。本 PR 修复 daemon 本地读取路径（Web Shell 使用的 workspace 限定路由、restore 投影、turn index、长活 ACP 子进程）的准入悬崖，并让新保留机制对快照有效性与内存保持诚实。

真实 daemon 验证（从构建 bundle 起隔离 qwen serve，同一 84,352 记录 / 204.6 MiB 夹具注入工作区，真实 HTTP 路由）：workspace 限定路由首页构建一次（1811 ms）、重复命中缓存（12.8–17.8 ms）、游标页 16.2 ms、`limit=500` 58.8 ms / 625 事件；追加一条记录后新快照获准入、其重复命中（11.4 ms）；等长原地改写使冻结游标返回 `409 transcript_snapshot_unavailable`。一次性冷重建期间，并发小会话 ping 保持 5–11 ms，仅一处解析后同步段例外（最大 358 ms）；热请求不阻塞并发客户端，daemon stall 监控记录为零。先验后逐场景也在合并树 bundle 上经 HTTP 确认：A+3 填充会话占满共享类（冷 330.4 / 255.8 / 212.7 / 203.2 ms，A 热重复 6.1 ms）；A 文件从 30.5 MB 增至 50.8 MB 后，被拒新首屏构建一次 352.6 ms，旧冻结游标 200 返回仅 6.5 ms 无重建，被拒快照重解析 337.2 ms（已记录残余），填充会话 5.7 ms 保持热，stall 监控为零。首个无游标 backward 页付路由既有的 live-flush 屏障（ACP 子进程独立进程一次性冷构建约 1.9 s；backward 重复 24.2 ms，文件 size/mtime 不变）——已记录的 ACP 子进程残余，非 daemon 本地缓存。 真实环境确认的残余：冷构建的一次性解析后同步段（worker 线程索引为已记录的后续项）、legacy singular 路由默认 idle timeout 下的每页子进程回收（workspace 限定路由是 Web Shell 使用的表面）。

评审：完整 high 力度 `/review`（17 agent + 2 verifier）在 base 收敛，0 Critical、两轮干跑反向审计；增量反向审计对发现一条 Suggestion（陈旧等长 build 可腾退 live 较新条目），已修复并配并发回归测试；对该修复的最终反向审计确认收敛。最新一轮分类处置复审的三条边界（两条已修、先逐出后拒收本轮修复）与 bot 评审的五条内联建议（R1-1/R1-4 修复，R1-2/R1-3 测试覆盖关闭，R1-5 复现并作为先存残余文档化、摘要修复暂缓）。再一轮复审复现两个并发 P1（等待方绕过共享构建的验证；准入前挂载的投影脱离预算）与一个投影转类 P2；三者均根因修复（共享验证完成、准入时记账、转类回收），连同 bot round-2 建议（瞬时 stat 失败、identity 分支无测试）。再下一轮复审发现 cap/stale 提前返回绕过复验；以复验先于所有返回修复，同提交含收缩方向谓词、offer 计数上限回收、夹具合并、route 级复用测试与文档修正（bot round-3）。每个修复都配回归测试与已执行的变异见证。

### 测试平台

🍏 macOS ⚠️ 未测 · 🪟 Windows ⚠️ 未测 · 🐧 Linux ✅ 已测。

### 环境

Node v26.12.1、vitest 3.2.7、tsx 源码级探针。daemon E2E 验证见验证评论。与最新 `origin/main` 的合并树上全量 build + bundle + core typecheck。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：每进程索引缓存最坏字节保留从 64 MiB 升至 320 MiB（估算口径；独立堆探针实测真实堆 ≈ 0.63× 估算——30k 记录探针上 heapDelta/estimate = 0.632——故 320 MiB 估算对应约 202 MiB 真实堆）。保留仍受两类预算、5 分钟 TTL、LRU 驱逐约束；小会话保留不变。Managed 投影与 hook 聚合按加入后条目所属预算类记账；保留正文使条目跨过共享预算时移入超大类，合并条目放不下时丢弃保留。一条低置信评审发现（超大预算与实验性 `--child-heap-mode enforce` 512 MiB 下限的协调）留给维护者堆策略讨论（该下限非默认；默认 observe 不施加任何限制）。
- 缓存之外的行为变化：文件被等长原地改写且 mtime 前进时，冻结游标或快照现在返回 `transcript_snapshot_unavailable`——与 turn-index 路径已有的校验一致。纯追加保持冻结前缀可读。这也关闭了小缓存索引上同样存在的旧快照洞。共享索引构建的并发请求现在共享其经验证的完成：快照在构建期间被改写或替换时，所有共享者收到 `transcript_snapshot_unavailable`（此前等待方可能拿到撕裂的构建结果）；构建后复验的瞬时 stat 错误（EMFILE/EIO/EACCES）不缓存返回已构建快照，而非 500。复验先于所有提前完成返回（超限拒绝、陈旧完成），除该已记录的尽力路径外不返回未验证的构建结果。被取代快照回收覆盖两个大小方向与 offer 门计数上限。
- 未验证/超出范围：保留 uuid 的等长原地改写后再追加不会被检出（先于本 PR 存在；此处新增的等长守卫因文件变长而看不到它，且页正文按冻结偏移活读、缓存命中亦然）——冻结前缀摘要校验已中英双语列为后续工作。legacy singular 路由在默认 `--channel-idle-timeout-ms 0` 下仍每页回收 ACP 子进程、丢弃其进程内缓存（`docs/users/qwen-serve.md` 已记载；缓解：正 idle timeout）——daemon 本地的 workspace 限定路由与长活子进程直接受益。冷缓存首次读取仍付一次性全量解析；追加使冻结键失效，较新快照在回收后放得下时通过腾退同文件被取代前缀获得准入（增量尾部扩展仍是后续项）。索引估算超过 256 MiB 的会话（稠密短记录可在远低于 256 MiB 文件上限处触达）仍逐页重建——常量注释已写明该悬崖。32 条目计数上限仍全局共享，超大条目可占用 warm 小索引的槽位（类预算至多容纳三个超大条目）。
- 破坏性改动/迁移：无。缓存为进程内部；无 API、cursor、schema 变化。设计文档中英已更新：[untrusted-persisted-transcript.md](../blob/main/docs/design/untrusted-persisted-transcript.md) / [untrusted-persisted-transcript.zh-CN.md](../blob/main/docs/design/untrusted-persisted-transcript.zh-CN.md)、[hook-execution-records.md](../blob/main/docs/design/hook-execution-records.md) / [hook-execution-records.zh-CN.md](../blob/main/docs/design/hook-execution-records.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联 Issue

Part of #17889 —— daemon 本地 transcript 读取路径的逐请求全量重解析成本模型已修复；legacy singular 路由默认 idle timeout 下的每页子进程回收与增量追加扩展仍为已记录的残余/后续项，故引用但不使用关闭关键词。

</details>
