auto_merge.commit_title: fix(cli): attribute daemon log lines and bind late channel restores to the boot conflict decline (#17904)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix(cli): attribute daemon log lines with pid and port

Daemons that share one log sink were unattributable line by line: the
stderr tee carried no process identity at all, and the file log carried
pid but no port, so counter-based diagnosis across sibling daemons
required guessing which process wrote which line (#17479 B.3).

Tee lines now carry pid= and, once listening, port=; file lines gain
port= after the existing runId=/pid=. The port is late-bound through
DaemonLogger.setPort(actualPort) in onListening, so ephemeral port 0
and EADDRINUSE fallback both report the real listening port; pre-listen
records carry pid only. Caller ctx.pid (worker pid) stays rendered in
the tee alongside the daemon identity.

* fix(cli): bind late channel restores to the boot conflict decline

A daemon whose settings-derived channel selection was downgraded at boot
because another instance held the channel-service lease re-admitted those
channels as soon as a non-primary workspace registered after boot and the
holder's pidfile record disappeared (holder exit, stale sweep): the runtime
lease re-check only sees the pidfile's current state, so nothing remembered
the boot decline. The duplicate then ran side-effecting channel workers
behind the operator's back (#17479 B.2).

The registration hook now skips the late restore while the decline stands,
before consuming the workspace's once-per-run restore mark and alongside
the operator-stop sibling, so a refused workspace gets its restore back
when an explicit selection commit clears the gate and it registers again.
addChannelsToSelection keeps a defense-in-depth refusal for any other
caller. Only a successful explicit commit clears the gate; a failed one
leaves it set. The boot downgrade itself stays non-fatal best-effort:
settings-derived channels must not block daemon startup.

* fix(cli): reserve daemon log identity keys and restate the channel decline reason

Address review R1-1/R1-2 on the log-attribution and channel-gate fix.

The tee rendered caller context unfiltered, so a worker pid passed as ctx.pid
produced a second, conflicting pid= key (a last-key-wins pipeline attributed
the daemon's line to the worker), and the bare diagnostics that bypass the tee
(write/rotation/retention warnings, queue overflow) carried no identity at all.
Both renderers now strip the reserved identity keys (runId/pid/port) from caller
context, the worker pid travels as childPid, and a shared identity holder feeds
the late-bound port to every stderr line including the bare diagnostics. The
file renderer's strip and the desktop smoke parser's first-pid= read are unchanged.

The refused late restore now restates the boot decline reason (the conflicting
holder, sanitized) in the skip line and the defense-in-depth refusal, so it stays
diagnosable after the boot warn rotates out on a long-running daemon. It records
no channelRestoreFailures entry, keeping parity with the operator-stop sibling.

* fix(cli): exclude the transient channel startup race from the boot decline gate

The boot conflict gate latched on channelServiceStartingConflictError too —
the transient exclusive-create race where no holder record was ever read —
so a daemon that hit the race refused automatic restores for the rest of the
run even though no instance held the lease, and the boot message's "retry
after the current startup finishes" invited a retry the gate then refused.
Mark that error `starting` and set the gate only on a real holder conflict;
the runtime lease re-check handles the transient race instead. A real holder
record (including one this machine cannot verify) still latches the gate.

Also make the gate suite portable and load-tolerant: match the rendered
workspaceCwd form (renderCtx quotes values containing whitespace, so a TMPDIR
with a space broke five cases), and give the file an explicit 60s testTimeout
(the first case pays the cold module load and sat 2.5s under the default 15s).
Adds a transient-race case proving the gate does not latch and the restore
fires once the race clears.

* docs(users): scope the channel decline recovery and per-record log attribution

Scope the boot-decline recovery instruction to automatic restores: a successful
qwen channel set re-enables automatic restores on later registrations and a
restart re-evaluates the lease, while starting a single channel independently
runs that worker without re-enabling automatic restores. Note the transient
"already starting" race is not latched. Describe log attribution per record
header (an error's stack frames follow as continuation lines under the pid/port
header), not per physical line.

* fix(cli): latch the boot channel gate on a live holder found in the reservation retry

The F2 narrowing marked every exclusive-create EEXIST retry as the transient
"already starting" race, but a competing process can acquire the lease after the
last pre-reservation read: writeInfoExclusive then sees a live holder under the
lock and rethrows EEXIST, and the retry handler threw starting:true, so the boot
gate skipped a real holder. Once that holder released, a registering workspace
auto-started a worker — the reported lease race, reproduced with the production
pidfile. Carry the holder identity out of the locked check (channelServiceHolder
on the EEXIST) and recover it in the retry handler (re-read as fallback); only an
unidentifiable owner is the transient race. Adds a live-holder regression case
beside the transient one.

Also address review R2-1/R2-2/R2-5: unsplice the two helper doc comments; rename
the worker pid to childPid in the paired "channel worker exited" message (it kept
a second daemon-meaning pid= key) and pin both ready and exit records with a
serve-level multi-workspace test; reuse renderIdentityPrefix for the tee identity
instead of a third inline copy. Clarify the defence-in-depth comment as an
intentional, currently-redundant backstop (R2-3, kept per maintainer F3 stance).

* docs: list the boot-decline exclusion in the sibling late-restore contracts

The channels overview, the developer adapter guide, and the protocol spec's
"That restore:" list still closed their exclusions after the --channel and
DELETE /workspace/channel cases. Add the boot lease-conflict decline (latched
until an explicit commit or restart; the transient starting race is not latched)
so an operator whose flagless daemon declined its boot restore reads the same
contract everywhere (review R2-4).

prs.title: fix(agents): keep A2A tasks recoverable after transcript read errors
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Session-based A2A requests return the existing retryable JSON-RPC error `-32012` when a filesystem error prevents reply lookup in an active or archived transcript. The failing observation saves no task result. Once reads recover, the same task can report `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` with its original reply.

## Why it's needed

A transient read error could make a recorded reply appear absent and cause a completed task to be permanently saved as `TASK_STATE_FAILED`. A permissions check can still succeed when the actual read fails. The linked issue reproduces this with injected `EIO`. [Issue #13738](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/13738), [earlier proposal and review](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13797).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From `packages/cli`, run `npx --no-install vitest run --coverage.enabled=false src/serve/routes/a2a.test.ts -t 'after an EIO'`. The regression cases inject a stream read failure in each transcript location. Check that `GetTask`, `ListTasks`, `CancelTask`, and a replay of `SendMessage` return `-32012` with no internal path details and no saved task result. After restoring the stream, poll the same task with `GetTask` and check that it returns and saves `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` with the original reply. The cases also check the oversized archive and unexpected-error paths.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The local JSON-RPC daemon probe used the same recorded-reply fixtures for both versions. On installed Qwen Code 0.27.3, polling under `EIO` returned and saved `TASK_STATE_FAILED` for both transcript locations. Polling after recovery returned the same state. In the fixed bundle, polling under the same fault returned `-32012` and the task mappings contained no result. The next poll returned and saved `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` with the original reply. Healthy, missing-transcript, and mismatched-reply controls produced the expected results on both versions.

Build, bundle, typecheck, focused ESLint and Prettier checks, and the focused CLI and core suites passed. The suites ran 22 CLI tests and 391 core tests.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status        |
| :--------: | :------------ |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ tested     |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

macOS 27.0 arm64 and Node 22.18.0 for the fixed bundle. The probe used a local `serve` daemon with experimental agent collaboration enabled and synthetic on-disk fixtures.

## Risk & Scope

- An unreadable active transcript takes precedence over the archived copy because the archive may hold a stale reply. The session loaders use strict reads by opt-in, with A2A as the sole caller that enables them.
- Previously saved failures, malformed reply records, and concurrent archive restoration are outside the fix. The existing cancellation decision and receipt behavior still depend on observing the task.
- The fix uses the existing task schema, storage format, and JSON-RPC code. It requires no data migration.

[Design document (Simplified Chinese)](https://github.com/water-in-stone/qwen-code/blob/350a7e3f7a3850d4f8bdb3b8b3784c897f832537/docs/design/managed-agents/a2a-transcript-read-recovery.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13738

## Why it's needed

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

## Risk & Scope

- 活动 transcript 无法读取时优先报告该故障，因为归档副本里的回复可能已过时。加载器以显式启用的方式使用严格读取，只有 A2A 调用方启用。
- 之前已保存的失败、损坏的回复记录和并发归档还原超出本次修复范围。现有的取消决策和回执仍依赖于观测任务。
- 修复沿用现有任务数据结构、存储格式和 JSON-RPC 错误码，无需数据迁移。

prs.title: fix(sdk): preserve notification envelope session scope
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Preserve the envelope’s session identity when converting legacy session updates and generic notifications with nested object payloads. Session subscribers continue to receive workspace events.

## Why it's needed

The WebSocket transport multiplexes several sessions on one connection. Legacy and generic notification envelopes could carry the session ID outside their data object, but conversion discarded that ID. The resulting event looked workspace-scoped and was delivered to subscribers for unrelated sessions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Subscribe through the public WebSocket transport, send a notification for another session with its session ID in the envelope, then send a workspace marker. The subscriber must receive the workspace marker first. Exercise legacy session/update, both type- and kind-tagged _qwen/notify, and the current update shape.

### Evidence (Before & After)

On unchanged base, 3 cases fail and the current-format control passes. After the fix, all 4 protocol regressions and 20 existing denormalizer tests pass: 24 passed.

No visual layout change; screenshots are not applicable.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Focused tests passed |

### Environment

Linux, Node.js 24.22.3 and Vitest 1.6.0. Tests use the public transport with a controlled WebSocket implementation; no network server is started. ESLint and Prettier passed. A strict closure typecheck was attempted but blocked by unavailable workspace type exports and resulting existing daemon/event diagnostics; it is not marked passed. Full repository preflight was not run.

## Risk & Scope

For valid object payloads, an explicit envelope sessionId has the same precedence as in the existing current-format path. Unscoped workspace notifications and their payload shapes are preserved. This does not change server-side authorization.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17996.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

转换旧式会话更新和带嵌套对象载荷的通用通知时，保留外层消息的会话身份；会话订阅仍接收工作区事件。

## 修改原因

WebSocket 在一个连接上复用多个会话。旧式和通用通知可将 sessionId 放在 data 对象之外，但转换时丢失该标识，导致事件被误认为工作区级别并广播到其他会话订阅。

## 审阅验证计划

### 验证方式

通过公开 WebSocket 传输订阅一个会话，发送外层携带另一个会话 ID 的通知，再发送工作区标记。订阅首先收到的必须是工作区标记。覆盖旧式 session/update、type 和 kind 两种 _qwen/notify，以及当前 update 格式。

Linux、Node.js 24.22.3、Vitest 1.6.0。公开传输使用可控 WebSocket 实现，未启动网络服务器。ESLint、Prettier 通过。已尝试严格闭包类型检查，但缺少工作区类型导出并产生既有 daemon/event 诊断，因此未标记通过。未运行完整仓库 preflight。

prs.title: fix(sdk): handle asynchronous stdin failures
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Handle asynchronous child-input errors, stop accepting writes and terminate the failed transport. Preserve the original write failure when the child subsequently exits.

Fixes #17658.

## Why it's needed

Node Writable streams report many write failures through a later error event rather than a synchronous throw. The transport only caught synchronous exceptions, so EPIPE could escape as an uncaught exception. It could also leave the transport marked ready after its input pipe had failed.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Exercise the real ProcessTransport with a controlled child and actual Node Writable streams. Deliver an unhandled-style error event, fail a write callback asynchronously, and emit a late error after explicit shutdown. Require the original cause to reach waitForExit, one termination request and no unexpected failure during deliberate cleanup.

### Evidence (Before & After)

On unchanged base, all 3 new regressions fail. After the fix, the new regressions and existing ProcessTransport suite pass all 125 tests.

No visual layout change; screenshots are not applicable.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Focused tests passed |

### Environment

Linux, Node.js 24.22.3 and Vitest 1.6.0. Child-process creation is controlled; the asynchronous write failure uses a real Node Writable callback. ESLint, Prettier and strict TypeScript checking of the changed source/tests and their import closure passed. No real CLI process, full workspace build/typecheck/preflight, macOS or Windows run is claimed.

## Risk & Scope

The first non-abort transport failure is retained instead of being overwritten by the later process exit. Errors emitted after explicit close are consumed as teardown events. Existing SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL escalation remains unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17658.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本次修改

处理子进程输入流异步错误，停止接受写入并终止失效传输；子进程随后退出时保留最初的写入失败。

## 修改原因

Node Writable 的许多写入失败通过稍后的 error 事件报告，而不是同步抛出。此前传输仅捕获同步异常，EPIPE 可能成为未捕获异常，输入管道失效后传输也仍显示可写。

## 审阅验证计划

### 验证方式

使用真实 ProcessTransport、可控子进程和 Node Writable，分别触发 error 事件、异步写入回调失败及显式关闭后的迟到错误。验证 waitForExit 保留原始原因、请求终止进程、正常清理不制造额外失败。

### 修复前后证据

未修改基线的 3 项新回归全部失败；修复后，新回归和既有 ProcessTransport 测试共 125 项通过。

不改变视觉布局，截图不适用。

### 测试平台

| 系统 | 状态 |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | 未测试 |
| Windows | 未测试 |
| Linux | 针对性测试通过 |

### 环境

Linux、Node.js 24.22.3、Vitest 1.6.0。子进程创建由测试控制，异步写入失败由真实 Node Writable 回调产生。ESLint、Prettier、变更源码和测试及导入闭包的严格 TypeScript 检查通过。未运行真实 CLI 进程、完整工作区 build/typecheck/preflight、macOS 或 Windows。

## 风险与范围

保留首次非中止传输失败，不再被后续进程退出覆盖。显式关闭后发出的错误作为清理事件接管；SIGTERM 到 SIGKILL 的既有升级行为保持。

## 关联问题

修复 #17658。

prs.title: fix(sdk): propagate prompt input failures to query consumers
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Reject the result iterator with the original input failure and close the query transport when a prompt generator or prompt write fails. Apply the same failure handling to single-turn and streamed prompts.

## Why it's needed

A prompt generator can fail after yielding an input, and a transport can fail while writing a prompt. The query factory previously logged these failures while leaving the result iterator waiting and the transport open. Callers consuming the query had no reliable way to observe the failure or finish cleanup.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Call the public query factory with an async source that yields and then throws, a stream whose prompt write fails, and a single string whose prompt write fails. The controlled protocol transport acknowledges initialization and otherwise waits for input. In all three cases require the result iterator to reject with the exact original error and the transport to close. Single-turn input still closes normally when its result arrives.

### Evidence (Before & After)

On unchanged base, all 3 new regressions fail because the result consumer remains pending. After the fix, the new regressions, existing Query tests and existing factory tests pass: 90 passed in total.

No visual layout change; screenshots are not applicable.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Focused tests passed |

### Environment

Linux, Node.js 24.22.3 and Vitest 1.6.0. The public query factory and real Query implementation run against a controlled ProcessTransport substitute; this is not a real subprocess E2E. ESLint and Prettier passed. Strict TypeScript checking passed for the changed source, new and existing factory tests, and their import closure. Full workspace build/typecheck/preflight was not run.

## Risk & Scope

Input errors now end the result stream and close the query instead of remaining log-only failures. Cleanup failures are logged without replacing the original input error. Abort handling and result-triggered single-turn EOF retain their existing behavior.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17993.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本次修改

提示生成器或提示写入失败时，让结果迭代器抛出原始错误并关闭查询传输。单轮和流式提示使用一致的失败处理。

## 修改原因

提示生成器可能在发送部分输入后失败，传输也可能在写入提示时抛错。此前查询工厂只记录错误，结果迭代器继续等待，传输继续打开；调用方无法可靠获知失败并完成资源清理。

## 审阅验证计划

### 验证方式

使用公开 query 工厂分别构造：先 yield 后抛错的异步输入源、写入失败的流式提示、写入失败的字符串提示。可控协议传输确认初始化后等待输入。三种情况均要求结果迭代器抛出同一个原始错误并关闭传输；正常单轮输入仍在结果到达时结束。

### 修复前后证据

prs.title: fix(sdk): preserve completed bridge prompt outcomes
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Keep a completed bridge prompt’s response and completion status stable when later events, cancellation or stream cleanup arrive. Unfinished prompts still resolve as interrupted on disconnection.

## Why it's needed

The event stream can deliver a final answer before the prompt request finishes acknowledging. During that interval, the collector remains attached to the stream. Later text could be appended to the answer, and stream termination or a late cancellation could change an already successful answer into an interrupted response.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Feed a final answer through the real bridge event consumer, then deliver unrelated text, EOF, an error event, stream cleanup or a late prompt_cancel call. Require the original answer and successful status to remain intact. Also verify that an unfinished collector still becomes interrupted on EOF.

### Evidence (Before & After)

On unchanged base, the six new regressions produce 5 failed and 1 passed. After the fix, the six regressions and 47 existing serve-bridge tests pass: 53 passed in total.

No visual layout change; screenshots are not applicable.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Focused tests passed |

### Environment

Linux, Node.js 24.22.3, Vitest 1.6.0, Zod 4.6.6 and MCP SDK 1.32.2. Tests exercise the real bridge event consumer and cancellation handler with a controlled event source. Local source aliases load the three existing bridge constants. ESLint and Prettier passed. Full workspace build/typecheck/preflight and live daemon/model E2E were not run.

## Risk & Scope

The first terminal outcome now wins. A late cancellation still sends the existing daemon cancellation request, but cannot rewrite an already completed local answer. This does not add retries or change server cancellation behavior.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17991.

## What this PR does

Exclude active prompt collectors from idle stream cleanup and restart the idle clock when a prompt settles. Genuinely idle streams keep the existing timeout and cleanup cadence.

## Why it's needed

A long-running prompt can remain quiet while a tool or provider is working. The cleanup timer previously treated 30 minutes without text as inactivity, aborted the stream and returned an interrupted response even though the prompt was still active.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Advance a controlled clock by 35 minutes with an active quiet prompt and require its stream to remain open. Verify idle streams still expire. Complete a delayed prompt through the real tool handler, then require a fresh idle interval before cleanup.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| OS | Status |

Snapshot the subscribers at the start of a notification and retain the existing check that skips listeners removed before their turn. A callback can rebuild its subscription without being revisited during the same notification.

prs.title: fix(sdk): wait for shared peer endpoint cleanup
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Retain one cleanup promise for the peer endpoint. Concurrent and later close calls wait for the same inbox and registry cleanup and observe the same result.

## Why it's needed

A second close caller previously returned as soon as the endpoint was marked closed, while the first caller was still removing its socket and session record. Callers could proceed with shutdown or replacement before cleanup completed, and later callers could miss a cleanup failure.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Hold inbox cleanup, call close twice and verify neither caller finishes. Release the inbox while holding registry cleanup and verify both remain pending. Complete removal, then check that cleanup ran once. Repeat with a rejected inbox cleanup and require the same failure for concurrent and later callers.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Both new lifecycle regressions fail on unchanged base and pass after the change. TypeScript checks for the changed source, tests and imported source closure passed, as did repository ESLint and Prettier.

No visual layout change; screenshots are not applicable.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Focused tests passed |

### Environment

Linux, Node.js 24.22.3 and Vitest 1.6.0 with controlled deferred I/O. Native Unix-socket binding is blocked in this environment (listen EPERM); no native socket E2E or full repository preflight is claimed.

## Risk & Scope

A failed close remains observable to later callers; cleanup is not restarted. The existing synchronous process-exit path remains separate. The regression replaces only OS inbox/registry I/O, retaining the public endpoint lifecycle.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17985.

prs.title: fix(sdk): reset replay cursors when the event epoch changes
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Reset the tracked replay cursor to zero when a known event-bus epoch changes, then advance it using events from the new epoch. A reconnect after an empty new-epoch stream also requests replay from zero.

## Why it's needed

After a daemon restart, event numbers can restart below a previously saved cursor. Keeping the old high number alongside the new epoch can skip events on later reconnects.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Seed epoch old with cursor 100. Return epoch new with event 2, consume the stream and reconnect; the request must carry cursor 2. Repeat with an empty new-epoch stream and require cursor zero. Unchanged and previously unknown epochs keep their existing cursor behavior.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The four new REST/SSE regressions fail twice on unchanged base (2 failed, 2 passed) and pass after the fix. Together with the existing session-client suite, 131 tests pass.

No visual layout change; screenshots are not applicable.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Focused tests passed |

### Environment

The real session client and REST/SSE transport run with controlled fetch responses. A local verification configuration maps three existing bridge runtime imports to their source files because workspace build artifacts are unavailable. ESLint and Prettier passed; full workspace typecheck/build/preflight and live daemon/model E2E were not run.

## Risk & Scope

Only a transition between two known, different epochs resets the cursor. A daemon that never supplied an epoch retains the legacy behavior. Event acknowledgement timing within one stream is unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17983.

## 修改原因

守护进程重启后，事件编号可能低于旧游标。将旧的较大编号与新 epoch 配对，会让后续重连遗漏事件。

## 审阅验证计划

### 验证方式

用旧 epoch 和游标 100 初始化，接收新 epoch 的事件 2，完整消费后重连并验证发送游标 2。再测试新 epoch 空流，验证发送游标 0；epoch 未变或之前未知时保持原有行为。

prs.title: test(managed-agent): use canonical schema initializer
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The restart-with-receipts test now uses the same schema initializer as the production path instead of maintaining a separate SQL splitter. The independent helper and its now-unused import are removed. No production code, schema, public API, assertion count, or test case is changed, and the precise index-column assertion remains intact.

The PR also adds a narrowly scoped SpotBugs baseline for a nullable blob-load branch whose existing fail-closed guard makes the reported dereference unreachable. The exclusion is limited to one class, one method, and one warning pattern, and retains all production validation; it does not disable SpotBugs globally or skip SQL tests.

## Why it's needed

The test's previous helper split the complete SQL resource at every semicolon, including a semicolon inside a quoted SQL comment. The first full MySQL gate after #17795 consequently failed before completing schema initialization. Reusing the production initializer exercises the parser that already handles SQL quoting, comments, and parentheses correctly and prevents the test helper from drifting from the real initialization semantics.

After that helper was fixed, the new full MySQL gate stopped during static analysis before executing the MySQL suites. The finding points to a blob-load path followed by a guard that throws `ContractViolationException` whenever the value is missing or is not a byte array. The cast and length access therefore cannot receive null on that path. Recording only this demonstrated analyzer limitation lets the genuine MySQL gate run without changing production behavior, hiding an actual null dereference, or granting a broad warning exemption.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Check that the test initializes through the production parser, the precise analyzer exclusion is limited to the guarded blob-load method, and all existing receipt, namespace rejection, model constraint, schema-version, and exact index-column checks remain unchanged. Confirm that the guard throws on an invalid or missing byte array before the cast and length access.
2. With JDK 21, install the sibling SDK and managed-agent modules into a task-local Maven repository and run `mvn -pl persistence -am -DskipTests -DskipITs -Dgpg.skip=true -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true -Dspotbugs.skip=false clean verify checkstyle:check checkstyle:check@runtime-broker-checkstyle`, using a private Maven repository and the module POM. Expect successful parent, contracts, and persistence modules, with SpotBugs explicitly enabled, `BugInstance size is 0`, `Error size is 0`, and zero Checkstyle violations.
3. Supply two disposable MySQL 8.4.6 instances, test-only credentials, and their JDBC URLs for the two-fork configuration.
4. Run `mvn -pl verification -Pmysql-integration -Dmysql.integration.forks=2 -Dit.test=WorkspaceCreationSchemaMySqlIT,ManagedWorkspaceArtifactMySqlIT -DfailIfNoTests=true -DfailIfNoSpecifiedTests=true failsafe:integration-test failsafe:verify checkstyle:check checkstyle:check@runtime-broker-checkstyle` with the corresponding MySQL system properties from the module directory.
5. Expect 19 tests with no failures, errors, or skips, and zero Checkstyle violations. Do not treat skipped test execution or a global `-Dspotbugs.skip=true` as proof that the static gate passes.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-UI change: N/A.

Real MySQL A/B at the #17795 squash merge used the same selected suites and two-container/two-fork topology. The previous helper produced the same SQL syntax error at the quoted `Active range identity; ...` comment: one error among 19 selected tests. The corrected helper passed all 19 tests.

The initial one-file SQL-helper commit `338a0c9d18`, based on `4947118326977307e358ec8ac669ba28247f8a36`, was rebuilt and verified independently with JDK 21.0.9 and two fresh MySQL 8.4.6 containers: `WorkspaceCreationSchemaMySqlIT` passed 4/4 and `ManagedWorkspaceArtifactMySqlIT` passed 15/15; total 19/19, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. Both requested Checkstyle goals reported zero violations, Maven exited 0, and both task-owned containers were removed. The reports are in `verification/target/failsafe-reports`; the retained execution log is `/tmp/qwen-schema-restart-verified.log` on the author's machine. These test inputs are unchanged by the analyzer configuration update.

Second-run #17795 full-MySQL evidence also repeats the two original failures: 4 schema tests with 1 SQL-splitting error and 15 artifact tests with 1 failure listing every expected index column twice. The old helper's failure is directly covered by this PR, while duplicate metadata has not been reattributed to the helper, hidden by deduplication, or declared fixed by the local 15/15 pass.

For the subsequent blocker, actual PR CI [job 136180713575](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44704460186/job/136180713575) stopped in SpotBugs at the guarded receipt-load branch, with `failed with 1 bugs and 0 errors`. It did not run the MySQL suite or produce a MySQL test report. This is not being relabeled as a SQL failure, a successful test run, or evidence that all production code has a null dereference.

The actual guard is fail-closed: `ToolPublicationContract.require` unconditionally throws on a false condition. The source checks `raw instanceof byte[]`, then casts and reads the length only if the guard returns, so the null path is unreachable. The baseline narrowly matches that guarded read rather than excluding a whole class, analyzer, or Maven phase. The repository already has a documented, class/method/pattern-scoped false-positive baseline mechanism; this change uses that mechanism rather than adding an annotation dependency, production cast helper, or error-contract change.

The current analyzer change was locally verified using JDK 21.0.9 and `/tmp/qwen-schema-restart-wNoitv/m2`, with SpotBugs explicitly enabled via `-Dspotbugs.skip=false`. The selected three-module `verify`/Checkstyle invocation used `-DskipTests -DskipITs` to focus on compilation and static analysis, not to suppress SpotBugs. The actual selected three-module reactor (parent, contracts, persistence) completed `BUILD SUCCESS` in 01:20. For persistence, the output contains `BugInstance size is 0`, `Error size is 0`, and `No errors/warnings found`; the two Checkstyle goals passed for all three selected modules. The retained log is `/tmp/qwen-pr17921-spotbugs-verification.log`. This is targeted static-analysis evidence, not a claim that the full repo, complete Maven profile, MySQL matrix, or every platform has passed.

A preceding dependency-install attempt encountered the same upstream `ToolPublicationAdmissionStore` finding before any selected test ran. Only that preparation phase skipped analysis; the subsequent 19 selected MySQL tests and Checkstyle ran normally. This temporary phase-specific setup is not the evidence relied upon for the new narrow exclusion.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: The PR aligns test initialization with the production parser and adds a narrowly scoped exception for a warning whose dereference is already unreachable after a fail-closed guard. It does not modify production behavior, suppress an entire module or analyzer, or widen the existing four-column index contract.
- Not validated / out of scope: The local 15/15 artifact-suite pass does not identify or fix the separately reproduced duplicate index metadata observation; its exact four-column assertion is unchanged. The DingTalk worker RPC failure and the separate Hosted reliable-close investigation are unrelated to this focused fix and have not been claimed as resolved.

prs.title: refactor(managed-agent-server): retire the receipt-catalog SpotBugs exclusion with an analyzer-visible assertion
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Retires the scoped SpotBugs baseline entry that #17921 added for `ToolPublicationAdmissionStore.acknowledgementReceiptCatalog`, replacing it with an analyzer-visible assertion at the guarded cast:

- `require(raw instanceof byte[], "Original receipt bytes are missing")` stays first — the type check and the `ContractViolationException` (HTTP 400) mapping are unchanged.
- The cast becomes `(byte[]) Objects.requireNonNull(raw, "Original receipt bytes are missing")` — visible to SpotBugs, unreachable at runtime (the `require` throws on null first); a two-line comment marks it so it is not "simplified" away.
- The `acknowledgementReceiptCatalog` / `NP_NULL_ON_SOME_PATH` `<Match>` and its rationale comment are removed from `spotbugs-excludes.xml`. The two older entries (`replay`, `rebuildBatch`) are untouched; `replay`'s retirement is tracked in #17931.

Net diff vs main: `ToolPublicationAdmissionStore.java` +3/−1, `spotbugs-excludes.xml` −12.

## Why it's needed

#17864/#17907 introduced the High `NP_NULL_ON_SOME_PATH` (dereference :180, known null :174) because SpotBugs cannot see through the fail-closed `require` helper. #17921 unblocked main's full-tier MySQL lane quickly with a narrowly scoped exclusion. The exclude-file header asks that the gate stay at zero findings **without growing the baseline**; the analyzer-visible assertion achieves the same zero with one fewer entry, and keeps the guard's runtime semantics identical. This is the same idiom the maintainer review of this PR's earlier revision already verified at code level.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

With JDK 21, from `packages/managed-agent-server`: `mvn -pl persistence -am -DskipTests verify` → `spotbugs:check` reports `BugInstance size is 0` with no baseline entry for this method, Checkstyle clean. Removing the `Objects.requireNonNull` line (keeping the entry removed) brings back the single High `NP_NULL_ON_SOME_PATH` — measured. `mvn -pl verification -am test -Dtest=ToolPublicationStoreTest` exercises the enclosing class (including `replay()`) on H2.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-observable behavior change. Local arms (JDK 21, `threshold=High`, shared exclude filter, task-local repository), on the merged current-main tree:

- main state (entry present, no assertion): `BugInstance size is 0`;
- this PR (assertion, entry removed): `BugInstance size is 0`, Checkstyle 0, BUILD SUCCESS;
- negative control (neither): `Total bugs: 1` — the High `NP_NULL_ON_SOME_PATH`, BUILD FAILURE (exit 1).

H2 `ToolPublicationStoreTest`: **113/113 green** on the merged tree.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  N/A   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

JDK 21.0.9 + Maven 3.9.11 task-local repository; spotbugs-maven-plugin 4.10.4.1 with the pom's `threshold=High`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none at runtime — the assertion never fires (`require` precedes it); the comment guards against its removal. The guard's exception-type regression test remains tracked in #17924 (the verification path has no production callers yet).
- Not validated / out of scope: the full reactor `verify` and the MySQL integration profile are left to CI. The fast-tier `RuntimeProviderPluginsTest` red on current main is a separately attributed #17949 regression (fix PR in progress), unrelated to this diff.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

References #17864 and #17907 (introduced the finding), #17921 (added the entry this PR retires), #17924 and #17931 (follow-ups). No closing keywords.

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): runtime-owned background observation (Phase 3b slice 1 + staging schema)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR implements the first slice and the staging schema foundation of Phase 3b, "Managed Runtime-owned background observation", whose design landed in #17912. Today a background Shell or Monitor watch keeps its running output digest inside the Harness process, so a Harness restart loses the capture and reports `producer_lost`, and a Session with live background work cannot suspend. This change moves the background capture into the worker: the worker builds the same `managed-tool-result/1` segments, pages and manifest revisions, runs the Monitor policy (line splitting, debounce windows, idle timeout and observation quota), and turns everything that must become durable into ordered, numbered delivery entries that carry the complete resources they introduce. While a Harness is attached the worker pushes entries to a resident applier that publishes the resources and commits the record idempotently; a failed push switches the run to a held mode that retains the entries instead of failing the capture, and a newer Harness replaces the publisher by writer generation rather than being refused. The Broker publisher-install path now carries the writer generation to the worker and the worker's observation-ownership signal back to the Harness, so the Harness skips its own observation loop when the worker owns it. The commit closure also walks a drained manifest's pages server-side, and a new `ma_runtime_stage` ledger table plus a `RUNTIME_STAGE` resource owner kind are introduced for the Broker staging that the next slice builds on. The whole worker-owned lane is gated by a worker capability that is off by default, so the existing foreground and background behavior is unchanged until it is explicitly enabled.

## Why it's needed

Background work should outlive the Harness that started it. Keeping the capture's running digest in the worker means a Harness restart continues the same capture instead of reporting `producer_lost`, which is the prerequisite for suspending a Session that still has live background shells or monitors (the goal of #17453). The delivery-entry contract makes retransmission idempotent at every level and keeps the worker's memory bounded with pipe backpressure, while a forced stop always produces its exit proof. This PR lands the resident mechanism and its characterization, plus the staging schema, without changing default production behavior.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The worker-owned capture must produce the same observable content as the Harness capture, and the legacy lanes must be unchanged when the capability is off.

- Capture equivalence: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/managed-runtime/local-shell-stream-capture.equivalence.test.ts` — identical input through the worker option set (256 KiB segments, 1024 per page) and the Harness set (1 MiB, 512) yields equal per-stream digest/byteLength/state and execution status, and byte-identical reconstructable output, while the worker segments strictly more finely. Covers a multi-MiB stream crossing several Harness segments, a UTF-8 character split across chunks, an empty stream and a single partial segment.
- Delivery and held-mode continuation: `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/managed-background-delivery.test.ts` — output/terminal entries settle the record, re-delivery is idempotent, the Monitor policy's observation is committed exactly once, an older writer generation is refused, and a capture with no attached publisher stays held (entries retained, not lost) and resumes on registration with the same identity.
- Legacy lanes unchanged: `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/managed-shell-publisher.test.ts src/serve/hosted-shell-publisher.test.ts src/serve/hosted-shell-publisher.background.test.ts src/serve/managed-monitor-runtime.test.ts` and `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/managed-runtime/local-shell-stream-capture.test.ts src/managed-runtime/http-managed-session-store.test.ts`.
- Java forwarding and schema: in `packages/managed-agent-server`, `mvn -pl verification -am -Dtest=HttpRuntimeTransportTest,WorkspaceRuntimeTest,RuntimeBrokerHttpServerTest,UnknownExecutionObservationTest,ManagedSchemaTest test` (an isolated local repository with the sibling `qwencode-sdk` installed via `-Dgpg.skip=true`), then the CI-equivalent `mvn checkstyle:check checkstyle:check@runtime-broker-checkstyle`.

Local results: core equivalence 2/2; cli delivery 5/5; foreground publisher 54/54; background publisher 26/26; monitor runtime 7/7; core capture 13/13; HTTP store 246/246; cli `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors. Java: `HttpRuntimeTransportTest` 86 (including a new test proving the writer generation reaches the worker request body and the observation signal is returned), `WorkspaceRuntimeTest` 54, `RuntimeBrokerHttpServerTest` 40, `UnknownExecutionObservationTest` 3, `ManagedSchemaTest` 27, all 0 failures; full reactor `test-compile` green; dual Checkstyle green.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible/TUI change; the worker-owned lane is gated off by default.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests via vitest (core/cli) and Maven (managed-agent-server, isolated local repository, JDK 21). No real-daemon E2E in this PR.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the worker-owned capture and the registration-chain changes are gated by a worker capability that is off by default (`QWEN_MANAGED_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION`), so default production behavior is unchanged; the characterization tests pin content equivalence before the gate is flipped.
- Not validated / out of scope: the rest of Slice 2 (the Broker staging transaction, the `observation-pull` transport and single-puller claim, the wake-hint fence, re-attach-then-drain, execution-row settlement and staging cleanup on delete), Slice 3 (background suspension eligibility, the seal certificate, probe-only release, detach with final acknowledgement, the reclamation guard and rollout gates), and Slice 4 (the real-process and MySQL 8.4 acceptance matrix and measurement). A real-process Harness kill+reload test across a fresh applier needs the Slice 2 drain watermark sync. The remaining work is tracked in the bilingual implementation plan under `docs/plans/`.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none while gated off. The schema adds a table and a resource owner kind; the publisher-install transport signature gains an optional writer generation and returns the worker response fields (all implementors, callers and test mocks updated).

Design document: [`docs/design/2026-11-19-managed-runtime-owned-observation.md`](docs/design/2026-11-19-managed-runtime-owned-observation.md) and [`docs/design/2026-11-19-managed-runtime-owned-observation.zh-CN.md`](docs/design/2026-11-19-managed-runtime-owned-observation.zh-CN.md). Implementation plan: [`docs/plans/2026-11-20-managed-runtime-owned-observation-implementation.md`](docs/plans/2026-11-20-managed-runtime-owned-observation-implementation.md) and [`.zh-CN.md`](docs/plans/2026-11-20-managed-runtime-owned-observation-implementation.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

References #17912 (design). Part of #17453.

prs.title: test(channels): make four managed DingTalk witnesses exclude what they claim
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Strengthens four managed DingTalk witnesses that passed for the wrong reason, and adds one that drives a delivery shape no existing case could reach. Test-only: no production behaviour changes.

## Why it's needed

These are the last four open items from the round-12 fix-audit of #17136, tracked in #17173. Each of the four assertions was satisfied by the very defect it was meant to exclude:

- **"drops a deterministically refused admission visibly"** asserted the claim was gone and never re-driven, but never read a log line. A silent drop passes it — the word "visibly" was untested.
- **"uses the newest webhook learned from a later inbound message"** pushed one frame into an empty cache. A first-wins cache passes that too; there was no earlier webhook to beat.
- **"drops a group frame under the private-chat policy"** discarded the handler's return value. A frame left unacked — redelivered forever — also satisfies "nothing was submitted".
- **Every multi-segment failure case** set a single failure flag up front, so segment 0 died and the partial-delivery shape was never reached.

The census behind this PR: of the 16 new R12 items, **12 are already landed** on main — the five production ones (pollInterval diagnostic, group-frame cache gating, the non-text drop log, the refusal latch, the removed dead `robotCode`) and seven test ones landed with the earlier batches and with #17691 / #17773. These four were the remainder, all in one file.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the DingTalk channel suite from `packages/channels/dingtalk` (`npx vitest run`): **1106 tests pass**, one more than before.

Each strengthening is pinned by the defect it excludes, applied to the production file and reverted:

| Mutation | Reds |
| --- | --- |
| the refused-admission drop goes silent | the "visibly" case |
| a transient send failure settles `rejected` instead of `unknown` | the new later-segment case |
| the webhook cache becomes first-wins | the newest-webhook case |
| a skipped frame is left unacked | the group-frame case |

The new case drives a three-segment reply whose **second** segment fails transiently. It pins the shape the ledger depends on: the delivered prefix keeps its own per-ordinal `accepted` receipt, and the failure settles the delivery `unknown` with no ordinal, so the tail stays re-drivable instead of the whole reply being recorded as never sent. It reaches that shape through the existing `beforeSend` hook — which runs after the send is recorded and before the failure check — so no harness change was needed.

Two expectations were corrected against the code rather than assumed: the refusal log names the platform event id (`dingtalk:msg-poison`), and a skipped frame is acked because `onMessage` returns true after staging regardless of whether a claim was staged.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no UI surface and no production behaviour change.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

## Risk & Scope

- Test-only. No production file is touched, so there is no behaviour, configuration, wire-format or persisted-state change.
- The four existing cases were **strengthened, not weakened**: every assertion they already made is still made.
- Not validated / out of scope: the four R12 items that merely restate earlier tracked entries are left as they are, and the legacy channel's connect-path hang stays with its own entry on #17173.

## Linked Issues

References #17173 — closes the four remaining new items from the round-12 fix-audit of #17136. Does not close the tracker.

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A——无 UI 面，也无生产行为变化。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

## 风险与范围

- 纯测试。不碰任何生产文件，因此没有行为、配置、线上格式或持久化状态变化。
- 四条既有用例是**加强而非削弱**：它们原有的每条断言都仍然在做。
- 未验证／范围外：R12 里仅重述既有条目的四条保持原样；legacy 频道连接路径的挂死仍留在 #17173 它自己的条目下。

prs.title: fix(core): correct usage token accounting across the dashboard and /stats
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Token usage in the daemon status dashboard and in the cross-session statistics view now comes from the per-request usage ledger, placed on the local day each response actually happened, instead of from session summaries that carry a resumed conversation's replayed history and attribute all of it to the day the session last ran. A session record is dropped whenever its run's day span touches any ledger-covered day, so the same requests are never counted twice; a run with no ledger overlap at all keeps the previous attribution. The span rule deliberately accepts undercounting an unseparable part of a mixed-coverage run rather than double counting it. Reasoning tokens are counted once in the output breakdown, so input plus output equals the reported total. What a run persists is now only what that run itself spent, including when an interactive session resumes another conversation, and the read side keeps every run instead of collapsing them to the last one. Session counts, duration, tool calls, changed lines, skills and the per-project breakdown still come from session records over the same whole-day window, which the ledger deliberately does not carry.

## Why it's needed

On one real heavy history the dashboard reported roughly twice the tokens actually consumed for the current day, five times for seven days and seven times for thirty days; the cross-session view was 2.06x over seven days and 6.25x over thirty days, with average latency inflated too because the request denominator was inflated. Two causes dominated. A resume replays the stored conversation's telemetry into the live metrics, and those cumulative counters were then persisted as if the current run had spent them — a seven-minute resume of a long conversation was billed 45.7M tokens across 506 requests, and every further resume appended another full copy. And every token was attributed to the day the session ended, so a session that ran across three days landed entirely on one day: one session contributed 335M tokens to "today" while only 1.07M of them were actually spent that day. Separately, the output tile added reasoning tokens that chat-completions providers already include in their output count, so the breakdown did not sum to the hero total.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open the daemon status Usage tab and toggle Today / 7D / 30D. The token totals, request count, input, cached and reasoning counters should equal an independent scan of the per-request ledger for the same window, and input plus output should equal the hero total. Each covered day's heatmap cell should equal that day's ledger tokens. Then open the cross-session statistics view, move to the Activity and Efficiency tabs, and cycle the range with `r`: the token total, session-independent counters, cache hit rate, average latency and per-model request counts should match the same ledger scan, and the period-over-period delta should compare two ledger-backed windows rather than a ledger-backed present against a record-backed past. To check the persist side, resume a long conversation and quit without sending anything: no usage record should be written. Run two turns of the same conversation in separate processes: both runs should survive a subsequent read, each carrying only its own spend. Note that the ledger lives under the runtime base directory, so when comparing against a frozen copy both the home and the runtime directory must be pinned, otherwise the UI reads the live, still-growing ledger.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Measured against an independent ledger scan on the same history. The "before" arm is the base revision's source driven directly; the "after" arm is this branch.

| Surface / window | Before | After | Ledger truth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cross-session stats, 7 days | 23,344,200,119 | 11,335,405,437 | 11,335,405,437 |
| Cross-session stats, 30 days | 253,761,756,717 | 40,624,370,019 | 40,624,370,019 |
| Dashboard output tile, today | 7,208,898 | 4,952,378 | 4,952,378 |
| Persisted record for a 400-response resume plus one live request | 401 requests / 400,000,005 input | 1 request / 5 input | 1 request / 5 input |
| Read side, two real runs of one conversation | 1 record / 30,778 tokens | 2 records / 72,818 tokens | 2 records / 72,818 tokens |

On a frozen copy of the ledger, all three dashboard windows matched the oracle exactly (`ALL_RANGES_EXACT=true`, zero day mismatches), as did the cross-session view's tokens, requests, average latency and cache hit rate.

Rendered in a real terminal from this branch's bundle (PTY capture, cross-session tabs): Activity for 7 days showed `Tokens 11492.1m` and `Sessions 28` against an oracle of 11,492,141,679; Activity for 30 days showed `Tokens 40781.1m` and `Sessions 389` against 40,781,106,261 / 389; Efficiency for today showed `Cache Hit Rate 97.2%`, `Avg Latency 5.7s` and per-model requests 943 + 108 + 21 = 1072 against 97.2% / 5,698 ms / 1,072. Two real headless runs of one conversation, the second resuming it, produced records of 3 requests / 42,040 tokens and 2 requests / 30,778 tokens — the second did not re-bill the first.

A real Chromium session against this branch's daemon now covers the previously open browser gap. With two ledger rows and deliberately matching session records, Today rendered hero `1,100`, input `1,000`, output `100` and cache `60%`; 7D rendered `3,300`, `3,000`, `300` and `60%`, with the daily-session series labelled `runs ended per day`. The route independently returned the same numbers, and the browser emitted no page errors. A separate real PTY lifecycle used only a local mock model: one 5,000-token request in A, resume B with 10,000 stored tokens, one 7-token request in B, then `/exit`. The final file contains exactly two run-scoped records, A=5,000 and B=7. The stored 10,000 never entered either record, and exit code was 0.

Every new guard is mutation-witnessed: reverting it turns the corresponding test red, and the existing history reduces byte-identically to before (2,065 raw records, both arms returning 2,043 records / 379,387,040,763 tokens with identical per-session keys).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local build and bundle, real Chromium and PTY capture, real headless and interactive CLI lifecycles against isolated temporary homes. Final focused suites: core 1160 passed, cli 161 passed, Web Shell 13 passed. The complete llm suite has 129 passes and three relaunch-provenance failures that reproduce identically on the base commit; its two exit-usage cases pass. Build, typecheck, lint and format gates are clean.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: summary windows now select whole local days, because day buckets cannot be split by hour, so the boundary day is counted in full instead of only the hours after a rolling cut-off; on the fallback path this is measurable and confined to that one day. The per-project token column stays record-derived — the ledger has no project dimension — so it now visibly disagrees with the corrected totals above it. A conversation that spans the upgrade keeps only its run deltas, so pre-upgrade activity for that id can be undercounted; undercounting an ambiguous overlap was chosen over double counting.
- Freshness and performance: every `/stats` open reparses the ledger for its selected window and the preceding comparison window; only concurrent opens share a pending read. A settled-cache shortcut cannot be used, because it hides spend from a turn completed between opens while the corresponding session record is already suppressed. The previous comparison window is shifted by whole calendar days on both boundaries so it stays disjoint and has exactly as many day buckets as the current window. Daemon requests retain their intentional 60-second source cache.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows and Linux. The session-count and per-project tiles remain incomplete for sessions that never persist a usage record — on the reference history the ledger knows 633 sessions in seven days while the record file knows far fewer — which needs a ledger-backed session census and persisting usage at session end, both left as follow-up.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. One optional record field marks run-scoped writes; every reader that filters on the record version keeps working, existing history is neither rewritten nor migrated, and the dashboard payload shape is unchanged.

Design document: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized, and they record two first-pass findings that did not survive an independent check: a claimed session-identity divergence that the ledger disproved, and a proposed "sum the segments" dedup change that would have been a 3.1x regression on existing records.

## Linked Issues

No issue to close. Builds on the per-request ledger introduced for #4479 and on the session-swap telemetry transaction from #9833.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

Daemon 状态用量面板与跨会话统计视图的 token 用量，现在取自逐请求用量台账，并落在每次响应**实际发生**的本地日上，而不再取自会话摘要——后者携带被恢复会话重放的历史，并把全部用量归到会话最后活动的那一天。一次运行的日期跨度只要触及任何台账覆盖日，其会话记录就会被丢弃，因此同一批请求不会被计两次；与台账完全不重叠的运行则沿用原有归属。对一个跨越覆盖与未覆盖状态的运行，此规则宁可少算无法安全拆分的部分，也不重复计算。输出明细中的推理 token 只计一次，因此输入加输出等于上报总量。一次运行落盘的用量现在只包含它自己花掉的部分，包括交互模式下 resume 到另一个会话的情形；读侧也会保留每一次运行，而不是收敛到最后一次。会话数、时长、工具调用、变更行数、技能以及按项目的明细仍取自同一个完整日窗口的会话记录——台账有意不携带这些。

## 为什么需要

在一份真实的重量级历史上，面板对当日报告了约两倍的实际消耗、7 天约五倍、30 天约七倍；跨会话视图 7 天为 2.06 倍、30 天为 6.25 倍，平均延迟也虚高，因为请求数这个分母被灌大了。主因有两个。其一，resume 会把已存会话的 telemetry 重放进实时指标，而这些累计计数随后被当作本次运行的消耗落盘——一次对长会话的七分钟 resume 被记为 506 个请求、45.7M token，且此后每次 resume 都再追加一份完整副本。其二，所有 token 都按会话结束日归属，于是跨三天运行的会话整体落在一天上：某会话向「今日」贡献了 335M token，而当天实际只花掉 1.07M。另外，输出 tile 还叠加了 chat-completions 类 provider 本已计入 output 的推理 token，导致明细之和不等于 hero 总量。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

打开 Daemon 状态的用量页，切换 Today / 7D / 30D。token 总量、请求数、输入、缓存与推理计数应等于对同一窗口的逐请求台账所做的独立扫描，且输入加输出应等于 hero 总量；每个被覆盖天的热力图格应等于该天的台账 token。然后打开跨会话统计视图，切到 Activity 与 Efficiency 页，用 `r` 循环区间：token 总量、与会话无关的各计数、缓存命中率、平均延迟以及逐模型请求数都应与同一次台账扫描一致，且环比应比较两个都走台账的窗口，而不是「台账口径的现在」对「记录口径的过去」。验证持久化侧：恢复一个长会话后不发送任何内容直接退出，应当不写入用量记录；在两个进程中各跑同一会话的一轮，后续读取应保留两次运行，且各自只带自己的消耗。注意台账位于运行时基目录下，因此与冻结副本对照时必须同时钉住 home 与运行时目录，否则界面读到的是仍在增长的真实台账。

### 证据（修前与修后）

以同一份历史上的独立台账扫描为准。「修前」臂直接驱动基线版本的源码，「修后」臂为本分支。

| 表面 / 窗口 | 修前 | 修后 | 台账真值 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 跨会话统计，7 天 | 23,344,200,119 | 11,335,405,437 | 11,335,405,437 |
| 跨会话统计，30 天 | 253,761,756,717 | 40,624,370,019 | 40,624,370,019 |
| 面板输出 tile，今日 | 7,208,898 | 4,952,378 | 4,952,378 |
| 400 条历史响应的 resume 加一次真实请求的落盘记录 | 401 请求 / 400,000,005 输入 | 1 请求 / 5 输入 | 1 请求 / 5 输入 |
| 读侧，同一会话的两次真实运行 | 1 条 / 30,778 token | 2 条 / 72,818 token | 2 条 / 72,818 token |

在台账的冻结副本上，面板三个窗口全部与 oracle 精确一致（`ALL_RANGES_EXACT=true`，0 个日不符），跨会话视图的 token、请求、平均延迟与缓存命中率同样精确一致。

用本分支 bundle 在真实终端中渲染（PTY 抓屏，跨会话页）：Activity 的 7 天显示 `Tokens 11492.1m`、`Sessions 28`，oracle 为 11,492,141,679；Activity 的 30 天显示 `Tokens 40781.1m`、`Sessions 389`，oracle 为 40,781,106,261 / 389；Efficiency 的今日显示 `Cache Hit Rate 97.2%`、`Avg Latency 5.7s`，逐模型请求 943 + 108 + 21 = 1072，oracle 为 97.2% / 5,698 ms / 1,072。两次真实 headless 运行同一会话（第二次恢复它）分别产出 3 请求 / 42,040 token 与 2 请求 / 30,778 token——第二次没有把第一次再计一遍。

真实 Chromium 连接本分支 daemon，已补上了此前唯一缺失的浏览器验证。两条台账记录配两条等值会话记录时，Today 显示 hero `1,100`、input `1,000`、output `100`、cache `60%`；7D 显示 `3,300`、`3,000`、`300`、`60%`，按日会话序列明确标为 `runs ended per day`。独立 HTTP 读取返回同样数字，浏览器无 page error。另一组真实 PTY 生命周期全程只访问本地 mock 模型：A 发一次 5,000-token 请求，resume 带有 10,000 存量 token 的 B，再发一次 7-token 请求，最后 `/exit`。最终文件恰好有两条 run-scoped 记录：A=5,000、B=7；存量 10,000 没有混入任一记录，退出码为 0。

每个新增守卫都做了变异见证：还原它会让对应用例转红；而存量历史的归约结果与之前逐字节一致（2,065 条原始记录，两臂都返回 2,043 条 / 379,387,040,763 token，逐会话键相同）。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

本地 build 与 bundle、真实 Chromium 与 PTY 抓屏、隔离临时 home 上的真实 headless 及交互式 CLI 生命周期。最终触及套件：core 1160 passed、cli 161 passed、Web Shell 13 passed。完整 llm 套件 129 passed，另有 3 条在 base 上同样失败的 relaunch provenance 用例；退出用量两条用例通过。build、typecheck、lint、format 门禁全部干净。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：汇总窗口现在取整个本地日，因为日桶无法按小时切分，因此边界日被完整计入，而不是只计滚动截点之后的那几个小时；在回退路径上该影响可测量且只限那一天。按项目的 token 列仍是记录口径——台账没有项目维度——因此它现在与其上方已修正的总量存在可见的不一致。跨越升级时点的会话只保留运行增量，因此该 id 在升级前的活动可能被少算；对有歧义的重叠，选择少算而非重复计算。
- 新鲜度与性能：`/stats` 每次打开都重新读取当前窗口及前一环比窗口的台账，只有并发打开共享一次未完成读取。不能复用已完成的缓存，因为已完成运行的消耗会被缓存隐藏，而对应的会话记录副本已经因台账覆盖被抑制。上一环比窗口的两个边界都按日历日回退，与当前窗口互不相交且日桶数相等。daemon 请求仍保留有意的 60 秒数据源缓存。
- 未验证 / 范围外：Windows 与 Linux。对于从未持久化用量记录的会话，会话数与按项目 tile 仍不完整——参考历史上台账知道 7 天内有 633 个会话，而记录文件知道的远少于此——这需要台账口径的会话普查以及在会话结束时落盘用量，两者都留作后续。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。新增一个可选记录字段标记按运行写入；所有按记录版本过滤的读取方继续可用，存量历史既不重写也不迁移，面板载荷形状不变。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.zh-CN.md)。两版完整同步，并记录了首轮两项未通过独立复核的发现：台账证伪的「会话身份分叉」，以及会在存量记录上造成 3.1 倍倒退的「分段求和」去重提案。

## 关联 Issue

无需关闭的 issue。构建在为 #4479 引入的逐请求台账与 #9833 的 session-swap telemetry 事务之上。

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): update sidebar logo for dark theme
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Changes only the dark-theme Web Shell sidebar logo: the original blue Qwen mark is replaced by compact single-path artwork suited to dark surfaces. The light theme deliberately keeps the original blue three-part mark, including when a custom logo image fails and falls back to the built-in artwork. The SVG remains inline, and the existing layout, host-provided branding, fallback behavior, and browser favicon are unchanged.

## Why it's needed

The dark shell benefits from a restrained light brand mark instead of the original blue geometry. This change is intentionally dark-only so users who switch to the light theme continue to see the branding they had before this PR.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open Web Shell with the default Qwen Code branding and the dark theme. Confirm that the new light single-path mark appears at the upper-left beside the product name. Switch to the light theme and confirm that the original blue three-part Qwen logo returns, without a new black or white replacement glyph. The surrounding navigation and product name should remain unchanged. A configured host or daemon logo should still replace the built-in mark, and a failed custom image should fall back to the mark appropriate for the selected theme.

The current head passes the 21-test sidebar brand suite, including an explicit preservation case for the blue light-theme artwork, Web Shell and full-repository TypeScript checks, ESLint and Prettier checks for the changed files, and the complete repository build. The dark and light Chromium mock-daemon visual scenarios also pass on the final implementation.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Only the dark theme changes. These are genuine 1280×800 Chromium captures from the same scenario, with daemon HTTP mocked. Select an image for its full-size rendering.

| Before (`origin/main`) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- |
| [![Old dark-theme blue sidebar logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17935-r2/dark-before.png)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17935-r2/dark-before.png) | [![New dark-theme light sidebar logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17935-r2/dark-after.png)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17935-r2/dark-after.png) |

**Light theme — intentionally unchanged, still the original blue logo:**

![Light theme retains the original blue Qwen mark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17935-r2/light-original.png)

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested locally |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested locally |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, Node 26.12.1, the Web Shell Vite visuals harness, and headless Chromium with daemon HTTP mocked. The jsdom brand suite ran with Node's experimental native `localStorage` disabled.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Low. The theme is already supplied to the sidebar and is now used to select between the original light-theme artwork and the new dark-theme artwork. The dark-only scope is covered by separate unit assertions for each theme.
- Not validated / out of scope: The complete unit-test suite, WebKit/mobile viewports, and live-daemon interaction were not exercised. The screenshots verify rendering only; they do not claim live-daemon E2E coverage.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. Custom branding, favicon behavior, configuration, and public APIs are unchanged.

## Linked Issues

N/A.

Linux、Node 26.12.1、Web Shell Vite visuals 测试环境及 headless Chromium；daemon HTTP 使用 mock。jsdom 品牌测试运行时关闭了 Node 的实验性原生 `localStorage`。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：低。侧栏原本就有主题参数，现在通过它选择亮色主题的原图形与暗色主题的新图形；两种主题分别有独立的单元断言保护暗色限定范围。

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve command migration destinations
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Creates migrated Markdown commands exclusively. If another file or symlink owns the destination when the write occurs, migration now reports a conflict and preserves both the competing destination and the original TOML instead of renaming or deleting the TOML.

## Why it's needed

The previous destination `access()` check and default-mode `writeFile()` were separate operations. A Markdown draft created in that window was truncated, and a pre-existing dangling Markdown symlink was followed so migration created its target and continued with the TOML backup/deletion. Exclusive creation enforces the existing no-overwrite contract at the actual write and rejects all occupied destination types, including dangling links.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. From `packages/cli`, run `../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/services/command-migration-tool.test.ts`. Confirm all 16 tests pass.
2. The competing-draft case schedules an independent real `wx` file creation immediately after a call-through destination `access()` returns `ENOENT`. Confirm the draft and original TOML bytes remain unchanged, no backup appears, and migration returns one `failedFiles` conflict.
3. On a platform supporting file symlinks, the dangling-link case confirms the link and original TOML remain intact, the unrelated target remains absent, and deletion/backup does not proceed.
4. The existing ordinary-existing-file and vacant-destination cases cover the friendly conflict and successful conversion/backup controls. Nearby parser and converter suites provide additional unchanged-path coverage.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, on main `f8d4f706eadee7481cc3059eb3ae2c0ce4b8f790`, an independent public `migrateTomlCommands()` probe with real temporary files reproduced **2 failed / 1 passed**: the competing draft was overwritten, the dangling link target was created, both conflicts incorrectly returned success and renamed the TOML, and the vacant-destination control passed. The two new tests also failed before the fix (`2 failed, 14 skipped`).

After, the public migration test file passes **16/16**, including both collisions and successful backup/deletion controls. `markdown-command-parser.test.ts` passes **13/13**, and `toml-to-markdown-converter.test.ts` passes **14/14**. Changed-file Prettier and ESLint checks plus `npm run typecheck` in `packages/cli` pass.

**CLI migration-path verification:** exercised the real public migration function against real temporary files in before/after and control runs. **TUI/UI drive: N/A** for additional visual verification because `AppContainer`'s existing prompt/error rendering is unchanged; the changed observable contract is the migration result and persisted filesystem state, which the public-function instrument observes directly. No lower-level check is being presented as a driven-TUI test.

A separate self-review found no correctness, test, simplicity, or Markdown-destination security issues. The local `qwen review` gate is **UNVERIFIED**: Qwen Code 0.28.0 was run read-only as `qwen review run --json --quiet --timeout-minutes 3`, but returned `completed: false`, `timedOut: true`, and no verdict after 190023 ms, so no clean-gate claim is made.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ Public-function real-filesystem tests and focused gates passed |

prs.title: feat(cli): add native historical statistics
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds historical Activity and Efficiency to native `/stats` and Settings → Stats. Reports combine the existing user history across projects with the selected live session, replacing that session's saved entry rather than counting it twice. Session metrics remain live.

Activity includes session, duration and token totals, comparisons, heatmap/streak, monthly trends and projects. Efficiency includes cache and tool success rates, weighted latency, tool and model breakdowns, and code impact. Existing range/month navigation and Settings focus rules are retained. Narrow views keep the complete selected tab, current range and key hints above a scrollable, wrapping body. The dedicated TUI gate includes the public history regression.

## Why it's needed

The native historical tabs previously repeated a current-session summary, so users could not inspect persisted usage even though the command and Settings entry were available. Narrow frames also needed to account for wrapping instead of assuming a fixed chrome height.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- With saved sessions across dates, models and projects, open `/stats`. Compare All time, Last 30 days, Last 7 days and Today; month navigation should stay within available data. Switch to Efficiency and verify per-model values and independent latency totals.
- Return to Session, close and reopen, then restart. Confirm that history and live-session usage are not duplicated. In Settings → Stats, statistics keys should follow content focus and Escape should return to the host before closing it.
- Resize through 120×40, 80×18, 40×18, 20×15 and 40×12. The selected tab and frame should remain visible; PageUp/PageDown should navigate the body without hiding labels or values permanently.
- Check empty history and one legacy transcript migration. Existing migration may append a rebuilt summary once; subsequent opens must not repeat it. Seeded valid history should retain its bytes while viewing reports.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: installed-global Ink established the history behavior; the paired native capture reached a live-zero Session but only a current-session Activity placeholder.

After, the independent Stats-only candidate passed full build/typecheck, seven CLI whole files (220 tests), existing Core usage-history tests (59), workflow metadata (424 passed, four skipped), full lint, formatting and bundle; the eight relocated public harness files also passed typechecking. The new artifact passed 13 public legs: Groups A–D on all three profiles and native five-size geometry, covering 16 case executions, 22 natural exits before helper cleanup and three closed loopback fixture-model requests (one per Group D). Independent saved-frame review passed for the 61 frames and 80 original inputs: complete frame bounds and selected labels across all five sizes/three tabs, top clamping and the original PageDown/return checks. This is fixture-layout coverage. Earlier combined-candidate results remain separate evidence.

### Tested on

| OS | Independent candidate status |
| :---: | :--- |
| macOS | Scoped normal and 13 public legs passed |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Pinned main88e3 source; validated renderer/runtime comparison is Node24+Ink, Bun1.4.4+Ink and strict Bun1.4.4+OpenTUI0.5.10. Source-bundle entry SHA-256: `07ad9eae84861fedeb7ce452626c8f8c6fc5981f345120fc0dd5db68f88b6dce` (1,454 bundle files), validated on 2026-11-16 Asia/Shanghai.

## Risk & Scope

- History is the current process user's existing store across projects. A mismatched or replaced live-session owner must not receive late results; it does not fall back to another runtime.
- Existing history migration and quit-time persistence remain in place, so this is not a blanket read-only storage API. No Core production/API, usage schema, renderer default, Trust, watcher policy or execution-confirmation change is included.
- Windows/Linux, installed packages, GUI, exhaustive Unicode, every tiny embedded region and overall migration are not qualified by this change. Remote CI is tracked separately on this PR. This does not qualify IME, long-run stability or the separate Bun+Ink Trust restart failure.
- Design: [English](docs/design/2026-11-15-opentui-stats-history.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-15-opentui-stats-history.zh-CN.md). Both preserve historical checkpoints. The current checkpoint is a completed documentation-only bridge: formatting/reference checks passed; all 17 other code/test/CI blobs and the 1,454 compiled files remain unchanged from the tested candidate.

## Linked Issues

No linked issue.

| :---: | :--- |
| macOS | 有限normal及13个公开leg通过 |
| Windows | 未测试 |

### 环境（可选）

固定main88e3源码；实际验证Node24+Ink、Bun1.4.4+Ink及strict Bun1.4.4+OpenTUI0.5.10。源码构建bundle entry SHA-256为`07ad9eae84861fedeb7ce452626c8f8c6fc5981f345120fc0dd5db68f88b6dce`（1,454个bundle文件），验证日期为2026-11-16 Asia/Shanghai。

## 风险与范围

- 历史来自当前进程用户的既有跨项目store。实时session owner不匹配或替换后不得接收迟到结果，也不回退至另一个runtime。
- 保留既有历史迁移及退出时usage持久化，因此不是整个存储API绝对只读。没有Core生产/API、usage schema、默认renderer、Trust、watcher策略或执行确认改动。
- 不授予Windows/Linux、安装包、GUI、全部Unicode、所有极小嵌入region及整体迁移资格；远端CI在本PR单独记录，也不授予IME、长期稳定性或另案Bun+Ink Trust重启失败资格。
- 设计：[English](docs/design/2026-11-15-opentui-stats-history.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-15-opentui-stats-history.zh-CN.md)。两版保留历史checkpoint；当前验证checkpoint的文档桥已完成format/reference检查，其余17个源码/测试/CI blob及1,454个编译文件均与已测候选完全一致。

prs.title: fix(sdk): bound concurrent peer discovery probes
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Limit concurrent inbox probes while discovering peers. Each distinct address is still probed once, and the final directory keeps its existing ordering and duplicate-session rules.

## Why it's needed

Discovery starts every socket probe at once. Under a finite descriptor budget, later probes return unknown even when their peers are alive, so valid sessions disappear from the discovery result. The send path already bounds concurrent descriptors; discovery previously did not.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Use a directory with 80 distinct live inboxes and a probe that models a 32-connection budget by returning unknown when full. Discovery should eventually include every session in the original order without exceeding the available capacity. Retain existing duplicate-address and newest-session cases.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The controlled capacity regression fails on unchanged base: only the first 32 of 80 live records are returned. It passes after the change, and all 15 focused directory tests pass. A native Unix-socket reproduction was attempted but this execution environment rejected listen with EPERM; no native socket result is claimed.

No TUI change; screenshots are not applicable.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Focused tests and checks passed |

### Environment

Linux, Node.js 24.22.3, Vitest 1.6.0. Focused tests, source-closure TypeScript checks, the repository ESLint configuration and Prettier checks passed using a local verification tool installation. Native socket E2E is blocked by EPERM. The frozen full workspace install, full repository build/typecheck/preflight, macOS and Windows were not run.

## Risk & Scope

Large directories with many stalled addresses take several bounded waves instead of starting every deadline simultaneously. This intentionally trades worst-case scan duration for descriptor headroom. This change only bounds the probe stage; it does not alter registry file reads or send admission.

No public signature or wire-format change.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17980.

prs.title: perf(sdk): drain buffered messages in amortized linear time
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Read queued SDK messages through a moving head and compact the storage occasionally. Consumed payload references are released immediately, while FIFO delivery, buffered errors and completion behavior remain unchanged.

## Why it's needed

Removing the first element for every buffered message repeatedly moves the remaining array. A consumer that resumes after a large output burst spends avoidable time draining already-received output.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Buffer 100,000 numbered messages, finish the producer, and consume them in order. Compare the complete drain on the unchanged base and this change. Also interleave a partial drain with a second producer burst, include undefined values, and check the error after the final buffered value.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The local four-sample 100,000-message benchmark took 584.73, 550.12, 729.72 and 554.10 ms before, versus 24.60, 15.32, 28.91 and 14.56 ms after. Median drain time decreased from 569.42 to 19.96 ms (about 28.5× faster in this microbenchmark). The existing and added stream tests pass: 25/25.

No TUI change; screenshots are not applicable.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Focused tests and checks passed |

### Environment

Linux, Node.js 24.22.3, Vitest 1.6.0. Focused tests, source-closure TypeScript checks, the repository ESLint configuration and Prettier checks passed using a local verification tool installation. The frozen full workspace install, full repository build/typecheck/preflight, macOS and Windows were not run.

## Risk & Scope

The measured gain applies to draining a large buffered burst on this local Node runtime; it is not a claim about model latency or complete query speed. Compaction briefly allocates a smaller array, and consumed objects are cleared before compaction.

No public signature or wire-format change.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17978.
