issues.body:
## Why this matters
Both the streaming decoder (`crates/engine/src/client/chat.rs` ~:4610-4623) and non-streaming parser (~:4005-4011) synthesize `call_{index}` for a missing tool-call id. A pathological provider that emits a literal `call_1` id alongside id-less calls collides → `validate_tool_call_ids_for_protocol` rejects the whole turn. Narrow, but a distinguishing prefix removes the class entirely.

## Current behavior
Fallback id is `call_{i}` — indistinguishable from a provider that literally sends `call_1`.

## Desired behavior
- Fallback ids use a reserved prefix (e.g. `call_missing_{i}`) in BOTH streaming and non-streaming paths (change only one and the mirrored contract breaks).
- Duplicate-check behavior unchanged otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] mixed `{"id":"call_1"}` + one id-less call at index 1 is admitted (no false duplicate)
- [ ] two id-less calls still get distinct ids; `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib fallback` passes

## Related
PR #7399 (audit V3), streaming regression test `decoder_assigns_unique_fallback_ids_to_parallel_tool_calls_missing_id`

prs.title: chore(catalog): refresh the Models.dev offline seed

prs.title: perf(engine): cache the item index across processes
prs.body:
## What and why

The first thread a process opens pays a pass over the whole items directory: an item's filename carries only its item id, never its turn, so the only way to learn which items a turn owns is to open the item records. The in-memory index made that a one-time cost per process, and the server already warms it at startup — but nothing about the answer outlived the process, so a restarted engine (or any other client process) paid it again. Against a 55,572-item store that is the entire open time of the first conversation.

The index is now cached beside the directories it describes (`item-index.json` at the store root) and rebuilt from a directory listing plus only the entries the cache does not hold. The listing decides membership, so the cache cannot make an answer wrong: an entry that names a deleted item is simply not consulted, and a missing, unreadable or out-of-date file costs one full read — exactly what every process used to pay.

Measured on the same 55,572-item store, first index build in a process:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| before | 3.9s |
| after | 93ms |

Three deliberate choices:

- **Reading never writes.** Caching is `RuntimeThreadStore::cache_item_index`, called only by the startup warm-up. A `GET` that created a file would break what those routes promise, and the existing tests that snapshot a store to prove a route is read-only cover it.
- **The cache is not fsynced.** Losing it to a crash costs the next process one full read, which is the state every process was in before it existed. The write is a rename over a per-process temporary, so a reader never sees a partial file.
- **The cold pass no longer materializes records.** Deserializing into a one-field reference instead of `TurnItemRecord` avoids allocating a tool result's `detail` and `metadata` to learn an id.

## Where this came from

A bug fix with no issue: reopening a long conversation after a restart sat on the previous conversation for seconds, with the delay growing with the store. Diagnosis and measurements are in the commit message.

## How I tested it

```
cargo fmt --all --check                                   # clean
cargo clippy -p codewhale-engine --lib                    # no new warnings
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib -- runtime_threads::tests
                                                          # 346 passed
cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib -- \
  thread_summary_search_does_not_scan_the_whole_store_per_thread \
  thread_summary_listing_never_walks_the_items_directory \
  turn_operation_lookup_is_authenticated_read_only_and_survives_restart
                                                          # 3 passed
```

New tests cover the cache surviving a process, learning items written while it was closed, forgetting a deleted item, falling back from a damaged or foreign-version file, a read-only handle never writing, and — the invariant above — a read leaving the store byte-identical.

One pre-existing failure, unrelated: `runtime_threads::tests::engine_withdrawal_retires_approval_and_unblocks_queued_events` is flaky on `main` (it fails 2 of 3 runs there and 1 of 3 here; it passes when run alone). The same module needs `RUST_MIN_STACK` raised in a debug build for two other cases to fit, also on `main`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] No user-facing docs or `docs/features.toml` row: this changes how fast a thread opens, not what it does

prs.title: test(tui): guard all four paste-burst chunk-flush sites
prs.body:
﻿## What and why

This closes the gap I flagged in #7403 and in #7422's review thread: the suite catches chunking stopping entirely, but not a *single* chunk check going away.

oversized_raw_and_bracketed_pastes_preserve_every_char_and_newline drives a mixed payload, and mixed is exactly what hides the problem — each CJK or emoji character re-enters the separate !c.is_ascii() branch in handle_paste_burst_key, whose own 	ake_chunk_if_full() flushes the same buffer. Delete the ASCII-path check and that test stays green.

Two new fixtures, one per append path, both with the same 60% progress probe:

- `ascii_only_raw_paste_over_the_chunk_cap_lands_complete` — pure ASCII, no newline, so every character takes on_plain_char → handle_paste_burst_decision and nothing else.
- `cjk_only_raw_paste_over_the_chunk_cap_lands_complete` — CJK plus an astral-plane emoji, no newline, so every character stays in the !c.is_ascii() branch.

No newline in either: an Enter reaches ppend_newline_if_active, whose own chunk check would flush the buffer and stand in for the path under test.

## Where this came from

Refs #7403

## How I tested it

Mutation matrix on a scratch copy. M = that fixture fails and catches the regression; every injection reverted afterwards.

| injected regression | ascii_only | cjk_only | mixed |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASCII-path 	ake_chunk_if_full removed | **M** | — | — |
| non-ASCII-path 	ake_chunk_if_full removed | — | **M** | — |
| push_bounded drop rule restored (#7403 itself) | — | **M** | **M** |
| 	ake_chunk_if_full always returns None | — | — | **M** |

The probe messages are the evidence: `the composer holds 0 of 273000 bytes` for the ASCII path, `3 of 342000` for the non-ASCII one.

**Why scii_only does not catch the original drop rule** — this is arithmetic, not a hole. Its bytes are one UTF-8 byte wide, so the buffer fills to exactly the cap every cycle and a `len + ch.len_utf8() <= cap` guard always admits the character: injecting the rule loses 0 bytes there. The CJK fixture is 3–4 bytes wide, so the buffer stops short of the cap, the crossing character is rejected, and the tail is lost. Both facts are written into the test docs so nobody later reads scii_only as coverage it does not have.

**Deliberately not covered:** the third 	ake_chunk_if_full, after ppend_newline_if_active. It fires only when a pasted newline pushes the buffer past the cap, and the next plain character flushes the same buffer one keystroke later — deleting it leaves the text complete (verified: all three tests green). It bounds peak memory, not correctness, so no content assertion can observe it. Noted in  eed_raw_paste's doc comment rather than faked with an assertion that cannot fail.

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
  -> clean

cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib paste -- --skip credential_paste_content
  -> test result: ok. 62 passed; 0 failed
```

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current main
- [x] cargo fmt --all passes, and tests cover the behavior
- [ ] Tests only, so no docs/features.toml row

prs.title: fix(execpolicy): propagate flag-word dynamic bit on nix and launcher flags
prs.body:
## What and why

When a command substitution is appended to a launcher flag word (such as `nix develop -c$(echo rm) x` or `nix develop --command=$(echo rm) x`), the substitution contributes no literal text to the token, leaving a static flag spelling (`-c` / `--command=`) with `dynamic[at] == true`. Because the matched flag arm did not propagate `dynamic[at]` (and the `nix` arm did not match attached `--command=` / `-c` forms), the runtime-resolved payload escaped deny rules under `AskForApproval::Never`.

This change:
- Updates the `nix` arm in `crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs` to match separated and attached `-c`/`--command` spellings and propagate `dynamic[at]`.
- Fixes the same dropped flag-word `dynamic[at]` bug in sibling flag scanners (`option_payloads`, `record_exec_flag_command`, `cmd`, `record_powershell`, `record_find_exec`, `shell_input`, and `find_entrypoints`).
- Leaves non-substituted spellings unchanged and adds deny-matrix plus unit regression tests covering both substituted bypasses and allowed ordinary commands.

## Where this came from

Closes #7401

## How I tested it

- Added 23 new deny-matrix rows in `crates/execpolicy/tests/shell_parse_policy.rs` and confirmed all 23 failed before the fix (`test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed` on `deny_rules_hold_against_runtime_resolved_and_reserved_word_spellings`).
- Ran `cargo test -p codewhale-execpolicy`:

prs.title: feat(ci): add the maintainer gate and regression stage (#7433)
prs.body:
## What and why

Implements the protocol in #7433: a maintainer gate before agent work, and a regression stage after it.

- **Part 1 — startability is a grant.** The Agent task form no longer self-applies `agent-ready`. The metadata contract test now rejects the default instead of pinning it. CONTRIBUTING, ISSUE_TRIAGE, AGENT_ETHOS (en/zh), FLEET (en/zh), the fleet-manager skill and the remote-smoke runbook say that absence means not startable.
- **Part 2a — behavioural guards.** `crates/engine/tests/behavioural_guards.rs` holds one positive assertion per promise, each citing its issue: the agent-ready gate (#7433) and the tool-call fallback id rule (#7423). A rename can no longer invert it silently.
- **Part 2b — behaviour statements.** `scripts/check-behaviour-line.py` requires `Behaviour: <old> -> <new>` or `No-behaviour-change: <why>` on fix/feat/perf/refactor commits in the push range; it is wired into `scripts/preflight.sh` and the helper-contract CI step.
- **Part 3 — regression stage.** `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` names the per-slice review receipt (`review --base <sha> --path <path> --write-receipt`, then `--check-receipt`) as the regression pass. A receipt with unresolved risk blocks the candidate until a maintainer reads the findings.
- **Part 4/5 — triage standards.** ISSUE_TRIAGE gains Startability, the regression threshold, the severity mapping (`p1` minimum, `release-blocker` by maintainer decision, `p0` only for data loss/security/release path), the closing standard, and the #7432 disposition.
- **Part 5b — docs drift.** `scripts/check-docs-drift.py` requires a touched feature row to update its summary and to name its flag or id on the docs page it points at.

## Where this came from

Refs #7433. The protocol is forward-looking; #7432 is left open for the maintainer to resolve by restoring the parent index or correcting the docs.

prs.title: fix(execpolicy): model additional tmux execution verbs
prs.body:
## What and why

Extend `crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs` to model the remaining command-executing `tmux` verbs with their per-verb option and operand-consumption rules so deny rules cannot be bypassed through them:

- `display-popup` / `popup`: parses popup options (`-b/-c/-d/-e/-h/-s/-S/-t/-T/-w/-x/-y` values and `-B/-C/-E/-k/-K/-N` switches) and expands the trailing shell command (both shell-string and argv forms), while keeping `-C` (close popup) and safe commands allowed.
- `confirm-before` / `confirm`: parses `-c/-p/-t` values and `-b/-y` switches, and expands the trailing command as both a nested tmux command and a shell payload.
- `command-prompt`: parses `-I/-p/-t/-T` values and `-1/-b/-F/-i/-k/-l/-N` switches; expands `-I` initial inputs (respecting `-l` comma-splitting) when no template is given, and expands the `[template]` both raw and with `%%`/`%%%`/`%1`..`%9` substituted from `-I`.
- `bind-key` / `bind`: parses `-N/-T` values and `-n/-r` switches, consumes the required `key` operand, and recursively expands the bound tmux command tail (multi-token or quoted single-string, as well as `;`-separated tmux command lists) without falsely treating tmux aliases like `ls` as shell commands.
- `source-file` / `source`: handled via the fail-closed `dynamic = true` path (matching `at -f` and `parallel ::::`) because the sourced file's commands cannot be inspected statically; `-n` (parse-only without `-F` and with non-dynamic arguments) stays allowed.
- Also models `run-shell`/`run`, `if-shell`/`if`, `pipe-pane`/`pipep`, `send-keys`/`send`, and `;`-separated tmux command chains with accurate per-verb flag specs so recursive tmux verbs such as `tmux bind-key k run-shell 'rm x'` and `tmux confirm-before "run-shell 'rm x'"` resolve cleanly on `main`.
- Inert tmux verbs (`list-sessions`, `ls`, `display-message`, `attach`, `-V`, etc.) remain allowed without setting `dynamic` or `nested`.

## Where this came from

Closes #7415

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-execpolicy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (0 warnings)

prs.title: fix(execpolicy): fail closed on whole-word dynamic flag and verb names
prs.body:
## What and why

A word whose entire flag or subcommand verb is runtime-resolved (e.g. `su $(echo -c) 'rm x'`, `nix $(echo develop) -c rm x`, `docker $(echo run) --entrypoint rm alpine`, `start-stop-daemon --start $(echo --exec) rm -- x`) parses as an empty (or non-`-`-prefixed) word with `dynamic = true`. Existing option and verb scanners required `token.starts_with('-')` or a literal verb/flag name, silently dropping the dynamic bit and allowing deny-rule bypasses under `AskForApproval::Never`.

This change makes launcher option scanners and verb-resolution paths fail closed when a runtime-resolved word appears in a flag or verb position, while preserving allow behavior for ordinary commands and non-executing subcommands with dynamic arguments:

- `option_payloads`: emit an unresolved `("", true)` marker on dynamic words in flag positions (bounded by the first inner command head for wrapper commands `runuser`/`flock`/`script`), fold flag-word dynamic bits into separated values, and avoid terminating option scanning on a dynamic `--`.
- `resolve_wrapper_targets` / `launcher_verb_targets`: mark the walk unresolved on dynamic verb/flag/operand words, while allowing quoted inline values on non-entrypoint known long options (such as `docker run --env="$FOO" alpine ls`).
- `command_heads` / `step_wrapper_option`: propagate dynamic bits through `env -S`/`--split-string` payloads, dynamic wrapper flag steps, and dynamic `Stop` words, and avoid treating a dynamic `--` as end-of-options.
- `nix`, `start-stop-daemon` / `record_exec_flag_command`, `find`, `cmd`, `powershell`, `shell_input`, `docker --entrypoint`, and `ssh`/`screen` short-circuits: propagate dynamic words in option/flag positions instead of silently skipping them.

## Where this came from

Closes #7408

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p codewhale-execpolicy`:
  - `src/lib.rs`: `test result: ok. 247 passed; 0 failed`
  - `tests/authorization_order.rs`: `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed`
  - `tests/redirection_policy.rs`: `test result: ok. 11 passed; 0 failed`
  - `tests/shell_parse_policy.rs`: `test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed` (added 30 deny-matrix vectors covering #7408 and related scanners plus 19 benign dynamic-argument allow assertions)
  - doctests: `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-execpolicy --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::nonminimal_bool`: passed with zero warnings in touched files (Rust 1.95 flags one pre-existing `clippy::nonminimal_bool` in untouched `crates/execpolicy/src/command_safety.rs:2101`)

prs.title: fix(execpolicy): tighten stdin_piped propagation and numactl --strict
prs.body:
## What and why

Addresses all six findings from #7416 in `crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs`:

1. **`||` vs `|` (`x || ssh host`):** Only `|` and `|&` (and newline continuations immediately after a pipe) mark the next command `stdin_piped`; `||`, `&&`, `;`, and `&` reset to the enclosing group's stdin so `x || ssh host` is not over-marked.
2. **Fd-aware `<` redirections (`ssh host 3< f`):** `consume_redirect_descriptor` distinguishes default / `0<` stdin redirections from non-stdin descriptors (`3<`, `{fd}<`, `3<<<`, `3<&0`, `3<<EOF`), preventing fd-3 redirections from falsely marking `stdin_piped` or clobbering heredoc/pipe state.
3. **`ssh` heredocs (`ssh host ls <<EOF ... EOF`):** Expand heredoc bodies as shell commands only when `ssh` has no remote command (`ssh host <<EOF`). When a remote command is present (`ssh host ls <<EOF`), keep the heredoc body as data (still scanning unquoted `$(...)`/backtick substitutions) while propagating `stdin_piped` into the remote command so `ssh host sh <<EOF` and `ssh host 'ssh host2' <<EOF` still fail closed.
4. **`find -exec` stdin propagation (`echo 'rm x' | find . -exec ssh host \;`):** Propagate parent `stdin_piped || heredoc` into `record_find_exec`, `slice_line`, and `build_prefixed_line` so `-exec` children inherit piped stdin.
5. **Brace/subshell group stdin sharing (`echo 'rm x' | { a; ssh h; }`):** Track nested brace/keyword and subshell groups so piped stdin (and post-group stdin redirections such as `{ a; ssh host; } <<< 'rm x'`) propagates to every group member and resets after the group closes.
6. **`numactl --strict`:** Move `"strict"` from `long_values` to `long_switches` in `WRAPPERS` so `numactl --strict rm` does not treat `rm` as an option value.

prs.title: fix(execpolicy): scan static awk and sed program payloads
prs.body:
## What and why

`awk 'BEGIN{system("rm x")}'` and `sed 's/a/rm x/e'` execute deny-listed commands from inside static program text that `crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs` previously treated as opaque. Under `AskForApproval::Never` with a `rm` deny rule, those commands were allowed through.

This change adds static program scanners for both families in `shell_expand.rs`:
- **`awk` / `gawk` / `mawk` / `nawk` / `goawk`**: extracts program text from positional operands, `-e`, `--source`, and `-W source=`, tokenizes awk code (handling strings with octal/hex escapes, `#` comments, and regex vs. division `/` disambiguation), and emits command payloads from `system(...)`, `expr | getline` / `|& getline`, and `print`/`printf ... | expr` / `|& expr` through `code_payload`. Non-literal command expressions (e.g. `system(cmd)`, `print "a" | c`), dynamic script operands (`awk $PROG`), and stdin/fd script files (`-f -`, `-f /dev/stdin`) fail closed by marking `Expansion::dynamic`.
- **`sed` / `gsed` / `ssed`**: extracts scripts from positional operands (including BSD `sed -i ''` / `-i .bak` forms), `-e`, and `--expression`, parses addresses and commands (respecting alternate delimiters, regex character classes, `a`/`i`/`c` text blocks, `y///`, labels, and `s///w` filenames), and emits payloads from `s/.../.../e` and standalone `e <cmd>` through `code_payload`. Bare `e`, `s///e` forms that can execute runtime pattern space, dynamic script operands, and stdin/fd script files mark `Expansion::dynamic`.
- Ordinary read-only and benign `awk`/`sed` invocations (`awk '{print}'`, `awk -F: '{print $1}' /etc/passwd`, `awk '/foo|bar/ {print}'`, `sed -n '/x/p'`, `sed 's/foo/bar/g'`, `sed 's/e/x/g'`, `sed -e 's/echo/echoed/g'`, `sed 's/a/b/w readme.txt'`) stay allowed with zero false positives.

## Where this came from

Closes #7413

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p codewhale-execpolicy`:
  - Unit tests (`src/lib.rs`): `test result: ok. 249 passed; 0 failed` (including new `awk_static_and_dynamic_command_payloads_are_scanned` and `sed_static_and_dynamic_command_payloads_are_scanned`)
  - `tests/authorization_order.rs`: `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed`
  - `tests/redirection_policy.rs`: `test result: ok. 11 passed; 0 failed`
  - `tests/shell_parse_policy.rs`: `test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed` (with new deny-matrix rows in `HIDDEN_RM` and benign allow-list rows in `ordinary_commands_stay_allowed_next_to_a_deny_rule`)
  - Doc-tests: `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-execpolicy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed cleanly
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed cleanly

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)

prs.title: fix(engine): classify local read-only deferred tools as Safe in get_tool_category
prs.body:
## What and why

`crates/engine/src/core/authority.rs` `get_tool_category()` still left a number of registered `ToolCapability::ReadOnly` local tools, canonical read-action targets, and legacy `tool_search` spellings unclassified, so they fell through to `ToolCategory::Unknown` and Auto-Review routed every call to `AskUser` (`auto_review.rs:1582`).

Each candidate tool from #7407 was audited individually against its implementation and capabilities before classifying:

### Classified as `ToolCategory::Safe`

| Tool / Target | Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| `is_tool_search_tool(name)` (`tool_search`, `tool_search_tool_regex`, `tool_search_tool_bm25`) | Replaces the literal `"tool_search"` arm with the shared `codewhale_tools::names::is_tool_search_tool` helper so legacy dispatchable spellings (`turn_loop.rs:1136-1146`, `:2238`) also classify as `Safe`. |
| `context_archive_get`, `context_archive_search` | `ReadOnly` / `Auto`. Bounded, secret-scrubbed in-process reads of the current session's compaction archive. |
| `session_get`, `session_search` | `ReadOnly` / `Auto`. Bounded, workspace-scoped in-process reads of prior session metadata/tails. |
| `memory_get`, `memory_search` | `ReadOnly` / `Auto`. Bounded, workspace-scoped in-process reads of `NativeMemoryStore`. |
| `project_map` | `ReadOnly`, `Sandboxable` / `Auto`. In-process directory walk (`"project"` was already in `Safe`, while the registered tool name is `"project_map"`). |
| `validate_data` | `ReadOnly`, `Sandboxable` / `Auto`. Parses inline or workspace-guarded JSON/TOML in-process (when `Feature::DataHost` is enabled, sends only structural descriptors — kinds/keys/counts — to the stock host). |
| `tui_help` | `ReadOnly` / `Auto`. In-process lookup over `CommandCatalog`, `KEYBINDINGS`, and `Settings::load_read_only()`. |
| `show_data` | `ReadOnly` / `Auto`. Pure in-memory terminal chart validation/formatting; zero I/O. |
| `present` | `ReadOnly` / `Auto`. Computes SHA-256 + byte size over 1–32 workspace-scoped files and returns a handoff receipt; never mutates, copies, or uploads. |
| `notify` | `ReadOnly` / `Auto`. Bounded, control-byte-stripped, redacted desktop notification via `host_terminal::host().notify_model(...)`, honoring `[notifications]` config/quiet/off; no filesystem, shell, or network side effects. |
| `lsp` | `ReadOnly` / `Auto`. Read-only queries (`diagnostics`, `read_lints`, `symbols`, `definition`, `references`) over the user-configured session `LspManager` (sibling to `diagnostics`, already `Safe`). |
| `git_merge_tree` (`Git{action:"merge_tree"}`) | `ReadOnly`, `Sandboxable` / `Auto`. Pure local `git merge-tree` object read with validated revisions (`validate_git_rev`); never touches working tree, index, refs, or network. Sibling to `git_status`/`git_diff`/`git_log`/`git_show`/`git_blame`/`git_commit_plan`/`git_review_scope`. |
| `agents/list`, `agents/wait` | `ReadOnly` / `Auto`, `is_read_only_for = true` (hidden replay compatibility tools). In-process read-only child coordination views; never spawn, wake, message, or cancel workers. |
| `task_list`, `task_read`, `pr_attempt_list`, `pr_attempt_read` (`tasks` read actions) | `ReadOnly` / `Auto` (`TasksTool::READ_ACTIONS`). Pure in-process `TaskManager` reads. |
| `automation_list`, `automation_read` (`automation` read actions) | `ReadOnly` / `Auto` (`AutomationTool::READ_ACTIONS`). Pure in-process `AutomationManager` reads. |

### Intentionally left as `ToolCategory::Unknown` (held for explicit review)

| Tool / Target | Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| `image_ocr` | Spawns external OCR binaries (`tesseract` / macOS Vision) and can fall back to the DeepSeek OCR API over the network. |
| `image_analyze` | Declares `ReadOnly` without `Network`, but uploads local image bytes over HTTP to a vision model endpoint. |
| `pandoc_convert` | Declares `WritesFiles` + `RequiresApproval` (`ApprovalRequirement::Suggest`) and spawns external `pandoc`. |
| `pr_attempt_preflight` (`tasks{action:"pr_attempt_preflight"}`) | Explicitly excluded from `TasksTool::READ_ACTIONS`; spawns `git apply --check` and declares `ApprovalRequirement::Required`. |
| `finance`, `verify`, `review`, `github_*` (`github_issue_context`, `github_pr_context`, `github_report_read`) | `ReadOnly + Network` surfaces reaching external HTTP endpoints, LLM APIs, or the `gh` CLI; kept held under `Unknown`. |
| Mutating / network siblings (`Git{action:"fetch"}`, `tasks` create/cancel/gate_run, `automation` create/update/delete/run, etc.) | Remain `Unknown` as before. |

## Where this came from

Closes #7407

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed
- `python3 scripts/check-dead-code-budget.py` — `[dead-code-budget] PASS: 109 suppressions (allow=79, expect=30), exactly at budget.`
- `python3 scripts/check-blocking-calls-budget.py` — passed (exit code 0)
- `codewhale-engine` unit tests compiled cleanly with `--deny=warnings` (`cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib`):
  - `core::authority` filter: `test result: ok. 120 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 7678 filtered out` (includes expanded `core::authority::tests::tool_category_keeps_deferred_read_only_tools_safe` verifying both `ToolCategory` and `AutoReviewPolicy::default().evaluate(...)` `Allow`/`AskUser` outcomes)
  - `authority` filter (with `RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608` and isolated `HOME`): `test result: ok. 196 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 7602 filtered out`
  - `auto_review` filter: 149 passed + re-run of `runtime_threads::tests::auto_review_force_prompt_is_denied_without_opening_a_modal` (`1 passed; 0 failed`)
  - `extension_host::tests::registry_` filter: `test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 7794 filtered out`

prs.body:
Bumps [parking_lot](https://github.com/Amanieu/parking_lot) from 0.12.5 to 0.13.0.
Release notes

Sourced from parking_lot's releases.

parking_lot-v0.13.0

  • Signficantly improved Mutex and RwLock performance under contention by deferring waking up parked threads until after the lock is released. (#545)
  • Added per-acquisition state to lock_api raw locks. RawMutex::Guard replaces GuardMarker; rwlocks have separate SharedGuard, ExclusiveGuard, and UpgradableGuard types. Unlock operations consume this state, while upgrade and downgrade operations return replacement state. Bump and raw condition-variable waits borrow and update the state. Consuming operations must release their acquisition on unwind; borrowing operations must restore ownership and valid state, or abort if restoration fails. (#544)
  • Raised the MSRV to Rust 1.95 and upgraded all crates to edition 2024. (#533)
  • Removed the hardware-lock-elision feature. (#533)
  • Removed automatic eventual fairness. Fair unlocking remains available through the explicit fair-unlock APIs. This removes UnparkResult::be_fair. (#533)
  • Removed the no-op lock_api/nightly feature. (#533)
  • Removed the legacy lock_api const_new methods and the redundant parking_lot const_* constructor functions; the corresponding new methods can be called in constant contexts. (#533)
  • Replaced the recursive read methods on RwLock with a dedicated reader-biased RecursiveRwLock type. The RawRwLockRecursive and RawRwLockRecursiveTimed extension traits have been removed from lock_api. (#533)
  • Added Once::new_completed for constructing a Once in the completed state. (#520)
  • Added Once::{is_completed, wait, wait_force} and the corresponding OnceState query methods. (#533)
  • Made additional lock, timeout, parking, and spin-wait accessors usable in constant contexts. (#533)
  • Added into_inner_with_raw to lock_api's Mutex, RwLock, and ReentrantMutex. (#524)
  • Added RawCondvar, RawCondvarTimed, and the generic Condvar wrapper to lock_api, and implemented parking_lot::Condvar using them. Custom raw condition variables may allow spurious wakeups; their notification methods must then return false or 0. parking_lot::Condvar still guarantees no spurious wakeups and exact notification counts. (#523) (#533)
  • Corrected the Send and Sync bounds of lock guards in lock_api. (#533)
  • Made RawMutex::is_locked and RawRwLock::{is_locked, is_locked_exclusive} required methods. (#533)
  • Renamed MappedRwLockReadGuard::try_map_or_else to try_map_or_err. (#533)
  • Clarified the safety requirements of raw lock implementations, including acquire/release synchronization, moving or dropping a locked raw lock, preserving the original lock mode on a failed upgrade, and stable thread IDs. Acquisitions may unwind without leaving a new acquisition held; consuming guard operations release their acquisition on unwind, while bump and wait operations must restore ownership or abort. (#533) (#544)
  • Clarified the aliasing requirements of unsafe raw-access, force-unlock, and guard-construction APIs in lock_api. (#533)
  • Guard unlocked and unlocked_fair operations now abort if re-locking panics. Default raw-lock bump implementations also abort if re-locking panics. (#533)
  • Guard with_upgraded operations abort if raw upgrading or downgrading panics, preserving continuous lock ownership. (#544)
  • Parking-lot operations in parking_lot_core are now guaranteed to never unwind. (#533)
  • Documented that parking-lot-based synchronization primitives must not be used

prs.title: chore(deps): bump rio-vt from 0.5.30 to 0.5.32
prs.body:
Bumps [rio-vt](https://github.com/raphamorim/rio) from 0.5.30 to 0.5.32.
Release notes

Sourced from rio-vt's releases.

v0.5.32

Full Changelog: https://rioterm.com/changelog

v0.5.31

Full Changelog: https://rioterm.com/changelog

Changelog

Sourced from rio-vt's changelog.

0.5.32 (2026-11-15)

  • Windows ships a modern ConPTY. The installer and the new portable .zip put conpty.dll and OpenConsole.exe from the Windows Terminal project (1.25, MIT) next to rio.exe, so Rio drives a current pseudoconsole instead of the one built into Windows: sixel, iTerm2 and kitty images render, the screen is restored when a TUI exits, and the IME candidate window follows the caret, with no manual sideload. The portable .exe remains for this release. Rio loads conpty.dll from its own directory only, so a copy on PATH is never picked up, and a pseudoconsole that fails to open or resize is reported instead of aborting Rio (#1767, #1764, closes #1759, #2031).

  • A long command can ring the bell or send a desktop notification when it finishes. The new [notify-on-command-finish] section is off by default (#2043). when is never, unfocused (the command's pane is not the one you are looking at: another window has focus, or another tab or split is active) or always. bell (default true) rings the bell through the [bell] settings, so the audio bell and the tab indicator follow them; notify (default false) sends a notification such as "Command Failed: Command took 2m 3s and exited with code 1."; after (default 5000) skips commands that ran that many milliseconds or less. It needs a shell that marks commands with OSC 133 C and D. Rio's zsh integration now sends those marks itself, so prompt navigation (ScrollToPrevPrompt, ScrollToNextPrompt) and this notification work in zsh with no setup: A and B around the prompt, carried inside PS1 so a redraw repeats them, P;k=s on continuation lines and PS2, C when a command line runs and D with its exit status when it ends. Hooks installed by your own rc files never see the marks, and a theme's PS1 is marked after the theme sets it. fish 4 already sends the marks; the PowerShell script still only reports the directory. librio hosts get Action::CommandFinished (RIO_ACTION_COMMAND_FINISHED, with the exit status in data_a and the duration in milliseconds in data_b).

  • librio: Sixel and iTerm2 images reach embedders, in one placement list with kitty. rio_render_state_image_count, rio_render_state_image_placement, rio_render_state_image_info and rio_render_state_image_rgba give every image placement on screen in draw order, each with its protocol, layer, z-index, viewport geometry, a change stamp to cache textures by, and RGBA pixels on request; rio_render_state_image_placements_generation says when the list changed so a host keeps its draw list otherwise. Sixel and iTerm2 pixels, which the terminal hands over once, were dropped by librio before; the rio_render_state_kitty_* calls stay as the kitty subset (#2045, closes #2034).

  • Rio no longer claims OSC 7501 support it does not act on. The program status query is answered only in librio hosts that set program_status_cb, and the reply lists the accepted states and kinds so a program can fall back (#2040).

  • More input bounds. An XTGETTCAP request over 1 MiB gets no reply and the next one is served normally; an OSC 8 hyperlink whose params and URI exceed 2047 bytes is ignored rather than opening or closing a link, and when id= repeats the last non-empty value wins; OSC 1337 SetUserVar is recognized and ignored instead of stored for the session, as other terminals do (#2042).

0.5.31 (2026-11-13)

  • OSC 8 hyperlinks keep their whole URI. Everything after the second ; is now the URI, taken verbatim, so a link like https://x.dev/a;b; no longer opens as https://x.dev/a, however many ; it contains (#1983). Clicking or hint-opening an OSC 8 link opens exactly what the program sent: post-processing (trailing punctuation, unmatched brackets) now only applies to regex matches. A URI with invalid UTF-8 starts a new link instead of being dropped, and an empty URI always closes the link, even when an id is given. The same parser change covers every OSC whose payload is free text, which used to be split on ; and cut at 16 parts: a window title (OSC 0/2) is kept exactly as sent, and one with invalid UTF-8 or over 255 bytes is dropped rather than shown as a guess; an OSC 7 or 9;9 working directory survives any number of ;, and an empty one clears the stored directory instead of leaving it stale; an OSC 9 or 777 notification shows its whole body, 9;4 progress splits as before, a bare 9;4 or 9;9 is a one-character notification, and the ConEmu sub-commands Rio does not implement are dropped instead of popping a notification with a junk body.

  • Pathological output can no longer exhaust memory or stall the parser. A long run of combining marks on one cell (e U+0301 repeated 65535 times with REP) took 8.6 s and 3.3 GB because every mark re-interned the cell's extras; a cell now keeps at most 64 marks and the same input takes 7 ms and 3 MB. An unterminated APC or OSC grew its buffer until the process died; sequences over 64 MiB are discarded whole and both buffers release capacity above 1 MiB between sequences, so one large image or paste no longer pins that memory. Kitty graphics chunked uploads follow kitty: one transmission in flight at a time, the declared S= size is no longer reserved up front (a bogus size tried to allocate gigabytes before any data arrived), and on Linux a FIFO under /dev/shm is rejected instead of blocking the parser (#2041).

  • librio: OSC 7501 program status reports reach the host. Programs report their state (idle, working, done, blocked, error, with a kind, a progress and a message) in one escape sequence, so a host can show which tab needs attention without per-tool hooks (#2039). Reports are validated against the spec (rev 0.4) with its size limits, and the host gets Action::ProgramStatus with the report, a prompt start on OSC 133 A/N and a reset on RIS; the C ABI adds program_status_cb. Rio's own windows do not display it yet.

  • 315be0f windows: load conpty.dll only from rio's own directory, keep the in-box resiz...
  • 312f62c windows: ship a modern ConPTY beside rio.exe for images, screen restore and I...
  • 8347333 librio: expose sixel and iTerm2 image placements alongside kitty (#2045)
  • 93983b7 osc 133: report finished shell commands, notify-on-command-finish (#2043)
  • d971083 rio-vt: bound XTGETTCAP requests and hyperlink lengths, drop SetUserVar stora...
  • 1e48195 osc 7501: answer the query only when the embedder handles reports (#2040)
  • aec5eb7 rio-vt: bound combining marks, APC size and kitty chunked uploads (#2041)
  • 57c49d0 osc: keep verbatim OSC payloads whole (#1983)
  • aaa6dc1 rio-vt, librio: support osc 7501 program status (#2039)
  • See full diff in compare view

  • Feishu/Lark bridge startup order is guarded. The bridge now keeps ThreadStore initialized before startup opens persisted thread state, with a regression test to prevent moving it below its first use.
  • /model picker opens instantly with the curated list again. Reverted the v0.8.38 live-catalog rework: the picker no longer makes a blocking network call on open and once again shows the curated auto / deepseek-v4-pro / deepseek-v4-flash rows. The /models command still lists the live provider catalog.

Denials keep the exact per-call fingerprint from #1617, so denying one call no longer over-blocks later, different calls to the same tool.
  • Docker first-run state directories are writable. The image now pre-creates /home/deepseek/.deepseek with deepseek ownership so the documented named-volume launch can create runtime thread state on first use (#1684).
  • Runtime API system prompt overrides survive the first turn. Threads created with a system_prompt override now keep that prompt through mode/context refreshes before the model request is built (#1688).
  • Compaction keeps a user text query in tool-heavy histories. Automatic compaction now pins the latest user text message when the retained tail only contains tool calls/results, avoiding OpenAI-compatible Jinja template failures on the next request (#1704).
  • Pager jumps land at the visible bottom. Pressing G or End in the pager no longer overshoots the render clamp, so k/Up scrolls upward immediately afterward, and mouse wheels now scroll pager overlays directly (#1706, #1716).
  • Mouse-wheel-as-arrow scrolling preserves composer drafts. When composer_arrows_scroll is enabled, Up/Down now scroll the transcript even with text in the composer instead of replacing the draft with input history (#1677).
  • Multiline composer arrows move between input lines. Plain Up/Down now move the cursor within multiline drafts before falling back to input history, while single-line mouse-wheel-as-arrow scrolling remains unchanged (#1721).
  • Third-party reasoning_content streams no longer corrupt text output. Generic OpenAI-compatible providers that stream answer text in reasoning_content now render it as normal text unless the selected provider is one whose reasoning-content semantics are supported (#1673).
  • macOS system theme detection recognizes Light mode. When COLORFGBG is missing or unusable, theme = "system" now falls back to macOS appearance detection and treats a missing AppleInterfaceStyle key as Light mode

prs.body:
Bumps [actions/setup-java](https://github.com/actions/setup-java) from 6.2.0 to 6.3.0.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/setup-java's releases.

v6.3.0

Behavior change: Java problem matcher is now opt-in

Starting with v6.3.0, setup-java no longer registers the Java problem matcher by default (#1326, fixes #1322). Java compiler warnings, compiler errors, and uncaught exceptions are no longer turned into annotations on pull request diffs unless you opt in.

To keep annotations, set problem-matcher: true:

- uses: actions/setup-java@v6
  with:
    distribution: temurin
    java-version: '25'
    problem-matcher: true

Compiler output still appears in the build logs, and compilation errors still fail the build. Only annotations are affected.

Why: inline annotations cluttered pull request reviews, and GitHub Actions caps annotations at 10 errors, 10 warnings, and 10 notices per step, and 50 per job. Larger Java builds therefore showed only a truncated subset of their diagnostics as annotations. See Java problem matcher (compiler annotations).

What's Changed

  • Architecture validation for JDK file installs by @​v-mahabaleshwars in actions/setup-java#1324
  • chore(deps): bump fast-xml-parser from 5.11.2 to 5.12.0 by @​dependabot[bot] in actions/setup-java#1323

prs.title: fix(execpolicy): bound repeated '--' deny-target expansion
prs.body:
## What and why

`Expander::record` in `crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs` previously invoked `record_extra_deny` for every unquoted `--` slice using a fresh child `Expander`, and each child re-scanned every remaining `--` in its own suffix. On a line with `m` `--` separators (`true -- a1 -- a2 -- ...`), that performed $O(m^{\text{MAX\_DEPTH}+1})$ redundant work even when `extra_deny` never hit `MAX_COMMANDS`.

This change bounds repeated `--` deny-target expansion:
- Reuses the active `Expander` in `record_extra_deny` (saving and restoring `dynamic`, `nested`, `arguments_dynamic`, `control`, `redirects`, and `deny_only`) so `extra_deny` and `seen_extra_deny` caps are shared across all `--` slices instead of resetting per child.
- Skips redundant `--` suffix re-scans inside `record_extra_deny` and launcher suffix recursive calls (`record_inner(..., false)`), since every remaining `--` in those suffixes is already visited by the parent loop at a shallower depth. Freshly parsed payloads (`expand` and `find -exec`) still scan their own `--` tokens.
- Short-circuits `expand`, `record_inner`, and the `--` loop once `extra_deny.len() >= MAX_COMMANDS` in `deny_only` mode, and memoizes the shallowest explored depth per `Line` in `seen_extra_deny_depth` (cleared between Windows passes) so repeated `eval -- eval -- ...` payloads remain bounded as well.
- Preserves existing deny-target emission and `dynamic` semantics, verified with a new regression test covering 512-segment `--`, 32-segment uncapped `--` ending in `rm -rf /`, repeated `eval`/`screen` `--`, nested `sh -c` after `--`, dynamic operands/heads, and Windows two-pass expansion.

## Where this came from

Closes #7400

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p codewhale-execpolicy`:
  - unit tests: `test result: ok. 248 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out` (includes new `shell_expand::tests::repeated_double_dash_segments_stay_bounded_and_preserve_deny_targets`)
  - `tests/authorization_order.rs`: `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed`
  - `tests/redirection_policy.rs`: `test result: ok. 11 passed; 0 failed`
  - `tests/shell_parse_policy.rs`: `test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed`
  - doc-tests: `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-execpolicy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (0 warnings in `codewhale-execpolicy`)
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

prs.title: ci(mirror): sync CNB and GitCode on every published release, with a half-hourly backstop
prs.body:
## What and why The CNB Cool (`cnb.cool/codewhale.net/codewhale`) and GitCode (`gitcode.com/HunterBown/Codewhale`) mirrors must stay current so users can always install and test the latest build. `main` pushes and `release.yml` already sync both mirrors, and both match `main` and `v0.10.2` today. Two gaps remain: a release published outside `release.yml` (its `GITHUB_TOKEN` publication fires no event), and a push or release whose sync never ran or failed. - `sync-cnb.yml` and `sync-gitcode.yml` now also run on `release: published`. Prereleases are skipped, as in `release.yml`. - Both workflows also run at :17 and :47 each hour. This backstop re-mirrors `main` and copies the **latest published GitHub Release** tag when a mirror lacks it, then verifies it with `verify-remote-tag.sh`. - On CNB the tag starts CNB's release build, so the run checks the release with `verify-release-inventory.js` before pushing. - If the CNB tag is already there, the run also requires its `codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt` to be downloadable. - Tags are never forced, and prereleases or tags still awaiting publication are never copied. Nothing creates a tag or release. A tag that differs on a mirror fails the run. `CNB_MIRROR` and `GITCODE_MIRROR` still switch the mirrors off. - `docs/CNB_MIRROR.md` (+ zh_hans) now describes these triggers. It no longer claims `fix/*`, `rebrand/*` or `work/v*` branches are mirrored, and it names GitCode as the second mirror, which carries source only. - No changelog hunks: per CONTRIBUTING.md, the entry is written on `main` at merge time. ## Where this came from Founder request to keep the CNB and GitCode mirrors updated in real time. This is a CI and docs change with no issue. The app mirror and the setup doc are in [codewhale-app#3577](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale-app/pull/3577) and [codewhale-ops#24](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale-ops/pull/24). ## How I tested it - `actionlint` on `sync-cnb.yml`, `sync-gitcode.yml` and `release.yml`: exit 0. - `node .github/scripts/release-workflows.test.js`: exit 0 ("17 checks passed"). - `verify-remote-tag.sh` for `v0.10.2` against cnb.cool and gitcode.com: OK (`ff466b2ed0`). The CNB `v0.10.2` manifest returns HTTP 200, and a wrong SHA exits 1. - Not verified: the first scheduled run and a `release: published` run on GitHub. These can only run after merge. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves) - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [x] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) ---

prs.title: 0.10.3 lane 8 batch 2: stop the repeated `--` stall in command policy
prs.body:
## What and why `f553b4a033` **repeated `--`**: each unquoted `--` makes `record_extra_deny` expand the suffix after it, and each child `Expander` then walked every later `--` again. Expansion time grew about 2.7× per pair of `--`: `npm` followed by 24 `--` took about 14 s, and 50 still hadn't finished after 20 minutes. Found by the adversarial review of #7385 ([comment](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7385#issuecomment-7004281767)); main `c5b484aa6` has the same problem. `record_extra_deny` now shares a map from each suffix (words, dynamic/odd/quoted flags, `literal_backslashes`) to the shallowest depth it was expanded at. The map is moved into each child and taken back afterwards. A suffix already expanded at the same or a shallower depth is skipped. Every suffix is still expanded at its shallowest depth, and its deny lines still reach the top expander. This is the first slice of lane 8's second batch, cut from `main`. More execpolicy follow-ups will stack here; the ones that touch the launcher arm wait for #7385. ## Where this came from Bug fix. Refs #7283, #7284 ## How I tested it On Linux x86_64: - `cargo test --locked -p codewhale-execpolicy`: 268 passed, 0 failed (246 unit, 1, 11, 9, 1 doctest). - The new test `repeated_double_dash_expands_in_bounded_time` runs `echo` and `npm` with 40 `--` and checks that `rm -rf /` is still a deny command. It passes in under 5 s. With the skip disabled, it was still running when `timeout` killed it at 120 s. - `cargo clippy --locked -p codewhale-execpolicy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p codewhale-execpolicy -- --check` and `sh scripts/sync-changelog.sh --check` are clean. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves) - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (n/a) ---

prs.title: fix(engine): distinguish missing tool-call fallback ids from literal call ids
prs.body:
## What and why

Both the streaming decoder and the non-streaming `chat/completions` parser synthesized `call_{index}` for a tool call that arrived without an `id`. A provider that literally sent `call_1` alongside an id-less call at index 1 therefore produced a duplicate pairing id, and `validate_tool_call_ids_for_protocol` rejected the whole turn.

This changes both fallback paths to the reserved `call_missing_{index}` prefix, so a synthesized id cannot collide with a provider's own `call_<n>` namespace. Duplicate detection and every other behavior stay unchanged.

## Where this came from

Closes #7402.

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib fallback_id_does_not_collide` — 2 passed (new mixed literal/fallback tests for streaming and non-streaming)
- `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib assigns_unique_fallback_ids` — 2 passed (existing uniqueness regressions)
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- The wider `--lib fallback` filter also selects unrelated existing tests that overflow the stack in this Windows debug build; none of them are touched by this change.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` — not applicable, this is an internal parser fix

prs.title: test(tui): prove raw and bracketed pastes stay lossless past 64 KiB
prs.body:
﻿## What and why

#7403 reports that a raw (non-bracketed) paste larger than `PASTE_BURST_MAX_BYTES` (64 KiB) loses its tail silently. I went looking for the drop and could not find one: main already turns the cap into a *chunk size* rather than a data limit — `PasteBurst::take_chunk_if_full` hands a full buffer to the caller, `FlushResult::TextContinuation` marks the remainder of an already-chunked paste, and all three raw-paste call sites in `crates/tui/src/tui/paste.rs` commit the chunk with `insert_str` before buffering continues.

What was actually missing was evidence. Nothing asserted the issue's acceptance criteria, and the existing large-paste tests stop at ~80 KiB — barely past the first chunk boundary, so a regression at the second or fourth chunk would not have been caught.

This PR adds the two regression tests the issue asks for, and nothing else. No product code changed.

## Where this came from

Refs #7403

## How I tested it

Two new tests in `crates/tui/src/tui/paste.rs`:

- `raw_paste_of_a_quarter_mib_lands_complete_in_the_composer` — drives a 256+ KiB payload through `handle_paste_burst_key` one key event per character, commits each chunk the way the event loop does, and asserts the composer holds every byte and the cursor lands at the end. The payload mixes ASCII, CJK and an astral-plane emoji, so a byte cap mistaken for a char cap shows up as a length mismatch instead of a passing test.
- `bracketed_and_raw_paths_agree_on_a_quarter_mib_payload` — pins the issue's second criterion: `insert_paste_text` and the raw path must deliver byte-identical text for the same payload, so chunking can never make one path preserve less than the other.

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
  -> clean

cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib paste -- --skip credential_paste_content
  -> test result: ok. 62 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
     (includes both new tests)

cargo test -p codewhale-tui-kit -- paste
  -> 17 passed; 0 failed
```

Two pre-existing failures in this environment, both reproducible on unmodified `main` and unrelated to this change:

- `tui::ui::tests::credential_paste_content_never_enters_traces_or_rendered_status` overflows its stack (`0xc00000fd`) on Windows; it fails the same way when run alone.
- `cargo clippy` stops in `crates/runtime/src/child_env.rs:811` (`chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`) and `crates/sandbox` before reaching `codewhale-tui`, because `[workspace.lints.rust] warnings = "deny"` promotes the lints added in clippy 1.100.0. Neither crate is touched here.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover the behavior
- [ ] Not a user-facing feature change, so no `docs/features.toml` row

prs.title: feat(tui): CW-8264 settle flash, plus the two v3 TUI fixes main lacks
prs.body:
## What and why This PR targets `main` (`c5b484aa6`, which has release-prep v2 squashed in as #7386). It contains three commits: 1. `fe717a57b` fix(tui): fold plain `task_shell_wait` polls into the shell's own row (carried from v3 `66699e11e7`) 2. `172f6b352` fix(tui): hold the composer border still while the transcript is scrolled away (carried from v3 `394d88c951`; the measured cause of the Terminal.app flicker from CW-8264 `ef51913d63`) 3. `8d7945310` feat(tui): flash a tool row's outcome once when it settles (CW-8264, new) v3's third commit, `4bee24fd7d` (Terminal.app scrollbar inset), is deliberately left out. codewhale-ops CURRENT_DECISIONS §231 drops it and keeps the scrollbar flush with the right edge. Commit 3: CW-8264 asks for color-coded running → done/failed transitions with a brief flash. `ef51913d63` (now on main) added the running-row sweep and breathing composer border. A finished row still switched to `done` in one silent repaint, though. `apply_settle_flash` runs on the visible lines after the transcript cache, so it invalidates nothing. It reads the existing `active_tool_entry_completed_at` timestamps and adds no new state. For 680 ms (2 × `MOTION_DURATION_PANEL_MS`, ease-out from `ACTIVITY_SWEEP_PEAK`), a row's status mark, family glyph and outcome word blend toward `tool_success` or `tool_failed`. A failed row whose ink is already `tool_failed` lifts toward `text_body` and back. Shell rows flash only the mark and, on failure, the `failed` word. The summary, path and command never flash. The contrast guard in `activity_sweep_ink` still applies. The `activity_sweep_allowed` gate turns the flash off under Reduced/Still, `fancy_animations = false`, sub-truecolor terminals, `NO_COLOR` and non-RGB themes. A visible flash keeps the 66 ms tier for its 680 ms only; activity motion requests no frames at idle. Design note with frames, reduced-motion path and perf budget: codewhale-ops `design/TUI-ACTIVITY-MOTION-20261119.md` ([ops #37](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale-ops/pull/37)). ## Where this came from Linear CW-8264 (TUI: a working session looks dead). `ci/cw-8264-motion-v3` and `claude-CW-8264-motion` are earlier versions of `ef51913d63` and do not contain the settle flash. ## How I tested it These runs were on `5d870582f`, which has the same settle-flash patch on the v3 base. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `sh scripts/sync-changelog.sh --check`: up to date (this head). - `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- settled_tool_rows`: 1 passed, 0 failed (new regression test; renders real generic success and failed rows and a failed shell row, and checks that the summary or command never changes and nothing is left behind at 680 ms) - `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- tui::widgets:: tui::history tui::transcript tui::ui::motion`: 479 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored - Two independent exact-SHA LAND reviews and a live TUI recording are in progress. ## Checklist - [x] Focused change on current `main` - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [x] No new feature flag or command, so no `docs/features.toml` row ---

issues.title: `openclaw update` 2026.11.3 → 2026.11.5: the baseline capture walks every file of the protected roots, and the DB set is copied 5 times; our window took 5409 s

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: clawsweeper:source-repro
labels.description: ClawSweeper found a high-confidence source-level issue reproduction.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦞 diamond lobster
labels.description: Very strong issue quality with high-confidence source-level or clear reproduction.

labels.name: maturity:stable
labels.description: Broken existing behavior primarily owned by an M4/M5 scorecard surface.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.11.5 (e13cf15), npm install, `openclaw update --tag 2026.11.5 --admission installed --no-restart --yes`, Gateway stopped for the run, Linux (WSL2), Node 26.12.1.
**State:** SQLite 6 DBs, 603.8 MiB (state 189 MiB, main agent 328 MiB, title-gen 73 MiB, 3 small agents), `~/.openclaw/credentials` 13 MiB in **3012 files** (3008 of them WhatsApp Baileys signal-store JSON under `credentials/whatsapp/default/`, 14 B to 140 KiB each), `telegram/` 2 files.
**Result:** the update succeeded, but `openclaw update` ran 5409 s (90 min) with the Gateway down; the Gateway was down 97.75 min in total (stop 07:48:02, health 09:25:47). The 2026.11.3 update on the same host took 4887 s.

## What the updater printed, and what it does and does not mean

### 1. "SQLite state schema inspection for credentials/whatsapp/default/<file>.json: 158 B, budget 301 seconds" (×3008, twice)

- **Verified in our run log** (`20261118T074732-run-2026.11.5.log`): before `Phase: requested` there is one such line per file, 3017 distinct paths (3008 WhatsApp files, `browser-extension-relay.secret`, 2 `telegram/` files, 6 `.sqlite`); the same 3008 lines appear again inside `openclaw doctor --fix` ("Preserve original state").
- **Where they come from** (2026.11.5 dist): `update-recovery-baseline-capture-DmtlIUpU.mjs:195-238` walks every protected root recursively (`readdir`, `visit()`), collects every regular file (`S`), SQLite files by header (`T`), and passes `additionalFiles: [...S.keys()]` to `createUpdateDatabaseBackup`; `update-database-backup-Rhmovy56.mjs:336,358,372-385` appends them to the database list (`T = [...discovered, ...additionalPaths, ...additionalFiles]`, sizes read in `readUpdateStateDatabaseSizes(T)`) and hands the list to `runUpdateStateInspectionWorker` as `databases`; `update-candidate-state.inspection-Buya4MQI.mjs:92` calls `resolveAggregateSqliteInspectionTimeoutMs("state schema inspection", e.databases)`.
- **Correction to how it reads:** "budget N seconds" is a **timeout allowance**, not elapsed time. `sqlite-readonly-worker-DLU0Tq7U.mjs:218-239`: `allowance = 300 s + ceil(40 × size / 32 MiB) s`, the debug line is printed whenever the allowance exceeds 300 s (so for any non-empty file), and `resolveAggregateSqliteInspectionTimeoutMs` **sums the allowances of all listed files**. For this tree that is ≈ 3017 × 301 s ≈ 910 000 s (10.5 days) as the timeout of one worker (arithmetic; the clamp `MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS = 2147e6` ms = 24.8 days, `number-coercion-D6u-4YD8.mjs:67,125-130`, is not reached). The lines are arithmetic in the parent, not work: the 3008 lines inside Doctor sit between two 10-second progress ticks (`Doctor: Preserve original state (54s elapsed)` at log line 4806 and `(64s elapsed)` at 7839), i.e. they took < 10 s.
- **So "3009 files × 301 s" is not a cost.** What it shows is that non-database files are put through the database path and that the worker's timeout stops meaning anything.

### 2. The actual time of `openclaw update` (5409 s), reconstructed from the report and file mtimes

The updater's own report (`update-reports/fb73e632-….md`): `Phases: requested (17.86s) → staging (1.59s) → validating (2212.23s) → activating (1894.33s)` = 4126 s. The log carries no timestamps, so the rest is from our wrapper's clock and file mtimes:

| Span | Duration | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| start → `Phase: requested` ("pre-phase") | ≈ 1173 s (19.6 min) | 07:48:49 start; report time 09:17:08 − 4126 s = 08:08:22 |
| – baseline capture `fb73e632…` (manifest `createdAt` 07:49:27 → manifest written 08:08:15) | 1128 s | `manifest.json` mtime; `database.databases` last write 08:07:15; `payload/` 3018 files written 08:06:09 → 08:07:44 (95 s) |
| validating | 2212 s | of which the 10 timed steps add up to 455 s (`updater-runtime-retention` 45.9, `package-install` 29.3, `candidate-state-snapshot` 48.8, `candidate-doctor` 188.4, `candidate-doctor-lint` 59.2, `candidate-gateway-startup` 76.3, small ones 7): **1757 s of the phase are in no timed step** (INFERENCE: between `candidate-state-cleanup` and `Phase: activating` the log only shows 2 × `[update/package-integrity] reader-started/settled`, `Package publication recovery`, and a 414.7 MiB `update state inspection`; where the time goes cannot be told without timestamps) |
| activating | 1894 s | `database snapshot` 884.4 s + `openclaw doctor` 524.3 s = 1409 s; 485 s untimed |
| after activating (plugin convergence, exit) | ≈ 101 s | 09:17:08 → 09:18:49 |

The same pre-phase appears in our 01:00 attempt (rolled back by us, an unrelated `managed-service-preflight` failure): `openclaw update` started 01:01:56 and failed at admission 01:23:49 = **1313 s** before any phase work.

### 3. The same DB set is copied/inspected 5 times (Verified) and two copies are very slow (Verified), the cause is unknown

Distinct full copies of the ~600 MiB DB set, from the log (sizes as printed):

1. baseline capture `~/.openclaw.update-captures/fb73e632…/database.databases`: 976.0 MiB basis, 33 progress lines, 07:49:53 → 08:07:15 (**≈ 1000 s**, DB part of the 1128 s capture; `du` of the capture dir is 615 MiB).
2. candidate canary `/tmp/openclaw-update-canary-SY1Csy`: 601.7 MiB; `candidate-state-snapshot` 48.82 s, of which the SQLite backup-API copies add up to 13.7 s (main 7.669 s, state 4.006 s, title-gen 1.678 s, 3 small 0.39 s; log lines 3212-3231).
3. `~/.cache/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-9i2WE1`: 601.8 MiB, 13 progress lines (log line 3140).
4. activation `database snapshot` = `.openclaw.package-backup-…databases`: 603.8 MiB, **884.38 s** (`update-command-post-update-CxP92Cxl.mjs:1994`, "snapshot databases before migrations").
5. Doctor's own "Preserve original state" capture `doctor-3360b07b…`: same 615 MiB and 3020 payload files, but **103 s** (manifest 09:19:20 → 09:21:03).

Plus partial reads of 414.7 MiB (`/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-wtEgMr`), 423.5 MiB and 610.4 MiB, and ~20 `read-only snapshot for state/openclaw.sqlite: 186.9 MiB` lines.

Two numbers stand out:
- **The same 615 MiB / ~3020-file capture takes 1128 s as the updater's baseline capture and 103 s as Doctor's capture** (same host, same state, 1.5 h apart; also 95 s vs 14 s for the 3018 payload files alone).
- **`database snapshot` 884 s vs `candidate-state-snapshot` 13.7 s** for the same databases: the candidate snapshot uses the SQLite backup API (`update-candidate-state-DZ6C1C7H.mjs:386`, "copying, attempt 1, 83984/83984 pages, 5.700 seconds"); the other two go through `createUpdateDatabaseBackup`.
- Cause unknown. INFERENCE only: load on the host (other processes were running; the Gateway was stopped) or the capture's integrity/verification passes (`integrityCheck: quick`) rather than the copy itself; the log has no per-step timestamps to separate them.

### 4. Our rehearsals did not reproduce it (Verified from the rehearsal logs, capture dirs and manifests; the cause is NOT found)

Two rehearsals of the same update on a full copy of this state (cold page cache, no network, dummy `credentials/whatsapp` of 3008 files and `telegram/` placed in the tree) ran `openclaw update` in 2011 s (channels `{}`) and 1732 s (the four channels enabled with dummy tokens), against 5409 s live. The updater's phases: `19.7 / 1.6 / 508 / 1138 s` and `19.4 / 1.6 / 435 / 982 s` (requested / staging / validating / activating) vs `17.9 / 1.6 / 2212 / 1894 s` live. Both rehearsal baseline captures (`createdAt` → manifest) took **171 s and 142 s with 7 payload files**; the window's took 1128 s with 3018. Neither rehearsal log has a single `state schema inspection for credentials/...` line, although the 3008 files were in the tree.
- **What differs for sure** (capture `manifest.json`): the live capture's `roots` / `protectedPaths` include `~/.openclaw/credentials` and `~/.openclaw/telegram`; the rehearsals' do not. Those paths come from `preparePluginDoctorMigrationBackupResources({ config: sourceConfig, ... })` (`update-recovery-baseline-capture-DmtlIUpU.mjs:121-135`; `doctor-contract-registry-DV0Hx1E3.mjs:643-656`), i.e. from the plugins' doctor **state migrations**.
- **Refuted:** that enabling the channels in the config is enough (rehearsal B: channels enabled, still 7 files).
- **INFERENCE, untested:** the WhatsApp/Telegram migrations declare their paths only for state in the format they migrate; our dummy files are not recognised. If so, the 3008-file walk is a consequence of an actual pending legacy-state migration, not of the tree's size.
- Not explained by file count alone: Doctor's own capture of the same 3020 files took 103 s.
- Not explained at all: validating +1700 s and activating +756 s over the rehearsals. The named steps add up to ≈ 450 s in both; the filesystem is the same; the data volume the snapshot lines print is the same. We cannot say more without timestamps in the updater's output (ask 3).

## Ask

1. **Treat non-SQLite files as files, not as databases**: pass only files that the header probe classified as SQLite (`T`) to the database inspection list and its timeout calculation, copy the rest as plain payload. The aggregate timeout over files is meaningless (≈ 10 days here).
2. **Reuse the baseline capture / one snapshot** instead of 5 copies of the same DB set: the capture taken at the start, the `database snapshot` before migrations and Doctor's own "Preserve original state" capture describe the same generation (`sourceGenerations`); reuse it when the generations are unchanged (the code already has `doctor-capture-reuse`).
3. **Put timestamps in the update progress lines** and a per-step duration for every step of `validating`/`activating`: 1757 s of `validating` and 485 s of `activating` are in no timed step.
4. **Say what the budget lines are**: "allowance", not "budget … seconds", or log elapsed time.

Related: #151546 (state schema inspection budgets on 2026.9.x).

issues.title: [Bug]: Mac app shows "Gateway update needs help" after every app update when the Gateway's --wrapper script is stored under ~/.openclaw

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: clawsweeper:source-repro
labels.description: ClawSweeper found a high-confidence source-level issue reproduction.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦞 diamond lobster
labels.description: Very strong issue quality with high-confidence source-level or clear reproduction.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
When the Gateway service starts through a `gateway install --wrapper` script stored inside the OpenClaw state directory, the Mac app ends its update flow in "Gateway update needs help: The installed Gateway service command could not be inspected", and Retry never clears it, although the Gateway is healthy.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install the CLI with npm and create an executable wrapper script at `~/.openclaw/service-env/my-wrapper.sh` that runs the working npm-installed CLI by its absolute path and forwards `"$@"`.
2. Register it: `openclaw gateway install --force --wrapper ~/.openclaw/service-env/my-wrapper.sh`. The LaunchAgent then runs `/bin/sh <env-wrapper.sh> <env-file> ~/.openclaw/service-env/my-wrapper.sh gateway --port 18789`.
3. Keep the default profile, the default CLI install policy (`exact`) and local connection mode.
4. Update the Mac app through Sparkle and let it relaunch.

### Expected behavior
The app treats this Gateway as externally managed and finishes the update without a recovery window. That is what happens with the same wrapper stored outside the state directory and the pending post-update record cleared: after moving it to another folder and running `gateway install --force --wrapper <new path>`, the app launched normally. The docs examples store wrappers in `~/.local/bin` (docs/cli/gateway/service.md, "Install with a wrapper").

### Actual behavior
The app opens "Gateway update needs help / Gateway verification failed" with:

> The installed Gateway service command could not be inspected.
> Repair this Mac app's managed installation, then retry recovery.

Retry shows the same window again, and it came back on every relaunch I observed. At the same time, `openclaw gateway status --deep` reports the Gateway running, connectivity ok, and CLI and Gateway versions matching.

### OpenClaw version
OpenClaw.app 2026.11.5 (first seen on 2026.10.10); CLI and Gateway 2026.11.6

### Operating system
macOS 27 (Apple silicon)

### Install method
Mac app + npm global CLI (Node 24 through nvm), Gateway as a LaunchAgent with a --wrapper script

### Model
Not applicable: the Mac app's post-update check, with no model call involved

### Provider / routing chain
Not applicable

### Logs
```shell
# LaunchAgent ProgramArguments (home directory shortened to ~)
/bin/sh
~/.openclaw/service-env/ai.openclaw.gateway-env-wrapper.sh
~/.openclaw/service-env/ai.openclaw.gateway.env
~/.openclaw/service-env/openclaw-nvm-node-wrapper.sh
gateway
--port
18789
```

### Impact and severity
- Affected: Mac app users whose Gateway LaunchAgent starts through a `--wrapper` script stored under the state directory. I observed it with the default profile (`~/.openclaw`).
- Severity: blocks the app's post-update flow. The window offers only a repair that cannot succeed.
- Frequency: every relaunch I observed after an update, until the wrapper was moved and the pending record cleared.
- Consequence: the user sees a "needs help" error for a healthy Gateway and has no way to clear it from the app.

### Additional information
Workaround: move the wrapper outside the state directory (for example `~/.local/libexec/openclaw/`), run `openclaw gateway install --force --wrapper <new path>`, then clear the pending post-update record with `defaults delete ai.openclaw.mac openclaw.postAppUpdateReceipt` and relaunch the app.

Cause, from reading `apps/macos` on main: two checks disagree about the same LaunchAgent.
- `CLIInstallPrompter.launchAgentUsesManagedCLI` counts any executable under the state directory as app-managed, except `tools/node/`. An operator wrapper there passes, so `PostUpdateController.ownsManagedRuntime` is true.
- `GatewayLaunchAgentManager.installedServiceCLI` only parses `node|bun <entrypoint> gateway`, so for `<wrapper> gateway ...` it returns nil.
- `resolveGatewayAction` then returns `.managedRuntimeUnavailable`, which is the dead-end window.
- That window also marks the stored update record as incomplete. So it returns on later launches, and the flag carries into the next app update. Once the service is seen as external, an incomplete record leads to "The Gateway could not be checked" instead, the state described in #169919.

Related: #169919. A fix with a test is ready, and I'll link the PR here.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.11.5, Slack Socket Mode input processing became stuck with `Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input`; retry counters reached 59 and 60, a Gateway restart did not restore processing, and operator intervention using `operator-skipped` restored service.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

This is a production incident report, not a deterministic reproduction. The observed incident and recovery sequence was:

1. Use OpenClaw 2026.11.5 with Slack Socket Mode on macOS 27.2.1, with a local Strata model backend.
2. During the incident, Compaction timeouts and repeated pending-input idempotency conflicts were observed.
3. Slack ingress retry counters reached 59 and 60.
4. Restart the Gateway: the stuck input processing did not recover.
5. Apply operator intervention using `operator-skipped`: service recovered.

The precise initial trigger, ordering of the first timeout versus first input conflict, elapsed outage duration, and exact recovery command are not established in this report. The counters are reported values, not a claim that there is a configured 60-attempt limit.

### Expected behavior

PR #193602 documents recovery of the same channel message after a failed, unconsumed attempt. A recoverable first-attempt failure should allow subsequent redelivery to run rather than repeatedly reject the same input. This is a reference to the intended behavior in that PR, not a claim that its fix was shipped in our installed build.

### Actual behavior

- Repeated `Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input`.
- Slack input processing remained stuck through retry counts of 59 and 60.
- Compaction timeouts were also observed during the incident.
- Gateway restart did not restore service.
- Service resumed only after operator intervention using `operator-skipped`.

The relationship between the Compaction timeouts and the input conflict is unknown. We have not established a transcript sequence collision, an external CLI transcript writer, changed request hashes, or the pending-input row state for this incident.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (reported installed version; exact installed commit and local modifications not verified)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1; Apple M1 Max, 64 GB unified memory

### Install method

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Model

`strata/qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs` (configured primary model in the environment record; effective model for each failing attempt not independently verified)

### Provider / routing chain

Slack Socket Mode -> OpenClaw Gateway -> local Strata OpenAI-compatible endpoint

### Logs

Exact reported error text:

```text
Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input
```

Reported observations, not verbatim log lines: retry counters 59 and 60; Compaction timeout; recovery using `operator-skipped`.

Raw logs, database dumps, message contents, and configuration files are not attached. This report is based on operator observations and the environment record; no new live reproduction was performed for filing.

### Impact and severity

The affected Slack workflow stopped processing normally and required manual recovery. Gateway restart alone was insufficient. One incident is reported here; recurrence rate and the number of affected messages are not established. Recovery by skipping an input restores service but does not demonstrate that the skipped message was processed successfully.

### Additional information

Related upstream work, checked on November 18, 2026:

- #193602 is **closed/merged** (November 5, merge commit `cb719feef55c307d473129525a41ec3ebdf1d0d6`). It addresses cancelled, unconsumed channel inputs being rejected on redelivery with a new run ID. Its documented scope excludes interrupted rows and changed request bytes; it does not fix the underlying transcript sequence collision.
- #199155 remains **open**. It documents a separate established trigger involving an external CLI transcript write and a resident Gateway actor. We link it because the downstream error and restart-resistant retry behavior overlap; we do not claim the same initial cause here.
- #199155 also has a stable-2026.11.5 Slack Socket Mode report: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/199155#issuecomment-6962955004. That contributor reports the #193602 logic is absent from the published stable bundle. This is external evidence, not an inspection of our installed bundle.
- Comparing the #193602 merge commit with `v2026.11.5` returns diverged ancestry, so that merge commit is not an ancestor of the release tag. This alone does not rule out an equivalent backport.
- #199365, the candidate fix for #199155, remains **open/unmerged**. No confirmed release date for resolution of this incident was found in the reviewed threads.

This is a new follow-up to the merged #193602, recording this operator's Slack/local-model incident and recovery. Please link or consolidate it with #199155 if maintainers establish the same root cause. Please clarify which published version contains the channel-redelivery fix and whether the Compaction/restart recovery path needs separate handling.

Privacy: credentials, tokens, workspace/channel/user IDs, event/run/session IDs, message contents, private URLs, machine names, and user-specific filesystem paths are omitted.

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: clawsweeper:source-repro
labels.description: ClawSweeper found a high-confidence source-level issue reproduction.

labels.name: impact:auth-provider
