issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` on the bundled `minimax` provider (`api: "anthropic-messages"`) intermittently fails tool-calling turns with a terminal argument-validation rejection. The Gateway logs it as:

```
[provider-error] Model request failed sessionKey="agent:main:main" runId="0ddcc441-…" requestId="…:model:57"
  requestNumber=57 provider=minimax model=MiniMax-M3.1-Flash name=Error
  code=malformed_tool_call_arguments causeCode=malformed_tool_call_arguments
  responseId=074e800fa73d93aeb04d5c92b2ca88e3
```

and the run ends with `isError=true`, `failoverReason=unknown`, and the user-facing `⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply.`

The same request against `minimax/MiniMax-M3` on the identical provider entry, account profile, and route never produced this error. Across the whole journal the split is **81 occurrences on `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`, 0 on `MiniMax-M3`** — but the same fleet ran **2,540 successful tool calls** on `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` that same day. So this is **not** a 100% failure and not a provider-wide outage: it is an intermittent, model-specific rejection, roughly **75 rejections against ~2,540 completed tool calls** (~3%) on 2026-11-19, concentrated in the largest sessions.

Two points of evidence, in case they save someone time:

- The `responseId` here does **not** mean MiniMax rejected the request server-side. It is set from the Anthropic-style `message.id` on `message_start`, so it only proves a response was started. The rejection is raised locally, after the stream completes, by the terminal argument validator.
- The failure is therefore at OpenClaw's terminal tool-call argument validation, not at the provider's request boundary.

### Steps to reproduce

Not deterministic. Observed across production traffic rather than a scripted minimal repro:

1. Configure the bundled `minimax` provider with `api: "anthropic-messages"` and expose both `MiniMax-M3` and `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`.
2. Run tool-using turns on `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` in a session with an accumulating context and a wide tool surface (my affected sessions carried ~700k-token contexts; cron jobs carried large system prompts).
3. A tool call whose streamed argument buffer fails terminal JSON validation is rejected. The turn ends with `stopReason=error`, no visible output, and `⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply.`
4. The identical workload on `MiniMax-M3` does not reproduce.

I attempted a scripted repro on 2026-11-20 and **could not reproduce it**: 5 subagent runs on `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (single `ls`; single `exec` with embedded quotes/backslashes/JSON; 4 KB `write` with quotes and escapes; 6 KB `write` with 40+ backslash-bearing lines) all completed normally with `stopReason=stop`. So the trigger is not a plain single-tool-call payload and I have not isolated it.

### Expected behavior

A tool call whose arguments do not parse should either (a) be repaired/recovered so the turn continues, or (b) fail with the bounded diagnostics that classify the defect (`argumentChars`, `argumentHash`, `repairAttempted`) attached to the user-visible failure. Today the failure is terminal and the diagnostics never reach the log.

### Actual behavior

- The turn terminates: `stopReason=error`, no assistant output, `failoverReason=unknown`, `⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply.`
- No fallback model is consulted even when `agents.entries.<agent>.model.fallbacks` is configured. `failoverReason=unknown` — not `null`, not a recorded "no fallback" reason.
- **The bounded diagnostics are dropped.** `errorBody` carries `argumentChars` / `argumentHash` / `repairAttempted`; the journal line shows only `code`, `causeCode`, `responseId`. `argumentChars` has 0 occurrences in the journal, so no operator can tell truncation from an unencoded buffer.
- **A scheduled job that writes its state file before the model call loses the alert permanently.** The run dies at the provider error, after state was written; the next run's dedupe sees the state and suppresses the re-emit. 10 distinct cron job IDs and 41 distinct sessions were affected; 758 tool calls still completed inside those same affected sessions.

### OpenClaw version

`2026.11.6` (`06afb10`)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Linux 7.0.0-43-generic x64

### Install method

npm global (`openclaw@2026.11.6`)

### Model

`minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (control: `minimax/MiniMax-M3`)

### Provider / routing chain

`openclaw -> minimax` — bundled provider, `api: "anthropic-messages"`, `baseUrl: https://api.minimax.io/anthropic`, `timeoutSeconds: 180`. Direct, no proxy or router in between.

### Additional provider/model setup details

One `minimax` provider entry carries both models under the same auth profile (`minimax:global`), with no `compat` overrides set on either model. Config shape (redacted):

```json
{
  "models": {
    "providers": {
      "minimax": {
        "baseUrl": "https://api.minimax.io/anthropic",
        "api": "anthropic-messages",
        "authHeader": true,
        "timeoutSeconds": 180,
        "models": [
          { "id": "MiniMax-M3", "...": "..." },
          { "id": "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash", "...": "..." }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Timeline observed:

| Window | Observation |
|---|---|
| First occurrence | 2026-11-17 23:35:55 ET — `agent:main:cron:wsb-sentiment-monitor`, request #41 |
| Peak | 2026-11-19 02:04 → 22:40 ET — 75 rejections |
| 2026-11-19 16:00 → 23:00 | 60 rejections, all `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`; same window, `MiniMax-M3` had 14 provider errors (HTTP 429) and **0** malformed-argument rejections |
| After 2026-11-19 22:40 ET | 0 further occurrences in the journal |

### Logs

Verbatim from `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway.service`:

```
Nov 19 14:25:06.490-05:00 [provider-error] Model request failed sessionKey="agent:main:main" runId="0ddcc441-6301-4118-b8fb-2395178aa57c" requestId="0ddcc441-6301-4118-b8fb-2395178aa57c:model:57" requestNumber=57 provider=minimax model=MiniMax-M3.1-Flash name=Error code=malformed_tool_call_arguments causeCode=malformed_tool_call_arguments responseId=074e800fa73d93aeb04d5c92b2ca88e3
Nov 19 14:25:06.509-05:00 [telegram] embedded run agent end: runId="0ddcc441-6301-4118-b8fb-2395178aa57c" isError=true model=MiniMax-M3.1-Flash provider=minimax failoverReason=unknown
```

User-facing result for that turn:

```
error="⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply. For details, open Settings → Logs in the Control UI or run `openclaw logs --follow` in your terminal."
```

Per-model totals across the entire journal (both models served the same fleet concurrently):

```
$ journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway.service | grep malformed_tool_call_arguments \
    | grep -o 'model=MiniMax-[A-Za-z0-9.-]*' | sort | uniq -c
     81 model=MiniMax-M3.1-Flash
      0 model=MiniMax-M3
```

Denominator for the same 2026-11-19 00:00→23:00 window: 2,540 completed tool calls, 75 rejections (~3%).

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO — no SSE capture is attached. OpenClaw does not persist the raw provider stream by default, and the terminal diagnostic that would identify the damage class (`argumentChars` / `argumentHash` / `repairAttempted`) is not present in the log line, so I cannot distinguish truncation from a never-JSON-encoded buffer from the outside. The raw rejected buffer would need to be captured (e.g. via the debug proxy described in #178907) to classify it.

Relevant source locations, for anyone triaging:

- `packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.ts` → `parseTerminalToolCallArguments()` throws with `errorCode = "malformed_tool_call_arguments"` and cause `{ code, argumentChars, argumentHash, repairAttempted }`.
- The Anthropic transport calls it with `{ repairStringLiterals: true }`, so the narrow string-literal-escape class is already repaired before rejection. What survives that repair is a different structural class (truncation, or a buffer that was never JSON-string-encoded).

### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** any deployment using `minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` on the bundled `minimax` provider (`anthropic-messages` route). Every agent on the fleet was hit — main chat, `research`, `qa-coder`, and 10 distinct cron jobs.
- **Severity:** high for unattended cron jobs (silent alert loss, no failure visible to the user); medium for interactive sessions (recoverable by re-prompting, but the reply is lost).
- **Frequency:** intermittent. 81 rejections total across 2026-11-17 → 2026-11-19, against 2,540 completed tool calls in the 2026-11-19 window alone (~3% of tool calls). Clustered in the largest sessions.
- **Consequence:** lost user-facing replies; silently lost cron alerts on the next run; wasted quota on the retry that also fails.

### Additional information

**Related issues, and why none of them cover this case:**

- **#155457** — "Agent tool calls to Anthropic intermittently fail with malformed streamed JSON arguments on large edits." Closest match by symptom and root cause (eager/fine-grained tool-input streaming skips server-side JSON validation; the client-side `repairJson` pass fixes only a narrow class). But it is scoped to `api.anthropic.com` with `claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-opus-5`, it was **closed 2026-11-06 as not planned** after a staleness notice — explicitly "the reported problem has not been confirmed fixed" — and it asks for a supported switch to disable eager/fine-grained tool-input streaming. That ask is still open, and it maps directly onto this report: the `minimax` provider is **not** `anthropic`, so `getAnthropicCompat()` defaults `supportsEagerToolInputStreaming` to `true` (`model.provider !== "fireworks"`), and the Anthropic-messages transport then sends `eager_input_streaming: true` on every tool. MiniMax's Anthropic-compatible endpoint has its own implementation of that beta, and OpenClaw cannot validate the resulting buffer before dispatch. A per-model `compat.supportsEagerToolInputStreaming: false` override would let an operator opt out — the field exists in the model registry (`AnthropicMessagesCompatSchema.supportsEagerToolInputStreaming`) but there is no documented way to set it for a bundled provider.
- **#178907** — "MiniMax M3.1 Flash (Ollama Pro) tool calls fail 100%." Different provider (`ollamapro`, `openai-completions`), different error surface (`Provider returned an incomplete or malformed tool call`), and reported as 100% reproducible — which does **not** match what I observe.
- **#160669** (closed) — M3.1-Flash on the OpenAI-compat route; the reporter closed it asserting the **anthropic-messages route is clean**. This report is on the anthropic-messages route, so that closure is contradicted for this model/route combination.
- **#135111 / #147040** — same error text, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`. #147040 was closed as implemented via #164274 (bounded continuation after settled tools).
- **#148257** (closed) — the design discussion for Anthropic-doc-style recovery (`INVALID_JSON` tool_result feedback, bump-budget retry). That recovery shape was never implemented; it remains the most likely durable fix.
- **#199537** (open) and **#201104** (closed) — the *continuation* path for a malformed call after a failed tool. Same symptom family, different trigger.
- **#193200** (merged) — coerces quoted tool arguments in OpenClaw's own validator. Not applicable here: the rejection happens at terminal argument validation, before the schema validator runs, and the `errorCode` is the terminal-argument code rather than a schema-type code.

**Questions:**

1. Can a provider-side rejection of this shape be classified **retryable / failover-eligible** so a configured fallback model is consulted instead of terminating the turn? Today `failoverReason=unknown` and the fallback chain is not engaged.
2. Can the bounded diagnostics (`argumentChars`, `argumentHash`, `repairAttempted`) be surfaced in the `provider-error` log line? Without `argumentChars` this class is not classifiable from the outside — this is the same ask #155457's reporter made and it is still unanswered upstream.
3. Should `compat.supportsEagerToolInputStreaming: false` be a documented per-model override for bundled non-`anthropic` providers that implement the Anthropic Messages API? #155457 asked for the equivalent switch for `anthropic`; the same reasoning applies to `minimax` and any other Anthropic-compatible endpoint whose implementation of the streaming beta differs.
4. For scheduled runs, should the delivery check happen **before** the state file is written (or be rolled back on a failed delivery), so a provider error cannot permanently suppress an alert? This is a distinct OpenClaw-side defect from the provider rejection, but it is what turns an intermittent 3% rejection into a silent, permanent loss.

**Note on evidence:** counts are from `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway.service` on the affected host. `status=200` never appears in that journal, so a per-request success rate cannot be derived from it; the denominator above is tool calls that actually completed, not HTTP responses. No raw argument payloads, session transcripts, or credentials are included in this report.

issues.body:
We want an enrolled user to text an iMessage project number and reach their own OpenClaw installation. The receiving gateway would use its existing linked person, current administrator role and private Knowledge permissions. Multiple installations can share the project number. Removing the link or demoting the person should take effect on their next private message.

On stock OpenClaw 2026.11.6 we exercised the published Photon 0.2.3 (Beta) and tagged 0.1.1 (Stable) receive handlers. Our disposable native profile store contained a person linked to the exact synthetic channel, account and sender ID. The permitted DM reached the reply dispatcher with the expected sender. The unlisted DM was dropped. Neither accepted context carried a requester profile, and neither handler called the registered host ingress resolver. These were offline synthetic inputs, not live provider events. A clean 0.2.3 ClawHub install loads as a community plugin with a clean scan and does not receive official-install trust.

What supported integration should the channel maintainers target for this on current OpenClaw?

1. For direct delivery over an authenticated provider connection, what sender/audience evidence and installation source would let a maintained external channel use native linked-requester authority? Are any phone-number channels already qualified on a published version?
2. If a project receiver routes an event to one of several installations, does OpenClaw support preserving verifiable original sender, private audience and destination provenance across that hop? If this mode is intentionally unsupported, it would help to know that before building a connector.

A successful test would read and save a synthetic private fact and perform a harmless owner-only operation from a real owner's DM. An unlinked sender, group, or revoked owner must not inherit those rights. We are looking for the supported integration or contribution route. The related provider-side question is [photon-comm/openclaw-photon#11](https://github.com/photon-comm/openclaw-photon/issues/11). [Channel identity documentation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/user-model#channel-identity-links).

issues.body:
### Summary

Measure and ship further lean-only reductions that pay for themselves.

### Problem to solve

Even the lean prototype idles at about 528 MiB after a fresh start and about 680 MiB after work, against 419 MiB on v2026.7.1. Its remaining always-on workers and native costs haven't been tuned.

### Proposed solution

Measure each candidate separately on top of lean, and ship only those with a clear RSS saving and an acceptable trade-off:

- the stall flight recorder off in lean (~106 MiB native measured on a large deployment);
- the session-archive worker started on demand and retired when idle (~48 MiB heap);
- the small always-on helpers (watch I/O, native lifecycle, heartbeats) consolidated where safe (~46 MiB heap total);
- lower V8 heap limits for lean and its workers;
- deferring code that compiles over time after startup (~45 MiB of main-isolate code growth by 35 minutes idle).

### Alternatives considered

None yet. Results go here.

### Impact

Could bring lean idle close to the 7.1 level. That's an estimate, pending measurement.

### Evidence/examples

Lean prototype per-worker heaps: session-archive 48 MiB, state heartbeat 19, watch I/O 9, native lifecycle 9, stall observer 8, gateway heartbeat 9. Main-isolate retained heap grew about 77 MiB between a fresh start and 35 minutes idle, mostly compiled code.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, for the candidates that measure well.

### Additional information

Part of #202373.

issues.title: [Bug]: Gateway logs "shutdown completed cleanly" then never exits — process killed by systemd SIGKILL on every restart (2026.11.6, Linux/systemd)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: impact:crash-loop
labels.description: Crash, hang, restart loop, or process-level availability failure.

labels.name: maturity:stable
labels.description: Broken existing behavior primarily owned by an M4/M5 scorecard surface.

issues.body:
## Summary

On SIGTERM (both `systemctl --user restart` and config-change restarts), the Gateway shuts down successfully — it logs `shutdown completed cleanly in 1665ms` — and then **the process never exits**. There is no further log output until systemd's `TimeoutStopSec` elapses and sends SIGKILL. Every restart therefore costs the full stop timeout, and the gateway is always hard-killed rather than exiting on its own.

This is distinct from #153899 (drain never finishing while closed-resource timers keep firing): here the drain **does** finish quickly and cleanly; the process simply stays alive afterwards with an empty log.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.11.6 (06afb10)**, installKind=package, npm
- Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (x64), WSL2 on Windows 11 host
- Node **v24.22.1** (`--max-old-space-size=14058`)
- systemd `--user` unit `openclaw-gateway.service`, `Restart=always`
- ~35 enabled plugins (feishu channel, memory-lancedb, lossless-claw, composio, sherpa-onnx-tts, typesafe, onnx, etc.)
- Gateway RSS ≈ 2.9 GB; `Threads: 42`; startup log reports `worker startup state: {"workerCount":20,...}`
- Child processes present at runtime: `dist/process/spawn-broker/worker.js` and a persistent `@esbuild/linux-x64/bin/esbuild --service`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the gateway under systemd with `Restart=always` (default unit from install).
2. Let it become healthy (`GET /health` → 200).
3. `systemctl --user restart openclaw-gateway`.
4. Observe `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway -f`.

## Expected

The process exits after the clean shutdown completes; systemd starts the new instance immediately.

## Actual

```
12:57:44.648  [admission] closed: restart-signal fence
12:57:44.648  [admission] closed: stop (SIGTERM)
12:57:44.648  [gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
12:57:44.896  [gateway] shutdown budget at shutdown: drain=14744ms shutdown=24744ms reserve=10000ms exitMargin=5000ms; source=systemd user openclaw-gateway.service TimeoutStopUSec=30000000
12:57:46      [gateway] shutdown completed cleanly in 1665ms
              ... 28 seconds of silence (process alive, nothing logged) ...
12:58:14      systemd: openclaw-gateway.service: State 'stop-sigterm' timed out. Killing.
12:58:14      systemd: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
12:58:14      systemd: Started openclaw-gateway.service
```

With the default `TimeoutStopSec=60` the identical pattern produced a 57-second silence instead:

```
12:45:25  received SIGTERM; shutting down
12:45:27  shutdown completed cleanly in 2063ms
12:45:27  shutdown step shutdown.gateway-close settled after 1027ms
          ... 57 seconds of silence ...
12:46:24  State 'stop-sigterm' timed out. Killing.  (SIGKILL)
```

Measured impact (external stopwatch around `systemctl --user restart`):

| TimeoutStopSec | stop phase | `restart` returns | health 200 again |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60s | 60s (SIGKILL) | ~61s | ~67s |
| 30s | 30s (SIGKILL) | 30.4s | 36.9s |

## Analysis / hypothesis

- The shutdown pipeline itself is fine: admission closes, connection work settles, plugin registry closes, memory managers close, `shutdown completed cleanly` is logged in ~1.7–2.1s.
- After that, the Node event loop apparently still has live handles, so `process.exit` is never reached: 20 `worker_threads` (per `worker startup state: {"workerCount":20}`), the `spawn-broker` worker child and a persistent `esbuild --service` child are the prime suspects. A `worker_threads` pool that is not `terminate()`d keeps the loop alive indefinitely.
- The drain budget is derived from `TimeoutStopSec` (`drain = timeout - 10000ms reserve - 5000ms exitMargin`), so shrinking the timeout does not fix the exit path; it only shortens the SIGKILL wait.
- Hard-killing during/after shutdown has not produced visible state corruption here (SQLite WAL; `openclaw doctor` is clean afterwards), but it means every restart is a kill -9 of a process that believed it had closed cleanly.

## Workaround in use

systemd drop-in `TimeoutStopSec=30` (halves the dead time; drain adapts to 15s). Not a fix — the process still never exits by itself.

## Related

- #153899 — drain waits out the full TimeoutStopSec because closed-resource timers keep firing (different signature: in this report the drain completes, then the process hangs with **no** log output)
- #200148 — macOS in-process restart (SIGUSR2) hangs forever after a failed close (pid alive, no force-exit)

## Ask

Please make the shutdown path terminate `worker_threads`/child pools explicitly (or `unref` them) and/or force `process.exit` once `shutdown completed cleanly` has been logged, so a clean stop actually exits instead of being SIGKILLed.

---

*Reported from a live WSL2 install; full journal excerpts and the reproduction command can be provided on request.*

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Upgrading a stable install that has heartbeats explicitly disabled to a 2026.11.5 beta cannot succeed without either side effects or a failure:

1. With the disabled heartbeat still configured (`agents.defaults.heartbeat: { agentId: "<agent>", every: "" }`), the candidate updater's admission check refuses the update: `Update refused: configuration is invalid ... agents.defaults: unrecognized key "heartbeat"`. The candidate's own Doctor knows how to retire this key (its docs say Doctor removes `agents.defaults.heartbeat` and `agents.entries.*.heartbeat`), but admission rejects the config before Doctor gets the chance.
2. If the operator follows the hint and unsets the key on the installed stable release, that release falls back to its default heartbeat interval. In our case 2026.11.3 immediately enabled a 30-minute heartbeat automation for the default agent, and on a second machine it created 26 system-owned heartbeat jobs within two seconds of the unset. So removing the key to satisfy the beta re-enables the very thing it was disabling.
3. With the key unset, a later attempt (2026.11.3 to 2026.11.5-beta.2) passed admission but failed in the candidate Doctor's final config validation, reporting `Unrecognized key: "heartbeat"` at `agents.defaults` and at three `agents.entries.<id>` paths, none of which existed in the authored config (`openclaw config get` reported all of them unset). The stable release synthesizes default heartbeat config at runtime while the beta does not, so the candidate may be validating runtime-materialized defaults. That part is not proven, because the updater removes the failed candidate directory.

### Steps to reproduce
- macOS 27.2.1 arm64, Node 26, npm global install, explicit multi-agent roster, SQLite state.
- Installed stable: 2026.11.4 (d843d6a), also reproduced from 2026.11.3 (847611d).
- Config: `agents.defaults.heartbeat = { "agentId": "<agent>", "every": "" }`; `openclaw health` reports `Heartbeat interval: disabled`.
- Run `openclaw update --tag 2026.11.5-beta.4 --accept-capabilities`.
- Result: `Admission checks: config: refuse, node-runtime: ok` / `Failed: candidate-admission (invalid-config)` / `agents.defaults: unrecognized key <key>`. The installed version stays on 2026.11.4 and remains healthy.
- Same result with 2026.11.5-beta.2.
- Then `openclaw config unset agents.defaults.heartbeat` on 2026.11.3: `openclaw health` changes to `Heartbeat interval: 30m (<agent>)` and an enabled `heartbeat-<agent>` automation appears.

### Expected behavior
Admission should accept the retired heartbeat keys (or defer them to Doctor) when the candidate's Doctor migrates them, so a disabled heartbeat stays disabled through the upgrade. If there is a reason admission must refuse, the hint should not tell operators to unset a key whose removal changes behavior on the installed version.

### Actual behavior
- 2026.11.5-beta.4 from 2026.11.4: `Admission checks: config: refuse, node-runtime: ok`, `Failed: candidate-admission (invalid-config)`, `agents.defaults: unrecognized key <key>`. Installed stable stays healthy.
- Unsetting the key on stable (2026.11.3) enables a 30-minute default heartbeat automation.
- With the key unset, 2026.11.3 to 2026.11.5-beta.2 passed admission but candidate Doctor's final validation rejected `heartbeat` at `agents.defaults` and three `agents.entries.<id>` paths that were not in the authored config.

### OpenClaw version
Installed 2026.11.4 (d843d6a), also 2026.11.3 (847611d); targets 2026.11.5-beta.4 and 2026.11.5-beta.2

### Operating system
macOS 27.2.1 (arm64)

### Install method
npm global, Node 26, LaunchAgent Gateway service, SQLite state

### Model
anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (Claude CLI runtime); not model-specific

### Provider / routing chain
Anthropic via Claude CLI, OpenAI Codex fallback; not provider-specific

### Additional provider/model setup details
Stable 2026.11.3 synthesizes a default heartbeat from Anthropic config defaults when none is authored; the beta's config defaults no longer do. That may be how the beta.2 rehearsal saw heartbeat keys absent from the authored file (unproven: the updater deletes the failed candidate directory).

### Logs
Redacted excerpts only; raw configs, update captures and support JSON contain credentials and are not attached.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
- Restoring the disabled heartbeat object on the stable release returns health to `disabled` and removes the extra jobs.
- In an isolated scratch state, the beta's `doctor --fix` correctly retires the disabled heartbeat object and the config then validates, so the migration itself works; the problem is ordering between admission and Doctor (and possibly runtime-materialized defaults in the rehearsal config).
- Related: #181130 (legacy heartbeat migration without blocking startup), merged before these betas; #200083 (failed HEARTBEAT.md archive write blocks the Doctor heartbeat migration), a different failure in the same migration.
- Raw configs, captures, and support JSON are not attached because they contain credentials; redacted excerpts available on request.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On my Mac Studio, the OpenClaw update from 2026.11.3 to 2026.11.5 installed the package but failed activation with update-executor-settlement-failed and state-migrated-no-rollback after a SQLite lock and schema verification error, and openclaw update repair --json still reports “Another update executor owns this installation” even though the Gateway is stopped, the recorded updater processes have exited, and the shared lease store reports no owner.

[openclaw-diagnostics-2026-11-21T02-57-46-736Z-94588.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35200109/openclaw-diagnostics-2026-11-21T02-57-46-736Z-94588.zip)

### Steps to reproduce

1. On the affected Mac Studio after the dashboard update from 2026.11.3 to 2026.11.5 failed activation, quit the OpenClaw desktop app and confirm openclaw gateway status --deep reports LaunchAgent (not loaded) and Runtime: stopped.
2. Run openclaw update repair --json.

### Expected behavior

openclaw update repair should complete pending repair for the installed version when it can safely acquire ownership, or report the specific condition preventing recovery. The failed update explicitly directed me to run this command after resolving the data-risk condition. 

### Actual behavior

The package activation status reported publication-complete, but post-update verification failed with This OpenClaw build cannot open your existing data; subsequent repair attempts returned Another update executor owns this installation while the Gateway was stopped and the shared lease lookup for the npm installation returned absent.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (e13cf15) after the failed dashboard update from 2026.11.3 (847611d)

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple Silicon (arm64), Mac Studio.

### Install method

npm global under Homebrew at /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw, with a loopback Gateway managed by the ai.openclaw.gateway LaunchAgent.

### Model

None. The failing command was local update maintenance.

### Provider / routing chain

None. The failing command was openclaw update repair --json run directly in macOS Terminal.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Update reason: update-executor-settlement-failed
Recovery condition: state-migrated-no-rollback
Doctor reported: database is locked
Post-update verification: This OpenClaw build cannot open your existing data.
Package activation phase: publication-complete
Gateway status: LaunchAgent (not loaded), Runtime: stopped
Shared lease lookup: Installation lease: absent
Repair JSON: {"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"Another update executor owns this installation."}}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

[openclaw-diagnostics-2026-11-21T02-57-46-736Z-94588.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35201109/openclaw-diagnostics-2026-11-21T02-57-46-736Z-94588.zip)

### Impact and severity

Affects one observed Mac Studio installation. Repair was blocked on repeated attempts after one failed dashboard update. The update flagged a data risk, so I kept the Gateway stopped and the local OpenClaw agents unavailable while recovery remains unresolved.

### Additional information

The recorded updater PIDs had exited, the legacy handoff table was empty, and the installed build’s shared lease-store reader returned absent for /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw. Recovery snapshots were preserved. OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d) was the prior running version, and 2026.11.5 (e13cf15) was the first version on which I observed this repair failure.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

Setup provisions an enabled **Proactive check** (`createDefaultProactiveJob`, `src/cron/default-proactive-job.ts`):
every 30 minutes, an agent turn in the owner agent's main session, `skipIfScratchEmpty: true`,
`delivery: { mode: "announce", target: "owner" }`. On a Gateway with no channel that can reach the owner
(Control UI / API only), every run still sends the whole main-session prompt to the model and then records
`Owner delivery unavailable (no-route)`. The default job has no scratch, and missing scratch is not "empty",
so the skip never applies. The work is thrown away every time.

On a hosted model this is a steady token cost. On a local server it is worse: each run is a full prefill of a
prompt that grows with the main conversation, it holds one of the server's few parallel slots, and it evicts the
cached prompt of whatever conversation was using that slot. `idleOnly` only sees OpenClaw's own activity.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh setup with any model and no channels (`channels` empty, no `commands.ownerAllowFrom`).
2. Use the main session from the Control UI for a while.
3. `openclaw automations list --all` after a few hours.

### Expected behavior

With no owner route and no scratch checklist, the default check does not call the model (as the legacy heartbeat
did: `heartbeat skipped: no-route`, under a second, no model request).

### Actual behavior

Measured on one Gateway (2026.11.3 source build, fa155ff; the job definition and scratch check are unchanged on
main 3f078860b54) with a local llama.cpp server (2 slots of 65,536 tokens), over 6 days:

- 307 runs, one every 1,800 s; every run `lastDeliveryStatus: not-delivered`,
  `Owner delivery unavailable (no-route); configure an authorized owner DM or edit this automation's delivery`.
- 344 model requests from the job, median prompt 51,212 tokens, 57 above 60,000: 62% of all prompt tokens the
  server processed, about 22 minutes of GPU time a day.
- The same install on 2026.11.2 (legacy heartbeat) skipped every run with `heartbeat skipped: no-route` in under a second.

### Possible directions (maintainer choice)

1. Before execution, skip an owner-targeted run when the owner route does not resolve and there is no scratch
   or pending notice for that occurrence (record it as skipped with the reason), i.e. restore the old no-route
   skip for `delivery.target: "owner"` only.
2. At setup, provision the default job disabled when no owner route resolves, and have `doctor` suggest enabling
   it once one exists.
3. Let local providers use the existing `resolveProactiveCadenceMs` hook (only Anthropic implements it) for a
   longer default cadence.

Related: #134994 (retirement design), #201282 (draft that removes `idleOnly`/`skipIfScratchEmpty` and lets the
check overlap foreground work, which would make this more expensive on local servers), #197938.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3 (source, fa155ff); behavior confirmed in source on main 3f078860b54

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (aarch64)

### Install method

Source checkout (`node openclaw.mjs gateway`)

### Model

Local llama.cpp server, OpenAI-compatible (`api: "openai-completions"`), 74B model

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> custom openai-completions provider on loopback

### Summary

Keep Google Lyria music output-format support in one existing plugin-local owner, consumed by provider metadata and execution validation.

### Problem to solve

When maintaining Google music format support, developers currently update the same model policy in two places. The metadata builder advertises Clip as MP3-only and Pro as MP3/WAV, while the execution validator independently recreates those lists. This maintainer-requested cleanup consolidates that policy with unchanged output behavior.

### Proposed solution

Use a small resolver in the existing `extensions/google/generation-provider-metadata.ts` module and consume it from both the metadata builder and `music-generation-provider.ts`.

Preserve these contracts:

- Exact Pro model: MP3 and WAV; Clip and unknown models: MP3.
- Fresh independent format arrays for generate/edit metadata and separate metadata-builder calls.
- The current validation error text and awaited API-key resolution order.
- The separate Pro/WAV filename fallback, request construction, retries, and resource lifetimes.

Derive the resolver's return type from the already exported `MusicGenerationRequest["format"]` contract. Keep the change plugin-local with the existing SDK and dependency surfaces.

### Alternatives considered

Retaining both declarations leaves the maintenance duplication. A shared mutable format table would introduce aliasing between metadata instances; returning fresh arrays preserves their existing ownership.

### Impact

Affected workflow: maintaining the Google music provider's model-format declarations. This is an internal maintenance improvement with no requested user-visible behavior change or performance claim.

### Evidence/examples

At reviewed source revision `6b0df8b93610b320210488d93e6e205aafb84e69`:

- [Metadata format declarations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6b0df8b93610b320210488d93e6e205aafb84e69/extensions/google/generation-provider-metadata.ts#L119)

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

issues.body:
# Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash). Not known to be a regression: measured only on 2026.9.6; we did not test an earlier version.

# Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

The `agent_end` plugin hook fires once per **model attempt**, not once per run. When an attempt fails with a retryable provider error (HTTP 429), the embedded runner rotates the auth profile or falls back to another model and keeps going under the **same `runId`**, but every plugin has already received `agent_end` with `success: false`. `PluginHookAgentEndEvent` carries no field that distinguishes an intermediate attempt from the terminal end of the run, so a plugin that acts on `agent_end` (closing work, reporting failure, releasing claims) acts on a run that is still alive.

The emission is inside `completeEmbeddedAttemptAfterTurn` (installed bundle `dist/builtin-openclaw-*.mjs`), which runs at the end of each `runEmbeddedAttempt`:

```js
// async function completeEmbeddedAttemptAfterTurn(input, settled, prompt)
if (attempt.operation !== "settled-tool-finalization" && attempt.sessionPersistence !== "detached" && !beforeAgentFinalizeRevisionReason) {
	const lifecycleForAgentEnd = projectAgentRunAttemptTerminal(executionState.terminal);
	const agentEndError = promptError && !lifecycleForAgentEnd.aborted ? formatErrorMessage(promptError) : void 0;
	...
	runAgentEndSideEffects({
		...
		event: {
			messages: projectNestedToolActivityForHooks(messagesSnapshot, nestedToolActivities ?? []),
			success: !lifecycleForAgentEnd.aborted && !promptError,
			error: agentEndError,
			durationMs: Date.now() - promptStartedAt
		},
		...
	});
}
```

The failover decision (`embedded run failover decision: ... decision=rotate_profile|fallback_model`) is taken **after** this point by the outer run loop, so the hook cannot know whether another attempt follows. The hook contract:

```ts
type PluginHookAgentEndEvent = {
  runId?: string;
  messages: unknown[];
  success: boolean;
  error?: string;
  durationMs?: number;
};
```

has no `final` / `willRetry` / `attempt` field. `success: true` is always terminal in practice; `success: false` is ambiguous.

A second, smaller defect on the same path: `durationMs` is `Date.now() - promptStartedAt` of the attempt, so on a run with N attempts no hook event ever reports the run's duration.

Related but distinct: #132721 (Codex harness `agent_end` omits structured abort metadata). That one is about a terminal abort lacking classification; this one is about non-terminal attempts being reported as terminal.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register a plugin with an `agent_end` hook that logs `runId`, `success`, `error`.
2. Configure an Anthropic agent with two auth profiles (or a model fallback chain).
3. Start a turn while the first profile is rate-limited (429).
4. The runner rotates profile / falls back and the turn completes normally.
5. Inspect the hook log: `agent_end` with `success: false` arrived for the 429 attempt before the run actually ended.

## Expected behavior

Either `agent_end` fires once per run, after the failover loop has settled; or the event carries enough to tell the two apart, e.g. `final: boolean` (or `willRetry: boolean`) plus `attempt` index, with `durationMs` measured from run start on the final event.

## Actual behavior

Gateway journal, OpenClaw 2026.9.6, 2026-10-03 (America/Sao_Paulo), `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway`. 45 `embedded run agent end ... isError=true ... 429` lines that day. Four runs that **continued and finished normally** after the failed attempt:

```
15:56:56.490 [agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: runId=f38395ea-0306-478b-aa6e-b098a6b3db37 isError=true model=claude-sonnet-5-5 provider=anthropic error=⚠️ API rate limit reached. Please try again later. rawError=429: {"error":{"message":"This request would exceed your account's rate limit. ...","type":"rate_limit_error"},...}
15:56:56.607 [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: runId=f38395ea-... stage=assistant decision=rotate_profile reason=rate_limit attempt=1 retry=0 rotations=0
15:57:57.174 [agents/agent-command] [agent] run f38395ea-0306-478b-aa6e-b098a6b3db37 ended with stopReason=stop

17:22:57.548 embedded run agent end: runId=a2e8aa39-8768-411d-9a4d-8220bef928f4 isError=true model=claude-sonnet-5-5 ... 429
17:22:57.662 embedded run failover decision: runId=a2e8aa39-... decision=rotate_profile reason=rate_limit attempt=1
17:23:16.740 [agent] run a2e8aa39-8768-411d-9a4d-8220bef928f4 ended with stopReason=stop

17:26:10.091 embedded run agent end: runId=3d7ce67c-72b7-48b8-86e5-87269cea3b7a isError=true ... 429
17:26:10.201 embedded run failover decision: runId=3d7ce67c-... decision=rotate_profile reason=rate_limit attempt=1
17:27:29.265 [agent] run 3d7ce67c-72b7-48b8-86e5-87269cea3b7a ended with stopReason=stop

17:46:36.123 embedded run agent end: runId=09ac3887-6658-4c8f-b082-44f385cd6f79 isError=true ... 429
17:46:36.239 embedded run failover decision: runId=09ac3887-... decision=rotate_profile reason=rate_limit attempt=1
17:54:20.573 [agent] run 09ac3887-6658-4c8f-b082-44f385cd6f79 ended with stopReason=stop
```

The 09ac3887 run lasted 7 m 44 s after the first `agent_end`. One run shows the multiplicity directly — four failed-attempt ends under one `runId` in 5 s, before the real terminal failure:

```
17:16:43.342 embedded run agent end: runId=1da22a00-1959-464e-9916-e1ecf6d02e54 isError=true model=claude-sonnet-5-5 ... 429
17:16:43.465 embedded run failover decision: runId=1da22a00-... decision=rotate_profile reason=rate_limit attempt=1
17:16:44.494 embedded run agent end: runId=1da22a00-... isError=true model=claude-sonnet-5-5 ... 429
17:16:44.581 embedded run failover decision: runId=1da22a00-... decision=fallback_model reason=rate_limit attempt=2
17:16:46.234 embedded run agent end: runId=1da22a00-... isError=true model=claude-haiku-4-5 ... 429
17:16:46.348 embedded run failover decision: runId=1da22a00-... decision=rotate_profile reason=rate_limit attempt=1
17:16:48.298 embedded run agent end: runId=1da22a00-... isError=true model=claude-haiku-4-5 ... 429
17:16:48.371 embedded run failover decision: runId=1da22a00-... decision=fallback_model reason=rate_limit attempt=2
17:16:48.443 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ agent errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=All models failed (2): ...
```

Only the fourth of those is the run's end; a plugin sees four identical `success: false` events and cannot tell which.

Plugin-side consequence: our ticket-dispatch plugin treated the first `success: false` `agent_end` of these runs as the end of the agent's turn, while each agent went on to finish the work and report the ticket afterwards.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (`build-info.json` commit `eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b`)
- Linux 7.0.14 (Proxmox LXC), Node 24.21.0
- npm global install, systemd user Gateway
- Models: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 with fallback anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5; 2 Anthropic auth profiles

## Provider / routing chain

Gateway -> embedded agent runner (`runEmbeddedAttempt`) -> Anthropic Messages API; on 429 the outer loop rotates auth profile, then falls back model.

## Additional setup details

Local plugins: `backlog-v2` (ticket dispatch; consumes `agent_end` to close the ticket a session was working on), `nexus-context` (context engine). No dist patches touch the agent-end path. Our mitigation, in plugin code: on `success: false`, query the run registry for the session and ignore the event while the session's run is still live. That is a liveness poll standing in for a field the event should carry, and it races with registry teardown.

## Impact and severity

Any plugin that treats `agent_end` as "the run is over" misbehaves exactly when the provider is rate-limiting, which is when operators are least looking. For us: 4 runs on 2026-10-03 were treated as ended by the plugin while they were still working; it surfaced only when the agents' reports arrived after the plugin had already acted, and was diagnosed from the journal. 45 failed-attempt `agent_end` lines in one day on a single gateway means every such plugin is exposed daily.

## Summary The `file` secrets provider reads its JSON file through `readSecureFile()` with a hard-coded default timeout (`DEFAULT_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000`). During a cold 2026.11.6 gateway start, file I/O is busy enough (plugin module preparation plus agent-database startup preparation running at once) that reading a **581-byte** secrets file takes more than 5 s. The read is cancelled, and depending on timing, one of two things happens: 1. **The gateway aborts startup:** `Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable.` 2. **The gateway starts, but an agent database stays degraded until restart.** The agent cannot take sessions, and `openclaw secrets reload` does not recover it. Case 2 is the more serious one. The gateway reports as running and healthy at process level while the agent silently can't answer, with nothing to bring it back short of a restart. ## Environment - OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10), fresh `doctor --fix` migration from 2026.10.4 - Windows 11 Pro, Node 24.19.0, x64 - Profile with 2 agents (one OpenAI, one Ollama), plugins: comfy, memory-core, ollama, openai, tavily - `secrets.providers.local = { source: "file", path: "~\\.openclaw-\\secure.json", mode: "json" }`, refs used by `gateway.auth.token`, plugin API keys and a channel token ## Reproduction Three consecutive cold starts (`openclaw --profile

gateway --port `) of the same migrated state dir, nothing else changed between #2 and #3 except `timeoutMs`: **Boot #1:** gateway aborts ``` [secrets] [SECRETS_PROVIDER_DEGRADED] file:local: secret provider failed. Affected owners: cold capability:plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey, cold gateway:ingress-auth. Retry: openclaw --profile

secrets reload. Gateway failed to start: Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable.. Run openclaw --profile

gateway status --deep for diagnostics. ``` (stack: `handleSecretsActivationError` in `server-startup-config-*.mjs`) **Boot #2:** gateway listens after 41.6 s; agent `echo` never becomes writable ``` [state/agent-admission] agent database startup preparation still running agentId=echo phase=secrets elapsedMs=60027 phaseElapsedMs=14556 [state/agent-admission] agent database remains degraded agentId=echo paths=[".../agents/echo/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite"] reason="File provider \"local\" timed out after 5000ms. | secure file read timed out after 5000ms | timeout | timeout" repairHint="Sessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, run \"openclaw doctor --fix\" ..." [plugins] memory-core: standing intent maintenance failed: AgentDatabaseAdmissionError: Agent echo (...): File provider "local" timed out after 5000ms. <- repeats every 30 s, for 20+ min ``` `openclaw secrets reload`, run ~20 minutes later with the machine idle, prints `Secrets reloaded with 2 warning(s).`, but the gateway logs: ``` [secrets] [SECRETS_DEGRADED] cold route:~\.openclaw-

\agents\echo\agent\openclaw-agent.sqlite: secret resolution failed. ``` and the agent stays degraded. The other agent (`echo-gemma`), which was in `publication-wait` behind `echo` rather than in the `secrets` phase, recovered normally. **Boot #3:** with `secrets.providers.local.timeoutMs: 60000`, clean: listening in 24 s, both agent DBs "recovered after background inspection and preparation" ~1m40s after start, agent turns and tools work. The secrets file itself is fine: owner-only ACL, valid JSON, 581 bytes, and the gateway-level reload reads it in well under a second once the machine is idle. ## Expected A transient slow read of a small local file during startup should not permanently break an agent or abort the gateway. Any of these would fix it: - Retry the file-provider read (with backoff) when it fails with `FsSafeError` code `timeout` at startup, instead of failing the owner for good. - Let `secrets reload` (or the 30 s maintenance loop) re-resolve a `cold` / degraded agent-database route, so the agent recovers without a restart. Today the repair hint says to run `doctor --fix` and restart, which seems disproportionate for a read timeout. - Use a larger default for the `file` source (a local file read should only time out on a genuinely stuck filesystem), or don't start the timer until startup I/O has settled. ## Workaround Set `secrets.providers..timeoutMs` explicitly, e.g. `60000`. The option already exists and is honoured by 2026.10.4 and 2026.11.6. ## Related - #200617 (secrets disk I/O error on first start after a SIGKILL), a different trigger but the same "secret read failure at startup is fatal" shape - #166894 / #158592: earlier reports of agents left stuck until restart after a busy boot; this is another path to that outcome that 11.6's publication self-heal (#181300) doesn't cover

issues.body:
## Bug type
Behavior bug (regression of the yield path; related to #200475, #195864, #179486, but a different trigger).

## Version
OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (`06afb10`), Linux x64 container, channel `webchat` (Control UI), agent `main`, model `claude-cli` / `claude-opus-5-5`. Also seen on 2026.11.5.

## What happens
1. In a long main session (hundreds of turns, ~500k tokens), the agent calls `sessions_spawn` (visible child on another agent, `context: "isolated"`), then `sessions_yield`. The yield returns `{"status":"yielded"}`.
2. The Claude CLI writes its final assistant text (`stopReason: end_turn`, imported into the transcript), but the run never completes. After ~5 min: `cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli ... durationMs=310068 error=CLI plugin runtime did not close after its run ended.` The user gets `run-failed-before-reply`, so the final text is never delivered.
3. The child finishes normally. Its completion announce (`announce:requester-settle:...`) then fails the same way (~185s, `GatewayClientRequestError ... UNAVAILABLE`).
4. Every later user turn in that session fails the same way (~185s each). None of them logs a new `cli live session start`, so they appear to reuse the dead live session. Diagnostics show `stalled session ... classification=stalled_agent_run lastProgress=deferred_maintenance:wait_ended`, then `reply watchdog ... no_semantic_progress`.
5. Only a full Gateway restart recovers the session. In one earlier occurrence the session ended up in `stale_session_state` (still reported after 49900s).

With model fallbacks configured, the failed turns silently fail over to the fallback model instead.

## Reproducibility
3 occurrences in 3 different long sessions, all with the same spawn + yield sequence. A deliberate test on 2026.11.6 in a small fresh session passed twice (hidden child and visible child: the parent resumed with the child result and showed no stuck markers). So the bug seems to depend on session length/size, or on state that builds up over a long session, not on the yield alone.

## Expected
After `sessions_yield`, the CLI run closes, the final text is delivered, the child completion wakes the parent, and later turns get a working live session (or a fresh one if the old one cannot close).

## Workaround
Do not call `sessions_yield` from claude-cli agents. End the turn normally and let the child completion event wake the parent.

## Problem

Slack's native-data-blocks module combines pure block rendering with provider-HTTP rejection inspection. Rendering-only consumers import that module even when they only need detection, text fallback or accessibility output.

## Proposed change

Move the existing pure detection/stripping, base-text occurrence accounting, rendering, accessibility and fallback functions, together with the malformed-data fallback constant, verbatim into the existing blocks-fallback.ts owner. Retarget the internal imports without forwarding exports or a new public SDK surface.

Exact scope: 11 existing files under extensions/slack/src/:

- native-data-blocks.ts
- blocks-fallback.ts
- action-runtime.ts
- actions.ts
- edit-text.ts
- monitor/message-handler/preview-finalize.ts
- monitor/replies.ts
- native-data-fallback.ts
- reply-blocks.ts
- send.ts
- native-data-blocks.test.ts

## Preservation requirements

Keep all three error/response classifiers, the response-shape helper, and the bounded HTTP response reader unchanged. Preserve repeated-text occurrence accounting, malformed-data handling, accessibility text, fallback ordering and delivery behavior. Caller runtime bodies and existing test assertions stay unchanged.

No dependency, permission, response-limit, public API or delivery-policy change is proposed. No performance benefit is claimed.

## Validation plan

Run the existing Slack rendering/fallback and affected message, edit, reply and preview tests, then targeted types, lint, format and the applicable build. issues.body:
## Summary

On 2026.11.5 the Control UI **Sessions** sidebar renders only the agent headers (`RPK-16`, `QQ 潘多拉`) and **no session rows**, even with the owner filter set to **All owners** and **Status: All**. Clicking an agent row does nothing, and the console shows no functional error (only avatar 404/401 and performance violations).

The grouping mode is stored client-side (`openclaw:sidebar:sessions:grouping`) and **defaults to `category`**, but the Sessions filter panel exposes no control to change it. So a user whose sessions have no `category` cannot get a flat list through the UI at all.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | `2026.11.5 (e13cf15)`, npm global |
| OS | Windows 11 `10.0.26300` |
| Node | v24.22.1 |
| Agents | 2 (`main`, `qq-lite`) |
| Sessions in store | 23 (`openclaw sessions list --json`) |

## Reproduction

1. Have a multi-agent install with sessions that have no `category`/section assignment.
2. Open the Control UI, Sessions view.
3. Set owner filter **All owners**, Status **All**, enable automation/system sessions.
4. Observe: only the 2 agent rows render; 23 sessions do not.

## Evidence

### 1) The server returns all 23 rows

```powershell
openclaw gateway call sessions.list --params '{"source":"agent-roster","rowMode":"sidebar","limit":100,"offset":0}' --json
```

```json
{ "count": 23, "totalCount": 23, "sessions": [ ... 23 items ... ], "owners": [ { "id": "gateway-owner", ... } ] }
```

The gateway log for the UI's own request agrees:

```
⇄ res ✓ sessions.list 1835ms source=agent-roster rowMode=sidebar limit=100 offset=0
  filterKind=includeGlobal+includeUnknown+configuredAgentsOnly+archived bytes=71619
{"operation":"sessions.list","selectedRowCount":48,"materializedRowCount":25,"handlerOutcome":"returned"}
```

### 2) Sidebar rows carry no `agentId`

`rowMode=sidebar` row fields:

```
key, kind, updatedAt, sessionId, rowMode, participants, expandedParticipants,
lastReadAt, lastInteractionAt, lastActivityAt, lifecycleRevision,
childSessions, sharedFacts
```

No `agentId`. The default CLI mode (`openclaw sessions list --json`) **does** include it (`"agentId": "main"`), so the client cannot group by agent from the payload alone.

### 3) The two visible rows are the agents, not sessions

```
openclaw agents list
- qq-lite (QQ 潘多拉（受限）)
- main (default) (RPK-16（潘多拉）)
```

These match the two sidebar rows exactly. Their subtitles are last-message previews, which makes them look like conversations.

### 4) Grouping defaults to `category` and has no UI control

In `dist/control-ui/assets/control-ui-boot-shared-*.js`:

```js
function Pme(e){return e===`none`||e===`person`||e===`project`?e:`category`}
function Fme(e,t={}){let n=t.grouping??`category` ...}
if (n===`none`){i.push(t);continue}
```

Storage keys present in the same bundle:

```
openclaw:sidebar:sessions:grouping
openclaw:sidebar:sessions:catalog-grouping
openclaw:sidebar:sessions:sort-mode
openclaw:sidebar:sessions:collapsed-sections
```

The **Display** section of the Sessions filter panel only offers: sort by, message preview, **+ New section**, session source. There is no grouping selector, although `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` documents grouping as a Display setting.

### 5) Workaround that works

In the browser console:

```js
localStorage.setItem('openclaw:sidebar:sessions:grouping','none');
localStorage.removeItem('openclaw:sidebar:sessions:collapsed-sections');
location.reload();
```

After this, sessions list flat. This confirms the data and the render path are fine — only the default and the missing control are wrong.

## Expected behavior

One of:

- Default `grouping` to `none` (or to a mode that still lists sessions with no category), or
- Expose the grouping selector in the Sessions **Display** panel (matching the documented behavior), or
- Render the `ungrouped` bucket when it is non-empty rather than leaving only agent headers.

## Notes

- Related but distinct: #198515 (roster headers ignore "Last updated" sort), #196664 (group-first "All owners" view).
- Local dist patch used to confirm the cause (not a source proposal): changing the two `category` defaults to `none` in the bundle restores a flat list without any localStorage key.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior / recovery UX bug (Goal state remains paused; no crash or data loss established)

### Summary
In a built-in local session with an existing Goal paused after a terminal run error, work on the objective continued through same-session scheduled/delegated turns. The operator tried **Resume** in the Control UI. The UI showed an unconfirmed Goal update and told the operator to retry the same request. During this Resume recovery episode the Gateway returned quick `Goal is being admitted; retry the same request.` responses; an overlapping long attempt eventually returned `This session still has active or queued work. Wait for it to finish, then retry the Goal.`. A subsequent Goal read still reported `paused` with the original Goal ID. Repeated ongoing work in the same session makes the operator's requested Goal continuation hard to admit, even though work on that objective is visibly occurring.

### Observed sequence (one live incident; not an isolated reproduction)
1. A pre-existing built-in OpenClaw Goal became `paused` after a terminal model/tool request error. Its objective, ID and progress remained intact.
2. The same conversation continued handling user messages, a periodic agent-turn watchdog, and a delegated worker for that unfinished objective. These are not evidence that the Goal became active again.
3. The operator used the Control UI **Resume** control during this activity. A screenshot showed: `Goal update not confirmed. Check its outcome before making another change. Goal is being admitted; retry the same request.`
4. Sanitized Gateway responses on 2026-10-30, local UTC+04:

```text
22:35:52 sessions.goal.update 56ms UNAVAILABLE: Goal is being admitted; retry the same request.
22:36:07 sessions.goal.update 45ms UNAVAILABLE: Goal is being admitted; retry the same request.
22:36:08 sessions.goal.update 46ms UNAVAILABLE: Goal is being admitted; retry the same request.
22:37:33 sessions.goal.update 133456ms UNAVAILABLE: This session still has active or queued work. Wait for it to finish, then retry the Goal.
```

5. A read-only Goal check after these attempts still showed the same Goal as `paused`. No committed Resume or accepted continuation was verified. The session's separate scheduled/delegated work continued. The reporter did not verify a later successful idle Resume.

### Expected behavior
A paused Goal should have an actionable, unambiguous recovery path that preserves the Goal and the currently running work. If Resume cannot be admitted while another turn is active, the UI should distinguish an in-flight same-operation retry from a definitive busy refusal, reconcile the saved operation, and tell the operator when/how to safely resume. Alternatively, a single idempotent Resume could be admitted behind current work under the existing session authority and start only once it settles. Do not interrupt existing work, create duplicate Goal turns, or blindly clear recovery on an outcome that could have committed.

### Actual impact and limits
- The Goal stayed `paused` while independent same-session work on the objective ran. The user could not use the Goal's automatic-continuation semantics and received a confusing unconfirmed state followed by a busy refusal.
- Only one live incident is established. This does **not** prove a permanent Gateway deadlock, that the Control UI still retained its recovery record after the final busy response, or that a retry during a genuinely idle interval would fail. No isolated reproduction or patch is included.
- This is distinct from the closed #174656: that issue concerned UI classification of an immediate typed `goal-session-busy` refusal and was closed by #174683. Here the observed sequence began with the distinct `Goal is being admitted` response, included a long overlapping admission, and left the operator without a successful Resume while same-session work continued. Please link/merge if maintainers determine it is the same remaining edge case.

### Environment
- OpenClaw `2026.10.7 (44dd89b)`, built-in local runtime, Control UI and Gateway RPC `sessions.goal.update`.
- Linux x64 Gateway host; Node `v24.22.1`. Browser version was not captured.
- Model/provider are not material to these observed Resume RPC errors; the prior terminal run error only supplied the paused Goal precondition.
- Screenshot and raw logs are not attached because the session contains private material. The excerpt above omits identifiers, hostnames, account names and conversation content.

### Regression coverage suggested
Exercise an existing paused Goal with same-session queued/active work; exercise the in-flight `UNAVAILABLE: Goal is being admitted` response and the definite busy response during an overlapping Resume recovery episode. Assert that the UI never creates duplicate Goal turns, does not leave an ambiguous recovery fence for a definite non-admission, and offers an actionable path to activate the original Goal once the session is idle. Keep genuinely unknown transport/ACK outcomes recoverable by the original operation ID.

### Bug type

Behavior bug: GUI shows an attachment card, external Telegram does not receive it.

### Summary

On a **native Telegram turn** (not WebChat), `message(action=send, channel=telegram, target=<chat>, attachments=[local zip])` failed with:

```text
Session "agent:<agent>:telegram:direct:<chat>:thread:<chat>:<topic>" was not found.
```

The agent then emitted a final `MEDIA:<absolute path>` line. Control UI/GUI rendered the attachment card, but the Telegram topic never received the file. The user replied “waiting” in Telegram. No Telegram send receipt existed.

This is distinct from #198388 (WebChat targetless progress inheriting composite Telegram DM-topic `threadId`).

### Reproduction (sanitized)

1. Native Telegram DM forum-topic session, key shape `agent:<agent>:telegram:direct:<chat>:thread:<chat>:<topic>`.
2. Agent assembles a valid local ZIP (~1.8 MiB, three JPEG members, `zipfile.testzip()` clean) and calls:

   ```json
   {
     "action": "send",
     "channel": "telegram",
     "target": "<chat>",
     "message": "...",
     "attachments": [{"type":"file","media":"/abs/path/final.zip","name":"final.zip","mimeType":"application/zip"}]
   }
   ```

   (also tried without explicit `channel`)
3. Result, twice:

   ```text
   {"status":"error","tool":"message","error":"Session \"agent:<agent>:telegram:direct:<chat>:thread:<chat>:<topic>\" was not found."}
   ```
4. Agent falls back to final text containing `MEDIA:/abs/path/final.zip`.
5. GUI shows the attachment; Telegram user says the file is absent; no send receipt.

### Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.11.3` (`f521fcf`), Linux x64, Node 24.22.1, user systemd Gateway.
- Run/provider: `omniroute/nr-deepseek-41f` on the historical failing run; Codex runtime observed on the same session class during live diagnosis.
- Session was visible/readable through `sessions_list` / `sessions_history`; only the `message` send path reported the session as missing.

### Source-level trace (read-only)

- The exact error text is produced by `prepareInProcessSessionRead` in `src/gateway/server-plugin-in-process-session-read.ts` (`Session "${key}" was not found.`), used by in-process `sessions.get`.
- `message(action=send)` is dispatched through `message.action` (`src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.ts` → `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`).
- The failing call supplies a Telegram numeric `target` but no valid explicit thread; the session-key-derived implicit route points at the threaded Telegram session, and the session-read/projection lookup rejects it as not found.
- Final `MEDIA:` is parsed by `src/media/parse-output.ts` (`MEDIA_TOKEN_RE`) and can be projected to GUI without an external-channel send receipt.

### Expected

An explicit `message` send with a valid Telegram target and attachment either delivers to Telegram with a receipt, or fails before GUI projection with a clear actionable error. A final `MEDIA:` in a native Telegram session should either attach in Telegram or be surfaced as not-delivered.

### Actual

Tool error says the existing threaded session was not found; fallback `MEDIA:` renders only in GUI; Telegram gets nothing.

### Impact

Repeated file/zip delivery failures in native Telegram threads. Users see attachment cards locally but receive no file externally.

### Related

- #198388 — different WebChat composite `threadId` failure; do not conflate.
- #194024 — `Session ... was not found` family, but for subagent settle, not this message/attachment path.

No private chat IDs, names, photos, absolute paths, or transcript bodies are included.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let the Control UI image viewer step through all images in the chat and show a thumbnail strip for jumping between them.

### Problem to solve

Opening an image fullscreen in Control UI chat shows only that image with zoom (− / 100% / +), Download image, and close. Previous/next controls and the position counter (#151981, #152027) only appear when the opened message itself has several images. When the images are spread across messages (the common case: one screenshot per message), there is no way to move to the next or previous image without closing the viewer, scrolling, and opening the next one. With several images there is also no overview or way to jump directly to a specific one.

### Proposed solution

Use the Telegram desktop media viewer as the reference UX (screenshot below):

- Previous/next arrow buttons on the left and right edges that step through the images in the current chat (session), not only within one message. Left/Right arrow keys do the same.
- When there are several images, a caption such as "Photo 4 of 5".
- A small strip of thumbnails at the bottom, with the current image highlighted; clicking a thumbnail jumps to it.
- Existing zoom, download, close, swipe, and focus-return behavior stays as is.

### Alternatives considered

Keeping navigation scoped to a single message (current behavior) doesn't help when each image arrives in its own message. Grouping consecutive images into one row (#153222) reduces scrolling in the transcript, but the fullscreen viewer still can't move between messages.

### Impact

Affected: Control UI users reviewing several screenshots or generated images in a chat
Severity: Annoying (repeated close/scroll/open)
Frequency: Every time images are compared across messages
Consequence: Extra steps and lost context when going through a set of images

### Evidence/examples

Reference: Telegram desktop media viewer, with side arrows, a "Photo 4 of 5" caption, and a thumbnail strip at the bottom (personal details blurred):

![Telegram media viewer as reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/5f409f7a002b4712bf61c901a08b9d139f666381/2026-10-30/control-ui-lightbox-telegram-reference-viewer.png)

OpenClaw Control UI today (2026.10.7, Linux, Managed package installation, Gateway launched as a systemd service): a single image with zoom, Download image, and close only (private details blurred):

![Current Control UI image viewer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/98e5f2f98c7c0de0c92b07e0b12dda3bcce13c82/2026-10-30/control-ui-lightbox-openclaw-current-viewer.png)

Code pointer: the navigation buttons and counter only render when the viewer gets a gallery with more than one item ([`image-lightbox-content.tsx` L640-L671](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0dad367a93cb5669baf8ceda88d7f2c67353cc0f/ui/src/components/image-lightbox-content.tsx#L640-L671)), and the gallery is currently built from the opened message's attachments.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

I'm willing to implement this later if nobody picks it up, but not right away.

issues.body:
### Summary

Tell `agent_end` hooks when a durable context engine already owns the finished attempt, by passing `ctx.contextEngineTurn = { logicalTurnId, enginePluginId? }`.

### Problem to solve

A plugin that provides a durable context engine (`commitTurn`) often also registers an `agent_end` hook as the fallback that captures turns the engine does not own (degraded leases, native Codex, CLI runners). Today the hook context does not say whether the finished attempt was engine-owned.

So the plugin either captures engine-owned turns twice (once in `agent_end`, once in `commitTurn`) or guesses ownership from its own state. That guess goes wrong when a lease degrades mid-run, because the host's ownership decision is not visible to the hook.

### Proposed solution

When the embedded runner finishes an engine-owned attempt (the engine supports durable turn advancement, the lease is not degraded, and the user turn has an admission receipt), pass

```ts
ctx.contextEngineTurn = { logicalTurnId: string; enginePluginId?: string }
```

to `agent_end`. `enginePluginId` is set for plugin-owned engines.

Advertise this as the `hostRequirements` capability `agent-end-context-engine-turn-v1` for `agent-run`, so an engine can require it and be refused on hosts that do not provide it.

No new API. Attempts the engine does not own carry nothing, so existing hooks see no change. The field assigns capture responsibility only; it does not claim that retention has completed.

### Alternatives considered

- **Infer ownership in the plugin from its own lease state.** Wrong when the host degrades the lease mid-run; the plugin cannot see that decision.
- **Capture everything in `agent_end` and dedupe in the engine.** The hook has no key to dedupe on. `logicalTurnId` is exactly the missing key.
- **Drop the `agent_end` fallback.** Loses turns on runners the engine does not own.

### Impact

- Affected: plugins that provide a context engine with `commitTurn` and also capture turns in `agent_end` (memory and retention plugins).
- Severity: data quality. Duplicate captures, or gaps when the plugin's guess is wrong.
- Frequency: the duplicate-or-guess choice applies to every engine-owned turn; wrong guesses happen on mid-run lease degradation.
- Consequence: duplicated or missing turn records, and host-state guessing code in each plugin.

### Evidence/examples

Reference implementation, two commits on top of main (+265/-1, 9 files including `docs/concepts/context-engine.md`), with tests for the hook context, attempt finalization and capability advertisement:

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/main...vernmic:openclaw:promote/context-engine-agent-end-turn

- `feat(agents): carry context-engine turn identity into agent_end hooks`
- `feat(context-engine): advertise agent-end-context-engine-turn-v1`

We have run this in production on a fork since 2026-11-15 with a memory plugin's context engine.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

Happy to open the branch as a PR if the contract is acceptable. Backward compatible: unowned attempts and hosts without the capability behave as today.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A WhatsApp group's session acquires a spurious `conversations` row with kind="direct" but peer_id equal to the group's own JID, gets promoted to role="primary" in session_conversations, and every subsequent inbound message for that group then fails with `UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'idx_agent_conversations_identity'`.

### Steps to reproduce

No confirmed deterministic manual repro. Observed correlation (not proven causal) across two independent occurrences on the same long-lived WhatsApp group session, both times while Control UI/dashboard `chat.history`/`chat.metadata` RPC calls against that session were failing with errorCode=UNAVAILABLE, errorMessage="session history is rebuilding; retry shortly" — i.e. dashboard access to the session's history while the WhatsApp channel is actively processing a message for that same session.

### Expected behavior

Inbound messages for a WhatsApp group should always resolve to the existing kind="group" conversation row for that peer_id. No kind="direct" row should ever be created with a peer_id that is a group JID, and session_windows.chat_type for a group session should remain "group".

### Actual behavior

conversations table ends up with two rows for the same peer_id (120363429459936309@g.us): one kind="group" (correct, original) and one kind="direct" (spurious). The spurious row is promoted to session_conversations.role="primary" for the session, demoting the correct group row to role="related". session_windows.chat_type for that session then reads "direct" instead of "group". Every subsequent inbound message for the group fails with:
Error: UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'idx_agent_conversations_identity'
Reproduced twice in one calendar day on the same session_id, both times yielding the identical spurious conversation_id hash (conv_183828435603d295e6cd182f3d908148) — consistent with the conversation-ref hash being deterministic over (channel, accountId, kind, peerId, parentConversationRef, threadId), so the same wrong inputs regenerate the same wrong row.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.1 (first occurrence), 2026.8.2 (second occurrence, same day, after upgrading)

### Operating system

Windows 11 Pro

### Install method

npm global install (openclaw package). Gateway run as a Windows Scheduled Task service, loopback bind.

### Model

deepseek-v4-flash (custom-registered model entry, not in built-in catalog)

### Provider / routing chain

WhatsApp channel -> OpenClaw Gateway (local, loopback) -> agent "wa" -> DeepSeek API (openai-completions-compatible, api.deepseek.com). Fallback chain (gpt-5.4, claude-sonnet-5) not implicated; failure occurs at the conversation/session bookkeeping layer, before any model call.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Custom deepseek-v4-flash model entry with manually-declared contextWindow/contextTokens. session.dmScope="per-channel-peer". tools.sessions.visibility="self". tools.agentToAgent enabled. No custom hooks touch conversation identity resolution.

### Logs

```shell
"message":"message processed: channel=whatsapp chatId=+52XXXXXXXXXX messageId=3AD1AC718294DC014478 sessionId=be37c314-124e-4823-9466-cb86754e8ef3 sessionKey=agent:wa:whatsapp:group:120363429459936309@g.us outcome=error duration=178ms error=\"Error: UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'idx_agent_conversations_identity'\""

Preceding, repeatedly, at the time of both occurrences:
"message":"⇄ res ✗ chat.history 133ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=session history is rebuilding; retry shortly"

conversations table excerpt (sanitized):
{"conversation_id":"conv_2954465dff82db10951e6b76b19da7a5","channel":"whatsapp","account_id":"default","kind":"group","peer_id":"120363429459936309@g.us", ...}
{"conversation_id":"conv_183828435603d295e6cd182f3d908148","channel":"whatsapp","account_id":"default","kind":"direct","peer_id":"120363429459936309@g.us", ...}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Sanitized SQLite excerpts and a full trajectory export (openclaw sessions export-trajectory) are available on request.

### Impact and severity

Affected: a single WhatsApp group channel used for team/business communication (one agent, one account). Severity: blocks workflow entirely — total inbound-message outage for the affected group until a manual database repair (delete the spurious row, restore role="primary" on the correct group conversation, respecting the partial unique index on session_conversations.role='primary'). Frequency: intermittent, but recurred twice within roughly 9 hours on the same session_id. Consequence: missed incoming business messages until manually detected and fixed; no automated alerting surfaces this failure mode.

### Additional information

Jarvis is the display name/persona of the WhatsApp bot as seen by the group's human participants, not an OpenClaw-internal name — included for context since it appears in session labels/logs. Not confirmed as a regression: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO on last-known-good version, as this was not deliberately bisected. Suspected root cause (unconfirmed): the dashboard/session-resolution code path may create conversation rows without the WhatsApp admission context (group vs. direct) available, defaulting to kind="direct" keyed by whatever raw JID it has, instead of resolving the existing kind="group" conversation for that peer_id.

issues.title: Windows: 2026.10.2 performance regression vs 2026.9.4 (startup 320s vs 55s, event loop blocked 112s per turn, pluginState.register 173s transaction)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr
