labels.description: Crash, hang, restart loop, or process-level availability failure.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

issues.body:
> Nota: medido en 2026.10.2 vs 2026.9.4; no se ha verificado en 2026.10.3.

- **Fecha:** 2026-10-13
- **Equipo:** Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Node 24.18.1, npm 11.16.0, 32 GB RAM,
  Intel Core Ultra 7 165U
- **Instalación:** npm global, Gateway como Tarea Programada, 7 agentes,
  22 plugins, canal de WhatsApp y Telegram
- **Resultado:** se volvió a 2026.9.4

## Medición

Mismo equipo, misma configuración, mismo historial, mismas bases de datos.
Tomado de `openclaw-2026-10-12.log` y `openclaw-2026-10-13.log`.

| | 2026.10.2 | 2026.9.4 |
|---|---|---|
| Arranque hasta "Listening for WhatsApp inbound" | **320–340 s** | **55 s** |
| Latencia de respuesta de WhatsApp (entrada → envío) | **142 s y 151 s** | **35.8 s** |
| Event loop bloqueado durante un turno | **112 s** | **0 s** |
| Arranques que no completaron | 1 de 6 | 0 de 2 |

## Desglose del arranque en 2026.10.2

```
startup phase: process.bootstrap        31.0 s   total=31.0 s
startup phase: state.schema-preflight    1.4 s   total=33.6 s
startup phase: config.auth               4.2 s   total=38.1 s
startup phase: startup.maintenance       3.8 s   total=46.4 s
startup phase: http.bound                0.0 s   total=54.6 s
startup phase: ready                      0.0 s   total=320.7 s
```

**266 segundos sin una sola fase instrumentada** entre `http.bound` y `ready`.
Durante ese tramo:

```
liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=163909ms elapsed=193909ms
liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization interval=189s
```

El event loop bloqueado **193 segundos seguidos, con la CPU del sistema al 0%**.
No es contención por carga: es trabajo síncrono en el hilo principal. Medido por
hilo:

```
hilo principal   410.9 s de CPU acumulada   estado Running   88% de un nucleo
```

## La pieza medible: `pluginState.register`

```
sqlite/transaction: slow SQLite transaction hold
  operation=pluginState.register
  database=state/openclaw.sqlite
  elapsedMs=173106
```

**173 segundos reteniendo una transacción de escritura** para 4,803 filas que
pesan 3.3 MB en total. Son ~36 ms por fila, que es latencia de `fsync`: parece
que sincroniza a disco fila por fila en vez de en lote.

Reparto de esas filas:

| plugin | filas |
|---|---|
| `memory-core` | 4,143 |
| `codex` | 608 |
| `core:memory-artifact-provenance` | 44 |
| `telegram` | 8 |

**La tabla no se poda nunca**: 4,802 de 4,803 filas tienen `expires_at` nulo, y
hay 2,611 filas en namespaces llamados `short-term-recall` y
`short-term-phase-signals` acumuladas desde el 1 de agosto. Parecen una fuga.

## Latencia de un turno

```
05:13:15  Inbound message (direct, 85 chars)
05:13:27  sqlite/transaction
          ... 1 min 48 s sin una sola linea de log ...
05:15:15  host timing gap attributed to event-loop load: gap 111783ms
05:15:15  WhatsApp Web connection closed (status 408)
05:15:32  [model-fetch] response provider=deepseek
05:15:37  Sent message
```

2 minutos 22 segundos en total, de los cuales **1 minuto 52 fue el event loop
bloqueado**. El modelo respondió en 5 segundos. Y el bloqueo fue tan largo que
el canal de WhatsApp perdió la conexión con un 408 por no poder mandar el
keepalive: **el bloqueo no solo retrasa, también tira el canal**.

El mismo turno en 2026.9.4: 35.8 segundos y cero bloqueos.

## Muerte silenciosa del gateway

Un arranque de seis no completó. El proceso abortó durante la inicialización de
plugins con código de salida -1 (`4294967295` en la Tarea Programada), **sin
dejar nada**: ni apagado ordenado en el log, ni evento en el Visor de sucesos de
Windows, ni archivo en `~/.openclaw/logs/stability/`.

## Efectos colaterales del arranque lento

Cualquier supervisión externa construida contra el comportamiento de 2026.9.4
se vuelve destructiva. En esta instalación había dos vigías propios que
reiniciaban el Gateway cuando no respondía —uno tras 40 segundos, otro tras 10
minutos—. Con un arranque de 33 segundos eso era correcto; con uno de 320, los
dos mataban el Gateway antes de que terminara de arrancar, en bucle. Tres
arranques abortados consecutivos antes de identificarlo.

Sugerencia: que el Gateway exponga un estado "arrancando, no me reinicies" desde
el primer segundo, y que `openclaw gateway start` no reporte
`Gateway start timed out after 90s` como si fuera un fallo cuando el proceso
sigue arrancando correctamente.

## Peticiones

1. **Instrumentar el tramo de 266 segundos.** Sin fases ahí dentro, el operador
   no tiene forma de saber qué pasa.
2. **Escribir `pluginState.register` en lote**, no fila por fila.
3. **Podar las filas `short-term` de `plugin_state_entries`**, o darles
   `expires_at`.
4. **Que `openclaw gateway start` distinga "sigue arrancando" de "falló"**, y que
   el estado de arranque sea consultable para los supervisores.
5. **Investigar la salida -1 sin registro** durante la inicialización de plugins.

## Nota sobre volver atrás

Volver a una versión anterior requiere seis pasos, y dos de ellos no están
documentados y rompen la instalación en silencio:

- Restaurar **la base de estado y las de los agentes** (el error solo menciona
  la de estado).
- Quitar de la configuración los marcadores de `meta.migrations` que añadió la
  versión nueva, o la versión vieja rechaza la config entera.
- **Reinstalar los plugins externos en la versión del anfitrión.** Al actualizar
  se actualizan ellos y sus generaciones viejas se borran; al volver atrás
  quedan pidiendo una API que ya no existe y se omiten en silencio. Si uno de
  ellos es el proveedor del modelo principal, el agente se queda mudo y el
  síntoma no apunta a esto en absoluto.

issues.title: Model picker: auto-expand "All models" when a provider has ≤ 4 models

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
## Problem

In the chat model picker, each provider group lists its `recommendedModels` first and collapses everything else under an **All models** expander. For providers with only a handful of models in total (2–4), the expander hides 1–3 rows behind an extra click without reducing any clutter — the worst case of the current design.

## Proposal

When a provider's total model count is ≤ 4, skip the **All models** collapsible and render all of its models directly in the provider group. Providers with more models keep the current recommended + collapsed behavior.

## Rationale

- **Users curate their own providers.** Custom providers (relays, self-hosted endpoints, token-plan gateways) usually carry a deliberately small set of models — every row was chosen on purpose. Hiding any of them behind an expander defeats that curation.
- **The global recommended list can't keep pace.** The centralized, hand-curated list updates on PR cadence, while new popular models — especially fast-moving Chinese open-weight releases (Qwen, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, MiMo, ERNIE, Hunyuan …) — get adopted by users within days of release. When few or none of a small provider's models are on the global list, the picker renders 1–2 rows plus an expander holding the rest.
- **N = 4 keeps it conservative.** Large providers are unaffected; only the small-provider awkward case becomes flat.

## Notes

- Provider groups already retain their expanded/collapsed state between picker opens; this request is about the intra-provider **All models** section (docs `web/control-ui/chat.md`: "Choose **All models** to browse the rest").
- An alternative/complementary knob would be a user preference to always expand **All models**.

issues.body:
## Summary

An admitted WhatsApp user should be able to ask, “Every morning, check my orders and summarize them here.” When the schedule fires, OpenClaw should check the orders using the same permissions the user has in chat and send the result to that DM. A simple text reminder is another use of the same scheduler.

## Problem to solve

On a shared Gateway, native automation management requires owner authority. An admitted WhatsApp user cannot schedule even a personal reminder in the reproduced configuration. [Baseline reproduction and results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187264#issuecomment-7055382385)

## Expected behavior

- Create one-time or recurring tasks from an admitted WhatsApp DM using the account’s existing access and tool policies, without maintaining a second phone allowlist.
- Let the creator list, reschedule, pause, or cancel their own jobs in a later DM. Keep jobs belonging to another contact or the operator private.
- Run the requested work with the creator’s applicable permissions when due. Return the result to the originating account and DM. Withdrawing the user’s access must prevent future execution and delivery.

## Acceptance example

Schedule a morning order summary, then change a synthetic order before the timer fires. Verify that the scheduled agent reads the updated order with an allowed tool and delivers the computed summary to the creator’s DM. A second user must be unable to inspect or change the job. After access is withdrawn, the next occurrence must skip the lookup and delivery.

## Related work

#202880 tracks the implementation. #187264 covers the broader same-conversation scheduling request.

## Implementation and verification

PR #202880 implements personal schedules under the existing WhatsApp DM policy for account-and-peer-isolated sessions. A task uses the native agent runtime, the original sender’s callable tools, and the current unattended approval policy. A literal reminder uses the same personal scheduler.

At `9457615e34`, a daily timer read changed synthetic order quantities and returned the computed total to the originating account and peer. Another due task marked both orders reviewed, confirmed by an independent ledger read. The loopback Gateway also exercised a queued WhatsApp DM, later management, cross-peer denial, operator job protection, and withdrawal before a subsequent occurrence. issues.body:
# Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash). Whether it is a regression is unknown: no earlier version was tested.

# Beta release blocker

No

# Summary

When the stuck-session watchdog kills a cron run because a tool call is blocked waiting for an approval that can never arrive (isolated cron session, no interactive approver), the classification it acted on is discarded at the `abort()` call. The run history keeps the cause-free literal `cron isolated agent run aborted`, and on a chat route the failure alert degrades further, to `Check automation history for details.`

The information exists at abort time and is thrown away one layer above the formatter, so no amount of cron-side formatting can recover it.

**1. Recovery knows the cause.** `resolveSessionAttentionClassification` classifies exactly this state (`src/logging/diagnostic-session-attention.ts`):

```ts
    if (
      params.activity.activeWorkKind === "tool_call" &&
      (params.activity.activeToolAgeMs ?? 0) > params.staleMs &&
      lastProgressAgeMs > params.staleMs
    ) {
      return {
        eventType: "session.stalled",
        reason: "blocked_tool_call",
        classification: "blocked_tool_call",
        activeWorkKind: params.activity.activeWorkKind,
        recoveryEligible: false,
      };
    }
```

`isBlockedToolCallRecoveryEligible` (`src/logging/diagnostic.ts`) then admits that classification for recovery, and the activity snapshot in scope carries the active tool identity (`activeToolName` / `activeToolCallId`), already used in the recovery warn line.

**2. The abort drops it.** `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` passes a reason (`src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts:274`):

```ts
      const result = await abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun({
        sessionId: activeSessionId,
        sessionKey: params.sessionKey,
        settleMs: STUCK_SESSION_ABORT_SETTLE_MS,
        forceClear: true,
        reason: "stuck_recovery",
      });
```

`abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` accepts `reason?: string` and uses it for staleness bookkeeping, but calls the abort with the session id alone (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts:1292`, shipped as `dist/runs-DkiZS9mO.js:607`):

```js
		let aborted = abortEmbeddedAgentRun(params.sessionId) || expiredReplyRun;
```

`abortEmbeddedAgentRun` aborts with `opts?.reason`, which is `undefined` on that overload (`dist/runs-DkiZS9mO.js:379`):

```js
			handle.abort(opts?.reason);
```

The single-session overload cannot carry one at all — its signature is `abortEmbeddedAgentRun(sessionId: string): boolean`, and the `reason` parameter exists only on the `sessionId: undefined` overload, typed `reason?: "restart"`. So the classification and the tool identity never reach the `AbortSignal`.

**3. The operator gets a string with no cause.** With nothing attached, cron's finalizer falls to its literal (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-finalize.ts:309`, shipped as `dist/isolated-agent-BbrXa1yO.js:279`):

```js
	if (finalRunResult.meta?.aborted === true && !cronPayloadOutcome.hasFatalErrorPayload) {
		const error = normalizeOptionalString(finalRunResult.meta.error?.message) ?? "cron isolated agent run aborted";
```

**4. On a chat route the alert does not even carry that string.** `emitFailureAlert` picks the detail lines by route (`src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts:326-332`): a webhook route prints `Last error: cron isolated agent run aborted`, while every chat route goes through `cronFailureDetailLines(errorReason, failureNotificationDetail)` (`src/cron/failure-notification-text.ts:18`). For this failure both inputs are empty — `errorReason` is `resolveCronRunErrorReason("cron isolated agent run aborted")`, which finds no `FailoverReason` (`src/cron/run-error-reason.ts`), and `failureNotificationDetail` only describes command/script payload failures, not an `agentTurn` one. So the notification body is the generic constant:

```ts
const GENERIC_FAILURE_DETAIL = "Check automation history for details.";
```

An operator watching the alert channel is told a named job failed and nothing else, while the cause was in the gateway's own diagnostics before the abort.

**A second, narrower gap on the same theme.** The immediate (non-hang) form of the same denial is also unclassifiable downstream. `deniedReason` for these is free text — `"allowlist-miss"` (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts:1288`) and `"approval-timeout: allowlist-miss"` (`:627`) — while `resolveEmbeddedRunFailureSignal` only recognizes `FAILURE_SIGNAL_CODES = ["SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED", "INVALID_REQUEST"]` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/failure-signal.ts:14`), read off `result.details.errorCode` / `result.errorCode` by `extractToolErrorCode` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-results.ts:445`). Those codes are produced by the approval-binding sites (`src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts:933`), not by the allowlist-miss path — so the coded failure-signal route that does surface a real reason never fires for the common denial.

# Steps to reproduce

1. Give an agent an enforced exec allowlist (`exec-approvals.json`, `security: "allowlist"`) whose default `askFallback` is `allowlist`, i.e. an unlisted command asks for approval.
2. Schedule a cron job for that agent with `sessionTarget: isolated` — no interactive approver exists in the run.
3. Have the job's prompt call `exec` with a command outside the allowlist.
4. Let the run sit until the stuck-session watchdog fires, and read the cron failure alert / run history entry.

# Expected behavior

The failure carries the cause the watchdog already classified: the blocking condition and the command it fired on, e.g. `blocked_tool_call: exec <command>`. Any other abort cause gets its own reason string instead of being flattened into the same text.

# Actual behavior

The run dies at ~150s and reports a cause-free string. Verbatim, from two of our incidents (gateway diagnostics and the cron run history):

```
11:01:23  stalled session  reason=blocked_tool_call  activeTool=exec  (no progress)
11:02:53  recovery abort_embedded_run → run aborted: "cron isolated agent run aborted" (152s)
```

The internal diagnostic names the cause (`reason=blocked_tool_call`, `activeTool=exec`) 90 seconds before the abort; the operator-facing failure never mentions it. Both of our incidents (2026-07-02 and 2026-07-05, same agent, different root command) were diagnosed only by reading the gateway journal by hand — the second one after the generic message had masked the real cause for weeks.

Scope of what was observed versus read: the `cron isolated agent run aborted` text and the diagnostic lines above are verbatim from those two incidents. The chat-route notification body (`Check automation history for details.`) is read from the code path in point 4 — we armed chat-route failure alerts fleet-wide only on 2026-09-04 and no failure of this class has fired since.

# Environment

- openclaw `2026.8.1 (ea80657)`, npm global install (`~/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`)
- Linux 6.17.2-1-pve x64, Node v22.23.2
- Verified unchanged on `main` at `d2a674a6c85` (paths and quotes above are from `main`; the two `dist/` quotes are from the installed 2026.8.1 bundle)
- Model-independent: the defect is in the abort/finalize plumbing, not in a provider path. Our affected runs were on `anthropic/claude-opus-5` and the `claude-cli` backend.

# Provider / routing chain

cron scheduler → `runCronAgentTurn` (isolated session) → embedded agent runner → `exec` tool → gateway exec-approval host → allowlist gate with no approver → stuck-session watchdog → `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` → `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` → cron `run-finalize` → `emitFailureAlert`.

# Additional setup details

Local customizations disclosed so they can be ruled out: one first-party plugin (`nexus-context`, prompt/context injection only — it does not touch cron, exec approvals or the embedded runner), per-agent enforced exec allowlists, and agent commands wrapped in shell scripts under `~/.local/bin`. No dist patch is applied for this defect; the quoted bundle lines are stock 2026.8.1.

# Impact and severity

- Every cron failure of this class reaches the operator with no cause. We armed `cron.failureAlert` on a chat route fleet-wide on 2026-09-04, across 31 scheduled jobs, so the generic body is now the default shape of a failure notification here.
- Time-to-notice is the cost: the alert fires immediately but says nothing actionable, so diagnosis requires reading the gateway journal for the `blocked_tool_call` line. In our second incident that gap ran for weeks of daily failures on a job that silently produced nothing.
- Each affected run also burns its full stall window (~150s of model/tool time) before dying.

# Fix shape

Thread the classification and the active tool/command from `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` through `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` → `abortEmbeddedAgentRun` → `handle.abort(reason)` as a real reason object (the single-session overload needs to accept one), and let cron's `resolveCronAbortReasonText` / `run-finalize` surface it as its own string rather than the generic aborted literal. A watchdog abort would then also have a classification to put on the chat route, which today can only print a cause it recognizes as a `FailoverReason`. Separately, attach a structured `errorCode` to allowlist-miss and approval-timeout exec denials so `resolveEmbeddedRunFailureSignal` can classify the immediate form too.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

In a Telegram direct chat, a turn finished normally and its reply was delivered with the `message` tool. About 3 seconds later OpenClaw posted the generic failure notice into the same chat:

> ⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this request. Check the conversation before trying again. For details, open Settings → Logs in the Control UI or run `openclaw logs --follow`.

Nothing had failed: the run is recorded as succeeded and the reply as delivered. The Gateway file log and the service journal contain no error, warning or cause for the notice, so the owner is told to "check the logs" and the logs have nothing.

### Observed (2026.11.3 847611d, Telegram DM, embedded runner, anthropic/claude-fable-5-2, `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`)

UTC 2026-11-15, one user turn in the owner's DM session (run `213d61d4…`), then the notice:

```text
03:10:36.300  audit  tool.action.started   message   (send, reply to the triggering message, final)
03:10:37.551  [telegram] outbound send ok … messageId=<N> operation=sendRichMessage deliveryKind=text replyToMessageId=<trigger>
03:10:38.050  audit  tool.action.finished  message   status=succeeded
03:10:38.627  audit  agent.run.finished    status=succeeded   run=213d61d4…
03:10:38.763  [auto-reply/message-tool-outcome] recorded message-tool-only run outcome  outcome="tool_delivered" runStatus="completed"
03:10:41.534  [telegram] outbound send ok … messageId=<N+1> operation=sendRichMessage deliveryKind=text      <- the failure notice, no replyTo
```

Between 03:10:38.763 and 03:10:41.534 the journal has no line for this session, and for the whole turn there is no `Embedded agent failed before reply`, no `lane task error`, no `incomplete turn detected`, no `empty response` line. The session transcript holds the delivery mirror of the reply (`openclawDeliveryMirror.kind = "message-tool-source-reply", final: true`) and no assistant error entry.

What else was happening in that window (correlation only, not shown to be the cause):

- A hidden subagent spawned by this turn with `completionTarget: "parent"` had finished 4 minutes earlier. Its private completion turn in the same session (`announce:v1:…`) began preparing about 0.45 s after the user turn finished (its `prep stages` line at 03:10:48.690 reports `totalMs=9612`), i.e. the notice was sent while that turn was being set up.
- Earlier in the same user turn the model had called `sessions_yield`, which returned `already_pending` (an unrelated child from two days before, `state: completing, wakeArmed: false`; see #189980), and the turn went on with tool calls and ended with the `message` send.

### Shipped code

Three places can produce this exact sentence. Two of them log before sending (`agent-runner` writes `Embedded agent failed before reply: …`; the incomplete-turn path writes `incomplete turn detected`). The third does not, and by elimination it is the one that fired:

`src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.execute.ts`, the `.catch` of the reply resolver (v2026.11.3 lines 500-516; unchanged on `main` at lines 546-562 and in v2026.11.5-beta.3):

```ts
// Gate collection, not just printing: diagnostic subscribers can export this cause.
if (isFileLogLevelEnabled("debug")) {
  replyResolverError = truncateUtf16Safe(formatErrorWithRedactor(error, { redact: redactToolPayloadText }), 2_048);
}
failDispatchReplyOperation(error, "failed");
if (!didDeliverVisiblePartialReply) {
  return adopted &&
    isRequiredReplyExpectation(state.replyOperationRunState.replyCompletion?.expectation) &&
    state.replyOperationRunState.replyCompletion?.outcome !== "blocked" &&
    !state.suppressDelivery &&
    !state.getObservedReplyDelivery()
    ? { text: GENERIC_EXTERNAL_RUN_FAILURE_TEXT, isError: true }
    : undefined;
}
```

Two things follow from the source:

1. The error that reaches this `catch` is kept only when the file log level is `debug`. At the default level the notice is sent and the cause is discarded, which matches the empty log.
2. The only delivery check is `getObservedReplyDelivery()`, which is set from the agent runner when it resolves the terminal reply completion. An error thrown after the run has ended and the message-tool reply has been delivered, but before that callback, leaves the flag false, so a delivered turn is treated as unanswered. The same run was recorded as `tool_delivered` / `completed` by `recordMessageToolRunOutcome` 2.8 s before the notice.

### Expected

1. A turn whose source reply was delivered (message-tool receipt for the current source, run finished ok) never gets the generic failure notice afterwards, whatever fails later in dispatch bookkeeping.
2. Whenever this notice is sent, its cause is written to the log at `warn` (redacted), not only collected at `debug`. The notice itself sends the owner to the logs.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d), Linux x86_64, Node 26.12.1, systemd user service. Telegram DM, embedded agent runner, `anthropic/claude-fable-5-2`, `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, `messages.queue.mode: "collect"`, file log level default (no `logging` block).

### Evidence scope

- Observed once with complete records (above). The run id, audit rows, journal lines and transcript entries were read after the fact; nothing was induced.
- Not reproduced on demand, and the thrown error is unknown because it was not logged. That the `dispatch-from-config` catch is the sender is an inference from the absence of the other two paths' log lines, not a captured stack.
- Whether the starting private completion turn or the earlier `already_pending` yield result plays a part is not established.
- Related but different: #192688 (same notice in groups after an empty final or a provider 429), #169229 (closed; successful Codex final replaced by this notice, also without a logged cause), #176330 (closed; `ActiveTurnClaimError` surfacing as this notice, with log lines).

issues.body:
### Summary
Expose provider-neutral finite-input realtime transcription through the plugin SDK.

### Problem to solve
A voice-satellite integration can stream audio while a user speaks, but it must eventually end input and wait for a complete final transcript. The existing realtime transcription session offers continuous audio and callbacks, without a provider-neutral end-of-input completion contract. Closing a session is not a reliable indication that every sample has been recognized. Integration plugins otherwise need to implement provider protocols themselves, or wait for recording to finish and use batch STT.

### Proposed solution
Add an optional finite-utterance capability to existing realtime transcription providers, an awaited write/finalize contract, and a lazy SDK operation that uses OpenClaw's configured audio provider/model and policy. It must return unsupported before touching input when the selection cannot be honored, and never silently replay partially uploaded audio after a streaming error. Preserve existing synchronous continuous sessions.

Implement ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime as the first provider adapter. Keep its manual commits and segment acknowledgments inside the provider. A consumer such as a Home Assistant bridge should call the same SDK operation, not import provider-specific WebSocket code.

### Alternatives considered
- Batch transcription remains the fallback and needs no core changes, but cannot start uploading during capture.
- Provider-specific bridge code duplicates OpenClaw's provider abstraction.
- A separate bridge-owned realtime service moves authentication and protocol ownership outside OpenClaw.

### Impact
Plugin developers implementing finite voice turns can use supported realtime providers without embedding each vendor's protocol. Existing voice-call/meeting continuous sessions retain their behavior. This is an additive SDK capability, not a new agent tool, automatic provider switch, or replacement of the batch path. Initial support deliberately leaves omitted models and unsupported batch-only options on the existing batch path.

### Evidence/examples
A local prototype with synthetic audio streamed input to the provider before input ended and retained the last word through finalization. The implementation uses serialized, acknowledged segments and bounded cancellation. A separate small environment-proxy fix is independent of this API. A focused implementation PR will link this issue, with prior-base proof clearly separated from current-head CI.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

issues.body:
**Environment**
- OpenClaw 2026.8.1-beta.3 (5831b80); first observed on 2026.6.10
- OL9 ARM64, rootful Podman Quadlets; Mattermost + Telegram channels

**Symptom**
The scheduler has no end conditions. `openclaw cron add --help` / `cron edit --help` expose no until / max-runs / expire flag (re-checked on 2026.8.1-beta.3, 2026-08-26), so every recurring job runs until someone disables it. Job `state` carries `lastRunAtMs` / `nextRunAtMs` / `lastRunStatus` and *consecutive* error/skip counters, but **no cumulative run count**, so "stop after N runs" cannot be enforced externally either without keeping a counter elsewhere.

**Why it matters**
"Ends after N occurrences / ends on a date" is standard recurrence vocabulary and the natural shape for finite delegated work ("check this daily for two weeks", "remind me 5 times"). Without it, bounded chores become unbounded standing jobs that need manual cleanup.

**Proposed direction**
(a) `--until <ISO>` and `--max-runs <N>` on `cron add` / `cron edit`, plus a `state.runCount` counter; at the bound the job **disables** (not deletes) so the audit trail survives. (b) Failing that, just `state.runCount` — external tooling can then enforce bounds cheaply.

**Workaround we're using locally**
A sidecar sweep that counts fires from the tasks ledger and disables the job at the bound.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On 2026.11.6, a turn that a Gateway restart interrupts in a Telegram chat is never resumed. Startup restart resume fails with `SessionBindingError: Session binding owner changed for telegram:default` and the user gets no reply until they write again. #191370 (merged Nov 2) fixes this on main and is in v2026.11.10-beta.1, but 2026.11.6, the current npm `latest`, branched before it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run 2026.11.6 with a Telegram account. I used a local fake Bot API and a mock model that takes 90 s to answer, so a turn is still running when the Gateway stops.
2. Send a message in two Telegram group chats, so both have a turn running.
3. Stop the Gateway with SIGTERM. The shutdown marks both sessions for restart resume. Start it again on the same state.
4. Result: both resumes fail about 0.2 s before the Telegram account starts, and neither chat gets a reply.

### Expected behavior

Both interrupted turns resume and reply, as they do on main and on v2026.11.10-beta.1.

### Actual behavior

Each interrupted session logs `Skipped restart resume` and `Restart resume input failed`, and its turn is dropped. Messages sent after the restart are still answered.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux x86_64)

### Install method

npm (pinned dependency)

### Model

Not model-specific (local mock model)

### Provider / routing chain

None (local mock)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
[gateway] Skipped restart resume for agent:main:telegram:group:-1001000000001: Error: SessionBindingError: Session binding owner changed for telegram:default
[gateway] Restart resume input failed for agent:main:telegram:group:-1001000000001: SessionBindingError: Session binding owner changed for telegram:default
[gateway] Skipped restart resume for agent:main:telegram:group:-1001000000002: Error: SessionBindingError: Session binding owner changed for telegram:default
[gateway] Restart resume input failed for agent:main:telegram:group:-1001000000002: SessionBindingError: Session binding owner changed for telegram:default
[telegram] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- 2026.11.6 as published: 4 of 4 restarts dropped both interrupted turns.
- 2026.11.6 with only #191370's change applied (`resolveBoundAcpSessionForCommandReset` keeps the explicit `null` binding context that system events pass, instead of rebuilding it with `??`): 3 of 3 restarts resumed both turns and both chats got their replies. A log line added inside that function shows both lookups ran about 2 s before the Telegram account started, so startup order didn't change; the one-line fix is what made the difference.
- v2026.11.10-beta.1 (2 of 2 restarts) and main 413368e: `startup restart resume: [{"agentId":"main","resumed":2,"skipped":0}]`, and both chats got their replies.
- `git cherry-pick de1880f4d03` (#191370's merge commit) applies cleanly to v2026.11.6.

#191370's description has the root cause: restart resume runs before the channel account registers its binding adapter, and session init rebuilt a binding context it had already decided to skip for system events.

### Impact and severity

Any stable user on an adapter-owned channel (Telegram, and per #191370 Discord and Matrix too) loses each turn that a restart, upgrade or deploy interrupts, with no reply and no error shown in the chat.

### Additional information

Ask: a 2026.11.6.x patch with #191370, or the next stable release that carries it. #202213 asks the same for compressed archive reads.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

On the native ChatGPT-backed Responses route (`openai-chatgpt-responses`), an explicit prompt cache key has no effect: the backend routes cache reuse by the `session_id` header, and OpenClaw always sets that header to the transcript session id. Every isolated cron run, and every request that uses a fresh session, therefore starts with 0 cached input tokens even though the key is stable.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Send two requests directly to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` (same ChatGPT/Codex OAuth account, same ~14k-token `instructions`, `store: false`, `stream: true`) a few seconds apart, varying only `prompt_cache_key` and the `session_id` header.
2. Compare `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` of the second request.

Observed on 2026-11-04 (warm-up request first, then each variant):

| second request | cached_tokens of 14 008 |
|---|---|
| same `prompt_cache_key`, new `session_id` | 0 |
| new `prompt_cache_key`, same `session_id` | 13 824 |
| same key + same `session_id` | 13 824 |
| new key + new `session_id` | 0 |

3. In OpenClaw, look at the first model call of consecutive isolated cron runs of the same job (stable `openclaw-cron-…` key, new transcript each run): `cacheRead` is 0 every time. The same holds for any caller that opens a new session per request.

### Expected behavior

When OpenClaw resolves an explicit `promptCacheKey` (isolated cron, webchat), requests that share it reuse the cached prefix on the ChatGPT route, as they already do on `api.openai.com`.

### Actual behavior

`prompt_cache_key` in the body carries the explicit key, but `session_id` (SSE header and WebSocket handshake) is always the transcript session id, so the ChatGPT backend never shares cache between runs.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.9 (8b18b55); the code path is unchanged on current `main`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (gateway host)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

openai/gpt-6.1-sol, openai/gpt-6-luna

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openai (ChatGPT/Codex OAuth, `openai-chatgpt-responses`)

### Impact and severity

Affected: isolated cron jobs and per-request sessions on ChatGPT subscription auth. Every first call reprocesses the whole stable prefix (system prompt, tools, Project Context), which spends weekly subscription limit and adds latency. In our deployment this is ~40k uncached input tokens on every customer turn.

### Additional information

Fix proposal in a linked PR: on this route, use the explicit cache key for the `session_id` header and keep `x-client-request-id` (and the WebSocket connection cache) on the transcript session id. Without an explicit key behavior is unchanged; `cacheRetention: "none"` keeps the transcript id.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The FaceTime audio pump respawns SoX in `clearPlayback()` (barge-in, `response-superseded`, non-completed outcome) and the next audio delta can be written a few milliseconds later. When that happens SoX plays only what was already queued on its stdin, exits with status 0, and the pump reports

```
[facetime] native audio bridge failed: SoX playback exited (0)
```

which ends the call (`call closed (talk-failed: SoX playback exited (0))`). To the caller the assistant simply hangs up mid-conversation.

Root cause: under Bun on macOS the child's stdin is a socket, not a pipe. SoX's `lsx_filelength()` tests `st.st_mode & S_IFREG`, which is non-zero for sockets (`S_IFSOCK` contains the `S_IFREG` bit), so `lsx_check_read_params()` takes `st_size` — for a socket, the number of bytes queued at that moment — as the total input length (`src/formats_i.c`). If nothing is queued when SoX opens its input, the length is 0 ("unknown") and streaming works. If audio is already queued, SoX reads exactly that many bytes and finishes.

### Steps to reproduce

Standalone (no call, same Bun binary the gateway uses, plugin's SoX arguments):

```js
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
const ARGS = ["-q", "--buffer", "8192", "-t", "raw", "-r", "24000", "-c", "1", "-e", "signed-integer", "-b", "16", "-L", "-", "-t", "coreaudio", "OpenClaw-Feed"];
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
const p = spawn("/opt/homebrew/bin/sox", ARGS, { stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"] });
p.on("exit", (code) => console.log("sox exited", code));
// await sleep(20);              // uncomment: SoX stays alive
p.stdin.write(Buffer.alloc(15360));
for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) { await sleep(57); p.stdin.write(Buffer.alloc(15000)); }
await sleep(3000);
```

In a call: use a realtime provider whose first audio delta arrives together with `response.created`, and start a new response while the previous one is still playing by the pump's playback clock (the caller answers the instant the assistant finishes, or a tool call is followed immediately by another spoken response). `startResponse()` calls `pump.clearOutputAudio()`, a new SoX is spawned, and `writeOutputAudio()` runs about 10 ms later.

### Expected behavior

Playback continues on the new SoX process; the call stays up.

### Actual behavior

Measured on the machine (0 ms into SoX from Bun: 8 runs; 10 ms: 3 runs; 20 ms or more: 15 runs; the other rows 2–6 runs each; every run of a row gave the same result):

| Parent / child stdin | First write after spawn | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bun 1.4.4 → SoX | 0 ms, then 7 chunks 57 ms apart | SoX exits 0 at ~370–400 ms, having played only the first 0.32 s chunk |
| Bun 1.4.4 → SoX | 0 ms, one 2.5 s write | SoX plays all 2.5 s, then exits 0 |
| Bun 1.4.4 → SoX | 10 ms | SoX exits 0 |
| Bun 1.4.4 → SoX | 20 ms or more | SoX stays alive |
| Bun 1.4.4 → `wc -c` | 0 ms | all bytes received |
| python3 pipe → SoX | 0 ms | SoX stays alive |
| python3 `socketpair` → SoX | 0 ms | SoX exits after the first chunk (writer gets EPIPE) |
| python3 `socketpair` → SoX | 300 ms | SoX stays alive |

A child spawned by Bun reports its stdin as `S_ISSOCK`, `st_size` 15360 right after a 15360-byte write, and `(st_mode & S_IFREG) != 0`. The same child behind a python pipe reports `S_ISFIFO` and `(st_mode & S_IFREG) == 0`.

In the real call the macOS log shows the old SoX context stopped at 01:09:04.333, the new SoX starting I/O at 04.402 and stopping it itself at 04.702 after 15360 frames, and the gateway logging the bridge failure at 04.715.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (76cbb32), `@openclaw/facetime` 2026.11.5 from ClawHub

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (Apple silicon), SoX 14.4.2 (Homebrew 14.4.2_6)

### Install method

OpenClaw.app-managed runtime (Bun 1.4.4)

### Model

Realtime voice; agent google/gemini-4-neon

### Provider / routing chain

FaceTime plugin → realtime provider id `openai` with `baseUrl` pointing at a local OpenAI-Realtime-compatible relay → ElevenLabs realtime. The relay is not needed to reproduce: the standalone script above uses only Bun and SoX. A fast provider just makes the 10 ms window easy to hit, because its first audio delta arrives 0–5 ms after `response.created`.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
[facetime] native audio bridge failed: SoX playback exited (0)
[facetime] call closed (talk-failed: SoX playback exited (0))
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

- Affected: FaceTime realtime calls on Bun; any path that calls `clearOutputAudio()` shortly before the next audio (barge-in, superseded response, cancelled response).
- Severity: the call is dropped.
- Frequency: intermittent, timing dependent. Replaying the delta timings of one 7-minute call through the plugin's rules gives two respawns, one of them inside the window.

### Additional information

Possible fixes, any one of which removes the failure:

- give SoX a real pipe (for example spawn it behind a FIFO, or through a tiny `cat |` stage), so `st_mode & S_IFREG` is false;
- do not write to a freshly spawned SoX until it has opened its input (a short readiness delay, or queue the first chunks);
- treat a clean playback exit as recoverable and respawn once instead of failing the bridge.

Local mitigation I am running in the relay: the next response's events are held until the previous one has finished playing by the same clock the pump uses, so `startResponse()` never supersedes, and audio is forwarded no earlier than 120 ms after its `response.created`.

This report was prepared with an AI coding assistant; every measurement above was taken on the machine as described.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

During a FaceTime realtime call, every `openclaw_agent_consult` tool call fails about 0.1 s after the voice model issues it. The gateway logs

```
[facetime] agent consult failed: Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.
```

and the realtime model receives `{"error":"Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly."}` as the tool result. The gateway is healthy at that moment (not draining, not suspended, other channels keep answering). No agent run is started.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `@openclaw/facetime` 2026.11.5 on OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (macOS, gateway on Bun 1.4.4), a realtime provider configured, `realtime.toolPolicy: "owner"`.
2. Call the Mac from an allowed handle and ask something that makes the voice model call `openclaw_agent_consult`.

### Expected behavior

The consult runs on the configured agent and its answer is spoken.

### Actual behavior

The tool result is the error above, every time. Depending on the voice model the caller hears an apology or an invented answer.

Cause, as far as I can trace it in the installed build:

`extensions/facetime/src/talk-consult-controller.ts` calls the shared helper directly from the realtime bridge's tool-call callback:

```ts
void consultRealtimeVoiceAgent({ cfg: params.fullConfig, agentRuntime: params.runtime.agent, ... })
```

`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` (`src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts`) starts with `beginSessionEffect(...)`, whose first statement is

```ts
if (isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()) throw new GatewayDrainingError();
```

`isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()` returns `currentRootWork.getStore().released` whenever the async context carries a root. The FaceTime runtime is a plugin service started during gateway startup (`sidecars.plugin-services.facetime.facetime-runtime`); its helper-event listener and the realtime bridge keep that startup root in their async context after it has been released. So the check is always true inside a call, and the default `GatewayDrainingError` message for a gateway that is neither draining nor suspended is exactly the text above.

Core's Talk handler opens a fresh root before calling the same helper (`tryBeginGatewayIndependentRootWorkAdmission("talk-agent-consult", { detachedWork: true })` then `admission.run(...)`), so it is not affected.

The FaceTime controller is unchanged in 2026.11.6, 2026.11.10-beta.1 and on `main` (checked 2026-11-21). `src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts` and `extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.ts` call the helper the same way; I have not tested whether their listeners retain a released root.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (76cbb32), `@openclaw/facetime` 2026.11.5 from ClawHub

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (Apple silicon)

### Install method

OpenClaw.app-managed runtime (Bun 1.4.4)

### Model

Agent: google/gemini-4-neon (API key, not a CLI runtime, so this is separate from #202208)

### Provider / routing chain

FaceTime plugin → realtime provider id `openai` with `baseUrl` pointing at a local OpenAI-Realtime-compatible relay → ElevenLabs realtime. The failure happens inside the gateway before any provider is involved.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
[facetime] agent consult failed: Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Reproduction without a call: I extracted `createFaceTimeConsultController` from the installed `dist/runtime-api.js` and invoked `handleToolCall` from an `AsyncResource` created inside a root that had since been released (real `gateway-work-admission` module, consult stubbed to do the same first check as `beginSessionEffect`). It delivers the same error and the same log line. From a context with no root, or with a live root, the consult goes through.

Local fix that works: wrapping the call with the public SDK helper gives it a tracked independent root, the same path core Talk uses.

```ts
import { runDetachedWebhookWork } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/webhook-request-guards";

void runDetachedWebhookWork(() => consultRealtimeVoiceAgent({ ... })).then(...)
```

With that change the extracted controller returns the consult result from the released-root context and no root is left active afterwards. On a real call (2026-11-21) the consult then ran to completion: tool call at +72 s, agent result delivered to the realtime session at +106 s, no `agent consult failed` line. A dedicated admission origin, or taking the admission inside `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent`, would be cleaner than borrowing the webhook helper.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: every FaceTime realtime call that needs the agent (lookups, memory, tools).
- Severity: blocks the feature; the voice model may invent an answer.
- Frequency: always.

### Additional information

This report was prepared with an AI coding assistant; every claim above was checked on the machine as described.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

For an inbound FaceTime call the plugin answers as soon as audio capture is ready and only then waits for the realtime provider. With a provider that needs a few seconds to accept the session, the caller sees the call connect and then hears nothing until the provider is ready and the greeting has been generated. It feels like the other side picked up and said nothing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `@openclaw/facetime` 2026.11.5, realtime provider whose session setup takes several seconds (here: about 5.5 s between `session.update` and `session.updated` with a 6,000-character instruction block).
2. Call the Mac from an allowed handle and time the gap between the call connecting and the first word.

### Expected behavior

The phone keeps ringing until the assistant can speak, then the call is answered and the greeting follows within about a second — the way a person takes a moment to pick up but speaks once they have.

### Actual behavior

Timeline of one call from the macOS unified log (`callservicesd`, `FaceTime`) and the gateway log:

| Time | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 01:02:17.25 | call reported as connecting |
| 01:02:17.656 | uplink muted (`realtime talk suppression ready`) |
| 01:02:17.663 | `Asked to answer call` |
| 01:02:18.817 | `Answer call action fulfilled` |
| 01:02:23.24 | provider `session.updated` |
| 01:02:23.298 | uplink unmuted; gateway logs `answered authorized FaceTime call` |
| ~01:02:24.6 | first audible audio |

The caller was connected for about 6 seconds before hearing anything.

This follows from the inbound handler order in `runtime-call-events`: `startCallTalk(call)` → `helper.answerCall(callUUID)` → `activateCallTalk(call)`. `startFaceTimeTalkDriver` returns after `pump.suppressionReady()`; the provider connection (`providerConnect`) continues in the background and is only awaited by `readyForAudio()` inside `activateCallTalk`, after the answer.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (76cbb32), `@openclaw/facetime` 2026.11.5 from ClawHub (handler unchanged in 2026.11.6 and 2026.11.10-beta.1)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (Apple silicon)

### Install method

OpenClaw.app-managed runtime (Bun 1.4.4)

### Model

Realtime voice; agent google/gemini-4-neon

### Provider / routing chain

FaceTime plugin → realtime provider id `openai` with `baseUrl` pointing at a local OpenAI-Realtime-compatible relay → ElevenLabs realtime. The order of operations is in the plugin and does not depend on the provider; a slower provider only makes the gap longer.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

- Affected: every inbound FaceTime realtime call; the gap equals the provider's setup time.
- Severity: annoying, and it reads as a dead line. Callers start talking over the silence, which then collides with the greeting.
- Frequency: always.

### Additional information

The plugin has no setting for this (`openclaw.plugin.json` exposes only `enabled`, `ownerHandles` and `realtime.*`).

Local change I have applied (not yet exercised by a real inbound call): one line before the answer that waits for `call.talk.realtimeActive()`, polling every 100 ms for at most 12 s (the plugin's own provider timeout is 15 s) and stopping if the caller hangs up or the call is no longer the active one.

```js
await params.callControl.startCallTalk(call);
for (let waited = 0; waited < 12e3 && typeof call.talk?.realtimeActive === "function" && !call.talk.realtimeActive()
     && !call.lifecycleAbort.signal.aborted && params.calls.active === call; waited += 100) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100));
```

An option such as `realtime.answer: "when-ready" | "immediately"` would cover both preferences. Generating the greeting while the phone is still ringing would remove the remaining second.

This report was prepared with an AI coding assistant; the timeline was read from the logs of a real call as described.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Realtime voice `consultPolicy: "substantive"` gives GPT-Live the wrong instructions in Voice Call, and Discord voice rejects the value entirely.

- **Voice Call:** with a GPT-Live model and `realtime.consultPolicy: "substantive"`, the session prompt says "Call openclaw_agent_consult before answering requests that need facts, memory, ...". GPT-Live has no such tool: it delegates natively. The docs (`docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md`, GPT-Live section) say GPT-Live may use `"auto"` or `"substantive"`.
- **Discord voice:** `channels.discord.voice.realtime.consultPolicy` only accepts `auto | always`, so there is no way to ask GPT-Live in Discord to delegate substantive requests. `always` is rejected on GPT-Live (correctly), and `auto` adds no guidance, so the model often answers facts and memory questions itself.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Voice Call realtime with an OpenAI GPT-Live model (`handlesAgentConsult`) and `realtime.consultPolicy: "substantive"`.
2. Place a call and inspect the instructions sent to the realtime bridge.
3. Separately, set `channels.discord.voice.realtime.consultPolicy: "substantive"` and run `openclaw config validate`.

### Expected behavior

- One shared rule decides which consult policies a surface may use and how each is worded for the selected model.
- On GPT-Live, `substantive` adds delegation guidance that does not name `openclaw_agent_consult`; `always` stays rejected.
- Discord and Voice Call accept the same three values (`auto`, `substantive`, `always`).

### Actual behavior

- Voice Call passes `substantive` to the shared session policy as `auto` (`extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.ts`, `configuredConsultPolicy: this.config.consultPolicy === "always" ? "always" : "auto"`), so the GPT-Live check passes, but it builds the prompt from the raw config in `extensions/voice-call/src/realtime-agent-context.ts` before the model capability is known. GPT-Live is told to call a tool it does not have.
- `resolveRealtimeVoiceSessionPolicy` (`src/talk/realtime-session-policy.ts`) types the policy as `auto | always`; the only prompt builder (`buildRealtimeVoiceAgentConsultPolicyInstructions` in `src/talk/agent-consult-tool.ts`) has no notion of native delegation.
- Discord's schema is `z.enum(["auto", "always"])`; Voice Call's is `z.enum(["auto", "substantive", "always"])`.

### OpenClaw version

main @ 684018d11

### Operating system

Linux

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

openai gpt-live-1 (realtime)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openai realtime (GPT-Live, native delegation)

### Impact and severity

Medium: on GPT-Live, `substantive` guidance is either wrong (Voice Call) or unavailable (Discord), so callers get answers the model made up instead of delegated agent results. No crash.

### Additional information

Out of scope: host-side forced-consult enforcement (`always`), which stays per surface (Discord `realtime-consults.ts`, Voice Call `scheduleForcedAgentConsult`) on the shared forced-consult coordinator.

Proposed fix: carry `substantive` through the shared session policy as a first-class value, let the shared prompt builder choose native-delegation wording when the model handles agent consults, build the Voice Call consult block after the routed model is resolved, and add `substantive` to the Discord schema. PR to follow.

issues.body:
## Summary
On 2026.10.10 (7dc3350) a Crabbox cloud-worker profile that used `settings.setupEnv` cannot be migrated to `setupSecrets`, and the setupSecrets design cannot deliver a Tailscale auth key at all, so cloud workers that must join a tailnet to reach a Tailscale-Serve-only Gateway have no supported path.

## Details
- Profile `aws` had `setupEnv: ["OPENCLAW_CW_TS_AUTHKEY"]`; its setup script runs `tailscale up --authkey=$OPENCLAW_CW_TS_AUTHKEY` so the worker can reach `gateway.publicOrigin` (a ts.net Tailscale Serve URL).
- Health check: "Crabbox profile aws uses retired plaintext setupEnv and needs repair (OPENCLAW_CW_TS_AUTHKEY: missing)". Docs say `doctor --fix` migrates to **same-name** protected store entries, but the crabbox provider rejects any setupSecrets name starting with `OPENCLAW_` ("setupSecrets name ... is reserved"). So the documented migration can never succeed for an `OPENCLAW_*` name; the doctor hint does not mention renaming.
- Even after renaming, setupSecrets only gives the command a placeholder that the egress proxy substitutes in HTTPS URLs/headers/bodies at bound hosts. `tailscaled` sends the auth key to the control plane inside the Noise (ts2021) protocol, so substitution cannot work; the worker joins with a placeholder and fails.
- Meanwhile `gateway/worker-environments` logs "Worker provider maintenance failed (crabbox)" every ~30 s with no reason in the log line (~1,650/day), and warm-image refresh stops.

## Expected
1. Doctor/health hint should say the name must be renamed (and which names are reserved) instead of implying same-name migration.
2. A supported way for cloud workers to join a tailnet when the Gateway is only reachable over Tailscale (e.g. first-class Tailscale join using an OAuth client held by the Gateway, or a documented pattern minting an ephemeral key via api.tailscale.com through the egress proxy).
3. The maintenance failure log should include the reason.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a subagent completion event is delivered to the parent session at a moment when the receiving turn is already closing down (the system turn-finalization path where tool calls are no longer permitted), the parent agent **cannot dispatch follow-up work** — even though the completion arrived correctly and the parent has every intention to continue the chain.

In our case a nine-step orchestration chain stalled for **~28 minutes**: the writing subagent finished successfully, its completion event reached the parent, but the parent could only post a text "settled" note (no tool calls allowed in that turn) and the follow-up figure-production step was never dispatched — until an inbound user message woke the session up.

This is distinct from delivery failures (#155019 fixed deliveries not arriving; #186541 covers results lost after plugin reload): here the delivery **succeeds**, but it lands in a turn that is barred from calling tools, so the chain breaks after delivery.

## Timeline (journal, 2026-11-04, CST)

```
13:39:22  Subagent run 1c7c1e83 (status=ok) completion event delivered to parent session.
          The receiving turn was in its finalization phase — tool calls disallowed.
          Parent's only output: a text note: "本回合工具调用已完成，此处收账"
          ("this turn's tool calls are complete; settling the account here")
          → follow-up step (figure production) never dispatched. Chain stalled.
13:39–14:07  No further dispatch activity (~28 minutes stall).
14:07:16  Inbound user message wakes the session; the follow-up run (69a07cb8)
          is finally dispatched by the parent.
```

Retrospective confirmed: the subagent itself was healthy and its acceptance records were intact — this was neither a subagent failure nor a parent logic omission. The single failure point was the receiving turn's tool constraint.

## Reproduction characteristics

- **Probabilistic**: earlier completion events in the same orchestration chain were delivered into turns that could still call tools, and follow-ups were dispatched normally. The failure requires the completion to land inside the finalization window — a race between "subagent finishes" and "receiving turn closing".
- Observable on any chained orchestration where step N+1 is dispatched from step N's completion event (multi-step pipelines driven by subagent completion rather than by user turns).

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (Linux x64, systemd --user gateway)
- Parent session: Feishu DM direct conversation; nine-step writing pipeline (write subagent → figure-production follow-up)

## Suggested direction

A delivered subagent completion that requests continuation should be able to **start a fresh turn in which tools are callable**, instead of being folded into an already-closing turn where the only remaining capability is text output. Concretely, one of:

1. If the receiving turn is finalizing, queue the completion as a **new turn trigger** (same as any other wake event) rather than delivering it into the closing turn;
2. Or allow the finalization path to grant a minimal "dispatch follow-up" capability for settled child completions;
3. At minimum, log and surface "completion arrived but tools disallowed — chain may stall" so operators can detect the stall without waiting for a user to notice.

## Related

- #155019 — delivery of subagent results (fixed not-arriving); our case is the step *after* delivery.
- #186541 — subagent results not reaching the parent after plugin reload; same event domain, different failure point.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let callers of the OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/responses` endpoint pass the standard `prompt_cache_key` field, and use it as the run's explicit prompt cache key.

### Problem to solve

An application that drives an agent through `/v1/responses` with a fresh `x-openclaw-session-key` per request (one isolated reasoning turn per customer event, transcript forgotten afterwards) can never reuse the prompt cache across requests: the cache key is derived from the new transcript session id. The request schema is strict, so sending OpenAI's own `prompt_cache_key` field is rejected with 400. In our deployment every such turn's first model call is ~40k input tokens with 0 cached, although the system prompt, tools and Project Context are identical between turns.

### Proposed solution

Accept optional `prompt_cache_key` (string, clamped like other OpenAI cache keys) in the `/v1/responses` body and pass it through the agent command to the embedded run as `promptCacheKey`, the same explicit key isolated cron and webchat already use. Without the field nothing changes.

### Alternatives considered

- Reusing one long-lived session key per agent: mixes unrelated customers' transcripts, not acceptable.
- A plugin hook to set the cache key: no hook exposes it today.
- Calling the model outside OpenClaw: loses the agent workspace and tool policy.

### Impact

Per-request integrations on any OpenAI-style route would share the stable prefix cache. On ChatGPT subscription auth this also needs #192318 / #192321, because that backend routes cache by the `session_id` header.

### Evidence/examples

Prior art: `resolveIsolatedCronPromptCacheKey` and `resolveWebchatPromptCacheKey` already set an explicit key for runs whose transcript is per-run.

The idle comes in the next push, `reason: "cron-binding"`, with `status: "done"` and no top-level `hasActiveRun`; only its nested `session` row says `false`. A client that applies pushes as deltas (omitted field means no change, like `docs/gateway/clients.md` describes for session events) stays at `hasActiveRun: true`.

On 2026.10.8 the wake's `phase: "end"` push already says `hasActiveRun: false`. A `chat.send` run gets `agent.input.settled` with `hasActiveRun: false` on both versions, so only the wake path changed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the repro in the gist (a fake model and one script, no channels): https://gist.github.com/eliavb43/cb538d83c8ba8fecaaa3204c5f10c2f3
2. It subscribes with `sessions.subscribe`, does one `chat.send` turn, then a cron wake into the same session, and prints each `sessions.changed` for it (top-level and nested run fields).
3. Look at the last two lines after `--- cron wake`.

### Expected behavior

The push that announces the idle carries top-level `hasActiveRun: false` and `activeRunIds: []`, as `agent.input.settled` does (and as the wake's `phase: "end"` did on 2026.10.8). Or the docs say the nested `session` row is the source for these fields.

### Actual behavior

```
2026.10.10
t+16.91 phase=end            top-level={"status":"running","hasActiveRun":true,...,"endedAt":"set"}
t+16.97 reason=cron-binding  top-level={"status":"done","endedAt":"set"}  nested session={"status":"done","hasActiveRun":false,"activeRunIds":[],...}

2026.10.8
t+15.57 phase=end            top-level={"status":"done","hasActiveRun":false,"activeRunIds":[],"endedAt":"set"}

fake OpenAI-compatible model (in the gist)

Gateway -> openai-completions (local fake)

We now read the session again on every push for it, so this is a heads-up, not a blocker. Related to #177065 (no idle push after a run the Gateway starts itself).

## Problem to solve
Generic JSON accessors live beside node invocation helpers even though chat, Gateway parsing, settings, voice and Wear consume them. Chat model identity policy also lives in a Compose picker but is used by controllers. Talk route parsing imports a model predicate from setup readiness while readiness imports that parser back. These dependencies make otherwise independent app logic harder to change and test.

## Proposed solution
Use the existing shared data owners, migrate every affected caller, and remove replaced implementations. Deliver narrow PRs with source/history evidence, focused Android validation and independent review.

Initial candidates:
- Move unchanged generic JSON accessors to the existing shared JSON owner.
- Move cron list parsing and summary contracts from runtime orchestration into the existing cron data owner.
- Consolidate model identity policy outside the picker.
- Remove the Talk config/readiness dependency cycle.

## Rejected consolidation candidates

Wear text projections accept different malformed-input shapes, so merging them directly would change behavior. Installed-skill readiness predicates are already shared; an additional classifier would add complexity for a negligible reduction.

## Impact and compatibility
Internal maintenance work; no intended user-visible behavior, protocol, permission, credential, persistence or dependency changes. Releases and deployments are outside scope.

## Alternatives considered
Keep feature-local helpers when their semantics differ. Avoid broad extraction-only rewrites, duplicate compatibility aliases and new abstractions without a concrete responsibility.

## Implementation intent
Maintainer-requested cleanup campaign. Each PR will link this issue and record its own validation and compatibility evidence.

## Delivery status

Remote-verified merges: 0. Nine reviewed candidates are published; the original delivery target remains unchanged pending scope review.

| Lane | PR | Local proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contracts/chat | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202840 | JSON owner; 108 tests per phone flavor |
| Voice/Wear | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202843 | Talk route policy; 138 tests per phone flavor |
| Settings/domain | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202848 | Cron summary owner; 41 tests per phone flavor |
| Contracts/chat | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202870 | Model policy owner; 216 tests per phone flavor |
| Voice/Wear | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202876 | Wear model state; 24 tests and unchanged picker captures |
| Settings/domain | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202877 | Cron text adapters; 32 tests per phone flavor |
| Settings/domain | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202892 | Installed-skill owner; 88 tests per phone flavor |
| Contracts/chat | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202903 | Runtime fixture lifetime; 41 tests per phone flavor and failing/passing teardown controls |
| Contracts/chat | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202898 | Connection state owner; 87 tests per phone flavor |

Compilation, focused tests, Kotlin lint, staged-content guards and independent source reviews passed for each candidate. Together they remove 48 production lines while removing duplicate state, an obsolete wrapper, cross-layer dependencies and compatibility adapters. The ninth closes previously unowned runtime fixtures using the existing teardown helper, adding 24 test lines without changing assertions.

Local proof is separate from PR-head CI. Five completed runs failed during Maven/UTP dependency setup; each PR records its gap. Wear, cron-text and connection-state PR CI passed. The runtime-fixture PR's CI is still running. Native preparation is complete for all nine; merge verification remains pending for all nine.

Deeper ownership audits identified the installed-skill wrapper and duplicate connection state after the initial six candidates. Other sampled opportunities did not justify a substantive cutover: history/session extraction overlaps active contributor work, and attachment, speech and settings adapters retain distinct contracts. Trivial dead fields and file-only splits are excluded from the delivery count.

issues.body:
## Summary

The Matrix channel's session-binding adapter drops plugin-owned metadata when a plugin binds a conversation, so a plugin-owned binding cannot be created through the documented API on Matrix.

## Versions

- `openclaw` 2026.11.6 with `@openclaw/matrix` 2026.11.6 (also present in 2026.6.1)

## Details

- In `@openclaw/matrix` 2026.11.6, `dist/.setup/thread-bindings-*.mjs`, the adapter's `bind()` builds the stored record with only `agentId`, `label` and `boundBy`. The plugin metadata passed by the caller (plugin id / root / owner fields) is not carried into the record.
- In core 2026.11.6, `conversation-binding-*.mjs` `bindConversationNow` then rejects the result with `plugin binding was created without plugin metadata`.
- Net effect: a non-bundled plugin that asks to own a Matrix room conversation (the flow behind `onConversationBindingResolved` / plugin conversation binding approval) cannot complete the binding on Matrix without patching the plugin.

## Repro

1. Install a non-bundled plugin that requests a plugin-owned conversation binding for a Matrix room (conversation binding approval flow).
2. Approve the binding.
3. Observe the binding call fail with `plugin binding was created without plugin metadata`; the Matrix binding store has a record without the plugin fields.

## Expected

The Matrix adapter's `bind()` preserves the plugin metadata it receives (as other channel adapters do), so core can verify and keep the binding plugin-owned.

## Note

Related Matrix issues seen on 2026.6.1 (plain messages treated as text-slash command turns, and Matrix replies skipping `message_sending`) appear fixed in 2026.11.x — thank you. This report is only about the remaining binding-metadata gap.

issues.body:
### Summary / 概要

SQLite write transactions are holding the write lock for **30–43 seconds**, causing severe stalls (slow agent replies, slow memory/session search). The slow-operation log records only the generic category `database.domain.execute`, which is a catch-all bucket — **no SQL text, table, or statement is logged**, making root-cause identification impossible from logs alone.

单个 SQLite 写事务持写锁 **30–43 秒**，导致明显的卡顿（回复变慢、记忆/会话检索变慢）。慢操作日志只记录兜底分类 `database.domain.execute`，**不记录 SQL 文本、表名或语句**，仅凭日志无法定位根因。

### Environment / 环境

- OpenClaw: `2026.10.9`
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), x64
- Node: v24.22.1
- DB: local SQLite agent store (`openclaw-agent.sqlite`)
- Model provider: deepseek (unrelated)
- Channel: WeChat direct message (unrelated)

### Observed behavior / 现象

Slow-op statistics from the agent log (most recent 12 MB of log):

| Operation | Count > 5s | Max duration |
|---|---|---|
| `database.domain.execute` | **51** | **43.2 s** |
| `session transcript export snapshot` | 34 | 38.9 s |
| `session context snapshot read` | 3 | — |

Stalls clustered in a short window and recurred dozens of times within a few hours — **reproducible**.

日志最近 12 MB 内的慢操作统计：

| 操作 | 超 5 秒次数 | 最长耗时 |
|---|---|---|
| `database.domain.execute` | **51** | **43.2 秒** |
| `session transcript export snapshot` | 34 | 38.9 秒 |
| `session context snapshot read` | 3 | — |

卡顿集中出现，几个小时内重复几十次，**可稳定复现**。

### Impact / 影响

While one write transaction holds the lock, all other writes queue behind it. In practice this shows up as:

- assistant replies stalling for tens of seconds
- memory / session search appearing "broken" or returning stale-timeout errors
- channel messages feeling dropped or out of order

一个写事务持锁期间，其他所有写操作排队等待。实际表现为：

- 助手回复卡顿数十秒
- 记忆/会话检索看似"失效"或超时
- 通道消息像丢了或乱序

### Root cause investigation / 根因排查

`database.domain.execute` is a **fallback classification** in the source: any write operation not individually named is bucketed here. The log records only the category name and duration — **not the SQL, table, or call site**.

Therefore it is impossible to determine from logs *which* write holds the lock for 30+ seconds. We confirmed the *nature* of the problem (a single long-held write lock) but could not identify the specific statement.

`database.domain.execute` 在源码中是**兜底分类**：任何未被单独命名的写操作都归入此类。日志只记录分类名和耗时，**不记录 SQL、表名或调用点**。

因此无法从日志判断具体是哪一个写操作持锁 30 秒以上。我们已确认问题的**性质**（单个长时间持有的写锁），但无法定位到具体语句。

### Suggested improvements / 建议

1. **Log the culprit** — when a write transaction exceeds a threshold (e.g. 2 s), log the SQL text (truncated), table name, and originating call/span name.
   - 建议：写事务超过阈值（如 2s）时，记录 SQL 文本（截断）、表名、调用来源/span 名称。

2. **Split the catch-all bucket** — give main write paths (transcript append, session snapshot export, memory index update, delivery bookkeeping) distinct operation names instead of one `database.domain.execute`.
   - 建议：把主要写入路径（会话追加、会话快照导出、记忆索引更新、投递记录）拆成独立操作名。

3. **Reduce lock scope** — shorter transactions / batching, so a single large export or index rebuild does not block all other writes.
   - 建议：缩短事务粒度/批量提交，避免单次大导出或索引重建阻塞全部写入。

4. **Expose diagnostics** — surface current `busy_timeout`, journal mode, and slow-write counters in a diagnostics command.
   - 建议：在诊断命令中暴露 `busy_timeout`、journal mode 及慢写计数器。

### Additional context / 附注

- `session transcript export snapshot` (up to 38.9 s) correlates strongly with the write-lock stalls and may itself be the lock holder, but this could not be confirmed because it also does not log the underlying SQL.
- Happy to capture deeper traces (e.g. `PRAGMA` sampling during a stall) if maintainers can point to the right hook / instrumentation point.

- `session transcript export snapshot`（最长 38.9s）与写锁卡顿时间相关性明显，可能本身就是锁持有者，但因同样不记录底层 SQL，无法确认。
- 若维护者指路，我们可以在卡顿发生时采样 `PRAGMA` / 连接状态以抓取具体 SQL。

## Summary
On 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), `openclaw memory index --agent <id>` never finishes when `memory.search.remote.batch.enabled` is `true` (OpenAI provider, `text-embedding-3-small`). The reindex waits on the OpenAI Batch API indefinitely. There is no timeout, progress or error.

## Reproduction
- Two Gateways (Ubuntu 24.04, Node 26), several agents, OpenAI embeddings through a store SecretRef.
- `memory.search.remote.batch.enabled: true` → `openclaw memory index --agent <id>` hangs (left for well over the normal rebuild time).
- Reproduced on a copy of one Gateway's state.
- `openclaw config set memory.search.remote.batch.enabled false` → the same reindex completes normally (for example 686/686 files in minutes).

## Expected
The batch path completes, or falls back to synchronous embedding / fails with a clear error after a bounded wait.

## Workaround
Disable batch embedding.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The hosted model catalog's DeepSeek recommendation list still contains `deepseek-v4-flash`, which DeepSeek no longer serves, and it does not contain the working canonical id `deepseek-flash`. After a catalog refresh, the provider's current model rows no longer include `deepseek-v4-flash`, so a fresh picker does not offer it; the stale recommendation entry remains anyway, `deepseek-v4-pro` is the only recommended DeepSeek row, and `deepseek-flash` is still collapsed under "All models". The repository seed also carries `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, which matches no provider model id.


### Steps to reproduce


Observed in the TUI on 2026-11-07 15:29:

1. Open the model picker:

```text
/models
```

The DeepSeek rows included `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`; the working `deepseek/deepseek-flash` was not in the visible recommended list.

2. Select the suspicious model:

```text
/model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
```

The TUI replied `model set to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`.

3. Send a message:

```text
hello
```

Result:

```text
run error: Unknown model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash.
```

4. Recover:

```text
/model deepseek-flash
```

The session works again on `deepseek/deepseek-flash`.

A later catalog refresh removed `deepseek-v4-flash` from `models.list`, so step 1 no longer shows that row. The stale recommendation data is still present, and `deepseek-flash` is still not recommended.



### Expected behavior

`/models` should show `deepseek/deepseek-flash` as a normal selectable DeepSeek model, and should not show `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`. The working canonical id should not be hidden behind "All models." The recommendation data should contain only models the provider actually serves; `deepseek-v4-pro` should remain only if a live API call still succeeds.

### Actual behavior

`/models` doesnot show `deepseek/deepseek-flash` as a normal selectable DeepSeek model, and shows `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`.

other information:
Current rows:

```text
deepseek/deepseek-flash      (default, not recommended)
deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro     (recommended, name says retiring 2026-09-14)
```

Cached hosted catalog:

```text
source_url: https://catalog.openclaw.ai/models/v2/catalog.json
providers.deepseek.recommendedModels:
  - deepseek-v4-flash
  - deepseek-v4-pro
```

Repository recommendation seed:

```text
scripts/lib/recommended-models.json
  line 10: "deepseek-v4.1-flash"   # does not match any provider model id
  line 11: "deepseek-v4-flash"     # removed/retired model, still seeded
  line 21: "deepseek-v4-pro"       # still recommended
```



### OpenClaw version

 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (kernel 7.0.0-38-generic, x86_64)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

deepseek-flash

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> deepseek

### Additional provider/model setup details


`models.providers.deepseek` uses `api=openai-completions` and `baseUrl=https://api.deepseek.com`. Its configured model rows are `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`. The installed DeepSeek provider manifest also contains `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`.

### Logs

```shell
$ openclaw models list --provider deepseek
deepseek/deepseek-flash
deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro



$ openclaw gateway call models.list --params '{"agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:config","view":"all","includeDetails":true}' --json
deepseek-flash    available=true  recommended=false
deepseek-v4-pro   available=true  recommended=true
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Historical TUI transcript, before the catalog refresh removed the v4-flash row:

```text
/model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
model set to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
hello
run error: Unknown model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash.
agent main | session config (config) | deepseek-v4-flash high

### Impact and severity

A fresh picker recommends a dated model (`deepseek-v4-pro`) and hides the working default; a stale cache or session can still present the removed `deepseek-v4-flash` and cause failed turns. The recommendation data is internally inconsistent because it names a model that has no current row. Severity: normal, limited to DeepSeek model selection and picker clarity.

### Additional information



The catalog refresh removed the `deepseek-v4-flash` row, which masks the visible symptom but does not fix the recommendation data or the missing `deepseek-flash` recommendation. This is the report to file; the TUI acceptance failure is retained only as historical evidence and is not filed separately.

Related: #144378 (original DeepSeek catalog drift report) and #144469 (merged fix for canonical Flash thinking controls). This is a separate recommendation-data defect.
