issues.body:
### Summary

When an automation's condition script (`trigger.script`) throws, the run keeps only the error string. Record the script's own console output and its tool-call count for the failed evaluation, so the author can see what the script observed.

### Problem to solve

A condition script that fails intermittently is hard to diagnose after the fact. The run's error is `cron trigger evaluation failed (<code>): <error>` and nothing else: no command output, no exit code, nothing the script logged.

A real case: a condition followed the documented pattern (run a command with `exec`, check `status` and `exitCode`, `JSON.parse(result.aggregated)`) and failed about twice a day with `SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Unable to parse JSON string`. The run history could not show what the command had returned. Finding the cause took a separate read-only watcher that copied the condition and waited for the next occurrence. (That cause is fixed separately: OpenClaw's note about a process the command left running was mixed into the command output.)

Where the facts are dropped:

- `src/cron/trigger-script.ts:652-657`: a failed headless run returns `scriptFailure(result.error, result.code)`. The failed result also has `output` (what the script wrote with `console.log` and the other `console` methods) and `toolCallCount` (`src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts:50-56`), and both are discarded.
- `src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts:290-296`: the run outcome is the error string plus the failure classification.

### Proposed solution

Keep a small, bounded record for a failed evaluation only:

- the script's `output` from the failed headless result, as a capped tail (for example the last 2,000 characters), redacted the same way other run diagnostics are when they leave the Gateway;
- `toolCallCount`.

Put them in the existing run diagnostics for that run, so `openclaw automations runs` and the Control UI show them where a failed payload's diagnostics already appear. A successful or quiet (`fire: false`) evaluation records nothing new.

This gives authors one supported way to leave evidence: `console.log` what the script saw before it throws. It needs no new capture inside the script runtime, because the output is already collected and bounded there.

### Alternatives considered

- Record the last `exec` result (status, exit code, output tail) automatically. More helpful with no effort from the author, but it persists command output the author did not choose to keep, for every failed evaluation. The console output is opt-in.
- Tell authors to put the evidence in the thrown message. This is what the docs example does after the fix above, and it works today, but the error string is a poor place for more than a line.

### Impact

- Affected: anyone running condition-triggered automations.
- Severity: diagnosis only; the automation itself behaves the same.
- Frequency: every failed evaluation.
- Consequence: intermittent condition failures take a custom watcher or guesswork to explain.

### Evidence/examples

The incident above, on a Gateway built from `main` at `4639df386419` (2026-11-20): 38 of 39 evaluations were clean, and the failing one could only be explained by capturing the `exec` result live.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Not yet. It changes what a run record retains, so the retained fields and their cap need a maintainer decision first.

### Additional information

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202852 fixes the cause of that incident (OpenClaw's note about a leftover process was mixed into the command output) and updates the docs example to put the evidence in the thrown message.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The PostgreSQL search DDL builders render a vector index's `dimensions` value directly into SQL, and only store admission (`admitPostgresSearch`) checks that it is an integer from 1 to 16000.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On main, call `postgresSearchSql` from `src/infra/database-engine/postgres-search-schema.ts` with a vector index whose `postgres.dimensions` is not an integer from 1 to 16000, for example `3.5`.
2. Read the rendered `CREATE TABLE` statement.

### Expected behavior

The builder refuses the value with the same error that `admitPostgresSearch` raises (dimensions must be from 1 to 16000), so no caller can render vector DDL from an unchecked value.

### Actual behavior

The value is copied into the statement as written:

```text
CREATE TABLE "vectors" (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES "notes"("id") ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE, embedding "public".vector(3.5) NOT NULL);
```

A string value is copied the same way, so a value that is a DDL fragment would become part of the statement. Table, column and schema names in the same statements are quoted with `pgSearchName`; only `dimensions` is not.

### OpenClaw version

main at b4a41aa642c (2026-11-20)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2

### Install method

pnpm dev (source checkout)

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not model related)

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not provider related; PostgreSQL database engine)

### Logs

```shell
# probe script calling postgresSearchSql with dimensions: 3.5, main at b4a41aa642c
RENDERED: CREATE TABLE "vectors" (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES "notes"("id") ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE, embedding "public".vector(3.5) NOT NULL);
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Unquoted uses of `source.dimensions` on main:

- `src/infra/database-engine/postgres-search-schema.ts`: `postgresSearchSql` (the backfill `INSERT`, `bit(...)`, `vector(...)` and the sync trigger body) and `rebuildPostgresSearch`.
- `src/infra/database-engine/postgres-vector.ts`: the projection refresh in `bindPostgresVector().write`.

The only check is in `admitPostgresSearch` (`Number.isInteger(dimensions)` and 1 to 16000). `postgresSchemaSql` in `src/infra/database-engine/postgres-schema.ts` also renders search extension definitions that `withPostgresSearchExtensions` parses from the stored `openclaw_schema_meta.search_extensions` value, and `verifyPostgresSchemaDefinition` runs that DDL in a scratch schema. That path does not check dimensions.

### Impact and severity

Affected: PostgreSQL stores with vector search.
Severity: low; defense in depth. No current path from an untrusted caller is known: values written through admission are checked, and the stored metadata path needs write access to the store's own schema metadata, which is trusted operator access under SECURITY.md.
Frequency: only with a malformed stored value or a future caller that skips admission.
Consequence: a malformed value becomes part of the executed DDL instead of a clear error.

### Additional information

The fix is small: check the value where the SQL is built, with the same message as admission. A draft PR with a unit test is ready.

issues.body:
## Summary

On an explicit restart, the Gateway logs `gateway is draining for restart` and then sits in systemd's `stop-sigterm` state for the **full `TimeoutStopSec` window** (5m30s here) before being killed. Two periodic tasks keep firing once per minute against resources that have already been closed, each logging a failure and apparently never unregistering their timers.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1), Linux, Node 24
- systemd `--user` unit from `openclaw gateway install`, `TimeoutStopUSec=5min 30s`
- 17 plugins loaded, no channel plugins with long-lived connections

## Observed

```
19:36:59  [agents/subagent-registry] subagent run sweep skipped: gateway is draining for restart
19:36:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:36:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
19:37:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:37:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
19:38:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:38:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
19:39:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:39:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
```

`systemctl --user show` during this period:

```
ActiveState=deactivating
SubState=stop-sigterm
TimeoutStopUSec=5min 30s
```

The unit became `active` again at 19:41:35, i.e. only once the stop timeout had elapsed and systemd escalated. The subagent sweep, by contrast, correctly notices the drain and skips itself — so the drain flag is reachable; these two tasks just don't consult it or don't clear their interval.

## Expected

After the drain begins, periodic tasks whose owning resources have been closed should unregister (or check the drain flag as `subagent-registry` already does), so the process can exit promptly instead of waiting out `TimeoutStopSec`.

## Impact

Every explicit restart costs ~5 minutes of downtime rather than seconds. With `Restart=always` this also widens the window described in #144976, where a stop that exhausts the drain window is followed by an unrequested restart — these two timers look like a plausible way to exhaust it.

## Notes on related issues

- #144976 — slow drain followed by unwanted auto-restart; this report may be one cause of the slow drain, but the symptom is different.
- #101720 (closed) and #128948 (closed) — timers outliving their owner in other subsystems; same shape, different components.
- #153153 — `TimeoutStopSec` too small on installed units; here the timeout is already 5m30s and is fully consumed.

This was observed while restarting to recover from #152965, so the two came up together, but they are independent: the hang reproduces on a plain restart regardless of what prompted it. Filing separately as offered in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152965#issuecomment-5751556093.

issues.body:
## Summary
In Code Mode, a `catalog.search()` whose result includes an MCP tool entry marks the `exec` cell as network content, even when no MCP or network tool runs. The marked `exec` result taints the turn. Every memory write later in that turn (daily notes via write/edit/apply_patch) is recorded `untrusted`, and so is any session-memory snapshot that covers the turn. The file mark never returns to `agent`, and memory-core dreaming never promotes untrusted candidates. Reading MCP declarations without calling the tool (`API.read("mcp/…")`, `MCP.<server>.$api`) marks the cell the same way.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (b556fdf), Linux, Gateway as a systemd user service
- OpenAI models on the OpenClaw runtime, Code Mode engaged by the default `auto` policy (catalog `compat.codeMode: "preferred"`)
- MCP servers configured: n8n, mslearn, resend (77 of 180 catalog entries)
- memory-core with dreaming enabled

## Evidence (one installation, agent `main`, 2026-11-08 00:00 to 2026-11-10 14:50 UTC)
- 972 of 2,409 assistant messages carry `turnTainted`.
- 411 Code Mode `exec`/`wait` results carry `resultContentSource: "network"`. 127 of them made no network or MCP call in that cell:
  - 43 only searched or described the catalog, or read MCP declarations. Example: `catalog.search("cron scheduler runs job history")` next to two local `read` calls.
  - 84 loaded a value that an earlier marked cell had stored (`load` / `results.load`). That propagation looks intended and is not part of this report.
- 15 of the 57 tainted turns made no network or MCP call at all. Their only marks come from catalog or MCP-declaration reads. They account for 114 tainted assistant messages, and 10 of the 15 are owner DM turns.
- Method: transcript `toolResult.__openclaw.resultContentSource`, nested calls from the trajectory, and the cell source. A cell counts as making a network call if it ran web_fetch, web_search, x_search, browser, canvas, decision_evaluate or any MCP tool.

## Where (2026.11.2 dist, plus source on main at 10d6744)
- Marking: `tool-search-CpXd2QC7.mjs:922` (search) and `:950` (describe) run `if (entry.source !== "openclaw" && options?.parentToolCallId) this.observeNetworkContent(options.parentToolCallId)`. Search runs it for every returned entry, so one MCP hit in the result is enough. Source: `src/agents/tool-search-runtime.ts:236-237` and `:304-305`. Code Mode's `catalog.search` passes the cell id (`src/agents/code-mode-bridge.ts:309`). Code Mode's own describe excludes MCP (`includeMcp: false`, `:342`). MCP declarations go through `$api`, which marks the cell (`:425`).
- Mark to taint: the `exec` result goes through `formatToolSearchControlResult`, which attaches `resultContentSource: "network"` when `hasNetworkContent()` is true (`src/agents/tool-search-runtime.ts:573-578`, called from `src/agents/code-mode.ts:235`). `toolResultTaintsTurn` taints the turn on that field (`packages/agent-core/src/turn-taint.ts:24-25`). #169560 connected this signal to turn taint. Before that it only fenced the text.
- Memory write: `agent-tools-D-SpOaZD.mjs:640` (`src/agents/agent-tools.assembly.ts:191-194`): a write to a memory path in a tainted turn records `untrusted`. A session-memory snapshot becomes `untrusted` if any assistant message it covers carries `turnTainted` (`src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.ts:154-155`).
- Sticky mark: `memory-artifact-provenance-p7kC0vvP.mjs:77` (`src/memory/memory-artifact-provenance.ts:151-155`): the mark returns to `agent` only if the previous mark was `agent` with a matching hash, so one tainted write is permanent for that file.
- Promotion: `short-term-promotion-CspvLaBp.mjs:36-39` (`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-consolidation-candidates.ts:11-15`), applied at `:829` (`extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-apply.ts:281`): untrusted candidates are never promoted. The comment there assumes that workspace memory files index as `agent`.

## Expected
Catalog results carry tool names, schemas and descriptions. The same MCP descriptions in the direct tool list never taint a turn. Taint comes only from tool results, and a direct MCP tool definition carries the server description while its `resultContentSource: "network"` applies only to execution (`src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts`). Code Mode's guest code also marks MCP metadata lazily, only when the program reads it (`src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts:548`, `:561`). The host, however, marks the cell as soon as a search result contains an MCP entry, even if the program only uses the callable name.

Fencing MCP-supplied text as external content makes sense. Tainting the turn for it is the problem. Either only the result of an executed network or MCP tool should taint the turn, or, if catalog and declaration metadata are meant to count, this should be documented, because in Code Mode it turns ordinary tool lookups into untrusted memory.

## Reproduction
Not run as an isolated test. From the code above: Code Mode model, one MCP server configured, owner DM. Ask for something that makes the cell run `catalog.search()` with a query that also matches an MCP tool, then ask the agent to save a fact to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` in the same turn. The `exec` result is fenced as external content and carries `resultContentSource: "network"`, the next assistant message carries `turnTainted`, and the file's provenance is `untrusted`. No network tool ran.

## Related
- #186638: the maintenance memory flush is always `untrusted`. On this install the two daily notes `main` wrote on 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09 are `untrusted`, but their last writer was that flush, so they are not counted here.
- #153426: sticky provenance has no supported recovery path.
- #169560: connected `hasNetworkContent()` to turn taint.

issues.body:
## Use case

A shared Slack builder can start an authorized coding task and receive private child completion, but cannot persist a later CI/review checkpoint for the same conversation. The requester is an admitted Slack user, not a Gateway owner. We need this to survive Gateway restarts without granting workspace users control-plane administration.

## Observed on 2026.10.8

- Native Slack request; configured agent permits `automations` (`cron` alias).
- Requester is not a configured Gateway owner.
- Native tool discovery omits `automations`; a real Slack probe could not create a one-minute same-thread reminder.
- `src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` includes `automations` in `GATEWAY_CONTROL_PLANE_TOOLS`, then `GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS`.
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` applies that owner-only deny to the admitted non-owner turn. An ordinary allowlist does not override it.
- The automation tool and creator-authority code otherwise describe requester-scoped new-job creation. It is unclear which non-owner channel surface can reach that functionality.

Reproduction: admit a non-owner human to a Slack channel and an agent whose tool policy allows `automations`; ask it to schedule one reply in that thread after one minute. Inspect the actual tool catalog and accepted job, rather than accepting the model's promise. In our test, no automation tool or job was available.

The same ingress restriction remains in upstream `main` at `a8fe857038f62b209d7ef0b81e62b4a49fdfdbee`: `resolveGatewayScheduledToolAccess` exempts a verified scheduled occurrence's self-job tool, while ingress turns retain the owner-only rule. The newer `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations.scope: "caller"` restricts administrative grants; it does not itself expose this tool to non-owner ingress.

## Requested native capability

An explicitly enabled, caller-scoped schedule/checkpoint for an admitted conversation, with the runtime binding the creator, agent, account and original session. It should retain the caller's effective tool restrictions, permit cancellation/inspection only within that scope, and resume the original conversation for reconciliation and delivery.

This does not require command jobs, arbitrary destinations, cross-session wakes, global job administration, or making ordinary Slack users Gateway owners. Those can retain their existing restrictions.

## Acceptance cases

1. An admitted non-owner creates one bounded same-thread checkpoint and receives an accepted job ID.
2. Another requester/session cannot inspect, change, cancel or redirect it.
3. Restart preserves the accepted checkpoint and its caller restrictions.
4. On execution the original conversation reconciles current state and replies once; intermediate/raw child output is not announced independently.
5. Expiry, cancellation and completion stop the obligation without duplicate effects.
6. Command payloads, broader tool grants and foreign delivery targets remain unavailable.

## Related work

[Issue #41586](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41586) was resolved by native child-completion delivery. That path works for us. This request concerns a later external-work checkpoint after the child is idle, rather than child completion.

We verified an operator-installed one-shot command calling native `wake` with delivery disabled as an operator maintenance procedure. It survives restart and returns to the parent conversation, but does not solve requester scheduling. We have not patched core, added a privileged CLI wrapper, or broadened channel users into owners.

Is a supported requester-scoped ingress path intended already, or should this be tracked as a separate native capability?

issues.body:
### Summary

Since plugin generation capture landed (#144252, first shipped in 2026.9.6), a Gateway with an external or workspace plugin that has a large package or dependency tree blocks its event loop for minutes. It happens at startup, and again whenever the prepared model runtime republishes. While the loop is blocked the Gateway accepts TCP connections but answers nothing, including `/healthz`, WebSocket RPCs and channel polling.

`capturePluginGenerationArtifact` (`src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.ts`) copies the plugin package synchronously on the main thread. When no `entryFile` is set, `copyPackage` copies the whole root. It then walks and copies the dependency tree through `capturePluginDependencies` → `linkDependency` → `copyPackage` → `copy`.

### Evidence

**Isolated repro on origin/main `4d4d99d`**, using a synthetic 878 MB context-engine plugin:
- The Gateway stalls for 219 s before it starts listening, then for another 168 s.
- It logs `prepared model runtime startup degraded after 120000ms (workspace plugins; agent main)`.

**Production Gateway on 2026.9.6.** The plugin root is a Bun global install: a 134 MB package whose sibling `node_modules` hold 1.5 GB across 221 packages.
- **Startup:** the process started at T+0 and logged `http server listening` at T+2m20s. `/healthz` timed out until about T+7m.
- **Stacks:** four inspector samples taken during the hang all show the same stack:
  ```
  realpathSync / path.join
  ← pluginNativeNamespaceMemberPath / resolvePreparedSource
  ← copy (recursive)
  ← materialize ← copyPackage ← linkDependency ← capturePluginDependencies ← captureDependencies
  ← materialize ← copyPackage ← capturePluginGenerationArtifact
  ← bindPluginInstanceModuleLoader ← loadPluginModule ← loadRuntimePluginCandidate
  ```
- **Earlier, during a prepared-runtime republish:**
  - The event loop was blocked for 124 s (`eventLoopDelayMaxMs=124352`).
  - Telegram polling stalled.
  - `config.patch` took 125 s and returned `UNAVAILABLE`, followed by `prepared model runtime reload failed after config commit: prepared model runtime publication (workspace plugins; agent main) timed out; restarting gateway`.
  - The Gateway then restarted, and startup blocked again.
  - Separately, the Control UI's provider sign-in stayed on a blank tab for the whole outage. That is covered by #160954.

A `thinkingDefault` patch alone hot-applies in 50 ms in the isolated repro. The republish in production was probably already pending. Candidate cause: #160120, a refresh loop triggered by an auth profile that fails to resolve. That link is being verified.

### Impact

- Any install with a large external or workspace plugin.
- The Gateway becomes unreachable for minutes on every startup and on every prepared-runtime republish.
- Config hot reloads can escalate into restarts, which block again.
- 2026.7.35 is not affected; 2026.9.6 (npm `latest`/`beta`) is.

### Expected

Capture should not block the Gateway event loop for more than a bounded time. An unchanged plugin should reuse its existing capture instead of being recopied.

issues.body:
**Environment:**
- OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (157d8c2), official image, Node 24.22.1, Linux cgroup v2.
- State DB 190 MB (WAL); agent DBs 0.57–0.93 GB (WAL, auto_vacuum=incremental).
- ext4 on a ZFS zvol throttled to 3,000 IOPS / 70 MB/s; page cache mostly evicted by host reclaim (cgroup file cache ≈0.5 GB, DB residency 0–3.5%).

**What happens:**
1. `state.admission.fast-path` (src/state/openclaw-state-db-fast-path.ts → `isOpenClawStateSchemaFastPathEligible`) calls `assertOpenClawStateRuntimeIntegrity`. When the handle has no borrowed current host proof, that falls back to `assertSqliteIntegrity` (full `integrity_check` + `foreign_key_check`).
   - Every CLI process that touches state, and every fresh Gateway worker thread (session-reclamation and read workers that retire on idle-TTL), pays a whole-file scan inside a deferred read transaction.
   - Over 24 h (2026-10-27): 345 such admissions ≥1 s totalling 5,089 s (Gateway workers 205 / 3,520 s; CLI processes 140 / 1,570 s), max 184.5 s.
   - 84 of the 141 main-thread `slow agent database reservation` events ≥10 s that day (2,039 s) coincide with one of these admissions inside a reclamation worker.
   - Example 2026-10-28: reclamation worker threadId 172823, `state.admission.fast-path elapsedMs=147792`; then `state.write` lock-contention; then `SQLite session reclamation Worker recovered cleanup failures: database is locked` on the writer store; then clean-close receipt `close-unconfirmed`.
2. After an agent writer reservation failed (`slow agent database reservation operation=direct outcome=error elapsedMs=435033`, codeops), the lease closed with receipt `active-leases`. The next opener, a worker with `admissionMode:"sync"`, ran `integrityGateReason:"no-proof" integrityGateMode:"full"` for **269,157 ms** on a 727 MB store.
   - Every write for that agent queued behind it (`session-entry.patch queueWaitMs=325659`, …).
   - Stuck-session recovery then aborted two runs whose last tool call was 12 minutes earlier.
   - No model response was logged Gateway-wide for 12 min.

**Expected:**
- Fresh workers and CLI readers borrow or reuse the host's current integrity proof, or a cheap check (`quick_check` or header/schema only), as the docs describe for native admission classes.
- A full scan never runs synchronously in a path that holds an agent's write queue. It should run in the existing background verifier, with admission granted metadata-only as for the documented "no verification receipt" class.
- The integrity scan should be bounded or made yieldable, and attributed in logs (caller, thread role).

**Related:** #164427 (60 s `cron.history-maintenance` sweep reads all cron run records inside one IMMEDIATE transaction: here 1,121 holds ≥1 s/day, 6,993 s, max 97.5 s, with 11.6k cron rows), #161439, #170496, #183036.

**Evidence available:** log excerpts with timestamps (above), cgroup io/memory counters, dist line references.

issues.body:
An explicitly enabled standalone plugin file in `plugins.load.paths` starts with the Gateway only while it has no manifest. Adding an `openclaw.plugin.json` beside it (for example just to set `reload.turnHandover`) silently makes it startup-lazy, and a plugin that only registers hooks then never loads: its `before_tool_call` policy stops enforcing, with no warning on any CLI surface.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A manifest without `activation.onStartup` beside an enabled standalone plugin file drops the plugin from Gateway startup, and `plugins list`, `plugins inspect` and `doctor` still show it as enabled with no warning.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Write a hook-only plugin `<dir>/hook-probe.ts` whose `register(api)` only calls `api.on("before_tool_call", …)` and blocks `session_status`.
2. `plugins.load.paths: ["<dir>/hook-probe.ts"]`, `plugins.entries.hook-probe.enabled: true`; restart the Gateway.
3. `POST /tools/invoke {"tool":"session_status"}` → 403 `tool_call_blocked` (hook live).
4. Add `<dir>/openclaw.plugin.json`: `{"id":"hook-probe","reload":{"turnHandover":true},"configSchema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false}}`; restart.
5. Repeat step 3, then run `openclaw plugins list`, `openclaw plugins inspect hook-probe`, `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`.

### Expected behavior

Either the plugin keeps starting, or something says why it no longer does. The docs ([manifest capabilities](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/manifest/capabilities)) ask every plugin to set `activation.onStartup` and say omitting it no longer startup-loads, so the startup change is documented; the silence is the bug. A warning such as "standalone plugin file has a manifest without activation.onStartup …; set it to true to start with the Gateway" on `plugins inspect`/`doctor` would have caught it.

### Actual behavior

**Live, 2026.11.6 and main `dce3c29`, identical:**

| Manifest beside the file | Boot line lists it | Hook fires (`/tools/invoke`) | `plugins.list` RPC runtime | `plugins list` / `inspect` / `doctor` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | yes | yes (403 blocked) | `active` | enabled, no warning |
| without `activation` | **no** | **no (200, tool ran)** | **`unloaded`** | **enabled, no warning** |
| with `activation.onStartup: true` | yes | yes (403 blocked) | `active` | enabled, no warning |

- The only signals are the Gateway's `plugins.list` RPC (`runtime.state: "unloaded"`) and, on main, `plugins inspect --runtime` (#191095). Nothing tells the operator the manifest is the cause.
- For a tool-policy plugin this fails open: the policy silently stops enforcing.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (06afb10); also main `dce3c29`

### Operating system

Linux x64, Node 26

### Install method

npm global; main as a packed build

### Model

N/A (no model turn; `/tools/invoke`)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Logs

<details><summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

**Cause.** `src/plugins/manifest-registry-build.ts` (main `dce3c29`, the `isManifestlessConfiguredFile` branch from #171330) gives a manifestless file listed in `plugins.load.paths` a synthetic manifest with `activation: { onStartup: true }`. Once a real `openclaw.plugin.json` exists in the file's directory, that manifest is used instead. In `resolveGatewayStartupPluginPlanFromRegistry` (`src/plugins/gateway-startup-plugin-plan.ts`) an explicitly enabled non-bundled plugin is then only reached through `canStartGatewayStartupPlugin` (needs a matching provider, channel, config path, contract, `onCapabilities: ["hook"]` or a `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks` policy) or `shouldConsiderForGatewayStartup` (`onStartup === true`, a slot, memory). A hook-only manifest has none of these, so it is skipped; registered hooks are not an activation trigger because they are only known after loading.

**Related.** #117243 (enabled plugin excluded from startup, no diagnostics) was closed on 2026-10-24 as documented, with status distinguishing installed-but-inactive plugins. This report is narrower: the same file's startup behavior flips when a manifest is added, a transition #171330 introduced, and the CLI surfaces an operator checks (`plugins list`, `plugins inspect` without `--runtime`, `doctor`) still say nothing. #155079 was closed as a duplicate of #117243. #191095 makes `plugins inspect --runtime` show the Gateway state, which helps once you suspect the plugin.

**Repro script.** One script, run unchanged on both builds: three phases (no manifest, manifest without `activation`, manifest with `onStartup: true`), each restarting a fresh test Gateway and recording the boot line, a `gateway_start` hook log line from the probe, `POST /tools/invoke session_status`, the `plugins.list` RPC entry, `plugins list`, `plugins inspect` and `doctor --non-interactive`. Paths and host details are left out; the plugin also carries the usual `record-missing` provenance warning in all three phases, unrelated to this.

**Suggested fix (small).** A registry warning when an explicitly enabled (`entries.<id>.enabled` or `allow`) plugin file listed in `plugins.load.paths` has a manifest that leaves `activation.onStartup` unset. It surfaces wherever registry diagnostics already do (`plugins inspect`, `doctor`, Gateway log), next to the existing `channelConfigs` metadata warning in the same file. `onStartup: false` silences it. A broader "enabled but no trigger can ever match" check for installed plugins would need the startup plan and is left to maintainers.

</details>

Fix PR: #202831

issues.body:
### Summary

Expose the resolved resource profile to plugins through the plugin SDK, and give Knowledge a lean policy: start storage and registry on first use, and retire them when idle only if no vault watcher is live.

### Problem to solve

Plugins can't adapt to small machines. Knowledge is the largest single feature cost: about 116 MiB idle and 186 MiB busy RSS on a single bot (on vs off). Its workers hold about 50 MiB of heap, even when unused.

### Proposed solution

- **SDK:** a read-only profile signal (`standard | lean`) with change notification.
- **Knowledge in lean:**
  - defer storage and registry startup until the first call;
  - retire them when idle with no live watchers;
  - keep maintenance obligations, catching up on the next start.
- **No shared host:** Knowledge stays out of the core shared host, as its own plugin with its own lifecycle.

### Alternatives considered

- One-second retirement, tried in the prototype: rejected because it stops watching and loses warm caches.
- Sharing Knowledge storage across vaults: opt-in only, because of the cross-vault stall cost.

### Impact

Single bot: up to ~116 MiB idle when Knowledge is unused. The first Knowledge call after a cold start is slower.

### Evidence/examples

Knowledge on vs off, single bot: idle 821 vs 711 MiB, busy 1,378 vs 1,194 MiB. Measured first-call latency after retirement: 275–575 ms, against 5–12 ms warm.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes.

### Additional information

Part of #202373. Depends on #202375.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After a SQLite store worker dies while a session-entry write that changes sharing authority is in flight, later `chat.send` calls on that session fail with `UNAVAILABLE: SessionMutationFactsUnavailableError: Session access facts are unavailable; retry after session storage is ready. <- Error: Session sharing acquisition is no longer current`. The failure happens even though the replacement worker is serving traffic, the database is intact and the unacknowledged write is absent.

The source suggests it doesn't clear until the Gateway restarts: the session key goes into a process-lifetime "unknown authority" set and nothing removes it.

### Steps to reproduce

Seen in a controlled fault-injection harness (not part of the repo) against a real Gateway built from source, on the default worker topology and on an experimental consolidated-worker build. The harness reproduced it in 2 of 4 runs.

1. Start a Gateway with one agent and a session that has completed a chat turn.
2. While a session-entry mutation is running on the SQLite store worker (after the mutation statement, before `COMMIT`), terminate that worker via `Worker.terminate()`. In-flight `chat.inject`, `sessions.groups.create` and `sessions.groups.put` return `UNAVAILABLE` (`SQLite worker stopped before its result was received`, `outcome-unknown`).
3. Let the pool start a replacement worker. Recovery writes on the same agent store then succeed.
4. Send another `chat.send` to the same session.

### Expected behavior

Once a replacement worker is serving and the store is consistent, a later `chat.send` on the session either succeeds, or fails only until the unknown outcome has been reconciled against committed state.

If fail-closed until restart is intended, the error should say a restart is required, not "retry after session storage is ready".

### Actual behavior

`chat.send` fails in 6–14 ms:

```
[gateway] request handler failed: SessionMutationFactsUnavailableError: Session access facts are unavailable; retry after session storage is ready. <- Error: Session sharing acquisition is no longer current
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ chat.send 6ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=SessionMutationFactsUnavailableError: ... <- Error: Session sharing acquisition is no longer current
```

The harness didn't retry, so whether it persists wasn't observed directly.

Inferred from source (not confirmed by a test):
- When a session-entry worker write that changed sharing authority loses its receipt, [`session-accessor.sqlite-entry-worker-publication.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ea953ed6ff3a/src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-worker-publication.ts#L395-L406) and [`session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ea953ed6ff3a/src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication.ts#L119-L128) call `markSessionSharingAuthorityUnknown`.
- That adds the key to `unknownSharingAuthorities`, a global set with lifetime `close-and-restart` ([`session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication-state.ts` L49–L52, L89–L97](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ea953ed6ff3a/src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication-state.ts#L49-L97)).
- `initialize` then throws `Session sharing acquisition is no longer current` for that key on every later acquisition ([L404–L410](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ea953ed6ff3a/src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication-state.ts#L404-L410)). The gateway wraps it as `SessionMutationFactsUnavailableError` ([`session-sharing-incognito.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ea953ed6ff3a/src/gateway/session-sharing-incognito.ts#L12-L17)).
- No code path removes keys from that set before restart.

### OpenClaw version

Source build at `01d20365e2ce5b57aa61114207712048d9365975`. The cited files are unchanged on `ea953ed6ff3a`.

### Operating system

Linux container (Debian trixie, `node:24.22.1-trixie`), 8 CPUs, 3 GiB memory limit, no swap.

### Install method

Source build (pnpm), run inside a container.

### Model

Local synthetic OpenAI Responses-compatible mock (`openai/membench-synthetic`).

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> local synthetic mock provider (loopback)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not provider-related. The failure happens before any model request.

### Logs

From the main-topology case (lean-topology case is equivalent, 07:51 UTC):

```
07:34:26.155 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ chat.inject 82ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=failed to write chat history: Session patch has no confirmed native completion and commit receipt | SQLite worker exited with code 1 | ... | outcome-unknown
07:34:27.021 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ sessions.groups.create 37ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=SQLite worker stopped before its result was received: SQLite worker exited with code 1
07:34:27.463 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ sessions.groups.put 38ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=SQLite worker stopped before its result was received: SQLite worker exited with code 1
07:34:27.872 [gateway] request handler failed: SessionMutationFactsUnavailableError: Session access facts are unavailable; retry after session storage is ready. <- Error: Session sharing acquisition is no longer current
07:34:27.873 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ chat.send 6ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE ...
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Storage stayed consistent in the failing runs:
- every acknowledged operation was present exactly once (34/34 across the four runs);
- every unacknowledged fault operation was absent (14/14);
- multi-statement transactions were all-or-none;
- `PRAGMA integrity_check` returned `ok` for all 7 databases in every run.

In the two runs that passed, the post-fault chat completed. The difference in fault ordering between passing and failing runs wasn't isolated.

### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** any session whose sharing-authority write was in flight when its SQLite store worker died, for example from an OOM kill, a crash or a forced termination. Small-memory installs are the most exposed: in the same study the default topology hit cgroup OOM kills in a 1.5 GiB container.
- **Severity:** that session can't accept new chat messages, likely until the Gateway restarts.
- **Frequency:** 2 of 4 controlled fault runs.
- **Consequence:** user messages are rejected after an otherwise recovered crash.

### Additional information

- Possibly related to #158379, which reports the same error for a different reproducer (concurrent first-session creation across agents). That one has no worker death involved.
- Suggested direction: once a replacement worker is serving, reconcile unknown-outcome keys against committed rows. The store is consistent and the unacknowledged write is absent, so the facts can be re-read. Alternatively, clear the marker on that reconciliation. If fail-closed is deliberate, surface a restart-required error and a health signal.
- Not tested: termination inside a native SQLite instruction, OOM-kill victim identification, and whether a retry or Gateway restart clears the condition.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A plugin counter registered through `api.metrics` drops `inc(labels, 0)`, so the Prometheus scrape cannot show a known label set at 0 before its first real event.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable `diagnostics-prometheus` and a plugin with `plugins.entries.<id>.allowMetrics: true`.
2. In the plugin, register a counter `jobs_total` with label `outcome`.
3. From a service, call `counter("jobs_total").inc({ outcome: "error" }, 0)` and then `inc({ outcome: "ok" }, 1)`.
4. Scrape `GET /api/diagnostics/prometheus` with Gateway auth.

### Expected behavior

The scrape shows both label sets, `{outcome="error"} 0` and `{outcome="ok"} 1`. Gauges from the same API already export 0, and initializing known label sets at 0 is standard Prometheus practice so `rate()`, `increase()` and `absent()` can tell an idle label set from a missing one.

### Actual behavior

Only `openclaw_plugin_zero_proof_jobs_total{outcome="ok"} 1` is exported. The `{outcome="error"}` label set does not exist until its first non-zero increment. The sample reaches the exporter, and `scalar()` in `extensions/diagnostics-prometheus/src/prometheus-metric-store.ts` returns on `mode === "add" && value === 0` before the series is created.

### OpenClaw version

main ed8f4e680cb (source checkout)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2

### Install method

source checkout, `pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`

### Model

Not applicable (no model call)

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable

### Logs

```shell
[plugins] zero-proof: jobs_total.inc({ outcome: "error" }, 0)
[plugins] zero-proof: jobs_total.inc({ outcome: "ok" }, 1)

# HELP openclaw_plugin_zero_proof_jobs_total Proof jobs by outcome.
# TYPE openclaw_plugin_zero_proof_jobs_total counter
openclaw_plugin_zero_proof_jobs_total{outcome="ok"} 1
```

### Impact and severity

Affected: plugins that publish counters through `api.metrics` (added in #198455, not yet in a release).
Severity: annoying; dashboards and `absent()` alerts treat an idle label set as missing.
Frequency: always, for any `inc(labels, 0)`.
Consequence: plugins cannot pre-initialize counters, and a plugin moving from its own metrics route to `api.metrics` loses its zero series.

### Additional information

Core counters rely on the same skip on purpose: `openclaw_model_cost_usd_total` receives `costUsd ?? 0`, and skipping 0 keeps an unknown cost from showing as a measured $0. So a fix should apply to plugin counters only.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators query automation history by whole-run completion status with `openclaw automations runs --completion-status`.

### Problem to solve

When a scheduled report is generated but its required delivery fails, the run can have execution status `ok` and completion status `failed`. An operator auditing failures with `automations runs --all --status error` misses that run. Filtering by `--delivery-status not-delivered` also matches successful runs that used best-effort delivery.

### Proposed solution

```sh
openclaw automations runs --all --completion-status failed --limit 20
```

- Accept `failed`, `succeeded`, and `unknown`. Match the completion status reported in run history. A missing value on an older entry stays unclassified.
- Support both `--all` and a single job ID. Combine the completion filter with the existing filters and apply it in the Gateway before pagination so totals and offsets describe the matching runs.
- Preserve the current behavior of `--status`, `--delivery-status`, and queries that omit the new flag.

### Alternatives considered

Page through the JSON output and use [jq](https://jqlang.org/manual/) to select `.entries[] | select(.completionStatus == "failed")`. That works today. A script still has to read and track every relevant unfiltered page to find the latest 20 failures. A plugin or shell wrapper using the current history endpoint has the same paging tradeoff.

### Impact

This affects operators who audit unattended reports, backups, or alerts from the CLI. During delivery incidents, a check based on execution errors alone can report no matching errors despite missing reports. The filter would also let incident reviews distinguish failed runs from runs whose delivery outcome is unknown.

### Evidence/examples

A direct call to the [v2026.11.6 completion resolver](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.6/src/cron/completion-status.ts#L48-L60) with synthetic inputs returned these outcomes:

| Execution status | Delivery status | Best-effort delivery | Completion status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `not-delivered` | No | `failed` |
| `ok` | `not-delivered` | Yes | `succeeded` |

The [CLI on v2026.11.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.6/src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-simple.ts#L167-L226) exposes execution and delivery filters. On the inspected [main Gateway schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8271ec9ee5d48655b6d41d39314bd4e44e73b7c0/packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts#L716-L750), `completionStatus` is available on history entries. The [CLI reference](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/cron#common-admin-commands) documents the current filters and pagination.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Related history search proposal: #202804 covers filtering by a time window.

AI-assisted proposal.

issues.body:
**What happens**

`migrations.memory.plan` (the Control UI's Settings → Import Memory) scans every project's auto-memory folder under the Claude home (`<claude home>/projects/*/memory`, dist/source-ClaZcYL7.mjs:75-114, :128). It then counts Markdown files across *all* of them against one cap: `CLAUDE_AUTO_MEMORY_MAX_FILES = 2e3` (dist/source-ClaZcYL7.mjs:10). Once the total passes 2000 the plan throws, for the whole provider (dist/memory-DQJ2_I8_.mjs:79-89):

> Claude Code auto-memory exceeds the safe import limit of 2000 Markdown files across all collections. Narrow or split the source memory before importing.

On a host where several Claude Code projects share one Claude home, a single agent's project can be small (about 400 files here) while the total is over 2000. Then no agent can import anything.

**Why the existing levers don't reach it**

- The plan params are a closed object, `{ agentId, overwrite? }` (dist/src-SkiwT5zi.mjs:2508-2511). There is no source or collection field, and the planner builds its context without one (dist/memory-import-CIhoE4LI.mjs:39-47).
- `migrations.memory.apply` can select `itemIds` (dist/src-SkiwT5zi.mjs:2517-2528). But the plan throws before any items exist, so there is nothing to select.
- `openclaw migrate claude --from <path>` can point at one project. But it needs the Gateway stopped (docs/cli/migrate.md:17-23). It also brings project CLAUDE.md into AGENTS.md, user CLAUDE.md into USER.md, MCP servers and skills unless each item is excluded (docs/cli/migrate.md:130-139). That is far wider than the memory-only import in docs/concepts/memory.md:73-102.
- "Narrow or split the source memory" means editing another tool's memory store, which the import otherwise promises to leave unchanged (docs/concepts/memory.md:97-98).

**Ask (either would do)**

1. Optional `collections` (ids or labels) on `migrations.memory.plan`, with the Control UI listing detected collections and letting the user tick them. Apply the 2000 cap to the *selected* collections.
2. Or count the cap per collection, and report an oversize collection as one skipped/error row instead of failing the whole provider.

**Workaround we used**

We copied the one project's `.md` files into `memory/imports/claude-code/<collectionSlug>-<id>/` ourselves, matching `buildAutoMemoryItems`' own target layout (dist/memory-DQJ2_I8_.mjs:83) and id (`autoMemorySourceId`, dist/source-ClaZcYL7.mjs:72-74). We backed up first and left the source untouched. The Gateway's file watch indexed it (docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md:154), and `memory_search` returns the imported files. It works, but it bypasses the verified backup and migration report that apply provides (docs/concepts/memory.md:100-102).

Version: OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), macOS.

issues.body:
**Version:** first seen on openclaw 2026.10.6, still reproducing on 2026.10.8 (2026-11-04: abort at 03:06:34 with age=379s, `dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=18 ...)` at 03:07:10, run status=ok, 434s). Same code in 2026.10.10 (latest) and 2026.11.5-beta.1: no progress calls in `dist/extensions/memory-core/index.js`, `DEFAULT_STUCK_SESSION_WARN_MS = 12e4` unchanged. Linux arm64, 16-18 dreaming workspaces.

**What happens**

The built-in "Memory Dreaming Promotion" cron runs `runShortTermDreamingPromotion` as an embedded run. It loops over every workspace in a plain `for (const { agentId, agentIds, workspaceDir } of workspaces)` loop (extensions/memory-core/index.js, ~L245-252). Each workspace takes about 15-25s, so with 16-18 workspaces the whole run takes 6-9 minutes.

The loop never calls `markDiagnosticRunProgress` / `markDiagnosticSessionProgress` / `emitCoreSemanticRunProgress`, so `lastProgress` stays at `embedded_run:started`. The stuck-session watchdog then:
- logs `stalled session ... classification=stalled_agent_run reason=active_work_without_progress` every 30s from about 120s on
- fires `action=abort_embedded_run` ("stuck session recovery") at about 360-383s (abort = max(300s, 3 x 120s warn))

The abort doesn't stop the plugin work. The loop keeps going and logs `dreaming promotion complete` 1-3 minutes after the abort, and diary files are written after that. The cron run record ends `status=ok`.

**Evidence (4 nights in a row, same every night, not tied to memory pressure)**
- 10/27: abort 03:06:32, complete 03:09:24
- 10/28: abort 03:06:40, complete 03:08:45
- 10/29: abort 03:06:23, complete 03:07:54
- 10/30: complete 03:06:10, 7ms before the abort would have fired
- Run durations over the last 5 nights: 371-564s, all status=ok. Output checked on disk: every workspace got its REM entry every night (144/144).
- Same pattern right after a fresh gateway restart at low RSS (~6.5 GiB, no heap warnings).

**Why it matters**
- Nightly false "stalled" / "aborted" log noise in any multi-agent install sends operators looking for a hang that isn't there.
- An abort that reports success but doesn't cancel the work is misleading. If the work ever really hung, recovery wouldn't free it.
- There's no workaround: `diagnostics.stuckSessionWarnMs` / `stuckSessionAbortMs` are retired (RETIRED_TUNING_PATHS), and cron `timeoutSeconds` doesn't feed the watchdog.

**Suggested fix**
1. In the dreaming promotion loop, report run progress once per workspace (and per phase), so the stall timer resets while real work is happening. This is the main fix.
2. Make `abort_embedded_run` pass an AbortSignal into plugin-hook embedded runs, and have the dreaming loop check it between workspaces, so an abort actually stops the work. Or, if a run can't be cancelled, don't log it as aborted.
3. Optional: let a cron/embedded-run declare an expected duration or stall budget, as asked for in #140401.

**Repro**
Multi-agent setup with dreaming enabled for 15 or more workspaces, then wait for the nightly promotion run. `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway | grep -E "Memory Dreaming Promotion|dreaming promotion complete|abort_embedded_run"`.

**Related (not duplicates):** #140401 (closed: watchdog threshold no longer configurable), #191822 (compaction not counted as progress), #171366 (Code Mode awaitResults aborted), #143396.

issues.body:
## Summary

Let users explicitly select `gpt-live-1.1-codex` for OpenClaw realtime voice over the existing ChatGPT subscription WebRTC route.

## Problem to solve

A ChatGPT subscriber can use `gpt-live-1-codex`, but selecting `gpt-live-1.1-codex` in OpenClaw 2026.11.6 treats it as an unlisted model. In a native Discord bridge test, the setting passed config validation but the bridge looked up only a Platform API-key profile and failed before opening a session. The same model classification controls eligibility for client-owned Talk WebRTC, including iOS.

## Proposed solution

List `gpt-live-1.1-codex` with the existing Codex voice profile and send it as the explicit model selector on the existing ChatGPT OAuth WebRTC route. Use the current iOS Talk and Discord transports. A subscriber can choose the model in Talk or set `channels.discord.voice.realtime.model` for Discord. Keep the existing defaults and Live-1 routing. Use the same OAuth-first credential order as Live-1 Codex. If the subscription profile is unavailable or cannot be loaded, allow existing Platform credentials. When a ChatGPT call attempt fails, show which route failed and retain the public API model as an explicit choice.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep using `gpt-live-1-codex`. That works today and remains the default on the subscription route, but it provides no explicit 1.1 selector.
- Use Platform API model `gpt-live-1.1`. That is a separate billing and authentication route covered by #202133.

## Impact

This affects ChatGPT subscribers who want to request 1.1 in native iOS Talk or Discord. Without the change, the explicit Codex selector consistently misses the subscription route.

## Evidence and examples

- [Codex CLI 0.171.0 source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.171.0/codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs#L118) sets `gpt-live-1.1-codex` as its v3 default.
- [OpenAI's GPT-Live-1.1 system card](https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-live-1-1/avoiding-deceptive-interactions-with-users) describes GPT-Live-1.1 as the product default for Plus and higher tiers, including Codex. That statement does not identify the model serving an individual session.
- An isolated official Codex app-server WebRTC session completed a turn with an OAuth-only login and an explicit 1.1 selector. A made-up selector also returned audio. Neither run exposed a served model ID in session or turn events.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add `--since` and `--until` to `openclaw automations runs` so operators can query a specific time window in retained run history.

### Problem to solve

During an incident, an operator often knows when a dependency was unavailable and needs to find which automations failed during that window. `automations runs --all --status error` narrows the results by status. If the incident falls outside the newest page, the operator still has to step through pages and compare timestamps manually or script the pagination and filtering.

### Proposed solution

```sh
openclaw automations runs --all --status error \
  --since 2026-11-20T09:00:00Z --until 2026-11-20T09:30:00Z
```

- Accept either bound independently as an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit timezone. Use an inclusive lower bound and an exclusive upper bound on the history timestamp returned as `entries[].ts`, the same timestamp used for ordering.
- Support both `--all` and a single job ID. Combine the time window with existing status, delivery status, and text filters.
- Apply the bounds in the Gateway before pagination so `total`, `hasMore`, and `nextOffset` describe the filtered results.
- Reject invalid timestamps and ranges whose upper bound is at or before the lower bound.

### Alternatives considered

- Use `--sort` and `--offset` to page manually. This works for a small history or an incident near one end of the result set.
- Page through `--json` output and filter `entries[].ts` with [jq](https://jqlang.org/manual/). This works today and requires the caller to fetch the relevant pages and manage pagination.

### Impact

Affects operators investigating incidents on Gateways with frequent scheduled jobs or many automations. The friction occurs when an incident window spans older history or when newer failures fill the first page. A bounded query makes it easier to identify which jobs were affected and to share a repeatable triage command.

### Evidence/examples

Source checked in [v2026.11.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.6/src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-simple.ts) and on [current main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/150edeea6e0e953c99d8723e19a78e6f9f1efa97/src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-simple.ts#L168-L225). Both expose status, delivery status, text search, sort, and offset for `runs`. The [history selector](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/150edeea6e0e953c99d8723e19a78e6f9f1efa97/src/cron/run-history.ts#L124-L201) already filters before slicing the page. The command above shows the proposed interface.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The request is scoped to querying retained history with existing Gateway visibility rules.

AI-assisted draft.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add **Copy link** to the action menu on a saved automation in the Control UI.

### Problem to solve

When writing a runbook or handing off a schedule change, operators need a link to the automation itself. A name can be ambiguous across agents, and an **Inspect run** link opens one historical execution. The automation detail menu has no way to copy a job-level link directly.

### Proposed solution

Add **Copy link** to the automation detail menu for saved jobs, including paused jobs. Copy an absolute URL using the existing job route, such as `/automations?job=<job-id>`, under the Control UI's current origin and base path. Opening the link should show the same saved automation through the existing Gateway access checks. Show a brief confirmation when the link is copied.

### Alternatives considered

Copying from the address bar or the sidebar is a workaround. A URL copied from an **Inspect run** page can include a specific run, so operators have to find the job-level link or edit the URL by hand. The menu action would always copy the job-level URL.

### Impact

This saves a few steps each time an operator bookmarks a job, documents it, or asks another authorized operator to review its schedule. It matters most when jobs have similar names or when the starting point is a run notification.

### Evidence/examples

For example, an operator investigating a failed nightly backup can open its **Inspect run** notification, then copy a link to the saved backup automation for the runbook.

On [upstream main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e5ccb878a104636e931255675363b4b5fcc9d53d/ui/src/pages/cron/view-controls.tsx#L76-L124), the job menu offers Clone and Remove. issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On an explicit multi-agent gateway, `openclaw message send --media` fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId.` even though the account binding resolves correctly and the text part of the same command would send fine. The failure occurs only when `--media` is supplied; text-only sends with identical flags succeed. No CLI flag exists to pass an agentId/agent-scoped session key through to the gateway's outbound media-staging resolver, and no config-level owner satisfies that code path.

This looks like the same class of bug as #186392 (iOS share attachment path resolves the agent from a raw/non-agent-scoped session key instead of the canonical one), but on the `message send` CLI → gateway outbound media path. I searched for an existing report of this exact surface and could not find one.

### Steps to reproduce

- OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10), npm global install, Linux arm64 (Raspberry Pi OS).
- Explicit multi-agent fleet: `agents.ownership: "explicit"` with 7 agents (`portfolio-guardian`, `sql`, `lead-scout`, `gmail-cleanup`, `ai-news`, `health-monitor`, plus a `default` Telegram account), each bound to its own Telegram bot account via `bindings[].match.accountId`.
- `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` set to `portfolio-guardian`.

1. Text-only send — succeeds:
   ```
   openclaw message send --channel telegram --account portfolio-guardian --target 6938637819 --message "test"
   ```
2. Same command plus a local media file that lives inside the bound agent's own workspace:
   ```
   openclaw message send --channel telegram --account portfolio-guardian --target 6938637819 --message "test chart" --media ~/.openclaw/workspace-portfolio-guardian/staging/test_chart.png
   ```
   → fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError` (verbatim below).

### Expected behavior

With a valid `--account` whose binding unambiguously resolves to a single configured agent (the verbose log shows this resolution succeeding before the failure), outbound media staging should use that same resolved agentId, as it presumably does for text-only sends.

### Actual behavior

```
[routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=telegram accountId=portfolio-guardian peer=direct:6938637819 guildId=none teamId=none bindings=1
[routing] binding: agentId=portfolio-guardian accountPattern=portfolio-guardian peer=none guildId=none teamId=none roles=0
[routing] match: matchedBy=binding.account agentId=portfolio-guardian
[routing] resolveAgentRoute: ... (second pass, also matches)
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId."
  }
}
```

Stack points at the gateway request path (`client-*.mjs` `GatewayClientRequestError`), i.e. the error is thrown gateway-side during media staging, not by CLI argument parsing. `--dry-run` with the same flags succeeds and echoes the correct `mediaUrls`, so the failure happens in the real send's session-agent resolution step.

### What I ruled out (no config workaround found)

- File location: fails identically for paths under `/mnt/...` (SMB mount), `/tmp`, and inside the bound agent's own workspace dir — not a media-root allowlist issue.
- `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId = portfolio-guardian`: already set; fixes CLI-owner resolution for other commands but does not affect this path (same finding as #186392: "systemAgent.agentId is not used on this path").
- `agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId = portfolio-guardian`: added, tested, still fails.
- Removing `agents.ownership: "explicit"`: rejected by config validation ("multi-agent rosters require agents.ownership=\"explicit\"..."), consistent with the note in #128637 that removing the flag is not a viable workaround.
- No `--agent` flag on `message send`, and no session-key flag either (`message send --help` has no session option), so there is no way to supply any of the three accepted owners (agentId / agent-scoped session key / fallbackAgentId) from this CLI surface.

Reading `resolveSessionAgentIdsStrict`/`resolveSelectedSessionAgentId` in `agent-scope-config`, the resolver accepts exactly those three owner sources; the outbound media path appears to pass none of them, falling through to `resolveDefaultAgentId`, which throws under explicit ownership with >1 agent.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (06afb10)

### Operating system

Linux 6.18.60+rpt-rpi-2712 (arm64), Raspberry Pi OS

### Install method

npm global (~/.npm-global prefix)

### Model

Not model-specific; fails before any model call (CLI → gateway media staging).

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw CLI → gateway WebSocket → telegram channel plugin (bot API)

### Additional provider/model setup details

No response

### Logs

```
AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId.
GatewayClientRequestError
    at Object.createRequestError (file:///.../dist/client-cecYKgQa.mjs:1037:31)
    at GatewayPendingRequests.handleResponse (file:///.../dist/client-cecYKgQa.mjs:469:43)
    at GatewayProtocolClient.handleMessage (file:///.../dist/client-cecYKgQa.mjs:875:17)
```

### Impact and severity

Blocks our nightly portfolio report automation: charts are generated and the text report delivers, but chart attachments cannot be delivered from any cron/script context on a multi-agent gateway. 100% reproducible for `message send --media`; single-agent installs are unaffected (consistent with this being introduced by the explicit-ownership refactor in #114388).

### Additional information

Likely-related prior reports, all same error family:
- #186392 — iOS share attachment path resolves agent from raw session key (closest root-cause match)
- #145217 — sessions.compact ignores explicit agentId on global-keyed sessions
- #128637 — umbrella multi-agent `AgentSelectionRequiredError` report; confirms removing ownership flag is not a workaround
- #159334 / #159080 — channel default routing has no explicit owner

Suggested fix direction: thread the already-resolved binding agentId (visible in the verbose routing log) into the outbound media-staging session resolution, or accept an explicit `--agent` on `message send` and pass it through to the gateway request.

issues.body:
### Summary

Scheduled automations should pick their model and inference account the way an interactive turn on the same agent or session does: the job's own explicit `model` or `model@profile` if it has one, otherwise the session's or agent's current selection, then the normal fallback chain. Remove the run-time refusal "Automation has no recorded inference account", and don't change any automation that runs today.

### Problem to solve

Since 2026.10.10 (#172590), a scheduled agent-turn run with no recorded account (`inferenceBinding`) is refused whenever it would use a stored account:

> Automation has no recorded inference account. Runtime openclaw would run anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 with stored account anthropic:manual. Record the account with openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model ...

#172590 set out to stop jobs from silently changing account or billing route when defaults or account order changed. Its PR describes that as something that *could* happen, with no user report. The refusal it added has drawn about 20 user reports in five weeks, and every one is a job that stopped running.

Observed on 2026-11-20 on a maintainer Gateway: a session-targeted babysitter job (`sessionTarget: "session:<key>"`, no `payload.model`) was created while the session ran on a configured key, so it recorded no account. The owner then explicitly switched that session to `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` on `anthropic:manual`. Every scheduled run after that was refused until the job was hand-edited to `…@anthropic:manual`. An interactive turn in the same session worked.

Where the refusal comes from:

- `createUnrecordedScheduledAccountRefusal` (`src/agents/scheduled-unrecorded-account.ts`), thrown from the embedded auth plan, the CLI runner, the cron CLI candidate and the session-event CLI candidate.
- Creation refuses routes whose credential is neither a stored account nor a configured key (`captureCronInferenceBinding`).
- Startup warnings and Doctor (`core/doctor/cron-inference-accounts`, `doctor --fix` adoption) exist only to work around the refusal.

### User evidence, grouped by complaint

About 20 user reports and 15 follow-up PRs in the five weeks since 2026.10.10.

**1. Changing the model, on purpose, breaks automations**
- #188761 (open): the default model changed; nine inherited-model automations failed the next day. The reporter asks for a preflight warning, explicitly *without* silently moving the account.
- #198486 (closed): jobs created without `payload.model` got no binding when `subagents.model` differs from the primary.
- #192555 (closed): session-targeted jobs were accepted at creation but could never run on a CLI-login runtime.
- #193855 (open): asks for jobs to follow their agent's account instead of a per-job binding. 21 enabled jobs in one install had no binding.
- 2026-11-20 maintainer report above: the owner's explicit session switch was refused.

**2. Upgrades left existing jobs unbound, and every run failed**
- #192195, #193418, #195887, #189908 (closed). #200600 (closed): jobs created on 2026.11.4 were refused after updating to main.

**3. The suggested fix (Doctor or `--model …@profile`) didn't work**
- #193345, #193517, #200775 (closed). #201550 (merged) now explains why Doctor can't restore an account.

**4. Some credential types can't be recorded at all**
- Plugin-created jobs: #192327 (open), PR #192376 (open), PR #193201 (closed).
- Bedrock `auth: "aws-sdk"`: #192524 (open), PR #192576 (open).
- `claude-cli` login: #191818, #200775 (closed), PRs #172735 (closed), #172794 and #180492 (merged), #190902 (closed).
- `main` and `systemEvent` turns: #199290 (open).
- `/hooks/agent` ephemeral jobs: #174167 (closed).
- Access-only OAuth: #180757 (closed). Grant regeneration or a secrets migration retires the authorization: #193345, #196381 (open).

**5. Fallback broke**
- #192463, #196928 (cross-provider), #196514 (same-provider, multi-account), #192009 (asks for explicitly authorized fallback accounts). All closed; #196539 (merged) lets other-provider fallbacks run live.

**6. The failure is hard to see and fix**
- #191936 (open): the Automations model picker shows no account.
- PR #195890 (open): catch a missing account at save. PR #195879 (open): the refusal hides its cause and retries ten times. PR #193643 (open): warn only for jobs that can run. PR #188850 (open): preview automation impact before a default-model change.
- Merged: #195901 (keep failure causes), #176911 (explain route mismatches). Closed: #189939 (stop suggesting `doctor --fix` for jobs Doctor skips), #195502 (Doctor copies the agent database per automation).

**Origin and design history:** #172590, #172792, #173509, #173411, #185070, #185341, #196539 (merged). #178811 and #178812 (closed tracking issues for parent-linked runs and the per-occurrence execution context).

### Proposed solution

**Rule:** a scheduled run selects its model, account and runtime the same way an interactive turn on that agent or session does. An explicit job `model` or `model@profile` overrides that selection, and the job's fallback chain applies as it does interactively.

- **`session:<key>` jobs** follow that session's current model and account selection, including an owner's explicit switch. (Decided: they follow the session, not the agent's primary.)
- **`current` jobs** keep the creation-time behavior from #185341.
- **Isolated jobs** use the agent's primary model and normal account order.
- **Explicit `model@profile`** keeps its recorded account strictly, as today.

#### Hard constraint: no existing automation may break

Phase 1 changes only outcomes that are refusals today. Any run that succeeds today takes exactly the same path afterward:

- Jobs that already record an account (explicit or automatically captured) keep using it on its provider, unchanged.
- Unbound jobs that run on a configured key or a CLI's native login keep that route, including native-login-only environment handling for CLI runs.
- Only runs that today end in "no recorded inference account" change: they now run on the account an interactive turn would use. That is the account the error message names. For a CLI runtime whose own selection forwards no stored account, the run uses the CLI's native login, as interactive turns do.
- Creating a job on a route whose credential is neither a stored account nor a configured key (for example AWS SDK chains) no longer fails at save. The job runs on live selection.

#### What goes away

- The run-time refusal and its four throw sites, plus `scheduledLiveProviderAuth` (it only exempted bound jobs' other-provider candidates from that refusal).
- The startup warning "automation has no recorded inference account; run openclaw doctor --fix …" and the CLI "never borrow a stored account" warning.
- Doctor's `cron-inference-accounts` lint check and `doctor --fix` adoption. Adoption would now turn a working live job into one pinned to a single account, which only adds ways for it to fail. Bindings Doctor already recorded stay and keep working.

### Non-goals (phase 1)

- Removing or migrating existing bindings. They stay authoritative for their provider.
- Making automatically captured bindings soft, so that a replaced or removed account falls back to live selection instead of refusing (#200600, #193345, #196381). That's phase 2: it changes a currently strict path and needs its own proof.
- Stopping automatic capture for new jobs (phase 2, together with the above).
- Automations picker account display (#191936).

### Phased plan

1. **Phase 1:** remove the unrecorded-account refusal, the creation refusal, the startup warning and Doctor adoption; update docs. Prove that previously working automations are unchanged and previously refused ones now run, on a real Gateway.
2. **Phase 2:** automatically captured bindings become a preference: use the recorded account while it's available, otherwise select live. Explicit `model@profile` stays strict. Stop capturing automatically for new jobs.
3. **Phase 3:** show the account a job will use in the Automations picker (#191936) and in run history.

**Open PRs this supersedes:** #195890 (save-time missing-account check), #195879 (missing-account refusal visibility and retries), #193643 (missing-account startup warnings), #192376 (plugin jobs record no account), #192576 (Bedrock `aws-sdk` account). With no refusal they have nothing to fix. #188850 (default-model preview) still has a model-policy half; its account half goes away. Issues expected to be resolved: #188761 (account part), #192327, #192524, #199290, #193855.

### Security and billing

On a Gateway, users share the owner's inference, so the run uses the same account an interactive turn would. Personal model accounts still need their owner's live authority, exactly as in chat. An explicit `model@profile` remains the way to pin billing identity for a job. The run history should show which account a run used (phase 3).

### Alternatives considered

- **Owner-authorized account sets** (this issue's first draft): record who made each session model choice and refuse runs on accounts the owner didn't authorize. Rejected as too complex for the actual risk; multiplayer Gateways share the owner's inference.
- **Keep one binding and improve errors** (#195890, #195879): still refuses working setups.

### Impact

Affected: scheduled agent-turn automations on stored or OAuth accounts, CLI logins, plugin-created jobs, Bedrock SDK routes and `systemEvent` turns. Severity: blocks workflow; every run fails until hand-edited.

### Evidence/examples

The 2026-11-20 maintainer Gateway (refusals at 11:24 and 11:34, recovered after a manual `@anthropic:manual` edit), plus the linked reports.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes. A phase-1 PR will link here.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)
