issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash).

### Beta release blocker

No.

### Summary

A targetless `message.send` progress reply from Control UI/WebChat in a Telegram-origin DM-topic session is reclassified as Telegram, inherits a composite session discriminator as `threadId`, and fails with `ToolInputError: threadId must be a positive integer.`

### Reporter clarification: zero deliveries, not an objection to Telegram mirroring

The important failure is **neither destination received the progress messages**: not the active WebChat conversation and not its corresponding bound Telegram DM topic. The inferred composite `threadId` is invalid for the Telegram transport, so selecting the external path did not result in a Telegram delivery either.

The reporter normally uses this conversation from Telegram and says that native Telegram-origin sends work in that workflow. This is a reporter-provided comparison, not a newly executed native-Telegram control test. The failing cases here were initiated from WebChat.

The reporter would explicitly welcome progress messages appearing **both in WebChat and in the correctly associated Telegram conversation/topic**. Thus this report is not asking maintainers to prohibit authorized cross-surface mirroring. Fixing the zero-delivery failure is the immediate issue; optional dual delivery is an acceptable product direction, not existing behavior proved by this report. The permitted external destination is the corresponding verified binding, not an arbitrary Telegram chat.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed workflow on the installed build:

1. Have an existing Telegram DM-topic session whose key has the shape `agent:main:telegram:direct:1000000001:thread:1000000001:42` (identifiers here are synthetic).
2. Open that same conversation in Control UI and submit a prompt **from WebChat**, not Telegram.
3. During the active run, issue an ordinary current-source progress reply, omitting **all routing arguments**:
   ```json
   {"action":"send","message":"Progress update","final":false}
   ```
4. Observe the tool fail with the error below instead of showing an ordinary progress message.

Two failures were captured in the attached user screenshots; one further controlled targetless call during diagnosis returned the same error. The screenshot text is original; the example message and all routing identifiers in this report are sanitized. A clean-stock end-to-end reproduction has **not** been run.

### Expected behavior

Current-source progress should remain visible in the initiating WebChat conversation. Authorized mirroring to its correctly bound Telegram topic would also be welcome; accidental route substitution that produces no delivery in either surface is the failure. The [documented WebChat contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073/docs/web/webchat.md#L93-L103) says targetless `message.send` from an active WebChat run is projected to that chat and mirrored to its transcript, and must not inherit `lastChannel`.

### Actual behavior

```text
ToolInputError: threadId must be a positive integer.
```

The tool cards show failed sends; the two progress messages were not displayed as ordinary messages in either WebChat or Telegram (user observation). The later automatic final answer did appear. The error concerns an inherited field: the agent supplied neither `threadId` nor `replyTo`, `channel`, `target`, or `accountId`.

The diagnostic `session_status` route had this shape (synthetic identifiers):

```json
{
  "origin": {"provider":"telegram","accountId":"default","threadId":42},
  "active": {
    "channel":"webchat",
    "to":"agent:main:telegram:direct:1000000001:thread:1000000001:42",
    "threadId":"1000000001:42"
  },
  "deliveryContext": {
    "channel":"telegram",
    "to":"telegram:1000000001:topic:42",
    "accountId":"default",
    "threadId":42
  }
}
```

### OpenClaw version

`2026.11.3`, reported build `d1da3d5`; managed local main-derived artifact, not a clean stock checkout. The short build SHA did not resolve through `repos/openclaw/openclaw/commits/d1da3d5` (HTTP 422). Upstream source references below are pinned separately to `3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073`; source equivalence does not establish an upstream end-to-end reproduction or a first bad release.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux x64; Node.js `24.22.1`.

### Install method

Managed local source-derived build, user-systemd Gateway service. Gateway remained running.

### Model

`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, OpenAI Codex runtime.

### Provider / routing chain

Control UI/WebChat input → existing Telegram-origin session → Codex `message` tool → session-derived current-channel projection → outbound threading → Telegram positive-integer parameter validation.

### Additional provider/model setup details

The failed calls carry a text message and `final:false` only. No invalid explicit routing argument, API credentials, actual user/session IDs, or private endpoint addresses are included in this report.

### Logs

```text
Observed targetless message.send result, repeated during diagnosis:
ToolInputError: threadId must be a positive integer.

session_status active.channel: webchat
session_status active.threadId shape: <chat-id>:<dm-topic-id>
```

No matching exact error signature was found in the bounded recent Gateway journal/current-day file-log inspection. The screenshots and live tool return, not an invented server stack trace, are the primary failure evidence.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

![Two targetless progress calls fail before an ordinary message is displayed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/4fbc5f14744a280458c339b4521e41cb44e227f1/2026-11-13/webchat-message-threadid/failure-collage.png)

The collage combines the two supplied failure screenshots with crop/labels only. No after/fixed proof exists: no fix was attempted. The image URL was verified as HTTP 200 and `image/png`.

### Impact and severity

Affected observation: WebChat progress replies in this Telegram-origin DM-topic conversation. Three targetless progress attempts failed (two original captures and one diagnostic repeat). The user reports recurrence in normal use, but deployment-wide frequency is unknown. Progress text is lost from ordinary chat display while tool-error cards remain; the final automatic answer still arrives. This report does not claim that every WebChat session or ordinary native Telegram send is broken.

### Additional information

#### Source-level trace (read-only inspection)

1. WebChat ingress is preserved and external delivery inheritance is intentionally excluded in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-origin-routing.ts`.
2. [`projectCurrentChannelContext()`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073/src/agents/tools/message-tool-discovery.ts#L334-L358) nevertheless substitutes the external provider/destination/thread inferred from the session key when `currentChannelProvider === "webchat"`.
3. The composite suffix is legitimate **session identity**: Telegram creates DM-topic suffixes as `${chatId}:${dmThreadId}` in [`conversation-route.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073/extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route.ts#L248-L271). The generic [`session-key-utils.ts` parser](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073/src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts#L140-L206) preserves it as a string.
4. [`message-tool-execution.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073/src/agents/tools/message-tool-execution.ts#L125-L141) initializes execution using the projected provider and inferred thread. Correct structured delivery metadata is not the same thing as this session discriminator.
5. The WebChat internal-source sink is therefore not selected; this is **not** a failed WebChat network send followed by an ordinary Telegram fallback. See the [internal-source predicate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073/src/infra/outbound/internal-source-reply.ts#L31-L85).
6. Telegram's [`readTelegramThreadId()`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073/extensions/telegram/src/action-params.ts#L20-L50) correctly rejects the composite value as a numeric transport topic ID. The repair should be at the route/identity boundary, **not** weakening numeric validation.

#### Upstream comparison and failure boundary

Read-only comparison against the pinned public commit above covered 24 source/documentation/test files: 23 were byte-identical to the installed source, including the defect-chain modules. The remaining assembly-file difference concerns inherited tool-denylist construction, not the relevant route mapping. The packaged distribution independently contains the same provider substitution and Telegram validation logic. This establishes matching source logic, **not a clean-stock runtime reproduction**.

The composite value is injected into copied action parameters by [shared outbound threading](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073/src/infra/outbound/message-action-threading.ts#L30-L52), using [Telegram thread inheritance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073/extensions/telegram/src/action-threading.ts#L4-L20). The exception occurs before the Telegram Bot API send and before `sendDurableMessageBatch()` ([ordering](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3bf446ef447518f801828118620c891e7e199073/extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.ts#L416-L465)); it is not necessarily before all network activity, since the Gateway RPC may already have occurred.

The internal WebChat persistence branch is bypassed, and external route persistence is success-only. Failed sends therefore do not produce a successfully persisted progress mirror or a delivered-answer completion fact; tool errors and ordinary run history can still be recorded. The `final` flag is consumed separately from route selection; source inspection indicates both flag values take this route, but only `final:false` has live failure evidence. No evidence identifies Codex as the component generating the invalid thread ID.

Existing coverage tests WebChat with a WebChat-shaped session key, native Telegram ingress, or WebChat-to-external inference without the composite Telegram DM-topic case. The missing regression is an **admitted WebChat turn inside a Telegram DM-topic session**, not merely ambient/stale channel context. Include dry-run, replay, failure, and local exactly-once persistence assertions as well as the routing matrix below.

#### Proposed direction — not implemented

- Preserve authenticated active ingress as the authority for current-source sends; a Telegram-shaped session key is history/identity, not permission to replace an active WebChat source.
- Keep internal WebChat conversation identity distinct from external provider transport IDs; for actual Telegram sends use validated structured transport metadata.
- Regression coverage should include WebChat into Telegram DM-topic and forum-topic sessions, plain WebChat, native Telegram DM-topic sends, explicit authorized external sends, and `final:false` versus `final:true` persistence/duplication behavior.
- Do not silently split arbitrary colon-delimited strings or relax Telegram validation. If authorized dual delivery is implemented, use the verified Telegram binding and its numeric transport topic ID, keep WebChat delivery independent of Telegram validation/send failures, and record per-destination success/failure without falsely claiming either was delivered.

Only `final:false` was exercised live; final=true and a clean-stock cross-channel matrix remain untested. No code/configuration edits, patch, tests/builds, installation or restart was performed.

Related but distinct: #100269 concerns explicitly supplied empty optional routing fields. Here the fields are omitted and the invalid value is inherited from session identity.

issues.title: [Bug]: Empty-response retry exhaustion (synthetic_no_response) mislabeled as reason="format", incorrectly skips fallback
issues.body:
**Version:** openclaw 2026.10.5 — confirmed on two independent hosts via direct source read (not log inference): Forge (`forges-mac-studio`, this report) and a second fleet host (Lumen), identical logic at matching line offsets in different hashed bundle filenames.

## Summary

When a model exhausts its empty-response retry budget, the resulting failure is mislabeled with the same `reason` tag used for genuinely malformed/unsupported requests (`"format"`). That tag is intentionally exempted from fallback at the retry-limit stage — correct for a real request-shape error, since switching models won't fix a bad schema. But "exhausted empty-response retries" is a completely different failure class that *should* be fallback-eligible (sibling failures like overloaded/unknown/server_error on the same host correctly fall through to the configured fallback chain). The shared label means a transient empty-response failure gets no fallback at all, even when `fallbackConfigured` is true.

## Where (two hosts, same logic)

1. `execute.runtime-*.mjs` (e.g. `execute.runtime-C7EfHxZr.mjs:1775`):
   ```js
   const reason = terminalFailure
     ? terminalFailure === "synthetic_no_response" ? "format" : "unknown"
     : classifyFailoverReason(message, { provider: params.provider }) ?? "unknown";
   ```
   `synthetic_no_response` (empty-response exhaustion) is hard-mapped to `"format"`.

2. `embedded-agent-*.mjs` (e.g. `embedded-agent-w-EKmRVf.mjs:1764`):
   ```js
   if (params.fallbackConfigured && reason && reason !== "timeout" && reason !== "format" && reason !== "session_expired")
     return { ...fallback... };
   // else: return_error_payload — no fallback attempted
   ```
   `"format"` is in the non-fallback-eligible set — correct for real malformed-request errors, wrong for relabeled empty-response exhaustion.

3. Related, lower severity: `embedded-agent-*.mjs:7071` hardcodes the empty-response retry budget:
   ```js
   if (!nextReasoningOnlyRetryInstruction && nextEmptyResponseRetryInstruction && retryState.emptyResponseAttempts < 1) { ... }
   ```
   literal `1`, no config key (checked `agents.defaults.emptyRetries` / `empty_retries` — neither exists in schema). Not the core bug here, and overlaps with already-closed #134918's suggestion 2 ("make the empty-response retry cap configurable") — flagging for context only, not asking to reopen that issue.

## Observed impact

On one fleet host: 1 of 77 relevant turns hit this exact path (empty-response exhaustion -> reason="format" -> fallback skipped -> error surfaced to caller) despite fallbackConfigured=true with a working fallback chain (fabric/balanced, ollama/qwen2.5:32b). The other 76 failures in the same window (overloaded/unknown/server_error) correctly fell through to fallback. Confirmed the same code shape exists on a second, independent host (this one) at matching logic/line offsets, same package version (2026.10.5).

## Suggested fix

Give `synthetic_no_response`-origin failures their own `reason` value (e.g. `"empty_response_exhausted"`) distinct from `"format"`, and treat that new tag as fallback-eligible in the retry-limit gate. Keep `"format"` reserved for genuine malformed-request/invalid-schema cases (400/422, `invalid_request` errorType) as it is today.

## Repro notes

This was found via direct source read on two hosts, not log inference — grep citations for both hosts available on request. Happy to share exact diffs/patch if useful.

issues.body:
### Summary

The multiplayer docs explain roles for people who sign in through Tailscale, an identity-aware proxy or OpenClaw ID, but nothing shows how to try roles locally before that infrastructure exists.

### Affected docs path(s) or URL(s)

docs/start/multiplayer.md (Step 5 "Bound what each person can do" and "Bootstrap administrators and assign roles"), docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md

### Steps to reproduce / verify

1. Read docs/start/multiplayer.md, "Step 5: Bound what each person can do". Roles apply to profile-based connections and are assigned with `users.setRole`.
2. Read docs/concepts/user-model.md: the shared owner profile used by token and password auth "cannot be merged with a personal profile or assigned an operator role".
3. Look for a local or test setup that gives two or more people their own sign-in on one machine. The only route is trusted-proxy auth with a same-host proxy (`allowLoopback`), and no page shows it end to end.

### Expected docs behavior/content

A short recipe for testing roles locally: a same-host proxy that signs test accounts in, the trusted-proxy settings it needs (`allowLoopback`, `allowUsers`, `identityScopes`), assigning roles with `users.setRole` after each first sign-in, and a clear warning that `allowLoopback` lets any local process impersonate any allowed account.

### Actual docs behavior/content

The pieces are spread across pages, and two required details are not stated for this case:

- The Gateway rejects proxied requests whose client address is loopback, so a same-host proxy in front of a same-host browser must send a non-loopback client address.
- A role only caps scopes. Each test account also needs an `identityScopes` grant (or a device grant), or it connects with no scopes.

### Impact

People evaluating multiplayer roles before choosing an identity provider have to build a proxy setup by trial and error, and can end up with a loopback setup that any local program can impersonate without knowing it.

### Evidence

Built and checked on OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (d119c6b), macOS, with Caddy 2.11.9 as a same-host basic-auth proxy:

```text
[alice] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.admin"]
[bob] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.read","operator.write"]
[bob] exec.approvals.get -> DENIED {"code":"FORBIDDEN","message":"missing scope: operator.admin",...}
[anon] HTTP 401
[direct-forged] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.admin"]
```

The last line is a local client that skipped the proxy and sent forged identity headers straight to the Gateway port. This matches the existing warning in docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md about `allowLoopback`.

### Additional information

Related: #200361 (trusted-proxy identity headers are trusted without verifying a signed proxy assertion). A draft recipe is ready as a PR against docs/start/multiplayer.md.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a Control UI connect without a device identity fails trusted-proxy auth, the Gateway answers "web app requires device identity (use HTTPS or localhost secure context)" and neither the response nor the Gateway log contains the `trusted_proxy_*` reason.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Gateway with `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"`, `trustedProxies: ["127.0.0.1"]`, `trustedProxy.allowLoopback: true`, `trustedProxy.userHeader: "x-eval-user"`, `trustedProxy.requiredHeaders: ["x-eval-proxy"]`, and an `allowUsers` list.
2. From the same host, open a WebSocket to the Gateway with `Origin` set to an allowed Control UI origin, `x-eval-user` set to an allowed user, `X-Forwarded-For: 10.99.0.50`, and no `x-eval-proxy` header.
3. Send `connect` as client `openclaw-control-ui` (mode `webchat`) with no `device` field.
4. Repeat with `x-eval-proxy: 1` and a `x-eval-user` value that is not in `allowUsers`.

### Expected behavior

The rejection names the trusted-proxy check that failed. `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` ("Troubleshooting") tells operators to look for reasons such as `trusted_proxy_missing_header_*`, `trusted_proxy_user_not_allowed` and `trusted_proxy_loopback_source`. Rejections that go through the Gateway's general unauthorized path already return `details.authReason` and log `reason=`.

### Actual behavior

Both attempts return the same error with no auth reason, and the Gateway log has only `failureCause=control-ui-insecure-auth`:

```text
CONNECT FAILED {"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"web app requires device identity (use HTTPS or localhost secure context)","details":{"code":"CONTROL_UI_DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED"}}
```

The message also points at HTTPS or a secure context, which was not the cause: the connection was on loopback and failed a proxy header check.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (d119c6b). Source path unchanged on main at b8b173b6697.

### Operating system

macOS 27.2

### Install method

npm global

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not model related; no agent turn involved)

### Provider / routing chain

client -> same-host reverse proxy (loopback) -> openclaw gateway (trusted-proxy auth)

### Logs

```shell
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ connect 0ms bytes=246 failurePhase=auth failureCause=control-ui-insecure-auth conn=4aa8fb7e…c50a
[ws] closed before connect conn=4aa8fb7e-... remote=127.0.0.1 fwd=10.99.0.50 code=1006 reason=n/a cause=control-ui-insecure-auth handshake=failed ... insecureAuthConfigured=false client=openclaw-control-ui mode=webchat
```

No `trusted_proxy_` string appears in the log lines written during the two attempts.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

In `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-auth.ts`, `evaluateMissingDeviceIdentity` returns `reject-control-ui-insecure-auth` for any device-less Control UI client whose trusted-proxy auth did not succeed. That branch sends `CONTROL_UI_DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED` and records the close cause without reading `authResult.reason`. The `reject-unauthorized` path in the same function returns `details.authReason` and logs `reason=`.

### Impact and severity

Affected: operators setting up trusted-proxy auth whose test or scripted clients connect as the Control UI without a device identity.
Severity: annoying; the connection is still rejected, so this is a diagnosis problem, not an access problem.
Frequency: always, for this client shape.
Consequence: the operator cannot see which trusted-proxy check failed, and the message suggests an HTTPS problem instead.

### Additional information

Not checked: what a real browser shows. A browser on localhost or HTTPS sends a device identity and takes a different code path.

### Summary

In the multiplayer quick setup, the "Shared secret" access option links to the model provider Authentication page instead of the Gateway token and password settings.

### Affected docs path(s) or URL(s)

docs/start/multiplayer.md (https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/multiplayer#step-1-give-the-team-access-to-the-gateway)

### Steps to reproduce / verify

1. Open docs/start/multiplayer.md, "Step 1: Give the team access to the Gateway".
2. Follow the "Authentication" link in the "Shared secret" bullet (line 80, `/gateway/authentication`).
3. The page that opens is titled Authentication, with the summary "Model authentication: OAuth, API keys, Claude CLI reuse, and Anthropic setup-token". Its first note says gateway connection auth is documented elsewhere.

### Expected docs behavior/content

The link opens the Gateway auth settings: `gateway.auth.mode` (`token` or `password`), `gateway.auth.token` and `gateway.auth.password`, documented in the Gateway section of /gateway/config-gateway.

### Actual docs behavior/content

The link opens the model provider auth page, which does not cover Gateway token or password auth.

### Impact

People setting up shared-secret team access follow the link and land on model API key and OAuth setup instead of the Gateway auth settings they need.

prs.title: fix: explicitly restore removed conversation workspaces
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A conversation whose managed workspace was removed needs an explicit recovery action before another turn can start. This reworks this PR's earlier automatic restoration design.

Product decision from Peter:

> "if there's an old convo and worktree is removed, we should show that in the UI as a warning above the picker; possibly with a button to restore fresh checkout and until that's done don't allow sending a prompt to the agent"

The composer shows the removal warning above its pickers and disables Send. Restore uses the existing worktree lifecycle: saved snapshots recover uncommitted work; records without a snapshot offer **Restore fresh checkout**, using the recorded branch/base. Progress and typed, actionable failures stay visible. Channels and API callers receive the existing Restore guidance without starting the agent. Session projection and its existing publication stream carry availability; no new polling, configuration, cache, or database schema is introduced. Restore retains its existing admin authority.

## Evidence

Native UI E2E passes all three snapshot, fresh-checkout, and archived-conversation cases through the native runner, including disabled Send, progress, typed failure/retry, preserved draft, and re-enabled Send. Real Gateway tests prove zero provider calls while removed, both explicit restore modes, saved bytes and Review, and concurrent Restore requests performing one checkout. Server and UI regressions fail on the preceding automatic design; a separate regression caught compact sidebar rows dropping availability. Existing early-inference preparation remains intact.

Published `openclaw@2026.11.6` upgrade proof creates and runs a synthetic session, removes its checkout with saved work, upgrades, then explicitly restores. Saved bytes, chat, direct agent execution, and Review all pass. The refreshed owner/admission/projection suite passes 40 cases; UI composer tests pass (81), plus Chromium keyboard tests (2). CLI GC preservation cases pass, including refusal to overwrite a damaged orphan checkout. Codex review of the full staged candidate is clean through P2.

`pnpm check:changed` completed on the final lifecycle candidate. Types, schema/storage/UI guards, formatting, scripts lint and import-cycle checks pass. Two lint findings in the new regression were repaired and the affected test lint passes. The remaining Knip export `LEAN_PROFILE_MEMORY_THRESHOLD_BYTES` reproduces on the exact original parent and was introduced by #202422 / `28aa5c88fd45a5ea39f2fb4d3322e759118aa667`; this is a main regression, subsequently fixed by #202785. Exact-head CI and the requested final-head ClawSweeper zero-item gate remain required.

An earlier unchanged local Review polling test returned an unfinished response after its fixed wait. It passed on the exact parent and candidate; the cause is unproven. This investigated local failure is retained, and passing replay is not an inherited-CI waiver.

Explicit-restore measurement on `3e9629d7` uses only synthetic data; subsequent repairs leave the explicit checkout owner unchanged: 62,000 files / 1.14 GB checkout, 10,000 sessions and a ~35 GiB agent database on APFS. Two A/A controls and five interleaved parent/candidate pairs give median restore wall time 8,919.79 → 7,441.92 ms, process CPU 4,880.90 → 4,938.47 ms, and main-isolate allocation 201,979,416 → 202,379,912 bytes. A/A wall varied 14,639.96 / 8,944.74 ms, so this is **not a speedup claim**. CPU excludes Git/state-broker child processes; APFS and compressible fixtures do not model btrfs/content entropy. All direct-restore samples and controls are retained in the task report.

Net production growth is 525 lines (generated validators and tooling reported separately): explicit composer action/progress/errors, existing session projection/publication wiring, and snapshot/fresh restoration handling. Automatic restoration and duplicated refusal guards are removed. Model/Incognito helpers moved into existing owners to meet file caps; no new cache or schema.

The first exact-head CI exposed a stale generated UI validator, per-file identity/test-size ratchet violations, an obsolete inbound auto-restore test, and chat boot byte growth. Repairs regenerate the validator, keep the fallback comparison at its original owner, consolidate fixtures, update inbound refusal proof, and defer restore-only copy. ClawSweeper also found an idle-command regression: activity refresh invalidated the record immediately before lease admission. A red/green regression now ages the restored checkout, and the existing run-lease owner alone refreshes command activity. The follow-up review resolved those three items and retained the chat-boot byte gate. The existing disabled-banner renderer now loads only when its state is present; focus, action, Stop and progress behavior remain tested. The paired local bundle comparison passes at 1,333,646 B versus 1,333,666 B on the selected main baseline (same 21 requests); the subsequent exact-head combined CI build also passes at 1,333,686 B against the 1,333,899 B ceiling (+20 B versus its base, same request count). Broader unit CI exposed old synchronous banner assertions; the test-only correction awaits visible content and passes all 202 cases across five consumers. The later lifecycle repair does not change UI bundle inputs.

The preceding CI also failed Android dependency resolution for two JUnit 1.13.3 artifacts; both Maven Central POM URLs returned HTTP 200 on targeted follow-up. No Android source or pins changed, and this fetch failure is not being claimed as an inherited regression or waived. Final-head CI and zero open ClawSweeper items are still required before merging.

An earlier ClawSweeper finding exposed manually deleted checkouts whose live registry rows are retained to protect local projection files. The lifecycle owner now preserves the observed missing checkout independently of registry retirement, and refreshes the existing session projection. The real Gateway regression fails on the prior head because inference runs; after the repair it refuses without inference, projects the removal state, and retains the unique files when Restore reports a conflict. Four Gateway cases and 42 focused owner/consumer/GC cases pass; the final sandbox replay also passes. Test growth remains within the existing allowance (395/400 lines). Production growth is +525 lines, needed for the explicit composer recovery flow, shared availability projection, and safe snapshot/fresh restoration; existing guards and duplicate recovery policy are removed. No schema, polling, configuration, or cache was added.

The final sibling-path correction preserves #200918 / `1619ecb28838309a2bf8691d98deb6145bddcc7e`: a removed requester workspace permanently refuses child completion delivery, while removal still in progress remains retryable. The existing classifier now recognizes the shared lifecycle error's clear wording. Its requester-settlement regression is red before this one-line repair; all 42 focused delivery/settlement tests pass afterward, including both permanent message forms and the transient-removal control. No retry scheduler or completion retention behavior changes.

The screenshots use the real bundled UI with synthetic garden conversation data, at 1280×900. Before is this PR's preceding revision `deb064d2`; after is the explicit-restore candidate. Browser fixtures drive the UI; separate real Gateway tests prove the backend restore effects.

![Before: removed workspace has no warning and Send is enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e535bd2-56b6-4dea-97f4-90b8d1d79912)

![After: workspace removal warning, explicit Restore, and disabled Send](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17286f60-d272-4f3a-a574-e6017be7e85e)

![Before annotated: Send remains enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97f0cd3f-31fc-4f8c-8f27-9b3d6d4ae3a1)

![After annotated: explicit workspace recovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d458e55b-b0fa-411a-9595-cefdc4ec126e)

![No snapshot: Restore fresh checkout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/183c3ca6-527e-460a-b158-f67bbff31d45)

![After restore: warning cleared and Send enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/faf42021-df4e-4695-b31a-215dcaa0ea60)

The preceding CI run also exposed a main regression from #202929 (`dc6e31a28597`): the aggregate-recovery fixture used .NET build paths that are now intentionally excluded. The same failure reproduces on the exact CI main parent `e309df612ed3986a3eb2aa139ddfb35b31a16143`. This PR moves only the synthetic payload to retained artifact paths; the actual 768 MiB limit and byte-preservation assertions remain. The repaired case passes on that parent and this candidate. No CI exception is requested for it.

prs.title: feat: run lean core workers in one shared host to cut small-machine memory
prs.body:
Fixes #202377
Related: #202373
Builds on #202422 (merged as 28aa5c88fd45)

## What Problem This Solves

On small machines the Gateway runs many background workers. Each worker loads its own copy of largely the same code, so worker memory grows past what a 1–2 GiB host can hold. The core SQLite, transcript, state-read and catalog workers are the biggest duplicates.

## User Impact

User impact: with the `lean` resource profile (auto-selected below 8 GiB of effective memory, or set explicitly), these four core workers run as endpoints inside **one** shared host worker. They load their common code once, which uses less memory. `standard` keeps today's worker layout; every new path is unreachable there.

Lean accepts one new failure mode: if a hosted task fails, is cancelled or times out, the whole shared host is replaced. Every hosted endpoint's in-flight work then fails with an explicit `Shared worker host failed: …` error, and the next request starts a fresh host. Callers never hang.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prototype in #202373 showed the memory saving but broke several guarantees. This version keeps them:

- **Code is shared, state is not.** Each hosted module starts once per endpoint with its own port, admission relay and queue. The per-worker SQLite admission upstream is now scoped to the endpoint instead of being isolate-global. The host samples its own memory; endpoints never do.
- **One live endpoint per kind** (per carrier class for the SQLite store). Extra slots of a kind keep their own dedicated workers: the state-read settlement floor of 2, bursts and the second agent carrier. Pool caps, floors, catalog custody (#161740) and retirement timings are unchanged.
- **Single writer per database.** Broker actor routing is unchanged. A hosted SQLite carrier stops logically only after every actor's native close is proven; any other stop replaces the host.
- **Real termination boundaries.** An idle stop (idle timeout, rotation, close, shutdown) is a logical stop. The endpoint first releases what isolate exit would have released (state-read retained readers, transcript history databases), with a 10 s deadline. Cancellation, failure, self-retirement or an unknown reason terminates the host. CPU-heavy and synchronous kinds (prompt state, skills discovery) are not hosted and keep their own killable workers.
- **Host failure is explicit and recoverable.** The host is created through the existing native-worker supervisor, so synchronous callers see its exit through `service()`. Host death fails every endpoint (error, exit and `terminalFailure`). A replacement starts only after the old host has exited: one host isolate at a time. The last endpoint's retirement joins the physical host.
- **Not hosted:** Knowledge (#202378), external databases, Postgres-engine installs, native-resource owners, non-canonical (update-generation or sealed) worker URLs, and runtimes whose explicit SQLite close is not qualified to release native resources (such as Bun on Windows), whose cleanup depends on worker exit.

The census reports the host as one worker. Its row adds `hosts N endpoints`, so budget admission (#202376) can charge one isolate. #202376 exports `registerHostedSlotPredicate(url, key?)`. Whichever of the two PRs merges second adds and registers a stateless predicate: lean, a canonical hosted entrypoint, not Postgres, and an `agent` or `shared-state` SQLite key. It is not the live `claimsSharedHostSlot` check, so a running hosted floor slot is still not charged as an isolate.

Accepted edge case: some agent-database reader caches are shared across the whole isolate. They are released by explicit close requests or when the host exits, not when a single endpoint stops.

## Review Repair (ClawSweeper 2/6 on `4795dee4`)

- **[P1] Unqualified native close keeps dedicated workers.** Confirmed in source: when `explicitSqliteCloseReleasesNativeResources` is false, `closeReadResources` and transcript discovery call `pool.rotate()` so worker exit releases native handles, sidecar locks and cleanup custody. A hosted endpoint treated `rotation` as a logical stop while a sibling kept the isolate alive. Of the two suggested fixes, I chose the smaller and safer one: `claimsSharedHostSlot` reuses the existing capability owner (`getSqliteRuntimeCapabilities`) and refuses every hosted kind when close is unqualified. The SQLite broker also requires its own captured close policy, so an early conservative broker never hosts a carrier. Forcing physical host termination would instead fail every sibling on each routine rotation. The capability is decided once and only moves from pending (false) to decided, so a slot hosted under qualified close is never retired under an unqualified policy.
- **[P2] Export guard.** `startHostedWorker` is registered in `workerProtocolModules` for exactly the four hosted modules, using the guard's existing subset check. Collision checking is otherwise unchanged.
- **Benchmark applicability.** On Node, `bun-sqlite-library.ts` decides `explicitSqliteCloseReleasesNativeResources: true` ("Node runtime") before any other branch, including early broker captures. The measured Linux Node v26.12.1 campaign path hosts the same endpoints as before, so the evidence below still applies. Only Bun runtimes with unqualified close (for example Bun Windows) change; they now use the standard dedicated layout.
- **Rebase.** Rebased once onto `main` `5a4f6a82681f` because `src/infra/worker-task-host.ts` conflicted with main commit `8bbb3539` ("keep Code Mode usable after read-only workers retire"). Resolution: hosted endpoints still return early, because the physical host registers its one thread for admission. Dedicated workers, including read-only ones, now track admission unconditionally, as on main. A hosted endpoint's logical stop closes its retained connections, which decrements their admission references. Range-diff: only that hunk differs. The three earlier fix commits are identical.

New tests (`src/infra/shared-worker-host.unqualified-close.test.ts`; both fail on `4795dee4` and pass after the fix):
- `never hosts a core worker when native SQLite close is unqualified`: all four kinds; it failed with `expected true to be false`.
- `rotates an unqualified reader by physical worker exit while a shared host stays up`: a real state-read pool with a live hosted sibling. The reader is a dedicated worker (census `hostedEndpoints: 1`; it failed with 2), and `closeReadResources` rotation removes its physical worker while the sibling stays up.

CI attribution for `4795dee4` (run 44849044890):

| Check | Cause | Evidence | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| check-source-contracts | PR | `lint:tmp:export-name-collisions`: `startHostedWorker` repeated in 3 modules | Fixed (P2) |
| checks-fast-baseline-ratchets | PR | `assertion-safety`: `src/infra/shared-worker-host.worker.ts: 1 > 0` (SAFETY comment not adjacent to the cast) | Fixed; ratchet OK locally |
| checks-node-changed-compact-large-8 | PR | Bun `session-history-read.imports.test.ts`: mock lacks `closeHistoryDatabaseScopes` | Mock completed; passes on Bun |
| checks-node-changed-compact-large-9 | Inherited | Bun `mcp-config-mutation.test.ts` keep/replace custody: `identity` 8/4, expected 0 | Same file fails identically under `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` at exact base `28aa5c88` (identity 8 and 4); the PR does not touch it |
| checks-ui-e2e (2/5) | Inherited | `route-asset-requests` plugins: `expected 57 to be less than or equal to 56` | Reproduced on main `2d13f968` (57>56); the PR touches no `ui/`. #202795 on the new base restores this budget |
| PostgreSQL conformance (pg16-smoke) | Not PR-caused (timing) | `server-database-engine-cron.postgres.test.ts` "drains accepted cron finalization…" timed out at 90 s | Local pg16 (same image) passed 4/4 on head and exact base; that test took 46.3 s and 45.4 s. Postgres installs never claim the shared host |

## Evidence

Current head: `40fc34f0df162c1d5bfdf0cb51b1bff7e46ac285`, rebased onto `main` `5a4f6a82681f`. The four feature commits match measured head `c58ffafd503d918fd1fc58f5ffade1cb9dc2b599` except for the `worker-task-host.ts` admission-tracking merge described above. Three review-repair commits follow. Fresh validation on this head: 42 focused files (shared-host, unqualified-close, worker-task host/pool/server, SQLite broker/relay, state-read, transcript worker/lanes/readers, catalog-read, history imports, resource-profile, status-resources, export guard), 476 tests in 6 Vitest shards; `pnpm tsgo:core`; type-aware oxlint and oxfmt on touched files; the export-collision guard; the assertion-safety ratchet; `pnpm config:docs:check`; and `git diff --check` all pass.

**Measured campaign (complete, on `c58ffafd503d`):** Crabbox Linux `local-container` leases on one Mac Studio, Node v26.12.1, 8-CPU quota, no swap, each arm pinning `gateway.resources.profile`, inspector detached. 24 matrix cases (single-bot and personal-assistant workloads × 1.5/3 GiB × lean/standard × 3 interleaved rounds), plus 3 qualifications and 4 fault cases. 29 of 31 exited 0. Every lease was stopped and every receipt matches its Crabbox terminal receipt. The measured commit is patch-equivalent to this head's four feature commits apart from the admission-tracking merge hunk; the review repair changes no hosting on Node (see above). The benchmark did not run on this head.

Completion:

| Workload | 1.5 GiB lean | 1.5 GiB standard | 3 GiB lean | 3 GiB standard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| single | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| personal | 3/3, no OOM | **1/3**: r1 and r2 `agent.wait timeout` with cgroup OOM kills (`oom_kill` 2 and 1); r3 completed | 3/3 | 3/3 |

At 1.5 GiB both arms reach the cgroup limit. Lean records reclaim pressure (`memory.events max` 5,082–22,740 on personal) but no OOM. The one completed standard personal-1.5 GiB round recorded 302,867 `max` events.

Gateway process RSS (excludes child processes; not heap), busy-phase median, median (range) across rounds, MiB:

| Workload | Memory | Lean | Standard | Paired lean − standard per round |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| single | 1.5 GiB | 1,124 (1,111–1,150) | 1,209 (1,207–1,212) | −88, −98, −57 |
| single | 3 GiB | 1,292 (1,250–1,313) | 1,337 (1,335–1,364) | −85, −71, −24 |
| personal | 1.5 GiB | 1,219 (1,197–1,241) | 1,244 (r3 only) | r3 only: −25 (busy peak +5) |
| personal | 3 GiB | 1,450 (1,448–1,493) | 1,578 (1,529–1,680) | −232, −85, −79 |

Lean busy-phase Gateway RSS is lower in all 10 paired rounds, busy peak in 9 of 10, and post-work median in all 10. Max registered physical workers is lower or equal in every pair (lean 18–26, standard 18–29), with 4–5 hosted endpoints on lean. Child-process RSS is reported separately and shows no consistent difference (−90 to +91 MiB). The informational event-loop stall p95 is comparable (lean 47–68 ms, standard 58–61 ms medians), except for the pressured standard personal-1.5 GiB round (210 ms p95, ~1 s worst). Full per-phase figures (fresh, busy, peak, post-work), cgroup, worker and stall data: `campaign-summary.md` / `.json` in the evidence bundle.

Shared-host fault (`f2-crash-3072-lean`): a fatal throw at a dispatched hosted request (`requestObserved=true`) produced explicit endpoint errors:

```
session-transcript         Shared worker host failed: Synthetic lean benchmark worker fault
sqlite-store:agent         Shared worker host failed: Synthetic lean benchmark worker fault
plugin-model-catalog-read  Shared worker host failed: Synthetic lean benchmark worker fault
```

Up to 4 endpoints were hosted during this case; errors were recorded for the 3 with in-flight or subsequent work, and the harness asserts that every recorded error carries this prefix, not that there is one error per endpoint. The Gateway survived and a replacement host started. The interrupted turn completed, the next turn was `ok`, history was preserved, 7/7 SQLite integrity checks passed and 33 turns were verified. The standard control (`f2-crash-3072-standard`, SQLite-store fault, no shared host) recorded no endpoint errors. Its interrupted turn failed (`'error' !== 'ok'`), and the Gateway survived and the next turn was `ok`.

Caveats: the built image carried three untracked legacy files that are not in the measured tree (`src/infra/lean-worker-host.ts`, `lean-worker-host.worker.ts`, `lean-worker-scope.ts`). They are not shown to have no runtime effect. Receipt manifest hashes are read at completion, so they do not identify the harness that ran. Per-result harness hashes are recorded: the matrix and f2 ran `version-bench` `c919a1e0`, and the qualifications and the earlier f-crash cases ran `eef0f878`. All results are process RSS and cgroup measurements on one host with n=3 per cell, so ranges are given and no significance is claimed.

Focused tests (all passing):
- `src/infra/shared-worker-host.test.ts` (7). The first two fail without the fix:
  - lean-only claims;
  - two endpoints share one physical host, and census reports `hostedEndpoints: 2`;
  - a cancelled endpoint replaces the host and its sibling fails explicitly; a replacement starts on a new thread;
  - idle stops detach logically, and the last one joins the host;
  - a synchronous caller observes physical termination;
  - a hosted state reader's file descriptor closes on rotation while a sibling keeps the host alive (Linux);
  - a refused host constructor fails its endpoints and frees the slot;
  - a stop retried after rejection settles once the host joins.
- Worker runtime, worker-task-pool, SQLite broker, state-read, catalog, transcript worker/lanes/readers, status/census and resource-profile suites pass. The PR-wrapper inventory closure passes.
- Core typecheck, targeted oxlint/oxfmt and docs formatting pass.
- `build:strict-smoke` on Linux emits `dist/infra/shared-worker-host.worker.js` (on the earlier head).
- `src/infra/shared-worker-host.unqualified-close.test.ts` (2), described above.

Independent Astra review ran four rounds. All verified findings are fixed, each with a regression test or a repro rerun:
- **Round 1:** a logical stop left reader handles open; synchronous callers could not see host exit.
- **Round 2:** the final retirement did not join the host; a refused constructor stranded endpoints; supervisor loss hung synchronous stops; a logical stop did not keep the process alive.
- **Round 3:** a stop retried after the host joined could hang.

- In the measured image itself (`dist/index.js` and `shared-worker-host.worker.js` hashes match the campaign build), a scan of all 27,603 `dist` text files, source maps included, found none of the 16 tokens that occur only in those files. The tokens included `./lean-worker-scope.js`, `createLeanWorker`, `openclaw.experimentalLeanHost` and their error strings. No `lean-worker*` file was emitted.

```

dist files=27603 bytes=398238811 namedLegacy=[] legacyUniqueInDist=[]  -> no-legacy-token-in-dist
```

A clean build of `40fc34f0` from a fresh clone had no untracked files (`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` and `git ls-files --others` were both empty) and scans `clean-no-legacy` across `dist` and the packed tarball.

**Upgrade from latest stable into lean.** `openclaw@2026.11.6` (npm `latest`) was upgraded to a candidate tarball built from `40fc34f0` (build-info commit `40fc34f0df16`). The run used a 3 GiB cgroup with no swap and `gateway.resources.profile: "auto"`. Stable predates resource profiles, so this setting was added after the package install; the install itself left the config byte-identical.

All 17 upgrade checks passed. The upgrade run recorded no `memory.events` `max`, `oom` or `oom_kill`. prs.title: feat(clawrouter): consume qualified native Google image offers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter image generation could not consume qualified native Google image offers. A provider serving multiple image protocols also needs model-specific geometry and reference limits, rather than applying one protocol's rules to every model.

## User Impact

Users can select `google/gemini-3.1-flash-image` or `google/gemini-3-pro-image` when their selected ClawRouter credential has a matching native or manifest offer. Direct Google generation and existing OpenAI generation/edit routes keep their contracts.

The client sends one bounded native request using the selected router credential, validates inline image results, and preserves the original deadline/cancellation behavior. It does not fall back to an upstream Google credential. Shipping Worker/SQLite image parity and accounting remain separate, unestablished proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google and ClawRouter share one Google image request/response codec. The image provider contract adds optional `capabilitiesByModel`; runtime selects those capabilities before normalizing geometry, while preserving normal provider acquisition, unsupported empty resolution lists and output dimensions.

The frozen-baseline reconciliation preserves incoming OpenAI `/images/edits`, mode-specific catalog grants, reference/byte preflight and cancellation tests. It also retains incoming readiness-first speech assertions and the original Tokenjuice ownership correction.

Release note: consume qualified Google image offers through ClawRouter with model-specific capabilities, without changing direct Google or OpenAI edit behavior. This repository keeps ordinary release-note context in the PR rather than editing release-owned changelog files.

## Evidence

Exact signed correction: `d173f1ae09324d1fb94e445fa4235a87fc175373`, parent `3fdddb50e4b7943d73bcadef2d8b356d8e0e7a27`, retaining frozen product baseline `1ed570fb2b288299e2e2a99036d2b9b1e1953a3e`.

The exact tested merge and relevant fixture/guard/catalog blobs were verified. This correction adds those fields at the HTTP response boundary only. Owning agents-tools test types, scoped lint, format and diff checks pass. Test budget passes at +494 net lines with the existing 401+87 allocations unchanged.

- Parent `1ed` → `3fdd` SDK/API comparison completes successfully and **reports an API change**: optional `ImageGenerationProvider.capabilitiesByModel`. No public entrypoint is added or removed; 174 reachable export records reflect that shared type change.
- **Parent `3fdd` full build fails** its declaration and UI budgets. Native preparation records this as an investigated local failure; it is not a passing build or a budget waiver. Original current-head CI and the full observed check census are green; final native merge admission remains separate.

The correction changes only one test file. All production, API, dependency and build inputs remain byte-identical to `3fdd`; its build/API receipts are retained with their original identity, not relabelled as executions on `d173`.

Correction timing: four files / two repository-selected shards took 57.528 s wall including worker preparation; shard times were 38.73 s and 14.42 s. prs.title: fix: show app update guidance instead of a failing Update button on app-managed Macs
prs.body:
Closes #198506 Prior work: #198562 tried this and was closed without merging because the update handlers it edited have since moved. This PR is written against current main. ## What Problem This Solves On a Mac where OpenClaw.app owns the Gateway, Settings > Updates still shows an enabled "Update Gateway..." button and an "Update status unavailable" row. Clicking the button gets a refusal from the Gateway ("Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."). The page then keeps that refusal as an update error with a "Retry update" button, and the error stays until the page is reloaded. A healthy install looks like it failed an update, and Retry cannot succeed because the Gateway marks the refusal as not retryable. ## User Impact User impact: on an app-managed install, Settings > Updates now says "Managed by OpenClaw.app" in the status row and shows the app's own guidance ("Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway.") where the update button used to be. There is no button to click, so no error appears and nothing is left to retry. Other installs (package, Git checkout, separately managed Gateways) look and behave as before. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway already knew the install was app-owned, but `update.status` dropped that fact, so the page had no way to tell this install from any other and offered the normal action. The Gateway now sends the owner under `schedule.install.host`, and the Settings page uses it. Ownership comes from the same install marker the Gateway's refusal already uses, so a Mac connected to a separately managed Gateway still gets the normal update flow. The protocol schema gains an optional `install.host` object and a `host` install kind, and the generated validators are regenerated from it. The Control UI adds four English strings. The updating doc notes where the owner is reported. Update behavior: this only changes what `update.status` reports and what Settings shows. How updates run is unchanged. An app-owned Gateway still refuses Gateway update requests with the app's hint, and package and Git installs keep their current update flow. ## Evidence I ran the same Settings > Updates steps in Chromium against disposable Gateways built from the base (`d119c6b`) and from this change (`0f678cb`). Both used the exact ownership marker written by the Mac packaging script, with fresh Gateway state and no model or credentials. The current head (`1b71766`, on main `dc6e31a`) has the same hand-written changes as `0f678cb`; only the generated `predicates.js` was regenerated on newer main. Before: Settings shows "Update status unavailable" and offers "Update Gateway…". Confirming it leaves "Couldn’t update OpenClaw. Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway." in the status row. `update.status` returned `schedule.install: null`. After: Settings shows "Managed by OpenClaw.app" and the guidance "Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway." There is no Gateway update button. `update.status` returned `schedule.install: {"kind":"host","host":{"owner":"macos-app","displayName":"OpenClaw.app","updateHint":"Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."}}`. With main's sources (`dc6e31a`) and this PR's tests, the new Settings test fails the way the issue describes: the status row reads "Update status unavailable" where it should say "Managed by OpenClaw.app". The 9 Gateway and schema cases that expect the owner fail the same way. On the current head, all of them pass.
Tests and checks on the current head (Node 26, macOS arm64) - `ui/src/pages/config/updates.test.ts`: 43 passed. The app-managed case took 34 ms. - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/config.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-install-status.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-startup-host-owned.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status-schedule.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status.test.ts`: 71 tests across the 5 files, run with a 60 second test timeout because this machine is slow. In the full run, 69 passed and the two "reads recorded progress without reconciliation during restart" cases in `update-status.test.ts` (a file this PR does not change) hit that timeout. Rerun alone with a longer timeout, both pass on this head and on main's sources. - `gateway:validators:check` and `ui:validators:check` report no drift. `predicates.js` was regenerated from the schema rather than merged by hand. - `oxlint` with the repository config on the 11 changed TypeScript files reports no diagnostics. `oxfmt --check` on the 13 changed files and `git diff --check` are clean. `ui:i18n:verify` passes. - `tsconfig.core.json` and `tsconfig.ui.json` report the same set of type errors with and without this change. All of them come from packages missing in my partial dependency install, and none are in the changed files.
Not verified: - No run inside OpenClaw.app itself, and no upgrade from a released version (such as v2026.11.6) with settings intact. The browser run above used a Gateway built from source with the Mac packaging marker. The issue's reporter offered to check a fix on their Mac. - A separately managed Gateway was not run in a browser; the existing `updates.test.ts` cases for the "Update Gateway…" action still pass. - `pnpm install`, the full `pnpm check:changed`, type-aware lint and a full typecheck were not run. Dependencies came from a scratch npm install using the versions in `package.json`.

prs.title: feat(opencode): sign in to OpenCode Console and OpenCode Go in the browser
prs.body:
## Problem

The only way to connect OpenCode (Zen, pay-as-you-go) or OpenCode Go in OpenClaw was to paste an API key. OpenCode Console now supports device authorization, the same browser sign-in flow other providers use in the Control UI and CLI, but OpenClaw didn't offer it.

## Solution

- `opencode` and `opencode-go` each register an `oauth` auth method (`opencode-console`, `opencode-go-console`) that runs OpenCode Console device authorization (`client_id=openclaw`):
  - shows the code and opens `opencode.ai/console/device`;
  - polls until the user approves or denies, or the code expires;
  - stores an OAuth credential in an auth profile and refreshes it.
- Each provider signs in separately. OpenCode refresh tokens are single-use, so one credential can't serve both providers without the two of them invalidating each other's refresh chain.
- The sign-in code lives in `console-oauth.ts`, copied into both plugins. Plugins can't share private code, and the only differences between the copies are the provider id and the audit context. A plugin-sdk device-code helper would remove the copy; that is a follow-up, not this PR.
- The picker names each method clearly: "OpenCode Console (browser sign-in)" and "OpenCode Go (browser sign-in)". Before this PR, both plugins showed only an API key field.
- Docs: `docs/providers/opencode.md` and `docs/providers/opencode-go.md`.

## Impact

- New users can connect OpenCode or OpenCode Go from **Settings → Models → Add account**, or with `openclaw models auth login --provider opencode` / `opencode-go`, without copying a key.
- Signing in with an API key works as before.
- No core, config schema or SDK change.
- Accepted edge case: a sign-in only offers "Start a new chat with …" when it also sets the agent's model. That happens when no model is configured yet; it is how every provider behaves. In the Go recording, the scratch Gateway already had a default model, so the dialog shows only Close.

## Evidence

Real E2E on isolated scratch Gateways (separate `HOME`, profile and port; real OpenCode Console approvals from a real account):

**OpenCode Console (pay-as-you-go), Control UI, fresh profile.** Models → Add account → OpenCode → browser sign-in → code → approve in OpenCode Console → "OpenCode Console (browser sign-in) is ready / MiniMax M3 is ready for your agent" → **Start a new chat with MiniMax M3** → the agent replies `opencode-ui-ok`. The video has the approval wait cut out.

**OpenCode Go, Control UI.** Models → Add account → OpenCode Go → browser sign-in → code → approve → "OpenCode Go (browser sign-in) is ready". Then a real agent turn on the same Gateway with `--model opencode-go/kimi-k3`:
- replied `go-ui-signin-ok`;
- `provider: opencode-go`, `model: kimi-k3`;
- `credentialSource: {kind: "profile"}`, `authMode: auth-profile`;
- no fallback.

**Failure paths seen in the UI:** an expired code shows "sign-in code expired. Start sign-in again." (recorded in an earlier Go run).

**Checks:**
- `ocx test extensions/opencode extensions/opencode-go`: 13 files, 130 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:changed`: all passed.
- oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files: clean.
- `tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.

Diff against `main`: +975 / −5 in 11 files. About 500 lines are the two `console-oauth.ts` copies, about 290 are tests.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): admit saved requesters once when work starts
prs.body:
## Problem

Saved operator work duplicated admission and carried permission checks into started runs. Serialization limits must not lose accepted work, and a live source must not acquire unrelated credential or resident-profile dependencies.

## Fix and behavior

Saved, queued, continuation and recorded sandbox operator starts call async `prepareOperatorAdmission` and synchronous `decideOperatorAdmission`. The decision uses prepared owners and committed config, freezes current profile/access/role/model/admin facts, and checks the actual runtime target agent against the role's agent ceiling. Restore's hand-built credential branches, reference counts, chat-deletion subscription and permission re-check closures are deleted.

- Live-only sources carry existing authentication, pairing, ingress and scope evidence in memory, independently of durable codec bounds. Canonical profile-backed live sources check that the profile still exists and re-read current role, without requiring every email binding; host-issued opaque grants with no canonical identity binding keep their issued role facts at the next same-process start, as on main. Credential/device/ingress/scope/target checks still apply. `canonicalIdentity` is required: an actual canonical profile binding or explicit `null` for a host-issued opaque grant. Production producers cannot omit it. No canonical profile is invented or newly required for an opaque grant; profile-not-found maps to the existing visible refusal type.
- Live paired devices require the same ID/key and no revocation. Their scopes use the handshake device ceiling union current identity grants, including OCID; saved Gateway facts additionally use current paired/token scopes and approved operator role. Device-less proxy/Tailscale scopes use the current grant.
- Remote ingress has no unrelated shared-generation dependency. Existing binding abort and scope ceiling are read at start; no identity index, subscription or callback is added. Capture pairing reads remain tokenless proxy/Tailscale only; failure preserves the live request without inventing device evidence.
- Disabled OCID visibly refuses; unpublished enabled lookup, missing generation state and pairing/profile-owner outages defer accepted work. Pending profile mutation is detected before waiting for its held writer.
- Cron's requesterOwner comes from the same decision/config. Parent-bound sources preserve the non-member owner rule; independent Gateway sources require admitted admin. Configured channel-owner receipt capabilities remain their existing separate domain.
- Already-admitted publication, completion and delivery transfer their frozen decision rather than admitting again during persistence or effects. Real session/creator/owner/target/physical-store/claim/receipt/plugin/Gateway fences remain. A claim is checked by the producer accepting work, not a restored authority callback.

Mixed-person collected inputs drop the requester sender identity and inherited command-owner capability. Single-sender starts recompute current owner status; mixed drains cannot reconstruct sender authority. No collected-run flag or queued parameter is needed in command-owner admission. An owner message cannot lend owner tools to another sender’s collected text.

Revocation affects the next start. Started work may finish; Stop still cancels. Initial dispatcher/connect migration and authority callback deletion remain later steps.

## Saved compatibility and explicit edges

Exactly one optional saved field is added: the trusted-proxy fallback password hash (`sha256Base64Url`). Fingerprints remain unchanged. Current role scopes intersect saved scopes; new snapshots stop writing `rolePolicy`, while old optional fields still decode.

- Browser origin is connect-only. Saved work follows its person, not its browser (owner decision2026-11-20). Old fallback rows without the hash retain legacy grant comparison, including `browserOriginAllowed`; an origin edit can still refuse that old row until it drains/is re-saved.
- Legacy Tailscale rows without device evidence preserve saved scopes when the grant fingerprint is unchanged; changed grants intersect current identity scope. New paired rows use exact evidence.
- A live ingress binding may abort on a role change, including widening; refusal at the next start preserves main's binding semantics.
- Native durable producers still omit recovery sources (`reply-source-admission.ts`, `dispatch-from-config.lifecycle.ts`, `get-reply-run-execute.ts`). Restart replay refuses these in `queued-chat-inputs.ts`: retained bytes are cancelled/unrecoverable, no reply is generated, and the warning asks for a new send. Existing native in-memory queue starts share admission; this PR does not broaden native restart behavior.
- Shared HTTP bearer system actors and Cron standing/management grants are explicit control rows, not new operator sources. Node-role serialization stays outside this step.

## Defined coverage

Typed `Record<Kind, Row>`: **39 operator/control kinds, 143 cases**, three real auth-mode pools and one real restart sentinel (**four Gateway boots**). Each kind defines before-start, after-start and Stop cases with row-specific control/independence assertions. Accepted durable WS/plugin rows use real `continueSessionQueuedInputs`; native channel uses its real in-memory queued lifecycle. No manufactured authority or production test hooks.

Additional cases cover grant/token/role/ingress narrowing, widening, empty scopes, unavailable-owner retry, legacy fallback/Tailscale, exact device key/revocation/approval, current OCID grant union, live credential rotation, and a real Goal whose role excludes its agent: the admitted turn finishes, the next turn visibly refuses with no provider request. The matrix also covers an owner-plus-non-owner native GROUP collection with no owner tools and a live continuation after removal of a secondary email. A profile-deleted-before-start row requires the existing visible refusal type, retained cancelled input and no queued provider call; it deletes the actual canonical row through the existing profile transaction/publication owner. Existing owner-specific tests retain alias/access-plugin/model/admin/channel-owner contracts not duplicated by the matrix.

## CI repair and evidence

Old-head CI assertions were classified file by file: real live-context/profile and next-target regressions were fixed; obsolete mid-flight/snapshot/wording expectations were rewritten without restoring permission callbacks. Main was integrated; removed-export consumers, fixture types, mock exports and session-identity comparisons were migrated. Both new import cycles are cut with leaf contracts, without scanner or ratchet exemptions.

Opaque manufactured test grants now use `createTestOperatorAuthority` in the existing admitted-run test-support module, so the null default lives in one test builder rather than per fixture. Production factory/module-identity tests, intentionally invalid raw authorities and direct channel-input API fixtures retain explicit required identity facts.

Direct touched-file oxfmt/oxlint and normal pre-commit hooks passed. **No local test suites, builds or typechecks ran.** New-head CI is the behavioral/type proof; no green-CI claim. The unrelated mocked UI asset/readiness and existing shutdown deadline failures remain untouched for comparison against main.

## Test consolidation and deltas

Removed matrix-subsumed cases (files remain for their distinct contracts):

- `operator-run-recovery.test.ts`: shared credentials rotating before restoration/after admission; device removed/token revoked re-admission; admitted-facts device-revoked/role-changed variants. Real matrix token/password/device/role before-/after-start cases replace these; retired-claim, mutation, alias and other distinct cases remain.
- `operator-run-recovery.native.test.ts`: tokenless proxy device remove/revoke/remove-without-token variants; replaced by real proxy-device/live-device/live-device-revoked matrix rows.
- `operator-run-recovery.trusted-proxy.test.ts`: widened identity grant, removed proxy user and leaving trusted-proxy mode; replaced by widened-grant, trusted-proxy refusal and the real mode-transition restart sentinel.
- `operator-run-recovery.effects.test.ts`: two duplicated direct/native-Cron write setups became one six-case table; **all six device/email reassignment/email restoration write contracts remain**.

Credential, ingress-consent, session-owner and completion/Stop builders are shared; duplicate decision-observer/frozen-shape scaffolding was removed. No further cuts to the requested matrix or unique aliases/access-plugin/model/admin/physical-store/receipt/claim/token-reissue/reconnect proof. The remaining test budget is accepted to retain these contracts.

Production TypeScript versus the PR merge base with `origin/main` (src/extensions/packages, excluding tests/support): **+2,429 / -2,775, net -346**. Tests/support: **+6,187 / -4,128, net +2,059** (238 fewer net lines than the preceding head); allocation **1,659** beyond normal400.

prs.title: fix(cli): reject non-decimal tool usage limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The tool-usage CLI accepted hexadecimal and exponent notation as bounded integers, so inputs such as `0x10` and `1e1` could silently select a range even though these options are documented as integer day/count values.

## User Impact

Decimal integer values within the existing bounds continue to work, while non-decimal, fractional, zero, and out-of-range values are rejected before any Gateway request is made.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `tools usage import --since` and `tools usage status --limit` now use the shared strict positive-integer parser. The help text keeps readable ASCII ranges, and the parser remains private to the CLI owner.

## Evidence

At head `88332fc3cbd3e0fc54aad7d8b1b20522cd6208bc`, the focused CLI suite passes all 17 tests, including both flags rejecting decimal-looking exponent and hexadecimal inputs before the mocked Gateway call. The shipped CLI also rejects `--since 0x10`, `--since 1e1`, and `status --limit 0x10` with the expected range errors; `tools usage import --help` displays `(1-90)`. `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted oxlint, and targeted oxfmt pass.

The repository stores these tracked CLI files with CRLF. `git -c core.whitespace=cr-at-eol diff --check` passes; the default check reports the existing CRLF representation as trailing whitespace and is not a semantic whitespace change. Exact-head GitHub checks are pending after the push.

The remaining product question is maintainer-owned: a prior review of the same proposal requested demonstrated user harm before changing acceptance of non-decimal notation. This PR now supplies shipped behavior proof and restores help text, but it cannot make that product decision on behalf of maintainers.
