prs.title: feat: let WhatsApp users schedule OpenClaw tasks from a DM
prs.body:
Closes #202884

Related: #187264 and #198119

## What Problem This Solves

An ordinary WhatsApp contact on a shared Gateway can ask the agent about their orders but cannot ask the native scheduler to do it every morning. The existing conversational scheduler requires owner authority. The baseline exercised create, list, update, and delete through the bundled WhatsApp adapter. [Baseline and reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187264#issuecomment-7055382385)

## User Impact

With `session.dmScope: "per-account-channel-peer"`, a contact admitted by the account’s ordinary WhatsApp DM policy can manage their own schedules in that chat. Sites with an explicit tool allowlist can include `whatsapp_automations`. No additional phone-number list is required. Literal reminders send the saved text. A task runs an isolated native OpenClaw agent turn and sends the computed result to the originating WhatsApp account and private peer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host binds the account and sender to the native private message. The scheduler captures the creator’s executable tool surface and intersects it with the due turn’s current permissions. The ordinary session MCP runtime supplies configured static tools and resolves requester-bound connections for that sender. Both partitions follow native unattended approval rules. Client-only tools, missing caller credentials, and grants requiring interactive approval cannot perform work on the scheduled turn. The Gateway owns delivery. Operators retain their existing management authority.

## Evidence

**Before.** On the upstream baseline, an admitted WhatsApp contact could ask for their orders, but the owner-only scheduler prevented that contact from saving the same request as a daily task.

**After.** In the bundled Gateway loopback test, the contact saved a daily task from a private DM. After the order data changed to 3 and 8 units, the native timer read the new quantities and delivered “You have 2 orders for 11 units.” to the originating account and DM. Withdrawing DM access prevented the next lookup and delivery. The contacts, orders and model were synthetic. Physical WhatsApp and production-model evidence are still outstanding.

### Static and requester-bound MCP reports at `e061185708`

On `249e62b67e`, the ordinary sender read a static MCP report interactively and saved it as a daily task. When the native timer fired, the embedded runner reported “No callable tools remain” despite the captured static tool. It never read the changed report. The personal task had selected a requester-only MCP runtime.

The corrected runner uses the same live MCP acquisition as the creating conversation. The bundled Gateway fixture exercised a static server alone, a requester-bound server alone, and both together. Each interactive report read 1 unit. After durable save the source changed to 17 units. Each naturally due daily report called its MCP server again and reached the same WhatsApp account and private peer. The connected server required the synthetic creator’s account and sender credential. The shared static report used its configured connection.

A second contact could not remove the saved job by ID. An amendment tool available interactively required consent and disappeared from the due model surface. The servers recorded zero amendment calls. After DM access was withdrawn, a subsequent occurrence was skipped with zero new calls or messages. A focused runner test also checked that an MCP App sees only creator-captured, unattended-approved tools. [Gateway scenario](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e061185708edfd67660f656e4f13f28c8e986e22/extensions/qa-lab/src/whatsapp-private-automations.qa.mts) · [Runner regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e061185708edfd67660f656e4f13f28c8e986e22/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.test.ts)

### Parent permission edits during an admitted run at `249e62b67e`

On `cc5d5837d8`, a naturally due task reached the loopback model. While the request was held, the operator enabled a tool in the parent chat. The scheduler then recorded a failed run with “The originating conversation's permissions changed.” The orders summary never arrived.

With this revision, the same held task finished its authorized orders lookup and delivered the 11-unit summary to the original WhatsApp DM. The shared scheduler reads permissions from the parent at each occurrence’s admission. Storage-backed tests changed both permission mode and tool overrides in either direction, verified the admitted caller retained its original settings, and checked that a newly admitted occurrence received the edits. Parent reset, cancellation and source-withdrawal checks still apply. [Storage-backed regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/249e62b67eef08065b04515d19774d37b14dc2ff/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-caller.compaction.test.ts) · [Bundled Gateway regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/249e62b67eef08065b04515d19774d37b14dc2ff/extensions/qa-lab/src/whatsapp-private-automations.qa.mts)

### Stored inference accounts and conversation lifecycle at `cc5d5837d8`

- On the previous head, a task created using a stored provider account had no inference binding in its scheduler row. Its natural occurrence stopped with “Automation has no recorded inference account.” The revised tool gives native cron the account selected by the running model attempt. The save holds its authorization through commit. The isolated turn receives the stored binding and checks it through native cron inference.
- The bundled Gateway fixture used two distinct synthetic accounts at the same loopback provider. Independent scheduler storage readback confirmed the first account on the job. After the default changed and the chat was reset, a new interactive request used the second account. The daily timer still used the first account to read the revised orders and returned the computed total to the original account and DM. A later naturally due task used the second account and marked those orders reviewed after manual chat compaction. The ledger confirmed the mutation.
- With the first model account disconnected, another occurrence failed before any new connector access or WhatsApp delivery, despite the second account remaining available. A known-ID edit from another contact was denied. With the original sender removed from the DM policy, the next occurrence was skipped.
- A separate storage-backed test committed a compaction successor with a new transcript ID under the same conversation key. The previous caller guard rejected the minted occurrence. The revised guard admits it under the current parent’s permissions and lifecycle. [Gateway assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cc5d5837d8145a00dfd9f0369c7b1a985b83065e/extensions/qa-lab/src/whatsapp-private-automations.qa.mts) · [Compaction successor regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cc5d5837d8145a00dfd9f0369c7b1a985b83065e/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-caller.compaction.test.ts)

### Earlier behavior and upgrade evidence at `9457615e34`

- A loopback Gateway ran the bundled WhatsApp/Baileys adapter with two synthetic contacts, Crabline, and a scripted provider. The first sender’s interactive lookup read one unit. A daily schedule was saved, the source changed to quantities 3 and 8, and the native timer invoked the tool again. The sender received “You have 2 orders for 11 units.” Another naturally due task marked both orders reviewed. Independent ledger readback verified the mutation, account, and sender.
- A held model request kept the session busy while an ordinary WhatsApp DM arrived. Native session status showed a queued follow-up. After the held request finished, the queued DM created a schedule, verified by a separate operator read. Removing just the deferred-turn binding made that same request return “Send a fresh private WhatsApp request.” A separate fresh-account run verified that the first ordinary DM could save an agent task and a later DM could list the same job ID. Later DMs listed, updated, and removed the sender’s schedule. A second contact could neither see nor remove it by known ID. The creator could not edit a protected operator job.
- The fixture confirmed a naturally due literal reminder and verified the account and peer on delivery. Removing the sender from the ordinary WhatsApp policy skipped a subsequent occurrence, produced no further connector access or outbound message, and prevented scheduling from a later DM.
- Focused tests cover successful-add accounting, the session association, active-hours and idle-only restrictions, one admission per occurrence, and omission of consent-required tools from the unattended MCP surface. All 180 focused tests across 14 files passed.
- The published stable CLI (v2026.11.6) created a disabled operator job. After stopping that Gateway, the candidate reopened the same state directory. Its operator client recovered the same job ID, payload text, disabled state, hourly schedule, and session configuration.

Run the end-to-end check with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/whatsapp-private-automations.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`.

[Bundled native regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9457615e3499e6058876b92d70ed2a9bb42ec35f/extensions/qa-lab/src/whatsapp-private-automations.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts) · [Scenario and assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9457615e3499e6058876b92d70ed2a9bb42ec35f/extensions/qa-lab/src/whatsapp-private-automations.qa.mts)

### Checks and limits

The bundled Gateway test passed all four cases (static MCP, requester-bound MCP, both partitions, and the existing plugin/literal reminder journey). The eight focused test files passed all 137 tests. Core and extension type checks, scoped lint, and formatting passed. The broader agent test type shard reported the same two missing `trigger` errors in `attempt.tool-search-run-plan.test.ts` on the parent and this revision.

The full build exceeded the existing SDK declaration limit of 5,385,536 bytes. The PR base measured 5,405,627 bytes, parent `249e62b67e` measured 5,407,510, and this revision measured 5,407,386. The maintainer CI approval request is already on this PR.

The native timer, Gateway, MCP transport and bundled WhatsApp adapter ran locally. The contacts, data, model, and WhatsApp network peer were synthetic. Physical WhatsApp and production-model proof remain outstanding.

## Maintainer decision

Should ordinary WhatsApp DM admission authorize personal scheduling for an account-and-peer-isolated conversation? The proposed shared channel security hook, `isDirectSenderAdmitted`, takes a resolved account and an adapter-verified private sender. The channel owns normalization, pairing and current DM policy. The shared scheduler asks once when a queued turn starts or a scheduled occurrence is admitted. The check must be side-effect free and grants no tool or operator authority. An absent hook denies deferred admission. Once admitted, an operation retains its ordinary lifecycle and cancellation fences.

The API placement is open for maintainer direction. The implementation keeps WhatsApp identity and policy in the bundled channel, with shared scheduling and permission checks in core. The related Telegram proposal and the cross-channel issue can inform whether this hook belongs on `ChannelSecurityAdapter` or a broader caller-scoped scheduling contract. [Proposed adapter contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cc5d5837d8145a00dfd9f0369c7b1a985b83065e/src/channels/plugins/types.adapters.ts)

prs.title: feat: move a conversation that has no project into one
prs.body:
Closes #202268

## What changes

On main, moving work from the default workspace into an existing project requires another conversation and a manual transfer of local edits.

Say **“let’s work on OpenClaw”** in the default workspace. The model can use `session_project` to move this conversation into a registered project and confirm the destination. The conversation keeps its messages and continues in the project’s managed checkout. The tool is available by default for eligible sessions, subject to tool policy. The Gateway refuses a second move.

Use **Move to project…** to choose the destination yourself. For a matching checkout, the dialog tells you how many files have changes to copy. The original checkout stays in place. The project checkout restores copied changes before repository setup, and links from the original workspace still open there.

Project moves and PR workspace preparation use the same checks for active runs, background processes, terminals, and child sessions. PR workspace preparation also checks that the original filesystem target is still current.

## Control UI comparison

Captured in the built Control UI with a synthetic project and two file changes. Main screenshot at `e309df612e`.

| Conversation menu on main | Project move dialog in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Main conversation menu without a project move action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/e12ca5c06db1fb176425bb65d8fd35c03cf65dde/images/2026/11/8ea3ec35-58db-4f9b-8e2a-0143e9ef7810.png) | ![Move to a project dialog showing Changes to 2 files will be copied](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/e12ca5c06db1fb176425bb65d8fd35c03cf65dde/images/2026/11/ac26f04c-e00c-4972-b493-62ce632fe8eb.png) |

## Evidence

- **Upgrade from 2026.11.6.** The released OpenClaw binary wrote a conversation with a user message, an assistant reply, and a project registration. The PR build loaded the same session ID, both messages, and the same project from that state. A manual move kept the session ID and opened a managed checkout at the original commit. Repository setup saw the copied edit, and the untracked note survived.
- **Real Control UI.** A real Qwen3-4B model moved the conversation into Juniper and confirmed the destination with the same session ID. A separate browser-driven manual move recorded the selected project and left the two original file changes in place.
- **Focused checks.** 29 tests passed across PR workspace adoption, workspace policy, project moves, and checkout carry. They cover active background work, queued follow-ups, and filesystem targets that change before adoption. Format, scoped lint, core typecheck, and import-cycle checks passed.
- **Sandbox carry.** The fixture closes the initiating turn before the tool handoff and verifies that committed and unsaved work reach the destination. Live Docker carry is pending.
- **Control UI boot.** Shared tool-display metadata keeps direct JSON imports out of startup. A paired removal experiment put chat boot 136 B over main, beyond the 64 B allowance.

Updates `actions/setup-java` from 6.1.0 to 6.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from actions/setup-java's releases.

v6.3.0

Behavior change: Java problem matcher is now opt-in

Starting with v6.3.0, setup-java no longer registers the Java problem matcher by default (#1326, fixes #1322). Java compiler warnings, compiler errors, and uncaught exceptions are no longer turned into annotations on pull request diffs unless you opt in.

To keep annotations, set problem-matcher: true:

- uses: actions/setup-java@v6
  with:
    distribution: temurin
    java-version: '25'
    problem-matcher: true

Compiler output still appears in the build logs, and compilation errors still fail the build. Only annotations are affected.

Why: inline annotations cluttered pull request reviews, and GitHub Actions caps annotations at 10 errors, 10 warnings, and 10 notices per step, and 50 per job. Larger Java builds therefore showed only a truncated subset of their diagnostics as annotations. See Java problem matcher (compiler annotations).

What's Changed

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.3 to 4.39.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202844

## What Problem This Solves

Google music output-format rules are declared separately in capability metadata and request validation. Maintainers must keep both declarations aligned when supported formats change.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Model-specific format acceptance, unknown-model MP3 defaults, authentication and validation order, rejection text, and response filename inference retain their existing contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing metadata module now owns one format policy used by both callers. Every call returns a fresh mutable array, preserving independence between modes and provider instances. No new module, public SDK surface, or dependency is added.

Production changes total +11/-3 lines; test changes total +41/-0 lines. The added cases protect metadata independence and request-format acceptance/rejection through the existing factory and provider.

## Evidence

- All 19 Google music provider/factory cases passed through the public repository test wrapper, with one file selected and zero skipped.
- Google production types, the maintained extension-test type graph, three-file typed lint, and three-file formatting passed. Normal signed hooks and independent committed-range source review also passed.

Typed lint plus its required maintained SDK declaration preparation took 125.04 seconds; production types took 1.46 seconds, extension-test types 28.97 seconds, and formatting 0.08 seconds. These are whole-command observations, not comparative performance claims.
- The format-request cases use synthetic MPEG responses. They do not prove real WAV generation or decoding, and no live paid Google call was made.
- Five nonfatal bundler directive warnings and normal lifecycle notices are retained in the local proof.
- Full build, exact-head hosted CI/security, and native preparation/landing remain pending. Local declaration preparation is not full-build or release-compatibility proof.

prs.title: fix(config): provider OAuth re-login drops null thinkingLevelMap entries
prs.body:
Closes #201558

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: re-authenticating an OAuth provider rewrites untouched configured model rows in `openclaw.json` and deletes authored `null` `thinkingLevelMap` entries (such as `"off": null`).

## User Impact

User impact: completing provider OAuth sign-in or re-login now writes only the credential/auth profile delta and leaves existing `models.providers.*.models` entries—including explicit `null` thinking-level mappings—intact on disk.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `src/config/merge-patch.ts`, ID-keyed object array diffing (`mergeObjectArraysById: true`) previously handled matched array entries via custom per-field logic that emitted `null` values even when both `base` and `target` already held `null`. Because RFC 7396 `applyMergePatch` treats `null` in a patch object as key deletion, an unchanged `"off": null` entry in `thinkingLevelMap` was emitted into `createProviderAuthConfigPatch` and subsequently deleted on write. Delegating matched ID-keyed array elements directly to `createMergePatch(baseEntry, entry, options)` removes the duplicate branch (`-4` net production LOC) so unchanged `null` properties produce an empty diff while newly nulled or deleted keys still emit `null`.

## Evidence

- **Production vs. Test LOC delta:** production `+1 / -5` (net `-4` in `src/config/merge-patch.ts`), tests `+29 / -2` (`src/config/merge-patch.test.ts`, `src/plugins/provider-auth-config.test.ts`).
- **Live ConfigIO + `writeProviderAuthConfig` disk verification** against an isolated `openclaw.json` seeded with `models.providers.openai.models[0].thinkingLevelMap = {"off":null,"minimal":"low","xhigh":"xhigh","max":"max"}`:

  - **Post-fix:** `createProviderAuthConfigPatch` emitted `{"auth":{"profiles":{"openai:default":{"provider":"openai","mode":"oauth"}}}}`, and `openclaw.json` on disk preserved `{"off":null,"minimal":"low","xhigh":"xhigh","max":"max"}` with `agents.defaults.models` untouched (`undefined`).

prs.title: fix: say "signed out" when an OpenClaw ID browser signs out
prs.body:
Related: Linear OCF-595

## What Problem This Solves

When you sign out of OpenClaw ID in a browser, the Gateway closes that browser's connections. It closed them with the same reason it uses when an owner removes a member: `1008 "removed from this claw"`. The Control UI and the Gateway log then said the browser was removed from the claw, when it had only signed out.

## User Impact

User impact: a signed-out browser now sees and logs "signed out of OpenClaw ID". A removed member still sees "removed from this claw". Sign-out still keeps membership and leaves other peers connected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The connection-close effect now takes a cause. Remote sign-out passes `signed-out`. The Gateway then closes with the internal reason `openclaw-id-signed-out` and the message `signed out of OpenClaw ID`. Membership removal and owner expiry keep `openclaw-id-removed` / `removed from this claw`.

The close code stays `1008`. I checked every client that reads the close code or reason, and none needs a separate code:

- Control UI (`ui/src/app/gateway-store.ts`) shows the Gateway's close reason as-is in the disconnect message. Its `1008` handling does not look at the reason text.
- claw-loader (`src/loader/states.ts` `CLOSE`, `sw.ts`) matches tunnel-session close codes (`not_a_member`, `revoked`, ...), not Gateway WebSocket close frames. It relays those frames to the page without reading them. The loader needs no change.
- Native Apple and Android clients do not compare against `removed from this claw` or `openclaw-id-removed`. The macOS "Removed from …" copy comes from its own removal record, not from the close frame.

## Evidence

- New unit test: closing with the `signed-out` cause invalidates only the signed-out peer's connection, with `{ reason: "openclaw-id-signed-out", code: 1008, message: "signed out of OpenClaw ID" }`. The removal test now also pins the removal message.
- The remote sign-out route test now requires sign-out to close with the `signed-out` cause.
- Both tests fail on the base commit and pass with this change.
- The other `closeConnections` consumer tests (membership, member role, tunnel API, owner expiry) still pass. `pnpm tsgo:core` and oxlint on the touched files are clean.
- Not run: a live staging sign-out. The issue was found by the OCF-333 staging proof, and this fix only changes the close reason.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/openclaw-id/removal-effects.test.ts src/gateway/openclaw-id/remote-signout.test.ts   # base: 5 failed; fix: pass
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/openclaw-id/{removal-effects,remote-signout,service.membership,authority.member-role,tunnel-api,owner-expiry}.test.ts   # 44 passed
pnpm tsgo:core
```

</details>

When the tmux text-wait helper cannot read a pane, it times out with a blank pane dump. A mistyped or closed pane looks like a pane where the expected text has yet to appear.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep a bounded session mode on CLIs with native tools
prs.body:
Stacked on #202941 (the Gateway enforces the session mode on every Gateway tool call); review the last commit.

## What Problem This Solves

After #202941 the Gateway bounds OpenClaw's tools to a session's permission mode on every runtime. A CLI backend that keeps its own native tools still ignored the mode: Gemini CLI (its native file tools are never mediated) and a Claude CLI chat placed on a node (it keeps Claude's native tools). A Read only / Ask me / Auto-review chat on those routes could read and write anywhere through the CLI's own tools.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI tool policy already has one owner for "this run must use only Gateway-mediated tools": the mediation path used for `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, restricted senders and delegated runs. A bounded session mode now joins that list for backends that are not already mediated:

- A backend that can run on the mediated surface (Gemini CLI with exact tool support) does so, and the Gateway enforces the mode.
- A run that cannot be mediated (node-placed Claude, a backend without exact tools or the Gateway MCP bridge) is refused before any CLI or node I/O: `CLI backend <id> uses its own tools here and cannot keep this chat's <mode> permissions. Change this chat to Full access, or choose another runtime.`
- Full access and sessions with no mode are unchanged. Ordinary Claude CLI turns are already mediated and unchanged.

No existing chat on our deployments has a bounded mode on these routes (Peanutto: 64 Claude CLI chats, none node-placed, all mode unset; team-metal: none).

## Evidence

- `prepare-tool-policy.delegation.test.ts`: a Gemini CLI turn with a `workspace` mode gets the mediated surface; a node-placed Claude turn with that mode is refused with the next step; `full` and unset keep the native surface. The two new mode cases fail on #202941's head and pass here.
- Real product, tier source (`ocx src`), isolated Gateway, Claude CLI agent, caller with full operator scopes:

| | #202941 head | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Node-placed chat (`execHost: node`) in `workspace` mode | dispatched to the node (no node present: `Paired node needs claude-cli-skills-v1…`) | refused before dispatch: `CLI backend claude-cli uses its own tools here and cannot keep this chat's workspace permissions. Change this chat to Full access, or choose another runtime.` |
| Ordinary chat in `workspace` mode, read inside the workspace | `FORK-READ-OK 7f3a` | `FORK-READ-OK 7f3a` |

Not proven live: Gemini CLI (not installed on the test host); covered by the unit test above.

prs.title: fix(tlon): require approval before responding in group DMs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tlon group DM messages carry author claims that the Tlon transport does not authenticate. OpenClaw could treat a claimed ship in a group DM as if it matched the verified 1:1 DM allowlist, admitting unapproved input to the agent.

## User Impact

User impact: the owner enables a group DM once per club by default, then the agent can respond automatically in that club. Operators can require approval for each message, disable clubs, or allow and deny specific club IDs. Existing clubs need one-time enablement after upgrade; claimed authors and legacy approvals do not grant standing access.

## Why This Change Was Made

Club admission now depends on the club's own policy and recorded decision. Claimed participants never provide owner or command authority. Approved club messages use a club-specific group session, and replies return to the club. The change also decodes Tlon's wrapped settings events so saved decisions work across restarts.

Enabling a club accepts unverified input delivered under that club ID with the agent's ordinary permitted tools. It does not authenticate the author or membership; the owner prompt and Tlon docs explain that tradeoff.

This is a replacement for #196109. Thanks to @mmaps for identifying the group DM author-claim boundary and preparing the first fix. This version keeps approval friction to once per club by default and adds explicit stricter modes and club reply routing.

## Evidence

- The two regression cases failed on the base and pass with this change: an allowlisted claimed author cannot admit an unknown club, and a club turn uses a group route rather than the claimed author's direct route.
- In an isolated Gateway with a real model, a bot-side Tlon club event claiming allowlisted `~nec` produced one owner prompt and no agent turn. A verified `~bus` DM approved the club; the saved message ran through the model, which read a proof file and replied inside the club. A later message claiming the owner received an automatic club reply without another prompt. After Gateway restart, the saved club rule still allowed an automatic reply.
- Upgrade check: the published `@openclaw/tlon@2026.11.5` plugin created a legacy pending club request in isolated ship state. The replacement plugin loaded it; owner approval replayed the saved message without adding the claimed ship to the DM allowlist or enabling the club. The next message prompted for a new club decision.
- Startup persistence check: with no saved club rules, an explicit file-config allow rule migrated into the real Urbit settings store as a JSON string. A regression test failed before this serialization repair and passes after it.
- All 322 Tlon tests in 35 files pass. Tlon production and test typechecks, focused lint and format, docs MDX/config examples/internal links, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- The generated config baseline records six intentional Tlon schema paths for club policy and rules at the channel and account levels. Relative to current `main`, core and plugin counts are unchanged; `pnpm config:docs:check` passes. The merged current-main tree also passes all 322 Tlon tests and the Tlon production typecheck.
- CI on merged head `dfc6c43b` passed the config baseline, docs, Control UI e2e, and `openclaw/ci-gate` checks; the earlier one-request Control UI asset-budget failure did not recur.
- Local autoreview of the complete staged source change against base `053fb62c` reported `scoped-clean` for P0–P2 with no actionable finding at `b293ba33`. The later commits add generated baseline files and merge current `main`; the Tlon source patch is unchanged. Its assessment covered the supplied patch, not a live Tlon round trip.
- Authenticated remote ingress proof: a test-only Gall agent on isolated fake `~ten` sent a native remote `%chat-club-action` poke over Ames to fake `~zod`, claiming author `~nec`. The remote poke was acknowledged and `~zod` stored the club message. The isolated Gateway emitted one approval prompt to verified `~ten` DM and no agent turn before approval. After that DM approved the club, the real model read a proof file and replied `papaya` into `~zod`'s club. A second remotely delivered message claiming owner `~ten` received an automatic club reply without another approval prompt; saved `clubRules` contains the allow rule and no pending approval.
- Remaining Tlon transport gap: stock club gossip failed to reach the peer in both hand-assembled current desks and Tlon's published prebuilt fake-ship fixture, despite successful direct-message exchange and successful native remote club pokes. The sender ship did not receive the bot's club reply, although it was present in the bot ship's club. This proof establishes the OpenClaw boundary on authenticated remote ingress but does not establish stock Tlon club propagation or a returned peer-visible reply; confirm that round trip on working Tlon ships before merge.

prs.body:
Closes #202356

## What Problem This Solves

The inline-output browser test can check its live subscription before the first-use renderer finishes loading. A controlled slow module load makes the unchanged test fail at that subscription assertion; waiting for module readiness fixes that reproduced race. The original CI run's exact timing remains unconfirmed.

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible change. This test-only change separates module readiness from subscription readiness without removing assertions or changing production code, retries, or timeout settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wait for Vitest-tracked dynamic imports after enabling inline commands, then retain the existing live-output subscription, admission, quiet-command recovery, DOM identity, composer, and rendering-work assertions. Production admits live output only after the inline presentation and tool body are loaded; import settlement alone cannot satisfy the subsequent subscription or recovery assertions.

Simplification: the supplied patch is unchanged (+2 test lines, zero production lines); no helpers or new state are needed. This intentionally removes cold-import latency from the subscription poll's budget, not from the overall test deadline.

## Evidence

The coordinating session independently reproduced the loading race in Chromium on the same base: adding a temporary 1,500 ms top-level delay to the real inline presentation module made the original test fail with `includeLiveToolOutput` undefined rather than true. The same delayed load passed with this patch. After removing the diagnostic, the exact final browser test passed. No diagnostic or production changes are included.

The readiness and quiet-output recovery owner suites also pass: 8 tests across 2 files. They cover held renderer readiness, load failures, retired requests, retry, and quiet/newer-output/terminal recovery. All subscription and rendering assertions in the changed test remain intact.

The initial local autoreview attempt failed before execution because its runtime rejected an unsupported provider-compatibility configuration key. A [completed ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202342#issuecomment-7034251446) on head `78e604e25ed2ca374b6b224f537261b1d8ad39b9` subsequently found no actionable findings; that review inspected source and did not run target code. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44699791931/job/136165821906) executed the changed browser case in Chromium and passed 1/1 in 3.53 seconds. The original CI failure's exact run/shard and timing were not supplied; the controlled reproduction proves the race mechanism, not that every reported CI failure has this cause.

- Tested base: `749e2aed737bf33a9ed6a42ddd45a5d39b39a34d`. Final target blob: `60859b341ac347ce120c067587c133ed386d576f`, identical to the supplied patch.

See the original-discussion/browser-verification session below.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-inline-command-readiness.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-live-output-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8/8 passed, 3.03 s Vitest duration, 3.95 s wrapper wall time; existing Solid untracked-read warnings remain.

prs.title: feat: let agents participate selectively in group conversations
prs.body:
## Problem and motivation

When mention gating is disabled in a group, the primary reply model receives admitted messages and decides whether to participate as part of an agent turn. Many of those messages are exchanges between other people, questions that have already been answered, or chatter where another reply would add little value. Starting the primary agent for every such message creates unnecessary work and conversation noise.

Requiring an explicit mention avoids some of that work but misses indirect invitations and useful opportunities to contribute. A configured Decision Model should make the participation choice using the existing group etiquette, while the primary model keeps generating replies in its usual voice.

## Solution

With the existing default-off Decision assistance setting enabled and a Decision Model configured, assess eligible unmentioned text messages in always-on groups and channels before primary generation.

The assessment receives the current message, reply reference, bounded recent model history, and bounded workspace identity text. Recent history uses the same reader as normal generation, preserving native message-tool calls and their actual delivery results. Identity context uses the existing workspace loader and context formatter, preserving heading/prose `IDENTITY.md` files and configured identity precedence.

History preparation runs inside the existing admitted Decision execution, after the selected model’s effective route limits are known. It reserves space for the current message, identity and question, then uses the existing history selector to keep a bounded suffix with complete tool-call/result pairs. In addition to the shared token-pressure estimate, aggregate state/question and request limits set a conservative UTF-8 byte envelope, checked against the complete serialized batch. Provider-specific encoded-input constraints keep their existing handling. It adds no second catalog preparation or provider hook call. If the required input cannot fit, or all prior context would be omitted, the existing ordinary-reply fallback applies. Diagnostics measure the prepared batch rather than its initial placeholder.

- **Reply:** continue through the ordinary agent generation and delivery path. The turn carries approval as the existing result-required completion policy, and turn context tells the primary model to generate its reply in its usual voice.
- **Silent:** record the incoming message through the existing transcript owner and finish the turn without primary generation.
- **Assessment unavailable:** use the ordinary reply path.

The existing admission, transcript, queue, cancellation, permissions, and delivery owners remain responsible for their normal work. A declined queued source is consumed after persistence, so the recorded input is not retried as an abandoned request. The completion owner uses confirmed current-source delivery evidence. `NO_REPLY` after message-tool delivery prevents duplicate output. An undelivered `NO_REPLY` remains an unfulfilled reply and follows existing bounded generation recovery and failure handling. Source-delivery retries retain that requirement; they do not make another participation choice. Exhausted or refused retries record failure through the existing runner, and system notices retain their existing permission.

## Scope and rollout

This uses the existing Decision assistance Labs flag and configured `decisionModel`; there is no separate participation setting. An already-saved enabled preference also enables this capability after upgrade.

Explicit mentions, commands, media inputs, ambient room events, internal events, and generic CLI backends keep their existing paths. When Decision assistance is disabled or unavailable, the primary model retains its ordinary participation behavior.

Assessments use the selected Decision provider and may incur its normal charges. The provider receives the identity and conversation evidence described above. Each assessment is bounded by the turn timeout and a maximum of 30 seconds.

## Validation

The existing approved-text case reproduced approval followed by primary `NO_REPLY` completing without an answer before the fix, then passed with normal generation recovery and delivery. The existing message-tool case still completes without a duplicate reply. A second revised existing case reproduced queued delivery retry being disabled by the stronger completion policy.

Focused validation covered 168 existing cases across five files. After the final source-receipt consolidation, all 73 affected immediate/queued consumer cases passed in 77.02 seconds. The unchanged terminal-resolution and stranded-recovery suites also passed. No test cases or fixture frameworks were added.

The final messaging type-check graph, formatting, syntax guards, whitespace checks, and source/test line ratchets pass. Independent source review is clean. It also traced private transcript receipts, exhausted retry settlement, and refused retry enqueue through the existing owners. The 180-line allocation covers the excess above the 400-line allowance: 580 net test lines retain participation, persistence, source settlement, delivery and prepared-input coverage. The budget repair extends existing cases without adding test cases or a fixture framework.

The history-input repair passes all 11 existing participation/queue cases, the messaging type-check graph, formatting, syntax guards, whitespace checks, and the runtime import-cycle check. An isolated synthetic SQLite transcript reproduces the prior omission and confirms that the shared model-history reader retains the reply text and matching settled source-delivery receipt in order. Independent review is clean; no tests were added for this repair.

A fresh live assessment reached TypeSafe and received HTTP 400 with token-limit wording; the earlier rejection traces remain unattributed. The budget repair passes 102 existing cases across seven focused files (109.38 seconds). After the final interruption correction, all 89 affected Decision host/native cases passed again (46.40 seconds). Messaging and agents-root type checks, formatting, syntax guards, runtime import-cycle and line ratchets pass. Independent source review is clean.

Live validation of that first budget repair still returned unsupported input. A controlled replay through the existing native Gateway Decision tool then compared reconstructed local history with all fields preserved: the approximate selection (85,580 submitted JSON bytes) was rejected; the byte-bounded selection (26,067 bytes, seven messages with complete paired turns) succeeded with 13,990 provider input tokens. A local protocol comparison confirmed HTTP 400 with token-limit wording for the former and HTTP 200 for the latter. These were reconstructed inputs, not captured copies of the original requests; no channel messages were sent.

The follow-up repair changes one production file (+12/-2) and adds no tests. All 13 existing participation/queue/history cases pass, along with the messaging type graph, formatting, focused guards, whitespace and source-line checks. Independent source review is clean. The byte envelope is conservative, not an exact tokenizer guarantee. Exact-commit package installation and live greeting, contextual follow-up and silent-branch validation remain pending.

This follows up #202334, which scoped only browser profiles on the client.

## User Impact

Conversations retain their model, member, process and session details through presentation-only writes. Config editors still receive every saved revision. Model, provider, authentication and agent-model changes still invalidate; unknown dependencies remain conservative. There is no config option, schema, cache, storage or prompt-refresh contract change.

## Why This Change Was Made

One exhaustive, typed reader projection replaces the separate server and UI exclusions. It covers the catalog/auth/runtime and session-row readers and recorded environment-reference facts. Commands and skill eligibility already republish after every accepted config commit, including arbitrary skill config requirements; that existing publication refreshes commands without declaring a changed catalog. Existing channel activation and configured-model-reference readers supply session dependency facts. Unknown roots and opaque plugin settings retain invalidation.

Source qualification matters: the old model key already excluded `ui`, and session scope already excluded `ui.prefs`. The UI predicate did not. The metadata owner regression independently reproduces needless rebuilds for `logging.level` and `browser.headless`. No claim is made that a preferences write alone explains every observed catalog event.

Other `chat.metadata.changed` sources include prepared catalog publication/failure, catalog observations, authentication-store mutations, skill refresh, model-selection policy changes, personal-account connect changes, user email linking/merge, and usage publications. Usage-only events explicitly say the catalog is unchanged. A no-reload burst needs its event payload or trace to identify its producer. PR #197288 separately owns config-commit model-policy comparison costs; this change does not touch its files.

Ephemeral browser profiles still use config persistence. Moving per-task profiles into browser runtime state is a separate config/state contract decision, outside this fix.

## Evidence

**Acceptance is blocked on a newly identified subscription gap.** The real Control UI registers `sessions.subscribe`, and `sessions.changed` with `profile-identity` refreshes chat member evidence. The native harness currently simulates config/metadata subscribers but never registers the broad session subscription. Its raw scope stream contains `profiles` on config writes. Therefore those simulated counts do not yet establish zero total unrelated client refetches. A real subscribed-client reproduction is being prepared; the next timing arm is held and no result is accepted. This does not establish the producer of the reported production burst.

The browser regression fails on base with extra agent/identity reads and passes with the change. Metadata-owner regressions fail on base for browser launch settings and logging; UI preferences already retain metadata on base, matching source inspection. Model/auth/runtime and unknown-dependency controls still invalidate. Existing commands publication preserves command eligibility without declaring a changed catalog.

Head **9fe577f35e5afca1416523eca193324f7ac55d99** preserves the metadata/config controls and scopes the client predicate from the same dependency owner. The root membership table is typed and exhaustive; lookup reads only the path root. The redundant UI wrapper is deleted and the new owner is included in the native PR-wrapper inventory.

The final local bundle comparison passes against the latest failed CI context (**merge b87a33e0, exact main parent ce74e423, Node 24.22.1**):

| Surface | Base gzip bytes | Candidate | Requests | Existing gate |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Chat boot | 1,333,658 | 1,333,877 (+219) | 21 → 21 | 1,333,899-byte cap |
| New Session boot | 821,314 | 820,613 (−701) | 17 → 17 | 822,243-byte cap |
| Startup | 90,969 | 90,869 (−100) | 3 → 3 | Unchanged |

The repair regenerates the native boot manifest and deletes waste in the already-touched identity owner: a placeholder promise, unused result wrapper, duplicate listener implementation, and repeated checks of facts retired by its synchronous generation owner. No await, refresh reordering, budget change, or runtime cache was added. Exact-merge regeneration produces the same manifest. Earlier +51-byte proof belonged to a prior parent; the bcc6 CI failure was +503 bytes and was treated as PR-caused. Failed size experiments remain excluded from acceptance.

Final focused proof: 26 config controls, 39 metadata-owner tests, 53 identity unit/isolated cases, five affected browser cases, and six reconnect/service-worker E2Es pass, including same-version reconnect followed by owned-terminal restoration. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. The final `pnpm check:changed --base bcc6c7991839312fbea01138c72fcdd7d79b11f4` passed. Exact-head CI run 44858415585 passes the performance budget and every other selected job except UI E2E shard 6: Logs scrolling reaches the bottom but Auto-follow remains off. The unchanged focused WebKit case passes **10/10 on PR head and 10/10 on exact CI main parent f546520e**, in alternating fresh runner processes. The Logs owners and test are byte-identical between tested merge b3640312 and that parent; the parent includes #202349’s delayed-input repair, whose original CI attribution also remained unproved. A separate initial run passed all three Logs cases on each revision, and an additional exact tested-merge replay at b3640312 passed all three cases. These passing replays do not prove a fix or meet the strict failure-on-parent rule. The Team perf-loop lead agent has been asked to decide classification; no waiver or CI retry is claimed. The preceding bcc6 run passed every job except the bundle check and its aggregate gate.

The first exact CI parent a90c174919aca859d2145b2e6bede683ec87177a also reproduces Plugins' 57>56 asset failure. Independent causal proof attributes it to **#202726 / 528df02f222738badc13cf2a9c51b7533bbdeee4**; **#202795** landed its import-boundary repair and restores the unchanged cap. This is a newly observed main regression, not noise. The earlier unused Skills exports from #202581 are fixed here by removing only the two export keywords, with exact-parent reproduction and passing browser/E2E proof; main has since independently made them private.

Exact earlier CI main parent **1a0ca7b3e953ea148115106e058568b89f3dd1bd** reproduces all five Plugins navigation failures and Plugins 57>56. Navigation attribution: Skills action rename **#202531 /856aca23**, installed-provider filtering **#202527 /c2c2effa**; **#202784 /26eb694b** landed the repair. These newly observed main regressions are recorded rather than ignored. The earlier CI-only Skills 30>28 failure passed both the exact-parent and matching-candidate local replay and the next CI run. Its cause remains unassigned; passing replays are not claimed as a fix. The ae77436f baseline-ratchet job separately lost runner communication; GitHub supplies that infrastructure annotation and no assertion log. No test-inheritance claim or waiver is made for it.

Production delta: **+56 TypeScript LOC**, plus **+19 generated boot-manifest lines** (+75 including generated build input). The growth records an exhaustive root-to-reader classification and conservative unknown dependencies; new schema roots require an explicit reader decision. The identity cleanup reduces runtime code. There is no new cache, config option, schema, or storage contract.

### Acceptance rule recorded before measurement

Use the committed `scripts/perf/config-reload-scope-herd.ts` with 14 real WebSocket clients on an isolated Gateway and a synthetic production-shaped btrfs fixture (about 35–40 GiB agent SQLite storage, thousands of sessions, 62,000 workspace files/about 1.1 GB). No production data or access. Base `1a60c2dc6c566bde74d26e5f561571f0593c8ece`; the baseline overlay includes both original server owners and the original UI predicate.

Warm every worker/burst class in each process. Run A/A controls and at least eight interleaved base/candidate pairs, admitting each arm below 8 one-minute host and Linux load and recording load. Measure UI-preference and logging writes, retained browser-profile controls, and positive model changes. Count automatic refetches separately from explicit `models.list` probes; measure owner/burst wall time, main and process CPU, probe median/p95, and separate sampled allocation/per-thread CPU diagnostics.

Acceptance: presentation writes produce zero unrelated automatic refetches, zero model-owner invalidations and retained session projections; config revisions still reach all 14 clients. Model changes still invalidate. Latency tails must stay within A/A spread or at most 10% adverse; any 20% adverse cell stops landing pending explanation/fix or explicit owner acceptance. Report every adverse metric. Previous rare-path acceptance belonged to the Team perf-loop lead agent and applies to #202334's measurements, not automatically to this new comparison.

Warmed comparison table: **pending**. The final Boat fixture is qualified at **36,927,832,064 bytes (34.39 GiB)**, schema 43, **10,800 sessions**, **208,765 transcript events**, and **62,002 workspace files /1,116,000,123 bytes** on btrfs. All 17 changed source hashes match **9fe577f35e5afca1416523eca193324f7ac55d99**. Both arms share this fixture and a native x86-64 Node 26.12.1 runtime, four container CPUs and 16 GiB RAM, pnpm 12.15.0, and the committed frozen lockfile. The host has eight CPUs and 15.62 GiB physical RAM; the container limits are reported separately from available hardware. There is no production data or access.

The committed generator used `--sessions 10800 --agents 1 --runs 0 --approvals 200 --cron 100 --projects 12 --transcript-mib 12000 --worktree-files 62000 --worktree-file-bytes 18000 --seed 2696`. Generation took 1,781.77 s, excluded from measurement. Qualification completed before admission with load 0.70; the admission controller records the actual load of every arm. All accepted A/A, interleaved pairs and separate allocation/profile diagnostics will come from this one host. No TTL, load, warmup, shape or sample requirement is relaxed.

A completed baseline arm on the preceding host is retained only as preflight evidence: 42 unrelated UI-preference refetches and 56 logging refetches, including 14 catalog reads; browser profile create/remove already have zero on this baseline. Its 488.706 s process cadence includes excluded native covered-transcript maintenance over all 10,800 sessions. That left insufficient lease time for the complete 22-process matrix. The old lease is released; the final lease uses corrected native setup and source-only transfer, with a fixed four-hour lifetime. No candidate was measured on the preflight host and no cross-host timing is pooled.

The raw session-change scope also includes the existing `profiles` notification, which retires identity presentation. The candidate must emit `config-presentation` without a broad `config`/topology invalidation; retained topology does not mean zero identity notifications. Prepared-runtime invalidation counts are distinct from metadata publications, whose automatic catalog reads and owner regression tests are also checked.

The original local A/A attempt remains excluded because native full-database integrity verification and transcript backfill overlapped counted bursts. The committed harness joins the existing startup-admission owner and backfill completion before warming all worker/burst classes again. The new campaign restarts from A/A under the unchanged load and acceptance rules.

Round 2 direction and acceptance belong to the **Team perf-loop lead agent**, not Peter. Earlier rare-path acceptance belongs only to #202334. Performance acceptance, exact-head CI and final-head ClawSweeper with zero open items remain required before landing.

## What Problem This Solves

Shared chat decoding, session-cache and executor contracts were tested only through the iOS app target. Their suite constructed an iOS transport that none of its assertions exercised, tying shared behavior to an unrelated app dependency.

## User Impact

No production or user-visible behavior changes. Shared contracts have one canonical test source, with all existing iOS assertions retained. No dependency, public API, stored-data, permission or credential changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the suite beside its shared owners and reuse the existing stateless transport fixture. Compile that same source in the existing iOS test target and preserve its CI selection. Five platform-independent tests also run through SwiftPM; the eleven nested-activity tests retain the iOS-only scope of the production model.

The small test-infrastructure increase supports both targets without duplicating the suite or changing assertions.

## Evidence

At corrected candidate `d59789d3be863de956e80f4fa8e462380596372b`:

- [App-hosted iOS proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44865047167/job/136727242340) passed all **16 chat test functions / 81 expanded cases**, with zero failures or skips. The xcresult's case identities exactly match the baseline. The full lifecycle artifact records 391 passing tests, zero failures/skips.
- All five portable macOS tests passed locally. The same-head macOS Swift package and test jobs also passed in that run.
- The 79 lifecycle-selection tests, tooling typecheck and targeted JavaScript lint passed before the four Swift platform directives were added; their exercised inputs are unchanged. The unchanged ingestion fixture passed its 16 tests.
- Swift formatting, parsing and whitespace checks passed. Strict SwiftLint still reports eight inherited suite/style findings; no rule was disabled.

The original migration incorrectly ran iOS-only nested assertions on macOS, failing 57 expanded cases. The correction scopes those tests to the existing production platform, preserving every assertion. A standalone iOS package attempt stopped before tests in unchanged credential tests using macOS-only `Process`; the app-hosted proof above supplies the required iOS execution.

The overall manual CI run is red on unrelated failures: two unused UI exports already fixed by [PR 202879](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202879), and Android UTP dependency resolution before tests. prs.title: fix(gateway): enforce the session permission mode on every Gateway tool call
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A chat set to a permission mode (Read only, Ask me, Auto-review) bounds file tools to its `sessionRoot` on the built-in runtime. On a Claude CLI chat it did not: the CLI calls OpenClaw's own tools through the Gateway (`mcp__openclaw__read` and friends), and the Gateway applied the session's mode only to restricted senders. An owner's Claude CLI chat in `workspace` mode read files anywhere on the host.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway runs these tools, so it owns the boundary. `resolveGatewayScopedTools` now applies the session's permission policy for every caller instead of only `inheritedToolPolicySource === "sender"` (that scope came from #165418, which kept "ordinary owner/profile authority unchanged"; nothing else relies on owners being unbounded). The prepared session workspace now also applies when the session has a mode, so relative paths resolve inside the same root the policy bounds.

Rule, now in `docs/gateway/permission-modes.md`: whoever runs a tool enforces the mode for it. The Gateway does for OpenClaw's tools on every runtime; Codex does for its own tools through its sandbox; host-only harnesses with their own tools (Muse, ACP) keep needing Full access. This replaces the paragraph from #202659 that said CLI chats use the CLI's own controls. A new sentence states that modes bound file tools and pick the exec reviewer; exec is not confined to `sessionRoot` unless the runtime sandboxes commands.

Effects:
- Sessions with no mode (the policy is undefined) are unchanged: cron, Skill Workshop, completion handoffs, subagents without a mode.
- Owner `POST /tools/invoke` on a mode-set session is bounded the same way (same resolver, already passed the policy).
- Subagent attachment roots stay readable: the Gateway builds tools through the same assembly that adds `subagentAttachmentRootForRun`.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts`: an owner's loopback `read` on a `read-only` session refuses a path outside the root and lists no `write`; with no mode it reads. Red on the merge base (`expected '{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"ou…' to contain 'escapes'`), green here.
- Real product, tier source (`ocx src`), isolated Gateway, a Claude CLI agent and a built-in ChatGPT agent, chat set to `permissionMode: "workspace"`, caller with full operator scopes, asked to read a file outside the workspace:

| | Merge base | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Claude CLI | read it: `OUTSIDE-SECRET 91c2` | refused: `Path escapes sandbox root (…/workspace): …/outside.txt` |
| Built-in | refused, same error | refused, same error |

Exec on that Claude CLI chat is unchanged by this PR (both: `exec denied: Headless runs cannot wait for interactive exec approval … security=allowlist ask=on-miss`), while the built-in chat's exec goes through the auto-reviewer; that difference predates this change and is tracked separately.

prs.title: fix(ui): move automation notices out of the Inbox
prs.body:
Closes #202913

## What Problem This Solves

Failed and overdue automations add to the Inbox count. Their run details live on the Automations page.

## User Impact

Automation notices leave the Inbox. The Automations clock shows a single red dot while any automation in the current agent view is failed. The settings guide points readers to Automations for the run details.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vyctor asked for the failure indicator on the clock. The rail shares the Automations sidebar’s failure styling and uses the same definition of a current failure. During startup, a model auth status read receives a retryable error. The Inbox keeps saved dismissals when the Gateway reports auth status as temporarily unavailable.

## Evidence

A real Gateway ran a failing backup in each fresh browser profile. The regression failed on main and passed on the branch. With two failed jobs, the dot stayed through the first successful rerun and cleared after the last. Clicking the clock opened Automations.

### Main vs PR head

### Existing-profile upgrades to the PR head

I tested upgrades to `002ecce1981` from three published releases: `v2026.9.37` extended-stable, `v2026.10.10`, and `v2026.11.6`.

In each release, I dismissed the Anthropic and OpenAI account warnings, saved Light mode and the blue accent, and ran Daily backup to produce a real failure. I kept the browser tab open while restarting the same Gateway with the PR build, then reloaded the same browser profile.

In all three upgrades, both settings survived and both account warnings stayed dismissed. The Gateway still reported the warnings. The same failed backup remained in Automations, the clock showed a red dot, and Inbox was empty.

prs.title: fix: keep session writes responsive during worker bundle cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing or pruning a worker bundle can recursively delete an extracted installation or staging tree through the Gateway's shared libuv filesystem pool. Slow unlinks can then hold up unrelated session reads and writes. Moving bundle construction into a worker thread does not isolate that pool.

Related: #202874.

## User Impact

Worker-bundle cleanup no longer contributes bulk unlink/rmdir work to the Gateway filesystem pool. Preparation still waits for cleanup to settle, and pruning keeps its existing retention and file protections. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the three whole-tree cleanup sites through the existing `nativeWorktreeFilesystem.remove` child-process owner and its content-operation budget. Keep ordinary tarball and temporary-file deletion nonrecursive. This completes the separately requested bundle follow-up without another cleanup service, cache, or setting.

The child startup/CPU/allocation tradeoff accepted in #202874 also applies here. That PR's production-shaped synthetic proof measured bulk-removal pool occupancy 4/4 → 0/4 and injected-slow-unlink patch/fs-write maxima 1,442/1,388 ms → 13.9/4.7 ms. Those are the existing owner's measurements, not a new bundle benchmark; compiled-release startup cost was not measured.

## Evidence

The existing archive-staging and retention/pruning tests now forbid recursive staging removal through the shared pool while retaining their real filesystem assertions. On exact parent `182493a8ef52cfce34ca8abd3de05909492b8dfb`, three cases fail at that boundary and file-only pruning passes. With the fix, all 24 bundle and real worker-thread consumer cases pass. Live public-npm verification was not exercised.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/bundle.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/node-bootstrap-artifact-worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed; 46.92 s including cold worker compilation, approximately 9.5 s executing tests. CI timing pending.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 182493a8ef52cfce34ca8abd3de05909492b8dfb`: passed, including production and affected-test typechecks, lint/format, and all three unused-export scans.
- Independent Codex autoreview: no P0–P2 findings; reviewer did not execute tests.
- Simplification: one existing owner replaces three recursive call sites. Production delta +8/−3, net +5 lines, for the owner import and staging/file branch; test delta +14, extending existing cases. No UI-imported module changed.

prs.title: feat(update): run every Git install from releases and delete the in-place Git runner
prs.body:
Slice 4b of the update foundation. Follows #199706 (slice 4), #201917 (releases outside `node_modules`) and #201538 (half-switched Git updates).

## Problem

Since #199706, POSIX Git checkouts with a Gateway service update through releases: a detached worktree at `<state>/git-install/releases/<id>/openclaw`, behind the link `<state>/git-install/openclaw`, started by a launcher that switches back after two failed starts. Three cases still used the in-place Git runner, which rewrites the checkout the Gateway runs from:

- Windows checkouts;
- package-to-Git switches;
- checkouts with no Gateway service.

That runner is RC1 of the update RCA: in-place replacement at a path running processes use. Keeping it meant keeping its rollback, retention, pack transfer, staging and handoff code.

## Change

Every Git install now updates through releases. The in-place Git runner and its command-side rollback are deleted on every platform in one cutover. `openclaw update` no longer moves the checkout `HEAD` or rebuilds its `dist`. (`scripts/update-gateway.sh`, a separate maintainer script, still rebuilds a checkout in place; it is unchanged.)

- **Windows:**
  - The release link is an NTFS junction, which needs no administrator rights. It is owned by the existing `package-release-slot*` code; the win32 exclusions there and in the release lease are removed.
  - Windows cannot rename onto a junction, so a switch removes the old junction and then renames.
  - The Windows task supervisor starts its Gateway child through the release launcher, so the child's starts count toward the trial.
- **Package-to-Git:**
  - The checkout is cloned and the target is built as the first release.
  - The global npm package's `openclaw.mjs` is rewritten once to import the release launcher, so the existing npm bin shims run the release. Without that, `openclaw` on PATH would keep running the old npm build, whose updater treats the install as npm.
  - The rejected alternative, re-pointing the npm package path at the release, would name the release through `node_modules/openclaw` again, the cause of #201874.
  - Installs whose switch was done by an older updater have the npm package path linked to the checkout, which releases never rebuild. A Git release update replaces that link (only a link to the checkout) with a directory holding `openclaw.mjs` and `dist/index.js`, both starting the launcher; the second keeps a service definition that names the package path working after a `--no-restart` update. Without this, the CLI and its updater stayed on the version the switch built (found by the package-to-Git upgrade lane).
- **No service:** a checkout run by hand updates through a release too. The next `openclaw gateway` runs it.
- **CLI on PATH:** after a Git release update, the installer's `openclaw` wrapper (POSIX and Windows) is rewritten once to run the release launcher. The launcher selects a `--no-restart` release on the next Gateway run and counts `openclaw gateway` / `openclaw gateway run` as trial starts; other commands (`gateway status`, `--version`) never count.
- **Service definition:** `serviceUsesUpdatedRoot` reads the service definition, not the running process. A `--no-restart` Git release update whose service still starts the checkout writes a definition that starts the launcher without starting or restarting the Gateway (`stage`; systemd reloads unit metadata only). Every OpenClaw restart route on macOS (`openclaw gateway restart` and the Gateway's own restart) re-bootstraps the job when the loaded command differs from the plist on disk; otherwise it still kickstarts. Only a failed write leaves an owed `service-definition` step.
- **Restart:** the converted service restarts once, not twice.
- **No manual steps (Ayaan, 2026-11-20):**
  - Releases built under `lib/node_modules` by `7db69bedeab6`-era updaters (#201874): bundled plugin public surfaces there load the built `dist/extensions/<plugin>/` JavaScript, so those installs update by themselves; the manual bridge in the #201874 comment is no longer needed.
  - A killed npm link swap leaves the link under npm's backup name; the next Git update restores it and retries.
  - The launcher finishes a Windows link switch killed between removing the old junction and renaming the new one.
  - npm -> Git -> npm: destination ownership recognizes this install's exact forwarding `openclaw.mjs`, so switching back is admitted.

## Impact

- One update path for Git installs on macOS, Linux and Windows.
- `openclaw` on PATH runs the current release after an update.
- **Accepted edge cases:**
  - Two checkouts that share one state directory share its single release install.
  - After a package-to-Git switch, the old npm package keeps its disk space until a switch back to npm replaces it.
  - A Gateway run for another profile through the default `openclaw` on PATH counts toward the default install's trial (accepted by Ayaan, 2026-11-20).
  - `--no-restart` selects the new release at the next start without the two-start switch-back.
  - A checkout installed at `<state>/git-install/openclaw` (the release link path; the installer default is `~/openclaw`) is left in place, and every update fails visibly with nothing changed, naming the fix: move the checkout or reinstall with another `--git-dir` (accepted by Ayaan, 2026-11-21).
  - Unchanged follow-up: when local commits conflict with every newer commit, the preflight reports `already-current` instead of naming the conflict. This predates the PR and gets its own PR.

## Size

Against the merge base, 24 commits:

- Production code: +816 / −2,150 (55 files).
- Tests: +1,362 / −8,875 (68 files). Cut tests covered steps a Git release no longer takes (checkout rollback, in-place staging, service stop before checkout); each is listed in the contract.
- Upgrade-survivor scenario: +831 / −104 (4 files): baselines `v2026.11.5`, `7db69bedeab6`, `main`; package-to-Git; no service; SIGKILL at stage, build, publish, link switch and launcher restore.
- Docs: +132 / −95.

## Evidence

Final head `20b6fec70e63` (the last two commits change only Windows supervisor starts, unit-proven, and the knip entry list). Each row names the head its end-to-end proof ran on.

| Invariant | Result | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| Release built where it serves; no `node_modules` in the link or realpath | Pass | Linux upgrade-survivor lanes; macOS launchd (isolated profile on a maintainer Mac); hosted Crabbox Windows Server 2025 |
| Gateway serves the new release and `tools.invoke web_search` works after every update | Pass | every hop on all three OSes |
| SIGKILL at stage, build, publish, link switch, launcher restore leaves a serving install | Pass | Linux kill-point lane (`8f63330`) |
| Two failed starts switch back and restore `.pre-` state | Pass | Linux lanes; macOS `8f63330` (`failed to start twice; switched back`); Windows `9cbc4b5`, automatic through the Scheduled Task, 67.5 s outage. Older-supervisor and pending cases: unit tests red on base (`6003675`, `75e7bd5`) |
| The release updates itself | Pass | Linux; macOS `8f63330`; Windows `9cbc4b5` |
| The checkout is never written (HEAD, status) | Pass | every lane and OS run |
| Every shipped layout reaches releases with no manual step | Pass | `v2026.11.5`, merge-base `main` (`8f63330`); `7db69bedeab6` (`6003675`) |
| npm → Git switch; `openclaw` on PATH runs the release | Pass | Linux `75e7bd5` |
| No service: the next `openclaw gateway` runs the release | Pass | Linux `8f63330` |
| `--no-restart` keeps the Gateway up; the next restart runs the release | Pass | macOS `8f63330`: 0 s outage, `gateway restart` reloads launchd arguments |
| Windows junction; a release held open is retained, then collected | Pass | hosted Crabbox (Windows Server 2025) |
| Windows without admin rights | Not run | S4U Limited stays admin on the Crabbox image |
| Installer-made partial clones (`--filter=blob:none`) | Not run | all lanes clone fully |

Reviews: local ClawSweeper on every head (last finding accepted above); Fable 5.2 contract reviews. Unit: release, update-runner, launcher, wrapper, service, launchd, systemd, restart, task-supervisor, plugin loader suites; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` clean.
