prs.title: feat: invite someone to help in one session without giving them Gateway-wide write access
prs.body:
Related: #201526

## What Problem This Solves

A session owner can't let one teammate type in one session without giving them write access to the whole Gateway. That access also lets them start their own Full-access sessions, send through channels, control nodes, loosen the owner's permission mode and approve the owner's commands. The only alternative is `operator.sessions.write`, which covers only a member's own sessions, so an invited member can watch but not type.

## User Impact

User impact: an admin can give a role an invite ceiling. A session's creator or an admin can then invite a person with that role into **one** session at **Can read**, **Can suggest** or **Can send**, without giving them any Gateway-wide write access. Gateways and roles that don't set the new field behave exactly as before.

- **Opt-in config:** `gateway.roles.definitions.<role>.sessions: { others: "invited", maxInvitedAccess: "read" | "suggest" | "send", invitedTools?: [...] }`. The invited person's role only needs `operator.sessions.read`. Example: `collaborator: { sessions: { others: "invited", maxInvitedAccess: "send" }, scopes: ["operator.sessions.read"], agents: ["main"] }`.
- **Choosing a level:** the creator picks the level when @mentioning someone (default **Can read**), and can change it later in the sharing panel. A new `session.members.setAccess` method backs this; `session.members.add` accepts an optional `access`.
- **What a Can send member can do:** `chat.send`, `chat.abort` for their own runs only, `session.typing`, and a `sessions.patch` that can only make the permission mode stricter, all in that session only. They can't create sessions or use channels, nodes or config. They also can't approve commands or change sharing.
- **How their turns run:**
  - Never looser than **Ask me**, worked out from the session's real effective policy, including Agent default.
  - Only the tools in a core-tool allowlist. The default list is `read, write, edit, apply_patch, ls, exec, process, web_search, web_fetch, tool_search, tool_describe, dispatch_action`, and `sessions.invitedTools` changes it per role.
  - Always queued as their own turn, never merged into another person's turn, and slash commands are ignored.
  - Only the OpenClaw runtime running locally on the Gateway; CLI, ACP, native harnesses and worker placements are refused.
  - `process` only sees commands from that session, and file tools stay inside that session's own workspace.
- **Approvals:** the session's creator approves commands from these turns, even without admin. The approval card says whose turn asked. The participant sees only a "waiting for approval" status.
- **Lowering or removing access** immediately cancels that member's queued and running turns. Re-inviting them does not bring those turns back.
- **⚠️ Database migration:** the agent database moves to **schema 44** (a nullable `session_members.access` column), which older builds cannot open. To downgrade, restore a pre-upgrade backup, as with any schema bump. This happens on every Gateway, opted in or not.
- **⚠️ Budget exception:** the Control UI **Chat** JS gzip budget goes from **1,332,637 to 1,336,683 bytes** (+0.3%), after making the invite bar and notices load only when needed (37.6% smaller than the first version). The SDK declaration budget is unchanged; the declarations are now 10.5 KB *smaller* than on the base.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sessions.others` was the only per-person control, and it doesn't separate seeing a session from acting in it. A stored per-member level, capped by the role, adds "this person in this session" without a new Gateway-wide scope. Admission to the fixed method list is checked against the exact existing session after membership is known, so nothing else is widened. Because a guest's turn uses the owner's agent, the limits on what that turn can do are attached to the input itself and travel with it through queuing, recovery, retries and model fallback. Changing the session's mode alone would not have been enough.

Design walkthrough and the decisions behind it: Josh's Participate design session. Builds on the role model in #201610 (OpenClaw ID members use the profile role). #201615's goals for invited members are covered here.

## Evidence

Real Gateway, real authenticated browser members (non-admin creator *Morgan*, collaborator *Alice*, viewer, admin) and a live model, in Crabbox containers on a Mac Studio. **Before:** `da816e2` (merge base). **After:** `9f459e5`. 1440×1000, dark theme, the same named test data. The images are wide, so each pair is stacked: before, then after.

### Clean comparison: invited member in the creator's session

**Before**: locked composer
![Before: invited collaborator sees "You need permission to send messages in this session" and a locked composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f8f6fa9-2716-4da5-80c7-4ecb9cebd594)

**After**: Can send; composer unlocked, turns limited to Ask me
![After: collaborator's composer is unlocked and the permission chip reads "Ask me · set by Morgan Creator"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/045aaa55-1d7d-4fb2-8487-8ff27831d8ca)

### Clean comparison: creator @mentions an invite-only person

**Before**: no way to choose access
![Before: creator's composer with an @mention of Alice Collaborator and no access choice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28d533f9-b010-4e84-852a-a3dd30a729bf)

**After**: invite level bar, default Can read
![After: a bar above the composer reads "Invite Alice Collaborator to this session as" with a "Can read" picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aab616dc-a059-4ee1-9699-e6e4630fc7f2)

### Annotated comparison

![Before, annotated: the "need permission" notice is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60636bf2-b73c-4990-984e-07488383c65e)
![After, annotated: the "Ask me · set by Morgan Creator" chip is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76367767-fbdf-4935-8be6-c3fbf372cf5d)
![Before, annotated: the composer with no access choice is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e02d306-0cb4-4521-b4a9-ce77aba3017c)
![After, annotated: the invite level bar is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35df6535-4143-4b13-b467-dc18303a9511)

### After only: approvals and notices

![Creator's approval card: "Requested during Alice Collaborator's turn" with Deny / Always allow / Allow once](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a2875d0-0fb5-49a0-9e06-14c9b0046845)
![Participant view: waiting-for-approval status and no approval buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/130a7de0-7fc6-495b-97a7-1b2513e6cbfd)
![Transcript notices: "Morgan Creator invited Alice Collaborator with read access" and "changed Alice Collaborator's access to send"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32d38655-d1a6-4098-bee1-dd5b1d6bec58)

### Behavior checked on the real Gateway (all passed)

1. **No opt-in:** without `maxInvitedAccess`, the invited member's composer stays locked and `chat.send` is refused, as on main.
2. **Can read:** a real @mention invite creates the membership; the participant and the viewer are both refused when sending.
3. **Can suggest:** Alice's suggestion reaches Morgan, who accepts it, and the live model answers it.
4. **Can send:**
   - In a Full-access session Alice's turn shows **Ask me**, with only Read only and Ask me offered.
   - The model was given exactly the allowed tools (no `sessions_spawn`, `message` or `skills_read`).
   - An `exec` was approved by the **non-admin** creator, and the command really ran (`PARTICIPATE_EXEC_OK`).
   - Alice saw only "waiting", and her attempt to approve was refused.
5. **No escalation:**
   - Alice can't create sessions, switch to Full or pick ACP.
   - A tighten-only patch succeeds.
   - Alice's message sent during Morgan's running turn ran as its own turn and also needed approval.
6. **Revocation:** lowering Alice to Can read stopped her turn that was waiting on approval and cancelled her queued input, which never reached the model.
7. **`invitedTools`:** `["read","ls"]` gave the model exactly those two tools.
8. **Migration:** a real schema 43 database was migrated to 44 on first boot.

**Tests (updated at `d0f030c`):** removed the 582-line Participate mock-Gateway Playwright suite and consolidated redundant cases after a test-value audit. Cleanup is net **−581 test/support lines and 45 fewer registered cases**, including five cheap replacement unit rows for unique mention/composer behavior. Retained authorization, containment, revocation and migration boundaries; six guard-mutation experiments supported the audit. **574 selected cases passed** (including existing sibling cases, not 574 new tests), along with core/UI/test typechecks, generation guards, formatting and typed lint. Two independent Astra reviews of the cleanup/integration found no verified P0–P2 issues. The missing frozen-wrapper dependency inventory was reproduced and repaired.

**Current readiness (`d0f030c`):** rebased onto `bd67a3f9a184`; main advanced again and GitHub reports conflicts. The paired clean build measures Chat startup JS at **1,337,099 bytes**, **416 bytes above** the existing 1,336,683-byte cap. New and largest-JS budgets pass; CSS and request-count limits already fail on the paired base. The unchanged test-line allocation is still **2,179 lines short**; no further audited security-test deletion is justified. No additional budget or allocation increases were made.

**Gaps:**
- The screenshots and live-Gateway observations above are historical proof for `9f459e5`, not final-head live-Gateway proof for `d0f030c`.
- A previous combined participation-test timeout did not reproduce in the final combined run; no timing workaround was added.
- Revocation was shown on a turn waiting for approval, not on a shell command that is already running.
- Downgrading to an older binary is untested; it needs a backup restore, as described above.
- Hosted CI hasn't run yet.
- This PR isn't rebased onto #201610 yet. I'll do that once #201610 lands.

prs.title: feat(update): capture PostgreSQL stores while the Gateway serves
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

On updates that take a pre-migration image, OpenClaw starts capturing PostgreSQL stores while the Gateway serves. It reuses unchanged captures after taking exclusive ownership and captures changed stores again. For a custom service or foreground Gateway, `openclaw update --wait-for-gateway-stop <seconds>` prepares the update first, then asks the operator to stop the Gateway before activation. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/196154

SQLite stores still get their capture after the stop. The default managed-service flow owns its stop and restart. The installed updater must contain this change. The landing scope retains both the stop handoff and default PostgreSQL capture; this is not approval to merge before verification.

### What Problem This Solves

The previous updater required exclusive state ownership to capture PostgreSQL, even though each store can be copied from a repeatable-read snapshot while the Gateway serves. A Gateway with an external owner could therefore require the operator to stop it before staging and validation, extending downtime.

### Root Cause

The updater now records the generation and reuse digest from the same snapshot as each capture. Under exclusive ownership, it compares the current digest and captures any changed or unreadable store again. This usually includes shared state because the updater records its run there. Restore still checks the existing generation fingerprint. The reuse digest has a theoretical collision risk when two row sets have the same count and sum of 64-bit hashes.

The low-space skip runs before the final capture copies any data. An earlier online capture can already have a server schema and manifest, so the skip retires the schema through the existing capture owner before removing files. A failed drop preserves the manifest. Online server copies use the existing PostgreSQL prune marker, keyed to the online capture directory. A later online server capture can reap a marked copy after its directory is gone. Retained captures and restored live schemas stay in place. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201579

## Verification

### Evidence

- **Pushed head `edca9115`:** [all four PostgreSQL conformance shards, `pg16-smoke`, and the required CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44860715131). The published-driver job was skipped. Static checks passed. Earlier CI on `466ab69d` covered [low-space cleanup and manifest retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44853257676/job/136691538342) and [orphaned PostgreSQL schema cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44853257676/job/136691537808).
- **Pushed head regression:** the mixed-store test failed on `edca9115`. The online pass privately copied the shared SQLite file before deciding whether the PostgreSQL export fit. On a nearly full Gateway volume, a temporary copy is enough to exhaust space.
- **Signed, unpublished correction `2c2f8fd234e639593bddf3e890f2f5c85ad7d063`:** read-only discovery preserves existing PostgreSQL registrations without staging SQLite. The mixed-store regression passed. With an 85,880,832-byte SQLite file and 48,336,896 bytes free, the optional PostgreSQL export was deferred, free space fell by just 4,096 bytes, and SQLite accepted another write. The existing registered agent row survived. Focused PostgreSQL 17 compatibility, retention, and recovery checks passed.

### Real behavior proof

- **Package:** built `2c2f8fd2` with the repository's published-driver CI recipe. The tarball checker passed; the embedded commit matched the signed SHA. Tarball SHA-256: `5ea5bded0703937e3b2568d89d25697aad5f535b79966df8d5ac10df086b609a`.
- **Latest stable → signed candidate:** on a disposable Linux VM, the published `2026.11.6` build (`06afb10d`) used a real systemd user service and PostgreSQL 17.11 for shared state and agent history. Its installed `openclaw update --tag <candidate.tgz> --yes --json` restarted the service onto `2c2f8fd2`. The serving build was checked by authenticated RPC, not by version alone. A pre-existing shared row and durable chat message survived.
- **Signed updater → forced rollback:** the repository's failing-Doctor successor activated, then Doctor exited 1. Database and package rollback both exited 0. systemd served `2c2f8fd2` again; both PostgreSQL store IDs, the shared row, and both acknowledged messages survived in restored namespaces. A separate successful update by that same installed signed updater preserved all three acknowledged messages. On both candidate-driven runs, `/readyz` responded while the original service PID and an online capture directory were present; the stopped-state receipt explicitly recorded reuse of the agent's online capture.
- **Retention:** both retained capture directories had manifests matching the PostgreSQL state and agent store IDs. Rollback retained the replaced namespaces for manual recovery. On the successful hop, Doctor reported an unknown writer after the snapshot; the updater retained the recovery image rather than risking those later writes.
- **Earlier contributor evidence:** the [foreground macOS Git test](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/commit/7da4339c06f71c3ae52f30f67a16168c16cf7e91) reported survival of a write between capture and stop and about 287 seconds of downtime versus 941 seconds on its stopped-first baseline. Those timings were not remeasured on the signed correction.

### What was not tested or remains blocked

The separate full source build still fails `check-plugin-sdk-exports`: **5,396,987 bytes vs. a 5,385,536-byte limit** on the untouched base, the pushed head, and the corrected production code. The published-driver tarball passed a distinct CI recipe; it does not make the full build green. Independent whole-diff review stopped before producing a verdict. The correction is not pushed, so hosted CI and [ClawSweeper's P1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200294#issuecomment-6932530027) are still tied to `edca9115`, not the tested correction.

## What Problem This Solves

Hourly CI reports the PostgreSQL state-admission subprocess fixture as an unused file. Its test launches it by filename, so Knip cannot discover it through an import.

## User Impact

The dead-code check recognizes this live test fixture. There is no runtime behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register the exact subprocess path in the existing test-aware entry list. Keep the fixture and the hard-zero unused-file policy intact; add no ignore or wildcard.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the [main CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44866145770/job/136730628988) on base `52cc86028d703a4820b688e726097842d05d2155`: production unused-files passed; full-tree unused-files reported only this fixture and exited 1.
- With this two-line change, `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` passed both scans with zero entries, and `pnpm deadcode:report` passed all three scans.
- All 56 tests in the three existing dead-code suites passed on Boat with Node 24.22.1. Targeted Oxlint and Oxfmt passed.
- The combined remote command later exited 139 at `git diff --check`. An isolated invocation reproduced the VM's Git 2.43.0 crash; the local diff check passed. The scan, lint, formatting, and test commands had already completed successfully.
- Local ClawSweeper completed the exact range `52cc86028d703a4820b688e726097842d05d2155..b7449cd0a6134bf7f2ad0617c560f3d92bf97d1d` with no actionable correctness or security findings. Its read-only review did not rerun Knip; the execution evidence above is separate.

prs.title: fix(skills): accept quoted field names when validating skills
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The bundled Skill Creator rejects a valid `SKILL.md` with quoted field names such as `"name"` and `"description"` on Python installations without PyYAML. The same file fails both validation and packaging.

## User Impact

Skill authors can validate and package skills that use single- or double-quoted field names in a standard-library-only Python environment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The simple frontmatter parser kept the surrounding quotes as part of each key. It now recognizes matching quotes around simple field names before the existing allowlist is applied. Both commands already share this validator.

## Evidence

On Linux with Python 3.12.3 and a fresh virtual environment without PyYAML, both commands went from exit 1 to exit 0 for single- and double-quoted fields. The generated `.skill` ZIP passed integrity checks and its archived `SKILL.md` matched the input byte for byte. Unquoted fields also packaged successfully, an unknown field still failed, and the PyYAML 6.0.3 control packaged successfully.

<details>
<summary>Commands and checks</summary>

Base `58e735cba37`, candidate `c83d7b31225`. Ran with a synthetic skill directory.

```sh
python3 -m venv --without-pip /tmp/skill-proof-venv
/tmp/skill-proof-venv/bin/python skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py quoted-skill
/tmp/skill-proof-venv/bin/python skills/skill-creator/scripts/package_skill.py quoted-skill out
python3 -m zipfile -t out/quoted-skill.skill
```

Before, both commands reported `Unexpected key(s) in SKILL.md frontmatter: "description", "name"`. After, validation reported `Skill is valid!` and the packager created the archive.

- `python -m pytest -q -c skills/pyproject.toml skills/skill-creator` passed 13 tests and 56 subtests. The two new quoted-key subtests failed on the base.
- Targeted Ruff lint and `git diff --check` passed. Ruff format flagged the same existing test line on both base and candidate.
- Codex autoreview covered the full local patch against the base at P0 and found no actionable findings.
- The broader changed gate reached an unrelated Reef plug-in metadata check and could not resolve `@noble/hashes/sha2.js` from the local dependency tree.

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): upgrade state in place at start instead of refusing for copy space
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a new OpenClaw build started on state from an older release, the Gateway upgraded its databases in a private shadow:
1. It copied every migration input of the state directory, which on a real install includes large trees such as Codex session history.
2. It ran Doctor on the copy and swapped the results into place.

That had two costs:
- **Space.** The copy demanded twice its own size in free space. On a replica-shaped install with about 70 GiB to copy and about 100 GiB free, the new build refused to start, and the Git release launcher then switched back.
- **Extra copies.** Doctor inside the shadow also took its own original-state capture and full pre-migration backups.

Separately, if the migration committed and the new build still failed twice, the launcher switched back to a previous release that cannot open the newer schema.

## User Impact

- **No refusal for snapshot space.** The Gateway now upgrades state in place.
- **One image per outdated database, plus the config.** Before migrating, the start keeps each as `<file>.pre-<buildId>`:
  - a copy-on-write clone where the filesystem supports one, which takes about no space;
  - otherwise a byte copy, made only when it still leaves the migration its room;
  - otherwise no image, with a warning. Once that migration commits, the previous release cannot be restored.
- **Revert only on evidence.** A Git release trial that fails twice switches back only on positive evidence that the previous release opens what the revert leaves. Otherwise it stays on the new release, says why, and points to `openclaw triage`.
- **A narrower revert.**
  - It restores the outdated databases and the config from their images.
  - It removes the databases the run created.
  - It stays forward when Doctor moved a legacy source the previous release reads (for example `cron/jobs.json`).
  - It no longer restores other files Doctor changed in place, such as migrated workspace or legacy files. The old copy-and-swap restored those too.
- **Fallback is the only path that replaces a database file.** That is the generic rebuild after a failed Doctor chain. A successful start migrates `state/openclaw.sqlite` in place, so it stays the same file.

## Why This Change Was Made

The owner approved option D in the copy inventory, fix-plan items 8 and 9:
- migrate in place;
- keep a pre-image only for outdated databases (clone or skip);
- never refuse a start for snapshot space;
- revert only onto a build that opens the state.

Every schema step commits in one SQLite transaction with its version bump.

This head also repairs the data-safety findings of the landing round on `d533da100e2`, verdicts below. It holds one rule everywhere:
- delete or replace a file only after its replacement is durable and verified;
- a failure at any step leaves the previous state recoverable;
- the launcher reverts only on positive evidence.

The state machine section lists every file family and step against that rule.

**Boot upgrade (`src/state/state-upgrade.ts`, `state-upgrade-tree.ts`)**
- **Images.** Under the start's exclusive custody, each outdated database is checkpointed through SQLite and imaged by the repository's native clone (`copySqliteFile`, `@openclaw/fs-safe`).
  - A byte copy is made only when it leaves the migration its room.
  - An image that cannot be taken is skipped with a warning, including on a full disk reported through a wrapping error.
  - A leftover image from a finished run is replaced only by renaming the complete new image over it.
  - The config image is written 0600, read through a symlink.
- **Chain.** Doctor runs on the live state. The 2× copy budget, the shadow copy and its code (`copyTree`, `diffTree`, prefix rewriting) are gone.
- **Resume record.** The work directory holds a durable inventory: the files before Doctor, the databases the run started on and the images it published.
  - A start that dies or fails after its migration began keeps the record.
  - The next start reruns the chain on every database the run started on, imaged or not, against the images that run recorded. It never images such a database again or trusts a same-named leftover.
  - An interrupted record is removed only after the new one holds its facts.
- **Fallback.** It rebuilds each outdated database from the live file as the chain left it, so rows Doctor already imported stay; the image stays the rollback baseline.
  - First it folds an imaged database's live WAL in through SQLite. If SQLite reports the checkpoint busy or refuses the mode switch, the start stops with every file in place.
  - It swaps through the durable plan, which now also carries the run's additions.
- **Config refusal.** The state is put back only as a complete set: images of every database the run started on and of an unlinked config, and no legacy source Doctor moved. It is put back through a durable `restore.json` that the next start finishes if this one stops, and the databases the run created are removed. Otherwise the databases stay migrated and the start says why. A linked config is neither imaged nor written through.
- **Additions.** Only databases the run created, and their companions, are recorded for the launcher.
- **No image, no trial.** When a database the run starts on has no image, the start ends the Git release trial (the existing settle operation) before anything migrates. Doctor does the same when it finds a pending store outside the start's discovery, since no launcher restores Doctor's backup of it. This is what makes the first hop safe under an older launcher.
- **Custody.** The start holds schema-maintenance ownership and lends it to the Doctor child. If another process takes it in between, this start stops and leaves the upgrade to that process.

**Doctor (`flows/doctor-health.ts`, `commands/doctor-*.ts`)**
- The boot chain already passes the existing hidden internal handoff `--state-upgrade-live-state-dir`. No new flag, environment variable or config key was added.
- When that directory is Doctor's own state directory, Doctor takes no original-state capture. It takes no version migration backup set either (`preImageOwner: "state-upgrade"`), unless a pending store lies outside the start's own discovery (a configured agent directory); then it takes its normal set.
- The heartbeat retirement backup still runs.
- Standalone `openclaw doctor --fix` keeps its backups.

**Launcher (`src/infra/git-release-launcher.ts`)**

After two failed starts, before changing anything, it reverts only when all of these hold:
1. The previous release declares `openclaw.schemaVersions`.
2. `node:sqlite` is available.
3. The upgrade records and the agent listing are readable, and every database the revert would leave is readable and at or below that release's limit. A restored image with a WAL preserved beside it is read together in a private copy. That is the image it restores, else the live file; for shared state it checks both the header and `state.schema.contentVersion`, the same admission facts that release applies. Databases the revert removes as additions are skipped.
4. After an upgrade ran, an unlinked config has an image.
5. No legacy source the upgrade records (or an interrupted run's inventory) list is gone.

Anything else keeps the service forward, with a message that lists what was not proven. No new `.trial` field.

**Update behavior for published updaters**
- The boot upgrade is new-build code and applies on its first start after any update path.
- The launcher text is written by the installed updater (`publishGitRelease`), so this rule applies from the first update after the updater that ships it.
- **First hop.** The earlier launcher restores every `.pre-<buildId>` file newer than the trial, which includes this start's images, so a first-hop revert lands safely whenever every outdated database was imaged. When one has no image, this start ends the trial before migrating, so the earlier launcher never counts the failed starts and cannot revert onto a refusing release. What the earlier launcher still does not check is a legacy source Doctor moved; on the first hop, a revert after such a move leaves that source archived, as the copy-and-swap upgrade's revert did not (its Doctor ran in the shadow).

**Steps left to a person:** none. A start that cannot fit the migration says so, and resumes once space is free. A trial that stays forward points to `openclaw triage`.
## State machine of the start's upgrade

**Rule held at every step:** a file that may hold committed data is deleted or replaced only after its replacement is durable and verified. A failure at any step leaves the previous state recoverable. The launcher reverts only on positive evidence.

**File families the start touches:**
- Each outdated database `D`, with `D-wal`, `D-shm`, `D-journal` and `D.seal`.
- The config `C`, which can be a symlink.
- The pre-images `D.pre-<gen>` and `C.pre-<gen>`.
- The resume record `.upgrade-<gen>-<pid>-<t>/`. It holds `inventory.json` (`{files, outdated, images}`), `chain.log`, the fallback's `fallback/` builds, `plan.json` (fallback only) and `restore.json` (refusal only).
- The applied record `.upgraded-<gen>.json`.
- Legacy sources Doctor moves into SQLite, and its archives of them (`.migrated`, `.migrated.<n>`, `.migrated-<stamp>-<id>`, by owner). The start never deletes or renames these. A source missing after the run is recorded as a `remove` op, and it blocks every revert.

In the table, "Restart" is what the next start does. "Test" names the test that covers the row: unit tests are in `state-upgrade.test.ts` unless another file is named, the kill sweep is "sweep" and the fallback kill sweep is "fb-sweep".

| # | Step | Creates, replaces or deletes | If killed right after | Restart | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Resume scan | Finishes an interrupted `restore.json` (idempotent). Applies an interrupted durable `plan.json` (idempotent). Reads an interrupted record of this build and keeps it. Deletes other builds' plan-less records (scratch only). | Nothing new. | Same scan again. | `releases retained handles before finishing an interrupted plan`; `records the fallback's additions when its swap is interrupted and resumed` |
| 1 | Create the record | `.upgrade-<gen>-*` (empty); fsync of the state directory | A plan-less record without an inventory. | Resume with nothing changed yet: images are taken or kept, and the chain runs. | sweep `pre\|0` |
| 2 | Image each outdated `D` | Checkpoints `D` through SQLite (never deletes `D-wal`). Writes `D.pre-<gen>.partial-<pid>` and renames it to `D.pre-<gen>`, which replaces a finished run's leftover only by that rename. A full disk, wrapped or not, skips the image. On resume, a `D` the interrupted run started on keeps only the image that run recorded, else none; it is never imaged after it may have changed. | Partial or complete image; `D` unchanged. | No inventory yet, so nothing changed: images are retaken. | `images only the outdated databases…`; `migrates without an image when a copy…`; `skips the image when a copy layer wraps a full disk`; `replaces a leftover image…`; `resumes only with images the interrupted run published…`; sweep `pre\|0/5/20` |
| 3 | Image `C` | `C.pre-<gen>.partial` (mode 0600, exclusive create), fsync, rename, fsync of its directory. A full disk skips it. A linked `C` is never imaged or written: the config writer does not follow a final link. | Partial or complete config image; `C` unchanged. | As in 2. | `images a config privately, and never writes through a linked one`; `keeps a config outside the state directory as a pre-image` |
| 3a | End the Git release trial if any `D` has no image | Removes the trial record of the running release (the existing settle operation), before anything migrates. | Trial ended; nothing migrated. | No launcher counts failed starts, so none reverts onto a release that refuses the state; failures are fixed forward. | `resumes only with images…` (`onUnimaged` called once) |
| 4 | Write the inventory | `inventory.json` (`{files, outdated, images}`) via tmp, fsync, rename, then fsync of the directory. | A record that names the files before Doctor ran, the databases the run started on and the images it published. | Reuses both for the additions and the resume set. | `keeps a database it started on without an image in a resumed run` |
| 5 | Retire interrupted records | Deletes the older records of this build, whose facts are now merged into step 4's record. | One record. | Resume. | `keeps its record when the disk fills mid-chain…` |
| 6 | Normalize text and run the chain (Doctor in place) | Doctor's own SQLite transactions on `D` (each step commits with its version bump), the config rewrite and archives of moved sources. | Each `D` at its old or new version; record present. | Reruns the chain on every database the run started on, against the same images. | sweep `abs\|*`, `wal\|*`; `finishes a chain a kill interrupted…`; `keeps its record when the disk fills mid-chain…` |
| 7 | Validate and check conservation | Reads only. | As in 6. | As in 6. | sweep |
| 8F | Fallback: fold the live WAL of each imaged `D` | SQLite checkpoint plus `journal_mode=DELETE`. A busy or refused fold stops the start with every file in place. | As in 6. | As in 6. | `stops the fallback with the live WAL intact when SQLite cannot fold it in`; fb-sweep |
| 9F | Fallback: rebuild from the live `D` as the chain left it | Writes `fallback/D` inside the record and checkpoints it. The live `D` is unchanged, so Doctor's imports are kept. | As in 6, plus scratch output. | As in 6; the scratch output is discarded with the old record. | `keeps rows Doctor committed before the chain failed…`; fb-sweep `fallback\|*` |
| 10 | Admit the config. On refusal, restore the images. | Only a complete set is restored: every database the run started on and an unlinked `C` have an image, and no file from the inventory is gone. First `restore.json` (files, suffix, created databases) is written durably. Then for each imaged `D` it deletes `D-wal`/`-journal`/`-shm` and renames the image over `D` (fsynced at step 2), restores `C`, deletes the created databases with their companions, and removes the record. | Some `D` restored, the rest still migrated with their images; `restore.json` present. | The resume scan finishes the restore before anything else. | `a start refused for invalid config restores the previous state` (e2e); `keeps the state migrated when Doctor moved a legacy source a refusal cannot put back`; `finishes a refusal's restore that a stop interrupted before anything else`; `keeps a database it started on without an image…`; `migrates in place, keeps the pre-image…` |
| 11 | Record diagnostics | A row in the live state database (or the fallback's output). | As in 6. | As in 6 (one more diagnostic row). | sweep |
| 12F | Fallback: durable plan, then apply it | Fsyncs `fallback/D`, writes `plan.json` (replace ops, companion removals and the run's additions) via tmp, fsync and rename, then applies it. Apply order: link `D-wal` to `D-wal.pre-<gen>` only where `D` has no image (otherwise it was folded at 8F), remove the companions, keep `D.pre-<gen>` (the image, or a hard link of `D`), rename `fallback/D` to `D`. Every step is idempotent. | Durable plan, partly applied. | Applies the same plan to the end and records it (additions included). | `records the fallback's additions when its swap is interrupted and resumed`; fb-sweep `plan\|*` |
| 13 | Write the applied record | `.upgraded-<gen>.json` via tmp and rename. It lists the additions (created databases) and, as `remove` ops, legacy sources that are gone. The plan carries the same ops; removing an absent file is a no-op. | Applied record present; work record still present. | Chain mode: the record is plan-less, so the chain reruns as a no-op and finishes. Fallback: the plan is reapplied (idempotent). | `names only the databases it created as trial additions…`; fb-sweep `applied\|*` |
| 14 | Finish | Prunes older generations' `.pre-*` images (never this build's or a pinned one), older applied records and the work record. | Done. | Current: nothing to do. | `prunes only owned file generations…` |

**Launcher after two failed trial starts** (`git-release-launcher.ts`; this build's launcher only, see the first hop below):
- The revert set is every `<file>.pre-<gen>` with ctime at or after the trial, plus the config image.
- It reverts only when every check below passes. Otherwise the service stays forward, the trial record is removed, and the message lists what was not proven and names `openclaw triage`.
  1. The previous release declares `openclaw.schemaVersions`.
  2. `node:sqlite` is available.
  3. The upgrade records (applied record, plans, interrupted inventories) and the agent directory listing are readable, no legacy source they name is gone, and every database the revert would leave is readable (an image together with the WAL preserved beside it, read in a private copy), at or below the previous release's limit, and, for shared state, has a content version at or below it too. That is the image it restores, else the live file. Databases the revert removes as additions are skipped.
  4. After an upgrade ran, an unlinked config has an image.
- On revert, it restores state first and moves the link last. An interrupted revert reruns from the recorded restore list.
- Tests (`git-release.test.ts`): `stays on the new release when no pre-image…`, `…content version is newer behind an older header`, `…declares no schemas`, `…cannot be read`, `reverts only when the upgraded config has its image`, `reverts when the only newer database is one the revert removes` (also its WAL), `stays forward when Doctor moved a legacy source… (applied record / interrupted inventory)`, `removes a store an interrupted in-place run created when it reverts`, `reads a restored image together with the WAL preserved beside it`, `stays forward when an upgrade record cannot be read`, `switches back and restores the pre-image…`, `stays on the new release when the image it would restore is newer too`, `resumes an interrupted rollback…`, `keeps a family's restored WAL…`.
## Landing round on `d533da100e2`: verdicts

Each "real" verdict comes with a test that fails on `d533da100e2` and passes on this head. The `state-upgrade.test.ts` and `git-release.test.ts` runs were swapped to the `d533da100e2` source to show the failure.

1. **Fallback deleted a live WAL when it could not checkpoint it** (`state-upgrade.ts:600-606` at `d533da100e2`). **Real.**
   - Fix: the fallback folds the live WAL in through SQLite and checks the result. If the checkpoint is busy or the mode switch is refused, it stops and deletes nothing.
   - Test: `stops the fallback with the live WAL intact when SQLite cannot fold it in`. A reader's open snapshot keeps a committed `update_runs` row only in the WAL.
2. **Launcher read only the header** (`git-release-launcher.ts:161-165`). **Real.**
   - Fix: shared state is judged by the header and `state.schema.contentVersion`. Anything unreadable blocks the revert.
   - Tests: `stays forward when the shared content version is newer behind an older header`, `…when a database it would leave cannot be read`, `…when the previous release declares no schemas`.
3. **Fallback from the images dropped rows Doctor had imported** (`:609-619`). **Real**: the rebuild read the image, while Doctor had already archived the moved sources.
   - Fix: the rebuild reads the live databases as the chain left them.
   - Test: `keeps rows Doctor committed before the chain failed in the fallback rebuild`.
4. **A database without an image was forgotten on resume** (`:453-463`). **Real**: the resume set was "still outdated or imaged".
   - Fix: the durable inventory records every database the run started on.
   - Test: `keeps a database it started on without an image in a resumed run`. That refusal now reports that nothing can be restored instead of restoring a partial set.
5. **Config image not private through a symlink** (`:528-533`). **Real**: `copyFileSync` carried the target's 0644.
   - Fix: the image is created 0600 with exclusive create.
   - Test: `keeps the config image private when the config is a link to a shared file`.
6. **First hop is governed by the old launcher** (`:503-515`). **Real for a skipped image; fixed.** The old launcher restores the images, so only a skipped image was unsafe.
   - Fix: when a database the run starts on has no image, the start ends the trial before migrating, through the existing settle operation that a serving Gateway already performs.
   - Test: `resumes only with images…` asserts the hook fires once.
   - Limit: the wiring to the real trial file is not covered by a test.
7. **Launcher counted databases the revert removes** (`git-release-launcher.ts:233-240`). **Real.**
   - Fix: the additions in the applied record and in interrupted plans are skipped.
   - Test: `reverts when the only newer database is one the revert removes`.
8. **Fallback additions lost across an interrupted swap** (`:705-709`). **Real**: the durable plan held only replacements.
   - Fix: the plan carries the additions.
   - Test: `records the fallback's additions when its swap is interrupted and resumed`. It interrupts the swap's first rename, then resumes.
9. **A wrapped full-disk error aborted the start** (`state-upgrade-tree.ts:450-459`). **Real**: only the top-level error was inspected.
   - Fix: causes and aggregated errors are walked, for both full disk and the space admission.
   - Test: `skips the image when a copy layer wraps a full disk`.

Two extra changes, found while writing the state machine:
- A leftover image of a finished run was deleted before its replacement existed. It is now replaced only by rename.
- The inventory was not fsynced before the interrupted records were removed. It now is.

## Rating round on `fa77fc2f102` (this PR's own round): verdicts

That round rated F / F / F with nine findings. Fixed failing-first on `2ab365b0946`, each red against `fa77fc2f102`:

1. **(P1) A refusal or revert dropped Doctor's imported legacy sources** (cron `jobs.json` archived as `.migrated`). **Real.** The fix is described under the next round's item 3, which replaced this round's first attempt (renaming `.migrated` archives back, which missed other owners' archive names).
2. **(P1) First hop with a skipped image.** **Real; fixed** as in item 6 above.
3. **(P1) Doctor's exemption was directory-wide.** **Real.**
   - Fix: Doctor keeps its normal backup set when a pending store lies outside the start's discovery.
   - Test: `copies only when Doctor owns the image (…, outside the start's discovery=true)`.
   - Not changed: the launcher still cannot see an agent database configured outside the state directory. The earlier launcher and the copy-and-swap upgrade had the same gap.
4. **(P1) An image was read without the WAL preserved beside it.** **Real.**
   - Fix: the pair is read together in a private copy.
   - Test: `reads a restored image together with the WAL preserved beside it`.
5. **(P1) Config symlink handling.** **Real.**
   - Fix: a linked config is neither imaged nor written through, and the launcher does not require its image.
   - Test: `images a config privately, and never writes through a linked one (linked: true)`, using a read-only link target.
6. **(P1) Resume trusted a leftover same-build image.** **Real.**
   - Fix: the inventory records the images the run published; resume keeps only those.
   - Test: `resumes only with images the interrupted run published, never a leftover`.
7. **(P2) An unreadable inventory was treated as empty.** **Real.**
   - Fix: an unreadable record, plan or agent listing keeps the service forward.
   - Test: `stays forward when an upgrade record cannot be read`.
8. **(P2) A created database's companions were left behind.** **Real.**
   - Fix: the launcher removes them with the database; the dead companion filter is gone.
   - Test: the WAL assertion in `reverts when the only newer database is one the revert removes`.
9. **(P2) Test-line budget.** **Real.**
   - Shared test helpers were consolidated.
   - The remaining growth is one test per state-machine row and per launcher rule, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/201716-in-place-state-upgrade.txt` with that reason.

## Rating round on `2ab365b0946` (this PR's own round): verdicts

That round rated F / F / F with six findings. Each fix below fails on `2ab365b0946` and passes on this head:

1. **(P1) An interrupted refusal restore consumed images.** **Real.**
   - Fix: a durable `restore.json` is written first, and the resume scan finishes it before anything else.
   - Test: `finishes a refusal's restore that a stop interrupted before anything else`, which stops at the second image rename.
2. **(P1) Configured agent stores outside the state directory were outside the launcher's view.** **Real.**
   - Fix: Doctor, as the start's chain, ends the Git release trial before migrating such a store, and keeps its normal backup set.
   - Test: `settleRunningGitReleaseTrial` is asserted in `copies only when Doctor owns the image (…, outside=true)`.
3. **(P1) Archive names differ by owner** (`.migrated-<stamp>-<id>` for auth profiles). **Real.**
   - Fix: instead of mirroring each owner's archive naming, the start compares its inventory. A file that existed before Doctor and is gone after is a moved legacy source; it blocks the refusal restore and is recorded as a `remove` op that blocks every revert. An interrupted run's inventory is read the same way by the launcher.
   - Tests: `keeps the state migrated when Doctor moved a legacy source…`, `stays forward when Doctor moved a legacy source… (applied record / interrupted inventory)`.
4. **(P2) Stores created before the applied record were missed.** **Real.**
   - Fix: the launcher treats `.sqlite` files absent from an interrupted run's inventory as additions, and a refusal restore removes the run's created databases.
   - Test: `removes a store an interrupted in-place run created when it reverts`.
5. **(P1) Directory entries not synced.** **Real.**
   - Fix: the state directory is fsynced after the record is created, and the config's directory after its image.
   - No test; this is a power-loss property.
6. **(P3) Docs overstated the guarantees.** **Real.** The update guide now states Doctor's remaining backups, the complete-set refusal rule, the revert conditions and which launcher governs the first hop.

**Product question it raised:** boot repair still changes workspace files in place that neither a refusal nor a revert restores. The coordinator accepted this narrower revert for this PR ("state the narrower revert plainly"); it is stated under User Impact and in the docs.
## Evidence

**In-place kill sweep through the real `gateway run` boot**
- Setup: 37 SIGKILLs on the 2026.10.10 release corpus (state v22, agents v27). The corpus holds about 180,000 transcript rows and an updater `update_runs` row written before the restart.
- Kill points:
  - fixed times from 1.25 s to 44 s;
  - 0, 5 and 20 ms after the first image;
  - when the WAL grows and at 30 KB;
  - 0 and 50 ms after the applied record.
- Checks after every kill:
  1. `integrity_check` is ok.
  2. `user_version` equals `schema_meta` and is exactly the old or the new version.
  3. Every pre-existing witness row is unchanged.
  4. A migrated database equals the uninterrupted run.
- Each surviving image is intact at the old version. The rerun serves and equals the uninterrupted run.
- Result on this head: rerun pending on this head (37 of 37 passed on `d533da100e2`).

**Fallback kill sweep (new)**
- Setup: the same corpus. The start's upgrade runs with the real Doctor chain, then an injected `ChainStepError`, so the generic rebuild runs (`fallback-driver.mts` calls `upgradeStateDirectory` with `createDoctorChain` and throws after Doctor).
- Kill points:
  - 0 and 50 ms after the first image;
  - 8 to 36 s inside Doctor;
  - 0 to 4 s into the fallback build;
  - 0, 5 and 40 ms after `plan.json`;
  - 0 and 30 ms after the applied record.
- Checks: the same checks after the kill. Then the real `gateway` start with no fault must finish, serve, reach v40/v43, and keep every witness row.
- An uninterrupted fallback run ends in `mode: fallback`, at v40/v43, with the images at v22/v27, and serves.
- Result: 16 of 16 passed on `9061cf9fc6f`; rerun pending on this head.

**Real updater into this build (macOS launchd Git source checkout install, release mode)**
- Setup:
  - its own profile, state directory and port;
  - a synthetic config with no channels, providers or credentials;
  - a 512 MiB agent database at schema 42;
  - the real `openclaw update --channel dev --yes`.
- Installed side: `6691acae` (the last commit before the 42 → 43 agent-schema bump) + #201463 + #201600 + this PR's launcher, built. The launcher is written by the installed updater, so only an updater that ships it can run the new rule.
- Target: this PR's head, and for the failing-candidate runs, this head plus an e2e-only patch that exits right after the state upgrade.
- Results: rerun pending on this head (busy and idle passed on `d533da100e2`: exit 0, schema 43, trial settled, writer alive, run `succeeded`)

**`update_runs` rows the updater wrote just before the restart** survive:
- the in-place path (sweep witness, unit test);
- the fallback (unit tests `keeps the update run … (fallback)` and `keeps rows Doctor committed …`, and the fallback sweep witness).



## Not proven or not changed

- **Doctor's repair-specific backups.** The credential cutover image for state below v29 and the legacy cron and session repairs still take their own scoped images. Routing them through the same owner decision is a follow-up.
- **First-hop revert with a skipped image** (see "Update behavior").
- **Boot time limit.** The 30-minute chain timeout is unchanged. In-place boot is about 50 s for about 230 MB of databases here; 4 GiB was not measured.
- **Platforms.** PostgreSQL, Windows, and Linux filesystems without clones were not run. Their byte-copy-or-skip path is covered by unit tests.
- **Review tooling.** `autoreview` does not run on this machine; an independent reviewer agent and ClawSweeper rating rounds reviewed the diff instead.

prs.title: improve: keep cold transcript checks lightweight
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201681

## What Problem This Solves

Cold transcript checks load write-side database and environment setup while preparing a read-only batch, even when there is nothing to archive. That gives a lightweight check an unnecessarily large worker import graph.

## User Impact

Cold preparation no longer loads mutation owners just to verify physical file custody. Archive, restore, cancellation, and source-identity checks retain their existing behavior; no configuration change is required. Actual mutation still loads its required owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the unchanged physical-custody assertion into a small shared module. Both callers import it lazily, preserving the canonical validation worker boundary as well as the cold preparation boundary. This removes the read-to-mutation import edge without adding a cache, worker, or alternate execution path. Net production change: +2 lines; regression tests: +188 lines.

## Evidence

The new real-worker regression fails on the baseline because cold preparation loads `session-cold-storage-worker.ts`; it passes with the fix. It verifies that preparation and physical custody actually execute, the prepared transcript is correct, the database stays unchanged, and the worker closes.

Integrated proof for `ba8573b2f07660843715b5daf8525cd5aebda7ef`: all 155 expected source/dependency paths matched, all 28 focused tests across four files passed, and the full build completed successfully. Both production and full-tree unused-file scans passed with zero entries. The build reported non-fatal Control UI size/request-budget violations; their attribution has not been established by this work.

Independent review found no actionable P0–P3 issue. The rebase preserves the patch: `git range-diff` reports equality, all six changed files have identical hashes, and dependency manifests and lockfile are unchanged.

## Performance qualification: HOLD

The serial, counterbalanced comparison used five observations per arm on Node 26.12.0 with 64 sessions, plus separate allocation profiles. It compared the sealed pre-rebase builds `a8bfb23243d8149954aefd2dd20022e62fb7ed62` and `2ecd430509a573e3a5807ff7841254fac290aa50`; it does not measure the surrounding rebased integration.

Process peak RSS median fell from 1,295,646,720 to 1,244,446,720 bytes (48.8 MiB, 3.95%). First-result worker heap and allocation profiles also improved. These are harness/process and worker measurements, not a whole-Gateway claim.

The unchanged 20% regression gate failed in five metric families:

- Canonical response time: median +29.15%, p95 +22.15%.
- Canonical worker CPU: median +25.06%.
- First cold request time: p95 +64.68%.
- Warm request time: p95 +57.53%.
- Warm main-thread CPU: p95 +53.71%.

With five observations, the canonical/first-request p95 is the observed maximum; warm tails use 195 requests per arm. The increases remain unresolved. This PR stays draft pending review of the timing regressions. The bounded diagnostic series is complete; its observations are additional causal evidence, not a replacement for the failed gate.

### Follow-up causal diagnostics

The unprofiled canonical diagnostic completed 20 fresh processes: five same-build A/A pairs and five counterbalanced A/B pairs. Median paired A/B changes were +0.15% wall time and +0.48% worker CPU, but ratios of the arm medians were +19.84% and +20.60%. The A/A control also varied. Worker CPU here spans thread birth through an external query, unlike the original observer interval. These results do not clear the original failures.

A separate 2x2 diagnostic completed 20 fresh processes and 800 sweeps, keeping 64 sessions and 40 sweeps per process. It compared the original RSS/event-loop observers with both observers disabled; allocation and worker profiling were absent. Warm measurements remain grouped by process. With observers disabled, the candidate was slower in all five cold pairs: median paired changes were +43.36% cold wall time, +49.61% per-process warm wall p95, and +66.29% per-process warm main-thread CPU p95. With the original observers, the corresponding paired medians were -9.94%, -24.14%, and -18.62%. This interaction does not establish a cause or isolate either observer individually.

Every diagnostic process passed its correctness and cleanup checks. The frozen build entries and all 2,178 shared package files retained their original aggregate seal. Both arms shared the same installed dependencies, but those dependency bytes were not proven identical to the original host; effective Node compile-cache state is unknown. Host contention was observed; its contribution remains unresolved.

A final timing-only segmentation diagnostic completed ten fresh processes (five counterbalanced A/B pairs), with 64 sessions and 40 sweeps per process. All 400 elapsed-time partitions reconciled, and every correctness and cleanup check passed. Both arms received the same bounded timestamp and worker thread-CPU probes; these probes can affect timing and are diagnostic instrumentation.

Cold archive-worker dispatch-to-reply improved in all five pairs, by 121.61–593.57 ms. Handler dynamic-import wall time fell 83.74–91.99%, and import CPU fell 84.45–92.53%. Between 91.42% and 96.87% of first-call wall time occurred before archive-worker construction; variation there dominated the whole-call differences in this pass. This localizes observed costs without establishing the cause of the original failures.

Warm results remained mixed. For per-process warm main-thread CPU p95, the median paired change was +9.81%, the ratio of cohort medians was +68.66%, and individual paired changes ranged from -35.58% to +148.30%. No measured segment was consistently enlarged across all five pairs. Whole-child host steal was elevated in several slow observations, but these observations do not isolate its contribution or resolve the CPU increases.

All five original regression families remain on HOLD. Improvements in the changed worker path do not clear the original gate. No acceptance waiver has been applied, and no further measurements are planned in this diagnostic cycle.

prs.title: fix(plugins): match peer-link host roots by physical identity (#201589)
prs.body:
Closes #201589

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, installing OpenClaw into a mixed-case directory (e.g. `D:\Personal\OpenClaw`) left every peer-declaring plugin permanently blocked: the installer's junction stored a different casing of the same directory (`D:\Personal\openclaw`), and the host-root audit compared realpath results with `===`, so one directory under two spellings was rejected as `missing-openclaw-peer-link` and the channel never started.

- Solution: when the spellings differ, compare physical identity (dev/ino) through the existing `sameFsObject` owner before falling back to standalone-manifest identity.
- What changed: `src/plugins/plugin-peer-link.ts` only; the shared matcher serves all three callers (peer-link audit, native namespace, native reference).
- What did NOT change: manifest-identity admission for relocated standalone copies, link repair/rebinding, rejection of genuinely distinct directories.

## Why This Change Was Made

Physical identity is the repo's established answer to Windows alias spellings: `src/plugins/path-safety.ts` already proves dev/ino identity for Windows physical aliases, and `sameFsObject` (`src/infra/path-case.ts`) is the canonical comparison owner (also used by `exec-safe-bin-trust.ts`).

- Alternative considered: case-folding gated by `isPathCaseInsensitive`. Rejected: it needs a filesystem probe per mismatch and only covers casing, while dev/ino covers any same-directory alias and never widens admission on case-sensitive filesystems.
- Stat failures fail closed inside the existing try/catch; no change to the standalone-manifest contract.

## User Impact

Windows installs whose directory casing differs from the plugin record keep their channels connected after plugin install/reinstall; `doctor` no longer reports a false peer-link mismatch for the same directory. No behavior change on case-sensitive filesystems.

## Evidence

Observed result — native Windows proof on a `windows-latest` runner (GitHub Actions, real NTFS): a fresh `npm install -g openclaw@2026.11.5` (latest stable, the reporter's version) into mixed-case `C:\proof\OpenClaw`, then `plugins install npm:@openclaw/feishu@2026.11.5` invoked through the lowercase spelling of the same install. The junction naturally stored the lowercase target — no manual fixture needed. BASE arm = pristine published package; HEAD arm = the same install with this PR's 5-line production diff mirrored into the published dist chunk (dist inventory entry recomputed); both arms share one state dir, so BASE→HEAD is also an in-place upgrade with existing settings.

```text
BASE (pristine 2026.11.5), openclaw channels status:
- Feishu default: enabled, configured, reason:Plugin feishu failed: configured plugin
  payload verification failed (missing-openclaw-peer-link) ... stopped, health:blocked
BASE gateway log:
- Plugin "feishu": ... peer link audit failed: ...\node_modules\openclaw
  points to c:\proof\openclaw\node_modules\openclaw instead of C:\proof\OpenClaw\node_modules\openclaw

HEAD (same install + mirrored diff), gateway log:
[gateway] startup trace: plugins.gateway-load.plugin.feishu ... loadFailedCount=0.0 ... registerFailedCount=0.0
[gateway] http server listening (15 plugins: anthropic, browser, canvas, cua-computer, device-pair, feishu, ...)
[feishu] starting feishu[default] (mode: websocket)
[feishu] feishu[default]: WebSocket client started
[info]: [ '[ws]', 'ws client ready' ]
HEAD openclaw channels status: - Feishu default: enabled, configured, running
HEAD openclaw channels status --probe: - Feishu default: ... running, connected
```

The channel connected to Feishu over a real websocket with real app credentials. The bot-identity health probe separately returned Feishu API error 21001 (platform permission policy on the test app, `bot open_id resolved: unknown`) — orthogonal to peer-link admission; the channel stayed `running, connected`.

Path identity captured on the runner (same object, two spellings):

```json
{"linkRealpath":"c:\\proof\\openclaw\\node_modules\\openclaw",
 "hostRealpath":"C:\\proof\\OpenClaw\\node_modules\\openclaw",
 "linkDevIno":[1422631540,1125899907154117],"hostDevIno":[1422631540,1125899907154117],
 "sameObject":true,"spellingsEqual":false}
```

| Cell (shipped CLI + Gateway, real NTFS) | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh mixed-case install + feishu plugin install | blocked: `missing-openclaw-peer-link`, `health:blocked` | admitted, feishu registered |
| `plugins install --force` reinstall (lowercase junction) | re-blocked (reporter symptom) | still admitted |
| Upgrade in place, existing state | — | gateway + channels config unchanged |
| Real Feishu channel connect (websocket, real credentials) | never starts (`health:blocked`) | `running, connected` |

Regression tests fold into `src/plugins/plugin-peer-link.test.ts` (`openClawHostRootsMatch physical identity`, `it.each`): same dev/ino under two spellings → `true` (red on base, green with the fix); distinct inode / distinct device → `false` on both arms. Full file: `48 passed` on the plugins shard config.

Checks: `oxfmt --check` clean; `oxlint` 259 rules, 0 findings; targeted `tsc` program over the two touched files: 0 errors in them (648 residual errors in unrelated files from the limited program).

What was not tested: end-to-end message send/receive (the proof asserts admission and websocket connection, not conversation). The HEAD arm is the published stable with only this PR's production diff mirrored into dist (disclosed above), not a full source build.

On PostgreSQL-backed state, plugin inspection can read the local SQLite anchor instead of the PostgreSQL install record. An npm-pack install then appears without its artifact kind, source path, or integrity. Closes #202891.

## User Impact

Operators can inspect the recorded provenance of locally installed plugin archives on PostgreSQL-backed profiles.

## Why This Change Was Made

The live SQLite metadata shortcut now checks the captured state backend and leaves PostgreSQL reads to the existing engine-aware worker.

## Evidence

A regression test wrote synthetic npm-pack provenance to PostgreSQL under a live Gateway owner. Before the source change, the read returned no row; after the change, it returned the recorded fields (2/2 tests passed). Focused metadata, install-record, and source-identity suites passed (27 tests; one macOS-only test skipped on Linux). Core and plugin-test typechecks, targeted lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed.

The path is redacted here; the full values were observed in local output. The task PostgreSQL container and Gateway were stopped afterward, and the working tree is clean.

prs.body:
Related to #202701.

## What Problem This Solves

On `main`, switching a macOS npm install to the dev channel can fail during cloning when the updater selects Apple's Git stub and no developer directory is active. An existing source checkout can be reported as an unmanaged install for the same reason.

## User Impact

This PR reports that `/usr/bin/git` needs the macOS developer tools and stops before invoking the stub. The message tells users to run `xcode-select --install` or select an installed Xcode, then retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The updater checks the active developer directory when its existing executable search selects `/usr/bin/git`. The existing search order still gives `/usr/bin` precedence over inherited PATH entries. Whether the updater should trust a standalone Git is a separate decision for maintainers.

## Evidence

- Native macOS comparisons used pinned main `b4a41aa` and candidate `2bb9c2ac0`. Main attempted the clone or classified the source checkout as unmanaged when Git execution was denied. With the developer tools hidden, the candidate reported the prerequisite for the package-to-source switch and the source checkout, with zero Git launches. With a working developer directory, the package-to-source switch completed.

prs.title: fix: keep Gateway follow-up work authorized after earlier requests end
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway follow-up work can lose its usable authority after the original request ends. A descendant may try to retain an already retired recovery claim, or be refused because an earlier invocation's failure was mistaken for revocation of the original source. Tokenless recovery must also preserve the original device's next-start revocation checks.

## User Impact

Authorized descendants can continue after the originating request ends. Source revocation still refuses the next start, without retroactively cancelling already-admitted work. No configuration, public API, or stored-data format changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continuation capture shares its already-acquired original/restored holds using idempotent reference-counted release, instead of reacquiring a retired ancestor claim. Each new start still checks both policy owners. Original Gateway reauthorization checks source-policy owners and signals independently of invocation-specific failure state, retaining device, committed-source, identity, role, profile, and model restrictions.

The current-main integration preserves the explicit tokenless device-revocation guard from #202318, along with current membership and trusted-proxy policy changes. The allowed/revoked tokenless regression moves into the focused invocation test file and now also exercises descendant capture and release of the preceding hold; existing coverage is retained without exceeding the test-file line cap. The scripted product fixture is unchanged from current main.

The simplification pass keeps the existing authority owners; no new manager, store, configuration, retry, or timeout was introduced.

## Evidence

- The two original regressions reproduced before repair: retaining a descendant after the recovery claim retired, and starting a descendant after the original invocation failed. The earlier stable-source proof passed 111 tests across seven files and two shards.
- Prior published head `d97af15f6a71819b280ef1179290d20c4151662a`: CI run `44532032648`, attempt 2, passed; hosted review completed with no findings. These are prior-head results, not evidence for the integration commit.
- Integration base: `7d1d7d035ce611b0d99f52f218ccd7b80297dac5`. Published commit: `b76eea52d58e9b35b2750d995c53c2ecca136f3b`. The focused final suite passed 47 tests across three files, including the relocated regressions and scripted Gateway product flow. An earlier post-integration four-file recovery/authority/device suite passed 83 tests before the test-only relocation.
- Scripted Gateway scenarios: allowed work produced one effect and one wake; device-revoked work produced no effect or wake and one refusal. The owned process tree was joined. These use scripted model responses, not a real provider.
- Production core and Gateway-root typechecks, targeted lint/format, and the scoped diff check passed. Gateway-root types and targeted lint were checked again after the test relocation.
- Fresh full-context independent review of the final four-file diff found no concrete P0–P3 defects. Canonical autoreview of the committed range from the integration base through `b76eea52d58e9b35b2750d995c53c2ecca136f3b` completed P0–P3 scoped-clean with no findings and exit 0 (OpenClaw engine, effective model `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`). Canonical review was supplied-diff only, without unchanged implementation context or test execution; it supplements the full-context review and focused tests.
- The integrated PR diff is four files (+207/-88); SHA-256 of `git diff --binary 7d1d7d035ce611b0d99f52f218ccd7b80297dac5 b76eea52d58e9b35b2750d995c53c2ecca136f3b` is `a49365fa7679f0fa843907dc5780ce6c5c6bc1eef2f234d01342c8424c650da7`.

- November 21 live proof: rebuilt the runtime from published head `b76eea52d58e9b35b2750d995c53c2ecca136f3b`, then used the supported isolated live-test launcher, an empty fixture HOME/config/state, a real agent, and OpenAI `gpt-5.4` inference. The selected descendant case passed (one test, 11 provider requests); no other live cases were selected. Native `sessions_spawn` calls preserved the hidden-subagent restriction against `sessions_send`, with completion handoffs disabled.
- The live sequence observed the original and continuation terminal results before allowing the descendant to proceed, accepted its next child, removed the original device through the real Gateway owner, and rejected its following child with the owner refusal “Operator access was revoked; start a new user turn.” The already-admitted descendant finished; the refused child made zero provider requests. The owned Gateway stopped and fixture state was removed. No production authorization changes were required.
- Exact published-head CI run `44735418115`, attempt 1, completed successfully. The live harness changes remain private/unpublished; the PR source diff and head are unchanged.

### Remaining proof limits

The real-agent/model sequence now passes on the published integration head using an isolated Gateway and actual OpenAI inference. It establishes parent terminal results before descendant admission, not a deterministic observation that every ancestor authority hold has already been released: `agent.wait` is a terminal-result barrier, and native registry custody can outlive the model turn. Exact release/closed-connection ordering remains covered by the deterministic production-owner regression in `operator-run-recovery.invocation.test.ts`. The live sequence is complementary end-to-end evidence, not a replacement for that regression or a real-provider restart/recovery test. Prior hosted review does not cover this integration commit. Unpublished quiet-steering live-test work remains excluded.

prs.title: fix(web-fetch): keep Gateway responsive during cold provider discovery
prs.body:
Fixes #166641

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway stalls caused by synchronous plugin source capture when `web_fetch` first discovers fallback providers, including providers that do not declare `webFetchProviders` in their manifest.

## User Impact

During cold fallback discovery, a worker prepares external plugin sources while the Gateway continues serving requests. Undeclared-provider discovery, configured selection, sandbox restrictions, and synchronous listing callers retain their existing behavior.

Plugin evaluation and `register()` still run in their original owner; this change does not make arbitrary plugin initialization nonblocking.

## Why This Change Was Made

The synchronous and asynchronous resolvers now share one decision sequence. Fetch execution awaits the existing asynchronous loader, which already owns source preparation, cache identity, and pending-load sharing. Registration reentry still avoids waiting on itself, and an inspection released during supplemental loading cannot publish providers.

No new cache, configuration, schema, or plugin-manifest requirement.

## Evidence

### Validation on the current branch

Validated PR head `a88fa90242512ac5ec29eb4d8fbba530a6c4d1cd` against upstream `b7bf937423f65c313c8fe98b81b112537286ecaf`. Synchronous and asynchronous setup discovery both forward the caller’s plugin install records and pending state migrations. The bundled-artifact test now runs the same asynchronous fetch resolver as production and checks that repeated lookups reuse each caller’s own artifact.

The same Gateway regression sent two concurrent requests for distinct URLs on each revision. On upstream it observed one synchronous plugin source capture and zero asynchronous preparations. On the PR it observed zero synchronous captures and one shared asynchronous preparation. Both requests returned the expected fallback content. A third, warm URL reused the same provider. The regression passed on Node 24.22.1 and the repository-pinned Bun runtime.

An independent Node process running `openclaw.mjs gateway run` exercised an undeclared fallback provider with 1,200 source files. All three fetches returned the expected content. During the cold requests, 169 health probes returned HTTP 200. Of those, 89 started and finished within a plugin preparation worker interval. The cold requests together added one registration and the warm request added none.

- 256 tests passed across 12 focused files. The Gateway regression above passed separately on both runtimes.
- Core and all four affected test TypeScript configurations passed. The change-scoped checks passed, including formatting, lint and unused-export scans. The test-line and mock-export checks also passed.
- The full build stopped at the public plugin SDK declaration budget on the PR and on a clean checkout of `b7bf937`. Both produced 5,406,356 bytes against the 5,385,536-byte limit.

### GitHub Actions

[Checks for the current PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194612/checks)

### Focused reproduction commands

```sh
pnpm test src/plugins/public-artifact-environment.test.ts src/plugins/web-provider-runtime-shared.test.ts src/plugins/web-fetch-providers.runtime.test.ts src/plugins/web-search-providers.runtime.test.ts src/plugins/tools.inspection.test.ts src/plugins/loader-load-context.test.ts src/plugins/contracts/web-fetch-provider.contract.test.ts src/web-fetch/runtime.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-tools.fetch.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-fetch.provider-fallback.test.ts src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts src/gateway/server.auth.guest-dictation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm build
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 pnpm test src/gateway/web-fetch-discovery.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 pnpm test src/gateway/web-fetch-discovery.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm check:changed --base b7bf937423f65c313c8fe98b81b112537286ecaf --head a88fa90242512ac5ec29eb4d8fbba530a6c4d1cd --delegate-compilers
```

### Initial reproduction on 2026-11-07

Base: `openclaw/openclaw` main `020ec24568b12416bf4315732532bae8762101aa`, fetched on 2026-11-07. Local Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, repository-pinned Bun, macOS arm64.

The initial regression ran a real isolated Gateway and `POST /tools/invoke` against a local HTTP 503 fixture, with provider selection unset and a synthetic external plugin lacking the web-fetch manifest declaration. Startup, discovery, registration, and loading were not mocked; spies observed the real source preparation. Acceptance was correct fallback content with no plugin source traversal on the Gateway thread.

| Observation | Base: one fallback request | Fixed: two concurrent URLs, then a warm URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP/content result | 200, expected provider text | All three 200, expected provider text |
| Main-thread source traversal | 1 | 0 |
| Asynchronous source preparation | 0 | 1 total |
| Request-time registrations | 1 additional | 1 additional; warm call adds none |

The base failed the main-thread traversal assertion. Startup had already registered the fixture once, so this demonstrates request-time recapture, not a never-loaded plugin. The final test extends that regression to concurrent and warm calls with distinct URLs to avoid response-cache sharing.

Validation:

- Across focused runs, 227 unique tests across nine files passed: 226 focused tests covering provider resolution, web-fetch runtime/fallback, web-search compatibility, CLI, and inspection lifetime, plus the dedicated real Gateway concurrent/warm E2E regression.
- Core and four owning test TypeScript configurations passed, including the final dedicated Gateway file.
- Targeted lint and formatting, diff whitespace checks, the test-line allocation check, and the mock-export ratchet passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed (exit 0), including plugin SDK declarations and Control UI.
- Independent Codex source review: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the local change.

### Shipped Gateway trace at `3bea597`

Executed at `3bea597ec8db7a4cca22ec803108673ba336acc4`, Node 24.22.1 on macOS arm64, against the rebuilt runtime. A separate process launched the package entry point with `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port "$GATEWAY_PORT" --bind loopback`. An external driver waited for `/readyz`, sent two concurrent `POST /tools/invoke` requests for `web_fetch` with distinct URLs, then a third warm URL, while polling `/healthz` every 20 ms. All three requests returned the fixture provider's expected text after direct HTTP 503 responses.

The isolated configuration used a synthetic external plugin with no `webFetchProviders` manifest declaration, no configured provider selection, and 1,200 referenced source files. Bundled discovery was disabled (`OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1` and `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR` pointing to an empty directory) to exercise the external-only, undeclared-provider inventory path. No Gateway, loader, discovery, or registration functions were mocked. This proof uses a synthetic HTTP fixture and does not require a model or external service.

A read-only `diagnostics_channel` subscriber, loaded with Node's `--import`, recorded the existing `openclaw.worker.task` completion events for `plugin-generation-preparation.worker.js`. Worker intervals are derived from completion timestamps minus reported `runMs`; 61 complete external health requests fell within those intervals.
