prs.title: improve: avoid a second workspace scan on the first sandbox send
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first send in a new managed sandbox scans and checkpoints the workspace again after creating protected skill directories. Those empty directories were added after the initial projection baseline was accepted, so even a ready template still leaves substantial work on the user's first-send path. The startup log misleadingly charges this checkpoint to `skills_sync`.

## User Impact

New managed sandboxes can accept their initial layout without a second full-workspace checkpoint. Existing projections still reconcile real changes, including authored empty directories. No configuration, schema, persistence, or retention change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing mount producer returns the directories it creates. Sandbox initialization establishes those directories before publication and carries their paths into the existing baseline replacement worker, alongside the prepared template manifest. Generic archive/recovery initialization stays unchanged. Materialized skills outside the projection no longer trigger its checkpoint.

Separate timing fields identify skill synchronization, mount preparation, checkpoint, session/registry owner resolution, and baseline worker preparation/publication. The layout function moves into its own module, and duplicate manifest-to-tree conversion is removed. Net production growth is 76 lines for the prepared facts and timing boundaries.

Direction: the Team perf-loop lead, an agent acting under Peter's standing unattended instruction. Acceptance is recorded below.

## Evidence and landing state

Final head `227432996bfbf1321fdf71e74f8f62a975d636ad` is fully qualified, **not merged**. Exact-head [CI run 44857318479](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44857318479) is green. Codex review is clean through P2. [ClawSweeper revision 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202803#issuecomment-7054623715) reviewed this head and has zero open items. The Team perf-loop lead has explicitly accepted the disclosed tail, other resource changes, and existing idle pauses below.

Baseline is main parent `8271ec9ee5d48655b6d41d39314bd4e44e73b7c0`. Final source/worker inputs match the pushed head. Two A/A controls precede five serial counterbalanced pairs (AB, BA, AB, BA, AB), each on a fresh snapshot. The physically reserved 64 GiB btrfs image holds 62,000 tracked files/~1.1 GB and a 35 GiB synthetic SQLite file with 5,000 session rows as storage pressure; the latter is not a loaded production-shaped agent database. No Team data/access and no task-owned build/test/review overlap with timing.

The pre-recorded rule requires zero extra post-layout capture, lower first-send latency, no material CPU/allocation regression, zero inline template builds, correct HEAD/index/source-dependent output, and projection/installed-skill equality against fresh preparation. The work-count and correctness conditions pass; the tail exception below has explicit owner acceptance.

## Final-head controlled campaign (227432996bfbf)

Two A/A controls and five serial counterbalanced A/B pairs on the unchanged 62,000-file/~1.1 GB btrfs fixture with 35 GiB synthetic storage pressure; no task-owned builds/tests/reviews overlapped timing. All 24 layouts equal fresh projection and installed-skill preparation, with 0 inline foreground template builds.

| Metric | Baseline median / maximum | Final median / maximum | Median change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Idle | 17.62 / 40.30 s | 15.82 / 42.98 s | -10.2% |
| First create | 1.44 / 2.35 s | 1.28 / 4.46 s | -10.7% |
| First send | 36.76 / 53.58 s | 17.56 / 38.37 s | -52.2% |
| Second fresh create | 1.63 / 5.26 s | 1.52 / 2.95 s | -6.7% |
| Second fresh-session first send | 17.43 / 46.28 s | 9.06 / 15.81 s | -48.0% |
| Total cgroup CPU | 106.63 / 146.03 s | 64.49 / 105.13 s | -39.5% |
| Main CPU | 3.67 / 5.72 s | 2.86 / 6.17 s | -22.1% |
| Process CPU including workers | 84.28 / 114.24 s | 43.75 / 77.77 s | -48.1% |
| Main transient allocation | 647.29 / 652.81 MiB | 632.12 / 653.74 MiB | -2.3% |

First-send pairs (ms): 28465→16264; 44190→17557; 53578→17847; 36759→38365; 26789→15888. Four of five improve; pair 4 is +4.4%. All five second fresh-session sends improve. Extra layout checkpoint medians: 12,874→0 ms and 9,689→0 ms; local manifest operations 4→2 on every send.

Resource totals cover disjoint idle + two creates + two first sends; setup/cooldown/correctness/cleanup excluded. Main allocation is cumulative V8 allocation, not retained/all-worker memory. Maxima are five-sample nearest-rank p95, not population tails. A/A controls: first-send 79,051/38,555 ms; second fresh-session send 44,456/22,868 ms; CPU 181,668/120,223 ms; main CPU 5,031/3,698 ms; allocation 645.08/656.94 MiB.

Accepted landing exception: first-create observed maximum rises 2,353→4,460 ms (+89.5%) despite median 1,437→1,284 ms. Candidate pair 4 spent 1,977 ms in mutation/allocation admission and 1,971 ms in checkout (inclusive, not summed with children). Its idle pass lasted 42,985 ms, exceeding the unchanged 30-second fetch-freshness window. Create therefore repeated the base fetch (remote/symbolic-ref/ls-remote/cat-file plus a second git-size operation). The 51,669 ms A/A baseline idle pass produced the identical Git operation counts and a 4,768 ms create. This attributes the tail to the existing expiry path but is not a silent waiver of the >20% performance gate. No template/freshness policy changes are included.

Other increased intervals: first-create median cgroup CPU +6.7%, main CPU +0.04%; second-create main allocation +15.9%; idle main allocation +1.4%. Total measured CPU improves in all five pairs, allocation in four. Main CPU observed maximum rises 5,717→6,174 ms (+8.0%); allocation maximum 652.81→653.74 MiB (+0.14%). These increases are retained and disclosed.


## Phase attribution and real Gateway proof

The old `skills_sync` phase was left open across mount preparation and a full projection checkpoint. Its 7.9 seconds therefore did not measure a 7.9-second skills scan. The fix closes the timing boundary and carries created protected directory paths into initial baseline publication, avoiding the second checkpoint while preserving authored-empty-directory detection.

Cold source-worker/import costs remain in this harness. No causal improvement is claimed for unchanged phases. The deterministic reduction is one checkpoint and two local manifest operations per send. Nested/inclusive timings are not added to their parents.

A final compiled Gateway replay on this head completed `sessions.create`, `chat.send`, and a real model reply. It also exercises the repaired filtered-ancestor case: tracked `.agents/.DS_Store`, absent parent in the filtered template manifest, newly prepared `.agents/skills`. HEAD, source-derived dependency output, source bytes and clean index are correct; create/send have zero inline template builds and no extra layout checkpoint.

Individual create times were 974→887 ms; send-to-model-reply 47,802→13,072 ms. The baseline build is unchanged; the final candidate replay adds the explicit filtered-ancestor fixture. These single runs attribute phases and prove the transport/model path, not paired latency statistics.

Owner paths: `src/agents/sandbox/workspace-layout.ts` owns skill sync, mount preparation and conditional checkpoint; `local-workspace-projection.ts` owns session/registry binding and required reconciliation; `local-workspace-store.ts` → `local-workspace-manifest-scan.ts` owns prepared-manifest tree construction and baseline publication. Source-harness owner latency is worker acquisition/import work, not repeated filesystem discovery in the warmed Gateway. Baseline preparation builds tree records/packs from the prepared manifest, without rescanning the filesystem. The initial required reconcile remains a future owner target. No transcript-wide skills-used scan or cache was added; the #196065/#200159 failure shape is not reintroduced.

Profiles still show >50 ms consecutive non-idle sample spans in the unchanged idle path. Baseline maximum was 224.521 ms. Final candidate initial eligible-pass maximum is 278.348 ms, entirely GC; the new-tip pass has 64.803 ms including 36.917 ms GC and 13.136 ms existing manifest `computeValue`. Timer-delay maximum is 264.596 ms. Native waits/descheduling can be included in V8 spans; no sub-50-ms claim or prior acceptance waiver is made. This layout-owner change does not alter idle scheduling or template decoding. Profile SHA-256: baseline `33a1fbac281500313470c4142a2cf9c804305a14dc698ecb0b0b2a3775e9a354`, final `1d7b1823e95debc78c12a11e47137173bf818aa57e9b9792916d37c7c41e1602`.

## Validation and review repairs

The real-Git registered-source regression fails on the exact main parent with an extra canonical scan in all three origin variants. It passes the candidate, still rejects authored empty directories, and accepts pristine/cache-only source. The final filtered-ancestor regression fails on preceding head `dce09af7db4c` in all three variants and passes final head, comparing against an independently prepared filesystem manifest without another install. All 41 final affected tests pass; earlier unchanged-owner proof has 74 passing tests and two existing skips. Final `pnpm check:changed --base dce09af7db4cdb0591284884be1400c69112784d`, runtime build, and Codex P2 review pass.

ClawSweeper's missing-ancestor finding was real: a filtered `.DS_Store` could hide `.agents` from the prepared manifest even though it existed on disk. The baseline assembler now supplies only ancestors of the newly prepared paths using its existing manifest facts; it performs no scan. [Numbered response and re-review request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202803#issuecomment-7056205366) led to the final zero-item review.

CI run 44851475330 exposed a PR-caused Madge type-import cycle after extracting the layout module. `dce09af7db4c` removed the back-reference and narrowed inputs; emitted runtime code was byte-identical. Final exact-head CI is green. The earlier inherited Knip failure from #202581 was fixed by integrated main #202694; no inherited-CI exception is needed. The real 31-second freshness wait is outside timing.

## Owner acceptance — Round 5

ACCEPTED: the first-create maximum 2.35→4.46 s. It follows the unchanged fetch-expiry path, which reached 4.77 s in your A/A control, so it's not attributable to this change. Accepted in exchange for the first-send median 36.76→17.56 s and CPU −39.5%. The other disclosed resource changes and the existing idle GC/manifest pauses are accepted as disclosed.

prs.title: fix(projects): let progressing clones finish and explain Git time limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large project clones can fail while they are still transferring data, then falsely report that GitHub could not be reached. One observed subagent startup waited 601.5 seconds for workspace readiness: index-pack ran for 600.4 seconds and wrote 5,036 MB (about 8.4 MB/s) before the clone was killed. Refresh fetches have the same wall-clock/classification defect.

## User Impact

Progressing clones can run for up to 30 minutes and project fetches for up to 10 minutes. Both stop after two minutes without output. An exhausted wall-clock budget reports `clone_failed`, the actual limit, and a retry/operator-log next step; stalls and connection failures retain the existing `network` result. No protocol value or configuration option is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

On base e8296ec71260, `src/projects/project-clone-runtime.ts:27` imposed a hard ten-minute clone limit; lines 119–126 classified wall-clock timeouts as network failures. Refresh applied the same classifier after the 60-second fetch budget at lines 409–427.

Clone and project fetch now force Git progress and use one shared two-minute no-output bound. The 30-minute/10-minute backstops bound resource use while allowing sustained transfers to finish. The generic Git wrapper also serves pinned-commit and unshallow fetches, so those receive the same progress/stall treatment. Its local inspection/config/ref commands retain their previous ten-minute budget.

Deadline tracing found no shorter fixed deadline on the default admitted path: chat defaults to 48 hours; subagents default to no run timeout. The 60–300 second subagent RPC response deadline is explicitly non-cancelling. Workspace preparation uses the admitted source's abort signal; configured/per-run cancellation remains authoritative. The project lease renews rather than imposing a total runtime ceiling. No live host or Gateway was contacted.

The existing 256 KiB capture retains a bounded tail and does not terminate on overflow unless explicitly requested; no process-runner change is needed. The existing retry owner retries neither timeout kind. Ordinary connection-error retries continue sharing their original total deadline. Docs searches found no statement of these project limits or error text requiring an update.

Both clone and refresh timeout rows expected `clone_failed` and limit text, but received `network` / “could not reach GitHub.” Cold wrapper wall time: 50.34 seconds, including 37.54 seconds of worker compilation.

prs.title: fix: keep known MCP catalogs from delaying new chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A new chat can spend ten seconds rediscovering tools from an MCP server that was already discovered successfully. An unresponsive catalog request blocks the first model request, even when healthy servers have already answered.

## User Impact

New chats, subagents, and Code Mode can immediately use a previously discovered MCP catalog while it refreshes in the background. Later turns receive successful catalog changes. A never-discovered server still uses the existing bounded listing deadline; its existing typed failure is included in the current model turn and remains visible in the tool inventory. Calls to unavailable servers retain the existing tool-error behavior and recovery guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lead decision by the Team perf-loop lead (an agent acting under Peter's standing unattended instruction), not Peter's.

Keep successful catalogs in the existing bundle-MCP manager, bounded by its existing runtime limit and keyed by server configuration, endpoint, and auth scope. Unchanged config reloads retain these facts; manager disposal clears them. Existing per-server concurrency and listing deadlines stay unchanged. Native capability-bound discovery remains private. No new configuration, persistent cache, or production schema change.

The tradeoff is intentional: a turn may advertise the last successful schema while refresh is pending. That turn's catalog remains stable; refreshed schemas apply to later turns. A ready connection can execute a known tool without waiting for catalog refresh. Catalog recovery moves out of send preparation while existing transport-specific tool-call recovery remains. Production source grows by 54 lines to retain bounded identity-scoped facts and expose existing diagnostics; the runtime module itself shrinks by one line.

Related overlap: #137594. This does not depend on that PR or add its Tool Search diagnostics; it uses the existing catalog diagnostic type.

## Evidence

Real HTTP MCP servers through manager acquisition and materialization, on a synthetic btrfs fixture with a 35 GiB agent database, 5,000 sessions, and 62,000 workspace files (1.14 GB). Five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, with healthy A/A controls:

| Materialization | Before median | After median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Known catalog, hung list | 10,049.057 ms | 1.940 ms |
| Known catalog, 3-second list | 3,009.913 ms | 1.804 ms |
| First-ever healthy list | 7.169 ms | 7.270 ms |
| Known healthy catalog | 8.368 ms | 1.998 ms |

Foreground CPU for the hung case falls from 147.205 to 8.048 ms; refresh-inclusive CPU is 154.898 versus 130.659 ms. Both arms make one initialize and one list request. Refresh work moves off preparation; it is not eliminated. Five-sample ranges and A/A controls show busy-host jitter; these are not population-tail estimates.

The retained-catalog and model-notice regressions fail on exact parent `2b5f1a88ba81e03d51010065c836f48490ebb498`. Focused runtime, reload, Code Mode, prefix-stability, and prompt-context tests pass (144 tests). MCP App browser test and both real Control UI/standalone conformance cases pass, including refresh overlap and cancellation.

A real isolated Gateway/QA channel with a local synthetic inference server delivered every expected reply. Across ten fresh-session sends after seed, first outbound median falls **10,293 → 252 ms**, final outbound **10,300.5 → 260 ms**. A separate first-ever hung run completed all eleven sends at the existing timeout; all eleven actual provider requests contained the unavailable notice and next step.

Separate sampled-allocation profiles (foreground / refresh-inclusive bytes): hung **14,897,816 / 18,062,632 → 3,083,512 / 17,424,304**; slow **4,705,328 / 4,901,840 → 3,531,696 / 4,714,144**; healthy **4,169,656 / 4,321,720 → 3,034,120 / 3,925,608**. These are diagnostic samples, not allocation tail estimates.

Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2. `pnpm check:changed` completed; its new test-array lint finding was fixed and targeted type-aware lint/format passed. All other gates pass except five unrelated unused exports, reproduced on the exact parent. Final exact-head CI run 44864878083 passed (60 successful jobs, zero failures). ClawSweeper revision 3 reports zero findings and zero open items on the final head. Introducing changes: publication transport export from #202654 (`39bcc3cc44447`); approval/session permission exports from #201615 (`2b5f1a88ba81e`); workspace-link exports from #202534 (`eb56951a4ca9e`, subsequently repaired by #202879). These are recorded main regressions, not ignored test noise. No task-caused failure is accepted.


Healthy repeat after our build/browser jobs finished: five further pairs measured median **8.557 → 7.781 ms**, maximum **15.124 → 8.566 ms**, foreground CPU **19.577 → 20.037 ms**, total CPU **20.003 → 20.390 ms**. The original candidate tail outlier and this baseline outlier are both retained; no consistent healthy-path regression was found. A/A controls were 8.022/9.131 ms baseline and 10.777/6.699 ms candidate. Other lanes still shared the host.

Reproduce owner measurements with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/mcp-materialize-measure.ts --workspace <synthetic-workspace> --mode hung` (also `slow`, `healthy`; `--cold` for a new identity; `--profile <dir>` separately). Gateway workload: `scripts/bench-channel-turn.mts --mcp-list-delay-ms=-1 --state-dir <synthetic-state> --workspace-dir <synthetic-workspace> --resources`, with `--mcp-first-ever` for cold timeout notice proof. No production data or access used.


The initial CI run exposed task-caused consumer failures, repaired before landing: prompt fixtures now include bundle-tools state, SSE tests observe asynchronous catalog publication, and disconnected stdio calls preserve their existing immediate typed error. Real configured-server tests now prove ready calls overlap a held refresh and the next request after grant revocation or lineage reassignment is rejected before server I/O. The unchanged post-await authorization-fence test also passes. All 54 tests across the six initially failed CI files, both late prompt-admission cases, and 75 owner tests pass; Codex reviewed the complete staged correction with no actionable P0–P2 findings. These failures were not classified as inherited.

A late native-discovery shard also exposed a real shutdown race: catalog reuse allows policy to retire an excluded stdio server during spawn admission. Graceful close previously aborted that admission, losing the process owner’s cleanup receipt. Graceful close now joins startup ownership; forced shutdown retains cancellation. The real app-server/CLI lifecycle test verifies retained calls and complete child retirement, and a held-startup transport regression covers the boundary. The transport repair adds zero production lines. Final transport/process-cleanup proof: 34 tests pass, one Windows-only test skipped locally. The held-startup regression fails on exact parent and passes with the repair.

Landed via native scripts/pr as `52934fb347d00592b947ada9f4a9bfdd15dbcddf`, from reviewed/CI head `ad7e28b5d06ddb1f9b1ede1beff0bd43eebf8bea`. Initial failed CI run 44861019763 was repaired; final run 44864878083 passed. [ClawSweeper final-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202902#issuecomment-7056803667) has zero open items; [numbered response and runtime capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202902#issuecomment-7057098414).

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.



## Round 3 (ClawSweeper re-review findings + live-Gateway proof)

Head `1e502cd5e72` (synced with upstream/main, 0 behind). All review findings addressed:

- **[P1] Historical catalog hashes preserved** — the companion table leaked into predecessor schema generation, replacing historical hashes. New generation-owned transform `withLegacySkillSelectionCompanionAbsent` strips the unreleased table + indexes from every predecessor layout (`getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema`, `state-before-provision-source`, `state-before-bootstrap-deferred` inputs). Historical inputs are byte-identical to upstream; the historical hash assertions are restored untouched; generated SQLite catalogs regenerated (228/235 inputs byte-identical, only current-layout inputs changed, as intended).
- **[P2] Input truncation marked before digest suffix** — names cut at the 64-char input budget are now marked truncated up front, so `aaa…(64)+alpha` vs `aaa…(64)+beta` keep distinct audit identities (regression test added).
- **[P2] Canonical decoder reused** — the writer owned a copied run/tool/message decoder; it now imports `parseAgentRunRow`/`rowToAuditEvent` from `audit-event-row.ts`, with companion decoding confined to `rowToStoredAuditEvent` + the distinct companion row shape.
- **[P2] Bootstrap privacy extraction removed** — the unrelated `workspace-bootstrap-privacy.ts` extraction is reverted; `src/agents/workspace.ts` is byte-identical to upstream again.
- **[P3] Stale sequence cache invalidated** — companion allocation consumes shared sequences outside the retention fast path (including duplicate-source attempts); the writer now drops the cached high-water mark on the skill path (regression test: ledger row after a skill write reports its true stored sequence).
- **Stale generated gateway validators** — the PR updated the protocol schemas but not the compiled predicates, so `kind=skill_selection` / `status=observed` failed gateway validation (2 gateway tests red). Regenerated via `scripts/generate-gateway-validators.mts`; 21/21 gateway tests green.
- **Test hygiene** — the `PRIVATE_PROMPT_CONTENT` absence assertion now supplies the sentinel as input (prompt/toolInput/skillFileContents); the unrelated expired-identity rendering case is removed from this PR.
- **Data-model compatibility proof** — new regression test builds a v39 pre-companion database with a stored legacy row, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, row intact), records a skill_selection (shared sequence continues at 2), and reads both rows back.

### Live-Gateway behavior proof (new, real Gateway + shipped CLI)

Production chain on a temp state dir — real tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` through `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` → observer → recorder → store → **running Gateway** (fresh build, `--auth none`, loopback) → shipped CLI:

```
$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection
TIME                          KIND             STATUS    AGENT  RUN           ACTION                     SELECTED
2026-11-14T23:42:01.167Z      skill_selection  -         -       observed  main   proof-run-1   skill.selection.observed  skill:proof--demo

$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json
{"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":2,"eventId":"2c71cbfc-…","sourceSequence":1,
"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main",
"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof","sessionId":"proof-session-1","runId":"proof-run-1",
"action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection",
"actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"proof--demo"}]}
```

Stored rows: ledger `agent.run.started` (seq 1) → companion `skill.selection.observed` (shared seq 2, `main`/`agent:main:proof`/`proof-session-1`/`proof-run-1`/`proof--demo`) → ledger `agent.run.finished` (seq 3). Metadata-only, no prompt/tool content persisted. (An LLM-driven variant was attempted with local ollama `qwen2.5:7b`/`gemma4:12b`; the agent loop stalled at the reply watchdog, so the trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool call — every stage after it is production code on a live Gateway.)

### Verification on this head

- `test/scripts/sqlite-schema-catalog-equivalence.test.ts` 203/203
- `runtime-skill-selection` + `audit-events.skill-selection*` incl. new upgrade/sequence tests green
- `audit-events` (37), `commands/audit` (36), `gateway/server-methods/audit` (21/21) green
- `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files, line-cap ratchet clean vs upstream merge-base


## Round 4 (re-review findings, head `883b4d8d003`)

Both P2 findings fixed, plus the requested proof/test adjustments:

- **[P2] Buffered run starts retained until acceptance** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path now keeps the buffered start for the existing paired-settlement contract when `writer.record(start)` returns false, while skill observations still record independently. Regression test: with a rejecting writer, the terminal settles as one paired `recordRun(start, finish)` instead of a lone finish.
- **[P2] Companion counts bound to transaction outcomes** (`audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — tentative counts stage `rollback`/`invalidate` hooks through `stageSqliteTransactionState`, as the canonical ledger does. Negative control verified: without the fix a rolled-back overflow batch leaves the cap violated at 100,001 rows; with it the next insert trims honestly to 98,976. Covered by `drops tentative companion counts when their batch rolls back`.
- **Upgrade proof targets v2026.11.3** — confirmed the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 (no companion table), so the regression test builds exactly that layout, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, `schema_meta` intact), and shows the stored audit row plus continued shared sequencing.
- **Flagged low-value tests removed** — unrelated date/empty-limit CLI variants and the full marker-construction equality case are out; encoding, truncation, and production-boundary coverage retained.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains best-effort: local ollama models (`qwen2.5:7b`, `gemma4:12b`) stall at the agent reply watchdog in this environment, so the trigger stays the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it (observer → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) is production code, demonstrated in Round 3.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7 (incl. rollback + v2026.11.3 upgrade), audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 5 (re-review: settlement intent + true v2026.11.3 fixture, head `4fd73e177bc`)

- **Buffered run-start settlement intent documented** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path flushes the buffered start as a best effort so the ledger holds the run before its independent skill rows arrive (readers join by run; legacy run/tool views stay coherent), while rejection retains the start for the existing paired settlement boundary. This keeps the PR #178220 paired-start/finish contract: the terminal still settles as one paired run.
- **Upgrade fixture is the true v2026.11.3 layout** — verified the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 without the companion table (release commit `50330aa9cf5`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 39`, no `audit_skill_selection_events`). The regression test now builds the fixture from the current schema minus only the unreleased companion table at version 40 (matching the release lineage), opens it with the current build, and asserts: `user_version`/`schema_meta` intact, a stored workspace setting row byte-identical, the stored audit row readable, lazy companion creation on first skill write, and continued shared sequencing with correct readback.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains environment-blocked (local ollama models stall at the agent reply watchdog; xAI cloud models need the `xai` extension whose dist build is broken by a pre-existing missing-`@solidjs/compiler` resolution from root, unrelated to this PR). The live-Gateway proof in Round 3 (production tool boundary → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) stands as the in-environment maximum.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7, audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 6 (head `a71b0be6d94`)

- **True v2026.11.3 upgrade fixture** — the reviewer correctly noted the published v2026.11.3 is schema v22 (verified: release tag → commit `847611dcaa3`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 22`, no companion table), not v39. The compat regression test now builds the fixture from `getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema(22)` (verified to reproduce the release's `audit_events`/`schema_meta`/`workspace_setup_state`/`config_machine_state` tables byte-identically; only later-dropped device/gateway tables differ, which audit admission does not touch). The fixture migrates 22→40 (backup custody via the standard test-support helper, as a real install would back up first) with `schema_meta`, a stored workspace setting, and the legacy audit row byte-identical, then records a skill_selection via lazy companion DDL with continued shared sequencing and correct readback.
- **Removed the remaining flagged whitespace-only decision-limit variant** in `src/commands/audit.test.ts` (restored the upstream single-case form).

Verification on this head: skill-selection 8/8, audit-events + commands/audit green, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 7 — product upgrade run from published v2026.11.3 (head `a71b0be6d94`, no new commits; proof only)

- **Genuine release write**: ran the published v2026.11.3 source (release tag → `847611dcaa3`, schema v22) to create a state dir and record a legacy agent run through its production audit writer (`sequences 1–2, run release-run-1, user_version 22`).

The trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it is production code on live Gateways, now demonstrated across a genuine published-release upgrade boundary.



## Round 8 — P2 rollback fix + missing proof piece (head `d541860e07a`)

- **[P2] Clear schema readiness when lazy creation rolls back** (`src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — `ensureSkillSelectionAuditSchemaOnce` now binds the `skillSelectionSchemaEstablished` flag to the owning SQLite transaction via `stageSqliteTransactionState` (rollback/invalidate drop both the readiness flag and the warm row-count). prs.body:
Fixes #202842
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202842

## What Problem This Solves

TTS automatic-mode normalization imports the broad core configuration schema to validate four mode values.

## User Impact

No intended TTS behavior change. Enum order, parsing, the exported Set and public SDK contracts stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing schema into a narrow canonical leaf. Core imports and re-exports that same object; normalization imports the leaf directly. The fourth file adds the leaf to the maintained PR-wrapper extraction inventory so extracted tooling retains its runtime dependency.

## Evidence

- Fresh independent ClawSweeper source review covered the full four-file range at `0aa91005decd9e3c901646aa9eda1927f29e0c8b`, with no actionable findings. Both commits have verified signatures and used normal commit hooks.
- The documented inventory preflight and all 23 existing eager-import-closure cases passed on bytes identical to the committed correction. Both macOS-applicable failed provisioning cases also passed; no test or guard changed.
- Reused unchanged-runtime proof from `cfd512531e73ee99fa13e915425d3686e708ddf1`: 34 TTS configuration/runtime-routing/tagged-dispatch cases, targeted core types, type-aware lint and formatting passed. Only the wrapper inventory changes after that head.
- One local `pnpm run build:ci-artifacts` passed at that incoming head, including runtime output, CLI import checks, package/Plugin SDK declarations, all 163 public SDK subpaths, UI and metadata. This remains reused build proof; the full unified declaration build was not run.
- The build's maintained report-only UI budget check reported six overages: largest CSS gzip, total CSS gzip/raw, chat boot JS requests/gzip and new boot JS gzip. These observations remain recorded without base/head attribution or a performance claim; no budget or check was changed.
- [Original CI run 44860999394](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44860999394) failed two wrapper/provisioning jobs because the new schema leaf was omitted from the inventory. The one-row correction addresses that PR-induced omission; the original failures remain recorded.
- [Corrected-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44863341382) and required security gates passed at `0aa91005decd9e3c901646aa9eda1927f29e0c8b`. [Linux provisioning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44863341382/job/136721892522) explicitly passed all three previously failing provisioning cases, including the Linux-only unsupported-source-filesystem case. No platform substitution was used.

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

Tracking: cbire880/the-roost#2473, OP#1548
