prs.title: fix(update): retire database snapshots of earlier updates after a verified update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Each update can leave a full copy of the databases beside the installation, in a `.databases` directory. Only the creating run's own verified completion removed it. Snapshots kept by failed updates, by updates whose automatic rollback was unavailable, and by older updaters stayed forever. On one host, eight of them held 63 GiB.

## User Impact

User impact: after a later update is verified healthy, update cleanup removes the snapshot directories earlier updates left behind, both automatically and through `openclaw update cleanup` (and the Gateway's `update.cleanup`, including dry run). The ones it keeps are listed with their size and reason. The latest verified update's own snapshot waits for the next verified update. Snapshots of a Git checkout outside the home directory are not found and stay, as do snapshots no listed update recorded. With `database.postgres.recoveryCaptures: "server"`, cleanup drops a snapshot's PostgreSQL capture schemas before deleting it, and keeps and reports the snapshot when that drop fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

A snapshot directory's name carries a transaction id, not a run id, and nothing inside it names a run (`schema-discovery-ownership.json` maps databases to owners only). The only record linking it to an update is the `database snapshot` location in update history. Cleanup now reads that location and treats a snapshot as superseded once a verified successful update started after its run finished. That is the rule original-state captures already follow, decided by run order and never by file times.

- Kept and reported: a snapshot of an unfinished run, of a run with a pending recovery, of the latest verified run or anything after it, and a snapshot-named directory no listed run recorded (`orphan-database-snapshot`; only file times could order it).
- Deletion reuses the capture retirement path: no symlinks, same directory identity as when selected, same cleanup authority.
- PostgreSQL server captures keep the lifecycle their owning update gives them (#196236). A snapshot's `<image>.postgres` export manifests are the only record of the capture schemas on the server. Cleanup passes them to the existing `discardPostgresSchemaCaptures` first, with the configuration cleanup already reads. If the drop fails, the directory stays and the item reports `failed` / `database-snapshot-retirement-failed` with `PostgreSQL capture cleanup remains pending at <directory>`; a later cleanup retries.
- Previous install roots are in scope only when a run recorded a location that still resolves. Update history shortens the home directory to `~` and redacts other install roots to `[path]`, so a checkout outside the home directory cannot be resolved. When the OpenClaw home and the OS home differ, `~` names two directories and attributes none.
- An earlier install root that is unreadable, or whose path is no longer a directory path, is skipped instead of failing the whole cleanup inventory.

Decisions for the maintainer:

1. Attribution parses a path-redacted diagnostic. A structured, unredacted receipt in the run record would also cover checkouts outside the home directory, but needs a schema change and would not help snapshots already on disk.
2. A run's own verified success does not release its snapshot here, because the updater says non-restorable snapshots remain available after activation. Captures do release on their own success.
3. Orphans are report-only; `--include-unmanifested` cannot select them.
4. Status now counts these snapshots under update captures. Doctor's `core/doctor/update-snapshots` check still advises manual removal.
5. The server-capture drop uses the current configuration's connection, as `openclaw update finish` does for its own receipt. Accepted: if the configuration now names a different PostgreSQL server than the one the snapshot was captured on, `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS` finds nothing there, the snapshot is deleted, and the capture schema on the old server stays.

## Evidence

- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-database-snapshot-cleanup.test.ts` (new) runs the real `updateCleanupCommand` and `cleanupCompletedUpdateRecovery` over a temp home with real update-history rows:
  - dry run reports each snapshot's run, bytes and reason and deletes nothing;
  - `--yes` and automatic cleanup remove only the two superseded snapshots (one under a previous checkout root, one package snapshot outside home);
  - kept: pending recovery, latest verified run, a failure after it, an unfinished run, an orphan; untouched: a non-updater name, a redacted-root snapshot, a recorded path replaced by a symlink, and home-relative snapshots while two homes are in play.
- Red before the fix: the preview returned no snapshots and every directory survived.
- Passing: the new file and `update-command-capture-cleanup.test.ts` (12 tests), `update-automatic-cleanup.test.ts`, `recovery-disk-usage.test.ts`, `update-backup-cleanup-policy.test.ts`; `pnpm tsgo:core`, the `cli-update` and `commands` test typecheck leaves, lint and format on touched files, `pnpm docs:check-links`.
- Review fixes in `a16170a`, each red on `5fb7e5a` and green with the fix:
  - Replaced install root: a recorded snapshot's former root is now a regular file, so inspecting its parent fails with `ENOTDIR`. Before: `openclaw update cleanup` exited with an error and removed nothing. After: that snapshot is not listed and the other superseded snapshot is retired.
  - Server captures, at the cleanup command with the drop stubbed: the drop receives the snapshot's export directory while its manifest still exists. When it rejects, the snapshot stays `failed`, the command exits 1, and a snapshot without server captures is still retired; the next cleanup removes it. Before: the drop was never called.
  - Server captures against real PostgreSQL 17 (`src/infra/database-engine/backup-schema-capture.test.ts`, through `scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs` and a disposable `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` container): a real update capture with `postgresSchemaCaptures` creates a `restore_…` schema, and `updateCleanupCommand({ yes: true })` runs twice. With an unreachable connection the schema and manifest both remain and the item reports `failed` with the pending message. With the real connection the capture schema is dropped, the live store's schema remains and the directory is gone. Before: the first cleanup deleted the directory and left the schema on the server. All 10 tests in the file pass.
  - `96e891b` shortens these tests to stay within the 400-line test budget (+399 net) without removing a case; `a16170a` had failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` at +447. Both test files were rerun on it, the PostgreSQL one against the same container setup.
  - `pnpm check:changed` on `96e891b`, with its dead-export scan skipped: typecheck, lint, format and the ratchets pass. On `a16170a` that scan failed on `extensions/knowledge/src/scribe-schedule-dialog.ts: CronSchedule`, a file this PR does not touch.
- Real-behaviour proof, through the real CLI and Gateway in Linux containers (Crabbox `local-container`, `node:24.22.1-trixie@sha256:f1e034976f94…ca38be`): a Git checkout cloned and built from source, state in the account's home, real `openclaw update` runs against real upstream commits. It ran on `5fb7e5a`, before the review fixes, and was not repeated on the later commits.
  - Scenario: the Gateway runs by hand from the checkout while `openclaw update` updates it. The updater cannot confirm the Gateway stopped, so the run keeps its `.artifacts/dist-runtime.openclaw-update-<uuid>.tmp.databases` snapshot. This happens once under `~/Projects/openclaw/.worktrees/live-main-ba9f1ea` and, after the install moves, twice under `~/Projects/openclaw`. Then the Gateway service is installed and a later `openclaw update` finishes verified (`serviceRunning`, `versionMatch`, `settled`, `coreReady`, no plugin errors).
  - Base `44ec89e`: the three snapshots (13.4 MB) are still on disk after the verified update. `openclaw update cleanup --dry-run --json` lists no `database-snapshot` artifact before or after it, and `--yes` removes nothing.
  - Head `5fb7e5a`: before any verified update, the dry run lists all three as `protected`, `awaiting-later-verified-update`, each with its run and bytes. The verified update's automatic cleanup then reports `Removed ~/Projects/openclaw/.worktrees/live-main-ba9f1ea/.artifacts/dist-runtime.openclaw-update-6d355544-….tmp.databases (4272383 logical bytes)` and the two under `~/Projects/openclaw` (4579583 bytes each). No snapshot directory remains.
  - Upgrade: an install of the base commit whose verified update installs this change. That update's automatic cleanup removed both earlier snapshots, including the one under the previous root.
  - Receipt wording of older updaters: in each run the first two update-history rows, written by the real updates, were then rewritten in the state database to the shapes recorded on the affected host (run `failed` / `post-update-failed`, a failed `database rollback` step after the receipt). One carries `…databases. Verified successful activation removes these snapshots; otherwise retain them with the update's recovery artifacts.` (builds of Oct 3 to Oct 20 2026), the other `…removes these snapshots only if automatic restoration remains available; otherwise retain them…` (Oct 27 2026 onward). Both were attributed and retired. The third row was left as written (`These snapshots require manual recovery and remain available after successful activation.`).
  - Substituted: the container has no systemd, so the service manager is the repository's upgrade e2e stand-in (`scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor`). The row rewrite above is the only state edit.
  - Leases `cbx_5fe14464ed65` (base, run `run_09360523664e0118af391b2adfa6b29f`), `cbx_892d7fe68601` (head, `run_c4da15d56c0371e8c8dc3e1e6e433611`), `cbx_f37a9e6d9f22` (upgrade, `run_811e06130265fc675fc902ea9934d0a7`); all exited 0 and were stopped.
- Observed limit: update history's secret redaction can mask part of a long checkout path (a first attempt recorded `/srv/p…law/.worktrees/…` for a checkout under `/srv/proof/xhead/home/Projects/openclaw`). Such a receipt does not resolve, so that snapshot stays, like one under a redacted root.
- Not proven: no run against the affected host's own update history, no upgrade from the latest stable release (the upgrade above is between source builds), Windows `~\` expansion, and receipt wording of updaters before Oct 3 2026. Through the real CLI, `openclaw update cleanup --yes` never had a snapshot candidate to remove, because automatic cleanup removed them first; that path and the kept latest-verified snapshot are covered by the test files only. The server-capture drop was not run through a full `openclaw update` cycle on a PostgreSQL install, and automatic cleanup of a server-capture snapshot is covered through the shared retirement path only. An install root that fails with `EACCES` is handled by the same guard as `ENOTDIR` but has no test.

prs.title: improve: recommend Gemini 4 Neon after Carbon
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gemini 4 Neon is missing from the curated model recommendations. The reviewed model-catalog advisory recommends including it as a distinct option without displacing the existing choices.

## User Impact

Users whose providers serve Gemini 4 Neon can see it among the recommended models after the next compatible hosted-catalog refresh. Neon is fifth in the global shortlist, immediately after Gemini 4 Carbon; every existing entry and its relative order are preserved. Availability, runtime defaults, model capabilities, and pricing are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: feat(gateway): connect approved trusted-proxy CLI and TUI devices within their grant
prs.body:
Related to #199692. Stacked on #199698.

## What problem this solves

A CLI or TUI guest approved only for session access can ask for broader operator scopes on its first connection. That files a scope-upgrade request for access the administrator already chose to withhold.

## How it works

Set `gateway.auth.trustedProxy.narrowToDeviceGrant` to let a paired CLI or TUI connect with the intersection of the requested scopes and its approved grant. The Gateway checks the trusted-proxy identity, paired device key, and effective operator role. The connection must have no browser `Origin`. The hello response reports the admitted scopes, so the client can use its session permissions on the first connection. A request for broader scopes with no overlap still follows the scope-upgrade flow. An administrator can use this option with manual enrollment or configure enrollment separately through `trustedProxy.deviceAutoApprove`.

The option defaults to `false` and applies only to devices with a current grant. Device enrollment and browser connections follow their existing policies. The TUI can store a device token under this opt-in. Human operators governed by named-role policy still receive no device token. Reserved Session Share grants use the dedicated publication-transport admission path.

Device tokens can authenticate a direct connection until revoked. `openclaw security audit` reports `gateway.trusted_proxy_narrow_to_device_grant` when this option is on. Keep the trusted proxy as the only Gateway ingress and remove a guest device when access ends. The core configuration baseline gains one boolean key, from 2,666 to 2,667. The trusted-proxy guide documents the option and its token behavior.

## Evidence

- **Main vs. PR head.** On `53fe7a0b11bd`, an approved session-only guest's broad TUI request files a scope-upgrade request. On `013f2b4e0e8f` with the opt-in enabled, the TUI receives only its paired session scope and a device token, with no pending upgrade. A CLI requesting `operator.read` receives `operator.sessions.read` when its grant covers session access. The option-off test on the PR head still files the upgrade. These cases run against the Gateway WebSocket server. The main run uses the option-off case from the PR test suite. [Exact base-to-head diff](https://github.com/daniel-lxs/openclaw/compare/53fe7a0b11bd656cfb8251dd4a311e9a59d10b52...013f2b4e0e8ffaa7d677eb65b849f2d22dab02c7)
- **Checks on `013f2b4e0e8f`.** 275 focused tests passed on macOS arm64. Separate suites covered the opt-in Cloudflare Access JWT verifier, trusted-proxy grant narrowing, Session Share publication request admission, CLI and TUI scope selection, config, and audit behavior. Core typecheck and all 12 baseline ratchets passed.
- **Shipped TUI and stable upgrade.** The runtime run at `a5b50ef7ff73` upgrades two paired guests and their Gateway from the published `2026.11.6` package. It preserves the settings, credentials, and grants. One guest reuses its stable-issued token. The other receives a token on the first connection and reuses it on restart. Both can run `/sessions` on the admitted WebSocket after identity resolution. The Access and GitHub responses came from test fixtures. [Upgrade evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199699#issuecomment-7052127488)

prs.title: fix: iOS reconnects keep replaying rejected push registrations
prs.body:
## Readiness update — 2026-11-21

**Still draft.** A local refresh against main `0abe03d` passed **111 focused Gateway/APNs tests across 5 files** and native localization verification. It has not been pushed. The refreshed SQLite catalog suite reported **11 failures**: the new `apns_registrations.relay_rejection_reason` column leaks into historical schema projections. Removing only that line reproduces both pinned v39/v40 SQL hashes; the corresponding historical catalog entries are missing from the candidate.

**Maintainer decision needed:** accept the persisted rejection design under the [storage review checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes), or choose a design without new durable state. The proposal adds a nullable column to the existing registration owner, with no backfill or index; null is not delivery proof. An in-memory marker avoids the new field but forgets rejection after restart. If persistence is accepted, preserve the historical catalogs and qualify supported SQLite/PostgreSQL upgrade and rollback before marking ready.

[Native simulator tests and lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191565#issuecomment-6691225879) and [Diagnostics captures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191565#issuecomment-6769314532) cover the published head. The final candidate still needs an authorized official-relay-capable build on a physical iPhone, actual alert receipt and background wake after a genuinely rejected registration, and a hosted check of whether reenrollment changes the relay handle/grant. Then recheck exact-head CI and request a fresh ClawSweeper verdict.

## Current maintainer review — delivery proof still missing

[Detailed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191565#pullrequestreview-5813972422). The existing rejection-persistence regression fails on main and passes on the private current-main integration. The iOS/Watch build, 24 native tests, 310 selected backend tests, core typecheck, scoped lint and generated PostgreSQL verification passed.

**Still Draft.** These tests do not prove restored alerts or background wake. The laboratory build is ad-hoc `localSandbox`; an authorized official signed physical-device run and hosted renewal-identity qualification are still required. The persistent recovery/retention contract and released-version upgrade/rollback also remain unqualified. No fabricated recovery screenshots, source fixes or merge were performed.

Tested author head `fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5`, private integration `5e97c3c229d6039fcf3ce77291f7cdf0b52be2f9`, frozen main `4d67ec34f59707df2d777912e9de9abd8d44aa32`. Later main `243e1c65` has no relevant input changes.

<details>
<summary>Original proposal and historical evidence</summary>

## Takeover coordination — publication unblocked 2026-11-06

The reviewed source is now published in this same PR at [fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5). Its public GitHub tree exactly matches reviewed/tested tree2975004a114019d7df70785d1f9875c17d8454f2. The final PR diff contains only the32 intended product files. Generated Bun caches caught during publication verification were removed in a follow-up commit; history was preserved. The publication gate was cleared under the authorized request; no global permissions were changed.

@ekinnee — thank you for the [579aa20d product candidate](https://github.com/ekinnee/openclaw/commit/579aa20dc9d9d2167c875de325d2c49435cfea79) and [source-bound handoff/checklist at6296e75f](https://github.com/ekinnee/openclaw/tree/6296e75fdf53bbba143c699a020cbc307a458456/handoff/pr191565). The APNs-specific cleanup was incorporated; unrelated demo/macOS baseline cleanup already superseded by upstream and evidence-only handoff files were not imported.

**Testing help requested:** if your Mac setup remains available, can you rerun the same selected Swift suites and simulator build on fc1fa6bc? Your earlier28-test/native-build result remains bound to579aa20d, not this refreshed source. Separately, can you run the signed-device checklist on your approved iPhone/test Gateway once a signing maintainer supplies an authorized official-relay-capable build tied to the final SHA? Personal Team signing alone is not that proof. Please confirm whether you can install the authorized build through its supported distribution channel. We need actual notification receipt and background-wake observations across rejected-cache recovery, reconnect/relaunch and bounded repeat attempts, without reinstalling/re-pairing as recovery. Share sanitized results only—no signing keys, tokens, grants or private device identifiers.

**Still draft:** maintainer acceptance of the recovery/persistence contract, official signing, current-source native/visual/device qualification and final-head CI remain pending. Restored notification delivery is not claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Official iOS apps can reconnect successfully while continuing to reuse relay enrollment that APNs rejected with `410 Unregistered`, leaving alerts and background wakes unavailable.

## User Impact

This proposes bounded, registration-scoped recovery and an in-app retry path without reinstalling or re-pairing. Permission, successful publication, and delivery health remain separate: renewed/published registration is explicitly **delivery unverified**.

**Draft — not ready to merge.** Maintainer acceptance of the recovery/persistence contract, native Swift build/test/lint checks, before/after UI screenshots, and signed official-device receipt testing remain outstanding. This PR does **not** establish that notification delivery is restored.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway preserves typed relay rejection on the existing registration owner. Republishing the same enrollment cannot erase the rejection merely by advancing its timestamp. Test pushes, wakes, and approval sends share the rejection-recording path; a stale result cannot poison a replacement enrollment.
- iOS consumes the existing authenticated `node.event` result, requests a current APNs token, and forces fresh relay enrollment for one automatic recovery cycle per unchanged token/scope. The existing publication flow serializes overlapping callbacks; failures stop automatic renewal and expose **Retry notification setup** in Diagnostics.
- Scoped Keychain enrollment caches retain rejected enrollment and consumed budgets across relaunches and Gateway switches. A matching shipped singleton is moved only after its scoped copy is saved. A new handle alone does not reset the budget; explicit manual retry or a changed token can authorize another attempt.
- Direct APNs behavior and unrelated registrations, pairings, Gateway credentials, and App Attest keys are preserved. No new RPC, configuration option, dependency, or version bump. Missing-registration #146791 is not folded into this fix.

## Evidence

**Current published source:** HEAD fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5, base2dc6deb7dd2fae392c03da64da175cc842ccdd70, tree2975004a114019d7df70785d1f9875c17d8454f2. The32-file patch independently reproduced the exact tree; the published GitHub tree and required human credit were verified. This is not current-source native build/device or broad-CI proof. Earlier dated results below remain historical/prior-head evidence.


**Revision qualification (2026-11-03):** `pnpm test src/infra/push-apns.store.test.ts src/infra/push-apns.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.apns-registration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **52 tests across 3 files**, 66.82s wrapper wall time. This proves those local boundaries, not the hosted relay, WebSocket authentication handshake, iOS consent/route revocation before actual enrollment/publication, or device receipt. Fresh independent review of the complete candidate completed three chunks with no P0–P2 findings.

The primary regression failed before the production change for the intended reason: after a fixed relay `410 Unregistered` response, store reconstruction and unchanged enrollment republication had no retained `relayRejection`. The seven existing store tests passed on that baseline.

prs.title: fix: send Telegram media from the selected agent on multi-agent setups
prs.body:
Closes #202794

## What Problem This Solves

On a setup where every agent is configured explicitly (`agents.ownership: "explicit"`), `openclaw message send --channel telegram --media <file>` fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner`, even though the account is bound to one agent and the same command without `--media` sends fine.

## User Impact

Sending a local image or file to Telegram from the CLI works again on multi-agent setups, using the agent the account is bound to. Text-only sends and single-agent setups are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host already selects the agent for the send and hands it to the Telegram action, but the action did not pass it on. Without a session key, staging the attachment then had no owner to resolve. The action now passes the selected agent into the outbound session, as the Discord and Nextcloud Talk plugins already do. The session and media-access setup moves into `action-delivery-context.ts` because `action-runtime.ts` is over its line cap and the ratchet rejects growth.

## Evidence

Scenario: `openclaw message send --channel telegram --account default --target 123 --message "test chart" --media <file in the ops agent workspace> --json`.

Run from source with `pnpm openclaw` against an isolated Gateway (own state directory and config, loopback port). The config has two agents with explicit ownership (`main`, `ops`), a binding of the `default` Telegram account to `ops`, and `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "ops"`, as in the report. Telegram's Bot API is a local stand-in (`channels.telegram.apiRoot`) that logs each method it receives, so no bot token or Telegram account was used. Before is this PR's parent commit `504f4a6ed` (Gateway and CLI), after is this PR's head `bdd98b6ff` (Gateway and CLI).

Before:

```text
AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId.
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "AgentSelectionRequiredError: ..." } }
```

After:

```text
{ "action": "send", "channel": "telegram", "dryRun": false, "handledBy": "plugin", "messageId": "1",
  "payload": { "ok": true, "messageId": "1", "chatId": "123", "receipt": {} } }
```

The stand-in Bot API logged one `sendPhoto` for the "after" run and none for the "before" run.

- New test `sends local media for the selected agent on an explicit multi-agent fleet` in `action-runtime.test.ts` calls the registered Telegram `send` action with the selected agent and a local image on that fleet. On the base commit it fails with the same `AgentSelectionRequiredError`; with this change it passes.
- `action-runtime.test.ts` and `channel-actions.contract.test.ts` pass (58 tests). `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` on the four changed files, and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` pass, and the pre-commit line-cap ratchet passes.
- Not covered: a real Telegram bot. The repository's Telegram Test Server proof (`telegram-e2e-userbot`) needs credentials from the maintainers' leased pool, which I do not have, so a maintainer would need to run that scenario on this head if it is required before merge.

prs.title: fix(gateway): session observer digests authenticate with the session owner's linked account
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #201585

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where, on a multi-user Gateway, every Control UI session observer digest for a session was sent through the agent-level auth order instead of the session owner's linked model account. When that agent-level profile is an unusable placeholder, every observer utility call returns 401 and the observer disables itself for the run, even though the session's own turns run fine on the user's linked account.
- Affected surface: Control UI session observer digests (`gateway.controlUi.sessionObserver`) on multi-user Gateways where sessions run on per-user linked model accounts.

- **Related:** #195172 (who pays for unattended utility-model calls); ClawSweeper confirmed current main drops the session's selected account on the observer path and no PR owns this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** The observer's utility model resolution and route-currentness checks now consume the session's established route — effective provider/model plus the session-sticky auth selection (linked account first, then the configured primary's profile on the same provider) — exactly like dashboard session titles already do per docs/gateway/config-agents/models.md (`utilityModel`). The derived utility modelRef carries the session's `@profile`, so preparation authenticates with the session owner's account.
- **Out of scope:** Explicitly configured `utilityModel` routes are preserved unchanged (the resolver returns them as configured); no changes to regular chat routing, auth order, or persistence.
- **Highest-risk area:** Route-currentness comparison (`modelStateIsCurrent`) must use the same session-scoped resolution as the claim that produced the state's ref, otherwise digests get demoted mid-run.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Both the model-slot claim and the currentness check share one `resolveUtilityModelRef(agentId, state)` helper; the route snapshot is captured once at admission from the session entry and refreshed on re-admission, so the comparison inputs cannot diverge.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** Two interleaved sessions on one agent, each with a different linked account and an unusable agent-level auth profile, now get observer digests authenticated to their own accounts (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5@<session-profile>` per session) instead of a shared 401 loop.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/session-observer.ts` (shared resolver), `src/gateway/session-observer-lifecycle.ts` (route capture at admission), `src/gateway/session-observer-model-slots.ts` + `src/gateway/session-observer-audience.ts` (session-scoped claim/currentness), `src/agents/session-model-ref.ts` (`resolveSessionAuthProfile`, extracted from the dashboard-title contract and now shared by both callers). Regression: `src/gateway/session-observer.test.ts` "routes observer utility digests through each session's linked model account".

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Isolated worktree at `aispace/worktrees/issue-201585` (openclaw main @ 02078202f31), Node 26.12.1, project vitest runner with a fixture plugin metadata snapshot declaring `anthropic`'s default utility model (auto-derivation path, no explicit `utilityModel`).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-observer.test.ts src/gateway/session-observer-model-slots.test.ts src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.test.ts
  # GREEN (with this patch): 3 files, 56 tests passed (exit 0)
  # RED (same test files with implementation reverted to origin/main, tests kept):
  #   AssertionError: expected [ 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5', …(1) ] to deeply equal [ …(2) ]
  #   - "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5@anthropic-alice"  + "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
  #   - "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5@anthropic-bob"     + "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
  # Regression scope: full src/gateway observer suite via validate.sh (2 vitest shards, all passed)
  # Type check: node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json (exit 0)
  # Format/lint: oxfmt --check + oxlint on all changed files (clean)
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  Test Files  3 passed (3)
       Tests  56 passed (56)
  prepareModel.modelRef (per session, sorted) = [
    "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5@anthropic-alice",
    "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5@anthropic-bob",
  ]
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Each of the two interleaved sessions on agent `main` (auto-derived utility model, unusable agent-level auth order) prepares its observer digest with its own session's `@profile`, so the digest call authenticates with the session owner's linked account; the agent-level placeholder is no longer used for those digests.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** RED on origin/main code with the same test: both sessions prepared `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` without a profile (the exact 401 `invalid x-api-key` loop from the issue log), 2 tests failed.
- **What was not tested:** A live multi-user Gateway with real Anthropic credentials (no live provider reproduction); the loopback fixture covers the route-selection boundary (which profile each digest call authenticates with) rather than provider HTTP itself.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review (CI lanes pending)

prs.title: fix(memory): bound heading-only chunk merges to the chunker maximum
prs.body:
Closes #198958

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` merges a heading-only chunk into the next chunk without any size bound, producing one oversized embedding input that non-native OpenAI-compatible endpoints reject, aborting the rebuild.

## User Impact

Heading-only runs stay within the chunker's ceiling while a heading still attaches to its following body. Existing indexes rebuild because the chunking version changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add `resolveMarkdownChunkMaxChars` as the single owner of the chunker ceiling and reuse it in `createMarkdownChunker`.
- Bound heading-only merges to that ceiling when the following chunk is also heading-only.
- Measure with the chunker's weighted CJK estimator, not raw UTF-16 length.
- Bump `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` so existing indexes rebuild across the boundary change.

## Evidence

- Unit: `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-index-preparation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 11/11 passed, including the 200-heading bound and a CJK case that distinguishes weighted from raw length. Red-on-base produces a 3689-character merged chunk against a 32-character ceiling.
- Real rebuild on the same 400-heading CJK corpus (`openclaw memory index --force --agent main`):
  - before (origin/main): 11 chunks, max chunk **8291 chars** (above the 8000-byte embedding cap);
  - this head: 25 chunks, max chunk **735 chars**, max span 73 lines.
- Real embedding endpoint (local OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings`, 8 dims):
  - `memory status --deep`: `Vector store: ready`, `Semantic vectors: ready`, `Vector dims: 8`, 25 chunks.
  - `memory search "第399章 中文标题"` -> top hit `memory/cjk-headings.md:734-800` (score 0.613).
  - `memory search "sapphire lighthouse"` -> top hit `memory/note.md:1-2` (score 0.898).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on all changed files.

### Latest-stable (v2026.11.6) index upgrade

```text
# index built by openclaw@2026.11.6 (chunking v6)
max chunk: 4496 chars, 13 chunks
$ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive   # agent schema 38 -> 43
Doctor complete.
$ (this head) openclaw memory index --agent main
Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed.
memory_index_meta_v1 ... "chunkingVersion":7 ... "vectorDims":8
max chunk: 735 chars
$ memory search "第399章 中文标题"
0.651 memory/cjk-headings.md:734-800
$ memory search "sapphire lighthouse"
0.884 memory/note.md:1-2
```

prs.title: fix(sandbox): view_image and read cannot open a channel image by media://inbound ref
prs.body:
Closes #196287
Related: #129269

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `view_image` ("Sandbox media reference is not staged") and `read` ("File not found") failing in a sandboxed session when given the `media://inbound/<id>` ref of a channel image (Matrix here). The staged copy is in the workspace and the prompt names both forms.

## User Impact

The model can open a current-turn channel attachment by either name the prompt gives. No new permissions or configuration. Security-sensitive path (CONTRIBUTING guard); needs `/allow-security-sensitive-change`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#129269 mapped only `file_*` upload handles to staged paths and left `media://inbound/...` refs on the flat path, where the staged copy never is. The map now also carries each staged fact's canonical `media://inbound/<id>`; the resolver and `read` use it when no workspace file exists at the flat path. Workspace-boundary checks run on the staged path unchanged. PDF goes through the same resolver.

## Evidence

Four tests: the real `stageSandboxMedia` then resolving the ref (`IMG_9854---8705be7d-….jpg`); `read` through tool assembly on a staged ref; `read` keeping a real workspace file over the alias; two facts sharing one ref dropping the alias (both staged copies exist, so only the ambiguity rule rejects it).

Before (main):

```text
Caused by: Error: Sandbox media reference is not staged: media://inbound/IMG_9854---8705be7d-aa4d-4744-aa9e-607677e85cde.jpg
 ❯ resolveSandboxedBridgeMediaPath src/agents/sandbox-media-paths.ts:69:13
Error: File not found: media/inbound/a.txt.
```

After: touched test files pass on macOS with the default temp dir. Wall time (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): `sandbox-media-paths.test.ts` 4.8 s, `agent-tools.read.staged-media.test.ts` 8.5 s, `stages-inbound-media-into-sandbox-workspace.test.ts` 6.4 s. Net test growth is +114 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/sandbox-inbound-media-ref.txt`: the four tests cover the staging-to-resolution handoff, sandboxed `read` assembly, workspace precedence and the ambiguity rule for media:// refs. The `realpath` in the staging fixture is needed because macOS tmp is a symlink and the media store must match the resolved source. `pnpm check:changed` fails only on the dead-export guard, in files this PR doesn't touch (`src/daemon/launchd.ts`, `src/plugins/provider-runtime.ts`, …).

Live check: v2026.11.2 (b556fdf) plus this PR's source changes (4c807210, 5e4173a2), as my gateway on macOS, podman sandbox backend, Matrix encrypted DM, photo sent with the message. Redacted tool calls:

```text
view_image {"path": "media://inbound/IMG_0099---69a0e34c-….jpg"}
→ success: "Loaded 1 image into private model context …" (image/jpeg, 169379 bytes), rewrittenFrom: "media://inbound/IMG_0099---69a0e34c-….jpg"
read {"path": "media://inbound/IMG_0099---69a0e34c-….jpg"}
→ success: kind "image", image/jpeg, 170913 bytes
```

Stock 2026.11.2 fails the same `view_image` call with "not staged".

Not covered: the Docker backend; a ref from an earlier turn (the map is per turn, so it still fails as before); spellings other than the canonical `media://inbound/<id>` (they fail closed as before); PDF has no specific test.

prs.title: fix: run scripts from symlinked checkouts
prs.body:
Related: #201528 and #201539 (the macOS packaging case).

## What Problem This Solves

Running a repository script by absolute path through a symlinked checkout can exit successfully without doing any work. For example, CI scope detection writes no outputs, and the Docker release policy command returns no JSON for its caller to read.

## User Impact

Developers can run the same repository script through a symlink or its physical path and get the expected output and exit status.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node normally resolves the main module's symlinks for `import.meta.url` while leaving the invocation path in `process.argv[1]`. The shared entrypoint check now resolves that path when its direct comparison misses. The direct comparison still handles Node's preserve-symlinks mode and Windows case matching. Four callers now reuse the shared check for behavior they previously implemented themselves.

## Evidence

- On Linux with Node 24.18.0 and main `02078202f31`, running `node "$linkedCheckout/scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs" --base HEAD^ --head HEAD` with an isolated `GITHUB_OUTPUT` exited 0 without creating the output or changed-paths manifest. prs.title: fix(claude-cli): store every reply in chat history, not just the final one
prs.body: Closes #195856 Related: #164293, #166511 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: with the `claude-cli` backend, replies sent before the final message vanish after a CLI session rotation, or after a run is killed or fails. ## User Impact User impact: completed user-addressed replies remain in the conversation after a session reset. Text from an interrupted run remains visible, marked "Interrupted". Yielded progress remains progress; scheduled execution prose retains its audit-only policy. ## Why This Change Was Made Previously, only the final reply was durable; earlier replies depended on the currently bound Claude log. This change buffers the latest revision per native UUID and persists it when the next assistant record arrives or the process ends. Writes retain normal preparation hooks and ownership checks. Final settlement deduplicates by native identity and awaits queued writes, including on failure. The change works with commentary streaming enabled or disabled. #164293 covers commentary-enabled persistence; #166511 covers a watchdog interruption slice. Settlement uses a closed assistant-metadata operation: content, identity, timestamps, topology and replay inputs cannot change. It preserves the transcript generation and returns the current anchor without relaxing generic rewrite invalidation or changing account admission. ## Evidence - Focused CLI parser, transcript, account admission, Gateway history, import closure, and Control UI regressions: 363 tests passed, 3 skipped across the proof runs. The focused Stop-before-flush regression passed again after porting its fixture to the current transcript owner. Changed test-project typechecks passed for agents, Gateway, commands, and chat UI. ### Upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.5 to head `7b3e9d23b50` Both builds were made from clean checkouts (buildstamps `e13cf15ece9` = v2026.11.5, and `7b3e9d23b50`). One throwaway Gateway state directory was used, with the `claude-cli` backend, driven through the real Control UI. - **Seeded on v2026.11.5:** a settled six-step narrate-then-tool run (`DONE-A`), then a ~120-word story streamed as visible text with Stop pressed while its `sleep 60` tool was running (tool start observed at 6.70 s, Stop clicked at 6.84 s). The story stayed visible, marked "Interrupted", live and after reload. - **Upgrade:** stopped the Gateway, switched to the candidate build, and ran offline doctor. SQLite `user_version` went from 38 to 42. `quick_check` returned `ok` before and after. A pre-migration backup was written, and its integrity check passes. - **Existing data:** the selected model and settings are the same. All 11 canonical transcript events match before and after the upgrade (field-by-field projection). The same session reopened **before** any new turn showed the old history: `DONE-A` once and the interrupted story once. - **First candidate turn (native replacement):** `REPLACEMENT-OK-196092` settled as a new message. The local session ID is unchanged, and the Claude CLI binding moved to a new native session. The imported reply matches the new binding. After reload, `DONE-A`, both interrupted stories and the new reply each appear exactly once, and two events are appended after the unchanged 11. - **Scope note:** v2026.11.5 never wrote non-final text to canonical storage; it showed it only from the bound Claude log. That covers the narration lines and the pre-tool text of completed runs. Once the first post-upgrade turn replaces the Claude session, that pre-upgrade text is no longer shown. This PR persists such text for runs from this version on; it cannot recover text the old version never stored. This upgrade's replacement came from `cli session reset … reason=mcp`. The resume-hash canonicalization in `bundle-mcp.ts`, which this PR does not change, now normalizes the openclaw server's `alwaysLoad`. As a result, bindings stored while tools were deferred do not match once after upgrading. v2026.11.5, story interrupted by Stop, after reload · after upgrading, same session before a new turn · after the replacement turn, after reload: ### November 18 conflict-repair update — `51bc1056a612` Updated against main `b609d22c129f2944c1abaec1d2895eb659493a36`, preserving the newer transcript-lease and stopped-first-session recovery behavior. - Held replies arriving without snapshot callbacks now use the same native-keyed settlement writer as streamed snapshots. Both paths retain each answer once, including transformed output and a final interim result. The separate recursive interim writer and its identity helper were removed. - Three held-history cases failed after a mechanical merge (one saved answer instead of two), then passed after reconciliation. The existing history matrix now also exercises streamed snapshot deduplication. - Independent review identified three P2 cases: saved commentary trimming an unrelated answer, an unterminated final revision losing to an earlier snapshot, and delivered-failure recovery skipping settlement. Seven regression cases failed before their repairs, including confirmed progress (`final: false`) delivery; matching mirrors are hidden without promoting progress into completed-answer evidence. - Repaired runner/parser/chat-consumer checks: **217 passed, 3 skipped** across 10 files (86.64 s). Final parser/framing/budget/reasoning/persistence checks: **229 passed, 3 skipped** across 8 files (54.67 s). The final progress/final delivery correction passed 90 tests (3 skipped) across history, transcript, and settlement suites (66.49 s). These selections overlap and are not additive totals. - Core and UI typechecks, targeted format/lint, `git diff --check`, and exact-base max-lines/test-lines ratchets passed. The test allocation is 860 lines beyond the ordinary 400-line allowance, covering native identity/settlement and the held-reply/commentary/terminal-revision/delivered-failure regressions. Whole-change net delta against this base: +831 production lines and +1,260 test lines. Stream framing and budget accounting now live together in the existing stream-limits owner, with unchanged limits, keeping the parser within its file-size cap. - **Independent review:** User-authorized, separate read-only source review covered the candidate against the stated base and the subsequent repair deltas. Three P2 findings were reproduced and corrected; the same reviewer confirmed all findings resolved. This was source inspection, not an independent test rerun. Native autoreview was unavailable: its bounded attempt timed out after 180 seconds without a report; no clean autoreview result is claimed. - **Proof limits:** the v2026.11.5 upgrade run above is a live run at head `7b3e9d23b50`. The other live Claude/Control UI evidence below is retained from the stated earlier revisions. Current-head hosted CI must be read separately; no prior-head result is represented as a current-head pass. ### Earlier implementation evidence - Native Claude CLI steering: three accepted steers (A/B/C), with one `DONE: STEER-A, STEER-B, STEER-C` live and after reload. Narration stays between the steers. - Stable upgrade from v2026.11.3: Doctor migrated schema 27 → 42. Old history loaded before the next turn; Claude recalled the seed and produced one settled reply, preserved once after reload. The durable reply has `stopReason: "stop"` and nonzero usage. - Hook visibility: two snapshot-persistence/stranding regressions failed before the fix and passed afterward, covering explicit `display: false` and `display: true`. - Steering and history/stream consumers: 79 tests passed. Saved-prefix replay, whitespace, foreign-run isolation, and idempotent reconciliation are covered. - Chat-entry gzip diagnostic: 132,226 B before and after the state-owner projection change (+0 B). - Pruned redundant saved-stream adapters and unused cached prefix state without changing reconciliation behavior; exact-head [control-ui-performance passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43852886496/job/133250595655). Final live settlement and after reload: ### Prior live-proof head `9bc5ccf5489`: Stop retention, native replacement, single narration Throwaway proof Gateway built at the exact head (buildstamp `9bc5ccf5489`, clean inputs), driven through the real Control UI with the `claude-cli` backend: - **Stop before flush:** a ~120-word story was streamed as visible text, then Stop was pressed while a `sleep 60` tool was pending. The story remains visible exactly once, marked "Interrupted", both live and after a full page reload; no tool card or error banner is left behind. - **Native replacement:** the next turn (`REPLACEMENT-OK-196092`) settles as a new assistant message; the interrupted story is retained exactly once, live and after reload. - **Single narration:** a 6-step narrate-then-tool run showed each `Narration N` line exactly once while streaming; the final accumulated assistant message contains each of the six lines exactly once (192 chars), with no duplicated narration live or after reload. - **Budget:** paired chat boot +222 B vs the merge base, 187 B under the CI cap; `control-ui-performance` and the max-lines ratchet are green at this head. - **CI:** the only red check is `checks-node-changed-compact-large-11-1` — 7 tests in `run.prepared-harness-source-delivery.integration.test.ts` failing with the `run-loop.ts:501 .providerOutcomes` TypeError introduced by main #200073. The identical 7 failures reproduce on the pure merge base `30e9d3ee295` (local attribution run); this PR touches no `embedded-agent-runner` files. Inherited from main, not caused by this change. Stop retention (live, then after reload): Native replacement (live, then after reload): AI-assisted: implementation and validation with Claude and GPT agents. Original PR author: @Marvinthebored. The work-session link below records the November 18 PR update. ## Work sessions Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public. - [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/67a23b12-5823-42b8-9aff-a9c829b2b8d8) ### Round 5 (head `267a360d9d7`): source-reply delivery no longer hides distinct snapshots Addresses the 16 Nov ClawSweeper P2 (`cli-assistant-settlement.ts:146`). When a message tool delivers the source reply, settlement now marks `display:false` only on saved snapshots whose text matches a delivered source-reply body (the dispatch-owned mirror). Distinct earlier snapshots such as `Findings: BLUE-HERON-42` followed by a tool-delivered `Done` keep their prepared visibility. - New regression `keeps distinct snapshots visible when the message tool delivers a different reply`, plus the settlement matrix now asserts per-row visibility (mirrored `Answer` hidden, distinct `Progress` visible). Both fail on `9bc5ccf5489` (2 failed) and pass after the fix. - Acceptance: `cli-run-transcript.test.ts`, `cli-runner.history-ownership.test.ts`, `cli-session-history.segments.test.ts` pass; `tsgo:core`, oxlint/oxfmt, max-lines and test-lines ratchets clean. - Stop, native-replacement and narration paths are unchanged by this commit; the live proof above (exact-head `9bc5ccf5489`) still covers them.

## What Problem This Solves

Installed-skill refreshes wrap their list in a second object, while the decoder and data contract live inside runtime orchestration instead of the existing skill-management owner. Maintaining the installed list therefore requires changes across both responsibilities.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Unknown or failed state remains distinct from a successfully loaded empty list; skill flags, Gateway switching, enable/disable behavior and install verification retain their existing contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the installed-skill contract and decoder into SkillManagement, remove the single-field GatewaySkillsSummary wrapper, and migrate every runtime, ViewModel, UI and test consumer to the list directly. The existing trimmed-string boolean reader moves unchanged to the shared JSON owner so the decoder can reuse it. All allowlist, agent-filter, trust and provenance fields remain intact.

Concurrent policy work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166166 touches these fields; this PR preserves the current policy.

## Evidence

- Both phone flavors compiled and passed six affected suites: 88 tests per flavor, zero failures/errors/skips. Kotlin lint and staged-content/freshness guards passed on exact tree `77baf6a26cc0f4418a66046a96c8124dbabb66f0`.

On Linux, the resource-host lifecycle test starts its child with the test runner's executable. Under stock Bun, that child exits before startup because the profiling preload requires Node's `registerHooks`; all five lifecycle cases fail before exercising their intended behavior.

## User Impact

No product runtime change. The lifecycle test now exercises the supported Node profiling host when Vitest runs under Bun, while retaining its clean-exit, signal, retained-state, operation-count, and error-log assertions.

Select the fixture executable through the existing `resolveTestNodeExecPath` helper and its shared Node runtime resolver. The production profiler already requires Linux Node. No preload workaround, runtime pin change, skip, or duplicate runtime-selection policy is added.

prs.title: fix(media): show retained generated images after delivery is blocked
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes generated images from blocked completion deliveries appearing only as filenames after users reopen the original session.

Fixes #184585

## Why This Change Was Made

Blocked completions prepare images independently, so an invalid image does not discard valid ones. If media ownership attachment fails after the transcript commit, a retry reconciles ownership without adding another completion message.

## User Impact

Users can reopen the original session and download generated images after completion delivery fails.

## Evidence

Validated on exact head `517b8fd84a202fce943b1f840851431ba092fcfe` after rebasing onto `ef5d3dcefec4c343a8429f5e9decf7356d9d65bc`. The deterministic local PNG provider fixture used no external provider credentials; I reran the production-path proof on this final head.

- Real production path: `OPENCLAW_MEDIA_RETENTION_PROOF=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs test/proofs/media-retention-live-proof.mts` exercised the `image_generate` tool, delivery wake and queue admission, blocked-completion persistence, WSS `chat.history`, and authenticated HTTPS artifact download. Changing the session-store path after generation makes production queue admission dead-letter delivery.
- The recorded pre-feature run on base `a3805cb6a2f413fbe17ac4470b20e1edf1c53483` had zero image blocks; rerunning the same command on exact head `517b8fd84a202fce943b1f840851431ba092fcfe` produced one. The head download returned HTTP 200 with 68 matching PNG bytes. A reader without `operator.read` is denied; the e2e test also verifies the revoked ticket returns 404 before file I/O.
- Rebase resolved the import conflict in `src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-completion.ts`, preserving main's queue/runtime imports with the PR's transcript and managed-media imports. The exact-head conflict receipt passed; focused tests passed 2 files and 30 tests.
- Canonical precedent: Gateway transcript media uses `createManagedOutgoingMediaBlocks` and `attachManagedOutgoingMediaToMessage`.

```text
$ OPENCLAW_MEDIA_RETENTION_PROOF=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs test/proofs/media-retention-live-proof.mts
entrypoint: image_generate -> production completion wake -> enqueueClaimedSessionDelivery -> blocked retention -> WSS chat.history -> artifacts.download -> HTTPS artifact route
base a3805cb6a2f413fbe17ac4470b20e1edf1c53483 => before-fix: blocked, image_blocks=0, missing-image assertion failed (exit 1)
head 517b8fd84a202fce943b1f840851431ba092fcfe => after-fix: blocked, image_blocks=1, HTTP 200, 68 PNG bytes
negative-control: missing operator.read rejected; revoked ticket 404; e2e confirms no file read
```

prs.title: fix(process): deliver secret input after an async stdin prompt
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI chat that signs in with a Claude subscription token stored in OpenClaw fails background CLI runs that send their prompt on stdin with `secret input file descriptor 3 is unavailable`. It happens on Gateways that run in the foreground (`openclaw gateway run`, containers, Windows), not under a service manager.

## Why It Happens

`createChildAdapter` (direct path) prepares the secret pipe with `using`, so the pipe is released when the function returns `{ adapter, ready }`. `ready` then awaits `prepareInput` (and the Windows Job) before it calls `deliverTo`, which finds the writer gone. The service relay path already hands the pipe to readiness and delivers it before stdin.

## Change

Readiness now owns the secret pipe until delivery settles (`DisposableStack.move()`); a construction failure before readiness still releases it. One file, 5 lines.

## Evidence

- New `src/process/supervisor/supervisor.secret-after-input.real.test.ts`: a real child reads a stdin prompt written after an async `prepareInput`, then the secret on fd 3. Red on `main` with `secret input file descriptor 3 is unavailable`, green with the fix.
- Real product, tier source (`ocx src`), foreground Gateway with no service marker, one Claude CLI agent signed in with an OpenClaw-held Claude subscription token, no API key: one chat turn, then `/btw`. The background Claude CLI completion right after the turn:
  - `main` (`22255926`): `[process/supervisor] spawn failed: runId=isolated-completion-… reason=Error: secret input file descriptor 3 is unavailable`, twice.
  - This branch: the same flow logs no such error.

prs.title: fix(gateway): count posted messages as session activity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A message appended to an existing session outside a run — `chat.inject`, a guest agent posting a reply into a shared session, a template receipt — never updated the session entry. Clients derive "unread" from `lastActivityAt`, so the session stayed marked as read while the new message sat in the transcript. Fixes #202707.

The stamp must not over-reach in the other direction: a hidden transcript row (private CLI/ACP completion, delivery mirror, subagent coordination) is bookkeeping, not a message the user can see. Advancing `lastActivityAt` for those rows would mark a read session unread with nothing visible in it.

## User Impact

A *visible* posted message now counts as session activity, the same as a reply from a normal run: the session reorders and shows as unread. Hidden rows keep the previous activity timestamp, so a private completion no longer produces a spurious unread dot or sidebar reorder — the visible-side-effect suppression that private coordination promises (see #175559) stays intact. Replayed or declined appends stay untouched, and a session that was reset or deleted while the write was in flight is not resurrected by the bump.

## Why This Change Was Made

`injectGatewayAssistantMessage` appended the transcript and broadcast the `chat` event, but nothing patched the session entry: `lastActivityAt` is otherwise advanced only by run lifecycles (`session-run-lifecycle-projection`, `updateSessionStoreAfterAgentRun`) which an injected turn never enters. The append itself already bumps `updatedAt` through the transcript-turn owner; only the unread-driving field was missed.

The fix stamps `lastActivityAt` in that same owner-built patch (`session-transcript-turn-state.ts`), so it commits atomically with the transcript append and the existing broadcast path. A replay or a declined append never reaches the fresh-append touch, so neither bumps the entry. An earlier revision patched the entry in a separate write after the append; review correctly flagged that a failure there would skip the broadcast and a replay would not repair it, so that write is gone.

**Private completion visibility (#175559).** The first revision of that atomic stamp applied to every fresh append, including rows that `projectAgentHarnessTranscriptMessageForDisplay` marks `display: false`. That silently widened "session activity" to cover invisible writes. This revision restores the original intent: `updatedAt` keeps its existing fresh-append condition, while `lastActivityAt` is gated on at least one appended row with `display !== false`. `display: false` is the single marker the projection sets for private completions, delivery mirrors, progress-card refreshes and subagent coordination, so the predicate tracks visibility exactly rather than guessing from provenance. Both directions are covered in `src/agents/command/transcript-persistence.test.ts` through the shipped CLI and ACP writers.

## Evidence

Live A/B on Windows 11, isolated Gateway (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` under a temp dir, port 28794, mock OpenAI-compatible provider on 28795). One `chat.send` creates the session and settles; then `chat.inject` posts one visible message; then a private completion (`privateCompletion: true`) is appended through the shipped CLI transcript writer (`persistCliTurnTranscript`) against the same live agent store. Every row is read back from `sessions.list`.

| Build | after `chat.send` settles (`updatedAt` / `lastActivityAt`) | after `chat.inject` | after hidden private completion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upstream/main` (`7e5cad36`, before the PR) | `1795230952360` / `1795230952349` | `1795230955735` / `1795230952349` — **unchanged**, posted reply stays read | `1795230979068` / `1795230952349` — nothing stamps it |
| earlier revision `00615d97` | `1795231119338` / `1795231119291` | `1795231122966` / `1795231122966` — bumped | `1795231145910` / `1795231145910` — **bumped, spurious unread** |
| this revision | `1795231279552` / `1795231279505` | `1795231283258` / `1795231283258` — **bumped** | `1795231305825` / `1795231283258` — **`updatedAt` advances, `lastActivityAt` frozen** |

![Live three-way comparison: posted message bumps activity, hidden completion does not](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/202707/visible-activity-proof.png)

Unit, through the shipped writers (`src/agents/command/transcript-persistence.test.ts`): the new `keeps {CLI,ACP} private completions out of unread activity` legs fail against the unconditional stamp (`expected 1795230519323 to be 1795230458484`, `expected 1795230521782 to be 1795230461666`) and pass here; `counts a visible {CLI,ACP} transcript append as unread activity` passes in both. `src/gateway/assistant-human-mentions.test.ts` still 11/11 with `counts a posted assistant message as session activity`.

Gates on the merged tree: `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0, test-services tsconfig exit 0, `oxfmt --check` clean, `oxlint` 0 warnings/0 errors, `check:line-cap-ratchet` OK, `check:test-lines-ratchet` +78 / allowance 400. Merged `upstream/main` (`7e5cad36`) in; merge commit only.

## What was not tested

- No real model: the rig uses a mock OpenAI-compatible stub; no provider credentials exist in this environment.
- The hidden leg drives the shipped CLI transcript writer out of process against the live Gateway's own agent store. It does not run a real subagent settle or an ACP child end to end, so the private-completion *trigger* is still covered by the existing suite rather than by a live run.
- The unread dot itself is not rendered; the evidence is the persisted `lastActivityAt` that `deriveSessionUnread` consumes.
- The replayed-append path keeps the entry untouched by construction (the bump sits after the `replayed` early return) but has no dedicated live leg.
- Windows only; no macOS or Linux live run.

prs.title: fix: keep first-use state writes working after peer schema changes
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

An updater can create a first-use table while another process still remembers that table as absent. That process can then fail its next write with `relation already exists`. This change checks the committed catalog before first-use creation and recovers writer admission before caller work starts.

## What Problem This Solves

First use after a peer schema change can fail or mistake an existing table for an absent one. This affects retained shared-state writers and updater bookkeeping.

## User Impact

A retained writer can use a peer-created table without a restart. A writer waiting across schema publication gets current admission before its callback runs.

## Root Cause

Physical schema facts are process-local. Fragment installation trusted cached absence, and in-transaction lookups could lose facts during a sibling publication. Metadata helpers then converted unavailable facts into empty results. On the unmodified base, the regressions produced SQLSTATE `42P07` from `createUpdateRun` and `present: false` for the existing `config_machine_state` table.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fragment owner checks catalog presence on an admitted cache miss under its existing writer lock. A peer-created fragment goes through schema-seal validation, including drift rejection. Both shared-state writer entry points use the existing bounded admission retry only after rollback and before caller entry. Metadata helpers inspect their transaction's catalog when admission facts are unavailable, which also preserves migration-time inspection.

Passive readers retain their existing cache lifetime. This repair refreshes peer-created fragments at first-use installation.

## Real behavior proof

Disposable server version 17.12, local trust authentication and a private Unix socket. Synthetic state only.

```sh
env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u OPENAI_API_KEY OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres \
  --connection "$TEST_PG_URL" -- \
  src/infra/database-engine/state-read-admission-owners.postgres.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

After the fix: `Tests 8 passed (8)`, 58.90 seconds wall time including compilation; test bodies took about 22 seconds. Test-case duration on the original hosted run totaled 66.3 seconds. Real cross-worker commit/publication scheduling and separate OS processes require the database fixtures rather than mocks. The updater test uses separate OS processes through `createUpdateRun`, then checks both persisted ledger rows. A companion case alters the peer-created table and confirms schema drift is refused. Publication-gated workers cover ordinary writes, existing-state writes, schema reads, and refusal to replay a callback that already began.

## Evidence

Local review of the full change, at `4b8fe05d905a82be01f90d42e63db828562693ab`, against `3587df70a233dc639b733b9169797d3abd138301`: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The simplification pass keeps the existing fragment, transaction, publication and retry owners. Growth covers catalog inspection and regressions; no new cache, retry policy, migration or schema version is introduced. Production code grows by 88 net lines; tests/support grow by 132 net lines.

## What was not tested

No foreground Gateway/UI, live channel, paid provider call, or server version 16/18 run. No claim about externally created tables becoming visible to a passive reader before first-use refresh.

## Verification

- Targeted state/infra TypeScript test project: passed.
- Changed-file source/test lint, formatting, SQL guardrails and import-cycle check: passed.
- Existing admission-retention unit suite: 28 passed with its ordinary fixture configuration.
- Shared-state bootstrap, retained handles, updater bookkeeping and historical migrations: 13 passed on the final source.
- Existing read snapshot/publication/deadline checks: 16 passed; schema-helper checks: 6 passed.

A standalone benchmark used the real shared-state writer entry point. Each case had five warmups, then 30 first-use transactions rolled back after installation or 100 warm transactions against the installed fragment. Same disposable server and workload, base followed by candidate under shared host load. Median / p95 milliseconds:

| Case | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First-use transaction with rollback | 55.960 / 61.565 | 58.191 / 64.369 |
| Warm writer + fragment ensure | 0.112 / 0.451 | 0.107 / 0.201 |

The extra catalog query is confined to first-use misses. These samples do not establish a warm-path speedup.

Fixture setup failures were corrected before the baseline reproduction: the database tests require the established owner suite and its fork/relay setup. An ordinary admission-retention unit test was initially invoked with database-conformance configuration; its ordinary fixture run passed 28/28. Initial implementation checks also caught and repaired unavailable-fact migration inspection, a connection-interface type error, and lint/SQL annotations.

## CI

[Original head run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44540769115): all four full database conformance shards, the version-16 Gateway smoke, build artifacts, and security checks passed. The committed eight-case owner regression ran and passed in shard 3.

The original aggregate CI gate failed because `operator-approval-placement-grants.test.ts:512` expects late authority closure to make `resolve()` return false. CI's merge parent already includes [the change to check approval authority at request start](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/de680e35f98f7ca5281bb67e6a6d856c4ba08b5c), which removed that late check. This PR changes no approval owner.

Attribution control: the unmodified PR base passed all 14 tests in that file. With the database fix completely absent, replacing only the four approval-owner files with their trusted CI-parent versions reproduced the identical `expected true to be false` failure at line 512. All task files were then restored byte-for-byte. This establishes an inherited merge-parent failure; a passing replay alone was not used as attribution.

Upstream [aligned the placement test with check-once authority](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/576b22128f23ce295efefdfe1af53bb2962a159a). The [matching hosted shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44556972628/job/135676451000) passed the exact case that failed on the original head. The revised test checks that the verdict is recorded, the stale launch is denied, and the next request cannot reuse the standing grant.

Replayed the database patch onto main at `9159d33262bf43105535184c977c53e5c918286c`. Git range-diff matched the patch and `git diff --check` passed. The refreshed head is `293f1a9ac06d6b2c0e4adab4312da3ca0d53120d`. [Refreshed CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44784182174).

The refreshed run failed a different test, `mcp-http.completion-lineage.test.ts:451`. Both the [PR shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44784182174/job/136455404522) and the [scheduled main shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44783201838/job/136452097010) fail the same test with the same assertion. The test file is unchanged across those inputs. The database patch does not touch the Gateway test or its owner. The [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44784182174/job/136468692313) failed on that shard. The [automated comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44784182174/job/136468505735) says “unknown” because it compared a different scheduled run by outer job name. The two linked logs establish the matching test signature directly.

All four PostgreSQL conformance shards and the [PostgreSQL 16 Gateway smoke](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44784182174/job/136455402360) passed. The [PostgreSQL owner regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44784182174/job/136455402736) passed all eight cases on the refreshed head. [Hosted re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201877#issuecomment-7011975704) covered the refreshed head and reported no actionable findings.
