prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:start -->
## Adoption decision and fresh distribution evidence — 2026-11-02

The Slack-owner decision remains whether to expose the compatibility-preserving `requireExplicitBotMention` opt-in. The current submission section below owns the latest head and CI status; maintainer edits remain enabled. Owner acceptance is still outstanding.

The historical [advisory review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177555#issuecomment-6274222081) reports no actionable findings and sufficient recorded isolated-Gateway output, and recommends accepting the opt-in. It does not record Slack-owner acceptance. Its two outstanding checklist entries both concern that same public-contract decision. The review is scoped to `39d01116dd2d5e01fa7f8ab50dbb1e44613a0e9a`; the earlier12-input comparison was bound to8fa0cc0d85711ab2ee19e488ec9e325309a476c2. That earlier integration retained11 byte-identical inputs; access-control documentation only adds accepted official Slack read-bound guidance. The strict opt-in authored delta and committed Gateway scenario are retained. The older proof retains its original head; that earlier head's CI supported its integration. No fresh live Slack run or current employee acceptance is claimed.

Recorded official distribution evidence confirms that the need remains after the implicit-thread silence repair: unmodified Core/Slack **2026.10.10-beta.5**, build `7e15622f37bd0ced194a3b0fccacb4ad6bc78d85`, still admits untagged bot messages through both `bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot` in the isolated distributed-function/compiled-gate fixture. The same 20-case matrix passes 17, with these two strict-admission requirements and the separate optional-completion policy remaining. Package integrity and the scope are recorded in the [release follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621). This is not a new live Slack incident or a claim that existing documented defaults were silently changed.

**Decision requested from the Slack owner:** accept or reject this optional public setting at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Omitted/false keeps existing implicit bot handoffs. With `allowBots: "mentions"` and the opt-in enabled, untagged bot activation is rejected while explicit bot requests, implicit human follow-ups, DMs, authorized commands, and existing sender restrictions retain their controls. This is the compatibility-preserving alternative to #160752's default change; no new default change is requested here.

This PR decides **admission**, not whether an already admitted explicit bot notification may finish empty. That latter product-policy question remains separate in #186514. A scoped acceptance/rejection of this opt-in is the missing adoption decision; existing code/proof work is not being represented as owner approval. No new review command or redundant behavior replay was added for this mechanical integration.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:start -->
### 2026-11-03: the same admission requirement remains in stable2026.10.10

Official npm/latest Core/Slack **2026.10.10**, distributed Core build`7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be`, was checked with the unchanged20-case synthetic matrix: **17PASS / 3FAIL**. The two untagged-bot admission cases (`bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot`) still admit the bot under existing mentions-only behavior. The two implicit-thread optional/silent conditions from merged #164877 nowPASS in stable; the third remaining failure concerns #186514's separate explicit-bot completion policy.

The [stable distribution follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621) fixes the verified immutable Core/Slack hashes and execution scope. This is actual distributed Core-function / verbatim compiled Slack-gate evidence, with unchanged cases/assertions and shipped package bytes. The existing native Gateway proof retains its original binding. This paragraph updates distribution evidence only; the current PR head and compatible opt-in proposal remain unchanged. Slack-owner acceptance or rejection remains unrecorded.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:end -->
<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:end -->

## Evidence

<!-- forone-current-submission:start -->
### Current main integration — 2026-11-17 UTC

Current head: `5be4aafbdcfd4ac7bd1c35af9ce2802864993a19`; pinned official main: `a958f1d25c1d77aff39bfcbf86d0d4c7bd8f539a`. The normal merge had only generated config metadata conflicts; canonical channel/config generators own the resolution. The Slack opt-in implementation and its tests are unchanged.

Focused current-head proof passed 45 Slack schema, hot-reload and message-handler assertions. Canonical channel metadata, config docs and staged diff checks pass. The prior live-Slack limitation remains: no production Slack message or owner adoption is claimed.
<!-- forone-current-submission:end -->

Candidate: `d7b47f3a7b33d16786c766b2768df0e0f92505d4`; ordinary merge parents are the previous accepted head `41974794c4ab5eb235d153d7926de7dedba834f6` and fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa`.

- 29 Slack schema/handler tests and 17 Gateway reload-planning tests pass on the integrated source.
- Canonical extension production types, scoped source/E2E lint/format, shrink-only line-cap, conflict/diff checks, and outgoing-diff secret scan pass.
- Canonical channel-metadata and config-doc generators/checks pass. Parsed metadata differs only by the existing option's four Slack schema projections and four UI hints; unrelated channel metadata is unchanged.
- Fresh P0-P2 reviews cover the integration/schema adaptation and the cohesive mention-owner move; no actionable findings. The only later adjustment selects the existing exported nested SDK input type, validated by production types and typed lint.
- Exact-head hosted [CI 39897283670](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39897283670) and `openclaw/ci-gate` pass. All 117 checks are terminal with zero failures. Previous-head native Gateway/package evidence below remains explicitly bound to that older head. No new configuration surface beyond this PR's existing opt-in proposal, employee runtime change, or private package distribution is introduced. External live-QA entitlement and Slack-owner acceptance below remain upstream prerequisites.

### Current mechanical integration (2026-11-18)

Exact head: `23a92f9b11de1f8b91a660ce1c0841764ec1b9d8`. Normally merged pinned official `main` `f7c6804343843245d8ab6f37a91675ecc257a7b9` and regenerated the conflicting config counts/hash with their canonical owner. The conflict resolution adds no routing or authentication behavior. All 45 focused Slack schema, reload, and bot-thread assertions pass; `config:docs:check`, authored-diff whitespace and publication secret gates pass.

The existing live-Slack proof limit and Slack-owner adoption decision remain open. Previous hosted review remains bound to its reviewed head; no redundant mechanical re-review, repeated adoption request, channel delivery, or maintainer workflow approval was performed. Current-head native CI is separate.

## Earlier accepted evidence (previous head)

Candidate: 41974794c4ab5eb235d153d7926de7dedba834f6. Current-head hosted CI completed **SUCCESS** with no nonpassing jobs: [run 39427790673](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39427790673).

Inspectable value-free runtime verdict (the same candidate; additional isolated prebuilt-Gateway replay):

```json
{
  "sourceHead": "41974794c4ab5eb235d153d7926de7dedba834f6",
  "gatewayProcess": true,
  "liveSlack": false,
  "receivedBeforePolicyPublication": [
    {
      "kind": "reply_to_bot",
      "nativeHttpAccepted": true,
      "acceptedMs": 16,
      "noProviderOrSendEffectsBeforePublication": true,
      "activeConfigPublicationComplete": true,

      "activeConfigPublicationComplete": true,
      "publishedMs": 390,
      "correlatedMentionGateRejection": true,

    }
  ],
```

Each additional bot input is signed and HTTP-acknowledged under the applied legacy policy, remains without provider/send effects during the initial 200ms, and is rejected only after strict policy publication is independently read back (`hash` and applied normalized revision agree). The configured debounce is 5000ms; native correlation rejects at 5217ms/5241ms. Each final provider/send delta is zero. This is received-before-publication final-effect proof; exact registration within the debounce queue is proved by the existing two fake-clock handler cases, not inferred from HTTP acknowledgement. Already-adopted work keeps its existing captured-policy lifetime. Scenario body 40.580s; Vitest 88.00s including worker preparation. Cleanup and original source-head readback pass.



- Baseline `b8f91cb249b8c702cfc02befd6d2fb11215928f3` had five focused failures for strict bot admission/schema; legacy controls passed. Current integrated candidate: **24 Slack tests + 17 Gateway reload-planning tests pass**. Queued-before-policy-publication tests use the real handler and both implicit kinds; already-adopted work retains the existing captured-policy contract.
- **Actual isolated Gateway, real Slack plugin and core/session processing, external HTTP simulations:** both authorized synthetic bot kinds reach a timestamp-correlated `bot-missing-mention` decision. Each rejection leaves the mock provider request cursor unchanged and produces no Slack send. Explicit bot, human implicit follow-up, and legacy false-policy controls produce four model HTTP requests and four stored same-thread replies including the seed. `conversations.replies` independently reads each reply exactly once. Child Gateway and fixtures stop successfully. The scenario body took 27.671s (Vitest 38.61s); a full Gateway is needed to observe the actual model and send effects, and this opt-in E2E stays outside the ordinary unit lane.

The base recipe preserves representative existing configuration and old Slack session metadata. It does **not** seed an old Slack channel connection/configuration; that boundary is not claimed. Legacy omitted/false bot-policy compatibility is separately covered by the owning schema/handler regressions and actual Gateway final-effect controls above. Package version alone is not the identity: this candidate has the same `2026.10.5` package version, pinned by build commit and tarball SHA256.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202818

## What Problem This Solves

The cron guard, device-pairing and approval runtime suites create their own NodeRuntime instances but never hand them to the existing teardown owner. Across 41 tests, those factories create 45 runtimes with independent coroutine scopes and database resources. NodeApp does not own these directly constructed fixtures.

## User Impact

Production behavior and all test assertions are unchanged. Each test now retires its runtime fixtures before Robolectric tears down the sandbox, preventing their background work from escaping the test lifetime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track instances in the existing factories and close them from JUnit teardown through closeNodeRuntimeTestFixture. That helper already owns disconnect, coroutine cancellation/join and database closure. No new cleanup framework, production seam or test case is added; the fix adds 24 net test lines to make lifetime ownership explicit.

## Evidence

- A temporary TestWatcher observed the actual runtime jobs after test teardown. One existing test from each suite failed on the baseline with one active runtime job, then all three passed with the cleanup. The observer cleaned up in finally and is absent from this PR. This proves job retirement, not a measured heap or RSS reduction.
- Both phone flavors compiled and passed all 41 affected tests, with zero failures/errors/skips. JUnit-reported suite times total 9.867 seconds (Play) and 8.717 seconds (ThirdParty); these exclude Gradle/build overhead.
- Kotlin lint and staged-content guards passed on exact tree `6675e6e2dd9a5df0b6c1f37da0680c8ca57cbb08`. Fresh independent source review found no issues and confirmed all assertions are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: keep workspace lease checks off the Gateway thread
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Publishing a session workspace can pause the Gateway while it waits for PostgreSQL to check the workspace reservation. Move those checks to the existing lease worker so the Gateway can keep serving other requests.

## What Problem This Solves

Local workspace publication and repository checkpoint publication both hold session workspace reservations. Their final effect checks call the native lease owner's synchronous ownership check, so PostgreSQL latency reaches the Gateway event loop.

## User Impact

Workspace publication no longer blocks the Gateway thread on lease SQL. If a Gateway exits before the worker can release an active reservation, the session can report busy until the lease expires, up to 60 seconds after its last renewal.

## Root Cause

The native lease owner's worker heartbeat renews the lease, but the final ownership check still reads it synchronously. A PostgreSQL probe of the production placement store on the base counted 120 lease statements on thread zero across 20 local workspace reservations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both reservation scopes now use the existing asynchronous lease owner. The effect guard checks the worker-published expiry and liveness, Gateway restart cancellation, and retained placement authority. The existing 60-second expiration makes an interrupted release recoverable.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

The production placement store ran against PostgreSQL 18.7 over a Unix socket using Node.js 26.13.1. After a warmup, the same 20-reservation probe counted `hostLeaseSql=120` on the base and `hostLeaseSql=0` with the fix. Time inside the effect guard went from 4.522 ms median and 9.340 ms p95 to 0.008 ms median and 0.014 ms p95. This measures the guard only.

The regression runs both public reservation methods and checks reads on the calling thread.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-database-workers.config.ts \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-workspace-reservation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

With the production code from main, each reservation case found six synchronous lease reads. With the fix, both cases passed. The focused run also exercised real publication handoffs through local Git fixtures, restart fencing, and competing turn and editor claims.

A disposable PostgreSQL process probe exited while holding workspace exclusion. A fresh process received the lease-held result before expiry and acquired the reservation after expiry.

### Verification

- Local runtime build passed.
- Focused Gateway database worker run: 9 files, 173 tests passed.
- Targeted type-aware lint, type checking, format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local autoreview at P0–P3 found no actionable defects in the two-file diff and supplied lease implementation. Base `f9ae6fd66f`, patch committed as `e1b4c35626`.
- The change reuses the lease worker and extends the existing two-mode regression. Net line count is unchanged in both files.

- Required CI finished with one failing workload, bundled UI E2E. The PR run and scheduled main fail the same three cases in `route-asset-requests.e2e.test.ts`: skills and plugins readiness timeouts and the same `deferred-ui-support-GykFjbvH.js` request assertion in skill settings. The automated classifier used an earlier main run and could not match the shard name. [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44811996749/job/136551578740) · [Scheduled main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44811259220/job/136548920086) · [Required gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44811996749/job/136558811907)

### What was not tested

Full foreground Gateway forced exit, live GitHub publication, WAN latency, and paid model calls.

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

A config command can fail after saving a change that the running Gateway applies moments later. The CLI now checks briefly for the saved revision and reports success when that revision is active.

### What Problem This Solves

The command could exit 1 and tell operators to inspect or reapply a change even when the config watcher applied it after the reply. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/196174

### User Impact

A recovered write reports that the Gateway applied the change. If the Gateway cannot confirm the revision, the CLI reports the original error and keeps its nonzero exit status.

### Why This Change Was Made

The CLI can confirm the result using the existing `config.get` response after the write RPC releases its admission. It never replays the write. A single two-second deadline bounds the confirmation reads.

## Root Cause

After a saved edit fails its first apply, the Gateway sends `UNAVAILABLE` with the saved revision. That reply lets the watcher retry under its own admission. The old CLI treated the reply as final and exited 1. The CLI now checks both the saved file revision and the applied runtime revision before it reports success. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f9ae6fd66fa349aa8b8492bc7b1d388c799e42a7/src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts#L193

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

An isolated Gateway rejected the first apply of `openclaw config set logging.level debug` after writing the setting to disk. On main the CLI reported `UNAVAILABLE` and exited 1. The regression sends a file observation with the same bytes, and verified that the CLI exits 0 and prints `Updated logging.level. The Gateway applied the change.` A persistent apply failure keeps exit 1 and the original error.

A control run on a disposable PostgreSQL 18.7 cluster sent 24 CLI-mode `config.patch` requests alternating an unused model entry. All 24 returned OK with the expected saved and active values. The test cluster was stopped and removed.

### What was not tested

The product tests made no paid model calls. The regression injects the initial apply failure and does not reproduce the original PostgreSQL worker exception. No throughput or latency benchmark was run. The tests validate the observable exit status on the error path.

## Verification

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/cli/config-owner-route.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 19 cases. The full test file took 110.83 seconds. The transient and persistent cases took 3.64 and 3.69 seconds.
- Targeted Oxlint, CLI test TypeScript project, Oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. The lint pass prompted a parameter rename after the process test, with the same behavior.
- Both regressions passed under the default Bun test runtime on the pushed head. With main's original CLI files and the final fixture, the transient test failed at the exit assertion with `UNAVAILABLE` and exit 1.
- Local autoreview covered P0–P3 on the pushed head against [the assigned main base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f9ae6fd66fa349aa8b8492bc7b1d388c799e42a7) and returned no actionable findings.
- Hosted CI reproduced three pre-existing failures in `route-asset-requests.e2e.test.ts`. The skills and plugins readiness selectors timed out, and skill settings requested 33 assets against the same limit of 31 and listed the same deferred bundle. The [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44812187989/job/136552224345) and [scheduled main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44802039471/job/136517215441) show all three matching signatures.
- The required CI gate is red. Its classifier compares job names and could not match the PR's 2-shard run to main's 10-shard run. The exact test signatures are linked above. Security review passed for this head. [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44812187989/job/136563863288) · [Security review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44812188297/job/136551468134)

prs.title: fix(doctor): validate legacy sessions in the configured store
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Doctor can write a legacy session to PostgreSQL and then report it missing. This fix checks the configured agent store before archiving the legacy index and runs SQLite compaction only for SQLite imports.

## Root Cause

The import writer uses the configured database engine. The pre-import and post-import checks opened the local SQLite file directly. With PostgreSQL selected, that file is an anchor and contains no session rows. The regression runs the real import workflow with a canonical key in a disposable PostgreSQL database. It reproduced `sqlite_entry_missing` after the importer reported one imported entry. After the validation read was corrected, the same workflow exposed an automatic SQLite compaction call that also targeted the anchor and blocked archival.

## Real behavior proof

Used a disposable PostgreSQL 17 server and an isolated state directory with a legacy `sessions.json`, a canonical `agent:main:main` key, and a JSONL transcript with one synthetic user message.

1. Ran `openclaw doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` with the published 2026.11.6 CLI. It exited 1 with `SQLite entry is missing for agent:main:main` and `Legacy session store requires migration`. PostgreSQL already contained the expected session row.
2. Ran the same command with the patched source CLI against the same state and database. It exited 0 and printed `Doctor complete.`
3. Checked the PostgreSQL session row and its two transcript events. Exactly one event contained the synthetic user message. Both files archived by Doctor matched their original bytes.

## What was not tested

No live Gateway, external channels, or paid model calls. The patched CLI ran from source. Import performance was not benchmarked.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with the PostgreSQL conformance preload. The same regression failed with `sqlite_entry_missing` on the base and passed with the patch.
- The production patch passed all 19 tests across the PostgreSQL regression and SQLite compaction suites. The follow-up commit changes only test stubs.
- The first CI run identified three recovery suites that still stubbed the prior reader. Moved the stubs to the configured-reader boundary. All 49 tests in the three suites passed under the pinned Bun runtime.
- Targeted lint and format checks, the commit freshness checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local autoreview could prepare the diff but could not start the reviewer in its isolated runtime. Hosted review is the fallback.

- The required CI gate is red from one UI shard. Its three failures match scheduled main at the individual test and error level. Skills and Plugins time out on the same readiness selectors, and Skill Settings fails on the same deferred asset. The scheduled run used different shard numbering, so the automated classifier could not match the job name. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44814474173/job/136560236375 https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44811259220/job/136548920086 https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44814474173/job/136572165166

prs.title: fix: let large PostgreSQL maintenance operations finish
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Large database upgrades and search rebuilds can fail at the same timeout on every retry. Give these maintenance transactions a one-hour SQL budget and matching bridge headroom, while keeping ordinary requests on their existing limits.

- Apply the scoped budget to schema admission/migration, including update generation fingerprints, first-use search extension builds, and explicit search rebuilds.
- Keep the 60-second lock limit. Restore the caller's SQL limit after nested maintenance; transaction completion restores the session default.
- Reuse the existing transaction owner and savepoints. No config, schema version, dependency, durability, or bridge wire-format change.
- Composes with #201856: that PR sends each request's host deadline to the worker and retires a silent connection 20 seconds before it. Maintenance requests therefore get a client cutoff of one hour plus 10 seconds instead of the ordinary 100 seconds.

## Root Cause

Runtime connections set a 90-second `statement_timeout`, and each synchronous bridge request has a separate 120-second deadline. Schema migrations and whole-store derived builds used these runtime limits too. A migration statement canceled at 90 seconds rolls back, so retrying cannot advance it. Generation fingerprinting can also exceed the bridge deadline across multiple statements.

On the base revision, a real `openEngineStore` migration with one retained row and an injected `SELECT pg_sleep(91)` failed after **90,028 ms** with `57014: canceling statement due to statement timeout`. The schema stayed at version 1 and the retained row was unchanged. This proves the deadline mechanism, not a production corpus-size threshold.

## Real behavior proof

On a disposable, Unix-socket-only PostgreSQL 17.12 server:

- The same 91-second migration passed after **91,119 ms**. The row survived, its migrated value was present, and the schema advanced to version 2.
- A 121-second migration also passed after **121,138 ms**, crossing both former deadlines. `SHOW statement_timeout` returned `90s` afterward in both runs.
- An isolated foreground Gateway using the repository's mock OpenAI config returned `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK_MAINTENANCE` through `agent --agent main --message 'Return marker OPENCLAW_E2E_OK_MAINTENANCE' --thinking off --json`: exit 0, readiness true, marker true. No paid model calls.

Release compatibility from the current stable release: the official npm `openclaw@2026.11.6` package (schemas state 36 / agent 38) ran a real foreground Gateway on a disposable PostgreSQL 17 server with the repository's mock OpenAI config and completed a turn. The candidate, this PR combined with #201856 on the PR merge base, then ran `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions`: it saved pre-migration backups and upgraded the schemas to 40/43. All **8 transcript events kept identical payload hashes**, a stored setting and selected config values survived, a new runtime connection reported `statement_timeout` `90s`, and the candidate Gateway reopened the same session and returned the mock marker. Service repair was disabled; no paid model calls.

The same harness fails on current `main` without this PR (built at the `main` commit this branch merged): candidate Doctor exits 1 with `This agent database scope still requires its existing native owner` after `maintenance finish`. The PR merge base passes it, so the failure was introduced on `main` after the merge base and is independent of this PR's code; this branch's current head inherits it through the conflict-resolving merge of `main`. An earlier run with `openclaw@2026.11.5` on this PR alone also passed.

A third regression runs a real `runTransaction(..., { maintenance: true })` with `SELECT pg_sleep(12)` on a connection whose runtime statement budget is 1 second. On the base it failed after **1112 ms** (`canceling statement due to statement timeout`); with this PR it returns after **12015 ms** and `SHOW statement_timeout` is `1s` afterward. 12 seconds also exceeds the 11-second client cutoff that #201856 derives from that 1-second budget, so this test guards the combination. On a scratch merge of this PR's earlier head with #201856's earlier head (fixed client `query_timeout`), the same test failed after **11078 ms** (`PostgreSQL connection lost; transaction rolled back`). On a scratch merge with #201856's current head it passes in **12024 ms**, together with #201856's silent commit and idle regressions (11134 ms and 10066 ms, peers kept).

The two earlier committed regressions were red on the base: a delayed bridge reply was rejected at the runtime deadline, and maintenance retained the caller's runtime SQL limit. They now pass. The server regression also exercises migration admission and restoration after nested success and rollback, preserving committed rows.

## Landing order

Land #201856 first, then merge `main` into this branch. The only code conflict is the request deadline line in `src/infra/postgres-sync/connection.ts` (and its policy import); docs merge cleanly. Verified resolution:

```ts
const deadlineMs =
  (this.maintenance
    ? POSTGRES_MAINTENANCE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS
    : (this.bridgeParameters.statementTimeoutMs ?? POSTGRES_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS)) + 30_000;
```

Either PR alone is safe: this PR alone has no client cutoff, and #201856 alone keeps the ordinary 100-second cutoff and 120-second deadline.

## What was not tested

- A production-sized corpus or corpus throughput benchmark. Injected SQL delays test the timeout boundary; they do not estimate migration speed. No production dataset was available to this test environment.
- A current-stable Doctor upgrade on this branch's exact head: it inherits the `main` failure described above. The combined PR code passed the same upgrade on the merge base.
- Managed-service package replacement through the updater. Release compatibility was tested through explicit Doctor with foreground Gateways and service repair disabled.
- Local PostgreSQL 16/18, remote TLS, or paid model providers. CI also passed its PostgreSQL 16 smoke lane.
- An hour-long timeout expiry. Maintenance still has a finite limit and can fail above it.

## Verification

- `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TEST_POSTGRES_CONNECTION" -- src/infra/postgres-sync/connection.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/schema-admission.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: base **2 failed, 49 passed**.
- With the disposable-server conformance preload, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/postgres-sync/connection.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/schema-admission.postgres.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/search-extension.postgres.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/postgres-search-admission.postgres.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/postgres-vector-search-schema.postgres.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/postgres-text-search-schema.postgres.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/adapters.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/open.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **75 passed** across eight files. Test shard durations: **1.02 s + 10.97 s**; total wrapper wall time **52.74 s**. Previous-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44538853149) passed, including all four PostgreSQL conformance shards and the PostgreSQL 16 smoke lane.
- Populated-search rebuild conformance: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/database-engine/postgres-search.conformance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with the same disposable-server preload: **10 passed**, including retained source rows, source deletion, rollback, and nonempty derived rebuilds. File duration **3.21 s**, wrapper wall time **52.18 s**. Total focused proof: **85 passed**.
- New regression durations: real-server migration/restoration **224 ms**; injected-clock bridge deadline **3 ms**.
- Current head (main merged in to resolve a conflict in `search-extension.ts`: main's new owner-requested rebuild path now runs inside the maintenance transaction): `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <disposable DSN> -- src/infra/postgres-sync src/infra/database-engine/schema-admission.postgres.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/search-extension.postgres.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/postgres-search.conformance.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/postgres-search-admission.postgres.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-rebuild.postgres.test.ts` on a disposable PostgreSQL 17 server: **45 + 132 + 2 passed**. `tsconfig.core.json` and test-infra typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check`: passed.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44789452960) on `e0836463f29`: SUCCESS, including all four PostgreSQL conformance shards and the PostgreSQL 16 smoke.
- Combined with #201856's current head (scratch merge, not pushed), the same files plus `port-command.integration.test.ts`: **45 + 160 + 2 passed**, including the maintenance composition test (12024 ms), #201856's silent commit/idle regressions (11134 ms, 10066 ms), and the lost-commit-reply port case.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`: passed.
- Focused `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on changed files: passed. `git diff --check`: passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed in **5m 1.2s**, with nonblocking UI budget warnings.
- Simplification pass: one existing transaction owner, no new persistent state or parallel maintenance connection. The added production code coordinates the SQL and bridge budgets; the tests protect timeout and restoration behavior.

## Evidence

Local autoreview on the current head (branch mode, P0 to P2, base `3587df70a233dc639b733b9169797d3abd138301`) is scoped-clean with no actionable findings. On the earlier head, local autoreview was attempted against base `3587df70a233dc639b733b9169797d3abd138301` and the complete local change, at P0–P2 coverage. Its CLI isolation preflight failed before a reviewer ran. [Hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201869#issuecomment-7011668561) covered head `a109443fa41cf70572e7365fa2cd847f9ce25e02` and reported no actionable code or security findings. It requested released-data compatibility proof; the real release-to-candidate Doctor upgrade above supplies that proof. Final maintainer review remains required.

prs.title: fix: let doctor --fix finish when an old Matrix room session has a pending heartbeat result
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Older releases could save a Matrix room session under a lowercased key. Doctor is meant to fix that key. But if the room also has a saved heartbeat result, `openclaw doctor --fix` stops with exit 1 before it gets to the key fix. The error tells you to run `openclaw doctor --fix`, so you are stuck in a loop. This change makes Doctor repair the session keys first when it hits that case, then import the heartbeat result. Doctor now finishes on SQLite. On PostgreSQL it also needs #201857, which fixes a separate artifact-upsert error in the same key repair; with both, Doctor finishes there too.

### What Problem This Solves

Say you upgrade from a release made before the session-key repair landed. Your store still has a lowercased Matrix room key, for example `agent:main:matrix:channel:!room:example.org`, while the real room is `!Room:example.org`. Heartbeats also left a result for that room. On every release since heartbeat outcomes moved to Doctor, `openclaw doctor --fix` then fails with:

```
non-canonical persisted row resolves to session key agent:main:matrix:channel:!Upgrade:example.org; stop the Gateway and run openclaw doctor --fix
```

Running the same command again fails the same way. The Gateway also refuses to read that room until the key is fixed.

### User Impact

`openclaw doctor --fix` exits 0 on these stores. The room keeps its history and artifacts under its real key, and the pending heartbeat result lands in that room's transcript. Doctor prints `Canonicalized N legacy session-key group(s) before importing their heartbeat outcomes.` Healthy stores take the same path as before.

### Root Cause

Doctor runs heartbeat retirement inside the config flow (`applyRetiredConfigStep` -> `retireHeartbeatWithDoctor` -> `migrateHeartbeatOutcomes`). That step reads each pending `heartbeat_outcomes` row's session with `readSessionEntryReadOnlyInWorker`. The reader enforces the canonical-key guard (`validateCanonicalSessionRowEntry`): a row whose stored key is a lowercased form of the room its delivery points at throws `SessionCanonicalKeyMigrationRequiredError`. Doctor's own fix for those rows, `repairCanonicalSessionKeys`, runs later in the session stage (`noteSessionTranscriptHealth`). So the earlier step reads a row that the later step would have fixed. The error ends maintenance, and the key repair never runs.

RCA proof. I captured the stack from the packaged CLI on current `main` against the failing store:

```
SessionCanonicalKeyMigrationRequiredError: non-canonical persisted row resolves to session key agent:main:matrix:channel:!Upgrade:example.org
    at validateCanonicalSessionRowEntry
    at parseReadableSessionEntryData
    ...
    at async withSessionStoreReaderInWorker
    at async migrateHeartbeatOutcomes
    at async retireHeartbeatWithDoctor
    at async applyRetiredConfigStep
    at async loadAndMaybeMigrateDoctorConfig
```

Before-behavior matrix. Each store was created with published `openclaw@2026.11.5`, then given the legacy rows described under proof:

| Store | Pending heartbeat on alias | 2026.11.5 doctor | main doctor | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SQLite, alias only | no | exit 0, repaired | exit 0, repaired | exit 0 |
| SQLite, alias only | yes | exit 1, guard | exit 1, guard | exit 0, repaired |
| PostgreSQL 17, alias only | yes | exit 1, same guard class (`invalid persisted session row requires repair`) | exit 1, guard | gets past the guard (see dependency) |

On SQLite without a heartbeat row, the key repair works on both versions. So the cause is the order of these two Doctor steps, not the repair logic and not the database engine.

### Why This Change Was Made

`migrateHeartbeatOutcomes` now catches only `SessionCanonicalKeyMigrationRequiredError`. On that error it runs the existing repair owner, `repairCanonicalSessionKeys({ apply: true })`. It takes the same `withDoctorSqliteMaintenanceLock` the session stage uses, then retries the import once. The key repair already moves `heartbeat_outcomes` to the canonical key, so the retry reads the repaired session. Outcomes imported before the error are idempotent: they are keyed by digest, and the source row is deleted after the append. Every other error is still thrown. A second guard error after the repair is thrown too.

Scope: 2 files, +26 production lines, +31 test lines. No schema, config, CLI, or runtime reader change. All callers (`applyRetiredConfigStep`, automatic heartbeat repair, config preflight) already run under Doctor maintenance.

Accepted edge case: if a lowercased alias row and its canonical row each have a pending heartbeat outcome, the existing key-repair merge keeps only the newer outcome (`heartbeat_outcomes` is keyed by `session_key`). The older outcome is not imported into the transcript and no warning is printed. The database backup Doctor takes before heartbeat retirement still holds it. This needs two pending heartbeats for the same room under both key forms, which is rare, and the dropped row is the older heartbeat status summary, not chat history.

PostgreSQL dependency: the key repair's artifact upserts fail on PostgreSQL with `42702 column reference "revision" is ambiguous` until #201857 lands (unqualified `ON CONFLICT ... WHERE` columns). With this PR alone, the PostgreSQL store gets past the guard and then hits that error. With both PRs it completes. #201857 alone still fails at the guard. The two fixes are independent, and either can land first.

## Real behavior proof

Environment: Linux, Node 26. Isolated `HOME`/state, bundled plugins disabled, no model credentials, service repair off. Disposable PostgreSQL 17.12 on a private Unix socket. Stores were created by published `openclaw@2026.11.5` installed into a throwaway npm prefix:

- SQLite: 2026.11.5 `doctor --fix` imported a legacy `sessions.json` that had a Matrix room session. That created a real agent database. I then rewrote the room's `session_key` columns to the lowercased legacy form and added one pending `heartbeat_outcomes` row for it with `sqlite3`. This reproduces the pre-repair on-disk state.
- PostgreSQL: 2026.11.5 Gateway started on PostgreSQL and created the agent schema through `sessions.create`. I then inserted a lowercased alias row (and, in a second store, the canonical row too) with board tabs, widgets, progress cards, and heartbeat outcomes, using SQL.

Command for every Doctor run, using the CLI built from each head:

```
node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions
```

Results:

- SQLite, base `main` (1129d4c0716): exit 1, `non-canonical persisted row resolves to session key agent:main:matrix:channel:!Upgrade:example.org`.
- SQLite, 2026.11.5 package: exit 1, same message.
- SQLite, this PR: exit 0, `Canonicalized 1 legacy session-key group(s) before importing their heartbeat outcomes.`, `Doctor complete.`. SQL readback: one row under `agent:main:matrix:channel:!Upgrade:example.org` with its original session id, 0 pending heartbeat outcomes, and the outcome text in that session's transcript. Then a Gateway from this PR started on the repaired store. `chat.history` for the canonical key returned the session (same session id, `totalMessages: 1`), with no guard errors in the Gateway log. `openclaw sessions --json` listed the canonical key.
- PostgreSQL, base `main`: exit 1, same guard message.
- PostgreSQL, this PR alone: past the guard, then exit 1, `column reference "revision" is ambiguous` (the #201857 defect).
- PostgreSQL, `main` + #201857 without this PR: exit 1, guard message.
- PostgreSQL, this PR + #201857: exit 0 for both the alias-only store and the alias-plus-canonical store. SQL readback: no alias rows; board tab, widget, and progress card under the canonical key (the newer source copy won); 0 pending heartbeat outcomes; outcome text in the canonical session's transcript. A Gateway started on the repaired store and served `chat.history` for the canonical key. `openclaw sessions --json` listed it.

### Latest stable upgrade (v2026.11.6 to this head)

This run has the PR commit applied on current `main` (package version 2026.11.6), so the Gateway accepts a config last written by 2026.11.6. The PostgreSQL run also includes #201857.

- SQLite. Published `openclaw@2026.11.6` `doctor --fix` imported a legacy `sessions.json` Matrix room session with one user message. The config also set `session.reset` (idle, 10080 min), `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`, and gateway port/auth. I then lowercased the room key and added a pending heartbeat outcome, a board tab and widget, and a progress card on the alias, with SQL.
  - 2026.11.6 `doctor --fix`: exit 1, `non-canonical persisted row resolves to session key agent:main:matrix:channel:!Upgrade:example.org`.
  - This head: exit 0. Every original config leaf is unchanged. There is one session row under the canonical key with the original session id `upgrade-source`. The tab, widget, and progress card moved to the canonical key. 0 pending heartbeat outcomes. The user message and the migrated outcome are both in the `upgrade-source` transcript. A Gateway on the repaired store returned `chat.history` for the canonical key: same session id, `totalMessages: 2`, the user message visible, no guard errors in its log.
- PostgreSQL 17. Published 2026.11.6 Gateway created the agent schema (`sessions.create`). I then seeded the lowercased alias row with tab, widget, progress card, and heartbeat outcome by SQL, plus the room's two transcript events (copied from a 2026.11.6 import).
  - 2026.11.6 `doctor --fix`: exit 1, `invalid persisted session row requires repair for agent:main:matrix:channel:!upgrade:example.org`.
  - This head + #201857: exit 0. Settings are unchanged. The session row, tab, widget, and card are under the canonical key with the original session id. 0 pending outcomes. The user message and the migrated outcome are in the transcript. A Gateway on the repaired store returned the same `chat.history` result.

Performance (healthy store, no alias): `doctor --fix` wall time on fresh copies of the same SQLite store with one valid pending heartbeat outcome. Same host and workload, first run counted as warmup. Base `main`: 11.5 to 12.3 s, median 12.0 s (5 runs). This PR: 11.2 to 17.2 s, median 12.2 s (10 runs). The two slow runs line up with host load around 9. That is no measurable change. The healthy path adds only a `try` frame, and the key repair runs only after the guard error.

### What was not tested

- A store produced by a real pre-July release, or a real Matrix channel. The legacy alias and heartbeat rows were made with SQL on 2026.11.5-created stores.
- The update-driven automatic heartbeat repair and config-preflight callers, end to end. They call the same function under Doctor maintenance, and their existing tests pass.
- PostgreSQL completion with this PR alone. It needs #201857, as noted above.
- The alias-plus-canonical case where both rows have a pending heartbeat outcome (see the accepted edge case above).
- Live channels and paid models.

## Verification

- Red on base: `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-outcome-migration.test.ts` fails the new case with `SessionCanonicalKeyMigrationRequiredError` (1 failed, 10 passed). Green with the fix: 11 passed.
- Consumers: the 14 test files that import the heartbeat retirement, outcome migration, or automatic heartbeat repair modules all pass (6 Vitest shards).
- `run-oxlint` on both files, `run-format --check`, and `run-tsgo` for `tsconfig.core.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands-doctor.json`: clean.
- Local autoreview (branch mode, P0 to P2): scoped-clean.
- pr-simplify: kept to one catch-and-retry in the existing owner and one regression in the existing suite. No new helper, module, or option.
- PR CI: every check passed except `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)`, which failed on both attempts in `ui/src/e2e/route-asset-requests.e2e.test.ts` ("bounds plugins ready-window asset requests", `Page readiness timed out: plugins (openclaw-plugins-page .plugin-catalog-card)`). This failure comes from `main`, not this PR: the scheduled `main` CI run at 5b50d1b89bf (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44793178209) fails the same test with the same readiness error in `checks-ui-e2e (2/10)` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44793178209/job/136486944793), and 7 of its 10 `checks-ui-e2e` shards are red, mostly in the Plugins catalog pages after that day's catalog redesign. This PR touches no UI or Gateway runtime code.

prs.title: fix(test): clear environment stubs after process.env replacement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tests can leak environment variables after `process.env` is replaced. Vitest 5.0.5 reads and writes through the current environment, but its `import.meta.env` proxy deletes from the object captured at worker initialization. As a result, both `vi.stubEnv(key, undefined)` and `vi.unstubAllEnvs()` can leave keys behind.

A plain `process.env = { ...process.env }` reproduces this on Node. On stock Bun, SHARE_ENV worker promotion triggers the replacement: upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/44371.

## User Impact

OpenClaw developers can rely on environment stubs being cleared across tests after an environment replacement. This changes the test dependency patch only; no application behavior, runtime pin, or existing test file is migrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing exact-version Vitest patch with `deleteProperty` and `has` traps in both bundled proxy copies. String keys resolve against current `process.env`, including DEV/PROD/SSR; ignored non-string keys retain the existing policy.

Enumeration and descriptors deliberately remain target-owned. A stale non-extensible target cannot forward a different key set, and a replacement's non-configurable descriptor can violate Proxy invariants. The regression checks `Object.keys` and spread of captured keys after a swap; replacement-only keys are not promised in enumeration.

All nine previous patch sections and insertion anchors remain byte-identical. Remove the new hunks when a Vitest release forwards proxy deletion and the Node regression passes unpatched.

## Evidence

The Node regression failed unpatched (5 failures, 1 pass) and now passes all six cases. The owning-boundary regression, existing mock-resolution tests, patch guard, exact-version guard, and dependency-guard tests pass together: 56 tests. Direct module-evaluator probing covers deletion, membership, boolean keys, symbols, and target-owned enumeration. Targeted typecheck, lint, and formatting pass. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues.

W457 baseline: all 60 assigned IDs in 25 files fail on stock and pass on the pinned fork. Already fixed: 0. Linux-only-unverified: 0. In the unpatched baseline, the auth-file failures occur earlier than the W457 record, at bundled-plugin discovery, because clearing `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS` hits the same stale proxy.

The complete 25-file replay passed all 60 assigned IDs on Node and the pinned fork, and 59 on stock. The full-file revert control restored the original patch and lockfile, reinstalled dependencies, verified all target hashes, and reproduced all 60 stock failures. The 59 repaired cases therefore changed from fail to pass to fail; the remaining fleet case stayed failed. The extended patch was then restored and verified again.

The new six-case regression takes 2.47s on Node, 2.05s on the fork, and 2.23s on stock, including the wrapper. The unpatched Node run took 3.31s and failed five cases. Assertions take only a few milliseconds.

Proof baseline: `6b0df8b93610b320210488d93e6e205aafb84e69`. Runtimes: Node 26.12.1; stock Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+2596ac5d3; pinned fork 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1. Already fixed on the baseline main: 0. Linux-only-unverified IDs: none.

### Concurrent-main resolution of the remaining stock failure

At the reviewed VP head, `src/flows/doctor-health.fleet-preflight.test.ts` — `preserves original config bytes before Doctor relocates and repairs legacy state` failed at line 126: `expected true to be false`, because the legacy directory remained present. prs.title: feat(ios): filter sessions by attention and work
prs.body:
Related: #162814

## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, finding conversations waiting for an answer or approval requires checking individual session rows.

## User Impact

Sessions gains All, Needs you, and Working filters with conversation counts for the selected Gateway, agent, and existing status scope. One conversation counts once even when it has multiple requests. Working includes active or queued runs and active child work; it can overlap Needs you. Request badges reuse the existing native preview and approval flow.

All preserves offline browsing. Live activity filters are disabled while disconnected, and incomplete rosters retain a + count qualifier.

This is a draft for the initial iOS design review. Physical Duo and VoiceOver checks remain before readiness. Android parity is a separate follow-up using the same filter meanings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Sessions screen consumes the existing live roster instead of keeping a second nonarchived snapshot. The existing owners retain question/approval matching, expiry, navigation, grouping, mutations, and Gateway policy. No server, protocol, schema, permission, or persistent setting is added.

Android's native SessionsScreen already has the needed roster and attention/run-state contracts. This PR does not modify or claim validation of Android.

## Native Sessions proof with a real Gateway

Captured on the Mac Studio with an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator running iOS 27.0. The comparison uses upstream `ed3230dd29d1` and published draft head `5c8b666d53e5`. Both apps used the same three fictional conversations from an isolated OpenClaw `2026.11.4` Gateway. The agent ran Qwen3 4B locally through llama.cpp. A test operator created and answered the ordinary question through the Gateway API, and the model generated the separate work turn.

### Clean comparison

| Upstream Sessions | Draft Sessions |
| --- | --- |
| ![Upstream Sessions shows three rows with no activity filter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e28e8bf-83a1-4663-b9a6-20923b75021e) | ![Draft Sessions shows the same three rows, with All 3, Needs you 1, and Working 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee20cc17-e197-439d-a1c0-984f26e77384) |

### Annotated comparison

| Upstream | Draft |
| --- | --- |
| ![The rows start immediately below the status scopes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2e07899-2d29-4309-b46e-9541c2e72b3c) | ![Activity controls and counts appear between the status scopes and the rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad6e8492-764d-4e94-866c-2401e19d519e) |

### Live updates

| Needs you selected | Working selected | After both settle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Needs you shows only Color review with a pending question](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9f2873e-da2d-4a86-8442-6b27f3315369) | ![Working shows only Launch checklist during a real model run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd7b47fe-cea3-49e2-9fe2-3a98893e1d4e) | ![After the question and run settle, All stays at 3 and both activity counts are 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad309f62-7f9f-45ce-af63-cf17e4183e86) |

The native Sessions screen stayed open during the transition. This trace records the visible filter values and the corresponding Gateway state.

```text
Pending question in Color review     All 3   Needs you 1   Working 0
Needs you selected                  Color review is the only row
Qwen starts on Launch checklist     All 3   Needs you 1   Working 1
Separate capture with Working open  Launch checklist is the only row while the model runs
Gateway accepts Fern                Question status: answered
Model finishes                      All 3   Needs you 0   Working 0
Gateway final state                 Launch checklist: done, no active run
```

The captured proof covers this simulator and the published Sessions screen. The broader design previews below are from separate work.

## November 17 draft update

Merged upstream `ed3230dd29d1` into the existing activity-filter branch. Resolved the four conflicts while retaining upstream session grouping, collapsed sections, and the partial-load retry. The Sessions clock now refreshes when the roster changes and continues to refresh when request or snooze deadlines expire.

Verified on the iOS 27.0 iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator at `5c8b666d53e5`:

- 19 focused Swift tests passed (3 activity logic and 16 typography).
- Both native Sessions flows passed against an isolated synthetic Gateway. The activity flow verified filter counts and live request/run updates. The recency regression verified that a planning row aged past “just now” when a different row changed, with no pending requests or snoozes.
- Native localization verification, SwiftFormat, app-target SwiftLint, and diff checks passed.

The layout images below are from the earlier design prototype. This draft is still asking for an iOS design decision on the focused activity filters.

## Layout prototype for design feedback

The latest local prototype puts a compact filter dropdown beside **Sessions** in the sidebar, with compact icon-and-count cards on the full Sessions screen. Both locations offer **All**, **Needs you**, and **Working**.

On the full Sessions screen, attention rows have one tappable hand or shield on the left. The hand means **Waiting for answer**; the shield means **Waiting for approval**. Both use amber status text and a subtle warning tint because both need a user response. Working rows and the Working card use informational blue. Text and distinct symbols convey the state as well as color. Status labels consistently use sentence case, including Recent, Working, Waiting for answer, and Waiting for approval. The existing native request previews remain available. The sidebar keeps its native attention badges and work indicators.

These images show eight fictional conversations: two waiting for an answer or approval, three working, and three idle. Each image compares **All / Needs you / Working**, with no before/after panels. They are native standard-iPhone simulator captures with synthetic Gateway state. No personal conversations, private Gateway addresses, or real agent tasks appear.

Feedback requested: does keeping the sidebar control beside Sessions make its scope clear? Do the compact cards and the attention-row styling feel clear without adding clutter? Feedback on wording, spacing, colors, and selection styling is welcome. Android parity remains a separate follow-up using the same filter meanings.

**Sessions screen: All / Needs you / Working**

![Latest local Sessions prototype with amber question and approval rows, blue Working states, and compact filter cards](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04f3b1a7-059a-4c8e-80d0-7aa24a343e14)

**Sidebar: All / Needs you / Working**

![Latest local sidebar prototype with filtering beside the Sessions heading and fictional conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49b52069-9ba1-41c3-b259-5b3b8bf28392)

These are design previews from uncommitted local refinements atop local prototype `4650e6cf067c249871fa7ee7871c466a450b6d01`. The sidebar placement, card styling, status-row cleanup, and adaptive scope control shown here have not been pushed to this draft's published head, `cbb83f9eff100aa5437f15c19c9c3383ee4657d4`. They are not exact-head merge proof. The PR remains a draft for design feedback.

Local refinement checks: 24 typography tests and four activity-owner logic tests pass, as do the native filter flows at standard and largest accessibility text sizes. The sole leading hand and shield were each tapped to verify that the correct native preview opens without leaving Sessions. Light and dark appearances were inspected. The latest local prototype, including sentence-case status labels, was installed and launched on the physical Duo as the separate OpenClaw Sessions build 10. The installed version was read back from the device. A fresh physical visual/interaction check of this revision and a full VoiceOver audit are still pending. The Evidence section below describes the earlier published implementation separately.

## Evidence

- Base: 42aab1ce38cdde59eaa3f2babc3eef488ea9db2c. The native baseline reaches All Sessions and fails because the activity filter is absent.
- Three focused native logic tests pass: distinct conversation counts, overlapping work/attention, terminal and explicit run-state precedence, resolution/expiry/agent matching, and offline/partial data. Test execution: 0.016 seconds; runner setup/execution: 20.805 seconds.
- Native iPhone UI flow passes with synthesized screen taps at rendered targets, selected-state and membership assertions, 44-point targets, and live count changes after run completion and question/approval resolution. Standard-size run: 53.400 seconds; largest system accessibility text: 47.326 seconds. The filters stack vertically at the largest size. Existing session-row text still elides at that size; this is not a full accessibility audit.
- XCTest AX hit-point lookup reports no hit point for the activity filters and existing status picker on this simulator. The test explicitly synthesizes screen touches rather than relying on AX activation, then checks the resulting state. VoiceOver is not covered by this result.
- 23 focused typography tests pass. Targeted SwiftLint/SwiftFormat, Node syntax, native i18n verification, docs formatting/MDX, link audit, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Fresh independent source review has no actionable P0-P2 findings. It caught an offline-cache cold-open regression and incomplete archive counts, both repaired before the final run.
- Full-app local qualification: unchanged base strict SwiftLint fails in the Apple review demo fixture, also tracked by #191296. Both UI comparison builds use an independently written, local-only extraction of two unchanged fixture branches, preserving guards, payloads, and timestamps. The synthetic Gateway path never enters those branches. No guard or lint configuration is weakened. That qualification and unrelated generated Info.plist changes are excluded from this PR. These results are not exact-tree full-app CI.

prs.title: fix: check publication read opt-in at request admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Turning off publication reads retires connections and reads that were already admitted, and keeps them retired even if the switch is turned back on. The switch should decide whether a new connection or request can start. It should not revoke work that was already admitted.

The writer transport from #202654 already follows that rule. The reader still carried a disable epoch, so the two purposes on the same transport behaved differently.

## User Impact

`gateway.sessionControl.publicationReadEnabled` stays off by default. It is checked when each signed-reader connection starts and when each read request starts.

- Off: new reader connections and new read requests are refused.
- A read that was admitted before the switch went off may finish.
- An existing connection can read again after the switch is turned back on. No reconnect is needed.

Unchanged: device and token revocation, the singleton signed-device scope, the Session Share source opt-in, approved device IDs, person and group selection, session and store identity, and disconnect handling. No configuration key is added or removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `src/gateway/publication-reader.ts`: the reader disable epoch and its captured recheck are gone. The handshake validates the caller first and then checks the purpose switch once, so an invalid caller still learns nothing about the switch. Reader and writer now share one admission path.
- `src/config/runtime-config-publication.ts`, `src/config/runtime-snapshot.ts`: `publicationReadDisableEpoch` is deleted.
- Per-request enablement stays in `src/gateway/server-methods/method-authorization.ts`, where #202654 put it for both purposes.
- `extensions/session-share`: the plugin no longer rechecks the host switch or config object identity in the middle of a read. An unrelated configuration write used to fail a read in progress. The plugin still checks its own source opt-in, approved devices and selection before disclosing.
- `config/knip.config.ts`: `prepareGatewayPublicationTransportV1` landed in #202654 with no production consumer until the Session Share writer handlers arrive, and the production unused-export scan flags it on `main`. It is registered as a staged audit root with a removal note.
- Docs and config help now describe the request-start rule.

This is the reader follow-up to #202299 and #202654. It was first written against an older `main`; it is now ported onto the shared transport that #202654 landed.

## Evidence

Blacksmith Testbox on the merged tree:

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server.auth.publication-reader.test.ts test/plugins/session-share-publication.gateway.test.ts extensions/session-share/src/config.test.ts`: passed. The signed-transport suite is 44 passed, 2 skipped across reader and writer.
- New gateway-seam test for both purposes: a request admitted before the switch goes off completes and discloses; a request started while off gets `FORBIDDEN`; a new connection while off is refused; the same socket works again after re-enabling.
- The Session Share signed-WSS test proves an admitted transcript read finishes after the host switch goes off, and that source-grant changes still withhold results.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: passed.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports`: `prepareGatewayPublicationTransportV1` no longer reported.
- `pnpm config:docs:gen`: baseline hashes regenerated (help text changed).
- `oxfmt --check` on the touched files: clean.

Size: production +17/-54 (net -37), tests +79/-159, docs +8/-8, plus the dead-code config entry and regenerated hashes.

Known gaps:

- `pnpm deadcode:exports` still reports `checkSessionWorkspaceFileLinks` and `openSessionWorkspaceManagedArtifact` in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace.ts`. Those are on `main` and not touched here.
- Fixture devices and content on an in-process Gateway; no live cross-Gateway delivery.

prs.title: fix(telegram): stop Plugin SDK deprecation warnings blamed on the bundled Telegram plugin
prs.body:
Closes #191786
Closes #191785
Related: #174937, #190243

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway logs `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` warnings blamed on "Plugin telegram", and the Plugins catalog marks Telegram as using APIs that retire on Dec 31, 2026, when the bundled Telegram plugin loads, or when a Telegram group message from another member steers an active run under collaborative steering.

## User Impact

User impact: Telegram operators no longer see the startup deprecation warning, the `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` warning on steering, or the retiring-API notice those two cause. A Telegram group message that steers another member's run under collaborative steering still logs `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint` and `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project`, and those still show as a catalog notice; that read is out of scope here (see "Not in this PR"). Discord, Slack, Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, iMessage, Signal and WhatsApp sessions now list `nativeApprovals` in the agent Runtime capabilities, and Telegram keeps it. Approval authorization, routing and delivery are unchanged. For those 8 channels the Runtime line gains one token, so their system prompt changes once after upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Telegram was the last bundled caller of the sync `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability`. It now uses `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapabilityAsync`, as #174937 did for Discord; `isNativeDeliveryEnabled` wraps the same check.
- `channelPluginHasNativeApprovalPromptUi` read only `native` and `nativeRuntime`. The async factories expose `nativeAsync` and `nativeRuntimeAsync`, so moving Telegram alone would have dropped `nativeApprovals` for Telegram, as it already had for 8 channels. The check now reads all four.
- `prepareFollowupRunToolAuthorityFingerprint` re-read its prepared fingerprint through the deprecated plugin-facing `fingerprint()`. Steering runs in the channel plugin's frame, so the warning and the deprecated-API record landed on Telegram. Core now uses a module-private reader with the same checks; plugin callers of `fingerprint()` still warn.
- Not in this PR: core's sync placement `getMany` (10 call sites, several inside synchronous commit guards; its warning has no fixed removal date), and the collaborative steering read that still calls `projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`. Both need their own core reader and proof.

pr-simplify: no production code removed. One test assertion on a statically defined factory output was removed. No new state, exports or test-only hooks. Production +30 -11 in 3 files; tests +117 -4; three test-line records totaling exactly the 113 net added test lines.

## Evidence

### Gateway run (2026-11-09)

A real Gateway from a built `dist` (`node --trace-deprecation dist/index.js gateway run`, Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64; Vitest also on Node), a local fake Telegram Bot API that grammY talks to as its transport, and a scripted Responses provider that records the `Runtime:` line of every request. Base: main `3855c896edd`. Head: this PR merged onto that main (`git merge-tree --write-tree 3855c896edd d096fe01a3c` = `8f366fba0b5`, no conflicts, same patch-id as this PR's diff). `messages.queue.mode: "steer"`. `channels.discord` and `channels.slack` are `{ enabled: true }` with no tokens, so the Gateway loads both plugins (`5 plugins: discord, memory-core, qa-lab, slack, telegram`) and `channels.status` shows both accounts `configured: false, running: false`. Two runs per scenario per build.

Steering. A run is held open at the provider and a second Telegram message arrives while it is active. In every run the second message is injected into that run (session controller `injection-outcome: consumed`, no "steering rejected" record), the provider gets it in the same session, and Telegram receives both answers.

| scenario | build | DEP_PLUGIN_SDK warnings, all "Plugin telegram" | `plugins.list` notices (of 268 plugins) |
|---|---|---|---|
| group, a second member steers, `allowCollaborativeSteering: true` | main | `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability` (startup); at the steer `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint`, `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`, `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` | telegram, those 4 APIs |
| same | this PR | at the steer `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`, `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` | telegram, those 2 APIs |
| DM, the sender steers their own run | main | `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability` (startup) | telegram, that 1 API |
| same | this PR | none | none |

Stacks from `--trace-deprecation` on main:
- `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint`: `fingerprint <- read <- prepareLegacyReplySteeringAuthority <- prepareReplyMessageJoin <- runActiveReplySteer`. Gone here.
- `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`: `<- read <- prepareCurrent <- prepareCurrent <- beginPreparedReplyMessageInjectionTarget`. Same stack here.
- `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project`: called from inside that `projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`. Same here.
- Startup: `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability <- channel-*.mjs` module load. Gone here.

Two things this shows that the description had wrong or left out:
- On main, a message from the run's own sender does not reach `fingerprint()` at all. A plain message is a `continue-existing` steer, which goes through `prepareReplyMessageContinuation` (since #177698) and never calls the deprecated reader. The fingerprint warning needs the legacy steering path, which a second member's message reaches under collaborative steering.
- On that collaborative path this PR leaves two warnings in place, `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint` and `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` (the second comes from inside the first), and both still put a retiring-API notice on Telegram in the catalog. The first is the collaborative read already listed under "Not in this PR".

Runtime capabilities. The provider's view of `channel=<id> | channel_capabilities=...`, the same in every run of a build. Discord and Slack turns come from the Gateway `agent` RPC with `channel` set and `deliver: false`, on fresh sessions:

| channel | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| telegram (DM and group turns) | `inlinebuttons,nativeapprovals` | `inlinebuttons,nativeapprovals` |
| discord | `threadbound-acp-spawn,threadbound-subagent-spawn` | `nativeapprovals,threadbound-acp-spawn,threadbound-subagent-spawn` |
| slack | `none` | `nativeapprovals` |

Telegram keeps `nativeApprovals` after moving to the async factory, and Discord and Slack gain it.


- At this head the three changed test files pass 37 of 37 (26 + 7 + 4). With the three source files from `19aff5bfd42`, they fail 1 of 26, 5 of 7 and 1 of 4.
- Red on base, green here, each with only that commit's source file reverted:
  - `extensions/telegram/src/approval-native.test.ts`: 5 failed / 2 passed vs 7 passed; the new test receives the deprecation message.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.test.ts` (follow-up read): fails with the `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` usage record vs passes.
  - `src/channels/plugins/approvals.test.ts`: `expected false to be true` vs 4 passed. Dropping either async field alone fails its own assertion.
- `--trace-deprecation` over the message-join and fallback-steering suites (101 tests): `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` warnings 3 -> 0.
- All 9 bundled approval capabilities: `channelPluginHasNativeApprovalPromptUi` true for 1 of 9 on base, 9 of 9 here.
- Prompt consumers 16 files / 174 tests, Telegram and Discord approval suites 9 files / 218 tests, core steering and authority suites 19 files / 371 tests: all pass. `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap, assertion-safety and test-lines ratchets pass against `19aff5bfd42`. If CI's test-lines job is red, that is main's own overage (main has been over its ceiling since `2a32ab046f2`, #191638); this branch adds 113 test lines and 113 lines of allocation.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `approval-native.test.ts` 26.1 s (cold worker cache, 20.2 s of it compiling) and 6.6 s wall, 413 ms and 376 ms of tests; `reply-tool-authority.test.ts` 8.8 s and 7.8 s wall, 1.3 s and 1.2 s of tests; `approvals.test.ts` 10.0 s and 6.2 s wall, 11 ms and 9 ms of tests. CI run 41606285186, Bun: `approval-native.test.ts` 744 ms of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1`); `reply-tool-authority.test.ts` 9.0 s Vitest duration, 1.6 s of tests (`checks-node-changed-7`); `approvals.test.ts` 50.1 s Vitest duration, 17 ms of tests (`checks-node-changed-channels`).
- Not covered end to end: real Telegram, Discord or Slack. The Discord and Slack sessions above came from the Gateway `agent` RPC with their plugins loaded and no accounts running, not from those services. Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, iMessage, Signal and WhatsApp were not run.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): post-call summaries fail after startup caller completes
prs.body:
Closes #191714

## What Problem This Solves

Voice-call summaries could reuse a startup caller's released root admission and fail with GatewayDrainingError. Clearing that root from all service startup also broke suspended reload recovery.

## User Impact

Service startup remains inside the admitted reload transaction. Later voice-call delivery runs through the existing service-owned scheduler, so it does not retain the startup caller's root. Closing the service rejects queued delivery rather than leaving its caller waiting indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep startup/recovery ownership separate from deferred delivery. This revision preserves operator, plugin-generation and Gateway-instance boundaries and does not add a public SDK capability.

## Evidence

176 tests passed across scheduler context, reload recovery, and voice-call lifecycle/delivery suites. The focused cases include post-release work, suspended recovery, scheduler results and queued-service shutdown. Formatting passed. This verifies the isolated runtime boundaries; a live provider post-call summary has not been reproduced here.
