prs.title: improve(ci): start long upgrade checks before the final validation wave
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two fully drained Full Release Validation (FRV) traces ended on a tool-bridge compatibility upgrade check that waited more than 23 minutes for matrix admission. These are required independent checks, not a reason to remove coverage.

## User Impact

At the existing 48-job hosted cap, replay models **5m36s and 5m32s less total FRV wall time** in those two traces. Two other traces model **zero total benefit**, including the newest one, whose first-hop job is already the longest path. These are conditional scheduling estimates, not measured after-change savings or a universal speedup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `acpx-openclaw-tools-bridge` to the existing long-job order, after `plugin-update` and before `legacy-operator-state`. Preserve package recovery, first-hop and restart-auth priority, every complete row, baseline identity, timeout, independent retry/failure, fresh-container isolation, current concurrency caps, and stable remainder order. No new planner, cache, timing data, setting, jobs, or runner capacity.

This builds on #198925 (`8656c447df05`, existing first-hop/legacy priority) and #199911 (`f947bdc94981`, early package recovery), rather than replacing their deliberate policy. It is independent of #202688 (48→64 cap); the incremental gain after that change is reported separately below, never added twice. Author simplification: one list entry plus its evidence comment; extend the existing real-CLI regression rather than add another suite. Production +2/-0, tests +3/-1, docs +5/-0.

## Evidence

All four traces have 92/92 successful targeted rows and fully drained parents, but other validation failures mean **none is claimed as passing release qualification**. Durations include runner setup, downloads, test execution, upload and cleanup. Replay uses the base planner order and earliest-free slots; its cap-48 residual versus observation is 0–3 seconds. Preserve that residual and all sibling/collector barriers in both projections.

| Parent / candidate child | Observed matrix | Base48→proposed48 | Total FRV gain at48 | Incremental total gain after64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|[44773914831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44773914831) / [44777975959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44777975959)|3150s|3148→2812s|336s|287s (2633→2346s)|
|[44790287992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44790287992) / [44794544663](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44794544663)|3032s|3029→2697s|332s|329s (2556→2227s)|
|[44635836314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44635836314) / [44639105831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44639105831)|2912s|2910→2902s|0s (8s hidden by CI)|0s|
|[44832835993](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44832835993) / [44835864437](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44835864437)|2704s|2704→2704s|0s (first-hop dominates)|0s|

- Candidate44777975959, C=Q `3f05d1ac58c19a4bc5417e4685af2ffff56f7b22`: matrix17:07:51–18:00:21 UTC Nov20. [Final ACPX row136440786047](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44777975959/job/136440786047) starts17:31:52 (1441s after matrix start), then runs1709s. Internal sibling floor17:39:49; external CI17:33:59; candidate tail44s and parent tail83s. Base parent ends18:02:28; proposed48 projects17:56:52. With64 plus this change, restart-auth2346s becomes the matrix floor, limiting incremental gain to287s.
- Candidate44794544663, C=Q `fae2f8f16fbd335566c2d9aa500887dedef4da8d`: matrix18:49:39–19:40:11. [Final ACPX row136497002115](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44794544663/job/136497002115) starts19:13:13 (1414s admission delay), then runs1618s. Internal sibling floor19:23:17; external19:22:14. Preserve3s residual,51s candidate tail and observed parent tail: proposed48 matrix ends19:34:39,332s earlier. With64 plus this change, first-hop2026.10.1 at2227s becomes the floor.
- Newest candidate44835864437, C=Q `35207ad56a84cc44cd596556955ce73feaf4d5f8`: first-hop2026.9.9 already occupies2704s in the first wave; no ordering-only gain is claimed. Sealed plan digests for this parent and44790287992 match their drained manifests, with no active children or requested cancellation.

### Coverage, capacity and uncertainty

The current-main 93-row output has **identical complete row objects before/after; only order changes**. Historical replays preserve their exact92-row inventory instead of inventing durations for current-only first-hop2026.11.6 and2026.11.10-beta.1; historical2026.9.36 is absent from the current inventory. Consequently these are frozen-workload estimates, not measured forecasts for all93 current rows.

No extra setup or concurrency is introduced. Work may overlap registry/artifact requests differently, so constant complete-job durations and available runners remain assumptions. Retained32-cap sensitivity on the same four duration sets is nonregressing (+141,+310,+17,+9s matrix gains in the table order), not an observed32-way campaign. Placing ACPX after legacy instead would regress one such replay by44s; that ordering was rejected. An unmeasured workload or severe contention can still erase the benefit.

## Proof

The existing real-CLI regression is red on base solely because ACPX rows remain late, then green with this entry. It asserts complete rows including labels, baseline/scenario identity, timeout, old priorities and stable remaining order. No new test case or timing fixture is committed. Changed suite:13 tests,22ms test bodies,274ms Vitest duration,982ms runner wall time.

All 740 tests across six affected planner, baseline, source-preflight, package-acceptance and release-workflow suites pass (134.41s runner wall time). Targeted tooling-test typecheck, two-file type-aware lint, three-file formatting, documentation MDX and `git diff --check` pass. Local independent review is waived by the task owner. No FRV or native campaign was dispatched. Logs are decision evidence, not a post-change runtime benchmark.

**Ready for review, verified November 21, 2026 at 03:26 UTC**, head `93897401daea0182b165e9138a9942deaa1541b7`: [CI44859542084](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44859542084) and [CodeQL44859541709](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44859541709) succeeded. Full current check rollup: 48 success, 65 skipped, 1 neutral; no failed or pending checks. GitHub reports OPEN, MERGEABLE, CLEAN. [ClawSweeper completed this exact revision at 03:22:27 UTC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202894#issuecomment-7056571971), with no findings and no before-merge items. Its remaining performance uncertainty is explicitly retained above; RFR does not claim measured production savings or authorize merging.

<details>
<summary>Exact replay inputs and method</summary>

Compare the planner at `684018d110ef6d5e38c9530616a65f74950837fe` with this PR using the input below. For historical replay only, expand `update-first-hop-compat` into the explicit version lanes from `scripts/lib/update-compat-inventory.json` at `3f05d1ac58c19a4bc5417e4685af2ffff56f7b22`, followed by `update-first-hop-compat-missing-load-path`. This restores the exact measured 92-row inventory; do not remove or invent current production coverage.

```json
{
  "lanes": "release-typed-onboarding doctor-switch update-channel-switch skill-install update-corrupt-plugin upgrade-survivor update-first-hop-compat published-upgrade-survivor root-managed-vps-upgrade update-restart-auth plugins-offline plugin-update plugin-binding-command-escape",
  "upgradeSurvivorBaselines": "openclaw@2026.10.33 openclaw@2026.11.5 openclaw@2026.11.6",
  "upgradeSurvivorScenarios": "base package-publication-recovery package-verification-recovery package-stranded-first-hop legacy-operator-state acpx-openclaw-tools-bridge feishu-channel bootstrap-persona channel-post-core-restore plugin-deps-cleanup configured-plugin-installs custom-plugin-siblings stale-source-plugin-shadow tilde-log-path meeting-transcripts-sqlite versioned-runtime-deps cron-scheduled-authority"
}
```

Fetch all jobs pages from each candidate run (`gh api --paginate --slurp repos/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/RUN/jobs?per_page=100`). Match each planner label to the final parenthesized label in its targeted-lane job name. Assert 92 matches, 92 successful conclusions, and identical complete row objects before/after. In planner order, assign each full `completed_at - started_at` duration to the earliest-free one of 32/48/64 slots. Compare the maximum slot finish, then retain observed residuals and the sibling/collector barriers above. No duration-weighted or oracle reordering is used. Actual proposed planner output also matches the modeled order. Observed timestamp/ID admission order differs from source order for some ties; the table deliberately uses source planner order on both sides.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): cache drop warnings blame max_completion_tokens when only the output cap changed
prs.body:
Closes #191648

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `[prompt-cache] cache read dropped` warnings blame `provider-input-change:parameters:max_completion_tokens` when the prompt prefix is unchanged and only the per-request output cap moved.

## User Impact

User impact: on Chat Completions routes, a cache drop with an unchanged prompt prefix now reads `provider-cache-reuse-lost:unchanged-prefix` with `providerPrefix=prefix-match`, so the warning points at the provider instead of an OpenClaw request change that did not happen. Prompt, tool, message and other parameter changes are still attributed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Chat Completions transport clamps `max_completion_tokens` (or `max_tokens`) to the remaining context budget on most requests (`openai-completions-params.ts:511`). `describeProviderPrefix()` compared every tracked request parameter, so the cap alone turned `prefix-match` into `parameters:max_completion_tokens`. An output cap bounds the completion; it does not change the prompt tokens a prefix cache keys on.

The parameter comparison now leaves out `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` and `max_output_tokens`:
- A cap-only change keeps `prefix-match`.
- When something else changed as well, the warning names only that: `parameters:temperature`, or `system`.

`docs/reference/prompt-caching.md` and `docs/logging.md` say so.

The provider-prefix description, with this filter, now lives in `prompt-cache-provider-prefix.ts`. With current main, `prompt-cache-observability.ts` would otherwise pass its 700-line cap; the functions moved unchanged.

Accepted edge case: if the cap changed and the only other difference is the JSON key order of the remaining parameters, the `order` signal is not reported.

## Evidence

- Production (details in #191648): on two hosts running a 2026.10.10-beta.5 based build, all 66 and all 83 drops labeled `parameters:max_completion_tokens` had equal `prefixHash` and `routeHash`. 35 and 17 of them went to 0 cached tokens.
- Unit: one new table in `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts` with 5 cases:
  - `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` and `max_output_tokens` alone -> unchanged prefix.
  - Cap plus `temperature` -> `parameters:temperature`.
  - Cap plus changed instructions -> `system`.
  - On base `19aff5bfd42` all 5 fail. The received values are `provider-input-change:parameters:max_tokens`, `...:max_completion_tokens`, `...:max_output_tokens`, `parameters:temperature+max_completion_tokens` and `system,parameters:max_completion_tokens`. With the fix the file passes 22/22.
- Consumers: 14 test files that use the observer pass (276 tests).
- End to end: an isolated `openclaw agent --local` turn against a scripted local Chat Completions server. Request 1 makes a tool call with 22560 cached tokens; request 2 reports 0. The bodies differ only by the two appended messages and `max_completion_tokens` (44468 -> 41385).
  - Base build: `provider-input-change:parameters:max_completion_tokens ... providerPrefix=parameters:max_completion_tokens`
  - This branch: `provider-cache-reuse-lost:unchanged-prefix ... providerPrefix=prefix-match`
- Checks:
  - `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files pass.
  - Against current main `3855c896edd`, with this branch merged locally:
    - CI's baseline ratchets (`ci-baseline-ratchets.mts --base 3855c896edd --no-merge-base`) pass 9 of 9, and the line-cap ratchet passes with `RATCHET_PR_HEAD_SHA` set. Before `a18dac5b480` it failed: `prompt-cache-observability.ts: 700 -> 712 counted lines (cap 700)`, because #192944 left that file at exactly its cap.
    - Test lines: main's test-line ratchet is now at its ceiling (slack 0; this branch measured 410 against its base), so `b094f0248d4` adds `config/test-lines-allocations/191649-cache-drop-output-cap.txt` with 30 lines, the net growth of the new table in `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts`, which is the regression test for this fix. The ratchet reads `Test lines OK: 6592398; ceiling: 6592398; slack: 0.`, and 31 is refused.
    - `check:changed --base 3855c896edd`: 35 of 36 lanes pass. The other, `changelog attributions`, reports the same 20 lines on unmodified main, in changelog files this PR does not touch.
    - The 12 test files that import the changed modules pass 191 of 191, under Node 26.12.1 and under Bun.
  - Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts` 32.1 s (cold worker cache, 20.2 s of it compiling) and 12.8 s wall, 7.2 s and 7.4 s of tests. CI run 41574334778, Bun: `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts` 36.0 s Vitest duration, 7.5 s of tests (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-40`).
  - The new cases run in 1-2 ms each.
- Not covered: a live provider run. The qa-lab mock serves only Responses and Messages and reports no cached tokens, so it cannot produce a cache drop.

prs.title: fix(ollama): refuse metadata and link-local base URLs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama used to allow a metadata or link-local base URL through the private-network SSRF policy, including the bearer token. Those base URLs now get no allow policy. Loopback and private LAN hosts stay allowed.

A supported local endpoint, `http://0.0.0.0:11434`, still opts into that private-network allow. The guard then treated `0.0.0.0` and `::` as blocked special-use addresses and threw before HTTP, so discovery reported the local server as unreachable. Exact-host trust, with no private-network allow, still rejects those addresses. Metadata and non-exempt link-local answers stay blocked.

Whether those metadata and link-local exclusions should override every explicit private-network opt-in, or only Ollama's automatic trust, is still a maintainer decision. This change does not narrow that scope.

## Evidence

Head `bd89f8052bf` on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, Ollama 0.40.11 listening on `127.0.0.1:11434`. Production `fetchOllamaModels` ran from `/tmp/oc-191588`.

Before this commit, `http://0.0.0.0:11434` threw and opened no socket:

```console
[security] blocked URL fetch (ollama-provider-models.tags) targetOrigin=http://0.0.0.0:11434 reason=Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address
RESULT: unspecified discovery SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
```

`curl` to that same URL returned HTTP 200 from the daemon. After this commit the production discovery call reached it.

```console
OK: loopback discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: unspecified discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: authenticated loopback header=bearer models=1
OK: literal metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: dns metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: unrelated redirect denied stolen=0
OK: lan address admitted 192.168.1.20
OK: podman exact-origin embed length=2 requests=1
OK: podman origin metadata newRequests=0 connects=
```

The unrelated redirect target was `proof-unrelated.test`. The guard stopped on the hostname allowlist. The second server received 0 requests. The Podman case used production `createOllamaEmbeddingProvider` against `http://host.containers.internal:11434`, resolved to `169.254.1.2`, where a listener accepted one embed POST. A metadata answer for that same origin opened no further request. The hosts entry and the /32 alias were removed after the trace. Default route stayed on `en0` via `10.0.0.1`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Authenticated Ollama discovery reaches loopback and `0.0.0.0`. Literal and DNS metadata are rejected before a socket opens. An unrelated redirect is denied. The exact-origin Podman link-local exception still delivers the embed, and a metadata answer on that origin does not.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, Ollama 0.40.11 bound to `127.0.0.1:11434`, head `bd89f8052bf` in `/tmp/oc-191588`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Called production `fetchOllamaModels` for `http://127.0.0.1:11434` and `http://0.0.0.0:11434` with a bearer token. Called `resolvePinnedHostnameWithPolicy` for literal `169.254.169.254` and for `ollama.example` resolved to that address. Posted through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` to a loopback server that redirected to `proof-unrelated.test`. Embedded through `createOllamaEmbeddingProvider` at `http://host.containers.internal:11434` while that name resolved to a listener on `169.254.1.2`, then repeated the origin with a metadata DNS answer.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched tree:

```console
OK: loopback discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: unspecified discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: authenticated loopback header=bearer models=1
OK: literal metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: dns metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: unrelated redirect denied stolen=0
OK: podman exact-origin embed length=2 requests=1
OK: podman origin metadata newRequests=0 connects=
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Loopback and `0.0.0.0` discovery both returned 3 models from the local daemon. The bearer was present on the loopback recorder. Metadata rejects opened no socket. The unrelated redirect delivered 0 requests to the second server. The Podman listener received exactly one embed and no metadata follow-up.
- **What was not tested:** A LAN Ollama on another machine. This daemon listens only on `127.0.0.1`, so the admitted `192.168.1.20` address had no server. The Podman hop was a listener on this Mac, not a Podman VM.

## Summary

The release note stays in this body. This branch does not edit CHANGELOG, which release tooling owns.

Metadata and link-local Ollama base URLs still get no private-network allow. `0.0.0.0` and `::` stay reachable when private networks are allowed, which is how Ollama names the local server. Exact-host trust still rejects them. A maintainer still needs to decide whether the metadata and link-local exclusions should override every private-network opt-in or only Ollama's automatic trust.

prs.title: improve(auto-reply): name the model whose connection failed
prs.body:
Closes #191299

## What Problem This Solves

When a model call fails to connect, the reply says "Couldn't connect to the AI service." (#168247) but not which model. With a fallback chain or several providers, the user can't tell which endpoint is down without the gateway logs.

## User Impact

User impact: the connection-failure reply starts with the failing model, e.g. `⚠️ gpufarm/qwen3.8-27b request failed: Couldn't connect to the AI service. ...`. The rest of #168247's copy is unchanged, including the completed-work caution. A failure without a provider or model reads exactly as before, and raw error text stays hidden.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveReplyFailoverFacts` already has the failover error's provider and model; the connection copy just didn't use them. It now prefixes the copy with the failing model through `modelKey`, which keeps a model id that already carries its provider as is (`openrouter/auto` is not doubled). Terminal replies and incomplete-turn replies both read `requestFailureText`, so both get the name.

When the error carries fallback attempts, the name comes only from the attempts whose own error is a connection failure, joined with ", " when there are several. A chain summary keeps the last attempt's model while its message joins every attempt's error, so taking the top-level model would blame a backup that connected and then timed out (ClawSweeper's P2 on the first head).

This partly reverses #163381 (#163368), which removed provider details from default errors to keep them short. For a connection failure, though, the failing model is the next recovery step (which server to check), not a diagnostic. Only the connection copy changes; rate-limit, auth and server-error replies are untouched. If maintainers want to keep #163381's rule here too, closing this is fine.

## Evidence

- New qa scenario `connection-failure-reply-names-model` (in this PR): real gateway, qa-channel, mock-openai with the provider's `baseUrl` set to `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1`, so every model call is refused. It sends a DM and reads the terminal reply from the bus. The reply is `isError`, so it is read directly rather than through the failure-aware transport waits, the same way `a2a-allowlist-denied-cross-agent-send` reads its expected warning.
  - main at `70c93a29f17` (this PR's base): fails with `unexpected connection-failure reply: ⚠️ Couldn't connect to the AI service. Check your connection, then try again. ...`
  - This branch at `a798fb3485e` (the scenario now requires two distinct named models before "request failed"): passes with `reply: ⚠️ mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna, mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna-alt request failed: Couldn't connect to the AI service. Check your connection, then try again. For details, open Settings → Logs in the Control UI or run `openclaw logs --follow`. Check the conversation for any completed work before trying again.` qa-lab configures `gpt-5.6-luna-alt` as the fallback, both on the refused provider, so this is the real fallback-chain path, and both refused models are named. The first head named only the last one: with its `request-error-facts.ts`, the scenario fails on `⚠️ mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna-alt request failed: ...`.
  - Command: `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario connection-failure-reply-names-model --concurrency 1 --fast`, after `pnpm build`.
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts`: 22 passed.
  - "names the model whose connection failed" covers the named copy, a provider-prefixed model id, and the unchanged copy without facts. With main's `request-error-facts.ts` it fails with `Received: "⚠️ Couldn't connect to the AI service. ..."`.
  - "names only the fallback attempts that failed to connect" builds the error with the real `throwFallbackFailureSummary`: the primary is refused and the backup times out, then both are refused. With the first head's code it fails with `Received: "⚠️ backup/llama3.3 request failed: Couldn't connect ..."`.
- 34 related test files at `e40cb6903e0`: 1,053 passed, 0 failed. They are the 13 that assert this copy or call `resolveReplyFailoverFacts` (`agent-runner-failure-reply`, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e`, `incomplete-turn*`, `settled-turn-finalization*`, `payloads.errors`, `session-lifecycle-run-failure`, `server-methods`, `assistant-error-format` and others), plus `model-fallback*` and `agent-terminal-snapshot`.
- qa-lab scenario catalog tests (19 files): 145 passed, run at `fc2d656c3bc`. The scenario file is unchanged since.
- `pnpm tsgo:all` exits 0. oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Test lines: main's test-line ratchet is now at its ceiling (`3855c896edd`: slack 0), so `35ed4298bdd` adds `config/test-lines-allocations/191301-connection-failure-names-model.txt` with this PR's exact net test-line growth, 61 lines. They are the tests that pin this change: Connection-failure replies name the fallback models that failed to connect. Merged onto `3855c896edd`, `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 3855c896edd --no-merge-base` reads `Test lines OK: 6592429; ceiling: 6592429; slack: 0.`, and an allocation of 62 is refused. This is not a fix PR, so per the openclaw-testing guide the record needs a maintainer's approval; could a maintainer approve it?
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts` 27.7 s (cold worker cache, 21.9 s of it compiling) and 6.5 s wall, 15 ms and 16 ms of tests. CI run 41570533435, Bun: `agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts` 4.4 s Vitest duration, 20 ms of tests (`checks-node-changed-4`).
- Gap: the end-to-end proof is mock-openai against a closed local port. The refused-then-timed-out chain is covered by the unit test only; I did not build an end-to-end case for it. My fork runs the same naming on two bots with local models; I have not captured a live provider outage with this exact build.

prs.title: feat: keep lean Gateway worker growth inside a memory budget
prs.body:
Fixes #202376. Related: #202373.

**Stacked on #202422**, now merged as `28aa5c88fd45`; this PR now targets `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

On small machines, Gateway worker pools grow to fixed caps regardless of how much memory is left, so a busy small container or laptop can run out of memory or stall turns. The lean resource profile from #202422 had no way to hold worker growth back.

## User Impact

User impact: in the `lean` profile, extra workers start only when they fit a memory budget; otherwise the work waits for an existing worker. `standard` is unchanged. `openclaw status` and `diagnostics.lanes` show the budget, its basis, waits and refusals. A new optional `gateway.resources.memoryBudgetMiB` overrides the default budget.

This is an admission rule, **not an OOM guarantee**. Memory already admitted (the main thread, floor workers, growth inside running workers, child processes) is measured, not refused. The proof below shows that the budget alone does **not** keep lean under a 1.5 GiB limit: floor workers alone reach it. The shared core host (#202377) is needed for that.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Budget by limit source** (provisional shares):

  | Limit source | Default budget | Memory use compared with it |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | cgroup v2 `memory.max` | 85% of the limit | `memory.current − inactive_file` of the limiting cgroup |
  | Host RAM (no container limit) | 40% of host RAM | The Gateway process RSS, including worker threads, **not** child processes |
  | `memoryBudgetMiB` set (lean only) | That many MiB | As above, by limit source |

  A container limit is sized for OpenClaw. A bare 4–8 GiB host is shared with everything else, and #202422 now selects lean below 8 GiB.
- **Floors always run.** Each pool keeps one worker (two for shared-state reads, so a held settlement read cannot block a fresh one), plus its point-read lane once used. Fixed direct workers keep their normal counts: native lifecycle supervisor, both state heartbeats, SQLite broker carriers, Knowledge registry and storage, PostgreSQL bridges, and the #202377 shared host. Floors are never refused, so admission cannot deadlock.
- **Growth waits.** A pool worker beyond its floor starts only if *measured use + reservations not yet running + that worker's estimate* stays under the budget. Running workers are counted by measurement and are not double-charged. Refused work stays in the same pool queue and is never dropped. Deadlines and cancellation are unchanged.
- **Floor warnings.** At startup the Gateway records its measured working set (the main isolate plus anything already running) and adds the per-kind floor estimates. It logs one warning if that exceeds the budget, and another if measured use exceeds the budget while only floor workers run. Either way, no growth is admitted.
- **Coverage:** main-isolate pools, including plugin SDK pools, get floors plus admission. Fixed direct families get floor reservations. Pools nested in worker threads stay at their floor in lean; the flag travels in worker environment data, never `process.env` or child processes. Plugin workers created directly, not through a pool, are measured once running but cannot be refused through their synchronous API.
- **#202377 seam:** `registerHostedSlotPredicate()`. A pool's first floor slot, or a SQLite `agent` / `shared-state` carrier, that the shared host claims needs no isolate reservation. The host itself is one floor entry. Neither branch imports the other.
- `WorkerTaskPoolCore` changes are confined to one helper (`worker-task-pool-memory.ts`): a lazily bound budget that rebinds after an in-process restart, a count-based bulk limit, and wait accounting. The core file stays within its line budget.

## Evidence

**Studio proof.** Crabbox Linux `local-container` leases on the Mac Studio, Node 26.12.1, `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`, inspector-free. The workload is the reused part 3 F personal-assistant harness (33 turns, 3 child runs, a Knowledge call, an automation, compaction, 5-minute idle). The harness copy changed only the arm selection (`gateway.resources.profile`), the budget snapshot reader and `memory.stat` sampling; SHA-256 sums of the original and modified harness are recorded. One fresh lease per case; all leases were released.

Rebased onto #202422 head `9d7f71d104cc` (including main’s #202407 allocator default). Range-diff against previous base `f110ba8d49c1` shows no feature-patch changes: only regenerated config baselines and schema context changed. Existing Studio evidence is retained; every case already set `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`, matching #202407. No new benchmark was run.

All cases ran build **`75e5303b`**. Rebasing onto `e57f84aa` and then `f110ba8d` left every file in this diff byte-identical. Subsequent changes add the host-RAM basis and override, wrapper extraction inventory, typed singleton initialization, conditional cleanup of the lean environment flag, test allocation and docs. These do not change the measured lean cgroup admission rule. Every case ran in a cgroup v2 container, where the 85% rule is unchanged, so these results apply to the current head.

| Case (1.5 GiB unless noted) | Completed | OOM kills | Peak anon | Peak `memory.current` | Workers | Growth admitted / refused / waits | p95 (info) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lean r1 | **yes**, 33/33 turns, 3/3 children, Knowledge, automation | 0 | 1,501 MiB | 1,536 MiB (limit) | 23 | 0 / 663 / 523 | 1.9 s |
| lean r2 | **yes**, 33/33 turns, 3/3 children, Knowledge, automation | 0 | 1,472 MiB | 1,536 MiB (limit) | 22 | 0 / 653 / 517 | 2.3 s |
| lean r3 | **no**: killed during startup, before the first turn | **1** | 1,092 MiB (last sample) | 1,536 MiB (limit) | 10 | 0 / 0 / 0 | — |
| standard | **no**: turn left pending after 26 turns | 0 | 1,508 MiB | 1,536 MiB (limit) | 24 | no budget | 6.4 s |
| standard, 3 GiB | **yes**, 33/33 turns | 0 | 1,799 MiB | 2,875 MiB | 28 | **no budget snapshot or events** | 0.9 s |

**Refusals and waits by family** (lean r1 / r2):

| Family | Refusals | Waits | Total wait (ms) | Longest wait (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| session-transcript | 449 / 442 | 395 / 391 | 7,159 / 7,764 | 194 / 220 |
| fs-safe-copy | 207 / 207 | 123 / 123 | 3,731 / 4,055 | 137 / 147 |
| provider-prompt-state | 7 / 4 | 5 / 3 | 39 / 17 | 22 / 15 |

Nothing was still waiting at the end of either round.

**Floor-only operation.** Lean admitted **zero** growth in every round: every lean worker was a floor worker. Even so, 22–23 live floor workers plus the main isolate drove the working set to about 1.52 GiB and anon to about 1.5 GiB.

**Startup warning, before and after.**
- **Before** (`871607f8` smoke): the estimate was per-kind floors only. Floors were 420 MiB at startup and 1,064 MiB at peak, against a 1,306 MiB budget, so **no warning** fired, although measured use reached about 1,522 MiB.
- **After** (`75e5303b`): the estimate is the measured startup baseline (590 / 592 MiB in r1 / r2) plus floors. It exceeded the budget early (1,354 / 1,415 MiB), and **the warning fired** in r1 and r2. Estimates peaked at 1,696 / 1,715 MiB.
- r3 was killed before the estimate crossed the budget.

**Conclusion.** The budget does what it claims: in lean it held growth to zero and queued about 520 tasks per run without dropping any, and standard is untouched. But it **cannot keep lean under 1.5 GiB by itself.** Floor workers and the main isolate fill the limit. r3 shows the startup peak alone (main RSS about 1 GiB plus three Gateway child processes of 294 MiB in total) can be OOM-killed. That is outside what admission controls, and is the gap the shared core host (#202377) and later lean reductions target. Lean completed 2 of 3 rounds; standard at 1.5 GiB completed 0 of 1.

**Startup peak** (saved samples only, every 2 s). Each Gateway's first start is its memory peak, before any turn and before admission has anything to refuse:

| Time after start | r1 main RSS / children / cgroup anon / workers | r2 | r3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 s | 468 / 76 / 479 MiB / — | 492 / 182 / 562 / — | 478 / 176 / 542 / — |
| 6 s | 876 / 294 / 1,006 / 10 | 995 / 294 / 1,125 / 5 | 962 / 294 / 1,092 / 10, then OOM-killed |
| 8 s | 1,283 / 294 / 1,413 / 19 | 1,289 / 294 / 1,419 / 11 | — |

- Main RSS includes every worker thread's isolate; the probe did not record main-isolate heap, so heap vs native vs worker isolates is not separable from these artifacts.
- The three children are Gateway child processes of 76 MiB (8 threads), about 107 MiB (11 threads) and about 111 MiB (11 threads). Their command lines were deliberately not recorded by the harness, so their identity is not established here.
- After the harness restart, the same three children run at 35–46 MiB each.
- Startup peaks happen before admission applies; reducing them belongs to the lean reductions (#202379), not this PR.

**Local checks on the current head:**
- Focused tests: pool admission (refusal queues on the floor worker, growth is released after exit, the point-read lane stays mandatory, rebind after restart; standard sizing is covered by the existing pool suites, which supply no budget) and the budget owner (pending vs measured, floor warnings by estimate and by measurement, hosted-slot claims including late registration, direct floors, restart and flag reset, each budget basis). Status, schema, profile and worker-runtime suites also pass.
- Typechecks: `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test`.
- Lint: oxlint on all changed files, `check:import-cycles`.
- Config: `config:docs:check`, `check:base-config-schema`. Core config count 2666 → 2667 for `gateway.resources.memoryBudgetMiB`.
- CI follow-ups:
  - Both new modules are in the extracted PR-wrapper inventory (ClawSweeper P1); wrapper closure and provisioning tests pass.
  - The budget singleton is typed instead of asserted.
  - Lifecycle reset no longer touches worker environment data unless lean published it. That fixes a test teardown that mocks `node:worker_threads`.
- Test-lines allocation of 85 lines (`config/test-lines-allocations/202507-lean-worker-memory-budget.txt`). This is new scheduling policy, and its regression tests cover queueing without drops, the point-read lane, restart rebinding, floor warnings, hosted-slot claims and each budget basis. Several of those came from verified review findings.
- Independent review: 4 verified findings, all fixed with regression tests (rebind after restart, flag reset on standard, refuse growth while floors exceed the budget, no double release after a failed close).

<details>
<summary>Proof identity</summary>

Build `75e5303b5e02f3a9def163044b57e37862bb724d` → image `sha256:34a664c2759358ee69b816235655b5ef5ed045bce02b97f88baee55fcfa42efc` (base `node:26.12.1-trixie`).

| Case | Lease | Run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lean r1 | `cbx_d6ed442aad8f` | `run_05e039570e43d6ba95734a2872f284db` |
| lean r2 | `cbx_cee412424a66` | `run_1806267e46381f1fcc287f06be87ffa7` |
| lean r3 | `cbx_5732bb293fb0` | `run_540d5afffae8fdee1ae939ff171d924a` |
| standard | `cbx_45a75e0af362` | `run_b8550bc32ab07fd1f7359e52c0af456d` |
| standard, 3 GiB | `cbx_7ccc56124678` | `run_9a8b524f80504978ca1d9e8d7b91e972` |

All released. Kernel `memory.peak` includes lease preparation; sampled `memory.current` and `anon` are taken every 2 s. Usage is the cgroup working set; `memory.current` includes page cache, so reaching the limit is not by itself an OOM.

</details>






### Main retarget and proof status

Rebased only this PR’s nine commits from `9d7f71d104cc` onto main `2d13f968e794`, after foundation #202422 was squash-merged. `git range-diff` against prior head `ffd3fa8939ca` shows eight identical patches and only regenerated config-baseline hashes in the ninth; feature production code is unchanged. Existing and pending prior-head proofs retain their original tested SHA, not the rebased SHA.

Diagnostics `usageBytes` is the last growth-admission sample and remains `null` until the first growth admission attempt; an idle null is not a failed RSS read. No-cgroup proof setup on `ffd3fa8939ca` observed `memory.max=max`, host RAM 134,884,679,680 bytes, basis `host-40`, and budget 53,953,871,872 bytes (exactly 40%). The host admission/override and stable-upgrade proofs below now pass. Earlier harness failures: v2 used an invalid fresh-RSS comparison against an unsampled null; v3 stopped on concurrent session creation (`AgentDatabaseRegistryChangedError`) before admission assertions. Both leases were deleted. The corrected isolated harness creates fixture sessions serially before concurrent turns; no product changes were made for these harness/setup failures.



### Host, override and upgrade proof — complete

Studio Crabbox `local-container`, Node 26.12.1, candidate package SHA-256 `d6b4993fda3fbc34810d768c7aae8a9fba2c520001863567c7e9af47493c50b4`, built from `ffd3fa8939ca`; production patches are equivalent to rebased head `059bab5adb9a` as described above. All cases serialized under the shared measurement lock; every lease deletion was confirmed.

- **Host basis PASS** (`cbx_4cfb988ede83`, followup-v4): `memory.max=max`, observed host RAM 134,884,679,680 bytes, `limitSource=host`, `basis=host-40`, budget 53,953,871,872 bytes, exactly 40%. Five real admission-event observations verified the Gateway PID and its process RSS (including worker threads, excluding child processes). A 512 MiB override reported `basis=configured`, budget 536,870,912 bytes.
- **Cgroup basis PASS** (`cbx_b03d26a12ef5`, followup-v4): 6 GiB limit, `basis=cgroup-85`, budget 5,476,083,302 bytes; the same 512 MiB override reported `basis=configured`, budget 536,870,912 bytes. Both basis cases rejected zero, negative, fractional and string values through `config validate` (exit 1), without accepting an invalid override.
- **Latest-stable upgrade PASS** (followup-v5): resolved npm latest stable `2026.11.6`, installed stable, created three synthetic Knowledge records and session state, then installed the candidate in the same prefix/state. Added the new resource settings once (stable predates them), selected `auto` under 6 GiB, observed lean and configured 2048 MiB, and verified all semantic user settings including resources, saved page bytes, record bodies/revisions and session messages. Package installation itself preserved the config bytes. Candidate startup adds doctor migration metadata, a wizard receipt and `plugins.entries.openai.enabled=true` through existing provider auto-enable normalization (not this PR’s behavior; a separate plain-main upgrade comparison was not run); the semantic comparison explicitly permits only these additions. v4's whole-file byte comparison was a harness error, not settings loss.

Artifacts: `studio-crabbox:~/crabbox-proof/lean-budget-202376-followup-v4/` (host/cgroup results and receipts), `...-followup-v5/` (upgrade result and receipt), including each `summary.json`, `out-*/upgrade-proof.json`, and `*-stop.log`. Earlier failed attempts are retained as history. v3 encountered a concurrent-first-session setup discovery error in the family tracked by #158379, before admission proof; serial fixture creation avoids it without changing product code.

### Current CI attribution

`checks-ui-e2e (2/4)` failed only `ui/src/e2e/route-asset-requests.e2e.test.ts:120`, “bounds plugins ready-window asset requests at 100 ms from a settled New Session,” at the line-145 asset-count limit (92 tests passed). [Job log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44836195528/job/136633900074). UI code is untouched. The failure is exactly **57 assets > 56**, matching the same assertion on main `2d13f968e794` in #202478’s paired fresh-production-build reproduction: Studio Crabbox run `run_7875f8579b36dd07c7fa99b0289ab3c7`, lease `6c28ab65a1e6` (released). The count is not higher on this PR. This is the prior-head CI result, not a hosted main CI run; the fresh rebased-head checks are recorded separately below. The CI gate failure follows this shard failure.





### Conflict-only rebase after review

After ClawSweeper’s 01:15:55Z verdict on `059bab5adb9a` (“no definite introduced defect”, 4/6), rebased once onto main `684018d110ef`, producing `483d2239059a`. Range-diff: eight identical feature patches; the override patch differs only in regenerated config baseline counts/hashes. No feature production or test patch changed, so that verdict and the documented prior-head behavioral proofs carry over; no new re-review was requested. Hosted-slot predicate integration remains for whichever of #202495 and this PR lands second.

Fresh-head validation: **41 focused tests passed** (budget/status/pool/profile: 21 + 4 + 16), `tsgo:core`, scoped lint, format, `config:docs:check` and `git diff --check` all passed. Fresh-head CI [run 44859763873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44859763873): all four UI-e2e shards passed, including formerly failing `(2/4)`; no fresh-head check has failed in the collected snapshot (80 success, 56 skipped, 2 cancelled, 1 neutral, 9 pending). Remaining work: Darwin, changed-compact-small-5, PostgreSQL conformance (four shards plus pg16 smoke), docker-seed-e2e and the aggregate status. PR is **MERGEABLE**, checks still block completion. Prior-head 57>56 attribution above is historical, not a fresh failure.

prs.title: fix: keep screenshots working for background tabs in headed Chrome
prs.body:
Root cause: extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.content.ts:250 makes a background tab paint before a Playwright capture only in headless Chrome (`bringToFront`, #201626). Headed Chrome skips that step so the user's tab never switches (#134400). Tool tabs open as background tabs (`cdp.ts:143`, #105356), and in headed Chrome a background tab produces no frames, so its capture never finishes and the tab's capture queue stays held (#135315).

Fixes #165312

Thanks @titan550 for the report, @Oldrich333 for the deterministic background-tab reproduction, and @potterdigital for tracing the headed case to background tab creation.

## What Problem This Solves

With headed Chrome (for example on an Xvfb display), the browser tool opens pages in background tabs. Chrome does not draw a background tab, so a screenshot of that tab waits for a frame that never comes and times out. After that, every screenshot of the tab failed straight away with "A previous screenshot or emulation action was cancelled but is still running", until the browser was stopped.

## User Impact

Screenshots of pages the agent opened in the background work in headed Chrome, for managed and attach-only profiles, and the tab no longer gets stuck. Nothing visible changes for the user: tool tabs stay background tabs, the user's tab stays active and focused, and no window appears or moves. Headless Chrome is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

In headed Chrome, a Playwright capture now runs inside a DevTools screencast on the page (`Page.startScreencast` with a 1x1 preview, stopped right after the capture). While a screencast is active, Chromium renders the hidden tab without activating it, so the capture gets its frame. Headless keeps the activation from #201626.

The stuck state after a timeout needs no separate change. The page's capture queue intentionally waits until Chromium finishes the native capture (#135315) so a late restore cannot overwrite a newer emulation change. The capture only hung because the hidden tab never produced a frame. Now the tab renders, the capture finishes in about 100-300 ms, and the queue is released.

Alternatives measured with headed Chrome for Testing 156 on Xvfb with openbox. Each row is 7 captures of a background tab while a 5 ms X11 sampler recorded the active and top-stacked window:

| Approach | Captures | What the user sees |
|---|---|---|
| Current main | 7/7 stall | nothing |
| Activate the tool tab, capture, reactivate the user's tab | 7/7 ok | the tool tab is shown for about 200 ms per capture (41 of 303 samples) |
| Own unfocused window (`newWindow`) | 7/7 ok | the new window is stacked in front of the user's window |
| Own window placed off screen | 7/7 ok | the window manager clamps it partly on screen, stacked in front |
| Own window minimized | 7/7 stall | the window is stacked in front |
| Launch flags (`--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows`, `--disable-renderer-backgrounding`, `--disable-background-timer-throttling`) | first capture stalls, later ones ok | nothing, but it only covers managed launches |
| Raw `Page.captureScreenshot` without a screencast | intermittent (4/7 stall) | nothing |
| **Screencast during capture (this PR)** | 7/7 ok for viewport, element, full-page and raw captures, and for the user's own visible tab | nothing (all samples: user tab active and on top) |

## Evidence

Observed proof lines: [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202878#issuecomment-7056414637)

Real Gateway from packed tarballs in a secretless node:24.22.1 container with Xvfb, openbox and Chrome for Testing 156. The agent's `browser` tool was called through the Gateway `/tools/invoke` endpoint: open a static page, snapshot it, take screenshots, open a second page, take more screenshots. The user's own tab was opened and focused first, and an X11 sampler recorded the active and top-stacked window every 5 ms for the whole run.

- Base (main 2b5f1a88ba81), managed headed profile: screenshots time out after 20 s, and the next one fails in 59 ms with "A previous screenshot or emulation action was cancelled but is still running". The attach-only profile also times out repeatedly.
- Candidate: all seven screenshots of both background tabs return images in 110-570 ms, for both managed headed and attach-only headed. Only one Chrome window ever exists.
- Control, headless: candidate screenshots all return images (#201626 behavior unchanged).
- Control, focus and stacking: every sample in every headed base and candidate run shows the user's tab active and on top.
- The capture-order regression case in `pw-tools-core.screenshots-element-selector.test.ts` fails on main (`expected [ 'screenshot' ]`) and passes here.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert fully undoes it; there is no state, config or contract change. Blast radius: Playwright screenshots on headed Chrome profiles whose launch mode OpenClaw knows (managed and attach-only). Each capture adds one short-lived CDP session with a screencast. Headless, unknown-mode and raw CDP captures are unaffected.

## What Problem This Solves

The overview and the detailed sidebar guide now describe the compact agent roster and its navigation. Selecting an agent row opens its main chat. **Sessions** in that row's options menu opens the filtered Sessions page.

## Evidence

I started an isolated OpenClaw 2026.11.3 Gateway (`9bf3e79c823a`) with two agents and drove the served Control UI in Chromium 149 on Linux. ```text

prs.title: feat: reset OpenClaw ID owner access from the claw's own computer
prs.body:
Related: OCF-319, OCF-323. Stacked on #201586 (base branch); retarget to `main` once that lands. Supersedes draft #198576.

## What Problem This Solves

If a claw's OpenClaw ID recovery kit is lost or leaked, there is no way to take back owner access: every owner browser and the old kit keep working, and the only fallback is relinking the claw as a new one.

## User Impact

On the computer that runs the claw, the owner can reset owner access from **Settings → OpenClaw ID** or with `openclaw id reset`. A reset makes a new recovery kit, removes every owner device, person, node and invite, closes their remote sessions, and gives the claw a new Gateway key. The claw's address, connection key and data stay. It needs both:

- **A direct connection to this computer's running Gateway.** The tunnel, reverse proxies and Tailscale Serve are refused (`not_local_operator`); the page explains why and keeps the button off.
- **A link code from the OpenClaw ID account that owns the claw.** The Control UI takes it from the signed-in account; the CLI prompts for it or takes `--code`. The Gateway checks it with Discovery before anything changes.

Until Discovery adopts code-gated root changes, a reset commits locally but its publication is refused, so **do not use this outside tests yet**. The PR stays in draft until Discovery is ready.

## Why This Change Was Made

This builds on the earlier owner-reset work (#198576) and adapts it to #201586: a reset stages a new Gateway key and publishes under it with the snapshot and the owner's code, the same path as a move to new keys. A copied Gateway key file therefore can't reset the claw.

Changes after review:
- Re-binds and resets share one lane, so cancelling a move can't delete the key a reset is committing to.
- Before resetting, Discovery must still publish this computer's root and binding. A restored backup is refused with `binding_superseded` instead of stranding the claw.
- Failures after the reset is stored come back as `followUpError` on a committed result, never as a refusal.
- The CLI shows the new kit and asks for it to be saved **before** committing.

The stopped-Gateway `openclaw id reset` path from #198576 is removed: reset is offered only through a direct connection to the running Gateway.

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway, loopback, recording Discovery stand-in:**
  - Without a code: `needs_link_code`; with a wrong code: `code_invalid`.
  - With the owner's code: one descriptor write signed by the **new** Gateway key, carrying the code, the snapshot and a `RootReset` that `verifyRootReset` accepts.
  - A tunnel client is refused before the service is asked.
- **Service tests (`owner-reset.test.ts`, 12):**
  - Removals happen; K_srv is kept and the Gateway signs with K_gw' afterwards.
  - Refused with no code, a wrong code, an unpublished claw, Discovery unavailable, or a superseded binding, and none of these change anything.
  - A queued re-bind cancel doesn't destroy the staged key. This test fails without the shared lane.
  - Follow-up failure reporting.
- **CLI tests (5):** the kit is shown once before commit; nothing is committed until "saved"; refusals are told apart from unknown outcomes; follow-up failures exit with code 2.
- **Control UI:**
  - Page tests: both requirements are shown, and the button is off over the tunnel or without a sign-in.
  - Browser e2e against a mocked Gateway: the full reset runs locally, both steps carry a link code, and the confirmation alert says "This can't be undone".
  - Screenshots were captured locally but not attached here.
- **Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- **Inherited failure:** `src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-role-recovery.test.ts` (2 tests) fails identically on `main` + #201586 without these changes.
- **Not run:**
  - Staging end to end: blocked on Discovery adoption.
  - The human-presence check (OCF-334) is still open.

prs.title: fix: stop a copied OpenClaw ID Gateway key from resetting a claw's owner
prs.body:
Related: OCF-319

## What Problem This Solves

Under the OpenClaw ID owner-reset spec, the claw's Gateway key alone authorizes replacing its owner key at Discovery. That key is a plain `0600` file on the Gateway host, readable by anything running as the Gateway user, including an unsandboxed agent session. Someone who copies it could reset the claw from anywhere, lock existing browsers out behind an "owner reset, set up again" prompt that points at their own kit, and repeat that after any legitimate reset, because a reset kept the same key.

## User Impact

No user-visible change yet: the Gateway doesn't implement owner reset and Discovery still refuses every root change. This changes the protocol contract so that, once reset ships, it needs the machine **and** a one-time link code from the account that owns the claw, and a leaked Gateway key stops working at the reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

A reset now has to name a **new** Gateway key (the connection key stays). Discovery already requires a new Gateway key's publication to be signed by the new key, carry its snapshot, and spend a one-time code from the owner account. That rule therefore gates every reset without a new endpoint. The old key still signs the `RootReset`, so pinned browsers can still tell a reset from a substitution, but that signature alone authorizes nothing.

- `verifyRootReset` requires the same K_srv and a different K_gw.
- `enrollment.md`, `discovery.md` and `statements.md` describe both requirements (the machine and the owner account) and the new key.
- Test vectors gain a second Gateway key; the fixture is regenerated from the builder.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test packages/openclaw-id-protocol`: 265/265 after the fix to the leaked-kit test. `reset.test.ts` covers acceptance with a new K_gw, a reset that keeps K_gw (`reset_mismatch`), and the earlier forgeries.
- Portable typecheck (`tsconfig.portable.json`), oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the package.
- The fixture test confirms `statements.json` is exactly the builder's output.
- Discovery `main` (`401734d`) still refuses every root change (`test/claws.test.ts`, "refuses a root change even with valid owner reset evidence"), so nothing deployed changes. Adopting this check there is a follow-up.

The Gateway, CLI and Control UI implementation is stacked on this in a separate draft PR.

prs.title: fix(onboard): reject token auth under Tailscale Funnel with accurate guidance
prs.body:
Closes #201385

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --tailscale funnel` tells users to "use --gateway-auth token", but Funnel always forces password auth, so following that advice reproduces the same failure. An explicit `--gateway-auth token` is silently replaced by password auth.

## User Impact

The error now names the real requirement: Funnel needs a password. It points at `--gateway-password` or `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD`, never at token auth. An explicit `--gateway-auth token` with `--tailscale funnel` is rejected with that reason instead of being silently overridden.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reject `--gateway-auth token` under Funnel the same way `trusted-proxy` is already rejected, instead of overwriting it.
- Make the missing-password error Funnel-aware so it stops recommending the path Funnel has already disabled.
- Keep the existing normalization for a token-only rerun that targets an already-password Funnel.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 30/30 passed.
- Red-on-base: reverting only `gateway-config.ts` makes both new cases fail; the existing token-only rerun case still passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on both changed files.

- Shipped CLI proof (real `openclaw onboard --non-interactive`, isolated profile, no daemon):
  - **Before** (upstream source): `--tailscale funnel` exits 1 with `Missing --gateway-password for password auth. Pass --gateway-password or use --gateway-auth token.`; adding `--gateway-auth token` exits 1 with the same message.
  - **After** (this head): `--tailscale funnel` exits 1 with `Tailscale Funnel requires password auth. Pass --gateway-password or set OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD.`; `--tailscale funnel --gateway-auth token` exits 1 with `Tailscale Funnel requires password auth and cannot use "--gateway-auth token". …`.
  - **After**, `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD` set: onboarding succeeds and writes `{"mode":"password"}` with `tailscale.mode=funnel`.

- Latest-stable upgrade proof (state and config created by `openclaw@2026.11.5`):
  - `2026.11.5` wrote `gateway.auth={"mode":"password"}` with `gateway.tailscale={"mode":"funnel"}`.
  - This head, run as an ordinary Funnel rerun over that config with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD` set, exited 0 and kept `{"mode":"password"}` + `funnel`.
  - The same rerun with `--gateway-auth token --gateway-token …` exited 1 with the actionable `cannot use "--gateway-auth token"` rejection.

prs.title: fix: wait for a busy gateway to restart before verifying a Git update
prs.body:
Split from #202692. This PR is only about Git release activation; it has no Inbox or Control UI changes.

## What Problem This Solves

A managed Git update can build the right release, request a restart, and verify the old process 90 seconds later while the Gateway is still legitimately draining active work. This can produce a failed run before the target starts, or mistake a healthy unchanged core for a completed plugin-only restart.

## User Impact

A fresh scheduling receipt from the resident Gateway gives it time to drain. If signal delivery is denied, the updater does not retry or extend the deadline; it keeps watching for an independent replacement within the original window. Native activation requires the managed service to be running, not just an endpoint that answers. An incomplete restart receipt triggers a fresh service poll. Cancellation and the operator’s overall timeout remain binding.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing local signal, scheduler and owner lease. The receipt is a reason to wait, not permission to restart or proof of readiness. For a same-build or plugin-only update, the updater also needs evidence of turnover. After the existing guarded cleanup retires a listener identified by the profile lock, its PID can be compared with a **different**, freshly bound, managed listener serving the expected target. Cleanup alone cannot settle the trial. There is no new authenticated transport, schema migration or service-control capability.

## Evidence

- **Published `54e87fd147af`:** [required hosted CI passed on this SHA](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44857465770). The last commit changes only the recovery message. A stale-listener identity mismatch under synthetic profile `work` previously advised `openclaw gateway status --deep`; now it advises `openclaw --profile work gateway status --deep`. The default profile still receives the original command. The verifier suite passed all 68 cases with the temporary reproduction, including refusal without restart or verification. Formatting, scoped lint, core typecheck and the session-identity ratchet passed.
- **Restart behavior on `fe44e771b899`:** 152 local tests passed across Git release, service, verification and restart polling. This includes a responding listener with a stopped service (must not settle), a stale child receipt followed by a running replacement (must poll), denied signals without retries, and successor-after-cleanup with matching and mismatched owner leases. The line/test limits were unchanged. All 12 baseline checks passed locally on `da333b500d3d`; the [previously failing diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44852375353/job/136686999178) was corrected without changing the process-identity guard or the ratchet.
- **Independent local review:** ClawSweeper reviewed the full `ce74e42351ed..212e3cd3f95d` range and each subsequent delta through `da333b500d3d`, `fe44e771b899`, and `54e87fd147af`. The final delta addressed the only remaining finding (the profile in the recovery message); its review found no correctness or security issues.
- **Installed Linux upgrade on the earlier candidate `66529a66987c`:** the [operator’s completed replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202735#issuecomment-7056175078) supersedes the [partial attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202735#issuecomment-7055443601). With a real systemd user service, the updater was still waiting 95 seconds after the receipt while work was active. It verified the distinct successor serving the candidate build and exited 0. Cancellation during verification exited 130 as interrupted, not success. `--no-restart` staged the candidate with zero launch attempts while the incumbent kept serving. The settings, agent and session markers survived. The held HTTP client’s response was not confirmed; the optional older-resident control was not run. This was not an installed-upgrade test of the final SHA.
- **macOS KeepAlive limit:** A fixture using the real launchd status parser and a mocked `launchctl print` showed a loaded, waiting job with no PID, listener or lease until its 30-second deadline expired. A sibling fixture shows a supervisor can instead bring the service up at 13 seconds. The updater deliberately does **not** issue a second native restart based on a timeout and a free port: that could interrupt the supervisor’s new process. The documented result is unconfirmed activation; inspect the affected gateway’s status before taking action. No live LaunchAgent was used in this check.
- **Real-clock macOS process handoff on `3108eecd9a1f`:** the resident received one native `SIGUSR2` at 35.315 s and committed a scheduling receipt at 35.348 s. At 91.032 s the old process still owned the lease and one work item; the updater was still waiting. Work finished at 127.880 s. After a lease-free interval of at least 2.312 s, the updater observed a different owner and process start identity and returned `changed` at 139.146 s. The successor’s distinct synthetic build and `ready`/`coreReady` passed an IPC probe. Clock, processes, signal, restart scheduler and lease storage were real; workload, supervisor and build identities were fixtures. This was not an installed upgrade, launchd activation or HTTP test.

prs.title: feat(ui): open the next chat after archiving the open one
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Archiving the chat you have open, from the sidebar, the chat header, or **⌘⇧A**, hides its row but leaves you on the archived conversation, with the composer replaced by "This session is archived. Unarchive it to continue the conversation." To keep working through your chats you have to click the next one every time.

## User Impact

- **Before:** archive the open chat, and you stay on it behind the archived banner. Click another chat to continue.
- **After:** archive the open chat, and the chat below it in the sidebar opens, or the one above when it was the last. Pressing ⌘⇧A again archives that one and moves on, the way archiving works in Apple Mail.

**Undo** still brings the row back instantly, without switching chats. When no other chat is listed, the archived chat stays open with its banner, as before. Archiving a chat you don't have open, or archiving from the Sessions page, never navigates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every archive entry point (sidebar row button and menu, chat header menu, ⌘⇧A, multi-select and tree archives) already goes through `archiveConfirmedSessionsWithUndo` and `holdArchive`. `session-archive-hold.ts` gains `subscribeArchiveStarts`, which runs once per archive as its Undo window opens.

The sidebar owns the visible order and session selection, so it is the subscriber (`app-sidebar-archive-advance.ts`, wired with three lines in `app-sidebar-session-navigation.ts`):

- **Order:** it keeps the order from its last render. An archive hides its rows before it starts, so a fresh read could no longer place the archived chat between its neighbors.
- **Choice:** it picks the next openable row below, then above, and skips every chat in the same archive (batch or tree).
- **Navigation:** it opens that chat through the sidebar's own `selectSession`, in a microtask after the Undo notice is shown, and only if the archived chat is still the open one.

`visibleSessionTreeInOrder` becomes public so the helper can read it; it has no side effects. There is no new Gateway call, setting, or string.

Undo deliberately does not navigate back. The existing e2e *held archive survives navigation, Undo restores it without a write* expects Undo to leave the route alone, and by then the reader may already be working in the next chat.

## Default behavior change

This replaces the current rule that archiving "keeps its conversation open" (docs, and the held-archive work in #194694). The open archived chat was a dead end: its composer is disabled, so the only next step was clicking somewhere else. Apple Mail moves to the next message instead.

The archived-chat presentation still exists and is still covered: it shows when no other chat is listed and when you go back to the archived chat. If maintainers prefer to keep staying on the archived chat as the default, this can sit behind a sidebar display option instead.

Four existing tests asserted "archiving the open chat does not navigate". They now assert the new behavior and keep their other checks:

- `app-sidebar-cases/interactions.ts` *hides an archiving current thread immediately and opens the next thread*: the thread opens once, and nothing else changes.
- `app-sidebar-cases/session-mutations.ts` *holds archive behind Undo without altering the active session's personal pin*: the pin and write assertions are unchanged; each archive of the open chat opens the next chat.
- `session-management.archive.e2e.test.ts` *keeps archive state after navigating away and back*: archiving now moves to the neighbor itself, and Back still shows the archived notice.
- `session-management.archive.e2e.test.ts` *keeps the selected session through archive refreshes and restores an empty composer*: after archiving, Back returns to the archived chat before the refreshes arrive, and every later assertion is unchanged. Its pane-title history now records the visit to the next chat.

## Evidence

Scenario: five synthetic chats, starting on "Deploy check: api-gateway". Playwright WebKit on Linux at 1280×800 with the mock Gateway fixture; the corner badge shows each key press (recording only, not part of the change). Before is `main` at 895091c9878, after is this branch.

| Before: ⌘⇧A leaves the archived chat open | After: ⌘⇧A opens the next chat |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: after Command-Shift-A, Deploy check stays open with the archived banner and a disabled composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76b1fbff-fb2d-4168-88aa-db0527944642) | ![After: after Command-Shift-A, Design review notes, the next chat in the sidebar, is open with the Undo notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7b5cec5-3b6d-496a-8101-9c4d81d9a922) |

After Undo, the archived row is back in the sidebar and the current chat stays open:

![After Undo: Design review notes is back in the sidebar while Customer import stays open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3eb1da9-1f3c-4aac-9a39-ce2abe098492)

### Recordings

After: ⌘⇧A opens the next chat; ⌘⇧A again archives that one and opens the next; Undo restores the row without switching chats.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08977ca9-77f2-4e60-ab26-3cd4c8f7f7e0

Before (`main`): ⌘⇧A leaves the archived chat open behind its banner.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0745f66-ef4f-453f-b690-811e4cec8ce9

### Tests

- **E2E** `ui/src/e2e/session-management.archive-advance.e2e.test.ts`, through the real sidebar and chat header with the mock Gateway:
  - Archiving the open chat from the header or the sidebar opens the chat below it, and Undo restores the row with no `sessions.patch` and no route change.
  - Archiving the last chat opens the one above.
  - Archiving another chat keeps the open chat.
  - With this branch's tests on `main`'s source, the first three fail and the last passes.
- **Unit** `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-archive-advance.test.ts`: below first, above for the last chat, skipping chats that can't be opened, batch archives skipping every archived chat, no navigation for other chats, outside chat routes, after disconnect or with no other chat, and no override when the reader already moved before the archive settled.
- **Checks** (Boat sandbox, head 5a949ef4082 on 895091c9878):
  - `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint on the changed files (0 findings) and oxfmt pass.
  - Unit tests pass: the new file, `session-organizer-archive`, `app-sidebar.sessions` and `app-sidebar.interactions` (219 tests).
  - Every archive e2e file passes, 7 files and 37 tests: archive, archive-undo, archive-batch, archive-automation, archived-actions, nested-archive and the new file.
- **Docs:** `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` (archive paragraph).

prs.title: fix(plugins): warn when a manifest stops an enabled standalone plugin file from starting with the Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #202830

## What Problem This Solves

An enabled plugin file listed in `plugins.load.paths` starts with the Gateway while it has no manifest (#171330). Once an `openclaw.plugin.json` that declares no `activation` sits beside it, it silently stops starting unless its config activates it. A plugin that only registers hooks, such as a `before_tool_call` tool policy, then never loads, while `plugins list`, `plugins inspect` and `doctor` keep showing it as enabled with no warning.

## User Impact

User impact: operators get a warning naming the plugin and the fix (`set activation.onStartup to true …, or false to keep it lazy`) wherever plugin diagnostics already appear. Which plugins load does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest registry is where a manifestless standalone file gets its synthetic `onStartup: true`, so the same place now warns when an explicitly enabled (`entries.<id>.enabled` or `allow`) standalone file has a real manifest that declares no `activation` at all. Any declared trigger (`onStartup` either way, `onCapabilities`, `onChannels`, …) silences it, since the author then chose how it starts. Plugins that policy keeps inactive (`plugins.enabled: false`, `deny`, an allowlist that leaves them out) get no warning; the adjacent `channelConfigs` metadata warning now shares that check.

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** one repro script run unchanged on throwaway Gateways: a hook-only plugin file whose `before_tool_call` blocks `session_status`, enabled through `plugins.entries`, called through `POST /tools/invoke`.

| Manifest beside the file | Runtime (`plugins.list` RPC), main → PR | `plugins inspect` / `doctor`, main | `plugins inspect` / `doctor`, this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | `active` → `active` (403 blocked) | no warning | no warning |
| without `activation` | `unloaded` → `unloaded` (200, tool ran) | no warning | **warning on both** |
| with `activation.onStartup: true` | `active` → `active` (403 blocked) | no warning | no warning |
| with `activation.onCapabilities: ["hook"]`, no `onStartup` | `active` → `active` (403 blocked) | no warning | no warning |

Warning text, as printed by `plugins inspect` (and by `doctor` under `[config] warnings: plugins.entries.hook-probe:`):

```
standalone plugin file has a manifest that declares no activation, so it starts with the Gateway only when its config activates it (registering hooks does not); set activation.onStartup to true to keep starting it with the Gateway, or false to keep it lazy
```

Apart from these two lines the main (`dce3c29`) and PR outputs are identical across all four phases, so load behavior is unchanged.

Tested on `4ebe01004e` (based on `dce3c29`; merges cleanly onto current main `684018d110`, which has not touched either file since).

- Tests: a table in `manifest-registry.diagnostics.test.ts`: warns for a file enabled through `entries` or `allow` whose manifest declares no activation; silent for `onStartup: false`, `onCapabilities: ["hook"]`, a disabled entry, `plugins.enabled: false`, `deny`, and an allowlist that excludes it. The warning cases fail on main and pass here; lint and typecheck pass.
- Review: autoreview (claude) on the first commit (`cdbaeee892`), clean; the two follow-up commits address ClawSweeper's findings (accurate wording, no warning for policy-inactive plugins or manifests that declare any activation).

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Why a warning rather than a behavior change: the docs (`docs/plugins/manifest/capabilities.md`) say leaving `onStartup` out no longer startup-loads a plugin, so making manifest-bearing files start again would contradict the documented contract. The gap is that nothing connects the two states for an operator. #117243 asked for a broader exclusion diagnostic and was closed as documented; this PR covers only the transition #171330 introduced, where the same file's startup behavior flips when a manifest is added, and needs no startup-plan data.

Not covered: installed (non-`load.paths`) plugins whose manifest has no trigger that can match. Detecting those needs the startup plan and per-trigger reasoning, so it is left to maintainers.

Repro script: four phases (no manifest, manifest without `activation`, manifest with `onStartup: true`, manifest with only `onCapabilities: ["hook"]`), each restarting the Gateway and recording the boot line's plugin list, a `gateway_start` hook log line, `/tools/invoke session_status`, the `plugins.list` RPC runtime state, `plugins list`, `plugins inspect` and `doctor --non-interactive`. The probe also carries the usual `record-missing` provenance warning in every phase, unrelated to this change.

</details>

Fixes #202819

## What Problem This Solves

Transcript storage, capture, migration, and Gateway code currently take their summary data contract from the module that generates and renders summaries. That leaves shared transcript data owned by a consumer of the data.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Summary fields, stored data, generation, and rendering stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the unchanged summary contract into the existing transcript types module and migrate all ten external type consumers. Remove the old private export without adding a forwarding alias or another abstraction.

## Evidence

The complete committed range was independently reviewed with no actionable findings. Source checks confirm the declaration is unchanged, all type consumers use the shared owner, and runtime function bodies and import ordering are preserved. Formatting and whitespace checks passed.

Seven existing transcript test files passed (99 tests passed, one existing skip), covering summary generation, model summaries, live summaries, storage, tool reads, Gateway reads, and migration. Core TypeScript checking, the two affected test-type graphs, and lint for all 12 changed files passed on `44660c4223ecb7ac4f3a5f3fb2b1b7240846ab65`.

The full build compiled the runtime and emitted declarations, but its Plugin SDK declaration-size check failed: 5,396,987 bytes exceeded the 5,385,536-byte limit. That failed result is retained; it is not a successful full build.

The [manual head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44855671482) also reports unused UI exports and a delayed-speech UI assertion. The unused-export failure matches [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44850136354/job/136679760264); the speech assertion has an [existing candidate fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199502).
