prs.title: fix: keep queued channel recovery replies alive
prs.body:
Related: #191476

## What Problem This Solves
Matrix recovery can lose a reply when the original turn releases its channel consumer before a queued follow-up invokes retained callbacks. A real Matrix/live-model reproduction failed with `Plugin matrix consumer is closed` during recovery.

## User Impact
Queued recovery replies remain deliverable after the original turn ends. Closed-consumer and operator-authority checks remain strict. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made
Give queued callbacks their own consumer lifetime, independent of one-shot ingress adoption. Release that lifetime through queue-source settlement, retain all contributing consumers when collecting follow-ups, and preserve custody through overflow compaction. Recovery acquires fresh custody rather than reusing the original ingress cancellation identity. Restore same-owner values before copying prewrapped reply options so native cancellation signals retain their identity.

## Evidence
- Real baseline Matrix/live-model recovery reproduced the closed-consumer error; the first failing callback was `onModelSelected`.
- The fixed real-model scenario triggered private-final recovery, delivered the visible marker exactly once, and produced no repeat during the following eight seconds.
- Initial proof: 134 focused tests and 28 sibling tests passed; after test-file extraction, 90 affected tests passed. Core typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, build, docs checks, line-cap ratchet, and diff checks passed.
- Independent and canonical local review found no remaining actionable P0–P2 issues after collection/overflow propagation fixes.
- CI exposed a type-import cycle. Moving the callback contract into a dependency-free leaf produced zero Madge cycles and 47 passing focused tests. The subsequent CI architecture gate passed at `09e9c9d5c5ba1b2456c54a0811abb55c91f9a259`.
- CI also caught three import-order formatting errors; repository formatting fixed them. Both docs and lint failures in that run originated from these same import blocks; all docs content checks passed.
- CI job `135274685539` exposed an introduced prewrapped-options regression: `AbortSignal.any` rejected a proxied signal. The existing delivery-custody suite passed 14/14 on frozen base, failed 1/14 on the candidate, and passed after restoring native option values before copying. Expanded the focused identity test to include prewrapped options; both files now pass 31/31 tests (59.36s wrapper wall time including compiler preparation; 57.37s Vitest duration). Targeted lint and formatting pass. Fresh independent review found no P0–P2 findings and confirmed callback fencing remains intact.
- At head `333f2682172dd9ee3f2fa1a461cfa854d7287448`, CI passes architecture, docs, lint, production/test types, and the delivery-custody test shard. ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head and reported no actionable findings.

### Retained real Matrix proof — sanitized excerpts
The isolated official Matrix plugin/live-model run used frozen base `d6f628897ad7830e7cd54063c18de41c9c4cc73e`. Baseline occurrence `70079534-2004-4f61-a67f-37c0d9ec1314` timed out after recovery hit the released consumer. IDs, local paths and model/provider details are omitted below; no message content or credentials are included.

```text
2026-11-19T00:55:19.460+00:00 [source-reply/private-final]
agent produced a private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool
(message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
channel=matrix chars=2924
2026-11-19T00:55:19.621+00:00 [turn/execution]
visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads: channel=matrix cause=completed
2026-11-19T00:55:19.900+00:00 Error: Plugin matrix consumer is closed
```

Fixed occurrence `40d72565-7593-4cce-b9bf-823e4be426c1`, from the reviewed original production repair before subsequent CI-driven corrections:

```text
2026-11-19T01:17:33.913+00:00 [source-reply/private-final]
agent produced a private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool
(message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
channel=matrix chars=2671
scenario: Matrix custody real-model diagnostic — pass
Prepare Matrix live — pass
recovers a substantive private final through one message tool retry — pass
recovered=1; WARN logged=true
scenario counts: passed=1 failed=0 skipped=0 total=1
QA scenarios passed, but cleanup failed
```

The scenario requires the private-final warning, asserts exactly one matching outbound marker, waits 8000ms, and asserts the count remains one. A direct first-answer send cannot satisfy this proof. Live provider-request counters were unavailable and are not evidence of request counts. The cleanup limitation is detailed below; the live scenario was not rerun on the later CI-correction head.

## CI Failure Classification
CI run `44440362497` completed with four failed jobs. These three signatures reproduce on frozen base `d6f628897ad7830e7cd54063c18de41c9c4cc73e`; none of their test files was changed:
- `src/gateway/operator-run-cancellation.test.ts:265`: two accepted-turn cases expect device revocation to throw, but it does not. Base and candidate each report 2 failed / 16 passed; repeated in current-run job `135280128892`.
- `src/gateway/server-plugins.user-profile.test.ts:143`: role-lifetime case expects rejection, but resolves `undefined`. Base reproduces 1 failed / 3 passed; repeated in current-run job `135280128930`.
- `test/cron-message-read.integration.test.ts:727`: the `claude-cli/channel-edit/native, disabled before undefined` case lacks `toolsAllowProvenance.channelRequester`. Frozen-base targeted run reproduces the exact missing-field assertion: 1 failed / 8 skipped, 33.07s Vitest duration (37.79s wrapper). Current-run job `135280128752` has the same signature. This is not introduced by the Matrix patch.

Current-run job `135280128915` fails `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts` because the yielded parent receives a child shutdown-completion input instead of `RESUMED_0_parent`. Important source distinction: CI tested merge `eb1e725093ef48832a1a6e36f0b771b16c4fbadb`, merging this head into `053fb62c6141c801fdd0f9bb2dfc3060a6fed912`, not the frozen branch tree alone. That base contains upstream #201544 (`82e52b648cf0`), which intentionally replaces quiet child shutdown with retained error completion. The unchanged restart fixture still expects quiet child settlement. This matches the observed failure path; exact matched-runtime baseline reproduction remains unproven. The earlier local frozen-base run failed before restart and is not evidence that this signature is inherited. No safe Matrix-scope correction is established, so the failure remains explicitly unresolved rather than reverting upstream behavior or weakening the test.

No assertions, baselines, or authority checks were weakened. CI remains red; passing gates are not a claim that all checks passed.

## Limits and Cleanup
The real scenario passed, but its QA process exited 1 during rootless Podman cleanup. Task-owned containers and networks were subsequently removed and the private service stopped; this is not reported as a wholly green QA command.

The original image/completion-plus-inbound overlap and encrypted Matrix transport were not separately exercised. This PR addresses the reproduced shared callback-lifetime failure, rather than claiming every report in #191476 is resolved.

prs.title: improve(ci): shorten FRV survivor critical path with bounded fanout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full Release Validation can wait for the final wave of package-upgrade survivor checks after other release branches drain. In candidate run44777975959, all92 targeted checks passed but their52m30s matrix set the end-to-end critical path. Other runs can instead be limited by a single first-hop job; raising concurrency cannot shorten that job.

## User Impact

**Modeled total-FRV savings range from0 to8m35s across four fully drained92-row traces.** Three traces benefit (6m21s,8m35s,7m53s); the newest trace gains **zero** because one44m04s first-hop job is already running in the first wave. These are conditional estimates, not measured cap64 savings or a promised minimum. No runtime product behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Raise only the existing GitHub-hosted expanded package-survivor cap from48 to64. Keep32 for self-hosted/custom runner groups, source-only runs, unspecified survivor scenarios and update-migration. Jobs, scenarios, per-container limits, fail-fast=false, deadlines, artifact identities and independent retries remain unchanged. No new planner, setting, helper or test scaffolding: workflow +1/-1; tests +1/-1. The existing eight-case expression test retains every exclusion. Both documentation pages now describe64 and its increase of16 over48; documentation +2/-2.

This builds on merged #201265 (32→48), without counting those gains again. **Tradeoff:** up to16 more simultaneous hosted jobs per matching matrix, but no added jobs or setup work. Concurrent campaigns multiply demand; hosted, npm and artifact contention can erase gains. The newest trace has no scheduling headroom for this change, so contention could make that case slower. No organization-wide capacity guarantee or universally nonregressing wall-time claim is made.

## Evidence

All four matrices have92/92 successful targeted rows. Parents are fully drained but have other validation failures: these are **not passing release qualifications or controlled A/B experiments**. Estimates replay complete measured job durations in observed admission order through an earliest-free-slot heap, retaining measured residuals, setup/cleanup, sibling barriers and collector tails.

| Parent / candidate | C=Q | Cap48→64 matrix replay | Modeled total-FRV saving |
|---|---|---:|---:|
|[44635836314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44635836314) / [44639105831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44639105831)|Frozen identities in run artifacts|2910→2335s|381s; CI clips575s component gain|
|[44773914831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44773914831) / [44777975959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44777975959)|`3f05d1ac58c19a4bc5417e4685af2ffff56f7b22`|3148→2633s|515s|
|[44790287992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44790287992) / [44794544663](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44794544663)|`fae2f8f16fbd335566c2d9aa500887dedef4da8d`|3029→2556s|473s|
|[44832835993](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44832835993) / [44835864437](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44835864437)|`35207ad56a84cc44cd596556955ce73feaf4d5f8`|2704→2704s|**0s**|

- Parent44773914831 ran16:29:33–18:02:28 UTC November20 to final job (92m55s). Matrix17:07:51–18:00:21; candidate receipt18:01:05; parent18:02:28. Internal sibling floor17:39:49; external CI17:33:59. Preserve2s replay residual,44s candidate tail and83s parent tail: cap64 projects17:53:53 parent finish.
- Parent44790287992: matrix18:49:39–19:40:11; candidate receipt19:41:02. Internal floor19:23:17; external19:22:14. Preserve3s residual and unchanged collector tails:473s total saving; projected matrix end19:32:18.
- **Newest limitation:** parent44832835993 starts22:55:20 November20 and final job ends00:17:36 November21. Matrix23:30:47–00:15:51; candidate receipt00:16:43; external CI00:08:52. [First-hop job136636875230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44835864437/job/136636875230) alone occupies2704s. It contains required sequential historical→candidate→future/unsupported update proof; more slots do not shorten it. Both newer sealed plan hashes match their final diagnostic manifest bindings, with activeRunIds=[] and no requested cancellation.
- Bounded capacity evidence for44773914831:2031 deduplicated jobs across its tree and18 overlapping CI runs, observed peak327 simultaneous ubuntu-24.04 jobs. Target refill median1s/max3s; additional same-label starts median2s/p953s. Five long external waits belong to separate four-row PostgreSQL matrix caps. This is not an organization-wide census. Counterfactual scoped peak343 lasts67s above observed peak.
- Sensitivity for44773914831 only:5% slower complete jobs leaves6m23s saving;10% leaves4m12s;15% leaves2m00s;20% loses12s. Break-even19.56% complete-job inflation. This headroom does **not** apply to the zero-gain newest trace. Unobserved queues, changed ordering, shared traffic and sibling delays remain risks. No64-way campaign was dispatched.

## Proof and review

The updated real workflow-expression case fails on base with “expected48 to be64”; all588 affected tests pass (124.11s; existing release-shell suite, no new test cases). Targeted tooling types, lint, format and complete workflow checks pass. Workflow checks initially rejected an empty ambient GitHub token; unsetting only that empty variable passed actionlint/zizmor without changing checks. Local independent review is waived by the owner. No new end-to-end Docker measurement is claimed.

ClawSweeper completed old-head review with one P3 documentation finding. Commit `7bc1837f7084c9afe9a8ebd9611828587d11c853` fixes both pages; MDX, formatting and diff checks pass. Unchanged workflow/test inputs retain the588-test proof. Prior-head [CI44803457258](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44803457258) passed.

**RFR verified November21, 2026 at03:14 UTC, exact head `7bc1837f7084c9afe9a8ebd9611828587d11c853`:** [CI44858892161](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44858892161) completed successfully. The full observed rollup contains46 successful checks/statuses,63 skipped and1 neutral, with no pending or failed checks. GitHub reports OPEN, MERGEABLE and CLEAN. [ClawSweeper revision2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202688#issuecomment-7049136949) completed at03:09:14 UTC on this exact head: zero findings, no before-merge items; the prior documentation finding is resolved. [Review handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202688#issuecomment-7056329182) completed at03:11:13 UTC. This is readiness for maintainer review, not a measured performance result or authorization to merge.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce complete-job scheduling estimates</summary>

Fetch all pages with `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44777975959/jobs?per_page=100 > jobs.json`, substituting each candidate run above:

```python
import json, datetime, heapq
pages = json.load(open("jobs.json"))
jobs = [j for page in pages for j in page["jobs"]]
assert len(jobs) == pages[0]["total_count"]
rows = sorted((j for j in jobs if "targeted lanes" in j["name"]
               and j["conclusion"] != "skipped"),
              key=lambda j: (j["started_at"], j["id"]))
assert len(rows) == 92 and all(j["conclusion"] == "success" for j in rows)
def timestamp(s):
    return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp()
def replay(cap):
    slots = [0] * cap
    for j in rows:
        duration = timestamp(j["completed_at"]) - timestamp(j["started_at"])
        heapq.heapreplace(slots, slots[0] + duration)
    return max(slots)
print(replay(48), replay(64), replay(48)-replay(64))
```

Retain each observed-minus-replay residual in both projections. Take the maximum with internal sibling completion, add candidate collector tail, take the maximum with external children, then add parent collector tail. Do not count component gains hidden by these barriers. Complete-job durations include setup/download/cleanup; do not subtract them again. Stable durations/admission and sufficient capacity are assumptions, not results.
</details>

prs.title: fix: stop recursive Git shims from exhausting agent sandboxes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent Git wrapper removes only its own directory from PATH before rediscovering `git`. A user forwarding shim can restore that directory and repeatedly re-enter the wrapper, exhausting a sandbox's process and memory limits. #202798 fixed recursive test fixtures; the product owner still needed repair.

## User Impact

Host, Docker, Podman, and private persistent Docker launchers now bake in a validated stable absolute native Git path during preparation. Realpath validates candidates; script shims and their symlink aliases are skipped without execution. Calls use the prepared path. Package-manager symlink upgrades keep working, and a missing path triggers one safe resolution attempt before an actionable error.

Normal nested Git calls keep working. Credentials, egress, identity, history/projection policy, and maintenance flags stay unchanged. No new environment variables, configuration, cache, or schema; the environment-name budget remains 462. The canonical-path binding and nesting sentinel from the first revision have been removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

One installer owns host and container launcher generation. It lives in a small sibling module to keep the runtime script within the existing source-size cap; the extracted command and launcher bytes are identical. Containers prepare from the read-only mounted source; private children install after configured setup. The executable PATH launcher stays on that resource mount and sources its prepared script from `/tmp` in the same shell, preserving default `noexec` mounts and read-only workspaces. Preparation utilities use `command -p`, so a restricted workload PATH cannot hide `mkdir` or `mktemp`. Installation preserves the existing 0755 directory mode. The fetch-failure regression now fails native Git's upload-pack transport rather than replacing Git through PATH.

Production grows by 76 lines for preparation, missing-target recovery, and container startup integration; the per-call PATH loop and environment handoffs are removed. The separate history-lock work in #199982 is untouched.

## Evidence

The current bounded regression fails on exact unchanged parent `f247afced37d159af27f7f019b950b6c696c125d` because the forwarding shim is executed. It passes with this repair. Unbounded-cycle reproduction ran only under hard caps (macOS RLIMIT_NPROC and Linux `pids.max=64`): base exhausts the cap; the repaired forwarding chain completes. Recovery skips a wrapper alias and returns 127 when no native Git exists. The upgrade regression replaces the native target and then removes the prepared path; both cases work without re-preparation, including shell-special characters in the path.

Actual Docker backend proof covers ordinary and private persistent execution with `workspaceAccess="ro"`, a read-only root, default `noexec` `/tmp`, and configured setup that exits 0. The native-Git control attempts transport for a missing-object probe; the mounted wrapper stays offline and creates no packs. The prior revision reproduces exit 126 on direct execution from `noexec` storage. A private absolute command with a restricted PATH reproduced exit 127 before the utility-path repair and now exits 0. Task containers were removed. Final five-file focused tests pass: **85 on Node**, **83 on Bun**, with two existing broker skips covered by Node. Full-diff Codex autoreview after the renderer extraction is scoped-clean at P0–P2. `pnpm check:changed` is green on the final source, including unchanged environment budget 462/462 and the source-size gate. Exact-head CI and ClawSweeper zero-item review remain required.

Host generated-launcher measurements use a synthetic **btrfs** repository with 62,000 files / 1.116 GB, native Git 2.39.5, five alternating A/B pairs of 1,000 calls and five A/A pairs. No production data. Allocation runs use separate five-pair 100-call batches; instrumented timings are discarded.

| Command | Wall median before → after | CPU median before → after | Allocation requests before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git --version` | 0.79819 → 0.73092 ms | 0.78911 → 0.73057 ms | 323,454 → 296,850 B |
| `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` | 1.07701 → 1.05357 ms | 1.08125 → 1.05870 ms | 343,727 → 321,704 B |

Allocation calls fall 488.29→431.29 and 647.29→598.29, with exact A/A matches. Counts cover malloc/calloc/realloc requests and amortized batch-shell overhead, excluding mmap/live RSS; the allocation-only interposer substitutes fork for vfork to isolate counters.

A/A wall medians: version 0.80959/0.83234 ms; probe 0.98134/1.03084 ms. CPU controls: 0.81020/0.83330 and 0.98481/1.03589 ms. The small probe gain is within A/A variation; this establishes no added median overhead, not a production speedup claim. This owner never reads session or agent databases. Reproduction scripts are in `scripts/perf/agent-git-wrapper*`.

The host launcher is byte-identical after the container delivery repair. A separate final-container run uses the same btrfs fixture and paired method. Paired median wall/CPU deltas are **−0.00484/−0.00083 ms** for version calls and **−0.19845/−0.19190 ms** for revision probes. Separate version medians are 0.89468→0.90874 ms wall and 0.89723→0.91167 ms CPU; that positive difference is smaller than the A/A variation (wall 0.95091/0.87510 ms). Both summaries are reported: the noisy version sample supports no demonstrated regression, not a precise speedup. Probe medians are 1.38057→1.18212 ms wall and 1.38454→1.19263 ms CPU. Container allocation requests fall 323,454→306,740 B and 343,727→316,746 B; calls fall 488.29→437.29 and 647.29→575.29, with exact A/A allocation matches.

ClawSweeper correctly found the noexec delivery regression, and Codex found preparation utilities depending on the workload PATH; both are repaired with actual Docker proof. The earlier budget-growth failure is eliminated. No inherited-failure exception is requested.

prs.title: fix(google): bind explicit router continuation to its original request
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter Google continuation must remain explicit and bound to the dispatched request. Managed SSE sanitization could hide terminal errors; intermediate checkpoints could poison a valid final receipt; and final host policy could change generation input after the replay binding was computed.

## Behavior

- A completed response may expose an opaque `providerReplay`; callers explicitly pass it as `GoogleContinuationOptions.googleContinuation` on a separate call. No automatic second request or upstream-secret fallback is added.
- Bind the final token-free input after host policy. Reject changed model, origin, session, profile, authority-bearing headers or generation input before dispatch; per-hop `x-request-id` remains excluded.
- Reject either token spelling injected by policy, including null/undefined. Append only the validated receipt token before recording the actual wire digest and byte counts. Enforce the final UTF-8 size without another media-dropping pass.

- Only the qualified ClawRouter native Google continuation route disables managed SSE sanitization. Terminal SSE errors and JSON error tails cannot produce a receipt.
- Valid intermediate checkpoints preserve text and usage but never authorize replay alone. A matching final `CONTINUATION` and complete HTTP EOF remain mandatory, including after an earlier `DONE` marker. Malformed/contradictory tokens, other final reasons, errors and aborts remain disqualifying.
- Direct Google/Vertex, selected credentials, URL ownership, deadlines, release and key rotation retain their existing behavior. The transport option type now includes its already-supported sampling seed.

prs.title: fix: preserve RFB cancellation and portable test ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Canceling a backpressured RFB connection can replace the owner's cancellation error with `Socket is closed`. Several runtime-qualification tests also depend on incidental behavior of unattached HTTP responses, query imports, global Worker diagnostics, spare heap capacity, or Linux process titles.

## User Impact

RFB callers retain their cancellation cause and queued writes settle before teardown completes. Runtime qualification keeps the same protected behavior with explicitly owned fixtures. The native Linux census remains unverified on stock here; its separate parser fixture preserves exact spaced/colon-bearing process names.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Duplex owns its terminal error, so cancellation retires it before destroying TCP and joins the active native write callback. The test corrections use an owned response flush gate, one native invocation per cache-maintenance pass, the existing Worker factory, explicit heap samples, and an independently observed `/proc/<pid>/comm` value.

The simplification pass retained one production owner and removed the query-reimport and global diagnostics dependencies. Production delta: +19/-4 lines; test delta: +80/-45. No assertions were weakened.

## Evidence

All nine portable assigned identities pass on Node, the pinned fork, and stock. Full touched files pass on Node and the fork; stock has one deliberately unchanged live `arrayBuffers` failure. All five revert controls reproduce the original stock mechanisms (nine portable identities); all 12 indirect lifecycle-consumer runs pass. Exact-head CI run [44853871267](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44853871267) and `openclaw/ci-gate` pass without reruns or exceptions.

Codex autoreview of the final nine-file snapshot against `6b0df8b93610` is scoped-clean at P0–P2. The reviewer assessed the diff; the runtime results below were verified separately.

Core and canonical consumer typechecks, nine-file lint, format, and `git diff --check` pass. The reviewed source is unchanged in head `f79cbf56172f206b5b601c5180b38501058bfb7a`.

| File | IDs | Stock before | Fork after | Stock after | Node after | Control | Wall s (before → after) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/desktop/rfb-probe.test.ts` | 1 | AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw error including 'desktop owner stopped' but got 'Socket is closed' | 18/18 | 18/18 | 18/18 | original production: cancellation cause replaced (49.60 s) | S 43.86 → 73.14; F 18.45 → 42.15; N 34.61 → 20.47 |
| `src/gateway/http-common.test.ts` | 3 | AssertionError: expected { Object (_events, _eventsCount, ...) } to match object { writableEnded: true, …(1) } | 18/18 | 18/18 | 18/18 | original fixture: writableFinished mismatch (40.02 s) | S 19.64 → 60.25; F 25.32 → 76.6; N 41.79 → 51.81 |
| `src/infra/node-compile-cache.test.ts` | 4 | Error: Test timed out in 120000ms. | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | original query imports: 120 s timeout (132.74 s) | S 128.81 → 15.74; F 26.82 → 30.92; N 32.37 → 13.65 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list.worker-recovery.integration.test.ts` | 5 | AssertionError: expected undefined to be defined | 1/1 | 1/1 | 1/1 | original diagnostics: Worker missing (118.49 s) | S 214.92 → 306.77; F 129.72 → 112.77; N 155.72 → 117.2 |
| `src/infra/worker-cpu.test.ts` | 6 (five) | AssertionError: heapTotal equals heapUsed (five cases) | 25/25 | 24/25; all five assigned pass | 25/25 | original heap samples: all five fail (5.89 s) | S 16.65 → 29.41; F 20.58 → 22.28; N 40.48 → 16.67 |
| `src/infra/ports.test.ts` | 7 | Linux-only, skipped | 47 pass, 3 platform skips | 47 pass, 3 platform skips | 47 pass, 3 platform skips | Linux-only-unverified | S 22.49 → 38.57; F 51.56 → 24.83; N 40.82 → 21.59 |

S = stock, F = pinned fork, N = Node. These are wall times for `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` with the runtime explicitly selected; cold compilation/builds are included. The catalog scenario exercises real Gateway/Worker failure and recovery. Its test time was about 48–71 seconds; wall time also includes runtime preparation.

Node loopback write benchmark: five warmed 10,000-write samples, 1 KiB per write; median 1.78 → 2.06 µs per write (observed difference: +0.28 µs). This is a synthetic shared-host measurement, not an end-to-end throughput claim.

Consumer gates: no production builtin import style moved, so no consumer override changed. The lifecycle audit includes the RFB owner plus host-source, managed-linux, environments, and the node desktop-stream command; all four files pass on Node, fork, and stock (107 tests per runtime).

prs.title: fix(ui): stage pasted images in the terminal composer
prs.body:
Closes #202645

## What Problem This Solves

In a Codex session opened in terminal mode, copying an image to the clipboard and pasting it into the OpenClaw chat input did nothing, while attaching the same image through the paperclip button worked.

The terminal composer wires three ways to add a file — the attach button, file selection, and drag-and-drop — into one staging owner (`createTerminalPanelUpload`). Paste was never wired, so a `ClipboardEvent` carrying an image reached an `<input>` with only an `onInput` handler and was dropped on the floor. The composer had no diagnostic for it: the paste simply produced no attachment.

## User Impact

A pasted clipboard image now stages as an attachment chip in the terminal composer, exactly like a dropped or selected file. Text pastes and other non-file clipboard payloads keep the input's native paste behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-view.tsx` rendered the composer input with `onInput` but no `onPaste`; `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-upload.ts` exposed `chooseFiles`, `handleFileSelection`, and `handleDrop`, all of which funnel into the private `uploadFiles(files)`.

The fix reuses that owner rather than adding a second path:

- `handlePaste(event)` reads `event.clipboardData.files`, returns early when it is empty so text pastes are untouched, and otherwise calls the existing `uploadFiles`.
- The composer input forwards `onPaste` to `upload.state.handlePaste`.

Nothing about submission changes. `uploadFiles` → `runBatch` → `insertPaths` already owns staging, quoting, size/type admission and retention, and it still never writes to the PTY: the path either becomes an attachment chip via `stagePaths` or is inserted as editable text, and Enter only happens on explicit Send. That invariant is asserted in both the unit and browser tests.

Fix classification: `behavior-completing` (a file-input surface accepted drag and selection but not paste).

## Evidence

### Real clipboard, real keystroke (Chromium, real composer)

`ui/src/e2e/terminal-upload.e2e.test.ts` → `stages a pasted clipboard image and keeps text pastes native`

Drives the shipped surface end to end: a real Playwright Chromium page, the real chat session route, the real chat side panel, the real rendered `.tp-composer input`, the **real OS-level clipboard** (`navigator.clipboard` with `clipboard-read`/`clipboard-write` granted), and an actual `Control+V` keystroke. No `ClipboardEvent` is constructed and no `DataTransfer` is injected. Only the Gateway transport is the repository's mock (`installMockGateway`).

1. Opens a chat session, toggles the Terminal side panel, dismisses the embedded session picker to reveal the composer.
2. Writes plain text with `navigator.clipboard.writeText` and presses `Control+V` → the text lands in the input and **zero** `terminal.upload` requests are issued (text pastes stay native).
3. Renders a 2×2 canvas, encodes it to a real PNG blob, writes it with `navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({ "image/png": blob })])`, then presses `Control+V` → asserts `terminal.upload` is called with a `.png` name and a `contentBase64` starting `iVBOR` (the PNG magic bytes), then resolves staging.
4. Asserts the `.tp-attachment` chip renders and that **no** `terminal.input` was sent before an explicit Send.

The headless Chromium clipboard was probed first and does deliver: writing the PNG succeeds (`{"ok":true,"types":["image/png"]}`) and a `Control+V` against a DOM input delivers exactly one file.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts \
  ui/src/e2e/terminal-upload.e2e.test.ts
```

- HEAD (`73c40fc3ce2`): **3 passed (3)**.
- BASE (`80c13f6a377` production files reverted, test kept): **1 failed | 2 passed**. The failure is the bug itself — `waitForRequest("terminal.upload")` times out at `terminal-upload.e2e.test.ts:330` because the real `Control+V` produced no upload. The other two pre-existing cases stayed green, so the failure is the missing paste wiring, not the harness.

With `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1` the suite also records the run and writes `terminal-composer-pasted-image.png` showing the staged attachment chip.

### Unit regression test

`ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-file-upload.test.ts` keeps one paste case: `leaves a text-only paste to the input's own handling` (an empty-file clipboard paste is not prevented and issues no upload). The previous lower-level pasted-image replay was removed — the browser test above covers that intake and the no-submit contract at the real boundary.

```sh
pnpm --dir ui test src/components/terminal/terminal-file-upload.test.ts
```

HEAD: **19 passed**.

### Acceptance set from the issue

```sh
pnpm --dir ui test src/components/terminal/terminal-panel.test.ts \
  src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-handoff.test.ts \
  src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-hosted-tabs.test.ts \
  src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-reconnect.test.ts \
  src/components/terminal/terminal-file-upload.test.ts
pnpm check:control-ui-controllers
```

HEAD: **5 files, 87 tests passed**; controller guard OK. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the changed files.

## Not tested

- No live macOS run. The report is from the Mac app; this PR was verified on Linux through headless Chromium with a real OS clipboard and a real `Control+V`. The clipboard payload is produced by a canvas-encoded PNG, not by a macOS clipboard, so macOS-specific WebKit clipboard behavior (for example HEIC-only payloads) is out of scope.
- The Gateway transport in the browser test is the repository's mock. A real Gateway + real PTY run was attempted locally and could not start: `@openclaw/proc-safe`'s native child reaper requires glibc ≥ 2.29 and this host is 2.28, so the supervised service-child layer refuses to launch. The upload RPC itself is unchanged by this PR; the changed surface is the DOM paste handler, which the browser test exercises directly.
- The Codex terminal-mode session itself is not exercised; the browser test asserts the composer/upload boundary the bug lives on.
- `terminal-panel-view.tsx` is not covered by a rendering unit test here (its test file is at the 1000-line cap). The browser test above exercises that exact `onPaste` wire end to end, so the missing-wire failure mode is covered by the BASE run.
- HEIC/other clipboard encodings from #165117 are a different boundary (native image conversion) and are untouched.

## Cleanup

All runs used the repository's existing test harness with an isolated jsdom environment, Chromium, and mock Gateway; no real Gateway, session, credential or macOS clipboard was touched.

prs.title: improve: reduce session sidebar work during streaming bursts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session events during streaming bursts can repeatedly recompute child activity for unrelated sidebar rows, consuming the Gateway main thread even when those rows do not change.

## User Impact

Unchanged child contributions remain reusable across session events and list subscribers. Row contents, audience visibility, and event ordering are preserved. No protocol, configuration, schema, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`bumpAgentRunIndexVersion` advances the run registry revision and emits a keyed runtime publication (`src/infra/agent-run-registry-state.ts:76–90`). The child owner already invalidates that key and its ancestors (`session-row-child-activity.ts:367–389, 415–417`), but did not acknowledge the registry revision. Its next read consequently took the broad fallback at lines 140–142 and dirtied **every cached child contribution**.

The fix acknowledges the revision through the existing runtime invalidation operation after the keyed ancestor walk. Broad and session-ID-only publications retain their existing handling. Production growth is **four lines**; there is no new cache or coalescing point. Existing audience/exclusion identities, time-based expiry, and private-source isolation remain in control.

This builds on #200899, #201420, #201591, #201758, #202117, and #202337. The measured repeated term is child activity. Existing freeze, selection, and sidebar sharing reuse already prevents proportional recomputation in this workload; this change does not redo those optimizations.

## Evidence

The interleaved work-count regression fails on base `9bb091e873e4c` and passes with the fix. It moves a real registered run between three parents, alternates owner/viewer audiences with different child visibility, checks activity and release state, and requires untouched children to remain unprojected. The new test and five related event/projection suites pass: **36 tests in six files**. Targeted lint, formatting, scripts typecheck, gateway-root test typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass.

The existing `sidebar-presentation-measure.ts` rig now exercises 15,000 persisted synthetic entries (100 parents with 149 children each), eight active child runs and their eight parents, six loopback WebSocket subscribers across two profiles, and 100-row sidebar pages every 47 events. Each arm handles 4,700 logical events / 28,200 delivered event frames and 600 list requests. Target input is 470 logical events/s; six-recipient fan-out is heavier than 470 outbound frames/s. Mix: 60% chat deltas, 20% activity publications, 10% model updates, 10% child runtime updates. These event kinds use the prepared event/list owners and registry publishers; their proportions are synthetic because aggregate stacks do not provide actual production ratios.

Acceptance recorded before measurement: lower repeated child work, main-thread CPU, and allocation; matching normalized event/final-row bytes and FIFO counts; no 20% regression in timing summary. Five serial alternating AB/BA pairs, separate timing and sampled-allocation campaigns, warm fixtures, Node 24.22.1 on a controlled Boat Linux VM (observed 8 CPUs, 15,991 MiB RAM; one-minute load 1.06–2.04). Allocation sampling is 32 KiB and includes collected objects. A = base owner, B = candidate; the workload is identical in both processes.

| Pair/order | Main-thread ms / 1k events, A → B | Worst synchronous CPU ms, A → B | Worst synchronous elapsed ms, A → B | Sampled bytes/event, A → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 (AB) | 2594 → 1148 | 88.66 → 24.00 | 88.55 → 23.75 | 2225000 → 752649 |
| 2 (BA) | 2580 → 999 | 89.77 → 3.41 | 89.76 → 3.72 | 2220471 → 744726 |
| 3 (AB) | 2402 → 953 | 83.62 → 3.01 | 84.10 → 2.54 | 2224971 → 742542 |
| 4 (BA) | 2385 → 858 | 102.99 → 2.00 | 103.06 → 1.93 | 2215440 → 741371 |
| 5 (AB) | 2351 → 913 | 95.78 → 2.99 | 96.58 → 2.59 | 2213713 → 740573 |
| Median | 2,402 → 953 | 89.77 → 3.01 | 89.76 → 2.59 | 2,220,471 → 742,542 |
| p95 across five runs (maximum) | 2,594 → 1,148 | 102.99 → 24.00 | 103.06 → 23.75 | 2,225,000 → 752,649 |

Median main-thread work improves **60.3%**, worst on-CPU slice **96.7%**, and allocation **66.6%**. All five pairs match normalized event digests and final list digests; every recipient receives sequence 0 through 4,699 in order. Normalization removes only generated fixture profile IDs/avatar versions and snapshot timestamps.

Separate instrumented attribution (inclusive CPU; child is nested within present, so these rows are not additive):

| Path | Calls A → B | Main-thread ms / 1k events A → B | Worst synchronous CPU ms A → B | Worst elapsed ms A → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Present, including child activity | 116,400 → 116,400 | 1922.55 → 181.45 | 25.689 → 20.001 | 25.093 → 20.274 |
| Child activity | 116,400 → 116,400 | 1749.28 → 29.81 | 24.896 → 1.011 | 24.989 → 0.372 |
| Select, including prepared rows/roster/policy/owners/sort | 600 → 600 | 17.23 → 12.51 | 1.955 → 1.009 | 1.309 → 0.543 |
| Freeze | 972 → 972 | 1.49 → 1.05 | 1.000 → 1.001 | 0.083 → 0.232 |
| Sidebar share | 600 → 600 | 0.21 → 0.43 | 1.001 → 1.007 | 0.016 → 0.033 |

Child contributions: **1,917,378 → 1,410 (−99.93%)**. Present still gets called for each consumer; its child owner now retains unchanged contributions. Freeze/selection/share counts are unchanged. These tiny unchanged paths are not improvement claims: instrumented share CPU rises 0.21 → 0.43 ms/1k and freeze maximum elapsed rises 0.083 → 0.232 ms. Their per-call CPU samples reach about 1 ms even for sub-ms wall durations; use the uninstrumented campaign for total/tail claims.

The controlled candidate sustains **470 logical events/s**; the baseline reaches 385–423 (median 414). Median event-loop delay improves at p95 **2.40 → 2.15 ms**, p99 **58.06 → 7.42 ms**, and maximum **98.11 → 17.09 ms**. Median GC elapsed/event is **0.0445 → 0.0277 ms**.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and focused checks</summary>

Save the original owner and run the same committed rig against each owner, alternating order for five pairs with fresh state directories (or the rig's existing `--repeats 5 --barrier-dir … --side base|fix` controls):

```sh
mkdir -p .local/session-surge/base
git show 9bb091e873e4c:src/gateway/session-row-child-activity.ts > .local/session-surge/base/session-row-child-activity.ts
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sidebar-presentation-measure.ts   --surge --sessions 15000 --page-size 100 --clients 6 --operations 4700   --state-dir .local/session-surge/base-1 --output .local/session-surge/base-1.json   --source-file .local/session-surge/base/session-row-child-activity.ts
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sidebar-presentation-measure.ts   --surge --sessions 15000 --page-size 100 --clients 6 --operations 4700   --state-dir .local/session-surge/fix-1 --output .local/session-surge/fix-1.json
```

Use separate fresh arms with `--allocations` for allocation and `--surge-detail` for coarse path attribution/work counts. CPU profiles are separate from the timing table. The rig records source hashes, load, CPU/wall slice pairs, event digests, and GC/event-loop metrics.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-row-presentation.fingerprints.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-row-event-parity.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.invalidation.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-event-trees.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.subagent-index.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.incognito.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

```

</details>

This is a synthetic production-shaped owner/transport workload, **not a booted Gateway or live-model test**, and does not establish production chat.history p95 or reproduce every reported one-second stall. An earlier macOS campaign on an overloaded shared host (load 50–66) also reduced median CPU 2,479 → 1,097 ms/1k and allocation 2.42 MB → 0.758 MB/event, but its timer-delay p95 moved 3.31 → 6.17 ms. No provider change or CI retry was used.

Production code is +4 lines, regression coverage +76 lines, and the remaining diff extends the existing rig/probe to make the requested workload, FIFO checks, and attribution repeatable. No production systems accessed. No autoreview or merge performed, as requested. prs.title: fix(ui): keep provider-pattern model maps editable in form mode
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Control UI → AI Agents → Agent Defaults → Models shows "Unsupported schema node. Use Raw mode." on a valid config, because provider model schemas (bundled vLLM) inject `patternProperties` into the models map and the form analyzer rejects that keyword.
- Solution: Admit `patternProperties` in the analyzer only where the existing editor can render the node (named properties or an object-valued/`true` `additionalProperties`); pattern-only object maps keep their Raw-mode fallback.
- What changed: `ui/src/components/config-form.analyze.ts` (representability-gated keyword admission), `ui/src/components/config-form.analyze.node.test.ts` (analyzer regression tests incl. the pattern-only counterexample), `ui/src/components/config-form.browser.test.ts` (real-Chromium coverage of both shapes).
- What did NOT change: Pattern-only object maps (e.g. the knowledge plugin's `stores`, `additionalProperties: false`) still report unsupported and keep the Raw-mode notice — the review counterexample is covered by tests at both the analyzer and browser level. Form validation and patch behavior are otherwise untouched.

Fixes #202721

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A valid config with a bundled-provider `patternProperties` refinement on `agents.defaults.models` was pushed into Raw mode, so the Models map was not editable in Form mode.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux x64, Node v24.20.0, worktree at `issue-202721` on `origin/main` (599bc4222a4), **system Chromium 138.0.7204.157 driven by the browser Vitest project** (Playwright provider, no download needed; the repo's `playwright-chromium.ts` helper selected it). The production analyzer and the real Solid editor were exercised before and after the patch.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # analyzer-level reproduction from the issue (synthetic schema, no config needed)
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts ui/src/components/config-form.analyze.node.test.ts
  # real-Chromium editor coverage (map editor edit/patch + Raw fallback notice)
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-browser.config.ts ui/src/components/config-form.browser.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ chromium  src/components/config-form.browser.test.ts (36 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  36 passed (36)
  ```
  In a real Chromium instance: a models map carrying `^vllm/.+$` patternProperties renders the `.cfg-map` editor (no Raw-mode notice), editing an entry's alias patches `["models", "vllm/local", "alias"]`, and a pattern-only map (`stores: {team:{agents:["main"]}}` with `additionalProperties: false`) keeps the Raw-mode notice, renders no `.cfg-map`, and issues no patches. Analyzer-level: before the patch the same synthetic schema failed with `expected [ 'models' ] to deeply equal []`; after, `unsupportedPaths` is empty for the models map and `["stores"]` for the pattern-only map.
- **Observed result after fix:** Provider-pattern model maps are analyzed and rendered as editable maps in a real browser; pattern-only maps keep their Raw-mode fallback; all 36 config-form browser tests and 30 analyzer/related node tests pass.
- **What was not tested:** Save/reload against a live Gateway (the browser tests assert the emitted patches at the editor boundary; the config write path is covered by existing fixtures). No live vLLM endpoint was involved (not needed for the analyzer/renderer boundary).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + real-browser component test
- Target test file: `ui/src/components/config-form.analyze.node.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/config-form.browser.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: (1) provider-pattern models map produces no unsupported paths and renders an editable map with key-path patches in real Chromium; (2) pattern-only maps (`additionalProperties: false`, entries defined solely by `patternProperties`) stay unsupported with the Raw-mode notice.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: both the admission boundary and the two render outcomes the review called out are pinned with the exact schema shapes from the issue and the review counterexample.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `SUPPORTED_FORM_SCHEMA_KEYS`/`SUPPORTED_CONSTRAINT_ONLY_KEYS` in `config-form.analyze.ts` never listed `patternProperties`; once `modelParamsSchema` started contributing it (#129434), every provider-pattern model map failed the analyzer's keyword policy and fell back to Raw mode. A global exemption would have over-admitted pattern-only maps the editor cannot render, so admission is gated on renderable structure instead.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test covered a map schema carrying `patternProperties`.

prs.title: fix(models): hide expired cooldown and disabled windows in auth list
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `openclaw models auth list` shows expired cooldown and disabled windows as if they were still active (with a past `until` time and a stale recovery hint), disagreeing with `openclaw models status`, which correctly ignores expired windows.
- Solution: Gate `cooldownUntil`/`disabledUntil` projection through the same `isActiveUnusableWindow(until, now)` check already used for `blockedUntil`.
- What changed: `src/commands/models/auth-list.ts` (window gating + reason/recoveryHint selection), `src/commands/models/auth-list.test.ts` (regression test).
- What did NOT change: Active windows are rendered exactly as before (same fields, same hints). Store contents are untouched; expired windows are only hidden from display, as `models status` already does. No other commands were affected.

Fixes #202004

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `models auth list` reported expired cooldown/disabled windows as active and printed misleading re-auth/billing hints, disagreeing with `models status` for the same profile.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux x64, Node v24.20.0, worktree at `issue-202004` on `origin/main` (627d692edf1), isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. A real auth store (`openclaw-agent.sqlite`) was seeded through the repo's own `saveAuthProfileStore`, then the **shipped CLI entry point** (`node openclaw.mjs models auth list`, built via `pnpm build` from this branch) was run against it.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # seed a real store with one expired and one active cooldown window
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs seed-store.mts /tmp/oc-202004/state/agents/main/agent
  # shipped CLI entry point, built from this branch
  pnpm build && node openclaw.mjs models auth list
  # regression test
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/models/auth-list.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  $ node openclaw.mjs models auth list        # built from this branch
  Agent: main
  Auth state store: /tmp/oc-202004/state/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
  Profiles:
  - openai:active-cooldown [openai/oauth; expires 2026-11-20T20:04:18.476Z; cooldown:rate_limit until 2026-11-20T20:04:18.476Z] — Wait for cooldown or switch provider.
  - openai:expired-cooldown [openai/oauth; expires 2026-11-20T20:04:18.476Z]
  ```
  Same store, CLI built from `origin/main` (before the patch):
  ```text
  - openai:expired-cooldown [openai/oauth; expires 2026-11-20T20:04:18.476Z; cooldown:rate_limit until 2026-11-20T19:03:18.476Z] — Wait for cooldown or switch provider.
  ```
  (the `until` above is already in the past at run time). JSON mode after the fix: the expired-cooldown profile contains only `id/provider/type/label/expiresAt` — no `cooldownUntil`, no `cooldownReason`, no `recoveryHint`.
- **Observed result after fix:** Expired cooldown/disabled windows produce no entry and no recovery hint; active windows are unchanged; text and JSON agree with `models status`.
- **What was not tested:** The state-store guard warned that the installed Gateway service's paths could not be verified under the isolated HOME (expected on this host); the command ran against the isolated store only. JSON-mode output was verified through the same `modelsAuthListCommand` path with `defaultRuntime`.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `src/commands/models/auth-list.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: `hides expired cooldown and disabled windows, keeping active-window reasons` — an expired cooldown shows no entry/hint; an expired `disabled` window no longer mislabels a still-active cooldown (reason stays `cooldown:auth`); an active cooldown still renders with its hint.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it exercises the exact projection boundary where expiry was ignored, in both text and JSON output.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `modelsAuthListCommand` only compared `blockedUntil` with `Date.now()`; `cooldownUntil`/`disabledUntil` were projected unconditionally and `disabledActive` was derived from mere presence, so expired windows rendered as active and an expired `disabledReason` could mislabel an active cooldown.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no expiry check on the cooldown/disabled display path, and no test covering expired non-subscription windows.

prs.title: fix: make onboarding next steps runnable when OpenClaw runs from npx
prs.body:
Closes #202822
Related: #192331, #202183, #201182

## What Problem This Solves

When someone tries OpenClaw with `npx openclaw@…`, as in the docs' "Try it in one command", and has not installed the CLI, there is no `openclaw` command on their PATH. In the closing lines of a foreground run, onboarding already prints the "keep the Gateway running in the background later" hint as `npx openclaw@<version> gateway install`, but the skipped-AI Next steps, the Local setup line, and the other foreground closing lines still use a bare `openclaw`. Copied into a new terminal, they fail with `openclaw: command not found`.

## User Impact

User impact: when onboarding runs from npx (or another temporary runner copy such as pnpm dlx or bunx), the skipped-AI Next steps, the Local setup line, and the closing lines printed while the Gateway runs in this terminal use the same `npx openclaw@<version> …` form as the existing background hint, so they no longer depend on an installed `openclaw` command in a new terminal. pnpm dlx and bunx runs get this npx form too, so they still need `npx` to be available. Outside temporary runners, output is unchanged unless a named profile or `--container` is in use; then these lines include `--profile <name>` or `--container <name>`, as the background hint already does. No new config, flags, or defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

On `084b631` (line numbers below are on that commit), `src/commands/onboard-quickstart-host.ts:91-95` already decides whether the CLI runs from a temporary runner copy (`isDisposableEntrypoint`) and, if so, prints the npx form. The next line, `:96`, and the other closing hints print fixed text. This change moves that decision into one exported helper in `src/daemon/durable-service-entrypoint.ts`, the module that already owns the check and the npx form, and uses it for these next-step commands:

- the reopen, pending-Gateway, and setup-only lines in the foreground summary;
- the skipped-AI Next steps, in both places that print them;
- the setup-only note during guided onboarding;
- the Local setup `gateway run` line.

The existing background hint now uses the same helper, with unchanged output. The three wizard locales use placeholders for these commands.

The docs' "Try it in one command" section still suggests installing the CLI for later use, and that stays true. These hints now also work before that step, the same way the background hint from #192331 does.

#202183 (draft) routes the skipped-AI next steps and the `gateway run` line through `formatCliCommand` so a named profile is kept; it does not change what npx runs print. Outside npx, this PR prints the same named-profile commands on those lines, since both go through `formatCliCommand`, and its three `nextStepsWithoutAi` strings match #202183's (head `11ac9b6`). #201182 is a related, different problem: it is about the wording and grouping after skipping AI, not about whether the printed commands run.

Unchanged on purpose: `formatCliCommand`, which the plugin SDK exports; the first-screen `openclaw onboard --classic` hint, shown before setup starts rather than as a next step; the team-setup error messages; the "You can always find me later — run `openclaw` in a terminal" note that some runs print at the end instead of opening the browser, since which command those runs should point to is a separate change; install-cli and install.sh installs, which do not run from a temporary runner copy; the docs.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `formatUserCliCommand(args?)` returns `npx openclaw@<VERSION> <args>` when `isDisposableEntrypoint(process.argv[1])` is true, and `formatCliCommand("openclaw <args>")` otherwise. With no arguments it returns `openclaw` or `npx openclaw@<VERSION>`, without a trailing space. Both forms keep the `--profile` or `--container` flag that `formatCliCommand` adds.
- `formatDurableInstallCommand` had one caller outside its module, the background hint. After the move it is used only inside the module, so it is no longer exported, and it is renamed `formatNpxCliCommand` because it now formats any command. The reinstall message in `resolveDurableServiceCli` is unchanged.
- `setup-apply.ts` loads the helper lazily in the branch where installation was explicitly skipped, like that file's other lazy imports.
- The skipped-AI commands in `onboard-guided.ts` are computed only when the Next steps are printed.
- Against `084b631`: production +59/−31 in 7 files, tests +276/−13 in 4 files.

</details>

"After" results were taken on `084b631` with this PR's change applied: the real run used a package built from `084b631` plus this PR's production changes (the same production files as commit `fdd35b6d16ea`), and the focused tests ran on that commit's full diff.

Onboarding choices: Quick start, One agent, Skip for now. The printed command was then copied into a new login shell (`bash -l`) with the same environment and stdin from `/dev/null`.
- **Before** (`npx --yes openclaw@2026.11.10-beta.1`):

prs.title: feat(gateway): opt-in Cloudflare Access JWT verification for trusted-proxy auth
prs.body:
Closes #200361

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway behind Cloudflare Access can trust an identity header from any process that reaches it from a configured proxy address. Operators need a way to require proof that their Access application authenticated the request.

## User Impact

Enable `gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAccessJwt` with the Access team issuer and the application's AUD tag to require a signed assertion. The setting is off by default. Enterprise browser delegation is unavailable with verification enabled. Nodes using an Access service token still authenticate with their own Gateway credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway verifies the assertion's signature, issuer, audience, and expiry before accepting the signed email. Usable keys are RSA of at least 2048 bits, the minimum RS256 permits per RFC 7518 §3.3, so weak or malformed key sets cannot displace a good one. A successful certs response with usable keys replaces the whole cached set, so withdrawn keys stop working. Failed refreshes and responses without usable keys keep the last good set and retain the 30-second backoff. The Gateway warns once when it first uses a set at least one hour after fetching it. At 24 hours the set expires and admission fails closed if a refresh cannot load usable keys.

## Evidence

- Cache regression tests: the unusable-response, weak-key, backoff, one-hour warning, 24-hour cutoff, and key-withdrawal cases failed on the pre-fix head and pass here; the weak-key case fails on the 512-bit minimum and passes with the 2048-bit minimum.
- 77 focused tests across the gateway authentication and Cloudflare Access suites pass at this head. Changed-file lint, typecheck, and guard checks pass; the repo-wide unused-export scan flags exports in files this PR does not touch.
- Live end-to-end proof through a running Gateway built from this head: empty and weak key responses keep the last good set, the endpoint going down serves old keys with the one-hour warning and fails closed past 24 hours, and a real replacement key set retires the old key — [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200376#issuecomment-7056033302).
- The packaged fresh install and three upgrade paths preserved configuration and stored automations and served Gateway HTTP responses on `546633d`. Live Cloudflare Access sign-in and HTTP admission ran on `c020d04`. [Package evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200376#issuecomment-7053960527) · [Live Access test commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c020d044187936fc31ff3cb0dbfd7d7efd272b9f)

[Compare main with the PR head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/9bb091e873e4c6761409d08aed68048db7ec9d1c...0c12ddd7213917c61b22e799e2d1625a7da8e36e)

prs.title: fix(telegram): send attachments from the selected agent
prs.body:
Closes #202794.

## What Problem This Solves

On a Gateway with explicit ownership and two agents, a Telegram send from the CLI can deliver text but fail while preparing an attachment. The durable send loses the agent selected by the caller.

## User Impact

A CLI send can stage attachments using the selected agent's workspace media policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the host-selected agent from the Telegram action context to the existing durable-send session context.

## Evidence

Windows, Node 24.22.3, and an isolated loopback Gateway. Built the CLI with `pnpm build qaRuntime` on base `9bb091e873e4` and again with the three independent patches. The changed Telegram production files in the repaired build match this PR.

Ran the built `openclaw message send` CLI twice against the running Gateway. The Telegram plugin sent Bot API HTTP requests to a loopback fixture with a synthetic token. The text-only run was the control and the attachment was a 68-byte PNG in the selected agent's workspace.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs message send --channel telegram --account default --target 12345 --message fixture --json
node openclaw.mjs message send --channel telegram --account default --target 12345 --message fixture --json --media <workspace>/pixel.png
```

| Build | Text exit and requests | Attachment exit and requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base | `0`, one `sendMessage` | `1`, `AgentSelectionRequiredError`, zero upload requests |
| Fix | `0`, one `sendMessage` | `0`, one multipart `sendPhoto` carrying all 68 bytes with the same SHA-256 as the original file |

The regression invokes the registered action and a loopback HTTP receiver. On the base it failed with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` while staging the file. This PR is a draft pending a Telegram Test Server capture. The local proof establishes the CLI-to-Gateway-to-Bot-API request path.

The final registered action regression passed on the patched source. The two related outbound suites passed 20 cases and the Telegram action contract passed 16 cases.

```sh
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'uploads media using the selected agent'
```

### Hosted Telegram receipt

On 2026-11-21, the built OpenClaw CLI sent one synthetic 160 × 120 PNG through an isolated Gateway with two explicitly owned agents and the selected bot account bound to `ops`. The relay verified that the bot and exact dedicated group matched, checked the uploaded file against the source bytes, and forwarded the multipart request to Telegram's hosted production Bot API.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs message send --channel telegram --account default \
  --target '<test-group-id>' --message 'OPENCLAW_202868_FEB497BE' \
  --json --media '<synthetic-png>'
```

```text
CLI exit: 0
Telegram method: sendPhoto
Telegram HTTP status: 200
Source PNG bytes: 42215
Source SHA-256: d09291df46dd559f166d2ea7aa743ecabe43c62a121f624e6fcc83b1da979a42
Photo sizes in Telegram's message receipt: 2
Telegram Desktop: received photo with caption OPENCLAW_202868_FEB497BE
```

At 10:48 UTC+08, Telegram Desktop displayed the incoming photo and the same caption in the dedicated test group. The previous base-failing result comes from the local Gateway and loopback Bot API run. This section adds a post-fix delivery observation on Telegram's production service. The separate Telegram Test Server run is still pending.

Android chat sending and Wear handling import the chat picker to use shared model identity and availability rules. Keeping those rules in the UI makes non-UI callers depend on presentation code.

No user-visible change. Model selection, unavailable-model messages, and send-blocking decisions retain the existing behavior.

prs.title: fix(cron): scope cron inner work to the owning agent
prs.body:
## Problem

Cron inner work shared a single `cron-nested` command-queue lane across every agent. One agent's cron turn could therefore occupy the lane another agent's heartbeat had to observe, so a slow or wedged run in one agent could stall unrelated agents' cron slots.

## Change

Scope the cron inner lane to the owning agent.

- `src/process/lanes.ts` — add `CRON_NESTED_LANE_PREFIX`, `isCronNestedAgentLane`, and `resolveCronNestedAgentLane`.
- `src/agents/lanes.ts` — `resolveCronAgentLane(lane, agentId?)` resolves `cron-nested:<agentId>` when the owner is known, and keeps the shared `cron-nested` lane when it is not (unscoped work cannot be attributed to an agent).
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/lanes.ts` — `resolveGlobalLane` reads `context.agentId` for cron lanes.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts` — pass `params.agentId` into `resolveCronAgentLane`.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts` — timeout matching accepts both the per-agent lane and the legacy shared lane.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-fallback-candidate.ts` — resolve the per-agent cron lane instead of using `CommandLane.CronNested` directly.
- `src/process/command-queue.state.ts` — per-agent cron lanes inherit the cron lane width.
- `src/process/command-queue.capacity-groups.ts` — capacity groups can claim dynamically named lanes by prefix, so per-agent cron lanes stay inside the shared cron/hook budget while each agent keeps its own lane queue.
- `src/process/command-queue.ts` — group clear removes prefix index entries.
- `src/gateway/server-lanes.ts` — the `cron-hooks` group declares `memberPrefixes: [CRON_NESTED_LANE_PREFIX]`.

## Why prefix membership

Per-agent cron lanes are named at run time, so an exact member list cannot enumerate them. A prefix keeps every agent's lane inside the same shared budget without publishing agent ids up front. Longest-prefix matching wins so a narrower prefix can shadow a broader one, and prefix-scoped lanes are validated against the same group-ineligibility rules as exact members.

## Tests

- `src/agents/lanes.test.ts` — cron inner work scopes to the owning agent; the shared lane is retained when no agent owns the work.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/lanes.test.ts` — `resolveGlobalLane` scopes cron lanes by `agentId`.
- `src/process/command-queue.capacity-groups.test.ts` — prefix-scoped lanes count against the shared budget and block siblings.

All three files pass; `oxlint` reports no problems on the changed files.

## Note on local verification limits

The `src/cron/**` Vitest shard exceeds this host's 1280 MiB memory bound and could not be executed here — the same failure occurs on untouched files, so it is a pre-existing host constraint rather than a regression from this change. `tsc --noEmit` was likewise killed by the same bound (the host has no `tsgo`/`@typescript/native-preview` available).

prs.title: chore(ui): cover selected-agent scope across owner filters
prs.body:
Related: #199621. Regression coverage for the selected-agent contract merged in #201207.

## What Problem This Solves

Changing sidebar owner filters used to change which agents' conversations appeared. #201207 fixed that behavior, but this PR's original real-Gateway diagnostic still expected the old cross-agent results and would fail when integrated with current main.

## User Impact

**Test-only: no shipped behavior or permission changes.** This PR now protects the already-merged rule that the selected agent scopes My sessions and All owners. It does not choose a new membership policy, claim a new product fix, or reproduce the reporter's installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regression uses the existing isolated Gateway/browser fixture to select My sessions → All owners → My sessions while keeping the chat URL and selected agent unchanged. Every sidebar request must retain agentId=main. My sessions shows Main mine; All owners shows Main mine + Main other; the Research mine conversation stays excluded throughout.

The cross-agent session remains seeded and included in the three-key locator, so the test catches leakage rather than ignoring that row. The narrow locator also preserves coexistence with the preceding request-rate test. No new production helper, test server, schema, configuration option, or real provider call is introduced.

The product decision is no longer open: #201207 landed as [5d106ddc20f8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5d106ddc20f8fc5176f4048fb24ee9c2ddd93790). Related #198985 covers a different navigation-triggered transition.

## Evidence

- **Reproduced the review finding through the real browser/Gateway flow:** on refreshed main base `39c3099189516d374bc1a74cd625b9ceaa5494e3`, the original full file produced **1 passed / 1 failed**, with the diagnostic failing at its agent assertion: expected undefined, received main. The sibling request-rate test passed.
- **After the assertion repair (published head `74b8ae4d37b7da3d1611fe153275fbbb48b33b86`): 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 unhandled errors**, together in the complete file with no test-name filter. Command wall time 58.25 s; Vitest 53.89 s; file duration 19.73 s; rate scenario 12.547 s; owner-filter regression 1.635 s. Gateway, contexts, and Chromium cleaned up successfully.
- Rebuilt the current source's QA runtime before testing. Chromium 156.0.8078.4, built Control UI, real disposable Gateway, synthetic owners/sessions, and the existing loopback provider were used. An initial setup attempt could not find the expired temporary Chromium executable and skipped both cases; installing the same browser into task-owned storage resolved setup before the recorded red/green proof. No live service or real provider credentials were used.
- Owning UI E2E typecheck, targeted lint, final formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. Initial formatting found a wrapping issue; the repository formatter corrected it, and the final check passed.
- **Simplification/test audit:** production delta 0; total PR test delta **+90/−0**, one file. The repair removes the obsolete conditional agent expectation and cross-agent personal membership expectation; it adds no machinery. prs.title: test(ios): count only the root roster in the sidebar lifecycle test
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Targets #198084's branch. `RootSidebarLifecycleTests` did not compile (`private` `@Observable` classes used outside their scope), and once compiled, `foregroundAdmissionSurvivesInactivityButEndsInBackground` failed on every run with `Background must cancel the event consumer`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test counted every `sessions.list` with `limit=200` as root sidebar work. The chat view model also reads 200 sessions when a `seqGap` arrives, and it is not paused in the background, so its read landed after the background snapshot. The test also took that snapshot as soon as the first 200-row read appeared, which was often chat's read rather than the roster's repair.

Request logging during the failing test showed that after backgrounding, the root roster sent nothing until the app returned to the foreground. Only chat's read arrived. #198084's production change is correct; the test was miscounting.

The fix counts only the roster's paged reads (they carry `offset`). This also makes the existing wait observe the roster's own repair before the snapshot. `Scene` and `Requests` become `fileprivate` so the file compiles. Test-only; no production change.

## User Impact

None. Lets #198084's lifecycle regression run and pass.

## Evidence

iPhone 18 Pro simulator, #198084 rebased on `main` `0eabe3398c9`, plus this commit:

- `RootSidebarLifecycleTests`: passed 3 of 3 runs. Before this commit: failed 3 of 3.
- Red on base: with `main`'s `RootTabs.swift` the test fails at `Transient inactivity must not restart shared tasks` (each of `sessions.list`, `usage.cost`, `cron.list` and `sessions.subscribe` goes from 1 to 2 after one inactive/active cycle).
- `RootSidebarLifecycleTests RootTabsPresentationTests RootSidebarModelSessionEventsTests RootEventSubscriptionTests`: 73 passed, 0 failed.
- `SidebarRefreshUITests` against `test-ios-shell-gateway.mjs --session-mutations`: passed; with `main`'s `RootTabs.swift`, 5 roster reloads in 5 same-agent switches.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` and `scripts/lint-swift.sh ios`: clean.

This commit sits on #198084's current head `f2947364545`. The test runs above used the rebased branch; this file is identical in both.
