prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): reset owner access on the claw's computer
prs.body:
Related: OCF-319 (Linear)

## What Problem This Solves

An owner whose recovery kit is lost or leaked, or who no longer controls the claw remotely, has no way to take ownership back short of relinking the claw as a new claw.

## User Impact

On the computer that runs the claw, the owner can now **Reset owner access** (Settings → OpenClaw ID, or `openclaw id reset`, which also works with the Gateway stopped). It makes a new recovery kit, shows it once, and removes every owner device, person, node and invite; remote sessions close and tunnel-issued sign-ins are revoked. Local access, the claw id, address, connection keys (K_srv, K_gw) and all claw data stay, and the membership seq keeps counting up. The old kit stops working.

**Not usable end to end yet:** the deployed Discovery still refuses any root change (see Dependencies), so a reset applies locally but its publication is refused until Discovery accepts `RootReset`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Implements the revised OCF-319 design on top of the protocol from #193777 (`RootReset`, `verifyRootReset`, descriptor `reset` evidence); the old remote RootRotation/epoch/freeze design is not brought back.

- **Gateway:** `openclawId.authority` `reset_prepare` / `reset_commit`, `local_operator` only (tunnel and other channels: `not_local_operator`, from the existing connection classification, not headers). The new root R' signs binding_seq + 1 with the same hostname, K_srv and K_gw; the Gateway signs `RootReset` with the current K_gw and publishes both in the descriptor's `reset` (no link code needed, same K_gw). Removal reuses the existing effects: capture/close connections, cancel member runs, revoke tunnel-bound tokens, drop node pairings, push the empty admission list.
- **CLI:** `openclaw id reset` routes through the running Gateway (bound to its state owner via `expectedOwnerId`) or, with the Gateway stopped, edits the claw record under the Gateway lock and signs the RootReset with the bound K_gw (publication then happens at the next start). Interactive only (typed claw name; the kit never reaches argv, JSON or logs). An uncertain outcome still prints the kit and exits 2.
- **Control UI:** new **Settings → OpenClaw ID** page (address, Discovery state, links to Your devices and People, Move to new keys, and a separate Reset owner access section). Reset needs the claw's short name typed, then shows the new kit in the existing recovery-kit presentation; only after "I've saved it" does R' sign and the Gateway commit. The resetting browser becomes the first owner device under the new root (decision 3 of 2026-11-05).
- **Placement (confirmed by Josh, 2026-11-13):** over the tunnel or any non-local connection the page shows the single line "Reset owner access is only available on the computer that runs this claw." instead of the button. This intentionally departs from OCF-319's "the UI doesn't show it"; the Gateway still refuses remotely. Existing account-menu items are unchanged; the menu gains only an **OpenClaw ID settings** link.
- **Ordering guards:** a reset is refused while a move to new keys is unpublished (`rebind_unpublished`), and a move or a second reset is refused while a reset is unpublished (`reset_unpublished`), because Discovery accepts a root change only from the exact binding it stores, and a descriptor can land before its snapshot fails.
- The recovery-kit-used notice now points to Reset owner access instead of relinking. Docs: `docs/cli/id.md`, `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md`.

Out of scope, follow-up: **OCF-334** (human-presence check before reset).

## Dependencies

- **Discovery (blocking end-to-end):** `openclaw/discovery` main (e57e741, 2026-11-13) `checkRepublish` pins the stored root without a K_gw and never calls `checkDescriptorRootReset`; its test "refuses a root change even with valid owner reset evidence" asserts the refusal. Discovery must adopt `checkDescriptorRootReset` (discovery.md "Owner reset") before a reset publishes. Not changed here.
- **claw-loader:** main maps `owner_reset` to the generic "can't verify" state; it does not yet show "The owner reset access to this claw. Set up this browser again." with re-enrollment.

## Evidence

Screenshots (mocked Gateway, synthetic data; the page is new, so there is no "before" state; the URL previously fell through to chat):

Local, on the claw's computer:
![Settings → OpenClaw ID on the claw's computer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd8eee45-846a-4561-9625-9bc50ca203be)

Over the tunnel:
![Settings → OpenClaw ID over the tunnel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0e91bf1-7be6-444f-99bd-c3cbbb0f907d)

Typed confirmation:
![Reset confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e385e8e-90e5-4d76-95d3-2cdb859d7eab)

New kit shown once before the reset:
![New recovery kit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c81e6b0e-433d-470c-a16a-520818bec476)

Checks run locally:
- `src/gateway/openclaw-id/owner-reset.test.ts`: tunnel/no-channel refusal; every removal (owner devices, members, nodes, invites, sessions closed, runs cancelled, tunnel tokens revoked, node pairings removed, empty admission); kept claw id, hostname, K_srv, K_gw, Discovery account; seq + 1; RootReset verifies with `verifyRootReset`, Discovery's `checkDescriptorRootReset` and a pinned browser's `verifyBindingForPin` (`owner_reset`), while a forged RootReset gets `root_mismatch`/refused; browser enrollment under R'; old root, stale binding and other keys refused with no change; reset/re-bind ordering guards.
- `src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-reset.test.ts`: real Gateway over loopback resets and publishes one K_gw-signed descriptor with the reset evidence and no code, then the snapshot; a relayed client is refused before the service; `openclaw id reset` with the Gateway stopped edits local state under the lock and prints the kit once.
- Re-ran `src/gateway/openclaw-id/**`, re-bind e2e and `id-cli` tests: 61 files / 385 tests pass.
- UI: `openclaw-id-page.test.tsx` (button present locally, single line and no button over the tunnel, nothing requested with Labs off), account-menu tests, and `ui/src/e2e/openclaw-id-reset.e2e.test.ts` (bundled build: full reset flow commits only after the kit is saved; tunnel shows no button).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap ratchet, `check:control-ui-controllers`, `ui:i18n:verify`.
- Independent review (separate model) found one P2: a second reset after a partial publication could chain to a binding Discovery no longer stores. Fixed by refusing a new reset until the previous one is confirmed published.

Gaps:
- No staging end-to-end yet (pinned browser re-enrolls with the new kit; forged root change refused): blocked on the Discovery change above and needs explicit approval before using staging.
- `pnpm ui:build` reports boot/CSS budget overruns on this host; the base commit (9156de83fa53) built on the same host reports the same overruns (chat boot 1284.4 KiB vs 1284.0 here, new boot 799.3 vs 799.0), so they are not from this PR.

prs.title: feat(voice-call): add optional Telnyx noise suppression for inbound realtime calls
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `telnyx.noiseSuppression` setting to Voice Call. When it is set, inbound realtime calls run Telnyx per-call noise suppression (`Denoiser`, `DeepFilterNet`, `Krisp`, or `AiCoustics`) on the caller's audio before it reaches the realtime model.

It is off by default. With the setting unset, calls without media streaming and outbound dials send exactly the same Telnyx requests as before.

## What Problem This Solves

Background speech from a TV or another person in the room reaches the realtime model as if the caller had said it. Telnyx can isolate the caller's voice per call, for example with Krisp's telephony voice isolation model.

Voice Call couldn't use that, because it starts streaming inside the `answer` command and Telnyx rejects `suppression_start` while streaming is active (422, code 90045).

## Change

When `telnyx.noiseSuppression` is set and the call streams media, `TelnyxProvider.answerCall` runs these steps in order:

1. `answer` without the stream fields.
2. `suppression_start` with the configured direction, engine and engine config. This step is capped at 5 seconds so the stream token stays valid. If it fails or times out, Voice Call logs a warning and streams without suppression.
3. `streaming_start` with the same stream settings the answer would have carried.

When the setting is unset, the single `answer` still carries the stream fields inline, unchanged from today.

The config is validated in both the manifest schema and `normalizeVoiceCallConfig`; `engineConfig` requires `engine`. The docs in `docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md` cover the direction semantics, the engine fields, and the Telnyx number setting below.

**Prerequisite:** set the number's own noise suppression to `disabled` in Telnyx. A number-level setting engages the default engine at answer, and a later `suppression_start` collides with it; Telnyx returns a 500 for that collision.

## Failure handling

| Step that fails | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `answer` (setting on) | Voice Call sends a best-effort hangup, then reports the answer failure. Telnyx may have answered before its HTTP response was lost; that answer carries no stream, so without the hangup the caller would sit on silence until duration cleanup. |
| `answer` (setting unset) | Unchanged. The answer carries the stream inline, so a lost response still connects media, and no hangup is sent. |
| `suppression_start` | Logs a warning and streams without suppression. The call continues. |
| `streaming_start` | Voice Call hangs up the answered call and reports the failure. |

Both hangups share one helper, and a failed hangup is only logged. This resolves the earlier silent-call window when the answer response is lost: the contributor-side cleanup option from the review is implemented in `2df6212`.

## Evidence

The live runs below are real inbound calls to a Telnyx local number through a source build of this branch, loaded as a bundled plugin. The setup used a Call Control app with number-level suppression `disabled`, a Tailscale funnel, OpenAI realtime, and `inboundPolicy: allowlist`.

Hostnames, call control IDs and the caller are redacted. Timestamps are local (UTC-5).

The current head, `50e97a8c67d`, is `2df6212` rebased onto main `24015bf60cb`, plus test-only commits for the review's P3 findings; the two generated config baseline files were regenerated, and `docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md` was merged with main's new Twilio call recording section. Since `2df6212`'s base, the only main change to the Telnyx provider, the runtime, the webhook or the media stream is one line in `runtime.ts` from #189687 that passes Twilio's `record` setting to the Twilio provider, so the runs below on `2df6212` exercise the same Telnyx answer path as the current head.

### Upgrade from current stable v2026.10.8, on head `2df6212`

All runs used one profile, one state directory and one config file.

**A. Stock `v2026.10.8` (`dc2523e`), config without `noiseSuppression`.** Four inbound calls were answered and streamed. The first three ended with the model calling `openclaw_end_call` (`endReason=hangup-bot`). The gateway was stopped during the fourth call's setup; v2026.10.8 closed that record as `completed` on shutdown.

**B. Checkout of this branch (`2df6212`), same profile, config untouched.** `openclaw doctor --fix` ran the core state migration for the newer build. That migration belongs to v2026.10.8 to main, not to this plugin. After it, the gateway started and three inbound calls behaved exactly as before:

```
22:12:37.815 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:28.983 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=8fea48a4-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:13:34.990 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:55.616 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=05f267e5-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:14:01.298 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:14:37.845 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=0a54b7ad-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**C. `noiseSuppression` added with `config set ... --strict-json`, no other change.** The config was Krisp with `krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef`. The call was a normal conversation with no suppression warning and no answer failure:

```
22:15:40.991 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:15:42.112 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 28ab70e0-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:16:14.703 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=28ab70e0-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**D. Rejected `suppression_start` on the same head.** The model was set to a name Telnyx does not accept, and two calls were placed.

Both calls had `suppression_start` rejected. On the first, Telnyx's own `streaming_start` then failed to reach the media destination, and Voice Call hung the answered call up through the shared helper. The second call streamed without suppression and finished normally.

```
22:24:50.955 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:51.486 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 70f2a343-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "10000", "title": "Invalid request",
    "source": { "pointer": "/noise_suppression_engine_config" },
    "detail": "The 'noise_suppression_engine_config' parameter model must be one of: krisp-viva-tel-v2.kef, krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef, krisp-viva-pro-v1.kef, krisp-viva-ss-v1.kef." } ]
}
22:24:52.886 [voice-call/events] Failed to answer inbound call v3:<redacted>: call answered but Telnyx streaming_start failed; hanging up: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "90046", "title": "Media Streaming failed", "detail": "Failed to connect to destination" } ]
}
22:24:53.750 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=70f2a343-... endReason=completed

22:24:57.684 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:58.077 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 { ...same 10000 error... }
22:24:58.939 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:25:17.777 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=3e06844d-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

Thirty seconds after the hung-up call, the existing realtime stream watchdog logged `Realtime stream WebSocket never connected within 30s` for `70f2a343`. That call was already finalized, and the warning had no effect on it or on the next call. The watchdog belongs to the stream token issued before the answer; this PR does not change it.

### Stored call history after the upgrade

prs.title: fix: reject out-of-range config array indexes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw config set` accepted array indexes beyond the current length and wrote null holes into the saved configuration.

Fixes #196098

## Why This Change Was Made

Array writes reject skipped indexes before modifying the array. The error points to an existing index for updates or the next index for appending; on an empty array it directs users to index 0. An index equal to the current length still appends, including when creating a nested value.

## User Impact

Invalid array paths fail without corrupting existing values, while append-by-index continues to work.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli-path.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 19 tests passed in 2.30s on the source tree committed as `664480c2c7598eb804ca464d48029a88e853c671`.
- The same test file failed on pinned base `999e873a916552e652239e47e9ad26dea4228517`: all 3 new out-of-range cases failed because the base did not throw; the other 16 tests passed.
- Existing live CLI proof at prior repair head `73db5be0b2b3b092baf2fe2f9993c697af3d7d30` demonstrated sparse persistence before the repair, rejection after it, and append-at-length. This update changes only the rejection guidance.
- A fresh CLI replay on the pinned base stopped before mutation because `run-node` could not verify that the affected Gateway was offline; the isolated config remained unchanged. This attempt is not counted as product proof.
- `openclaw-preflight.sh --profile auto` passed at head `664480c2c7598eb804ca464d48029a88e853c671` against pinned base `999e873a916552e652239e47e9ad26dea4228517`; format, lint, core TypeScript, core test typecheck, and focused tests passed (19 tests). Merge compatibility was clean against observed main `d6f628897ad7830e7cd54063c18de41c9c4cc73e`.
- Established contract: an array index equal to the current length still appends.

```text
$ pnpm openclaw config set 'plugins.entries.demo.config.tags.5' z
before: base 0eabe3398c9e0334e8c3b9b03f6a12040c7a1c12 => exit 0; saved tags=["a","b",null,null,null,"z"]
tested head SHA: 73db5be0b2b3b092baf2fe2f9993c697af3d7d30 => exit 1; Array index 5 is out of range for an array of length 2; saved tags=["a","b"]

negative-control: `pnpm openclaw config set 'plugins.entries.demo.config.tags.2' z` => exit 0; saved tags=["a","b","z"]
```

<details>
<summary>proof-live.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

expect_out_of_range="${EXPECT_OUT_OF_RANGE:-reject}"
pnpm_home="${PNPM_HOME:-}"
if [ -z "$pnpm_home" ]; then
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin*) pnpm_home="$HOME/Library/pnpm" ;;
    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) pnpm_home="${LOCALAPPDATA:-$HOME/AppData/Local}/pnpm" ;;
    *) pnpm_home="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/pnpm" ;;
  esac
fi
scratch="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$scratch/home" "$scratch/state" "$scratch/xdg"
export PNPM_HOME="$pnpm_home"
export HOME="$scratch/home"
export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$scratch/xdg"
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$scratch/state"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$scratch/state/openclaw.json"

reset_config() {
  printf '%s\n' '{"plugins":{"entries":{"demo":{"config":{"tags":["a","b"]}}}}}' > "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"
}

saved_tags() {
  node - <<'NODE'
const fs = require("node:fs");
const config = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, "utf8"));
console.log(JSON.stringify(config.plugins.entries.demo.config.tags));
NODE
}

case "$expect_out_of_range" in
  reject) expected_status=1; expected_tags='["a","b"]' ;;
  allow) expected_status=0; expected_tags='["a","b",null,null,null,"z"]' ;;
  *) printf 'EXPECT_OUT_OF_RANGE must be reject or allow\n' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

reset_config
if pnpm openclaw config set 'plugins.entries.demo.config.tags.5' z > "$scratch/out-of-range.log" 2>&1; then
  out_of_range_status=0
else
  out_of_range_status=$?
fi
printf 'out-of-range exit=%s\n' "$out_of_range_status"
if grep -Fq 'Array index 5 is out of range for an array of length 2' "$scratch/out-of-range.log"; then
  grep -F 'Array index 5 is out of range for an array of length 2' "$scratch/out-of-range.log"
else
  sed "s|$scratch|<temp>|g" "$scratch/out-of-range.log" | tail -n 20
fi
actual_tags="$(saved_tags)"
printf 'saved tags=%s\n' "$actual_tags"
if [ "$out_of_range_status" -ne "$expected_status" ] || [ "$actual_tags" != "$expected_tags" ]; then
  exit 1
fi

reset_config
pnpm openclaw config set 'plugins.entries.demo.config.tags.2' z > "$scratch/append.log" 2>&1
printf 'append exit=0\n'
grep -F 'Updated plugins.entries.demo.config.tags[2].' "$scratch/append.log"
actual_tags="$(saved_tags)"
printf 'saved tags=%s\n' "$actual_tags"
[ "$actual_tags" = '["a","b","z"]' ]
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(apple): remove two unused chat UI declarations that fail the dead-code scan
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The "macOS Periphery Dead Code" workflow fails on every pull request whose scope triggers the shared OpenClawKit scan, including pull requests that change no Swift file. Its "Intersect shared OpenClawKit dead code" job reports two declarations that are unused on `main`, so the failure is inherited rather than caused by the pull request under test. The workflow is not a required check, but the default auto-merge landing route refuses a pull request with a failing check, so routine landings stall.

## User Impact

User impact: none. The two declarations have no callers, so no app behavior changes. Maintainers and contributors get a passing shared dead-code check again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both declarations lost their last use in c9285dde971 (#200592), which rebuilt the chat transcript:

- `ChatObscuredPresentation` was replaced by the `ChatPresentationActivity` modifier in `ChatView.swift`. That modifier reads `openClawChatIsObscured` itself and applies the same stream pacing and composer presentation, plus scene activity. The `openClawChatIsObscured` environment entry stays; the iOS root tabs still set it.
- `OpenClawSessionColorDot` was drawn only by the old sidebar row. The stripe and the color menu remain in use.

The dot held the only use of the "Session color" string, so the native string inventory drops that one entry. The locale refresh regenerates the string catalogs after merge.

Nothing else is touched: the job reports exactly these two declarations.

## Evidence

- Failing run on an unrelated pull request (#202397, no Swift changes): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44767862374, attempt 1. The "Intersect shared OpenClawKit dead code" job ends with `struct OpenClawSessionColorDot` and `struct ChatObscuredPresentation`.
- Neither name is referenced anywhere in the repository after this change, tests included.
- SwiftLint reports no violations in the two edited files, and the native string inventory check reports no drift after regenerating it.
- This pull request changes `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/`, which is in the scan scope, so its own Periphery run and the Apple build and test jobs in CI are the proof that the scan passes and nothing depended on the removed code. I did not build the Swift package locally.

prs.title: fix: keep Code Mode usable after read-only workers retire
prs.body:
Related: #198187

## What Problem This Solves

Fresh Code Mode workers can exhaust their default 64 MiB heap before executing even a no-tool script after enough read-only database workers retire. Departed workers leave database references behind, keeping closed databases' metadata in every new worker's startup data.

## User Impact

Code Mode and automation trigger scripts can keep starting after those workers retire, without increasing the heap allowance, changing configuration, or restarting the Gateway. This repairs a reproduced path to #198187; the reporter's specific 28–37-hour traffic pattern has not been captured, so other sources of startup-data growth are not ruled out.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read-only task workers now use the existing native-exit admission cleanup. That owner settles interrupted work, removes departed references, and releases closed-database metadata while preserving live siblings. Production remains net -1 line with +39 regression lines. Permissions, read-only admission, model eligibility, native harnesses, executor isolation, and heap allowance are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Causal startup OOM:** the original baseline retained all 800 closed database admissions and a fresh Code Mode worker failed before bridge dispatch under the default 64 MiB heap. The same workload with the repair retained zero closed admissions and completed at approximately 14.8 MiB. Retained-native-handle and explicitly-closed-handle regressions fail before and pass after the repair, while the host connection and live siblings remain usable.
- **Prior sustained acceptance:** the real isolated Gateway completed 888 tool-bearing turns, 2,341 automation-gate evaluations, and indexing of 444 transcripts over 60 minutes without workload, gate, or provider-fixture errors. At the same work count, positive database references were 131 on the base versus 16 fixed; quarantine zero-reference cells were 133 versus 17. This complements the causal replay rather than claiming to reproduce every uptime failure.
- **The old UI CI failure is now causally attributed:** the unchanged 1 px reader-position regression moves 22 px on both exact CI main base `db9df01b…` and tested merge `ae10e92d…`. Their three reader-production blobs are identical to the parent of the canonical repair, [#200482](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200482), commit `e44a7e36817e…`. Applying only those three canonical production files to the old merge makes that regression and all six unchanged snapshot-fidelity E2Es pass. The controlled test holds a Solid refresh and delivers an actual DOM-measured predecessor through `resizeItem`; it does not reconstruct the historical natural ResizeObserver interleaving. [Old CI run 44432331724](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44432331724) remains red, not relabeled green.
- **Named-gate main integration prepared:** local head `f74a14fa70e5d4ffc11046643bcfe9c26cf4c7fb` integrates main `ce30edaf…`, including the canonical reader repair. No duplicate UI fix was added. The one worker-start conflict retains main's diagnostic arguments and unconditional admission cleanup. Against that main pin, this PR still changes only the two original files (+41/-3).
- **Fresh resolved-tree proof:** 71 worker/lifecycle tests across five files pass; all six unmodified cached-transcript fidelity E2Es pass; real read-only worker retirement leaves zero of three closed admissions retained, and a fresh Code Mode worker completes at approximately 13 MiB under the unchanged limit. Production and affected-test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and branch-delta whitespace checks pass. The older 800-database and one-hour results remain prior-head evidence; the unchanged algorithm/regression plus these affected checks cover the mechanical integration without a redundant soak.
- **Review and CI scope:** independent P0–P2 autoreview of the original complete repair was scoped-clean with surrounding lifecycle context. Its published `f7d99c17…` tree matched that reviewed candidate. The refreshed integration preserves that repair; no additional production design was introduced. Exact-new-head CI is still required after publication. No CI rerun-for-green, weakened assertion, budget exception, or permission bypass was used.

The Gateway workload uses isolated synthetic state and a loopback model-response fixture, not paid/live inference. No production Gateway was changed or restarted.

## Contributor credit

Thanks to @alexph-dev for the issue report and Vincent Koc (@vincentkoc) for requesting and directing this repair.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/43ff77dc-01d9-443c-87ee-fa92f18788da)
- [Causal CI baseline verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/acf76096-53d6-4524-8304-eebd49993068)

- @vincentkoc

prs.title: docs: document isolated PostgreSQL restore drills
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

The PostgreSQL restore guide now shows how to rehearse a full archive restore while the source Gateway keeps running. Use separate CLI state and config paths, a fresh filesystem target, and a dedicated staging database. The backup CLI reference links to the procedure.

## Root Cause

Archive restore takes offline ownership of the state directory selected by the CLI. `--postgres-connection-env` changes the PostgreSQL import connection, so running with the source profile still encounters the running Gateway's ownership lock. On the base commit, the CLI returned “requires exclusive offline state ownership” even with a separate restore target and staging database.

## Real behavior proof

On disposable PostgreSQL 18, `openclaw backup create --no-include-workspace --verify` produced the archive. A second process held the source Gateway ownership lock throughout both attempts. The restore from the source profile exited 1, cleaned its incomplete target, and preserved the archive.

I ran the new guide's shell example against the same archive. The backup parser and command handlers ran from source. The output included:

```text
PostgreSQL stores imported through: $STAGING_PG_DSN
```

The restore exited 0. Readback found the restored file and row, the new anchor's namespace only in the staging database, and the archived connection reference in the restored config. The source process still held its lock.

## What was not tested

Gateway boot, restored installation activation, and paid model calls were outside the drill. The fixture held the real Gateway ownership lock without starting the full Gateway. The backup outcome ledger emitted a best-effort warning in the fixture.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `oxfmt --check docs/cli/backup.md docs/gateway/postgresql.md` passed.
- The repository-wide anchor audit reported seven errors on untouched pages. Neither changed page nor either new link appeared in the diagnostics.

## Evidence

The simplification pass retained one restore drill procedure and linked it from the CLI reference. The local autoreview helper prepared the complete docs diff at P0–P3 but its isolated Codex launcher could not start. Hosted ClawSweeper review is the fallback.

prs.title: fix(cli): reject a blank working directory when editing an exit-triggered automation
prs.body:
Related: #129714

## What Problem This Solves

An edit that supplies an empty or whitespace-only `--on-exit-cwd` can succeed and replace the saved schedule without the requested working directory. The watched command would then use the default directory.

## User Impact

An invalid directory value stops the edit before any automation settings change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate `--on-exit-cwd` at the edit command boundary, using the same nonblank check as automation creation.

## Evidence

Windows, Node 24.22.3, and an isolated loopback Gateway. Built the CLI with `pnpm build qaRuntime` on base `9bb091e873e4` and again with the three independent patches, including this PR's initial commit `bd32067ccefe`. The follow-up reuses the existing `parseCronStringOption` validator for the same guard. The registered Commander regression passed again after that follow-up.

Created a disabled `every` automation. Ran this edit and read the saved record through `cron.get` in the same Gateway.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs automations edit <id> --on-exit 'node --version' --on-exit-cwd ' ' --json
```

| Case | Edit exit | Saved schedule |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Base | 0 | Changed from `every` to `on-exit` with no `cwd` |
| Fix | 1 | Original `every` schedule retained |
| Fix, valid directory control | 0 | `on-exit` with the supplied directory |

The fixed CLI returned `--on-exit-cwd must not be blank`. The job stayed disabled during the proof.

The new Commander regression failed on the base because the edit resolved successfully. It also checks that the rejected command makes no Gateway RPC.

All 78 cases in the focused CLI suites passed on the repaired source. The compiled runtime and touched-file formatting also passed.

```sh
pnpm test src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/schedule-options.positional.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/schedule-options.onexit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Closes #200749

## What Problem This Solves

When you sign in to a provider with `openclaw models auth login` while the Gateway is running (for example xAI or OpenAI device-code sign-in), the multi-line instructions are shown as one run-on paragraph with literal `\n` sequences in it. The code, its expiry, and the warning not to enter a code someone else gave you are no longer on their own lines, so the warning is easy to miss.

## User Impact

Gateway-backed sign-in shows the instructions the way the Gateway wrote them: the message, the code, the expiry, and the device-code warning each on a line of their own. Login itself is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway builds these steps as several lines. The CLI passed the whole message through `sanitizeTerminalText`, which is a single-line sanitizer and turns every newline into the two characters `\` and `n`. It now sanitizes each line and joins them again, the same way `sessions-import.ts` and `transcripts/read.ts` already do, so terminal control characters are still removed from every line.

## Evidence

Scenario: `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code` against a running Gateway.

Run from source with `pnpm openclaw`, against an isolated Gateway (own state directory and config, loopback port) started from the same commit, using OpenAI's real device-code endpoint. The sign-in was never approved. The one-time codes below are replaced with `XXXX-XXXX`; nothing else is edited. Before is the base commit `81a962707` (Gateway and CLI), after is this PR's head `79e8a8df7` (Gateway and CLI).

Before:

```text
◇  OpenAI Codex device code ──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                         │
│  Enter this one-time code on the sign-in page.\nCode: XXXX-XXXX\nCode  │
│  expires in 15 minutes.\nContinue only if you started this sign-in      │
│  yourself. If a website or another person gave you this code, cancel.   │
│                                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

After:

```text
◇  OpenAI Codex device code ────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                       │
│  Enter this one-time code on the sign-in page.                        │
│  Code: XXXX-XXXX                                                      │
│  Code expires in 15 minutes.                                          │
│  Continue only if you started this sign-in yourself. If a website or  │
│  another person gave you this code, cancel.                           │
│                                                                       │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

The later "Waiting for device authorization…" note had the same problem before (`cancel.\n\nWaiting for device authorization…`) and renders on its own lines after.

- New test `renders a gateway device-code step on separate lines and still strips terminal controls` in `auth-login-gateway.test.ts` drives a real `WizardSession` device-code step through `runGatewayLoginWizard`. On the base commit it fails because the note text contains literal `\n`; with this change it passes. It also checks that an escape sequence in the message is still removed.
- The whole `src/commands/models` suite passes (35 files, 324 tests). `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the two changed files, and `pnpm tsgo:core`, pass.
- Not covered: completing a sign-in with a provider account.

prs.title: fix(ui): inline widgets flash an empty box before loading on warm chat reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: inline widget cards in a cached chat show an untitled empty box, then "Loading…", then another empty frame before the widget appears, on every warm reload.

## User Impact

User impact: a reloaded chat shows each inline HTML widget's title in its reserved card from the first frame, and the card fills in place with the live widget, with no empty or "Loading…" state and no layout movement.

Risks and required actions, kept visible:

- **CSS budget (approved by Peter, recorded).** The overlay and the canvas-card outline add 137 B of raw CSS to the chat route stylesheet; startup CSS is unchanged (+0 B) and total CSS gzip grows 14 B, within build variance. Main already exceeds `totalCssRawBytes` (1,783,379 B measured on 6b0df8b9 against a 1,740,234 B ceiling), and the gate allows only 64 B of growth over an over-cap base, so the entry resets the ceiling to this PR's measured 1,783,516 B plus 64 B, absorbing main's inherited raw debt as earlier approvals did. The original parked layout cost 335 B; the overlay is the smallest CSS form of an opaque titled cover I found.
- **Security boundary.** `src/agents/sandbox-host.ts` (sandbox proxy shell) is in the `execution` category of `.github/security-review-policy.yml`; no `CODEOWNERS` entry covers it, so it needs an independent maintainer review. The host-facing message, params and validation are unchanged; only the timing moves (details below).
- **Other `onRendered` consumers** now run 3 frames after load instead of at load: board widgets show content and post host state for legacy saved widgets on the presentation signal (which also removes the same empty-frame flash there), and offscreen board widgets acknowledge after the 1 s fallback. HTML previews in strict mode are script-free and keep load timing.

- **Recovery status kept.** Rebasing onto main (6b0df8b9, including #202220) showed that deleting the owner's generic pending notice had also dropped "Disconnected. This view reconnects automatically." for scheduled read retries, an offline Gateway and sandbox proxy restarts. A narrow `reconnecting` flag now carries exactly those states and the titled overlay shows the status, so nothing in flow moves. Still removed on purpose: the 10 s slow-read notice (it said "Disconnected" while connected) and the in-flow notice above an already-rendered iframe (it shifted rows on every revalidation).

Accepted edge cases (not coded): a rendered widget whose Gateway drops shows no per-card status (the app's connection status covers it, and the card is inert until the next validated read); a widget whose main thread stays busy for more than 1 s after `load` falls back before it paints (the previous behavior); a tab hidden during load acknowledges by fallback and may show one empty frame when it becomes visible again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The acknowledgement now means "the document's post-load frames are with the compositor", carried by the existing message:

- The trusted proxy shell prepends one more guard script to scripted widget documents. After the document's `load` (capture, once), it waits three `requestAnimationFrame` callbacks and posts a params-free `sandbox-resource-loaded` to the proxy. A third frame can only begin after the first post-load frame finished raster and activation; two frames only prove a commit.
- The proxy acknowledges the host with the unchanged message and `renderId` only after it observed the inner `load` itself and the witness arrived from the current inner window. Script-free documents keep load timing. Hidden or offscreen frames run no animation frames, so they acknowledge 1 s after load.
- Host validation (`source`, `origin`, `renderId` in `ui/src/lib/widget-sandbox-host.ts`) is unchanged, no message type was added, and inner `ui/notifications/sandbox-*` messages are still never relayed to the host.

On that signal, the Control UI reapplies the parked L315 change in a smaller form: scripted canvas documents show their title in the lazy, admission-held and canvas reservations as one opaque overlay (`.chat-tool-card__reservation`, absolutely positioned over the already-positioned `.chat-tool-card__preview`). The space is held by whatever is in flow beside it (the lazy box, a spacer, or the mounted iframe, which stays paintable and is never hidden), and the overlay retires synchronously on the validated acknowledgement. The generic pending/"Loading…" notice machinery in the canvas owner and the parked two-frame host delay are deleted; only the automatic-recovery status remains, inside the overlay. Only frames that hold a title until the acknowledgement show one (`widgetReservationTitle`); MCP Apps, strict documents, plain frames and script-free canvas documents keep untitled placeholders so they never regress from titled to untitled.

<details><summary>Sandbox boundary analysis</summary>

`src/agents/sandbox-host.ts` matches the `execution` category of `.github/security-review-policy.yml`; no `CODEOWNERS` entry covers it or the UI files.

- The host-facing message, its params and its validation are unchanged; the change is timing only.
- Widget code shares the witness's realm and can post the same witness, but the proxy never acknowledges before the `load` event it observes, so a forged witness can at most restore the previous load-time acknowledgement for its own card. Withholding it only delays the widget's own placeholder by the 1 s fallback; the existing 30 s render timeout is unaffected.
- The witness captures `postMessage`, `requestAnimationFrame` and its `load` listener before stored scripts run (the same pattern as the existing shortcut and scroll bridges), and a superseded render can never acknowledge.

</details>

## Evidence

**Rebased head (5a1ded31 on main 6b0df8b9), Team archived fixture, compositor captures.** Same bench command as below, without the three sidebar flags: on current main, `--sidebar-view online` lands on the People → Activity page during setup, so the chat (and the widget) never shows; that is a bench/fixture follow-up unrelated to this PR. Every delivered frame of the "Team metric 12" card was classified by a pixel classifier over the bench's `frames.json` and the DOM geometry probe, and the transition crops were inspected by hand.

| Reload | First card frame | Empty-outline frames | Card box / scroll while visible | Handoff | Bench anchor (movement / excess / missing) |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| r1 priming | titled (548 ms) | 0 | one signature (525,689 668×220, scroll 17099) | titled → live at 1,331 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| r2 priming | titled (546 ms) | 0 | same single signature | titled → live at 1,346 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| r3 priming | titled (763 ms), after 7 frames of an unpainted transcript column | 0 | same single signature | titled → live at 1,496 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| r4 priming | titled (560 ms) | 0 | same single signature | titled → live at 1,360 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| r4 measured | titled (562 ms) | 0 | same single signature | titled at 1,262 ms → live on the next frame (1,278 ms) | 0 / 0 / 0 |

Six other capture processes stopped on the bench's own setup refusals on this loaded host (load average 20–80): five `Invalid or backward compositor timestamp; no paint verdict` and one paint-holding calibration miss. On current main the Team active fixture requires `--transcript-witness`, which appends fresh live turns and opens at the transcript end, so the "Team metric 12" card is never in the viewport (the geometry probe sees no widget host in any sample; bench anchor excess 0, missing 0; the 209 px movement is the expected end-follow). The active-fixture card evidence below is therefore from the pre-rebase head only.

The mechanism probe and the remaining Team fixture captures below ran on the pre-rebase head (base d2bfdb0d).

"Team metric 12" card on a Team archived warm reload, delivered compositor frames top to bottom (synthetic fixture data):

| Main: untitled box (1,380 ms) → "Loading…" (1,397 ms) → empty box (1,797 ms) → live (1,947 ms) | This PR: unpainted transcript (847 ms) → titled card (863 ms) → still titled (2,147 ms) → live on the next frame (2,163 ms) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Main warm reload card frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc5b2491-40bd-44f5-97e1-baf71c34a06b) | ![This PR warm reload card frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7371477a-f79b-485f-abbd-747d397c8e93) |

The live canvas card also gains a 1px `--border` outline, so its frame matches the reservation.

**Mechanism probe (compositor).** A standalone harness served the real proxy shell from an isolated sandbox origin and a host page with an opaque titled cover over the iframe, retired on `sandbox-resource-loaded`. Chromium 156 headless with paint holding, CDP screencast of every delivered frame; a trial fails if any frame between the cover and live content shows the empty card. Stress = busy host main thread plus a raster-heavy SVG widget.

| Acknowledgement timing | Trials with an empty card frame |
| --- | ---: |
| Inner `load` (main) | 23 / 80 |
| `load` + 2 host frames (parked L315) | 10 / 80 |
| Proxy-side rAF pair after `load` | 2 / 140 |
| Paint Timing `first-paint` inside the widget | 8 / 80 (an occluded surface gets no presentation feedback, so it falls back) |
| Inner rAF pair after `load` | 15 / 290 (12 / 150 under stress) |
| **Inner third rAF after `load` (this PR)** | **0 / 290** |
| This PR's shell, unmodified, stressed | 0 / 100 |

Offscreen frames run no animation frames; the real shell acknowledged them through the fallback at ~1,027 ms.

**Team fixtures (`scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts --warm-reload --visual-proofs --paint-holding`, 1720×1180, production bundle, `--fixture-now-ms 1781000000000`).** Every delivered frame of the "Team metric 12" card was classified (absent / empty outline / titled / live) and transition crops were inspected by hand.

| Build | Reloads | First card frame | Empty-outline frames | Movement while visible |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| This PR, archived | 6 | titled (6/6) | 0 | 0 px (one row/box/scroll signature; bench anchor probe 0 px, excess 0, missing 0) |
| This PR, active | 3 | titled (3/3) | 0 | 0 px (one signature; cached→live anchor shift 0 px) |
| Earlier absolute-iframe layout, same acknowledgement | 15 | titled (15/15) | 0 | 0 px |
| Main, archived + active | 3 | untitled box, then "Loading…" | live content arrives after ~10 frames of an empty box | — |

In 6 of 16 candidate reloads the transcript settled its scroll position by 1 px before its first painted frame (off-screen rows; the card's row height never changed). It was not seen in the 3 main reloads, and no painted frame shows it.

These captures ran on a loaded Mac (load average 13–57 from other lanes), so they are visual verdicts only, with no timing claims. 14 of 18 capture processes stopped early with the bench's own setup refusal (`Invalid or backward compositor timestamp; no paint verdict`, 13 processes; one warm-up timeout), on main and on this branch alike, and a 19th was stopped deliberately once enough reloads had completed; completed reloads before each refusal are kept.

**Tests (rebased head, `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`).**

| Files | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/mcp-app-sandbox-http.test.ts` | 6/6 (red on main's shell: 2 failures; red on a two-frame witness) |
| `ui/src/components/canvas-widget-view-layout.test.ts`, `canvas-widget-view.test.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/components/widget-card.test.tsx`, `chat-message-deferred.test.tsx` | 73/73; main's #202220 sandbox-startup recovery test was red on the bare rebase and is green with the restored status |
| `ui/src/lib/board/widget-sandbox-host.test.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-html-preview-element.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/board/board-widget-frame.test.ts` (other `onRendered` consumers) | 92/92 |

`ui/src/e2e/dashboard-fullscreen.e2e.test.ts` (new on main since the original base): CI caught the touch variant's `expectWidgetReady` taking an instant snapshot of every board skeleton right after the first widget became ready, while an offscreen neighbor was still inside its 1 s presentation fallback. The helper now polls for zero skeletons (3 s); a widget stuck loading still fails. 11/11 locally.

Also on the rebased head: `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped oxlint (exit 0; two pre-existing Solid reactivity warnings on main's lines), `oxfmt --check`, stylelint, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (+184 of 400), and `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` against 6b0df8b9 (passes: total CSS raw 1,783,379 → 1,783,516 B under the recorded 1,783,580 B ceiling; startup CSS +0 B; total gzip +14 B). Local review: three Codex autoreview passes at P2 before the rebase, and one P2 pass over the whole rebased candidate, whose only finding (the dropped recovery status) is the fix in this push.

Production delta: +52 lines net (+37 sandbox, +15 UI).

prs.title: fix(update): reclaim abandoned updater runtimes on a busy host
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Each update keeps a copy of its running code in an `openclaw-update-runtime-XXXXXX` directory and leaves removal to the next update or `openclaw doctor --fix`. On a host that always has other OpenClaw processes running, that removal never happened. One host accumulated 12 runtimes (46.5 GiB), each refused for one of two reasons:

- `no recognized runtime marker`: a runtime was recognized only by projecting the inspecting installation's own package root into it, so a runtime created from any other install root (another checkout, an upgrade proof) was never recognized.
- `other OpenClaw processes are still running (PIDs: ...)`: without knowing who created a runtime, the process census treated every OpenClaw process it could not rule out as possibly the creating updater. On that host today the census blocks on about 30 processes that use no runtime: Gateway children (tailscale route owner, tunnel child, service child anchors), test workers started with a preload, and a containerized installation whose scripts do not resolve on the host.

## User Impact

User impact: updater runtimes left by earlier updates are now removed by the next update or `openclaw doctor --fix` even while a Gateway, agents, test runs, or containerized installations are running, and whichever installation runs the cleanup. A runtime is kept while the update that created it is still running, or while any process's executable, arguments, working directory, or preload points into it. Runtimes created by updaters older than this change carry no record and keep the previous checks, so those already on disk may still need manual removal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the update command creates a runtime, and it loads code from it until it exits. The updater now writes `owner.json` (PID, process start time, Linux PID namespace) into the runtime when it creates it. Cleanup uses that record instead of guessing:

- The record marks the directory as an updater runtime for any installation.
- Creator alive (same PID and start time): kept, with `the creating update (PID n) is still running`.
- Creator exited: the census runs with `creatorExited`, where a process holds the runtime only through a path into it. Pathless OpenClaw processes and commands that cannot be classified but name no runtime no longer hold it. Resolved preload aliases and unresolved runtime references still do.
- A bare preload (`--require preload`, `--import @scope/preload`) is resolved the way Node resolves it for that process: the nearest `node_modules` above its working directory, followed through links. It holds the runtime it resolves into. With the creator exited, one that resolves elsewhere, or cannot be loaded from that working directory at all, holds nothing. A process whose working directory cannot be read stays unknown and blocks.
- A record from another PID namespace, or a creator whose identity cannot be read, falls back to the previous conservative census.

Accepted edges, named in code: a reboot that reuses both the creator's PID and its start time keeps that runtime until the impostor exits; `NODE_PATH` is not read when resolving a bare preload.

No config options, schema, or state changes. The record is a file inside a directory the updater already owns.

## Review notes

- **Unresolved bare preloads (fixed in `6e6c72511eee`).** The finding was real. With the creator exited, `node --require preload service.js` whose `node_modules/preload` links into a retained runtime was released, and cleanup would have deleted code that process loads. A working directory inside the runtime already held it; the gap was a link from an unrelated application. Holding every unresolved preload again, as #191284 did, would block busy development hosts once more (test workers started with a bare preload were among the blockers on the affected host), so the census now resolves the specifier instead.
- **`owner.json` and "State and caches: SQLite, not new JSON/JSONL/sidecar stores".** The record stays a file, deliberately. It is a marker inside a disposable directory that describes that directory, like the files already there: the updater writes `retained-files.json` and `update-native-gate.mjs` beside it, cleanup already recognizes a runtime by reading the projected `package.json`, and update captures carry `.openclaw-private-update-capture` the same way. It must be readable by a Doctor from any installation and any state directory, including when no state database of the creating installation is reachable, and it must disappear with the directory. A state-database row would belong to one state directory, would outlive or be orphaned from the directory it describes, and would defeat the cross-installation recognition this PR exists to provide (last row of the table below). The repository's own `database-first legacy-store guard` passes on this branch.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on the affected host with the real census: `inspectOtherOpenClawProcesses(<runtime>)` returned 31 to 35 blocking PIDs for a runtime nothing uses; with `creatorExited` it returns none.
- Real-process run on that host (isolated `TMPDIR`, real census, no mocks): an abandoned runtime and one whose creator PID was reused are removed; a runtime with a live creator is kept and names its PID; a runtime a live process executes from is kept and removed after that process exits; recordless and foreign-namespace runtimes keep the old refusal.
- `src/infra/temp-artifact-cleanup.test.ts` (new): the same cases against a live child process as creator, inspected from another installation's package root. `src/infra/openclaw-process-census.test.ts`: with the creator exited, another update, Doctor, Gateway children, a containerized script and a preload outside the runtime release it; a script in it, a preload alias into it, a working directory in it and an unresolved reference to it still hold it. `src/infra/update-retained-runtime.test.ts`: the updater writes the record.
- Bare preloads, `src/infra/openclaw-process-census.test.ts` (new case): with the creator exited, a bare preload found through an ancestor `node_modules` link into the runtime holds that runtime and no other; a scoped preload installed elsewhere and one installed nowhere release it; an unreadable working directory stays unknown and blocks; without a known creator all four still block. Red on `d32cd1d21a44`: the linked process was missing from the holders.
- Bare preloads, real processes and the real census on the development host (read-only, in a scratch directory no installation scans): `node --require preload` started from `linked-app/packages/service`, where `linked-app/node_modules/preload` links into the runtime, and the same command in an application with its own `preload`. On `d32cd1d21a44` the census returned `{"pids":[]}`; on `6e6c72511eee` it returns only the linked process, and none of the host's other OpenClaw processes.
- Red on base: with the source change reverted, the new maintenance test fails on the missing `owner.json` and the new census test fails with every pathless process still holding the runtime.
- Passing: the three files above (109 passed, 1 skipped for a case-insensitive volume, before the preload case; the census file alone is 73 passed on `6e6c72511eee`), `src/flows/doctor-retained-runtime.test.ts`, `src/flows/doctor-retained-runtime.settlement.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-cancellation.test.ts`; `pnpm check:changed` on `6e6c72511eee` except the dead-export scan.
- Inherited failure: the dead-export scan reports `extensions/knowledge/src/scribe-schedule-dialog.ts: CronSchedule`, a file this PR does not touch.

### Real update and Doctor runs, base against head

One scenario, run through the real CLI on the base commit `44ec89e71877` and on `d32cd1d21a44`, the head before the bare-preload commit, each in its own Linux container (Crabbox `local-container` on a Mac Studio, `node:26.12.1-trixie` `sha256:97fa0f1b5903…`, leases `cbx_71a15582a673` and `cbx_f0e93d01f040`). Both runs exited 0 with 30 of 30 checks passing against the expectation for that commit. They were not repeated on `6e6c72511eee`, which changes only how the census classifies a bare preload; no process in the scenario uses one.

- Installation: a Git checkout built in place (`pnpm install`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm ui:build`), tracking a local bare repository as its upstream, plus a copy of that build at a second install root.
- Updates: three real `openclaw update --channel dev --yes --no-restart` runs, each after the upstream advanced one commit. Each took the in-place runner, finished `status=ok` with 56 steps (retention, preflight build, activation, Doctor), and retained a 4.0 GiB runtime of about 185,000 entries.
- Busy host, alive from before the first update to the end: the second installation's Gateway with its directory-watch and spawn-broker workers, `openclaw logs --follow`, and `openclaw mcp serve` started from the installation being updated. None of them points into a runtime.

| Step | Base `44ec89e71877` | Head `d32cd1d21a44` |
|------|------|------|
| Update 1 exits and leaves runtime 1 beside the installation | no `owner.json` | `owner.json` is `{"name":"openclaw","pid":11129,"startTime":10050682,"pidNamespace":"pid:[4026532820]"}`; PID 11129 has exited |
| A Gateway runs from runtime 1's own code (working directory inside it, then by absolute path from outside); `doctor --fix` | kept: `other OpenClaw processes are still running (PIDs: 136148, 136342, 136820, 137709, 5866, 5870, 5883, 5890)`, the last four being the unrelated CLIs | kept: `(PIDs: 135243, 135437, 135917, 136810)`, exactly that Gateway and its three workers, each with a working directory or argument inside runtime 1 |
| That Gateway stops; update 2 starts (the next update) | runtime 1 kept: `other OpenClaw processes are still running (PIDs: 5866, 5870, 5883, 5890)` | runtime 1 removed before update 2 retained its own |
| `doctor --fix` from the second installation while update 2 is still running | runtime 2: `no recognized runtime marker; inspect it before manual cleanup` | runtime 2 kept: `the creating update (PID 157721) is still running` |
| Update 2 has exited; `doctor --fix` on the updated installation | both runtimes refused: `other OpenClaw processes are still running (PIDs: 5866, 5870, 5883, 5890)` | `Removed abandoned updater runtime: /var/tmp/ocproof/tmp/openclaw-update-runtime-WyiPhy` |
| Update 3, then `doctor --fix` from the second installation (a different install root) | runtimes 2 and 3: `no recognized runtime marker`; three runtimes, 12 GiB, left on disk | `Removed abandoned updater runtime: /var/tmp/ocproof/tmp/openclaw-update-runtime-HxO1nm`; no runtime left |

The four PIDs that block every cleanup on the base are `node …/openclaw.mjs logs --follow`, `node …/openclaw.mjs mcp serve` and the `openclaw` child of each. On both commits the Gateway and both CLIs were still alive after every step.

While an update runs, its own child processes execute from the runtime with the runtime path in their arguments (`spawn-broker/worker.js`, `directory-watch-host.worker.js`, `sqlite-readonly-location.worker.js`, `update-candidate-state.worker.js`). That is the shape the head census held in the second row.

What the container changed, and what stood in for what:

- OpenClaw refuses the process census inside a container (`Host process visibility cannot be established from this container`), on the base and on this head, so nothing is reclaimed there. An earlier run on `d32cd1d21a44` showed that refusal for every runtime. The scenario moved `/.dockerenv` aside so the container stood in for a host; all its processes share one PID namespace. Inside a real container runtimes are still never reclaimed, which this PR does not change.
- There is no service manager, so the Gateway was started by hand. A standalone `doctor --fix` cannot enter maintenance while a Gateway holds the same state directory, and an update stops such a Gateway, so the Gateway that kept running belongs to the second installation and its own state directory. The Doctor runs "from the second installation" used a third state directory for the same reason.
- The upstream was a local bare repository advanced by empty commits, not GitHub.

prs.title: fix: give scripts only the command's output when a command leaves a process running
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled automation whose condition script runs a command and parses its output failed about twice a day with `cron trigger evaluation failed (internal_error): SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Unable to parse JSON string`. The command had succeeded and printed one line of valid JSON.

The cause: when a command exits and leaves a child process running, OpenClaw adds a note about that process to the end of the command's output. Here `gh` left its detached `gh send-telemetry` helper behind, so the script received the JSON followed by `pid <n> (... gh send-telemetry) keeps running as background session <id>: ...`. The script follows the pattern in the automation docs: check `status` and `exitCode`, then `JSON.parse(result.aggregated)`.

## User Impact

User impact: a script that runs a command with `exec` now gets exactly what the command wrote in `aggregated`, so it can parse it. What OpenClaw has to say about the run (a process the command left running, or process cleanup it could not confirm) is in `warningText`, with the session ID to pass to `process`.

For an agent calling `exec` directly, the note is still in the result text. It now comes before the command output instead of after it, like other exec warnings. The `/bash` chat reply now shows exec warnings above the output, so it keeps showing this note.

## Why This Change Was Made

The note was written into the command's output, the one value that programs read. It now goes through the warning channel that `exec` already has and that the docs already describe for Code Mode callers (`warningText` plus the visible text). No new field.

A command that was already running in the background when it exited is unchanged. It returned its tool result earlier, so its `process` log and its approval follow-up are the only places left to carry the note.

Alternatives I did not take:

- A new details field for these notes. `warningText` already means "what OpenClaw says about this call", and a second field would give scripts two places to look.
- Stripping the note when building the script-facing result. The output and the note would still be one string at the source, and each reader would have to know how to split it.
- Keeping the note at the end of the visible text. That needs a second text channel beside warnings, and text at the start survives truncation of long output.

Not changed, by decision:

- With the tokenjuice plugin, a compacted result's `aggregated` is the compacted visible text, as before. That includes warnings.
- The Gateway approval follow-up for a diagnostics export parses the same output a note can be appended to. It already falls back to showing the raw text, and that command is not expected to leave processes behind.

Second defect, not fixed here: a failed condition evaluation records only its error string, so the run history could not show what the command had returned. The docs example told authors to "inspect this automation's run diagnostics", which hold nothing for that case; it now puts the evidence in the thrown message. Recording more is a retention decision and is filed separately: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202853

## Evidence

Reproduced through the real condition-script path (cron script runtime, Code Mode worker, real `exec` on the Gateway host), with a command that prints `{"ok":true}` and leaves a `sleep` running:

- On `main` at `1673d20f5d0e` the evaluation fails with `internal_error: SyntaxError: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 13 (line 3 column 1)`. This is the reported failure; the wording differs because the test runs on Node and the report came from a Bun Gateway.
- With this change the same script parses the output, reads the session ID from `warningText`, stops the leftover process with `process kill`, and returns its state.

Tests, run on a Blacksmith Testbox (Linux) with the production files at `main` first and then with the fix:

| Test | `main` | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts`: a trigger gets only the command's output | fails (error above) | passes |
| `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-group-cleanup.real.test.ts`: real processes, whole output parses, note in `warningText` and visible text | 2 fail | passes |
| `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.cleanup.test.ts`: foreground reports a warning; backgrounded keeps the note in its log | 2 fail | passes |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/bash-command.stop.test.ts`: `/bash` shows the warning | 1 fails | passes |

Also green with the fix: `code-mode.agent-loop`, `bash-tools`, `trigger-script.secret-egress`, `session-tool-result-guard` and `code-mode.tool-result-middleware` tests (131 tests in 4 shards on the first full pass). `pnpm check:changed` for these files: core and test typecheck, format, import cycles and the other guards pass; core lint passes after one test-file fix.

CI on head `4e2c5363dbc`: run 44854283429 green, `openclaw/ci-gate` success.

Gaps:

- Not run against a live Gateway with a real `gh`. The test uses a shell command that leaves a `sleep` behind, which takes the same path.
- The dead-export scan fails on `main` itself for `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace.ts` (two exports, from #202534). This change touches no `ui/` file.
- macOS: a child that leaves the command's process group is not tracked there (documented), so no note is produced for it. Unchanged.

Local review: autoreview (default Codex engine, helper `source-sha256:edb41e63c868`), committed branch against `origin/main` (merge base `1673d20f5d0e`, head `4e2c5363dbc`), priorities P0-P1: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Run twice; the second pass had six unchanged consumer files as source context. The reviewer could not see the call sites that decide when a command becomes backgrounded, so I checked them by hand: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-run.ts:662` does not background a command that is already finalizing, and `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts:1137` marks an approved run backgrounded before its process can settle.

Size: production +16/-4 in three files (six of the added lines are comments); tests +79/-19; docs +17/-5. The new trigger test takes about 0.4 s in an existing file.

prs.title: fix: honor current home and stabilize runtime regression tests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor's implicit legacy-state migration can use the process's launch-time home after `HOME` changes. Several regression fixtures also depend on unspawned native child-process internals, stdin module execution, or runtime-specific loader/drain behavior, preventing the same checks from running on current stock Bun.

## User Impact

Doctor selects both the legacy and destination directories from the current OS home. Existing `OPENCLAW_HOME`, explicit state-directory, and config-path exclusions remain intact. The other changes are fixture-only and preserve the original migration, refusal, publication, alias-resolution, diagnostic-output, and process-close assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Six commits separate the mechanisms: OS-home selection; owned child stdio setters; owned unspawned-child state; an explicit module file for the workflow heredoc; a joined stderr drain; and a runtime-native TypeScript alias fixture.

The home fix belongs in `resolveLegacyStateDirMigrationCandidates`, which supplies both paths, following #199469. The installer fixture removes HOME before launching its native reference child, matching the shell's environment. Synthetic process fixtures follow #199446; production spawns before consuming stdio and is unchanged. The stderr fixture gates real output events through drain completion and retains the final diagnostic bytes and close-ownership checks. The SDK fixture disables competing tsconfig SDK aliases so the native resolver remains responsible for the asserted resolution.

Runtime references: upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/42599, upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/44933, upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/43068, and upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/45033.

Two assigned IDs remain unchanged. `mac-runtime.test.ts` exercises production `scripts/stage-mac-runtime.sh`, which itself uses `node -e` with argv; a fixture-only workaround would hide that boundary. The `qa-report-cli.test.ts` parity blocker already imports the default module object and genuinely requires `registerHooks` interception; omitting it would weaken the unavailable-runtime assertion. Its four earlier interception IDs also remain upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/35690.

## Evidence

All 19 retained identities fail on the original Darwin stock source, pass on the original Node/pinned-fork source, and pass after the repair on all three runtimes. Reverting only the corresponding change reproduces all 19 original failures; each control restores the exact reviewed bytes afterward. Linux-only-unverified identities: none.

Counts refer to the assigned identities; candidate-admission's selected pattern also covers two adjacent cases. Wall times include repository-runner startup and generated worker preparation on a shared host. The package-acceptance full-file baseline was interrupted during unrelated planner stress cases; only the three assigned summary cases are claimed for that file, with comparable before/after timing. No sleeps, retries, timeout extensions, new production test seams, or weaker assertions were added.

The migration owner's nine tests and all 31 home-directory helper tests pass on Node, the pinned fork, and stock.
