prs.title: fix(agents): keep bundle MCP access for turns woken by an exec completion
prs.body:
Closes #183589

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a backgrounded host exec exits and `tools.exec.notifyOnExit` (default `true`) wakes the originating session, the woken turn has no bundle MCP tools although the run that started the exec had them (Code Mode telemetry `sources: {openclaw: 51, mcp: 0}`, `tools.effective` notice `mcp-not-yet-connected`), and any child spawned from that woken turn inherits the restriction.

## User Impact

User impact: a turn woken by an exec completion keeps exactly the MCP access of the run that started the exec, and children it spawns do too: an unrestricted run keeps every configured server, a run capped to `fixture__*` wakes a turn that can reach only the `fixture` server, an exact-name policy such as `fixture__read` keeps only that tool. Runs with no `mcp.servers`, or whose cap excludes bundle MCP tools, behave exactly as before, so a woken turn never gains access the producer run did not have. No config, schema, or wire change; `notifyOnExit` no longer has to be disabled to keep MCP in long-lived sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createOpenClawCodingTools` (assembled in `src/agents/agent-tools.assembly.ts`) builds each tool's Gateway caller with a default `sessionEventSourcePolicy` whose `toolsAllow` lists the finalized coding tools. Bundle MCP tools are materialized afterwards (`attempt-bundle-tools.ts`), so no `server__tool` name or `bundle-mcp` marker is ever in that list. The exec tool records the policy as the completion event's `producerPolicy`; `captureSessionEventTarget` intersects the woken turn's `toolsAllow` with it; `shouldCreateBundleMcpRuntimeForAttempt` then finds no bundle name and creates no MCP runtime for the woken turn or its children.

The fix captures the producer's final surface instead of predicting it (revision 5). `createOpenClawCodingTools` now fills a caller-owned array (`sessionEventToolsAllowRef`) with the coding tool names and hands that same array to every Gateway caller as `sessionEventSourcePolicy.toolsAllow`. The embedded attempt (`attempt-bundle-tools.ts`) appends the bundled MCP/LSP tools that survived the attempt's runtime allowlist, `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy`, and schema projection, by exact name, in the same place it already captures the cron creator cap and the spawn allowlist. The exec tool reads the policy when it records the completion, so the woken turn gets exactly the tools this run could call:

- sender-scoped denials (`tools.toolsBySender["id:alice"].deny: ["admin__*"]`) already removed `admin__reset` from the producer's final surface, so the senderless woken turn never sees it;
- intersected caps, partial globs (`fixture__read*` ∩ `fixture__*All`), and namespace-reaching globs (`fixture*`) are resolved by the existing runtime matcher on real tools, not approximated;
- a refresh replaces the previously appended bundled names, so a tool quarantined or filtered on refresh drops out;
- no marker or glob is ever added, so the continuation cannot widen past the producer.

The surface stays under the existing 512-name bound the target reader enforces (`SESSION_EVENT_TOOLS_ALLOW_LIMIT`, now exported from `session-event-target.ts`); past it, the attempt logs a warning and the woken turn keeps only the coding tools. Revision 5 deletes `agent-tools.session-event-policy.ts` and its tests (revisions 1–4 projected MCP access from allow patterns, which the review showed cannot preserve denials or every glob shape).

## Evidence

Regression in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.test.ts` (`session event tool surface`, 9 cases through `prepareEmbeddedAttemptBundleTools` with `fixture` and `admin` servers materializing `fixture__read`, `fixture__readAll`, `fixture__write`, `admin__reset`; each captured cap is then run through the woken turn's `intersectSessionEventToolsAllow` → `shouldCreateBundleMcpRuntimeForAttempt` → `applyEmbeddedAttemptToolsAllow`):

- unrestricted producer → all four MCP tools; `["exec", "fixture__*"]` and `["exec", "fixture*"]` → the three fixture tools; `["exec", "fixture__read"]` → `fixture__read`;
- intersected `[["exec", "fixture__read*"], ["exec", "fixture__*All"]]` → `fixture__readAll` (revision 4 returned nothing here);
- `["read", "exec"]` → no MCP tool and no bundle runtime in the woken turn;
- producer final policy drops `admin__reset` (the sender-scoped denial shape) → the woken turn never admits it;
- refresh after a projection drops `fixture__readAll` → the cap shrinks to `["exec", "fixture__read"]`;
- a coding surface at the bound → MCP names are not appended.

Red on `main`: the attempt never appends to the cap, so every case expecting an MCP tool fails, the reported loss.

Suites: `attempt-bundle-tools` 23/23; `bash-tools.exec-notify`, `tools/gateway-caller-context`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `attempt-tool-prepare.web-search`, `session-event-handoff`, `session-event-context`, `session-event-permissions` 115/115. Oxlint clean; `git diff --check` clean.

### Live Gateway run (revision 5, head 18721460f1e, shipped entry point, scripted provider)

Built dist from this head (`build-all gatewayWatch` with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1`), isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, non-interactive onboarding with `--custom-no-auth` against a loopback OpenAI-compatible provider written for the proof. The provider scripts each step from the conversation and logs every request's offered `tools[].function.name`.
Two loopback streamable-http MCP servers, `fixture` (`echo`) and `admin` (`reset`), each log every JSON-RPC request. Config: `mcp.servers` for both, `tools.profile: full`, `tools.codeMode: false`, `tools.toolSearch: false`, `tools.exec.security: full`, `tools.exec.ask: off`, `tools.exec.notifyOnExit: true`; Gateway `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 18399`.
Every scenario's producer turn runs `exec` with `background: true` and ends. Its woken turn then calls `fixture__echo`, `sessions_spawn` (child task: `fixture__echo`, then `admin__reset`) and `admin__reset`. The provider emits each call whether or not it was offered, so the Gateway has to refuse what the turn may not use.
Policy changes were applied with `node openclaw.mjs config patch --file …` while the Gateway was running (log: `config hot reload applied (…)`). Times are UTC; tool results come from the session transcript in the agent SQLite store.
No credentials, all loopback; the host was heavily loaded, which explains the minutes between exec exit and wake.

**S1: allowed completion-turn MCP call** (`tools.allow: ["read","exec","process","sessions_spawn","fixture__*"]`, session `agent:main:s3d`, dispatched with `node openclaw.mjs agent --agent main --session-key s3d --json`)

```text
18:40:53.533  provider  producer   offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> exec {"command":"sleep 5; echo PROOF_EXEC_DONE","background":true}
18:40:53.686  provider  producer   -> "started" (turn ends, exec still running)
18:56:00.145  provider  woken      last user msg "[OpenClaw exec completion] Exec completed (… code 0) :: PROOF_EXEC_DONE"
                                   offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
18:56:00.155  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
18:56:00.158  toolResult fixture__echo  "fixture.echo ok: {\"text\":\"from-woken-turn\"}"
18:56:00.279  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: initialize / tools/list only, no tools/call
```

The turn woken by the exec exit got `fixture__echo` and its call reached the fixture server; `admin__reset`, outside the producer's cap, was not offered and was refused before any request left the Gateway.

**S2: sender-scoped admin denial preserved** (no `tools.allow`; `tools.toolsBySender: {"id:alice": {"deny": ["admin__*"]}}`). The producer message entered through the **qa-channel** plugin: the repo's qa-lab bus ran on loopback and `POST /v1/inbound/message` carried `{"conversation":{"id":"alice","kind":"direct"},"senderId":"alice"}`. The producer request shows `"sender":{"id":"alice","name":"Alice"}`.

```text
19:30:58.826  provider  producer (sender alice)  tools=70  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> exec background
19:31:06.503  provider  woken (senderless)       tools=70  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> fixture__echo
19:31:06.598  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
19:31:06.995  toolResult sessions_spawn  accepted  childSessionKey=agent:main:subagent:61a17295-…
19:31:07.206  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: no tools/call
control, same config, CLI sender (not alice), session agent:main:s2ctl:
19:38:41.052  provider  producer  tools=71  admin__reset=yes
19:38:48.506  admin     tools/call reset {"reason":"from-woken-turn"}
```

The denial applied only to alice's run, and the senderless woken turn inherited it: `admin__reset` was absent from the woken turn's tools and its call was refused. The same config still gave `admin__reset` to a non-alice sender, so the denial is sender-scoped and not global.

**S3: inherited restrictions in a spawned child** (children spawned from the S1 and S2 woken turns)

```text
S1 child agent:main:subagent:0e4cffe3-…
18:56:00.479  provider  child  offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo
18:56:00.488  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-child"}
18:56:00.505  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
S2 child agent:main:subagent:61a17295-…
19:31:10.113  provider  child  tools=51  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> fixture__echo
19:31:10.254  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-child"}
19:31:10.536  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: no tools/call in either run
```

A child spawned from a woken turn keeps that turn's MCP access (`fixture__echo` works) and its restrictions: the S1 global cap and alice's denial still exclude `admin__reset`.

**S4: revocation after capture, before the woken turn** (S1 config; session `agent:main:s4`; exec `sleep 240`)

```text
19:10:29.444  provider  producer  offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> exec {"command":"sleep 240; …","background":true}
19:10:30Z     producer turn returned (agent exit 0; exec still running, its completion target captured while fixture__echo was allowed)
19:11:52.750  gateway   config.patch write changedPaths=tools.deny            (tools.deny: ["fixture__echo"])
19:11:52.877  gateway   [reload] config hot reload applied (tools.deny)
19:29:59.180  transcript user "Exec completed (oceanic-, code 0) :: PROOF_EXEC_DONE"
19:30:02.327  provider  woken     offered=exec,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo
19:30:02.575  toolResult fixture__echo  isError "Tool fixture__echo not found"
fixture server: last tools/call at 18:56:00.818 (S1), none after the revocation
```

The cap captured `fixture__echo`, but the woken turn applied its own current policy. After the hot-reloaded `tools.deny` the tool was not offered, and the call was rejected before any `tools/call` reached the fixture server.

Discovery (`initialize`/`tools/list`) still connects both configured servers during each run, as on `main`; policy filters tools, not discovery.

prs.title: fix(ci): isolate Git PPA index refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Boat CI jobs fail before testing when Git setup refreshes every configured APT repository. An unrelated PHP PPA changed its release label, causing all 20 Boat jobs in [hourly run 44838379805](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44838379805) to fail during setup.

## User Impact

CI can install the required Git version without being blocked by unrelated repository metadata changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Refresh only the dedicated, signed Git PPA, including stale-index recovery. Preserve other cached indexes and normal installation sources. Signing checks, release-info safeguards, timeouts, retry limits, and the final Git capability check stay intact.

## Evidence

- Real Ubuntu Boat VM, 4 CPUs / 8 GiB: the original helper exited 100 with the observed PHP label-change error. The patched helper installed Git 2.56.1, passed `git --no-lazy-fetch --version`, and preserved every unrelated APT index byte-for-byte.
- Ran the committed shell fixture directly through a dependency-free probe: both new cases failed on the base and passed on the patch, including stale-index recovery.
- Bash syntax, TypeScript syntax, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. Targeted Node test jobs passed in both diagnostic and normal PR CI; the shared local dependency installation remains unqualified.
- Independent local ClawSweeper review completed with no actionable findings. Replayed onto current main with both changed files byte-identical to the reviewed and tested patch.

Direct main publication was refused by the repository ruleset; this PR uses the required fallback.

## CI Status and Attribution

The diagnostic [exact-head run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44849781593) passed Git setup, targeted tests, build, security, and baseline checks. Its `check-dependencies` job failed on unchanged UI exports: `checkSessionWorkspaceFileLinks` and `openSessionWorkspaceManagedArtifact` in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace.ts`. The actual job log reports these unused exports in the production/full-tree dead-code scans. This PR changes only Git provisioning and its shell fixture; the UI, checker/configuration scripts, package manifest, and lockfile are identical to the recorded main baseline in the tested PR merge. This is a separate baseline failure, not a Git setup failure.

The normal [PR CI run, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44850586112/attempts/2) completed successfully, including targeted tests, build, lint, type checks, and baseline ratchets. Attempt 1 lost communication with its GitHub-hosted baseline runner and published no checker result or downloadable log; only that failed job and its downstream gate were recovered, retaining all passing jobs. The separate [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44855768738) also passed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): let delegated OpenClaw changes work from CLI-backend agents
prs.body:
Related: #136036, #137017

## What Problem This Solves

Delegated `openclaw.chat` calls from CLI/subprocess and worker harnesses failed with `delegated OpenClaw approval requires an active run authority`. Fully in-process agents retained the ambient caller identity, but harness tool calls crossed the Gateway WebSocket boundary, where that process-local identity is intentionally unavailable.

## User Impact

CLI and worker-harness delegated calls retain their signed source ownership and approval guard, including when optional wire delegation metadata is absent. Existing run, tool-abort and worker-lifetime fencing remains fail-closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

The approval gate only consulted the process-local Gateway tool caller identity. OpenClaw already has a host-minted, HMAC-signed `agentRuntimeIdentityToken` for trusted cross-process calls, including the exact admitted run authority and worker turn claim, but `openclaw.chat` was not included in that transport.

The first revision attempted to mint replacement authority from the delegated session id. Review identified that as unsafe. The signed-identity revision then exposed two narrower defects:

- Distinct calls in one source run receive distinct tool-bound lease claim ids. Approval reconciliation compared those claim ids, so a later call retired the original pending decision even though its exact lease was still live.
- The wire fallback retained the generic 30-second request timeout although delegated human interaction is budgeted for 900 seconds and the approval owner can wait 600 seconds before staging/application completes.

## Design

This revision carries the existing source-run authority instead of synthesizing or transferring it:

- `openclaw.chat` is eligible for the signed agent-runtime identity token.
- The host binds the exact tool abort signal into the delegated run authority before signing it.
- Explicit host-prepared Full Access is transported only for `openclaw.chat`; model-authored parameters cannot create it.
- On Gateway arrival, signed agent/runtime/session/routing facts establish delegation even when the optional wire field is omitted; model-supplied metadata cannot override or opt out of that binding.
- Ambient in-process identity remains authoritative when present. Wire calls use the verified signed runtime identity.
- Pending-approval reconciliation first validates the original exact application lease, then compares both callers' active canonical source owner plus local/worker kind and exact worker turn claim. It never replaces the authority stored on the pending record.
- The delegated wire call uses the existing 900-second human-interaction budget. The generic Gateway default remains 30 seconds, and the Codex owner retains its separate 30-second completion grace.
- Run release/replacement, original tool abort, Gateway replacement, worker-claim loss, and delegated-session replacement still fail closed.

No new configuration keys, SQLite surfaces, dependencies or retries are introduced. The existing transient signed-identity token carries an optional host-prepared Full Access fact. Existing canonical owner and human-wait helpers were sufficient.

## Security properties

- No authority is derived from a session id or model-authored delegation fields.
- The signed identity can only be minted by the host holding the local runtime-token secret.
- Full Access is a host-prepared restrict-only fact; omission never bypasses approval.
- Reuse grants observation of an existing pending decision only after its original exact application lease is revalidated.
- The original record retains its exact lease, signals, and application predicate. Closing a later sibling lease cannot transfer or cancel that authority; closing the original lease still blocks application.
- Worker authority remains bound to the canonical placement/turn claim.

## Evidence

- Published head `cea0acc7028934a9609bb656a14cb21a3496db94` integrates GitHub-confirmed current-main conflicts against pinned upstream `3260d7b41a8c2404b8b3dc800240573dfb1cc7e1`. Preserves upstream compact delegate-test layout and PR timeout/permission/session-continuation contracts. Production authority changes merged without manual conflict; removed a now-unused moved import and compacted a local parameter name to satisfy changed-file lint. Validation passed: 91 focused authority/identity/delegate tests across five suites (55.731s wrapper), production core types and all three affected test-type shards, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, pinned-main diff check, line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets. The newly integrated cron fixture needed a true-or-undefined permission normalization in its test transport only; its affected integration suite and Gateway-method types pass after that correction. Fresh independent scoped review of the frozen production tree found no actionable P0/P1; retained for the final one-line test-adapter correction. No fresh real delayed-human transport proof, replacement-head hosted verdict, or maintainer signed-carrier acceptance is claimed.

- Prior published head `fad89b4b638381fbb5e964c5d0cade97d01b0afc` reconciles a GitHub-confirmed approval-test conflict onto pinned upstream `d1618ccd0b276f985711ff297b1b87a77bdad35d`. Upstream removed a redundant ambient-only parameter case; the later maintained cross-lease wire/ambient approval coverage remains intact. Seventeen patches replay identically; the first differs only in its upstream conflict context. Prior independent review is retained for this mechanical delta, not claimed as fresh review. All 10 local gates passed: 99 tests across five focused suites (56.058s wrapper), production core types, all three affected test-type shards (agents-root, agents-other and Gateway-methods), changed-source type-aware lint, formatting, diff, line-cap and assertion-safety checks. The initial lint attempt could not load the newly required eslint-plugin-solid; refreshing the isolated installation from the unchanged frozen lockfile resolved it without source or lockfile workarounds. No replacement-head hosted verdict or fresh live-runtime result is claimed. Real delayed-human-decision proof and area-owner signed-carrier acceptance remain outstanding.

- Prior published head `db8ec1bb286e5b9bd9a77a7fcaea911869673b9a` addresses revision 24’s test-quality feedback: removed the synthetic delayed-decision mock test and unused fake-timer cleanup. The retained relay test verifies the requested 900-second budget and returned approval outcome. All 15 delegate-tool tests passed (`pnpm test src/agents/tools/openclaw-delegate-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 8.655s wrapper / 6.67s Vitest); affected agents-other test types, type-aware changed-file lint, formatting, diff check, line-cap and assertion-safety gates passed. Production sources are byte-unchanged from the prior validated head, whose exact-head hosted CI was observed SUCCESS at 07:13 UTC and durable revision 24 found no production defect. Those prior-head results are historical. That prior head’s hosted CI was observed SUCCESS at 2026-10-08 17:53 UTC; durable ClawSweeper revision 25 reviewed that head and reports no actionable findings, with area-owner acceptance still outstanding. No fresh independent production review or live run is claimed for this test-only deletion.
- A real human decision after 30 seconds remains unverified by the historical CLI evidence. The removed synthetic timeout test did not establish that transport behavior; the historical timeout RED/GREEN results below are synthetic test evidence only.

- Prior published `4cde0ad5c4cd3cbe31b96320f8a7e01954e2d74b` reconciled a confirmed import conflict onto pinned upstream `2f1f73ccb2224bbe7d961b4c0d3b29cfdd51e7f8`. The maintained hosted-routing suite retains the delegated signed-identity case and drops an obsolete Workshop approval import removed upstream. All other patches replay unchanged; delegated authority, method-scoped Full Access and exact approval-lease intent remain unchanged. Fresh validation of the source committed as `4cde0ad5c4cd3cbe31b96320f8a7e01954e2d74b`: 103 authority tests across five focused suites passed (50.477s wrapper); production core types and all three affected test-type shards (agents-root, agents-other and Gateway-methods) passed. Changed-source type-aware lint, formatting, diff, line-cap and assertion-safety gates passed. Prior independent scoped review is retained for the mechanically reconciled delta, not claimed as a fresh review. Prior 27-test URL-boundary proof is retained for the unchanged canonicalizer. No fresh live-runtime proof or replacement-head hosted CI result is claimed. Assigned-reviewer acceptance of the signed Full Access carrier remains outstanding.

Tested head: `cea0acc7028934a9609bb656a14cb21a3496db94` (base `3260d7b41a8c2404b8b3dc800240573dfb1cc7e1`).

- Resolved current-main conflicts without changing delegated authority intent. Migrated the one PR-specific signed Full Access wire/lifetime case into the maintained hosted-routing suite; the retired baseline suite remains deleted. Preserved current-main admitted identity reconstruction and inherited permission schema.
- Omitted-delegation RED/GREEN regression: the real `openclaw.chat` handler test failed before the repair, choosing connection ownership instead of signed source ownership. The parameterized regression checks both omitted and spoofed wire metadata, signed session ownership, and delegated-only operator approval. Both regression variants pass after the repair.
- Prior published `c6ab9511e93f586626135c67633e5240db04ea32` validation: 107 tests across five focused suites passed (36.14s wrapper); production core types, type-aware changed-file lint, formatting, diff check, line-cap ratchet and assertion safety passed. Fresh independent review: the sole P1 concerned the old index version; the reviewer explicitly recognized this working-tree repair as addressing it and reported no other concrete P0/P1 defect. The corrected index was verified and committed. Affected Gateway-method test types: passed (exit 0).
- Prior published head `bd1287586199249975f6a268ccbf2553686ad3f0` had successful exact-head hosted CI; those are not current-candidate CI results. The earlier 27 core-test compiler shards passed with the documented aggregate-wrapper exit-124 limitation. Current validation reruns affected proof rather than claiming those prior results as fresh full coverage.
- Historical RED/GREEN timeout evidence: test-only `06648dac970` failed at the generic 30-second timeout ([red runtime job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33936113189/job/101224617458)); `537130294ac2e1360700ab2f094df4b8e9a8b05d` passed 241 files / 5,013 tests ([green runtime job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33936776749/job/101226276241)). These are not current-head CI results.
- The earlier real CLI proof below is historical transport evidence, not a fresh live run of this rebased candidate. No serving runtime was changed for this reconciliation. Hosted CI for prior head `db8ec1bb286e5b9bd9a77a7fcaea911869673b9a` was observed SUCCESS at 2026-10-08 17:53 UTC; security-owner/maintainer acceptance remains an external gate.

### Earlier real CLI harness proof

Verified against a locally built Gateway through the real `openclaw agent` Codex app-server path:

1. **Active Full Access succeeds:** an admitted `finance-worker` Codex turn invoked the `openclaw` tool over the Gateway WebSocket and changed `update.checkOnStart` from `true` to `false`. The terminal receipt recorded exactly one successful `openclaw` tool call. An independent CLI read observed `false`; the test then restored and schema-validated `true`.
2. **Source abort fails closed after dispatch:** a second admitted CLI turn emitted the `openclaw` tool call, then received `SIGINT` through the CLI's same-connection abort path. The persisted tool result was `OpenClaw dynamic tool call aborted.` and an independent CLI read remained `true`.

## Observer-cancellation ownership

Proposal-failure retirement belongs to the caller that installed the pending approval. A later same-source observer whose distinct lease closes fails its own live-authority check without clearing or force-denying the original owner's still-live approval. Original-owner cancellation remains fail-closed. The current focused approval-authority suite includes this order-sensitive regression.

prs.title: fix: keep dismissed automation failures out of the Inbox
prs.body:
Closes #202650
Closes #202652
Closes #202653
Closes #202661

## What Problem This Solves

A failed automation can come back after you dismiss it if browser storage is full, two tabs dismiss different failures at once, or you pause and re-enable the automation. Opening the same Gateway from a different browser or address also brings the failure back.

## User Impact

A dismissed run stays hidden for your account on that Gateway, including when you switch browsers, addresses, or devices. A dismissed auto-disable stays hidden after a successful manual run. A later failed run still appears. A dismissal that the Gateway refuses because a restart is in progress is saved for the same browser profile to submit when the Gateway returns. Update notices can reappear after a Gateway restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway saves the latest dismissed failure for each automation in the signed-in operator’s existing profile preferences. The profile writer merges acknowledgements in one transaction, and the existing preference event refreshes open tabs. A structured restart refusal uses the existing per-profile reconnect queue with the exact failure timestamp. Pausing an automation leaves its last-run identity intact. For an auto-disabled job, dismissal covers the failed run and the automatic disable shown in the same row.

The Inbox imports existing account-scoped browser dismissals. Those records contain job IDs, so the first import uses the failure timestamp the Gateway knows for that job. Later imports preserve the first receipt. Import requires a browser record tied to the signed-in profile.

## Evidence

The current comparison uses main `2b5f1a88ba81` and this PR at `3245e9ff38e2`. The targeted Plugins readiness check passed on both builds.

On the PR head, 207 focused tests passed, including the Inbox, profile preferences, and Gateway method order. Both Inbox opening latency cases and the Gateway protocol and generated validator checks passed.

### Product captures

The paired captures compare main `e6d441549fe2` with the Inbox persistence implementation at `2720891948c5`, each against a copy of the same isolated Gateway state. The stable-upgrade captures use `2eda19b546a`. The isolated Gateway comparison below also covers that upgrade at `18b3695e8ad`. The receipt regressions compare main `5fe76f0073b4` with PR head `2dfaed67aaab`.

| Browser storage full after two dismissals | ![Main shows Archive check again](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/ae8c7e84-96fc-4c48-a11d-b035dfa86004.png) | ![Both failures stay hidden](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/e57fbd94-8c5e-4178-9f0f-32a72cc2874f.png) |
| Automation paused and re-enabled after dismissal | ![Main shows Archive check with Index check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/acd96639-1811-4223-99ff-a6f924fc3fcb.png) | ![Only Index check remains](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/aa7d9fbd-47aa-4bde-ac9f-030104e74e03.png) |
| Same Gateway opened at another address in a separate profile | ![Main shows both failures in the other browser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/b90930a5-0eae-4bd7-a4c5-8e285976d63d.png) | ![The other browser shows only Index check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/4e67960e-177d-4273-8b25-ca05c0f31de6.png) |

- **Two tabs.** Main lost one dismissal when both tabs clicked at the same timestamp. The PR build hid both rows in both tabs, and the Gateway held both run timestamps.
- **Browser migration.** A dismissal carried over from the old browser while the job was paused. It stayed hidden in a fresh profile after re-enable. A genuine later failure appeared even when another browser still held an old dismissal.

| Imported dismissal in a fresh browser | A later failed run |
| --- | --- |
| ![Only Index check after importing the Archive check dismissal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/a0fe65c8-c529-4cb5-ba12-18860a11450d.png) | ![A new Archive check failure appears](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/ff223519-afd7-49df-a707-ddd3e830c4a3.png) |

### Control UI behavior against isolated Gateways

I built main `3ac8d23a2cb6` and PR head `18b3695e8ad` and exercised both in Chromium against isolated Gateways.

| Scenario | Main | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dismiss a failed automation, reload, and restart the Gateway | Stays hidden in the original browser | Stays hidden in the original browser and in a fresh browser after restart |
| Dismiss with browser storage full | Returns on reload | Stays hidden on reload |
| Two tabs dismiss separate failures | Both stayed hidden in this run | Both stayed hidden and the Gateway stored both receipts |
| Upgrade from v2026.11.6 with a browser dismissal and a profile setting | The setting and original browser dismissal survive, and the failed run appears in a new browser | Imports the dismissal, preserves the setting, and hides the original failure in a new browser. A later failed run appears |
| Update notice and execution approval | The snoozed notice returns after restart. Pending approval requires a decision | Same behavior |
| Dismiss a seeded mention | Stays gone after reload and restart in a fresh browser | Same behavior |

A real Gateway refused the dismissal as shutdown began at `3106387303e`, and the original request never stored a receipt. At `18b3695e8ad`, I reproduced the same structured refusal during a real shutdown. After restart the dismissal was submitted, the Gateway saved it, and a fresh browser showed the failure hidden. The focused regression was red on `3106387303e` and green on the exact head. The runtime build, 108 focused tests, and targeted lint and format passed.

Overdue automation dismissal stayed browser-local on both builds. Built-browser fixtures covered model-auth dismissal, read-only scope guidance, and OpenClaw ID recovery notices and the other OpenClaw ID rows that require action. The browser outbox suite passed on both builds with simulated delivery rejection. The update test seeded a release check result. The mention test seeded an already-received mention and used the real Gateway for dismissal and persistence.

### Auto-disable followed by a manual run

In a built Control UI with an isolated Gateway and a scripted model response, a real one-shot automation failed and was automatically disabled. I dismissed its Inbox row, ran the job successfully without re-enabling it, and reloaded the page. At `05a4906c5d4`, the row came back. At `3106387303e`, it stayed dismissed and appeared again only after a later failed run.

The new regression failed on `05a4906c5d4` and passed on `3106387303e`. The 107 focused Inbox and Gateway preference tests passed on `3106387303e`, along with the runtime build and targeted lint and format checks.

### Upgrade from v2026.11.6

I dismissed Archive check in the published v2026.11.6 Control UI, saved a profile theme preference, and paused the job. I replaced the stable Gateway with a build of `2eda19b546a` using the same test state and browser profile. The Gateway imported the dismissal for the paused run and preserved the theme preference. Re-enabling the job kept the original run ID and timestamp, and a fresh browser profile on `localhost` kept the row dismissed after reload. Running the job again produced a new failed run and a visible Inbox row.

| Dismissal on v2026.11.6 | Relaunched browser on the PR build | Later failed run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Stable Inbox after dismissing Archive check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/bcf459336474b7f522107bd24a0615360b425109/images/2026/11/489910f9-3477-48ae-95ac-ba5d4aba4d08.png) | ![Only Index check after import and reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/bcf459336474b7f522107bd24a0615360b425109/images/2026/11/ce7c7cf3-07fb-42f3-ad74-3739d91f6b48.png) | ![Archive check appears for a new failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/bcf459336474b7f522107bd24a0615360b425109/images/2026/11/851cc5c1-ecbf-4d08-8fc2-1441b8c7788b.png) |

### Protocol and performance checks at `2eda19b546a`

- 218 focused tests and three selected browser tests passed, along with the UI typecheck and Gateway validator check. The legacy advertised method list keeps its order with the new RPC appended.
- Compared with main `8253356c9864`, the SQLite worker ratchet stayed at 166 main-thread calls. The Control UI comparison passed. Chat boot JavaScript went from 1,333,213 to 1,333,042 gzip bytes, with 21 requests on both sides. The existing absolute CSS overruns are present on main.
- Skills and Plugins readiness timed out on the original CI base as well. Skill Settings and both Inbox latency cases passed on the merged head.

### Receipt regressions on main and the PR

The main checkout at the CI base `5fe76f0073b4` received only the two test cases. The same tests passed on `2dfaed67aaab`.

| Regression | Main `5fe76f0073b4` | PR head `2dfaed67aaab` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Import a browser dismissal for a job outside the selected inventory | Failed because the Inbox made no `cron.acknowledgeFailure` adoption request | Passed. The browser ID remains until the Gateway confirms the import |
| Merge simultaneous receipts and keep the original timestamp on legacy adoption | Failed because the preference writer returned no acknowledgement timestamp | Passed. Both receipts persist and the adoption returns the original timestamp |

- The cron-event fixture waits for the lazy import and first preference read. The original incident-row, event-projection, and inventory-read assertions passed. All 69 focused tests passed.
- The deferred-storage scan checks storage before entering the loop. Targeted lint passed on main and the repaired head. The Control UI comparison passed, with Chat boot JavaScript 315 gzip bytes smaller than the CI base.
- The Skills ready-window check saw 30 requests against its limit of 28 on both main and the repaired head. Skill Settings passed on both replays. Both Inbox latency cases passed on the repaired head.

In an independent two-tab storage probe, an artificial delay between reading and writing let one-time legacy cleanup erase a concurrent dismissal of a different browser-local alert.

The live run used desktop Chromium with independent browser profiles. Native apps, a second physical machine, and PostgreSQL were outside that run.

The generated validator diff contains 4,333 added and 4,298 removed lines, mostly predicate renumbering.

Android cron summary types and list parsing live in the large runtime orchestrator, although they contain no runtime state. Maintaining the cron data contract therefore requires editing connection orchestration, and its parser cannot be tested directly at the data boundary.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Automation summaries retain their enabled-state coercion, schedule labels, prompt previews and last-run status precedence. Scheduling, mutation guards and stored data are unchanged.

Move the summary contracts and pure parsing into the existing cron data owner, and remove the old implementations from the runtime. All live and screenshot callers use the same parser. prs.title: fix: report failed Dreaming workspaces in automation health
prs.body:
Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/143206

## What Problem This Solves

The managed Memory Dreaming Promotion automation can finish with one or every workspace failed while recording a successful run, resetting its error streak, and requesting no failure notification. Operators then need a separate journal watcher to discover failed sweeps.

## User Impact

Synchronous workspace failures and synchronous narrative degradation now make the managed run fail and count toward the existing failure-notification policy. Healthy workspaces still finish their promotions and reports, and pending detached narratives alone remain healthy. Partial failures are logged at warn.

The failed-workspace count and first error remain in the job record and failure webhooks. Chat alerts retain their existing normalized-cause contract and do not expose arbitrary error text. There are no new configuration options or public hook/SDK fields.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sweep returns its known failure through the existing handled `before_agent_reply` reply with `isError: true`; both runner paths preserve that payload and cron already owns error persistence, failure streaks, and notifications. The sweep retains the first workspace/phase error and synchronous narrative error until it has processed the remaining workspaces.

A small cron classification correction consumes the existing `providerStarted: false` fact: a synthetic failure cannot be inferred from its text to be a provider auth failure or a provider-transient retry signal. Existing terminal classifications and restart precedence remain intact.

**Covered:** failures already known when the sweep returns, including whole-workspace exceptions and synchronous degraded narrative outcomes. **Still open for the product decision in #143206:** eventual detached narrative settlement, whether to wait for publication or report later, and retry design. This change adds no retries and does not change narrative detachment or the promotion apply path.

## Evidence

- Before the repair on main `dda8da4b5666f0b7411b528309c16bf150ccef65`, scheduled partial failure, total failure, and synchronous degradation all persisted as `ok` with `consecutiveErrors: 0`. The healthy pending control passed. Those failure cases now persist as `error`, increment the streak, and request the configured alert. The webhook case preserves the failed-workspace count and first error.
- The scheduled regression composes the real registered Dreaming hook, CLI synthetic-reply adapter, isolated cron finalization, CronService persistence, and alert dispatch. Workspace phase failures and synchronous narrative results are controlled fixtures; external notification transport is mocked. This is not live Gateway proof.
- Existing real-file narrative tests verify healthy promotion/report/diary output despite another workspace failing, phase/report error propagation, and unchanged detached publication with `narrativesPending=1`.
- The `providerStarted: false` regression failed before the classification correction and passed afterward; true and omitted values preserve existing classification behavior.
- **378 tests passed across 21 files** using `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks`: all 14 memory-core `dreaming*.test.ts` files; cron timer-outcome, failure-alert outcome, silent-failure alert, meta-error and watchdog-cause tests; CLI before-reply tests; and embedded shared integration tests. Four selected runner shards completed in 286 seconds locally. The final scheduled regression rerun passed all four cases after making later workspace errors distinct, proving the first error is retained. Its final standalone wall time was 50 seconds including compiler preparation, with about 5.4 seconds of test execution. CI timing is not yet available.
- Passed `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, and the cron test typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental`). Targeted type-aware oxlint on all changed TypeScript files, oxfmt checks, the changed-document MDX check, and `git diff --check` passed.

**Incomplete validation / draft status:** Auto Review did not complete; it stalled and was stopped at the requester’s instruction. No clean independent-review result is claimed. A full package build, full-repository test/lint suites, hosted CI, and live Gateway verification were not run. No packaging, dependency, or public-boundary changes require a new build in this patch.

**Live proof still required before landing:** the requester will run the managed Dreaming automation on a real Gateway with one deliberately broken workspace, capture the job record before and after (status, error, consecutive error count, and failure-notification request state), verify healthy workspaces still complete, and attach the evidence as a PR comment. A maintainer owns review and landing. The submitted head is frozen after handoff unless the requester asks for changes.

Co-authored with Holger Gruenhagen, who supplied the operational report, bounded scope, and validation plan.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0da26e55-3455-491e-803b-71d29720792c)

Co-authored-by: holgergruenhagen <60438604+holgergruenhagen@users.noreply.github.com>

prs.title: fix: keep required replies from becoming optional through plugins
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A channel plugin could forward an internal-only option that made a required-result turn silently accept `NO_REPLY`. The public SDK boundary copied that option into core reply handling instead of leaving silence permission with the host.

## User Impact

Required replies keep their host-selected completion policy when called through the plugin SDK. Trusted host notifications can still explicitly allow silence, and normal visible replies remain unchanged. No configuration change or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exclude `replyExpectation` in the existing shared public-reply sanitizer, both in public parameter types and at runtime. This adapts the boundary repair from [68bf43c87e27](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/68bf43c87e271aab1c71b90a81b756e9dd20f8e4) to main's current owner without changing trusted host dispatch or treating provenance as permission.

The existing sanitizer remains the single public boundary: no new wrapper, state, or policy owner. Production delta is +3/-1 lines; regression tests add 123 lines plus one broker-runtime routing entry.

## Evidence

- **Red before the fix:** the public dispatch regression received `replyExpectation: "optional"`; the public generation/CLI-flow regression selected `optional` where `result-required` was expected.
- **Green with the fix:** 33 tests across five focused suites. Real session-event admission, reply preparation, and CLI terminal handling preserve permitted silence, reject required silence, retain visible replies, and strip the forged SDK option. External CLI output is deterministic fixture I/O, not a live provider.
- Focused compiler check for the changed TypeScript files and their imports, scoped Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Type-aware lint emitted SDK boundary declarations successfully.
- Full `pnpm build` passes at committed source `2d112a0efc5a7929bcf7450758478830dda8fc6c` (172.15 seconds wall), including declaration generation and SDK export validation. The unchanged UI build emits CSS-size and boot-request budget warnings; no UI files changed and those warnings were not attributed in this task.
- Independent local **autoreview**, GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Reviewed base `de5f46d8f63b5c375c5e30e1882b0a4df327d868` through the complete staged snapshot committed as `2d112a0efc5a7929bcf7450758478830dda8fc6c`. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; this is the documented fallback route, not a ClawSweeper result. Exact-head CI and hosted review remain before landing.

No live channel/provider run was performed. The proof covers the real core admission/reply/CLI owners with controlled external output, not authenticated provider behavior.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands and test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime.contract.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-reply-expectation.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-expectation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/legacy-sdk-reply-dispatch.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/reply-dispatch-owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The changed SDK contract suite took 17.45 s; the new session/CLI integration suite took 12.19 s (5.01 s test execution). Wrapper wall times were 94.05 s and 41.41 s, including subprocess compilation. CI seconds are not yet available.

The focused compiler project extends `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.shard.json` and includes the sanitizer and both changed TypeScript test files. The imported release regression builds a complete current system-prompt report through its existing owner rather than the old empty fixture.

</details>

Thanks @vincentkoc for the audit and repair direction. Adapted from the original repair by @holgergruenhagen, with existing contributor credit preserved for Ayaan Zaidi and @RomneyDa.

prs.title: fix: keep agent memory trusted after edits from project sessions
prs.body:
Refs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180796
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165452, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/153426

## What Problem This Solves

A session rooted in a project or worktree can edit the agent workspace's memory without updating its provenance. The next clean tracked edit then quarantines the file, removing MEMORY.md or USER.md from automatic context.

## User Impact

Host-rooted sessions retain provenance and hash continuity when OpenClaw file tools edit the canonical agent workspace's memory. Session-local memory keeps its existing workspace records, and sandbox writes remain isolated to the sandbox filesystem.

This does not loosen quarantine, change the hash-continuity rule, rehabilitate existing untrusted rows, or track shell writes. CLI turn-taint and native-writer coverage are addressed separately in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201478.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the canonical workspace from the execution agent, then let the existing memory-write observer classify that workspace before the session root. Record each artifact under its owning workspace without changing origin classification, rollback, or quarantine policy. The additional host workspace is never passed to a sandbox observer.

## Evidence

- [Live before/after proof from Holger](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201509#issuecomment-6995176114): an isolated Linux Gateway with deterministic model responses exercised real rooted-session write/edit tools, provenance reads, and fresh-session `/context list`. Before: stale hashes followed by quarantine and missing MEMORY.md/USER.md. After: matching agent-origin hashes and both files injected. Session-local ownership and rooted network-taint controls also passed. The after build combined this head `8cd5bf449788214a2e9a3a46143f848700f61193` with PR #201478 head `44fd853a85b0ffeed0ca9ba01d6efeded374f458`; the rooted path exercises this PR's change.
- On base da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf, rooted write/edit regressions left stale provenance hashes; the next clean edit recorded untrusted and excluded MEMORY.md and USER.md from bootstrap.
- All six new cases pass with the fix: rooted write/edit, canonical control, tainted-write quarantine, session-local ownership, and sandbox isolation. Tests use real provenance storage and cover MEMORY.md, USER.md, and nested memory notes, followed by clean tracked edits and bootstrap assertions for the curated files.
- 160 existing tests passed across provenance, bootstrap (including personal and remote), coding tools, sandbox, prefix stability, and the session-memory hook. Commands used pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks.
- Targeted TypeScript checks, changed-file lint, formatting, and git diff --check passed. Simplification pass retained the existing observer and provenance store; no schema or new state owner was added.
- New regression file: approximately 4 seconds test time (43 seconds including cold compilation); existing suite approximately 117 seconds in the test runner. Hosted CI has not been run as part of this local proof.

**Review status:** Local Auto Review did not complete and was stopped at the requester's direction; no clean local autoreview is claimed. The [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201509#issuecomment-6994557545) of this head reported no actionable findings. Maintainer review and applicable security approval remain separate; no merge or landing is requested.

**Live-proof limits:** The linked rooted-session proof used a real Gateway and deterministic OpenAI-compatible mock model, not a real Claude model. Sandbox isolation was not exercised live because the test host has no Docker/Podman; shell writes remain out of scope.

Contributor: Holger Gruenhagen (@holgergruenhagen).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix: let Doctor inspect Codex sign-in on PostgreSQL
prs.body:
Closes #201059

## What Problem This Solves

After porting shared state and agent databases to PostgreSQL, Doctor can warn that it cannot inspect working OpenAI OAuth profiles and suggest a general state repair.

## User Impact

Doctor can inspect stored Codex sign-in profiles on PostgreSQL. Missing profiles still get sign-in instructions, and inspection errors only get a repair hint when the underlying error recommends repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inspection was entering the agent database writer's setup, which tries to take a SQLite file snapshot. It now uses the existing PostgreSQL read-only worker path.

## Evidence

- On upstream main (`dda8da4b566`), focused Doctor lint reported a SQLite snapshot refusal and full lint reported a shared-state ownership conflict for both migrated agents. Both commands reported zero Codex findings with the patch.
- The new PostgreSQL CLI regression failed on main with the snapshot refusal and passed with the fix. PostgreSQL catalog verification, adjacent auth tests, core and extension type checks, lint, and formatting passed.
- Local author review traced the read and error paths through the final diff. No independent autoreview was run.

<details>
<summary>Doctor terminal output on the same two migrated agents</summary>

JSON is filtered to the Codex check. The full command also checks unrelated host configuration.

```console
# upstream base dda8da4b566
$ pnpm openclaw doctor --lint --json --only codex/native-profile-recovery
{
  "checksRun": 1,
  "findings": [
    {
      "checkId": "codex/native-profile-recovery",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "Could not inspect OpenAI auth profiles for agent \"main\": PostgreSQL cannot use SQLite file-snapshot; stop the Gateway and back up/restore the PostgreSQL schema with its matching anchor (P3-6 export support pending).",
      "fixHint": "openclaw doctor --fix"
    },
    {
      "checkId": "codex/native-profile-recovery",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "Could not inspect OpenAI auth profiles for agent \"worker\": PostgreSQL cannot use SQLite file-snapshot; stop the Gateway and back up/restore the PostgreSQL schema with its matching anchor (P3-6 export support pending).",
      "fixHint": "openclaw doctor --fix"
    }
  ]
}

# upstream base dda8da4b566
$ pnpm openclaw doctor --lint --json
{
  "checksRun": 47,
  "findings": [
    {
      "checkId": "codex/native-profile-recovery",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "Could not inspect OpenAI auth profiles for agent \"main\": Agent database execution belongs to another shared-state database; drain its existing resources before changing the state directory.",
      "fixHint": "openclaw doctor --fix"
    },
    {
      "checkId": "codex/native-profile-recovery",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "Could not inspect OpenAI auth profiles for agent \"worker\": Agent database execution belongs to another shared-state database; drain its existing resources before changing the state directory.",
      "fixHint": "openclaw doctor --fix"
    }
  ]
}

# PR head 2fbae92ebd6
$ node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json --only codex/native-profile-recovery
{
  "checksRun": 1,
  "findings": []
}

# PR head 2fbae92ebd6
$ node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json
{
  "checksRun": 47,
  "findings": []
}

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Published stable to pull request head with PostgreSQL state</summary>

The direct PostgreSQL upgrade was refused at schema admission. Store IDs and the synthetic profile fingerprint matched before and after the refusal. I then used the published stable CLI to port the fixture back to SQLite, ran Doctor from the head build on the same state directory, and ported it back to PostgreSQL. The hashes below cover the agent roster and normalized synthetic OAuth record. JSON is filtered to the fields shown.

OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15)
$ openclaw database port --to postgres --json

prs.title: fix(memory): keep Dreaming promotions trusted through later edits
prs.body:
Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164866
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180796 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/153426

## What Problem This Solves

A successful Dreaming promotion can change MEMORY.md without refreshing its artifact-provenance hash. The next clean tracked edit then marks the file untrusted and excludes it from automatic bootstrap context. This fixes that writer path, not the other writer or recovery work in the related issues.

## User Impact

Acknowledged promotion refreshes the hash so the next clean tracked edit preserves trusted memory eligibility. Previously untrusted files stay untrusted; hash continuity and quarantine are unchanged. There is no schema, configuration, retention, or migration change.

**Still draft:** the live proof below covers the previous head, not this core-ownership revision. A rerun on the new head, including upgrade from the latest stable with existing provenance rows, remains pending. Landing is left to a maintainer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Addresses [ClawSweeper's P2 finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201507#issuecomment-6994509032) and restores the ownership intent of [#126489](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126489): the packaged Memory Core provenance facade is read-only. Neither that facade nor the file-operation facade exposes the raw provenance recorder or clearer.

The existing local/IPC file publication implementation now lives in core at src/memory/memory-file-publication.ts. Core reads and checks the pre-image, performs the actual publication, and refreshes provenance through its private recorder. This is a file-publication operation, not a renamed recorder or a caller-supplied publication callback. All bundled callers use it; promotion markers remain plugin-owned. The old plugin publisher is removed, and shared mode/remote-maintenance helpers move with their owner rather than being duplicated.

The Gateway still owns provenance when files live remotely. Rejected or uncertain publication leaves the artifact row untouched. Known-committed failures retain committed semantics, including when recording fails after publication, so callers cannot roll back entry origins or replay a committed replacement. A crash or store failure between file publication and recording can still leave a conservative hash gap; no cross-filesystem/database transaction is introduced.

## Evidence

- The existing facade guard failed on the previous head `c5da6d82ea4d` because it exposed `recordMemoryArtifactWriteProvenance`. Both complete facade contract suites now pass. The regression additionally rejects raw recorder/clearer exports from the file-operation facade, while retaining the high-level publisher.
- Real-store promotion → clean tracked edit → bootstrap regression and all controls pass after the core move. Serialized file-client/worker tests cover remote success, known-committed errors, and lost replies; these are in-process IPC-contract tests, not live remote-Gateway proof.
- Broader focused run: **294 passed; one existing ACL case could not execute** across 18 files. The only failure was the setfacl-dependent case in workspace-file-mode.test.ts because setfacl is unavailable here. No skip or weakened assertion was added.
- Final publisher/error-path rerun: **19/19 passed** across the two promotion publication/provenance suites. Tests used `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks`. The final new regression file's seven test bodies took about 4.41s; the two-file run took 45.02s including cold worker preparation. Hosted CI timing is not yet available.
- Core production, extension production, extension-test, and plugin-platform test typechecks passed. Targeted lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. The assertion-safety check and pnpm build passed; a direct import of both built package facades also confirmed that raw provenance mutation is absent and the core publisher is available.
- The previous independent autoreview **did not complete** and was stopped at the requester's instruction; it has not been restarted. This revision does not claim a completed independent review. The hosted review linked above is the prior-head review whose P2 this revision addresses.
- Simplification: remove the raw SDK mutation export and the plugin-owned publisher, retaining one core publication owner and the existing trust algorithm. Against the base, production TypeScript is +143/-83 and tests are +277/-12, including the initial regression; most of the ownership repair is relocation and caller-import changes. The retired unsafe cast is replaced by the existing error-code extractor, and its old assertion-baseline allowance is removed rather than moved or expanded.

### Live proof — previous head

Revised head for the requested rerun: `f32f28475b4fb51601956429798bd02aa7935a32`.

[Holger's real-Gateway before/after CLI proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201507#issuecomment-6995176989) covers c5da6d82ea4d53b3f0ec5dd99e9ece511c7b937c on an isolated Linux Gateway with Dreaming enabled, Node 24.22.3, FTS-only search, default promotion thresholds, and real tracked write/edit tools driven by a deterministic mock model.

It reports a matching agent hash after CLI promotion, no duplicate on repeated apply, agent classification after the next clean tracked edit, and MEMORY.md in a fresh session's context. The previously-untrusted control remains untrusted and excluded. This does not establish the cause of the earlier production incident.

**Live gaps:**
- No scheduled/nightly Dreaming run.
- No live remote-workspace/IPC publication path (automated serialized coverage is separate).
- No upgrade-from-latest-stable check with existing provenance rows yet.
- No live publication-failure scenario.
- The proof must be rerun against the new head after this core-owned publication change. The requester will supply that rerun, including the upgrade check, as a PR comment.

The branch is frozen again at handoff unless the requester asks for changes. No merge is requested.

Worked on by:
- @holgergruenhagen

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/fdb36d42-abc9-44bd-8724-01d7b9d9462f)

prs.title: fix: show automation model warnings for the selected route
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reopening a saved automation’s Settings could tell you to refresh models even when its selected model was available. When that model really was unavailable, the same warning could hide the reason.

## User Impact

Settings keeps the selected model. A failed listing for another provider no longer looks like a problem with an available selection. If the selected route is known to be unavailable, the editor names its model and provider, explains why, and offers recovery. This is advice, not a new restriction on saving or running the job.

## Why This Change Was Made

A successful, agent-scoped Codex listing without a signed-in account is not a failed acquisition. The account remains unavailable and gains no readiness. Count failures from the original provider/native acquisitions, not from a display list that can contain a copy of the native outcome. Settings reads the selected route’s availability instead of throwing a catalog-wide status as a page error. Actual read and save errors keep their existing paths.

## Evidence

Chromium opened and reloaded `/cron?job=5e79bb17-64c2-460e-aba6-20937527f80b&tab=settings` against built, isolated Gateways on base `17f7164704570520b4f6bf27f91c01cad4cae513` and head `a4e8138f0608b028ad7b16f3485cc76327723df2`. Each page consumed its own `cron.get` and `models.list({agentId:"clawforce",view:"configured"})` responses. There was one saved, disabled `agentTurn` job, harmless text, isolated session target, and no delivery. No inference or job mutation occurred. The Gateway, plugins, catalog projection, scheduler store and UI were real; only external HTTP/stdio services and accounts were fixtures.

| Isolated case | Before | After (same saved selection) |
|---|---|---|
| Direct OpenAI signed out, Terra available through ClawRouter | Terra `available:true`; generic refresh warning | Same row and selection; no warning, `refreshFailed` and `refreshFailures` absent. Public OpenAI account outcome still `unavailable`. |
| Unrelated Codex `model/list` failed with JSON-RPC `-32603` | Terra `available:true`; generic warning | Terra still selected, no job warning. Explicit refresh still fails; Gateway and the page’s catalog response retain `refreshFailed:true`, `refreshFailures:[{acquisition:"native"}]`. |
| ClawRouter account missing; backup available | Terra row present but `available:false`, `unavailableReason:"missing-auth"`; generic warning | Same rows and selection. “GPT-6.1 Terra needs a ClawRouter account. Add one in Models or choose another model.” |

A separate ClawRouter catalog HTTP 401 did **not** make Terra unavailable for execution. The third case used a genuinely missing synthetic account, not the presence of that 401 or of a model row.

**Keep #199137.** Same source, fixture, state, and browser UI, with only `186db3a17736cf5dc7cb528c654b27b9af6ae59f` reversed: explicit refresh aborted on the empty `{}` with `AgentHarnessPreflightError`, before any Codex RPC. With the patch present, refresh completed. The saved Settings screen showed the same generic warning both ways. That patch changes the legacy auth-file guard, not the UI. The November 17 report on `5484e18dab2b` and later observation on `58cd522` are consistent with the fixture; they do not establish which historical acquisition triggered it.

### Saved Settings: available Terra, signed out of direct OpenAI

Before

![Before: available Terra selected with a catalog-wide error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc3380c4-a887-4da0-9a93-c04efdcd1c3e)

After

![After: the same job and selection without the misleading warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20fa22ad-c63f-4a08-98b8-2d0ea49826e9)

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The general error above the editor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e03843b-8a11-416a-845c-96c92bf024e5) | ![The original model selection retained](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75a9cd1d-ba29-4872-a2a7-cf0c5ff44e23) |

### Control: the selected ClawRouter route is genuinely unavailable

![Terra needs a ClawRouter account; recovery is beside the model control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c7118a4-f714-4fa9-bdf2-a346178750b7)

<details>
<summary>Request-correlated payload excerpts, commands, and independent review</summary>

**Published-head replay:** The publisher added an attribution-only commit, `a55b122000abe8ad74d8f145fddcf3c43d26ec77` (identical reviewed tree). We rebuilt this exact SHA with `pnpm build:runtime`, verified its build stamp, then opened and reloaded the same saved job for all three cases again. All wire and DOM assertions passed in all six documents; browser-observed job mutations: zero.

| Exact published HEAD, reopened Settings | Page’s `cron.get` → `models.list` request IDs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Signed out | `18:e566d6d4-2545-499e-8e8b-59738505ccb0` → `25:f3073551-d74c-47c3-bc44-21a45c0a2fbf` | Terra available, no false refresh failure or job warning |
| Unrelated listing failed | `19:98686df2-4c2e-4039-90a8-7389231b13e8` → `24:776e7110-38aa-47e4-b82a-d2746a92b9ee` | Terra available, native failure retained, no job warning |
| ClawRouter account missing | `17:1c514d0c-148c-4ae9-82b3-e307e331dcc5` → `24:9b52dbec-4094-4c55-a8e7-bbd09712a2e2` | Explicit `available:false, unavailableReason:"missing-auth"`, backup available, route-specific recovery |

All browser scenarios used `payload.model:"clawrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-terra"`; the returned row was `{provider:"clawrouter",id:"openai/gpt-6.1-terra"}`. `openai` is not this route’s provider. The fixed reopened `cron.get` / `models.list` IDs were:

- Signed out: `19:a42e426c-c5bc-4b9a-ae78-4f0cd39f7433` / `24:2053fbc9-c4c7-4998-a88b-2551107b85dd`; before catalog `24:19cdd968-2146-422e-aee5-d9da5a6532d5`.
- Unrelated failure: `19:bd17a379-99e5-40ac-80d7-f3e12b3c19d6` / `24:b423cc3b-fa80-4ac5-9215-11a4381fe4a1`; before catalog `24:89f27afa-9920-497c-a7e0-015450386988`.
- Missing ClawRouter account: `18:aa309763-bf96-42b7-a143-f8da3d3328ce` / `25:b5ac5584-32c7-49ea-87c8-5d6d6142bd71`; before catalog `24:eaf6a431-8dd4-4c73-bee8-2ccca1517665`.

Baseline explicit refresh `3:0754feea-4460-4387-8082-41201f56710d`: router HTTP 200; native `account/read` → `{account:null,requiresOpenaiAuth:true}`; `model/list` → `{data:[],nextCursor:null}`; final `account/read` still signed out. At the projection boundary provider inventory was `[]`, native inventory was `{codex:[{provider:"openai",status:"unavailable"}]}`, and the latter appeared in projected `providerOutcomes`. The full view labeled both failures `openai`; the configured view kept both acquisition kinds but omitted their provider labels. Fixed explicit refresh `3:928eeeac-579d-4d56-b337-320dca4b5029` saw the same raw RPC success. The native observation carried a private `no-account` reason, and neither acquisition was reported failed.

Guard-off explicit refresh `3:c453d89c-3e65-4d2c-aea2-1aa2783de8e6` reached the router but never started Codex. Retained read `5:f32e7deb-bd1f-4d8d-a53e-4dfb1ae67fe8` and browser `25:66563309-63d2-4d0f-9b51-8122891a4a80` still served available Terra with a native failure. Fixed unrelated explicit refresh `3:81216dad-0d49-4c6e-a146-86e60b408b7f`: router HTTP 200; native `account/read` succeeded; `model/list` returned `error.code:-32603`. Unknown is not relabeled as an auth failure. The full request-correlated sanitized packet was delivered in the work session.

- Matched builds: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build:runtime`; guard-off used `git show --format= 186db3a17736 | git apply -R` in a separate checkout of the same base. The empty legacy file was unchanged throughout.
- Checked-in real-Gateway browser regression: `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/model-catalog-partial-refresh.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **2 passed** on the built head. Focused catalog/Codex tests: **51 passed**; cron lifecycle/notifications: **35 passed**. Codex absent-account and saved-editor controls were red before the repair. Targeted lint, formatting, core/UI/extensions typechecks, and i18n verification passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview, P0–P2: **no actionable findings**. The complete 14-file diff was byte-verified against the committed tree `e3c04d29fca6d6586c7733c0d5de76af08b57092` (patch SHA-256 `9f215b8358c2250e16feab009191ddc0f1a7a79980491561467465378f2df961`).

</details>

Reported and reproduced with @hannesrudolph.

prs.title: fix(update): restore WAL journal mode after database rollback
prs.body:
Fixes #202772

## What Problem This Solves

Update rollback restores verified SQLite snapshot images, and those images are single DELETE-journal files by design. Restoring them as-is left every database in `journal_mode=DELETE` on a WAL-policy filesystem (local APFS/ext4), so the next update's activation Doctor failed to acquire its maintenance lease (`store unavailable (sqlite-busy)` against the updater's own readers) and every retry rolled back into the same broken state until the operator converted the files by hand.

## Why This Change Was Made

After publishing each restored database, the rollback now re-establishes the journal mode that `resolvePathJournalPolicy()` resolves for its path while the database exclusion window still keeps every other holder out. The client credential store is excluded — its exclusive custody design requires DELETE mode, and the credential restore path verifies exactly that. A conversion failure fails the rollback loudly after all files have been attempted, naming the exact recovery (`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` while no process holds the files) instead of leaving the failure loop invisible.

## User Impact

A failed-and-rolled-back update no longer poisons the next update attempt: restored databases return to the same journal mode they had before the snapshot, so the following update's Doctor acquires its maintenance lease normally. Credential-store custody semantics are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real update CLI protocol on a scratch `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (Linux, Node 26.12.1): a **v2026.11.6** (`06afb10d32`) gateway created the WAL state; `openclaw update migrate --backup-root` snapshotted 4 databases (receipt JSON reported); `openclaw update restore --backup-root` executed the real rollback.

| Phase | Build | Observation after `update restore` |
|---|---|---|
| RED | v2026.11.6 (unpatched) | `state/openclaw.sqlite → {"journal_mode":"delete"}` — the bug reproduces through the shipped protocol |
| GREEN | this branch (`edfd2dfbeb`) | `state/openclaw.sqlite → {"journal_mode":"wal"}` and `client/credentials.sqlite → {"journal_mode":"delete"}` — WAL re-established per policy while custody semantics stay intact |

Red/green unit regression (`pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/update-database-restore.test.ts`, 24/24 pass at head `edfd2dfbeb`): "restores databases back to the filesystem's WAL journal policy" fails on the unpatched restore (`expected { journal_mode: 'delete' } to deeply equal { journal_mode: 'wal' }`) and passes with the fix, including the credential-store DELETE exclusion. `test-lines` ratchet: net +23, allocation credit 23 via `config/test-lines-allocations/202772-update-rollback-wal.txt`.

Gap: the reporter's macOS/APFS host and the live npm-global update loop were not reproduced here (Linux host, supervised migrate/restore protocol); the sqlite-busy Doctor failure itself is asserted by the issue's forensics and follows from the DELETE mode this fix removes.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and git log to analyze issue #202772, locate the rollback restore path in `src/infra/update-database-restore.ts`, and implement the policy-driven journal-mode re-establishment with the credential-store exclusion. The implementer understands the code: restored snapshot images are DELETE-journal by design, the exclusion window makes this process the only holder, and `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` on each restored non-credential database returns it to its pre-snapshot mode. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.
