prs.title: fix: let unpinned automations use live inference accounts
prs.body:
Related: #202699 (first, non-breaking cut)

## What Problem This Solves

An automation created without a recorded inference account can stop running after its session switches to a stored account, even though an interactive turn works. The same refusal blocks otherwise valid fallback routes and some credential types at creation.

## User Impact

Unbound automations can use the account an interactive turn would select instead of failing with “Automation has no recorded inference account.” **Existing recorded bindings—including automatically captured ones—remain authoritative.** Explicit model/account choices, account replacement/revocation checks, native-CLI credential isolation, schedules and run history are preserved. No migration or manual adoption is required for unbound jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the refusal rather than build another account-authorization system around it. Remove its startup warning and Doctor adoption/check; keep Doctor's recorded-account upgrade restoration. Reuse the existing live-selection planner and fallback chain. Creation-time binding capture and `current` target behavior are unchanged.

This deliberately does **not** soften existing bindings or stop capturing them for new jobs. Those change a working path and belong in a separate change.

## Evidence

- **82 tests passed across all six selected files on `e074ade1a0a53ef0cad0e1b4c9620af9219cfdaa`**, in a Mac Studio Crabbox `local-container` lease: 26 infra, 54 cron and 2 Doctor tests. Regression expectations fail on the base.
- Independent Astra review of the implementation and final private-helper export cleanup: no verified P0–P2 findings. Static review, not a substitute for runtime proof.
- Changed-file format, lint, production/test typechecks and other ratchets passed. The dead-export guard still reports `src/infra/gateway-resource-profile.ts: LEAN_PROFILE_MEMORY_THRESHOLD_BYTES`; reproduced identically on base `e5ccb878a104636e931255675363b4b5fcc9d53d`, in an untouched file. It is not claimed green.
- Real isolated Gateways on the Studio were compared on base and fix against a **synthetic OpenAI Responses endpoint**. Five cases completed: both recorded-account paths and the configured-key path were unchanged; the session-switch and fallback refusals became successful runs. See captured results below. This is not real-model proof.
- **Draft / blocked:** the real external OpenAI attempt reached the service after the fix, but returned HTTP 401; its automation failed authentication. No real-model success is claimed. A router credential-availability preflight returned HTTP 403; no inference was sent there.
- A focused session run using the maintained SSE fixture confirmed the **main request uses B** (1024-token limit). The smaller A request is the existing Activity recap utility completion: its 240-token limit and exact 1490-character encoded system content match the unchanged [recap owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e074ade1a0a53ef0cad0e1b4c9620af9219cfdaa/src/gateway/session-activity-summaries.ts#L76-L86) and [utility completion call](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e074ade1a0a53ef0cad0e1b4c9620af9219cfdaa/src/gateway/session-activity-summaries.ts#L385-L420). This is not the main automation turn switching accounts.
- Original logs and run records are retained. Managed artifact upload returned HTTP 401, so there is **no claimed downloadable artifact bundle**; captured observations are attached inline below. No UI change: screenshots not applicable. Earlier failed harness setups are not product proof.

### Captured Studio Gateway comparison

| Scenario | Base | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Unbound session job after explicit account switch | Refused before provider request | Succeeded on B; separate Activity recap on utility account A |
| Explicit account A after default/order drift | Succeeded on A | Succeeded on A |
| Automatically captured account A after drift | Succeeded on A | Succeeded on A |
| Configured-key route | Succeeded | Succeeded |
| Failing configured-key primary, stored-account fallback | Fallback refused | Fallback succeeded |

Read-only SQLite snapshots confirmed `source: "user"` and `source: "auto"` account-A bindings in the second and third cases; no binding was synthesized by modifying stored state. Delivery was disabled.

<details>
<summary>Captured run records and external-provider result</summary>

```text
Base: e5ccb878a104636e931255675363b4b5fcc9d53d
Fix:  e074ade1a0a53ef0cad0e1b4c9620af9219cfdaa
Provider: Crabbox local-container, launched on the Mac Studio
Image: node:24.22.1-trixie
Image digest: sha256:f1e034976f948cf212ef1f659c12e5dd58ac7eab947831813e81a62401ca38be

Six-file tests:
  lease cbx_2afa94a200b0
  run run_9a18ff4e7feaed7580efab8529345a4a
  infra: 2/2 files, 26/26 tests
  cron: 3/3 files, 54/54 tests
  Doctor: 1/1 files, 2/2 tests
  unit-exit=0; leaseStopped=true

Gateway comparison + live attempt:
  lease cbx_79da8fd8a92f
  run run_81fda8622732694afa156cc63a04f084
  command duration 478705 ms; leaseStopped=true
  base real-model session case: status=error, completion=failed,
    no provider request (unrecorded-account refusal)
  fixed real-model session case:
    POST /openai/v1/responses model=gpt-4.1 alias=stored-b HTTP 401
    POST /openai/v1/responses model=gpt-4.1 alias=stored-a HTTP 401
    status=error, completion=failed (authentication)

Focused account-attribution check (same fixed head, maintained SSE fixture):
  lease cbx_6cc22244a6cb
  run run_aa141bfc8faabc3a8d421f4a0497b0ad
  main request: alias=stored-b, max_output_tokens=1024
  Activity recap: alias=stored-a, max_output_tokens=240,
    encoded system-content length=1490 (exact source match)
  automation status=ok, completion=succeeded; leaseStopped=true
```

The pass-through relay resolves synthetic aliases to one task-authorized real API credential at egress; it does not establish distinct billing identities. It logged aliases/statuses, never credentials or headers. Harness command exit zero is not a passing real-model verdict: per-case failure above is authoritative. No external chat message was sent.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Focused command and file walkthrough</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-continuity.integration.test.ts \
  src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts \
```

prs.title: fix: explain why computer use is unavailable on text-only models
prs.body:
Closes #202433.

## What Problem This Solves

A text-only model cannot use the computer tool. The session capability list
can still say the tool is available, so the user has no reason to switch models.

## User Impact

The capability list identifies image input as the missing requirement for the
selected model. Existing tool-policy exclusions keep their own reasons.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the selected model's input metadata when building the capability list.
That lets the existing tool builder enforce the same vision requirement in
the preview and at runtime. Add the reason to the tool access report.

## Evidence

At `8d0cd99f4b09`, the real inventory builder listed `computer` for a
text-only model. With the fix, the text-only model reports that it cannot
accept image input. A model with image input still lists `computer`.
The test uses local model fixtures without a provider request or a paired desktop.
The three focused suites passed all 19 tests on Windows with Node 24.22.3.
The new file took 58.1 s including test setup and transformation.
Core typechecking and the touched-file lint and format checks passed.

```sh
pnpm test src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.computer.test.ts src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.test.ts src/agents/tools/session-status-capabilities.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

### Running Gateway proof

Built the QA runtime with `pnpm build qaRuntime` and started
`node openclaw.mjs gateway run` with a fresh state directory on Windows
(Node 24.22.3). The build used base `8d0cd99f4b09` plus the three review
patches in this local batch. The inventory source file matched this PR's
head `bad375fae610` byte for byte.

Configured two local model definitions with `input: ["text"]` and
`input: ["text", "image"]` and set the tool profile to `full`.
Created a separate session per model through `sessions.create` with the
model explicitly selected. Queried each with
`openclaw gateway call tools.effective --params '{"agentId":"main","sessionKey":"<session key>"}' --json`.
The provider URL was local and the inventory requests made no inference calls.

Redacted projection of the two RPC responses (`listed` checks
`groups[].tools[]` and the other fields come from `toolAccess`):

```text
review-local/text-only  listed=false  status=unavailable  reason="The selected model does not support image input"
review-local/vision     listed=true   status=available    reasons=[]
```

Red-on-base: with only this PR's regression test applied to
`8d0cd99f4b09`, the following command exited 1 with
`expected [ 'agents_list', 'apply_patch', …(39) ] to not include 'computer'`.
The same test passed with the production fix.

```sh
pnpm test src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.computer.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: fix: open legacy session links from the terminal
prs.body:
Closes #202569.

## What Problem This Solves

An older Control UI link can open in the browser and return
`No session found` in the terminal when its literal key looks like a short ID.

## User Impact

`openclaw tui` and `openclaw attach` can reuse those links to open an
existing session. If the short ID matches more than one session, the CLI
still asks the user to disambiguate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The URL parser already provides the exact key. Keep it through CLI
resolution and ask the same Gateway for that key after a short lookup
reports no match.

## Evidence

At `8d0cd99f4b09`, the production CLI resolver returned
`No session found: deadbeef` for `/chat/ops/release-deadbeef`.
The same local Gateway response fixture resolves the exact key after the change.
The suite also checks that ambiguous short IDs still stop resolution. The
three focused suites passed all 56 tests on Windows with Node 24.22.3
(61.2 s runner time). Core typechecking and the touched-file lint and format
checks passed.

```sh
pnpm test src/cli/session-ref.test.ts src/cli/session-target.test.ts src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

### Running Gateway proof

Built the QA runtime with `pnpm build qaRuntime` and started
`node openclaw.mjs gateway run` with a fresh state directory on Windows
(Node 24.22.3). The build used base `8d0cd99f4b09` plus the three review
patches in this local batch. The two changed CLI source files matched this
PR's head `8355e969898e` byte for byte.

Created `agent:main:release-deadbeef` through the running Gateway's
`sessions.create` RPC. In that same Gateway, called `sessions.resolve`
with `{"shortId":"deadbeef","slugHint":"release","allowMissing":true}`.
Then ran the built CLI against the legacy URL using an explicit Gateway
token and a 30 s grant lifetime. The loopback address and tokens are
redacted below. The final line is a projection of the printed config.

```text
sessions.resolve (short ID) -> {"ok":false}
node openclaw.mjs attach http://<loopback>/chat/main/release-deadbeef --token <redacted> --ttl 30000 --print-config
exit=0  sessionKey=agent:main:release-deadbeef  scopedGrantIssued=true
```

The CLI opened the existing literal session key after the Gateway's short-ID
miss. I revoked the scoped grant after checking the returned config.

prs.title: fix: report terminal errors in model fallback logs
prs.body:
Related: #201443

## What Problem This Solves

After the primary model fails, a backup model can return a terminal error while the fallback log says `candidate_succeeded`. That makes the log disagree with the error shown in chat.

## User Impact

The fallback log shows when a backup stopped with an error. The original error reply is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run entry records a chain stop when the result has a failed terminal status and no retry classification. The existing checks for retry eligibility still apply.

## Evidence

I sent a turn through the built CLI to an isolated Gateway with synthetic providers. The primary returned HTTP 402. The backup ran a workspace write and then returned a terminal error. The CLI preserved the failure reply, and the Gateway stopped the fallback chain.

```text
build-stamp {"head": "927df2e1ff9ebe52a96f046485eb10e48a39d7f8", "inputsClean": true}
model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=proof-primary/proof-primary candidate=proof-primary/proof-primary reason=billing next=proof-backup/proof-backup
model fallback chain stopped: reason=returned_terminal_error candidate=proof-backup/proof-backup
agent {"status": "error", "isError": true, "replyExcerpt": "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply."}
agent.wait {"status": "error", "terminalReply": "fixture_terminal: Synthetic terminal failure"}
provider requests ["proof-primary", "proof-backup", "proof-backup"]
candidate_succeeded events 0
third-model requests 0
```

The original regression reproduced the false success on `1fae66036cc`. The error-only payload case also failed on `19f84ca7f1e`, where the terminal status was `ok`. On the follow-up, both regressions pass. An error-only reply without terminal metadata now reports `error` and keeps the original payload. The follow-up passed 65 focused tests, core typechecking, targeted lint, formatting, and the runtime build. The original change passed 230 focused tests.

The Gateway fixture covers billing followed by a terminal failure after tool execution. The reporter's live provider rotation and transcript collision remain unverified.

prs.title: fix: keep automatic memory saves out of project repositories
prs.body:
Related: #161253
Related alternative implementation: #162142 by leapdragon.

## What Problem This Solves

When a conversation runs in a selected project or managed worktree, automatic memory saves can create and write daily notes inside that repository instead of the configured agent workspace. This dirties the checkout and risks accidentally committing personal memory alongside project changes.

## User Impact

Automatic file-based memory saves stay in the configured agent workspace while ordinary turns retain their project context. Existing project-local memory is not moved or deleted; users should review any previously misplaced notes themselves. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the configured agent workspace at memory-flush preparation and use it consistently for the maintenance-only working directory, detached transcript, target creation, and execution. Tools-based memory plans retain their existing execution context.

For sandboxed flushes, the detached maintenance session owns the workspace identity while the original session still supplies the sandbox policy. Ordinary worktree containment checks remain in place.

This is our alternative to #162142: rather than carrying a new bootstrap workspace field through queued follow-up runs, it resolves the workspace at the maintenance owner and also handles the current sandbox identity/policy boundary. Credit to leapdragon for the related work; the other implementation was inspected, not executed, so this is not a claim that it fails. The memory documentation now explains placement and treatment of existing project notes.

## Evidence

- **Deterministic reproduction before the fix:** the real flush preparation, runtime/tool assembly, and append writer ran with a synthetic streaming provider. The aligned-workspace control passed; both selected-project cases (main and nondefault agents) wrote into the project instead of agent memory. These regressions pass with the fix.
- **Real UI verification after the fix:** the committed candidate Gateway and Control UI, built-in OpenClaw runtime, and an approved OpenAI subscription completed automatic memory saves for both a direct project and a managed worktree. Nonempty notes appeared only in agent memory; existing project/worktree notes remained byte-identical. Subsequent ordinary turns retained the correct project context. The documented flush threshold was lowered for the test; conversation compaction itself is not claimed. This is deterministic-red/live-green evidence, not a live-model before/after comparison.
- **Focused checks:** final affected-boundary batch: 72 tests across four files passed. An earlier broader batch passed 132 tests across 11 files; it was not wholly rerun after the final sandbox correction, and these overlapping counts must not be added. Targeted typechecks, lint, formatting, documentation sanity, and whitespace checks passed.
- **Container persistence:** two real rootless Podman cases passed with a synthetic provider, verifying agent-root mounts and durable writes, preserved project files, ordinary ownership rejection, and read-only flush skipping. This does not cover Docker or a full ordinary-worktree container lifecycle.
- **Review:** independent read-only agent review inspected every changed hunk in the nine-file local candidate based on `69bc33255cee52904ef42fe27acfdb79d060b740`, subsequently committed as `da0e5cca9d6106ee76aff3eecac28243ba4a2ce8`. No defect findings remained. This was not canonical autoreview, ClawSweeper, or maintainer/security approval; reviewers did not independently rerun the reported tests.
- **Build:** full build exited successfully; the committed-head rebuild also exited successfully and reused the Control UI content cache. The earlier build reported four nonfatal UI-budget findings (largest CSS gzip, total CSS gzip/raw, and chat boot request count). No base comparison attributed these findings to this change; they are not claimed resolved.

**Validation limitations:** the first live attempt selected native Codex implicitly and did not enter this maintenance path; configuring the intended built-in OpenClaw runtime corrected the test setup. Test isolation was imperfect: an initial container attempt created a generated skill mirror outside the task root and was rejected as isolated proof; the corrected run's mounts were verified. During live setup, Doctor deleted 58 shared legacy archive-cache files outside the isolated profile. Deleted contents were not recovered and downstream impact was not established. Isolated Gateway shutdown also reported plugin cleanup errors; task processes and listener were subsequently verified stopped. These observations are disclosed, not attributed to this patch or claimed fixed.

Hosted CI and applicable sensitive-product-change approval remain pending; no upstream validation is claimed.

## Inspectable behavior evidence

Captured on 2026-11-18; these are excerpts from retained outputs, not a new run. Live Gateway/Control UI proof used committed head `da0e5cca9d6106ee76aff3eecac28243ba4a2ce8`; the candidate build stamp and build-info matched that head. The Podman run preceded the commit on the same retained candidate source snapshot, not a separate committed-head rerun.

Each Podman case had its own temporary root, shown as `<CASE_ROOT>` within that case. Paths are replaced with `<LIVE_ROOT>` / `<CASE_ROOT>` / `<CONTAINER_ROOT>`; private model labels and irrelevant UI chrome are omitted. File contents and SHA-256 values below are unchanged synthetic fixture data. No raw configuration, credentials, endpoints, or private diagnostic logs are attached.

Setup: built-in OpenClaw runtime, real approved subscription inference, `agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.forceFlushTranscriptBytes=1`. Each scenario used ordinary UI turns, not a direct flush invocation. The agent-memory directory started empty; the captured note appeared after the first ordinary reply, before its follow-up. The automatic maintenance transcript is detached and is not displayed in the ordinary chat. These file captures plus the visible follow-up text are the retained behavioral evidence; this is not a recording of the hidden maintenance turn.

```typescript
          workspaceDir:agentWorkspace,cwd:agentWorkspace,config:cfg})).rejects.toThrow("Local sandbox managed workspace owner changed");
```

</details>

**Scope and limits:** deterministic pre-fix regression plus live after-fix proof, not live-model before/after. Lowering the memory-flush threshold does not demonstrate conversation compaction. Read-only coverage is flush admission skipping, not a guest write rejection. Docker and a complete successful ordinary-worktree container lifecycle were not exercised. The isolation/setup/shutdown incidents disclosed above still apply; only the corrected Podman run is included here. Maintainer security approval and hosted CI remain separate gates.

Closes #201390

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, Doctor tells you to run `--fix` for stray launchd jobs even when that invocation will refuse the repair. A relocated state directory can put you in that loop.

## User Impact

Doctor explains why it cannot remove the jobs and gives you a next step. Gateway status directs you to Doctor for cleanup guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor uses the same eligibility checks for its advice and for the repair. The repair still verifies each job against launchd before unloading it and keeps operator plists.


## Evidence

Native `launchctl print` found the job loaded with the same plist hash after each command.

prs.title: fix: preserve memory trust after Claude CLI file edits
prs.body:
Refs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180796
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165452, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/153426

## What Problem This Solves

Explicitly selected native Claude `Edit`/`Write` can change saved memory without updating its provenance, causing the next clean edit to quarantine it. CLI loopback and native network results could also lose turn taint, allowing untrusted memory to retain agent trust.

## User Impact

Local Claude CLI memory writes retain their hash continuity and turn origin: clean tracked files remain eligible for automatic memory, while tainted, non-owner, and already-quarantined files remain untrusted. Native tool permissions do not expand; Agent/Workflow-only selections still deny native Edit/Write.

This does not rehabilitate existing quarantine, change the schema or hash-continuity rule, or track shell writes, paired-node writes, or other harnesses' native tools. The session-rooted tool-builder repair is separate in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201509.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share one host-owned admitted-turn taint state across CLI events, transcript recording, native observations, and loopback write/edit/apply_patch. Capture the canonical preimage after an allowed native `PreToolUse` and observe the actual file after successful `PostToolUse` through the existing provenance owner. Native execution and rollback remain native-owned.

The P1 follow-up reuses the backend's existing `projectNativeToolAuthority` capability mapping to classify native network results, including Claude `WebFetch` and `WebSearch` when no projected MCP network-tool metadata exists. It does not guess from native tool spelling or accept client-supplied taint. MCP and display-only events do not acquire native capability metadata. Simplification retained the existing owners; no new capability API, store, schema, or recovery path was added.

## Evidence

### Current repair

- Native WebFetch and WebSearch regressions failed against prior PR head `44fd853a85b0ffeed0ca9ba01d6efeded374f458`: provenance remained `agent` after native mutation and a clean tracked follow-up, and the root files remained in bootstrap. They pass with this repair.
- The regressions use the production Claude backend's metadata, actual stdio transport and parser/event/tracking path, actual PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks, a synthetic native executable, and real filesystem/provenance/bootstrap. They seed `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, and `memory/nested/note.md`. Native-only cases intentionally have no projected MCP network metadata. Clean, non-owner, stale-hash/quarantine, failed-mutation, retired-callback, and Agent/Workflow-only controls remain covered; separate controls reject name-only, MCP, and display-only classification.
- Focused native, loopback, taint, transcript, permission, and protocol suites: **160 tests across 9 files passed**. The final native fixture also passed all **6 cases** after the small test-table simplification. Commands used `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks`.
- Core and affected agent-test type lanes, scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. An initial lint preparation hit the host's OS-thread limit; the same supported lint path passed with `GOMAXPROCS=2`. No checks were disabled.

### Real Claude proof — prior combined build

[Holger's live proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201478#issuecomment-6995176499) reports 20 real Claude CLI turns on an isolated Gateway. Before: `da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf`. After: this PR's **old head `44fd853a85b0` plus PR #201509 head `8cd5bf449788`, merged locally**. All live turns were owner turns via `chat.send` with `operator.admin`.

That proof covers clean and network-tainted **loopback** writes, native Edit/Write hash continuity and bootstrap eligibility, failed native edits, sticky quarantine after shell-induced hash drift, and Agent/Workflow-only denial. It supersedes the previous blanket statement that no real Claude proof had been performed, but **does not cover the native-network P1 flow or this new head**.

Coverage limits:
- The native Edit/Write live runs used **agent-level** `tools.exec.host: "node"` while Claude still ran locally. **Per-session** `execHost: "node"` instead selected paired-node placement and failed without a paired node (`missing execNode`). Paired-node writes remain out of scope.
- A missed PostToolUse and a retired callback/grant could not be forced live; those remain synthetic-boundary controls.
- **Required live rerun on head `5656d83c6340d84137ced409b63fafc0682193ff`:** native WebFetch/WebSearch → native Edit/Write → clean tracked edit → provenance and fresh-session bootstrap checks. This rerun remains reserved to Holger; prior-head combined-build proof is not current-head proof.

### Review status

[ClawSweeper's P1 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201478#issuecomment-6993425706) covers old head `44fd853a85b0` and identified the native-network defect addressed here. It is prior-head review evidence, not a fresh review of this repair. The earlier Auto Review helper was unavailable; no clean local review or new hosted re-review is claimed. **Remain draft: live rerun and current-head independent/security review are pending. No landing performed.**

Contributor: Holger Gruenhagen (@holgergruenhagen).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @holgergruenhagen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/692b31b0-d814-47d4-aa85-65f70a3d4c48)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f5c7778d-2e4d-4562-9405-715610c495a5)

## Worked on by

- @holgergruenhagen

prs.title: fix(templates): preserve Unicode in template draft inventory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When drafting a Template from an agent, an emoji or multilingual text in the agent inventory can turn into replacement characters if its UTF-8 bytes arrive in separate CLI output chunks. The inventory can still look valid and feed the damaged identity text into the draft flow.

## User Impact

Create a Template preserves names, emoji, and other Unicode text in the inventory it uses to prepare a draft.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inventory now sets UTF-8 encoding on child stdout so Node's streaming decoder carries partial characters across chunk boundaries before parsing the JSON. All inventory lookups pass through this reader. [Node documents this behavior for readable streams.](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.20.0/docs/api/stream.html#readablesetencodingencoding)

## Evidence

I ran the bundled inventory script on Linux with Node 24.18.0. A fixture child process running the `agents list` lookup wrote valid JSON to a real stdout pipe in two writes, with the split after the first byte of the four-byte `🧭` emoji.

| Inventory script | Split write | Single-write control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upstream base `eac13241108` | `����` | `🧭` |
| Fixed | `🧭` | `🧭` |

All four runs preserved the ASCII identity name `Research assistant`. The standalone probe ran `node "$workspace/before.mjs" "$workspace" --agent demo --draft 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 --json`, repeated it with `after.mjs`, and read `.agent` from stdout. Only the child CLI responses and chunk timing were supplied by the fixture. The probe ended at inventory output, before the Control UI review card.

The regression command `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/create-template-inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` failed on the base with four replacement characters and passed with the fix in 3.10 seconds wall time. Targeted oxfmt, oxlint, Node syntax, and diff checks passed. Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P3 issues. The production change replaces one line and the existing test covers the split pipe.

AI-assisted.

prs.title: feat: dismiss browser completion notifications after viewing replies
prs.body:
Related: #202178

## What Problem This Solves

Browser/PWA completion notifications can remain after the corresponding reply has been read, leaving stale alerts to dismiss manually.

## User Impact and Read Boundaries

Dismiss only the notification for an exact final reply visibly viewed in the foreground. Preserve unrelated sessions, newer/unseen replies and legacy alerts without reliable identity. Cleanup is local to the same browser/service-worker registration, not cross-device recall.

Payload and transcript identity match on agent/session/run/message/recipient. Message identity prefers the persisted idempotency key and otherwise uses the row ID. Session opening, history loading and notification tags alone do not acknowledge a completion.

The layout review finding is corrected: read presentation requires an active row, settled initial position and release of the transcript's hidden state. Resource preparation remains independently enabled. Layout/foreground/connection/profile ownership fences queued callbacks synchronously.

At most 512 page-memory visibility receipts are retained for six minutes (five-minute push TTL plus margin). The worker's after-display hint reconciles late pushes while a page is visible. Closing all pages forgets receipts; there is no durable cross-restart acknowledgement guarantee. Support is limited to the serving Gateway's origin and registration scope.

## Evidence

Current head: `45b07b2be25bbbeddafde2ba4511c3a15f88bd12`.

- [Final-head formatting, allocation and input-equivalence proof](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44847422160): **passed**. The runner verified the exact formatter-only transformation from the preceding tested head plus allocation 704 → 706, with every other tracked entry unchanged. No browser/test rerun is claimed at this formatting-only head.
- [Behavioral proof at 81b1d5daa9e6853930dd70637261d89998ecda84](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44846626872): Chromium upgrade/notification test, 2 identity tests, 8 runtime tests and the required scoped canonical lint wrapper **passed**. That run's sole failure was the formatter line-wrap now corrected and verified above.
- Chromium installs the pinned released v2026.11.5 worker, retains its identity-less notification, updates the same registration without clearing storage, verifies the running candidate's embedded build identity, and preserves exact legacy notification data. It then verifies unread/newer/other-session preservation, exact foreground-read dismissal, emulated foreground return and delayed-delivery reconciliation. Listener installation is acknowledged before injection. The redundant key-inequality test was removed; observable identity-separation coverage remains.
- Reuse inventory SHA-256 versus the behavioral head, excluding only the exactly verified formatter/allocation files: `ce5102240c16f636e511e8c8dca8085292eeede95f053412ec2497073a982668`. Final browser-test bytes SHA-256: `18202c2d781d9021027d5964ed34384d218bb82a836d343eb5403646085ed1e4`.
- Production/dependency/configuration inputs independently match the previously tested layout repair at `e0b0cb680c18b19585d52f72d65cb00e5f9dab89`; only two tests, the historical worker fixture and allocation differ. Inventory SHA-256: `8de953c2417347cb9d5fd655abe535e218627ef3b20b9b79feaa5675f36cc227`. The [full production build and real-renderer regression](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44801786340), [affected layout suites, UI production types and UI build](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44800188759), and independently unchanged [core-type proof](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44797497267) retain their original scopes. Historical format/lint failures in the core-type run were separately repaired; its entire run is not described as passing.
- The real-renderer regression covers hidden initial positioning, settlement, inactive preparation/forecast rows, queued callbacks, parking and disposal.
- Final ratchet: 1,106 net test lines, 400 allowance plus 706 explicit allocation. The pinned historical-worker fixture is separate from test logic. No assertions, checks or baselines were disabled.

## Tested Scope and Remaining Decisions

This is desktop Chromium behavior using real ServiceWorker/Notification APIs, CDP-injected push, mocked Gateway transport and emulated visibility transitions. It does not establish real encrypted Web Push transport, native OS notification shade/suspension, Safari/mobile behavior, or a complete old UI/Gateway upgrade. No device access or mobile acceptance is claimed. Android-specific validation is not automatically a prerequisite for this browser feature; the stated tested scope remains for reviewer acceptance.

[Final-head upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44847326518) remains `action_required`; maintainer admission and required upstream results are separate from the fork evidence. Maintainer acceptance of automatic exact-read dismissal, receipt lifetime/capacity and serving-origin scope remains pending.

Previously disclosed non-failing test-length and CSS/chat-boot diagnostics remain. Renderer Solid strict-read warnings were [traced to unchanged lifecycle call sites](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44803275112); no warning suppression, baseline runtime comparison or performance improvement is claimed.

prs.title: feat: keep unused Knowledge workers asleep in lean mode
prs.body:
Fixes #202378. Related #202373. Originally **Stacked on #202422**, now merged as `28aa5c88fd45`; this PR targets `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Under the updated auto-selection rule, Gateways with less than 8 GiB of effective memory—including ordinary 4 GiB and sub-8 GiB laptops and VPSes—get lean by default regardless of CPU count; watched Knowledge vaults keep watching.

Knowledge starts its registry even when nobody uses it, and plugins have no supported way to adapt their resource use to the Gateway's selected profile. Aggressively retiring Knowledge workers also breaks vault watching and can interrupt multi-step operations.

## User Impact

User impact: in **lean** mode, Knowledge starts storage and its registry on first use. Watched vaults stay live; unwatched storage and an idle registry can release their workers after 60 seconds. The first call after retirement pays a cold-start cost. **Standard mode keeps its existing residency and startup behavior.**

Plugin authors can read `standard | lean` and subscribe to future changes through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/resource-profile`. Selection remains owned by the Gateway; changing the configured profile still requires a restart. There is no new configuration flag, shared Knowledge worker host, or data migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK reads the existing startup owner's singleton rather than inspecting configuration or machine limits again. Knowledge retires unwatched storage only after its serialized operation lane settles, so an upload spanning several RPCs is not mistaken for inactivity. Registry retirement waits for all pending replies and joins physical termination before reopening.

Lean maintenance initializes on first use, including an authorized maintenance-status read. Initialization, scheduled work, and shutdown settle together; persisted overdue work catches up after the next activation. Native watcher notifications remain active across idle periods. The rejected one-second retirement policy is not included.

## Evidence

### Periphery attribution by construction

The shared kit's `GenerateGatewayProtocol` SwiftPM plugin calls `scripts/prepare-native-protocol.mjs --language swift`; that owner bundles `packages/gateway-protocol/scripts/native-codegen.ts`, which calls `generateSwiftProtocol()` from the schemas. Both macOS and iOS consume this same generated model target. Native source/project files, scanner setup, pinned Swift dependencies, schemas, generator and its real source inputs are unchanged.

```bash
# At head 135a37a0562a; exact stacked base 7c19a0c70480:
git diff --stat 7c19a0c70480..HEAD --   ':(glob)**/*.swift' apps config pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml   tsconfig.json node-version.mjs packages/gateway-protocol   packages/normalization-core src/gateway/methods   packages/plugin-package-contract/src/recommended-prompts.ts   src/infra/directory-walk.ts src/gateway/session-method-policy.ts   src/gateway/operator-scopes.ts src/shared/gateway-method-policy.ts   src/gateway/events.ts scripts .github/workflows/macos-periphery.yml   .github/workflows/ios-periphery.yml   .github/workflows/shared-openclawkit-periphery.yml   .github/actions/setup-node-env ':(exclude)scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-entrypoints.json'
# Output: empty (exit 0).
```

Root `package.json` is deliberately accounted for separately, not silently excluded: comparing parsed base/head manifests after removing the one new `exports["./plugin-sdk/resource-profile"]` entry yields exact equality. The excluded SDK-entrypoint registry likewise only adds `resource-profile`; it is not consumed by the native generator. The native manifest's root-package fingerprint therefore invalidates generation/scan scope without changing generated Swift.

```bash
# Run once in each exact revision's checkout, with distinct fresh output directories:
node scripts/prepare-native-protocol.mjs --language swift --out "$OUT" --check
cmp "$BASE_OUT/GatewayModels.swift" "$HEAD_OUT/GatewayModels.swift"
# Output: empty (exit 0).
sha256sum "$BASE_OUT/GatewayModels.swift" "$HEAD_OUT/GatewayModels.swift"
# Both: 23bd8b729f9ed407fd93758129bb4715a4ddc562463da9aad424798a14d03e57
```

Thus the source and generated Swift input scanned for `OpenClawSessionColorDot` and `ChatObscuredPresentation` is identical on base/head. These findings cannot be introduced by this Knowledge change. This is an input-equivalence proof, **not** a claim that the skipped base scan was run or passed.

### Latest-stable → candidate in-place upgrade

The upgrade proof below was added after ClawSweeper’s 13:21 UTC review of this same unchanged head (`135a37a0562a`, zero findings); the single requested [re-review was superseded](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202478#issuecomment-7041051418), and the existing source review remains applicable.

**Passed** on Linux ARM64 in a fresh Studio Crabbox container. Installed the published `openclaw@2026.11.6`, then replaced it in the **same npm installation prefix** with the canonical self-contained package built from `135a37a0562ab9a0c93c874675b8de08164df9b9`. Preserved the same config path, state directory, registry, vault, and agent session; enabled `gateway.resources.profile: lean` for the candidate. No source-code change was needed for this proof.

- Stable Gateway created three records through real admitted agent/tool calls with the deterministic loopback Responses provider. The operator-readable store was watched. A real one-minute maintenance schedule completed a pass, then persisted its last result and next slot before shutdown.
- Read-only registry inspection after shutdown confirmed the saved next slot and last pass. No schedule timestamps, database rows, or clocks were modified to manufacture catch-up.
- Candidate startup after the saved slot elapsed had **zero Knowledge workers**. Its first Knowledge use read the pre-upgrade content; status then returned the exact persisted last run and overdue slot.
- Maintenance caught up after the production 60-second activation delay, for exactly the missed slot, with the existing store successful and no failed stores. Next schedule was armed.
- For an independent idle-watch assertion, disabled further scheduled passes through the documented config and restarted the same upgraded installation. Read all three records, waited **65 real seconds** without Knowledge calls, and observed storage still resident while the registry retired. An external edit produced `plugin.knowledge.changed` **before** a read, and the subsequent read returned the edit.
- All three original record identities and revisions survived upgrade/catch-up. Every persisted page byte was unchanged until the deliberate external edit; afterward only that edit differed. The other two records retained their original content and revisions. All Gateway processes stopped cleanly.

**Reproduction:** `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --allow-unreleased-changelog --output-dir /tmp/knowledge-candidate --output-name candidate.tgz`; install `openclaw@2026.11.6` via npm; drive the sequence above through `chat.send`, `agent.wait`, `plugins.sessionAction`, `diagnostics.lanes`, and native watcher events; replace the same prefix using `npm install ... /tmp/knowledge-candidate/candidate.tgz`.

**Evidence identity:** `run_9446929159ec93cd373a90c50b59bd06`, lease `cbx_a70863ad6e23` (released), exit **0**. `node:24.22.1-trixie`, runtime image `sha256:f1e034976f948cf212ef1f659c12e5dd58ac7eab947831813e81a62401ca38be`. prs.title: fix: update the checkout a macOS Gateway actually runs
prs.body:
Related: #200833

## What Problem This Solves

When a macOS LaunchAgent still starts a Git checkout, clicking **Update** in the Web UI or typing `/update` can select a new release on disk while the Gateway keeps serving the old checkout. A later update can then mistake a release that never served for the build it should roll back to.

## User Impact

With the corrected updater installed, both Web UI entrypoints update the checkout the service actually starts. Services already using the stable launcher keep their existing release-switch behavior. This is preventive: it does **not** bootstrap the already-affected `5484e18dab2b` or `caa595355fe6` updaters. Those builds choose the update path before invoking the target.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both entrypoints submit `update.run`, so the decision belongs in the shared updater, not in the UI. On macOS, a Gateway-initiated update uses the existing in-place transaction if the service does not own the selected release. A later independently started update also stays in place if an unused selection already exists. Neither path adopts, deletes, or repoints that selection. Service ownership and self-install safeguards are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Independent local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete `8271ec9ee5d4..f7c32f22c584` range and found no introduced correctness or security defect. All four first-visit browser budget tests passed locally and the [hosted browser shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44843476842/job/136658056387) passed. All 12 baseline-ratchet checks passed locally on that exact head.
- **macOS 27 arm64 / Node 26.12.1, integrated head `c55f20af7feb`:** the same selector test failed on main `7af829afeef7` at the managed-handoff condition and passed with the fix. All 16 Git-release tests passed, with core typecheck, targeted lint and formatting.
- A real disposable LaunchAgent served fixture checkout A while unused release B was selected. Native service inspection identified A as owned and B as foreign. The same job starting through the real release launcher served B and identified B as owned.
- Production runtime promotion at A's entrypoint started the integrated OpenClaw build. The job owned the listener; `/healthz`, `/readyz` and authenticated `health` RPC passed; `/startupz` matched build ID `2026.11.6-c55f20af7feb-2026-11-20T20-40-42.298Z`. Production runtime restore then served A again under a new PID, byte-identical at its entrypoint, without changing B or its unstarted trial.
- **Limit:** this is native launchd, serving identity and runtime-rollback evidence, not a full Dashboard `update.run` on a user installation. The native management guard did not admit the disposable HOME for that operation; it was not bypassed. No Git-ref/database rollback or live-profile update is claimed.
- Earlier Linux fixture/repository tests: **408 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed** against `8f2cfd47eac1d600a779780a5462def8b8b997ce`. Both Web UI entrypoints submitted one `update.run`; a failed later target restored the verified checkout, not the unused selection. Independent review found no actionable source findings on the original head.

## Worked on by

- @hannesrudolph

After an uncertain session sharing write, later chat attempts are denied with advice to retry when storage is ready, even though the denial lasts until the Gateway restarts.

Affected users now receive the required restart action. Temporary storage failures still advise retrying, and access remains denied until restart.

The session authority owner now identifies its persistent unknown state so the Gateway can give distinct guidance without changing access decisions.

prs.title: fix: let plugin counters show a label set at 0 before its first event
prs.body:
<!-- Template: .github/pull_request_template.md at ed8f4e680cbfc32182fee0b9286ef40c112bb1c3 -->

Closes #202816

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that publishes counters through `api.metrics` cannot show a known label set at 0 before its first event. `counter(name).inc(labels, 0)` is dropped, so the series appears only after the first non-zero increment. Dashboards and `absent()` alerts then cannot tell an idle label set from one that is missing.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors can call `inc(labels, 0)` to export a label set at 0 on the Prometheus scrape, the usual way to pre-initialize counters. Core metrics and existing plugin series are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exporter's store skips counter increments of 0 before creating the series. Core counters rely on that: the model cost counter receives `costUsd ?? 0`, and skipping 0 keeps an unknown cost from showing as a measured $0. So the change applies only to plugin counter samples: a value of 0 uses the store's existing `max` mode instead of `add`. A new label set is created at 0 under the usual per-family and total limits. An existing series keeps its value and its cached output. Negative and non-finite values are still refused. The plugin families section of the Prometheus docs now says what `inc(labels, 0)` does.

## Evidence

- A scrape from a real Gateway with a path-loaded plugin shows the new `{outcome="error"} 0` series on this branch and not on main (Runtime output below).
- New store test, red on main for the missing `{outcome="error"} 0` line, green with the fix, red again with the fix reverted. It also checks that negative, NaN and Infinity values create no series, that core `counter(..., 0)` still creates none, and that a later 0 on an existing series does not re-render it.
- `pnpm test:extension diagnostics-prometheus` (77 passed) and `src/plugins/plugin-metrics.test.ts` (11 passed).
- `pnpm check:changed`: all checks pass except the dead export scan, which fails the same way on main ed8f4e680cb (`ui/src/pages/skills/skill-page-route.ts`: `createSkillPageReads`, `createSkillPageRoute`). `git diff --check` clean.
- Local review: ClawSweeper `--local-range` (Claude runner, claude-opus-5-5), base ed8f4e680cb, head 1a1127b7d58, full committed range, complete and checkout access verified; outcome: patch is correct, no findings, rating D (proof D, patch A) after 1 round; the proof rating is from the local range only, which cannot see this body's runtime output; remaining findings: none.

### Runtime output

Setup: isolated Gateway built from the checkout, own state folder, token auth with a throwaway token, loopback port 19455, `diagnostics-prometheus` enabled, and a path-loaded plugin `zero-proof` with `allowMetrics: true`. Five seconds after its service starts, the plugin logs and calls `inc({ outcome: "error" }, 0)`, then `inc({ outcome: "ok" }, 1)`. No model, channel or provider. On main, `pnpm build` exits 1 on the plugin SDK declaration size check after the build output is written; the Gateway runs from that output on both SHAs.

<details>
<summary>Plugin and config used on both runs</summary>

```js
// <tmp>/zero-proof/index.cjs (with package.json and openclaw.plugin.json { "id": "zero-proof", "activation": { "onStartup": true } })
module.exports = {
  id: "zero-proof",
  register(api) {
    const metrics = api.metrics?.register({
      families: [
        { name: "jobs_total", type: "counter", help: "Proof jobs by outcome.", labels: ["outcome"] },
      ],
    });
    const jobs = metrics.counter("jobs_total");
    let timer;
    api.registerService({
      id: "zero-proof",
      start() {
        timer = setTimeout(() => {
          api.logger.info('zero-proof: jobs_total.inc({ outcome: "error" }, 0)');
          jobs.inc({ outcome: "error" }, 0);
          api.logger.info('zero-proof: jobs_total.inc({ outcome: "ok" }, 1)');
          jobs.inc({ outcome: "ok" }, 1);
        }, 5000);
      },
      stop() {
        clearTimeout(timer);
      },
    });
  },
};
```

```json
{
  "gateway": { "mode": "local", "port": 19455, "bind": "loopback", "auth": { "mode": "token", "token": "<synthetic-token>" } },
  "plugins": {
    "allow": ["diagnostics-prometheus", "zero-proof"],
    "load": { "paths": ["<tmp>/zero-proof"] },
    "slots": { "memory": "none" },
    "entries": {
      "diagnostics-prometheus": { "enabled": true },
      "zero-proof": { "enabled": true, "allowMetrics": true }
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

**Before, on main `ed8f4e680cb`**

```sh
pnpm build
OPENCLAW_HOME=<tmp>/home OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<tmp>/state/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=19455 \

sleep 45
```

prs.title: improve(knowledge): speed up project recall after vault edits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After any Knowledge vault edit, project recall repeats a directory walk and scalar validation for unchanged records. This can consume the first send's 1,000 ms recall budget even though most records were already loaded and validated.

## User Impact

Project recall does less work after vault edits while retaining the existing deadline, candidate contents, and ordering. There are no configuration or schema changes.

Native-provider qualification completed on the private synthetic fixture. Changed-vault sampled allocation falls 66%; the larger native fixture still exceeds the recall budget, as detailed below.

## Lead Decisions and Follow-ups

Lead decisions, made by the Team perf-loop lead (an agent acting under Peter's standing unattended instruction), not by Peter.

1. ACCEPTED: the 3.3% unchanged-vault allocation increase, in exchange for median recall at 50k notes falling 6.40 s → 0.93 s.
2. ACCEPTED as a follow-up, not a blocker: the 50k p95 of 1.65 s is still over the 1,000 ms budget. Late-context delivery stays the documented follow-up too.
3. APPROVED: upgrade the private synthetic fixture clone from schema 42 to 43 with the candidate's canonical `openclaw doctor --fix` migration path (no hand-written SQL), so native qualification can run. This is synthetic test data only. It is not a product schema change and does not touch Team.

## Why This Change Was Made

The vault owner now carries the freshness walk's entry types and stamps into loading instead of enumerating and statting them again. It reuses date, temporal-metadata, and recall-approval validation for immutable metadata from its previously valid records. Changed bytes still use the guarded reader; cross-record references, ontology, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and ranking remain checked. No additional persistent cache is introduced.

The Team perf-loop lead agent directed preserving the first-answer context wait and fixing this producer. Late-result consumption is a follow-up: it needs a turn-owned pending result, append-only delivery before an already-required model request, and a skipped outcome if the turn ends first. This PR adds no such delivery path.

Production delta: **+34 lines** to carry request-local scan metadata and reuse existing validation facts. That replaces repeated filesystem and validation work without adding a state owner.

## Evidence

The extended storage-owner regression fails on exact parent `5fe76f0073b4eed58253fe21c73ddefb1c7e6390` and passes with the fix: an unchanged approved record is statted four times after an unrelated edit on the parent, versus three with the fix. The retained reads are freshness plus Git's before/after publication snapshots. Candidate contents remain equal and the unchanged record is not reparsed or reapproved.

**119 focused tests pass**, including Knowledge reads, external-change/evidence handling, native provider entry, project bootstrap, and prompt-prefix stability. Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

The synthetic first-send harness uses the real prompt preparation, Agent, and request serializer. Fast-provider request median is 2.17 → 2.08 ms with project context in every sample; 1 s and 4 s providers still reach the first request at approximately 1,004 ms and preserve late lease cleanup. No-project and minimal/subagent-default prompt paths make zero candidate calls. This verifies the retained wait contract, not a full Gateway/network round trip.

`pnpm check:changed` has one inherited failure: Knip rejects `createSkillPageReads` and `createSkillPageRoute` in `ui/src/pages/skills/skill-page-route.ts`. The same guard reproduces both findings on the clean exact parent. Commit `1ee9f29e6668e32ecfade57a540d10326ad3b8de` / #202581 introduced both exports. This is a main regression requiring repair, not ignored noise. All other selected checks passed.

Serial macOS storage-owner measurements: two A/A controls, then five fresh-process A/B pairs with three changed-vault calls each (15 calls per arm). All selected candidate bytes match. These exclude worker transport and caller admission.

| Notes | Before median / sample p95 | After median / sample p95 | CPU median before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 | 152 / 190 ms | 30 / 51 ms | 167 → 50 ms |
| 10,000 | 1,419 / 1,744 ms | 179 / 258 ms | 1,408 → 243 ms |
| 50,000 | 6,397 / 8,005 ms | 931 / 1,655 ms | 6,117 → 1,152 ms |

At 50k, metadata reads fall **550,068 → 50,044**. Separate heap sampling estimates changed-vault allocation **1.98 GB → 667 MB/call**, unchanged **198 → 205 MB/call**. Instrumented timings are excluded above. The initial 10k cold sample maximum rose from 6.16 to 11.43 seconds during a host-load jump; a subsequent untraced five-pair comparison was faster in every candidate pair (cold median/max 4.32/5.23 → 3.63/4.15 seconds). The original outlier is retained and cold/tail guarantees are not claimed.

Native Linux qualification used the private production-shaped synthetic btrfs clone: 37.9 GB agent database, 5,001 sessions / 222,797 events, 62k notes across 2,000 project keys, separate 62k-file / 1.116 GB workspace, Node 24.22.1, 8 CPUs / 32 GiB. The approved candidate `pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` migration upgraded only the clone from schema 42 to 43; the final full qualification exited **0**. All capture/build/temp storage stayed on external scratch. Earlier capacity failures were resolved through the canonical migration and snapshot owners, with no hand-written migration SQL. Doctor's expected `gateway.mode` notice reflects a non-Gateway fixture; this is native-provider proof, not a real Gateway/model-network round trip.

Two serial A/A controls (warm settlement medians 5.983 / 6.008 s), then five fresh-process A/B pairs with three changed-vault calls per process. Scanner source hashes identify the exact parent/candidate arm, including the worker. Modules load outside timing; all measured native leases settle before the next sample.

| Native 62k-note path | Before median / sample p95 | After median / sample p95 | Total CPU median before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Changed-vault settlement, 15/arm | 5,291 / 6,837 ms | 2,371 / 2,918 ms | 5,261 → 2,465 ms |
| Cold settlement, 5/arm | 39,846 / 48,257 ms | 30,003 / 43,252 ms | 40,173 → 31,992 ms |

**Remaining budget gap:** all 15 changed-vault calls per arm timed out, returning at median 1,003 / 1,003 ms while work continued and closed its lease. Native timed omissions contain no project context; candidate equality is established by the direct-owner and unchanged controls, not empty timed-out prompts. The complete native path is larger than the direct 50k owner benchmark, so this PR does not claim the 4 s and 16 s production cases now fit 1,000 ms. Native admission/global validation/cold work and late-context consumption remain follow-ups. Main-thread CPU is a small part of settlement (changed median 5.8 → 6.1 ms; cold 33.3 → 34.8 ms); total CPU improves. The first A/A cold run was 83.3 s versus 44.9 s for the second, and is kept separate from the paired cold results.

The unchanged-vault native control delivered context in all five calls per arm, with identical prompt SHA256 (`2aec53284a444ed9d14f7ff82d25a0c955e0a92a021f128b344b66b6c7595ac2`). Median / sample maximum: **350 / 355 → 348 / 360 ms**; total CPU median **383 → 380 ms**. This single-process-per-arm control verifies preserved prompt delivery; it is not claimed as a speedup. The private capture and fixture are removed after qualification.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and acceptance</summary>

Seed new isolated fixtures at 1k, 10k, or 50k notes, then run the same measurement script serially against parent and candidate sources:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/project-memory-vault-fixture.ts --root "$fixture" --records 50000
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/project-memory-storage-measure.ts --root "$fixture" --iterations 3 --edit-record notes/00049999.md
```

Run `--allocation` separately; omit `--edit-record` for unchanged-vault samples. The native bootstrap benchmark also accepts `--edit-record` for its existing synthetic fixture.

Acceptance: identical candidates, fewer filesystem operations, improved changed-vault latency and CPU, and explicit investigation of any >20% cold/unchanged/allocation regression. Native qualification is complete; the larger fixture still misses the budget, explicitly documented above. The accepted direct-owner tail and allocation tradeoffs remain as stated by the agent lead.
</details>

prs.title: fix(discord): keep /codex detach and rebind after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
Closes #178330
Related: #175379

## What Problem This Solves

In Discord, `/codex detach` and re-running `/codex bind` with another workspace reply with success, but the change is not saved. After the Gateway restarts, the conversation is bound again with the workspace from the first bind, as if the detach or rebind never happened. #178330 has the reproduction on a real Discord bot.

## User Impact

User impact: in Discord, `/codex detach` and `/codex bind` to another workspace now stay in effect after a Gateway restart, and one such command no longer leaves Discord's binding storage memory-only for the rest of the Gateway process.

- If a binding change reaches Discord after the Discord plugin instance that created the relevant binding manager has shut down, the change is now refused with an error instead of reporting success and reverting at the next restart. Discord's deprecated synchronous binding helpers refuse it as well. This holds while Discord is still saving binding changes to its store; Not covered lists the cases that keep the previous behavior.
- No config, schema, or stored-data change; stored bindings load at startup as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

This carries forward the Discord-only repair from #178622, which its author closed unmerged on November 5 and whose branch was then deleted. The production change is that PR's repair ported to current `main` with the same logic, and its author, HeZ2z, is credited as co-author of the commit. The differences from #178622 are listed in the details below.

When I closed my earlier #178333 on October 20, I expected a complete fix to overlap with the core-side approach in #177691, in which runtime-owned plugin-state stores refuse retired runtimes with a typed error, a change to public SDK behavior. Since then, ClawSweeper's last review of #178622 (November 4) found the Discord-only repair complete in scope, without new configuration or public SDK surface, and listed nothing before merge; #178622 and #177691 were both closed by their authors without being merged; and the focused reproduction still fails on current `main` (see Evidence).

Discord's binding code opened its store with the runtime of whichever plugin instance was current at write time. `/codex` commands run in the Codex plugin's instance, where Discord's runtime is not available, so the write failed. The failure was handled as a storage failure: the change was kept in memory only, Discord stopped saving binding changes for the rest of the process, and the command reported success.

The thread-binding manager now keeps the runtime of the Discord instance that created it and writes through that runtime whichever plugin calls it, as the Telegram repair merged in #175379 does. Session-wide helpers that change bindings outside a manager (idle timeout, max age, and unbind by session) look up the account's manager and use the runtime it keeps.

Unlike Telegram's, Discord's binding storage switches to memory-only after a failed write, so Discord also has to tell a retired owner apart from a storage failure. After a failed store write, it reopens its store through the kept runtime with the V2 opener, which the plugin SDK documents as bound to the plugin lifetime. If that reopen is refused and the store has not yet confirmed the targeted row, the write is refused: it is not kept in memory, and persistence is not switched off. If the reopen succeeds, the failure is handled as a storage failure, as before. While Discord is still saving to its store, the synchronous compatibility paths check the kept runtime before they write. As #178622 noted, a typed retired-runtime error needs a core public-contract change and can come later; this PR changes no core production code, public SDK contract, or config.

Thanks to HeZ2z, the author of #178622, for the repair and its regression tests, and to the author of #177691 for the earlier discussion of this bug.

<details>
<summary>Changes from #178622</summary>

- Production: the same logic in the same five files under `extensions/discord/src/monitor/` (`thread-bindings.state.ts`, `thread-bindings.manager.ts`, `thread-bindings.persistence.ts`, `thread-bindings.session-shared.ts`, `thread-bindings.lifecycle.ts`). One comment in `thread-bindings.persistence.ts` is reworded to describe the documented V2 opener behavior.
- Tests: five of #178622's six regression cases moved into the existing `src/plugins/conversation-binding.cross-instance.test.ts` as a `describe` block next to the Telegram cases from #175379, plus one new case for the synchronous session idle-timeout helper. The Discord helpers the tests use come from the existing `runtime-api.js`, except two that `extensions/discord/test-api.ts` now exports: the thread-binding test harness and the state reset used to simulate a restart.
- Diff against `9f20b63e7796`: 7 files changed, 362 insertions(+), 20 deletions(-) (production: 5 files, +98/-19; tests and test exports: +264/-1).

</details>

## Evidence

"Before" results were taken on main `9f20b63e7796` with only the test change. "After" results were taken on the same commit with this PR's full diff (commit `e942926e771a`).

Focused tests: six new Discord cases in `src/plugins/conversation-binding.cross-instance.test.ts`.

- Detach from another plugin instance (Codex): the stored row is deleted, and the binding stays gone after a simulated restart.
- Rebind from another plugin instance: the new binding is stored and comes back after a simulated restart.
- After such a change, Discord's own next binding write is still stored.
- With Discord's plugin registry retired, a detach from another plugin instance is refused, and memory and stored rows are unchanged.
- The same refusal through the deprecated synchronous unbind-by-session helper and through the deprecated synchronous idle-timeout helper.

Results:

- The focused reproduction still fails on current `main`: on `9f20b63e7796` with only the test change, 6 of the file's 9 cases fail and 3 pass. Each Discord case fails at the check it targets: the detach and rebind from the Codex instance report success, but the stored row is unchanged; Discord's next own write is not stored; and the three retired-owner cases accept the change instead of refusing it. The three existing Telegram cases in the file pass.
- With this change, all 9 cases in the file pass. Vitest reported about 6.9 s for the file.
- Mutation checks (not part of this PR):
  - with the manager no longer keeping its runtime, all six Discord cases fail and the three Telegram cases pass;
  - with the retired-owner check turned into a no-op, only the three refusal cases fail; the other six pass;
  - with the synchronous refusal detection always false, only the synchronous idle-timeout refusal case fails.
- `pnpm test:extension discord`: passed (260 files, 2,649 tests).
- `pnpm test:contracts:channels`, run once as a cross-check although no shared channel surface changed: passed (49 files, 221 tests).
- Targeted checks:
  - `oxfmt --check`, oxlint, and `git diff --check` on the changed files: clean (oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors);
  - `pnpm check:changed --base 9f20b63e7796` (34 steps, including `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, and the mock-export ratchet): passed;
  - test-lines ratchet: OK, net +259 of the 400-line allowance.
- Local review: autoreview on the full diff against `9f20b63e7796` reported scoped-clean with no findings (overall: patch is correct, confidence 0.85).
- CI: pending at the time of opening

Not included yet: a real Discord run. It is planned with a dedicated test bot in a DM, before the fix on `main` and after it on this head, to show a typed `/codex detach` and a rebind to another workspace surviving a full Gateway stop/start. As in the original reproduction, the run uses only `/codex` text commands and sends no ordinary message, so no model turn is made; the bug and this fix are in the binding writes those commands make, which a model turn does not reach.

Not covered:

- The focused tests simulate a restart by clearing Discord's in-process binding state and rebuilding the manager from the store; a real Gateway stop/start is part of the planned Discord run.
- The refusal cases retire Discord's plugin registry directly in the test; a real plugin reload or disable was not run.
- Once Discord's binding storage has switched to memory-only, async commits and synchronous updates go straight to memory without checking the kept runtime, as on `main`, so a retired owner's change there is not refused. If the kept runtime is refused partway through a store write after the targeted row was already written, the change is kept, as on `main`.
- Tests ran on Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Node v24.22.1) only; the change has no platform-specific code.

prs.title: improve: offer a name for an added provider account
prs.body:
Related: #202626

## What Problem This Solves

When you connect another account for the same provider, the saved profiles can show identical emails. The account list leaves you to recognize an opaque ID or check usage to tell work from personal. Reconnecting a previously named account can also drop its name.

## User Impact

User impact: an interactive CLI sign-in or Models sign-in offers an optional name after saving another account. Press Enter to keep the prefilled label. Chat `/login` still signs in without prompting, and reconnecting a recognized account keeps its saved name, including `--force`. If a name cannot be saved, the sign-in stays connected and Models or the Gateway-backed CLI shows what happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prompt surfaces opt in to optional text; the chat adapter does not. Credential persistence completes before the question, so dismissing the name or failing to write it cannot undo the sign-in. A custom name uses the existing profile `displayName`: config-authored names keep precedence, and saving a label does not create an auth-order declaration. The suggestion uses an existing provider-supplied name or email when available. If neither exists, the provider label is suggested and is saved when accepted. Subscription tiers are not assumed to be workspace names.

## Evidence

**Main integration (`72a8d6a99174`):** After #202626 landed, this branch incorporated `main`, including the #202795 Plugins asset-budget fix. The merge keeps the shared-store reconnect matcher authoritative for saved names; a different API key or token or an unresolved secret reference does not inherit an existing name. The original visual flow is unchanged. All 130 focused shared login, auth naming, wizard, and Models runner tests passed on the integrated tree; targeted typed lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent full-diff local Codex review through P2 found no actionable findings. Fresh hosted CI is still required on this head.

On unpatched main (`31ce94f0a`), seven new account-name cases failed at the absent prompt or lost name; the first-account and chat controls passed. With the change all ten pass against the real isolated auth store, including the additional review regression for a provider that supplies no name or email. The hosted CLI prompt-error case also fails before its fix and passes after. Shared auth, reconnect, chat-adapter, and WizardSession/Clack checks pass. Focused TypeScript, lint, format, diff check, and a bounded local runtime build pass.

The real CLI in a PTY and the real Models UI through an isolated Gateway use a synthetic local provider, not real OpenAI credentials. The CLI saved both profiles and one Enter kept the default. Models submitted **Work** with Enter and read back both saved profiles, with **Personal** unchanged. The screenshots show the same added-account interaction before and after. The production UI build completed, and the report-only budget check still flags limits that were already exceeded before the UI change. No budget was changed.

A real Models regression reproduced a stale name form after clicking **X**. With the fix, that click reaches the sign-in confirmation without another input, and both accounts remain saved with the new one unnamed. The narrow UI regression also fails before the fix; the runner, Models, and login-dialog suites pass afterward.

After repairing the draft ancestry onto `c1f70d3b7`, all 14 authored files matched the tested patch byte-for-byte. The affected core and UI suites were rerun on that base: 68 tests passed.

Independent excerpt review identified the missing fallback-label save and Models dismissal problems; both were fixed and reverified. The full diff was self-reviewed. The packaged Auto Review executable was unavailable in this worktree, so no completed Auto Review report is claimed.

[Follow-up review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202667#issuecomment-7048414949) found that replacing the account in an explicit `--profile-id` slot could inherit the old account’s name. Matching reconnects now keep the name; a replacement does not, and gets the optional offer when another account exists. The replacement case failed before that fix; all 55 tests in the three affected auth suites now pass, including explicit same-account reconnect. Focused typecheck, lint, format, and the CI mock-export ratchet also pass.

### OAuth accounts without a provider matcher

The [maintainer follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f4153f88310ff6f004f34b2daa66531114c02760) keeps the provider matcher authoritative. Without a matcher, a reused OAuth slot keeps the saved name only when the provider-supplied account ID and OAuth registration match. A different or unknown account can be named without inheriting the old label. Credential writes, profile selection, config-authored labels, and API key/token behavior are unchanged.

Both regression cases failed against `66e6da85`: the naming prompt was skipped for a different account and when no account ID was available. After the fix, both cases and the same-account control passed; 61 tests passed across three focused auth suites. The naming suite took 33.34s locally; CI timing on the follow-up is pending. Targeted typecheck, typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Local Auto Review found no P2-or-higher issues in the follow-up diff. Tests used synthetic credentials, not a live xAI sign-in.

### Failed name saves are visible and nonfatal

The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202667#issuecomment-7048687460) found that a name-write failure only reached the Gateway log. The saved sign-in now sends an optional plain note through the existing wizard channel. Models displays it rather than silently acknowledging it; the Gateway-backed CLI prints it. The note says the account is connected, explains that the name was not saved, and shows where to set a display name in configuration. Dismissing it still retrieves the successful sign-in receipt. No Gateway protocol change.

Three real-store cases reproduced missed or rejected name writes with no client notice; one Models runner case reproduced the hidden notice and one reproduced the stale cancellation receipt. All are green with the repair. The seven affected test files pass 160 tests, including the Gateway CLI reader and wizard cancellation logic; core/UI typecheck, lint, format, mock-export ratchet and diff check pass. The real Models before/after below runs a loopback Gateway and Chromium with synthetic credentials and injects a null name-write result only. Before, Models went straight to confirmation. After, the warning is visible; clicking **X** still finishes sign-in, and read-back confirms both accounts remain saved and the new account has no custom name.

### Latest-stable existing-state upgrade

Built and ran latest stable `2026.11.6` from the exact source tag `v2026.11.6` (`06afb10d3272`) with frozen dependencies. Used an isolated profile and synthetic OAuth fixture only. Seeded and read the state using the stable CLI, then ran the candidate’s supported `doctor --fix --full-integrity-check` on the same isolated state (exit 0). Before any post-upgrade sign-in, all of these matched the stable readback:

| State | Stable and immediately after upgrade |
| --- | --- |
| Profile IDs | `example-upgrade-proof:personal`, `example-upgrade-proof:work` |
| Saved names and effective labels | Personal → Personal; Work → Office override (configured) |
| Saved auth order and first profile | Work → Personal; Work first |
| Resolved selected model | `example-upgrade-proof/example-v1` |

A real CLI sign-in then saved **Travel** as a third account without changing either existing profile or selected model. Reconnecting **Work** did not prompt for a name, refreshed that same profile ID, and kept both the saved **Work** label and the **Office override** config preference. Normal sign-in promotion changed first-profile order only after those new sign-ins. No live credentials, external provider endpoints, or inference were used; no naming migration was added.

### Required CI background

The reviewed-head [compaction job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44801338049/job/136514993232) failed `compact.queued-successor.test.ts:781` (during branch read: expected false to be true). A separate unmodified checkout of the published base `c1f70d3b7` reproduced that exact failure (18 pass, one fail). The [UI E2E job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44801338049/job/136514992833) failed the same plugin and skills readiness selectors and skill-settings request budget (33 > 31) that a local base replay reproduced without the PR’s UI change. These broader checks are not waived or fixed here.

### Models: failed account-name save

**Before**

![Models confirms sign-in without showing the unsaved name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f2a5099-38b1-49c4-b76b-5fb413167d64)

**After**

![Models explains the name was not saved while the account remains connected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88dc74bd-e151-4b37-8231-adba6c7d143d)

### CLI: adding a second account

**Before**

![CLI: sign-in saves the account without a name offer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da1ee446-cd8c-4422-8493-6e76abef1e69)

**After**

![CLI: the saved sign-in offers a prefilled optional name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a36c4cb-22fc-4df8-b779-de8d4d22f5b6)

### Models: adding a second account

#### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Models: the saved sign-in goes straight to confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69ee5150-d068-4f26-a327-526f1cad6d46)

**After**

![Models: the saved sign-in offers a prefilled optional name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8d92a88-cef3-4f54-9ddc-c0851ce87c16)

#### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Models before: highlighted sign-in confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fce90167-fda2-4555-86cd-9ff7c5fac3de)

**After**

![Models after: highlighted name field that accepts Enter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5028fe10-f765-410c-945c-93468e2dcdfe)

Report, starting patch, and design requirements supplied by Vítor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @TheAngryPit](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/56f989b2-27a6-40b1-b1c0-7620a6f39e55)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/fed6a27b-739a-492c-82e8-f0ae748769d3)
- [Account-identity follow-up: discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/50d1678c-66b7-4950-bc7b-1593640b730a)

- [Main integration and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/9996b9b1-fb39-4908-a04b-8b6eaa848833)

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)
