prs.title: fix(onboard): wait for a freshly started Gateway with --skip-health
prs.body:
Closes #201394

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw onboard --install-daemon --skip-health` starts a fresh Gateway service, then makes one 1.5 s probe and reports the healthy service as unreachable because it has not started listening yet.

## User Impact

Interactive onboarding now waits with the normal Gateway startup timing whenever it started or restarted the service, even with `--skip-health`. `--skip-health` still skips the health RPC, but no longer hides the Control UI link, suggests a restart, or drops the TUI into local mode for a Gateway that is still starting.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Treat a freshly started or restarted Gateway as a startup wait even when `--skip-health` is set.
- Do not re-probe that started Gateway with the single short probe after the wait.
- Keep the existing single-probe behavior for skipped/failed installs and reused Gateways.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/wizard/setup.finalize.trusted-proxy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 6/6 passed, including the real-finalizer `--skip-health` regression.
- Red-on-base: running the same regression against `ee37dd3`'s finalizer fails because the short probe path runs instead of the startup wait.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on both changed files.

- Interactive PTY proof (real `openclaw onboard --classic --flow quickstart --install-daemon --skip-health`, isolated `--profile`, provider redacted):
  - **Before** (same dist built from the unmodified docs branch): `Installed systemd service: …openclaw-gateway-onboard-proof4.service` followed by `│ Gateway: not detected (connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:19797) │` and `Gateway not detected yet. The managed systemd did not become reachable after setup… Retry the managed service`, while the service was already `active (running)`.
  - **After** (dist rebuilt from this PR head): the same wizard over the same managed systemd start printed `◇ Gateway service installed.`, `│ Web UI: http://127.0.0.1:19798/`, `│ Gateway: reachable`, `│ Your workspace is ready.`, and `└ Onboarding complete.`; `gateway call health` returned `ok: true` and the service was `active`.
  - Both proof services were removed afterward; no OpenClaw unit or listener remains.

prs.title: feat: let Talk and Discord request GPT-Live-1.1 with ChatGPT sign-in
prs.body:
Closes #202806

Related: #202133, #174084.

## What Problem This Solves

When a ChatGPT subscriber selects `gpt-live-1.1-codex`, OpenClaw treats it as an unlisted GPT-Live model and asks for Platform credentials. The subscriber cannot explicitly request that model through the existing Codex voice route.

## User Impact

User impact: Talk users can select `gpt-live-1.1-codex`, including in native iOS Talk, and Discord operators can choose it in realtime voice settings. The Codex selector prefers ChatGPT sign-in and can use a Platform key when the subscription profile is unavailable. Users can still select a public API model directly. Existing model defaults stay in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI plugin recognizes the selector from Codex CLI 0.171.0 and reuses its existing Codex model catalog, voice profile, and WebRTC call creation. iOS submits its offer through Talk's existing client WebRTC path. Discord uses the Gateway-owned WebRTC bridge. Existing iOS builds with GPT-Live WebRTC can use the selector. If a ChatGPT offer fails, the provider reports a safe, route-specific error to the gateway. The released browser Talk UI displays a generic WebRTC setup error.

## Evidence

- **Browser Talk.** The released Control UI running in Chromium connected through the isolated gateway, sent and received audio, and received input and reply transcript events. [Redacted browser results and HTTP 403 behavior](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202807#issuecomment-7054806575).
- **Live OAuth relay.** Applied the exact PR diff to an isolated OpenClaw 2026.11.6 runtime and used its Gateway relay over WebRTC. The probe verified the selector on the outgoing ChatGPT offer and waited for audio and a completed assistant transcript. The server did not report its selected model. This was a headless relay test. Native iOS Talk and a human Discord call with this revision are pending.
- **Failure handling.** With test credentials, the runtime fixtures exercised configured and environment Platform keys when a subscription profile could not load. The source-mode tests exercise HTTP 403 in the Talk broker and a network rejection in the Gateway relay. They verify the public message omits provider details and each failed ChatGPT offer sends one request. No live Platform call was made.
- **Comparison against base.** Copied the three published test files onto base `8271ec9ee5d4` and ran the same 11 selected cases with Node 24.22.3 and Vitest on the base and published commit `01245008b74c`. Base missed the catalog entry, did not project the OAuth startup error, and failed selector assertions. All 11 cases passed on the PR commit. The broader focused source-mode run passed 114 tests.
- **Model contract.** [Codex CLI 0.171.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.171.0/codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs#L118) uses this selector as its v3 default. In an independent Codex WebRTC probe, a deliberately nonexistent selector also returned audio. The evidence establishes OpenClaw's requested selector and transport, and the backend model identity remains unverified.
- **Hosted CI.** The local full build stopped at its memory preflight. [Required CI is waiting for a maintainer to approve the run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44844277283).

<details>
<summary>Redacted live relay output and regression results</summary>

```json
{"requestedModel":"gpt-live-1.1-codex","oauthOffer":true,"responseStatus":201,"serverSessionStarted":true,"nonzeroAudioFrames":146,"assistantTranscriptDone":true}
```

```text
Base auth routing: 6 failed | 19 skipped (exit 1)
Base Talk broker and Gateway relay: 4 failed | 1 passed | 38 skipped (exit 1)
PR auth routing: 6 passed | 19 skipped (exit 0)
PR Talk broker and Gateway relay: 5 passed | 38 skipped (exit 0)
```

</details>

## Maintainer decision

The fallback intentionally covers both listed Codex models when the ChatGPT profile cannot be loaded. The existing Platform key selection can run before sending an offer. A network error or rejection after sending a subscription offer is reported to the caller without a second request on the Platform route.

prs.title: fix(onboard): wait for a Gateway this run started under --skip-health
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw onboard --install-daemon --skip-health` installs and starts the Gateway service, then skips the startup wait and judges the fresh service from one 1.5 s probe. On a host where the Gateway binds slower than that, setup reports the Gateway it just installed as unreachable: the Control UI link is hidden, the outro is the "Gateway not detected" recovery summary that suggests restarting the service, and the TUI opens in `{ local: true }` mode. `--skip-health` should skip the health RPC, not the readiness of a service this run started.

Closes #201394.

## User Impact

A first-time `--install-daemon --skip-health` setup waits for the service it started, then shows the dashboard link and ends with the normal completion outro instead of a false recovery prompt, and the TUI connects to the Gateway instead of running local. `--skip-health` still skips the health RPC, and runs that awaited nothing (no service started this run, e.g. `--skip-daemon`) keep the single-probe fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The readiness block in `finalizeSetupWizard` is guarded by `!opts.skipHealth || sessionGateway`, so `--skip-health` with a fresh service install never reaches `waitForGatewayReachable`; the later single `probeGatewayReachable` then decides the verdict with `timeoutMs = max(1500, ...)`.

The decision is now planned from the service outcome in a sibling module (`setup.finalize-gateway-readiness.ts`, keeping `setup.finalize.ts` under its line cap): a Gateway this run started (`status === "ready"` and not reused) is awaited with `resolveGatewayStartupTiming()` even under `--skip-health`, and only a run that awaited nothing keeps the single-probe fallback. The health RPC itself stays gated on `!opts.skipHealth`. This matches the non-interactive path, which already waits with the startup timing whenever it installed the daemon.

`OnboardOptions.skipHealth` is optional, so the helper takes `boolean | undefined` and normalizes it (`skipHealth === true`); the earlier revision compared the optional value directly and failed strict type checking for every onboarding caller that omits the flag.

## Evidence

### Shipped `openclaw onboard` CLI, before / after / control

The real CLI was spawned through a Windows ConPTY (`node-pty`), so `process.stdin.isTTY` is true and the classic wizard runs its prompts; defaults were accepted with Enter. Per leg: wiped state dir, no service installed, port 28793 free, isolated `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=proofcli201394`. Only `src/wizard/setup.finalize.ts` and the new readiness helper differ between the legs.

```
node openclaw.mjs onboard --classic --flow quickstart --install-daemon --skip-health
  --skip-ui --skip-channels --skip-skills --skip-search --skip-bootstrap --accept-risk
  --auth-choice skip --gateway-auth token --gateway-port 28793 --agent-name main
```

| Leg | Service | Output | Elapsed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before (`setup.finalize.ts` from main) | login item installed at +27.9 s | `Gateway not detected yet. The managed Scheduled Task did not become reachable after setup.` at +39.0 s | 40 s |
| After (this branch) | installed at +25.1 s | `Gateway: reachable` at +38.9 s, then `Onboarding complete. Use the dashboard link above to control OpenClaw.` at +47.7 s | 49 s |
| Control (this branch, `--skip-daemon`) | nothing started | `Gateway not detected yet. Start now: openclaw --profile proofcli201394 gateway run` at +19.9 s | 21 s |

The before run's Gateway log records `{"message":"gateway ready"}` at 23:28:06.697 local, while that onboarding process had already exited at 23:27:58.975: the service was ready 7.7 s after setup declared it unreachable, which is the false negative this PR removes. The after run waits (`Gateway: reachable` at +38.9 s) and ends in the normal outro; the control still fails closed without spending the startup budget.

![Shipped onboarding CLI before/after/control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/201394/proof-cli-onboard.png)

### In-process rig (same finalizer, scripted prompter)

Earlier evidence, still valid: the finalizer invoked directly with a real per-user Windows service install (`OPENCLAW_PROFILE=proof201394`, port 28793), only the wizard source differing between legs.

| Run | Wizard source | Service action | Outro | Elapsed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | `upstream/main` | real install (per-user Startup login item) | `Gateway not detected yet. The managed Scheduled Task did not become reachable after setup.` | 16 s |
| After | this branch | same install | `Onboarding complete. Use the dashboard link above to control OpenClaw.` | 50 s |
| Control | this branch | `--skip-daemon` (nothing started) | `Gateway not detected yet. Start now: openclaw --profile proof201394 gateway run` | 69 s |

After the before leg's "not detected" summary, `127.0.0.1:28793` was already LISTENING, the same false negative seen through the shipped CLI above.

![Live before/after onboarding readiness on the isolated Windows profile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/201394/live-onboard.png)

![Verbatim rig log excerpts for the three legs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/201394/live-logs.png)

### Tests and gates

- `src/wizard/setup.finalize.test.ts`: the `win32`/`installed` row now runs with `skipHealth: true`; on `upstream/main` it fails with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times` for `waitForGatewayReachable`, and passes here. Two other tests in the file (`passes physical catalog routes…`, `skips the doomed hatch seed message…`) fail identically on clean `upstream/main` on this Windows checkout.
- `src/wizard/setup.test.ts` has one pre-existing failure on this checkout (`re-prompts for auth when applyAuthChoice requests retry selection`), reproduced with the upstream `setup.finalize.ts`; the other 28 pass.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` exits 0 on this revision (it flagged the optional `skipHealth` argument before the fix).
- `check:line-cap-ratchet` (899 -> 898 counted lines) and `check:test-lines-ratchet` (net 0) pass; `oxfmt --check` clean.

## What was not tested

- Prompt answers are the wizard defaults accepted with Enter through a real ConPTY, not hand-typed; nothing else about the shipped CLI run is simulated. The pty capture mis-decodes box-drawing glyphs (cosmetic only; the ASCII lines quoted above are verbatim).
- Provider/model auth is skipped (`--auth-choice skip`), so onboarding makes no real model request.
- Only the Windows per-user Startup login item was exercised; no macOS launchd or Linux systemd run.

prs.title: feat: open Command-K on your unread and recent chats, like Slack
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Command-K opens on a fixed list of pages (New session, Sessions, Meetings, Automations, Skills, Settings…). Those pages are already one click away in the sidebar, so the empty palette rarely helps. The common reason to press Command-K is to get to a conversation, usually the one that just got a reply. Slack's Command-K does exactly that: it opens on your unread and recent conversations, and Enter takes you to the top one.

## User Impact

Before: Command-K, then type part of a chat's name, wait for search, then Enter. Unread chats are not marked.

After: Command-K opens on **Unread** (unread chats, newest activity first) and **Recent** (the most recently active other chats), up to eight in total, above the same page commands as before. The first row is selected, so Command-K then Enter opens the newest unread chat, or the most recently active other chat when nothing is unread. Unread rows are bold with the sidebar's unread dot, here and in search results. Typing still searches sessions, messages, settings and commands exactly as before.

The chat you are viewing, archived and snoozed chats, cron and system sessions, Dock sessions, and subagent runs are left out, using the sidebar's own visibility rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rows come from the sidebar's retained roster (`sessions.presentation.result`), which already carries `unread` and the activity clocks and stays live through row events. It is the same roster the sidebar keeps on screen during a same-client reconnect, when `sessions.state.result` is cleared, so the chats do not vanish while the Gateway reconnects. The palette only projects it: no new Gateway method, no extra `sessions.list` read when it opens, and the projection is cached per roster publication (`sessions.revision`), current chat, and next snooze deadline. When a snoozed chat's deadline passes while the palette is open, a timer re-renders it so the chat comes back, matching the sidebar. The palette already subscribes to the session capability while open, so rows update in place when a reply lands.

Order reuses `compareSessionRowsByActivity` (the sidebar's "Last updated" order) behind an unread-first key, and filtering reuses `filterVisibleSessionRows` plus `isSessionSnoozed`. Selecting a row goes through the existing `onSelectSession` path. The shell passes the open chat's key through a new `currentChatSessionKey()` on the navigation owner so the palette can leave it out.

## Default selection

This changes what an empty Command-K selects first: the newest unread chat (or the most recently active other chat) instead of "New session". That is the point of the change, the same default as Slack's quick switcher, where Command-K then Enter jumps to the conversation that just got a reply. "New session" and the other page commands stay in the same list, one Down-arrow press or a typed word away, and Compose mode, Search mode and typed queries behave as before. If maintainers prefer to keep "New session" first, the chat groups can move below the page commands without changing the rest of this PR.

## Evidence

Scenario: six synthetic chats, two of them unread, opened from "Release notes draft". Playwright WebKit on Linux at 1280×800 with the mock Gateway fixture; a key badge in the corner shows each key press (recording only, not part of the change). Before is `main` at 6018bc9ce69, after is this branch.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: an empty Command-K lists only page commands such as New session and Sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ed1acdb-369c-447e-8502-4c21c875c6f5) | ![After: an empty Command-K lists Unread (Deploy check, Customer import, each with an unread dot) and Recent chats above the page commands, with the newest unread chat selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84b2ac08-464f-4412-8679-82511b65ca87) |

### Recordings

After: Command-K, Enter opens the newest unread chat; again for the second unread chat; with nothing unread, Command-K then Enter opens the most recently active other chat; typing still searches.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7d09802-fb21-44b8-ad70-f2c0296adef8

Before (`main`): Command-K opens on page commands only.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed3e59f6-662d-4f37-aef4-dcad9f149b75


- **E2E** `ui/src/e2e/command-palette-quick-switcher.e2e.test.ts`: from one chat with two unread chats, Command-K lists Unread, Recent, then Navigation, with the newest unread chat selected; Enter opens it; the next Command-K leads with the remaining unread chat; once nothing is unread, Enter opens the most recently active other chat and no row is marked unread.
- **Unit** `ui/src/components/command-palette-recent-sessions.test.ts`: unread-first ordering by activity; the open chat, archived, snoozed, cron, subagent and Dock rows are left out while a snooze that has ended comes back; the eight-row limit keeps unread rows; the mounted palette selects the first unread row and opens it with Enter; a roster publication while open reorders the rows; typing a query replaces them with search results.
- **Reconnect** (unit, real session capability): after a refresh, a same-client `reconnecting` publication clears `state.result` while the palette still lists both chats in the same order. This test fails on the previous head (3fc558b4662), which read `state.result`.
- **Snooze deadline** (unit, fake timers): a chat snoozed for 5 s is left out, the palette is notified 1 ms after the deadline, and the next read lists it again.
- **Checks** (Boat sandbox, head 48dd2d8de00): 7 unit files (87 tests: the palette files plus `chat-header-session-menu`), the new E2E plus `command-palette-mode` and `command-palette-shortcuts` E2E, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint (0 findings on changed files) and oxfmt pass. Stylelint, `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` (no baseline change) and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed on 3fc558b4662; the fix commit changes no CSS or strings.
- **Docs**: `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` (Command palette section).

Not tested: the macOS app's own WKWebView and the Tauri desktop app; both render this same Control UI page.

prs.body:

Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Write for someone who uses OpenClaw but has not read the code. The title and
opening problem statement should make sense without the diff or linked issue.

type: <what changes for the person affected>
Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
Use a parenthesized scope only when it helps that reader.

Good: fix: keep automations running when you open another chat
Bad: fix(cron): guard missing session IDs during authority restoration
Good: fix: let users sign in again after their session expires

For internal-only work, name the actual developer or operator workflow affected.

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Closes #201437

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
In 1–3 short, plain-language sentences, explain what someone is trying to do,
what goes wrong or is missing, and why it matters. For a fix, include the trigger
when known. For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.

Good: "Opening another chat can turn off a reply watcher, so it stops checking
until you notice and re-enable it."
Bad: "Fixes incorrect operator-authority invalidation on session identity mutation."

Describe the experienced problem, not just the code change. Save function names,
missing checks, and the root-cause walkthrough for the explanation below.
-->

Saving subagent state locks the database writer before the host has granted initial admission. While that decision is pending, other writers cannot acquire the database even though this write has not yet been admitted.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: subagent persistence leaves the native writer available during its initial host-admission wait. There is no public API or schema change, migration, or required user action. This is a reproduced lock-order invariant, not a measured user-visible speedup.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Move only the initial write-ID grant ahead of opening the native transaction. The FIFO row owner remains authoritative; terminal-event admission, final authority checks, commit admission, and receipt handling retain their existing placement and behavior.

The author simplification pass retained the one-line owner move, one regression using the existing native-lock fixture, and direct ownership documentation. The full diff adds 22 lines and removes one; no new production mechanism is introduced.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For visual web/macOS/iOS/Android changes, follow
the PR visual-proof standard and its screenshot delivery gate:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/.agents/skills/openclaw-pr-maintainer/references/media.md#pr-visual-proof
Keep the clean before/after pair visible first, then the annotated pair.

Start with the behavior checked and the result in plain language. Reviewers will
inspect the code, tests, and CI; do not make them decode command lists to learn
what was verified. Put exact commands, commit hashes, and long output in links
or optional <details>. Keep the useful evidence summary and meaningful gaps visible.
-->

A separate real SQLite connection probes native writer availability at each host-grant boundary. With current-main production ordering, the new regression fails with `transaction:held, commit:held`; with this fix it passes with `transaction:free, commit:held`. The complete receiver suite passes all 24 cases, including initial/commit denial, FIFO publication, terminal settlement, lost acknowledgments, missing receipts, and uncertain-outcome recovery.

Validated commit: `96ee46f545a`, based on `b400e8deed133ac0fa084072424fe1285f162952`, on Windows ARM64 / Node 26.13.0 / pinned pnpm 12.15.0. Two independent Copilot subagent code reviews covered the base-to-candidate change at P0-P2 and reported no significant issues. Codex CLI was unavailable; these were narrative reviews, not the shared helper's isolated/frozen-input machine result.

<details>
<summary>Exact local commands and results</summary>

- `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "leaves the native writer free while initial registry admission waits"` with only production ordering restored to the base: **expected failure**, 1 failed / 23 skipped, specifically the held/free assertion.
- `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on the restored final commit: **passed, 24/24**; Vitest duration 163.75 s, including cold worker compilation (129.268 s). The new regression itself took 33 ms. Existing receiver coverage uses real worker/database composition rather than mocked lock state.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: **passed**.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --incremental`: **passed**.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.store.worker.ts`: **passed**.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-worker.test.ts`: **passed**.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.store.worker.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-worker.test.ts docs/reference/database-schemas/worker-access.md`: **passed**.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- `pnpm build`: **passed (exit 0)**, 7m 31.8s, including runtime, declaration and Control UI builds.

</details>

The successful build also reported UI budget warnings: largest CSS gzip 57.3 KiB versus 56.9 KiB; total CSS gzip 331.0 KiB versus 329.4 KiB; total CSS raw 1707.2 KiB versus 1699.4 KiB; chat boot JS requests 21 versus 20. This PR changes no UI files; a separate base budget comparison was not run, so no attribution or budget improvement is claimed.

CI seconds are unavailable before PR CI. Earlier storage/dependency-layout setup failures are not counted as regression evidence. No native Gateway, live provider, deployment, or before/after speed benchmark was run for this candidate; the earlier text-only diagnostic workload did not establish this subagent path on its critical path.

**Additional production runtime proof:** the built production registry client and SQLite worker were exercised outside Vitest with initial host admission deliberately delayed. An independent native SQLite process was refused before the fix and acquired the writer before the real initial grant after the fix; both recorded `committed` events report successful mutation acknowledgment and native readback before orderly owner shutdown. This measures **lock availability**, not production latency or a user-visible speedup.

<details>
<summary>Delayed-admission runtime method, build identity, and sanitized trace</summary>

The same standalone Node driver and isolated synthetic state were used for both runs. It imports the built `mutateSubagentRuns` client, creates a canonical synthetic row through that client, and updates its label through the same production FIFO/persistence/worker path. No Vitest, mocks, test seam, replaced admission function, or manual grant is involved.

Node Inspector binds a breakpoint to the real host callback created by `runSubagentRegistryWorkerWrite`, immediately before its first statement reads the worker request. The paused frame verifies `stage=transaction`, `phase=waiting`, `kind=registry`, and the request's exact write-ID match. This proves the worker has reached host admission, rather than a pre-dispatch wait. The controller holds that actual callback paused for at least 350 ms and runs an independent `node:sqlite` process against the same temporary database:

```js
const db = new DatabaseSync(databasePath);
db.exec("PRAGMA busy_timeout=0");
// Read the existing synthetic row, then probe only the native writer lock.
try {
  db.exec("BEGIN IMMEDIATE");
  db.exec("ROLLBACK");
  availability = "free";
} catch (error) {
  if (error.errcode !== 5) throw error;
  availability = "held/SQLITE_BUSY";
} finally {
  db.close();
}
```

The probe releases any acquired lock before the controller resumes the production callback. The same observation at the final commit callback confirms that the writer remains held where it should. The real callback performs its existing authority checks and calls its real grant function; the controller only pauses, reads the frame, and resumes it.

Builds: **BEFORE** uses existing build `6fdf5abb9fef568d12029f90c8ef2ac70ef8b2fa`, whose differences from base `b400e8deed133ac0fa084072424fe1285f162952` are developer-tool/test changes only, with no production `src` changes. **AFTER** uses exact PR head `96ee46f545a048925c3a0a4501b006c9c2dcbaf6`. Both existing builds were used read-only. The built client is byte-identical across builds (SHA-256 `ea87a91b2e4efad62fad92d94d39914eaf323683e58cabb057851e964ee83083`), and the complete built registry-worker module is byte-identical after moving only the initial-admission statement back inside the native transaction. The baseline worker retains the pre-fix ordering; the candidate has the submitted ordering.

| Identity | BEFORE: `<baseline-build>` | AFTER: `<candidate-build>` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build root `git HEAD` | `6fdf5abb9fef568d12029f90c8ef2ac70ef8b2fa` | `96ee46f545a048925c3a0a4501b006c9c2dcbaf6` |
| `build-info.json` commit | `6fdf5abb9fef568d12029f90c8ef2ac70ef8b2fa` | `96ee46f545a048925c3a0a4501b006c9c2dcbaf6` |
| Build ID | `2026.11.5-6fdf5abb9fef-2026-11-18T21-28-55.093Z` | `2026.11.5-96ee46f545a0-2026-11-18T21-00-49.497Z` |
| Built registry-worker SHA-256 | `3eab8bc37300c796538be548e8f826cff7ed2d34a6f78df6c51f98e5d5397173` | `3eac969971928f6cba08c201dd60486583311a1420647a9051c952261c785138` |
| Source against base `b400e8deed133ac0fa084072424fe1285f162952` | `git diff b400e8deed133ac0fa084072424fe1285f162952 HEAD -- src`: **empty** | Worker ordering move plus its regression: **2 files, 17 additions, 1 deletion** under `src`; the worker is the only non-test production file |

The worker hashes differ as expected. Exact comparison replaced the candidate string ``requestSqliteWorkerOperationAdmission({stage:`transaction`,facts:n});t.write(t=>{`` with ``t.write(t=>{requestSqliteWorkerOperationAdmission({stage:`transaction`,facts:n});``. It matched exactly once and made the complete module equal to the baseline.

Environment: Windows ARM64, Node `26.13.0`, pinned pnpm `12.15.0`, probe SQLite `3.54.0`. No build, dependency install, Gateway, model, real profile, or unrelated runtime was used or changed during this proof. Paths and the task-owned ephemeral debugger endpoint are omitted below.

Sanitized driver invocation shape (both **exit 0**):

```text
node registry-admission-runtime-proof.mjs control <baseline-build> <new-empty-before-state> BEFORE
node registry-admission-runtime-proof.mjs control <candidate-build> <new-empty-after-state> AFTER
```

Commit evidence is the original driver-produced `{"event":"committed","readback":"after-mutation"}` row in **each** recorded run, emitted only after the awaited production mutation and successful native readback. The controller's exit 0 alone does **not** certify commit: its completion resolves on `owners-closed`, and the numeric host exit code was not recorded or separately asserted. Each independent probe's numeric exit status was asserted to be 0 before its output was accepted.

The build-specific client import resolves `mutateSubagentRuns` from its actual export map (`o` in these identical bundles). The controller uses CDP `Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl` at `const o=e.facts` in the built callback, reads `({stage:e.stage,phase:t,registry:n.kind,writeIdMatches:e.facts===n.writeId})` with `Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame` and `throwOnSideEffect=true`, launches the separate native probe above, and calls `Debugger.resume`. Both callback locations were bound and reached for the actual mutation.

```text
BEFORE production client ready; production callback breakpoint bound
BEFORE initial admission paused: stage=transaction phase=waiting kind=registry writeIdMatches=true
BEFORE independent native writer: BEGIN IMMEDIATE -> SQLITE_BUSY; existing label=before-mutation; host pause=473 ms
BEFORE resume unchanged real initial host grant
BEFORE commit admission paused: stage=commit phase=transaction kind=registry writeIdMatches=true
BEFORE independent native writer: BEGIN IMMEDIATE -> SQLITE_BUSY; host pause=444 ms
BEFORE resume unchanged real commit host grant
BEFORE mutation acknowledged; native readback label=after-mutation; production owners closed

AFTER production client ready; production callback breakpoint bound
AFTER initial admission paused: stage=transaction phase=waiting kind=registry writeIdMatches=true
AFTER independent native writer: BEGIN IMMEDIATE -> acquired; ROLLBACK; existing label=before-mutation; host pause=449 ms
AFTER resume unchanged real initial host grant
AFTER commit admission paused: stage=commit phase=transaction kind=registry writeIdMatches=true
AFTER independent native writer: BEGIN IMMEDIATE -> SQLITE_BUSY; host pause=433 ms
AFTER resume unchanged real commit host grant
AFTER mutation acknowledged; native readback label=after-mutation; production owners closed
```

The recorded pauses are injected debugger delays, not database timings or speedup measurements. This is the requested production worker/client fault trace, not a Gateway or model end-to-end benchmark.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ai): keep reasoning across tool calls on OpenAI-compatible proxies
prs.body:
Related: #177871

## What Problem This Solves

A reasoning-capable Chat Completions proxy configured under the name `openai` silently loses the model’s earlier reasoning on the request after a tool call. That is the configuration used by [Joël Niklaus’s Harness Leaderboard](https://huggingface.co/spaces/joelniklaus/harness-leaderboard/blob/main/hlb/wiring.py#L480-L500).

## User Impact

Reasoning-capable proxies named `openai` now get the same replay behavior as other proxy names, under the field the proxy streamed. Native OpenAI still omits those fields by default, even when configured under a different name. No configuration changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Chat Completions serializer now uses the existing native OpenAI endpoint check instead of comparing provider names. The explicit `reasoning_content` compatibility option, Foundry and other provider-specific replay, and model-switch rules are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Baseline: both transport modes dropped a synthetic reasoning marker after a tool call on an `openai`-named loopback proxy. Native OpenAI configured under another name incorrectly retained the field in the serialized request.
- Fixed: 68 focused wire/replay tests and 16 agent prefix-stability tests passed. An isolated `openclaw agent --local` run returned a real file-read tool result and preserved the streamed `reasoning` and `reasoning_content` fields in separate runs. The explicitly forced field also passed. Core typecheck, changed-file lint and format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local ClawSweeper flagged Foundry as a distinct protocol. The fix was narrowed to native OpenAI and a regression test covers that case. Local Codex autoreview (P0–P2) and hosted ClawSweeper found no actionable findings on the final replay patch. After integrating main, all 40 focused replay tests and changed-file formatting passed again; the published four-file diff is patch-identical to the reviewed fix.
- The earlier Plugins asset-budget and browser-test failures are now covered by the independently landed #202795 and #202784. The branch kept main’s UI fixes and drops its superseded UI changes; this PR’s final diff contains no UI changes.
- The full paid leaderboard was not rerun; these checks measure the missing replay on the wire, not a particular score.

Contributor credit: Peter Steinberger (@steipete); benchmark diagnosis by Joël Niklaus.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/05351ac7-82e9-4051-b492-98c85ca45af1)

prs.title: fix: show earlier attachments in Session files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Files in a long chat could show only the recent uploads. A file shared at the beginning could be missing until someone scrolled back through the conversation.

## User Impact

Session files now includes older attachments without loading earlier chat pages. Files keep their native previews, and “Show in chat” goes to the source message. A partial-list notice remains when the Gateway really cannot supply the whole list.

## Why This Change Was Made

Files already requests the session’s artifacts. The Gateway collects attachment references in that same transcript pass and reuses its revision-aware cache. There is no new table, migration, history preload, or extra catalog request. A 4 MiB ceiling bounds the extra metadata; if it is reached, the panel retains both the collected references and attachments from the loaded chat. Older Gateways retain their existing fallback.

## Evidence

- In Chromium, with the same paginated chat fixture, the original project brief was missing on `abd8b92cfa` and present on `b63c38fb27`. Both versions made one catalog request. This verifies the Control UI, not a native macOS run.
- 58 focused UI tests, the real Gateway integration test, core and UI type checks, and the UI production build passed. The build reported advisory bundle-budget overages; no budgets were raised.
- In a local synthetic session with 1,204 messages and 27 messages carrying attachments, the catalog RPC took 13.9 ms on the first request after appending history, then 3.7 and 2.6 ms. The response was 6,469 bytes. These are local observations, not a production latency guarantee.

prs.title: fix: schedule Template automations in the adding device’s time zone
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Template that says “Monday at 9 AM” now creates a cron job for **9 AM on the device that adds it**. Before, the job used the Template’s declared zone, which could run it hours earlier or later than expected. New jobs use the adding client’s validated IANA time zone, falling back to the Template’s declared zone if the client supplies no valid one. The source `CLAW.md`, cron expression and interval schedules are unchanged.

Catalog and chat previews show the schedule in the viewing device’s time zone. Viewing or retrying from a second device does not change existing jobs. Retry uses stored job identity and declaration keys to add only missing declarations; it does not move, duplicate, overwrite or re-pause an existing job.

This diff is limited to the time-zone behavior and its tests and docs. The earlier Skills/Plugins route changes were removed in favor of main’s [Skills pages](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202581) and [Plugins route checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202687). Template automations use main’s inline rows unchanged; this PR does not add a dialog.

## Evidence

All five requested local checks passed without waivers. Published `f7af676696ed` and locally tested `6ada1b98a996` have the same tree: `24211f349bb8594f860573bbd3372ac7becaf802`.

| Local check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Bundled Chromium route assets | **4/4 passed:** Skills, Skill Settings, Plugins and Plugin Settings. The previous PR head needed 57 Plugins asset requests before the page was ready. After integrating [the upstream Plugins fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202795), the same cold visit measured **55 requests**, below the unchanged limit of **56**. |
| Template, cron, subagent and scenario regressions | **244/244 passed**, including deterministic New York Add → Tokyo Retry. Only the missing declaration was created in New York time; existing jobs, including an operator-edited Paris schedule, were preserved. |
| UI owner tests | **278/278 passed.** |
| Device-zone and pending-job fixtures | **35/35 passed.** |
| Default `pnpm check:changed` | **Passed**; all three Knip scans found zero unused exports. |

The three-dot diff against integrated main `150edeea6e0e` is still the same 30-file time-zone patch as on the previous PR head. Of those files, 29 are byte-identical. `docs/cli/templates.md` also contains main’s independently added Template-drafting paragraph; the time-zone and Retry edits are unchanged. No branch-only route, budget, or presentation changes were added. These are local results, not hosted CI or review clearance. The standalone Tools catalog interaction probes and paired startup benchmark were not rerun on this tree.

### Scope of the earlier compatibility evidence

The isolated upgrade and readback covered **only tree `e3ceec9db23ba955a94541ea5b3f8753eeae0937`**, not this published tree. In that fixture, a shipped Gateway’s enabled Paris job and paused Tokyo job retained their IDs, declaration keys, cron expressions, time zones and enabled states; nine selected settings matched. No new upgrade was run for this revision.

**Real-model two-device Retry remains unproven.** The earlier hosted run did not create the jobs needed to exercise Retry. The deterministic regression above covers job reconciliation, not a completed model-driven setup.

prs.title: fix(matrix): polls show as unsupported events in Element X
prs.body:
Closes #191678

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: polls sent by the Matrix channel show as "Unsupported event" in Element X, so people on Element X cannot see or answer them.

## User Impact

User impact: polls the agent or `openclaw message poll` sends to Matrix render and can be answered in Element X as well as Element Web; votes cast by the `poll-vote` action are counted by Element X too. No config or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel sent poll starts as `m.poll.start` with the MSC3381 unstable content layout, and votes as `m.poll.response`. Element X (matrix-rust-sdk) renders polls only under the unstable names (`org.matrix.msc3381.poll.start` / `.response` / `.end`, kinds `org.matrix.msc3381.poll.disclosed` / `.undisclosed`); Element Web sends those names itself and reads both, which hid the problem. This PR sends starts and votes under the unstable names. The read side already accepts both namespaces, so existing polls in history keep parsing.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `poll-types.ts`: `buildPollStartContent` puts the poll under `org.matrix.msc3381.poll.start` with the unstable kind names; `ORG_POLL_START` / `ORG_POLL_RESPONSE` exported.
- `send.ts` / `actions/polls.ts`: send with those event types (vote content already carried both keys).
- `SPEC-SUPPORT.md`: poll rows updated (stable names parsed; unstable names sent).
- matrix-rust-sdk reference: `crates/matrix-sdk-ui/src/timeline/event_handler.rs` handles `UnstablePollStart` / `UnstablePollResponse` / `UnstablePollEnd`; ruma `poll/unstable_start/unstable_poll_kind_serde.rs` accepts only the `org.matrix.msc3381.poll.*` kind names.

</details>

## Evidence

- Live observation before the fix (2026.9.4): every poll sent by the channel was drawn in Element Web and shown as "Unsupported event" in Element X Android, in the main timeline and in threads.
- Focused tests on this branch (Windows, Node 24): `poll-types`, `actions/polls`, `actions/messages`, `poll-summary` under the extension-matrix config — 40/40 passed; `send.test.ts` under the extension-database-workers config — 46/46 passed. New test checks the outbound content shape and that it round-trips through `parsePollStart`.
- Targeted typecheck of the changed files: no new errors (only pre-existing core errors unrelated to this change, from the local Windows setup).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on the changed files; pre-commit hook passed.
- Not run: the QA Matrix live lane (no Docker on this machine); no Element X re-test against this build yet.

prs.title: fix: isolate sidebar sessions opened in managed clones
prs.body:
Related: #196206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the sidebar **+** flow starting a new session on a shared clone’s `main` checkout when it restores that clone as a folder instead of a project.

## User Impact

The composer shows **New worktree** for a saved folder that points to a managed clone root. The session opens in an isolated checkout and can delegate to child worktrees. Ordinary local folders and already-accepted direct sessions keep their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway resolves an admitted folder path to its registered managed clone and applies the same worktree policy as a project selection. The composer displays that Gateway decision rather than inferring it from the folder name.

The same Chromium test produces the same count and final `app-sidebar-customize` request on the unmodified PR base, `e5ccb878a104`.

prs.title: feat: only link file paths that open in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat replies often mention file paths that don't exist on the machine running the Gateway: files on another host (Crabbox, a paired Mac), files that were since deleted, or repo-relative paths that the Files panel resolves from the wrong folder. Today all of them render as file links. Clicking one opens the Files panel, which then shows "Couldn't open file".

## User Impact

User impact: in a settled chat transcript, a file reference confirmed unavailable by the Gateway becomes plain text, keeping its label and full path on hover. Confirmed files stay openable. Uncertain or failed checks leave the reference usable; this is not an access grant.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **New Gateway check, `sessions.files.stat`.** It takes up to 64 references and answers `file`, `missing`, or `unknown` for each. It follows the same rules as opening a file from the Files panel: same session folder, sandbox path mapping, permission check for files outside the workspace, and filename-only search. Filename-only references go through the same Files search the reader runs; one walker now serves both. The check uses the reader's admission rules, including a bounded one-byte prefix read; it does not return file contents. Repository-backed cloud sessions and remote workspaces answer `unknown`, so their links behave as before.
- **Transcript links.** The existing Markdown blocks owner hands over file links once their message stops streaming. The chat workspace's lazily loaded file runtime checks them, one request per session, and replaces each link answered `missing` with a plain `<span>` that keeps its label and hover path. No stylesheet rules or boot-path chunks are added. Availability is invalidated on permission changes, ordinary run-completion workspace refresh, and workspace retirement. Retained references are restored/rechecked through the Markdown owner; late retired checks cannot demote them. See the measured boot cost below.
- **Agent prompt.** One line now says that relative paths in replies are read from the working directory, so files elsewhere should be written as absolute paths. The source comment cites this PR's incident.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, real session.** The comparison images below are the earlier real-Gateway proof: before is `main` at `3b63f9ea1f55`, after is branch revision `5fb9bab1f13f`. They show the central presentation behavior, not the later permission/cache repairs. The session is real; its transcript has one assistant message naming `~/crabbox-work/ocid-hidden/reset-profile.sh`, which doesn't exist on that host, and `src/app.ts`, which exists in the session workspace. The model provider is a non-answering fixture, because no turn runs.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the remote path renders as a file link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0b870ea-99b1-43c0-8874-0008786fa649) | ![After: the remote path renders as plain inline code](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/955df841-aaae-4ad9-b49e-b8466cfa333a) |
| ![Before: clicking it opens the Files panel with "Couldn't open file"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f291ed78-3c09-4c30-a27c-eab0c84c1d68) | ![After: clicking it opens nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3edf0ebd-d095-4019-b4b0-f5a93b39a129) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Remote path link; click opens an error panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb64a5c7-c261-4689-896a-5125a315eb99) | ![Remote path as text; click opens nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/039af70f-a659-4b3c-a9d0-7a6682cdb26f) |

After this change, the real file still opens:

![After: clicking app.ts opens its contents in the Files panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4d86ca6-240e-4b64-829a-9440e4e528cd)

The Gateway traffic recorded from the browser's WebSocket matches the screenshots:
- **Before:** `sessions.files.get` for the remote path failed with `session_file_not_found`, and the panel opened to an error.
- **After:** one `sessions.files.stat` answered `missing` for the remote path and `file` for `src/app.ts`. Clicking the remote text sent no request, and clicking `app.ts` succeeded with `sessions.files.get`.

**Current repair proof (`a37d8b432a4d`; its UI and Gateway source are identical to this head apart from one test-only lint fix).** A narrow Control UI E2E against a real Gateway built/stamped at this exact head passed. A real session starts in Workspace mode with a real `report.md` outside its workspace: stat answers `missing`, and the reference becomes text. The test uses the actual permission picker to switch to Full: a second stat answers `file`, the retained anchor returns, and clicking it successfully reads the file. The nonexistent other-host reference remains text and sends no get when clicked. No model turn runs; its provider is intentionally non-answering. The initial rebuild attempts were refused by asset readiness after comparison-build output; the reported pass is after rebuilding at the stated head, not those refused attempts.

Production-owner Solid regressions fail before and pass after their respective fixes: Workspace → guarded → Full with a late denied response; file created → ordinary workspace refresh; hidden pane → workspace retirement → same-scope reveal. Follow-up read-only review on this head found no additional P0–P2 in these lifecycle fixes.

**Matches what actually opens.** Gateway tests run the check and a real file open side by side and require the same answer. They cover:
- workspace files, `./` paths, and directories
- files outside the workspace, with full and read-only permissions
- unique, duplicate, and missing filename-only references
- hard links, including a filename-only match that is a hard link
- a touched path when the session's working folder is a subfolder of the workspace
- a touched `./@name` reference

**Cost.** On a test Gateway in a Mac Studio container, seeded with 30 sessions of real reference sets (297 references) and 400 file tool calls each: checking one session's links took 27 ms p50 and 35 ms p90. That compares with 5.9 ms p50 for a single `sessions.files.get`. These numbers predate the review fixes, which add one file open for each reference that exists, plus a touched-file fold in the uncommon cases above. **Chat boot budget: cost approved by the maintainer.** Josh Lehman (maintainer) approved this feature's chat boot cost on 2026-11-20. Following the repository's convention for approved costs, `chatBootJsGzipBytes` now records it: CI on `ad13a19` measured 1,333,835 B, +477 B over the paired base 1,333,358 B at `d5a99b07`, plus 64 B headroom, for 1,333,899 B. The paired base was already over the previous 1,332,637 B ceiling. Before approving, the attempted cuts that moved link discovery out of the Markdown DOM owner were reverted, because they broke the Control UI controller ratchets (`querySelector` and `manualImport` counts). No other budget or ratchet changed. The full build still fails only the inherited Plugin SDK declaration budget, byte-identical to the base (5,394,009 B versus 5,385,536 B allowed).

<details><summary>Validation</summary>

- On the rebased candidate: 3 Gateway file suites / 72 tests; 5 focused UI suites / 62 tests before the final lifecycle regression extension, then 3 affected suites / 30 tests after it. Core/UI and core-test typechecks passed; line-cap, assertion-safety, controller and test-line ratchets passed (net +368/400 test lines).
- Earlier broader validation (before the latest lifecycle changes): `sessions-files*.test.ts` (7 files) and `system-prompt.test.ts`, 166 tests.
- UI: `chat-file-link-availability.test.ts`, `markdown-element-refs-solid.test.ts`, `markdown-file-links.test.ts`, `ui/src/lib/sessions`, chat session-workspace tests (1,119 tests), and `ui/src/e2e/chat-file-links.e2e.test.ts` (12 tests).
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`, line-cap ratchet, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm protocol:check`, `pnpm ui:check-performance` compared against the base build.
- Real-Gateway proof: an uncommitted Control UI real-Gateway E2E harness, run on `main` and on this branch.

</details>

**Not covered.** No test covers a filename-only miss in a message from an earlier workspace; it is left `unknown`. Document-relative links in side-panel file previews aren't checked. Out-of-band file changes without an owner refresh are not watched continuously; cached answers can remain until the next workspace refresh or permission/lifecycle change.

prs.title: fix(cron): prune expired jobless hook base sessions
prs.body:
Fixes #202621

## What Problem This Solves

Isolated webhook hook runs (`POST /hooks/agent`) build an ephemeral cron job with a random `jobId` that never enters the cron store, and execute in the reusable base session key `agent:<agent>:cron:<jobId>`. Nothing ever pruned that base record: the session reaper only sweeps `:run:` keys and `cron.remove` only covers store-backed jobs, so every hook dispatch leaked one base session row forever and pushed real conversations past UI pagination.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron session reaper now also prunes expired base cron rows whose job id is absent from the cron-store inventory, reusing the same lifecycle mutation and transcript archiving as run rows. Base rows are only considered when job inventory was readable (an unavailable store never risks deleting a live stored job's base session), and stored-job base rows keep their existing `cron.remove`-owned cleanup. `cron.sessionRetention: false` and zero/invalid retention keep disabling pruning entirely.

## User Impact

Gateways receiving webhooks no longer accumulate `agent:<agent>:cron:<uuid>` sessions; retention-configured cleanup removes them like run sessions. Stored automations keep their reusable base sessions and conversation history.

## Evidence

Real Gateway + real HTTP hook + SQLite observation (branch head dc8b97b3de, Node 26.12.1, Linux; isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `cron.sessionRetention: "1m"`):

| Step | Command / trigger | Observed result |
|---|---|---|
| Leak state | `curl -X POST .../hooks/agent` (Bearer hooks token, `sessionMode: isolated`) → `{"ok":false,"error":"hook agent run did not start before admission timeout","runId":"eb0c17fa-efd8-4975-bbaf-a28999cdee98"}` (this host has no model credentials; dispatch still prepared the session rows) | `session_nodes` gained `agent:main:cron:608047a1-c9b7-439b-b8e0-5857cba16672` plus its `:run:` row |
| Retention sweep | Real gateway `cron-maintenance` tick (2026-11-21 03:22 +08, retention 1m) | both hook rows gone from `session_nodes` |
| Stored-job base preserved | memory-core dreaming job `76d195eb-a3f4-4b72-9c07-5d8e6d72d448` (in cron store) | its `agent:main:cron:76d195eb-…` base row retained through the same sweep |

Unit regression (red/green), `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts`: the two new tests fail on the unpatched reaper (2 failed / 18 passed) and all 20 pass with the fix. `test-lines` ratchet: net +26 covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/202621-hook-cron-base-retention.txt`.

Gap: the "forever" half of the leak was not re-run against unpatched main on this host (no model credentials available); it is evidenced by the reporter's released-version observation (430 leaked rows after ~7 days at ~60 hooks/day) and by the unpatched reaper never considering base keys (red unit run).

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and git log to analyze issue #202621, locate the retention gap in `src/cron/session-reaper.ts`, and implement the inventory-gated base-row sweep. The implementer understands the code: the reaper partitions expired candidates by base-vs-run cron key shape and prunes only jobless base rows when store inventory is readable. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(ui): remove resting chrome from Customize settings gears
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The settings gear on Customize pages shows a square outline at rest, and the light theme adds a faint shadow. That makes the gear look raised even when it is not being used.

## User Impact

On Plugins, Skills, and Skill Workshop, only the gear is visible at rest. The icon, hit area, hover and press feedback, keyboard focus ring, and existing actions stay the same. Templates has an Import button, not a gear, and is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make the shared Customize gear's resting border transparent and remove its inherited shadow. Keeping the border geometry avoids shifting the icon. The hover and focus rules are unchanged.

## Evidence

Verified all four routes in the Control UI in Chromium (1280 × 800, synthetic Gateway data), in both light and dark themes. Plugins and Skills settings open from the keyboard; Skill Workshop's menu opens with Enter and closes with Escape. Templates still opens its Import file picker. Focused stylesheet lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.

The screenshots show the four real Customize routes. Dark comparison: main `7af829afeef7` versus this patch. The light comparison isolates the remaining shadow after the border was made transparent.

prs.title: fix: keep the compact Skill workshop heading accessible
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Plugins navigation checks expected installed providers in ordinary browsing and an “Install” action on Skills after those flows changed. They also exposed an accessibility regression: the compact Skill workshop layout removed its page heading from assistive technology.

## User Impact

The compact Skill workshop keeps an accessible heading with the same visible layout and learning menu. Browser checks cover the current catalog, search, pagination, and Skills actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep installed video providers in search, clear search before testing pagination, and use the Skills “Add” action. Visually clip the compact workshop heading instead of hiding its entire row from accessibility, while preserving the existing learning menu’s docs link.

## Evidence

- [Diagnostic browser run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44840083042/job/136646580798): the phone/tablet failures located the heading under a parent with `display: none`.
- [Final CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44844222173) passed at `f5bff5d231bbac1aec8c71e272d4e23a5f754eb2`, including [navigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44844222173/job/136660516474), [performance budgets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44844222173/job/136660516590), lint, and the broader selected checks.
- Focused stylelint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh local ClawSweeper review of the complete committed range found no actionable correctness or security issues.
- The final CSS preserves separately indexed selectors. No budgets or lint baselines changed.

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS CI lint step fails because the OpenClaw ID sign-in window mixes multiple initializer arguments on one line within a multiline call.

## User Impact

This restores the macOS lint check without changing sign-in behavior or the window appearance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Put each NSWindow argument on its own line to satisfy the existing SwiftLint rule. The diff changes whitespace only.

## Evidence

- Reproduced both `multiline_arguments` errors from [the main CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44836724351/job/136644584083) on base `9d892ccd1068116d5a76b52a297e7c351ae12e91`.
- With the fix, SwiftLint 0.65.1 passes for the affected file with `--strict --config config/swiftlint.yml`.
- SwiftFormat 0.63.1 passes for the affected file with `--lint --config config/swiftformat`.

- `git diff --check` passes; removing whitespace from the before/after source produces identical text.
- The local commit hook cannot finish its global native string inventory in the sparse checkout (Android sources are absent). This whitespace-only change uses the documented targeted-validation commit route; the complete native string inventory subsequently passed in PR CI.
- [Final PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44844968141) passed at `726f4771c4e416bb7ba84fa6261087191d11d42c`, including the native string inventory.

prs.title: fix(ui): align Plugins hub navigation checks with current actions
prs.body:
## Superseded by #202784

While this investigation was running, #202784 landed as `26eb694b8089af578f6af1e90dab80fda53f7785`. It repairs the same Skills action selector and Media expectations, and also fixes the real compact Workshop accessibility defect. Its final-head CI (`f5bff5d231bbac1aec8c71e272d4e23a5f754eb2`, run 44844222173) is green, including UI e2e and performance budgets.

This duplicate will not merge. In particular, this candidate's `includeHidden` expectation would accept the inaccessible compact heading; the landed repair correctly retains the accessible heading instead. The diagnosis below remains valid for the reported Plugins Install timeout: Plugins buttons render; the failing caller is Skills, whose action is Add. No Plugins schema/asset rollback is justified.

The before/after screenshots below compare pinned main with this unmerged test-only candidate; both show the same production Plugins buttons. They are not screenshots of the peer's accessibility repair. Independent verification of the landed repair is in progress.

## What Problem This Solves

The Plugins hub navigation e2e reports a timeout waiting for an Install button, but the timeout occurs after navigating to Skills. Plugins Install buttons render correctly. Skills intentionally renamed its action to Add in #202531; this test continued searching for Install.

The same file has two other stale expectations: #202527 hides installed plugins from discovery, and #202537 replaces the narrow Skill workshop heading with learning controls and moves its documentation link into their menu.

Related: #202531, #202527, #202537, #202687, #202795.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. This repairs false failures in the navigation checks; users did not lose Plugins Install buttons through #202687. The settings and markdown deferrals remain intact, as do all route asset budgets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use exact accessible action names, Install Matrix and Add Calendar, while preserving visibility and full computed-style equality across all four viewports. Keep the Media category/pagination fixtures available so discovery can list them. Check the intended compact Workshop layout and open its learning menu to verify the visible documentation link. The optional historical screenshot scenario reloads after changing fixture revisions so it does not reuse the before-overview.

Simplification: one existing test file, no new test or production helper. Production LOC delta: 0. No schema, cache, config, dependency, timeout, or budget changes.

## Evidence

Native production UI runner on pinned main `8271ec9ee5d48655b6d41d39314bd4e44e73b7c0` and purported last-green `4b74fd5a979df` reproduces 5 failures / 5 passes: four timeouts at the Skills caller (line 538), plus the installed Media fixture. The Plugins caller (line 530) succeeds first. Therefore the supplied hourly last-green boundary does not match this pinned-source reproduction; #202687 is not the origin of these test failures.

Source attribution: #202531 (`856aca23d7fb`) introduced Add at 18:33Z; #202527 (`c2c2effaeddb`) introduced installed filtering at 18:18Z; #202537 (`31ce94f0ad89`) introduced compact Workshop at 18:11Z, all on November 20. Native proof on the parent before #202527 passes Media; its earlier Skills style mismatch is a different condition, subsequently repaired by #202531.

All four viewport transitions and Media category/pagination pass through the native production e2e runner. The optional Media capture scenario also passes. The unchanged route-asset suite passes all four cases, including Plugins <=56. `pnpm check:changed` passes; final isolated Codex autoreview of the complete diff and owner/test source is scoped-clean through P2 (base `8271ec9`, no actionable findings).

One full-file run reported an intermittent unchanged LTR scroll-edge assertion (both edge flags true despite overflow); earlier base and candidate runs passed it, and an isolated replay on exact main parent `8271ec9` passes. This is retained as unresolved local evidence, not claimed fixed or dismissed as noise. No scroll assertion changed and no inherited-failure merge exception is claimed; exact-head CI must pass. Browser screenshots use the real production Control UI and synthetic mock-Gateway fixtures, not a live Gateway or registry.

Performance acceptance: production source and bundle inputs are unchanged. Record five serial A1/A2/B observations of the same production artifact using the existing 300-agent/1,000-catalog fixture and 100ms synthetic network; report readiness, renderer CPU, assets/bytes and a separate allocation pass without a speedup claim. Storage size is outside this browser/mock boundary.

![Before: Plugins Install buttons already render on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ed0612e-0016-46c3-9607-483e64fa38f7)

![After: Plugins Install buttons remain unchanged after the test repair](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/112b7396-1817-4916-b9c9-a969e276d258)

![Skills uses Add Calendar, the action the navigation test now checks](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f4be063-df8f-46d3-9a01-bc9a8e3de9d6)

prs.title: fix(onboard): reject --secret-input-mode ref when the provider API key flag differs from the env var
prs.body:
AI-assisted: yes

Closes #201401

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --secret-input-mode ref` with a provider API key flag (for example `--anthropic-api-key`) while the provider's environment variable holds a *different* value would silently end up with a reference to the stale environment variable; the explicitly passed key was discarded with no warning, and onboarding reported success.
- **Related:** #201401; the Gateway credential flags already reject this exact mismatch (`src/commands/onboard.ts`), so provider flags now follow the same contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** When `--secret-input-mode ref` is used and both the provider flag and its env var are set to different values, onboarding now fails with the same error shape the Gateway credential flags use, instead of silently keeping the env value. Matching values, env-only, and flag-only (plaintext) flows are unchanged.
- **Out of scope:** No changes to reference serialization, plaintext flag precedence, or the Gateway credential checks themselves.
- **Highest-risk area:** The shared non-interactive resolver used by provider methods, custom-provider onboarding, and reset validation.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The comparison is added only to the existing ref-mode branch, after the existing malformed-input check (preserving the current malformed-input error precedence), and both values are normalized the same way as today. The error message contains neither value.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=A openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --secret-input-mode ref --anthropic-api-key B` (A ≠ B) now exits 1 with `--anthropic-api-key does not match ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Set the environment variable to the same value or omit the flag.` and persists no credentials; when A = B the env reference is stored exactly as before.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/api-keys.ts` (single comparison in the ref-mode branch) and the new regression tests in `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/api-keys.test.ts` (`stores the env reference when a ref-mode flag matches the env var`, `rejects a ref-mode flag that differs from the provider env var without leaking either value`).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Isolated worktree of this PR branch, shipped CLI entry point (`node scripts/run-node.mjs`) with local runtime build, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR` pointed at temp dirs; synthetic (non-secret) key values.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # mismatch case (should now fail, before it silently stored the env reference)
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-stale-env-key \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk \
    --secret-input-mode ref --anthropic-api-key sk-ant-rotated-flag-key
  # matching case (should keep working, with --skip-health)
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-same-key \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health \
    --secret-input-mode ref --anthropic-api-key sk-ant-same-key
  # regression tests
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/api-keys.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-stale-env-key ... --anthropic-api-key sk-ant-rotated-flag-key
  → exit 1
  --anthropic-api-key does not match ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Set the environment variable to the same value or omit the flag.
  (no credential profile persisted; neither key value appears in the output)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Conflicting ref-mode inputs are rejected before any credential is persisted; the matching case still exits 0 and stores `keyRef: {"source":"env","id":"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"}` as before. Unit suite `api-keys.test.ts` 14/14 green via validate.sh (oxfmt + oxlint + tsgo:core).
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** On origin/main @ f5b717d232f the same mismatch command was accepted silently: onboarding proceeded past the API-key stage and stored `anthropic:default` with `keyRef: {"source":"env","id":"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"}` — the passed `--anthropic-api-key` value was never used.
- **What was not tested:** Live provider authentication (synthetic key values only; no real Anthropic credentials were involved). Gateway health checks beyond `--skip-health` (requires a running gateway; unrelated to this change).
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review; CI lanes pending.

prs.title: fix(skills): accept comments after multiline quoted descriptions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill Creator rejects an otherwise valid skill when its multiline quoted description has an inline comment containing angle brackets after the closing quote. Authors running Python without PyYAML hit this error in both validation and packaging.

## User Impact

Skill authors can validate and package these skills using a standard-library-only Python environment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dependency-free validator now applies its existing quote-aware comment handling to the assembled quoted value, so an editor's note after the closing quote is excluded from description validation. Both commands use the same validator. The change adds nine net production lines and three test cases.

## Evidence

On Linux with Python 3.12.3 and no PyYAML installed, the real validation and packaging commands rejected both single- and double-quoted fixtures on OpenClaw v2026.11.6 and base `150edeea6e0`. With this patch both commands exited 0, the ZIP integrity checks passed, and the archived `SKILL.md` matched the input byte for byte. A fixture with angle brackets inside the description still exited 1 and produced no archive. A plain multiline description with a trailing comment succeeded on both the base and the patch.

PyYAML 6.0.1 independently parsed both valid fixtures and returned the folded description without the comment. The distinction follows the [YAML 1.2.2 rules for comments](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#66-comments) and [quoted flow scalars](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#73-flow-scalar-styles).

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and focused checks</summary>

Create `meeting-notes/SKILL.md` with this content and run the same commands on the base and the patched checkout.

```yaml
---
name: meeting-notes
description: "Summarize team
  meeting notes." # <editor note>
---
```

```sh
python3 -m venv --without-pip /tmp/skill-proof-venv
/tmp/skill-proof-venv/bin/python skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py meeting-notes
/tmp/skill-proof-venv/bin/python skills/skill-creator/scripts/package_skill.py meeting-notes out
python3 -m zipfile -t out/meeting-notes.skill
```

On the base both Python commands exited 1 with `Description cannot contain angle brackets (< or >)`. On the patch validation reported `Skill is valid!` and packaging wrote the archive. Replacing the quote pair with single quotes gave the same before/after results.

- `python -m pytest -q -c skills/pyproject.toml skills/skill-creator/scripts` passed 12 tests and 57 subtests. The two new positive subtests failed on the original parser. The standard-library unittest run also passed all 12 tests without PyYAML.
- Targeted Ruff lint and `git diff --check` passed. Ruff format flagged the same pre-existing test line in the base and candidate.
- Codex autoreview covered the uncommitted two-file patch against `150edeea6e0` at P0–P3 and returned `scoped-clean`. The reviewer assessed the supplied patch and did not independently rerun the CLI.
- Local CLI evidence is from Linux. Broader checks are left to GitHub CI.

</details>

AI-assisted.

prs.title: fix: keep the conversation visible when switching sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a chat for the first time briefly replaced the previous messages with gray placeholders and then an empty conversation. This is the transcript flash visible in the after-video on #201318, not the sidebar list jump that PR fixes.

## User Impact

User impact: switching chats keeps the previous conversation readable, but not interactive, until the selected conversation can be shown. Already-loaded conversations still switch immediately. If a first load takes longer than half a second, the selected chat shows its own loading state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Having message rows in the page does not mean they are visible: the transcript deliberately hides them while it restores the reading position. The handoff now covers both preparation and positioning. It reuses the mounted conversation rather than copying messages between sessions or blocking navigation on history.

## Evidence

Four first visits in the actual desktop Control UI, with distinct synthetic histories, Chromium at 1100 × 760, and 4× CPU slowdown. We checked the pixels in the conversation body on every frame of the 25 fps switch clips (initial app startup excluded). On main (`abd8b92cfa49`), messages disappeared on all four switches for 9–12 frames each: 44/297 frames in total. On the tested change (`c342aa29cbf9`), 0/296 frames lost message text. Each click reached the correct transcript.

The UI typecheck, both focused component/browser tests, and all ten bundled navigation tests passed, including slow startup, retained scroll position, and typing focus. This was not a live Gateway test.
