prs.title: fix: make proactive checks opt-in on fresh installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a fresh install, the Proactive check can revisit the main conversation every 30 minutes and spend the user’s model allowance even when they haven’t asked OpenClaw to monitor anything. Having it on by default can be confusing for new users: setup gives them little guidance on what belongs on the checklist, and OpenClaw doesn’t reliably choose useful items or keep the list current as their needs change. That can leave them unsure what OpenClaw is watching, what they need to maintain themselves, and why their allowance is going down.

## User Impact

The check is still there, but it has no next run until enabled. Find it with `openclaw automations list --all`, then run `openclaw automations enable <job-id>`. Existing checks keep their enabled or disabled state, and manually created automations are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Periodic checks are useful when someone wants them. Making the first check opt-in lets new users decide when that benefit is worth the background usage, without turning it off for people who already rely on it. Only first-time setup changes; Doctor and template imports keep their existing migration rules. This is independent of #201282 and changes no scheduler, delivery, or global automation policy.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main (`1ac1fa353ab9`): a fresh baseline setup reported an enabled 30-minute check, and the new regression failed on `enabled: true`. On the patched Gateway, listing all jobs showed the check disabled with no next run. Enabling it scheduled a run; disabling it cleared the next run. Fresh non-interactive team onboarding also reported periodic checks off.
- All **71 tests across four suites passed**: default provisioning, baseline setup, first-agent persistence, and Doctor heartbeat cadence migration. Coverage includes rerunning setup with disabled, enabled, and deleted defaults, a same-name manual job, and both states of legacy heartbeat monitors.
- Two independent upgrades from the published `2026.11.6` package through `doctor --fix` and repeat setup preserved the choices: the enabled check retained its 30-minute cadence; the explicitly disabled check retained its ID and had no next run.
- The CLI build, core typecheck, touched-file lint and format, and docs link audit passed. Guided and classic interactive entry points were source-traced to the shared owner, not driven end to end. No live model call was needed to verify scheduling.
- Local autoreview preflight did not launch a reviewer: its required scratch directory must be outside the reviewed checkout, whereas this task’s scratch is inside it.

### Required UI check: also fails on upstream main

The [PR shard `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` on `cf62a09e`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44799208062/job/136507514773) and the [completed scheduled-main shard `checks-ui-e2e (2/10)` on `a3bd84cc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44802039471/job/136517215441) both report these three failures in `ui/src/e2e/route-asset-requests.e2e.test.ts`:

| Test under `First-visit route asset requests` | Failure in both job logs |
| --- | --- |
| `bounds skills ready-window asset requests at 100 ms from a settled New Session` | Timed out waiting for `.skill-discovery [data-skill-id]`. |
| `bounds skill-settings ready-window asset requests at 100 ms from a settled New Session` | 33 asset requests; limit 31. |
| `bounds plugins ready-window asset requests at 100 ms from a settled New Session` | Timed out waiting for `openclaw-plugins-page .plugin-catalog-card`. |

I ran `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/route-asset-requests.e2e.test.ts` in a clean checkout of upstream main at [`792134b51d1fb16105d553a8be8d67f29bc72ff6`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/792134b51d1fb16105d553a8be8d67f29bc72ff6), without this PR: the same three cases failed, and `plugin-settings` passed (3 failed, 1 passed). An [independent PR’s shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44798650717/job/136505673978) also shows all three signatures. This attributes the failures to the upstream UI suite; it does not clear or waive the [required CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44799208062/job/136512887796).

prs.title: fix(windows): distinguish invalid Scheduled Task inspection responses
prs.body:
Related: #199617

## What Problem This Solves

Windows update failures report the same “invalid response” for malformed PowerShell JSON, invalid access facts, and an invalid task snapshot, hiding which inspection step failed.

## User Impact

Operators receive a specific, privacy-safe failure category in service errors and bounded update reports. Service-stop verification and existing refusal behavior remain unchanged.

**This is a diagnostic improvement, not a verified fix for the terminal-origin beta.2 → beta.3 update failure. The original failure category and root cause remain unknown. Native Windows proof of the patched diagnostic through the installed updater remains outstanding.** The inspecting runtime must contain the change; a newer candidate cannot change probes executed by an older installed updater.

Peter’s related mitigation [#199918](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199918) merged on November 16 as `ae678bf4c6b808b3ffc69b67e62d3a54c5e0d67f`. It refuses Gateway-started Windows Scheduled Task updates before mutation; it does not repair the terminal-origin invalid-response failure reported in #199617.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep classification in the existing Task Scheduler probe and formatting in the existing service-error owner. Attach a closed stage at each of the three existing invalid-response branches, then carry it through the existing service and report paths. The labels identify the failed inspection step, not its underlying cause. Emit no raw PowerShell output, task definitions, account values, or parser exception text; retain the generic message when no stage is available. Parsing acceptance, access checks, retries, state, and service mutations are unchanged.

## Evidence

The source remains `7b970278f1b469973fc59ce62c4e7bbabf391b28`. The November 20 follow-up changes this evidence description only; it does not claim a new implementation, new test execution, or a repaired Windows update.

### Original implementation evidence

Retained from the implementation report, not independently rerun during this evidence-only follow-up:

- Three synthetic native-response regressions fail on the unchanged implementation and pass with this patch. They distinguish JSON, access-fact, and snapshot failures while keeping a synthetic secret out of the error and cause.
- 99 focused tests passed across `schtasks-state-probe.test.ts`, `service-command-read.test.ts`, `update-command-service-report.test.ts`, and `update-command-service-unavailable.test.ts`, using `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`. The report cases preserve the category within the 200-character failure-fact bound and assert that service stop/install/restart remain uncalled.
- Core production typecheck, services and config/CLI test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Auto Review (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) assessed the complete local diff against `7d7d86bb79ca24bfaf9343290cb22f80d705ab20`: scoped-clean, no findings; it did not independently execute tests. The existing [hosted source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199651#issuecomment-6897019692) also reports no findings on the unchanged published head. Neither review substitutes for native Windows proof.

### Incident and CI follow-up

- The [November 19 reporter update](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/199617#issuecomment-7023968687) confirms terminal-origin updates from installed 2026.11.5-beta.2 (`c0f42f6`) to beta.3. The retained failure report lacks the underlying native output, exit code, HRESULT, and elapsed time. Later successful probes in other contexts cannot identify which branch failed originally. No access, locale, execution-policy, CLIXML, or Windows Job cause is established.
- The exact-head [baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44079742929/job/134028115017) records GitHub’s hosted-runner communication-loss annotation; its log remains unavailable. The [ci-gate log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44079742929/job/134053671804) fails on that job and labels its main comparison as **job-name-only**, not matching failure signatures. **The required PR ci-gate remains red.** Successful lint/typecheck/changed-test checks do not make the overall gate green.
- The later [scheduled-main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44092629110/job/134072440272), at `f1d40db4d99bca224aac35d4f71a7d5dc925c216`, shows all ten ratchets passing in the available log tail. This follow-up independently compared its `checks-baseline-ratchets` job definition with this PR’s: identical definitions, but different events and source trees. That result neither proves this PR’s ratchets pass nor identifies the cause of its runner disconnect.
- The reporter separately summarizes November 19 R2 run `5df0df8e-88b7-48b0-a710-9ef95b671cc6`: installed 2026.11.5 (`e13cf15`) → 2026.11.10-beta.1, with npm/package-swap failures. Those artifacts were not retrieved in this follow-up; the comment supplies no artifact download links. This separate run is not evidence for the inspection error or this diagnostic patch.

**Remaining proof:** redacted output from a native Windows updater containing this patch must show the category reaching a bounded CLI/update report while inspection uncertainty still prevents mutation. The original beta.2 → beta.3 failure and a successful repair of that incident remain separate investigation work. No live Gateway/service changes or additional reporter update run were performed or requested here.

<details>
<summary>Simplification and follow-up validation</summary>

The requested `pr-simplify` pass reviewed the full diff against `7d7d86bb79ca24bfaf9343290cb22f80d705ab20`, direct callers, and the earlier inspection-diagnostic and Windows-access changes. No further source reduction was justified: the patch uses the existing probe, formatter, and report owners without adding a helper, logging pipeline, retries, or state. The generic no-stage diagnostic preserves the existing error contract.

Each test group protects a different failure: the probe tests catch lost classification and raw-output disclosure; service-command tests catch loss during strict command inspection/sanitization; report tests catch truncation or propagation loss and unintended service mutation. The native proof-helper schema change prevents its existing parser from stripping the optional stage; it is not proof that a native run occurred.

Whole-change delta remains production +15/-6, tests/support +73/-42, documentation +6/-0 across seven files. Follow-up source delta is zero. The imported tree exactly matches the published head, and `git diff --cached --check 7d7d86bb79ca24bfaf9343290cb22f80d705ab20` passes. Unchanged focused/type/lint/format evidence is reused rather than represented as freshly executed. Native Windows proof is still absent.

</details>

Reported and requested by Donniefi.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1956c2fd-32f7-43ce-bdd7-546240eba2b4)
- [Follow-up discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/235176eb-04cb-46e9-b356-c63ff16f0f5f)
- [Follow-up evidence rework and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3f291ee2-7535-44a8-804a-43833e327c66)

prs.title: fix(test): prevent recursive Git processes in workflow fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workflow tests can create an unbounded chain of Git processes when the configured Git executable is itself a wrapper that looks up its backend through PATH. The security-fast fixture delegates with its own fake Git still first on PATH, so the backend can repeatedly rediscover the fixture.

## User Impact

Developers can run these workflow fixtures behind the agent Git wrapper without recursive process growth. This is a test-only repair: production behavior, configuration, and database schemas are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonicalize the configured Git path before fixture setup, reject temporary fixture backends, restore the original lookup PATH when delegating, and propagate a sentinel that rejects re-entry with an explicit error. Keep the network-command prohibition and local-only Git environment. Use shared JavaScript and shell preambles for the forwarding Git shims found through both executable writers, including workflow, release, checkpoint, opengrep, and PR worktree tests; preserve package acceptance's existing bounded synthetic backend contract.

The inherited PATH is the cause reproduced with the actual agent-wrapper source. Missing target variables throw, and the Bun probe preserves the parent environment; no Bun environment-sharing workaround is added. Production LOC delta is zero; test/support growth provides target validation and the missing behavioral regressions.

## Evidence

- Security-fast: all 22 cases pass with Node and the pinned Bun runtime. The bounded nested re-entry regression returns 0 on the original shim and 98 with the repair. Prior-fixture and symlink targets are rejected; clone/fetch/ls-remote still fail with the network prohibition.
- Capped direct self-target reproduction: the original shim exhausts its process allowance; the repair exits 98 with `recursive test Git shim invocation refused`.
- Capped actual agent-wrapper reproduction on a synthetic 62,000-file / 1.116 GB workspace: the original cycle reaches 26 processes and 599 MiB aggregate RSS before its five-second deadline; the repair completes in 50 ms. Native-Git A/A and fixed controls each take 30 ms wall / 20 ms CPU. No healthy-path speedup is claimed.
- Focused proof: 33 Bun cases across security-fast, opengrep, and checkpoint admission; seven release-ancestry / PR worktree cases; the release-candidate forwarding case; and five sparse-acquisition cases. Final Node security-fast: 22 cases in 18.23 seconds. Linux-only fallback-history and updater coverage is supplied by the passing PR CI run. The longest selected fixture group was sparse acquisition at 184.31 seconds.
- Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. `pnpm check:changed` passed formatting, all root typechecks, scripts/test lint and its other guards, but its production/full-tree export scans found the unrelated `LEAN_PROFILE_MEMORY_THRESHOLD_BYTES` export introduced by #202422 (`28aa5c88fd45a`). The same export failure reproduces on exact untouched parent `3ac8d23a2cb6d92f8b76b1d60351a58ed0e9b78f`; #202785 has since fixed it on main. This is recorded as a main regression, not a passing local check. Final-head CI [44842764257](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44842764257) passed on `a052fa443c7764018b08b3d857f794f28a783184`; the exact-head watcher reports GREEN. [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202798#issuecomment-7053817825) reviewed that same head with zero open items.

All deliberate pre-fix recursion probes used a verified hard process limit and a process-group deadline. The committed re-entry regression redirects to native Git after one re-entry if the sentinel is broken, so the regression itself remains bounded.

prs.title: fix: hide redundant “Message” labels in chat replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Template welcome can show an envelope labeled “Message” above the greeting and another above the plugin card. Both refer to content already displayed in the same conversation, but look like separate actions the reader should inspect.

## User Impact

Chat shows the greeting, setup activity, status, plugin card and closing text in order without separate rows for sending those replies. Sends to other conversations, failed sends and unconfirmed deliveries still appear as activity. No Template changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing delivery receipt when deciding which completed sends belong in the activity list and its summary. This changes presentation only; the tool still sends the reply and its underlying call remains recorded. An external channel’s transcript mirror is best-effort: its receipt confirms delivery to the current conversation, not that mirroring succeeded.

## Evidence

The same browser regression found two standalone “Message” rows on `b413b8e19667` and none on `07264f8106a7`. Both show the greeting, other setup activity, status, install-ready Travel Themes card and final reply. prs.title: fix: keep same-email ChatGPT workspaces connected
prs.body:
Related: #83627

## What Problem This Solves

Signing into a second ChatGPT workspace under the same email can replace the first connected account. People with both Personal and Business workspaces need to keep both connected to use their separate limits.

## User Impact

User impact: ChatGPT workspaces with distinct account claims can stay connected under the same email. Existing profile IDs remain unchanged; an account already overwritten must be signed in again. If OpenClaw cannot safely reuse an occupied automatic ID, it leaves the saved credential untouched. Choose a different `--profile-id` when signing in from the CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

New sign-ins share an email-based profile ID. When the saved credential belongs to a different workspace, OpenClaw appends the new workspace ID instead of replacing it. Imported profiles can supply their saved workspace ID if the access token does not include it. OpenClaw reuses a verified reconnect first, including one under a custom ID, and checks the final automatic ID against the credential store before writing. For shared reconnects, OpenClaw can also use saved Codex import identity when the old access token is missing claims; both the user and workspace must match, and contradictory evidence prevents reuse. A failed refresh can recover the generated slot only when the saved workspace and the provider-verified email both match. No storage migration is required.

## Evidence

**Stable reconnect follow-up (`a4a5f487477a`):** the exact 2026.11.6 CLI imported a synthetic Codex profile whose access token lacked workspace and user claims. After running the candidate’s native schema maintenance on a copy of that SQLite state, the candidate matched and updated the original profile and preserved its configured order. A different user in the same workspace did not match. All 69 focused tests passed, along with targeted lint, formatting and OpenAI typecheck. Independent local P0–P2 review found no actionable findings in the follow-up scope. No live OAuth exchange or Gateway session was used.

**Maintainer follow-up (`0a6e087c6e4f`):** addressed [Sally’s five review findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202626#issuecomment-7048413565). The OpenAI OAuth/device-code, shared login, and reconnect identity suites passed on the final patch. The adjacent SQLite persistence suite also passed before a line-neutral login wiring refactor. OpenAI extension typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Final local Codex autoreview of the staged delta against `271d878295cd` found no actionable P0–P2 issues in scope. The follow-up was not exercised with live OpenAI credentials or a live Gateway.

**Live device-code proof, supplied by the reporter:** on macOS arm64 in isolated named-profile state, Personal → Business → Personal reconnect → Business reconnect retained exactly two stable profile IDs. Each reconnect refreshed only its own profile. Selecting each profile separately returned its own usage and the expected distinct plans (`pro` and `team`). The two-profile order was restored afterwards. The reporter tested the original patch described below; the existing Gateway and normal state were not changed.

**Independently run on the original patch:** both regression cases fail on the unmodified base at the same-email collision. With the fix, OAuth and device-code cases keep profiles distinct across repeated logins and the existing matcher selects only the matching workspace; all 20 focused tests passed. Plugin and focused test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.

Live browser-OAuth, Gateway/Models/chat login, model inference, and an unpatched live reproduction were not exercised. The browser-OAuth entry point is covered by the synthetic regression test, not claimed as live-tested.

**Reporter’s live results (redacted):** four local `models auth login --provider openai --method device-code` runs with `models auth list` after each. The account identifiers below are consistent placeholders, not credentials.

| Observation | `openai:<same-email>` | `openai:<same-email>:<business-id>` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Personal sign-in | Saved | — |
| Business sign-in | Unchanged | Saved |
| Personal reconnect | Refreshed | Unchanged |
| Business reconnect | Unchanged | Refreshed |
| `status --usage` with only that profile selected | `authProfileId` matched; `pro`, 168h window | `authProfileId` matched; `team`, 5h and weekly windows |

<details>
<summary>Reporter’s redacted CLI usage excerpts</summary>

The reporter selected one saved profile at a time, confirmed the order with `models auth order get --provider openai --json`, then ran `status --usage --json --timeout 30000`. The lines below are projections of the reporter’s CLI output, not a fresh run or a terminal recording. Usage percentages, reset timestamps, billing, and account identifiers are omitted or redacted.

```text
Personal order: ["openai:<same-email>"]
Personal usage: {"authProfileId":"openai:<same-email>","plan":"pro","windows":["168h"]}
Business order: ["openai:<same-email>:<business-id>"]
Business usage: {"authProfileId":"openai:<same-email>:<business-id>","plan":"team","windows":["5h","Week"]}
```

After the reconnects and usage checks, the reporter restored the two-profile order and verified both IDs remained present.

</details>

The live proof ran against the original published production code. Commit `271d878295cd` preserved the OAuth test mock’s real module exports, fixing the CI mock-export ratchet without changing production code or the baseline. The ratchet failed on the prior head and passed after the change; all 20 focused tests, touched-test typecheck, lint and format passed again.

**Latest-stable existing-state compatibility (synthetic, real CLI):** I built the official **2026.11.6** release tag (`06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638`) from source with its frozen lockfile and dependency policy intact. Its CLI imported a synthetic pre-existing OAuth profile into SQLite and persisted its order. I copied that isolated state and ran the patched CLI from the source corresponding to PR head `271d878295cd801e7b6c29eebf05952f898431ac` (base version string 2026.11.5; no version bump in this PR). Normalized `models auth list`, `models auth order get`, and `auth` config matched byte-for-byte. No provider requests, real credentials, or live Gateway were used.

<details>

```text

Candidate CLI: OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (7c1671a), with the exact PR diff

```

- Base: `7c1671a05f62c091cec5d548d1edd77b85330a60`.

## What Problem This Solves

When an older session received a live update, Activity moved it to the top—even if you were reading it. The row could jump completely out of view.

## User Impact

You can scroll through older sessions without losing your place. Titles, status, and recaps still update. When you return to the top and stop scrolling, the latest sessions appear automatically. There is no refresh button.

## Why This Change Was Made

Activity holds the displayed row order and day groups while you read, not the underlying data. Returning briefly to the top and reversing direction does not reshuffle the list. Once scrolling settles at the top, the feed resumes its newest-first order using the existing list animation, which respects reduced motion. Changing filters starts a fresh list.

## Evidence

[Before and after: the same live update at phone width](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201448#issuecomment-6991169321)

In production-bundled Chromium with synthetic Gateway updates, the reading row moved 881 CSS pixels on desktop and 922 on an emulated phone before the fix. On both layouts it now moves less than 1 pixel in the same scenario. The tests also cover recap growth above the reader, new arrivals, reversing at the top, automatic catch-up, and a filter that introduces a previously unseen session. The 28 existing Activity view tests and UI typecheck passed. Independent re-review found no remaining P0–P2 issues after a filter-scope correction. prs.title: fix: retain diagnostics for VM-created errors in logs
prs.body:
Related: #200439

## What Problem This Solves

When a subsystem logs an Error created in a Node VM, the file log and console can show `error: {}` instead of the failure message and stack. That leaves operators without the details needed to investigate the failure.

## User Impact

VM-created errors retain the same diagnostic fields as ordinary errors: name, message, error code when present, and stack. File logs keep the full stack; the console keeps its existing six-line limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each VM has its own Error constructor, so the host's `instanceof Error` check misses these native errors. The existing metadata preparation step now also uses Node's native-error check. The fix reuses the current field selection and sink handling without adding a formatter or changing plain-object metadata.

This is a reproduced remaining error shape, not a confirmed explanation of the original reporter's warnings in #200439. That issue should remain open until its actual caught value is identified.

## Evidence

- The new VM case failed on the original implementation while the same-realm control passed. With the fix, all 84 tests across the subsystem, logger redaction, console capture, and console timestamp suites passed on Node 24.22.1/Linux.
- A separate source-level Node process used normal logging configuration, `createSubsystemLogger`, and `flushLogger`, with no logger mocks or overrides. Both the real JSONL file and JSON console changed from `{"error":{}}` to an error record containing `name: "Error"`, `message: "VM operation failed"`, and the stack. prs.title: fix: keep a run going after a long tool call fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's tool call stayed open for more than about six minutes and then failed, OpenClaw could stop the whole run as "Reply operation stalled" before the agent saw the result. Examples of failed results: an exec killed by the host exec memory budget, an exec that hit its timeout, or a tool that threw. The run is stopped only if the next model request has not started within about a second of the tool settling. That happens when something runs between the tool result and the next request, such as a context engine that owns compaction (for example lossless-claw) assembling context or compacting. A plain nonzero exit is not affected: exec reports it as `status: "completed"` with the exit code, which already counts as success.

## User Impact

A long tool that fails now hands its result back to the agent, which can react to it, instead of the run being cut off as stalled. Aborted tools still do not count as progress, so stopping a run behaves as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session watchdog keeps a run alive while a tool is open. When the tool closes, it restarts the stall timer only if the tool reports progress. The embedded tool wrapper reported progress only for a successful result. A long tool that failed therefore closed without progress, and the stall timer fell back to the last model progress, which by then was well in the past. Until the next model request registered its own deadline, the next one-second tick could stop the run.

The success-only filter comes from #166997. It decides when to clear the diagnostic "repeated requests without progress" evidence, and it is meant to ignore failed tools there. #175837 reused that same flag for the session watchdog. This change separates the two:

- The watchdog now counts any tool settlement that was not aborted, whether it succeeded or failed.
- Clearing the repeated-request evidence stays success-only, as #166997 intended.

The CLI runner and worker turn paths already count failed tool ends as progress, so the embedded wrapper now matches them. A loop of failing tool calls still cannot run forever on this alone, because each retry requires a model call.

Production change: two files, a net reduction of one line. The watchdog decision code is unchanged.

## Evidence

**End-to-end reproduction, red on base and green with the fix.** This ran on two isolated Mac Studio Gateways side by side: base `b413b8e` and PR head `2a6ce2d`. Each had its own home, state directory and port, and used a real model (`clawrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol`) with Code Mode off. Each Gateway also loaded a proof-only context engine that owns compaction and passes history through unchanged, but waits 5 seconds in its tool-loop `assemble()`, like a slow lossless-claw assembly. The agent ran exec once with `sleep 900` and `timeoutSeconds: 400`, which returns `status: "failed", timedOut: true` after 400 s.

| | Tool result | Post-tool `assemble()` delay | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base `b413b8e` | 22:52:03.116Z, `failed`, `timedOut: true` | 22:52:03.134Z → 22:52:08.135Z | `reply watchdog ... action=blocked` at 22:52:04.656Z, then `lane task error ... error="Reply operation stalled" staleReason=no_activity pendingTools=[]`; the CLI got `Reply operation stalled \| OPENCLAW_SESSION_WATCHDOG` and no reply |
| Head `2a6ce2d` | 22:52:03.106Z, `failed`, `timedOut: true` | 22:52:03.129Z → 22:52:08.129Z | Final reply at 22:52:12.400Z: `RESULT=timeout The sleep command was terminated after 400 seconds, as expected.` |

Base stopped about 1.5 s after the tool result, in the middle of the assembly delay, with the same signature as the incident (`staleReason=no_activity`, `pendingTools=[]`). Without the delay engine, base and head both survived, in a pass with a plain `exit 3` and again with the same timeout. The next model request started immediately, and its deadline kept the watchdog from stopping.

- Observed on a maintainer Gateway (2026.11.4) on 2026-11-18. A subagent exec started with `timeoutSeconds=2400` and was killed by the host exec memory budget after about 20 minutes (`isError=true`). Within about one second the run aborted with `SessionWatchdogError: Reply operation stalled` (`staleReason=no_activity`, `pendingTools=[]`, `durationMs=1653365`). The run was in lossless-claw assembly and compaction before its next model request.
- The new regression test drives the real tool wrapper against a real session watchdog. A tool stays open past the six-minute stall horizon and then settles in one of five ways: success, a failed result (`status: "failed"`, exit code 137), an error result, a thrown error, or abort. **On the base, the failed, error-result and thrown cases fail** (the watchdog decides `stop`). With the fix all five cases pass, and the aborted case still decides `stop`.
- Tests of the affected consumers pass (11 files): session watchdog, CLI runner command progress, worker turn run owner, controller recovery integration, the exec-deadline stuck-session test, code-mode bridge lifecycle, stalled-turn runner, tool-search scheduling, before-tool-call diagnostics and approval recovery, and the liveness carrier.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and the agents-root test typecheck shard pass. oxfmt and oxlint report no problems on the changed files.
- An independent local review found no P0–P2 issues.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: automation failure alerts blame every failure in a streak on the last run's cause
prs.body:
Closes #201183

This covers the cron alert defect, which the ClawSweeper review on the issue names as the remaining one.

## What Problem This Solves

When an automation fails several times in a row, the failure alert says "failed 4 times in a row" followed by "Cause: timeout". The count covers the whole streak, but the cause is only the last run's. If the first three runs failed on provider auth and the fourth timed out, the alert reads as four timeouts. The reporter's agent read it that way and rewrote a job that was fine.

## User Impact

User impact: a streak alert now says "Latest cause: timeout", so the cause is tied to the last run and not to every failure in the count. The notice sent when an automation is auto-disabled after repeated failures is worded the same way. A single failure still says "Cause:".

## Why This Change Was Made

The service records one cause, for the latest run, next to a count that spans the streak. Labeling the cause as the latest keeps the alert short and needs no stored history of causes or new setting. It applies to chat and webhook alerts.

## Evidence

- A streak of five failures with mixed causes, ending in a timeout, now alerts with `Automation "daily report" failed 5 times in a row` and `Latest cause: timeout`. A webhook streak gets the same label, and the auto-disable notice after 10 failures says `Latest cause: ...`.
- These tests fail on main with `Cause: timeout` and pass with the change.
- Ran locally: `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`, `src/cron/service/timer.batch-finalization.test.ts`, `src/cron/failure-notification-text.test.ts`, `src/cron/service/timer.timeout-watchdog.test.ts`, `src/cron/service/timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts`, plus oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files.
- Live Gateway run: isolated Gateway built from this head (`openclaw --version` shows 9889859), a command automation "daily report" with a failure alert webhook to a local receiver, threshold 4. Three runs exited with code 3, the fourth timed out. The receiver got one POST:

```
Automation "daily report" failed 4 times in a row
Latest cause: timeout
Last error: command timed out
```

- Not run locally: `src/cron/cron-delivery-outcomes.e2e.test.ts` (its runtime build does not complete on my machine), typecheck, and the wider suites. Those are left to CI. The Gateway run above delivered over a webhook, not a live chat channel.

prs.title: fix: update status repeats verified transcript filename mismatch warnings
prs.body:
Closes #201369

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update status` keeps reporting transcript filename/header ID mismatch warnings after a completed session SQLite migration already imported that exact source under its header identity, including replaying the same notice from the saved update report.

## User Impact

Verified mismatches disappear from plain and saved update status, and no longer count toward the saved “warnings need attention” headline. Incomplete, ambiguous, unreadable, or unimported sources still show the warning. Manifests and doctor JSON keep the historical detail.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Revalidate `transcript_filename_mismatch` alongside the other transcript findings.
- Suppress it only after verifying the exact source content exists in the owning store under the header identity, reusing the existing transcript-verification owner. Archived originals are resolved through the manifest move mapping.
- Keep it visible when the store is missing or unreadable, the source content is unimported or conflicting, or the header ID cannot be parsed.
- Require the recorded saved claim itself to verify; a matching store with no recorded claim stays visible.
- Apply the same current-state classification when replaying saved update warnings, while leaving the stored run record untouched.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-warnings.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3/3 passed, including an archived verified source, a bare saved claim, and an unimported source.
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-run-report.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 59/59 passed, including saved-warning filtering and headline attention count.
- Red-on-base: reverting only the source fix makes the verified-mismatch case fail while the unverified case still passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on all changed files.

- Shipped CLI proof with a crafted state (`openclaw update status`):
  - verified archived source: `✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.1.1 (from 2026.1.0).` — no mismatch warning, no attention count;
  - unverified identity: the manifest warning, the replayed saved warning, and `1 warning needs attention` all remain.

- Latest-stable upgrade proof: state was created with `openclaw@2026.11.5` (schema 36) containing a verified archived mismatch, an unverified mismatch, and a saved update-run warning. The stable binary reported both warnings plus `1 warning needs attention`. After `doctor --fix` migrated the state and this branch rendered status, only the unverified warning remained; the verified and saved warnings were gone.

prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #201388

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users who follow the documented `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install-cli.sh | bash -s -- --onboard` one-liner get a completed install followed by exit code 1: the final `openclaw onboard` step inherits the curl pipe as stdin, onboarding's interactive TTY guard refuses to start, and `set -euo pipefail` turns the already-successful install into a failure.
- **Related:** #201388; the clawsweeper review endorsed reusing the controlling-terminal handoff already shipped in `install.sh` (labels: P0, impact:ux-release-blocker, clawsweeper:queueable-fix).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** `--onboard` in the piped form runs onboarding reading from the user's terminal, the same handoff `install.sh` already uses; with `--json` the event stream on stdout stays parseable as independent NDJSON records; with no terminal available the installer defers onboarding with a visible setup command and keeps exit status 0.
- **Out of scope:** onboarding's own TTY guard is unchanged (not weakened); `install.sh` is unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** the terminal handoff at the end of `main()` in `scripts/install-cli.sh`.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The `has_controlling_tty` / `controlling_tty_path` helpers are copied from the merged sibling installer (`scripts/install.sh`, including the macOS #200244 note), and new regression tests pin the piped, no-terminal, and `--json` paths.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** `curl … | bash -s -- --onboard` now drops the user into onboarding after the install and exits 0; headless runs get `No terminal available; run …/bin/openclaw onboard to finish setup.` on stderr plus an `onboarding` skip NDJSON event, and still exit 0.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `scripts/install-cli.sh` (terminal handoff at the end of `main()`) and `test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts` ("runs onboarding with stdin from the controlling terminal, not the installer pipe", "defers onboarding without a terminal and keeps exit status and JSON output clean", "keeps onboarding output out of the JSON event stream when a terminal exists").

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux (EL8) worktree at main `ee37dd3b033` + this patch. Real piped-installer simulation: the unmodified installer script is fed to bash through a pipe (`cat harness.sh | bash -s -- --onboard …`), run inside a real PTY (util-linux `script -qefc`) and under `setsid` without a controlling terminal. Only the network-bound install steps are stubbed (same override technique as the repo's own `test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts`); `has_controlling_tty` / `controlling_tty_path` and the whole `main()` flow are the shipped code.

## What Problem This Solves

Piping a UTF-8 CodexBar report into the Model usage skill can fail when Python's standard input uses a different encoding. A report containing a non-ASCII project name can fail before the skill prints any model costs.

## User Impact

The skill can summarize the same UTF-8 report from a pipe or a file, including reports with a UTF-8 byte-order mark.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stdin import decodes bytes as UTF-8, matching the existing file import and using the same BOM handling.

## Evidence

I ran the bundled CLI with Python 3.12.3 on Linux and forced CP1252 for standard I/O. The UTF-8 fixture contains the project name `東京支店`.

- Before, both `e5ccb878a104` and the stable `v2026.11.6` tag exited 1 on the pipe with a `charmap` decode error. The same bytes worked through the file import with CP1252 and through the pipe with UTF-8 standard I/O. This isolates the failure to stdin decoding.
- After, the pipe exits 0 and reports `claude-sonnet-4-6` at `1.25` USD. The committed regression fails on the base for both plain UTF-8 and UTF-8 with BOM, and passes for both on the fix.
- `pytest -q -c skills/pyproject.toml skills/model-usage` passed all 12 tests. Targeted Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Codex autoreview of the complete patch against `e5ccb878a104` returned scoped-clean at P0–P3.
- The proof uses a synthetic report and Python's CP1252 stdio setting. Native Windows and live CodexBar collection were outside this check.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce with the shipped script</summary>

```bash
cat > cost.json <<'JSON'
[{"provider":"claude","projects":[{"name":"東京支店"}],"daily":[{"date":"2026-11-20","modelBreakdowns":[{"modelName":"claude-sonnet-4-6","cost":1.25}]}]}]
JSON

cat cost.json | PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 python3 skills/model-usage/scripts/model_usage.py --provider claude --input - --mode all --format json
PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 python3 skills/model-usage/scripts/model_usage.py --provider claude --input cost.json --mode all --format json
```

[Python standard stream encoding](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/sys.html#sys.stdin) and [CodexBar cost report format](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/blob/main/docs/cli.md#cost-json-payload).

</details>

prs.title: refactor: unify async SQLite descriptor admission
prs.body:
Related: #197510, #202771

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway stall refactor left separate SQLite descriptor-preparation pipelines for ordinary worker opens and private staging. The root worker relay also kept a synchronous filesystem path for creation requests that had no creation authority.

## User Impact

No user-facing behavior, configuration, or database format changes. Facts-only relays still cannot create files; their cold requests no longer probe the database pathname synchronously on the Gateway thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both async open paths use the same descriptor owner to open, verify, and publish the file and its clean-close facts. Private staging still cleans up an unpublished descriptor; ordinary descriptors keep POSIX lock custody. The root relay uses async preparation, nested relays keep their existing grants, and the broker consumes the verified identity without comparing it a second time. The native synchronous open path, FIFO, and accepted-create settlement are unchanged.

Net: **75 fewer production lines**, **2 added test lines**, no test cases removed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a creator submits a Template, **View submission** on the pending card links to the public listing. That URL does not tell ClawHub the creator wants to follow the submission while it is being checked.

## User Impact

The pending action requests the submission view. Once the Template is published, **Copy link** still gives the creator the normal public listing URL.

## Why This Change Was Made

The card appends the fixed `?view=submission` intent only to its pending link. The canonical listing URL in the publication receipt stays unchanged. The link adds no credentials or redirect destination, and this does not change sign-in before publication. ClawHub handles the view; this change covers the OpenClaw sender only.

## Evidence

Observed in Chromium on the actual chat card, using a synthetic Gateway publication receipt:

| Action | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending → View submission (anchor href) | `https://example.test/maker/templates/research-brief` | `https://example.test/maker/templates/research-brief?view=submission` |
| Published → Copy link (clipboard) | `https://example.test/maker/templates/research-brief` | `https://example.test/maker/templates/research-brief` |

The regression failed on the base with the bare listing URL and passed with the fix. All 12 creator-card tests, all three Chromium chat-review scenarios, and `pnpm check:changed` against the exact commit parent passed locally.

prs.title: fix: name the agent when a followed-up child finishes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a parent chat sends a follow-up message to one of its child sessions, the "finished" notice for that follow-up run says "An agent finished" instead of the child's name. The child session already has a name (for example "Cross-thread message summaries and video proof"), so readers can't tell which agent finished.

## User Impact

User impact: completion notices for follow-up runs now show the child session's name, the same way the first run's notice does.

## Why This Change Was Made

The completion notice takes its name from the run record. The first run gets the spawn label, but a follow-up run sent with `sessions_send` was registered without one, so the UI fell back to its generic "An agent" text. The follow-up registration now copies the child session's current label onto the new run. Steered follow-ups already reuse the existing run and its label, so they are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression test: the existing watched-child follow-up test now gives the child session a label and asserts that the follow-up run record carries it. It fails without the fix (`label: undefined`) and passes with it.
- Focused sibling tests pass: the raw-entry registry suite (15 tests), plus the `sessions_send` follow-up and owner-continuation suites (14 tests).
- Live symptom: a Team session showed "An agent finished" for a follow-up run of a labeled child session. Its completion receipt had the child's session key but no label.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ac7e7bd9-05ee-4dc6-9b97-6b345f667731)

prs.title: fix: keep terminal formatting out of Meme Maker SVGs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Meme Maker accepts captions copied from colored terminal output and reports that it saved an SVG. The saved file can contain raw control characters that prevent SVG viewers from opening it.

## User Impact

Local SVG and PNG renders preserve the visible caption text when it includes terminal formatting, so users can paste colored output directly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Clean captions at the shared local layout step, before wrapping and sizing. Node's terminal-code stripper removes formatting sequences and the XML 1.0 character filter removes any remaining characters that SVG cannot represent. XML escaping continues to preserve printable punctuation and Unicode text. The existing CLI regression now parses the output and verifies that the caption survived.

## Evidence

- On Linux with Node 24.18.0 and a downloaded Drake template, both main (`dce3c298384`) and the v2026.11.6 tag's renderer exited 0 and wrote SVG that Python's XML parser rejected.
- The repaired CLI produced valid SVG and a 1200 × 1200 PNG with Chrome for Testing 156. Both files were byte-identical to renders from the same captions with the terminal and XML-invalid characters removed manually. The SVG readback preserved the ampersand, accented and Chinese text, and emoji. FFmpeg decoded the PNG.
- The CLI regression failed before the fix because Resvg rejected an ESC character. After the fix, the focused suite passed both default tests. Its opt-in browser case was skipped in the default run and the separate real Chromium CLI proof covered the PNG path.
- Focused TypeScript, lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues on the same two-file patch before a base update that left the owning files unchanged. The change adds six net production lines and eleven net test lines.

<details>
<summary>Local reproduction</summary>

Run from the repository root with an isolated cache directory.

```bash
proof_dir=$(mktemp -d)
XDG_CACHE_HOME="$proof_dir/cache" node skills/meme-maker/scripts/meme.mjs \
  render drake --text $'before\033[31mRED\033[0m after' --text 'Control' \
  --out "$proof_dir/meme.svg"
python3 -c 'import sys, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET; ET.parse(sys.argv[1])' \
  "$proof_dir/meme.svg"

OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  test/scripts/meme-maker.test.ts \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

prs.title: feat(cron): back automation off when a provider pushes back
prs.body:
Related: #196859

## What Problem This Solves

Main adds an automation run on each queue drain when free memory allows. A provider can keep rate-limiting requests even while retries let individual jobs finish successfully.

## User Impact

A rate limit or overload pauses extra work for the provider that reported it when more than eight automation and hook agent sessions share the budget. The provider response describes its own capacity, so other providers and command or script jobs can still use extra slots.

The eight default slots stay available. Running jobs fill those slots as they free up. One extra slot returns per quiet minute at the next drain. A parked occurrence keeps its receipt, completed condition check, and transferred event. Running jobs can finish, and an extra run that falls back counts against the provider it switches to.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queue hands out slots in order and reassigns freed default capacity before applying provider allowances. Each charge follows its receipt while that receipt uses extra capacity. A provider waiting on an extra slot releases the provisional slot so other work can proceed. The Gateway logs each reduction and keeps the backoff in memory.

[Compare main with this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/main...b92c72a87ec8b9bdd3f3ac03f9598e64b27ecfec)

## Evidence

- A Gateway running OpenClaw 2026.11.6 wrote a recurring job and successful history. The candidate opened the same isolated state, retained the authored configuration, job definition and history, and ran that job again successfully.
- Two loopback providers exercised real Gateway requests. Provider A returned HTTP 429 at 16 overlapping requests. The original eight default jobs finished, provider B used an extra slot, and the same parked A occurrence resumed as the ninth request in the first quiet minute while the eight former extra runs were still active.
- 236 focused tests passed on macOS. The core, cron and messaging typechecks, targeted lint and formatting passed. The added regression lines cover the 16-run burst and the completion order that exercises slot reassignment.
- The live run used loopback fixtures. Full CI and vendor services are outside this evidence.

prs.title: feat(plugins): let the memory slot owner query passive memory backends
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Only one memory plugin can run today: every other memory plugin is disabled before its code runs. This PR lets other memory plugins load as passive **backends** of the slot owner. A fusion-style slot owner asks for them in its manifest (`memoryBackends: true`), so installing and selecting it is the only step: every other enabled memory plugin then joins, and `plugins.entries.<id>.memoryBackend: false` keeps one out. Without such an owner, an operator can still opt a single plugin in with `memoryBackend: true`. A backend loads with a registration mode that accepts only its neutral `providerRuntime`, and the selected memory slot owner (for example a plugin that fuses several stores) can list and open backends under the authority of its own `open()` call. Backends get no tools, hooks, services, prompt or corpus injection, recall grant, or slot role. With no owner that requests backends and no `memoryBackend` entries, everything behaves exactly as before.

Follow-up to #198445. #198446 ran a second memory plugin fully live beside the slot owner and needed host-minted audiences plus new enable and slot rules; it was closed as too complex. This is a different, narrower design: backends are inert data sources reached only through the slot owner, the way a search-fusion plugin reaches several web search providers.

### Problem

`resolveMemorySlotDecision` disables every single-kind memory plugin that does not own `plugins.slots.memory` before `register()` runs (`src/plugins/loader-runtime-candidate.ts`). A plugin that wants to combine several memory stores therefore has to ship its own client for each store; it cannot reuse installed memory plugins, even read-only, through the existing provider-neutral `providerRuntime` contract (`open` / `search` / `get` / `health` / `candidates` / `close`).

### Exact change

- **Owner request (one new manifest field).** `memoryBackends?: boolean` on the plugin manifest (type, parser, manifest record, `plugins/manifest` docs). While the plugin that declares it owns `plugins.slots.memory`, every other enabled memory plugin defaults to being a backend. One shared policy, `resolveMemoryBackendPolicyIds` / `isMemoryBackendRequested` in `src/plugins/memory-backend.ts`, drives all three places that decide backends: the loader (via the per-load loop state), the Gateway startup plan, and the standalone memory runtime lookup. Denied, disabled, and not-allowlisted plugins never qualify, and normal enable policy still applies in the loader. The loader loop-state type and its memory-slot decision helper moved into `loader-load-loop-state.ts` to keep the loader files under the 700-line cap.
- **Opt-in key (one new config option).** `plugins.entries.<id>.memoryBackend: boolean` in the plugin entry schema, normalization, labels, help, and the config docs baseline. It does not enable a plugin; normal enable/allow/deny policy still applies first.
- **Loader.** When a memory plugin would be disabled only because another plugin owns the slot, and its entry opts in, it loads in a new `"memory-backend"` registration mode instead (only from `full` and `discovery` loads). Slot `"none"`, `tool-discovery`, setup, and CLI-metadata loads are unchanged. Logic: `isMemoryBackendRequested` in `src/plugins/memory-backend.ts`, used at the three existing memory-slot decision points in `loader-runtime-candidate.ts`.
- **Gateway startup plan.** `shouldConsiderForGatewayStartup` only considered memory plugins that own the slot or are the dreaming sidecar, so a backend would never load in the Gateway. Opted-in backends of a configured slot owner are now considered too; normal activation (`enabled`, allow/deny) still decides. The startup metadata scope already includes every `plugins.entries` id.
- **Capability-gated registration, not stripping.** `resolvePluginRegistrationCapabilities("memory-backend")` decodes a `memoryBackend` capability; `createApi` then hands the plugin only `registerMemoryCapability`. Every other registrar keeps its inert default from `pluginApiDefaultHandlers` (no per-registrar edits). Node host commands, reload/security-audit registrations, dashboards, and runtime-registration completion are skipped for the mode.
- **Separate registry list.** The memory registrar routes a backend's `providerRuntime` (and nothing else) into a new `registry.memoryBackends` inventory. Backends never enter `memoryCapabilities`, so slot resolution and every host consumer (`memory.search`, Active Memory, Memory Wiki, voice fast context, flush, `/learn`) still see only the owner. The memory registrars moved unchanged into `registry-registrars-memory.ts`, following the existing `registry-registrars-*` split, which also brings `registry-registrars.ts` back under the 700-line lint limit.
- **Caller authority.** `getActiveMemoryProviderCore` passes `params.backends` (`list()` / `open(id)`) only to a native slot owner, and only when backends loaded. `backends.open(id)` uses that `open()` call's caller context, agent, and purpose; the owner supplies only a backend id and never mints or changes authority. It runs the same steps as the owner's own open (caller currency before and after, handle-shape validation, `bindMemoryProvider` with the backend's provider id and plugin instance). A caller-supplied `backends` value is dropped. When the owner's lease closes, access ends and the host closes any backend lease left open. The shared open steps moved into `src/plugins/memory-provider-open.ts`.
- **Lifecycle.** Backend runtimes join the existing reload drain and Gateway shutdown drain. Retention keys already include entry policy, so toggling the key hot-reloads the plugin like any other `plugins.entries` change, and a retired backend's leases fail on their next call through the bound instance check.
- **Config validation.** A backend's config validates as a loaded plugin (no "plugin disabled but config is present" warning). Setting the key on the slot owner, while the slot is `"none"`, or on a non-memory plugin warns that it has no effect.
- **SDK surface.** `PluginRegistrationMode` gains `"memory-backend"`; `MemoryProviderOpenParams` gains optional `backends` with `MemoryBackendAccess` / `MemoryBackendInfo` types, reached through the already-public `MemoryPluginCapability["providerRuntime"]`. No new subpath or export.
- **Docs.** `plugins/sdk-overview/memory-and-context` (new "Memory backends" section), registration-mode table, `sdk-runtime` mode list, `gateway/config-extensions`.

### Design questions answered

1. **Opt-in.** Choosing a slot owner whose manifest requests backends is the opt-in, the same way installing a search-fusion plugin is; `memoryBackend: false` opts a single plugin out, and `memoryBackend: true` opts one in under any owner. It is not on for everyone because a non-owner memory plugin is fully disabled today: loading it runs its setup code and may open its store, and the owner gains read access to its memory. Without an owner request or the key, enabled non-owner memory plugins are still disabled before `register()` and run no setup code (tested).
2. **What a backend can register.** `register()` runs, but only `registerMemoryCapability` is wired, and only `providerRuntime` is kept. Services never start and workers are never registered, so a backend's provider runtime must open its store lazily, which the neutral runtime already has to do for non-activating CLI loads. Backend code still runs in-process like any enabled plugin; the gate limits host registration, not what plugin code can do, which is why it needs explicit operator opt-in.
3. **Authority.** Backends are opened only through the host-issued capability inside the owner's `open()`, under that call's authority; status-purpose opens stay status; denial and session-audience semantics are unchanged because the same context and binding are used.
4. **Interactions.**
   - Dreaming sidecar: keeps its consolidation role, never becomes a backend.
   - Dual-kind plugins that lose the slot already load for their other role; with the key, their `providerRuntime` is also published as a backend.
   - Slot `"none"`: no backends.
   - Disable/deny: still win.
   - `openclaw plugins enable <id>`: unchanged (selects the slot).
   - CLI root help/descriptors and skill/hook root contributions: unchanged, so backends contribute none.
   - Hot reload: covered by retention signatures and reload drain.
5. **Scope.** Core plumbing, types, tests, docs. No bundled fusion plugin and no bundled plugin changes.
6. **Narrowness.** The registration gate needed no registrar changes because `buildPluginApi` already defaults every unprovided handler to a no-op.

Size: production +507/-196 across 23 files. About 120 of those lines are moves: the memory registrars into `registry-registrars-memory.ts`, and the shared open steps into `memory-provider-open.ts`. Tests +466, docs +86/-4.

### Scope boundary

Not included: a fusion plugin; legacy file-shaped `runtime` backends (backends must register `providerRuntime`); backend CLI commands; status/inspect display of the backend role beyond the record's `memoryBackend` flag.

Accepted edge case: in standalone CLI lookups, a backend runtime's `closeAllMemorySearchManagers` is not called by `closeActiveMemorySearchManagersCore`; backend leases still close with the owner's lease, and the registry retires with the process.

## Verification

Run in an isolated worktree on Linux x86_64, Node 24.22.1, against base `e79905a180b`.

New tests (red on base, green on head; run with each file's Vitest project config):

| Test | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/plugins/loader.memory-backend.test.ts`: real loader with two fixture memory plugins, `full` and `discovery` loads, disabled controls (no key, slot `"none"`), and a standalone `getActiveMemoryProviderCore` lookup where the owner lists and searches the backend and closing the owner closes the backend lease | 5 failed | 5/5 pass |
| `src/plugins/memory-backend-provider.test.ts`: registration gate (tool, hook, service, CLI ignored; only `providerRuntime` kept), forged `backends` dropped, backend open reuses authority/agent/`status` purpose, owner rewrites of the authority object or operator scopes do not reach the backend, cross-provider reference rejected, access ends with the owner lease | 1 failed | 3/3 pass |
| `src/config/config.memory-backend.test.ts`: backend config validates as loaded; no-effect warnings | 4 failed | 4/4 pass |
| `src/plugins/gateway-startup-plugin-plan.memory-sidecar.test.ts` (new table): Gateway startup plan starts a non-owner memory plugin only for `memoryBackend: true` or an owner manifest request, and honors `memoryBackend: false` | n/a | 5/5 cases pass |
| `src/plugins/loader.memory-backend.test.ts` (owner request): owner manifest `memoryBackends: true` loads the other memory plugin as a backend in `full` and `discovery` loads and through the standalone lookup; `memoryBackend: false` keeps it disabled | 3 failed with the owner flag forced off | 4/4 pass |
| `src/plugins/memory-backend.test.ts`: shared policy (owner request, explicit entries, opt-out, disable, deny, allowlist, owner never its own backend, mode and slot gates) | n/a (new module) | 5/5 pass |

Consumer test updated: `memory-provider-runtime.test.ts` mocks `memory-state.js` and needed the new `listMemoryBackendRegistrations` export (41/41 pass).

Suites (direct `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.<project>.config.ts`):

- `extension-memory` 490 passed; `extension-active-memory` 249 passed.
- `plugins` 5731 passed. Remaining failures also fail on base with the same counts in the same environment: `marketplace.download.native`, `plugin-module-generation.sdk`, `plugin-source-build.process`, `wired-hooks-llm`; `runtime.retention` failed once in the full run and passes in isolation.
- `runtime-config` 6100 passed. `mcp-repair.integration` and `session-transcript-reconcile.*` fail on base with the same counts. Every `state-startup-corpus*` failure is the host's temp-directory permission check ("No safe OpenClaw temp root is available"), not memory code. The failing subset changes from run to run: parts 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and main in the full run; parts 3, 4, 7, 8 and main in an isolated rerun. The base run of those files happened to pass.
- `unit-fast` 13857 passed; every failing file fails on base with the same count, including the two existing `memory-sidecar` metadata-scope cases.

Checks:

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: clean.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on every touched file: clean. `registry-registrars.ts` was already over the 700-line `max-lines` limit on base (704); moving the memory registrars into `registry-registrars-memory.ts` brings it under.
- `pnpm config:schema:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check` (baseline regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`), `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports`: clean.
- Review: two local review rounds on the committed branch. Both rounds found that the owner could change the authority a backend receives through the shared context object: first by rewriting it, then by appending to operator `scopes`. Backend access now keeps a frozen host-owned copy of the caller context, taken before the owner's `open()` runs. Each fix has a regression test that fails on the previous code.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff --base e79905a180b --head HEAD`: 21 reachable declarations changed, all additive (`memoryBackend` on plugin entries, `memoryBackends` on the registry type, the `"memory-backend"` mode, optional `backends` on `MemoryProviderOpenParams`). Acknowledgement digest `cc9745ed`.

Benchmark: plugin load and provider open with the default config (slot owner plus three enabled non-owner memory plugins, no opt-in). Same machine and Vitest project, alternating base/head twice. Each run has 30 warmup + 200 measured `loadOpenClawPlugins({ cache: false, activate: false })` calls, then 100 warmup + 1000 measured `getActiveMemoryProviderCore` open+close calls through the standalone path:

| Run | load p50 / p95 / mean (ms) | open p50 / p95 / mean (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base 1 | 6.43 / 8.53 / 6.76 | 0.181 / 0.224 / 0.185 |
| head 1 | 6.19 / 11.63 / 6.97 | 0.185 / 0.232 / 0.188 |
| base 2 | 6.30 / 10.81 / 6.74 | 0.188 / 0.354 / 0.209 |
| head 2 | 6.43 / 10.91 / 6.89 | 0.186 / 0.243 / 0.191 |

The differences are within run-to-run noise. Backend-enabled load cost was not benchmarked: it is one extra plugin import and register per opted-in backend.

## What was not tested

- No live Gateway or real model run. The startup-plan selection and the active-registry open path are covered by unit tests; end-to-end coverage is the standalone loader path.
- No real third-party memory plugin (for example LanceDB) as a backend; fixtures stand in for it.
- No fusion plugin exists, so no end-to-end merged-results scenario.
- Hot reload toggling `memoryBackend` relies on the existing retention signature, which already includes entry policy, plus the existing reload drain; no dedicated reload test.
- The repo test runner (`pnpm test`) refused to prepare runtime artifacts on this host because it could not verify separation from a managed Gateway. Suites ran through direct Vitest project configs instead. CI is the broad proof.

Owner-request update (head after rebase on current `main`):

- `pnpm check:changed` against `origin/main`: green (types, lint, line-cap and mock-export ratchets, config docs baseline, boundaries). The dead-export scan reports only names in files this PR does not touch.
- 78 loader, manifest, Gateway startup, memory and slot test files: 1090 tests pass.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports`: clean. `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff`: 23 reachable declarations changed, all additive (adds manifest `memoryBackends`). Acknowledgement digest `a770a8af`.
- Review of the owner-request change: scoped-clean at P1.
- Test-line budget: this change adds 614 net test lines against the 400-line allowance. `config/test-lines-allocations/201340-memory-backend-providers.txt` records the remaining 214: the new registration mode and backend authority boundary are covered through the real loader with fixture plugins, the registration gate, config validation, the shared policy, and the startup plan. The startup cases were folded into one table first.
- The memory registrars moved into `registry-registrars-memory.ts`, so its existing `typescript/unbound-method` suppression moved with them; the production suppression allowlist in `test/scripts/lint-suppressions.test.ts` follows the file.
- `src/agents/tools/message-tool-discovery.test.ts` ("preserves foreign discovery for primary telegram") fails identically on the merge base; this PR does not touch that code.

prs.title: fix: fill each plugin category preview when installed plugins are hidden
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawHub picks up to eight plugins per category. Control UI then hides installed plugins, including disabled ones. On one real gateway this left Channels with three installable plugins and Models with one, although ClawHub lists more than 200 in each category.

## User Impact

When the registry supplies a continuation cursor, the Plugins page fills short previews with the next installable plugins in the same ranked order (pins first, then downloads). The overview appears immediately. Registries without cursors keep the previous behavior. The [companion ClawHub change](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4867) is merged; production did not return cursors when checked on November 20.

## Why This Change Was Made

Control UI knows which plugins are installed; ClawHub owns the ranking. The Gateway requests an optional `previewCursor` on each overview category and passes it through `plugins.catalog.browse`. The client asks for the next page only when a category has fewer than eight available entries. Installed IDs never go to ClawHub. Continuations are limited to two concurrent requests, three pages per category, and 32 requests per overview. View all, Search, Featured and Trending keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Real Control UI in Chromium against a mocked Gateway and synthetic catalog. The first comparison uses base `5458e9614f17` and the initial fix, with the same fixture, viewport and crop (1440 × 1180, light). This is not a live Control UI–Gateway–ClawHub run.

### Clean comparison

![Before: Channels shows three plugins and Models shows one](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ebcca46c-7b06-4ab4-82ab-3ed1247e429a)

![After: Channels and Models each show eight plugins; Memory is unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d19dabf7-4918-4842-8d2a-3277c2d5e3e8)

[Annotated before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a66e81e7-35ed-4e35-ac52-161831aaa29e) · [Annotated after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9569b40e-53d6-45aa-9f3c-4b5d627507a6)

### Loading state

A category reserves only the missing card slots while its next page is pending, even if all its initial candidates are installed. Loaded cards stay visible. If the continuation fails or runs out of results, unused slots collapse once and the page keeps the available cards.

[Clean loading state: before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd01e48f-c184-4953-9da8-fedeaf3b3dd5) · [Clean loading state: after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1070441-5d71-405c-ae8d-09fd5288976f)

![Before the layout repair: Memory begins 320 px above its settled position](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eebd266e-1d13-48ed-adf6-8cbaa91b1243)

![After the layout repair: placeholders reserve the final section positions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bbcb077-bd14-4ad0-8014-74e4611b4aa5)

Chromium layout-shift scores during two sequential refills. Paired values are for one / zero initial Models. The loading screenshots isolate the layout repair before main's artwork update; post-integration browser checks confirmed stationary headings in all seven cases.

| Width | Before repair | After repair |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 400 px | 0.1237 / 0.1719 | 0 / 0 |
| 820 px | 0.1461 / 0.1846 | 0 / 0 |
| 1280 px | 0.0740 / 0.1114 | 0 / 0 |
| 1440 px | 0.0689 | 0 |

At 1440 px, Memory moved down 320 px before the repair and stayed fixed afterward. At 400 px, reserving two summary lines makes short rows less dense: the settled Models and Memory headings sit about 96 px and 192 px lower, respectively.

### Validation

- 207 Plugins unit tests and 34 Chromium tests passed: 25 Plugins, 5 plugin-skill preview, and 4 first-visit asset-budget cases. UI typecheck, controller guard, scoped reader lint and formatting passed. Catalog and Gateway suites passed (32 + 37 tests).
- The unchanged cold Plugins visit budget is 56 requests. Unmodified main `d5a99b07e88` and the integrated layout repair both used 57. Loading the Markdown reader only when opening a skill document reduced this to 54. Browsing fetched neither the frontmatter parser nor the Markdown runtime. The regression assertion failed before the repair (one parser request) and passed afterward (zero). Opening and reading a skill remains covered.
- The published source tree matches the locally tested tree. Production verification is outstanding: the live overview returned zero cursors across 22 categories at the November 20 check.

prs.title: fix: keep the profile avatar quiet on hover and focus
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hovering or focusing the profile avatar could put the account-menu label, name, and build information over the chat composer, even when everything was connected.

## User Impact

The avatar stays quiet during normal use. It still opens the account menu by mouse or keyboard, and screen readers still receive the full button name. During reconnection, the existing status hint can still show “Reconnecting” without repeating the account information.

## Why This Change Was Made

The button used its accessible name as its tooltip. Only the connection status belongs in the visual hint; the separate status flag still suppresses it when visible.

## Evidence

Verified in Chromium against the real Control UI with a synthetic account and Gateway: hovered and focused the avatar, opened the menu with Enter, and disconnected the Gateway to check the status-only fallback. The keyboard navigation test and both affected bundled browser scenarios passed. UI typecheck, changed-file lint, and formatting passed.

### Profile avatar hover
