prs.title: feat(voice-call): elevate one realtime call's consult tools with a keypad PIN
prs.body:
Related: #193571

## What Problem This Solves

Realtime phone calls run every consult at one fixed `realtime.toolPolicy`. Operators who keep it at `safe-read-only` (the safe default) cannot do owner-level work from a phone call, and raising the policy globally gives every admitted caller owner tools on every call.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator can turn on `realtime.elevation`, and on a call with a trusted number (an inbound caller, or the callee of an outbound call, in `allowFrom`), the person on the line can press `*`, a PIN, and `#` to give that one call the elevated consult policy (default `owner`) until hangup. Everything else keeps the configured `toolPolicy`. Elevation is off by default, so nothing changes for existing configs.

Risks and limits, kept visible:

- Twilio only. Digits come from Twilio Media Streams `dtmf` messages. Config validation rejects other providers while elevation is on.
- Only calls whose other party is in `allowFrom` can elevate: the caller of an inbound call, or the callee of an outbound call. Whoever answers an outbound call still has to enter the PIN; elevation is never automatic. Elevation requires `inboundPolicy: "allowlist"` or `"pairing"`. Caller ID can be spoofed (see #193571 for STIR/SHAKEN attestation), so the PIN is the credential; the allowlist only narrows who may try.
- Wrong PINs count per hashed number across calls (inbound and outbound share one budget) within `lockoutMs`, so hanging up and redialing does not reset the budget. After `maxAttempts` the caller is locked out for `lockoutMs`. Failure counts and lockouts are in memory; a Gateway restart clears them.
- Elevation ends when the call's media stream ends. A stream reconnect within the same call drops the tool policy back to `toolPolicy` (the caller re-enters the PIN), but the call's later consults stay in its isolated elevated session, because the call's transcript still carries answers from owner tools.
- A consult that is already running keeps the policy it started with.

## Why This Change Was Made

The realtime handler already owns each call's telephony binding, so it now also owns that call's keypad state and passes the call's current consult policy to the consult tool handler, which uses it for `toolsAllow`. A new `DtmfElevationGate` collects digits after the prefix, submits on `#`, after 3 seconds without a key, or at 12 digits (not at the configured PIN length, so the length stays private), and compares with `safeEqualSecret`. On success the realtime model gets a short notice so it can tell the caller; on a wrong PIN it gets a "not accepted" notice; failures are counted per hashed caller number across calls (a window of `lockoutMs`), so redialing cannot reset the attempt budget. After `maxAttempts` the call is hung up and the caller is locked out for `lockoutMs`. During a lockout any entry hangs up the call without checking the PIN, so retries reveal nothing. A correct PIN clears that caller's failure count.

Digits never reach the realtime model, the transcript, or logs. Logs record only the outcome, attempt count, and the hashed caller number on lockout. Caller audio is withheld from the model between the prefix key and submission, in case the carrier leaves tones in the media.

The PIN is a secret input (`realtime.elevation.pin`, registered in `configContracts.secretInputs` and marked sensitive), resolved the same way as `twilio.authToken`. It must resolve to 4 to 12 digits; the startup error never echoes the value.

Config surface: this raises the plugin config budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` from 5080 to 5087 (the `realtime.elevation` object and its six fields). The feature is opt-in and needs an operator-set PIN, so it cannot ride on an existing field.

To stay within the line-cap ratchet for `realtime-handler.ts`, the existing caller-transcript buffer helpers and `withFallbackConsultQuestion` moved unchanged into `realtime-transcript-text.ts`.

<details>
<summary>Config</summary>

```json5
realtime: {
  enabled: true,
  toolPolicy: "safe-read-only",
  elevation: {
    enabled: true,
    pin: { source: "env", provider: "default", id: "VOICE_CALL_ELEVATION_PIN" },
    prefix: "*",               // one key: 0-9 or *
    elevatedToolPolicy: "owner", // or "safe-read-only"
    maxAttempts: 3,              // 1-10
    lockoutMs: 3600000,
  },
}
```

</details>

## Evidence

Focused tests, all passing locally:

- `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: eligibility (inbound + allowlisted only), prefix gating, `#` submit, `*` restart, inter-digit timeout, 12-digit submit, wrong PIN, failures counted across calls (redial does not reset), failure window expiry, success clears failures, lockout across calls and expiry, close drops pending entry.
- `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts` (real WebSocket path): consult before the PIN gets `safe-read-only`, after the PIN gets `owner`; caller audio is withheld while entering the PIN; the PIN never appears in manager events, model notices, or console output; a stream close drops elevation; `maxAttempts` wrong PINs hang up the call, and during the lockout the correct PIN on the next call hangs up without a notice.
- `runtime.test.ts`: a consult with call policy `safe-read-only` runs with the read-only `toolsAllow` list, and with `owner` runs with `toolsAllow` undefined (normal agent tool policy).
- `config.test.ts`: defaults, runtime and manifest schema agreement, validation errors, PIN resolution.
- `stream-frame-adapter.test.ts`: Twilio `dtmf` frame parsing; Telnyx frames stay ignored.

Also updated: two `realtime-handler.test.ts` assertions now expect the consult context to carry `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"`.

Results:

- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 52 files, 633 tests passed; database-workers lane 15 files, 182 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm lint:extensions`: clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: every lane green except the dead-export scan, which reports only pre-existing entries outside this change (for example `extensions/google/provider-catalog-runtime.ts`, `src/config/sessions/session-history-types.ts`).
- `pnpm config:docs:check`: OK after `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

- `runtime.test.ts` (added in 6f93e38): an elevated consult runs in the session `<caller session key>:elevated:<callId>`; consults before the PIN and on later calls keep the caller's normal session.
- **Reconnect isolation (8a6d57d, the P1 from the last review).** The gate remembers which call ids were elevated (pruned after a day), so `wasElevated` survives a new binding for the same call. `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: "keeps a call marked elevated across rebinding while its tool policy resets". `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts` (real WebSocket path): elevate, end the stream, reconnect the same call; the next consult gets `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"` **and** `elevated: true`. Together with the `runtime.test.ts` case above, the reconnected call's consults run in `…:elevated:<callId>`, so its retained transcript never enters the shared per-phone session, and a later call without the PIN can't read it.
- **Outbound (4277a5a).** `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: "opens only when the other party is allowlisted, in either direction", and "shares failures and lockout between inbound and outbound calls with one number".

Rebased onto `main` at ae0d37b3c4 (2026-11-17). The only conflict was the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen` (`config:docs:check` OK). On the rebased head:

- The PR's test files (`config`, `runtime`, `realtime-dtmf-elevation`, `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation`, `realtime-handler`, `stream-frame-adapter`): 6/6 files pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- `pnpm lint:extensions`: the only errors are `max-lines` in `extensions/crabbox/…/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts` and `extensions/tlon/…/monitor/index.test.ts`, both on `main` and outside this change.
- Full `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: failures only in `index.call-scope.test.ts` and `src/manager.async-store.test.ts` (steering/end_call admission). Neither file is touched here, and the same tests fail or hang on unmodified `main` at ae0d37b3c4 on this host.

### Live Twilio proof (2026-11-16)

Host: OpenClaw 2026.11.4 with this change backported onto `v2026.11.4` and installed as a local `npm-pack` build of `@openclaw/voice-call`. The feature code is the same as this branch; only the base differs. Inbound Twilio calls from one allowlisted number, OpenAI realtime, `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"`, `elevatedToolPolicy: "owner"`, PIN as a store SecretRef. Log excerpt below: phone numbers, Twilio call SIDs and IPs removed. The PIN never appears in any log line.

What the calls show:

- **Read-only before the PIN.** `bf202c8f` and `7992d6c1`: the first consult asked for current alerts; the agent had only the read-only tool list, couldn't reach Grafana, and said so.
- **Elevation.** After `*<PIN>#`: `Realtime keypad elevation granted … toolPolicy=owner`. The next consult in each call used Grafana MCP tools and reported the firing alerts.
- **Reset on hangup.** `52e9a519` (call-back after `bf202c8f`): the consult ran with the read-only tool list again, and the owner tools (Grafana MCP) were not in its catalog.
- **Wrong PIN.** `f10831ae`: `Realtime keypad elevation rejected … attempt=1/3`, and the model received the "not accepted" notice. I stopped after one attempt to avoid locking out the test number; the 3-attempt hang-up and lockout are covered by `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts`.

**Found live and fixed in 6f93e38.** With the default `sessionScope: "per-phone"`, the call-back in `52e9a519` couldn't run owner tools, but its consult answered from results the elevated call had left in the caller's shared session. ### Upgrade and compatibility

- Upgrading this host from 2026.10.7 to 2026.11.4 kept the existing voice-call config (Twilio store SecretRef auth token, realtime provider settings, allowlist, tool policy). `realtime.elevation` defaults to `enabled: false`, so existing configs load and behave as before.
- Operator note: when a newly installed plugin version adds a secret input path (here `realtime.elevation.pin`), the Gateway reads the secret-input registry only at startup. Until a Gateway restart, voice-call fails to start with `unresolved SecretRef`; `secrets reload` and a plugin reload are not enough. This is core behavior, not something this PR introduces.





### Live reconnect + callback proof, and upgrade from v2026.11.5 (2026-11-18)

Elevate → forced stream reconnect → consult → unauthenticated callback on a real Twilio call: after the reconnect the tool policy resets, but the call's consults stay in its isolated session, and the callback's shared session never sees the elevated answer. Also covers the upgrade and data-model proof from the current stable release (v2026.11.5) in a sandbox. prs.title: chore(deps): refresh dependencies through the November 13 cutoff
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw’s runtime, native apps, and build tooling are pinned to older dependency releases. This sweep picks up compatible updates while keeping the seven-day supply-chain cooldown in place.

## User Impact

The Gateway and bundled WebSocket consumers move to the [ws 8.23.0 security release](https://github.com/websockets/ws/releases/tag/8.23.0). Other changes refresh install, native, release, and CI dependencies without introducing new settings, migrations, or user actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audit fixed an inclusive cutoff of **2026-11-13 22:51:20 UTC**. It updates 91 distinct npm pins or existing overrides, 22 Fastlane transitive gems, and five Cargo locks, plus qualified scanner and container pins. It adds no cooldown exclusions or patches. TypeBox advances to 1.4.5, the newest qualifying release that preserves OpenClaw’s namespace contract. parse5 8.1.x and fs-safe 0.27.2 were deferred after the UI build and a filesystem test found regressions. Updates under separate review ([Android #200037](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200037), [Actions #201745](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201745), and [Ruff #198356](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198356)), and major or toolchain updates without compatible consumer proof, are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Fixed-cutoff audit: **230** newly resolved pnpm identities, **47** new identities in standalone npm locks, **154** introduced Cargo lock entries, and all **22** updated gems. Compared retained dependency edges; no downgrades or too-young new identities were found. Frozen pnpm/npm and Bundler installs and locked Cargo metadata passed.
- The CI artifact build, production typechecks, focused Gateway/provider/lockfile and filesystem tests, workflow validation, lint, and formatting passed locally. The repository’s paired Control UI budget check passed in a clean exact-commit checkout using CI’s Node 24.22.1. The Vercel and Sandbox CLIs materialized from the pinned lock and exposed the expected release subcommands; no deployment ran.
- Locked Rust workspace, watch engine, and both iroh binding suites passed. The Linux desktop suite has one failure reproduced on the exact base (an Ubuntu multicall fixture); opt-in logind cases exceeded the local socket path limit. Fastlane Supply and Deliver loaded from the frozen mobile locks. Native-platform CI is still required.
- OpenGrep changed-path scanning and SARIF conversion, zizmor validation, PostgreSQL and Node container smoke tests, and a local Litestream restore/rollback passed. The local OpenGrep Vitest suite stalled in the host Git wrapper; the direct scanner checks do not count as a passing Vitest run.
- Local Codex autoreview covered all 105 changed paths of the committed tree against `d5a99b07e88e`; no actionable P0/P1 findings were reported. Build and registry checks provide separate evidence.

Co-authored by [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4d3824c3-fe0d-415b-851e-ff25e582759f)
- [Rust implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f306fe93-057b-462b-b205-b096aa6f496d)

## Worked on by

- @steipete

prs.title: fix: write Blobster previews to the requested directory
prs.body:
Related: #199950

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw agents render-blobster` can return success after writing a preview to the wrong directory. When `--out` contains a symlink followed by `..`, the command collapses the path before opening it and can overwrite a neighboring file.

## User Impact

On POSIX, Blobster previews land where the supplied path points. The JSON summary reports that destination, and a missing directory before `..` produces an error before anything is written.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the shared filesystem resolver introduced in #200031 at the one output boundary used for SVG and PNG. The design reader already delegates traversal to the filesystem.

## Evidence

- Linux, Node 24.18.0, isolated state and the design guide's sample JSON. On main `3d0900e4ac0`, the built CLI read `selected/../design.json` and overwrote the lexical neighbor when rendering to `selected/../preview.svg`. The bundled skill CLI did the same for PNG.
- After rebuilding, both renderers wrote to the directory named by the symlink traversal and reported the correct path in JSON. Both neighboring files kept their original bytes. The rendered SVG and PNG matched the baseline artifacts byte for byte, and ordinary output still created its parent directory. An output with a missing segment before `..` exited 1 and preserved the neighboring file.
- The regression failed on the base at the overwritten-neighbor assertion. The fixed command and shared resolver suites passed all 40 tests. Core and command-test type checks, targeted formatting, and lint passed, and independent autoreview through P2 returned no actionable findings. macOS and Windows were outside the local run.

<details>
<summary>Commands and timing</summary>

```sh
pnpm openclaw --version
node openclaw.mjs agents render-blobster selected/../design.json --out selected/../preview.svg --json
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agents.blobster.test.ts src/infra/home-dir.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/commands/agents.blobster.test.ts src/commands/agents.commands.blobster.ts
```

Replay the CLI command from a temporary directory with `selected` pointing to `physical/nested`, the guide's sample saved as `physical/design.json`, and a sentinel file at `preview.svg`. Use the checkout's absolute entry path when running from the fixture directory. The passing Vitest run took 65 seconds wall time, including a cold compiled-worker build. CI timing is pending.

</details>

prs.title: feat: generate PixVerse image videos through ClawRouter
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter can advertise a PixVerse image-input route, but OpenClaw cannot currently select it through video generation. Falling through to another provider after an uncertain paid submission could also create a second video.

## User Impact

Users whose selected ClawRouter key grants the exact input profile can generate image-to-video with `clawrouter/pixverse/v6` or `clawrouter/pixverse/c1`. One local PNG, JPEG, or WebP image is submitted through the Router. Direct PixVerse behavior and ordinary pre-submit fallback stay unchanged.

The Router route must actually be enabled and present in the selected key's fresh catalog. This client change does not activate it. Shipping SDK-to-Worker/SQLite composition remains a separate qualification step. The current video request API has no caller signal; this PR does not claim caller-abort or pre-header disconnect propagation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new registration admits only `clawrouter.pixverse-image-input.v1` with matching offer/endpoint metadata, native image-video formats, and the two supported models. It snapshots at most 8 MiB of image bytes plus 32 KiB of multipart framing and scalar controls. Caller image IDs, URLs, receipts, and grants are rejected.

The Router owns upstream upload/create and its separate fixed upload/generation policies. The client sends one composed POST with an operation-owned idempotency key, then polls only the original video ID with the original selected Router key. Returned media URLs remain opaque.

A narrow SDK helper reuses the existing terminal-failure registry. Once create invocation begins, escaping response, polling, asset-validation, deadline, and cleanup failures stop automatic media fallback before callbacks or another provider. Frozen errors retain identity; non-Error reasons retain their exact cause. Independent body and cleanup failures remain ordered. No error-name/status heuristics or provider-secret fallback are added.

## Current Candidate and Reconciliation

Signed candidate **`b0d33f09ba5d8d0e6db804f01cbf79dcf269a351`**, tree **`3ef374ed98c55f0e3e55e55b5d9868771fed1bd7`**, ordered parents **[`caf56e1f5e5bda520fa2f2472f731f71f5d24cc9`, `a90c174919aca859d2145b2e6bede683ec87177a`]**. The native materializer resolved exactly chunk grouping and skills-library readiness using bound source/base/fork blobs. Provider implementation and documentation remain byte-identical to `caf56`; frozen install inputs remain unchanged.

The incoming explicit Search-settlement and held-library setup replace obsolete empty-grid polling. Recovery opens the installed shelf before selecting its detail. Failure, no-false-empty, reload and zero-write assertions remain. Incoming attachment visibility sampling is preserved. These are source-supported test corrections, not an attribution of the prior hosted Escape failure.

The two retained grouping mappings keep neutral truncation with the existing plugin-catalog group and catalog-discovery with settings controls. Incoming routed Skills pages, single SkillTile owner, installed/browse separation, 1,000 records, category counts/cursors/deduplication and request/DOM identity stay intact. The original 100 ms delay, deadlines, **28/31/56/61 asset ceilings**, and zero eager-reader/tooltip guards remain. Inventory opens during benchmark preparation; the measured action is filtering only.

## Verification and Timing

- **Fresh on signed `b0d`: 54 contract/registered HTTP cases pass**, 32.011 s wall / 28.85 s Vitest. The 22 video-runtime cases pass in 6.223 s wall / 4.41 s Vitest. Real unfinished HTTP responses, operation deadlines, original release and terminal no-fallback joins require the transport layer; compiler/registration startup contributes to invocation walltime. Fake clocks alone cannot establish those joins. Hosted seconds for this head remain pending.
- Core production types (8.951 s), extension production types (9.901 s), extension test types (14.355 s), and the owning core-test-other graph (7.126 s) pass. The actual test graphs are checked as well as production types.
- Test-line guard passes against frozen `a90`: **711 net LF growth <= 400 + 317 existing justified credit**. Allocation is unchanged. Diff checks pass.
- Exact **`a90` to `b0d` SDK/API comparison passes in 104.624 s**, with no public API changes. Diff SHA256 `16eb6f4a2c62f6fc310b2c62864e833978757dfe9129c7a2e7c7452086055595`; evidence SHA256 `9013348bb0678a3ed217d9d54ec59a6eda2e423ee4ecf02625d806c52858e581`. This does not replace full-build qualification.
- **Explicit proof reuse:** this candidate's entire UI tree `9eb3281881f00253f99acd467826546617d47d0a` and scripts tree `cc5867378b8c2bff90e1342c4f73e73791f51e53` equal OpenCode `dad3cce339d3173679979a1c92c1a5e3c2c92380`, with matching package/lock/runtime inputs. Its 10 chunk-boundary cases and four original production asset cases passed (45.044 s wall / 43.04 s Vitest); two strict local interaction cases also passed. These remain executions on `dad3`, not new PixVerse runs or hosted parity. UI fixture compilation, real Chromium readiness and held-reader release explain the over-30-second file invocation.
- Prior normal built-registry acceptance on `5b` used `generateVideo(params)` without provider-lookup overrides: malformed create produced one composed POST and zero direct requests, while a missing offer reached the configured direct upload/create/GET; acquisition cleanup and process closure passed. That receipt remains historical. Shipping SDK-to-Worker/SQLite composition is separately coordinated.

## Investigated Build Failure and Remaining Gates

The exact signed **`b0d` full build failed exit 1 after 218.093 s**, without timeout or capture fault. Public SDK declarations are **5,394,718 > 5,385,536 bytes** (9,182 over). Raw output: 621,087 B, SHA256 `f408ca8dafb7f0cf32a4a48072dd8e774ca0b2b12ce01127010635bab4ac9408`. Runtime/plugin/UI phases completed, but the full build did not pass.

The same execution reports largest CSS 58,500 > 58,315 B; total CSS 345,436 > 337,312 gzip / 1,783,340 > 1,740,234 raw; chat 21 > 20 requests and 1,334,208 > 1,332,637 gzip. New Session is within its recorded ceiling at 822,164 <= 822,243 gzip. No unmodified `a90` baseline-build attribution, budget increase, API removal or green-build claim is made.

All prior source, failed runs and diagnostic receipts remain retained. In particular, `caf56`'s hosted 390px Escape failure remains causally unresolved; a local strict pass is not baseline or Linux parity proof. The separate scaffold archive-timeout retry completed successfully on unchanged `caf56`. The existing 768px portrait Workshop visible-title gap remains a separate follow-up; hidden metadata is not accessibility proof.

Native preparation records `tests.result: fail` with this exact-head investigated evidence. `github_pending` is not successful hosted qualification. Fresh exact-head CI and final native admission remain required. No merge, coupled cleanup, deployment, release, live paid provider request or shipping Worker qualification is claimed.

prs.title: fix(models): read the published owner inventory for picker menus after a config republish
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

After any runtime config change, the Telegram `/models` picker (and the Discord and Mattermost pickers built on the same data) could show only a provider's configured or manifest models instead of its discovered inventory. Live, a Gemini OAuth provider with 6 discovered models showed its 3 manifest models after a click, while `models.list` on the same Gateway kept returning 6. It stayed that way until a Gateway restart. Published-policy readers now look up the published owner the same way they select it, so they get its full inventory again.

### Root Cause

`withPreparedModelCatalogOwnerPolicy` (`src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.ts`) does two lookups:

1. `resolvePreparedModelCatalogOwnerSnapshotWithPolicy(request, configPolicy, ...)` selects the owner snapshot. With `configPolicy === "published"`, it accepts the published owner even when `request.config` no longer matches the owner's config (`policy === "published" || preparedModelRuntimeConfigsMatch(...)`).
2. `publishedReadOnlyOwner` decides whether a read-only request materializes that owner's full inventory (`materializeRequestedModelCatalog`) or returns the raw snapshot. This always used `getPreparedModelCatalogOwnerSnapshot`, an exact-config lookup.

When the caller's config is older than the published owner, lookup 1 returns the published owner and lookup 2 returns `undefined`. The `request.readOnly && !publishedReadOnlyOwner` branch then returns the raw snapshot. Its `modelCatalog` holds only configured or manifest rows, because a generation keeps discovered rows apart until a reader materializes them.

Which callers hit this depends on the config they pass:

- `loadModelsProviderData` (`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-models-catalog.ts`) passes the command's `cfg`, which was captured when the turn or command started. After a republish that config is stale, so the picker got configured rows only.
- `models.list` (`src/gateway/server-model-catalog.ts`) passes `getRuntimeConfig()`, the current config. The exact lookup matches, so it kept returning the full inventory. That is why the two disagreed on the same Gateway.

Observed before this change: the picker's provider button showed the discovered count, and the model list behind it showed the 3 manifest rows. A safe Gateway restart rebuilt the owner and fixed it until the next config write. The plugin logged no failed discovery refreshes, and `models.list` returned 6 rows on 12 consecutive polls.

## Exact change

- `prepared-model-catalog.ts`: for `configPolicy === "published"`, `publishedReadOnlyOwner` now uses `getPublishedPreparedModelCatalogOwnerSnapshot(request)`. Exact-policy readers keep `getPreparedModelCatalogOwnerSnapshot`. One ternary plus a comment.
- `prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`: a regression test that publishes an owner under a newer config, reads it through `loadPublishedPreparedModelCatalogOwnerSnapshot({ readOnly: true })` with an older config, and asserts the full discovered inventory comes back with no discovery call and no activation.

## Scope boundary

- No config, schema, storage, protocol or SDK change.
- Exact-policy readers, writable reads and `refreshFullCatalog` paths are unchanged.
- Materialization reads the owner's already-built inventory (`readFullModelCatalog`). It does not start discovery, and the test asserts `loadFullModelCatalog` is not called.
- Not addressed here: why the picker reader gets a config older than the published owner. Passing the current runtime config to every turn-path reader would be a broader change. This PR makes the published policy behave the same for stale and current configs.

## Real behavior proof

Regression test, run with `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`:

```text
base (d874bf532f4)  reads the published full inventory for picker menus after a config republish  FAIL
                    - "id": "discovered"   + "id": "configured"
                    Tests  1 failed | 14 passed (15)
this head           Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Related suites at this head, all passing: `prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`, `server-model-catalog.test.ts`, `commands-models.test.ts`, `commands-models.catalog-recovery.test.ts`, `directive-handling.model.test.ts`, `local-request-context.test.ts`, `sessions-mutations.catalog-queue.test.ts` (4 Vitest shards, 121 tests).

## What was not tested

- Not deployed to a live Gateway yet, so the picker has not been clicked after a config write on this head.
- No before/after benchmark. The change swaps one in-memory owner lookup for another and, for stale-config published reads, adds the same materialization fresh-config reads already did.
- A wider run over 68 catalog, picker and channel test files hit failures in `src/sessions/session-diff-revisions.test.ts` (6) and `src/agents/simple-completion-execution.test.ts` (13). Both fail the same way on the base commit with this change reverted, so they are unrelated. That run also stopped at its 40-minute local cap, so some shards never finished.

## Verification

- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both touched files: clean.
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`: exit 0.
- `$autoreview` (commit mode, P1 cap): no accepted findings, "patch is correct".

prs.title: fix(ui): resume Logs auto-follow after delayed wheel input
prs.body:
Closes #202354

## What Problem This Solves

When a reader wheels back to the newest Logs entry, Auto-follow can remain off if the input’s first scroll arrives after the existing idle deadline. This change protects that event-ordering case; the original WebKit CI flake has not been reproduced natively in this environment.

## User Impact

User impact: returning to the live tail keeps the reader’s intent through the first input frame, without increasing the 200 ms idle window. Programmatic movement after idle, horizontal-wheel expiry, and manually disabling follow at the end retain their existing behavior. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Logs view currently starts its idle countdown at input dispatch, before the browser necessarily applies the scroll. Start that countdown at the first layout frame instead, or immediately when a scroll is observed. The existing shared frame scheduler owns the pending callback, which is cancelled on observed scrolling and unmount.

This is a production behavior fix with a regression, not a test-timeout increase. The controlled regression establishes the ordering defect, but does not establish that this was the cause of the reported WebKit CI failure. Browser frames suspended in a hidden tab retain intent until a frame or scroll is observed; no new wall-clock fallback is introduced.

## Evidence

### Clean comparison

Before

![Logs before: native wheel returns to tail with Auto-follow enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce7d0ed0-fdbd-4786-a67a-d72f33a4ca29)

After

![Logs after: native wheel returns to tail with Auto-follow enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e261636-3706-46d3-904c-7142f88eb192)

### Annotated comparison

Before

![Logs before annotated: native happy-path follow](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ec709d1-e75d-450a-a91d-96ba6b346b28)

After

![Logs after annotated: native happy-path follow](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5495195d-94d0-475a-88f2-dd5c89aad559)

Chromium 156.0.8078.4, 1200×800, synthetic Gateway fixture: before production base `749e2aed737bf33a9ed6a42ddd45a5d39b39a34d`; after published head `365a635c135624a3932ff909bca719eadbb9724e`. Both show the preserved native happy path. The delayed-first-frame defect is proven separately by deterministic red/green tests, not by these screenshots.

### WebKit main vs PR

Local run reported by @daniel-lxs:

> I tested the bundled Logs route in Playwright WebKit 27.2 on macOS with a mock Gateway and 200 log rows. On main `e7d7704`, I used one native wheel gesture to return to the newest log and stalled the wheel task for 350 ms and 1,000 ms. In both cases, I observed the 200 ms idle timer fire before the first trusted scroll, leaving Auto-follow off at the bottom. My separate controlled delayed-first-scroll case also failed: **3 failed, 2 passed** overall.
>
> On PR head `365a635`, I observed Auto-follow resume in every case: **5 passed**. With no stall, I observed both builds resume. I did not test a live Gateway, and I do not know how often this ordering occurs in normal use.

- Original production: existing Logs view suite passes (11 tests, 2.91 s). With the new delayed-input regression only, returning to the end fails because the last Auto-follow update remains `false` (10 pass, 1 fail, 1.68 s).
- Patched production: Logs view and page-consumer suites pass (29 tests, 2.01 s, one worker). Covers reader release/resume, append/trim anchoring, pointer holds, End, filters, horizontal/no-motion wheel expiry, and subsequent programmatic return.
- UI typecheck, changed-source lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass. Lint reports four warnings on unchanged reactive closures; existing runtime tests also emit Solid strict-read warnings.
- Independent review attempted with the bound Auto Review tool, P0–P2 scope, against base `749e2aed737bf33a9ed6a42ddd45a5d39b39a34d`; unavailable before assessment because the configured model compatibility schema rejects `cachesInstructions`. This is not a clean review.
- Native Chromium 156.0.8078.4 proof passes on both the original production source and the patch, using the real built Logs route with synthetic Gateway rows at 1200×800. Wheel-up disables follow, an append preserves reader position, wheel-down resumes follow at a zero-pixel bottom gap, and explicit re-enable returns to the tail. Baseline: 4.59 s scenario / 16.68 s run; patched: 3.49 s scenario / 15.48 s run. These are correctness runs, not a performance claim. Both captured 35 virtual rows and two `logs.tail` reads.
- Matched clean and annotated screenshots were captured during those native scenarios and inspected. They show the unchanged happy path, not the delayed-first-scroll failure covered by the WebKit comparison above. The clean and annotated comparisons are embedded above; originating-chat delivery is coordinated separately.
- Attribution to the original scheduled CI failure remains unverified. The task-local Chromium libraries were extracted without system installation; no host configuration or validation bypass was used. CI seconds are unavailable before publication.
- First capture attempt failed because the custom page host was not a rendered screenshot surface; the actual Logs stream was then selected. No product assertion or timeout was relaxed.

<details>
<summary>Exact local commands and change size</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ui/src/pages/logs/view.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ui/src/pages/logs/view.test.tsx ui/src/pages/logs/logs-page.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p ui/tsconfig.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig ui/tsconfig.json ui/src/pages/logs/view.tsx ui/src/pages/logs/view.test.tsx
node scripts/run-format.mts --check ui/src/pages/logs/view.tsx ui/src/pages/logs/view.test.tsx
git diff --check
# Run once per production revision, with temporary capture-only instrumentation:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/logs-autofollow.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'turns auto-follow off when the reader scrolls up and back on at the end'
```

Simplification pass: one existing intent owner and shared frame scheduler; no new abstraction or test-only production seam. Production +13/−3 lines; tests +19/−5. No effects, native listener registrations, DOM queries, or owner API calls added. The 200 ms timeout and release threshold are unchanged.

</details>

Patch supplied by @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_gg7nds)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/abd652d1-1750-43b8-aa12-aecbb92b952e)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: fix(ui): keep chat rows aligned before the first scroll
prs.body:
Closes #202357

Related: #198500

## What Problem This Solves

Opening or expanding chat content can expose an earlier transcript row before the first reader gesture. If that row enters normal flow before its actual height is measured, messages already on screen move by the difference from its estimated height.

## User Impact

User impact: retained chat rows stay aligned when a newly exposed predecessor is measured after initial placement. This is a narrow correction, not a complete fix for every disclosure or canvas-resize jump. No configuration, migration, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing measure-before-flow mechanism once initial placement has completed, rather than waiting for the first reader gesture. Initial placement and end-preparation exceptions remain unchanged; no new state, timers, or compensation writer is introduced.

Contributor credit: supplied patch from @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_gg7nds) — also final browser, end-to-end, and visual verification.
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/3d17abff-11f1-4b77-9fa0-d813394a4e88) — source preparation and focused owner/static checks.

## Evidence

### Review follow-up: built Control UI admission trace

[The added production-bundle E2E regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e840f76cd0554b3b2b0bde1e8b27085d0678b7f5/ui/src/e2e/chat-transcript-cold-resize.e2e.test.ts) now exercises the changed behavior, rather than only the unchanged disclosure flow pictured below. It opens a fresh synthetic 40-turn tool-bearing conversation at 1200×800, waits for fonts and settled layout at the end, and increases native window height to 1000 without wheel, touch, or keyboard input. No measurement, virtualizer, or positioning owner is invoked by the test.

The taller viewport exposes previously unmounted predecessors. A read-only exploratory lifecycle trace confirmed completed placement with reading=false/preparingEnd=false and size-cache misses at admission. The committed regression observes only real DOM positions and row admission. It measures the retained text's distance from the viewport bottom, accounting for the intended 200 px viewport increase.

**Original production fails at 112.609375 px; the unchanged production fix passes at 0.78125 px maximum error**, against the same **2 px** limit. No new production changes were needed. The baseline control restored only the original admission condition; the candidate was restored afterward. Both versions recorded zero wheel/touch/keyboard inputs.

| Resized frame | Original alignment error | Patched alignment error | Patched new predecessors |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 112.609375 px | 0 px | Rows 108/109 held outside flow |
| 2 | 0.390625 px | 0 px | Rows 108/109 still held |
| 3 | 0.78125 px | 0.390625 px | Rows 108/109 admitted; row 107 held |
| Maximum over 32 resized frames | 112.609375 px | 0.78125 px | All eventually measured and admitted |

Initial transcript viewport height was 689 px, then 889 px. Initial retained-row offset from the viewport bottom was -342.4375 px. In the original first resized frame it was -455.046875 px; with the patch it remained -342.4375 px. This is a native window-resize case, not a claim to have reproduced the separately reported 112 px canvas-resize symptom.

The finalized E2E passed in **1.486 s test time / 16.73 s Vitest including the production build**. The existing **33 Chromium geometry cases and 16 initial-range cases** also passed. Targeted E2E typechecking, lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. The frame budget begins when the resize is observed, so a slow automation command cannot consume it before the action occurs; the observer and input listeners are disposed afterward.

Pr-simplify ran before edits and again on the new test: removed the exploratory private-state hook, unrelated width/disclosure probes, and broad diagnostic output; retained one native-resize regression. This follow-up adds 167 test lines and no production lines. The independent Auto Review attempt was stopped after stalling and returned no assessment; it is not claimed as a clean review. No tests were weakened, and no force push or review comment was used.

The new browser regression fails against unchanged production with **48 px** of unexpected retained-row movement (allowed maximum: 2 px). With the exact supplied patch, the entire Chromium geometry suite passes **33/33 tests** (4.317 seconds tests; 7.36 seconds Vitest; 8.86 seconds wrapper). Existing initial-range owner tests pass **16/16**. Targeted lint, formatting, UI typechecking, and diff whitespace checks pass.

The existing completed-work/tool-disclosure and raw-details end-to-end cases pass **2/2 on both baseline and candidate**, using the real built Control UI with synthetic Gateway data. They cover expansion/collapse at the end and middle of a transcript. Candidate E2E test time: 6.956 seconds; invocation duration: 25.46 seconds including the UI build. All recorded row-top displacements in those scenarios were 0 px on both versions. Their screenshots are matched context/parity evidence, not a claim to show the intermittent jump.

**Limits:** the supplied 47.61 → 0.39 px disclosure measurement and separate remaining 112 px canvas resize were not reproduced. The targeted browser regression establishes the cold-row admission defect, not the original scheduled-CI failure or a complete fix for #198500. WebKit has no successful local execution result. Exact-head CI remains pending; CI seconds are not yet available.

For the original two-file candidate, Auto Review prepared the change and unchanged owner/caller context against base 749e2aed737bf33a9ed6a42ddd45a5d39b39a34d, but configured reviewer execution failed before assessment. The later follow-up review was stopped after stalling, as noted above. Neither attempt is claimed as a clean independent review.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and scope</summary>

Apply only the new browser test to baseline 749e2aed7 and run:

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-geometry-updates.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1 --configLoader runner -t 'keeps measured rows aligned when the cold viewport admits a shorter predecessor'

The first-frame assertion fails with 48 > 2. Applying the production change makes the full file pass. An earlier concurrent-build attempt timed out before test collection; the serialized runner attempt produced the actual red result.

Focused E2E:

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/chat-transcript-disclosure-anchor.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'keeps completed-work and tool disclosures|keeps raw tool details anchored'

The original supplied two-file fix remains unchanged: production +3/-2 lines and its browser regression +30 lines. This follow-up adds the separate 167-line built-UI E2E regression (total test delta +197 lines). No issue was created or reopened.

</details>

### Visual evidence

Matched light-theme screenshots were captured at a 1400×800 viewport (604×756 chat-region crops) on baseline 749e2aed7 and the supplied candidate. Synthetic fixture text only. The clean baseline and candidate images are byte-identical and intentionally share an uploaded asset. These stills show the preserved disclosure context, not timing; the separate regression above supplies the 48 px red/green evidence.

#### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: baseline disclosure context](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8eb69a17-755a-4d67-82ab-86778007f9ee) | ![After: unchanged disclosure context with the patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8eb69a17-755a-4d67-82ab-86778007f9ee) |

#### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Original disclosure context; timing measured separately](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e3a437b-857b-49ad-9231-e8eb2fba340f) | ![Patched disclosure context; timing measured separately](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa384d4a-ce6c-4b50-a91f-5088a3078a60) |

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: fix: explain when profile avatar uploads need a retry
prs.body:
Closes #202728

## What Problem This Solves

In Settings → Profile → Identity, choosing an avatar just as the profile refreshes can discard the selection without an error or an upload request.

## User Impact

The chooser now shows when the profile is busy. If a selection arrives while the profile cannot accept it, the page tells the user to wait and choose the image again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The file picker stays mounted across a refresh of the same profile, so the page can handle a selection from an already-open chooser. Upload authorization and validation are unchanged.

## Evidence

A browser test with a mocked Tailscale Gateway observed no upload during the pending refresh, verified the visible retry message, and confirmed that choosing the image again sent `users.setAvatar`.

|---|---|

| ![before annotated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qodelicious/openclaw/pr-media-202728/before-annotated.png) | ![after annotated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qodelicious/openclaw/pr-media-202728/after-annotated.png) |

prs.title: refactor(ui): remove dead Settings text (Labs, Updates, forms, devices, memory)
prs.body:
Related: #201187 (the same cleanup for `newSession.hint`)

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI English catalog still carries 42 strings for Settings: Labs, Updates and About, settings forms and appearance, devices and systems, memory and the dream diary that no screen shows anymore. Translators keep paying for them on every locale refresh, and they make it harder to tell which copy is live.

## User Impact

User impact: none visible. These screens look and work the same. After the next locale refresh, translators stop seeing 42 dead strings.

## Why This Change Was Made

This removes only the English source and the code that existed just to hold it. Translated locale files and translation memory are left for the post-merge locale refresh, per `ui/AGENTS.md`.

- `labs-loading.test.ts` drops its swarm samples; the Labs features keep their coverage.

prs.title: feat: add llmman to the Models page Add provider list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI -> Models only lists hosted providers in the "Add an account" picker. Someone running llmman, a local OpenAI-compatible model server, has no way to add it from the UI and has to hand-edit `models.providers.llmman` in config.

## User Impact

User impact: llmman now appears in Models -> Add an account, with its own logo, next to the hosted providers. Saving a key (any non-empty value works for a local server; `llmman-local` is the documented marker) sets up the provider and discovers the models your llmman server reports, so you can pick one as a default and chat with it. Models are listed by a short name: `docker.io/ai/gemma4:latest` shows as `gemma4` and `docker.io/ai/qwen3.8:27b` as `qwen3.8:27b`. A model from another namespace, host, or tag keeps it (`docker.io/alternate-ai-place/gemma4` shows as `alternate-ai-place/gemma4`). Existing manual `models.providers.llmman` configs keep working unchanged, and an explicit `baseUrl` still wins.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker only shows providers whose plugin manifest declares an API key auth choice for guided setup. llmman had no bundled plugin, so it could never appear. This adds a small bundled `llmman` plugin modeled on the existing local-server providers: default base URL `http://127.0.0.1:17434/v1`, models discovered from `/v1/models`, and the `llmman-local` non-secret marker. It also ships llmman's own manatee mark, shown in full color instead of the flat mask used by monochrome marks (source, checksum, and Apache-2.0 license are recorded in the attribution files). llmman reports models by their full reference and no display name, so the plugin shortens the display name by dropping the default `docker.io/` host, `ai/` namespace, and `:latest` tag. Only the display name changes: the model id, which is what the server is sent and what config stores, is untouched (llmman rejects a bare `ai/gemma4` as an unknown Hugging Face repo, so ids cannot be shortened safely). A display name the server supplies itself is kept. No core auth, catalog, or capability code changes, and no other provider's behavior changes.

## Evidence

Clean before/after pair (Models -> Add an account, searching "llm"). Before, only LiteLLM matches; after, the llmman row, with the llmman manatee logo, is listed too:

| Before (origin/main) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: searching "llm" in the Add an account picker lists only LiteLLM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c20dd403-81ac-4500-b079-7559d07706c4) | ![After: searching "llm" lists LiteLLM and a separate llmman row with the llmman manatee logo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eecb0fc9-4e00-4c7e-bf86-3374daaf47a3) |

The rest of the flow on this branch, run end to end on an NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64) against a live llmman 0.1.652 server:

| Choose llmman, enter a key | Provider card after saving | Model dropdown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![The llmman API key dialog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68eb3409-5b90-420b-9884-8a665aa4dffb) | ![Models page: llmman card with 5 models](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/655767ca-84a0-4d81-b9c6-16ca5d514538) | ![Model dropdown listing the five models discovered from the llmman server](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ebf0e39-7fff-46d6-bc80-d56a1b2fc0ed) |

| Chat with the discovered model | Test access on the llmman card |
| --- | --- |
| ![Control UI chat: two turns answered by gemma4 via llmman](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09d7cde4-1de4-449e-9bfc-aa558879f9da) | ![Models page: gemma4 selected as default; llmman card shows Access verified, request round-trip 3331 ms](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e5c4120-fc21-441b-9dd1-43e96d2e0f2c) |

What was checked:
- **Real chat round trip, on the Spark:** the Control UI chat got replies from `gemma4` (llmman id `docker.io/ai/gemma4:latest`) through llmman (two turns). `qwen3.8:27b` also answered through the Gateway (`openclaw infer model run --gateway`, about 20 s). `openclaw models list --provider llmman --all` shows all five discovered models as Local with Auth yes.
- **Same-build comparison:** the "before" is the exact upstream parent commit (`4ea2deb`) built and run on the same machine as this branch, with the same search and dialog framing.
- **Tests and checks:** plugin tests (manifest shape, discovery against a stub `/v1/models` server, marker and key handling, explicit-config precedence, no-server case, short display names), gateway capability test, Models page data test, provider icon tests, API key flow test, plugin inventory check, and docs format check pass. Type checks and the dead-export scan from `pnpm check:changed` pass on the rebased tree, and oxlint and oxfmt are clean on every file this PR changes. The repo-wide lint step of `check:changed` still reports three `max-lines` errors in files this PR does not touch (`src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts`, `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.test.ts`); they are present on the upstream parent commit.

Notes for reviewers:
- **Where the full reference still shows:** the model dropdown, the default Model row, and the chat composer use the short name. The line under **Test access** ("Profile llmman:manual · llmman/docker.io/ai/gemma4:latest" in the last screenshot) still prints the exact provider/model reference the check used. That line is built by the gateway's shared probe code for every provider, so I left it alone here rather than add docker-specific logic to core. It would be a small follow-up if you want it shortened too.
- **Notice right after saving:** the card can show "API key saved, but the check didn't finish. No model is available for this provider." until you pick an llmman model. The post-save check tests with a model you have configured and has nothing to try on a fresh setup. Once a model is selected, **Test access** on the card passes (screenshot above). I left that shared check alone to keep this PR small.
- **Reasoning models:** discovered models are registered with `reasoning: false`, so for a model like gemma4 the Gateway logs that it emitted reasoning that was hidden. Replies still work. Reading reasoning support from the server would be a reasonable follow-up.
- **Bundle budget notices:** the Control UI build prints the same six size-budget notices on this branch and on the parent commit; this change adds about 0.1 KiB of raw CSS.

<details>
<summary>Agent transcript (condensed excerpt; the user request is paraphrased)</summary>

**User:** The Control UI Models page only offers hosted providers and no local one. Add llmman so it appears in that list, test it thoroughly through the UI, open a PR with screenshots and the agent transcript, then add the llmman logo, and run the end-to-end test on a DGX Spark with gemma4 and qwen3.8. Address the gaps listed in the first PR description and leave the PR in a mergeable state.

**Agent (investigation):** The "Add an account" picker is built from provider capabilities, and a provider only gets one when a bundled plugin manifest declares an `api-key` auth choice with `appGuidedSecret: true`. llmman was documented as "Plugin: none", so it could never be listed.

**Agent (implementation):** Delegated the code change to opencode (claude-sonnet-5-5, high thinking) with a scoped prompt: a new bundled `extensions/llmman` plugin modeled on the litellm and lmstudio plugins, manual configs unchanged, no changes to other providers, plus tests, docs, and registry updates. Reviewed the whole diff myself.

**Agent (logo):** llmman's brand mark is its manatee image, which llmman publishes in its docs-assets release and pins by SHA-256. Downloaded it, checked the hash, wrapped it in a square SVG for the Control UI, added a CSS rule so it keeps its colors instead of being masked to one color, used it for the plugin package icon, and recorded source, checksum, and license. A first attempt pasted extra text into the attribution file through a shell quoting mistake; a scan of the diff caught it and the commit was rewritten.

**Agent (testing on the DGX Spark):** Built the branch on the Spark (aarch64) and ran a throwaway Gateway there, with headless Chrome driving the real Control UI against the Spark's llmman server (gemma4, qwen3.5, qwen3.8). Picker, key dialog, save, provider card, and model dropdown all work and list the four discovered models. gemma4 answered in the chat UI, and qwen3.8:27b answered through the Gateway CLI. Tried marking the key choice `credentialOnly` to avoid the post-save notice; that made setup two steps and still showed a notice, so it was reverted. Found that the notice clears once a model is selected (Test access then reports Access verified).

**Agent (cleanup):** Squashed the branch to one commit, rebased it onto current main, rebuilt the exact upstream parent for a like-for-like "before" screenshot, and re-ran the checks on the rebased tree.

**Agent (model names):** Feedback was that docker.io is the default host, ai the default namespace, and latest the default tag, so docker.io/ai/gemma4:latest should read as gemma4 everywhere, while other namespaces, hosts, and tags stay visible. Since llmman only reports the full reference and rejects a bare ai/ prefix, I kept the ids as they are and set the display name in the plugin, with tests for the default host, namespace, and tag, another namespace, another host, another tag, and a server-supplied name. Amended into the same commit, rebuilt on the Spark, and retook the screenshots that show model names.

</details>

prs.title: fix(media): read owner WebChat reply media without the toolsBySender overlay
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With a restrictive `tools.toolsBySender["*"]` wildcard — the documented way to give unknown DM senders a small tool set — the owner's own WebChat replies can no longer attach local files. A reply with a `MEDIA:<path>` line for a workspace file becomes an `attachment_error`, while the same turn's tools still run, because owner WebChat turns deliberately skip the sender overlay for tools (`senderPolicyMode: "never"` in `resolveConversationCapabilityPolicy`) but the reply-media read did not.

This lands on the Control UI's default session too: `agent:main:main` has no channel segment, so the first version of this fix (which reconstructed the surface from the session key) still failed there. Both paths are fixed now.

Closes #200661.

## User Impact

An owner using the Control UI (or a `cli`/`chat.send` client with `operator.admin`) gets their attachments back — on the default main session and on channel-scoped sessions alike — while the wildcard keeps protecting every other sender. Non-owner WebChat clients, `operator.read`/`operator.write` clients without `operator.admin`, every channel delivery, the `message` tool, and real external senders keep the sender policy unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveAgentScopedMediaAccess` always folded `resolveSenderToolPolicy` into the read check. `WebchatReplyMediaRequesterContext` already carried the caller facts but dropped `GatewayClientScopes`, so the media read could not tell an `operator.admin` requester from a guest, and `resolveChatSendCallerContext` already resolves that scope set for `chat.send`.

The change carries the scope-derived owner fact from the WebChat requester context through `createReplyMediaPathNormalizer`/`createReplyMediaSourcePreparer` into the resolver, and the resolver skips the sender policy when `isInternalOwnerRequester` holds — the same predicate the tools side uses. Global, agent and group policies still apply; `senderIsOwner` is only ever set by the Gateway requester context (scope check) and the harness attempt, never by reply text.

Session-scoped reply-media staging drops `messageProvider` and the sender-policy resolver treats the session key as authoritative, so the surface the owner check needs cannot be reconstructed for a main-session key: `parseSessionDeliveryRoute("agent:main:main")` is null and its channel segment reads `"main"`. The resolver therefore now takes an explicit `requesterSurface` — set from the authenticated `Surface` on the Gateway call sites and from the inbound `messageChannel`/`messageProvider` on a harness attempt — and only falls back to the delivery route and session key when it is absent. Sender-policy lookups themselves are unchanged: they still prefer the session route over the caller's provider.

## Evidence

Live A/B/C on one machine with one script. Isolated shipped Gateway (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` under an empty temp dir, port 28794, mock OpenAI-compatible provider on 28795), config `session.dmScope: "per-channel-peer"` and `tools.toolsBySender["*"] = { allow: ["web_search"], deny: ["read", "write", "exec", "group:fs"] }`. Each run sends `chat.send "please send me probe.txt"` through a GatewayClient and reads the assistant parts back from `chat.history`. For the "before" leg only the four source files of this PR were reverted to `c46be04` and `dist` rebuilt; the session, config and script are identical.

Main-session path (the `[P2]` finding):

| Run | Session key | Client scopes | PR head source | Last assistant parts | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | `agent:main:main` | `operator.admin` | `c46be04` (reviewed head) | `[{"type":"text"},{"type":"attachment_error","label":"probe.txt","code":"delivery-failed"}]` | P2 reproduced |
| After | `agent:main:main` | `operator.admin` | `5dbde12` (+ main-session fix) | `[{"type":"text"},{"type":"attachment","label":"probe.txt","size":17}]` | fixed |
| Control | `agent:main:main` | `operator.read`, `operator.write` | `5dbde12` | `[{"type":"text"},{"type":"attachment_error","label":"probe.txt","code":"delivery-failed"}]` | control holds |
| Regression | `agent:main:webchat:afterfix2` | `operator.admin` | `5dbde12` | `[{"type":"text"},{"type":"attachment","label":"probe.txt","size":17}]` | channel-scoped path unchanged |

![Main-session before/after/control on the isolated Gateway](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/201414/main-session-proof.png)

Channel-scoped path (earlier head `c46be04`, same rig):

| Run | Source | Client scopes | Assistant part |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | `upstream/main` (3bc20e28) | `operator.admin` | `attachment_error` (`code: delivery-failed`, `probe.txt`) |
| After | `c46be04` | `operator.admin` | `attachment` (`probe.txt`, `text/plain`, 17 bytes) |
| Control | `c46be04`, same session surface | `operator.read`, `operator.write` | `attachment_error` (`code: delivery-failed`, `probe.txt`) |

![Channel-scoped before/after/control on the isolated Gateway](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/200661/owner-reply-media-proof.png)

Tests and gates (branch merges `upstream/main` @ `da8fd166`):

- `src/media/read-capability.test.ts` — the owner test gains `agent:main:main` + `requesterSurface: "webchat"`; a new control asserts the same key with no authenticated surface keeps the wildcard. 25 passed; the 3 failures are pre-existing Windows path-literal assertions (`toContain("/Users/peter/Pictures")` vs `path.resolve` → `C:\...`) that fail identically on clean `upstream/main`.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-reply-media.workspace.test.ts` — new `keeps the owner waiver on the main session the Control UI opens by default` stages `agent:main:main` through the real WebChat display path (admin stages the image, `operator.read`+`operator.write` keeps `probe.txt: Delivery failed.`); 15/15 pass.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and the core test tsconfig both exit 0; `oxfmt --check` clean on the six files.

## What was not tested

- No real model: the rig uses a mock OpenAI-compatible stub that returns a fixed `MEDIA:` line. No real provider key is available in this environment, so the "real model" leg of the proof policy is still missing.
- The `message` tool path noted in the issue (media resolved through the message-action turn capability) is unchanged and still has no owner fact.
- Only the `operator.admin` scope rule is mirrored from `command-auth`; owner-by-identity on an internal surface (an owners allowlist entry matching a WebChat sender) still keeps the sender overlay for reply media.
- Local CI on the PR is pending first-time-contributor approval, so the repo-wide gates are not visible on this head yet.

prs.body:

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

Closes #201405

## What Problem This Solves

An unattended run can have an allowed MCP tool hidden behind Tool Search controls, so the model overlooks a reachable tool named in its instructions. Prompt plugins currently cannot see the attempt's incoming allowlist or which allowed tools were actually deferred, making a reliable discovery hint difficult.

<!--

when known. For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.

until you notice and re-enable it."
Bad: "Fixes incorrect operator-authority invalidation on session identity mutation."

Describe the experienced problem, not just the code change. Save function names,
missing checks, and the root-cause walkthrough for the explanation below.
-->

## User Impact

User impact: prompt plugins can name the deferred tools reachable in an embedded attempt without re-reading job configuration. This only exposes information: it adds no hint by default, changes no model-facing tools, and grants no authorization or policy-widening capability. No migration or configuration changes are required.

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

## Why This Change Was Made

Add optional read-only `toolsAllow` and `deferredToolNames` fields to the `before_prompt_build` event. The first preserves the incoming allowlist, including omitted versus empty; the second reads executable, non-direct identifiers from the catalog the attempt registered. Unique callable names remain names; collisions use exact catalog IDs instead, preserving the complete view without emitting ambiguous selectors. Consumers must not blindly intersect qualified IDs with a name-based allowlist. Catalog preparation already precedes prompt assembly, so no execution reordering is needed.

All handlers, including authorized enrichment, receive the same pre-hook scope snapshot; earlier returned restrictions still intersect afterward and do not rewrite it. Supplied arrays are detached/frozen and cannot be replaced. The existing mutable event-envelope convention is otherwise preserved. Generic harness and CLI paths omit unsupported scope fields; the docs explicitly distinguish informational scope from finalized `ctx.toolAuthority`.

<!--

Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

## Evidence

Native Gateway integration proof passed at `13df52115ee2511778a078388fc2d1abfca6821e`: a real isolated cron attempt loaded a prompt plugin, delivered `toolsAllow: ["read", "proof__lookup"]` and `deferredToolNames: ["proof__lookup"]`, and carried the plugin's hint into the actual provider request. The model-facing tools contained only `read` and the three Tool Search controls; a non-allowlisted MCP sibling was excluded. The real controls searched, described, and dispatched exactly one stdio MCP lookup, its result reached the next provider request, and the cron run finished `ok`.

This uses deterministic local model responses, not a live model. It proves Gateway/plugin/MCP integration and prompt delivery, not spontaneous model discovery or production cron reliability. No operator Gateway or real provider credentials were used.

The initial 59 focused tests passed at `65385cdc1e2`, covering absent/empty allowlists, Tool Search off/on, actual MCP deferral, earlier narrowing without widening, authorized snapshot stability, array mutation isolation, and unsupported harness omission. The initial five embedded regressions failed for missing scope fields before implementation.

The collision follow-up reran 21 tests successfully. Two new regressions first failed on deduplicated bare names, then passed with exact IDs for direct/deferred and deferred/deferred collisions. They dispatch every reported ID through the real Tool Search runtime and verify the intended tool executes. The isolation test also confirms caller arrays remain mutable: the existing graph clone already detaches them before freezing. Earlier-handler narrowing was already covered for both ordinary and authorized handlers and remains green.

Independent Copilot code review completed with the operator's approval after canonical autoreview could not start (Codex absent; Claude workspace authentication rejected). One suggestion to prevent adding initially absent event properties was declined: no run-state array is exposed in that case, and sealing/proxying the existing event envelope would broaden compatibility changes beyond this additive view. Supplied scope arrays remain frozen and non-replaceable.

Fresh independent review of the collision follow-up found no actionable P0-P2 issues.

Production and test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, docs, and policy checks passed. The broad `pnpm check` remains red on 20 unrelated max-lines errors; every failing source is byte-identical to the pinned upstream base.

Production catalog-before-hook ordering, generic harness/CLI omission, and Code Mode exclusion were source-traced; only the finite-allowlist/MCP-deferral scenario above was exercised through the native Gateway. Other scope variants retain their focused-test proof. Fork CI has required maintainer workflow approval; no CI success or CI seconds are claimed here.

<details>
<summary>Native Gateway behavior proof: setup and redacted output</summary>

Linux source checkout at the exact head above. A task-owned controller ran with Node 24.21.0 (`node <task-proof>/run.mjs`, exit 0) and launched the supported `pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --port <ephemeral>` entry point. State, agent credentials, workspace, and configuration were isolated through the documented `OPENCLAW_*` paths. It waited for `/readyz`, authenticated with the public `GatewayClient` SDK, then used the native `cron.add`/`cron.run`/`cron.runs` RPCs. The prompt plugin was loaded from an explicitly enabled local path; an SDK-based stdio MCP server advertised `lookup` and an excluded `delete` sibling. The OpenAI-compatible endpoint was local, with a nonsecret fixture key.

The plugin registered an earlier handler, a later ordinary handler that derived a hint from the event, and an authorized handler. All three independently recorded the same allowlist/deferred identifiers and frozen arrays. The provider received the derived hint before any tool call. Canned streaming responses then exercised the real `tool_search` -> `tool_describe` -> `dispatch_action` path; no catalog, hook, or tool execution was substituted.

Actual controller output (only local paths, random ports, and identity values omitted):

```text
SETUP isolated state, loaded prompt plugin, real stdio MCP server, deterministic local model
GATEWAY startup and fresh-chat admission ready through /readyz
GATEWAY authenticated public SDK client
RPC cron job: deferred, incoming=["read","proof__lookup"]
{"scenario":"deferred","status":"ok","toolsAllowPresent":true,"toolsAllow":["read","proof__lookup"],"deferredToolNames":["proof__lookup"],"frozen":{"toolsAllow":true,"deferredToolNames":true},"modelToolNames":["dispatch_action","read","tool_describe","tool_search"],"hintReachedProvider":true,"finalAuthorityToolNames":["dispatch_action","proof__lookup","read","tool_describe","tool_search"]}
PASS: CLI-launched Gateway cron admission -> loaded plugin -> embedded scope -> provider request -> Tool Search -> stdio MCP result
PASS: frozen snapshots, excluded non-allowlisted MCP tool, and 1 real stdio MCP call
LIMITATION: deterministic local model responses; no live-model discovery or production cron reliability claim
```

Independent receipts recorded four provider requests: search, describe, dispatch, then final text with `noteResultPresent: true`; the MCP server recorded exactly one `proof__lookup` execution. Gateway logs showed no hook or MCP failure in this successful run and confirmed an agent-database clean-close receipt and clean shutdown.

Earlier probe setup failures were corrected before this successful run: obsolete fixture configuration, missing explicit stdio child environment, and starting before full readiness. One-shot configuration/inspection CLI processes did not terminate promptly, so cron control used the public SDK against the CLI-launched Gateway instead; those CLI commands are not claimed as passing evidence. No production source changes were needed for this proof.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Exact local validation</summary>
