## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter OpenCode sessions must retain the selected native provider's request and replay semantics through proxy routing. This change restores Console Responses search aliases and dynamic-record arguments, preserves exact assistant-history identity on request-local copies, and carries native Go Pro/Flash thinking and exact bundled Qwen reasoning admission.

The latest correction reuses the native Go sanitizer for **Kimi K2.5, K2.6 and K2.7-code only**, after valid Go Chat offer selection. It removes the same four replay fields, unsupported reasoning blocks and effort fields, and preserves the native empty-message placeholder. K3 keeps its reasoning. Both stream hooks and native/unified proxy routes are covered; Console, other APIs, unknown identities and stale/foreign associations remain excluded. The original history is never mutated.

## Contract and Scope

Selected proxy credentials, URL, session and model association remain authoritative. No provider-secret fallback, native Go headers, first-event timers or broad reasoning heuristic is introduced. Catalog-ID restoration applies to the selected Console response/error object without replacing the original error. Existing transcript and retirement guards remain intact.

The sanitizer is a new **private** provider-stream-shared export. The exact public SDK comparison reports no public API changes; that does not mean no internal export was added.

## Current Test-Type Correction

Signed current candidate **322cfc608526dca6bf60cfef05210b231461c1db**, tree **945e83d1b8053cf933a2093dc2908b663900129a**, sole parent `dad3cce339d3173679979a1c92c1a5e3c2c92380`.

Original [dad3 CI 44835532625](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44835532625) found TS2698 in the replay negative-control fixture: its onPayload callback spread an unknown value. This test-only child rejects non-object, null and array inputs before preserving the ordinary payload fields and all injected controls. All original assertions remain. Production, SDK, UI, dependency and build inputs are unchanged.

- Exact owning agents-root test-types graph passes in **7.813 s**.
- All **44 replay cases pass**, **12.098 s wall / 10.04 s Vitest**; scoped type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Test-line ratchet passes at **1,809 net lines**, with unchanged 400 allowance + 1,410 allocation.
- Prepublication census of the original dad3 run: **37 success, 11 running, 22 skipped, one failure**, only the identified TS2698 job. Unfinished jobs are not treated as passes.
- No unchanged whole build, API comparison or baseline build was rerun. Fresh exact-head CI remains required.

## Frozen Reconciliation

Signed source parent **dad3cce339d3173679979a1c92c1a5e3c2c92380**, tree **c7df444caf3e6a8464d77b4b470b355c1b6a4369**, ordered parents:

1. K2 correction `37a30898330edff4195e30a893138302c8c6d35d`.
2. Frozen incoming base `a90c174919aca859d2145b2e6bede683ec87177a`.

All nine K2 files are byte-identical to the signed correction. Supported native reconciliation resolved two files: incoming Skills readiness is retained exactly, and chunk configuration adds only the neutral truncation and catalog-discovery mappings missing from the incoming groups. Incoming skills-shared/skills-page, catalog grid/card/skeleton, routed reader and startup isolation remain intact.

The incoming attachment visibility sampler, explicit empty-search readiness and intentional held-roster setup are preserved. Installed and browsed inventories remain distinct. The 1,000-row population, eight-card shelf, pagination, request/DOM identity, original 100 ms delay, deadlines, **28/31/56/61** asset ceilings and eager-reader/tooltip guards remain enforced. Benchmark preparation opens the installed shelf; the measured action is filtering only, not the superseded open-and-filter measurement.

## Retained dad3 Validation

The following executions bind the signed dad3 source parent. The current child changes only the replay test fixture, whose fresh type/runtime proof is above. These receipts are not relabeled as new-head executions.

- **110 provider/native/replay cases pass**, 39.881 s wall: actual native/proxy replay, K2 stripping, K3 preservation, both hooks, route and foreign-history boundaries. The original four failing proxy controls remain retained.
- **16 prefix-stability cases pass**, 10.564 s wall. Core and extension types pass in 8.544 s and 9.496 s.
- **10 chunk-boundary cases pass**, 2.339 s wall, including lazy reader/Markdown and Workshop isolation.
- **Four production route-asset cases pass**, 45.044 s wall / 43.04 s Vitest. Skills 3.764 s, skill-settings 3.312 s, plugins 3.691 s and plugin-settings 3.741 s. Real Chromium, emitted production assets, delayed delivery and held-reader release require this layer; fake clocks cannot establish these request counts.
- **Two original strict interaction cases pass locally**, 14.267 s wall, with temporary passive metadata observers subsequently restored. Escape closed the menu and returned trigger focus. The update observer was lost across navigation, so its ordering capture is incomplete. Neither local pass establishes the cause or inheritance of the hosted Linux failures.
- Exact public SDK comparison `a90 → dad3` passes in **102.202 s**, digest `ff7b090f43d2d90e4cd883d95840d6b752475a7a1769e295fb4cbb558a6ffb64`, no public API changes. Workflow, head and comparison inputs bind this candidate.
- Fresh hosted case timings remain pending. Prior head results are retained separately, not relabeled.

## Investigated Local Build Failure

**The retained dad3 full build failed**, exit 1 after **217.703 s**, without timeout or capture fault. The declaration gate measured **5,394,718 > 5,385,536 bytes**, an overage of **9,182 bytes**. Runtime, plugin and UI compilation completed; the full build is not green.

This total is five bytes above the prior composed graph total. No unmodified `a90` full build or new byte-identical-baseline attribution is claimed. The historical matched `b4` comparison remains historical. No declaration ceiling increase, public API removal or speculative provider/type change was made.

Global UI reports also retain their exact failures: largest CSS **58,500 > 58,315** gzip bytes; total CSS **345,436 > 337,312** gzip and **1,783,340 > 1,740,234** raw bytes; chat **21 > 20** requests and **1,334,208 > 1,332,637** normalized gzip bytes. New Session is within its current limit. Passing route-asset tests do not waive these separate reports.

The test-only child retains that source-bound failure without a repeated full build. Native preparation uses the documented investigated-local-failure record with `tests.result=fail`; hosted qualification and final admission remain required.

## Remaining Qualification and Risk

Original [c85 CI 44829694889](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44829694889), its UI failures, conflict closure and all prior source/build evidence remain retained. The two local interaction passes are not hosted-causality proof. The historical speech-discovery timeout and 768px portrait Workshop visible-title gap remain separate unresolved observations.

Fresh exact-head CI is pending. Actual shipping Worker/session/SQLite composition is separately coordinated against the published immutable pin; registered synthetic HTTP and local UI tests do not establish it. No old CI or downstream proof is transferred.

Final native/CI admission and coupled cleanup authority remain pending. Release-note context is recorded here; release-owned changelogs are unchanged. No live paid provider request, release or deployment was performed.

prs.title: fix: stop background exec completion wakes from landing mid-line
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A background exec's completion wake lands mid-line when the output is long. The wake embeds a fixed 2,000-char slice of the command output, and on a long run that slice starts where the bytes happened to be, so the woken turn cannot tell whether the last line is the command's result or just where the cut landed.

This PR makes the wake carry the last non-empty line of the output instead, but only when the retained tail was actually truncated. Output that fit in the tail keeps the full tail exactly as before.

How it works: when the session's total output exceeded the retained 2,000-char tail, the wake producer selects the last non-empty line of the tail, strips a leading `OK: ` or `ERR: ` marker when one is present, trims it through the same 2,000-char cap when it is longer, and falls back to the previous slice when there is no usable last line (empty output, structured tails). When the output fits, the content is the trimmed tail, byte-identical to the pre-change behavior. Header, duration, output-file pointer, routing and delivery are unchanged.

## Evidence

- 10 unit cases in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content.test.ts`: last line, trailing blank lines, `OK: ` / `ERR: ` markers, empty marker line, empty and whitespace fallback, JSON object/array tails.
- 2 wake-owner cases in the same file drive the real path (`appendOutput` + `maybeNotifyOnExit` -> `prepareExecExitWake`): a truncated oversized tail surfaces the stripped `OK: ` summary with the truncation header, and output that fits keeps every line of the tail.
- The existing wake tests in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` pin the header, the `with no output.` case, the bounded tail and the file pointer. Their fixtures end in a single line, so the selected line equals the old tail and those assertions hold unchanged.

Behavior proof (review host): `pnpm install`/build/test are not available on this host, so the proof runs the patched sources directly under Node 26 type-stripping through an ESM hooks loader (`node --import ./loader.mjs proof.ts`). The loader resolves the repo's `.js` specifiers to `.ts` sources and maps workspace packages to their `src`; the only shims are delivery plumbing the wake path does not exercise (logger, system-event queue, terminal-core pass-throughs, published `@openclaw/fs-safe`/`@openclaw/proc-safe` bindings, `chalk`/`tslog`/`semver`/`string-width`, and the parameter-property-only leaves `retry`, `runtime`, `env-substitution`, `plugin-instance-error`). Wakes are rendered through the real entry point (`maybeNotifyOnExit` -> `prepareExecExitWake`) with three synthetic fixtures:

```
=== (a) short multi-line output that fits the retained window (input 27 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-0, code 0, 0s):
line one
line two
last line

=== (b) oversized multi-line output truncated mid-line, last line is an OK: marker (input 2009 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-1, code 0, 0s), last 2000 of 2009 output chars (process log has the rest):
done

=== (c) structured multi-line JSON tail (input 2008 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-2, code 0, 0s), last 2000 of 2008 output chars (process log has the rest):
yyyy...yyy            (1,994 y's, abbreviated)
{
  "a": 1
}
```

(a) fits, so the full tail is kept, the pre-change content, unchanged. (b) is truncated mid-line and ends in an `OK: ` marker, so the wake carries just `done`. (c) is a structured tail whose last line is a JSON closing bracket, so the whole tail is kept.

Cut from upstream main `375daf6d3` (rebased after review). Verified against the main tip that no open PR or recent commit covers this.

One ask: the fork CI run needs a maintainer to approve it before hosted CI executes. Could a maintainer approve https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44219905140 ?

prs.title: fix(ui): keep the reader’s place while chat refreshes
prs.body:
Closes #202344

## What Problem This Solves

While chat history refreshes, measuring a row above the text being read can move the scroll offset before the displayed transcript moves with it. The reader briefly loses their place.

## User Impact

User impact: the displayed text stays aligned while a refresh holds the previous row window on screen. No configuration changes or migrations are required. The existing 1px regression limit is unchanged; no sleeps, retries, or wider tolerances were added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the displayed block's measured position aligned with the native scroll correction in the same turn, then reconcile its position through the existing renderer commit callback. The renderer owns the block reference; measurement and rendering reuse the same positioning operation.

## Evidence

Comparison: main base `d865e3d6cf55e10024e81b0f357108cc60c03fa8` versus this branch's prepared head `39afb9950949df1cb2e4aef652ab018a92be5a98`. Evidence below covers that comparison only. Managed publication rewrote commit metadata: published head `ad02e694165d9eeebeb1aaa12aba0685a6ffb8b8` has the identical source tree `55ca063e6a225ee6dbb682e78926f290ac1d4a39` as the prepared head. Its publication parent also has the identical tree as the tested main base.

- Main production plus the new regression, without the repair: `expected 22 to be less than or equal to 1`; 1 failed, 32 unselected.
- This head: all 33 geometry-update browser tests passed in Chromium. Another 18 geometry/resize-delivery tests and 14 direct reader tests passed.
- All 6 original `chat-snapshot-text-fidelity.e2e.test.ts` cases passed with this head, including the bundled production build. They also passed on base; this is not a claim that the natural intermittent E2E failure was reproduced locally.
- UI typecheck, focused six-file lint, Solid ownership guard, formatting, and diff checks passed. Manual pr-simplify completed.

The new regression delivers an actual DOM-measured predecessor height through `resizeItem` inside a held Solid action and checks both the pending frame and the settled window. This is deterministic browser-component proof, not natural ResizeObserver or live-Gateway reproduction.

### Review follow-up: runtime proof remains incomplete

The follow-up ran pr-simplify first and found no justified source simplification. It repeated the component negative control on the accepted base: **22 px** against the unchanged **1 px** limit. With the candidate restored, all **47 touched browser cases**, the **6 original snapshot E2E cases using a production bundle**, UI typecheck, focused lint, Solid ownership guard, formatting, and diff checks passed. The source tree still matches the published head.

A separate built-product investigation used synthetic 160-message history, real snapshot persistence/reload, native wheel input, and history accepted through the production session-subscription protocol. Separately built baseline/candidate chat-chunk hashes were verified. At wheel distances 240/600/900/1600, maximum recorded displacement was **0.4375/0.390625/0.390625/0.390625 px on baseline** and **0.4375/0.265625/0.390625/0.390625 px on the candidate**. Natural predecessor measurements occurred, but neither version reproduced the overlap between a held Solid frame and native correction. Snapshot flushing was setup-only; no layout owner was invoked and no DOM geometry or measurement result was injected.

**The requested changed-path product demonstration is therefore still missing.** Those passing-on-both-sides probes and diagnostic screenshots are not presented as proof of the fix, and no redundant E2E was added. WebKit remains unqualified in this sandbox: required native dependencies are unavailable through its system-library validation path, and task-local libraries do not satisfy its system-cache-only dlopen check. No validation bypass was used. A qualified WebKit environment and a reproducible real product trigger for the held-frame overlap are still needed. Independent automated review previously did not execute because of a reviewer configuration error.

### WebKit follow-up: main vs PR

Results supplied by @daniel-lxs from a local **macOS arm64** run with **Playwright 1.64.1, WebKit 27.2, and Vitest 5.0.5**; not independently rerun by RoboClaw. Comparison: main `f3992db5` versus PR head `ad02e69`.

- **Focused browser regression** — `keeps the displayed reader still when a predecessor is measured during a pending refresh` in `chat-transcript-geometry-updates.browser.test.tsx`: main jumps **22 px** (`retainedTopPx: 23` versus baseline `1`) and fails the unchanged **1 px** limit. The PR moves **0 px** (`retainedTopPx: 1` in both pending and settled states) and passes.
- **Bundled Control UI E2E** — all **6** `chat-snapshot-text-fidelity` cases pass on both main and the PR, using a mock Gateway.
- **Shared WebKit failure** — `retains the accepted history-header space while a touch holds the older row model` fails on both with **`Illegal constructor`** because synthetic `Touch` is unsupported there; this is not introduced by the PR.

This supplies the WebKit browser-component red/green evidence missing from the earlier sandbox run; the bundled E2E results establish parity, not reproduction of the natural intermittent failure. **Not tested: a live Gateway or manual Safari.**

Thanks to @daniel-lxs for the investigation, supplied fix, and regression test.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @daniel-lxs](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_7rsa4x)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/264c394e-f16c-4e2b-a6eb-f210ac8a2d07)
- [Runtime proof follow-up](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f538636b-3260-4ccb-9ae9-ca5af4d09d9a)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: refactor: share sandbox skills filesystem worker custody
prs.body:
Related: #197510

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway stall refactor moved sandbox skill copying and mount preparation to the same worker, but left two implementations of the host authority relay, native-work settlement and error handling. This makes changes to the worker boundary harder to review and easier to apply to only one path.

## User Impact

No user-visible change, migration, or configuration change. Sandbox skill files and mount sources still use the worker; the Gateway still owns live mutation authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one private worker dispatch and native settlement path for skill sync, mount planning and mount-source creation. Keep their successful results distinct, preserve the original host refusal and sync-specific filesystem error details, and leave the sync queue and filesystem kernels untouched. Production delta: +73/−119 (net −46); no tests removed or changed.

## Evidence

103 focused tests passed on both baseline and candidate. These exercise actual worker custody refusal for mount-source creation and skill sync, FIFO wait attribution, copy reuse and recovery, protected mounts, and native filesystem error reporting across worker reuse. Core typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. This is a consolidation, not a new latency claim.

[ClawSweeper’s independent review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202771#issuecomment-7052966002) covered head `a56b916b4972` against main `9a0efcd60b9d` and reported no actionable findings. Local autoreview could not start under its temporary-directory isolation check.

[Exact-head CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44833307941) passed the scoped Node checks, type/lint checks and `security-fast`; the required CI gate is red because the [Plugins first-visit asset budget test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44833307941/job/136624233077) completed 57 assets against a limit of 56. The same assertion failed with 57/56 when replayed on both this head and the untouched PR base `d5a99b07e88e3`. That browser test uses a mock Gateway and does not invoke the changed worker. No UI thresholds or CI rules were changed.

**Contributor:** @steipete requested this follow-up.

prs.title: improve: draft a Template from a description, not only from the current agent
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Someone asked an agent to "create a new template using the heygen plugin that has an automation where each morning at 3am in the users timezone we look at the PRs merged on a given repo, that we ask for from the user, and create a short video explaining what got merged." The agent loaded the bundled `create-template` skill, decided it did not apply, and spent about thirteen minutes hand-building a package elsewhere instead of producing a draft and a review card in chat.

The skill only described sharing the current agent. It told the agent to use its own role, to take dependencies only from the inventory's ClawHub refs, to choose routines only from automations that already exist on the agent, and to copy the agent's avatar. A Template that is described rather than copied fits none of those.

## User Impact

User impact: asking an agent to make a new Template from a description now gets the same quick private draft and review card as asking it to share itself. Sharing the current agent works as before. Nothing is published unless the person chooses Publish.

## Why This Change Was Made

The skill now names both kinds of request and sends both through the same four steps. For a described Template it says where the content comes from instead:

- The role, scope, instructions and automations are written from the description, and an automation does not have to exist on this agent.
- This agent's avatar, routines, and any skill or plugin the person did not name stay out.
- A named plugin or skill may be declared when the inventory has no ref for it, but only with an exact published release the agent looked up, for example with `plugins(action="search")`. If it cannot find one, it says so and leaves the dependency out. The inventory reports a plugin installed from a local file as not portable even when the same plugin is published, which is what blocked the request above.
- Things only the new owner knows, such as a repository or their time zone, are asked on first run by a package `BOOTSTRAP.md`. The automation is declared disabled with a UTC placeholder, and the first-run script sets the time zone on that declared job and enables it once the owner agrees. This matches the existing guidance in `docs/cli/templates.md` for disabled automations and first-run instructions.

The skill's `description` now covers both requests. The "Create with an agent" docs section describes the second case. `inventory.mjs`, the sidebar draft prompt and the existing tests are unchanged: the sidebar action is still a request to share that agent, and the inventory is still the right first step for both cases because it starts the draft.

No test was added. The failure was a model's reading of instruction text, and a test that asserted on the wording would pass whether or not an agent follows it.

## Evidence

**Skill text, before and after.** The sentences that turned the request away, and what replaced them:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `description: Turn this agent into a shareable Template for a person to review.` | `description: Draft a shareable Template for a person to review, either from this agent or from their description of a new one (a role, plugins, automations).` |
| "Use the agent's role and working instructions already in context. … If there's no single coherent role, ask which one to share." | The same, introduced by "To share this agent", plus: "For a described Template, write the role, scope, instructions and automations from the description. Its automations are new and need not exist on this agent." |
| "Choose routines only from the active automations in this inventory." | "When sharing this agent, choose routines only from the active automations in this inventory." |
| "Use the inventory's exact ClawHub ref and version." with no path for a published plugin the inventory counts as not portable | Unchanged for the inventory's refs, plus the lookup described above and "If you can't find an exact published release, say so and leave it out instead of guessing a ref or version." |
| "`avatar` is the inventory's `avatar` value, copied unchanged … omit the field when the inventory has none." | "… omit the field when the inventory has none or the Template is not based on this agent." |

**Model check with the quoted request.** This is a paper exercise with a real model, not a run of the product. The same prompt was given to a model through a read-only, ephemeral Codex CLI session, once with the old `SKILL.md` and once with the new one. The prompt contained the request above, a fixture inventory result for an agent with an avatar, no automations and one plugin counted as not portable, and a fixture `plugins` search result naming `openclaw-plugin-heygen` 0.1.0 (the live search returns the same package and version). The model was asked what it would do and what it would write to the draft.

| Skill text | Runs | Says the skill covers the request | Writes a proposal | Opens the review card |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| After | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |

With the old text both runs ran the inventory and then stopped, quoting "Choose routines only from the active automations in this inventory" and "Use the inventory's exact ClawHub ref and version", and replied along the lines of "This skill packages an existing agent for private review. It doesn't cover creating the requested automation from scratch." That is the reported behaviour.

With the new text each run wrote one proposal. Each of the three proposals was then run through the real draft review builder (`prepareTemplateDraft` in `src/templates/draft.ts`) in a throwaway workspace, and each built an archive with these review items:

```text
file        BOOTSTRAP.md
plugin      openclaw-plugin-heygen   clawhub · 0.1.0
automation  Daily merged PR video    0 3 * * * · UTC · Disabled
archive     BOOTSTRAP.md, CLAW.md, package.json   (no avatar)
```

Two further prompts checked the edges of the change with the new text. When the plugin search returned nothing, both runs told the person they could not find a published release and left the plugin out of the draft. For the request "Create a new template from this agent" on an agent with a ClawHub plugin, a weekday routine and a personal reminder, the old text (1 run) and the new text (3 runs) produced the same shape: avatar kept, the inventory's ref and version, the weekday routine with its original schedule and time zone, the personal reminder left out, no extra files.

The builder caught two problems in earlier wording, both fixed in this head: proposals that mapped `BOOTSTRAP.md` under `workspace.bootstrapFiles` were rejected, and the first-run guidance leaked into the shared-agent case and disabled its routine.

**Local checks on this head.** `pnpm check:changed` (docs lane), `pnpm check:docs`, and the two existing tests that touch this skill (`src/skills/loading/workspace-skill-snapshot.test.ts` for discovery, `test/scripts/create-template-inventory.test.ts` for the inventory) pass.

**Not verified.** The change was not run end to end on a live Gateway with a real agent: no chat turn executed the inventory command or wrote a draft, no review card was rendered in the Control UI, and the resulting Template was not added or published. The model check used one model with small run counts, so it shows the direction of the change and not a rate.

prs.title: fix: keep live state reads free of repeated filesystem checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Live state reads started resolving filesystem identities synchronously after #202608. The unchanged MCP mutation custody tests now see 8 and 4 host identity reads where they require zero, blocking main CI.

## User Impact

Admitted Gateway readers again avoid synchronous owner identity and sidecar reads. Read-only inspection still avoids copying the live database; CLI/offline readers without local custody retain their existing persisted-owner verification.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read admission already publishes exact path custody in the process owner's existing `readOwnerPaths`. The common live-owner verifier now consumes that fact. Owner loss, release and maintenance already clear it. There is no new cache, schema, configuration or worker message. Six added production lines preserve the separately necessary offline verifier.

Related: #202608 and #202715. The latter moves the repeated metadata check into a worker; this repair removes that repeated check for admitted local owners and also covers artifact-preserving selection. There is no changed-file overlap.

## Evidence

The two unchanged MCP custody cases reproduce 8/4 identity reads on base `0f236526a9f319b811c216c2256379c408f169f0` and pass at zero with this fix. The extended existing owner test fails on baseline (2 identity reads), passes for three consecutive admitted checks with zero identity/owner-file reads, and verifies that release revokes the fact. The original #202608 no-copy and offline-preservation tests remain unchanged and pass. Five focused owner/diagnostic/state files pass 94 cases; the two MCP custody cases also pass. Focused wrapper wall time: 56.52 s plus 9.43 s for MCP.

The existing committed owner benchmark now supports `--live-owner`. Five serial A/A/B triplets, 4,000 checks per sample, separate CPU/timing and allocation passes; synthetic 35 GiB sparse identity-only file, 5,000 session paths and 62,000 workspace files (~1.1 GB logical). This measures the owner boundary on APFS, not SQLite content throughput, whole-Gateway latency or btrfs behavior. Real SQLite reads/no-copy behavior are covered by the tests above. Acceptance: zero synchronous identity reads, preserved no-copy behavior, improvement beyond A/A variation.

| Median (p95), n=5 each | Baseline A1 | Baseline A2 | Fixed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Identity reads/check | 2 (2) | 2 (2) | 0 (0) |
| Main CPU µs/check | 51.398 (52.703) | 53.102 (54.952) | 0.749 (0.764) |
| Wall ms/4,000 checks | 206.023 (211.522) | 212.767 (220.354) | 3.404 (3.463) |
| Sampled V8 bytes/check | 13,939 (14,112) | 14,039 (14,192) | 1,278 (1,313) |

Run with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/state-owner-identity-measure.mjs --live-owner --iterations 4000`; `--source-dir` selects exact baseline source. CPU improvement is 98.5% versus 3.3% A/A median variation; sampled allocation falls 90.8%. Production +6 LOC, tests +19, benchmark +27, docs +3. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. No Control UI production imports are affected.

Release-note context: eliminate repeated synchronous live-owner filesystem checks while retaining direct read-only inspection and offline safety.

`pnpm check:changed` completed; all selected gates pass after a targeted benchmark lint repair except two inherited unused Skills exports (`createSkillPageReads`, `createSkillPageRoute`). Both reproduce in the clean exact baseline `0f236526a9f319b811c216c2256379c408f169f0` and were introduced by `1ee9f29e6668e` / #202581. They are a main regression for the Skills owner, not waived noise. The full-tree and production Knip scans both report the same pair. No Skills source or budget is changed here.

## Final CI qualification

Exact-head [CI run 44830705577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44830705577) completed with 50 successful jobs, 28 skipped, and the UI route-budget job plus its aggregate failed. Security checks passed. All three route-asset failures reproduce unchanged on exact main parent ed2f2afbbbdd1df13270913b2e8fa03afe660568. Skills 30>28 and skill-settings 33>31 were introduced by #202581 / 1ee9f29e6668e32ecfade57a540d10326ad3b8de (preceding Settings graph #202531). Plugins 58>56 was introduced by #202726 / 528df02f222738badc13cf2a9c51b7533bbdeee4: reversing only that UI change on the exact parent makes the unchanged Plugins budget test pass (70.84s). These are separate main regressions, not green CI. #202694 has since landed the Skills budget repair.

The CI checkout was merge `8c096047e6c36dde8deab3c455b6781baa9d4105`, whose ordered parents are the baseline above and reviewed head `dd4a2dc275c9c10d557617e46debc1b6e44c71ab`. Its only changes from that parent are this PR’s four files; UI source and test inputs are unchanged. Linux reproduction verified all 66,290 tracked baseline blobs and matched CI’s emitted assets. The Plugins causal control verified all 11 reversed files and the unchanged budget test. No UI fixes or budget changes are included here.

prs.title: fix: keep installed plugins in the Featured list instead of hiding them
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People browsing plugins in the Control UI see a different Featured list depending on what they already have installed. An installed plugin disappears from the Featured shelf and from Featured → View all, and the next plugin moves into its place, so the curated lineup looks shorter or reordered.

## User Impact

User impact: Featured shows ClawHub's curated lineup, in its curated order, for everyone. A plugin that is already on the Gateway stays in place and shows **Installed** instead of an **Install** button, including when it is installed but disabled. Trending, category shelves, search and install eligibility are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two Control UI filters removed installed plugins: one before the Featured shelf was capped at eight cards, and one in Featured → View all. The Gateway already returned those entries with their local state, so this removes the two filters for Featured only and adds a visible label to the existing status indicator. The status dot, tooltip and accessible label still say whether the plugin is enabled or disabled.

## Evidence

### Clean comparison

**Before**

Featured shelf on the Plugins page, where the first curated plugin (Memory Plus) is installed but disabled. Before is `main` at `5458e9614f17`; after is this change at `41a49a618071`. Both were captured from the bundled Control UI in Chromium at the same viewport and theme against a mocked Gateway, so the plugin names are test fixtures.

What was checked:

- The Featured shelf and Featured → View all keep ClawHub's order whether or not a plugin is installed, and an installed plugin shows Installed rather than Install.
- Installing a plugin from Featured leaves its card in View all, and it is still there after a page reload, with exactly one install request sent.

prs.title: feat: show Gateway resource profiles and live worker memory
prs.body:
Closes #202375. Foundation for #202373.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators investigating Gateway memory use cannot see one resource-profile decision or the live workers and policies behind it. The upcoming small-machine changes also need one shared profile decision instead of separate per-pool settings.

## User Impact

User impact: `gateway.resources.profile` now accepts `auto` (default), `standard`, or `lean`. `openclaw status` (text and JSON) and `diagnostics.lanes` report the selected profile, selection reason, effective memory limit, CPUs, and a live worker census with floor, cap, idle policy, and sampled heap use.

**This PR does not reduce memory consumption or change pool behavior.** Standard and lean still behave identically. Follow-ups #202376, #202377, and #202378 consume the profile. Restart the Gateway after changing it.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single startup owner resolves default `auto` to lean iff effective memory is **strictly below 8 GiB**. Exactly 8 GiB or more selects standard. Effective memory is the minimum of host RAM and visible cgroup-v2 `memory.max` limits; cgroup v1 limits are not detected and fall back to host RAM. Explicit choices win. CPU count is reported but never selects the profile. This memory-only rule ships enabled by default.

The census projects the existing native-worker registry and cached heap samples; it does not introduce another registry, sampler, timer, or worker. Task-pool policies come from their existing owners. Direct workers without pool metadata report unknown policy, not invented limits; missing/stale heap samples remain unknown. Counts cover directly registered native workers, including pending retirement, not every logical role or nested isolate.

## Evidence

Real Gateway proof used a Mac Studio Crabbox **local-container** lease, Linux ARM64 / Node **24.22.1**, with the pushed runtime commit `8f3fb6a400596db2f66b88f634f32e7dc194f5b1`. This is historical runtime evidence: later commits fix documentation/integration and commit `f110ba8d49c10acaf83fcc1f7c6b806f997e0f0d` changed auto selection to the requested strict 8 GiB memory-only rule. Census behavior is unchanged.

| Actual container limit | Configured | Reported profile / reason | Status census |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.5 GiB, 8 CPUs | auto | lean / memory | 9 live workers, 9 sampled |
| 4 GiB, 8 CPUs | auto | standard / capacity **on the old rule only** | 14 live workers, 14 sampled |
| 4 GiB, 8 CPUs | lean | lean / explicit | 14 live workers, 14 sampled |

All three cases passed assertions through **status text, status JSON, and the diagnostics RPC**, including exact cgroup limits, CPU count, census totals, and nonzero heap coverage. The 1.5 GiB observer ran outside the Gateway cgroup over a forwarded port. Its diagnostics request later saw 8 workers after idle retirement, with all 8 sampled, rather than retaining a stale count.

Example status output:

```text
Resources: lean (auto: memory) · 1536 MiB cgroup-v2 · 8 CPUs · 9 direct workers
logger-file.worker.js: 1 writer · floor 0 · cap 1 (point reads 2) · idle timeout
openclaw-state-read.worker.js: 1 other · floor 0 · cap 2 (point reads 3) · idle timeout
```

**Observed limitation:** a second full CLI process inside the 1.5 GiB container OOM-killed the Gateway running today's unchanged pool behavior. Moving the observer outside that cgroup allowed the requested profile/census proof without tuning Gateway heaps or pools. This illustrates why #202376/#202377 matter; this PR does not fix that OOM or claim a 1.5 GiB workload budget.

**Pre-rebase CI (historical):** `f110ba8d49c10acaf83fcc1f7c6b806f997e0f0d` has successful `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses as of 2026-11-20 16:10 UTC ([gate run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44769411799)). No failed checks remain; an earlier PR-context run was cancelled. The completed hosted review covers the previous `e57f84aa3843` policy; requesting reassessment of the substantive 8 GiB memory-only change, with the live-proof limitation below preserved.

**Latest conflict resolution:** published `00102c7539514972be68e7d1aa75d31e10bcd5df`, rebased onto main `8253356c986427d888cbe24b2c3d6f3b702a2f79`. The sole conflict was the generated configuration-baseline hash; resolved at both replay steps with `pnpm config:docs:gen`. Range-diff confirms unchanged feature patches; only generated hashes changed. On this candidate, **116 focused tests**, `config:docs:check`, and `git diff --check` pass. Exact-head CI is complete: the inventory shard passes. The only failing job is the inherited UI asset-budget failure documented below, plus its aggregate gate. The completed `f110ba8d49c1` source review remains applicable to this mechanical rebase; no redundant hosted review requested. The previously disclosed live-proof limitation remains unchanged.

**Current rule and proof coverage:** at 4 GiB auto now resolves to **lean / memory**; at exactly 8 GiB it resolves to **standard / capacity**, including on one CPU. Current-head focused tests cover these boundaries, a 16 GiB host constrained to 4 GiB, explicit overrides, and cgroup-v1 host-RAM fallback. **116 tests passed**, plus production typecheck, targeted lint/format, and `config:docs:check`. Isolated Astra review was collected; its stale Gateway-index wording finding was corrected before commit. The Studio lease has already been deleted and no task-owned built image remains, so rerunning 4/8 GiB requires fresh allocation/install/build rather than a cheap status-only rerun. No current-head 4/8 GiB Studio execution is claimed; the historical table above is not proof of the new threshold.

### Inherited CI failure accepted for landing

On head `00102c7539514972be68e7d1aa75d31e10bcd5df`, [checks-ui-e2e (2/4)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44818537411/job/136573964859) fails the Skills and Skill Settings first-visit asset limits (30 > 28 and 33 > 31); `openclaw/ci-gate` is downstream. #202581 introduced dedicated Skills pages and the additional requests. The [upstream baseline failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44812417546/job/136553156130) has the same affected limits; #202694 repaired the asset grouping and merged at 2026-11-20 22:43 UTC. The UI tree and benchmark entry points are unchanged between this run's baseline `f6298a194416e113d20bdad9a3d78498507cc2a0` and tested merge `d29ce1e45b981383911231b0d191a5a9943faba4`. Exact-base main CI skipped UI E2E; no matching baseline execution is claimed here.

Josh explicitly authorized landing despite this inherited failure, without rebasing onto the repair. CI remains failed, not relabeled green. The current-rule live-proof limitation above remains disclosed.

### Review and CI follow-up

At `7c19a0c7048086e283a90bd4e3db4c2b89830f5c`, both verified ClawSweeper findings are fixed:

prs.title: fix(codex): keep the installed app-server after a cancelled startup
prs.body:
Related: #201130

## What Problem This Solves

A caller can cancel while the managed Codex app-server is starting. When startup reports that cancellation as an `AbortError`, including as the cause of a diagnostic error with stderr, the gateway can mark the installed binary as failed and use the bundled binary for subsequent requests until restart.

## User Impact

A cancelled acquisition returns its error to the caller and leaves the installed app-server available to later requests. Genuine spawn, initialization, compatibility, and timeout failures still use the existing fallback path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed fallback decision now checks for cancellation before publishing fallback ownership or rejecting the installed binary. The change uses the existing cleanup and request-currentness checks. It requires no configuration or migration.

## Evidence

- The startup regression failed before the fix. The new cases exercise cancellation during initialization and a spawn error with cancellation in its cause.
- On this PR head, all 192 shared-client and managed-binary tests passed. The Codex package-boundary compile, formatting, and lint passed.

### Real app-server startup cancellation

Linux, PR head `edb5d705162d`, installed Codex CLI `0.170.0`, bundled Codex CLI `0.169.0`. A credential-free probe called the production managed acquisition with the shipped stdio launcher. It confirmed the real installed native app-server was running, then injected a one-shot owner `AbortError` through the startup currentness callback at the post-spawn registration boundary. The acquisition signal stayed live. The production client wrapped the abort with stderr emitted by the real app-server. The probe checked that both launcher and native child exited before opening a new acquisition, then compared the new client's launcher and native executable identity with the installed selection and checked its initialize response.

Redacted probe output:

```text
installedVersion=0.170.0 bundledVersion=0.169.0
actualNativeAppServerObserved=true acquisitionSignalAborted=false
firstOutcome=rejected stderrWrappedAbortError=true
launcherReaped=true nativeProcessReaped=true
nextHandshakeVersion=0.170.0 nextUsesSameInstalledBinary=true nextUsesBundledBinary=false
```

The same probe on the parent commit `7ce2d10eced` reproduced the regression. Both cancelled processes exited, then the original acquisition switched to bundled `0.169.0`, and the next acquisition in the same OpenClaw process also initialized bundled `0.169.0`.

```text
actualNativeAppServerObserved=true launcherReaped=true nativeProcessReaped=true
firstOutcome=acquired firstVersion=0.169.0 firstUsingBundled=true
nextHandshakeVersion=0.169.0 nextUsesSameInstalledBinary=false nextUsesBundledBinary=true
```

prs.title: feat(compaction): make the safeguard summary reserve ceiling configurable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #201397. Safeguard compaction caps the reserve of its summary requests at 20,000 tokens, so an ordinary summary gets at most 16,000 output tokens (80% of the reserve), even when `compaction.reserveTokens` is larger. A reasoning summary model can spend that whole allowance on thinking and return no visible text (`summary output budget (16000 tokens) was exhausted without visible text`), and the long session then cannot be compacted. Operators had no supported way to raise the allowance: the remedies were turning summary thinking off, switching the compaction model, or patching the installed package.

## Change

Following the review of the first revision, this keeps the default ceiling and adds an explicit opt-in control instead of removing the cap:

- New `agents.defaults.compaction.maxSummaryReserveTokens` (integer, minimum 1000, default 20000) and the per-agent `agents.entries.<id>.compaction.maxSummaryReserveTokens`, resolved like `maxSummaryChars` (agent entry first, then defaults) and carried in the session's compaction settings to the safeguard.
- `resolveSummaryReserveTokens` uses the configured ceiling. The compaction reserve and the summary model's `maxTokens` still bound the request, so the key can raise or lower the allowance but never exceed either limit.
- Omitting the key keeps today's behavior: sessions that raised `reserveTokens` only for input headroom get no larger summary allowance unless they opt in.
- Schema, help text, labels, the config reference and the compaction troubleshooting paragraph are updated; the config doc baseline is regenerated.

Accepted edge case: a value written directly into a per-agent settings file bypasses schema validation, as `maxSummaryChars` does; a nonsensical value there produces a visible, recoverable compaction failure.

## Evidence

Tests (passing locally):

- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts`: the summary request follows a configured ceiling (raised to 65,536; lowered to 8,000), stays under the compaction reserve (30,000) and under the model output limit (128,000). The existing case that expects 20,000 without configuration is unchanged. Dropping the ceiling argument at the safeguard call site makes all four new cases fail with `expected 20000`.
- `src/agents/agent-settings.test.ts`: the global and per-agent values reach `getCompactionSettings()`; omitting both adds nothing.
- `src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults.test.ts`: both scopes accept 1,000 / 20,000 / 65,536 and reject 0, 999 and 20,000.5.
- Also run: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, `git diff --check`, `config:docs:check`, `config:schema:check`, `config:channels:check`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (+67 lines).

Live behavior on the 2026.11.5 release build with the equivalent change. One long-lived channel session in safeguard mode with `reserveTokens: 65536`; a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash quantization (model `maxTokens` 256,000); summary thinking `ultra`. Between the two runs the only change was the safeguard ceiling literal, raised locally from 20,000 to 65,536, which is what `maxSummaryReserveTokens: 65536` configures in this PR:

```text
ceiling 20,000 (summary allowance 16,000)
  manual sessions.compact -> [compaction-safeguard] Compaction summarization failed; cancelling compaction to preserve history.
                             [compaction-diag] end trigger=manual outcome=failed reason=guard_blocked durationMs=583759

ceiling 65,536 (summary allowance 52,428), same session 17 minutes later, after a restart
  manual sessions.compact -> ok after 718796 ms
  persisted compaction entry: tokensBefore 86300, tokensAfter 11166, summary 16000 chars
```

Under the 20,000 ceiling the same install and model also logged the explicit cause on an automatic attempt: `Summarization failed for 1003 messages: Summarization failed: summary output budget (16000 tokens) was exhausted without visible text ... (model maxTokens: 256000)`. Other long sessions on the install failed the same way until the change.

Not covered: #178805 reports an allowance already below this ceiling (6,553 tokens from a smaller reserve); this key does not change that path.

## Why

A documented, explicit setting replaces a hidden literal while keeping the default cost bound introduced in #119447. Deployments that need room for reasoning summaries opt in globally or per agent.

prs.title: fix: report OpenRouter spending caps as billing failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenRouter returns HTTP 403 when an organization or workspace spending budget is exhausted. OpenClaw currently labels several documented budget responses as authentication failures and tells the operator to sign in again, which cannot resolve the spending cap.

## User Impact

OpenRouter spending-budget failures are identified as billing problems instead of failed sign-ins. Existing fallback behavior remains intact; ordinary permission refusals, authentication failures, rate limits, and timeouts keep their existing handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenRouter plugin recognizes the documented `limit_source` values and narrowly identified budget messages before the generic HTTP 403 classification. This stays within the existing provider hook: no core classification policy, retry contract, configuration, or new failure reason is introduced. Provider documentation explains the reset/admin remedy, including lifetime budgets.

References: [OpenRouter budget errors](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/errors-and-debugging#budget-errors), [budget limits](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/limits#handling-403-budget-errors), and [workspace budgets](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/workspaces/workspace-budgets).

## Evidence

- The included provider regression fails on the unchanged implementation and passes with this fix. The focused provider suite and two provider-precedence/structured-signal consumer suites pass: **32 tests**. The provider test file took **4.94 seconds wall time** on its final run; hosted CI timing is pending.
- A real local HTTP 403 fixture through the production embedded agent and model-fallback runner changed from `auth` plus sign-in guidance on the base to `billing` on the fix. The raw provider message retained its administrator/reset guidance. Both versions sent exactly one primary request and one fallback request. A second patched case with neutral message text proved that the structured budget metadata reaches the classifier through the real transport.
- A separately launched, built, isolated Gateway completed `chat.send → agent.wait → chat.history` against the local HTTP fixture. Its persisted fallback notice says `billing`, the fallback answer is present, and the fixture observed exactly two inference requests. No paid provider calls or existing Gateway state were used.
- `pnpm build:runtime`, extension production and test typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, documentation links (0 broken), and `git diff --check` passed. The runtime build emitted Control UI asset-budget warnings outside these changed files; this is not a claim that the separate asset-budget gate is green. Full package/declaration and hosted CI checks remain separate.
- Simplification kept one provider-owned decision, reused existing JSON/coercion helpers, and added no state or framework: **+22 net production lines, +53 net test lines**, plus documentation.
- Local Auto Review was attempted against base `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea` and the complete three-file working-tree candidate. It failed without a report because its handoff response file was missing. No clean-review claim or retry is made; hosted review remains required.

The transport/Gateway fixtures are temporary acceptance harnesses rather than committed additional runtime suites. Real OpenRouter budget exhaustion was not induced; the error envelopes come from its current public contract. This fix does not claim attribution to a particular historical support incident.

<details>
<summary>Retained before/after terminal evidence</summary>

### Inspectable retained terminal evidence

These excerpts were extracted from the original local proof logs, not regenerated model runs. ANSI color escapes were removed. HTTP records below are literal JSON output lines; the Gateway block is an explicitly selected-field projection of its larger recorded JSON line, omitting synthetic session identifiers and unrelated transcript metadata.

Sign in again under Models in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw configure`.","rawError":"403 Org member budget limit exceeded (weekly limit). Contact your org admin. $52.00 of $50.00 used; resets 2026-10-12T00:00:00.000Z.","reason":"auth","status":403,"code":"403","provider":"openrouter","model":"openrouter/budget-fixture"}],"result":[{"text":"Fallback answered","replyToTag":false}]}

**Fixed** — tested provider files byte-match published head `19b37e70e02acd2a2834552a9b5cc16c43c0f034`; same HTTP scenario (original log line 8):

Contact your org admin. $52.00 of $50.00 used; resets 2026-10-12T00:00:00.000Z.","reason":"billing","status":403,"code":"403","provider":"openrouter","model":"openrouter/budget-fixture"}],"result":[{"text":"Fallback answered","replyToTag":false}]}

prs.title: fix(onboard): stop pointing Funnel runs at token auth
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw onboard --non-interactive --tailscale funnel` fails and tells the operator to rerun with `--gateway-auth token`. Following that advice fails the same way, because Funnel always switches the Gateway to password auth.

## User Impact

User impact: the Funnel rejection now names the password requirement instead of pointing at token auth, so the printed next step actually works.

## Why This Change Was Made

`applyNonInteractiveGatewayConfig` forces `authMode = "password"` whenever `tailscaleMode === "funnel"` (`src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.ts:80-89`), then rejects with `"Missing --gateway-password for password auth. Pass --gateway-password or use --gateway-auth token."` (`:145-148`). For a Funnel run that second sentence is unreachable advice. The rejection is now Funnel-aware and points at `--gateway-password` / `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD`.

Scope note: this changes the rejection text only. Funnel winning over an explicit token request is existing, tested behaviour (`keeps password auth when a token-only rerun targets an existing Funnel`), so this PR does not turn that override into an error. The other half of #201385 — the token being dropped without any notice — is left for a maintainer call, since any notice has to stay compatible with the one-JSON-object-per-run promise of `--json`.

## Evidence

New case in `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.test.ts` drives the real `applyNonInteractiveGatewayConfig` with an existing token-auth config plus `tailscale: "funnel"`, and asserts the rejection names the password requirement and no longer suggests `--gateway-auth token`.

Base (production change stashed, test present) — `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-projects.mts src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.test.ts`:

```
× points Funnel runs at the password instead of token auth
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ StringContaining{…} ]
Tests  1 failed | 28 passed (29)
```

With the fix:

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  29 passed (29)
```

Neighbouring suites: `src/commands/onboard.test.ts` 66 passed (the non-Funnel rejection string it asserts is unchanged); oxlint 0 warnings, 0 errors on both changed files.

**Real shipped CLI run (isolated state).** Built the branch (`pnpm build`) and ran the real CLI with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`HOME` pointed at an empty temp dir, so the run hits the Funnel rejection before any Gateway/Tailscale contact (no network, no live Tailscale needed).

Base — the upstream checkout's pre-fix CLI build:

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp>/state-base OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<tmp>/state-base/openclaw.json \
    node dist/index.js onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --tailscale funnel
Missing --gateway-password for password auth. Pass --gateway-password or use --gateway-auth token.
EXIT: 1
```

This PR's head — same command, branch build:

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<tmp>/state/openclaw.json \
    node dist/index.js onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --tailscale funnel
Missing --gateway-password for password auth. Tailscale Funnel requires password auth, so --gateway-auth token does not apply; pass --gateway-password or set OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD.
EXIT: 1
```

No IPs, keys, phone numbers, or endpoints appear (the rejection is produced before any Tailscale/network call); the only other line was a local log-file warning from the empty temp state, unrelated to the message.

## AI Assistance

Written with AI assistance (DeepSeek Harness agent); the reproduction, tests, and command output above were run on this machine.

---

机制对位: 症状输出在 `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.ts:145-148`，我在同一处 `:145-155` 改，因为 `:80-89` 已把 funnel 的 authMode 强制成 password，旧文案仍在推荐 `--gateway-auth token`
复现: 新用例在 base 上 1 failed（断言 error 含 "Tailscale Funnel requires password auth"），修复后 29 passed
证据类别: 非交互 onboard 的 auth 解析（纯函数 + 已有测试桩），本机可得: 是
契约核对: `--tailscale funnel` 的密码要求由 `gateway-config.ts:80-89` 拥有；`--json` 单对象承诺由 `src/commands/onboard-options.ts:19-26` 的 `rejectOnboardingOption` 拥有 ⇒ 只改文案、不加 stderr 通知

prs.title: fix: let shared sessions recover after a storage worker crash without a Gateway restart
prs.body:
Fixes #202366 (supersedes the guidance-only approach in #202396 if accepted)
Related: #202373

## What Problem This Solves

If the session storage worker dies in the middle of a write that changes who can access a shared session, OpenClaw can't tell whether that write landed. Today it then refuses every new `chat.send` to that session until the Gateway restarts, and the error tells the user to "retry after session storage is ready", which never works.

## User Impact

User impact: after a storage worker crash, the next chat to the affected session works again without a Gateway restart. This happens once OpenClaw has confirmed what is actually saved on disk. Any access granted before the crash stays revoked. If OpenClaw can't confirm what was saved (conflicting receipts, or no proof the dead worker has stopped), the session stays blocked as before. The error now says to restart the Gateway, and `health`/`status` show the affected sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

**This PR deliberately changes the contract introduced in #170539.** Under that contract an unknown sharing-authority outcome is denied until the owner restarts. Fresh reads, reopening the database and later writes cannot clear it ([Peter's direction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170539#issuecomment-6137864684)). Josh decided to replace "deny until restart" with "deny until settled from committed state". @steipete, this needs your sign-off because it reverses your earlier decision.

Why this is safe:
- **The dead writer can't commit later.** Recovery is registered only when the native operation settled as `completed`, or as `unknown` with broker-proven native retirement (`nativeStopped`). Without that proof the denial stays, with reason `native-unsettled`.
- **Recovery reads what is actually saved.** It runs at most once, on the next fresh acquisition, and waits its turn behind other writers to the same database. It reads the session entry and its members together in one native read through the current worker, bypassing actor and row caches. A mismatched database identity or a failed read keeps the denial (`replacement-unavailable`).
- **Old grants are never revived.** Readers acquired before the crash are marked `authorityLost` permanently, even after later successful writes. Only a new acquisition can use the recovered state.
- **Ambiguous outcomes still fail closed.** A rejected or conflicting native receipt is not treated as "no receipt", so it stays denied with `conflicting-receipt`.
- **Only the affected keys are cleared.** Each marker belongs to the publication that created it. Settlement deletes a marker only if it hasn't changed, and a repeated unknown write cancels an earlier pending recovery.
- **The failed write stays failed.** The original write is never acknowledged or replayed.
- **Recovery is observable.** Events on the `openclaw.session-sharing.reconciliation` diagnostics channel (`reconcile-attempted`, `reconcile-settled`, `still-denied`) carry only a count, never session content.

**Relationship to #202396.** #202396 by @chelsealong improves the error message under the old deny-until-restart contract. This PR changes the contract so the session recovers once settled. It keeps the same idea for the cases that still require a restart: those get restart guidance (`SessionSharingAuthorityUnknownError`) instead of "retry later". If this PR is accepted, it covers what #202396 does. If Peter would rather keep the old contract, #202396 is the right, smaller fix.

**#158379 is a separate bug.** It hits the same wrapper error from concurrent first-session creation and registry-publication invalidation, with no worker death. This PR doesn't change it.

<details><summary>Design notes and changed old-test assertions</summary>

The native read that settles recovery lives in a lazily imported runtime module, so the entry-publication owner never statically reaches the execution owner.

Recovery ownership: the entry-publication owner registers recovery after settlement (`prepareAuthorityReconciliation`). Every producer that can create the unknown marker is wired up: entry replacement, sharing store, entry patch, transcript initialization, SessionManager publication and ACP session-meta writes. The actor adapter publishes only after a confirmed commit, so it never creates the marker.

Why recovery waits for the next fresh acquisition instead of running eagerly: running it inside the failing mutation reused an execution that was closing and hit `AdmissionClosedError`. The next acquisition runs after closing owners finish. It also leaves the normal path synchronous until its existing capture, which avoids a same-path replacement regression. There is no automatic retry loop.

A batch of recoveries is claimed all at once before the first await, so overlapping acquisitions can't replay an attempt. Store matching uses the existing sibling-family candidate matcher, so custom stores (`shared.json` → `shared.ops.sqlite`) recover too.

Changed assertions in `session-sharing-store.worker.test.ts` (lost-reply `it.each` over membership/category/invitation × receipt × closeBeforeFailure):
- **valid receipt:** used to expect permanent unavailability. Now expects a fresh acquisition to recover with the committed membership, because native completion plus the receipt proves the outcome.
- **missing receipt:** used to expect permanent unavailability. Now expects recovery from the committed rows, because native settlement proves the writer stopped, and the authoritative read decides committed versus absent.
- **conflicting receipt:** unchanged. It still expects denial.

`docs/reference/database-schemas/worker-access.md` was rewritten to describe the new contract.
</details>

## Evidence

**Live Gateway proof (Studio Crabbox `local-container`, Node 24.22.1 image, real model through ClawRouter).** One Gateway process and one durable session per run:
1. A real control chat completes.
2. The native SQLite worker is killed after its mutations but before `COMMIT`, during `chat.inject`.
3. A new `chat.send` goes to the same session from the same Gateway process, without a restart.

- Base `04d1dd10d05e`: the chat fails with `UNAVAILABLE`: `SessionMutationFactsUnavailableError: … retry after session storage is ready … Session sharing acquisition is no longer current`.
- Fix `1cdad5aefdc3`: the chat is accepted, `agent.wait` returns `ok` and the real model's answer marker appears. Health shows `sessionSharing.restartRequired` with reason `reconciliation-pending` after the fault, then clears after the chat.
- Both runs: `proofComplete: true`, exit 0 and `leaseStopped: true`. The comparison confirms the same session and the same process, and that the original failed write was preserved and never replayed.

This live harness doesn't exercise conflicting receipts or stale grants; the worker tests below cover those.

**Real-worker tests**, 6 files and 25 tests, all passing:
- Committed and rolled-back worker death recover through a fresh acquisition, and old grants stay invalid even after a later write. One case covers a custom suffixed store.
- Rejected native receipts stay denied, for both entry replacement and transcript initialization.
- A SessionManager initialization whose reply was lost after commit recovers.
- Without native settlement proof, restart guidance stays, with reason `native-unsettled`.
- Overlapping acquisitions don't replay a recovery.
- `health`/`status` show restart-required sessions, and session keys are visible to admins only.

On pinned base `04d1dd10d05e`, the recovery regression fails both fresh acquisitions.

**Other checks:**
- Core typecheck, plus the `agents-sessions`, `config-cli` and `gateway-methods` test graphs, pass.
- Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, the line-cap ratchet and `git diff --check` pass.
- Two independent review passes found producer-coverage, receipt-classification, custom-store and overlapping-replay issues. All are fixed, and the final pass found no P0–P2 issues.
- Gap: the aggregate `check:changed` ran past its time cap in its dead-code phase, so it hasn't completed.
- First CI run on `1cdad5aefdc3` caught four branch-caused failures, all fixed in `ca8dc38a7955`: an import cycle (the native recovery read now loads lazily from `session-sharing-authority-reconciliation.runtime.ts`), strict test types, the PR wrapper inventory missing the new modules, and the test-lines allowance (the restart test now reads the health owner directly; admin-only key exposure through the RPC stays covered by `health.owner-routing`).
- Known behavior, unchanged from main: right after a worker crash, the first fresh acquisition can briefly get "retry after session storage is ready" while the replacement worker finishes registry discovery. The next acquisition then either recovers or shows restart guidance.

prs.title: fix(ui): give installed skills their own page
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installed skills open inside ClawHub discovery today. The Installed chip duplicates the Installed skills button, and a discovery query can carry over into the inventory.

## User Impact

The existing **Installed skills** button opens a dedicated page with its own search. It uses the same page container, rows, icons, and status indicators as Skills discovery. **Skills** takes you back to your discovery query and position; a skill opened from Installed takes you back to that inventory and its filter.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the duplicate chip and separate discovery from inventory navigation without changing how skills look or are managed. The inventory shares the existing Skills route renderer and agent-scoped reads. Its first grid waits for the workspace and library reads to settle so late library rows cannot move workspace rows that are already visible. This does not change ClawHub categories or Skills settings.

## Evidence

- [Before and after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202766#issuecomment-7052344401), clean and annotated, from the Control UI with a synthetic Gateway. The final inventory matches the published after image pixel for pixel in the installed content area.
- Browser walkthrough verified opening Installed while searching, filtering the inventory, opening a skill, and returning through both levels with the discovery query, exact scroll offset, and keyboard focus restored. Also verified direct reload and the single-column layout at 390 px.
- Chromium’s `layout-shift` observer recorded no entries while delayed reads settled at 400, 820, and 1280 px, in either arrival order, from the Installed button and a fresh direct link. Before the follow-up, a late library response could move workspace rows down by 160, 124, and 64 px respectively. These measurements used the running Control UI against deterministic Gateway fixtures, not a production deployment.
- 45 focused UI tests, including both first-load orders, and 4 Chromium component tests passed. UI translation, controller, and stylesheet checks passed on the original implementation. Production bundling remains unverified: the regular build could not write Vite’s temporary config under the read-only dependency tree, and Vite’s runner stopped in the social-card plugin before transforming app modules.
- Local independent review could not run with the task’s configured scratch directory; hosted review has picked up the draft.

Opening Templates on a fresh Gateway used to send people to Settings → Labs. The CLI also rejected a valid local Template until an administrator enabled that switch.

## User Impact

Administrators can still disable discovery and Add with `gateway.controlUi.experimental.templates: false`. Existing agents, permissions, and installation approvals are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Templates no longer needs an experimental opt-in. The Gateway reports availability during bootstrap so viewers do not need permission to read or edit configuration just to discover Templates.

## Evidence

[Real Gateway upgrade proof and screenshot](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202740#issuecomment-7052178489): upgraded three v2026.11.6 profiles in place. Existing agents, labeled sessions, workspace files, and authored opt-outs were preserved; the omitted setting stayed omitted and opened the live catalog.

After (`01fe50fd539`), it loaded the catalog with one request. The Templates switch disappeared from Labs; neighboring settings remained. Real Chromium UI, fixture Gateway and catalog.
- **CLI:** the baseline rejected the local `minimal` package with `templates_labs_disabled`. At `af05e3bbacd`, the real CLI returned `status: complete` and exit 0 with no Templates flag. Verified `minimal` in `agents list` and its installed `SOUL.md`. Its opening chat used a loopback model fixture, not a live provider.

prs.title: fix: hide Users navigation on single-user gateways
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Single-user Gateways showed a Users destination even when there was nobody else to find. Simply removing it on current main would also remove the way into Activity and eligible Remote access.

## User Impact

Users is hidden on confirmed single-user Gateways. Activity and eligible Remote access are in Pages instead. On multi-user Gateways the Users rail stays, including when everyone else is offline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Gateway policy rather than online presence. A restored Users selection falls back to Sessions; if its rail button held keyboard focus, Sessions receives focus. The original change was reapplied to main after the sidebar rail was rewritten.

## Evidence

Focused sidebar tests and a production-build Chromium flow passed. The flow opens Activity and Remote access from Pages with the Users button hidden. The screenshots use the actual Control UI, dark desktop at 1100 × 760, with a synthetic solo Gateway. Before: `352cf811a87b6`. After: the reworked rail immediately before commit `19fc6fee3ca6c` moved the focus handoff into the sidebar controller; the focused regression passed on that commit. Broad CI and a live multi-user Gateway were not run locally.

prs.title: fix: show how to set up secure access when Connect a device can't make a code
prs.body:
Fixes #202045

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway on a new install accepts connections only from its own computer. When an owner tries to create their first phone setup code, the dialog reports a configuration error and leaves them to figure out how to make the Gateway reachable.

## User Impact

**Connect a device** guides phone pairing through **Set up secure access** and announces that title to screen readers. Choose Tailscale Serve, a trusted home network, or an existing public HTTPS address. **Device** pairing keeps its existing setup error and **Reload** action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway sends a structured detail for the loopback refusal and keeps the error message available to the CLI and other setup flows. The Dashboard uses the detail only for phone pairing and keeps the instructions outside the title’s live region.

The Dashboard leaves configuration changes to the owner. Tailscale Serve keeps the Gateway on loopback and encrypts connections. The trusted-home-network option opens a plaintext LAN listener and explains how to undo it. Phone codes created over plaintext LAN have Limited access, which includes chat history and approvals.

## Evidence

Built the Control UI and ran Chromium against isolated Gateways on Roobook with synthetic credentials and unrelated plugins disabled. The comparison uses `main` at `4eb94c89588f` and this PR at `05317529cc37`.

| Setup | Main | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phone on loopback | ![Phone setup shows the configuration error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/eac5096e9bf0719d5862337ccd5a394692096080/images/2026/11/25cc6844-e621-405a-9311-ea32265d8dea.png) | ![Phone setup shows Set up secure access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/eac5096e9bf0719d5862337ccd5a394692096080/images/2026/11/8bd6261a-72ee-4093-b14d-bfdf0f88ad8b.png) |
| Device on loopback | ![Device setup shows its existing error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/eac5096e9bf0719d5862337ccd5a394692096080/images/2026/11/585e7da0-9cff-48e1-92ef-010387f9284c.png) | ![Device setup keeps its existing error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/eac5096e9bf0719d5862337ccd5a394692096080/images/2026/11/4359255f-67db-4a52-96e0-9148527ed061.png) |

| Setup | Main with callouts | This PR with callouts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phone on loopback | ![The error is the announcement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/eac5096e9bf0719d5862337ccd5a394692096080/images/2026/11/5a3b700c-0f52-4f79-a087-a06156985e8e.png) | ![The live region contains only the title](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/eac5096e9bf0719d5862337ccd5a394692096080/images/2026/11/d1b03400-7188-40c1-89c5-d8520f7b849f.png) |
| Device on loopback | ![The selected Device setup shows the error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/eac5096e9bf0719d5862337ccd5a394692096080/images/2026/11/d5035070-3a7c-45eb-8780-6c85187ae53f.png) | ![The selected Device setup still shows the error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/eac5096e9bf0719d5862337ccd5a394692096080/images/2026/11/70527fae-a891-43d0-9864-75cc38cd45c7.png) |

Chromium’s accessibility tree showed a polite live region containing only **Set up secure access** after **Create setup code**.

Opened **Use your home Wi‑Fi instead**, applied the displayed `gateway.bind lan` command, and restarted the isolated Gateway. The same Dashboard tab reconnected. Reopening **Connect a device** and creating a code returned **Limited access** even with Full access selected. The QR and LAN address are masked in the capture.

![Limited access shown on the setup code screen after LAN restart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/eac5096e9bf0719d5862337ccd5a394692096080/images/2026/11/9f0e8308-1462-4129-b477-9a6e57696faa.png)

- 70 focused tests passed across the Gateway setup-code handler, device setup state, and dialog. The Device error and phone announcement regressions fail without the dialog fix.
- UI and core typechecks, protocol, i18n, controller guard, lint, formatter, and production UI builds passed.
- Main and the PR build emitted the same five budget warnings. Compared with main, New Session boot JS was 535 B larger gzip, Chat boot JS was 413 B larger, and total CSS was 6,460 B smaller. Boot request counts matched.
- Codex autoreview found no actionable findings through P2 in the dialog fix.
- Skipped screen-reader playback, Tailscale Serve end to end, and the full UI and Gateway suites.

When you use ClawRouter, the model picker can show only the router’s logo, even when the catalog knows who makes the model. That makes it harder to distinguish OpenAI, Anthropic, and other models at a glance.

## User Impact

ClawRouter stays recognizable: its full-size mark anchors the icon, with the model maker inset in its upper-right corner. Direct connections and routed models without known maker artwork keep their single icon. Names, selection, and routing are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maker mark replaces one corner of the full-size ClawRouter art. The cutout reveals the actual composer or picker surface, so it matches light and dark themes and row highlights. The icon stays in the same 16 × 16 px slot at the captured viewport. Provider tabs are unchanged.

## Evidence

Chromium captures of the built Control UI against a synthetic Gateway catalog at 1040 × 750 CSS px, DPR 2. Before: `5a8a71814fab` (router-only baseline); after: `a8a361590b82`. The focused browser regression verified the full-size base, inset overlay, unchanged icon slot, direct and unknown-maker fallbacks, and selection of the original routed model ID. - The [failing UI unit job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44812647990/job/136553913022) reports `expected null not to be null` in this test before the model assertions.
