prs.title: fix: preserve lower-token guidance for unaffordable requests
prs.body:
Related: #25395, #151377

## What Problem This Solves

A provider can reject one request because its maximum token budget costs more than the available credit or key allowance. OpenClaw currently replaces the provider’s “more credits, or fewer max_tokens” advice with generic billing guidance, hiding the option to lower the output limit.

## User Impact

User impact: request-affordability failures explain that lowering maximum output tokens is an alternative to checking the account balance or key spending limit. Explicit key-limit failures get distinct guidance. Generic billing and genuine rate-limit messages retain their existing behavior; an affordability rejection does not establish an empty account.

No configuration migration, automatic token reduction, new retry, provider switch, or credential change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing billing-message owner now uses the retained provider detail before selecting safe, fixed recovery text. The distinction survives assistant errors, structured fallback attempts, and final reply normalization without exposing provider response bodies or help URLs. Classification, cooldowns, and retry policy are unchanged.

Simplification: reuse the existing raw-error and fallback-attempt fields rather than add new state or classifier categories. Billing copy has one implementation in a small focused module, extracted to keep the existing user-copy module within its enforced line limit. The existing export remains a forwarding export, not a second implementation.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI proof requested by review

Executed the actual `pnpm openclaw agent exec` command on the unchanged candidate for head `9e86caad82cc1f29a2b80d43b109cac422a82eb4` (workspace tree `383749c396e0a2bea9cde0fb07758aaba1714311`). The normal package entry point prepared current build artifacts. Isolated HOME/config/state/workspace, one fake credential, one local synthetic HTTP 402 server, and no fallbacks were used. No live Gateway, external provider, or paid request was involved.

Command (only fixture paths replaced with placeholders):

```sh
pnpm openclaw agent exec "Reply briefly without tools." --config <isolated-config> --cwd <isolated-workspace> --state-dir <isolated-state> --code-mode direct --json --timeout 60
```

Actual CLI stdout (only the isolated session ID redacted):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "status": "error",
  "final": "",
  "payloads": [],
  "model": null,
  "provider": null,
  "sessionId": "<isolated-session>",
  "error": {
    "message": "⚠️ This request exceeds the available credit or spending allowance. Reduce the maximum output tokens (`max_tokens`), or check your account balance and key spending limit before trying again.",
    "kind": "exception"
  }
}
```

Independent HTTP fixture observation, printed from received requests after the CLI exited:

```json
{
  "exit": {
    "code": 1,
    "signal": null
  },
  "physicalRequestCount": 1,
  "requests": [
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/v1/chat/completions",
      "model": "model",
      "max_tokens": 217003
    }
  ]
}
```

Actual stderr excerpts (isolated session ID redacted):

```text
[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: runId=<isolated-session> stage=assistant decision=surface_error reason=billing attempt=1 retry=0 rotations=0 from=affordability-fixture/model profile=-
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=affordability-fixture/model candidate=affordability-fixture/model reason=billing next=none
[session-suspension] failed to persist quota suspension sessionId=<isolated-session> error="Session history database read was revoked"
⚠️ This request exceeds the available credit or spending allowance. Reduce the maximum output tokens (`max_tokens`), or check your account balance and key spending limit before trying again.
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main
```

**Result:** the expected provider-error exit is **1**, not a failed proof. Affordability guidance was printed; the endpoint physically received exactly **one** request with unchanged **max_tokens=217003**. The fixture asserted those observations and exited **0**. The stderr suspension-persistence warning is retained above: this run proves presentation and request behavior, not successful quota-suspension persistence. The CLI child exited and the fixture closed its listener.

- Reproduced on `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea`: the production reply-dispatch path sent generic billing copy instead of the lower-output-token remedy. The same regression passes with the fix and asserts exactly one final delivery, one resolver invocation, and no block/tool delivery.
- A real `agentExecCommand` run with isolated state and a synthetic HTTP 402 server passes through actual request assembly and transport. The server observed exactly one request with `max_tokens: 217003`; the terminal result retained affordability guidance. No paid provider or production credential was used.
- Structured-body, fallback-attempt, key-cap, exhausted-credit, and existing genuine rate-limit coverage passes. Seven focused test files: **184 tests passed** across six shards, **104.43 seconds wall time** including compilation/startup. The real-agent proof’s shard took 13.19 seconds; dispatch took 7.54 seconds. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, the four affected test typecheck graphs (agents-root, agents-other, commands, messaging), targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` completed successfully in 150.7 seconds. It printed advisory existing-surface UI bundle-size violations; this PR changes no UI assets or bundle policy. This command omits full declaration emission.
- Local Auto Review was cancelled after more than 40 minutes without a report. **No clean local-review result is claimed.** [Hosted re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201392#issuecomment-6989465826) completed for `9e86caad82cc1f29a2b80d43b109cac422a82eb4`: **Ready for maintainer review**, **5/6 overall readiness**, **5/6 proof confidence**, **5/6 patch quality**, and no actionable findings. The [exact-head CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44379458558/job/135076704339).

Proof limits: the provider responses are synthetic, not live OpenRouter billing observations. The real product entry point exercised is the shipped `pnpm openclaw agent exec` command, plus the production channel reply-dispatch boundary; no browser/native-app screenshot or live-channel delivery claim is made. Base refresh was unavailable through the managed action, so evidence is pinned to the base above rather than a newer main revision.

The [first CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44377654609/job/135062109969) found an omitted PR-wrapper extraction dependency. Commit `9e86caad82cc1f29a2b80d43b109cac422a82eb4` adds only that inventory entry; the 23 wrapper tests pass locally. Production source and the prior single-request proof are unchanged. The exact repaired-head CI gate passed: [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44379458558/job/135076704339).

<details>
<summary>Inspect retained before/after terminal output and wrapper-repair verification</summary>

### Retained terminal evidence

    },

Number of calls: 1

⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯[1/1]⎯

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A message from another chat only shows a generic update count until you open it. That hides what the sender wanted you to know and makes it hard to scan the receiving conversation.

## User Impact

Cross-thread messages now appear on the left in a native incoming chat bubble with a link back to the source thread. A sender can supply a one-line preview; readers can expand it to see the original message. If the sender omits the summary, the original message is shown directly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The optional `sessions_send.summary` is stored separately from the original message. Each message retains its own timestamp, disclosure, and reply and copy actions. Passive notifications and automation messages keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

A real model sent a message using `sessions_send` on an isolated Gateway. Chromium verified the summary, keyboard expansion and collapse, the link back to the original thread, and persistence after reload. The same flow covered no-summary delivery and the narrow light-theme layout. The conversations used synthetic data.

Local checks passed: 67 UI sibling tests, 23 send-admission tests, 16 prompt-prefix stability tests, and 13 provenance tests. The runtime/UI build, UI typecheck, targeted lint, stylesheet lint, and generated validator check also passed. Local review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Broad CI results are not claimed.

prs.title: fix: explain Discord mention requirements in channel diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: #200429 (distinct session-status activation reporting)

## What Problem This Solves

Discord's targeted capability check can report that every required permission is present without explaining why an ordinary message still does not start a turn. Operators cannot see whether that channel requires a mention or which guild/channel/account setting is responsible.

## User Impact

User impact: the Discord channel capabilities command now explains the configured mention requirement and channel access separately from Discord permissions, and points to the responsible configuration scope. It recommends mentioning the bot in an allowed channel from an allowed sender for the first test.

No admission defaults, allowlists, permissions, configuration options, or public denial replies change. This is a local-config diagnostic, not a sender authorization decision or a live Gateway connectivity check. Name-based policy bindings and bound-thread route activation are explicitly left unverified rather than guessed; use numeric guild/channel IDs and check channel status separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Discord's existing mention-policy and channel-access owners. The mention resolver returns its winning configuration scope alongside the unchanged decision. The existing permission lookup already retrieves the channel, parent, guild and bot facts needed by the targeted diagnostic, so no additional Discord requests are added. The explanation loads only when requested.

Simplification: no new subsystem, cache, configuration, or parallel admission implementation. The remaining production growth is the operator explanation and source paths; the regression exercises the real permission lookup with fixed external REST responses.

## Evidence

- Actual CLI reproduction on base bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea with isolated synthetic config/state and a loopback Discord API: before, permissions were complete but mention policy was absent; after, the same command reports channel access, requireMention=true, its exact channel config path, and sender/connection limitations. Both runs issued the same six read-only HTTP requests. No live Discord messages were sent.
- Corrected regression was red on the base because messagePolicy was absent, while the permission-success assertion passed; green after the repair. Controls cover account-vs-root inheritance, channel/guild/default precedence, disabled channels, empty account guild overrides, bot-owned thread parent settings, and unresolved names.
- Focused channel, mention-policy and send-permission suites: 105 tests passed. Final focused invocation wall time: 42.8 seconds (40.4 seconds runner duration, mostly cold compilation); individual new regression executes in milliseconds. CI seconds pending.
- Full pnpm build, Discord package typecheck, targeted lint, seven-file formatting check, and git diff --check passed. Build emitted existing UI asset-budget warnings; its exit status was 0. No UI source is changed.
- Local Auto Review (P0–P2, complete local candidate against the pinned base) was cancelled after stalling without a report. It is incomplete, not a clean review. Hosted review remains required.
- Live proof gap: the supported Discord QA readiness command failed during Convex lease acquisition before any Discord checks. No credential was obtained or borrowed, and no transport/reply claim is made. Cold-import screening completed; qualification was unavailable while the source tree was dirty.

### Inspectable CLI evidence

Actual retained stdout excerpts; synthetic config/state and local Discord REST fixture, not a live Discord send. Base: `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea`. After: repaired head `d8a62ed574e58c7ec8b6e5a68ee3f7f8c4499780`.

Command: `pnpm openclaw channels capabilities --channel discord --account default --target channel:222`

Before:
```text
Permissions (222): SendMessages, ViewChannel
Missing required: none
```

After:
```text
Permissions (222): SendMessages, ViewChannel
Missing required: none
Message policy (local config): groupPolicy=allowlist (source: channels.discord.groupPolicy)
Channel access: allowed (source: channels.discord.guilds["123"].channels["222"])
Mentions: requireMention=true (source: channels.discord.guilds["123"].channels["222"].requireMention)
Sender access: not evaluated; no sender context was supplied. Guild/channel users and roles still apply.
First test: mention the bot in this allowed channel from an allowed sender. Check channels status --probe separately for Gateway connectivity.
```

Retained after-run exit and request trace (unchanged from the baseline):
```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "requests": [
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/users/@me"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/oauth2/applications/@me"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/channels/222"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/users/@me"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/guilds/123"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/guilds/123/members/999"
    }
  ]
}
```

### CI repair

The first head failed [the permission-response integration check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44376909315/job/135059455016): diagnostic metadata had escaped into ordinary permission-tool responses. The fix makes that context opt-in only for the operator diagnostic and preserves the existing public response; the existing exact-response assertion is unchanged. Reproduced locally red, then all 55 metadata-read authority integration tests plus 100 channel/send tests passed (17.74s total focused run). Targeted typecheck/lint and actual CLI reproduction passed again. The standard failed-CI helper was unavailable (`spawn gh ENOENT`); the exact job log was read through the managed GitHub reader instead.

### Policy/transport distinguishability verification

Seven additional focused cases passed on the repaired head, reusing the earlier 155-test and capabilities-CLI proof:

- **Four admission cases:** the real Discord dispatcher/live-policy/preflight path distinguishes an unmentioned message (`reason=no-mention`), a disallowed channel, and a disallowed sender. All three denied cases made **zero agent-processing calls and zero outbound REST writes**; only the unmentioned allowed message entered pending history. An allowed-sender/channel mention passed the positive admission control, which intentionally stopped before model execution or outbound delivery.
- **Three status-command cases:** a reachable-Gateway RPC fixture rendered `Discord default: enabled, configured, running, disconnected, check failed`; existing controls preserved Gateway protocol rejections and config-only transport-failure fallback. Separately, the actual `channels status --channel discord --probe --timeout 1500` CLI against an isolated closed loopback endpoint reported `Gateway not reachable; showing config-only status.` Its exit 0 denotes the documented fallback, not a successful live probe.

The actual `channels logs --channel all --lines 20 --json` CLI retrieved the produced admission records. Channel/sender denial records require existing **`logging.level=debug`** (or trace) during the event. Use the all-channel/general Gateway log view: these legacy denial records are not tagged with the Discord subsystem, and `discord-auto-reply` is not the narrow `discord` log root. An empty `channels logs --channel discord` result therefore does not prove no denial occurred. Sender-denial logs deliberately omit the sender ID; correlate a controlled input/time rather than infer a per-sender decision.

This is isolated synthetic-boundary proof, **not live Discord transport or reply proof**. Target-only capabilities still have no sender context and correctly report sender access as unassessed. The earlier QA lease failure remains unresolved; no credentials or public messages were used. Temporary proof source was removed/reverted; no additional product changes were made. Current-main verification at `b413b8e1966780121c211abbf3f91adb5c173afa` found the admission/status owners unchanged and only three unrelated threading lines changed in `channel.ts`.

Worked on by:
- @etzelm

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ba8717b3-cf77-4a25-bcd9-79ff4fd42b6b)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/ba4b03bf-e9fe-4063-affb-642a421e722b)

prs.title: fix: sample attachment menu height only while visible
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202500

## What Problem This Solves

The attachment-menu height test samples hidden panels after the overlay animation change. Its opacity-only filter accepts `display: none` elements whose computed opacity is 1, so it can report two heights before the menu becomes visible.

## User Impact

No runtime change. The browser test continues to require one measured height throughout visible reopening and retains its reduced-motion assertion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the browser's `checkVisibility` predicate with opacity and CSS visibility checks before sampling height. This excludes the hidden pre-open frame without relaxing the one-height assertion, delaying sampling until after the animation, or increasing timeouts.

## Evidence

- [Ready-event browser proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44829527466/job/136611397200) passes all 14 attachment-menu cases on `ac5f52d9de212`. The reopening-height case, including reduced motion, passes in 1.467 seconds; the full file takes 38.621 seconds. The [earlier exact-head run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44828886476/job/136609138524) also passes all 14 cases.
- [The failing browser job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44825803181/job/136598948136) reports two distinct heights in `reopens at its measured height instead of growing upward`.
- The unchanged test and overlay styles are present on the selected main base. The overlay animation change leaves hidden panels at default opacity while the shared stylesheet hides them with `display: none`.
- Fresh local review found no actionable correctness or security findings. Formatting and whitespace checks pass. Production delta: 0 lines. Test delta: 1 addition, 1 deletion; no new cases.
- The local checkout has no qualified dependencies; browser proof is hosted.

## Unrelated CI Failure

The [completed ready-event run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44829527466) fails only a separate unit-test shard: `chat-pane-history-cursor-custody.test.ts` observes a null live-run ID during setup. The CI report calls this new because its latest scheduled-main sample passed.

The [earlier Cron PR run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44824805865/job/136595179559) has the identical failure before this attachment change. The cursor test, live-event dispatcher, runtime handler, and mounted-pane fixture are byte-identical between those failing inputs. This PR changes only a browser-test visibility predicate; the unit-test inputs are unchanged in its tested merge.

The separate cursor setup repair is merged in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202752 with green exact-head CI. Native landing evidence records this explicit attribution and retains the failed CI result.

## What Problem This Solves

The New session button in the sidebar header looks exactly like the filter and collapse buttons next to it. All three are faint ghost icons, so the most common action in the header is easy to miss. It also sits between filter and collapse instead of at the edge.

## User Impact

User impact: New session is now the last button in the Sessions header. It has a hairline outline and full-strength icon color, so it stands out without an accent color. The collapse toggle moves to the start of the button group, in the order collapse, filter, New session.

The People and Automations headers follow the same order: collapse, then the panel's filter. Because the collapse toggle now comes before each panel's actions, its position changes slightly between panels that have different numbers of actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared sidebar panel header now places each panel's actions after the collapse toggle, so the panel's own actions hold the trailing edge. The header title or owner picker takes the free space, which keeps the collapse toggle next to the actions. Before this change, the filter button's own auto margin created that space. The New session outline is an inset ring, so the button keeps the same 28px geometry as its neighbors.

## Evidence

Scenario: Sessions sidebar with "My sessions" selected, default sidebar width, light theme, 1280×800 viewport at 2× scale. Synthetic session data comes from the Control UI E2E mock Gateway. Before is `origin/main` at `6018bc9ce69a`. After is this branch.

prs.title: fix: preserve identical macOS Gateway service files during updates
prs.body:
Closes #200170

## What Problem This Solves

A macOS Gateway update can replace the LaunchAgent plist, environment file, and generated wrapper even though their bytes and permissions already match. These updates leave unnecessary service-definition backups behind.

## User Impact

The Gateway still reactivates during an update. Matching files keep their original identities, and an updater that supports unchanged-definition receipts skips the backup set for that refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service writer compares the rendered bytes and required mode at the existing publication boundary. The installer still checks ownership, unloads the old service, and bootstraps the Gateway. A real change still saves the originals before publication. Rollback revalidates the live files and rejects intervening edits, including on the path with no backup files.

The installed updater opts in through its existing private command input. If an older updater still owns service activation, the candidate sends the existing receipt and retains the backups that the older rollback reader expects. When the published updater hands finalization to the patched candidate, the candidate can opt into the unchanged receipt during that same upgrade.

## Evidence

### Published npm upgrade on Apple-silicon macOS

Installed the npm stable release `openclaw@2026.11.5` (build `e13cf15ece9b`) into a disposable prefix. A dedicated macOS profile and native LaunchAgent served the running Gateway. The installed CLI ran `openclaw update --tag <loopback-candidate.tgz> --yes --json`. Both builds have version `2026.11.5`, so I verified the installed build ID and commit.

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Published stable → packaged `667cf68eac0` | Updater exited 0. The recorded driver handoff, native installer, and Gateway verification all succeeded. |
| LaunchAgent after the upgrade | Gateway started with a new PID. All three service files retained their SHA-256, inode, mode, mtime, and ctime. Zero new backup files. |
| Existing data after restart | `/readyz` and the Gateway health RPC passed. The saved `tools.profile` setting and a disabled cron job with its original ID and payload loaded successfully. The release migrated the state database from schema 36 to 40. Doctor also rewrote the config, while the seeded settings remained usable. |
| Published stable → candidate with injected activation failure | The scoped launchd fault prevented candidate readiness. The updater reported `state-migrated-no-rollback` and did not attempt to roll back across the migrated state. |
| Legacy service-definition rollback reader | The candidate installer received the shipped legacy update marker without the opt-in. It repaired a wrapper mode from `0750` to `0700` and returned the legacy receipt with three backed-up payloads and a durable receipt file. The strict parser and native restore owner from the published `2026.11.5` package accepted that receipt and restored the original `0750` mode with the same bytes. |

```text
published update: status=ok, run=succeeded
update-driver-handoff: exit 0
managed-service-install: exit 0
managed-service-reconciliation: Reactivated Gateway with the existing LaunchAgent definition.
gateway verification: exit 0
artifact comparison: 3/3 unchanged, 0 new backups, new Gateway PID
persisted checks: setting retained, same cron ID and payload, cron still disabled
```

### Compatible updater and rollback on schema 40

- **Upgrade from packaged `667cf68eac0` to packaged `8ba765f877f`.** The updater exited 0 and reported that it reactivated the Gateway with the existing LaunchAgent definition. A new PID served `/readyz` and health RPC. The three service files kept their full identities, and the isolated profile gained zero backup artifacts. The config was byte-for-byte identical and the disabled cron job still loaded.
- **The same package pair with an injected activation failure.** The update reported `restart-unhealthy` and `rollbackOutcome.status=succeeded`. Package rollback, native service restart, and rollback Gateway verification all exited 0. The previous build `667cf68eac0` served a new healthy PID. The three file identities, config bytes, saved setting, and original disabled cron record all matched the pre-update snapshot. The profile gained zero backup artifacts.

<details>
<summary>Package identity and regression results</summary>

Both builds passed the repository package build and tarball integrity checks.

- Published-driver candidate `667cf68eac003455a81b4f5ca7a8ba9400e32bd8`, tarball SHA-256 `c45cc95a8fa1feafca024c5cd057a0cbfffabdc95ce41f4eb558080923a26884`.
- Follow-up candidate `8ba765f877f60b67e800d446245c5b546a372e9c`, tarball SHA-256 `a3026f2843812620415f9be43996a251dcec823e5f03820bd08e12dadcf0d37d`. This commit only changes one test predicate for typed lint.
- Base `9fbb4b6f39f`: the initial unchanged-definition regression failed all three cases when the file-state comparison observed replacement during activation. The same native LaunchAgent reproduction on the base replaced three identical files and added three backups plus a receipt.
- Patched suite: 187 focused tests passed across 10 files. The five targeted reconciliation cases passed again after the test-only lint fix. These cover both receipt formats, mode repair, injected activation and backup failures, and rejection of an intervening edit.
- Local Codex re-review found no actionable issues after fixing deferred-backup failure settlement. Typed lint for the follow-up, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The wider unused-export check still flags symbols in two files outside this branch's diff.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): tweakcn theme imports are lost in other browsers and devices
prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski, who is the intended reviewer for this change.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/883de5f4-29a0-436b-9b14-bd0167001845)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e6c2c44d-1746-4a0f-8948-6e93174b160d)

Related: #184960 (theme discovery and personal-theme removal; it keeps this importer unchanged)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a theme imported from tweakcn in Settings → Appearance disappears in every other browser or device, and after browser storage is cleared, even when the person is signed in to a Gateway profile.

## User Impact

User impact: when you are signed in with a profile you can edit, a tweakcn import is saved as a personal theme. It appears in the theme grid like agent-created themes, is selected right away, and follows you to other browsers and devices. Importing the same tweakcn theme again updates that personal theme instead of adding a duplicate.

Existing users keep their imports. The importer shipped in stable releases (v2026.10.2 through v2026.11.3), so a browser that still holds an import from an earlier version moves it to the profile the next time it connects with write access. If it was the active theme, it stays active. If the save fails, the browser keeps its import and retries on the next connection.

Without a profile or without write access, nothing changes: the import stays in the browser-local slot with its Replace and Clear controls.

**Decision for review:** the docs from #152460 promised that existing browser-local imports are “never uploaded automatically.” This PR intentionally reverses that promise, as requested, and the docs now describe the one-time move. Please confirm this is acceptable.

Fonts that exceed the portable theme limits, such as tweakcn’s long system font stacks, are replaced by the default theme fonts. All 19 semantic colors are kept.

## Why This Change Was Made

The importer stored one derived token map in browser settings under the special `custom` theme, which profile sync deliberately skips. Signed-in imports now go through the existing `themes.import` Gateway method, the same path agents use, as `user/tweakcn-<id>`. The imported token map still contains the original tweakcn colors and fonts, so one small mapping produces the personal theme definition for new imports and for the one-time move.

The import response primes the theme catalog before the new theme is selected. Without this, switching from a theme such as Knot briefly rendered Claw while the catalog refreshed. No storage layer, schema, or Gateway change is added. The browser-local slot stays only for connections that cannot write to a profile, so its Replace and Clear controls are still used there.

Known gap: Appearance has no control to delete a personal theme on `main`. Before this change, signed-in people could clear their one browser-local import. Now an import becomes a personal theme, like agent-created themes. #184960 adds personal-theme removal.

## Evidence

The before screenshots come from current `main` (`e6c7c5e0da4b`); the after screenshots come from this branch. Both use the real Control UI against a real local Gateway with a signed-in trusted-proxy profile that has write access, in dark mode with a 1440×1000 viewport. The tweakcn response is the real `amethyst-haze` payload, served by a Playwright route. No Gateway RPCs are mocked.

### Before: a fresh browser on the same profile after importing Amethyst Haze

The import is missing and Claw is selected.

![Before: fresh browser on main shows Claw and no imported theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac355c88-050a-45f9-bf76-5fe36d83d664)

### After: a fresh browser on the same profile after importing Amethyst Haze

Amethyst Haze is a personal theme and is selected, and the appearance scope reads “Saved to your profile”.

![After: fresh browser shows the Amethyst Haze personal theme selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36c52ffa-ddde-4c87-a79b-6ff529685bd7)

<details><summary>The importing browser, right after import</summary>

Before: the import fills the browser-local slot (Replace and Clear controls, “Stored in this browser only”).

![Before: importing browser on main with the browser-local slot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/755dd567-13ca-4757-a2a9-8166457659b5)

After: the import is a personal theme card, and the Import card stays available for the next import.

![After: importing browser with the personal theme card and the Import card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b28c167-bf6c-4bd6-a4ce-7edd27da13b3)

</details>

- **Red on base, green with the fix:** `config-page.custom-theme.test.ts` › “saves a signed-in import as a personal theme instead of browser storage” failed on `main` (`themes.import` was never called, and the palette was written to browser settings) and passes on this branch.
- **New focused tests:** a test proves that the real tweakcn payload is saved with all 19 original colors, that the derived palette matches the import, and that an over-long font stack falls back. Another test proves that a browser-local import is moved to the profile on a writable connection and that the selection follows it.
- **Real Gateway run:** importing while on Knot went straight from Knot to the new theme, with no Claw flash. A reload and a second browser context both kept the personal theme.
- **Checks passed:** `pnpm test` on `custom-theme.test.ts`, `theme-catalog.test.ts`, `config-page.custom-theme.test.ts`, `view-appearance.browser.test.tsx`, `bootstrap-theme.palette.test.ts`, and `server-prefs.profile.test.ts` (all passed, about 1–4 s per file). `pnpm tsgo:ui` and the UI app and pages test typecheck shards passed. oxlint and oxfmt passed on the changed files, as did `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers` and `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` (no baseline drift).
- **Local review:** autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, branch mode) found nothing actionable.
- **Not run locally:** the full UI and E2E suites. The existing mocked-Gateway Appearance E2E covers the connection without a profile, whose behavior is unchanged; PR CI covers the broad suites.
- **Seen but not changed:** while a personal or imported theme is active, the Import card looks light grey. Imported palettes derive `--bg-hover` from the muted text color. This already happens on `main` whenever an agent-created theme is active, so it is left for a separate fix.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: agent-selected themes keep the previous accent and fonts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the agent selects or applies a different theme, an accent or font chosen earlier in Appearance keeps covering the new theme, so the theme the person asked for does not look like itself. Choosing the same theme in Appearance already resets those overrides, so the result depended on where the theme was chosen.

## User Impact

User impact: selecting a different theme shows that theme's own accent and fonts, whether it was chosen in Appearance or by the agent with the `theme` tool (`set`, or `import` with `apply: true`). Changing only light/dark/system mode, reselecting the current theme, and importing a theme without applying it keep the person's accent and font overrides. Accent or font values sent together with the selection still win, so Appearance behaves exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reset rule lived only in the Control UI, which sends `accent: "theme"` and cleared fonts alongside the new theme. The Gateway `themes.set` and `themes.import` handlers, which both Appearance and the agent tool use, now apply the same defaults whenever the selected theme changes, so there is one owner for the rule. The Control UI keeps its own reset because it also updates the browser immediately and covers connections without a profile; its requests already carry explicit values, so its stored result is unchanged. Tool description and docs now describe the behavior.

Accepted edge case: like Appearance today, choosing a different theme stores `ui.accent: "theme"`, which uses one profile preference key. A profile already at the preference key limit cannot apply a newly imported theme until a key is freed; the existing limit test was adjusted for that.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway and Control UI (synthetic owner profile, no live data). Steps on each build: select Claw, save a custom pink accent (`#ff2d95`) to the profile, then send `themes.set {"id":"phosphor"}` from the CLI, which is the same request the agent's `theme` tool sends. A fresh browser then opened Settings → Appearance. No model or agent turn was involved.

- Before (current `main`, e6c7c5e): profile keeps `ui.accent: "#ff2d95"`; Phosphor renders with the pink custom accent, next to the caption "Choosing a different theme resets its fonts and accent colors."
- After (this branch): profile stores `ui.accent: "theme"`; Phosphor renders with its own green accent and Accent color shows "Theme default".

Before (current `main`):

![Before: Phosphor selected but the pink custom accent remains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e80701b0-e451-481f-8b44-0558a1518d8b)

After (this PR):

![After: Phosphor selected with its own green accent, Accent color shows Theme default](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8fe2a28-9020-4609-a7d8-fe9228b3a623)

Tests:
- New regression in `src/gateway/server-methods/themes.test.ts`: failed on base (accent stayed `#aabbcc`, fonts stayed after `themes.set {id: "tide"}`), passes with the fix. It also covers mode-only change, reselection, import without apply (overrides kept) and import with apply (reset).
- Existing Settings-shaped test with explicit appearance values in the same batch passes unchanged.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/themes.test.ts src/agents/tools/theme-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 22 + 12 passed (themes file about 17 s wall time).
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14 passed (tool description changed).
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, format, docs baseline and guards pass. The dead export scan reports existing unused exports in files this PR does not touch (for example `scripts/lib/ios-behavior-grade.mts`).
- Local autoreview (branch mode, P0–P2): scoped-clean.

prs.title: fix(install): honor --beta for git installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installing with `install.sh --install-method git --beta` still installs the latest stable release. The flag is accepted, nothing warns, and the ref that gets checked out is `latest` instead of `beta`.

## User Impact

User impact: `--beta` now installs the beta channel for git installs, the same way it already does for npm and Bun installs. Explicit versions and branches are unchanged, and a flag-selected `--beta` whose beta dist-tag is unavailable (e.g. no npm on a fresh host) falls back through latest resolution instead of failing to check out a nonexistent `beta` ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolve_git_openclaw_ref` (`scripts/install-policy.sh`) builds its request from `OPENCLAW_VERSION` alone. `--beta` only sets `USE_BETA=1` (`scripts/install.sh`), and that flag is read by the npm and Bun engine paths — after the git ref was already resolved. The resolver now prefers the beta channel when `USE_BETA` is set and the request is a channel (`latest`/`next`/unset), keeping an explicit pin or branch authoritative. Because the git ref resolution precedes `ensure_node`, a fresh host without npm made the beta dist-tag lookup fail and returned the literal `beta`; flag-selected beta now falls back through latest resolution, while an explicit `--version beta` keeps its literal meaning.

Scope note: this PR covers the `--beta` half of #201335.

## Evidence

**Real registry + real checkout (base vs this head).** Channel selection is exercised without any stubbed npm: the installer read the public registry and checked out real upstream tags.

```
$ npm view openclaw dist-tags --json
{ "latest": "2026.11.6", "beta": "2026.11.10-beta.1", "extended-stable": "2026.10.33", "alpha": "1.10.0-alpha" }
```

The checkout target was a blobless clone of `github.com/openclaw/openclaw` (`--filter=blob:none`, the same form the installer uses), driven through `--git-dir`; `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` were isolated and a settings file plus a workspace marker existed before the runs and survived them.

Base (upstream main `416b357`), `--beta` on a git install — the flag is accepted but latest is installed:

```
$ bash scripts/install.sh --install-method git --beta --no-onboard --git-dir <repo>
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: v2026.11.6
$ git -C <repo> describe --tags --exact-match HEAD
v2026.11.6
```

This PR's head, same command, same registry, same checkout (an upgrade from latest-stable to beta):

```
$ bash scripts/install.sh --install-method git --beta --no-onboard --git-dir <repo>
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: v2026.11.10-beta.1
· Fetching requested version
· Checking out v2026.11.10-beta.1
$ git -C <repo> describe --tags --exact-match HEAD
v2026.11.10-beta.1
$ git -C <repo> status --porcelain | wc -l
0
$ cat "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"
{ "gateway": { "mode": "local" }, "agents": { "defaults": { "workspace": "<isolated>/ws" } } }
```

Latest-stable baseline on the same checkout without `--beta` (this head): `Using git ref: v2026.11.6` → `Checking out v2026.11.6`, HEAD `v2026.11.6`.

**Missing-beta fallback (stubbed npm).** The public registry always publishes a `beta` dist-tag, so the fallback cannot be produced against it. That case keeps the stubbed-`npm` environment (controlled `dist-tags`, local git checkout with `v2026.11.5` and `v2026.11.6-beta.2`): base (policy before the fallback) prints the literal `beta` and the checkout fails, this head falls back to latest.

```
# base commit (policy before the fallback)
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: beta
# this PR's head
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: v2026.11.5
```

**Unit/regression coverage.** The `resolves the git install ref` cases in `test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts` source the real `scripts/install-policy.sh` in bash with a stubbed `installer_npm`, including the flag-selected beta fallback and the explicit-beta literal cases.

Base (policy change stashed, test present) — `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-projects.mts test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts`:

```
× resolves the git install ref: --beta selects the beta tag
× resolves the git install ref: --beta without a requested version
AssertionError: expected 'v2026.11.5' to be 'v2026.11.6-beta.2'
Tests  2 failed | 9 passed (11)
```

With the fix:

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  14 passed (14)
```

```
机制对位: 症状在 scripts/install-policy.sh:317 resolve_git_openclaw_ref（只读 OPENCLAW_VERSION，--beta 只设置 install.sh 的 USE_BETA），我改同函数加上 USE_BETA 分支与 beta 缺失回退
复现: base(416b357) --beta → Using git ref: v2026.11.6；head → v2026.11.10-beta.1 且 HEAD 切到该 tag
证据类别: 真实 npm registry + 真实 GitHub 仓库 checkout，本机可得: 是（上述 transcript）
契约核对: git 安装的 ref 由 scripts/install-policy.sh 的 resolve_git_openclaw_ref 独占决定，调用点 scripts/install.sh:2997
风险: 1 生产脚本 + 1 测试；不跨层、不触碰状态机
```

## AI Assistance

Implemented with an AI coding agent (OpenClaw contributor workflow). All quoted output above is from runs on this machine; the settings file and workspace marker were created before the runs to show they survive the checkout.

prs.title: fix(ui): stale theme colors return when an older catalog read finishes late
prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski, who is the intended reviewer for this PR.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/883de5f4-29a0-436b-9b14-bd0167001845)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e7367350-e2f2-4120-a576-3babb785e62a)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI can show outdated theme colors, or bring back a removed plugin theme, when an older theme catalog read finishes after a newer refresh has started on the same connection and profile.

Two reproduced cases on `main`:

1. A first `themes.list` is still pending, a `users.prefs.changed` event starts a second refresh that applies background `#222222`, and the first read then finishes with `#111111`. The older `#111111` palette wins.
2. A `themes.get` for a plugin theme is still pending, a `plugins.changed` refresh removes that theme from the catalog, and the pending read then finishes. The removed theme becomes available and is applied again.

A profile or client change already discarded these late reads; a refresh on the same connection and profile did not.

## User Impact

User impact: after a profile preference change or a plugin reload, the Control UI keeps the newest theme colors and does not reapply a plugin theme that the catalog no longer contains. There is no visual or settings change otherwise.

## Why This Change Was Made

The theme catalog already owned the decision about whether a response may still publish (connection, client, and profile). It now also records a refresh generation: each refresh supersedes earlier list and palette reads, so only reads started under the newest refresh can publish. A palette read also publishes only while the current catalog still lists its theme, because a palette read started during a refresh can otherwise finish after the new list removed the theme. Dropped palette reads are requested again by the existing path, since each refresh already clears the requested set. No new UI, cache, or state layer was added.

## Evidence

- Two regression tests in `ui/src/app/theme-catalog.test.ts` cover the cases above through the real application theme and Gateway store test harness. Both failed on `main` (`e6c7c5e0da4b`): the first kept `#111111` instead of `#222222`, and the second applied `space-pack/xenovessel` instead of staying on `claw`. Both pass with this change.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/theme-catalog.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 20 of 20 tests pass, about 2.6 seconds.
- Consumer tests that import the theme catalog or application theme (11 files, including `bootstrap-theme.palette`, `config-page.appearance-catalogs`, `config-page`, and `appearance-background.browser`): all pass.
- `tsgo:ui` and the `tsgo:test:ui` shards pass; oxlint and oxfmt are clean on both files; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode against `origin/main` at `e6c7c5e0da4b`, P0–P2, with the catalog, its test file, and `bootstrap-theme.ts` as source context): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Not run locally: broad UI suites and Control UI end-to-end runs; PR CI covers broad proof. This is not a visual change, so there are no screenshots.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.body:
Related: #201267

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, the **Connect your AI** page splits logins, API keys, and local models across several sections. ChatGPT sits under **More sign-in options** as **Codex login (browser)**, and the sign-in sheet asks for a code or redirect URL without saying what to copy.

## User Impact

- Pick ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, an API key, or a local model from one list. **More providers** opens the other options. Detected logins are labeled **On this Mac** or **On your Gateway** and are tested when picked.
- The selected provider's steps and connection test appear in the page. **Choose another AI** returns to the list. Gemini offers an API key when a Google sign-in is unavailable. The Gemini form keeps its provider when setup refreshes after a Gateway change.
- ChatGPT opens the browser directly. If OpenClaw cannot receive the browser response, it asks immediately for the address from the browser's address bar. Otherwise, the paste field appears after the 15-second wait and the existing one-second grace period. The browser can still finish sign-in while the field is open. The terminal login uses the same prompt.
- A failed ChatGPT test names ChatGPT and marks the card **Not connected**. The setup mascot has dark eyes without the teal highlights.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mac groups the options the Gateway reports and shows the selected provider's steps inline. The Gateway owns detection, sign-in, and the live connection test. The OpenAI plugin supplies the sign-in prompts for both the app and CLI.

## Evidence

The macOS VM captures compare main (`4442518e379`) with the onboarding build (`603cee2b93a`). [Independent macOS VM verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201296#issuecomment-7026820075) also checked the picker and inline ChatGPT card.

prs.title: fix(install): honor --beta and warn when a git install cannot resolve a release tag
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #201335 (reported by anmol0b). `install.sh --install-method git` ignores `--beta` and silently falls back to `main` when the latest release tag cannot be resolved.

Two defects in `resolve_git_openclaw_ref` (`scripts/install-policy.sh`):

1. **`--beta` is ignored for git installs.** `--beta` only sets `USE_BETA=1`; the resolver reads only `OPENCLAW_VERSION`, and `USE_BETA` was used only by the npm/Bun engine resolution that runs after the ref is already picked. So a git install with `--beta` checks out the stable release (or `main`), never the beta tag the install plan already advertises ("Beta channel: enabled").
2. **A fresh host without npm silently gets `main`.** `installer_npm view openclaw dist-tags.latest` runs before `ensure_node`, fails on a host that has not installed Node yet, the error is swallowed (`2>/dev/null || true`), and the resolver returns `main` — building unreleased `main` with no visible warning beyond a plain `Using git ref: main` line.

## Solution

Fix both in the shared release-resolution boundary (`resolve_git_openclaw_ref`):

- When `USE_BETA=1` and no explicit version is given, resolve the `beta` dist-tag instead of `latest`, matching how the npm and Bun engine channels already honor `--beta`. An explicit `OPENCLAW_VERSION` is never overridden.
- When the `latest` dist-tag lookup fails, keep returning `main` (the current behavior) but print a warning to stderr instead of doing so silently.

Review follow-up (commits `8a29688dda3` and `524a56ed00d`, ClawSweeper P1): routing `--beta` into the beta lookup without a fallback returned the literal string `beta` when that lookup failed (npm missing on a cold host, or no published beta tag). No `beta` git ref exists, so `checkout_git_openclaw_ref` aborted the install with `Requested git version not found: beta` — turning a working install into a hard failure. The resolver now honors the documented channel contract (`--beta`: use beta dist-tag if available, else fall back to `latest`, per the installer flags reference): a failed beta lookup retries `latest` with a stderr warning; only when both lookups fail does it fall back to `main` with the existing warning. This matches the npm engine path (`Could not resolve beta tag; using latest`) and the Bun engine path (beta → latest fallback) that already implement the same contract. The follow-up commit also normalizes npm variants that print `undefined`/`null` for a missing dist-tag (guarded the same way in install.sh's `resolve_beta_version`) so they resolve as unresolved instead of producing a literal `vundefined` ref.

The `main` fallback remains a visibility-only repair, not a behavior change: the offline/bootstrap fallback still installs `main`, exactly as today — but the user is now told. Resolving tags without npm (e.g. raw registry HTTP) would bypass the npm registry config (mirrors/`.npmrc`) that `npm view` honors — the same constraint the pre-existing `latest` lookup has on main — so this PR keeps npm-based resolution and makes every failure visible instead. The issue's expected behavior explicitly asks for this ("It does not quietly build `main`"); resolving the tag after Node is installed or failing outright would change bootstrap behavior and is a maintainer call, which this PR deliberately does not make. No new options, config, or persistence.

Explicit versions (`v1.2.3`, `beta`, `main`) behave exactly as before.

## Impact

Real user fault on first-run setup: a git install with `--beta` now checks out the beta tag, a host without npm is told that `main` is being used instead of silently building unreleased code, and the beta path can no longer abort on a nonexistent `beta` ref. ~20 production lines in one function.

## Evidence

- Regression (red/green): new tests in `test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts` —
  - `falls back to the latest release when the beta tag cannot be resolved` fails on base (`beta-missing=beta`) and passes with the fix (`beta-missing=v2026.5.12` + stderr warning); this is the P1 hard-failure regression.
  - `falls back to main with a warning when beta and latest both fail on a cold host` fails on base and passes with the fix.
  - `applies --beta to the git install ref when no explicit version is given` now actually clears `OPENCLAW_VERSION` for the empty case (review finding: it previously repeated the `latest` input).
- Installer-entry chain proof (new `installer entry` tests): the shipped resolver and checkout owner run against a real clone of a real local remote (offline fixture; npm presence controlled via PATH):
  - warm host `--beta` → selects `v2026.5.12-beta.3`, checks out the real tag (`kind=immutable`).
  - cold host without npm on PATH → selects `main` with `Warning: could not resolve the beta release tag (npm registry lookup failed); falling back to the main branch.`, checks out the real `main` branch (`kind=moving`) — previously a hard `Requested git version not found: beta` abort.
  - existing-install rerun with an explicit pin and `--beta` → `OPENCLAW_VERSION=v2026.5.12` wins, checkout moves off the beta tag to the pinned stable tag.
- Real-registry entry proof (local run against registry.npmjs.org, redacted): `npm view openclaw dist-tags.beta` → `2026.11.5`, `dist-tags.latest` → `2026.11.5`; shipped `scripts/install.sh` (sourced with `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_SH_NO_RUN=1`, the repo's `test-install-git-ref.sh` pattern) resolved `v2026.11.5` and checked out the real tag; rerun with `OPENCLAW_VERSION=v2026.11.4` moved the checkout to the pinned tag; cold-host rerun (Node toolchain dropped from PATH) selected `main` with the warning above and checked out `main`. All three scenarios PASS.
- **Normal-invocation proof (new — addresses the re-review blocker).** The shipped installer was executed end to end as a plain process (`bash scripts/install.sh --git …`, no `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_SH_NO_RUN`, no sourcing), covering all four required behaviors. GitHub was mirrored to a local bare remote through a per-run `git insteadOf` rewrite (installer code unmodified); dist-tag lookups hit a local registry stub via real `npm view` (the machine sits behind a proxy, so registry.npmjs.org is unreachable from the test host); every scenario ran with a fresh `HOME`. All four scenarios PASS:
  ### Setup
  - GitHub is mirrored to a local bare remote via per-run `git config url."file://…".insteadOf`; the installer still clones `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git` and runs unmodified (`bash scripts/install.sh`, no `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_SH_NO_RUN`).
  - npm dist-tag lookups go to a local registry stub (real `npm view` against a real HTTP registry); `dist-tags` are switched per scenario.
  - Fresh `HOME` per scenario; cold host = `PATH` limited to a tool symlink dir (git + coreutils; no node/npm/corepack/pnpm/curl/wget).
  - Fixture remote refs: `main` (1 commit past `v2026.11.6`), tags `v2026.11.4`, `v2026.11.5-beta.1`, `v2026.11.6`.
  
  ### S1 — warm host, `--beta`, beta tag available (dist-tags: latest=2026.11.4, beta=2026.11.5-beta.1)
  ```console
  · Installing OpenClaw from GitHub (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git)
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.5-beta.1
  ✓ Node.js v24.22.1 found
  🦞 OpenClaw installed successfully (0.0.0-fixture)!
  HEAD: d263ff48168c950087bb478c42671f1c3e9a0e83   # == tag v2026.11.5-beta.1 (remote)
  PASS — beta channel selected and installed.
  ```
  
  ### S2 — warm host, `--beta`, registry has no beta tag (dist-tags: latest=2026.11.4 only)
  ```console
  Warning: could not resolve the beta release tag; falling back to the latest stable release.
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.4
  🦞 OpenClaw installed successfully (0.0.0-fixture)!
  HEAD: 791b07e91a52edb736dae3329a42845fa1e52e12   # == tag v2026.11.4 (remote)
  PASS — warned, fell back to the latest stable tag.
  ```
  
  ### S3 — cold host (no npm on PATH), `--beta`
  ```console
  Warning: could not resolve the beta release tag (npm registry lookup failed); falling back to the main branch.
  · Using git ref: main
  · Checking out main
  · Node.js not found, installing it now
  ✗ sudo is required for system installs on Linux
  HEAD: 678a43df36b1f14ecae8ceff833a43fc0e8a2649   # == remote main (describe: v2026.11.6-1-g678a43d)
  PASS — warned and checked out main instead of hard-failing on the literal "beta".
  The run then stops at Node.js system provisioning ("sudo is required…"), which is outside this change and matches main-line behavior on hosts without a usable runtime.
  ```
  
  ### S4 — existing latest-stable install, rerun after `latest` moves; settings intact
  Pre-seeded user settings at `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (custom gateway port + marker field). Run 1 with dist-tags latest=2026.11.4:
  ```console
  · Installing OpenClaw from GitHub (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git)
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.4
  ✓ Doctor complete
  🦞 OpenClaw installed successfully (0.0.0-fixture)!
  HEAD: 791b07e91a52edb736dae3329a42845fa1e52e12   # == tag v2026.11.4 (remote)
  ```
  Registry `latest` bumped to 2026.11.6, installer rerun (no flags):
  ```console
  · Installing OpenClaw from git checkout: /tmp/<sandbox>/s4-rerun/home/openclaw
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.6
  ✓ Doctor complete
  🦞 OpenClaw installed successfully (0.0.0-fixture)!
  HEAD: 409fe81f540af1d78294202f0ae703016bbecd23   # == tag v2026.11.6 (remote)
  settings sha256 identical across runs: 5f82362402a7ecef8dc913604a76b3633fc0c31198f9cb8c0fa58673bfcc13b6
  PASS — checkout moved v2026.11.4 → v2026.11.6; user settings untouched.
  ```

- **Real latest-stable proof (new — addresses the remaining re-review item).** The shipped installer was run against the real GitHub remote and the real npm registry (no mirror, no registry stub) on actual latest-stable `v2026.11.5`, then rerun with a locally staged "next release". Normal invocation end to end, real clone (blobless), real `pnpm install` (~18 min build), real `openclaw doctor`. Machine facts: Linux host behind a corporate proxy (proxy host redacted), Node v24.22.1, per-run `HOME` under `/home/<user>/pr201349-s5`; UI build fails on this host (proxy) and the installer continues by design (warn-only).
  ### S5-1 — real install of actual latest-stable (registry.npmjs.org + github.com)
  ```console
  $ npm view openclaw dist-tags.latest        # real registry, through proxy
  2026.11.5
  $ bash scripts/install.sh --git --no-onboard --no-prompt
  · Installing OpenClaw from GitHub (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git)
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.5                 # resolved from real dist-tags
  · Checking out v2026.11.5
  · Active Node.js: v24.22.1
  ✓ pnpm ready (repo-pinned 12.15.0 via Corepack)
  · Installing dependencies
  · Building OpenClaw                           # full real build, ~18 min
  ✓ Doctor complete
  installer_rc: 0
  HEAD: e13cf15ece9bbd969b736292c90c97ff        # == tag v2026.11.5
  wrapper version: OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15) # installed CLI runs
  ```
  ### S5-2/3 — upgrade reruns from the real stable install
  The real registry's `latest` is still `2026.11.5`, so the "next release" was staged locally and disclosed as such: a registry stub reports `latest=2026.11.6` / `2026.11.7` and a bare remote (seeded by pushing the **real installed clone**, plus one marker commit per release) is wired through per-run `git insteadOf`; installer code unmodified. Staged releases carry the real v2026.11.5 content plus a marker file, so the CLI self-reports version `2026.11.5` (cosmetic only — the git checkout moves).
  ```console
  # settings created product-natively on the real install:
  $ openclaw config set gateway.port 18789
  Updated gateway.port. Restart the gateway to apply.
  settings sha256: f6db85b8359e…                              # before upgrade reruns

  $ bash scripts/install.sh --git --no-onboard --no-prompt    # latest=2026.11.6
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.6
  ✓ Doctor complete
  installer_rc: 0   HEAD: 6d86b492b62a…   describe: v2026.11.6   # moved off v2026.11.5

  $ bash scripts/install.sh --git --no-onboard --no-prompt    # latest=2026.11.7
  · Using git ref: v2026.11.7
  ✓ Doctor complete
  installer_rc: 0   HEAD: 235059ea2624…   describe: v2026.11.7
  settings sha256: 3417b8021fb5…                                # after doctor migration
  openclaw config get gateway.port → 18789                      # user value intact
  ```
  Doctor's one-time migration between those hashes is additive only — it appends default `agents`/`skills`/`wizard` bookkeeping blocks; the user-set `gateway.port: 18789` and all prior content are preserved verbatim (full diff available on request).
  ### S5-4 — settings stability across a further rerun
  ```console
  $ bash scripts/install.sh --git --no-onboard --no-prompt      # same release, rerun
  installer_rc: 0   describe: v2026.11.7
  settings sha256: 3417b8021fb5…  (identical to before the rerun — byte-for-byte)
  openclaw config get gateway.port → 18789
  PASS — on a real latest-stable install, upgrade reruns move the checkout and preserve existing settings.
  ```

- Commands (all green locally):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts test/scripts/install-sh-beta.test.ts test/scripts/install-sh.provisioning.test.ts test/scripts/install-git-ref.test.ts test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 239 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing), no regressions in the touched suite.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (the other consumer of `install-policy.sh`) — passed.
  - `/bin/bash -n scripts/install-policy.sh scripts/install.sh scripts/install-cli.sh`; `git diff --check`.
- Local review: shared autoreview helper attempted (codex engine) — unavailable in this environment (`api.openai.com` 403 on the model websocket), no report produced; gap disclosed rather than claimed. Independent local review of `origin/main...HEAD` (both commits) by a fresh reviewer agent instead: **no P1/P2 findings**; three P3s — two fixed in `524a56ed00d` (undefined-dist-tag guard; beta-missing test mock now mimics real npm exit-0-empty behavior), one recorded here as a pre-existing follow-up: `--version next` with an unresolvable `next` dist-tag echoes the literal `next` and fails checkout identically on current main (no documented fallback contract for `next`, so behavior intentionally unchanged).

## Collision note

#201350 was opened 94 seconds after this PR for the same issue. It fixes only the `--beta` half and defers the silent-main fallback to a maintainer call; this PR covers both reported defects, the review-found beta fallback hard failure, and now includes installer-entry proof.

## Related precedent

#188005 fixed the npm-only `--beta` path on a fresh host; this closes the git-install gap in the same shape, and the beta→latest fallback mirrors the Bun engine channel's existing behavior.

prs.title: fix: show why a trusted-proxy sign-in was rejected when the web app has no device identity
prs.body:
Closes #202750

## What Problem This Solves

When a Control UI connection without a device identity fails a trusted-proxy check, the Gateway replies "web app requires device identity (use HTTPS or localhost secure context)" and drops the trusted-proxy reason. Operators following the trusted-proxy troubleshooting guide look for reasons such as `trusted_proxy_missing_header_*` or `trusted_proxy_user_not_allowed`, but neither the response nor the Gateway log shows one, and the message points at HTTPS instead.

## User Impact

The rejection now includes the failed check as `details.authReason`, and the Gateway's close log records it as `authReason`. The error code, message and the decision to reject are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The device-less Control UI branch in the connect handler sent `CONTROL_UI_DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED` without reading the auth result. It now adds the auth reason when auth did not succeed, the same field the general unauthorized path already returns. Successful auth adds nothing, so token and password clients that only lack a device identity see the same response as before.

## Evidence

- Base, live: OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (d119c6b, same code path as `main` at b8b173b6697), trusted-proxy Gateway on loopback. A device-less Control UI connect with a missing required header, and one with a user outside `allowUsers`, both return the same error with no reason. The Gateway log for both has only `failureCause=control-ui-insecure-auth`, and no `trusted_proxy_` string.
- Head, live: the same two probes against a Gateway built from this branch (same trusted-proxy settings, scratch config and state) now return `authReason: "trusted_proxy_missing_header_x-eval-proxy"` and `authReason: "trusted_proxy_user_not_allowed"`, and the Gateway close log records the same reasons. Code, message and rejection are unchanged.
- Head, tests: `pnpm test src/gateway/server.auth.control-ui.test.ts` passes (50 tests). The existing loopback case now asserts `authReason: "trusted_proxy_loopback_source"`, and a new case asserts `authReason: "trusted_proxy_missing_header_x-forwarded-proto"`.
- Mutation check: with only the fix reverted (`git apply -R`), both assertions fail with `authReason` missing from the details.
- Related tests pass: `src/gateway/server.auth.modes.test.ts` (asserts the same error code for token auth without a device) and `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-policy.test.ts`.
- Local review: ClawSweeper `review --local-range` against `origin/main` at head 547d90f, `review_status: complete`, checkout access verified. Patch B, "patch is correct", no findings, security cleared ("unauthenticated clients already get the same `authReason` values on the unauthorized path"). Proof D and overall C because a local-range review sees only the commits, not the runtime output above.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, format and the other guards pass. The dead export scan fails on `extensions/knowledge/src/scribe-schedule-dialog.ts: CronSchedule`, a file this change does not touch.

<details>
<summary>Runtime output, base (2026.11.5)</summary>

```text
--- A3: required header x-eval-proxy missing
CONNECT FAILED {"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"web app requires device identity (use HTTPS or localhost secure context)","details":{"code":"CONTROL_UI_DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED"}}
--- A4: user not in allowUsers
CONNECT FAILED {"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"web app requires device identity (use HTTPS or localhost secure context)","details":{"code":"CONTROL_UI_DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED"}}
--- gateway log
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ connect 0ms bytes=246 failurePhase=auth failureCause=control-ui-insecure-auth conn=4aa8fb7e…c50a
[ws] closed before connect conn=4aa8fb7e-... remote=127.0.0.1 fwd=10.99.0.50 code=1006 cause=control-ui-insecure-auth handshake=failed ... insecureAuthConfigured=false client=openclaw-control-ui mode=webchat
--- any trusted_proxy_ reason in the new log lines:
0
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Runtime output, head (this branch, built with pnpm build)</summary>

```text
--- A3: required header x-eval-proxy missing
CONNECT FAILED {"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"web app requires device identity (use HTTPS or localhost secure context)","details":{"code":"CONTROL_UI_DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED","authReason":"trusted_proxy_missing_header_x-eval-proxy"}}
--- A4: user not in allowUsers
CONNECT FAILED {"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"web app requires device identity (use HTTPS or localhost secure context)","details":{"code":"CONTROL_UI_DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED","authReason":"trusted_proxy_user_not_allowed"}}
--- gateway log
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ connect 2ms bytes=303 failurePhase=auth failureCause=control-ui-insecure-auth conn=74c81617…4b14
[ws] closed before connect conn=74c81617-... remote=127.0.0.1 fwd=10.99.0.50 code=1006 cause=control-ui-insecure-auth handshake=failed ... insecureAuthConfigured=false authReason=trusted_proxy_missing_header_x-eval-proxy client=openclaw-control-ui mode=webchat
[ws] closed before connect conn=2145ef3b-... remote=127.0.0.1 fwd=10.99.0.50 code=1006 cause=control-ui-insecure-auth handshake=failed ... insecureAuthConfigured=false authReason=trusted_proxy_user_not_allowed client=openclaw-control-ui mode=webchat
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Mutation check output (fix reverted)</summary>

```text
FAIL  src/gateway/server.auth.control-ui.test.ts > gateway server auth/connect > requires device identity when loopback trusted-proxy authentication is rejected
- Expected
+ Received
  {
-   "authReason": "trusted_proxy_loopback_source",
    "code": "CONTROL_UI_DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED",
  }
FAIL  ... > reports the trusted-proxy reason when a required proxy header is missing
-   "authReason": "trusted_proxy_missing_header_x-forwarded-proto",
```

</details>

Not checked: a real browser. A browser on localhost or HTTPS sends a device identity and takes a different path; this change only affects device-less Control UI connects.

prs.title: fix(ui): restore Skills first-visit asset limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Skills after a settled New Session exceeds the existing first-visit asset limits. Dedicated skill pages added requests before the list becomes ready.

## User Impact

Skills and Skill Settings reach readiness within their existing request limits. Installed-skill and ClawHub detail renderers remain lazy; no limit or performance tolerance changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep list boundaries with their pages, catalog cards with their loading skeleton, and shared Skills presentation with dependencies those consumers already load. Preserve the existing `skills-shared` chunk name. Make two route helpers private because their only caller is in the same module.

The shared presentation also serves Agents; card-only consumers receive the small catalog skeleton. No page renderer is added to either shared group.

## Evidence

- The [original browser baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44812417546/job/136553156130) measured 32 Skills requests against 28 and 33 Skill Settings requests against 31.
- The [ready-event browser job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44827859230/job/136605819805) passes all four first-visit route cases on `8a66e6a2d166`, including both unchanged Skills limits and the installed-detail lazy-loading interaction.
- The [ready-event performance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44827859230/job/136605819342) passes. The [earlier exact-head measurement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44825803181/job/136598947794) reports Chat startup gzip of 1,333,245 bytes versus 1,333,213 bytes on its base: +32 bytes within the unchanged 64-byte allowance.
- Formatting, whitespace checks and fresh local review pass. No actionable correctness or security findings. Local dependencies are unqualified; execution proof is hosted.

## Inherited CI Failures

The [completed ready-event run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44827859230) remains red on two independent browser jobs. Every failed case also fails on scheduled main; the tested merge changes none of their test or runtime inputs. The job-name-only CI classification was checked against actual failures across shards:

prs.title: fix: let Docker config and channel commands work while the Gateway runs
prs.body:
Fixes #202040

## What Problem This Solves

With the shipped Docker Compose file, `openclaw-cli` cannot change config or add a channel once the Gateway is running. Before a write, the CLI checks that the running Gateway owns the shared state, and `openclaw-cli` runs in a different PID namespace from the Gateway, so the check cannot verify the owner and the write is refused. The documented `docker compose run --rm openclaw-cli channels add ...` step hits this. So does `./scripts/docker/setup.sh`, which writes config through `openclaw-cli` after starting the Gateway: it can print `WARNING: Failed to reset agents.defaults.sandbox.mode to off`, and with `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX=1` it cannot turn sandbox mode on.

## User Impact

User impact: with the default Compose stack, `openclaw-cli` config commands and `channels add` reach the running Gateway instead of being refused, and `setup.sh` applies its sandbox settings.

### Upgrade notes

- Update the Compose file, not just the image. Pulling a new image leaves an existing `docker-compose.yml` as it was, and without the new `pid` line on `openclaw-cli` these commands stay refused while the Gateway runs. Take the Compose file from the release you are upgrading to (`git pull` in a source checkout). If you maintain your own `openclaw-cli` service, set both `network_mode` and `pid` to `service:openclaw-gateway` and drop `init: true`.
- Stopping or recreating the Gateway container now also ends any open `openclaw-cli` session or TUI. Start it again once the Gateway is back.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openclaw-cli` already shared the Gateway's network, and with it the hostname, so the PID namespace was the only part of the ownership check that could not match. The service now sets `pid: "service:openclaw-gateway"`, the line the Compose operations guide used to suggest as an override. The decision to make PID sharing the default is recorded in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202288#issuecomment-7051833433).

The CLI service also drops `init: true`. In the shared namespace the Gateway's docker-init is PID 1 and reaps orphaned processes. A second docker-init would not be PID 1 and would print a warning on every command.

Once the CLI can see the Gateway as the owner, its writes go to the Gateway's listener. `setup.sh` issued them right after `docker compose up -d`, before the listener accepts connections. It now runs the image's own health check through `docker compose exec` and waits up to 180 seconds before those writes. If the Gateway never reports healthy, it prints a warning with the logs command and continues, so a slow Gateway does not abort setup.

The Docker docs describe the shared PID namespace, and the security note says the CLI container can see and signal Gateway processes; it already receives the same Gateway token and state mounts. The `compose-setup` Docker E2E gains a config write through `openclaw-cli` while the Gateway runs, read back from inside the Gateway.

Compose has resolved `pid: service:<name>` since v2.1.0. The file's `env_file` `required:` entries already need a later Compose release, so this adds no new version requirement.

## Evidence

Real Docker Compose runs:

- Config write while the Gateway runs, on Linux arm64 under Colima (Docker 29.5.2, Compose 5.5.1), with the same source-built image on both sides. On the base, `openclaw-cli config set agents.defaults.sandbox.mode off` was refused with `cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process` and exited 1, and the Gateway still read back `non-main`. With this change it printed `Updated agents.defaults.sandbox.mode. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.`, exited 0, and the Gateway read back `off`. Screenshots are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202288#issuecomment-7048270977).
- The shipped `scripts/docker/setup.sh --offline` on this head, on Linux arm64 (Docker Engine 29.10.0, Compose 5.7.1). Plain setup reached `Waiting for gateway health...`, the Gateway became healthy, and `sandbox.mode` changed from `non-main` to `off`. With sandbox enabled, setup exited 0 and the recreated, healthy Gateway read back `mode=non-main`, `scope=agent` and `workspaceAccess=none`. Details are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202288#issuecomment-7050521450).
- An upgrade from the published v2026.11.6 image over the same state. This head still reports 2026.11.5, so the candidate stopped at the older-binary guard as designed, and the saved credential record and workspace bytes were unchanged. With the same patch applied to a 2026.11.6 `main`, the candidate Gateway became healthy and kept a custom setting, the saved credential record and the workspace bytes (same comment).

Local checks, without a Docker daemon:

- `test/scripts/docker-setup.test.ts` passes 27 of 27 with this patch on current `main`, where none of the six changed files differ from this head. The new test, "waits for Gateway health before runtime CLI config writes", fails against `main`'s `setup.sh` (the health-wait index is `-1`) and passes with this change in about 1.8 s. The five sandbox-path tests bind a Unix socket to stand in for the Docker socket, which my environment refuses, so they ran from a copy that links an existing socket instead, with the assertions unchanged.
- `docker compose config` resolves `openclaw-cli` with `pid: service:openclaw-gateway` and no `init`.
- `bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` are clean on `scripts/docker/setup.sh` and `scripts/e2e/compose-setup.sh`. oxlint is clean on the test file. `oxfmt --check`, docs markdownlint with the repo config and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local autoreview was not available in my environment. ClawSweeper reviewed this head and reported no findings.

Not run: `channels add` with real channel credentials (it goes through the same ownership check as `config set`), `pnpm test:docker:compose-setup`, and Docker Desktop on macOS or Windows.
