prs.title: fix(database): report disabled memory search after a port
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

A successful database port reports `disabled` when an agent has memory search turned off. The terminal and JSON output omit the retry warning for that agent.

## What Problem This Solves

With `memory.search.enabled: false`, the port completed with exit 0 but printed `Memory index (main): failed.` It advised running `openclaw memory index --agent main`, which exited 0 and printed `Memory search disabled.`

## User Impact

Terminal output and `--json` distinguish disabled memory search from an index failure that needs attention.

## Why This Change Was Made

The port uses the memory runtime’s acquisition result to distinguish disabled search from a real failure. Real failures still get retry guidance.

## Root Cause

Memory Core returns a null manager without an error for disabled search. The port used only the manager field and treated all null managers as unavailable plugins. The regression reached a completed PostgreSQL port on the baseline and received `failed` plus retry guidance where it expected `disabled`. The port now reads the acquisition error and still reports real failures with the existing warning.

## Real behavior proof

RAN on Linux, Node 26.13.1 and disposable PostgreSQL 17.12 over a private Unix socket. Seeded an agent SQLite store with Memory Core selected and `memory.search.enabled: false`. Built the runtime and ran these commands with isolated state.

| Command | Baseline | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node openclaw.mjs database port --family agent --to postgres` | Exit 0, `Memory index (main): failed.` and a retry warning | Exit 0, `Memory index (main): disabled.` and no rebuild warning |
| `node openclaw.mjs memory index --agent main` | Exit 0, `Memory search disabled.` | Exit 0, `Memory search disabled.` |
| `node openclaw.mjs database port --family agent --to sqlite --json` | Exit 0, `phase: complete`, `status: failed`, and a warning | Exit 0, `phase: complete`, `status: disabled`, and no warning |

## What was not tested

- Paid model calls, live embedding providers, a running Gateway, and stable-release upgrades.
- Port throughput was not measured. The change only reports the outcome of manager acquisition.

## Evidence

The existing mixed-engine round-trip now checks both port directions with the real bundled memory runtime and search disabled. It asserts the full per-agent result, including the absence of retry guidance. It also checks that the seeded agent row survives and the unrelated Workboard database stays unchanged.

Autoreview covered the full diff from the [base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1fbcec108f4e4ed21c698d82e31e7ce23498b342) through the [candidate](https://github.com/VACInc/openclaw/commit/8d3222dbc6cca5920c1366756829780792c8f22c) at priorities P0 through P3. It found no actionable defects. The committed diff matches the reviewed snapshot.

## Verification

- The candidate applies cleanly to [current main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9159d33262bf43105535184c977c53e5c918286c).

- `pnpm build:runtime` passed on the baseline and fixed source.
- `git diff --check` and focused formatting passed.
- `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$DISPOSABLE_PG_DSN" -- src/infra/database-engine/port-command.mixed.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The agent round-trip failed on the baseline with `failed` plus retry guidance. All 8 tests passed with the fix (267 seconds wall time). The regression adds assertions to the existing round-trip and adds no port operations.
- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-database-port-memory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed (6 tests, 116 seconds wall time).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and focused `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json` passed.

- Repeated the focused agent round-trip on current main with a disposable PostgreSQL 17 cluster and the CI extensions. Main failed with `status: failed` and retry guidance. Applying the candidate to the same main revision passed both port directions. An initial local setup lacked `unaccent` and stopped before the assertion.

Related: #202146, #134994, #201282

## What Problem This Solves

People who run OpenClaw on a local model server don't learn from the docs that the default Proactive check sends
the main conversation's whole prompt to their model every 30 minutes, even when it has no way to reach them. On a
server with one or two parallel slots it also pushes the conversation they are using out of the prompt cache.

## User Impact

The local models page now says what the job costs on a local server, how to find it, and how to turn it off, run
it less often, or move it to a smaller model. Docs only; no behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cost shows up only in server logs. On one install with a local llama.cpp server (two 65,536-token slots), the
default job made 344 requests in 6 days with a median prompt of 51,212 tokens: 62% of all prompt tokens the server
processed. No channel was configured, so every run ended with `Owner delivery unavailable (no-route)` (details in
#202146). The section points to the existing commands. If #201282 lands and removes `skipIfScratchEmpty`, the
second bullet should go.

prs.title: fix: keep search current after small PostgreSQL transcript rewrites
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Small PostgreSQL transcript rewrites now update search in the same transaction. Ingress health counts and cold transcript archive totals are numbers in the returned data.

## What Problem This Solves

Rewriting an existing transcript that fits the synchronous byte budget can briefly hide its messages from search while the index catches up. PostgreSQL can also return quoted counts and byte totals where readers expect numbers.

## User Impact

Search reflects a small rewrite as soon as it commits. Queue and archive clients can read counts and byte totals as numbers. No migration is required.

## Root Cause

PostgreSQL returns `SUM(bigint)` as `numeric`. The PostgreSQL driver leaves `numeric` as text, while OpenClaw's existing `bigint` decoder returns safe integers as numbers. A real server replay returned `"5000"` for the raw sum, yielding `"5000300"` when adding 300 incoming bytes. The invalid total crosses the 4 MiB rebuild cap. The ingress and cold inventory queries similarly returned their sums as text. The cold inventory regression received `"203"` for a 203-byte embedded archive.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cast these integer aggregates to `BIGINT` in their existing queries. The queries keep their filters, null handling, and rebuild caps. The casts use the numeric result path already used by nearby transcript queries and count fields.

## Real behavior proof

The focused transcript rewrite regression was replayed on the PR base `8832901915fb` with PostgreSQL 18 and `unaccent`. With the test alone, Vitest failed with `expected true to be false` at the in-transaction reconciliation assertion. With the sizing fix applied to that base, one selected test passed. The test also queries search after commit for both the replacement and the old text. Use the conformance command below with just the search test file and add `-t "indexes a small replacement"`.

With PostgreSQL 18.7 on a private Unix socket, the production replacement transaction left `needsReconcile: true` on the base for a roughly 54 KB transcript. The same production transaction left `needsReconcile: false` with the patch. A search of the committed replacement found the new message and no longer found the replaced message. On the same private server, the ingress worker returned three quoted counts on the base. After the fix, the foreground Gateway returned `{"pendingCount":1,"claimedCount":1,"blockedCount":1}` via `openclaw health --json`.

## Evidence

The rewrite replay seeded a fresh session for each sample on the same local server. Across five warmups and 20 measured replacement transactions, median commit time was 8.31 ms on the base and 10.74 ms with the patch. p90 was 10.56 ms and 16.27 ms. With the fix, the measured transaction also publishes the search projection. The measurement excludes deferred reconciliation and does not estimate total rebuild cost.

Autoreview covered the complete patch against base `1fbcec108f4e4` at P0–P2 and reported no actionable findings. Simplification kept the casts inside the three existing queries and reused the existing search and archival fixtures.

## Verification

A fresh `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` on the pushed head also completed successfully. The Control UI build printed advisory size-budget warnings.
Seven PostgreSQL tests and 54 SQLite sibling tests passed. Focused type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Local PostgreSQL project durations were 135 seconds for the search suite, 27 seconds for cold inventory and selection, and 49 seconds for ingress health, including setup. The local runs used the pushed patch and its original base. A three-way merge against current main completed cleanly. Hosted CI passed on this head, including the artifact build, all four PostgreSQL conformance shards, the PostgreSQL 16 smoke job, and the required CI gate. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44785119876

```sh
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TEST_DSN" -- \
  src/infra/database-engine/session-search-product.postgres.test.ts \
  src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage-selection.postgres.test.ts \
  src/infra/database-engine/ingress-queue-health.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

## What was not tested

Production state, paid model providers, other PostgreSQL server majors, and total background reconciliation latency were outside this proof.

prs.title: docs: show how to test roles locally with a same-host proxy
prs.body:
Closes #202751

## What Problem This Solves

Someone evaluating multiplayer roles on one machine has no documented way to give test accounts their own sign-in. Token and password auth sign everyone in as the shared owner, which cannot hold a role, and the trusted-proxy pages assume a real identity provider. Two details also trip up a same-host setup: the Gateway rejects a loopback client address from a proxy, and a role only caps scopes, so an account without an `identityScopes` grant connects with none.

## User Impact

Operators can try roles locally with a short, tested recipe, and the recipe states plainly that this setup lets any local process act as any allowed account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new "Test roles locally" section in the multiplayer quick setup uses only existing settings: trusted-proxy auth with `allowLoopback`, `allowUsers`, `identityScopes`, `gateway.roles`, the local Gateway password for maintenance commands, and `users.setRole` by profile ID after each first sign-in. The proxy example is a Caddy basic-auth site that overwrites `X-Forwarded-User` and sends a fixed documentation address (`192.0.2.10`) as the client address. The warning repeats the `allowLoopback` risk from the trusted-proxy page in this context, and lists how to keep the test narrow.

## Evidence

The recipe was run on OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (d119c6b) on macOS with Caddy 2.11.9. Ports in the run were 18830 (Gateway) and 18831 (Caddy) instead of the 18789 and 8080 in the docs; nothing else differs.

- The Gateway config from the recipe passes `openclaw config validate` (`"valid":true,"warnings":[]`). The Caddyfile passes `caddy validate`.
- First sign-in creates each profile with the default role. `users.setRole` by profile ID then assigns `administrator` and `member`; by email it is refused.
- After reconnecting, Alice has `operator.admin`, Bob has `operator.read` and `operator.write`, and Bob is denied an administrator method.
- Through the proxy without credentials: HTTP 401. Bob sending his own `X-Forwarded-User: alice@example.test` through the proxy still connects as Bob.
- A local client that skips the proxy and sends forged headers straight to the Gateway port connects with `operator.admin`. This is the behavior the warning describes.
- `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` (the new JSON5 block is schema-checked) and `pnpm check:changed` pass. `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` finds no broken link in `docs/start/multiplayer.md`; it reports 7 broken links elsewhere that are already present on `main`.
- Local review: ClawSweeper `review --local-range` against `origin/main` at head 6262add, `review_status: complete`, checkout access verified. Overall B, patch B, proof not applicable (docs only). No findings; security cleared ("describes an existing opt-in loopback trust mode with an accurate impersonation warning").

<details>
<summary>Runtime output (2026.11.5, credentials not printed)</summary>

```text
=== 1. First sign-in through Caddy (creates each profile)
[alice] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.sessions.read"]
[bob] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.sessions.read"]
=== 2. Profiles after first sign-in
alice@example.test id=219e263c-... role=- effectiveRole=viewer roleSource=default
bob@example.test id=4f383f74-... role=- effectiveRole=viewer roleSource=default
=== 3. Assign roles by profile id
alice -> administrator: ok
bob -> member: ok
--- users.setRole with an email instead of a profile id:
```

prs.title: fix: reject blank audit filters instead of listing every record
prs.body:
Root cause: src/commands/audit.ts:587 builds the activity query with truthy spreads (`...(options.agentId ? { agentId } : {})`), so a blank `--agent`/`--session`/`--run`/`--channel`/`--cursor` is dropped and the query widens to every record; the Gateway owner does the same for whitespace ids at src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts:109-111, where `normalizeOptionalString` turns `" "` into no filter.

Fixes #199947

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw audit --agent ""` (for example from an unset shell variable) exits 0 and lists every agent's audit records, the same as running `openclaw audit` with no filter. The same happens for `--session`, `--run`, `--execution`, `--channel` and `--cursor`, and for any Gateway client that sends a whitespace-only `agentId`, `sessionKey` or `runId` to `audit.list` or `audit.activity.list`.

## User Impact

User impact: a blank audit filter now fails instead of silently widening the report. The CLI prints `<flag> must not be blank.` and exits 1 before calling the Gateway; the Gateway answers a whitespace-only id with `invalid <method> filters: <field> must not be blank`. Valid filters, padded ids such as `" main "`, the reader scope and the returned fields are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI now checks its free-text flags up front, using the existing `<flag> must not be blank` wording from the cron and capability CLIs (`src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts`, `src/cli/capability-cli/shared.ts`). The Gateway already rejects `""` through the protocol schema (`minLength: 1`) but trimmed whitespace-only ids away afterwards, so its list handlers now reject those before reading the store, next to the existing filter and cursor checks.

Thanks @wangmiao0668000666 for the clear report and @ericcurtin for the CLI fix this builds on.

## Evidence

- Real CLI against an isolated fixture Gateway with records for two agents: on main `openclaw audit --agent "" --json`, `--agent " "`, `--channel ""` and `gateway call audit.activity.list --params '{"agentId":" "}'` all return both agents' 4 records with exit 0. On this head they exit 1 with `--agent must not be blank.`, `--channel must not be blank.` and `invalid audit.activity.list filters: agentId must not be blank`. Control: `--agent alpha` and `{"agentId":"alpha"}` return only alpha's 2 records on both. Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201762#issuecomment-7006067953
- The added cases in `src/commands/audit.test.ts` (6) and `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts` (2) fail on main and pass here; `audit.trim.store.test.ts` still passes, so padded ids keep matching.

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert restores the old behavior and nothing is written or migrated. Blast radius: only callers that send blank audit filters, which now get an error instead of an unfiltered page.

<details>
<summary>Agent transcript (trimmed)</summary>

**User:** Find the open issue you are most confident fixing that has no PR, and open a PR. Keep code deduplicated, comments and messages very short.

**Agent:** Listed open issues with a clear fix shape and no open PR. Picked #199947 (small, source-proven, earlier fix #193704 was only closed to free quota).

**Agent:** Added one blank-value check at the top of `auditListCommand` covering the six selectors, plus six test cases.

**Agent:** Ran the tests without the fix (6 failed) and with it (31 passed). Ran `pnpm openclaw audit --agent ""` and got `--agent must not be blank.` with exit 1.

</details>

The multiplayer quick setup lists three ways to give a team access to the Gateway. The "Shared secret" option says token or password auth works for small teams and links to "Authentication". That page covers model provider auth (API keys, OAuth, Claude CLI reuse), so someone setting up team access lands on the wrong topic.

People following the multiplayer guide reach the `gateway.auth` token and password settings from that link.

## What Problem This Solves

Opening a skill from a Customize plugin detail page shows the entire bundle and its assets in a wide file browser. The file tree takes space away from the document people clicked to read.

## User Impact

Plugin skill rows now open a narrow, read-only `SKILL.md` dialog. The header pairs the skill icon and name with the plugin publisher and the first sentence of the skill description, when available. The frame stays put while the document loads or is retried, and long documents scroll inside it. The reader has no file-browsing or installation controls. Skills marketplace pages, Templates, and Skill Workshop are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing versioned skill-read request already returns the declared entry without fetching sibling bodies. The reader uses just that entry, renders sanitized Markdown, keeps ordinary external links, and leaves bundle-relative labels as text instead of navigating elsewhere. It uses the native modal without rerendering the launching row on preview updates, so Close and Escape can return focus to that row.

prs.title: fix: preserve the running installation when an agent updates its Gateway
prs.body:
Related: #200978

## What Problem This Solves

The current agent guidance requires an exact revision before an agent can use Git to update its own Gateway, even when the service already runs directly from that checkout. Selecting a different method can change how the Gateway starts: [the built-in Git updater can redirect a directly served checkout to a release launcher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/053fb62c614/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-git.ts#L657-L685).

## User Impact

Standard installations still use the built-in updater. On a directly served Git checkout, an ordinary owner update request can use the documented in-place procedure without an exact revision, but only when the host independently authorizes it for that caller. Other Git updates retain the exact-revision requirement. The agent reports a blocker rather than guessing, and switching installation methods remains a separate operator request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identifying the installation was not enough: in the earlier live Git test at `59120292`, the agent checked status and still chose the built-in updater, which deferred to the external supervisor. The shared prompt now distinguishes standard installs from the narrow source-server exception and tells the agent to consult the host or installation documentation. Runtime permissions and the built-in slash-command, Control UI, and scheduled update routes are unchanged. The chat update guide reflects the distinction.

## Evidence

**Gateway owner regression (`bc86ee2`):** Both Slack/launchd and Discord/foreground cases reproduced the old prompt-anchor failure before the test-only fix. The updated test reads the advertised built-in `update.run` action and still exercises the real tool and handler path, checking requester attribution and restart handoff. All 17 Gateway owner tests passed locally (60 seconds wall time); targeted Gateway-methods typecheck, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. No runtime code changed in this commit.

**Separate baseline CI failure:** The two Skills route asset-request assertions that failed on [the previous PR head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44821779869/job/136586308496) also failed on [scheduled `main` CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44820277164/job/136579802901), down to the same deferred asset. This is evidence for those two assertions, not a blanket exception for another failure or a later head.

**Prompt proof (`a813c514`):** The four new prompt regression cases failed on the prior renderer and passed with the narrowed guidance. All 125 focused tests passed, including regular/native prompt parity and tool-prefix stability. Six generated prompt snapshots matched; targeted agents typecheck, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Codex autoreview (P0–P2, `7a4298bf` to `a813c514`) produced a scoped-clean report. The live update scenarios below were run on the earlier `c7371f38` head, not rerun on the later heads.

**Stable-to-candidate upgrade (operator-driven npm).** Started the integrity-verified public npm release 2026.11.5 (`e13cf15e`) with 13 existing configuration values, upgraded the same npm installation to the reviewed runtime (`c7371f38`), and restarted the Gateway. The candidate had an unpublished fixture version label; all 17,065 packaged JavaScript files matched the reviewed build.

| Observation | Public stable | Candidate after restart |
|---|---|---|
| Serving PID | 111 | 412 |
| Health / readiness / startup | 200 / 200 / 200 | 200 / 200 / 200 |
| SQLite schema / quick_check | 36 / ok | 40 / ok |

The CLI and config paths stayed the same. All 13 original values survived unchanged; migration added 14 keys. Authenticated `config.get` confirmed seven selected values on the running candidate, including a 343-second agent timeout and disabled cron. This verifies upgrade compatibility, separately from the agent-driven tests below.

**The Git installation successfully updated in place.** On PR head `c7371f38`, the authenticated owner sent only **“Update yourself.”** In an isolated directly served Git installation, a real model inspected the checkout, installation docs and host lifecycle commands. It chose and ran the documented source update under the existing supervisor. No operator performed the update or supplied a target or command in chat.

Independent observations across restart (780 samples):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Checkout and serving build | `c7371f38` | `101b2f54` (test target integrating upstream #201557) |
| Gateway PID | 133 | 5973 |
| Health, readiness, startup | 200 / 200 / 200 | 200 / 200 / 200 |

The checkout path, Gateway launch command, service definition and configuration matched before and after. The source updater logged `OK 101b2f5447a (main)`; the new process and its build identity were checked independently, not inferred from the agent's reply.

**Global npm installation: same request, different procedure.** The starting fixture was an unpublished npm prerelease containing this PR's runtime, labeled `2026.11.5-beta.201570`. The agent read the installed documentation and selected `update.run`. The updater used npm to stage the genuine public stable `2026.11.5` package (build `e13cf15e`, npm exit 0). Activation was correctly refused: the starting state used schema 40 and the release supports only 36. Across 176 observations, the original package path, serving build, PID 177 and config stayed unchanged and healthy. This verifies npm selection and safe refusal, **not** a completed npm upgrade. An explicitly requested migration was not live-tested.

Both disposable test Gateways and their temporary model credentials were removed.

ChatGPT sign-in in macOS setup starts with technical OAuth instructions. The paste step also asks for an authorization code or redirect URL, which can be unfamiliar when someone is setting up OpenClaw.

Choosing ChatGPT starts browser sign-in immediately. About 16 seconds later, OpenClaw offers to accept the address from the browser's address bar while sign-in stays active. If OpenClaw cannot start the callback listener, it shows paste instructions immediately. The same wording and timing apply in the terminal. Remote and VPS sign-in keeps its walkthrough.

## Evidence

I ran `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --method oauth` with isolated state on macOS. Times start at the CLI's browser handoff. A separate listener held the callback port for the unavailable-listener case. I deferred browser interaction for the delayed case.

| Scenario | [Main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c2e7b54ab6f5adc693d04fe53a992d4c0458bb43) | [PR head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8245e0b31f47018ea1356e838c4d9bd318625100) |

prs.title: fix(control-ui): retain dismissed failures across cron pause
prs.body:
Closes #202652

## What Problem This Solves

Dismissing a failed automation in the Inbox, then pausing and enabling its schedule, brings the same failure back even though no new run occurred. This happens when the All agents inventory refresh treats the paused job's hidden row as a resolved failure.

## User Impact

A dismissed failure stays hidden across pause, enable, and page reload. A later failed run or automatic-disable incident still appears. Existing saved dismissals are retained; recovered or removed jobs stop retaining them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dismissal retention now follows the underlying failure instead of whether its row is currently visible. Failures are identified by their recorded run or automatic-disable time, and existing job-only dismissals are bound to the currently known failures. A row may represent both a failed run and an automatic-disable incident; dismissing it acknowledges both, so clearing one cause does not revive the other. Paused-job visibility and other Inbox categories are unchanged.

## Evidence

The actual built Control UI was exercised in Chromium through the repository's E2E harness with synthetic Gateway WebSocket responses. On the base revision, dismiss → pause → enable returned the old row and failed the assertion. With the fix, the old row stayed absent and a distinct later failure appeared. This verifies the UI boundary, not a live scheduler or provider.

Before: the same dismissed failure returns after enabling.

![Before: Archive check returns in the Inbox after pause and enable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b3fe9cd-d7f3-434d-9c77-e6185894ca21)

After: the same failure stays dismissed.

![After: the Inbox remains empty after enabling the same failed job](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9d1d592-cfc3-44e0-8a4f-8245a5268544)

Both captures use the same 1440×900 viewport, light theme, synthetic job and All agents scope. Before is `dc73ec0bac`; after is this patch. No layout or styling change.

The permanent store regression covers persistence across a paused reload, a later failure, recovery, removal, and legacy job-only dismissals. Additional regressions reproduced automatic-disable transitions, failed and successful manual runs, and legacy history without a run timestamp. The repair retains each present failure independently so enabling or manual recovery does not revive an acknowledged incident.

<details>
<summary>Validation details</summary>

- Base regression: two expected failures because pausing removed the saved dismissal.
- Final related suites: 4 files, 61 tests passed.
- Changed store suite: 41 tests passed, 2.40 s Vitest duration / 5.52 s command wall time with one worker. Net test growth: 124 lines. CI seconds are not available yet.
- Browser base: `Same failed run after pause/enable: 1`, expected 0; exit 1.
- Browser fix: `Same failed run after pause/enable: 0`, `Distinct failed run after pause/enable: 1`; exit 0. [New failure screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/179b166c-a974-41f4-84b2-904f52002d17).
- Changed checks, UI production/component test types, lint, format, controller guard, test-line budget and diff checks passed. The three dead-export scans passed with zero entries and were reused on the final changed-check rerun. Earlier line-cap and test-table typing failures were corrected without dropping coverage.
- Independent local review was completed after correcting its automatic-disable findings.

Focused suite command:


prs.title: fix(cli): request scopes a session-only device grant covers
prs.body:
Related: #199692

Depends on #199693. This branch is stacked on it, so until #199693 merges the diff also shows its commits.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a device paired with only `operator.sessions.write`, as the multiplayer guide recommends for guests, can't use `openclaw gateway call` or `openclaw tui`. The CLI asks for `operator.read` and the TUI for admin, read, write and approvals, so every connect becomes a scope-upgrade request for the admin.

## User Impact

User impact: a session-only guest can list, read and create its sessions from the CLI and use the TUI within its grant. Once the TUI has stored the grant with a device token, its connections and `gateway call` file no upgrade request. Behind trusted-proxy auth the Gateway issues the TUI no device token and `gateway call` stores none, so there each connection is refused once with a scope-upgrade request and then works within the grant. #199699 removes that refusal as a Gateway opt-in.

Devices whose grant holds the general scope are unchanged, and a device that needs a real upgrade (for example `operator.read` to `operator.admin`) still files one.

In the TUI, a session-only device gets no command list or pending approvals, because those need `operator.read` and `operator.approvals`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Where the client learns its grant:**
- `gateway call` projects its least-privilege scopes through the stored device grant with the existing `projectOperatorScopesForMethod`. It narrows only when the method's session-scoped alternative still authorizes the call.
- The TUI connects within a stored grant that holds `operator.sessions.*` and none of its default scopes, unless `--token` or `--password` is given.

**A device approved before it ever connected:** it has no stored grant, so its first request can exceed it. The Gateway's scope-upgrade refusal already reports `approvedScopes`, and the client uses that:
- The gateway client gains an opt-in `fitScopesToApprovedGrant` hook that reconnects once within the reported grant, which the TUI uses.
- `gateway call` retries once with the session grant.
- The TUI stores the device token it receives with the grant, so its later connections, and `gateway call` reading that stored grant, fit it. `gateway call` keeps its read-only storage mode on the retry and stores nothing.

Until a grant is stored, each connection still files that request first, because nothing tells the client its grant before it asks. Behind trusted-proxy auth nothing is stored, so that holds for every connection. The opt-in Gateway change in #199699 removes it.

**Moves:** two moves keep the touched files within the line-cap ratchet without changing behaviour:
- CLI scope selection, including the existing `sessions.create` cwd escalation retry, moves to `src/gateway/call-scopes.ts`.
- The gateway client's host-dependency defaults move to `packages/gateway-client/src/client-host-deps.ts`. `client.ts` re-exports their types, so the package API is unchanged.

**Docs:** `docs/start/multiplayer.md` and `docs/cli/tui.md` describe the guest behaviour and when the first-connect request remains.

## Evidence

- **New tests:**
  - `src/gateway/call.stored-grant-scopes.test.ts` 5/5. A session-only grant reads with `operator.sessions.read`; a read grant and a method without a session scope keep their request; a refused request retries with the reported grant and keeps read-only storage on both attempts (this case fails without the read-only fix); a grant that can't serve the method does not retry.
  - `packages/gateway-client/src/client.approved-grant.test.ts` 3/3, against a real WebSocket server that refuses with a scope upgrade: reconnects once within the reported grant; pauses without the hook, or when the hook keeps the request.
  - `src/tui/gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 16/16, adding session-only, read, `operator.pairing` and `--token` grants.
  - Without this change, the session-only, retry, `operator.pairing` and `--token` cases fail; the keep-behaviour cases pass on both.
- **Existing tests:** `call.test.ts` 91/91, `client.test.ts` 95/95, `client.handshake.test.ts` 22/22, `client.device-auth.test.ts` 25/25, `reconnect-policy.test.ts` 19/19, `tui.test.ts` 51/51.
- **Static checks:** typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Restack onto #199693's pairing hint:** this branch now sits on `a675d1b23b7`, which adds the `openclaw gateway call` hint for an unpaired edgeAuth device and keeps an explicit `--url` in it. `git range-diff 3411a94ae50..48d8e528f08 a675d1b23b7..74994fa1a99` shows this branch's two commits unchanged, and the runs below were made at `48d8e528f08`, before the restack. On `74994fa1a99`: `call.edge-auth.test.ts` 6/6, `call.stored-grant-scopes.test.ts` 5/5, `call.test.ts` 91/91, `gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 16/16, `client.approved-grant.test.ts` 3/3, typecheck clean, line-cap ratchet OK. On `71857425b24`, the same two commits on #199693's first hint commit: `client-bootstrap.auth.test.ts` 6/6, `client.test.ts` 95/95, `tui.test.ts` 51/51.
- **Live run** at `48d8e528f08` (built with `pnpm build:runtime`): a loopback Gateway with `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"`, behind a small TLS proxy standing in for Cloudflare Access (it answers 302 unless the request carries `Cf-Access-Token`, then injects the identity headers). The guest config has only `gateway.remote.url` and `gateway.remote.edgeAuth`: no token, no password, no stored device token. `--tls-fingerprint` is there only because the test proxy uses a self-signed certificate. The output is trimmed, and IDs and ports are from throwaway test state. The admin approves only `operator.sessions.write`. The Gateway has `narrowToDeviceGrant` off, as it is by default and as it is without #199699.

- **Upgrade from 2026.11.3, stored credentials kept:** the same loopback trusted-proxy setup, starting on the published `openclaw@2026.11.3` package for both the Gateway and the guest. The guest device is approved for only `operator.sessions.write` and stores that grant with the device token 2026.11.3 issues it. 2026.11.3 has no shipped command that leaves this grant behind a trusted proxy (its TUI gets no device token there, `gateway call` stores none, and its other commands ask for scopes the grant refuses), so the grant is written by 2026.11.3's own CLI Gateway client from its public `plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime`, asking for exactly that scope. 2026.11.3 will not dial without a credential, so that client sends a placeholder password, which trusted-proxy auth does not check (the two `auth=password` frames). Then the guest CLI moves to `48d8e528f08` with the same state directory and runs the documented update step, `openclaw doctor --fix`; then the Gateway does the same. Related: #201256

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS 2026.11.6 source-branch packaging failing its runtime portability audit on a bundled Codex TUI voice helper.

## User Impact

Unblocks qualification of the macOS app without changing the published v2026.11.6 tag or npm package. Native qualification remains required before app publication.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the exact four-file backport of merged commit 0eabe3398c9e0334e8c3b9b03f6a12040c7a1c12 (#201256), onto release/2026.11.6. It omits the unused TUI voice resources from the private staged runtime instead of rewriting Mach-O binaries. The Codex executable, nonvoice resources, canonical source, and release-tag staging behavior are preserved.

Original work by Daniel, with Jason (Json) credited in the upstream commit; original authorship and coauthor credit are preserved.

## Evidence

- Original ARM64, x86_64, and universal packaging attempts all failed on the missing `codex-voice-host.runfiles/_main/_solib_darwin_*` LC_RPATH. This is a real portability failure, not a waived gate.
- Focused suites: 23 tests passed; 96 macOS-only cases skipped on the Linux host. The added source/release staging regressions therefore still require native CI.
- Targeted tooling typecheck and lint passed; formatting, shell syntax, and whitespace checks passed. Normal staged pre-commit safeguards passed on this exact patch.
- Independent local autoreview: base a3fd8046eb509334636cd5f05a4bd11b28aec57e, complete four-file snapshot, P0-P2, OpenClaw engine, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. The patch is unchanged in this commit. Local ClawSweeper checkout was unavailable; one hosted review will be requested when ready.
- Upstream's final head did not receive native macOS proof; earlier-head evidence is not being reused as native qualification. Native PR CI and fresh matching-source release preflight/validation remain required.

No tag movement, npm publication, binary audit weakening, or app artifact promotion is included.

prs.title: perf(worktrees): keep template inventory and pack work off main thread
prs.body:
## Outcome: withdraw this candidate

Round 3 does not justify a production change. The final broker-qualified campaign regresses median sandbox foreground wait **3.257 → 4.266 s (+31.0%)**, observed maximum **4.855 → 12.400 s (+155.4%)**, and total CPU **+9.6%**. Main CPU falls 12.1% and main allocation falls 39.2%, but that does not meet the requested latency objective. No performance acceptance is requested for this rejected candidate and no merge will be submitted. Rounds 1 and 2 (#202383 and #202464) remain shipped.

The branch at `e2b5ef497f825dd11170e2a998c8d9ac89dae05f` preserves the committed real-Git measurement harness and experimental changes for reproduction. They are not merged production behavior. Prior acceptance belongs to the **Team perf-loop lead, an agent acting under Peter’s standing unattended instruction**, not Peter personally, and does not apply to Round 3.

## What the 10.8-second first send measured

That benchmark ended at workspace preparation; it excluded container startup, skills layout, MCP and model execution. A fresh exact-parent reproduction took 10,628.8 ms: owner resolution 2,838.7 ms, baseline publication 2,830.3 ms, projection checkpoint/reconciliation 4,110.1 ms, allocation 401.6 ms, initialization 284.7 ms, and about 163 ms elsewhere. Initialization contains template selection 102.8 ms and private native clone **114.6 ms**. Nested fields must not be added twice. Protected reconciliation accounts for independent host/guest edits; HEAD/index cannot replace it.

The final compiled Gateway first send took 19,504 ms including a real model reply. Existing fields: template selection 65 ms, private clone 132 ms, baseline 978 ms, projection checkpoint/reconcile 4,409 ms, skills synchronization 7,935 ms (copy_tree 52 ms), actual container start 44 ms, MCP materialization 1 ms. Both after-idle create and first send have zero inline generation builds and exact target HEAD/index/source/source-dependent installed outputs. These inclusive fields overlap; this instrumented run is correctness/profile proof, not a paired latency statistic.

## Final sandbox comparison

Two A/A controls plus five serial counterbalanced triples (ABC, CBA, BAC, CAB, ACB), with the existing Gateway spawn broker active in every arm. A is exact-parent joining, B is the proposed compressed-inventory/broker-input candidate joining, C is private advancement plus source-dependent reinstallation on the candidate. Same clean 62k-file/~1.1 GB btrfs seed and synthetic 35 GiB database with 5k sessions; database shape is not concurrent SQL traffic. No lane-owned heavy workload overlaps. Every arm asserts exact HEAD/tree/index/source/installed outputs, unchanged previous generation and one foreground clone. C omits generic installation-output containment validation, so it is an optimistic bound rather than a shippable implementation.

Written rule: require measured latency benefit, retain all controls/samples and resource regressions, and never dismiss a >20% regression as spread. Sample p95 at n=5 is the observed maximum, not a production-tail estimate. Whole-window cgroup CPU includes broker/reparented guest processes; overlapping phase CPU is not summed. Main allocation is transient cumulative V8 allocation, not retained heap or all-worker allocation.

| Metric | Baseline join median / sample p95 | Candidate join median / sample p95 | Private advance median / sample p95 | Candidate vs baseline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Foreground wait (ms) | 3,257.0 / 4,854.7 | 4,266.0 / 12,400.1 | 3,913.1 / 5,203.0 | +31.0% |
| Idle build (ms) | 3,905.9 / 5,357.1 | 4,851.8 / 12,135.1 | 5,737.6 / 8,141.1 | +24.2% |
| Whole window (ms) | 4,359.5 / 5,711.8 | 5,232.7 / 13,554.7 | 5,794.4 / 8,193.7 | +20.0% |
| Total cgroup CPU (ms) | 9,326.2 / 10,077.6 | 10,225.2 / 13,293.0 | 12,238.3 / 12,971.2 | +9.6% |
| Main CPU (ms) | 225.0 / 273.5 | 197.8 / 322.7 | 198.6 / 283.9 | -12.1% |
| Main allocated bytes | 64,750,672.0 / 69,819,864.0 | 39,349,392.0 / 44,079,376.0 | 45,599,600.0 / 50,199,152.0 | -39.2% |
| Projection checkout (ms) | 1,028.2 / 2,549.1 | 2,032.5 / 5,083.2 | 987.0 / 1,795.8 | +97.7% |

A/A foreground controls: 2,051 and 2,906 ms. Baseline→candidate pairs: 4855→12400, 3497→3210, 2350→2118, 2220→4266, 3257→4562 ms. Only 2/5 improve. The 12.4-second result remains included. Checkout and clone work dominate its delay; no causal claim that the unchanged checkout algorithm caused the regression is made.

Private advance is 8.3% faster than the regressed candidate join median, but **20.1% slower than original joining**, and beats original joining in only 1/5 pairs. Its total CPU is 31.2% above original joining. Git-only advancement demonstrably leaves stale installed output with an unchanged lockfile; reinstalling is required for exactness. Neither managed nor sandbox advancement has a demonstrated shipping benefit.

prs.title: fix: show sender phone number for quoted WhatsApp messages (#202554)
prs.body:
Closes #202554

## What Problem This Solves

When replying to a quoted message in a WhatsApp group where the quoted sender is identified by an internal `@lid` (such as `1234567890@lid`), the agent's inbound reply context displays the opaque `@lid` JID rather than the contact's phone number or display name, even though the receiving account already has the contact's reverse mapping stored in its local credentials folder (`authDir`).

## User Impact

User impact: When someone quotes another user in a WhatsApp group, the AI agent correctly sees the sender's phone number (e.g. `+15555550123`) in the quote context instead of an unreadable `@lid` identifier.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inbound quote extraction (`describeReplyContext`) was not provided with the receiving account's `authDir`, so the participant lookup fell back to the unmapped identifier. Additionally, `resolveComparableIdentity` retained the raw identifier in the `label` property even after resolving the phone number, causing the downstream reply envelope formatter to render the stale raw `@lid`.

This patch:
1. Passes `authDir` from delivery intake and message enrichment into `describeReplyContext`.
2. Updates `resolveComparableIdentity` to update `label` to the resolved `e164` when the existing label is a raw identifier (`@lid` / `@s.whatsapp.net`).
3. Explicitly normalizes and asserts `sender.lid` (and `sender.label = e164`) in expectations, preserving the existing identity normalization contract.

## Evidence

### Behavior comparison

- **Before:**
  Quoted group message with sender `1234567890@lid` mapped to `+15555550123`:
  Agent sees: `[Replying to 1234567890@lid]\noriginal message\n[/Replying]`
- **After:**
  Agent sees: `[Replying to +15555550123]\noriginal message\n[/Replying]`
  Identity data cleanly retains `lid: "1234567890@lid"`, `e164: "+15555550123"`, and `label: "+15555550123"`.

### Automated Tests Verified

All tests pass cleanly across unit, visibility, and monitor integration suites:
1. `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/extract.test.ts`: Added unit test `resolves quoted LID sender to phone number via authDir mapping` asserting `sender.lid`, `sender.e164`, and `sender.label`.
2. `extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-helpers.test.ts`: Added visibility context test `resolves quoted LID sender to mapped phone label via authDir` asserting `resolveVisibleWhatsAppReplyContext` yields mapped phone label.
3. `extensions/whatsapp/src/monitor-inbox.reply-context.test.ts`: Added monitor inbox test `resolves quoted LID sender to phone number using account authDir` verifying full delivery through Baileys event emission.

prs.title: fix(codex): let Doctor migrate legacy completion records
prs.body:
Closes #201337
Related: #197515

## What Problem This Solves

After an upgrade, Codex can stay disabled because Doctor rejects otherwise-valid saved native assignments that use the historical completion label `turn_completed`. Re-running `openclaw doctor --fix` preserves the binding as malformed and cannot clear the pending migration.

## User Impact

Operators can complete the Codex state upgrade without deleting completed assignments or editing SQLite by hand. Doctor preserves the recorded result and assignment ownership, canonicalizes the old label once, and converges on later runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pending-assignment schema correctly keeps runtime reads strict, but the migration normalization path parsed that strict schema before it could repair this shipped historical value. The change rewrites only an exact `recordedCompletion.statusLabel === "turn_completed"` to `recorded_task_result` before strict validation; all other fields and malformed states remain governed by the existing schema and repair owner.

## Evidence

- Production diagnosis on Linux with official OpenClaw and Codex 2026.11.5 found one active binding with two completed assignments. Both had valid, matching session/lifecycle/connection ownership; both used `turn_completed`. Doctor reported `Preserved malformed Codex native assignments`, left `deferred-plugin-migration:codex` pending, and kept the runtime unavailable.
- A copied-state probe under a scratch directory converted exactly 2 legacy labels in 1 copied binding to 2 canonical labels. The live database remained unchanged.
- Regression on unpatched current main: **1 failed / 19 passed**. The new case fails because the migration emits the malformed-state warning instead of canonicalizing.
- With this change: **20/20 passed** in `extensions/codex/src/migration/native-assignment-repair.test.ts`; the test verifies field preservation, canonical replacement, and repeat no-op convergence.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed for the two changed files.
- Independent read-only Codex review: **PASS** — narrow compatibility rewrite, preserved fields, convergent regression coverage.

No production config/state was changed and no Gateway was restarted while preparing this fix. Full shipped-CLI upgrade replay was not run; the regression exercises the registered plugin Doctor migration owner with synthetic state matching the observed binding shape.

prs.title: fix: stop the session sidebar jumping while subagents run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a session in the sidebar is running subagents, a blank placeholder row keeps flashing under it. Every session below it jumps down and back up each time one of its subagents reports progress, which can be several times a minute, so the list is hard to read or click while that session works.

## User Impact

User impact: the session list stays still while sessions run subagents or publish to GitHub; rows no longer move under the pointer.

## Why This Change Was Made

A session can be expanded in the sidebar even when all of its children are hidden there (subagent runs and GitHub publication sessions). Each time one of those children changed, the sidebar re-checked the children and treated that re-check as a fresh load. With no visible child rows to keep on screen, it drew the loading placeholder every time.

Now only the first load of a session's children can show the placeholder. Later re-checks keep what is already displayed, which is how sessions with visible children already behaved.

The first load also showed the placeholder immediately, so a fast read still flashed it for a frame or two before collapsing it. The placeholder now waits 300 ms and only appears when the read is actually slow.

## Evidence

Videos below use the mocked Control UI with synthetic sessions. A running "Audit automations feature" session has one GitHub publication child and three subagent runs. The session is expanded (child read takes 120 ms), then five child updates arrive with child reads taking 800 ms, like the team server, and another session is opened midway. Before is current `main`, after is this branch.

The recording script measured the row below the running session on every animation frame:

- **Before:** the placeholder showed on the expand and on every update (about 48 frames each), and the row below moved 32 px each time.
- **After:** no placeholder frames and 0 px of movement, through the expand, all five updates and the session switch.

**Before** (current `main`):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0eeed8f1-8c40-4f6f-a0b2-a0b550eb7a05

**After** (this branch):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01b0230a-1bbd-43ac-bd73-4f40c0f7ec99

Other checks:

- New sidebar tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix: one for a child re-check under a session with only hidden children, one for a fast first read (no placeholder within 300 ms, placeholder after that while the read is still pending).
- The sidebar unit, isolated and browser suites pass (1,216 tests), the sidebar stability browser E2E passes (7 variants, including the slow first-load placeholder), and the UI typechecks pass.
- Local autoreview found no issues.
- The diagnosis came from a real recording: the affected live session had 15 GitHub publication children and 40 subagent runs, all hidden from the sidebar.

Gap: not yet exercised against a live Gateway in a browser. A first child read slower than 300 ms still shows the placeholder once, which is intended loading feedback.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/db28c1b4-b42f-4c5b-a870-03e5a59d2811)

prs.title: fix: show saved child results when idle delivery expires
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A child interrupted during Gateway restart can retain a pending completion while its requester stays idle. At the 30-minute hard deadline, the registry discarded that completion without telling the requester or logging its retirement.

## User Impact

An expired required completion now records a visible failure notice containing the saved public result, with the existing truncation bounds and full-history recovery guidance, plus an operator warning. The requester can recover the result or start replacement work without needing another turn to discover the failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Idle and suspended expiry now share the existing retirement and notice owner. The separate quiet discard implementation is removed: net production LOC is -13. Idle expiry still releases orphaned reservations, defers delete cleanup to the sweeper, and does not run an ended hook or model turn. Queued deliveries, active producers, requester cohorts and not-required deliveries retain their existing behavior. No config/schema/cache/tool change.

The Team perf-loop lead, an agent acting under Peter's standing unattended instruction, requested this scoped repair and landing. This is the agent lead's decision, not Peter's personal acceptance. Related: #202664, #202708.

## Evidence

On base `8253356c986427d888cbe24b2c3d6f3b702a2f79`, the real SQLite/transcript sweeper regression fails because idle pending expiry produces zero visible notices; suspended expiry and not-required controls pass. The fixture restores a drain-interrupted terminal outcome with captured text, leaves the requester idle, and sweeps before and at the deadline. With the fix, the visible notice includes the saved answer, expired reason, restart-interruption status, truncation marker and full-result recovery instructions; full stored text survives unchanged.

All 37 focused tests pass across five files (76.26 seconds wrapper time). The changed expiry file's three cases take 5.257 seconds. Existing tests also cover reservation release, queued/deferred-delete custody, sweep cadence, backlog warnings, private-result isolation and notice bounds. Codex P0–P2 autoreview is clean. This is synthetic persistence/sweeper boundary proof; no production data, transcript content or live-model claim.

Complete `pnpm check:changed` passes lint, production and all test typechecks, format, SQLite/schema ownership guards and import-cycle checks. Its only failed gate is the export scan: `createSkillPageReads` and `createSkillPageRoute` in `ui/src/pages/skills/skill-page-route.ts`. Both reproduce on exact main parent `8253356c986427d888cbe24b2c3d6f3b702a2f79` and were added by #202581 (`1ee9f29e6668e32ecfade57a540d10326ad3b8de`). This is a main regression for the UI owner, not a green check. The parent-only voice-call dependency-link diagnostics are excluded from that attribution; the full-tree scan matches exactly.

The first CI run exposed a PR-caused suspended-yield ordering regression. The correction preserves cleanup/hook ordering and records the notice in `finally`, so tail failure cannot skip it. All 10 worker-boundary cases and three expiry cases pass after correction (73.99 seconds wrapper time); fresh Codex P0–P2 autoreview is clean. Final-head ClawSweeper reports zero findings and zero open items.

Final CI [44823493541](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44823493541) on `32ffe6aab90ccf9ab80ea7a72686455fc5515801` passes the repaired Node shard and every other root check except UI shard 1: skills loads 30 assets against 28, skill settings 33 against 31. Both reproduce exactly on CI's actual main parent `3bf86304325f0ccfbe2c868081cfa004294dc159` on Linux (109.056 seconds command, 289.001 seconds including sync). The two local export diagnostics also reproduce there. The current extra skill-page-boundary/detail-loading-hero imports and unused exports come from #202581 (`1ee9f29e6668e32ecfade57a540d10326ad3b8de`). These are main regressions for the UI owner, not noise. The tested merge changes no UI/scenario inputs. Landing uses the scoped inherited-failure route; CI and the export scan remain explicitly failed.

prs.title: refactor: reduce CPU spent preparing state reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

State reads copy freshly built command payloads before native worker messaging copies them again. Large session and workspace selectors therefore spend avoidable CPU and allocation preparing a read.

## User Impact

Read results, worker serialization, admission budgets, and database behavior stay the same. Read preparation allocates less and uses less CPU. Borrowed mutable selectors remain isolated from edits made while a read is preparing or queued; session-version selectors are now captured before lazy snapshot preparation, closing an existing gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The internal transport in `src/state/openclaw-state-read-worker.ts` adopts commands from their producers. The caller audit covers 174 direct calls in 120 files, plus the lease reader's direct transport call. Fresh private commands need no copy or frozen-object inspection. Producers capture borrowed arrays/records; configuration and mutable filesystem evidence retain their necessary snapshots; skill query producers capture borrowed parameters and pins. Descendants retain the registry-owned immutable topology and stop freezing the outer command.

No new cache, configuration, schema, or migration. Session-row projection is unchanged. Production code grows by five lines after formatting for the ownership contract and retained producer snapshots; the transport clone/inspection and redundant outer freezing disappear. Tests shrink by 13 lines.

## Evidence

The regression mutates session selectors during lazy preparation and again while worker dispatch is queued. It fails with the original producer and transport restored at `7a4298bfb55f40918d636eae8dea3c882c24ca0e` and passes with the fix. Existing transport tests retain their byte-budget and routing assertions.

Five serial A/A/B triplets use synthetic 5,000-session and 62,000-file command shapes. Native MessagePort serialization and unchanged admission accounting are included below; these are command dispatch measurements, not SQL or whole-Gateway throughput.

| Payload | Base dispatches/sec | A/A control | Candidate | Allocated bytes/read, base → candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5,000 shared session facts | 61.1 | 61.3 | 110.8 | 10,061,415 → 4,951,606 |
| 5,000 borrowed session refs, including producer capture | 256.7 | 255.1 | 443.3 | 2,914,385 → 1,684,978 |
| 62,000 prepared workspace files | 7.1 | 7.0 | 12.1 | 77,570,621 → 38,545,281 |

The real source-capture/transport/empty-close benchmark independently reduces large-command setup from 6.8 ms and 56.7 ms CPU/read to about 4.7 µs. The retained-config-copy control is unchanged within variation. Already-admitted frozen objects were a cheap WeakSet hit; removing that lookup alone is a small gain. Node 26.12.1; no production data or live system access. Reproduction options are in the two existing `scripts/perf/state-read-*` benchmarks.

Focused consumer proof: 308 passed across 24 files, plus 66 passing tests across three files after the final library-producer refinement. One existing PostgreSQL-only case was skipped. The worker build initially hit a full volume; relocating task-owned build artifacts and fixing their dependency resolution recovered the run without changing test expectations.

The full `pnpm check:changed` and final-delta run passed their type, dead-code, boundary, format, and other static gates. Three task-caused lint findings were fixed; only the affected lint was rerun after the last fix, and it passed. The original failed command exits remain recorded rather than being described as clean whole-command runs. Codex autoreview of the final local candidate against the base above is scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings. It covered the changed code and supplied ownership context; some unchanged adapters were outside the review bundle, so the complete caller audit is source-audit evidence rather than an exhaustive second-review claim.

## Final review and CI qualification

Final head: `6769d120e97926e0a15cc7127f4c6720fa826861`. [ClawSweeper's final-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202731#issuecomment-7051151574) has zero findings and zero open items. Codex autoreview is clean through P2; the automatic GitHub Codex review also has no findings.

[CI run 44820171602, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44820171602) completed with 67 successful and 26 skipped jobs. Two root jobs and their aggregate failed. Security passed. The actual tested merge is `74862906a15e6cd34624026ba6e2bfbb35119672`, with main parent `c2e7b54ab6f5adc693d04fe53a992d4c0458bb43` and this exact PR head.

- Skills route asset budgets: exact-parent Linux reproduction sees the identical asset names and counts, 30 against 28 and 33 against 31. The eager page-boundary/loading-hero graph is from [#202581](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202581), commit `1ee9f29e6668e32ecfade57a540d10326ad3b8de`; the earlier Settings over-budget graph was introduced by [#202531](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202531). All UI inputs are unchanged by this PR. The macOS Settings replay passes and is not the qualifying proof.
- MCP mutation ownership: both cases reproduce on that exact main parent with eight/four synchronous identity reads instead of zero. Stacks point to the live-owner check reached after [#202608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202608), commit `22255926f9cf4fd7a297d5a6dc3f6abe58c52d97`, broadened the metadata-read condition. Reversing only those two introduced lines makes both tests pass. Diagnostic edits were restored; this PR changes only ownership documentation in the implicated operation module.

These are recorded main regressions for separate owner repair, not green CI. The native inherited-failure exception retains exact-parent reproductions, introducing commits, checkout identity, unchanged source evidence, scoped passing proof, and the failed run. No CI rerun, test-budget increase, or product/review/security exemption was used.

prs.title: improve: avoid rereading workspace files when opening a Template
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Opening a Template made the Gateway read its declared workspace files twice: once to verify the downloaded release, and again to generate the excerpts shown in the catalog.

## User Impact
The same Template detail page now takes fewer local file reads. The UI, catalog ordering, SOUL.md preview, skill summaries and inline automations are unchanged. The Gateway still downloads and verifies the archive. No migration or configuration change is needed. This is not a general page-latency improvement: a fresh-connection replay showed a slower tail.

## Why This Change Was Made
The Gateway now builds workspace excerpts from the bytes it already reads for verification, and returns them only after the whole release passes verification. Explicit file previews and install checks are unchanged. The earlier UI, pagination and archive-free inventory changes are excluded: the live registry did not supply the complete display data the current UI needs.

## Evidence
For `myfitnessclaw@0.2.5`, seven archive replays per build measured **30 → 20 local workspace file opens per detail**. Both builds made four registry requests, including the same 896,242-byte archive. Parsed detail responses matched, and all 12 Chromium opens showed the title, excerpt and enabled Add action; Show more opened the full SOUL.md on both builds.

| Measurement (main → candidate) | Median | p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Chromium, live registry via relay, five repeated opens per build | 875 → 825 ms | 1,358 → 1,338 ms |
| Live registry via relay, eight warm details on fresh connections per build | 610 → 632 ms | 682 → 730 ms |
| Captured release, 59 warm details on fresh connections per build | 47 → 47 ms | **54 → 72 ms** |
| Captured release, 60 details on persistent connections per build | 44 → 41 ms | 48 → 45 ms |

The first Chromium open in each fresh browser context took about 1.59 seconds on both builds. The measured local win is fewer file reads, not fewer downloads or a guaranteed speedup. Focused catalog, reader and Gateway tests, targeted lint/format, core typecheck and the runtime build passed. The performance-only tree was checked against `7af829afeef7d`; later main integration did not change these files. Independent local autoreview of the committed four-file range (base 7a4298bfb55f, head ccdc4f509f43, P0–P2) finished with no actionable findings. GitHub’s test merge 5e1290d4ac76 against main 3bf86304325f changes only those four backend/test files; the Files tab may compare against the older PR base snapshot.

Contributors: @Patrick-Erichsen and @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @Patrick-Erichsen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f55045c5-faef-4527-8ff5-3df5e0579516)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/fe7d5b2a-04ad-4825-aade-61e9464fbab4)

prs.title: fix(cli): restore dashboard Gateway start and install recovery
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #202037

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where `openclaw dashboard` could never start or install the Gateway when it was stopped or absent: the command printed "Use the owning environment or supervisor to start or repair the selected Gateway." and exited 1, even with `--yes` or after accepting the prompt, so the documented start/install recovery never ran and the usual `gateway start` / `gateway run` hints were suppressed.
- **Related:** #202037 (traced in source at main @ 59ca885df59). The readiness probe forwarded the dashboard's internally resolved URL as a probe override; the daemon status reader classifies any URL override as diagnostic-only, so the native service was never the recovery target and the start/install branch was unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Readiness probes the same endpoint the dashboard selected. It can start or install the native service only when that service owns the selected endpoint; explicit `gateway status --url` remains diagnostic-only.
- **Out of scope:** `gateway status --url` keeps classifying explicit URL overrides as diagnostic-only (intended and already tested in `status.gather.test.ts`); externally supervised or non-default-identity targets remain unrecoverable from the dashboard.
- The [maintainer correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202085/commits/b15f9564fc30a49ba29de63ebbafb0977bf8444a) addresses the [P1 endpoint-selection finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202085#issuecomment-7024074987), including a caller-only port override that is absent from the installed unit.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** With the Gateway stopped or absent on a default local install, `openclaw dashboard` offers to start or install the background Gateway service (or does so immediately with `--yes`) and prints the `openclaw gateway start` / `openclaw gateway run` hints again instead of the misleading supervisor message; `dashboard --json` still never installs or starts a service.
- The status-boundary regressions cover mismatched service/CLI ports and a matching service port. Dashboard tests still cover JSON mode without service recovery and re-probing a changed custom-bind endpoint.

## Evidence

### Maintainer correction: exact-head Linux proof

Verified commit `b15f9564fc30a49ba29de63ebbafb0977bf8444a` on a disposable AWS Linux VM with a real systemd user manager. Built the CLI and Control UI with `pnpm build:ci-artifacts`.

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Healthy foreground Gateway on 28900; installed native service on 28789 stopped | Both `dashboard --no-open` and `dashboard --yes --no-open` exited successfully, printed the dashboard URL on 28900, and left the native service inactive. |
| Native service absent, then installed but stopped | `dashboard --yes --no-open` installed or started the native service as appropriate and returned the real Control UI on 28789 in both cases. |
| Native service absent; `dashboard --json` | Exited nonzero and left the native unit absent. |

Two status-boundary cases failed on the original PR head and passed with the correction. All 86 focused tests across daemon status, dashboard, and Gateway readiness passed; formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Browser launch, clipboard delivery, and interactive-prompt acceptance were not part of this headless run.

### Independent live Linux systemd verification (original PR head)

Tested the built CLI and Control UI from exact PR head `e3df91f68298c53d8198d233c046dc2e387c230b` on a disposable AWS Crabbox VM with a fresh systemd user, real loopback Gateway, and no model-provider credentials. Built with `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` and ran the production CLI entry point, `node openclaw.mjs dashboard --yes --no-open`.

| Starting state | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| No service installed; `dashboard --json` | Exited nonzero and left the unit absent. |
| No service installed; `dashboard --yes --no-open` | Installed the real user unit, reached `active`, and printed `Dashboard URL: http://127.0.0.1:28789/dashboard-proof/`. |
| Installed unit explicitly stopped; `dashboard --yes --no-open` | Printed `Started systemd service: openclaw-gateway.service`, reached `active`, and printed the same dashboard URL. |

In both recovery cases, an independent HTTP request returned the actual OpenClaw Control UI document; a follow-up `dashboard --json` returned `ok: true`, port `28789`, and a one-time browser pairing URL (not included here). `--no-open` was intentional: interactive prompting and browser launch/pairing were not exercised. The VM lease was released after verification.

### Contributor's original Linux verification

- **Real environment tested:** Linux (EL8) with the real systemd user manager and live port probes; the worktree CLI sources were executed directly (tsx) against the machine's real service discovery and ports — no mocks in the evidence path.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Real gatherDaemonStatus comparison, pre-fix call shape vs fixed call shape
  # (profile-isolated unit absent, port 18790 free):
  OPENCLAW_PROFILE=evid202037 OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18790 DASHBOARD_PROBE_PORT=18790 \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs evidence-composition.mts
  # Real dashboard command, before (origin/main) and after (this patch), no TTY:
  OPENCLAW_PROFILE=evid202037 OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18790 \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs evidence-dashboard-driver.mts
  # Regression tests (RED on main, GREEN with this patch) via validate.sh:
  #   src/commands/gateway-readiness.test.ts, src/commands/dashboard.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```json
  {
    "before": {
      "callShape": "old: rpc:{url:<dashboard-resolved wsUrl>}",
      "serviceTargetRole": "diagnostic-only",
      "gatewayLooksStopped": true,
      "nativeServiceTargetsGateway": false,
      "canStartService": false,
      "recoveryBranchReachable": false
    },
    "after": {
      "callShape": "fixed: rpc:{}",
      "serviceTargetRole": "target",
      "gatewayLooksStopped": true,
      "nativeServiceTargetsGateway": true,
      "canStartService": true,
      "shouldInstall": true,
      "recoveryBranchReachable": true
    }
  }
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The real `dashboard` command (no TTY, no `--yes`) in the same environment now prints `Gateway is not running.` followed by `Run "openclaw gateway start" to start a managed gateway.` and `Run "openclaw gateway run" for a foreground gateway.`, and the install/start recovery branch is reachable (`canStartService: true`, `shouldInstall: true`). On main @ 73a53a58eba the identical run printed `Use the owning environment or supervisor to start or repair the selected Gateway.` (exit 1) with the recovery branch unreachable.
- **Before evidence:** main @ 73a53a58eba, same environment and driver: `Gateway is not running.` / `Run "openclaw gateway status --deep" for details.` / `Use the owning environment or supervisor to start or repair the selected Gateway.` — exactly the reported symptom, including the suppressed `gateway start` / `gateway run` hints.
- **Scope of the original proof (L2):** The Linux driver established the hints and recovery decision, not service installation, startup, or dashboard delivery; those are covered for `--yes` by the independent Linux verification above. A [separate Windows reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202037#issuecomment-7040662412) reported successful install and dashboard delivery on the second invocation, but did not test this exact head.
