prs.title: fix: slow macOS dashboard reconnects when the app keeps refusing native sign-in
prs.body:
Related: #168743 ## What Problem This Solves When the macOS app keeps refusing native sign-in for an open Dashboard page, that page reconnects to the Gateway every 9 to 15 seconds for as long as it stays open. On 2026.11.5, which already includes #185963, one Mac still produced hundreds of `code=4008 reason=native authorization unavailable` closes overnight. #185963 stops closed and replaced pages; a page that is still open has no limit. ## User Impact A native Dashboard or chat page that the app keeps refusing now retries quickly about ten times, then about once every five minutes. Coming back to the window (focus, or the window becoming visible again) still retries at once, but it no longer starts a new fast series. The page still connects by itself as soon as the app grants it again, and short refusals recover exactly as before. ## Why This Change Was Made The Control UI client marks every native refusal as retryable, and its reconnect loop has no attempt limit, so the 15 second backoff ceiling repeats forever. The page's native auth adapter now counts consecutive refusals. From the tenth one, the refusal carries a five minute retry floor, which the shared reconnect loop already honors for retryable errors (300 to 360 seconds with jitter). Any native grant resets the count. The count lives in the native auth adapter, which is created once per page, not in the connection client. Page activation (focus, visibility, Retry) replaces the client. With the count on the client (the first commit, `2d4b7f498c1`), every activation started a new fast series, and the packaged app still logged 38 closes in 600 seconds. Recovery is not removed: no stop, no new state, no new setting, and the page activation recovery is unchanged. This bounds the retry side for every native page. In the app runs below, hiding the app, restarting its SSH tunnel and showing it again leaves the visible Dashboard page refused until the Dashboard is reopened. Whether that is the path on the reporter's Mac is not known (the window state was not recorded). The app-side cause is a separate fix and is not part of this change. Maintainer decision: the issue carries `needs-product-decision` because ending retries would change the recovery contract from #159860. This change keeps that contract (retries never stop) and only lowers the pace after ten consecutive refusals. ## Evidence - Packaged macOS app (release 2026.11.5, its own WKWebView and native auth bridge), Dashboard served by a test Gateway with the Control UI of the commit under test, 600 seconds of a refused, visible page: - main `9ebaece1079`: 66 closes, steady to the end. - first commit `2d4b7f498c1`: 38 closes, with new fast bursts after the window became visible again. - this branch `1426dc12ce3`: 12 closes. After the first ten refusals: one scheduled attempt (308 seconds after the previous one) and one attempt for each of the two times the window became visible again. Activating the app afterwards gave exactly one refusal. Reopening the Dashboard connected about 1.2 seconds later. - Real Gateway and headless Chromium with a refusing native bridge stub, 420 seconds: main made 35 attempts, one every 12.5 to 14.6 seconds; this branch made 11 (ten fast, then one at +378.2 seconds). A focus event gave 3 attempts within 3 seconds on main and 1 on this branch. - Regression test `slows reconnects after ten consecutive native refusals until a grant` in `ui/src/app/native-gateway-auth.node.test.ts` (real `GatewayBrowserClient` and application gateway store, fake native bridge). It checks ten fast refusals, one immediate attempt on page activation without a new fast series, the five minute floor, recovery on a grant, and fast backoff again after the grant. It fails on main (13 sockets after a minute and one activation, expected 11) and on the first commit alone (19 sockets five minutes after the activation, expected 11), and passes on this branch. - Mutation checks: reverting the second commit's source fails the same way as the first commit (19, expected 11); removing only the grant reset fails the last step (13 sockets, expected 14). - Related suites pass on this branch: `native-gateway-auth.node.test.ts`, all of `ui/src/api`, `gateway-page-activation.test.ts`, `gateway-store.auth.test.ts`, `local-error-copy.test.ts` (16 files, 284 tests). - `pnpm check:changed` at `1426dc12ce3` against a freshly fetched `origin/main` (merge base `9ebaece1079`): format, lint, UI and core test typechecks, i18n and the ratchets pass. The dead export scan fails the same way on `9ebaece1079` without this change (two unused exports in `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.authority.test-support.ts`). - Local review: ClawSweeper `--local-range` (Claude runner), base `9ebaece1079`, head `1426dc12ce3`, full committed range, complete and checkout access verified; outcome: patch is correct, no findings, rating C (proof D, patch B) in the second round; remaining findings: none. Its proof rating does not see the runtime output below and asks for a macOS app run. Gaps: the main and first-commit app runs are from one session and the `1426dc12ce3` run from a later one, on the same two Macs. The Mac was in normal use during the `1426dc12ce3` window: other apps covered the test window twice (12:36:52 to 12:38:00 and 12:43:15 to 12:43:49), and the test window was not refocused. The packaged app is the release build; only its served Control UI changes between runs. ### Runtime output #### Packaged macOS app Setup: release `OpenClaw.app` 2026.11.5 with its own profile connects over an SSH tunnel to a test Gateway on another Mac (own state dir, loopback port 19743). The Gateway's `gateway.controlUi.root` serves the built Control UI of the commit under test, so the app's WKWebView and native auth bridge run that client. Steps: open the Dashboard, hide the app, restart the app's SSH tunnel, show the app, watch 600 seconds, activate the app once, reopen the Dashboard. Counts come from the test Gateway log: `lines` are the logged `closed before connect ... code=4008` lines in the window, `closes` adds the `suppressed=N` closes the Gateway folds into each line. App lines come from the app's unified log (`com.apple.WebKit:ViewState`).
main 9ebaece1079: 66 closes in 600 seconds Window 10:33:47 to 10:43:47 (Gateway log, UTC-8). The `suppressed=5` on the first line may include closes from just before the window. ```text 2026-11-20T10:33:47.197-08:00 [ws] closed before connect conn=b0daa5cb-d0a1-4701-b0a8-1988af576531 peer=127.0.0.1:61109->127.0.0.1:19743 [...] code=4008 reason=native authorization unavailable phase=ws_upgrade_started suppressed=5 [...] 2026-11-20T10:34:17.552-08:00 [ws] closed before connect conn=7f664138-5a65-4d96-9168-dd23a31728e3 peer=127.0.0.1:61159->127.0.0.1:19743 [...] code=4008 reason=native authorization unavailable phase=ws_upgrade_started suppressed=5 [...] 2026-11-20T10:35:00.448-08:00 [ws] closed before connect conn=c45f1413-7f98-47ef-82aa-81687afdab0c peer=127.0.0.1:61271->127.0.0.1:19743 [...] code=4008 reason=native authorization unavailable phase=ws_upgrade_started suppressed=2 [...] 2026-11-20T10:35:43.550-08:00 [ws] closed before connect conn=bdabdac2-a355-4ef3-80ec-f7149c87a227 peer=127.0.0.1:61308->127.0.0.1:19743 [...] code=4008 reason=native authorization unavailable phase=ws_upgrade_started suppressed=2 [...] 2026-11-20T10:36:24.299-08:00 [ws] closed before connect conn=583ae437-abb7-4e52-94bc-34bdcc685f33 prs.title: fix: make plugin catalog artwork easier to recognize
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Customize → Plugins, publisher images sit inside a second tile with enough padding that they look like tiny square stamps. That makes it harder to recognize a plugin by its artwork while scanning the catalog.

## User Impact

User impact: Plugin artwork is larger and has softer corners, without making the rows taller or moving the titles, publishers, or Install buttons. Plugins without an image still show the neutral plug icon.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the 40 px artwork slot, but let the image use a 38 px face instead of adding padding and a second background. The artwork retains its aspect ratio and original colors. The styling is limited to plugin catalog rows; templates, detail pages, and installed-plugin icons are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Compared Featured at 1280 px and 393 px in Chromium with the real Control UI, mocked Gateway, and current ClawHub publisher artwork for Shopify, Lossless, and Expedia. Calendar Bridge and Signal Studio are fixtures for missing artwork and a wide SVG. The capture verified unchanged row and control geometry and keyboard focus. Baseline `b4a41aa642ce0`; the upstream UI sources were unchanged through `8ebcc3bb311c2`.
- The original three artwork cases failed with the old styles. After removing the extra tile wrapper, all 44 catalog unit and Chromium tests passed, along with UI typecheck, targeted lint/format, and the production-build performance comparison against `b4a41aa642ce0`. The revised build added 3 bytes of raw CSS and 22 bytes gzipped in that comparison; no budget was changed. Desktop and phone screenshots confirm the same artwork size and row geometry.
- [ClawSweeper identified the original CSS growth failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202719#issuecomment-7050736326). This revision addresses it at the artwork renderer, without widening the change to other views.

### Clean desktop comparison

**Before**

![Before: publisher artwork appears as a small square within a larger row tile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9a11cf2-d728-470b-be8f-d6df2bb0f519)

**After**

![After: the images fill the same row slots without a second tile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe887846-cdbc-47c2-8f1b-3393da521ea0)

### Annotated desktop comparison

**Before**

![Before: Expedia’s image is about 18 pixels wide within its tile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a573aafd-63c6-46bf-80c7-33a9113e15a1)

**After**

![After: Expedia’s single rounded artwork face is 38 pixels wide](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d96e2f4b-6b96-4acc-97a9-e788d0422bf4)

### Clean phone comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: small publisher images in the phone layout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15106d43-a3c4-438b-9534-c1ab24fdf6db) | ![After: larger publisher images and the plug fallback in the phone layout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26f03d9a-18f2-4877-9b80-33966d9f2a36) |

Reported and design direction by @vyctorbrzezowski. Customize intake credit: @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f55045c5-faef-4527-8ff5-3df5e0579516)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/cec172dc-68e8-4ceb-8097-d0481e9f1b93)

prs.title: fix: restore queued compaction writer-fence coverage
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202547

## What Problem This Solves

Main CI's queued-compaction test fails because its writer-replacement hook still watches the old transcript reader. The hook never runs after the production reader migration, so the test no longer exercises the intended writer takeover.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. CI again tests that a queued maintenance rewrite is rejected after another writer takes over, while preserving the replacement writer and original transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

Intercept the existing symbol-based transcript reader used by production rewrites. Load the symbol after the harness resets modules, alongside the real session manager. Keep the original reader forwarding and all existing rejection and persistence assertions.

## Evidence

- [Main CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44802039471/job/136517217680), head `a3bd84cc50639a4bd377db3d286d5ae1c3c3d273`: the during-branch-read case reports `rewriteRejected=false` at the assertion requiring rejection.
- Source inspection ties the stale spy to the reader migration in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/018e2fb364bb977d8f537a671b8df0fa35933910. The affected fixture and production reader remain unchanged at this branch's base `e439f84888d098c26667e46184f0fbc0be4b5d62`.
- Syntax, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh full-range local review of `e439f848..0ceae759` found no actionable correctness or security findings.
- Scope: one test file, ten added and five removed lines; production delta zero. Existing writer-replacement, rejection and unchanged-transcript assertions are preserved.
- [Current-head Node proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44813679285/job/136557165965) passes all 19 queued-compaction cases, including the original during-branch-read failure. [Current-head typecheck](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44813679285/job/136558075652) passes. Local dependency-backed execution remains unavailable.

The [prior candidate Node job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44811644321/job/136550280745) passes all 19 queued-compaction tests, including the formerly failing during-branch-read case. Its typecheck exposed a widened symbol import; this revision retains the imported module namespace to preserve the unique-symbol type. Fresh full-range review found no actionable findings. The updated-head typecheck and all 19 runtime cases now pass. [Ready-event CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44815339959) completed with 47 successful or skipped jobs and one failed non-aggregate job: [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44815339959/job/136562835070). Its runner lost communication with GitHub during the check; the job log is unavailable (HTTP 404), and no assertion failure was reported. The aggregate CI gate is red. The passing changed-test job checked out merge `6af18e604e8963e6fa2bf053a7d641989cdaaa71` and passed all 19 queued-compaction cases. The workflow, scripts, configuration, and dependency inputs match its baseline. The native verifier accepted the evidence for an exception limited to this unrelated runner loss, with review and security checks preserved. This does not mark the failed CI attempt as passing.

prs.title: fix: keep Windows managed updates alive when the task stops
prs.body:
Related: #169844

## What Problem This Solves

Windows Scheduled Task updates can kill their own helper when stopping the Gateway, leaving the Control UI at **Activating**, no terminal result, and the task disabled.

## User Impact

This draft keeps the managed update helper alive through the task stop while retaining cleanup of ordinary Gateway children. **Blocked on merging and releasing [proc-safe#31](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/31), then updating this dependency:** the declared dependency and lockfile intentionally remain at 0.4.2; its released API cannot run this integration. All 24 required checks now pass on native head `9e91dcc8e9cafc09be31a7374327345b8ce93ef9`, but that PR is still unmerged: `roboclaw-bot` has only READ permission in proc-safe and cannot land it. A maintainer with merge permission must merge it first. Then publish the paired native package, update the shipping dependency/lockfile, and revalidate before marking ready. No native merge commit exists to reference yet.

Already-installed affected updaters need one [manual npm, pnpm, or Bun hop](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d514bf8157581542d8a3d55747a4e898e5124bb2/docs/install/updating/update-methods.md#alternative-manual-npm-pnpm-or-bun) from outside the Gateway to a fixed release. The installed driver owns the first handoff, so downloading a candidate cannot repair it. The documented service refresh restores the task definition and enabled state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the task-launcher Job and inner command Job permit explicit breakaway, and only the Scheduled Task managed update helper requests it. Kill-on-close stays enabled and ordinary children remain contained. The existing runtime staging owner retains the matching spawner outside the installation being replaced; stdin/stdout and optional JSON IPC still reach the existing lease, cancellation, recovery and terminal owners.

The proc-safe launcher PID differs from the helper PID. The current handoff already verifies and settles the helper independently of its launcher. Mapped staged native files can remain for existing stale-directory cleanup after process exit; no new cleanup store or protocol is added.

## Evidence

- Spawn selection and outer/inner Job regressions fail on base and pass with the fix. Retained-runtime tests cover loading the copied public spawner after removing the source installation, executable validation, and process creation identity.
- Production and affected test typechecks, lint, formatting and docs links pass against the paired API, locally pinned to proc-safe PR commit `ec55427cacc83115f80b42750dc2aea28e470991`; the temporary dependency/lock changes are excluded from this PR.
- Final focused owner/consumer check: 73 tests passed across five files in 153.92s (runtime/compiler preparation included); the two previously interrupted systemd recovery cases also passed (64.09s including compiler preparation). Prior interrupted run completed 43 native lifecycle, 27 launchd recovery, 25 systemd recovery and 6 engine cases before termination. Initial full lifecycle batch: 79 passed, 4 failed, 5 skipped. The four existing profile-notice cases reproduce host `fs.watch` EMFILE and subsequent cleanup assertions on the base as well; no timeout, retry, skip or assertion relaxation was introduced.
- Test allocation adds exactly 204 net regression/support lines for spawn, nested Job permission and retained native runtime boundaries. The shared ratchet still reports 1,036 lines of inherited debt after this allocation; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- pr-simplify completed: existing staging and handoff owners retained, the FreeBSD-only stage export replaced without an alias, and non-service Windows staging remains independent of proc-safe. Net production growth: 47 lines; tests/support: 204 lines. Fresh independent Codex P0–P2 review: scoped-clean.
- [Native Windows CI](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/actions/runs/41144054731): all four x64/ARM64 × Node22/24 jobs passed at `9e91dcc8e9cafc09be31a7374327345b8ce93ef9`, including native Node/Bun main-thread/Worker Job, pipe/EOF, JSON IPC and strict OS-argv proof. The native production/API bytes match the locally tested commit. All 24 required native-PR checks, including every other platform, have now completed successfully. Windows Scheduled Task/Control UI package-upgrade, failure/recovery and cancellation E2E remains unrun here. Crabbox rejected Windows before allocation; it was not retried. No full-symptom closure is claimed.

Root-cause analysis credit: @alexcousins-muratec. The contributor's release-specific patch was read only and never executed or adopted. The separate historical 1ms readiness-budget starvation was already repaired by 9405010d01e (#169787), first containing tag v2026.10.10-beta.1; no timeout changes are included.

## Work sessions

[Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

prs.title: fix: restore plugin SDK builds and keep Skills and Plugins discovery within request limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Plugin SDK builds exceeded the declaration-size limit. Separately, checking MCP configuration ownership resolved filesystem paths on the Gateway thread. The Skills and Plugins pages also fetched resources they didn't need on first visit, and Workshop lost its heading at tablet width. These regressions reproduced on the base of [the Template sign-in PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013); this companion keeps their repairs out of that feature.

## User Impact
The collapsed Skills shelf shows the full installed count. Skills and Plugins stay within their existing request limits, Workshop has a heading on tablets, and plugin developers can build the SDK without a public signature change. No migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made
- Reuse the named tools schema instead of duplicating its SDK declaration.
- Move SQLite owner verification for registered metadata reads off the Gateway thread. The owner remains authoritative for exact file identity and revocable clean-close proof.
- Load Skills reader/upload and Settings-only copy on demand. Settle discovery against actual installed and registry inventory; keep Install disabled until inventory confirms availability. Measure painted attachment-menu frames, not hidden ones. No request caps, timing windows, or retry thresholds were relaxed.
- Merge with `main` at `8253356c9864`, which now opens skills as pages ([#202581](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202581)) and includes the [Plugins performance repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202687). The merge keeps main's skill detail page rather than the earlier dialog. It adds two integration repairs: the phone header actions get an inline fallback so a pending inventory read cannot keep the Skills page and its filter from mounting, and the Skills inventory helpers and their English copy share one chunk so the page stays within its request limit.

## Evidence
[Clean and annotated Skills and Workshop screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202715#issuecomment-7050055796). The screenshots predate the merge with `main`.

Current head, tree `6d9b500cebbd71bc99b98a68304fbdfaf87be1c8`, local macOS Chromium, not hosted Linux CI:

- Full build passed, including the SDK declaration-size check. 199 focused tests passed with no skips or retries: 110 UI unit, 29 browser component, 49 browser end-to-end across nine files, and 11 benchmark unit tests.
- Navigating to Skills while its inventory read is pending failed in both the resolve and reject cases before the header repair (9/11) and passes after it (11/11).
- Requests by page readiness, single cold runs against unchanged caps: Skills 28 (cap 28), Skills Settings 26 (cap 31), Plugins 53 (cap 56), Plugin Settings 52 (cap 61). Before the chunk repair the merged tree measured 29 and 32 on the two Skills pages.
- Skills became ready with 1,000 installed skills and 20 registry cards, and correctly did not become ready with 999. Opening the last skill made one card request and rendered its Markdown on the full page route with no dialog. Workshop kept its heading at 768px and its floating title at 393px.
- All 148 main-only paths match `main`. Of the 34 prerequisite-only paths, 33 match the previously reviewed head; the Skills toolbar is the exception. The 17 SDK and state files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head.

Earlier results on the pre-merge tree `006888272bbadb0e08143c04066b88e2475c4d6b`:

- On pinned main `fe9694b8733c`, 77/86 browser cases passed; on that tree all 86 passed across eight files, including both Template phone journeys.
- SDK declarations were 5,323,175 of 5,385,536 bytes, with no signature changes across 3,908 public exports. Net test lines: +149/400.
- The unchanged MCP keep/replace assertions, which call the mutation helper directly, went from 8/4 synchronous path resolutions to zero. Keep still mutates; replacement refuses without changing the bytes.
- A real local Gateway edit (`mcp tools fixture --include search`, isolated loopback state, disabled OAuth fixture, no credentials) persisted the filter and still made four synchronous `realpath` calls on the Gateway thread, all from `assertStateDatabaseAccessAllowed` during the lifecycle lease. The zero figure above therefore applies to the direct helper assertions, not to a whole operator edit. A write with a stale revision was refused and left the config bytes unchanged. Physical owner replacement was not exercised on a running Gateway, and this run has no baseline comparison.
- A separate sign-in rehearsal retained the feature's 40 changed paths and lines. Full build and real local Gateway/Chromium clipboard → approval tab → private draft review → Preview passed using a loopback provider. No external account connection or Template publication.

Known boundary: the state-only Gateway consumer run returned 48 passed, 1 skipped, 1 inherited failure on live physical database replacement. The untouched base refused the same replacement. No assertion, live-takeover policy, or restore contract was changed here.

The previous head's `checks-ui (2/3)` job stalled for 15 minutes in `chat-pane-inline-output.browser.test.tsx` and was stopped by the watchdog. The same test passed in 3.1 seconds in a local replay of that exact CI merge and shard order, so the cause of the hosted stall is not identified and this PR does not change chat code.

The [landed plugin contract changes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202666) are preserved. Compare [Skills readiness](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202694) for partial overlap.

prs.title: fix: every tracked process names its chat; stop ended cron runs' processes and survivors' later children
prs.body:
Related: #201157, #199079

## What Problem This Solves

#201157 made a hidden subagent's task end and archive stop the chat's processes. Four gaps of the same class remained, all reproduced on isolated Gateways:

- **Isolated cron runs.** A cron run session (`agent:<id>:cron:<job>:run:<id>`) takes no turn after its run, but its `background: true` services, `yieldMs` hand-offs and `nohup … &` survivors kept running until the session reaper ran. The run session is hidden, so nothing showed them. Reproduced with `openai/gpt-6.2-sol`: after a successful cron run, its HTTP server and `nohup` process were still alive.
- **Children a survivor forks later.** Adopted survivors were stopped per pid. A survivor that starts a child after adoption (a Gateway respawning a worker) left that child running untracked after chat end.
- **macOS without the service marker.** An unmanaged macOS Gateway did not hand survivors off, so they were neither tracked nor stopped.
- **The bad state was representable.** `ProcessSession.scopeKey` was optional, so a process could be tracked without an owning chat (`adoptSurvivor` passed `scopeKey ?? ""`, `stopSessionExecProcesses` filtered `!== undefined`, `resolveProcessToolScopeKey` could return `undefined`), and records were built and registered separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat stays the one owner of its processes, and `stopSessionExecProcesses` stays the one stop.

- **Ratchet.** `ProcessSession.scopeKey` is a required `string`. `registerProcessSession(params)` is the only exported way to track a process; it replaces `createProcessSession` plus `addSession` at the four spawn paths (exec runtime, survivor adoption, durable restore, lost-ordinary report). `resolveProcessToolScopeKey` always returns a scope; an exec tool without a session resolves its agent once through the session-agent owner (`resolveExecToolScopeKey`, used by tool assembly and `createExecTool`). `runExecProcess` and `processGatewayAllowlist` require the scope, so a spawn call without one does not compile.
- **Teardown census.** The shared per-file test teardown fails a file that leaves a live process (not durable, no stop requested) in the scope of a hidden subagent whose rows have all ended, and kills it.
- **Group stop.** A survivor carries the process group it ran in at hand-off. Chat end and Gateway stop signal that group (SIGTERM, 5 s grace, SIGKILL) while the survivor still runs in it and it is not the Gateway's own group. `process kill` on one survivor still stops only that process, so it cannot take siblings with it.
- **Relay on every POSIX host.** Agent exec owns its process tree on macOS too, not only on Linux (where it was added for the memory budget, #193044) or under a service marker. The memory budget stays Linux-only.
- **Cron run sessions.** The isolated run's context disposal (moved from `run.ts` to `session-cleanup.ts`) stops the `:run:` session's processes. A yield on the run's commands resumes inside `executeCronRun`, so it has settled by then. Persistent cron targets are not `:run:` sessions and are unchanged.
- **`canStop: false`** (audit note) is not a defect: `openclaw gateway call` connects with least-privilege scopes (`operator.read` for `sessions.processes.list`), and `canStop` correctly says that client may not stop. A write-scoped client (the Control UI) gets `true`, as `session-processes.test.ts` asserts. No UI change.

## User Impact

- An isolated cron run's services and leftover processes stop when the run ends. To keep one, use `durable: true`.
- At chat end (reset, delete, archive, subagent or cron run end) and Gateway stop, a leftover process's later children stop with it.
- On a macOS Gateway started outside launchd, `cmd &` and `nohup` survivors are tracked, listed by `process list`, and stopped at chat end, as they already were on Linux and under launchd.
- Main chats, visible spawned sessions, yielded subagents and the one-shot `agent --local` hand-off are unchanged.

## Evidence

Tests with real child processes, red on `origin/main` `9d6f4a94adf5`, green here:

- `subagent-task-end-processes.lifecycle.test.ts`: the survivor now forks a child after adoption. Base: all 5 stop rows fail with that child alive; branch: all pass. New row "complete without a service marker": base leaves the survivor and its child alive; the branch stops both.
- `run.session-processes.test.ts` (enters `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn`): base leaves the run session's service alive; the branch stops it.
- `subagent-process-census.test.ts`: the census reports an ended subagent's live process and ignores a running subagent's or one already being stopped. The census ran over the subagent and exec suites with no leak found.
- Ratchet: `tsgo` core, core tests and extensions pass. Removing `scopeKey` from a `registerProcessSession` or `runExecProcess` call fails to compile (`Property 'scopeKey' is missing`).
- Consumers of the process-registry API (95 files) and the cron `run.*` suites (39 files): green. Three failures in that run were checked on base: two are load-timing flakes that also fail on base, and one matches the worktree path (it contains "process").
- Full build with declarations and a packed install smoke (`pnpm pack`, global install, `--version`, `cron add --help`).

Fault matrix on isolated Gateways (`env -i`, scratch state, service marker unless noted, scripted model). R2 `yieldMs` hand-off, R3 `background: true`, R4 `nohup &`, R5 child a survivor forks after adoption, R6 `setsid` double fork. Alive after the cell:

| Cell | Base | Branch |
|---|---|---|
| Isolated cron run completed | R2 R3 R4 R5 R6 | R6 |
| Subagent kill | R5 R6 | R6 |
| Parent delete, child running | R5 R6 | R6 |
| Archive | R5 R6 | R6 |
| Subagent completion / failure, parent delete after completion | R6 | R6 (#201157 cells stay clean) |
| Subagent yielded on its hand-off | R2 kept, resumed | R2 kept, resumed |
| No marker: subagent completion | R4 R5 R6 (untracked) | R6 |
| Main chat completion | all alive, counted | unchanged by design |

Real model (`openai/gpt-6.2-sol`, isolated Gateway): an isolated cron job ran a `background: true` HTTP server, a `nohup` process and a foreground command; the run ended `ok`. Base: server and survivor alive afterwards. Branch: nothing left. `ps` excerpts are in the comment below.

The live Gateway was untouched (launchd pid unchanged, config equal to its backup), and every process the proof started is gone.

## Merge danger and blast radius

- Two-way door: no schema, stored row, protocol or config change. Durable rows written before this keep loading (`scopeKey` falls back to the row's `sessionKey`).
- Cron jobs whose isolated runs started services meant to outlive the run lose them at run end; `durable: true` keeps them.
- Group stop signals only a group created for the command; it is never the Gateway's group, and the survivor must still be in it. Accepted edge: a group that empties in the instant between the survivor's exit and the final SIGKILL could be reused.
- macOS agent exec now runs through the relay anchor: one small Node process per command, as on Linux and launchd-managed macOS.
- Size: production +324/−188. About 60 of those lines are re-indentation; the remaining growth is group stop (~50), the cron stop (+49 in `session-cleanup.ts`, −34 in `run.ts`) and the scope resolver. Tests and fixtures: about +380/−140, mostly mechanical fixture moves.

prs.title: fix: let large memory forget operations complete
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory forget selection contains more chunk IDs than SQLite can bind in one query, preview or purge can fail with `too many SQL variables` instead of reporting or completing the requested operation.

## User Impact

Large forget operations can count and remove the selected chunks and vectors while retaining unrelated indexed rows.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `sqliteStringSet` helper represents an ID set with one bound value. The FTS count, vector count, and SQLite purge deletes now use that existing owner; PostgreSQL keeps its existing bounded-set query behavior.

## Evidence

At head `64883380d39`, shipped-entry CLI runs against an isolated synthetic state containing 34,000 selected chunks plus an unrelated keeper row:

```text
$ pnpm openclaw memory forget --agent main --session target --dry-run --json
{"dryRun":true,"artifacts":{"indexChunks":34000,"ftsRows":34000,"vectorRows":34000},"refusals":[]}

$ pnpm openclaw memory forget --agent main --session target --json
{"dryRun":false,"artifacts":{"indexChunks":34000,"ftsRows":34000,"vectorRows":34000},"refusals":[]}

After apply, read-only database verification:
{"remainingChunks":["keeper"],"remainingVectors":["keeper"]}
```

Both CLI commands exited 0. The focused owner regressions also pass: `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget.sources.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "counts fts and vector rows past the sqlite bind-variable limit|applies a forget past the sqlite bind-variable limit"` reports 2 passed and 13 other tests filtered out. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, targeted oxlint, targeted oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.

The full `memory-forget.sources.test.ts` run passed both new regressions, then made no further progress in existing tests and was interrupted after three minutes; it is not claimed as a complete pass. The new regressions were not run against the base, so no base-failing test result is claimed. Exact-head CI is awaiting maintainer authorization (`action_required`, zero jobs).

prs.title: fix(ui): keep the right-docked Home actions clear of the window controls
prs.body:
Closes #162448

## What Problem This Solves

On Linux and Windows desktop windows the caption buttons (minimize, maximize, close) are drawn over the top-right corner. The right-docked Home panel starts at the top of the window, so its three header actions (open Home, dock, close) sit underneath those buttons: the glyphs overlap and the caption buttons receive the clicks.

## User Impact

The Home panel's actions can be used again when it is docked on the right. Panels docked at the bottom, macOS and fullscreen windows are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel header is a rail header, and rail headers reserve space through `--rail-header-padding-end`. The page toolbar already adds the desktop shell's `--openclaw-native-window-controls-width` as trailing padding. The right-docked panel now does the same under `html.openclaw-native-desktop`. The shell publishes a width of 0 on macOS and in fullscreen, so those keep the default 8px.

Accepted edge case: when a terminal, browser or link reader reserves the right edge, the panel is no longer at the corner but still keeps the extra padding. That costs only some header space, so I did not add code for it.

## Behavior proof

Scenario: Home docked on the right in a 1280x900 desktop window with Linux caption buttons.

Captured from the production Control UI build in Chromium (English, light theme) with the repository's Control UI e2e harness. The window chrome is the Linux app's real `window-chrome.js` and `window-chrome.css` with a stubbed window API, and the Gateway is the harness's mock with synthetic data. No real desktop host was used. Before is the base commit `c2e7b54ab` and after is this PR's head `0f8013be5`. The frames are unannotated.

### Full window

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the Home panel's actions are drawn on top of the minimize, maximize and close buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62aa5f94-f304-4ead-8fe8-3ae9df5b910b) | ![After: the Home panel's actions sit to the left of the window buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a507b2d0-04b3-4443-8400-3e9116fe191c) |

### Top-right corner

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before, corner: panel action glyphs overlap the caption buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd9a0fec-6d5e-4640-a920-3f611426627a) | ![After, corner: panel actions are spaced clear of the caption buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cb778d7-3208-4353-88a1-aaf189a9f015) |

## Evidence

- New browser test `keeps the right-docked Home actions clear of the %s window controls` (Linux and Windows). prs.title: fix: show chat progress while Codex retries
prs.body:
Closes #202578

## What Problem This Solves

A chat can spend minutes showing typing while Codex retries a model request, leaving people in the group unsure why the answer is taking so long.

## User Impact

Chats that show model-wait progress display “Still working. Retrying…” once while Codex retries. The notice clears when the reply arrives.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app-server’s `willRetry` notification feeds the same progress path as a wait for a model slot. The channel’s preview settings control whether that progress appears.

## Evidence

### Telegram during the second capacity retry

Both screenshots show the second retry in the same private Telegram chat, with a loopback fixture supplying capacity errors.

**Before on main (`1129d4c`)**

![Telegram on main showing only the typing indicator](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86c7f538-1c17-44b2-9946-9d7cbcb35692)

**After on the PR head (`08de645`)**

![Telegram on the PR head showing “Still working. Retrying…”](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e2c54b4-2ca5-4c81-ba03-5640cbbfbaa4)

### Reply and removal on the PR head

![Telegram showing the final reply after the retry notice was removed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8386e8da-8378-46ef-9691-cc57b0f4759f)

An isolated Gateway with bundled Codex and automatic text replies enabled received five overload responses from the fixture, then a successful text response. The trace records the live Telegram Bot API receipts. Message IDs are replaced with labels.

```text
+00.000s  Telegram accepted the private test prompt
+06.413s  Codex request 1: capacity error (Retry-After 2s)
+08.542s  Codex request 2: capacity error (Retry-After 12s)
+08.846s  Telegram sendMessage accepted [notice] "Still working. Retrying…"
+20.638s  Codex request 3: capacity error (Retry-After 2s)
+22.735s  Codex request 4: capacity error (Retry-After 2s)
+24.831s  Codex request 5: capacity error (Retry-After 2s)
+26.923s  Codex request 6: successful final text response
+28.170s  Telegram sendMessage accepted [reply] "I can reply now."
+29.108s  Telegram deleteMessage accepted [notice]
```

Ran the issue’s loopback Telegram supergroup reproduction with the real Gateway and bundled Codex. Both builds made six generation requests with five overload retries and shortened delays.

| Scenario | Observed Telegram delivery |
| --- | --- |
| Main (`2aca1a1`) | Typing during retries, then one final answer. The retry-notice assertion failed. |
| This change | One notice during the wait, then the final answer and deletion of that notice. |
| Previews off | One final answer. |
| Healthy first response | One final answer. |

After pr-simplify, 101 tests passed across the reply runner, queued follow-ups, Codex terminal events, and Telegram progress lifecycle. Core and extension type checks, targeted lint and formatting, and the Gateway build passed. Local Codex autoreview of the full diff found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The supergroup reproduction used loopback Telegram and Responses fixtures.

prs.title: feat: reorder agents in your personal sidebar
prs.body:
Related: #155039. Builds on the sidebar interaction proposal in #155139; this implementation uses personal profile preferences rather than Gateway-wide ordering.

## What Problem This Solves

People using several agents cannot keep their most-used agents near the top of the sidebar without changing unrelated configuration.

## User Impact

Drag an unpinned agent's six-dot handle, use **Move up / Move down** in its menu, or **Reset agent order** from the workspace menu. The default order stays unchanged until customized.

The order syncs across the signed-in user's browsers. Other users' layouts, pin membership, agent configuration, routing, Agents home, and the New conversation picker are unchanged. Oversized orders are rejected visibly without changing the previous saved order.

## Why This Change Was Made

This reuses the existing sidebar controls and profile-preference sync path, with no new dependencies. Saved positions survive temporarily unavailable agents; new agents follow the saved order. Moves stay within the pinned or unpinned section.

**Review status — 10 November:** updated the branch with upstream `63f4933167bf8fa7eb682829bd5ec6196173cc0a` and resolved four merge conflicts without changing the personal, profile-synced, sidebar-only scope. The last hosted code review covered `290aad3` and found no actionable findings; it is historical evidence, not a review of this merge. Human maintainer acceptance remains outstanding. No merge or production installation has been performed.

## Evidence

### Upstream conflict refresh — 10 November

Head: `3bdbc32f067d72455a08a115574c22ca1cf6a96f`; tested tree: `544d11d00b9781806212efa7dff3279198c55fbb`; upstream merge parent: `63f4933167bf8fa7eb682829bd5ec6196173cc0a`. This is a normal merge update, not a history rewrite.

No scope expansion, dependency changes, or budget increases relative to that main revision.

The initial browser launch failed for a missing local shared library; the browser lane passed using retained process-local test libraries, with no host installation.

- **Fresh 50-agent real-Gateway Chromium proof passes:** durable preference, same-profile push sync, profile isolation, reload, fresh context, synchronized reset/reload and final-row reachability. Scenario: 100.005 s; Vitest: 294.01 s excluding cold runtime preparation. Served entry `/assets/index-wekNpLav.js`, SHA-256 `b9e8f1dd1e333b20d76a1aad7926dd2ae97a9a4ceab66899b1bd002ac76ce622`. Source tree: `a26272254e4d5505f1ef611f83d0eeba37d8c428`.

prs.title: fix: distinguish a recovered gateway from its failed update checks
prs.body:
Follow-up to #202678, which fixed #202657. This PR does not reimplement Inbox retention.

## What Problem This Solves

A failed update report can show a green running service beside a red version check after the intended build has recovered. The report does not say whether that target is now serving or when the checks were measured.

## User Impact

When the connected Gateway matches the recorded update target, the report says so. It labels the old checks **Verification at the time of the update**. An unrelated later build or ambiguous rollback is not labeled as recovery. The original failure remains recorded.

prs.title: feat(msteams): send private and shared channel files to the channel's own SharePoint site
prs.body:
Closes #185926

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bots cannot send files in Microsoft Teams private or shared channels unless an operator configures a single central `sharePointSiteId`, which exposes every private channel's files to that site's members and still shows "request access" to channel members.

## User Impact

User impact: in private and shared channels, file sends now land on that channel's own SharePoint site, where exactly the channel's members already have access, and the file card opens without extra permissions. No organization-wide sharing link is created for those files. Standard channels, group chats and explicit `sharePointSiteId` keep their current behavior. No new Graph permissions and no config changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on #189339. Teams keeps a private/shared channel's site membership in sync with the channel, so the channel's own site is the only upload target that preserves the channel audience. For a non-standard `membershipType`, the resolver reads `GET /teams/{groupId}/channels/{channelId}/filesFolder`, then `GET /drives/{driveId}?$select=sharePointIds` (drive resources spell it `sharePointIds`; driveItems use `sharepointIds`), and builds the site ID `{hostname},{siteId},{webId}`. Results are cached per account, tenant, bot, team and channel, like the team-site cache.

`resolveMSTeamsSharePointSiteId` now returns `{ siteId, memberScoped }`. Member-scoped uploads skip `createLink`: the organization link that channel sends create would let anyone in the tenant holding its URL read a private-channel file, and channel membership already grants access through the file card's `webDavUrl`. An incomplete drive response fails closed before upload.

## Evidence

- **Focused tests:** `vitest` msteams config, 92 files / 943 tests pass. New cases run the real send paths (proactive and reply) against stubbed Graph `fetch`: private and shared channels upload to the channel site, never call `/groups/.../sites/root` or `createLink`, and cache the channel site (one `filesFolder` call across two sends); member-scoped uploads create no link; incomplete `sharePointIds` fails closed.
- **Static:** `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: typecheck (extensions and extension tests), lint, plugin boundaries and the other guards pass. The dead-export scan fails only on `src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-prepared-read.ts` (`retireControlUiSessionPrState`), unrelated to this change.

### Real behavior proof (production)

Multi-team production deployment, private channel, `sharePointSiteId` absent.

**Before** (#189339's behavior; private channels rejected). Gateway file log, redacted:

```
14:00:01Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 3 rows of test data"
          conversation: 19:<private-channel-id>@thread.tacv2;messageid=<id>
14:00:01Z [msteams] dispatching to agent
14:02:57Z [tools] tool_call failed: msteams file send failed: Automatic SharePoint site discovery
          supports standard channels only. Set channels.msteams.sharePointSiteId to upload to a specific site.
14:03:02Z [msteams] dispatch complete — counts: { tool: 0, block: 0, final: 1 }
```

The user received a text-only reply. No file reached the channel.

**After** (this change, backported onto the deployed release). Same private channel, first file send after a gateway restart (empty cache):

```
11:24:17Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 4 rows of test data"
11:24:17Z [msteams] dispatching to agent — sessionKey: agent:main:msteams:channel:19:<private-channel-id>…
11:24:36Z [msteams:send] sent native file card — fileName: <report> 1.csv
```

Graph check after the send (bot application credentials):

- `<folder>/<report> 1.csv` (created 11:24:35Z) sits on the private channel's own site (`/sites/<team>-<private-channel>`).
- Item permissions are only the channel site's Owners / Members / Visitors groups. No `organization` link.
- The parent team site has no entry for this send.
- The requester opened the file card from the channel.

During rollout, the first build read `sharepointIds` from the drive and failed closed ("incomplete SharePoint IDs") without uploading anything; Graph returns `sharePointIds` on drive resources. A later build still created the organization link; Graph showed it on the item, which is why member-scoped uploads now skip `createLink`.

### Access check (member, non-member, removal)

Same private channel. Each person opened the file's direct document URL in a browser, signed in with their own work account. Times are UTC.

| Step | Who | File | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Channel member | `<report-1>.csv`, sent by the bot | Opens (09:14) |
| 2 | Owner of the parent team, not a channel member. Also tried with their admin account | `<report-1>.csv` | Access denied (09:16) |
| 3 | The step 1 member, removed from the channel about 6 minutes earlier | `<report-1>.csv` | "You need access" (09:24) |
| 4 | Bot sends a new file in the same channel. No gateway restart, so the channel site comes from the cache | `<report-2>.csv` | Lands on the channel site (09:23). Inherits the library permissions; no sharing link |
| 5 | The removed member | `<report-2>.csv` | "You need access" (09:26) |
| 6 | A channel owner | `<report-2>.csv` | Opens (09:25) |

The removed user left the channel site's Members group without any bot action (checked 09:18). Access follows Teams channel membership.

Before step 1, an organization link on `<report-1>.csv` was deleted. A manual "Copy link" in the Teams client had created it, not the bot. After that, both files grant access only to the channel site's Owners, Members and Visitors groups (checked through SharePoint REST as a channel owner).

prs.title: fix: allow up to 100 ordinary subagents per parent
prs.body:
Closes #202263

## What Problem This Solves

A parent using ordinary `sessions_spawn` runs hits a configuration ceiling of 20 active children.

## User Impact

A parent can run up to 100 ordinary subagents at once by setting both `maxChildrenPerAgent` and `maxConcurrent` to 100 under `agents.defaults.subagents`. The default child cap remains 5. The existing nesting limit and Swarm limits still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

Raise the configuration ceiling and document how the admission and execution limits work together. The existing per-parent admission logic enforces the configured cap.

## Evidence

The same isolated Gateway scenario ran on pinned main and the PR head. One parent used `sessions_spawn` with Swarm disabled and both ordinary-subagent limits set to the values below. A loopback OpenAI Responses fixture held every child reply until the extra spawn was rejected. The run then checked each child through `agent.wait` and `chat.history`.

**main** ([`c2e7b54ab6f5`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c2e7b54ab6f5adc693d04fe53a992d4c0458bb43))

```text
config set saved 20, rejected 100, and retained 20.
20 distinct ordinary children simultaneously awaiting their model replies (0 replies released).
Child 21 refused while all 20 were active: sessions_spawn has reached max active children for this session (20/20; agents.defaults.subagents.maxChildrenPerAgent).
20/20 child runs completed with distinct final replies verified through agent.wait and chat.history.
```

**PR head** ([`ba2443839939`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ba244383993912529f57df182e686d447e5fa50e))

```text
config set saved 100, rejected 101, and retained 100.
100 distinct ordinary children simultaneously awaiting their model replies (0 replies released).
Child 101 refused while all 100 were active: sessions_spawn has reached max active children for this session (100/100; agents.defaults.subagents.maxChildrenPerAgent).
100/100 child runs completed with distinct final replies verified through agent.wait and chat.history.
```

Both focused Gateway runs passed with deterministic fixture replies. Both Gateways logged warnings for pending completion notices to the parent during shutdown, after all child replies had been verified.

prs.title: fix(openai): embed system prompt in input on ChatGPT Responses when uncached (#202372)
prs.body:
Closes #202372

## What Problem This Solves

On `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` and other models using the ChatGPT Responses backend (`openai-chatgpt-responses`), top-level `instructions` are not cached by the provider, but the request builder always placed the system prompt in `instructions` and disabled input prompt conversion. This resulted in the entire system prompt being reprocessed uncached on every turn, causing excessive subscription quota usage and avoidable prefill latency.

## User Impact

User impact: Restores prompt caching for system prompts on GPT-6.2 models accessed via ChatGPT OAuth subscriptions by embedding the prompt in leading developer input as indicated by `cachesInstructions: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model catalog already configures `cachesInstructions: false` for GPT-6.2, but the ChatGPT Responses adapter hardcoded `includeSystemPrompt: false` and always populated `instructions`. Consulting `cachesInstructions` enables system-prompt input conversion and omits the uncached `instructions` field when `cachesInstructions` is `false`, while preserving existing `instructions` behavior for models that support and cache it.

## Evidence

### Wire Comparison (`openai-chatgpt-responses`)

| Field | Base (before fix) | Head (with fix, `cachesInstructions: false`) |
|---|---|---|
| `instructions` | `"You are an autonomous agent."` (uncached on 6.2) | `undefined` (omitted from payload) |
| `input[0]` | `{ type: "message", role: "user", ... }` | `{ type: "message", role: "developer", content: [{ type: "input_text", text: "You are an autonomous agent." }] }` |
| `input[1]` | Next user turn message | `{ type: "message", role: "user", ... }` |

### Multi-turn WebSocket Continuation & Cache Reuse Trace

Verified over unmocked `WebSocketServer` via `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`:

1. **Turn 1 (Cold request, initial developer prompt)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "developer", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "System Prompt 1" }] },
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 1" }] }
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: `instructions` omitted; system prompt placed in leading developer input for prefix caching.

2. **Turn 2 (Continuation with unchanged prompt)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "previous_response_id": "resp_1",
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 2" }] }
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: `previous_response_id` continues the stored chain. The delta input carries only the new user turn without duplicating the developer prompt or breaking prefix caching.

3. **Turn 3 (System prompt changed to `System Prompt 2 (Changed)`)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "developer", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "System Prompt 2 (Changed)" }] },
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 1" }] },
       ...
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: Continuation is safely invalidated (`previous_response_id` omitted) and a full replay is dispatched with the new developer prompt.

### Automated Test Suite Execution

- **Reproduction**: Unit test proved red failure on base (`AssertionError: expected { model: 'gpt-6.2-sol', ... } to not have property "instructions" (received "You are an autonomous agent.")`) and passes green with the fix.
- **Suite Results**:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`: **35 passed** (including uncached prompt placement, cached prompt retention, and multi-turn WebSocket continuation).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.replay.test.ts`: **4 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses-streaming.test.ts`: **9 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses-protocol.test.ts`: **5 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-uncached-instructions.integration.test.ts`: **4 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-payload-policy.test.ts`: **28 passed**
- **Standards & Code Quality**:
  - `oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `run-format.mts` & `git diff --check`: Clean.

prs.title: fix(cli): connect through gateway.remote.edgeAuth without a Gateway token
prs.body:
Closes #199691

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw tui`, `openclaw tui --url` and `openclaw gateway call` refuse to dial a Gateway behind Cloudflare Access (or another identity-aware proxy) when the client has `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` but no Gateway token or password. A guest's device therefore never files its first pairing request.

## User Impact

User impact: a CLI configured with `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` connects to a trusted-proxy Gateway without a shared Gateway secret. On first contact `openclaw tui` gets `device pairing required` and leaves a request for the admin, as the [Cloudflare Access guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/cloudflare-access#verify) already describes. Configurations without edgeAuth, and targets on other origins, still require credentials as before. A Gateway on token or password auth still needs its credential: edgeAuth only gets the connection through the proxy, and the Gateway then refuses the missing token. A device that has never connected pairs through `openclaw tui`; its `openclaw gateway call` now says so instead of answering with a bare `missing scope: operator.read`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three local prechecks reject a connection that has no token, password or stored device token: one in `callGatewayWithScopes`, `ensureExplicitGatewayAuth` for `--url` targets, and the TUI's connection resolver. None of them knew that the proxy authenticates the upgrade. Each now skips the shared-credential requirement when edge-auth headers are configured for the target's origin, using the existing `gatewayEdgeAuthValueForTarget` origin match. The Gateway's device pairing then decides access, so nothing new is trusted on the client.

First pairing stays in `openclaw tui`. `openclaw gateway call` is read-only, so on a device that has never connected it has no device identity to pair; the Gateway accepts the connection and refuses the method with `MISSING_SCOPE`. When edge-auth headers are set, the call has no device identity and the Gateway answers `MISSING_SCOPE`, the error now adds `Fix: this device is not paired with this Gateway yet. Run \`openclaw tui\` once to pair this device, ...` (`withEdgeAuthPairingHint` in `src/gateway/call-device-auth.ts`). When the call was given `--url`, the command in the hint keeps it (`openclaw tui --url <url>`), as the existing stored-device-auth recovery message does, because a bare `openclaw tui` can select another Gateway, such as a local one. `call.ts` is over its line cap, so its edge-auth header lookup is inlined, as the TUI's already is, to keep the file from growing.

`docs/cli/tui.md` and `docs/gateway/remote.md` say that, when the Gateway uses trusted-proxy auth, the first connection through edgeAuth needs no token and sends a pairing request, and that a Gateway on token or password auth still needs its credential.

## Security

Based on a source comparison against `main`, the CLI connects through Cloudflare Access as another interface to the same Gateway, using Access headers instead of the web UI's browser cookie. Both paths use the same server authentication, scope caps and role limits. This change grants no new scopes. Access headers do not replace Gateway token or password authentication.

New TUI devices still need pairing approval under the Gateway's existing policy. A fresh `openclaw gateway call` can connect without a device identity, but the server clears its claimed scopes. That device-less session receives scoped access only through explicitly configured identity grants, capped by role limits, as with the existing device-less web UI path. Without those grants, pair through `openclaw tui` before making scoped calls.

## Evidence

- **Tests:**
  - New `src/gateway/call.edge-auth.test.ts` (6 cases) and one new case in `src/tui/gateway-chat.connection.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(discord): keep the Gateway responsive when a reply has long slash or www. runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Discord reply that mentions someone and contains a long run of slashes or `www.` without spaces freezes the Gateway before the reply is sent. A 16,000-character run of `/` takes 2.4 seconds to prepare and a 32,000-character run takes 9.2 seconds. Every other session and channel waits for that time, because the work runs synchronously on the Gateway main thread. The text comes from the model, so a prompt injection in fetched content can ask for such a reply.

## User Impact

User impact: Discord replies with long slash, `www.` or letter runs are prepared in a few milliseconds, and other chats keep working while they are sent. Mentions, bold text and links in Discord replies render exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before a reply is sent, OpenClaw marks bare URLs in the text so mention rewriting and bold normalization leave them alone. `findDiscordUrlRanges` in `extensions/discord/src/url-ranges.ts` does that marking. It had two quadratic paths.

1. After it found a URL start (`//`, `www.`, `mailto:` or a scheme), it scanned to the end of the URL. The next search then started right after the URL start, so every `//` or `www.` inside that URL started another scan to the same end. A run of 16,000 slashes produced 8,000 ranges, each scanned to the end of the run.
2. The scheme pattern `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:\/\/` was retried at every letter of a long word. Each try walked to the end of the word before it failed.

The fix keeps the same pattern and checks with two changes.

- After a range is found, the search continues from the end of that range. A URL start found inside a range only produced a range nested inside it, so the covered text is the same.
- A scheme is only tried where a run of scheme characters begins (`(?<![A-Za-z0-9+.-])`). The run may start with digits, `+`, `.` or `-`, and the range still starts at the run's first letter, as it did before.

## Evidence

Time for `prepareDiscordOutboundText` (render, then mention rewrite) on `@alice here is the output:\n<body>\nthanks` with a configured `alice` alias. Single calls in one process.

| Body | Chars | main `4b74fd5` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prose (`word ` repeated) | 32,034 | 0.7 ms | 0.6 ms |
| `/` repeated | 8,034 | 628 ms | 2.0 ms |
| `/` repeated | 16,034 | 2,385 ms | 1.3 ms |
| `/` repeated | 32,034 | 9,174 ms | 3.8 ms |
| `www.` repeated | 16,034 | 1,491 ms | 1.7 ms |
| `www.` repeated | 32,034 | 4,679 ms | 1.7 ms |

`findDiscordUrlRanges` alone at 16,000 characters:

| Input | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` repeated | 2,535 ms (8,000 ranges) | 1.9 ms (1 range) |
| `www.` repeated | 1,279 ms (4,000 ranges) | 0.9 ms (1 range) |
| `http://` repeated | 686 ms | 1.1 ms |
| `a` repeated | 345 ms | 0.2 ms |
| `-a` repeated | 168 ms | 0.2 ms |

Equivalence checks:

- A differential fuzzer ran 1.8 million random strings built from URL starts, scheme characters, punctuation, parentheses, `<`, `>`, `_`, `@`, spaces and non-ASCII letters. For every string the branch returned exactly the main ranges that sit outside every earlier main range, and both covered the same characters. It found 0 differences. 1,343,173 of these strings produced ranges, and the branch left out 1,005,719 nested ranges.
- `renderDiscordMarkdown` followed by `rewriteDiscordKnownMentions` ran on 100,000 random replies with mentions, `__bold__`, `**`, links and code spans. The output digest is identical on main and on this branch. 15,792 of those replies were changed by the rendering.

Tests on this branch:

- `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/url-ranges.test.ts`: 2 passed. On main both fail. The first test shows main returning a nested `www.c.d` range inside an outer URL. The second takes 14,775 ms on main against its 500 ms bound and 12 ms here.
- `npx vitest run` on the Discord markdown, mentions, outbound and send tests (18 files): 205 passed. The 6 failures in `send.voice.test.ts` also fail on main on this machine. They come from a group-writable parent directory that the temp-workspace guard rejects.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: clean.
- The change adds 25 test lines, inside the 400-line allowance.

Not tested: a live Discord bot. The measurements call the same reply preparation function that both the bot and webhook send paths use.

prs.title: improve: flag Docker-backed automation streams in Doctor
prs.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Draft for code-owner review. Not ready to land.

## What Problem This Solves

Before retiring a Docker-backed command stream, an operator needs to know which saved automations used Docker. A paused job or one held in quarantine can still have a container left over from an interrupted Gateway.

## User Impact

User impact: Doctor lists affected job IDs and explains how to confirm cleanup on the original Docker daemon. The advisory does not display the saved command or treat a paused definition as proof that the container stopped. Existing jobs are not converted, paused, or deleted by this change; Docker and Gateway streams continue to behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the Doctor inventory slice of the stream cutover. It reads the saved definitions and quarantine records Doctor already has, without adding a runtime reader or contacting Docker.

The bundled Gateway event source, the backed-up migration of Gateway definitions, and the automatic pause and safe settlement of Docker streams are still outstanding. The existing plugin event path only handles agent-turn payloads and does not evaluate stored stream condition gates on event admission, so rewriting schedule kinds now would not be lossless. The final cutover also needs to preserve approvals, output matching/batching and restart behavior, then remove the old runtime and authoring surfaces together.

Expected sibling overlap: cron Doctor findings and tests, and the shared schedules guide. This slice does not change the protocol, scheduling semantics, or Control UI.

## Evidence

- The Doctor cron suite passed 29 tests; the targeted regression passed again after the test fixture was simplified. The SQLite fixture includes an ordinary Gateway stream, a disabled Docker stream, and a quarantined Docker stream; it verifies which jobs are reported, that command text is omitted, and that the stored row is unchanged.
- Core typecheck, targeted lint and format, and `git diff --check` passed. Local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues in the Doctor change before the test-only trim. Simplification reused one advisory for structured and interactive Doctor without adding stores or execution hooks (+42 implementation/docs, +44 test lines).
- No Control UI change; no screenshots. No live Docker cleanup or stable upgrade was tested.

prs.title: fix: make the Plugins catalog clear when disconnected
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Gateway disconnects while the Plugins catalog is open, search results show a full-width pill with small reconnect copy, while the catalog landing page can say there are no matches. Neither shows clearly why results are missing.

## User Impact

Both views show the same readable unavailable state. Search text and filter selection stay in place, and results load when the Gateway reconnects. The existing shell remains the place for connection status and retry; the catalog does not show stale install actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog uses the existing panel empty-state component before choosing how to display results. The change adds no new storage or reconnect logic, and keeps connected ClawHub errors, permission denials, and actual empty results separate.

## Evidence

- Chromium on the real Control UI with a simulated Gateway: grouped landing and search both switch to the unavailable state, search retains focus, and reconnect restores search results and the selected category. Cold admission, a ClawHub read failure, a typed permission denial, and a successful empty response were checked separately.
- 47 focused catalog and discovery tests passed. Both new cases failed on the baseline. Control UI typecheck, formatting, and i18n verification passed.

prs.title: refactor: run the Gmail Pub/Sub watcher as a bundled plugin
prs.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Draft for code-owner review. Not ready to land.

Co-authored by Vyctor Brzezowski (`vyctorbrzezowski`).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with Vyctor Brzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/ab752961-46e2-42cb-9b74-07a56df10671)

## What Problem This Solves

Gmail Pub/Sub watches have their own start, reload, and shutdown paths in the Gateway. That makes them harder to maintain than other mail triggers, which use the standard plugin lifecycle. This draft moves watcher ownership first; it is not the complete Gmail cutover.

## User Impact

The bundled `gmail` plugin starts and renews the watcher. Existing `hooks.gmail` settings, HTTP mappings, `openclaw webhooks gmail` commands, and stored automations are unchanged. This slice does not rewrite, pause, or delete jobs, and adds no Doctor migration. If you restrict `plugins.allow`, include `gmail` for the Gateway-managed watcher; if plugins are disabled, the Gateway will not start it. Restart the Gateway after configuring the watcher for the first time so it loads the plugin. `OPENCLAW_SKIP_GMAIL_WATCHER=1` still opts out of Gateway startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin uses the existing scheduled service contract for startup, reload, and shutdown instead of a second Gateway lifecycle. The move exposes the shared process helpers needed to preserve executable lookup, Windows wrapper quoting, bounded diagnostics, and process-tree cleanup; it adds no Gmail-specific SDK API. The generated config inventory counts 23 additional standard plugin-entry fields for `gmail`; this slice adds no Gmail settings and leaves the core and channel counts unchanged.

Still to do before landing the full cutover: move the persisted settings and mapping defaults, add Doctor migration and upgrade proof (including restrictive plugin policy), remove the Gmail-specific model/reasoning precedence and startup model check, and move CLI registration and Gog Doctor diagnostics out of core. Likely sibling overlap is in Gateway reload, automation model selection, Doctor migrations, and generated config/plugin inventories. Jobs without saved accounts are left untouched unless an earlier owner transfer left the job awaiting a new account choice. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` before starting a manually upgraded Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model field already accepts an account suffix, so the billing choice can live alongside the model instead of in a second hidden record. This also removes the old account-adoption flow. Parallel automation cleanup PRs may touch the automation editor, scheduling API, or Doctor’s cron repair flow; this draft does not redesign them.

prs.title: fix: check recorded automation owners before running
prs.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Draft for code-owner review. Not ready to land.

## What Problem This Solves

An older automation can look like it has a human owner even though the owner was never saved. A scheduled trigger or command can also start after its recorded owner's profile is gone. This draft addresses those two cases; it is the first slice of the single-owner cutover.

## User Impact

- A scheduled occurrence with a recorded human owner checks for that profile before running its trigger or payload. If the profile is gone, the run stops before doing that work and tells an administrator how to select a new owner.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` backs up the cron store and saves a directly recorded creator profile as the owner when no owner was saved. It leaves an existing owner (including a transferred one), the tool list, and the enabled state intact for those jobs.
- If the record says the creator was a profile but provides no usable profile ID, Doctor pauses the job and reports how an administrator can claim it on the Automations page. No job is deleted by this repair. Other unattributed jobs retain existing behavior in this slice.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now writes the owner once instead of having each store read infer it. The scheduler checks the saved owner at the start of the occurrence, before either the trigger or payload can act.

## Risks and Remaining Work

This slice does not loosen existing tool, channel, approval, sandbox, session, or provider checks. It adds a refusal when the profile catalog is unavailable, the saved owner is gone, or a direct-profile record still needs Doctor. Migration trusts only the same direct creator stamp previously used by the runtime reader; it does not infer a person from delivery or channel settings. Profile presence is not a substitute for permission to use a tool or target.

The full owner-based permission snapshot is not implemented. Other stored authority fields, per-effect rechecks, account-bound scheduled Discord `channel-edit`, and pauses for jobs with no direct creator profile remain out of this slice. Gateway wire types, CLI, agent tool schema, and Control UI are unchanged. Expect overlap with sibling changes in scheduler admission, Doctor cron repair, and automation docs.

## Evidence

- 135 focused tests passed across the scheduler occurrence, Doctor SQLite repair, and store migration suites. The scheduler test checked missing and present profiles; the Doctor test checked persistence, backup reporting, transfer preservation, pause guidance, and repeat repair.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, focused lint, touched-file format, and `git diff --check` passed. Local Codex autoreview of the diff against `2b58c8e5224ee0` found no actionable P0/P1 issues within the supplied diff; it did not assess unchanged dependencies independently. The pr-simplify pass kept the existing owner field and Doctor writer (+61/−8 production TypeScript lines; +64 test lines; +8 docs lines).

prs.title: fix: let updates proceed when catalog model compat overrides are kept for review
prs.body:
Related: #200224

## What Problem This Solves

Updating from an install that still has a retired heartbeat setting (for example a disabled `agents.defaults.heartbeat`) is refused before anything changes when the config also overrides a capability flag on a catalog-known model, such as `compat.supportsJsonSchemaResponseFormat: true` on an Ollama Cloud model. 2026.11.10-beta.1 reports only `models.providers: Invalid configuration field`, and 2026.11.5 and 2026.11.6 misreport it as `agents.defaults: unrecognized key <key>`. `openclaw config validate` passes, so users have no way to find the cause.

## User Impact

User impact: these installs now update normally. The compat values are kept as written and Doctor still lists them for review. A disabled heartbeat stays disabled through the update, retired into a disabled automation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor treats a catalog-known model's compat value that differs from the provider catalog as something to show the operator for review. It deliberately never removes it, as the custom-provider docs describe. That finding was registered as a legacy config rule, though. When update admission projects the retired heartbeat repair, automatic config repair rechecks legacy rules after migrating and treats any remaining one as unresolved. This finding can never be resolved by migration, so admission refused every config that carried it alongside a retired heartbeat.

The rule is now marked review-only. Doctor keeps reporting it, but automatic repair and update admission no longer count it as blocking. Other legacy rules are unaffected: schema-invalid configs, such as a tool policy with both `allow` and `alsoAllow`, still block. Thanks to @FtlC-ian for isolating the exact model entries and message.

## Evidence

- **New admission test** (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-admit.heartbeat.test.ts`): a disabled heartbeat plus a divergent compat flag on the bundled Ollama Cloud catalog model `gpt-oss:20b`.
  - On `main` it refuses with the reporter's exact `models.providers: Invalid configuration field`.
  - With the fix it admits, and live config and state are unchanged.
- **Consumer tests:** `legacy.shared`, `automatic-config-repair`, `legacy-config-migrations.runtime.models`, `update-command-config-failure` and `update-command-admit` pass (125/125). `check:changed` shows typecheck, lint and guards green. The one failure is a dead-export finding in `extensions/knowledge` that already fails on `main`.
- **Live run** on Crabbox AWS Linux with real npm installs. The config has a disabled `agents.defaults.heartbeat` and `supportsJsonSchemaResponseFormat: true` on two Ollama Cloud catalog models and one custom model.

  | From → to | Result |
  |---|---|
  | 2026.11.4 → current `main` (CLI) | Refused: `models.providers: Invalid configuration field`. 2026.11.4 keeps running. |
  | 2026.11.4 → `main` + fix (CLI) | Succeeded in 281 s, `/readyz` 200 |
  | 2026.11.4 → `main` + fix (managed `update.run`) | Succeeded in 312 s, `/readyz` 200 |
  | 2026.11.5 → `main` + fix (CLI) | Succeeded in 274 s, `/readyz` 200 |

  After the fixed updates:
  - All three compat values are unchanged.
  - `config validate` returns `valid: true`.
  - Health reports `Heartbeat interval: disabled (main)`, and the heartbeat became the disabled automation `Proactive check (main)`.
- **Review:** autoreview is scoped-clean at P2. An independent Codex review of the same head found nothing.

Workaround for releases without this fix: remove the compat flags that differ from the catalog on catalog-known models, then update. Setting them to `false` still differs from the catalog.
