prs.title: fix(state): name the state directory when it cannot be made private
prs.body:
Refs #137242

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw onboard` and `openclaw gateway install` stop with "State ownership directory must be a user-owned real directory" or "State ownership directory permissions are not private" when `~/.openclaw` is on a mount that shows files as root-owned or ignores chmod (Apple VirtioFS shares, SMB, NFS). The message does not say which directory failed or what the user should change.

## User Impact

The error now names the directory, the uid that owns it, and that the state directory has to be on a local filesystem that supports file ownership and permissions. Nothing changes about what is accepted: these mounts are still rejected.

This does not close #137242. Making install work on these mounts would mean relaxing the state-ownership lock, the `@openclaw/fs-safe` sidecar lock and the 0600 systemd environment file, which is the open security decision on the issue. This PR covers the "name the state directory and a safe local-filesystem recovery path" option from the issue review.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ensureOwnerDirectory` (`src/infra/gateway-state-owner-directory.ts`) owns the check that the state-ownership lock directory (`<stateDir>/tmp/openclaw-<uid>`) is user-owned and mode 0700. It is the first check these mounts fail on current main, before the systemd environment file named in the issue is reached. The ownership and permission checks are unchanged; only the two error messages change. The non-directory error keeps its existing text.

<details>
<summary>Where current main stops on a chmod-less state dir</summary>

- Files shown as root-owned: `gateway install` fails in `ensureOwnerDirectory` on the uid check. `onboard` fails earlier with a bare `EPERM: operation not permitted, fchmod` from the `@openclaw/fs-safe` sidecar lock (`createNativeExclusiveFile` → `fchmodSync`, reached through `withSetupMigrationTargetLock`).
- Files owned by the user but chmod silently ignored: both commands fail in `ensureOwnerDirectory` on the 0700 check.
- The lock directory moved under the state dir on purpose (`resolveGatewayLockDirForCanonicalStateDir`, "clean break" from process temp), so a state dir on such a mount always reaches this check.

</details>

## Evidence

Linux container (`node:24.22.1-trixie-slim`), non-root `testuser`, account home as `HOME`. Main (`e5f1a21`) and the candidate were each packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` and installed with `npm install -g`. `systemctl`, `loginctl` and `busctl` are the shims from `scripts/e2e/lib/doctor-install-switch/shims`, not a real systemd user manager. `~/.openclaw` is a vfat loop mount: with `umask=000` files show as uid 0, writes work and `chmod 600` returns EPERM, the behavior the issue describes for VirtioFS. With `uid=<testuser>`, chmod returns 0 but has no effect. Commands: `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --mode local --auth-choice skip --skip-daemon`, then `openclaw gateway install --port 18789`.

Root-owned mount, `gateway install`:

```
main: ... failed to acquire gateway state ownership at /home/testuser/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1001/state.<hash>.lock | State ownership directory must be a user-owned real directory. Stop the Gateway and other state owners for this profile, run `openclaw doctor --fix` against the same state/config, then restart the Gateway.
fix:  ... | State ownership directory /home/testuser/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1001 is owned by uid 0, not this user (uid 1001). Run OpenClaw as the user that owns its state directory, and keep that directory on a local filesystem that supports file ownership and permissions. Stop the Gateway ...
```

User-owned mount that ignores chmod, `onboard`:

```
main: State ownership directory permissions are not private
fix:  State ownership directory /home/testuser/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1001 permissions could not be set to 0700. Run OpenClaw as the user that owns its state directory, and keep that directory on a local filesystem that supports file ownership and permissions
```

Control, `~/.openclaw` on the container's own disk, same on main and fix: `onboard exit=0`, `Installed systemd service: /home/testuser/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service`, `install exit=0`.

Not changed by this PR:
- On the root-owned mount, `onboard` still prints the bare `EPERM: operation not permitted, fchmod` from `@openclaw/fs-safe`.
- The migration retry text that follows the error still suggests `openclaw doctor --fix`; it is shared by all legacy-migration lock failures.

Tests: `src/infra/gateway-state-owner-directory.test.ts` (1 test) fails on main's `ensureOwnerDirectory` and passes on the fix. `pnpm test src/infra/gateway-state-owner-directory.test.ts src/infra/gateway-state-owner.test.ts src/infra/gateway-lock.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.lock.test.ts`: 63 passed. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main` passes (+26).

Production delta +14/-2; test delta +26/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; only error text changes, with no config, state or behavior change. Blast radius is the two `ensureOwnerDirectory` errors, which are surfaced wherever state ownership is acquired.

prs.title: fix(doctor): heartbeat migration stuck after a full-disk archive write
prs.body:
Closes #200083

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` can never migrate `HEARTBEAT.md` again when its archive write once failed partway, for example on a full disk. The warning says "Rerun doctor to retry safely", but every rerun reports `heartbeat migration archive collision` until the user finds and deletes the stranded file under `state/backups/heartbeat-migration/` by hand.

## User Impact

After freeing space, the next `doctor --fix` migrates the heartbeat file as the warning promises. That includes users already stuck on an earlier release: an empty or partial archive of the same `HEARTBEAT.md` is replaced on the next run. Any other mismatching archive is still kept and reported as a collision.

## Why This Change Was Made

`archiveSource` in `src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-scratch-migration.ts` creates the archive with an exclusive `writeFile(..., { flag: "wx" })`. A failure other than `EEXIST` means either this call created the file or no file exists, so the change removes that path before rethrowing. Same shape as the merged #199426 (plugins pack) and #199447 (templates create).

Earlier releases already left such files behind, so upgrading alone would not unstick those users. The `EEXIST` branch now compares bytes. An archive equal to the source is accepted as before. One whose bytes are a strict prefix of the source (empty or cut short) can only be a failed write of this same file, because the archive name is the source's SHA-256; it is removed and the exclusive write retried. Anything else still throws `heartbeat migration archive collision` and is kept.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

The archive code dates from #112967. When the content write fails after the exclusive create, the empty or partial file stays behind. On the next run the exclusive create fails with `EEXIST`, the partial bytes fail `hashCronScratchSource`, and migration throws `heartbeat migration archive collision`. Nothing ever removes the file.
</details>

## Evidence

Built `dist` for main `0aafe6691b8` and for this branch, then ran `node dist/entry.js doctor --fix --non-interactive` (Node 24.22.1, macOS) with isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`. `state/backups/heartbeat-migration` was a 2 MiB HFS+ disk image filled to 16 KiB free, so the 63 KiB `HEARTBEAT.md` archive could be created but not written: a real ENOSPC, not an injected one. Script: `hdiutil create` + `dd` + `truncate`, then three Doctor runs, freeing the space before the second.

- Main: run 1 `ENOSPC ... write. Rerun doctor to retry safely.` and a 0-byte `main-<sha>.md` stays behind. Runs 2 and 3, after freeing space, both fail with `heartbeat migration archive collision ... EEXIST`, exit 1, and `HEARTBEAT.md` is still present.
- This branch: run 1 shows the same ENOSPC warning and leaves no archive file. Run 2 prints `Migrated <tmp>/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md into cron`, exits 0, and writes a 63013-byte archive with mode 0600. Run 3 has no heartbeat warnings, exits 0.
- Control on main: with the disk completely full, the exclusive create itself fails (`ENOSPC ... open`), nothing is stranded, and the retry migrates. This branch keeps that behavior and the ordinary migration: mode 0600, archive name `main-<sha256>.md`.
- Regression `retries the migration after a failed archive write` in `doctor-heartbeat-source-archive.test.ts` writes 8 bytes and then throws ENOSPC. It fails on main (`expected [ 'Checklis' ] to deeply equal []`) and passes here.
- Regressions `repairs a partial archive left by an earlier release` and `keeps a different existing archive` seed the archive path with a prefix or with different bytes. The repair case fails without the `EEXIST` change (collision warning) and passes here. The different-bytes case keeps the file and reports the collision on both. `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-source-archive.test.ts src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-scratch-migration.test.ts`: 37 passed.
- Targeted oxlint (including the 700-line `max-lines` limit), format check, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` and `git diff --check` pass. The ENOSPC reproduction above was rerun on head `74d0229b021` with the same result.

<details>
<summary>Main vs branch output (paths shortened)</summary>

```text
== [main-0aafe66] free space on archive volume: 16 KiB
run 1: <tmp>/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md was not migrated: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write. Rerun doctor to retry safely.  exit=1
       -rw------- 0 main-ebb31a2a…34e1.md
run 2 (after freeing space): HEARTBEAT.md was not migrated: heartbeat migration archive collision at <tmp>/state/backups/heartbeat-migration/main-ebb31a2a…34e1.md | EEXIST: file already exists … Rerun doctor to retry safely.  exit=1
run 3: same collision, exit=1, HEARTBEAT.md present: yes

== [fix-final] free space on archive volume: 16 KiB
run 1: <tmp>/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md was not migrated: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write. Rerun doctor to retry safely.  exit=1
       archive dir: (empty)
run 2 (after freeing space): Migrated <tmp>/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md into cron  exit=0
       -rw------- 63013 main-ebb31a2a…34e1.md   HEARTBEAT.md present: no
run 3: no heartbeat warnings, exit=0
```
</details>

Upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.6 (`npm install openclaw@2026.11.6`, `06afb10`) to this branch (head `74d0229b021`), same isolated state, two agents (`main`, `ops`) with their own workspaces, legacy `agents.defaults.heartbeat` plus unrelated settings (`gateway.port`, `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`). Script `upgrade.sh <clean|pending|stranded>`. Scratch is read from `cron_job_scratch` in `state/openclaw.sqlite` with `sqlite3 -readonly`.

1. **Data migrated by 2026.11.6 stays intact.** 2026.11.6 `doctor --fix` migrated `main`. Across three Doctor runs from this branch, two of them with the archive volume refilled:
   - the `main-071c…` archive (52 bytes, hash matches its name) is unchanged;
   - the `cron_job_scratch` row is unchanged (same row hash);
   - `gateway.port`, `thinkingDefault` and the agent list are unchanged;
   - no heartbeat warnings appear. A `HEARTBEAT.md` added after the migration is left alone, because 2026.11.6 already retired the legacy heartbeat config.
2. **A migration left pending on 2026.11.6 completes after a full disk.** 2026.11.6 `doctor` without `--fix` left both files pending. The first run from this branch, with 16 KiB free:
   - migrates `main`;
   - reports `ENOSPC ... write` for `ops` and leaves no `ops` archive.

   After freeing space, the next run migrates `ops`, writing a 63017-byte archive whose hash matches its name and a second scratch row. The `main` archive, the `main` scratch row and the settings are unchanged, and a rerun changes nothing.
3. **An archive already stranded by 2026.11.6 is repaired.** 2026.11.6 itself hit the full disk and left a 0-byte `ops-146e….md`.
   - On head `88043b82529`, before the repair commit, every run from this branch still reported `heartbeat migration archive collision` for `ops`.
   - On head `74d0229b021`, the first run after freeing space migrates `ops`: the archive becomes 63017 bytes and its hash matches its name, `ops` gets a scratch row, and the legacy heartbeat config is retired. The `main` archive, the `main` scratch row, `gateway.port`, `thinkingDefault` and the agent list are unchanged, and a rerun changes nothing.

Credit: @wangmiao0668000666 reported this and published a similar cleanup in the closed #200091. This PR is a smaller variant against current main, with a real full-disk reproduction.

Production delta +10/-2; test delta +39/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door. Reverting restores the stranded-file behavior with no state or config migration. Blast radius is the HEARTBEAT.md archive step of `doctor --fix` when its exclusive write fails or finds an existing archive that is a prefix of the source.

prs.title: fix(channels): configure and onboarding save channel tokens as plaintext
prs.body:
Closes #175333

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a channel token entered in `openclaw configure`, `openclaw onboard --classic` (also the Gateway's `wizard.start` setup flow), `openclaw agents add` or the chat's channel setup is saved as plaintext in `openclaw.json`, while the same token entered through `openclaw channels add` goes to the protected secret store since #169732. Doctor then warns about plaintext secret-bearing fields, and the prompt option itself says "Stores the credential directly in OpenClaw config".

## User Impact

A new or changed channel credential entered through any of these setup paths is saved in the shared secret store, and `openclaw.json` keeps a `store` SecretRef, as with `openclaw channels add`. Config saved by earlier releases is not rewritten: only credentials that differ from the config the channel step started from are moved, so existing plaintext values, env references and SecretRefs stay as they are.

## Why This Change Was Made

#169732 put the protected-store step inside `persistChannelPluginConfig`, which only `channels add` and the Gateway's channels wizard use. The other setup paths run the same `setupChannels` prompts but commit through `writeWizardConfigFile`, `commitSetupConfigFile` or `commitConfigWithPendingPluginInstalls`, so they never reached it.

- The store loop moves unchanged into `storeChannelSetupCredentials` in `src/commands/channels/plugin-config-persistence.ts`. `persistChannelPluginConfig` calls it as before, so `channels add` keeps its authority checks and its retained-entry notice.
- `configure`, onboarding, `agents add` and `runHostedChannelSetup` call it right before their config commit. The hosted chat setup passes its existing `beforePersistentApply` and `assertPersistentEffectCurrent`, so it uses the same checks it already applies to the config write.
- The plaintext option's hint becomes "Saves the credential in the protected secret store". `docs/cli/channels.md` and `docs/start/wizard-cli-reference.md` say where the credential goes.

No new authority checks: writing the credential to the store needs no more authority than the plaintext config write these paths already did. Each flow's authority is still checked where it already is, when the flow starts and at its commit, per the "check authority one time, when work starts" rule in `AGENTS.md`. This is the main difference from the closed #175334, which added mid-flight revocation checks and grew to +611/-91.

Accepted limit: if the config commit fails after the store write, `configure`, onboarding, `agents add` and the hosted chat leave an unreferenced store entry without the "retained" notice `channels add` prints. The config keeps its previous value, and a retry stores the credential under a new name.

## Evidence

Built `dist` and drove the real interactive CLI in a pseudo-terminal (same step file on both builds), Node 24.22.1 on macOS, with isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` and a synthetic Telegram token.

`openclaw configure --section channels` → Add or update channels → Telegram → Enter Telegram bot token:

| Check | Main `0aafe6691b8` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Entry option hint | "Stores the credential directly in OpenClaw config" | "Saves the credential in the protected secret store" |
| `channels.telegram.botToken` | `"123456789:AAsynthetic…"` | `{ "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "CHANNEL_SETUP_7618…" }` |
| Token text in `openclaw.json` | present | absent (0 matches) |
| `doctor --lint --json` | "openclaw.json contains plaintext secret-bearing config fields." | no plaintext warning |
| `secrets audit --check` | not run | "clean. plaintext=0, unresolved=0", exit 0 |

- `openclaw onboard --classic --flow quickstart` (other steps skipped by flags) → Select channel → Telegram → token: this branch saves `{ "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "CHANNEL_SETUP_7505…" }`, with no token text in `openclaw.json`. I didn't build main again for this path; the main-side output is the reporter's capture in #175333 (`"botToken": "123456789:AAsyntheticOnboardToken…"`).
- Control: `openclaw channels add --channel telegram --token …` on main still saves a `store` SecretRef. That path runs the same moved loop.
- Regression `registered configure saves a new channel token in the protected store` (`src/cli/program/register.configure.persistence.test.ts`) drives the registered `configure` command. It fails on main (`expected null to match object { source: 'store', … }`) and passes here.
- `hosted-setup.runtime.test.ts` asserted that the plaintext token reached the config writer. It now expects the store ref.
- Consumer suites (22 files across setup, configure, onboarding, `agents add`, hosted chat, Gateway wizard and cold-import tests): 297 passed. Targeted oxlint, format check, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, the test-lines ratchet and `git diff --check` pass.

Hosted Gateway chat setup (this branch): isolated `openclaw gateway run` with a local OpenAI-compatible mock model as the verified inference route. Typed `connect telegram` through the `openclaw.chat` RPC (`openclaw gateway call openclaw.chat`), then answered each wizard step the same way (token source 1, synthetic token, allowFrom, skip admin):

- The token-source step shows "Saves the credential in the protected secret store".
- The run finished with "Done — telegram is configured.", and `channels.telegram.botToken` is `{ "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "CHANNEL_SETUP_687B…" }`. The token text is absent from `openclaw.json` and from every file in the state directory (0 matches).
- `secrets audit`: `unresolved=0, storeResidue=0`. Its only two `plaintext` findings are `gateway.auth.token` and the mock provider `apiKey` that the harness config seeds.

Upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.6 (`npm install openclaw@2026.11.6`, `06afb10`), same isolated state for both versions. An earlier run from v2026.11.5 gave the same results.

1. On 2026.11.6: config with a plaintext `channels.slack.botToken`, an env SecretRef `channels.slack.appToken` (`SLACK_APP_TOKEN`) and unrelated settings (`gateway.port`, `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`), then `openclaw channels add --channel discord --token …`. That release stores the Discord token itself: `channels.discord.token` → `CHANNEL_SETUP_0576…`.
2. On this branch: `openclaw configure --section channels` adds Telegram.

| Path | After this branch's `configure` |
|---|---|
| `channels.slack.botToken` (plaintext from 2026.11.6) | unchanged |
| `channels.slack.appToken` (env ref) | unchanged |
| `channels.discord.token` (store ref written by 2026.11.6) | unchanged |
| `gateway.port`, `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` | unchanged |
| `channels.telegram.botToken` | new `store` ref `CHANNEL_SETUP_6308…`; token text absent from `openclaw.json` |

- Other config changes: only `channels.telegram.*`, `plugins.entries.telegram`, `wizard.lastRun*`, two `meta.migrations` flags from current main, and `meta.lastTouchedVersion`, which shows the checkout's package version.
- `secrets store list` shows both entries: the one 2026.11.6 wrote and the one this branch wrote.
- `secrets audit` (with `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` set): `plaintext=1` (the existing Slack bot token, left as it was), `unresolved=0`, `storeResidue=0`.
- `openclaw gateway run` on the upgraded state reached `[gateway] ready`. Discord, Slack and Telegram each started their provider with a resolved credential, and each got the expected 401 / `invalid_auth` from its API for the synthetic tokens. That shows the 2026.11.6 store entry, the env ref, the plaintext value and the new store entry all load at runtime.

Not run end to end: `agents add` and the Control UI rendering of the chat setup. `agents add` calls the same function at its commit point; the chat setup's Gateway path is the run above.

Production delta +100/-56 (mostly the moved loop); test delta +53/-1; docs +8/-3. `channels add` is the only path that prints the retained-entry names, and `docs/cli/channels.md` says so.

Merge risk: two-way door. Reverting brings back plaintext saves for these paths; entries already stored stay valid because config refers to them by name. Blast radius is new or changed channel credentials entered in `configure`, onboarding, `agents add` and chat channel setup.

prs.title: fix: preserve child results after source lifecycle changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A background child can finish before an authority or source-lifecycle change prevents its completion turn from starting. The source-lifecycle refusal was classified as intentional non-delivery, leaving the captured answer invisible to the requester.

## User Impact

The requester now receives the existing visible failure notice containing the saved public answer, with the existing per-result and per-notice bounds and full-history recovery instructions. A revoked continuation still cannot execute.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify the source-owner refusal as permanent failure so the registry's existing notice owner handles it. This is one changed production line, net zero production LOC. No new state, configuration, schema, tool or requester-reader path.

The Team perf-loop lead (an agent acting under Peter's standing unattended instruction) requested this scoped correction and landing; this is the agent lead's decision, not Peter's personal acceptance. Related: #202664.

## Evidence

The boundary harness captures an operator continuation, changes the real policy generation, and runs delivery through actual registry persistence and requester transcript notice writing. On main parent `b4a41aa642ce0f8016527e964c5015b21487d654`, the revoked-authority requester-batch case already preserves the captured answer; it needs no production change. The source-lifecycle case fails there with no visible notice and passes with this classification correction. Both cases verify that no model executes on the revoked continuation.

169 focused tests pass, covering these two boundary cases, existing captured-result caps/private-result handling, and announce/direct-delivery consumers. No production data or transcripts were used. This correctness-only classification change reuses the notice owner without adding hot-path work; no new performance claim is made.

Final `pnpm check:changed` passes core/script lint, production and all test typechecks, format, SQLite ownership/schema guards and import cycles. It remains failed on two unrelated main regressions, both reproduced by the actual scans on the actual tested CI main parent `7af829afeef7d8ca9c07225b1efbf40e98433ea4`: `AccountTokens` from #202411 (`4da7f93e9a31fbc06f60f7818f1e42bdf7d2077c`), and the three fake-transport/prefix-journey exports from #201723 (`336bc3cb723f14946df5901d99366036bcfe3944`). These need separate main-owner repair and are not counted as green checks. Final source is `b69164d8f4fe61cda72ed510d73d739e3dd04800`; a fresh syntax-only Codex review and two-case boundary rerun also pass.

Exact-head [CI run 44811494833](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44811494833) is complete and remains failed only on the three inherited UI assertions. All three reproduce on actual tested merge parent `7af829afeef7d8ca9c07225b1efbf40e98433ea4`: skills readiness and Linux skill-settings asset budget (33 versus 31) from #202531 (`856aca23d7fb5557162db8613a93ae1f2e2f6d19`), plugins readiness from #202527 (`c2c2effaeddb1ed99db0788fb2dfa61cf7ae03c7`). The checked-out merge changes no UI/scenario inputs. These are main regressions for their owners, not ignored noise. All other CI jobs pass or skip, including security-fast.

Codex autoreview is clean. ClawSweeper's latest review on final head has zero findings and zero open items. Landing uses the documented native pre-existing-failure exception under the agent lead's scoped instruction; CI is not represented as green.

prs.title: fix: publish a valid gateway hostname for long hostnames
prs.body:
Closes #202665

## What Problem This Solves

When a machine's hostname is longer than 63 characters, OpenClaw truncates it for the wide-area DNS-SD zone. The truncation can leave a trailing `-`, so the advertised SRV target (and its `A` owner) is not a valid hostname, violating the LDH rule the module already enforces for configured domains.

## User Impact

The gateway now advertises a well-formed hostname, so clients that validate the SRV target as a hostname (TLS/SNI, strict HTTP clients) are not handed an invalid name.

## Why This Change Was Made

`dnsLabel()` stripped leading and trailing hyphens before truncating to the 63-character limit, so truncation could re-expose a trailing `-`. The label is now re-trimmed after truncation.

## Evidence

**Launched Gateway (shipped entry point), not a test harness.** I built this head with `scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup` and ran:

```
node dist/index.js gateway run --allow-unconfigured
```

with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `discovery.wideArea.domain = openclaw.internal`, and a `--require` preload that sets `os.hostname()` to a 68-character name (`aaa…a-bbbbb`) and reports a Tailscale IPv4 interface. The Gateway logged:

```
[discovery] wide-area DNS-SD updated (openclaw.internal. → …\dns\openclaw.internal.db)
```

and wrote this zone (truncated host label is `aaa…a`, 62 chars, no trailing hyphen):

```
$ORIGIN openclaw.internal.
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa IN A 100.64.0.1
_openclaw-gw._tcp IN PTR aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa._openclaw-gw._tcp
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa._openclaw-gw._tcp IN SRV 0 0 18789 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
```

I served that exact file with CoreDNS 1.15.0 and resolved it with a real DNS client:

```
PTR ["aaa…a._openclaw-gw._tcp.openclaw.internal"]
SRV [{"name":"aaa…a.openclaw.internal","port":18789,"priority":0,"weight":0,"type":"SRV"}]
A   ["100.64.0.1"]
```

Base comparison: the same 68-character hostname through `startGatewayDiscovery()` on `HEAD~1` (a base `dist` build was not available on this host) publishes `aaa…a-` (63 chars, trailing hyphen) as the SRV target and `A` owner — not a valid hostname.

Scope note: CoreDNS also serves the trailing-hyphen label from the base zone (DNS wire format allows any octet in a label), so this is not a hard resolution failure. The defect is that OpenClaw advertises a name that is not a valid hostname.

- Red on base, green on head: `keeps truncated host labels as valid DNS hostnames` in `src/infra/widearea-dns.test.ts` asserts the SRV target matches `^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$` and that its `A` record exists (selected via the SRV target, not the `ns1` nameserver record). Full file: `10 passed | 1 skipped`.
- `oxlint` on both changed files exits 0; formatter check is clean.

Known environment limitation, unrelated: `src/infra/widearea-dns.boundary.test.ts` fails on this Windows host with `EPERM: operation not permitted, rename …` inside `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s atomic replacement. I reproduced the same failure against the base source with this change reverted.

Not run here: full `pnpm check` / repo-wide typecheck. Required CI workflows on this external PR are waiting on maintainer approval, which I cannot grant.

This change was AI-assisted and verified against the evidence above.

prs.title: fix(ui): restore plugin route performance checks
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202527

## What Problem This Solves

The plugin route benchmark cannot reach catalog readiness because its fixture marks every entry installed, and browsing intentionally hides installed entries. After correcting the fixture, the same route makes 59 asset requests against its 56-request budget: discovery eagerly imports settings schema analysis and secret-field preparation.

## User Impact

Plugin discovery avoids loading settings-only code. Installed plugin settings keep their existing schema, permission, secret-field, retry, and editing behavior. The benchmark retains its 1,000-item discovery and installed Settings workloads and all existing request budgets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give installed inventory and available catalog entries distinct identities. Move schema analysis, schema selection, and acquisition of the existing secret-field owner into the existing lazy detail and Advanced settings views. The shared page passes raw schema and context; no alternate settings or secret owner is added.

Update the existing settings fixtures to cross that boundary with real root schemas. The permission test also checks that a retained field calls the current patch callback after props change. Schema identity memos retain the existing normalization guard; the same-version schema test now counts analysis calls across unrelated updates and schema replacement. The Advanced focus test uses the supported `plugins.slots.memory` path through the real schema selector and opens the intentionally collapsed Slots group before editing.

## Evidence

- [Original readiness failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44796218464/job/136497502162): the fixture hides all discovery cards. The relevant fixture and assertions are unchanged at this branch's base.
- [Fixture-only browser proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44803148089/job/136521248000), head `00f20d124a1c8148f236f98c4d3504a53fda3eeb`: production UI builds and plugins reaches its asset assertion, reporting 59 requests against 56. That completed run also reports a skills readiness timeout, skill-settings 33 requests against 31, and unused-export failures. Plugin-settings passes. This is baseline evidence, not proof of the new lazy-import fix.
- Lazy-import change independently reviewed before commit: no actionable source findings. Static import tracing excludes schema analysis, secret fields, stored-secret source, and settings model from discovery. Current-head browser validation now passes the plugin discovery and plugin-settings asset cases.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh full-range local ClawSweeper review found no actionable correctness or security issues for `0e44574217ec7b4ed55c001ddf70a422699a1c01..998f873a7e91203121399cc96f8be758e7d322b9`, including the Slots disclosure correction.
- Simplification: existing lazy boundaries and state owners reused. Full-range production delta: 61 additions, 58 deletions across the fixture and three UI modules; test/fixture delta: 78 additions, 25 deletions across five files.
- [Prior lazy-import browser proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44806180258/job/136531788822) passes the plugin discovery and plugin-settings asset cases, including the unchanged 56-request discovery limit. Its 2 failures are the separately tracked skills readiness timeout and skill-settings budget. Overall job result remains failed: 17 tests passed, 2 failed.
- [Prior-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44806180258) completed for `f815f61f7941d7b16e69bb027c1b51adacd43648`. The Advanced focus fixture failed because the nested Slots group was never opened; this revision adds that user action and preserves the typing, focus and patch-path assertions. Its other failures are the known Skills cases and unrelated baseline helper/UI exports.
- [Corrected-head browser proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44809677334/job/136543648090): plugin discovery and plugin-settings both pass their unchanged asset budgets. The only two failures are the separately tracked Skills readiness and asset-budget cases.
- [Corrected-head UI proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44809677334/job/136543648910): all 19 settings-editor cases pass, including typing and focus in Advanced settings. The UI shard passes 802 files and 8,557 tests; its WebKit suite passes 78 files and 794 tests.
- Local dependency-backed execution remains unavailable. Ready CI has completed; the documented inherited-failure exception is used for the unrelated failures below, with security and other enforced gates retained.

- [Ready CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44812647990), exact head `998f873a7e91203121399cc96f8be758e7d322b9`: both plugin asset cases pass again. Remaining failures are the two unchanged Skills cases (repaired by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202694) and `keeps a saved model and reasoning level the catalog does not list`, which fails finding the cron edit button before model assertions. The cron test, mount/wait helpers and lazy detail owner are unchanged from the tested baseline. Types, lint, ratchets and security pass. Overall CI remains failed; no claim that these inherited failures are fixed by this PR.

prs.title: fix: show why a model tool call was rejected as malformed
prs.body:
Related: #202672

## What Problem This Solves

When a model streams a tool call whose arguments never arrive as a complete JSON object, the turn fails with a malformed-tool-call error. The `provider-error` log line for that failure showed only the error code and the provider's message id, so an operator reading the logs could not tell a truncated argument buffer from a buffer that was never JSON-encoded at all, and could not see how large the rejected buffer was or whether the string-literal repair had been attempted.

## User Impact

User impact: the `provider-error` log line for a rejected tool call now carries `argumentChars`, `argumentHash`, and `repairAttempted`, so operators can distinguish truncation from a never-encoded buffer without opening provider payloads. No argument text is added to the log, so the content-exclusion contract is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`parseTerminalToolCallArguments()` already builds content-free diagnostics (`argumentChars`, `argumentHash`, `repairAttempted`) and attaches them to the error `cause` plus a mirrored `errorBody`. `assignTransportErrorDetails()` built the `provider-error` metadata from only `causeCode` / `code` / `type` / `requestId` / `responseId` / `status`, so those diagnostics never reached the log.

This change propagates the bounded diagnostics into that metadata and adds the transport-to-log regression coverage requested in #202672. The propagation is deliberately narrow:

- Only the fields produced by `parseTerminalToolCallArguments()` are surfaced, and only for the `malformed_tool_call_arguments` code.
- The argument hash is accepted only when it matches the base-36 digest shape OpenClaw produces, so a provider-crafted `cause` cannot smuggle argument text into the log.
- `errorBody` is **not** logged. For other error classes it can carry provider prose (prompts, tool results), so it must stay out of the log.
- Rejection behaviour, JSON repair, streaming, recovery, and failover are unchanged.

## Evidence

New coverage:

- `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` — *"surfaces bounded tool-call diagnostics in the provider-error log"* drives a truncated `tool_use` argument buffer through the loopback HTTP transport and asserts the `provider-error` metadata carries `argumentChars` / `argumentHash` / `repairAttempted` matching the terminal error body, that no `toolcall_end` is emitted, and that the rejected argument text appears in neither the log nor the error body.
- `packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts` — *"logs bounded tool-call diagnostics without the rejected argument text"* pins the metadata contents for a rejected buffer, and *"does not log tool-call diagnostics that are not an OpenClaw digest"* proves a non-digest hash is dropped rather than logged.

Existing coverage kept green: the truncated-sibling case in `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` still requires truncated sibling arguments to stay rejected, the bounded diagnostics to survive in `errorBody`, private argument text to stay excluded, and no sibling `toolcall_end` to be emitted.

Focused tests:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  81 passed (81)
```

Whole package suite:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts packages/ai/
 Test Files  167 passed (167)
      Tests  2455 passed | 3 skipped (2458)
```

Format and lint on the touched files:

```
$ node scripts/run-format.mts --check packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <same files>
✓ No problems in 3 files
```

<details>
<summary>Log line before and after</summary>

Before, the failure was indistinguishable from any other malformed tool call:

```
[provider-error] Model request failed ... code=malformed_tool_call_arguments causeCode=malformed_tool_call_arguments responseId=msg_...
```

After, the metadata additionally carries the bounded diagnostics (no argument text, only a length, a digest, and a flag):

```
[provider-error] Model request failed ... code=malformed_tool_call_arguments causeCode=malformed_tool_call_arguments responseId=msg_... argumentChars=52 argumentHash=jiqoxq1e07seo repairAttempted=true
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: stop Mac app updates from getting stuck when your Gateway wrapper is stored in ~/.openclaw
prs.body:
Related: #202215 (this fixes new occurrences; Macs that already hit it keep an incomplete-update record, see User Impact)
Related: #169919

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway install --wrapper <path>` lets you start the Gateway through your own script, such as a secrets shim or a Node version picker. If that script is stored inside the OpenClaw state directory (for example `~/.openclaw/service-env/` or `~/.openclaw/scripts/`), the Mac app ends its update flow in "Gateway update needs help: The installed Gateway service command could not be inspected." Retry cannot clear it, because the app has nothing it can repair.

## User Impact

User impact: the Mac app now treats a Gateway that starts through your own wrapper in the state directory as externally managed. A fresh app update finishes without the recovery window, and you keep updating the Gateway with the CLI, the same as when the wrapper is in `~/.local/bin`. Services the app installed itself are still detected as app-managed.

If you already saw this window, the app has stored an unfinished-update record, and this change does not clear it. You may then see "The Gateway could not be checked" until that record is cleared with `defaults delete ai.openclaw.mac openclaw.postAppUpdateReceipt` (see #169919).

## Why This Change Was Made

The app decided that it managed the Gateway whenever the service's executable was anywhere under the state directory. It then could not parse the wrapper command into a CLI it could run, so it stopped in the managed-runtime-unavailable state.

Now only two locations prove ownership by themselves: the managed launcher path (`bin/openclaw`) and the seeded runtime subtree (`runtime/`). Other executables under the state directory go through the existing `node`/`bun` entrypoint check. So `tools/node` is detected as before, and versioned installs such as `tools/node-v24.x/bin/node` now follow the same rule: managed when the entrypoint is in the state directory, external otherwise. A wrapper placed inside `runtime/`, or registered at the launcher path itself, is still treated as app-managed, as it was before.

## Evidence

**Real app update and relaunch, in a disposable macOS 26.6.2 VM (tart):** an onboarded install of the official 2026.11.4 release, Gateway CLI 2026.11.6 from npm, and a LaunchAgent started through `~/.openclaw/service-env/my-wrapper.sh` (the same `/bin/sh <env-wrapper> <env> <wrapper> gateway --port 18789` shape as the report). Both runs start from the same saved app settings: last launched version 2026.11.4 and no pending receipt. Each then installs a 2026.11.5 app build over the release and launches it, so the app records the 2026.11.4 → 2026.11.5 update itself.

- **Before, `main` at `9745e409c50`:** "Gateway update needs help / The installed Gateway service command could not be inspected". The receipt is left with `gatewayUpdateIncomplete: true`.
- **After, this PR at `38ef5159778`:** no window. The update finishes quietly and the receipt is cleared. The app connects to the Gateway (`client=openclaw-macos … version=2026.11.5`), and the Gateway keeps the same PID with `Connectivity check: ok`. The LaunchAgent is unchanged, and the app settings are unchanged apart from the two last-launched markers.

### Clean comparison

![Before: main shows "Gateway update needs help" for a healthy Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d48100f-c149-4459-a12b-e2edf71dc3af)

![After: this PR, no recovery window, app running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6431430b-19c4-4092-a089-fee39fc45709)

### Annotated comparison

![Before, annotated: recovery window for a healthy Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3bbabcc-8ac6-4f17-b0cf-5513bd36aec0)

![After, annotated: app running with no recovery window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/556f8f2c-21f8-4478-92c8-42f8118114f8)

Both builds come from `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` with `BUILD_CONFIG=debug BUNDLE_ID=ai.openclaw.mac ALLOW_ADHOC_SIGNING=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_MLX_TTS=1 BUILD_ARCHS=arm64`, so they share the release app's settings domain. The Sparkle download and install step itself was not exercised; the relaunch into the newer build was. The unpatched 2026.11.4 release showed the same window on its own launch in this setup.

### Upgrade from the latest stable release (2026.11.5)

Same VM and wrapper. The official 2026.11.5 release (Developer ID, team `FWJYW4S8P8`) shows the same window after its own update from 2026.11.4. With its pending receipt cleared (last launched 2026.11.5, Gateway still running), I replaced it with this PR's build and relaunched. Result: no window and no receipt left behind. The app connects as `version=2026.11.6`, the Gateway keeps the same PID with `Connectivity check: ok`, the LaunchAgent still runs `my-wrapper.sh`, and the app settings are unchanged apart from the two last-launched markers.

This build is `38ef5159778` with only the root `package.json` version set to 2026.11.6 for the packaging run (not committed), because packaging requires the app version to match the JavaScript build and the app records an update only when the version changes.

![Before: official 2026.11.5 release shows the recovery window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/110d3c06-2dd2-43f2-b7bd-da152e808dd6)

![After: upgrade from 2026.11.5 to this PR, no recovery window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ff58c12-65d8-45e6-8f9f-bfc7a68898e0)

![Before, annotated: official 2026.11.5 release](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1289b141-00f4-4091-abf9-a404ce54fa3e)

![After, annotated: upgraded from 2026.11.5 with no window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a197218a-4da5-4647-b897-6d930a3d864a)

- **New test, fails without the fix and passes with it:**
  - Operator wrappers in `service-env/` and `scripts/`, given bare, behind the env wrapper, and behind `/bin/sh` plus the env wrapper, are not app-managed.
  - For such a service, `resolveGatewayAction` returns no action on a fresh receipt instead of `managedRuntimeUnavailable`. An incomplete receipt keeps the existing ownership-check failure.
  - A versioned `tools/node-v24.x` Node with an outside entrypoint is external; with a state-directory entrypoint it is managed.
  - The stable service Bun (`runtime/service/bun`), the per-build Bun, and the managed launcher behind the env wrapper are still managed.
  - With the source change reverted, the test fails with 15 failed expectations.
- **Existing tests still pass:** the 6 other runtime-ownership and repair-gate tests in `UpdateOrchestrationTests`. All 7 are pure path and decision checks with no file, defaults or service access. I ran each one on its own on a development Mac.
- **Formatting and lint:** `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` and `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` pass with the pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1.
- **Local review:** autoreview (openclaw/agent-skills `0a5ba4b`, helper `source-sha256:2ea67c44…`, Codex engine), `--mode branch` against base `9745e409c50`, head `38ef5159778`, max priority P2: scoped-clean, with no actionable findings.
- **Original report:** on the reporter's Mac (app 2026.11.5, Gateway 2026.11.6 on npm under nvm), a wrapper in `~/.openclaw/service-env/` brought the recovery window back on every relaunch, while `openclaw gateway status --deep` showed a healthy Gateway. Moving the wrapper out of the state directory and clearing the pending record worked around it.
- **Gap:** I did not run the full macOS suite. `docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md` asks for a disposable VM for that, so I'm relying on the `macos-swift` PR CI for it.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests
scripts/format-swift.sh macos
scripts/lint-swift.sh macos
python3 <agent-skills>/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base 9745e409c50 --engine codex --max-priority P2
```

The single tests were run with one exact `--filter` each, for example
``--filter 'UpdateOrchestrationTests/`[^`]*operator wrappers stored'``. Other native tests in this package need the isolated setup in `docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md`.

</details>

prs.title: fix: keep past update failures in the Inbox
prs.body:
Closes #202657

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI Inbox drops a recent failed update when the Gateway reconnects on a different build, even if nobody has dismissed the failure. The serving build has changed, but the recorded update still failed.

## User Impact

The Inbox keeps the recorded failure available to review within its existing acknowledgement and 24-hour window. A newer available update keeps its own notice and dismissal. The old report opens in read-only mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Project historical failures into the existing navigable Inbox row using the run's acknowledgement key. Current update notices keep their separate controls and dismissal. The Updates page uses the connected Gateway version before cached configuration to classify the report consistently.

## Behavior proof

Scenario: a recent update run failed (`post-update-failed`) while the Gateway served `before-build`. The Gateway then restarts and serves `after-build`, and the Control UI reconnects. Nobody dismissed the failure.

Captured from the production Control UI build in Chromium (1440x900, English, light theme), driven by the repository's Control UI e2e harness against its synthetic mock Gateway. Fixture data is synthetic. The Gateway restart is emulated by closing the socket and changing the advertised serving build id. Before is the base commit `c1f70d3b7` (this PR's parent) and after is this PR's head `f8639d052`.

### Clean comparison

State before the restart, identical on both revisions: the failure is in the Inbox.

![Inbox before the Gateway restart: the update failure is listed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/188ffe8c-29f0-4f3e-a46a-65c060495569)

After the restart on `after-build`:

| Before (`c1f70d3b7`) | After (`f8639d052`) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Base: the Inbox is empty, "No requests or alerts yet"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1eb972ac-0484-4ba7-ae04-5cec9df60554) | ![Head: the Inbox still lists "Last update run failed (post-update-failed)"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff54e799-05be-4c47-9a32-d478406eeb28) |

### After this change: independent dismissal and read-only report

A newer update notice was dismissed on its own and the historical failure stayed. The failure opens the Updates page, which shows the run as failed and offers no Retry action.

| Historical entry kept after dismissing the newer notice | Read-only report |
| --- | --- |
| ![Inbox still lists the failed run after the newer update notice was dismissed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97d3594f-e469-426e-a8ae-c8878b5d4a22) | ![Updates page: "Last update run failed (post-update-failed), Gateway is serving build after-build; recorded serving build was before-build", no Retry update button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cddcf03e-2c5e-42d1-a810-70f3437bac1e) |

### Request trace from the same runs

Counts read from the mock Gateway after each step.

| Step | Gateway `connect` requests | `update.run` requests | Retry update buttons |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Failure shown, serving `before-build` | 1 | 0 | n/a |
| Reconnected on `after-build`, base: historical entry absent | 2 | 0 | n/a |
| Reconnected on `after-build`, head: historical entry present | 2 | 0 | n/a |
| Head: newer notice dismissed, historical entry still present | 2 | 0 | n/a |
| Head: report opened | 2 | 0 | 0 |

The committed browser test `keeps an unread update failure in the Inbox after the Gateway build changes` covers the same flow and fails on the base.

## Evidence

- On commit `f8639d05234a`, formatting, targeted lint, and the UI typecheck passed. The four focused unit files (86 tests) and the update browser suite (7 tests) passed 20 repetitions per case.
- A focused test reproduces the report error when the connected version differs from cached bootstrap metadata. The candidate presents it as historical.
- Independent adversarial review identified the update-control and stale-version cases. The production revision was rereviewed with no blocking findings. The repository's optional autoreview helper was unavailable locally.

prs.title: feat(ui): open skills as pages instead of dialogs
prs.body:
Stacks on #202548. **This changes navigation**: a skill now opens as its own page at its own address, in place of a dialog over the list.

## Before
Opening any skill opened a dialog over the Skills list. The dialog had no address of its own, so a reload, a shared link or the browser's Back button left it. Links that pointed at a ClawHub skill (`/skills?clawhub=<ref>`, from chat skill cards and the macOS install link) opened the list with the dialog on top.

## Now
A skill opens as a page with the plugin page's layout:
- the way back ("Skills ›"), then a header with the skill's tile, name, `@owner` and state;
- the actions on the right: the Enabled switch for an installed skill; Add → Adding… → the switch for a ClawHub skill (Import in personal-library mode);
- the reading column: description, Requirements (only when declared), Skill card, and the latest version notes for ClawHub skills;
- the facts rail on the right: Security check with Audit, Package, Source, Homepage, Version, Updated, License, Platforms, as the data has them.

On a phone it is one column, and the facts close the page in two columns.

Everything the dialogs showed is on the page in the same relative places:
- admin-access note, invalid-link alert, blocked reasons;
- key-config read error with Retry;
- install, save-key and toggle results;
- security verdict states;
- card loading, error and Retry;
- ClawHub loading, not found and error;
- read-only gating.

### Addresses
| Page | Address |
| --- | --- |
| Installed skill, opened from Skills | `/skills/installed/<skillKey>` |
| Installed skill, opened from Settings › Skills | `/settings/skills/<skillKey>` |
| ClawHub skill (added or not) | `/skills/clawhub/<reference>`, e.g. `/skills/clawhub/@steipete/gog` |

- Installed skills are identified by `skillKey`, as the installed list identifies them.
- ClawHub skills are identified by the reference the ClawHub dialog was opened with. The registry is the Gateway's configured one, as before.
- `?agent=` is kept on every address.
- These follow the plugin pages (`/plugins/<id>`, `/settings/plugins/<id>`). `/skills/workshop` keeps its own route.
- The old `/skills?clawhub=<ref>` link is replaced with `/skills/clawhub/<ref>` when it opens, so chat cards and the macOS install link land on the page.

### Navigation
- Skills: installed rows and ClawHub rows open their pages. Settings › Skills rows open `/settings/skills/<key>`. Chat skill cards open the ClawHub page.
- "Skills ›" returns to the list it came from. The list stays mounted behind the page, so its search, chip, filter and open groups are as they were.
- Browser Back returns to where the person came from. Reload stays on the page.
- A key or reference that does not exist shows "Skill not found." under the same way back.
- The route reads only the first-paint inventory, as before. Opening or leaving a page does not reload it. The card and the registry detail each load and retry on their own, scoped to the connection, agent and revision. While a page's code or inventory loads, its header space is held.

### Removed / kept
- Removed:
  - the installed-skill dialog and the ClawHub dialog;
  - their shared dialog shell (`SkillReaderDialog`);
  - the dialog-only state (`skillsDetailTab`, `onClawHubDetailClose`, the loader's `clawhubRef`);
  - the dialog layout CSS;
  - the dialog shell browser test, replaced by a page layout test.
- Kept: the own-skill library dialogs (detail, editor, import) and their `SkillDialogBoundary`. They still have their callers.
- The own-skill editor works as before: Settings › Skills → your skill's row → its dialog. From Skills, your library rows open the same dialog.

## Checks
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/skills/`: 88 passed. This includes a new route test (opens, the way back keeps the same list, not found) and address tests.
- `ui/src/e2e/skills-any-bin-requirements.e2e.test.ts`, now on the page: opens, reload stays, Back returns. `ui/src/e2e/skills-clawhub-external-install.e2e.test.ts` passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm lint:ui:styles`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` (no new strings), `oxfmt --check`, `pnpm ui:build`. The budget warnings are the same as on the base branch.

## Evidence
Captured from the built Control UI against the mock Gateway, before (base branch) and after, at 1440×1000 and 390×844 @2x.

prs.title: feat: use one check script for model-free automations
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

## What Problem This Solves

Today, writing an automation that checks something without a model starts with a choice between a condition script and a script payload. They share the same saved state, but have different result formats and cannot be combined.

## User Impact

- Use one JavaScript check to stay quiet, post a message through the automation’s delivery, or append a message to a configured agent prompt and run it. Configure it in the Control UI, use `--check-script` in the CLI, or send `check` through the automations tool or Gateway. Shell command jobs keep their separate operator policy.
- Run `openclaw doctor --fix` after upgrading. Doctor backs up cron storage, reports each conversion, and carries over saved state, once behavior, execution limits and tool restrictions for jobs it can convert. If it cannot preserve what a job does—such as a script waking an existing conversation, a condition starting a shell command or system event, or a result it cannot safely translate—it pauses the job and reports why. Recover the original definition from the backup, edit the check, then re-enable it.

## Why This Change Was Made

One executor and one check result replace the two JavaScript execution paths. Shell commands do not become agent-callable checks. The draft touches shared automation schema, run finalization, Doctor, CLI flags, and the Control UI editor; those are likely conflict points with the sibling automation cleanup PRs.

## Evidence

The focused SQLite Doctor test passed conversion, backup, state and tool-cap preservation, pause, and repeat-run checks. The scheduler tests passed the three quiet/post/wake routing cases. The bundled Control UI browser run passed check authoring and rejected-draft behavior. Core/UI production typechecks and changed-file formatting passed locally. The cron job-validation and CLI option suites passed after correcting two old-shape fixtures. Other suites still contain old trigger/script fixtures and need the test cutover. A released-install upgrade and in-flight legacy script recovery are not verified.

Workspace health automation in the real Control UI bundle, using a mocked Gateway with synthetic data. Before shows the condition contract; after shows the check script help and wake result.

The before/after captures were inspected locally. GitHub did not serve the uploaded media and the artifact-store fallback rejected the upload, so the screenshots are not attached.

Co-authored with [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/81435859-bcde-4ac4-bc9a-01240508cd25)

prs.title: improve: set automation hours in the schedule builder
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

## What Problem This Solves

The automation editor gives you an hours picker in the schedule and a second hours setting under Advanced. A cron job can even show “all day” in the schedule while Advanced restricts it, and the two time-zone inputs can disagree.

## User Impact

Use **Between hours** and one **Time zone** field in the schedule builder for interval and cron jobs. The start is included and the end is excluded: 08:00–22:00 does not include 22:00. Overnight windows work too.

**Existing jobs:** No jobs are rewritten, paused, or deleted on upgrade, and no Doctor action is required. Existing windows still apply on resave, including to forced runs. If a saved cron job already uses different zones for its schedule and window, the editor keeps both and explains the difference. Editing the one time-zone field applies the new zone to both.

## Why This Change Was Made

New cron windows use hour ranges when the schedule can express them directly. Elapsed intervals, such as every 45 minutes, keep their cadence and use the existing runtime window. Minute-level windows also keep their runtime restriction when a cron hour range cannot express them. The Gateway API, CLI, agent tool and stored job format are unchanged: translating existing runtime gates to cron ranges would change when a manual run is allowed, so this removes the duplicate editor path rather than migrating jobs in Doctor.

Expected sibling overlap: automation editor and Advanced settings layout, the schedule docs, and editor-save and browser test fixtures. This PR does not change the other settings or the runtime policy contracts.

## Evidence

Chrome against the built Control UI with a synthetic Gateway verified saving a whole-hour range, editing custom cron, and focusing invalid time fields. Save tests passed for a 45-minute interval with its existing anchor, whole-hour and overnight cron ranges, minute-level fallback, and a saved split time zone. Control UI typecheck, targeted lint, and formatting passed. No live Gateway, full CI, or stable-source upgrade run; no persisted schema change.

Before and after screenshots were captured in Chromium using the same synthetic weekday inventory digest, light theme, and viewport. Media upload is pending for this draft.

Co-authored with [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

prs.title: improve: simplify proactive checks and automation delivery controls
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

Co-authored by [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/07129d2b-6d52-42e2-bb0c-db750762cf73)

## What Problem This Solves

The Automations editor exposes several options left over from heartbeat, even though the default Proactive check can use the same schedule and routing as other recurring jobs.

## User Impact

The editor, CLI, agent tool, and Gateway no longer offer Wait until idle, Skip empty scratch, Block direct messages, or the primary `last` channel. **Send to me** still resolves the owner’s direct-message destination. The default Proactive check keeps its cadence but may now run while another session is working on the same agent.

Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair stored jobs. Doctor backs up the store, removes the retired switches, and reports the changes. It pauses affected jobs when a custom execution policy has no safe replacement or when removing a direct-message block could allow an unintended send. Jobs are not deleted. For primary `last` chat routes, Doctor pins the most recent recorded successful destination, including the account and thread when recorded. Without a recorded destination, it reports the fallback and leaves normal routing to choose the destination. Owner targeting stays dynamic. The separate failure-alert `last` setting is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Routine checks now use normal scheduler admission, and new jobs can either name a specific chat route or let OpenClaw resolve it automatically. This removes heartbeat-only controls without guessing where existing jobs actually sent results. Expect overlap with the sibling automation cleanups in the editor, Gateway schemas, scheduler, Doctor, and documentation; this draft does not implement those changes.

## Evidence

The SQLite Doctor repair suite passed all 17 tests, including backup creation, most-recent *actual* delivery rather than a newer failed attempt, no-trace fallback, and pausing without deleting jobs. The heartbeat cadence suite and three Gateway protocol conformance tests also passed. Touched-file lint and formatting checks passed. The UI editor test could not load a workspace package in the standalone Vitest configuration; broader focused suites and independent local review are not confirmed green. The local reviewer stopped before starting because its input exceeded the selected pass budget. Full CI and live upgrade checks were not run.

The before and after show the actual Control UI with a mock Gateway and synthetic automation data.

prs.title: improve: give automation failure alerts one switch
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

Co-authored by [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/8ccabdf7-8443-418a-899c-24cf8116588d)

## What Problem This Solves

Turning on an automation's failure alerts meant choosing among several overlapping settings. An option for best-effort delivery could also make a failed send count as a success and suppress the default alert.

## User Impact

User impact: The automation editor has one **Failure alerts** switch. The CLI uses `--failure-alert` or `--no-failure-alert`; the automation tool takes a boolean. Eligible automations ask the owning conversation to repair the problem. Otherwise the notice goes to the configured global failure route or the job's result destination. The Gateway-wide `cron.failureAlert` policy controls timing and routing. Failed required delivery stays failed, and the auto-disable safety notice still applies even when failure alerts are off.

After upgrading, run `openclaw doctor --fix`. Doctor backs up cron state, converts custom job alert objects to On, preserves Off, and reports settings it drops per automation. It retires per-agent and per-creator alert routes and the best-effort delivery option. It pauses jobs whose old behavior cannot be represented, so operators can review them before re-enabling. It does not delete jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single switch makes the per-automation decision clear; timing and fallback routing belong to the Gateway policy. The likely overlap with sibling automation cleanups is in the editor, CLI/tool schema, Gateway protocol and its generated validators, scheduler tests, and Doctor's cron migration. Those sibling feature changes are not included here.

## Evidence

The bundled Control UI test turned the switch off and verified the saved update left the result destination unchanged. Core and UI typechecks and commit-time formatting and baseline checks passed. Both new Doctor cases passed during the targeted run before the broader Doctor shard timed out; the store migration case was then moved to its own file to satisfy the repository line cap. The larger scheduler run did not finish, and local P0 autoreview timed out before producing a report. Full CI, native UI validation, and an in-place upgrade from stable were not run.

Weekday inventory digest, Control UI in Chromium at 1360 × 940. Before: the task's main baseline `2b58c8e`; after: the one-switch editor at `2dcb7e0`. The captures use the real bundled editor with a fixture Gateway.

prs.title: fix: move ended one-time automations to run history
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

## What Problem This Solves

A one-time automation that failed or had unconfirmed delivery stayed in the Paused list, even though nothing was scheduled. Over time those entries accumulated, and Run history did not offer a way to try the task again.

## User Impact

- After its final attempt, a one-time automation leaves the list whether it succeeds, fails, or has unconfirmed delivery. Failure notices point to Run history rather than telling people to re-enable an ended job. Transient retries and explicitly scheduled next checks still work.
- Administrators with unrestricted run-history access can select **Retry** on eligible failures in **Automations → Run history**. Retry starts a fresh attempt, not a delivery replay; check uncertain delivery before retrying. Jobs with authority tied to their original identity aren't automatically recreated.
- Doctor reports the old entries it finds. On repair it backs up cron state, moves recognized ended failures to Run history, and preserves the existing run or reconstructs the last recorded outcome if older history has expired. When an explicit keep-after-run or cleanup policy has no faithful conversion, Doctor keeps the definition paused and explains why. It does not rerun anything. The retired option is removed from the CLI, tool, protocol, and editors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler records history and retains the definition privately in the same transaction that removes the ended job from the list. This lets Retry look up the original run without putting the job back in Paused or returning its definition in the history response. The implementation reuses the existing history retention, scheduler admission, and Doctor backup, rather than introducing a separate archive service.

Related automation cleanup PRs may overlap in schedule settlement, Doctor cron repair, Gateway/agent tool schemas, and the Control UI automation editor. Those cleanups are not folded into this change.

## Evidence

The real Control UI with a deterministic mock Gateway displays a failed staging-build check. The browser test verifies that Retry targets the exact failed run. Before: `2b58c8e5224e`; after: UI candidate included in `d6a3bcd72148`. Core and UI typechecks and generated Gateway validators passed on the implementation before the final fixture and Doctor refactor. Focused runtime tests exercised failure, unknown delivery, and silence; the broader restart suite exposed old retained-job expectations, which were updated. Exact-candidate Doctor, Gateway Retry, and restart test results are not yet confirmed. The local autoreview was invalidated by a changing source snapshot; no clean review or live upgrade is claimed. No full CI, native-device run, or production database was used.

### Clean comparison

**Before — failed run has no Retry and the ended job still has a Paused group**

![Run history with a failed staging-build check and no Retry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8d099e8-b593-42a6-a9ab-f827272913e2)

**After — Retry is available on the failed run; the ended job is off the list**

![Run history with Retry on the failed staging-build check](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f856dc0-dc39-4746-b8c3-4a5b0a6b872e)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![The failed run before the Retry action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25d5fef6-06fc-4e82-b361-6b2b9b31f806)

**After**

![The new Retry action highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d23a41b-f076-46c3-93bc-10e98c53b58c)

Co-authored with [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

Plugin and skill recommendations reserve a 640 px-wide card for a short listing and two actions. That leaves a large gap between the publisher and the Install button in chat.

The shared card uses up to 384 px of the available chat column so that its desktop width stays stable when the action changes. Only the stylesheet and Chromium regression test changed; installation and authorization behavior are unchanged.

In the compiled Control UI, the Higgsfield MCP card measured **640 × 84 → 384 × 63 CSS px** at a 1440 px viewport. The ready-to-install and sign-in-needed states retained the same size. At a 390 px viewport, it measured **293.39 × 132 → 293.39 × 104 px**, with both actions visible.

prs.title: fix: recover stale Windows gateway locks after the holder dies
prs.body:
Closes #198757

## What Problem This Solves

After a crash on Windows, OpenClaw can refuse to start the Gateway ever again: the stale lock left behind names a PID that no longer exists, but the liveness check answers "alive", so recovery never happens and every start ends with `GatewayLockError: cannot verify Gateway ownership`. The reporter's gateway had been dead for 51 days and still could not restart.

## User Impact

User impact: Windows users can restart the Gateway after a crash or forced shutdown instead of manually deleting lock files under the state directory.

Two Windows-specific gaps made the dead holder look alive: `readNativeLiveness` treated the native helper's `access-denied` error as liveness evidence, but the Windows kernel deliberately answers `ACCESS_DENIED` for nonexistent PIDs (PID-reuse protection keeps "missing" and "hidden" indistinguishable); and when native evidence was unavailable at all (for example the helper fails to load without the VC++ redistributable, #200371), `isPidDefinitelyDead` had no Windows fallback for the `EPERM` signal-probe result. POSIX `EPERM` semantics are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

On Windows only, `access-denied` now maps to "unknown" instead of "alive", and when the signal probe returns `EPERM` with no native evidence, a bounded PowerShell oracle asks Windows itself: `GetProcessById` reports the kernel's table, and the oracle claims absence only when it answers with the not-found (`ArgumentException`) verdict — live-but-protected processes still resolve. Any other outcome (timeout, missing shell, unexpected exception) stays conservative, so a protected live owner is never declared dead. The probe is synchronous and bounded at two seconds, paid once per stale-lock inspection on startup, and never runs unless native evidence was already unavailable. One pinned expectation that encoded the old "hidden means alive" reading on Windows was updated to the ambiguity semantics; the same test still pins that behavior for macOS and FreeBSD.

## Evidence

Behavior checked: a stale Gateway lock naming a dead PID is classified dead and recovery proceeds, on the exact states the reporter hit (helper unavailable, and access-denied), without ever declaring a live or protected owner dead.

Red/green through the real classifier (`pnpm test src/shared/pid-alive.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 37 passed on the fixed tree):

- On base `392506102468`, the four new regression cases fail exactly as the issue describes: `isPidDefinitelyDead` returns `false` for `helper-unavailable + EPERM` and for `access-denied + EPERM` on win32, and the absence oracle is never consulted.
- On this branch those states recover (dead ⇒ `true`) while the conservative variants (`absent=false`, protected live, successful signal probe) stay not-dead, and the updated pinned case keeps `access-denied`-with-`ESRCH` recovering as before. POSIX hidden-process behavior remains `[alive, not-dead]`.

The oracle module itself is covered by direct unit tests (`src/shared/windows-process-absent.test.ts`, same run): absence is claimed only for the not-found verdict, every other verdict or probe failure stays conservative, the PowerShell call carries the two-second bound and hidden window, and nothing spawns off Windows or for invalid PIDs.

Live oracle proof on Windows (real PowerShell, real process states):

```
dead pid=24028   isWindowsProcessDefinitelyAbsent=true   (expect true)
self pid=908     ...=false
protected csrss pid=588 ...=false   (live-but-protected is never absent)
invalid pid=0    ...=false
```

Live Gateway stale-lock recovery, run end to end from the built `dist` on this Windows host:

- Dead holder (fresh gateway PID captured, gateway killed, lock left stale, gateway restarted): the lock is reclaimed and the gateway reaches listening state — verified twice, once with the native helper enabled and once with `PROC_SAFE_NATIVE=off` (the reporter's helper-unavailable condition).
- **The added `EPERM` branch, executed live and connected to the recovery decision:** a stale lock whose holder is a real protected live process (csrss.exe, `kill(pid,0)` → `EPERM`, helper disabled) with a matching start-time identity — so the pre-existing PID-reuse guard cannot shortcut — is **not** reclaimed: the PowerShell oracle answers `present` and the second gateway stays blocked. The same experiment with a mismatched start-time is correctly reclaimed by the pre-existing reuse guard, which also demonstrates why the oracle's conservative verdict matters.

```
[EPERM live] holder=csrss pid=588 startTime=2026-11-10T06:40:09Z heartbeat=2000-01-01 PROC_SAFE_NATIVE=off
RESULT: BLOCKED (oracle answered present; live protected holder not reclaimed)

[reuse-guard control] same holder pid, startTime left from the dead gateway
RESULT: lock reclaimed (existing PID-reuse protection) — gateway listening
```

**Positive classifier-to-reclamation path on a genuinely dead PID, real oracle, one injected errno:** this host's kernel answers `ESRCH` for dead PIDs (the reporter's Windows 11 kernel answers `EPERM`), so the probe injects exactly that single kernel-dependent errno for the signal probe while everything else stays real — a real killed PID, the real production classifier, `PROC_SAFE_NATIVE=off`, and the real PowerShell oracle:

```
dead pid=5816 (helper=off), signal probe injected EPERM (reporter's kernel behavior)
isPidAlive=true (conservative) isPidDefinitelyDead=true -> RECLAIMED (oracle answered absent)
```

Combined with the blocked protected-holder run above, both directions of the new fallback (absent ⇒ reclaim, present ⇒ keep blocked) have now been executed against real process states through the real oracle; the only non-real input anywhere is the one errno this host's kernel cannot produce, which is exactly the reporter's own kernel observation from the issue.
