## What Problem This Solves

When creating an automation, Advanced settings exposes a raw routing field and lets you save a job that never starts or keep a one-time job around after it has succeeded. The editor also shows a second copy of the prompt you just typed.

## User Impact

New automations start active, and new one-time automations use the Gateway’s existing cleanup default after a successful run. The create and edit forms no longer show **Session key**, **Turn on after creating**, **Delete after it runs**, or the duplicate **Prompt preview**. You can still choose **Runs in**, read the saved prompt, and pause or resume an automation after creating it.

Existing automations are not migrated, rewritten, or deleted by this change. Saving an unrelated edit leaves the job’s existing routing, pause state, and cleanup policy alone. The Gateway API and CLI are unchanged. A duplicate retains its source’s routing but starts active and uses the new-job cleanup defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor now relies on the Gateway’s defaults instead of maintaining its own. The revamp had kept the editor’s Markdown **Prompt preview** under Advanced → Task; this removes that duplicate, not the saved prompt shown outside the editor.

Related work: #201211, #201213, and #201214 were already merged into the base. #201218 may touch the same editor, English strings, and stylesheet; the model and reasoning pickers are unchanged here. Other automation cleanups may touch the same form and save code; this PR does not change the backend or job migrations.

## Evidence

- The built Control UI created a one-time job in Chromium with a mocked Gateway. The test checked that the four controls were gone and the create request left routing, activation, and cleanup overrides unset.
- 96 focused UI tests passed, including the pause, duplicate-routing, and edit-preservation cases. The UI typecheck, targeted lint and format, controller guard, and i18n verification passed. Local Codex autoreview against `a45edd342c6b14` found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- Before/after screenshots were captured from the built Control UI with the same synthetic one-time checklist and are pending GitHub attachment. No live Gateway or full CI suite was run locally.

prs.title: fix: resume model catalog publishing when a release ships minified code
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The hosted model catalog has not published since 2026-11-19 12:29 UTC. Every scheduled `openclaw/catalog` publish since 16:26 UTC fails in the released-reader gate with `released reader entry point not found in .../2026.11.10-beta.1/node_modules/openclaw/dist: refreshRemoteModelCatalog`. Users keep seeing a catalog that is more than a day old.

## User Impact

The catalog publisher can check `openclaw@2026.11.10-beta.1` again, and publishing resumes. Future releases ship a fixed file for the gate, so a bundler change in a release can no longer stop catalog publishing. The gate stays strict: a release that reads the feed but has no runnable refresh still fails. No change for OpenClaw users.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gate runs each tagged release's own catalog refresh. It found that function by a source-name search that expected pretty-printed chunks: a declaration at the start of a line and `export {` with a space. 2026.11.10-beta.1 is the first release with whitespace-minified chunks (`}async function refreshRemoteModelCatalog(e){`, `export{…}`), so neither pattern matched. The function itself was not renamed, moved or inlined.

- Releases now build `dist/model-catalog/remote-refresh.js` as a named entry. The gate runs the refresh from it, and runs the config reader from the existing `dist/config/config.js`. If one of these files is present but does not export its function, the gate fails.
- Releases without the entry (2026.10.33, 2026.11.6, 2026.11.10-beta.1) are still searched by declaration, with whitespace-independent patterns. This search can be removed once every tagged release ships the entry.
- A `tsdown-config` test fails CI if either entry leaves the build or stops exporting its function under the name the gate uses.

## Evidence

- **Real gate, real releases (TMPDIR in scratch, live catalog files):** before the fix, `catalog-compare-released.mts --check` on the live v3 file fails with the exact publisher error for 2026.11.10-beta.1. With the fix:
  - v3: `2026.11.6`: no v3 reader, skipped; `2026.10.33`: no v3 reader, skipped; `2026.11.10-beta.1`: updated, 1414/1414 rows.
  - v2: `2026.11.6`, `2026.10.33` and `2026.11.10-beta.1`: updated, 1392/1392 rows each.
- **Regression tests** (`test/scripts/catalog-compare-released.test.ts`) run `--check` against fake releases. Minified chunks and the stable entry fail on the base with the production error and pass with the fix. A stable entry without the export fails. A v3 reader without a runnable refresh fails.

**Merge risk:** two-way door. A revert restores the old search. It writes no state and changes no package export; the only new artifact is one internal dist file. Blast radius if wrong: the catalog publish gate (publishing stays blocked, and the last good catalog stays live). OpenClaw runtime behavior does not change.

prs.title: fix(sessions): accept text as an alias for message in sessions_send
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `sessions_send` rejects payloads that use `text` instead of `message`, while the `message` tool already treats `text` as an alias — so models emit `text`, the call is rejected at the tool-validation boundary, and every dispatch wastes a failed tool call plus a self-correction round trip.
- Solution: Accept `text` as an alias for `message` in `sessions_send`, at both the schema boundary and the input reader.
- What changed: `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.schema.ts` (message optional, text alias added), `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.input.ts` (alias resolution mirroring the message tool's first-non-empty semantics), `src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts` (regression tests).
- What did NOT change: `message` remains the canonical field; an explicit non-empty `message` always wins over `text`. Missing/blank content still fails with `message required`. `PlacedSessionsSendSchema` (the gateway-protocol worker-placement variant in `packages/gateway-protocol`) is untouched — out of scope, would be a named follow-up if wanted.

Fixes #202615

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A scheduled dispatcher agent calling `sessions_send` with `text` instead of `message` got the call rejected; the two tools disagreed about the same concept.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux x64, Node v24.20.0, worktree at `issue-202615` on `origin/main` (599bc4222a4). The payload was run through the production argument validator (`validateToolArguments` in `packages/llm-core/src/validation.ts`, the same validator the agent loop applies) against the real `SessionsSendToolSchema`, and the real tool `execute` was exercised in the `sessions.test.ts` suite.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # production validation boundary, before and after the patch
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs validate-alias.mts
  # regression tests
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  VALIDATION OK: {"sessionKey":"agent:main:other","text":"hello via text alias","timeoutSeconds":0}
  ```
  Before the patch the same payload was rejected with `Validation failed for tool "sessions_send": - message: must have required properties message`. After the patch, the tool-execution test shows the aliased text delivered to the Gateway `agent` method (`message` param contains "hello via text alias"), and the suite passes 33/33 (the two new tests failed before the fix).
- **Observed result after fix:** `{text: ...}` payloads validate and are delivered as the session message; `{message: ...}` behaves exactly as before; blank/missing content still throws `message required`.
- **What was not tested:** No live model turn was driven end to end (the rejection and recovery happen at the tool-validation boundary, which was exercised directly with the production validator and the real tool execute path).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: `accepts text as an alias for message` (tool execute delivers aliased text to the Gateway) and `accepts a text-alias payload at the schema boundary` (schema admits `text`, still accepts `message`).
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: both layers that used to reject the alias (schema validation and input reading) are pinned with the exact payload shape from the issue.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `SessionsSendToolSchema` required `message` and `readSessionsSendMessage` read only `message`, while the `message` tool resolves its send text from `[message, text, content, caption]` — the inconsistency invited models to emit `text`, which `sessions_send` then rejected.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test covered the alias payload at either the schema or execution layer.

prs.title: improve: faster update recovery capture for large WhatsApp credential folders
prs.body:
Related: #201251

## What Problem This Solves

When the WhatsApp channel is enabled, `openclaw update` copies its whole credentials directory into the original-state recovery capture before anything changes. On real installs that directory holds about 3,000 tiny signal-store files. The capture flushed each copy to disk before starting the next one, so every file waited for its own disk commit. On a busy disk (a WSL2 virtual disk, or anything else writing heavily) that costs about 50 ms per file: more than two minutes added to every update, with the Gateway down for the whole time.

## User Impact

On a contended disk, the original-state capture of a WhatsApp-sized credentials tree is about 3x faster: 147 s → 49 s for 3,008 files. When the disk is idle it goes from 22 s to 16 s. Recovery guarantees are unchanged. Every copied file is still flushed to disk before the capture's manifest is sealed, and a failed flush still fails the capture.

## Why This Change Was Made

The per-file flush was the measured cost: 49 ms per file under contention, the same figure the reporter measured independently on their WSL2 host. The change copies all files first, then flushes them together (up to 32 at a time), so the filesystem can commit many of them in one journal commit. If any flush fails, the capture waits for the in-flight flushes to settle before failing, so incomplete-capture cleanup never races open handles (matters on Windows).

What was left as is:

- **The WhatsApp root:** narrowing it was rejected. The whole credentials directory really is that migration's recovery resource.
- **SQLite timeout accounting:** the separate defect where non-SQLite credential files are counted in the SQLite inspection timeout belongs to the backup/inspection sizing owner. It only inflates a ceiling and debug log lines and costs no wall time, so it stays a follow-up.

This does not explain the reporter's entire 90-minute window. It removes the part of the capture that scales with file count under disk load.

## Evidence

The real `captureUpdateRecoveryBaseline` was run on AWS (c7a.8xlarge, ext4 on EBS, Node 24.22.1) with base `b8b173b6697`. The capture covered a 3,008-file WhatsApp-shaped credentials directory; only the plugin's recovery-resource declaration was synthetic. Each configuration ran 3 times. Contention was a continuous buffered 3 GB `dd` to the same disk.

| | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Idle (median) | 21.97 s (7.3 ms/file) | 15.81 s (5.3 ms/file) |
| Contended (median) | 147.4 s (49.0 ms/file) | 49.2 s (16.4 ms/file) |

A copy+fsync microbenchmark of the same 3,008 files under contention gave 40.7–58 ms/file serial and 11.3–12.1 ms/file batched. Flushing 8, 32 or 128 at a time made no difference.

<details><summary>Checks</summary>

- `src/infra/update-database-backup.test.ts`: 39/39, which includes the original-capture payload byte/hash, sealing and cleanup cases
- `src/infra/doctor-capture-reuse.test.ts`: 11/11
- `src/commands/doctor-original-capture.test.ts`: 34/34
- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-fresh-preview.test.ts`: 8/8
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint and guards green. The only failure is the existing dead export `CronSchedule` in `extensions/knowledge` (from #202416), which this PR does not touch.
- Autoreview (P2): scoped-clean on both commits. Independent Codex review: no findings.
- Production LOC: +17/−2.

prs.title: fix: reduce Gateway work when Linux commands start and finish
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting and releasing Linux agent commands repeatedly checks the Gateway's own cgroup placement and delegation with synchronous filesystem calls. The command setup also re-reads an unchanged memory policy and copies a freshly merged environment a second time.

## User Impact

Linux command preparation spends less time blocking the Gateway thread while preserving session placement, memory protection, and the no-delegation fallback. Service delegation is discovered once per process; restart the Gateway after changing delegation. No configuration or data migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cgroup startup owner now invalidates one snapshot before refreshing policy. Starts, placement and release consume that snapshot. The populated-root check remains in initial discovery, and actual kernel placement writes still handle errors. Commands await the first memory-budget write and reuse it until budget bytes change, startup refreshes policy, or a write fails. Session leaf recreation and asynchronous reclamation retain their existing owners.

Environment preparation stamps its already-owned merged result with the existing marker helper, eliminating a second full copy without mutating caller inputs. Per-command broker options remain uncached. The Node buffer gate remains unchanged: Node 26.8+ already uses the faster native one-shot reader.

Production delta: +44 lines for the explicit snapshot lifecycle and shared awaited policy write. No additional census, configuration, schema, or background process.

## Evidence

Two new start/release regressions fail on the original code and pass with the fix, including no delegation. The cgroup/exec suites pass 51 tests (2 platform skips); command, supervisor, PTY and sandbox consumers pass another 139 (5 skips). Total local runner wall times, including compilation: 31.31s and 43.63s. No changed module is imported by the Control UI.

Synthetic owner replay on Node 26.12.1/macOS, five interleaved A/B pairs plus five A/A controls; CPU and allocation captured separately:

| Per 1,000 cgroup start/placement/release cycles | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Sync read calls | 17,000 | 1,000 |
| Sync access calls | 11,000 | 0 |
| Main-thread CPU ms | 606.721 / 733.390 | 247.088 / 368.439 |
| Process CPU ms | 637.201 / 774.942 | 272.321 / 392.815 |
| Wall ms | 627.685 / 968.558 | 266.800 / 588.315 |
| Sampled allocated bytes | 104,771,992 / 106,217,760 | 32,195,856 / 32,894,736 |

Placement writes stay 3,000 and async cleanup reads stay 1,000. The one remaining sync read supplies session IO limits. Cold setup uses 100 initializations per run: median 0.665→0.480 ms; median per-run p95 0.751→0.528 ms. A/A main CPU medians are 600.516/582.188 ms; allocation 105,728,808/105,734,144 bytes. Five-sample nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. All paired CPU results improve.

Separately, 10,000 Git environment preparations with 180 synthetic keys: CPU 274.701→71.728 ms and sampled allocation 801,111,240→251,178,560 bytes; values match and inputs remain unchanged. A/A CPU medians are 275.692/272.783 ms; allocation 797,851,120/800,141,848 bytes.

Acceptance was zero warm discovery reads/accesses, unchanged placement/writes, lower CPU/allocation, and no >20% cold/tail regression. The replay uses actual local file I/O over a synthetic cgroup tree with 15 active sessions and 4,000 synthetic identities. It does not exercise real Linux cgroup enforcement or whole-Gateway/database/workspace throughput. Database and workspace contents are not inputs to this owner. No live deployment or production data was accessed.

Reproduce with committed `scripts/perf/exec-cgroup-discovery-measure.mts` and `scripts/perf/exec-env-measure.mts`: materialize the respective baseline modules beside their imports from `4eb94c89588f86934a36ebf8ca13e7df24553356`, then pass those paths to `pnpm exec tsx <script> <baseline-module>` (cgroup cycles: 1000). Remove temporary baseline modules afterward.

Final-source core, all core-test shards, script typechecks, targeted typed lint, formatting and diff checks pass. The owner suite was rerun: 40/40 passed (42.15s including compilation). Codex autoreview of the complete final local snapshot against `4eb94c89588f86934a36ebf8ca13e7df24553356` is scoped-clean at P0–P2. Initial patch-caused type/brace lint errors were fixed and their affected checks rerun.

`pnpm check:changed` remains red only for nine unused-export findings reproduced exactly on that clean baseline. These are main regressions: Knowledge `AccountTokens` (#202411, `4da7f93e9a31f`); test helpers `FAKE_TRANSPORTS`, `TURN_KINDS`, `randomJourney` (#201723, `336bc3cb723f1`); `installTemplateCatalogGateway` (#202535, `6f6525e4457dd`); and four Skill Workshop exports (#202572, `e6d441549fe25`). No failed owner is changed here. Source history identifies the added or orphaned exports, and the exact baseline export command reproduces all nine without module-resolution errors.

The separate unused-file scan is red on the Knowledge Slack normalizer added by #202411. Neither new benchmark is reported; both are covered by the existing performance-driver entrypoint declaration. This scan is not claimed green or used as baseline CI-failure evidence.

Exact-head CI [44808259791](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44808259791), attempt 1, completed **failed** on `d3036ad9242cff0c98f292f8d8ea0fbcc5eff1d4`. The actual tested merge is `5cc26722d01ffa567bcc3b49e7ac1a425738a7e6`, with main parent `b4a41aa642ce0f8016527e964c5015b21487d654`. All failed assertions reproduce on that exact main parent:

- Plugin skill-authoring refresh: XML-only test parser sees zero entries after #202326 (`5efe765e9cfa315f22f4769c7b7ff777475a90ab`) switched the reader-enabled prompt to a compact catalog. Exact-parent test reproduces the same failure.
- Skills readiness and skill-settings asset count: #202531 (`856aca23d7fb5557162db8613a93ae1f2e2f6d19`) changed the installed-skills shelf/chunk graph. Local exact-parent readiness fails; configured Boat Linux reproduces **33 assets > 31** on verified parent tree `a30e53e0adbeeb50b56b8dea40797f441e2b35c7` (1 failed / 3 skipped, 46.63s Vitest).
- Plugins readiness: #202527 (`c2c2effaeddb1ed99db0788fb2dfa61cf7ae03c7`) filters the fixture's installed catalog entries; exact-parent readiness reproduces the same timeout.

These are main test/fixture regressions, not ignored noise. No failed owner changes in the PR; UI/scenario and skill prompt/test sources are identical between parent and tested merge. Local setup failures are excluded from reproduction evidence. No CI reruns or expectation changes. `security-fast` passed independently. The lane lead's standing pinned-head inherited-failure exception applies; this is agent-lead authority, not Peter's personal acceptance.

Codex autoreview is clean, hosted Codex review has no findings, and [ClawSweeper's final-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202703#issuecomment-7049787652) has **0 findings and 0 open checklist items** on `d3036ad`. The review's Linux runtime evidence limitation remains explicitly disclosed above. Native `scripts/pr` preparation is complete in `github_pending` mode; merge will use retained exact-head inherited-failure evidence, without claiming failed CI is green.

prs.title: docs: name the export command in the disk-budget cleanup advice
prs.body:
Supersedes #201175 (branch rebuild for freshness closed it; reopen was refused).

Closes #190687

## What Problem This Solves

When a session store goes over its disk budget, the docs tell you to fix it by "exporting and deleting unneeded sessions" — but nothing on that page names the export mechanism. If you go looking for the command that does it, it isn't referenced from the page that recommends it.

## User Impact

Someone hitting the disk-budget warning can now go straight to the command that does the export instead of hunting through the slash-command reference — and can see at the same time which first-party command covers archiving other sessions headlessly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The export mechanism exists and is documented elsewhere: the owner-only in-chat `/export-session` command (alias `/export`) writes the current session as a self-contained HTML transcript inside the workspace. The sentence now names it, links to its reference, and states its scope so it doesn't read as a bulk-archival recipe. Because `/export-session` covers only the current session, the paragraph also links `openclaw sessions archive` (first-party headless/multi-session archival via the running Gateway) so the "export and delete" advice doesn't strand headless users.

## Evidence

- Before: the only mention of exporting in the disk-budget section was the phrase "exporting and deleting unneeded sessions" — no command named, no link, no scope.
- After (this diff): the same sentence is followed by the `/export-session` link, the owner-only / current-session / HTML-in-workspace scope, and a pointer to `openclaw sessions archive` for archiving other sessions headlessly.
- Clawsweeper's 11-01 review on #190687 independently confirmed the gap against current main and prescribed the core fix: "Update the disk-budget paragraph to link /export-session and state its owner-only, current-session, workspace-HTML scope."
- The `sessions archive` link target and its multi-key usage (`openclaw sessions archive "agent:main:scratch-1" "agent:main:scratch-2"`) were verified against `docs/cli/sessions.md` and the CLI registration in `src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.ts`.

Verified `docs/tools/slash-commands.md` uses the same scope wording for `/export-session` ("Owner-only. Export the current session to HTML inside the workspace. Alias: `/export`"), and both linked anchors (`#core-commands`, `#archive-sessions`) are the sections containing the referenced commands.

prs.title: feat: prepare worker placements for recovery after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a worker is confirmed lost, Codex recovery needs to know which placement it is replacing, even if the Gateway restarted. The shared database has no field for that fact yet.

## User Impact

This prerequisite adds storage only; it does not enable recovery or change existing placements. Shared state advances from v40 to v41 (the agent schema is unchanged). Older builds require restoration of the verified pre-upgrade backup before downgrade.

Related: #201026, #201032. The existing shared branch and both PRs are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing placement row and migration owner: one nullable field on SQLite and PostgreSQL, no backfill, no automatic loss inference, and no reader or writer for the new field in this PR. The placement owner can later record the predecessor with its existing placement update; a separate store would add another write and rollback boundary. No repository reset, permission change, or new retention policy is included. [Maintainer design acceptance](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2d5e4b6d-a60b-4a09-a054-d919b7a422c0).

## Evidence

- Fixtures from the published stable v36 and beta v40 SQLite schemas preserved the seeded rows and original schema when commit was refused, then upgraded successfully through the existing owner. The new field was NULL; this was not a package-update/restart run.
- Isolated PostgreSQL 18.6 passed 16 focused cases, including old schemas with and without the optional repository table. Repository fragment SQL is unchanged. Generated schema checks, focused typechecks, lint, formatting, and the test-line budget (+248 net; 400 allowed) passed on the tested patch against `4b74fd5a979d`. Local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the reviewed scope.
- **Upgrade cost:** one nullable ALTER on `worker_session_placements`, no backfill or row rewrite; SQLite retains existing idempotent index checks and quick/placement integrity checks. The scoped SQLite backup copies placement rows and publication metadata; the package updater retains its existing full rollback capture. PostgreSQL takes its normal DDL lock and publishes the version. Largest-deployment row counts and backup/lock timings were not available; packaged update/restart and a Swift build are still unverified.

Original implementation: @galiniliev, selectively ported from `a1b9b73924b6`.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2d5e4b6d-a60b-4a09-a054-d919b7a422c0)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6687be0c-f3a4-4c4b-be8b-f381289c2f8f)

prs.title: fix(mcp): mcp login prints an unusable sign-in link when the client ID is a JWT
prs.body:
Closes #197356

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw mcp login` prints a sign-in link that cannot be opened when the MCP provider issues a JWT as the client ID. ClickUp's hosted MCP server does this.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can sign in to OAuth MCP servers such as ClickUp from the link `openclaw mcp login` prints, and tools that read that link from the command's output get a working one.

Before, the middle of `client_id` was replaced with `…`, and the provider answered `401 invalid_client`. No error was shown by OpenClaw.

One behavior to know: the link line is now written to stdout as plain text in every console style. With `logging.consoleStyle: "json"`, that one line is no longer a JSON log line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The login printed the authorization URL through the console logger, which masks token-shaped text. A JWT client ID matches that mask. The URL holds no secret (client ID, PKCE challenge, state, redirect, scope), and it is printed for a person to open, so it now goes straight to stdout the way other commands write output that must reach the caller unchanged. Everything else the command prints is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Update: head `960c193877c0995fd86759caa5b6d2027218dd46`, merged with `main` at `4b74fd5a979df8afd4d018094ef6520f74ce7d5e`.** #200538 added a Gateway-backed login branch that printed `result.authorizationUrl` through the same redacting logger. This revision writes that URL with `writeStdout` as well, so both login branches in `src/cli/mcp-cli-oauth.ts` now print the link unchanged.

- Regression, red then green: the existing test `routes login and logout through a live Gateway owner and prints its sign-in link` now gives the Gateway a JWT-shaped `client_id` and asserts `writeStdout` receives the whole URL. With the test change only: `expected "writeStdout" to be called with arguments ... Number of calls: 0` (1 failed, 3 passed). With the source change: passes.
- `pnpm test src/cli/mcp-cli.login-loopback.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.oauth.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.oauth-integration.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 59 passed in 4 files (Node 24.22.2, macOS arm64).
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: `Test lines OK. Net test lines: +11; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 0.`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, and `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the two files changed in this revision: pass.
- Not rerun at this head: the live ClickUp run below (it exercises the offline branch, whose source line is unchanged) and a complete `pnpm check:changed`. On macOS that command stopped at `SQLite worker ratchet`, where the tool ran out of heap (exit 134); I did not rerun it on unmodified `main` on macOS.

The evidence below is from the earlier head named there.

Head `cdadc1b492bc54a49ed127fb2a4070f97b966851`, rebased on `main` at `de6dc6249746de070d49c0ed521f39addd63cbb6`. The live output, tests and checks below were rerun at this head.

Since the first revision (`ec60bef41a9`): the source change is the same; the new test was shortened from +29 to +7 test lines after the test-lines ratchet failed in CI, and the branch was rebased.

**Live, real CLI path.** `openclaw mcp set` then `openclaw mcp login` run from source (`src/entry.ts`) in a fresh home against `https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp`, with real discovery and dynamic client registration. `state` and `code_challenge` are replaced below; nothing else is edited.

Before (`src/cli/mcp-cli-oauth.ts` as on `main`):

```
Open this URL to authorize "clickup":
https://mcp.clickup.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=mcp-client-eyJhbG…Nu1I&code_challenge=<challenge>&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Foauth%2Fcallback&state=<state>&scope=read+write&resource=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.clickup.com%2Fmcp
After approval, run openclaw mcp login clickup --code <code>.
```

After (this branch):

```
Open this URL to authorize "clickup":
https://mcp.clickup.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=mcp-client-eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjEifQ.eyJ0b2tlblR5cGUiOiJqd3RfY2xpZW50X2lkIiwidXJpX2hhc2hlcyI6WyJlZWxHRHBqekpOTU9yZ0FJLW5JWTlBIl0sImlzcyI6ImNsaWNrdXAtbWNwLXNlcnZlciIsImlhdCI6MTc5NDQ5NzEzOH0.nYKl0LbVhLkKQUA4ZmxciuCZOEW-BBSu62tTdZfHeMg&code_challenge=<challenge>&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Foauth%2Fcallback&state=<state>&scope=read+write&resource=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.clickup.com%2Fmcp
After approval, run openclaw mcp login clickup --code <code>.
```

The masked link sent to ClickUp's authorize endpoint returns `401 {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Invalid client_id"}`. The client ID shown is a throwaway registration for a callback at `example.com`.

**Tests.** `pnpm test src/cli/mcp-cli.login-loopback.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.oauth.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.oauth-integration.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 56 passed in 4 files (Node 24.22.2, Linux arm64). An existing loopback test now gives the login a JWT-shaped client ID, asserts that `redactSensitiveText` would change that URL, and asserts the URL is written whole. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: `Test lines OK. Net test lines: +7; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 0.`

**Checks.** `pnpm check:changed` (Node 24.22.2, Linux arm64 container): 32 of 34 steps pass, including format, lint, `typecheck core`, `typecheck core tests`, the tsgo graph boundary, import cycles and plugin boundaries. The two that fail do so identically on unmodified `main` at `de6dc624974` in the same container, and neither touches a file in this PR:

- `dead export scan`: `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.pending-inputs.ts: bindSessionPendingInputMentionInvitation` and `src/config/sessions/session-pending-input-source.ts: readPendingInputSource` are reported unused.
- `SQLite worker ratchet`: the tool stops with `An error was suppressed during disposal` and outcome `failure` (a tool error), not `rejected` (a finding). This PR adds no SQLite call.

Format and lint of the changed files pass inside `check:changed`.

**Local review.** Autoreview (`openclaw/agent-skills` at 16121cf, helper `source-sha256:edb41e63c868269e193951a1fd9abe02494cff54885d541b2d5f20e1fc0f9700`), `--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`, run on this patch before the rebase (base `0e966cc6e0927ddc539d79f6937a8a7dc51e9b82`, head `d225043955abe3cb06a5a3c8b588866a1fd8b007`; `git patch-id --stable` equals this head's, `72d7d11e6851`): `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings, one pass. Engine `claude` (`claude-fable-5`); the Codex CLI was not available for this work. The reviewer listed three things it could not confirm from the bundle; each was checked by hand: `writeStdout` appends the newline (`src/runtime.ts`); no other test reads the authorization URL from the log spy (the four `mcp login` CLI test files above are the ones that run this path, and all pass); and `mcp login` has no mode that routes logs to stderr for machine-readable stdout (`routeLogsToStderr` is used by JSON output, ACP, completion and doctor only).

**Not covered.** No macOS or Windows run. No completed sign-in against ClickUp: the run stops at the printed link, which is the changed behavior. The full test suite is left to CI.

prs.title: fix: recover longer session history text within response bounds
prs.body:
Related: #64970

## What Problem This Solves

Agents reviewing long conversations cannot request visible message text beyond the fixed 4,000-character `sessions_history` preview, even when the complete message fits within the existing response budget.

## User Impact

Callers can opt into `maxChars: 1..64000` for bounded visible-text recovery. Omitting it preserves the 4,000-character default. The 80 KiB response cap, access checks, physical-session checks, and existing reasoning/tool-preview limits remain in place.

This is not an unbounded export: oversized source rows remain explicitly incomplete, and historical/pre-reset discovery is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool requests a bounded read through its existing authorized `chat.history` owner and applies the requested limit to visible text locally. Reads retain at least the existing upstream preview size so smaller text requests do not shorten reasoning/tool previews. It preserves upstream truncation facts and marks a source-row group incomplete when the local byte cap splits its display siblings, rather than silently treating the surviving sibling as complete.

The existing Control UI full-message/export path serves interactive readers; it does not supply this model-facing reader option. Unlike the closed environment-override proposal in #65029, this is a bounded per-call option, not a new global setting or a higher default. It builds on the pagination owner in #97101 and structured truncation in #126342.

## Evidence

Current published head: `3faaa5a937f1b1eb298911f04a5e4a67640edb6a`, integrated with upstream `6b3c804312d7e3b3e4d45ce226c0feac590cf581`. The published tree `ee244f4afdfa9293cff092ec7cbc40ada0c643e1` matches the validated workspace exactly. Earlier conflicts were limited to generated prompt artifacts and resolved by the canonical generator.

- **95 affected tests passed** across five files: history, anchor budgeting, embedded adapter, real-storage composed history, and prompt-prefix stability. Three-shard wall time: 50.52 seconds.
- Both canonical production and agents-tools test typechecks passed. Scoped repository lint and formatting passed, as did whitespace checks against the integrated base. Prompt snapshots (6 files) and assertion-safety checks passed before the adapter-only repair; their inputs are unchanged. Net test growth is +354 lines, within the 400-line allowance.
- The original recovery regressions fail against the unmodified implementation. Preview-bound regressions for tool-result aliases/envelopes, nested results, and small text limits were reproduced and fixed.
- **Hosted review finding addressed:** the embedded adapter discarded `maxChars`, clipping at 8,000 before the tool could recover 16,000 characters. The existing adapter now forwards the parsed option to the shared text-limit owner. The new `sessions-history-tool.embedded.test.ts` writes through `SessionManager.appendMessageAsync` into isolated real storage, then invokes the real tool, embedded adapter, and history reader without replacing the adapter/reader/storage with mocks. It fails at exact 16,000-character recovery before the fix and passes afterward, then verifies two byte-capped pages recover the original 16,000-character message plus three 40,000-character messages in order, without omission or duplication. Each response remains at or below 80 KiB. Its normal runner uses the established host-owned database lane; the composed case completes in about three seconds of test time.
- Prior full-feature and CI-repair Auto Review passes were P0–P2 `scoped-clean`. The fresh three-file embedded repair received an independent narrative P0–P2 source review with no findings, including its test-lane registration. That reviewer inspected supplied sources but did not execute tests or independently verify the checkout SHA; this is not an Auto Review machine receipt or maintainer approval. The native Auto Review service currently rejects its own runtime configuration before execution.
- **Current-head CI gates passed:** [CI finalizer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44606766159/job/135862438343) and [consolidated gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44609653987), both on `3faaa5a937f1b1eb298911f04a5e4a67640edb6a`. Production/test types, prompt snapshots, security-sensitive/dependency review, and applicable security lanes passed. The bounded checks reader does not expose the entire 141-check inventory, so this is a verified gate result, not a claim that every job ran or passed.
- **Current-head hosted re-review completed:** the [durable review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197807#issuecomment-6828977121) confirms the embedded-adapter repair, reports no findings and no Before-merge items, and marks the PR ready for maintainer review. Overall readiness/proof remain **1/6**, patch quality **4/6**—not Diamond.

The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197807#issuecomment-6828977121) also asks for an isolated live-Gateway/real-agent demonstration. The new test supplies real-storage/tool/adapter integration evidence, **not live Gateway or model proof**. prs.title: fix(goals): allow Goals on OpenClaw cloud workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting or resuming a Goal in an otherwise usable OpenClaw cloud-worker conversation is rejected before the worker can admit its input. Goal admission recognizes Codex workers but omits built-in OpenClaw workers in `worker-turn` mode.

## User Impact

This change enables Goal Start and Resume admission on OpenClaw cloud workers. The Goal, input turn, and operation receipt commit together after runtime admission. Setup failure, a lost placement claim, or a blocking/throwing input-policy hook must not create or reactivate the Goal. Explicit runtime choices retain their precedence.

Automatic continuation to completion is not yet proven: it failed after Resume in the live Azure run described below. No new configuration, persistence schema, migration, or required user action is introduced. Policy rejection remains terminal for that input's operation ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generalizes the existing runtime Goal admission, input staging, source guard, and acknowledgment owner to include OpenClaw workers while preserving local/Codex behavior and visible-spawn eligibility.

- `e29da7a951c` prevents blocked-message audit persistence from applying a Goal mutation or successful Goal-operation receipt. It retains an existing worker-turn placement when runtime policy is implicit, without overriding explicit choices.
- `55f66bba1c6` fixes the three fixture lint errors caught by CI without changing behavior.
- `07610fc6348` merges `main` at `bd67a3f9a18` into the PR branch. The sole conflict resolution retains the authenticated-operator check for both runtime-admitted Goals and active steering.

The same owners handle these decisions; no parallel manager or compatibility path was added. Hook fixtures share the existing Goal test-support owner rather than exceeding the worker-support file's line cap.

Original implementation by @galiniliev. The linked work session covers review and follow-up corrections.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1982ca1f-7dc1-485c-9af9-265bbf8c3d61)

## Evidence

**Landing blocked:** Live Pause/Resume did not lead to durable automatic completion on `07610fc63480827693622e419b074237d1d41ea2`. Resume returned a success receipt, but the automatic worker turn lost authority during transcript commit. The Goal returned to paused with zero settled continuation turns. The [required CI gate passed on the same head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44789793338), but that does not override the failed live case. Trace which authority expired, fix the responsible lifecycle path, and rerun the live case through durable completion before landing.

### Live Azure worker-turn proof

OpenClaw `2026.11.5` ran from PR head `07610fc63480827693622e419b074237d1d41ea2` in a disposable Azure Container Apps Gateway. The installed package reported that commit and matched SHA-256 `a2f538a76b57afc596f51aa07195f8ea508d2cd3dbe905032670a0b6d472f861`. The Azure Sandbox worker bundle SHA-256 was `090e62ef54d1e3e0cc27c0dc54c7d818f6dc6199a44d490ec90d069ad327e452`. The Gateway enrolled a Linux node, and a separate Azure lease read found a model-created file on the worker. The worker hostname differed from the Gateway hostname, and the same path was absent on the Gateway.

| Scenario | Result | Observed state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start in an idle worker session | **Pass** | Active worker-turn placement with zero user turns, no Goal, and no receipt. Successful `chat.send` left one user turn, an active Goal, and a SQLite Start receipt with the same Goal ID. |
| Pause and Resume to automatic completion | **Fail** | The same Goal moved from active to paused. Resume returned a successful receipt and the model finished phase two. The next automatic worker turn ended with `worker turn authority changed` during transcript commit and `worker turn cancelled`. The Goal returned to paused with zero settled continuation turns and one human turn. A later Resume also ended with the Goal paused. |
| Worker setup rejection | **Pass** | A separate idle worker's disposable workspace was temporarily moved. `chat.send` returned `UNAVAILABLE` and said it had not committed Goal input. Before and after were identical for the admission checks. No Goal, zero user turns, and no SQLite operation receipt. The workspace was restored. |
| Blocking input policy | **Pass** | A live `before_agent_run` policy blocked both requests. Start left no Goal. Resume left the same Goal paused. Neither committed a successful operation receipt. Each transcript showed the policy's replacement input and omitted the original blocked text. |
| Implicit Codex selection on an unpinned worker session | **Unrun** | Access to a real implicit-Codex model route was unavailable. The OpenAI Platform credential returned HTTP 401, and the inference route used for this run returned HTTP 403 for `gpt-5.5` and `gpt-5.6-luna`. An explicit provider override control exercised a different policy source. |

<details>
<summary>Redacted live receipts</summary>

```text
18:32:45Z  Linux cloud node enrolled, version 2026.11.5
Start      worker-turn / idle / Goal absent / user turns 0 / receipt absent
           accepted / Goal active / user turns 1 / SQLite Start receipt present
Pause      same Goal paused / active run false / user turns 1
Resume     accepted / SQLite Resume receipt present / phase two completed
18:33:46Z  worker transcript commit failed: worker turn authority changed
18:33:46Z  node worker exit 1: worker turn cancelled
After      same Goal paused / settled continuations 0 / user turns 1
Rejection  UNAVAILABLE: Goal input was not committed
           before and after: Goal absent / user turns 0 / receipt absent
Policy     Start blocked: Goal absent / receipt absent
           Resume blocked: same Goal paused / receipt absent
```

</details>

Azure Sandbox inventory returned zero leases after the run. The temporary allocator role was removed and verified.

- **42 focused tests passed on the refreshed candidate tree**: 30 active-steer cases and 12 OpenClaw/Codex worker Goal cases. [AWS proof run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_81ddacf6dccee860355778f6a757edaf) verified tree `a526a6fb09d0f0bce1c85d2a3f2e38f0fe73de33` before running tests. Independent P0–P2 Codex autoreview of `07610fc6348` against `bd67a3f9a18` found no actionable findings in the supplied static review scope; `git diff --check` passed.
- The [pre-refresh CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44268778221) on `55f66bba1c6` passed the required gate, build artifacts, production types, and `check-lint-core-5`. The PR itself has not been merged into `main`.
- The earlier [AWS proof run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_41a4959c0545f270058daff7d98c3c01) passed seven worker Goal RPC tests and 71 recorder/runtime/prompt-stability tests. Both review defects were reproduced before correction through the public RPC path. Blocked Start and Resume now preserve Goal state without replaying a successful receipt, and the simulated unpinned implicit-runtime worker case passes.
- Earlier touched-file formatting, `git diff --check`, line-cap and test-budget checks passed (+320 test lines / 400 allowance). No baseline exception or weakened behavioral assertion was added.

**Proof limitations:** Gateway RPC, SQLite, queue ownership and worker admission are real in the focused AWS tests; worker transport and inference are simulated in those tests. The separate live Azure run had the failure and unrun case above. Upgrade proof was not run.

<details>
<summary>Validation provenance and retained failure evidence</summary>

- Incoming head `fba536ef71b` passed **66/66** Goal cases in isolated AWS run `run_549134cf99b8dbe6e387ea3d7d6452f5`.
- A corrected-suite run passed **69/70** before the implicit-runtime fixture received synthetic auth. The remaining failure was fixture auth setup. After that correction all seven worker cases passed on focused tree `21807b430e96bd7e5560df007e0e202593d7332c`; this was not an exact-SHA run of later fixture changes.
- The original correction and the CI fixture repair received independent P0–P2 static review with no actionable findings. CI at `e29da7a951c` failed on three PR-caused fixture lint errors, fixed in `55f66bba1c6`. The old failed run was not rerun or relabeled green.
- Standalone package declaration build failed on both the unmodified incoming source and the correction due to six nonexported types in unchanged `hook-model.types.ts` and `plugin-metrics.ts`. Local full typechecks and lint boundary preparation encountered the same diagnostics; a broad dead-export scan reported untouched paths. [Retained baseline reproduction and changed-check run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0e1590525e4d25f537239ce61cae0811). These results are distinct from the successful build/type/lint checks on `55f66bba1c6`.
- The original author's first run passed 65 tests and failed `keeps pursuing after an owner's silent exec completion`: expected `Exec completed` but received an automatic Goal nudge. Bounded first-15-case replays passed on base (111 seconds) and candidate (99 seconds). This remains unclassified; later passing runs are not a claimed repair.
- Refresh proof used an isolated, no-hydration AWS Crabbox lease, pinned Node/pnpm, and the exact candidate tree. Ran `chat-steer-now-handler.test.ts`, `sessions-steer-active.test.ts`, and the OpenClaw/Codex worker cases of `server.chat-goal.test.ts`. The lease was released.

</details>

prs.title: feat: prepare restricted connections for Session Share steering
prs.body:
Supersedes #201173. Builds on #202397.

## What Problem This Solves

A remote publication integration needs a narrowly scoped transport for steering, without granting its device a human identity or general chat/admin access. A genuine person also needs to discover the exact active backend before submitting an active-only correction.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can opt into a restricted, signed-device writer transport. It only admits `session-share.steer.target` and `session-share.steer.send` when the Session Share plugin registers those handlers with the matching scope. This PR does not implement those source handlers or enable any live configuration.

`gateway.sessionControl.publicationWriteEnabled` defaults off. Each new request, including retries, passes admission; disabling denies new requests but does not revoke admitted work. Work admitted immediately before disable may still deliver. `gateway.sessionControl.steeringEnabled` separately gates genuine-person host target discovery and active steering. Publication reader access remains independent and its current epoch behavior is deliberately unchanged for a separate correction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared transport owner preserves signed singleton device tokens, exact plugin/method ownership, minimal hello/tick disclosure, current device grants, and no human fallback. `sessions.steerTarget` uses the same personal session-write authority and physical controller as `sessions.steerActive`. Discovery does not inject input; replacement, idle and unsupported backends cannot become implicit new runs. Accepted/indeterminate steering retains the original message ID; retries reconcile, never replay under a new key.

Writer and steering revocation-generation machinery and obsolete writer off/on test variants are absent. Reader-only revocation tests remain with the unchanged reader contract. The keyless transformed-text retry test no longer repeats the same active-steer branch for pending/transcript labels. Existing signed-WSS, token rotation/revocation, target and receipt tests cover distinct boundaries.

## Evidence

- 107 focused tests passed: 104 Gateway/steering/retry/rotation tests and 3 schema tests. Two intentional reader-only skips; no writer revocation variants retained.
- Both affected typecheck lanes passed (`gateway-methods`, `gateway-server`), as did typed lint across 31 files, formatting, and both runtime/Madge cycle checks (zero cycles).
- Gateway suite: 412.68s, including cold fixture compilation; schema suite: 2.23s. The signed transport suite protects real handshake, scope and token-lifecycle boundaries that a mocked helper cannot cover. CI timing is not yet available.
- All 12 baseline ratchets passed, including lifetime checks and the test-line budget.
- Against main `599bc4222a48594445c7d531c063be828be3482a`: production +326/-147 (net +179, excluding generated artifacts); tests +747/-434 (net +313), below the 400-line allowance, with no new allocation. Production growth is the restricted transport integration and exact-backend discovery; the existing publication owner file was retained and expanded rather than duplicated or renamed. The first ratchet run flagged the rename as a new per-file lifetime check; retaining the owner preserves the unchanged device check without a rule exception.
- Local source `818804675b9d75ea2f34f573ebc45610edceb48d`, tree `d0110418a2e7992bd2874f7f5863a8d238a93ca5`. A new regression tests disabled admission through an existing signed socket. The earlier gate implementation was not rerun with this new test; no new red/green baseline claim.

Sibling Codex inspected at `4b0d9669cc46ba97bf85fa6312431b630d80498d`: `turn_processor.rs` validates the expected turn and handles non-submission; `codex_thread.rs` makes a started turn unreachable in steer mode. OpenClaw's acknowledgment-versus-consumption and uncertain accepted-custody behavior remains unchanged.

Limits: local synthetic Gateway/device fixtures are not live native-model delivery, full release/build proof, hosted CI, or Mac exact-head review. No merge is requested here; fresh Mac review and CI remain required. No Swift changes or live configuration, enablement, deployment or restart.

prs.title: improve: avoid repeated history scans before replies in long chats
prs.body:
Related: #185111

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: repeated history scans before replies in long SQLite chats. Demonstrated with Codex: recording the accepted prompt invalidates the history index, forcing another full scan before the next reply even though the conversation's structure has not changed.

## User Impact

User impact: later replies can reuse the history index instead of scanning the entire saved conversation again. In the 200,003-event Gateway proof, the second and third reads examined 325 and 327 navigation rows instead of about 200,000.

**The first uncached read is still slow.** Restarting the Gateway or genuinely changing the history can require another full scan. This addresses repeated scans between replies, not all of #185111. No settings, database format, or upgrade action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing navigation index when a canonical user-message rewrite changes only private `__openclaw` metadata. Continue rotating the normal transcript generation, refreshing changed page sizes, and reading selected message payloads afresh. Real edits, replacements and copied histories still invalidate navigation; a read from an older SQLite snapshot cannot certify the next read's index. PostgreSQL retains its existing generation-based reuse.

When account usage and chat history share the agent database, updating usage also invalidates the history index. This PR prevents that unrelated invalidation while the existing auth receipt still refreshes account usage/health. Credential and shared-state writes retain their existing behavior.

Most of the diff in `session-accessor.sqlite-model-context.ts` is re-indentation; view it with whitespace hidden.

This complements #190615, which removes unnecessary additional history reads within a reply. It neither includes nor depends on that PR.

## Evidence

### Full-product repro on main

A built Gateway, native Codex app-server and QA channel processed three incoming messages against a seeded 200,003-event conversation. On main `b03fd2fed06`, the Gateway returned all three expected answers but scanned the entire archive before every turn:

```text
navigation rows: 200003 / 200005 / 200007
history read ms: 8452 / 7791 / 7694
```

### Live Gateway run: isolating the two causes

The same workload on `059db8a7c5a` shows why both corrections belong together:

| Change applied | First navigation read | Second | Third |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| History correction alone | 200,003 | 200,005 | 200,007 |
| Auth correction alone | 200,003 | 200,005 | 200,007 |
| Both corrections | 200,003 | 325 | 327 |

Captured combined-candidate summary:

```json
{
  "scannedRows": [200003, 325, 327],
  "historyMs": [5226, 528, 421],
  "messages": [3208, 3214, 3216]
}
```

With both, whole-history reads took 5,226 / 528 / 421 ms. All three answers were correct; selected message counts remained 3,208 / 3,214 / 3,216. Actual auth usage writes ran on every turn without clearing the history index. These are single-run timing observations, not a statistical speedup claim; work counts are the acceptance measure.

Proof artifice: synthetic saved history, temporary count/timing instrumentation, and a local scripted model with a declared 1,048,576-token capacity to avoid fixture-induced fallback. Built-in context handling was used; this is not a real-provider or Lossless Claw qualification.

### Regression and compatibility checks

The permanent tests cover bounded navigation work after prompt recording, fresh content after edits/replacement, an older read snapshot followed by a committed write, and auth-state freshness without unrelated history invalidation. Test lines are net +234 against `main`: reuses the existing model-context fixture (one case now also wraps the write-receipt reader to commit a rewrite mid-rebuild) and agent/shared-state table to protect distinct navigation-work, read-snapshot and auth-publication contracts; no permanent Gateway harness is added. The navigation-work and auth-scope assertions fail on unpatched code; the snapshot test also rejects the unsafe candidate that omitted the read-lifetime guard. Each remaining case was rerun on 20 Nov with its guarded code removed and fails (fix removed: 1,101 rows scanned against the 512 bound; receipt comparison removed: the stale parent returns; final currency check removed: the next read scans nothing).

Earlier validation on `059db8a7c5a` passed 8 real PostgreSQL tests and exact returned-history/error comparisons across byte/event limits. The existing PostgreSQL inline-auth startup probe also fails on main with a missing `openclaw_engine_anchor`; the separate admitted-owner PostgreSQL tests passed. No schema or stored transcript bytes are changed by this optimization.

## What Problem This Solves

The automation audit found three unused options: sending model reasoning with a result, sending a second copy of a chat result to a webhook, and copying recent chat into a new reminder. The last option duplicates what the `current` run style already provides.

## User Impact

The automation editor no longer shows **Include reasoning**. The corresponding CLI switches and API field are gone, as are the secondary webhook destination and the automations tool's `contextMessages` option. Model thinking settings, primary webhook delivery, failure alerts, and the `current` run style are unchanged.

`openclaw doctor --fix` backs up cron state before rewriting saved jobs. It removes the reasoning flag silently. It removes secondary webhook settings and reports the job and webhook host, not the full URL. An enabled job that would have sent to both chat and a webhook is paused with an explanation; its primary route stays configured. Review that route before re-enabling the job. Doctor does not delete these jobs or rewrite any existing reminder text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removing these paths keeps automation setup and delivery simpler without changing the supported single-destination routes. prs.title: improve: remove the On exit automation schedule
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A one-time wait for a command to finish did not need a saved automation. The On exit schedule added re-enable and restart behavior on top of a wait that a conversation can already handle directly.

## User Impact

On exit is no longer a schedule choice or filter in Control UI, and the API, CLI, and agent tool no longer accept it. For a new one-time wait, run a background command in the conversation and let its exit wake that conversation.

For existing jobs, Doctor backs up cron state before pausing the jobs and retains the original definitions in the cron recovery store. Existing run history is left intact. Doctor reports why the jobs were paused and what to use instead. It does not convert the jobs or rerun their commands, which could repeat side effects.

## Why This Change Was Made

There is no safe automatic conversion that preserves an existing one-time wait. This change removes the dedicated process watcher and its re-enable and cleanup states while keeping ordinary background command wakes independent of the scheduler. This may overlap sibling automations cleanups in the schedule schema, CLI and agent tool, Control UI forms and filters, and Doctor's cron repair path.

## Evidence

The bundled Control UI was exercised in Chromium with a mock Gateway and realistic inventory jobs. The Schedule filter no longer lists On exit; the other schedule choices remain. The Doctor migration regression passed and verified the backup, retained definition, unchanged run history, and repeat repair. All 93 protocol tests passed. Core and UI typechecks, changed-file lint and formatting, and the generated Gateway validator check were run. Full CI, a native Android build, and a live upgrade from stable were not run locally.

prs.title: refactor: use task prompts for scheduled reminders
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduling a reminder in an existing conversation shouldn’t require a special action just for the agent’s main conversation. The editor, CLI, and agent tool offered two ways to schedule that work, with different delivery and execution rules.

## User Impact

Use an agent task with `session:<key>` to continue an existing conversation, including the main conversation. Control UI no longer offers **Post to main session** or **Runs in: Main session**. CLI scripts should replace `--system-event` and `--session main` with `--message` and the actual conversation key, for example `--session session:agent:main:main` or `--session session:global` on a global-scope install.

After upgrading, run `openclaw doctor --fix`. Doctor backs up cron state and reports each conversion. It rewrites eligible jobs in place, retaining their ID, schedule, enabled state, run history, scratch, and valid delivery settings. The target is the owning agent’s main conversation, with `session:global` for global scope. If Doctor cannot faithfully continue a job (for example, a headless script that used the old main-session notification behavior, a missing prompt, or an unresolved owner), it pauses the job and explains what to review before enabling it. The model now sees the reminder as a **task prompt**, not as a system notice.

## Why This Change Was Made

An explicit conversation key uses the same queue and execution path regardless of which conversation it names. Immediate hook wakes, channel join and lifecycle notices, and post-run notices from scheduled plugin commands still use the internal notice path where applicable: they report an event to the conversation, rather than being user-authored automation prompts. Backup schedules already run an isolated command and do not need the removed mode.

Expected overlap with the sibling automation cleanups: the shared cron schema and generated validators, Doctor’s cron repair, scheduler routing, CLI and agent tool descriptions, and the Control UI editor and docs. This change does not redesign the remaining modes or wake policy.

## Evidence

- Doctor’s SQLite repair tests passed for a named agent with a custom main key and for global scope (2 tests). They cover backup creation, preserved job ID, disabled state, schedule, last-run state, delivery, prompt, and a no-op second repair.
- Cron protocol validation passed (93 tests); generated-validator parity, core and UI typechecks, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. The focused CLI run was interrupted by a source change while the subprocess compiler was building; the full CLI, scheduler, native client, and upgrade suites were not verified here.
- Local Codex autoreview (P1, three passes) found that same-kind payload edits had lost their field updates. The update logic was restored; the follow-up core typecheck passed. The final delta was not independently re-reviewed.
- The real Control UI was exercised in Chromium with a mocked Gateway and a fictional weekly garden-inventory reminder. Both capture checks passed. The before capture used the original worktree UI source, which matched `origin/main` outside translation artifacts. The captures show the Action picker; no live model or channel delivery is demonstrated.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

“Now / Next heartbeat” looked like it controlled when an automation would run. In practice, both choices ran the job when its schedule came due. The setting gave people a choice that did nothing.

## User Impact

**User impact:** Set an automation’s timing with its schedule. The Android editor no longer offers Wake mode, and automation create/edit commands and API requests no longer accept `--wake` or `wakeMode`. The current web editor already didn’t render the picker; this removes its leftover data handling and fixtures.

On upgrade, or with `openclaw doctor --fix`, Doctor backs up stored cron state and silently removes the old job field. It does not delete, pause, or reschedule jobs, change what they do, or reset their run state. Current approval references are carried forward; stale ones stay stale.

## Why This Change Was Made

A separate agent `automations` wake action can still send an immediate notice to a session. It has no timing selector: the previous default already sent immediately for a targeted session. Use a one-off automation for a later follow-up. The `next-heartbeat` **script result** is different: it can attach a notice to a real upcoming scheduled run, so it still works and is documented separately. The inbound `/hooks/wake` endpoint, hook mapping wake modes, and `openclaw system` are unchanged and can be reviewed separately.

This shares automation form data, Gateway job contracts, Doctor cron repair files, and generated validators or tool snapshots with the parallel automation cleanup PRs. The changes here are limited to Wake mode. The migration scans existing cron definitions and rewrites only affected jobs after one backup; it does not rewrite run history. Largest-deployment upgrade cost was not measured.

- Focused Gateway, agent tool, scheduler, Doctor, and editor assertions passed. prs.title: feat: switch sessions with Command-1–9 and Control-Tab in the desktop apps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Switching conversations needs the mouse, or Command-K and typing part of a name. With several sessions running at once, this is the most frequent navigation in the app, and the desktop apps have no direct key for it, unlike Slack, Linear, or browser tabs.

## User Impact

User impact: in the macOS app and the other desktop apps, Command-1 through Command-8 (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) open that session in the sidebar, and Command-9 opens the last one. Control-Tab goes back to the session you were in before; hold Control and press Tab again to go further back, or add Shift to go the other way.

**Changed default:** in the macOS app's Gateway menu and the web identity menu's Gateway picker, Gateway shortcuts move from Command-1–9 to Control-Command-1–9 (Control-Option-Command for a new window), so Command-1–9 can open sessions.

Web browsers keep both chords for their own tabs, so nothing changes in a browser tab.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar owns the visible order (pinned, groups, expanded children, then the rest, minus collapsed sections and catalog sessions), so the sidebar handles the keys and opens sessions through its normal row navigation. The keys are bound only when the page runs in a desktop host (`isNativeWebChromeHost()`), the same split New Session already uses for Command-N. They work from the composer, ignore key repeat and text composition, and leave open dialogs alone.

Control-Tab walks a most-recently-used list of up to 20 sessions opened in this window. Holding Control freezes that order for the walk, as app switchers do; releasing Control makes the session you stopped on the most recent one. Sessions that can no longer be opened are skipped. Before a second session has been opened, Control-Tab moves to the next sidebar row.

In the macOS app the Dashboard web view sees key equivalents before the main menu, so the page claims Command-1–9 and the Gateway menu items move to Control-Command so both keep working. The shortcuts dialog lists the new keys in desktop apps only.

Related: #182559 (jump to the next session waiting for you) is navigation by state; this is navigation by position and recency.

## Evidence

Keyboard shortcuts dialog (Command-/), Sidebar section, in the Control UI with the macOS desktop host emulated by the existing `installNativeWebChrome` fixture, Chromium at 1440×900 and 2×, synthetic sessions. Before is `main` at 39250610246, after is this branch.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the Sidebar section lists only the multi-select click chords](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4477ce9-c0c5-49eb-a12a-1db31d1040ee) | ![After: the Sidebar section also lists Command 1–9 to open a sidebar session and Control-Tab to switch to a recent session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2509f99d-4377-4b30-9c1f-67ce31430537) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Sidebar rows outlined: no session switching keys](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb598459-6395-4cfb-bb27-5b64c6add9ff) | ![New rows outlined: session switching keys, desktop app only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13027694-19eb-4800-b49c-ed7bca1c7b7e) |

- **E2E** `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-session-shortcuts.e2e.test.ts`: with the desktop host emulated and focus in the composer, Command-3, Command-9 and Command-2 open the third, last and second sessions; Control-Tab returns to the previous one and back; holding Control and pressing Tab twice walks two back, and releasing Control keeps that session; Control-Shift-Tab walks the other way. A second case checks that a plain browser page leaves Command-2 unclaimed and ignores Control-Tab. Passes.
- **Unit** `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-shortcuts.test.ts` (13 tests): position targets and Command-9, the held-Control walk and its final promotion, skipped unavailable sessions, the 20-session bound, AZERTY-style digit keys, repeat/modifier/composition/browser/modal guards, the next-row fallback, and listener removal. `app-sidebar-native-gateways.test.ts` now expects the Control-Command hints. Both pass.
- **Checks**: `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` pass.

Not verified: the macOS app itself. The two Swift edits only change the Gateway menu items' modifier masks and the native card's hint text, and were not built locally; macOS CI covers the build. The claim that the Dashboard web view sees Command-digits before the menu comes from WebKit's `WebViewImpl::performKeyEquivalent`, which hands key equivalents to the page first when the web view is first responder and passes them on to the menu only if the page leaves them unhandled. The Dashboard's own Command-W handling relies on the same order.

prs.title: fix: keep chats at the latest message after switching back in the Mac app and Safari
prs.body:
Related: #159857 (closed as stale, same symptom)

## What Problem This Solves

In the macOS app and Safari, switching to another chat and back often leaves the chat a little above its latest message, with the last lines behind the composer. If a reply arrives while you are in the other chat, it stays out of view, and the chat stops following new replies until you scroll down yourself. Chrome is not affected.

## User Impact

User impact: a chat you left at the bottom opens at its latest message when you come back, including replies that arrived while you were away. A chat you left scrolled up comes back at the same place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recently opened chats stay mounted, and the hidden ones use `content-visibility: hidden`. When WebKit hides a pane, it moves that transcript's scroll position up (19 to 42 px in the test fixtures) and fires a scroll event. The chat read that event as the reader scrolling up, so it saved a reading position above the end and turned off end-follow. Coming back restored that position, and replies that landed meanwhile did not pull the view down.

A hidden pane now ignores its own scroll events, because it has no reader; the saved position and follow state stay as the reader left them. When a retained pane is shown again, it goes back to that saved position (the end, or the reader's scrolled-up offset), because WebKit's movement stays in the hidden DOM. Only settled retained transcripts are corrected; a newly built pane keeps its existing first placement.

The macOS app's default Web experience renders the Gateway's Control UI, so the fix reaches the app through the Gateway; no app change is needed.

## Evidence

Scenario: open Alpha at its end, switch to Bravo, back to Alpha, then to Charlie. A reply lands in Alpha while Charlie is open; switch back to Alpha. Playwright WebKit 27.2 on Linux at 1512×921 (the app's default window) and 2×, with the macOS app's web chrome emulated by the existing `installNativeWebChrome` fixture and synthetic long chats. Before is `main` at 39250610246, after is this branch.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: back in Alpha, the last answer is cut off behind the composer and the reply that arrived meanwhile is out of view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60fbf8b1-5911-48c9-8f43-dcef24683916) | ![After: back in Alpha, the reply that arrived meanwhile is the last message, right above the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f78b3e0-6209-4314-b0a4-4810088f3c67) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Cut-off answer outlined: the latest reply is hidden below, 114 px above the end](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d210ee2-da58-4950-a2e7-8cf42bafecb2) | ![Late reply outlined: the latest reply is in view at the end](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c75bfb9-7d4e-421f-b101-d653f3a564e3) |

- **New E2E test** `ui/src/e2e/chat-session-switch-scroll.e2e.test.ts`, in Chromium and WebKit: six switches (retained panes, and one rebuilt after three other chats), a reply that lands in the background, and a reader who scrolled up and comes back to the same offset. On `main`, Chromium passes and WebKit fails at the first return: `Bravo -> Alpha: expected 42 to be less than or equal to 8`. With this change both pass.
- **Measured landings in WebKit**, `main` → this branch: returning to Alpha 42 px above the end → 0; returning after the background reply 114 px above the end with the reply out of view → 0 with the reply in view.
- **Cause trace on `main`** (instrumented run, not part of the PR): while Alpha's pane is hidden there is no script `scrollTop` write or `scrollTo`/`scroll`/`scrollBy` call on its transcript; the only change is a native scroll event 56 ms after the pane loses `chat-pane-cache__pane--visible`, 41 px above where the reader left it.
- **Checks**: `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files pass.

Not tested: the macOS app's own WKWebView (this used Playwright's WebKit build), iOS/iPadOS Safari, and split view.

prs.title: fix(update): keep protected files out of SQLite backup inspection
prs.body:
Related: #201251

Thanks to @eliavb43 for the detailed report and measurements.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

## What Problem This Solves

The pre-update recovery capture (and Doctor's "Preserve original state") passes every regular file in the protected roots to the shared database backup launcher as an additional file. Those paths are sized, listed for the SQLite inspection worker and given the per-database allowance (300 s plus a size term) each, even though the backup child later discards non-databases by header. With ~3,000 small WhatsApp credential files this produces thousands of misleading "SQLite state schema inspection … budget 301 seconds" lines and a worker allowance summed over every file.

## User Impact

Updates and Doctor size and budget SQLite inspection from the databases they actually capture. Ordinary protected files still go through the existing plain-file payload copy, sync, digest and manifest, and the recovery reader still checks every file's size and SHA-256.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared backup launcher now classifies unknown candidate paths with the existing isolated SQLite header probe (a separate process, so the updater's POSIX locks are preserved) and admits only recognized databases to sizing and backup; duplicate path spellings no longer add allowances. Declared and discovered databases keep their admission, missing-source and verification behavior.

This does not explain the full 98-minute window in the report: the slow baseline capture and activation snapshot timings come from different spans and need per-stage measurement first. The source-level analysis and a concrete instrumentation follow-up are left on #201251.

## Evidence

- New regression in `src/infra/doctor-capture-reuse.test.ts`: on base the production capture passes 29 entries to the backup worker; with the fix it passes exactly the 3 databases with a 903-second allowance. The recovery verifier accepts the capture, the header-identified database keeps its row, and all 24 synthetic JSON payloads match their original bytes.
- Focused backup, Doctor capture and recovery-reader suites pass; formatting, focused lint and `git diff --check` pass.
- Gap: no latest-stable installed-upgrade run or WSL2 timing yet.

prs.title: feat(ui): switch failed chats to an available same-provider default

## What Problem This Solves

After a failed chat on an explicitly selected alternate model, switching back to an available same-provider configured default requires finding it in the model picker.

## User Impact

Control UI offers **Switch to configured default** for eligible failed chats. The action changes the model for the next message; it does not retry the failed message, resend the original prompt, or alter completed tool work. Existing confirmation preferences still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action uses the existing selection and session-patch owners, preserves pinned runtime/auth choices, and rejects stale selections, sessions, failures, connections, agent inventories, locks, permissions, or unavailable targets. It only offers catalog-confirmed available models on the exact same provider.
