prs.title: fix: Doctor no longer recommends restore when snapshot storage is full
prs.body:
Closes #200604

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor tells operators to restore their database from backup when a disposable inspection snapshot runs out of disk space. The failed copy does not establish database corruption. Following that advice can discard newer history unnecessarily.

## User Impact

Operators get free-space/quota retry advice for classified snapshot-capacity failures. Doctor and deep Gateway status still refuse unverified readiness. Corruption, source-open errors, unresolved cleanup, ownership and schema guards retain their existing behavior. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot worker already preserves a typed capacity failure. Final readiness ignored it; early Doctor, lease diagnosis and deep status discarded it while converting the report to text. Carry the original failure from the existing inspection-owned WeakMap into the existing formatter and reuse the capacity classifier. Keep report rows serializable and preserve the Doctor error class.

This does not duplicate #199689 (implicit Linux TMPDIR), #192699 (optional Memory Core inspection), or #176779 (contention guidance). It changes no snapshot placement, service environment, backup, rollback or admission policy.

## Evidence

Actual Linux filesystem proof uses a private 1 MiB tmpfs, a synthetic 4 MiB SQLite/WAL database, the real snapshot worker and the built CLI. No filesystem mocks, production data or service changes.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unchanged-base readiness reproduction | Real ENOSPC, source family unchanged, incorrect restore advice |
| Regression before each repair | Final-readiness capacity cases: 2 failed / 2 controls passed; early Doctor: capacity failed / corruption passed |
| Fixed built `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | Exit 1 as required; correct retry advice; no restore advice; config/database/WAL/SHM bytes unchanged |
| Owner and consumer tests | 149 passed across five files: 25 readiness, 55 status, 69 Doctor/maintenance |
| Build and checks | `qaRuntime` build passed; four typecheck lanes, targeted typed lint, format, whitespace and both Knip unused-file scans passed (zero entries) |

Final CLI capture:

```json
{"exit":1,"enospc":true,"sourceAndConfigPreserved":true,"recommendsRestore":false,"correctGuidance":true}
```

Coverage includes direct ENOSPC, worker-hydrated EDQUOT, contention, corruption, raw source-open ENOSPC, cleanup aggregates and mixed-agent advice. Existing lease, recovery-settlement and status tests pass.

Independent Codex subagent review covered the complete final diff against `8f223d9d5860bacf0c0f51357cf9148cdfcadf82`, producer/worker transport and sibling consumers: no P0–P3 product findings. Its two missing-export fixture findings were fixed and the affected suites rerun. Original product-reviewed diff SHA-256: `289915964303c502063752b9b410822e7f4d5cc1cfbf08b646e12fdf4e3e20a0`. The standalone local autoreview helper was unavailable; this is an independent subagent review, not a local ClawSweeper result.

Simplification: reuse the existing cause store, classifier and formatter; no new state or framework. Production +33/−8 (net +25); tests/support +123/−27 (net +96). Growth carries the cause across three consumers and checks distinct entry points.

**Limits:** the stable-to-candidate source transition required update repair after its activation deadline; it was not an uninterrupted successful update. No complete published-package upgrade or native systemd recovery was run. Package archive validation failed on missing runtime worker-loader references, including after a full build. This proves the diagnostic correction after a real stable-to-candidate transition and repair, not recovery from every ENOSPC update failure. Maintainer approval admitted CI run 44094011555 attempt 2. Its baseline-ratchet job identified two stale closed-mock entries after the fixtures switched to real-export pass-through. The follow-up repair uses `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --prune` to remove exactly those entries (6213 → 6211), preserving all runtime code and tests. The focused check reproduced the failure before pruning and passed afterward without `--prune`; whitespace validation and fresh independent review passed. Required exact-head CI after publication remains pending. ClawSweeper’s earlier product review found no actionable findings; the prior product and real-filesystem proof below remains applicable because only this generated baseline metadata changed.

### Follow-up: real latest-stable transition and recovery

Resolved npm `latest` to **2026.11.5** and installed it into an independent prefix, home, cache, config, state, workspace and temporary root. Stable Doctor completed with exit 0. Seeded synthetic retained history in its real shared database and captured gateway mode/port/bind, workspace and plugin settings. No production state, credentials or services were used.

Ran the real stable updater through its source-checkout route, pinning the candidate to `e2d3c18cd7ceae0c974545681ae39dae4f5efd27`. The candidate retains the checkout's **2026.11.4 version label**; no version metadata was changed. Candidate preflight ran Doctor, lint, configuration/plugin/recovery checks and a disposable Gateway startup. The candidate activated, but the overall update hit its **600-second deadline** and returned exit 1 (`update-activation-timeout`), with recovery pending. This is not reported as a clean update.

The activated candidate's supported `update repair --no-restart --yes --json --timeout 180` then returned **exit 0**, `status: warning`, `coreUpdate: completed`, and reconciled the timed-out run. Error-level Doctor lint returned exit 0 with no findings. Warnings concerned deliberately disabled plugins/model tooling in the synthetic fixture and deferred agent-path repair. No service restart was requested.

After repair, the actual installed CLI reported `OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (e2d3c18)`. Repeated the capacity failure on that same upgraded state with live WAL and a private 1 MiB tmpfs:

```json
{"exit":1,"enospc":true,"correctGuidance":true,"restoreAdvice":false,"databaseWalAndConfigBytesPreserved":true,"shmCoordinationBytesChanged":true,"stableHistoryAndSettingsPreserved":true}
```

The database, WAL and configuration bytes stayed identical during the failed inspection; the stable history row and captured settings also remained intact. SQLite's transient SHM coordination bytes changed, so this upgraded-state capture does **not** claim SHM byte preservation. The original fresh-fixture capture above remains separate evidence.

Full source build also passed in **4m 20.2s**. Both QA-build packaging and full-build packaging failed the repository archive validator on missing `runtime-worker-loader.mjs` references; no invalid archive was installed and no validator was bypassed. The source update was the alternate proof route. No product code changed during this follow-up; head and working tree remain unchanged/clean.

Exact transition commands, within the isolated environment:

```sh
OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR="$SOURCE" \
OPENCLAW_UPDATE_DEV_TARGET_REF=e2d3c18cd7ceae0c974545681ae39dae4f5efd27 \
openclaw update --channel dev --no-restart --yes --json --timeout 600
# exit 1: activated candidate, then update-activation-timeout
openclaw update repair --no-restart --yes --json --timeout 180
# exit 0: warning, coreUpdate completed; error-level Doctor lint clean
```

CONTRIBUTING and the PR template were fetched in full and rechecked before this update: unchanged blobs `c512054589531fd1e1d9f3c8a39965f7675f69c4` and `7c6ec91e869fd0ee6bdcb5e3f7e3124d03b8277b`. Current upstream observed: `5230147ebfe95e1717987f1f82e18280829614eb`. Current root instructions, review flow and the applicable update contract were rechecked. The earlier workflow admission block was resolved by maintainer approval; required CI is tracked on the repaired head.

<details>
<summary>Commands, timing and contribution requirements</summary>

Base: `8f223d9d5860bacf0c0f51357cf9148cdfcadf82`. Node 26.13.1; pinned project pnpm and Bun test runtime. Own checkout, physical dependencies, build, home, config, state, caches and workspace.

```sh
pnpm test src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# 25 passed; final owner shard 64.97s (includes cold preparation)
pnpm test src/commands/doctor-database-preflight.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-maintenance.agent-lease-wait.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-maintenance.settlement.test.ts \
```

prs.title: fix: repair PostgreSQL session keys with boards
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Repairing a session key with a board fails on PostgreSQL with `column reference "revision" is ambiguous`. Qualify the destination columns in the shared artifact upserts so normal session-key replacement and Doctor can finish.

## User Impact

Session-key repair keeps boards, progress cards, and heartbeat outcomes under the canonical key. Existing revision and timestamp precedence stays unchanged. No schema, configuration, permission, retention, or durability change is needed.

## Root Cause

`copySessionNodeArtifactsForRepair` compares bare `revision`, `updated_at`, and `occurred_at` columns inside `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE`. PostgreSQL exposes both the target row and `excluded` there, so these references are ambiguous even when the destination row does not exist. Ten target-column qualifications cover tabs, widgets, progress cards, and heartbeat outcomes.

On baseline `3587df70a233dc639b733b9169797d3abd138301`, the real runtime replacement entry point and Doctor repair both fail with SQLSTATE `42702`; the same two SQLite cases pass. The regression uses a disposable PostgreSQL 18.7 UTF8 database with socket-only connections and synthetic session state.

## Real behavior proof

Command, with a disposable database URL substituted for `$TEST_DSN`:

```sh
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TEST_DSN" -- src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-lifecycle-artifacts.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

After the fix:

```text
sqlite: runtime session-key replacement PASS
sqlite: Doctor artifact repair PASS
postgres: runtime session-key replacement PASS
postgres: Doctor artifact repair PASS
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 5 passed (5)
```

The runtime case asserts the board moved and the alias disappeared. Doctor exercises missing, older, newer, and equal-revision destinations, timestamp ties, heartbeat run-key remapping, and an idempotent second repair. Assertions read persisted rows through the real database owner. The regression extends the existing artifact conformance suite in its host-broker fork lane. The original cleanup case also passes.

### Stable-created data and packaged Doctor attempt

Built latest stable [v2026.11.5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.5) at `e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff` with its frozen dependencies. Its real database owner created two synthetic session nodes plus source/destination rows for all four artifact types. Captured PostgreSQL and local-anchor backups and verified both inventories before updating the same isolated state to this fixed build with its own frozen dependencies. Builds used the `cliStartup` profile.

Ran the packaged entry point in an isolated HOME/state/config, with plugins disabled, external service ownership, activation disabled, no reachable user bus, and no model credentials:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions
```

Observed exit 1 before canonical-key repair:

```text
Doctor: relative session store
Doctor: Config repairs
Doctor: maintenance finish
Doctor could not complete maintenance.
non-canonical persisted row resolves to session key agent:main:matrix:channel:!Upgrade:example.org; stop the Gateway and run openclaw doctor --fix
```

Independent PostgreSQL reads and recursive comparison of original config fields afterward confirmed:

```text
board_tabs: original source and destination payloads preserved
board_widgets: original source and destination payloads preserved
session_progress_cards: original source and destination payloads preserved
heartbeat_outcomes: original source and destination payloads preserved
PASS: all original config values, session nodes, and four artifact types survived
```

This proves persisted-data survival through the code upgrade and refused maintenance attempt, **not successful packaged Doctor key repair**. The separate canonical-row admission guard is unchanged and remains a proof blocker for that entry point. Initial clean-environment setup needed an explicit disposable database role and private temp-directory permissions; these were corrected before the reported CLI attempt. No older code ran on upgraded state, and no service was changed.

## What was not tested

No production state, live channels, paid models, or running Gateway were used. The owner tests invoke Doctor’s production repair owner and offline maintenance lock directly. A separate packaged-CLI stable-state upgrade attempt reached a different canonical-row guard before that repair and exited 1; successful full-CLI key repair remains unproven (details in "Stable-created data and packaged Doctor attempt" above). A successful before/after latency benchmark is unavailable because the baseline operation fails; test durations are not a performance comparison. Full package declaration/release builds were not run.

## Verification

- Consolidated artifact conformance suite: 5/5 pass (three PostgreSQL cases, two SQLite controls). The four repair regressions previously produced 2 PostgreSQL failures (`42702`) and 2 SQLite passes on baseline; their behavior is unchanged by the test relocation. Final file duration 15.22 seconds; runner wall time 61.25 seconds including compiled-worker preparation. Hosted CI reported 15.70 seconds of test-body time across the five cases; its owning shard passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44539997718/job/135616652486.
- Existing consumers: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-session-canonical-keys.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 63 tests pass, two shards, 96.60 seconds runner wall time.
- Targeted format and lint pass for both changed files; `git diff --check` passes.
- Production typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental`: pass.
- Test typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --incremental`: pass. The earlier Doctor test shard also passed before consolidation.
- CLI build: `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u OPENAI_API_KEY node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`: pass in 1m 16s.

## Evidence

Simplification pass: ten column qualifications in the existing owner and regression coverage in its existing artifact conformance suite. No new production helper, fallback, state, migration, or query was added. The final candidate is committed as `f371678866817e42c2032d465f937966bbf01f81`, based on `3587df70a233dc639b733b9169797d3abd138301`. Production delta: 10 substitutions; existing test suite: 196 insertions and 2 deletions. No new file or routing entry remains.

Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. Autoreview was attempted on the original complete candidate at P0–P2 with model/provider fallback disabled. The production change is identical; regression placement changed afterward. It produced no assessment: its isolated runtime could not start the configured shared Codex launcher. This is an unresolved local-review gap, not a clean review. The original-head hosted review found no code defects but requested packaged-entry-point and stable-state proof. One final-head re-review was requested: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201857#issuecomment-7011415685. It completed with no findings and marked the patch ready for maintainer review: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201857#issuecomment-7011379278. It noted the product-flow proof gap; the later stable-state attempt and its explicit CLI blocker are recorded above. Independent maintainer review is still required before merge.

Earlier local setup attempts used an ASCII test database, the wrong fixture write path, and an unhosted worker lane. Those failures did not reach the defect. The UTF8 database, matching physical write path, CLI admission, and existing host-broker fork lane produced the reported baseline and after-fix results. The initial PR CI found an introduced capacity failure: the extra test file/host-lane entry made the scheduled inventory exceed 77 jobs (78 planned). This was reproduced locally, then fixed by moving the same regressions into the existing artifact conformance suite and removing both additions. All four capacity cases now pass, and the full planner suite passes 174/174 tests (100.02 seconds runner wall time). No CI limits, packing rules, or test expectations changed. Consolidated PostgreSQL/SQLite proof, targeted lint/format, and the affected test typecheck were rerun. Production types, the 63 consumer tests, and the CLI build are reused because those inputs did not change. Current-head CI passed, including build, all four PostgreSQL conformance shards and PostgreSQL 16 smoke: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44539997718. The introduced old-head capacity failure is repaired, not waived. The separate full-CLI Doctor proof blocker remains.

prs.title: fix(gateway): clean up transient isolated hook base sessions after run (#202621)
prs.body:
Closes #202621

## What Problem This Solves

Every isolated webhook run (`POST /hooks/agent`) creates an ephemeral agent execution session that was never cleaned up after completion. Over time, gateways running automated webhooks accumulate hundreds of orphaned base session records (`agent:<id>:cron:<jobId>`) that cannot be purged by standard cron retention sweeps.

## User Impact

User impact: Prevents unbounded session record leaks and database bloat on gateways handling webhook triggers, ensuring transient isolated hook sessions are immediately purged after execution while preserving history for persistent hooks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Isolated hook runs create ephemeral jobs with `sessionTarget: "isolated"` but previously omitted `deleteAfterRun`. Setting `deleteAfterRun: value.sessionMode !== "persistent"` marks transient hook runs for post-run base session cleanup in `cleanupCronRunSessionAfterRun` once finished, while keeping conversation history intact when `sessionMode === "persistent"`.

## Evidence

Verified that the new unit test fails red on base (`expected undefined to be true` for `call.job.deleteAfterRun`) and passes green with the fix.

Targeted test suites:
- `src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts` (21 passed)
- `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-lifecycle.test.ts` (33 passed)
- Linters and formatting: `oxlint` (0 errors, 0 warnings) and `run-format.mts` clean.

prs.body:

Thanks to @richkuo for the report, including the exact trigger SQL and the rollback details.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can refuse to upgrade a schema-27 agent database when it still has the historical memory revision triggers on only one of its two index tables. The refusal leaves the database on the older schema and blocks the upgrade.

Doctor can upgrade affected SQLite agent databases that have one complete, canonical trigger group. Unknown or altered trigger definitions still block migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each historical revision trigger group is optional in SQLite schemas 27–30. Doctor uses the exact published definitions to validate any group it finds. The schema 31 migration then removes both groups as part of its existing transaction. No schema or protocol version changes.

prs.title: fix: point doctor to the config file when validation fails
prs.body:
Closes #202032

## What Problem This Solves

When Doctor encounters an invalid setting it cannot migrate, its recovery hint sends users to `config unset`. That command also requires a valid config, so users get stuck when they follow the hint.

## User Impact

Doctor now shows how to locate the active config and tells users to correct the reported setting there. The command includes the selected profile when one is active.

## Why This Change Was Made

`config file` can resolve the path while the config still fails validation. The fallback uses that read-only command and preserves any more specific repair hint supplied by the check.

Thanks to @anmol0b for reporting the recovery loop and to the ClawSweeper review for the invalid `gateway.port` test case.

## Evidence

On Windows I ran the built CLI with an isolated profile and set `gateway.port` to a string. On the base, Doctor recommended `config unset`, which exited 1 and left the invalid value in place. On this branch, Doctor gives the active-profile lookup command. I used the returned path to correct the port, and the same final-validation check then passed.

Terminal excerpts show the actual output. I redacted the fixture directory and kept only the relevant fields in the final JSON.

```text
> node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive
Location: gateway.port
Next step: Run `openclaw --profile proof-pr202032-fixed-followup-built doctor --fix` to migrate or remove retired keys. If no migration applies, find the active config with `openclaw --profile proof-pr202032-fixed-followup-built config file`, correct or remove the reported setting manually, and rerun Doctor.

> node openclaw.mjs config file
<isolated-profile>\openclaw.json

# After correcting gateway.port in that file
> node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --only core/doctor/final-config-validation --json
{"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"findings":[]}
```

I updated the existing final-validation regression to check the new hint and removed the separate converter test. The existing case failed on the prior PR head and passed after the test update.

- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 94 tests in 496s locally.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-lint-flow.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 5 tests in 34s locally.
- Changed-file lint and formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The follow-up changes tests only. It reuses the Windows runtime build from the preceding commit, which has identical production sources. The required hosted CI gate passed on `a581cc465b29`.

Independent Linux check on the published `openclaw@2026.11.6`: with a string in `gateway.port`, Doctor recommended `config unset`, but that command exited 1 without changing the profile. `config file` located the same file, and final validation passed after correcting the port there. This confirms the bug on stable. It does not verify upgrading that profile to the PR build; the published-driver update job was skipped.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

## What Problem This Solves

After a managed update replaces OpenClaw, the running helper can load recovery code from the new package into a process that still holds the previous package’s SQLite registry. The probe can then crash (`captureExchange is not a function`) before it reports whether the Gateway is serving, and the update is left unverified with the Gateway stopped. Starting the probe can also consume part of the time reserved for health polling.

## User Impact

An updater with this fix runs both recovery probes (observation and restoration) in an owned child that loads the installed package’s own SQLite registry. Observation and restoration get their configured polling time plus a bounded five-second allowance for the probe process. When rollback cannot be verified and migrated data is at risk, the Gateway still stays stopped for repair. The shipped 2026.11.4 updater still needs a corrected updater for its first hop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both probes use the existing owned child runner that terminal recording already uses. The helper checks health, version and build ID after the child exits and records the outcome through the existing recovery path. The child deadline adds five seconds for admission, Node startup, module loading and result delivery; the installed health check receives the original polling budget. The existing `state-migrated-no-rollback` verdict is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New `update-managed-service-handoff-recovery-source.test.ts` exercises observation and restoration with a predecessor registry, checks the 3,000/8,000 ms and 4,000/9,000 ms inner/outer budgets without elapsed-time thresholds, and covers lease rebind, `recovery-probe.json` cleanup and the unsafe verdict that issues no service start.
- Formatting, focused oxlint and `git diff --check` pass locally. The regression run (base-red/fix-green) is left to PR CI; packaged npm/systemd recovery proof is still pending.

prs.title: fix: show saved child results when completion delivery fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a requester times out or loses access before announcing completed children, the visible failure notice lists child IDs and statuses but omits their saved answers. Expiry notices also omit those answers.

## User Impact

Failure and expiry notices now show captured child results that owe a visible reply, with explicit truncation and instructions for reading the retained full message. Ordinary visible-result fallback behavior is unchanged. Private-only handoffs keep their captured answers internal; the existing admitted visible-final yield marker preserves an owed fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The completion-notice owner formats the already captured results without changing delivery state or stored text. Notices sort by run ID and cap each result at 2,000 characters and the complete notice at 32,000, including framing and recovery guidance. Oversized batches share space between result heads and identify omitted children.

Recovery uses existing Gateway `chat.history` and `chat.message.get` reads under their normal access and retention limits. No new tool, configuration, schema, or cache. The bounded renderer adds 68 net production lines; test coverage adds 158 lines and one existing database-test pool assignment.

Related: #202592.

## Evidence

Real-SQLite regressions fail on main `5b50d1b89bfd1` because failure and expiry notices omit captured answers. The repair passes those cases, including a 16-child batch and oversized-batch bounds. Additional checks cover the per-result cap, Unicode boundaries, deterministic ordering, unchanged stored text, and byte-exact ordinary result fallback.

All 106 focused tests pass across completion storage, requester wake/expiry, history retrieval, and prompt-prefix stability. The five new database-boundary tests total 8.224 seconds; the complete six-file command took 167.03 seconds. Existing history proof includes full retrieval of a 5 MB message. Codex autoreview is clean at P0–P2. Targeted production/test typechecking and lint pass. The complete changed-file check passed except for a corrected test-only narrowing annotation; the supported corrected-file check then exited 0. After ClawSweeper identified private-result visibility, two added mixed-batch regressions failed on the initial PR head. The correction reuses the settlement owner’s privacy predicate: all 64 affected tests pass, targeted types/lint pass, and fresh Codex autoreview is clean. The correction’s full `pnpm check:changed --base 098b9201f14d8` passed, including all types, lint, dead-export scans and guards. ClawSweeper re-review has zero findings and zero open items on final head `6a2f7b2607695`; final CI is accounted for below. No live production data or transcript content was used; the proof is synthetic.

## CI investigation

Initial-head CI run 44796243412 found an unrelated stale inventory entry in both `test/vitest-scoped-config.test.ts` and `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts`. Both fail on exact main parent `5b50d1b89bfd1`; commit `5ec2039594b3b07826f5e2a30d80609d3ff601b9` / #202428 deleted `src/agents/cli-runner/history-boundary.incognito.test.ts` without removing its inventory entry. Main subsequently fixed the stale entries in #202655 (`c45faa87221cf`), and peer #202663 closed. Final-head CI run 44798650717 no longer reports those failures.

Final-head CI 44798650717 attempt 1 failed only `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` (job 136505673978) and its downstream aggregate. Security and all other root checks passed or skipped. Actual checkout `5663aff2a3b1b8cbc73ecd94d560707ea26c1d9e` has main parent `d874bf532f4cb87f3c3b69502d200d8e934e86fb` and PR parent `6a2f7b260769521e03e410b36be801169913db8e`.

All three failing assertions reproduce on that exact main parent. Skills readiness waits for removed discovery rows, introduced by #202531 (`856aca23d7fb5557162db8613a93ae1f2e2f6d19`). Plugins readiness waits for installed catalog cards now filtered out by #202527 (`c2c2effaeddb1ed99db0788fb2dfa61cf7ae03c7`). The skill-settings budget reproduces on configured Boat Linux: 33 requests versus limit 31, with the two new `skill-page-parts` and `middle-truncated` chunks from #202531. The focused Linux test took 59.67 seconds; setup failures are excluded. The UI tree and scenario inputs are identical between baseline and tested merge.

prs.title: fix: let Doctor archive retired state on Windows
prs.body:
Related: #201180

Thanks to @tiptop24swiss-wq for the detailed report, including the capture-directory layout and the five reproductions across two Node versions.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

## What Problem This Solves

On native Windows, `openclaw doctor --fix` can stop with `EPERM: operation not permitted, fsync` while archiving the retired restart sentinel. `backupLegacyStateSource` reopens the verified `.migrated` archive read-only and then flushes it; Windows' `FlushFileBuffers` needs a writable handle, so the flush fails and the pending state repairs (auth profiles, pairing stores) never run.

## User Impact

Doctor can flush the retired-state backup with the access Windows requires and then remove the original after verification, so the remaining repairs complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor already verifies the archive and flushes it before removing the source. The fix reopens the verified archive through fs-safe's existing non-truncating writable open (`writeMode: "update"`), refusing to recreate it if it disappeared, so the file flush can succeed on Windows. The flush still has to succeed before the original is removed. The "missing a root entry" capture message in the report is advisory; a separate fix for one known cause of it is already on main (#199654).

## Evidence

- A new archive test simulates Windows' read-only flush restriction. On base it fails at `backupLegacyStateSource` with `code: EPERM, syscall: fsync`; with the change it flushes the retained archive while the original still exists, then verifies the exact archived bytes and the source removal.
- Focused suites pass: `state-migrations.retired-archive`, `state-migrations.retired-runtime` and `doctor/cron/legacy-repair` (31 tests). Formatting, focused type-aware oxlint and `git diff --check` pass on the touched files.
- Gap: no native Windows end-to-end `doctor --fix` run yet; the original report has no syscall stack, so the cause is source-supported and reproduced at the archive boundary rather than confirmed on Windows.

prs.title: fix: let PostgreSQL agents start turns with plugin tools
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

A healthy PostgreSQL Gateway can reject an agent turn with the full tool profile before contacting the model. Load missing plugin tools through the existing asynchronous loader so their readiness read runs in a worker.

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin needed by the turn may not yet be registered in its runtime generation. Cold tool construction then reports `PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker`, even though Gateway readiness succeeds.

## User Impact

Agent turns can load those plugin tools and complete. Synchronous compatibility entry points remain synchronous. This changes no configuration, schema, permissions, retention, or durability.

## Why This Change Was Made

Async tool construction now carries its execution mode through the existing tool-resolution generator, including callers without workspace-readiness state. Plugin selection, registry reuse, factories, and tool policy keep their existing owners. The synchronous API selects the existing synchronous loader.

Existing consumer test doubles follow that same generator contract. The database regression reuses the existing forked plugin inspection suite and its fixture. An explicit conformance target keeps both PostgreSQL cases in database CI. One unchanged diagnostic helper moves into the existing tool inspection module to satisfy the source-file size limit.

## Root Cause

On the base, `resolvePluginToolsFromRegistry` calls `loadPluginRegistryHandle` for missing owners. That synchronous loader skips the readiness worker step and falls back to `readPluginStateMigrationReadiness` on the Gateway thread. Opening the PostgreSQL connection there is correctly refused. The asynchronous agent adapter also previously selected the synchronous resolver when no workspace-readiness context existed.

The regression runs with the actual Gateway process role on thread zero, prepares metadata as startup does, and loads and invokes a synthetic cold tool. Both PostgreSQL cases fail on the base at `readDeferredPluginMigrations` / `readPluginStateMigrationReadiness`; both SQLite controls pass. Each case uses an independent store and plugin cache.

## Real behavior proof

RAN on Linux, Node 26.13.1, PostgreSQL 17.12, with a disposable Unix-socket-only server and isolated foreground Gateways. The model endpoint is the repository's loopback OpenAI mock fixture. Configuration uses `tools.profile: "full"` and disables memory search.

The turn command was:

```sh
openclaw agent --agent main --session-id <isolated-session> \
  --message 'Return marker <marker>' --thinking off --json
```

Temporary session and marker values are placeholders above. On the base, readiness returned `ready: true`, the command exited 1 with the worker-only connection error, and the mock received zero requests. With the fix, eight turns completed with `status: "ok"`, `summary: "completed"`, and the requested marker in the reply. The SQLite control also completed eight turns.

## What was not tested

No paid or external model calls, live channels, production state, TLS deployment, other server majors, or database port/upgrade workflow. The mock-backed turns prove tool construction and model reachability, not the functionality of every registered tool. PostgreSQL successful-turn latency has no baseline comparison because the base fails before model dispatch.

## Verification

- RAN: exact regression on the base: two PostgreSQL failures at the readiness read; two SQLite passes. With the fix: four passes.
- RAN: full `pnpm build`, focused consumer tests including prompt-prefix stability, core and changed-test typechecks, targeted lint/format, mock-export ratchet, and `git diff --check`.
- RAN: 198 focused consumer tests passed, plus four real-database regression cases. The consolidated registry suite passed 16 cases in 39.52 s including collection (about 4 s test time); its wrapper took 41.06 s. CI conformance shard 3/4 also passed all 16 cases, with 6.439 s summed per-case execution time.
- RAN: same SQLite full-profile mock workload on the base and final source, three warmup turns then five measured fresh-session turns. CLI-to-reply median: 949 ms before, 877 ms after; ranges 863-982 ms and 801-1048 ms. This small shared-host sample is a control, not a throughput or tail-latency guarantee.
- Simplification: reuse the existing async loader and generator. No new worker, registry, cache, or state owner. Production delta: 41 added / 29 removed lines; test, fixture, and conformance-routing delta: 128 added / 17 removed lines. The diagnostic helper move is included in those counts.

## Evidence

Local autoreview of the production repair, P0-P2, reports `scoped-clean`. The complete option-construction and loader owners were supplied. Local autoreview of the CI inventory repair also reports `scoped-clean`. The current-head diagnostic only adds refusal details to an existing assertion; it changes no expected response, request, wait, retry, or production behavior.

### CI inventory repair

The first CI run found 78 jobs against the scheduled 77-job cap. The regression now reuses the existing forked inspection suite. No extra host-worker inventory entry or increased limit remains. RAN the four scheduled-capacity cases and eleven conformance-routing cases: all passed.

### Repeated Bun failure investigation

Both failed CI attempts tested the same merge commit. Their avatar-subscription test received `ok: false`:

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44545665684/job/135637036420
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44545665684/job/135658712659

RAN the actual `scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` entry with its three-file `agentic-gateway-server-isolated-hosted-3` selection, Node 24.22.1 and the checksum-verified repository Bun pin, `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`. On base `3587df70a23`, the avatar case passed three of three runs. On PR head `271b8a34a6d`, it also passed three of three. The full shard had a separate terminal-subagent timeout once on each ref; these are separate outcomes, not avatar failures.

Three runs each on CI's exact main parent and tested merge ref also passed the avatar case. A further clean-home, four-CPU run reproduced the exact avatar refusal on the PR head, while its base control passed. Thus the repeated CI failure remains unclassified. No inherited-failure claim is made.

A verified main-branch snapshot contains the same test and passed it:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44598233217/job/135823119335

The diagnostic commit retains `ok: true` and the same subscribed-session payload assertion while reporting the RPC error code and message when that assertion fails. This is diagnostic evidence collection, not a claimed fix for the CI refusal. Focused lint, formatting and the gateway test typecheck pass. Equivalent temporary assertion diagnostics passed three head and three base Bun shard runs with fresh homes and four CPUs.

Current head: [649f80c3e072](https://github.com/VACInc/openclaw/commit/649f80c3e072be27bcfb52808d2c7f9843c95322). Production source remains unchanged.

### Current diagnostic CI result

The original avatar case passed in the same three-file Bun group, taking 2.943 s:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44616678138/job/135888545902

CI also advanced its main base. The pass does not establish that the assertion diagnostic repaired the historical refusal; that cause remains unclassified.

The current run is red on a different test: `session-message-events.history-worker.test.ts > delivers selected-session count updates after worker overload` times out:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44616678138/job/135888546116

The CI classifier labels this **unknown** with no matching job on main. RAN that exact two-file Bun group three times on base and three times on this head: all six local runs passed. These replays do not classify the CI timeout as inherited or fix it. No timeout, retry, expected response, or gate was relaxed. Merge readiness is not claimed. No merge or auto-merge was requested.

prs.title: fix: report channel plugin download failures to scripts without prompting
prs.body:
Closes #201990

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw channels add` cannot download a required plugin, it can find a local copy and ask whether to use it. A script has nobody to answer, so the prompt can hide the download error. The [earlier fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5c9389a5ba9c21efa4b0c97dd55c57d0bc9c3112) already stopped the command from reporting success after a failed install.

## User Impact

Scripts see the download error once, exit with status `1`, and leave channel configuration unchanged. People running the command at a terminal can still choose the local copy. No migration or new flag is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer used to offer the local copy even when the command had already determined that it could not ask questions. The [five-file follow-up against `main`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/a3bd84cc50639a4bd377db3d286d5ae1c3c3d273...4a13c9dc3faf3fabba7b7454c04363fc5dc72d60) ties that one question to terminal input and output. Guided setup, source selection and capability consent are unchanged.

## Evidence

Ran the built `openclaw.mjs channels add --channel fixture-chat --name Example` at [the published head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4a13c9dc3faf3fabba7b7454c04363fc5dc72d60) with a local copy present and a loopback registry returning HTTP 404. With stdin closed there was no prompt. In a real terminal the local-copy prompt appeared; answering **No** preserved the same error. Each run made one registry request, printed the cause once, exited `1`, and left the config byte-for-byte unchanged. The public registry was not contacted.

```text
Closed stdin:
Could not install the plugin for channel "fixture-chat". Install the plugin manually or verify the install source, then retry.
Package not found on ClawHub.

Real terminal:
Use local plugin path instead? ([fixture workspace]/plugins/fixture-chat)  → No
Could not install the plugin for channel "fixture-chat". Install the plugin manually or verify the install source, then retry.
Package not found on ClawHub.
```

The CLI regression test failed against the original implementation because it asked one question instead of zero. On this head the command, setup-adapter and installer suites passed, as did scoped typecheck, lint and formatting. Independent autoreview of the complete five-file range found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202091#issuecomment-7024309261) verified the terminal proof on `4a13c9dc` and listed no findings or before-merge actions.

[Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44804403623) is **not green**. The [failing UI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44804403623/job/136525382964) timed out waiting for rows on Skills and Plugins; Skill Settings loaded 33 assets against a limit of 31. The tested merge changed no UI or benchmark files. The [Skills and asset-count failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44803148089/job/136521248000) and [Plugins timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44796218464/job/136497502162) also occurred on independent runs. Related upstream work: [#202694](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202694) and [#202687](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202687). These are not passing checks for this PR.

Contributor: Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm). Reported by Anmol (@anmol0b).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2edc3159-c613-4611-ac1c-48d712e40c67)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/e22c0f1b-d725-4148-b4d3-3a6437d47641)
- [Local fallback correction and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/d7d74ff2-50f8-4b78-a6d7-f10ac7918e37)
- [Landing discussion and verification with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dfbb8805-b4f2-4c40-ac84-ea5b941703a5)

prs.title: fix(gateway): bind loopback caller conversation tool-policy assertion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #201195. When a session runs through a CLI runtime (tools reached via the OpenClaw MCP bridge), `github_read` always fails with:

```
GitHub reading requires an active github_read tool invocation.
```

The check in `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts` requires `caller.assertToolAllowed`, but the loopback caller identity built by `createAdmittedGatewayToolCallerIdentity` carried no `assertToolAllowed` assertion. Direct-RPC callers (inside the Gateway's own agent loop) get that assertion from `agent-tools.caller.ts`; MCP-bridged calls never did.

## Solution

Bind the loopback caller's effective conversation tool-policy assertion in `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts`'s `createCallerIdentity`. The loopback grant already carries the `conversationToolPolicy` that filtered the served catalog; this wires it through the same standard path so tools that re-assert the active invocation's policy can verify it. Plugin-id and `group:plugins` allowances expand through the served catalog's own plugin ownership (`expandPolicyWithPluginGroups` + `buildPluginToolGroups`), matching the catalog pipeline rather than introducing different policy semantics at invocation.

This preserves the existing authority model:
- Direct-RPC refusal is unchanged.
- If the conversation policy denies the tool, it never appears in the served catalog (already filtered at construction), and the bound assertion also rejects it.
- No policy means "allow all not denied" — matching the catalog's own default, so an admitted permitted GitHub read now passes instead of being rejected unconditionally.
- Plugin-group allowances (`"github"`, `"group:plugins"`) expand to concrete tool names exactly as the catalog pipeline does.

## Impact

Behavioral fix for a real user fault: permitted GitHub reads through the MCP bridge from a CLI runtime now work. No new options, config, or persistence. ~12 production lines.

## Evidence

- Root cause chain verified at source (ClawSweeper's `source-repro`): rejection at `tools-github.ts:73` when `caller.assertToolAllowed` is absent; loopback identity at `mcp-http.ts` lacks the assertion; working sibling at `agent-tools.caller.ts:82` supplies it.
- Collision check: no open PR touches `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts`, `src/agents/tools/gateway-caller-context.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts`, or `src/agents/tool-policy-match.ts`; no open PR claims issue #201195.
- Regression (red/green): new `src/gateway/mcp-http.loopback-caller-policy.test.ts` fails on base (`assertToolAllowed` is `undefined` → `expected 'undefined' to be 'function'`) and passes with the fix. Plugin-group expansion is covered separately: with `allow: ["github"]` the base assertion rejects the admitted `github_read` (red), and the fix accepts it (green). Full `mcp-http.test.ts` suite: 63 passed, no regressions.
- Review finding addressed: the [P2] readonly `McpLoopbackTool[]` parameter now passes the mutable array to `buildPluginToolGroups` (head `785af5e3`); scoped `tsc` typecheck of the changed files is clean.
- Containerized end-to-end attempt (Docker `ubuntu:24.04`, Node 24, pnpm 12.15.0; a scripted claude-cli child speaking real MCP JSON-RPC over the loopback bridge; real `api.github.com` fetch of issue #201195), run as a 4-variant matrix on head `785af5e3`:

  | Variant | Conversation policy | Served loopback catalog | `github_read` call |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `plugin` | `allow: ["github"]` | `[]` | `Tool not available: github_read` |
  | `concrete` | `allow: ["github_read"]` | `[]` | `Tool not available: github_read` |
  | `none` | (no policy) | 37 core tools | `Tool not available: github_read` |
  | `native` | `allow: ["github"]`, realistic native tool surface | `[]` | `Tool not available: github_read` |

  Reading: with no policy the bridge serves 37 tools, so the grant→`toolsAllow`→catalog chain works end to end in the harness. But `github_read` is absent from the CLI loopback projection even unrestricted, so the call fails at "Tool not available" before it can reach the policy assertion this PR fixes. In the reported production scenario `github_read` *is* served — the user's error came from the tool's own policy assertion — so the remaining gap is harness fidelity of this qa-lab lane (plugin tools are not projected into its CLI bridge catalog), not the policy path changed here.
- **Real behavior proof (shipped-run)**: isolated Gateway in a container (Ubuntu 24.04), genuine Claude Code CLI runtime as the agent backend (`agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" }`), conversation policy `tools.allow = ["github"]`, production `github_read` through the loopback MCP bridge. Full detail and red/green trajectories in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201228#issuecomment-7001240050):
  - HEAD `785af5e3`: `tool.call github_read` → `tool.result ok`; agent replies with the exact title of #201195. Gateway log: 0 occurrences of the rejection string.
  - BASE `f7c68043` (merge-base, identical environment): `github_read` ×3 and `github_search` ×1 all rejected; agent reports the Gateway error verbatim: `GitHub reading requires an active github_read tool invocation.` — the exact #201195 production failure.
- An earlier containerized harness experiment (scripted MCP client over the loopback bridge) reached only catalog lookup because that scaffolding does not project plugin tools into its CLI catalog; it is superseded by the shipped-run proof above.
- `openclaw/ci-gate`: fork-PR workflow requires maintainer approval to run; all local gates above are green.

prs.title: fix(daemon): Linux updates run out of space on a RAM-backed /tmp when TMPDIR was never set
prs.body:
Refs #199559 (one of its causes; the rest stays open there)
Related: #199030

Scope: this PR fixes one defect, the Linux service installer writing a `TMPDIR` the operator never set. It does not change how an explicit `TMPDIR` ranks against the state volume (the open decision on #199030), and it does not repair units installed before it, Doctor recovery, hidepid hosts or update cleanup, which stay on #199559.

## What Problem This Solves

On Linux, `openclaw gateway install` freezes the host default `/tmp` into the gateway's systemd unit as `Environment=TMPDIR=/tmp` when the operator never set `TMPDIR`. Update staging treats that as an explicit operator choice and stages on `/tmp` first, so on a host where `/tmp` is a small tmpfs, `openclaw update` runs out of space even when the state disk has plenty free.

## User Impact

User impact: on Linux, a gateway service installed or refreshed without `TMPDIR` in the installer's environment no longer gets `TMPDIR` written into its unit, so update staging ranks the state volume first instead of a RAM-backed `/tmp`. Operators who set `TMPDIR` keep it exactly as before. macOS (state-dir `tmp`) and Windows are unchanged. Existing units lose the frozen `TMPDIR=/tmp` on the next `openclaw gateway install --force`; reinstall already drops the old unit's `TMPDIR` rather than replaying it (shown below).

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveServiceTmpDir` returned `env.TMPDIR || os.tmpdir()` on Linux, so the host default was frozen into the unit as if it were an operator choice. Update staging (`update-candidate-snapshot.ts`, `update-retained-runtime.ts`) treats any `TMPDIR` as explicit and ranks it ahead of the state volume. On Linux the function now returns `undefined` when `TMPDIR` is unset or blank, so the unit omits it (`renderEnvLines` skips non-strings) and the process still resolves `os.tmpdir()` at run time. The darwin-only callers in `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-*` keep a `string` return through an overload.

## Evidence

Real systemd run on a throwaway Debian trixie host (systemd user services with linger, `/tmp` a 160 MiB tmpfs, state on the root disk), Node 24.22.3. "Stable" is npm `openclaw@2026.11.5` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15)`, the current `latest`). "Fix" is this PR's two commits applied to the `v2026.11.5` tag, same patch-id as the PR head, packaged with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (23254fc)`). Installer shells had no `TMPDIR`. Full redacted transcript below.

- **Before (stable 2026.11.5, fresh `openclaw onboard --install-daemon`):** unit has `Environment=TMPDIR=/tmp`; the running service process has `TMPDIR=/tmp`; `Connectivity check: ok`.
- **Upgrade from 2026.11.5 through the fixed installer:** with the stable gateway running and a cron job stored, `openclaw gateway install --force` from the fix (no other step). The unit diff against the backed-up 2026.11.5 unit changes only `ExecStart`/`PATH` to the new build and drops `Environment=TMPDIR=/tmp`. Service `active`, `Runtime: running`, `Connectivity check: ok`, `openclaw health` ok, service process has no `TMPDIR`.
- **Existing settings and data after the upgrade:** `openclaw.json` byte-identical (same SHA-256), gateway auth token unchanged (hash compared), `state/openclaw.sqlite` (`user_version` 36, 103 tables), the agent database (`user_version` 38, 58 tables) and `control/services.sqlite` unchanged in schema version and table set, and the stored cron job is still listed with the same id and schedule. The change writes no stored data and no schema; it only changes which `Environment=` lines the installer renders.
- **Explicit TMPDIR kept:** `TMPDIR=/var/tmp openclaw gateway install --force` (fix) → `Environment=TMPDIR=/var/tmp` in the unit and in the running process; `Connectivity check: ok`.
- **Update snapshot selection:** the shipped `assessInitialUpdateSnapshotCapacity` (from the fix's `dist/update-candidate-snapshot-*.mjs`), run with each unit's environment:
  - stable 2026.11.5 unit: `explicit-tmpdir /tmp: 71 MiB needed; 107 MiB free.` ranked first, then `state-volume`.
  - fix unit: `state-volume /home/oc2/.openclaw.update-captures: 71 MiB needed; 15 GiB free.` ranked first, then `system-tmpdir /tmp`.
  `allocateSnapshotRoot` takes the first candidate that fits, so the stable unit stages on the tmpfs while the fix stages on the state volume. A full `openclaw update` is not exercised here: the updater skips this host as `container-image-install` before staging.
- **Earlier run, 2026.11.3:** the same checks from a 2026.11.3 unit (including `openclaw gateway stop --force` + `openclaw doctor --fix` before the reinstall) gave the same result; that transcript is in this PR's history.
- **Tests:** five cases in `src/daemon/service-env.test.ts` (Linux unset, Linux blank, Linux explicit, macOS state dir, Windows host default); three fail without the fix. `pnpm test src/daemon/service-env.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 35 passed on the PR head, on `v2026.11.5` + this PR, and on current `main` (5fb231527f4) + this PR; the commits cherry-pick onto both without conflict.
- **Wider tests and checks (PR head):** `pnpm test src/daemon src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts src/commands/daemon-install-path.test.ts src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-lease-path.test.ts src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-cleanup-repair.test.ts` pass except two cases in `src/daemon/service.test.ts` that fail identically on `main`. `pnpm check:changed`: format, lint, all typecheck graphs and every other guard pass; the dead export scan fails with 36 entries, none in touched files.
- **Local review:** autoreview (Claude engine, since Codex is not used), complete committed range of the first commit, P0 threshold: clean, 0 findings (comment above).

<summary>Redacted transcript (2026.11.5)</summary>

```text

OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15)
$ (stable) openclaw onboard --non-interactive ... --install-daemon     # installer TMPDIR: <unset>
```

prs.title: fix: stop reporting removed paths that never existed
prs.body:
Closes #202026

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw uninstall` and `openclaw reset` print `Removed <path>` even when the path never existed. On a Mac without `/Applications/OpenClaw.app`, `openclaw uninstall --app` claims it removed the app. Users cannot tell what was actually deleted and what still needs removing.

## User Impact

User impact: cleanup output now says `Not found: <path>` for targets that did not exist, so an uninstall report matches what was actually removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`removePathPreserving` checks the target with the existing `pathExists` helper before `fs.rm` and chooses `Removed` or `Not found` accordingly. Successful removal and dry-run output keep their current wording. This covers uninstall, reset, and the other callers that share this helper.

## Evidence

- New tests in `src/commands/cleanup-utils.test.ts` cover a missing path and an existing path.
- Red on base: with the existence check reverted, the missing-path test fails with `- "Not found: ..."` / `+ "Removed ..."`.
- Green with the fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/cleanup-utils.test.ts src/commands/uninstall.test.ts src/commands/reset.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 3 shards passed.
- Formatting and lint pass; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Real CLI proof on macOS without the app, using an isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`:

  ```text
  $ node scripts/run-node.mjs uninstall --app --yes --non-interactive
  Not found: /Applications/OpenClaw.app
  CLI removal instructions: https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/uninstall
  ```

prs.title: fix(auth): classify and explain model-route credential mismatches
prs.body:
Related: #185064

## What Problem This Solves

Configured credentials can be rejected with a generic authentication error, while the availability check can misclassify profiles whose inference requirements differ from their stored credential type. For example, token-sharing OAuth serves an API-key route, but the incompatibility check previously treated it as subscription-only OAuth.

## User Impact

Route-mismatch errors explain the required authentication class and API adapter, and the class supported by the configured profiles. Model availability correctly distinguishes an incompatible credential contract from a compatible account that is temporarily unavailable; identity-only sign-ins remain explicitly denied inference.

This addresses a bounded classification/diagnostic problem found while investigating #185064. Successful Terra execution on an unmodified current-main Gateway remains unverified, and this PR does not close that issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use each profile's existing `authRequirement` when classifying route incompatibility, matching the actual selector. Treat `null` as an explicit inference denial. Reuse that classification to append a bounded explanation only when all configured profiles have known incompatible requirements. A configured route remains authoritative in the explanation.

The new suffix contains auth categories and API adapter names. It adds no credential values, profile identifiers or endpoint URLs. Physical route selection, profile ordering and native account ownership retain their existing algorithms; the corrected availability classification is intentionally consumed by model admission and Doctor. Native catalog transport metadata and static model lists are unchanged.

## Evidence

Regression assertions were run against base `b48d16bf6e98f0b9c1e110548fc46b3b35f2becd` before applying the production fix: 4 expected selector failures, 3 availability-consumer failures, and 4 runtime auth-preparation failures. The same assertions pass with the fix.

| Focused suite | Final result |
| --- | --- |
| Provider model route auth | 30/30 |
| Model auth availability: existing session/account pins | 49/49 |
| Model auth availability: native accounts | 17/17 |
| Runtime auth preparation | 40/40 |
| **Total** | **136/136** |

Scoped lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, the production core typecheck, and both relevant test typecheck leaves pass. The runtime tests exercise observed/authored Platform routes with automatic/explicit profile order, exact credential-safe errors, and successful selected-OAuth forwarding on the subscription route.

Self `pr-simplify` and an independent code review completed with no remaining actionable findings. The reviewed, tested, and published file contents match.

Validation environment: Node 24.22.1, pnpm 11.25.0, Vitest 5.0.5. Used the documented Node runner and serial projects after a parallel cold worker startup exited 137 before any tests; that setup failure is not counted as defect evidence. Lockfile unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation commands</summary>

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_SERIAL=1 pnpm test \
  src/agents/provider-model-route-auth.test.ts \
  src/agents/runtime-plan/prepare-auth.test.ts \
  src/agents/model-auth-availability.native.test.ts \
  src/agents/model-auth-availability.session-pin.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1

OPENCLAW_LINT_TOOL=oxlint node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs \
  --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json \
  src/agents/provider-model-route-auth.ts \
  src/agents/provider-model-route-auth.test.ts \
  src/agents/runtime-plan/prepare-auth.test.ts \
  src/agents/model-auth-availability.native.test.ts

OPENCLAW_FORMAT_TOOL=oxfmt pnpm format:check \
  src/agents/provider-model-route-auth.ts \
  src/agents/provider-model-route-auth.test.ts \
  src/agents/runtime-plan/prepare-auth.test.ts \
  src/agents/model-auth-availability.native.test.ts

git diff --check
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json --incremental
```

</details>

Implementation and review were AI-assisted. Regression inputs are synthetic; these tests perform no provider inference or account sign-in. Upstream [main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43221545984), [CodeQL security](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43221545557), and [Critical Quality](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43221545746) all succeeded on head `3321155e3853b5f87a26e207ad468e165ced9c8c`.

The [current-head security notice](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197737#issuecomment-6824089483) requires an upstream maintainer to review and post `/allow-security-sensitive-change` before merge. The aggregate merge gate is blocked on that approval, not on a test failure. Maintainer review remains pending.

### Runtime behavior proof — November 12

Added the running CLI/Gateway evidence requested in the [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197737#issuecomment-6824675590), at unchanged source and build commit `3321155e3853b5f87a26e207ad468e165ced9c8c`.

The normal `pnpm openclaw --help` source build completed; the CLI reports OpenClaw 2026.11.3 and `dist/build-info.json` identifies the full commit above. These runs use the actual CLI, a running Gateway, the real bundled OpenAI provider, and the canonical SQLite credential writer. No provider-policy, selector, availability, authentication-preparation, or Gateway-dispatch functions were mocked.

Each case has separate disposable `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and workspace paths. Provider credentials were excluded from the inherited environment. The sole account in each case is synthetic, persisted with the packaged `upsertAuthProfileWithLockOrThrow` SDK function; `models auth list` verifies the stored OAuth account. `plugins list --json` reports the bundled OpenAI plugin as enabled and loaded. The fixtures use an authored `openai/gpt-5.5` row, the OpenClaw runtime, and unpinned model selection.

| Case | Actual runtime result | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary, unexpired OAuth; authored `openai-responses` route | Local agent CLI exits 1 with the complete new mismatch diagnostic below. | The user-visible error identifies the incompatible authentication classes. |
| `chatgpt-token-sharing`; expired at `1`, no refresh token; canonical `https://api.openai.com/v1` + `openai-responses` | `models list` reports `available: false`; Gateway spawn returns `accepted`, `modelApplied: true`; `agent.wait` then reports the same run's ordinary auth failure. | Compatible credential class with unavailable credentials passes model-choice preflight, while the later execution authentication boundary still refuses the run. |
| Unexpired `chatgpt-identity`; authored `openai-chatgpt-responses` route | Gateway spawn returns a tool-level model-preflight error, with no accepted run ID. | Identity-only authentication remains authoritatively denied on the subscription route. |

The public Responses endpoint in the token-sharing case is intentional: OpenAI's actual token-sharing policy requires that canonical endpoint. An earlier loopback setup mixed endpoint incompatibility with expiry and is excluded from the evidence.

<details>
<summary>Actual commands and captured output</summary>

All setup/readback commands returned exit 0:

```bash
pnpm openclaw config validate --json
pnpm openclaw models auth list --provider openai --agent main --json
pnpm openclaw plugins list --json
pnpm openclaw models list --all --provider openai --json
```

The account fixtures are written through the packaged canonical API, with explicit disposable state and agent directories:

```js
import { upsertAuthProfileWithLockOrThrow } from
  "./dist/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-api-key.js";

await upsertAuthProfileWithLockOrThrow({
  stateDir,
  agentDir,
  profileId: "openai:fixture",
  credential
});
```

Each credential uses OAuth storage, provider `openai`, and a synthetic access value. The ordinary and identity-only fixtures have future expiry; the latter specifies `authFlow: "chatgpt-identity"`. The compatible-unavailable fixture specifies `authFlow: "chatgpt-token-sharing"`, `expires: 1`, and an empty refresh field, which the canonical store normalizes away.

**1. Actual local agent CLI — mismatch**

```bash
pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main \
  --message "Proof only; no inference should start." --json
```

Exit 1. Captured JSON:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai. Selected model route requires api-key authentication (openai-responses); configured profiles support subscription authentication. Select a model route compatible with the configured account, or select a compatible account."
  }
}
```

**2–3. Actual Gateway model-choice consumer**

The disposable Gateway config explicitly includes the documented `gateway.tools.allow: ["sessions_spawn"]` exposure setting. Both cases run a real `pnpm openclaw gateway run` process and wait for its ready log.

```bash
pnpm openclaw gateway call tools.invoke \
  --params '{"name":"sessions_spawn","agentId":"main","args":{"task":"Proof only; no inference should start.","model":"openai/gpt-5.5","runtime":"subagent","context":"isolated","mode":"run","runTimeoutSeconds":10,"expectsCompletionMessage":false}}' \
  --json --timeout 20000
```

The RPC exits 0 in both cases. The significant result is the nested `output.details`, not merely the RPC envelope's `ok: true`.

Compatible but unavailable token-sharing profile, selected fields from the actual `output.details`:

```json
{
  "status": "accepted",
  "runId": "<proof-run>",
  "resolvedModel": "openai/gpt-5.5",
  "resolvedProvider": "openai",
  "modelApplied": true
}
```

Then the public wait RPC, using that same returned run ID:

```bash
pnpm openclaw gateway call agent.wait \
  --params '{"runId":"<proof-run>","timeoutMs":15000}' \
  --json --timeout 20000
```

Exit 0; selected fields from the actual terminal result:

```json
{
  "runId": "<proof-run>",
  "status": "error",
  "error": "No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai."
}
```

The Gateway log independently records that same run's authentication failure. The run ID is redacted consistently above; matching of the original receipts was verified. This is observed terminal failure, not an assumption based on spawn acceptance.

Identity-only profile on the subscription route, actual `output.details`:

```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "error": "sessions_spawn model \"openai/gpt-5.5\" is not usable: The selected account or native runtime is unavailable for openai/gpt-5.5. Restore that account before spawning this model."
}
```

No accepted child run ID was returned in the identity-only case.

**Cleanup and scope**

The two Gateway logs confirm intentional shutdown and clean completion (146 ms for canonical token sharing; 118 ms for identity-only). After shutdown, both Gateway ports were closed and the actual offline `models auth list` command succeeded, confirming release of state ownership. The pnpm wrapper's -15 status records the fixture owner's intentional SIGTERM cleanup.

The mismatch and identity-only cases use loopback sentinel endpoints, each recording zero requests. The canonical public endpoint in the compatible-unavailable case was not instrumented; its receipt demonstrates authentication-preparation failure and makes no measured zero-outbound-traffic claim. No valid account credential or successful inference is claimed.

prs.title: fix: keep shell setup instructions visible after installation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a successful shell install, the terminal that launched it may still lack npm's bin directory on PATH. The installer prints a repair early, then buries it beneath Doctor or verification output and ends with an unconditional success message.

## User Impact

The final summary now says **“Installed; one shell setup step remains”** when the original shell needs PATH setup, followed by the existing shell-specific repair command. Immediate onboarding instructions continue to use the verified, quoted executable path, so users can run the CLI before repairing PATH.

Already-correct PATH keeps the normal success summary. No new settings, profile writes, migration, install-method change, or Gateway lifecycle change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer is a child process and cannot change the parent shell's environment. This moves the existing PATH guidance into the final summary after successful Doctor/verification, reusing the original-PATH detector and shell-aware renderer rather than adding another repair mechanism. Fatal checks still return before success.

The quoting issue addressed by #187612 is already represented in this base and is not reimplemented here. #200381 and #201043 concern separate build/onboarding behavior.

## Evidence

- **Red → green:** the real assembled installer installed public stable OpenClaw 2026.11.5 under an isolated HOME/npm prefix containing spaces. On the base, installation exited 0 and declared success while the original shell's bare command exited 127; the final-summary assertion failed. With the change, the same original shell consumed the actual emitted immediate command and PATH repair, then reached both onboarding help and CLI help.
- **Native shell coverage:** Bash 5.2, zsh 5.9, and Fish 3.6 passed that original-shell handoff. An already-correct Bash PATH control retained normal success and a working bare command. No real user state, services, or shell startup files were changed.
- **Focused regression:** a main-entrypoint table covers missing/correct original PATH, fresh setup, and configured Doctor completion, then executes emitted commands with space-containing paths. It fails on the base for the intended missing final handoff and passes on the candidate.
- **Owning suites:** 240 passed, 1 existing Darwin-only availability skip across the installer and standalone-assembly suites; 13.16 seconds runner wall time, approximately 11.9 seconds aggregate test time. After moving readiness calculation beside the summary, all 12 affected lifecycle/handoff cases passed again in 2.09 seconds runner wall time, and the real Bash installer replay passed again in 10.05 seconds. The [exact-head CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44374440877/job/135056389704) passed; aggregate CI seconds are not recorded here.
- **Checks:** standalone installer build, Bash syntax, targeted lint, script-test typecheck, formatting, MDX validation, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- **Review:** simplify pass complete. Local Auto Review was started for the complete local delta, P0–P3, but produced no report and was cancelled after stalling; it is **incomplete**, not a clean review. The [initial hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201383#issuecomment-6988768423) found no actionable code defects and requested inspectable terminal evidence; the retained output is included below. Evidence re-review is pending.

Limitations: no native macOS Bash 3.2 run or real Git-method installation; the unchanged quoting renderer and existing Git lifecycle tests remain the coverage for those paths. ShellCheck is unavailable. The real installation used compatible Node 24.20.0 with SQLite 3.53.4 and retained the existing security-patch recommendation. This is terminal-output behavior, not a web/native visual change.

### Inspectable terminal handoff evidence

These excerpts come from the retained real assembled-installer runs, not the synthetic unit fixture. Paths shown below are task-owned test homes; no user data or credentials are included. Omitted package-manager and long CLI-help lines do not change the recorded order.

**Before — base installer, isolated writable npm prefix absent from the original Bash PATH:**

```text
[3/3] Finalizing setup

! PATH missing npm global bin dir: /workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/baseline home/npm prefix/bin
  This directory was not on PATH when the installer started.
  For this shell, run:
    export PATH='/workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/baseline home/npm prefix/bin':"$PATH"; hash -r
  For future shells, check your shell startup file.

🦞 OpenClaw installed successfully (2026.11.5)!
I'm in. Let's cause some responsible chaos.

· Skipping onboard (requested); run /workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/baseline\ home/npm\ prefix/bin/openclaw onboard later

FAQ: https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/faq
Support: https://community.openclaw.ai/
INSTALLER_EXIT=0
/bin/bash: line 6: openclaw: command not found
ORIGINAL_SHELL_BARE_EXIT=127
```

**After — exact candidate installer bytes, real public OpenClaw 2026.11.5:**

```text
[3/3] Finalizing setup

! Installed; one shell setup step remains (2026.11.5)
  A piped installer cannot change its parent shell environment.

! PATH missing npm global bin dir: /workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/final-bash home/npm prefix/bin
  This directory was not on PATH when the installer started.
  For this shell, run:
    export PATH='/workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/final-bash home/npm prefix/bin':"$PATH"; hash -r
  For future shells, check your shell startup file.
· Skipping onboard (requested); run /workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/final-bash\ home/npm\ prefix/bin/openclaw onboard later

FAQ: https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/faq
Support: https://community.openclaw.ai/
```

The same parent Bash process launched the assembled installer through a pipe, then read these commands directly from its final output. The onboarding command was run **before** PATH repair (with `--help` to avoid configuration writes), followed by the repair, `command -v openclaw`, and `openclaw --help`. Its negative control required bare `openclaw` to remain absent before repair.

Actual extracted command files:
```sh

export PATH='/workspace/.openclaw/tmp/installer-path/final-bash home/npm prefix/bin':"$PATH"; hash -r
```

Selected lines from that original parent process, in recorded order:
```text

OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15) — All your chats, one OpenClaw.
Usage: openclaw [options] [command]
```

The final parent process exited **0**, with empty stderr, in **10.045 seconds**. Bash’s `set -eu` and `pipefail` made failed installation, immediate handoff, repair, or CLI help fail the proof. The initial PATH was `/usr/bin:/bin`; HOME, OPENCLAW_HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, npm prefix, and npm cache were isolated. The real installer invocation was:

```sh

```

The retained sibling receipts show the same output-driven replay succeeded in native zsh 5.9 (**10.674s**) and Fish 3.6 (**8.845s**). The already-correct Bash PATH control passed in **8.588s**, printed ordinary success and a bare onboarding command. No source change or CI rerun was made for this evidence addition.

<details>
<summary>Scope and reproducible checks</summary>

Base: `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea`. The installer and shared policy were byte-identical to live main `7ce2d10eced5f379e31a0b01a96fbcbf9741ccbe` when reproduced.
