prs.title: fix: show device-code sign-in steps on separate lines when the Gateway runs the login
prs.body:
Closes #200749

Related: #198327 closed without merging; this is a new, separate change for the same symptom.

## What Problem This Solves

When the local Gateway is running, `openclaw models auth login` shows multi-line sign-in steps with the text `\n` instead of line breaks. The device-code box becomes one run-on paragraph: the instructions, URL, code, expiry and the warning not to continue if someone else gave you the code all run together. The login still works, but the step that carries the phishing warning is hard to read. This affects every provider that signs in through this path (xAI and OpenAI Codex device codes, and any other multi-line note or progress step).

## User Impact

User impact: people signing in to a provider through the CLI while the Gateway is running see the instructions, URL, code, expiry and warning on separate lines, as they do in the offline sign-in path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway builds these messages with real newlines on purpose. The CLI then ran the whole message through the terminal sanitizer, which is written for single-line text and turns each newline into a visible `\n`. The CLI now sanitizes each line of a step message separately and joins the lines with real newlines. Control characters and color codes are still stripped on every line, and a stray carriage return is still escaped. The terminal note renderer already wraps each line on its own, so the restored newlines reach the screen as line breaks.

The shared single-line sanitizer is left alone, because other callers rely on it, and the URL, device code and error text keep using it. The fix stays in the login command since this is the only caller that needs line-preserving output. I did not add a shared multi-line helper; that can come once a second caller needs one.

## Evidence

A regression test in `src/commands/models/auth-login-gateway.test.ts` sends a progress step and a select prompt through the Gateway login loop. It uses the message shape from the issue (`Code: ABCD-1234` followed by a blank line and a completion note) with CRLF and LF breaks, color codes, a bell and a lone carriage return mixed in. It checks that the line breaks are kept, the controls are removed and the carriage return is still escaped.

- On the base commit (29ce933) with only the test added, the test fails. The note receives `Enter this one-time code.\r\nCode: ABCD-1234\n\nxAI OAuth complete` as literal backslash sequences, which is the reported bug.
- On this head (7372c8e), all 11 tests in the file pass. The new test takes about 50 ms.
- Also clean on this head: oxfmt and oxlint on both changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src` and `git diff --check`.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts --maxWorkers=1 src/commands/models/auth-login-gateway.test.ts
node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/commands/models/auth-login-gateway.ts src/commands/models/auth-login-gateway.test.ts
oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json src/commands/models/auth-login-gateway.ts src/commands/models/auth-login-gateway.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm tsgo:test:src
```

</details>

Not verified yet: a live Gateway-backed login. I built this head (`openclaw --version` prints `OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (7372c8e)`) and started an isolated local Gateway, but my test environment denies the CPU and network-interface queries the Gateway makes at startup, so it shut down before a login could run. The `pnpm test` wrapper's worker also could not start in that environment, so I ran Vitest directly with the same project config and have no wrapper wall time to report.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After an update, OpenClaw prints the saved report path without explaining how to read it. Pasting that path alone into Bash tries to execute the private Markdown file and fails with `Permission denied`.

## User Impact

Saved update reports now include a copyable **Read report** command beside the existing path: `cat` in a POSIX shell, or explicitly labelled PowerShell `Get-Content` on Windows. Paths containing spaces, quotes, or shell metacharacters are quoted. Report permissions, update behavior, and JSON stdout are unchanged; nothing is opened or uploaded automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

One small CLI formatter reuses the existing shell-quoting helpers across final update output, interactive report fallback, and the legacy post-plugin Doctor diagnostic on stderr. It appears only where a saved report path is already printed. The update reference explains that reports are text files, not commands.

## Evidence

- **Real CLI before/after:** ran `pnpm openclaw update --dry-run --channel stable` with isolated synthetic state, never a real update or the hosting Gateway. On base `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea`, copying the generated report path into Bash exited 126 with `Permission denied`. With the fix, copying the emitted command read exactly the generated Markdown bytes and exited 0; permissions remained `0600`. The final proof used a state path containing spaces, an apostrophe, `$HOME`, backticks, a semicolon, and brackets.
- **Regression:** the Linux and Windows output cases fail on the base for the missing read command and pass with the fix. Existing exact JSON assertions pass; failed artifact writes produce no read instruction. Sibling interactive and resumed-Doctor tests check their output destinations.
- **Focused checks:** 86 tests across progress, progress observation, rollback report, Doctor authority callers, and shell quoting passed. The combined command took 94.32 seconds including cold compiled-worker preparation; the existing Doctor-authority suite took 40.68 seconds and exercises real isolated state/Doctor subprocess boundaries. The new command cases each took 2 ms. CI duration is pending. Production and CLI-update test typechecks, targeted lint, format check, docs listing, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Build:** the normal source CLI build completed (50.4 seconds), then the changed CLI copy/paste proof passed.
- **Simplification:** one reused seven-line formatter, three two-line caller changes; no new state or policy. Net delta: +13 production lines, +37 test lines, +6 docs lines.
- **Independent review gap:** bound Auto Review (`local`, base above, P0–P2, complete 9,934-byte change bundle) prepared one pass but its OpenClaw execution timed out without a report. This is not a clean independent review.
- **Platform limit:** Windows command formatting, including apostrophes, typographic quotes, and literal wildcard characters, is regression-tested. prs.title: fix: keep database workers healthy after silent connection loss
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

A silent database connection could block a worker for two minutes and then reset healthy connections on the same I/O service. Enable TCP keepalive and retire the silent connection before the host watchdog fires, so ordinary transport loss fails only the affected connection. The worker's cutoff now follows the deadline the host sends with each request, so longer maintenance requests from #201869 are not cut at the ordinary 100 seconds. Idle validation can reconnect before caller SQL; a lost commit reply remains uncertain and is never replayed.

- Bridge data clients enable TCP keepalive (10-second initial delay).
- Each bridge request carries `deadlineMs`, the time left before the host resets the I/O service. For query and recovery-generation requests, the worker ends that request's client 20 seconds before the deadline. With runtime defaults: deadline 120 s, cutoff 100 s, server statement timeout 90 s (unchanged).
- Connection setup and idle validation queries keep separate 10-second client bounds.
- One internal worker-message field. No public API, config, schema, stored-data, or dependency change.

## Root Cause

The data bridge configured a connection timeout and server statement timeout, but no client query timeout or TCP keepalive. A server timeout cannot deliver an error through a black-holed return path. The host's 120-second watchdog therefore became the first effective bound and retired the entire assigned service.

The regression reaches the real synchronous connection through a socket proxy. It forwards a transaction's COMMIT to a disposable server and discards the reply. On the base, the call took **120001 ms**, failing the under-20-second assertion.

The first revision of this PR fixed that with a fixed client `query_timeout` of statement timeout + 10 s. That bound is set once per connection and cannot see a longer request budget. #201869 gives maintenance transactions (migrations, search rebuilds, search-extension admission) a one-hour transaction-local statement timeout and a one-hour-plus-30-second host deadline. Combined with the fixed client bound, every maintenance statement over the ordinary cutoff would be killed on the client. On a scratch merge of the two earlier heads, a maintenance `pg_sleep(12)` on a connection with a 1-second runtime statement budget failed after **11078 ms** with `PostgreSQL connection lost; transaction rolled back`.

This revision makes the host the single owner of the request budget. The host deadline is now the connection's statement timeout plus 30 seconds (still 120 s in production, where the statement timeout is always 90 s), it is sent with each request, and the worker's per-request timer ends the client 20 seconds early. Ending the client fails the pending query without an SQLSTATE, which the host already classifies as connection loss with the existing outcome-unknown rules.

## Real behavior proof

RAN on Linux against a disposable PostgreSQL 17 server (loopback and Unix socket only), through `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <disposable DSN> -- <files>`.

This PR alone at the exact pushed head, `src/infra/postgres-sync` (all 11 files):

```text
isolates a silent commit connection without replaying writes            11231ms
isolates a silent idle connection without replaying writes              10085ms
keeps a statement running until shortly before a longer request deadline 12034ms
Tests 42 passed (42) + 92 passed (92)
```

- Silent commit and idle cases use a 1-second statement budget, so the host deadline is 31 s and the worker cutoff 11 s. The commit is outcome-unknown, written exactly once, and four peer connections keep their backend IDs (no service reset).
- The new long-deadline case sends a 45-second request deadline and runs `SELECT pg_sleep(12)` under `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '1h'`. With the previous worker it failed after **11067 ms** (`PostgreSQL connection lost; transaction rolled back`); with this worker it returns after 12 s.

Combined with #201869 (local scratch merge, not pushed; the only conflict is the deadline line in `connection.ts`, resolved as below), `src/infra/postgres-sync` plus `src/infra/database-engine`:

```text
lets maintenance statements outlive the runtime statement limit and client cutoff 12024ms
keeps a statement running until shortly before a longer request deadline          12019ms
isolates a silent commit connection without replaying writes                      11134ms
isolates a silent idle connection without replaying writes                        10066ms
restores runtime statement limits after maintenance commits and nested rollbacks    156ms
```

A second scratch merge against #201869's current head (which merged `main` for an unrelated conflict) passed `src/infra/postgres-sync`, the schema-admission, search-extension, search-conformance, search-admission and port-command PostgreSQL suites, and the memory search-rebuild suite: **45 + 160 + 2 passed**, including the lost-commit-reply port case. The numbers above are from that run except the 156 ms admission case (first run).

The maintenance case is a real `runTransaction(..., { maintenance: true })` on a connection with a 1-second runtime budget; it ran past the old 11-second cutoff, and `SHOW statement_timeout` returned `1s` afterward. The combined database-engine run had 15 local failures, all environmental and rechecked: 14 from this host's group-writable temp directories (passed after rerunning with `umask 022`) and 1 lost-reply proxy case that needs a TCP listener (failed the same way on the base revision; passed on the combined branch once the disposable server listened on loopback).

Combined resolution of the deadline line:

```ts
const deadlineMs =
  (this.maintenance
    ? POSTGRES_MAINTENANCE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS
    : (this.bridgeParameters.statementTimeoutMs ?? POSTGRES_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS)) + 30_000;
```

## Landing order

Land this PR first. #201869 then needs `main` merged with the resolution above (code conflict only in that line and its import; docs merge cleanly). Either PR alone is safe: this one alone keeps production at 100 s / 120 s, and #201869 alone has no client cutoff.

## What was not tested

- Full Gateway/channel flows or paid model calls.
- Real hardware suspension, kernel TCP keepalive timing, or a production failover.
- The full default 100-second cutoff or a one-hour maintenance budget in wall time; the real-I/O regressions use the same calculation with a 1-second statement budget.
- The accepted edge case where the cutoff fires during the brief window in which an idle reconnect has closed the old client but not yet created the new one; the reconnect happens at request start and the cutoff at least 10 s later, so the window is not reachable in practice. The host watchdog still covers it.
- General throughput, full package/release builds, or upgrade migrations. No schema or stored-data changes.

## Verification

- Red-on-previous-head regression for the long deadline (11067 ms connection lost), then green; silent commit/idle regressions still green.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.infra.json`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on changed files, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`: passed.
- Unit suites `connection.test.ts`, `protocol.test.ts`, `bridge-prestart.test.ts`: passed (message expectations now include `deadlineMs`).
- pr-simplify pass: no further reduction; the fixed client timeout was replaced, not layered. Production delta against the merge base: 43 added / 15 removed lines (this revision: 20 added / 5 removed).
- Local autoreview (branch mode, P0 to P2) against base `3587df70a23`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44786397524) on `8430fc80d91`: SUCCESS, including all four PostgreSQL conformance shards and the PostgreSQL 16 smoke.

prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #202645

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users pasting a copied image into the terminal-mode chat input (for example a Codex session opened from the session catalogue) would get nothing — the image was silently dropped, while picking the same image via the attach button worked.
- **Related:** #202645; clawsweeper review confirmed the gap ("file selection stages attachments, but the input never forwards pasted images to that path") and requested a base-failing, fix-passing PNG ClipboardEvent regression through `.tp-composer`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** A paste carrying image files into the embedded terminal composer input now stages those images through the exact same path as the attach button and drag & drop: upload admission, quoting, editable attachment chips, and explicit submit (no PTY input before Send). Text-only pastes keep the native input path.
- **Out of scope:** No changes to the desktop (non-embedded) terminal panel, PTY paste behavior, or upload policy; non-image clipboard files are not intercepted (matches the composer-level image-paste precedent in the command palette).
- **Highest-risk area:** Accidentally swallowing text pastes or double-pasting into the PTY.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The handler returns early when no image items are present (native paste untouched), and the existing upload owner already refuses any PTY write before explicit submission — both covered by the new regressions.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** With a live terminal session open, copying a PNG and pasting into the chat input shows an editable attachment chip; Send submits the text plus the quoted uploaded path; no PTY input happens before Send.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-upload.ts` (`handlePaste`), `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-view.tsx` (composer `onPaste` wiring); regressions in `terminal-panel-handoff.test.ts` ("stages a pasted image as an editable attachment without sending PTY input before send") and `terminal-file-upload.test.ts` ("uploads a pasted clipboard image as an editable quoted path", "leaves text-only pastes on the native input path").

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** worktree at commit `cdfa4e7fd42` (rebased on `origin/main` @ `a3bd84cc506`), Node 26.12.1, jsdom component harness with a real DOM paste event through the Solid view wiring + real-Chromium Playwright e2e lane.

prs.title: feat: let Knowledge learn from Slack
prs.body:
Related: #202410 (Slack `channel-list` and `readAs`, which this scribe reads through; land that first)

## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge can learn from conversations, Granola meetings and Memory, but not from Slack. That's where a lot of decisions, commitments and project news actually happen. Getting that into Knowledge today means pasting or importing by hand.

## User Impact

The Scribes page gains **Learn from Slack**. Once a Slack account is connected, the owner can run it once or keep it running on a schedule. Each run reads the channels the Slack bot is in and saves the substantive discussions (decisions, commitments, plans, project news) to Knowledge with sources.

Two opt-ins, both off by default:
- **Use my Slack user token:** also read every channel the owner's user token can access. Only offered when the account has a user token.
- **Include DMs:** also read direct messages and group DMs.

It reads only through the Slack plugin's `channel-list` and `read` actions, and it never sends or changes anything in Slack.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Same setup as the Granola scribe:**
  - a scribe catalog entry with fixed options (how far back to start, user token on/off, DMs on/off) and a weekday schedule;
  - a checkpoint note page;
  - an agent-run procedure in the `knowledge-source-ingest` skill (`references/scribe-runs.md#learn-from-slack`).
- **Readiness** also checks `channels.status`, because the Slack channel plugin has no MCP sign-in for the page to check. Without a configured, running Slack account the page shows "needs sign-in".
- **Every Slack call passes `readAs` explicitly.** Bot-member channels are listed and read as the bot. The user token is used only with the opt-in, and DMs are read with the token that listed them. Without `readAs`, the plugin would fall back to the user token whenever one is configured.
- **Each run:**
  - re-reads a 3-day window so recent edits are picked up;
  - keeps threads with replies in the last 90 days and revisits them in rotation;
  - reads newly joined channels first;
  - advances a channel's checkpoint only after its ingest is published and verified.
- **Snapshots are always recorded as `partial`.** Slack reads can't prove every thread reply was seen, so a missing message is never treated as a deletion.
- **New `slack-read-normalize.mjs`** turns saved `read` results into the normalized chat format the Discrawl adapter uses. Each row has a content hash that leaves out context-derived labels, so overlapping reads don't show unchanged replies as changed.
- Existing scribes' generated run messages are byte-for-byte unchanged, so upgrade recognition is unaffected.

## Evidence

- **Not yet run end to end:** no live Learn from Slack run from the Scribes page yet; it needs a real Gateway and Slack workspace after #202410 merges. The Slack actions it depends on are proven live in #202410. Opened for review at the maintainer's request with that proof still outstanding.
- **User-only Slack accounts (ClawSweeper P2, fixed in `1a64c498`):** an account with no bot token can run the scribe only after the owner explicitly turns on the user-token option; the dialog explains why and blocks Start until then, and runs never switch tokens silently. Astra re-review: no findings.
- **Independent review:** an Astra review with two follow-up passes. It found one P0 (the run steps called `member-info`, which bypassed the user-token opt-in). It also found four P1s: edits never re-read, revived threads missed, new channels starved, and overstated snapshot completeness. Plus one P2 (an unstable reply hash). All are fixed, and the final pass found no remaining P0 or P2. Its last P1 was fixed by making every snapshot `partial`, a Markdown-only change that wasn't re-reviewed.
- **Tests:** 7 scoped test files, 62 tests:
  - scribe state and readiness, the view, and the Slack dialog fields;
  - the normalizer, including an overlapping-snapshot hash regression;
  - chat transcripts, the source manifest and skill packaging.
- The reviewer also checked that all 12 Slack option combinations regenerate as current, and that the run messages of the existing scribes are unchanged (46 prompt variants).
- oxlint on the touched files, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, the skill-reference sync check and `git diff --check` all pass.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: wait for three conversations before showing the community invite
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
The first time someone opens the Control UI, the sidebar promotes the community before they have used a conversation. Freshly imported history or conversations used by someone else should not make a newcomer look active.

## User Impact
The invitation stays out of the sidebar until the signed-in person has sent messages in three distinct conversations. Three messages in one count once. No pop-up opens. Previously dismissed cards stay dismissed in that browser, and **Profile → Help → Discord** remains available without waiting. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made
Ownership and recent activity can both exist without the person sending a prompt. The Gateway now filters its existing prompting-participant records, including merged profile aliases. The sidebar requests one compact row and uses the Gateway's total before pagination; it neither fetches transcripts nor keeps a second participation counter. Cron, system, subagent and dock sessions are excluded. Missing or failed reads do not qualify a new visitor.

## Evidence
- Gateway filters and catalog-import integration: 37 tests passed on the final filter. A real import containing a question did not qualify the importer. Other-person-only, assignment, ownership, mentions, timestamps, and merged aliases were checked separately.
- Isolated real Gateway + Chromium + local synthetic inference: observed **0 → 1 → 2 → 3**, including three replies to prompts in the first conversation. The card appeared without reload in the third and remained dismissed after reload. The prebuilt Gateway in this run preceded a behavior-preserving viewer-ID refactor; the Gateway source tests above cover the final implementation.
- Focused browser E2Es passed for the below-threshold state and desktop/mobile layout and dismissal. Playwright WebKit on macOS also verified the hidden card and visible voluntary Discord link at zero, and the card at three. This exercised the shared web surface, **not** a native app launch.

prs.title: feat: give small local models a smaller prompt with Agent Profiles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt already fills about 45% of the window before the user says anything. The only existing switch, lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`), now trims very little and removes the scheduling tool. It also cannot follow the model: if one agent uses a hosted model and a local model, there is no way to slim the prompt for the local model only.

## User Impact

Set `agentProfileId: "openclaw/small"` on one `provider/model` entry, on an agent, or as the default. That model then gets a smaller prompt and keeps every tool:

- reference sections (documentation, execution style, model aliases, UI presentation) are left out, while reply, owner and channel guidance stay;
- the skills catalog lists no entries while skill search is available, so skills stay findable;
- injected workspace files are capped at 12,000 characters in total.

`openclaw/lean` keeps the old lean mode exactly, for anyone who relies on it. `openclaw/base` is the default.

Required action for users of the old flag: run `openclaw doctor --fix`. It moves `experimental.localModelLean: true` to `openclaw/lean` at the same scope. `false` was the default and is removed, except on an agent that opted out of a lean default, where it becomes `openclaw/base` so the opt-out survives. Until then, config validation reports the retired key and points to doctor. `agent exec --local-model-lean` keeps working and selects `openclaw/lean`.

With no `agentProfileId` set, the system prompt and tool list are byte-identical to `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the first code slice of the Agent Profiles RFC (openclaw/rfcs#18). It follows the RFC's names and precedence:

- one resolver with three built-in profiles and no prompt text;
- selection by explicit config only: agent, then default, then the agent's exact model entry, then the default exact model entry, then `openclaw/base`;
- a doctor migration of the old flag;
- the selected profile and the scope that chose it in the run's system prompt report.

There is no size-based binding and no tool removal in `openclaw/small`. Each prompt-size setting only narrows: a smaller configured workspace budget still wins, and the skills limit is skipped when skills could not be found any other way. Compact prompts use their own stable-prefix cache entries.

Config surface: three keys added (`agentProfileId` at defaults, per agent, and per model entry) and two retired (`experimental.localModelLean` at defaults and per agent, plus the now empty per-agent `experimental` block). The core config budget goes from 2656 to 2657 for that net one key.

Open for maintainers, in short: whether the `openclaw/small` values (no listed skills, a 12,000-character workspace cap) are the right defaults beyond the tasks measured below.

## Evidence

Behavior checked:

- **Default config unchanged:** with no `agentProfileId`, a real agent turn on `main` and on this branch sent a byte-identical system prompt (37,835 characters, same sha256) and tool list (14,592 characters, same sha256).
- **Exact migration:** doctor maps both cases exactly. Defaults `false` with an agent `true` becomes no default setting plus `openclaw/lean` on the agent. Defaults `true` with an agent `false` becomes `openclaw/lean` plus `openclaw/base` on the agent. Each migrated config validated, a second doctor run changed nothing, and a turn on the agent reported the expected profile.
- **Local model run:** the shared local-model test scope (10 tasks x 3 runs, 32,768-token window) on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash served by oMLX. Baseline: OpenClaw 2026.11.5 stock. Candidate: this branch with each profile bound to that model entry.

| | First request (server count) | Tasks passed |
| --- | ---: | :---: |
| 2026.11.5 stock | 14,548 tokens | 30/30 |
| 2026.11.5 lean flag | 13,050 tokens | 27/30 (scheduling fails) |
| this branch, no profile | 14,824 tokens | footprint only |
| this branch, `openclaw/lean` | 14,629 tokens | footprint only |
| this branch, `openclaw/small` | 11,987 tokens (-19.1%) | 30/30 |

`openclaw/small` kept all 13 direct tools, with the same schemas. The saving comes from the skills catalog (about 7,800 characters) and the reference sections (about 2,900 characters). Every one of the 93 model calls on the candidate run returned the requested model.

CLI backends and `/context` use the same effective workspace budget. A CLI run whose model entry selects `openclaw/small` reports a 12,000-character total even when the configured total is 150,000.

Known gaps: the Codex app-server and agentsapi harnesses do not pass the model to workspace context, so a profile bound only to a model entry does not cap workspace files there. Profiles set on an agent or as the default do apply. The CLI system prompt report does not name the selected profile yet.

<details>
<summary>Commands and results</summary>

- Red on the previous commit with the new tests: 25 failing tests. Red without the CLI and `/context` budget change: the CLI budget test and the `/context` budget test each fail.
- Green on this branch: all targeted tests pass, including the CLI runner prepare and system prompt suites.
- Mutation (`openclaw/small` without its prompt-size settings): 2 profile tests fail. Mutation (stable-prefix key without the compact flag): the cache test fails. Mutation (CLI budget call without the model): the CLI budget test fails (150000, expected 12000).
- `pnpm check:changed --base <merge-base>`: every check passes except the Plugin SDK surface budget, which also fails on the base commit (3908 > 3894).
- Local ClawSweeper review of the committed range: 7 rounds, P0 to P2 findings fixed. The last round: patch is correct, no security concerns, ratings D (overall), D (proof, mock-only by its reading) and B (patch). Two P3 notes remain: the harness workspace gap above, and whether compact mode should keep the UI presentation section for tools it keeps.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`check-lint` fails for any PR whose changed-lint scope includes `test/vitest/vitest.extension-signal.config.ts`. []), …]` may spread a string. It surfaced on #202663 and was attributed to #145981.

prs.title: fix: resume the same provider sign-in after returning from the browser
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Returning from a provider’s browser sign-in should not send someone through login again. Reloading first-run Model Setup could open another provider tab; reopening Mac onboarding could replace the view that owned the attempt. A Mac sign-in that offered optional redirect paste could also stay on that prompt after the browser had finished.

## User Impact
Return to the same sign-in in the Control UI or Mac onboarding. A restored web page still offers a link if the original tab was lost. The Mac setup window can be minimized and brought forward without replacing a busy setup. Manual input remains available only when requested by the provider wizard.

## Why This Change Was Made
The clients read the original wizard session; focus does not start another login. The Mac observer reads without submitting an answer and hands a changed result back to the existing completion and model-verification path. The existing request/attempt identity and Gateway lease scope the result. There is no new credential store, activation mechanism, RPC or provider callback handler.

## Evidence
- Chromium: 3 end-to-end tests passed with a synthetic Gateway/provider page. The return regression opens one provider tab, switches focus, reloads the setup page, reads the same session ID without starting another login, then reaches the onboarding destination on the terminal result without a second activation.
- WebUI: 21 tests passed across the wizard runner and reconnect suites, including late replies after cancellation and after switching Gateways. Focused TypeScript lint and format passed.
- macOS: the app and native test bundle compiled. SwiftFormat and SwiftLint passed on the three changed production files. Native fixtures cover the normal callback, late replies after cancellation or a route change, and minimizing/reopening the same AppKit window.
- **Not verified:** native test execution and interactive Mac sign-in require a disposable macOS runner; no real provider account, callback URL or code was used for the browser proof. No full-repository typecheck or CI result is claimed. Independent local autoreview was stopped before a verdict because its preparation scanned the whole checkout, outside the requested validation scope.

prs.title: feat(templates): sign in to ClawHub from a private draft
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Trying to review a private Template draft while signed out of ClawHub led to a `clawhub login` error. **Retry review** repeated it. Creators had to leave the conversation and sign in on the Gateway host.

## User Impact

The card starts with **Sign in to ClawHub**. Select **Sign in** to request a code without leaving the conversation. The code replaces the subtitle and the same button becomes **Copy & open ClawHub**. Select it, paste the code into ClawHub, and approve. Review resumes on the original unpublished draft. A blocked clipboard or popup offers manual recovery; cancellation or expiry leaves the draft private. **Preview** shows the files without publishing. Only **Publish** uploads the draft.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway binds the pending approval to the original person, registry, conversation and draft. It stores the verified credential in the existing private SQLite identity store for that person and registry; another administrator cannot borrow the host account. The card displays the short approval code, never the device credential or API token.

## Evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c1c0ce8-c4bd-423d-a12e-f38f633f2e46

[13.36-second before/after recording](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7028869474). Before, ClawHub opened with an empty field and no code on the clipboard. After, the first click stays on the draft; the second copies the code and opens one approval tab. A keyboard paste fills the field. Approval opens exactly one review of the original unpublished draft. Opening and closing Preview sends neither chat nor a publish request. The card and button kept their dimensions and positions at 400, 820, 1280 and 1440 px.

The recording shows tree `715f2b57bf28`. It uses Chromium, a rebuilt Control UI and Gateway, the [pinned ClawHub approval component](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/blob/63a48631a855dfda27254b4a767962ca7a4ece8b/src/routes/cli/device.tsx), and a local fixture account and authorization backend—not a production sign-in. On later tree `c8956918ccff`, sign-in and review screenshots were pixel-identical and all four layout measurements matched.

### Current integration

Published head `b9cb09145eec` and locally tested integration `d7522079bc6c` have the same tree, `ca7161a96c520df62389816d44a3b8761b82c4cf`. This brings in the [landed iPhone Settings fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202634); the feature patch ID is unchanged. All four Settings-repair files match main. Of the 40 feature files, only `components.css` overlaps incoming changes, and it retains both independent rules.

- 242 focused tests and 12 bundled Chromium cases passed without retries, including the formerly failing Settings route and light/dark iPhone editing. One opt-in real-Gateway authority case was skipped. A separate real Gateway + Chromium run exercised the two-click sign-in, clipboard handoff, same-draft review, and Preview/Close with no chat or publication.
- The [stable-to-candidate test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7046623878) was repeated from shipped `v2026.11.6` against the current tree. The existing owner login and private draft remained byte-identical and mode `0600`; the original team secret still matched. The new personal credential survived restart and stayed isolated from the other person, another registry and another registry path on the same host. Seven Gateway processes exited cleanly; zero publication requests. This is an application-state upgrade with loopback registries, not a production sign-in or installer certification.
- Core/UI typechecks, protocol generation/drift, formatting, lint, i18n and changed-test-line checks passed. Chat boot measured +1 byte JS and +18 bytes CSS gzip against the landed base; no budgets changed.
- **Local full-build limitation:** `pnpm build` failed the public Plugin SDK declaration-size check on both the unchanged base `5b8b0c15596e` and the integration. Both generated the same 349 declaration files byte-for-byte: 5,394,009 bytes against a 5,385,536-byte limit (+8,473; PR delta 0). No exception or budget change. [Hosted CI for this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44792697148).

**Earlier recordings:** [CSS repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7028406678) · [Conflict repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7027856897) · [Before conflict resolution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7027187181) · [Manual-entry version](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7021694420) · [Original sign-in proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7019878271).

prs.title: feat: let agents list Slack channels and choose which token reads them
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents can read a Slack channel's history, but only if they already know the channel. There is no way to ask "which channels can I read?", so anything that wants to work through a workspace (such as a Knowledge scribe learning from Slack) has to be pointed at channels by hand. Reads also silently switch to the user token whenever one is configured, so a caller cannot keep a read to what the bot itself is allowed to see.

## User Impact

Agents can call the Slack `channel-list` message action to list the conversations they can read, and pass `readAs: "bot" | "user"` to `read` and `channel-list` to choose the token explicitly. Leaving `readAs` out keeps today's behavior. No new Slack scopes are needed, and nothing is sent or changed in Slack.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `channel-list` uses the existing `actions.channelInfo` gate (default on), the same setting Discord uses for its `channel-list`.
- With the bot token, it lists the conversations the bot is a member of. With a user token, it lists what that user can access.
- By default it lists public and private channels. DMs and group DMs are listed only when requested, and archived conversations are excluded unless asked for.
- Paging uses the core `pageToken` field and returns `nextPageToken`.
- Results report the workspace `teamId`, so callers can build stable keys like `slack:<team>/<channel>`.
- Every listed conversation passes the same policy check `read` uses: disabled channels, group allowlists and DM rules.
- `readAs: "bot"` forces the bot token. `readAs: "user"` requires a configured user token and fails clearly without one.
- `read` already accepted an omitted `teamId`, and that could skip `team:`-qualified channel denials. This PR fixes that by resolving the selected token's workspace for the policy check.
  - The monitor's recorded workspace is reused only for the token the monitor actually authenticated.
  - Current-conversation matching keeps the caller's own qualification.
  - An explicit `teamId` that doesn't match the token's workspace is rejected.

## Evidence

- **Live proof through an isolated Gateway**, using the QA Lab Slack lane on a leased workspace (read-only, no Slack writes):
  - `channel-list` (bot token, delegated caller) returned the workspace `teamId` and exactly the leased channel. Each entry had `id`, `name`, `type`, `isMember`, `isArchived` and `purpose`.
  - `read` with `readAs: "bot"` returned 5 messages with `hasMore: true`.
  - `readAs: "user"` was rejected because the QA account has no user token.
  - Not covered live: `readAs: "user"` with a real user token, and paging across several pages (the QA allowlist yields one channel).
- **Independent review:** an Astra review with two follow-up passes. It found and verified two P0s and two P1s, all about workspace-qualified policy and token/workspace matching. All four are fixed with regression tests, and the final pass found no remaining P0, P1 or P2.
- **Tests:** 26 scoped Slack test files, 515 tests, cover:
  - bot-token member filtering, user-token listing, type and archived filtering, and paging;
  - all `readAs` modes on both actions;
  - workspace-qualified denials with an omitted `teamId`;
  - mismatched bot and user workspaces, and user-identity monitors;
  - the current-DM exceptions.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint on `extensions/slack`, oxfmt check, `pnpm lint:docs` and the line-cap ratchet all pass.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <26 Slack test files>`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/slack`
- `pnpm openclaw qa slack --doctor` and a one-off read-only `--scenario-file` run (1/1 passed, about 22s)

</details>

prs.title: improve(ci): speed up forced-exit lint checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The focused CI boundary lint resolves JavaScript bindings even when a file or destructuring property cannot contain a forbidden process termination. Across the repository, that creates avoidable work in a frequently run check.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior or lint coverage changes. The focused CI check finishes faster on the measured workload; this does not establish whole-job or billing savings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skip files only when they contain neither a forced-exit spelling nor an escape, build the binding lookup only when needed, and inspect destructured property names before resolving their receiver. Escaped spellings, imports, aliases, and shadowing retain the existing AST and binding checks.

## Evidence

Five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs of the complete focused CI oxlint command passed the predeclared gate: at least 10% lower median wall time, no higher median CPU, at most 10% higher peak RSS, and identical diagnostics/file counts/exit status.

- Median wall: **33.585 → 26.847 seconds (20.1% lower)**.
- Median CPU: **80.75 → 67.22 seconds (16.8% lower)**.
- Maximum RSS: **550,464 → 531,212 KiB (3.5% lower)**. Median RSS increased from 511,816 to 526,752 KiB.
- All ten samples: **50,414 files, zero diagnostics, exit 0**, identical full sorted diagnostic digest.
- **28 tests passed**, focused lint and format parity passed, and both script and owning test type checks passed. Script type proof predates only the final test-assertion repair; production inputs are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Complete measurements and reproduction</summary>

| Pair | Baseline wall (s) | Candidate wall (s) | Baseline CPU (s) | Candidate CPU (s) | Baseline RSS (KiB) | Candidate RSS (KiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 33.585 | 26.847 | 80.75 | 59.94 | 550464 | 526752 |
| 2 | 28.616 | 24.119 | 62.06 | 55.12 | 511816 | 521544 |
| 3 | 31.995 | 26.565 | 71.63 | 67.22 | 511032 | 531212 |
| 4 | 43.308 | 34.575 | 101.37 | 76.88 | 516684 | 519356 |
| 5 | 38.956 | 33.703 | 92.19 | 81.07 | 506160 | 529724 |

Wall p95 (nearest rank, five samples): **43.308 → 34.575s**. Wall ranges: **28.616–43.308s → 24.119–34.575s**. CPU p95: **101.37 → 81.07s**.

Baseline: `5c15d796c6b6a36705ee85cdacfcc1c4c1b0d8dc`.
Candidate: `df9381914b54507997c94820263881a66ff35bd4`, tree `9a492744c15ba7e5254400f363ea6cfbf7b67799`.
Verified transport tree matched; carrier `980b4094a7572e1cd89ebe542fa44018aae42772`.
Boat / Crabbox run `run_972202780481a7422e31cfac356d1863` on one Linux machine, observed 8 available CPUs and 16,768,802,816 bytes RAM. Each sample ran a fresh process with a fresh Node compile cache. Only the forced-exit rule and plugin came from the compared revision; other workload inputs were identical.

```sh
CI=true node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/boundary-reference-measure.mts REV
CI=true pnpm test test/scripts/oxlint-boundary-guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
CI=true pnpm format:check test/scripts/oxlint-boundary-guards.test.ts
CI=true node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json test/scripts/oxlint-boundary-guards.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.scripts.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --noEmit
```

Diagnostic SHA-256: `4f53cda18c2baa0c0354bb5f9a3ecbe5ed12ab4d8e11ba873c2f11161202b945`.

</details>

The new destructuring guard reduced forced-exit rule lookup requests from 4,348 to 308 (92.9%) compared with the preceding unmerged candidate, with identical file counts and diagnostics. This is a work-count result, not a timing claim.

Regression coverage includes escaped identifiers and strings, uppercase `reallyExit`, aliases, and unrelated destructuring. The work-count regression fails on the preceding candidate and passes with the guard. Local source review found no substantive correctness or security issues.

prs.title: improve: ship less JavaScript when opening Chat or New Session
prs.body:
Related: #200929

> **Status (14:55 UTC): parked, will be superseded.** The same validator change (commit 865b4c28) is now integrated in #200929 at `2cd21004`. Against main `e43b1461`, that PR's paired builds measure Chat −747 B and New Session −1,044 B gzip. Merging this one separately would only conflict with #200929, so it stays open but unmerged. If #200929 lands, this closes as superseded; if #200929 is dropped or loses the change, this lands on `main` as is. The `checks-ui-e2e` failures on this head are inherited New Session failures on `main`; #201268 fixes them. cc @vyctorbrzezowski

## What Problem This Solves

Chat and New Session download repeated protocol validation code when they open. The duplicate checks take up space in both routes’ startup bundles, which are already over budget.

## User Impact

No visible change. Chat downloads 1,105 fewer gzip bytes of JavaScript and New Session 1,352 fewer. Validation rules and request counts are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The activity, session-input, and transcript validators already shipped in the same shared boot chunk. The generator now compiles them as one group, so TypeBox emits repeated checks once, without moving any validation to a later load. Validator groups that load independently stay separate.

## Evidence

The paired performance comparison against `392506102468cb92aeb66a6a39ef7b3130583070` passed: Chat boot JS −1,105 B gzip (21 → 21 requests), New Session −1,352 B (17 → 17), startup unchanged. Against the newer base `fb34e996` (after other paydowns landed) it still measures −293 B Chat and −310 B New Session. Generator reproducibility, schema parity, focused consumer tests, `ui:validators:check`, `ui:boot-manifest:gen`, lint, and the UI and scripts typechecks passed.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: fix: explain why guarded plugin state calls are blocked
prs.body:
Related: #183790

## What Problem This Solves

When operators investigate “Plugin state authority is unavailable,” an overlapping write and an earlier unknown publication outcome currently produce the same diagnostic. That makes it difficult to tell which fail-closed condition stopped a guarded call.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish those two conditions and correlate the same database within one process without exposing its path, plugin scope, or stored values. Each diagnostic gives a branch-specific wait instruction and explicitly warns not to replay a write whose outcome is uncertain. Guard behavior and recovery are unchanged. This addresses diagnostic question 3 only: it does not establish the cause or delivery outcome of the reported Telegram incident, fix worker OOM, or authorize replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing publication owner now supplies branch-specific reasons, a process-local keyed identity reference, and conservative publication-state labels. Native commit remains explicitly unconfirmed. The diagnostic key has its own singleton so an already loaded reconciliation owner keeps its existing shape. No new public schema, retry, or recovery path is introduced.

## Evidence

- Both denial states fail the new owning-boundary/caller diagnostic checks before the repair: 5 intended failures, 12 passing tests.
- Final complete reconciliation and native-binding-facts suites: **18 passed**, including real SQLite worker/foreign-writer and unknown-installation cases, old-guard invalidity, later recovery, and synthetic private-data nondisclosure through the real error formatter. Latest test time: approximately 0.64 s and 4.07 s per file; combined Vitest wrapper wall time 43.41 s. These are local suite timings; the separately verified current-head CI result is listed below.
- Core and owning-test typechecks, targeted lint (three TypeScript files), four-file formatting, and diff checks passed on the updated candidate.
- **Current-head CI passed:** [run 44313746337](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44313746337), attempt 1, succeeded for `58e4185df842595a0034b4837d49cb7bcd221892`. The audit at **2026-11-18 13:52:26.840 UTC** verified 68 terminal CI jobs with no bad jobs and successful current `openclaw/ci-gate`, security-sensitive review, and dependency review. This is the recorded audit result, not a claim about later metadata-triggered checks.
- **Current-head hosted review completed:** [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201189#issuecomment-6979497221) reviewed `58e4185df842595a0034b4837d49cb7bcd221892` at **2026-11-18 13:46:58.201 UTC**, with **zero findings**, “Before merge: None,” and “Ready for maintainer review.” The prior P2 safe-next-action finding is resolved: pending diagnostics say to wait for publication settlement, unknown-outcome diagnostics say to wait for committed-state confirmation, and both prohibit uncertain-write replay. The owning/caller guidance assertions failed before that correction (5 expected failures, 13 passed) and pass afterward.
- Independent provided-source narrative review covered all four changed files and the complete supplied owner/caller/formatter context. It found one P2: an older reconciliation singleton could lack the new key. The suggested separate-key repair is applied; a focused regression failed with the HMAC key TypeError before the repair and passes afterward. No actionable finding remains unaddressed. The reviewer did not re-review that exact recommended correction.
- Review limitation: the human-approved narrative route replaced interrupted/timed-out canonical AutoReview. It has no helper-enforced isolation or frozen-input machine validation; read-only instructions are not enforced isolation. The exact diff was intact, while paginated full-file evidence normalized separating newlines in long files. Hashes are implementer evidence, not reviewer machine attestation. No Telegram/Codex live proof or full-incident resolution is claimed.
- **Built-Gateway proof is partial; the aggregate two-case run failed.** A disposable source-bound QA runtime on Node 26.12.1 started through the maintained compiled-process/Gateway fixture. An authenticated local synthetic-plugin RPC used the real keyed-store owner, read-availability guard, and error formatter. The controlled pending write was denied with the correct reason, guidance, and non-sensitive reference, then became available after settlement. Privacy and actual-Gateway PID correlation checks passed.
- The attempted unknown-outcome stimulus used a public worker-owned operation adding 34 near-limit values. It committed 35 total rows, but **did not produce an observed unknown denial**; that assertion was not weakened. Therefore the built-runtime unknown case and cross-branch same-process identity correlation remain **unproven**. This is an unqualified stimulus, not evidence that the product’s unknown-outcome handling failed. No further fault framework or uncertain-write replay was introduced. The owned Gateway/client/state cleanup completed; no model, live channel, production Gateway, or user installation was used.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized built-Gateway observation and source binding</summary>

```text
Plugin state authority is unavailable (reason=overlapping-publication-pending; identityRef=7e74914d876cbbdd; settlement=pending; committed=unconfirmed; installation=unconfirmed). Wait for the pending publication to settle before continuing. Do not replay the write while its outcome is uncertain.
```

The tracked workspace matched head `58e4185df842595a0034b4837d49cb7bcd221892` before and after execution. The maintained `qaRuntime` build and repository E2E runner produced build ID `2026.11.4-58e4185df842-2026-11-18T13-34-22.599Z`; built entry SHA-256 was `6d90382770a71fd23199aceaf95857c3928d7adaee0f7647210a34a8cd1cf2bc`. Build-info uses the supported explicit commit input; local freshness stamps retain the managed checkout’s older guest HEAD and `inputsClean=false`, so this is content-bound runtime evidence, not a clean-checkout stamp attestation or released-package proof. The first fixture attempt stopped at config validation; removing a retired fixture-only heartbeat setting and running canonical Doctor on disposable config allowed the actual Gateway run. All stimuli were synthetic diagnostic checks, not reproduction of the Telegram/OOM incident.

</details>

- Simplification: one private error-construction helper serves the four existing denial sites; no parallel authority owner or diagnostic registry was added. Production delta is +33/-4 lines; necessary test growth covers the two diagnostic branches, real caller privacy, and the review-found singleton-shape case.

Prior-head CI limitation: head `e6ede3437d2046df482e44b8c05c62e9fdafa3de` failed [PostgreSQL conformance (1/4)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44308164326/job/134816046689): the interactive crestodian setup test expected exit 130 but received 1 after the Gateway reported “Originally observed agent target requires its captured creating reference.” The [failure classifier](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44308164326/job/134829252061) labels this **unknown**, with scheduled-main evidence unavailable. The determining test, onboarding process adapter, and agent-execution throw site are unchanged from the tested base; that source comparison alone does not prove an inherited failure. No baseline PostgreSQL reproduction, flake attribution, named upstream repair, or CI waiver is claimed. The current-head success recorded above does not establish the cause or flakiness of this historical failure.

<details>
<summary>Exact focused commands and source</summary>

Base: `427c8572025e099df2674a6bfc2fac74792bf523`. Updated diff SHA-256: `a748c5fa92e1883e9a365d8851bc9230442389d683799b078262229dc26a4b7d`.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-state/plugin-state-publication.reconciliation.test.ts src/plugin-state/plugin-state-native-binding-facts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
GOMAXPROCS=2 node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
GOMAXPROCS=2 node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.state-logging.json --incremental

git diff --check 427c8572025e099df2674a6bfc2fac74792bf523 --
```

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled worktree cleanup logs a summary at info level even when nothing needs attention. One operator counted 1,175 empty summaries in 31 days.

## User Impact

Operators can still inspect empty passes with debug logging. Routine logs continue to show actual cleanup and deferrals, and partial failures remain visible as errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already has the outcome at the point where it logs scheduled cleanup. It now selects the level from that result, keeping maintenance activity, scratch cleanup deferrals, and unknown or exceeded limits visible. This addresses the worktree cleanup part of the report.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on upstream by driving the scheduled Gateway maintenance callback with a simulated clock. An idle pass produced no debug summary.
- On the fix, the same test confirms an empty pass logs at debug only, then a removal logs at info. The existing partial-failure case still logs at error.
- The new regression took 80 ms. The full maintenance test file passed all 38 tests in 99.79 s including setup and transformation.
- The two additional suites covering telemetry and SQLite snapshot maintenance passed all 10 tests (33.64 s). Targeted lint reported zero warnings and zero errors.
- Core typechecking, formatting and git diff --check passed. Independent Codex review through P2 found no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix: stop stale file writes after session database replacement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Replacing an agent's session database could leave tools from a retained background session able to modify files. The existing database-replacement regression on main demonstrated the stale write.

## User Impact

Retained sessions refuse host file mutations after their database is replaced. Already-admitted calls keep the existing permission-change behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry explicit storage preparation from the session-generation owner through tool admission and host write, edit, and patch operations. The session worker validates the physical database; the final mutation check uses the retained in-memory admission. This restores the storage fence without synchronous filesystem/SQL probes or ambient permission rechecks.

The write owner also absorbs redundant outer directory creation. The remaining adapters preserve the same storage capability.

## Evidence

- Existing main failures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44773320124/job/136417317466 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44783201838/job/136452097158.
- Reproduced on base `1129d4c0716c7dcc6fba86753ec214584ec8ebd1`: replacing the database let the retained write change `original` to `completed`.
- Fixed production admission regression passes on isolated Linux/Node 24.22.1: the write reports `SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE`, and the original file remains intact. The other 33 session-event cases passed unchanged.
- 16 host-write integrity tests, 15 source-authority tests, native generation checks including the no-main-thread-probes case, and 62 Gateway, session-event handoff, cron admission, and harness lifetime tests passed.
- Four compiler scopes and formatting of all 24 changed files passed. The final source change after those runtime checks only renames a shadowed local variable.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete committed range `1129d4c0716c7dcc6fba86753ec214584ec8ebd1..106f70f194fe5d4ddace1972b1cf112a9dc22104` with high reasoning: no actionable correctness findings; security cleared. The reviewer did not execute tests.

- Exact-head CI on the original candidate passed the build and final lint checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44790529249.
- Refreshed onto `31ce94f0ad89639e4cf3a0b77edddb0a010f6aaa` because the UI comparison used newer baseline inputs. The full database patch is byte-identical before and after the native refresh.
- Corrected the X retirement assertion to accept either existing owner guard, retaining checks for no child creation, no extra public share, and no success reply.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete refreshed range `31ce94f0ad89639e4cf3a0b77edddb0a010f6aaa..a7b20c4e814b81133eed786ecacccf183529b77d` at high reasoning: no actionable correctness or security findings. The reviewer did not run tests.

- Exact refreshed-head CI passed the UI differential and the X production-owner test (1/1): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44794144114. Production/test types, core/general lint, and dependency checks passed.

The exact-head manual CI run completed with five failing test jobs plus its aggregate gate. Four test jobs match stale admitted-call expectations repaired in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202655. The remaining real-Gateway test rejected the synthetic key correctly but took 2.745 seconds against its 2-second limit (job https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44794144114/job/136490200232). That Save/auth/probe path performs a zero-tool isolated completion and does not call the changed session/file storage hook; its source inputs are unchanged by this patch. The latency cause remains unresolved; no threshold was raised and no repair is claimed. Normal PR CI [44796218464](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44796218464) has also completed: 53 successful jobs, 25 skips, five test failures and the failed aggregate gate. Four node jobs have the same stale admitted-call expectations repaired in PR202655. The fifth is [route asset requests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44796218464/job/136497502162): plugin and skill readiness timeouts plus 32 requests against a 31-request skill-settings limit. These browser tests use mocked Gateway responses and do not execute this storage admission path. The complete UI and scripts/lib trees and all four failing node test files are identical between baseline and the tested two-parent merge. Their causes remain visible; this PR claims no fix for those browser failures.

prs.title: fix: resume new chat turns in retained tasks after a restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A restart could leave your new request unanswered in a chat kept from a finished task. Recovery went to the old parent chat instead.

## User Impact

If a graceful restart interrupts a user’s request, the Gateway resumes it automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

The input that started the turn determines where it resumes: a direct request stays in its own chat, and a delegated task stays with its parent. The existing requester and access checks are unchanged.

## Evidence

An isolated production Gateway accepted `chat.send` and shut down while a real Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct model was generating its reply. Before the fix, recovery marked the parent and the task got no answer. After the fix, one continuation answered in the task and none answered in the parent.

**Stable upgrade:** v2026.11.6 wrote an interrupted root-chat marker without `directChat`. The fixed Gateway opened the same database, answered that root chat once, and cleared the marker. The kept task’s identity, label, transcript, thinking setting, and both existing tool restrictions were unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal output and checks</summary>

```text
Before — 5c15d796c6b6
shutdown_marker: task=False parent=True fields=
gateway_admitted_restart_inputs=1; model completed; both chats idle
after: task_replies=0 parent_replies=1 recovery_model_requests=2

After — fixed runtime
gateway_admitted_restart_inputs=1; model completed; both chats idle
after: task_replies=1 parent_replies=0 recovery_model_requests=1

Upgrade — v2026.11.6 → fixed runtime
shutdown_marker: task=False parent=True fields=queuedInputIds
gateway_admitted_restart_inputs=1; model completed; both chats idle
after: task_replies=0 parent_replies=1 recovery_model_requests=1
retained_task_identity+label+requester_tool_limits+thinking+transcript=preserved; markers=consumed
```

All 82 focused tests passed on `f7b01f83319b`, including identical chat keys in different databases. Runtime build, core typecheck, lint, and formatting passed. The latest change is documentation only; formatting passed for that file. [CI for `f1f9608be294`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44799607066).

</details>

Reported by @VACInc.

prs.title: fix(ci): publish performance reports through pull requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled performance reports fail to publish because `clawgrit-reports/main` requires pull requests. All three publishers in [the failed run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44679926102) received GH013 when pushing directly to `main`.

## User Impact

Performance reports reach their existing repository through its required PR flow. Report contents and artifact-only release validation remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the generated-PR publisher for branch, PR, and exact-head squash-merge ownership. Scope its existing App tokens and GitHub operations to the report repository, with one branch per producing run and lane. Queue each lane through publication so concurrent runs cannot race on its latest pointer. Remove the separate direct-push retry loop and obsolete fixtures.

Wait for known mergeability before requesting a merge. The destination currently disables auto-merge and requires PRs with zero approvals, no status checks, and no merge queue. The GitHub CLI immediately merges a clean PR; a request that would require deferred auto-merge fails. This serialization relies on those current destination rules. No permissions or rulesets are changed.

## Evidence

- Original failures: [mock deep profile](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44679926102/job/136106148673), [live OpenAI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44679926102/job/136106148752), [mock provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44679926102/job/136106148754).
- Reproduced the concurrent latest-pointer conflict in the shared publisher. The queue regression fails on the old workflow. Final focused validation passed: four publisher/performance/release guard suites, 374 tests passed and 8 skipped; all 11 locale-finalizer consumer tests passed.
- PR CI exposed an environment-ordering issue in the generated publisher fixture. The existing multi-path case reproduces it before repair; all 28 generated-publisher cases pass after preparing the fixture before expression resolution.
- Workflow validation, scoped TypeScript lint, syntax, formatting, and the tooling test typecheck passed. Both tooling and scripts test typechecks passed after correcting the assertion context.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete `cc849dd810e3642f5e73b47b8886dd804c05ba32..ca96021d9ef686b6b63ffa6d5971aa44e37a2215` range with high reasoning effort. Its earlier pointer-race finding is addressed by lane serialization. Its remaining deferred-merge finding is declined for the current destination policy described above, independently rechecked against the live API and [GitHub CLI merge behavior](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.103.3/pkg/cmd/pr/merge/merge.go#L593). Security review cleared.
- [GitHub documents the queue setting](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency); the narrowly scoped actionlint allowance follows existing repository policy for this unsupported linter field.
- Simplification removed the separate publication/retry owner: production/config/docs +81/-152 lines; test/support +89/-332 lines against the base.
- The extra full `ci-git-owner` consumer run was stopped after an unchanged release-ancestry fixture recursively invoked its fake Git executable. Its task-owned process group was terminated; this remains an investigated local test gap outside the publisher change. The four targeted publisher suites passed separately without that fixture.
- A successful natural report publication remains the live proof requirement after landing. Hosted PR CI remains the broad pre-merge gate.

prs.title: test(prompt-cache): extend the prefix journey with cron, steer, overflow and a concurrent chat on five transports
prs.body:
## What was wrong

The prompt-cache journey is the CI check that each provider request in a chat extends the previous request byte for byte, except where a rebuild is expected. It skipped four triggers that real chats hit: a scheduled job that comes due in the chat, a user message steered into a running tool call, tool results that fill the context window, and an unrelated chat that compacts while this one runs. It also covered only three transports. A break in any of those paths could land without CI noticing.

**Example:** a scheduled job sent its reply to the model twice on every route. On Chat Completions and Gemini the copy merged into the next tool-call message, which rewrote history and lost the cache from that point on. Fixed in #201838. This journey would have caught it.

## Fix

- Adds the cron, steer, tool-result overflow and concurrent-compaction steps to the stability journey. It now runs on five transports: Anthropic, Responses, Chat Completions, Gemini and Bedrock.
- Adds a seeded randomized journey: 15 turn kinds on five transports, plus a variant with Tool Search turned off.
- Lists the breaks main still has, each with its owner. Entries expire: when a fix lands, the journey fails until its entry is removed. Each entry checks the whole request, so a known change cannot hide a second one.
- Rebuild steps are excused only when the rebuild actually happened. A compaction must put its new summary into the next request, and a model switch must make the next request come from the selected model.
- The steer step holds the tool open until the Gateway reports that the run has taken the steer. Before, it slept for a fixed 3 s.

## Numbers

| | main (before this PR) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Triggers covered | ordinary turns, tools, compaction | + cron, steer, tool-result overflow, concurrent compaction, cron-first chat, 15-kind randomized journey |
| Transports | 3 | 5 |
| Stability journey | n/a | 5/5 |
| Randomized journey (default seeds, 6 files) + negative controls | n/a | 12/12 + 5/5 |
| Anthropic and Tool Search off, seeds 1 and 6 | n/a | 2/2 and 2/2 |

<details><summary>Breaks still on main (accepted entries)</summary>

| Where | Change | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini, tool-result overflow (other chat) | the pre-request pressure check trims tool results that were already sent | #199530 |
| Bedrock, randomized | a dropped silent reply merges the user turns around it | accepted gap (#201654 closed) |
| Tool Search off, randomized | a provider switch adds `skills_read`/`skills_search` on turns started by a subagent completion or inter-session message | #201710 / documented exception of the opt-out surface |

Removed because their owners landed: the cron reply twice (#201838), the Chat Completions silent-turn merge (#201843), the cron-first `message` growth (#201710), and the skills rebuild after `config.patch` (issue #202150, which no longer reproduces on Anthropic seeds 1 and 6).
Bedrock refuses `cron.add` for AWS-SDK auth by design, and the journey expects that refusal.
</details>

<details><summary>Steer signal</summary>

- The steer is sent with `queueMode: "steer"`, as the chat composer sends it. The test waits for `sessions.changed` with reason `agent.input.steering`, which the Gateway emits when the active run accepts the steer into its queue. The tool is released only after that event.
- On all five transports the event arrives about 200-260 ms after the send is acknowledged, while the tool is still held.
- Negative control: releasing right after the acknowledgment lost the race on Gemini (1/5). The steered input became a separate turn.
- A default `chat.send` steer exposes nothing before release. Its pending input stays `queued` with no `steerNow`, and `agent.input.steering` only fires when the tool ends. So the step uses the composer's steer path.
</details>

<details><summary>Rebuild evidence checks</summary>

- Compaction: the fake numbers each compaction summary. The step needs a new summary, and the turn after it must contain that summary.
- Model switch: the alternate provider has its own model id. Every request after the switch must name exactly the selected model, read from the request body or the URL (Gemini, Bedrock), and at least one request must arrive.
- Teeth: with `sessions.compact` turned into a no-op, all 10 randomized seeds failed. With `sessions.patch` pinned to the first model, all 10 failed too.
</details>

<details><summary>Cron-first red on base</summary>

On the parent of #201710 with this PR's test files (no entry), the cron-first step fails on Anthropic and Responses at the owner turn's tool list (`at: 1, change: tools`). On main the step passes.
</details>

<details><summary>Harness fixes</summary>

- Each seed uses its own session keys. A retained subagent from the previous seed made every turn fail with `Retained subagent payload is unavailable`.
- After a silent reply, the fake acts only on the newest step marker, because main drops silent replies from replay.
- Every request is assigned to its session by its runtime line. A request from an unexpected session fails the journey.
- The Advisor fork check is dropped. Forks never arrived in earlier runs. When they did arrive, their requests differed from the parent's on all transports, which needs its own investigation.
</details>

<details><summary>Gates</summary>

- `ocx test` from source with an in-process Gateway and fake provider endpoints: 5 stability files, 6 randomized files and the known-breaks unit, 17/17. Anthropic and Tool Search off at seeds 1 and 6, 2/2 each. A second stability pass, 5/5.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files, and the test-lines ratchet all pass.
- Local review on this head: patch is correct, no findings.
</details>
