prs.title: fix: reuse prepared plugin configuration during agent runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pricing preparation and lazy agent middleware repeatedly derive plugin configuration facts already owned by the current generation, causing avoidable allocation and CPU work.

## User Impact

Less allocation during agent preparation, preserving pricing, plugin enablement and registration behavior across config replacement. No configuration, schema, dependency or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pricing prepares the existing installed-plugin enablement predicate once per requested pricing context, instead of rebuilding it for each manifest. Its normalized policy comes from the existing config owner; mutable control-plane inputs remain fresh. Runtime inventory can outlive a requested policy, so pricing must still evaluate that policy rather than trusting boot-time enabled bits. The existing pricing-context cache owns reuse.

The normalized plugin-policy owner retains registration hashes by both runtime and authored-source policy identity. The loader, registry binding and provider resolver consume that owner; physical source and workspace scope remain in the enclosing loader key. Production grows by 30 lines for explicit paired ownership inside existing snapshot records, without a separate global cache, timer or persistence.

## Evidence

Both regressions fail against pinned base `af65923ec1b4b683443bd86eb129d538dfaf7967`: three runtime/source pairs derive 6 hashes instead of 3, and two requested pricing policies over retained inventory prepare activation 6 times instead of 2. Requested enable/disable outcomes are preserved. The pricing test also rejects the superseded candidate that trusted stored inventory enablement.

Owner/sibling tests passed 122 cases; the corrected pricing suite passes all 31. Policy normalization's unchanged suite passes 61. CI repairs pass 24 wrapper tests, 5 registration tests and 2 macOS-supported provisioning cases; Linux-only provisioning remains for CI. Full static import-cycle guard is green. Core and affected test types, formatting and scoped lint pass. Final staged Codex autoreview is scoped-clean P0–P2.

Five fresh serial A1/B/A2 rounds of the corrected candidate, 2,000 warm operations after 100 warmups; 44 synthetic plugins, eight agent configs and a real file-backed lazy middleware plugin. Node 26.12.1 cumulative V8 allocation includes collected objects. Each arm verifies outputs and records source hashes and host load. This is in-memory owner proof, not whole-Gateway/storage-scale proof. The written acceptance rule predates measurement: correct output/reload behavior, lower warm CPU/allocation, cold/warm separation, no affected metric regressing more than 20%.

| Flow / phase | Metric | A1 median / max | Candidate median / max | A2 median / max |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| pricing / cold | wallMs | 4.740 / 4.910 | 2.397 / 3.061 | 4.691 / 4.937 |
| pricing / cold | mainCpuMs | 4.795 / 4.961 | 2.458 / 2.952 | 4.750 / 4.975 |
| pricing / cold | processCpuMs | 18.288 / 19.778 | 9.921 / 15.003 | 18.474 / 19.355 |
| pricing / cold | Allocation MB | 6.299 / 7.167 | 1.206 / 1.600 | 6.389 / 6.745 |
| pricing / warm | wallMs | 1879.158 / 1953.291 | 420.887 / 429.253 | 1870.725 / 1931.752 |
| pricing / warm | mainCpuMs | 1868.183 / 1942.073 | 416.508 / 424.519 | 1862.111 / 1919.639 |
| pricing / warm | processCpuMs | 2000.580 / 2082.850 | 527.005 / 540.617 | 1994.180 / 2058.657 |
| pricing / warm | Allocation MB | 4957.995 / 4959.218 | 969.980 / 971.053 | 4960.157 / 4963.551 |
| middleware / cold | wallMs | 35.332 / 95.307 | 34.288 / 42.249 | 34.211 / 36.285 |
| middleware / cold | mainCpuMs | 34.449 / 94.795 | 33.928 / 34.761 | 33.560 / 35.657 |
| middleware / cold | processCpuMs | 53.563 / 116.625 | 51.830 / 53.252 | 51.327 / 54.546 |
| middleware / cold | Allocation MB | 16.574 / 21.255 | 15.479 / 17.049 | 16.069 / 19.011 |
| middleware / warm | wallMs | 201.039 / 203.622 | 68.183 / 72.510 | 195.950 / 197.175 |
| middleware / warm | mainCpuMs | 200.671 / 203.247 | 68.096 / 72.021 | 195.554 / 196.761 |
| middleware / warm | processCpuMs | 232.873 / 239.496 | 100.429 / 116.211 | 229.294 / 230.932 |
| middleware / warm | Allocation MB | 200.671 / 202.189 | 111.144 / 112.052 | 203.163 / 205.930 |

Maximum is the empirical p95 of only 5 samples, not a service-tail estimate. Relative to A1 medians, warm pricing allocation improves 80.4% and main CPU 77.7%; middleware allocation improves 44.6% and main CPU 66.1%. Cold medians improve against A1. Candidate cold middleware wall maximum 42.249 ms is lower than A1's 95.307 ms and 16.4% above A2's 36.285 ms; A/A cold spread is retained. No final cell exceeds the 20% gate.

The original candidate's five pairs remain retained as superseded evidence: it violated pricing policy correctness and had cold middleware max 55.887 ms. The final implementation required a fresh complete measurement; no sample from either set was dropped. The old tail-acceptance request was not answered and is not counted as approval.

Reproduction:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/plugin-config-rederivation-measure.mjs \
  --owner "$CHECKOUT" --fixture-root "$SCRATCH" --iterations 2000
```

Run baseline/candidate/baseline serially five times. Separate 5,000-operation CPU profiles show inclusive registration derivation 384.650→0.467 ms, entry normalization 2564.965→56.393 ms, pricing builder 4312.115→521.678 ms, and middleware entry 624.504→196.860 ms. These samples are attribution only, not acceptance timing. No changed production module is imported under ui/src.

`pnpm check:changed` is red only for three independently reproduced main dead-export regressions: settingsParentRoute after #202521 (`b7b72dc5`), and installSpawnAttachmentFixture/installSpawnThreadBindingFixture after #202522 (`c23cb9f0`). Clean exact parent reproduces all three. Every other selected check passed. These are reported main regressions, not ignored noise.

Initial CI found PR-caused wrapper inventory and type-import-cycle omissions. The wrapper inventory now includes the hash helper; its type import points directly to the existing shared definition. The actual CI checkout is `3e247d3890af3179cf283a44390017b568e48807`, with main parent `28dafe848af537769acc869ed7370098f026c1d2` and PR head `7a0f6ac86dd614fd612d4251a492c5d1ef847225`. A clean checkout of that exact main parent reproduces the identical extra path. PR #202428 (`5ec2039594b3b07826f5e2a30d80609d3ff601b9`) deleted the test but retained it at `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs:211`. The failing test, inventory and planner are unchanged between baseline and tested merge. This is a new main regression requiring repair, not noise; this lane leaves it attributed and uses the authorized inherited-failure route. CI is not described as green.

Final-head ClawSweeper has zero findings and zero open checklist items. Native evidence binds the exact failed attempt, checkout, reproduction, introducing commit, unchanged sources and aggregate failure.

Expedia Travel showed a generic plug on its chat install card. Its ClawHub package has no icon of its own, but its publisher profile supplies the Expedia Group logo.

## User Impact

When a plugin has no catalog icon, its chat card can now show the publisher’s image. A plugin’s own artwork still wins, and the generic plug remains when no usable image is available. Installation and permissions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The details page already knows about the publisher image. The chat card read the same catalog response but discarded that field. It now passes the fallback URL to the existing authenticated image loader; there is no new endpoint, direct browser request to the publisher, or brand-specific logic.

## Evidence

The real Control UI in Chromium rendered the same Expedia recommendation on base `09bef75c4ff` and candidate `c03a3a8ac65`. The fixture used Expedia’s public ClawHub detail response, the actual publisher PNG, and a simulated Gateway transport. No plugin was installed. prs.title: chore: separate managed playback test coverage
prs.body:
Related: #191517

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway playback coverage was mixed into the native-client fix in #191517. This requested split lets reviewers assess the Gateway test organization and its test-line allocation independently of the two native fallback expressions.

## User Impact

There is no production behavior change. The tests continue to protect managed-media publication, scoped downloads, byte ranges, and playback preparation/recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Playback cases move into a focused suite using one shared HTTP/mock fixture with the remaining managed-attachment tests. The busy-inspector case follows the real publication and ticketed HTTP owners from absent metadata through original bytes, preparing, and the ready rendition; ffprobe/ffmpeg I/O remains a fixture, not real codec proof. Existing non-playback coverage stays in its original suite.

### Explicit maintainer approval for the split and baseline

On November 9, 2026, the maintainer explicitly requested moving these six paths out of #191517 into a separate PR, with justification and explicit baseline approval in its body. This PR carries exactly that authorized test work: the existing 135-line `native-media-unknown-playback.txt` allocation and the removal of three obsolete closed-mock entries from `test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`. The allocation is unchanged; the scalar baseline, exclusions, assertions, and production code are not relaxed. The shared mocks preserve real module exports instead of creating new baseline exceptions.

This is approval to publish the split, not approval to merge this PR.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.test.ts src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.playback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **46/46 passed**, two suites, 58.12 seconds total (55.13 seconds in Vitest). The extended busy-inspector recovery case passed in 56 ms.

- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base HEAD --staged`: **passed**, 6,354 grandfathered factories. No new exception was added.
- `git diff --check` passed. Independent review of the complete extraction found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Validation ran on the new composition based on main `8633af9341852740eb176d22840a46c521064a1b`. Earlier #191517 results are not substituted for this proof. Broad CI remains pending. This is a test-only extraction, so no production red/green mutation or new live codec/device run was performed.

issues.title: [BUG] WebUI channel secret fields get overwritten with the WebUI access password by browser autofill

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Every channel credential input in the WebUI is autofilled with the saved **WebUI access password** by the browser's password manager, and pressing Save writes that value into `config.json`, silently destroying the real credential.

The inputs are rendered as plain text inputs with `autocomplete="off"`:

- `webui/src/components/settings/channels/CredentialForm.tsx:236` → `autoComplete={field.secret ? "off" : undefined}`

Chrome ignores `autocomplete="off"` for credential-like fields. Because the WebUI login form is declared as `autocomplete="current-password"` (`webui/src/App.tsx:236-237`) and its password is `channels.websocket.tokenIssueSecret`, Chrome offers to save that password and later autofills it into **every** channel secret input: Telegram bot token, Email IMAP/SMTP password, WeCom secret, Slack tokens, etc.

The field is masked, so the UI looks unchanged — the corruption is only discovered on the next gateway start, when the channel fails with `bot token rejected by Telegram`, and every other channel saved through the same page shares the same broken value.

Impact: silent credential corruption with a misleading screen state; irreversible unless the user happens to have a backup of the original secret.


### Steps to Reproduce


```
1. Run nanobot 0.4.1 with the WebUI reachable over HTTP(S); log in with the access
   password and accept Chrome's "Save password?" prompt.
2. Open Settings → Channels → Telegram. Do not type anything in the bot-token field.
3. Chrome autofills the bot-token input with the stored WebUI access password.
4. Click Save.
5. ~/.nanobot/config.json now has channels.telegram.token = the WebUI access password
   (19 chars, no "bot_id:" prefix) instead of the real "<bot_id>:<secret>" token.
6. Restart the gateway → the Telegram channel fails to start (logs below).
7. Email / WeCom / Slack settings render through the same component
   (CredentialForm) and the same manifest field type, so saving them from the same
   browser session overwrites imapPassword / smtpPassword / secret the same way.
   (Telegram is reproduced end-to-end; the other channels are source-level findings.)
```


### Expected Behavior


- Secret inputs must never be autofilled by the password manager. Use `autocomplete="new-password"` (Chrome honours it; `"off"` does not), or give each field a unique non-credential `name` attribute.
- On save, refuse or at least warn when a secret value equals `channels.websocket.tokenIssueSecret` or another channel's secret.
- Optional but useful: validate the shape of well-known secrets at save time (e.g. Telegram bot token `^\d+:[\w-]{30,}$`), so a corrupted value is rejected in the UI instead of at the next restart.

### Relevant Logs

```shell
2026-11-20T14:16:19.405+0800 | INFO  | -        | Telegram channel enabled as telegram
2026-11-20T14:16:19.660+0800 | INFO  | telegram | Starting bot (polling mode)...
2026-11-20T14:16:21.108+0800 | ERROR | telegram | bot token rejected by Telegram
2026-11-20T14:16:21.108+0800 | ERROR | -        | Failed to start channel telegram
RuntimeError: Telegram bot token was rejected by the server
  File ".../nanobot/channels/telegram/runtime.py", line 659, in start
    raise RuntimeError("Telegram bot token was rejected by the server") from None

config.json before/after (redacted):
- "token": "8607714666:AAE********************************"
+ "token": "<webui-access-secret>"          # 19 chars, no "bot_id:" prefix

After restoring the real token, opening the same WebUI settings page and pressing
Save once reproduces the corruption again.
```

### nanobot Version

0.4.1

### Python Version

3.12.14

### Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), x86_64 — gateway running on bare metal, no container

### Channel / Platform

Websocket (WebUI); affected settings pages include Telegram, Email, WeCom, Slack

### LLM Provider

OpenAI-compatible custom provider

### Model

deepseek-v4.1-flash

### Browser

Google Chrome, desktop stable, password manager enabled for the WebUI origin (exact version not recorded)

### Connection

Remote host — WebUI served over HTTPS and proxied to the gateway

### Configuration (Optional)

```yaml

```

### Additional Context

Every credential input in the WebUI shares the same defect (`main` branch, snapshot 2026-11-20; line numbers from that snapshot):

| Settings page | Location | Control | `autoComplete` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Login password (entry point) | `webui/src/App.tsx:236-237` | password/text | `"current-password"` |
| Channel credentials (Telegram / Email / WeCom / Slack / …) | `webui/src/components/settings/channels/CredentialForm.tsx:236` | text (secret) | `"off"` |
| Linear OAuth / client secret | `nanobot/channels/linear/webui/LinearSecretField.tsx:93-94` | password/text | `"off"` |
| Model provider API key (existing provider) | `webui/src/components/settings/models/ProviderSettings.tsx:832` | password/text | **not set** |
| Model provider API key (new custom provider) | `webui/src/components/settings/models/ProviderSettings.tsx:1004,1014` | password/text | `"off"` |
| Web search API key | `webui/src/components/settings/capabilities/WebSettings.tsx:186` | password/text | **not set** |
| MCP preset secrets | `webui/src/components/settings/system/McpManagementDialog.tsx:664` | password/text | **not set** |
| Network proxy password | `webui/src/components/settings/shared/SharedProxyEditor.tsx:48` | password | `"new-password"` (the only correct one) |

Out of 24 `autoComplete` usages in the WebUI source, exactly one uses `new-password`. In the 0.4.1 channel manifests, 14 channels declare 23 `field("secret")` entries, so the blast radius covers nearly every channel.

Verification status: the Telegram path is reproduced end-to-end (save → restart → `token rejected`); the provider / web-search / MCP rows are source-level findings, not yet reproduced in a browser.

Backend notes:

- Empty secrets already have the right semantics: `coerce_channel_value` returns `_SKIP_FIELD` for `kind == "secret"` with an empty value (`nanobot/webui/settings_system.py`), so "leave blank to keep the current value" works. The gap is that autofill supplies a **non-empty** value, which the backend cannot distinguish from a deliberate edit.
- Changing `config.json` alone does not rebuild the channel; the config watcher only calls `invalidate_runtime_config()`. The value is applied on the next channel enable/restart, which is why the damage surfaces later rather than immediately.
- This still reproduces on `main`: `CredentialForm.tsx:236` still uses `autoComplete={field.secret ? "off" : undefined}`.
- Related but different: #6191 refactors these inputs into a shared `SecretInput`; whatever the outcome, the autocomplete attribute should be `new-password` there as well.

prs.title: feat(webui): edit and resend messages in the same session
prs.body:
**Hold for performance.** Editing is functionally verified, but the end-to-end edit did not meet the frozen baseline. Across 64 pairs it was 9.27 ms slower at the paired median (95% interval +3.27 to +14.12 ms); its acknowledgement alone was 1.57 ms faster. Not ready for approval.

Related to [NAN-92](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92/webui-支持编辑并重新发送已发送的用户消息).

## What users get

In a saved topic, **Message actions → Edit message** opens an inline draft. **Cancel** preserves the conversation and composer. **Resend** replaces the selected message and its suffix and generates a reply in the same topic. **Fork** still makes a separate topic. This does not undo external tool effects. Only persisted plain user text is editable; attachments, quotes, mentions, commands and special inputs are not silently converted to plain text. [User guide](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/e42f74689b0e41915d0c7d52939092cd50f4b062/docs/webui.md#edit-a-sent-message).

## Correctness

- One owner serializes ordinary input and edits. The SQLite transaction checks the page-independent source identity, original text, revision and retry receipt, then changes both model history and display history. Admission failure leaves the old histories intact. Once accepted, a model failure belongs to the new turn. A transport retry does not schedule a second model request.
- **White-box:** reviewed admission/dispatch, cancellation, storage/crash boundaries, outbound ownership, HTTP pagination and frontend draft/connection lifecycle. Fixed canonical `input_id` on replacement and a late idle event that could leave its original run marked active. The late event releases only that owner and does not publish into a replaced history. Final focused Python selection: 81 passed.
- **Black-box:** two Chromium clients, production-built UI, real local gateway/SQLite/WebSocket and a deterministic HTTP model. Mouse, keyboard and touch; cancel with an outstanding composer draft; middle, first and paginated edits; reload and actual disconnect/reconnect. The provider saw exactly 3, 0 and 174 retained user inputs respectively, followed only by the edited input, once per edit. Older retained rows remained pageable; the topic/identity did not change. Two editors of the same revision produced one winner; reconnect/retry, busy/stale source, provider refusal and ordinary fork were checked independently. No uncaught browser exceptions. No physical device or external model was used.
- **Formal concurrency check:** [two TLA+ models, assumptions and reproduction commands](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/tree/e42f74689b0e41915d0c7d52939092cd50f4b062/verification/history-edit). All invariants held over 484 admission states and 132 delayed-delivery/reconnect states, with no unexpected deadlock. Removing transactional source validation or the retired-generation fence gave the expected counterexamples. These are bounded single-owner models assuming atomic SQLite commits, not an exactly-once guarantee for external side effects.

## CI and snapshots

[Test Suite 44722331397](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/44722331397) passed, including `CI required`. PR head `e42f74689`; Actions checked out `5a0fd420d`, merging that head onto `db0306b40`. The local correctness and timing runs use the PR head; ordinary timing uses its frozen integration parent `cd75dbfaa`, not moving main. No check or size/coverage budget was relaxed. Attempt 1's Windows native upgrade/recovery test reached the second `metadata-loss` journey, then `inspect_profiles()` raised `ValueError` while checking readiness after the second restart. The exact target's push CI skipped native acceptance. The preceding PR candidate passed the same step. Only that Windows job and downstream aggregate were re-requested on the unchanged merge; the original failure is not attributed to the edit without evidence. [First attempt's failure report](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/44722331397/artifacts/14624090600).

<details><summary>All seven performance gates, sample variation and diagnosis</summary>

### Performance

**Performance is not signed off:** Latest page, 8 turns, Latest page, 192 turns, Ordinary input → completed reply, Navigate → latest message painted, Edit → completed reply. Do not treat passing CI as performance approval.

Windows, real same-version gateway/WebUI with a deterministic loopback model. Ordinary operations vs `cd75dbfaa` (integration parent); edits vs `d06d326ad` (previous edit implementation). Four fresh gateway pairs, 16 measured pairs each, per metric. Snapshots on the same volume. AB/BA balanced at startup and randomized within adjacent pairs; warmups excluded, no other observations discarded. Reads decode eight real HTTP responses per observation. Render requires the expected message in view followed by an animation frame. Edit replaces turn 49 of 96, with one provider execution and the exact retained prefix. All durations are ms.

| Path | Baseline median | PR median | Paired Δ [two-sided 95% interval] | One-sided upper / margin | Gate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Latest page, 8 turns | 13.21 | 14.36 | +0.88 [-0.28, +1.62] | +1.54 / 1.00 | Not established |
| Latest page, 192 turns | 14.70 | 15.27 | +0.64 [-0.51, +1.60] | +1.19 / 1.00 | Not established |
| Ordinary input ACK | 6.07 | 5.85 | +0.05 [-0.38, +0.53] | +0.48 / 1.00 | Pass |
| Ordinary input → completed reply | 70.04 | 72.48 | +1.91 [-1.51, +6.17] | +5.22 / 5.00 | Not established |
| Navigate → latest message painted | 99.65 | 95.45 | -0.15 [-7.80, +7.20] | +5.30 / 5.00 | Not established |
| Edit ACK | 13.19 | 10.79 | -1.57 [-2.25, -0.85] | -0.92 / 1.00 | Pass |
| Edit → completed reply | 86.31 | 100.96 | +9.27 [+3.27, +14.12] | +14.02 / 5.00 | Not established |

The gate is the one-sided 95% upper bound on the paired median delta (candidate minus baseline), strictly below max(5% of the baseline median, 1 ms for reads/ACKs or 5 ms for completed turns/render). Intervals use 12,000 deterministic stratified bootstrap draws across observations within the four blocks. Cross-block and machine-to-machine variability, tails, physical-device latency and the latency of an external model are not bounded by this test.

On the previous `aa18f9e45` snapshot (48 pairs; gateway blocks separated in time), short/long reads had paired medians +1.67/+2.24 ms and upper bounds +2.80/+3.43 ms vs a 1 ms margin. Ordinary ACK, paint and edit completion also failed to establish non-inferiority. Profiling identified a duplicate SQLite snapshot-header lookup. This candidate reuses immutable headers only within one transaction and sends the regular 40-event page after replacement, with a cursor for the rest. The previous samples were retained, not pooled.


| Path | Baseline / candidate block medians (ms), in measurement order | Min–max of all samples: baseline / candidate (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Latest page, 8 turns | 19.14 / 20.84; 11.75 / 14.21; 13.03 / 12.07; 12.95 / 12.93 | 6.92–24.56 / 6.77–26.59 |
| Latest page, 192 turns | 22.50 / 17.84; 13.20 / 14.74; 12.98 / 12.78; 14.03 / 14.99 | 7.40–25.67 / 8.04–26.99 |
| Ordinary input ACK | 5.75 / 6.21; 7.06 / 7.07; 5.77 / 5.41; 5.77 / 5.77 | 4.70–24.72 / 4.66–37.74 |
| Ordinary input → completed reply | 66.80 / 70.06; 84.42 / 92.85; 68.16 / 69.86; 67.26 / 69.63 | 59.76–114.63 / 59.57–130.79 |
| Navigate → latest message painted | 90.60 / 90.45; 102.80 / 108.55; 102.30 / 100.40; 92.70 / 90.90 | 65.50–163.60 / 67.20–149.50 |
| Edit ACK | 11.10 / 10.02; 12.36 / 9.92; 16.95 / 13.63; 13.63 / 12.48 | 10.03–25.28 / 7.71–186.72 |
| Edit → completed reply | 74.88 / 87.17; 78.57 / 82.53; 114.81 / 123.42; 93.31 / 109.56 | 68.64–346.62 / 70.84–463.34 |

**Where to investigate next:** on an equal 48-input context, the interval between the fixture provider returning and the client receiving `turn_end` was 16.8–16.9 ms (old edit), 23.6–24.7 ms (candidate edit), and 22.6–24.6 ms (ordinary input on the integrated main baseline), as ranges of two diagnostic block medians. Independent tracing found prompt-context observation and four display-history appends on both current main and the candidate, versus two appends on the previous edit implementation. This explains a candidate path to optimize; it does not assign the full end-to-end difference to one function. Recheck the shared delivery path on a quiet runner without dropping context graphs, persistence or generation checks. In ordinary HTTP reads the candidate already makes fewer SQL statements (25/37 vs 27/39), selects the same 24/42 records, and does not load full model history. These diagnostics do not override the failed timing gates. [Raw paired timings and a relocatable Windows benchmark harness](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92#comment-e64c8f32-6625-410f-b27e-ac69baf99db7).

</details>

prs.body:
## Why
Changing how the composer palette opens meant finding its animation in `globals.css`, then finding the reduced-motion and forced-colors exceptions separately. prs.title: feat(webui): collapse long user messages exceeding half viewport height
prs.body:
## Summary
- Collapse long user text bubbles in `MessageBubble` (`UserTextBubble`) by default whenever their natural height exceeds **50% of the visible thread viewport height** (falling back to `window.innerHeight` outside `ThreadViewport`, with a `200px` minimum threshold floor).
- Fold triggered bubbles down to **38% of the viewport height** (`160px` minimum floor), providing built-in hysteresis so messages that barely cross the half-screen threshold still fold meaningfully (~3–4+ lines saved) without awkward micro-collapses.
- Replace generic chevron arrows with a quiet **stacked paper edge** beneath collapsed user bubbles (two tucked, inset rounded hairline sheets that subtly fan on hover and fold smoothly into the bubble on expand) paired with a plain text `Show more` / `Show less` toggle localized across all 10 supported locales (`message.expandUserMessage` and `message.collapseUserMessage`).
- Fade the bottom edge of collapsed text using CSS `mask-image` on the clipped inner text wrapper rather than an opaque gradient overlay, keeping light mode, dark mode, temporary dashed bubbles, pending/sealing edge overlays, and custom-wallpaper frosted-glass surfaces seamless (with `mask-image: none` under `forced-colors: active`).
- Preserve the existing `[data-user-text-bubble] > p` DOM contract, context menu alignment, `data-thread-disclosure` auto-scroll handoff, `prefers-reduced-motion`, full-text copy while collapsed, `ResizeObserver` updates on window/font-size changes, and scroll anchoring back to the bubble top when collapsing from the bottom of an expanded message.

## Screenshots

### Desktop Light (Collapsed vs. Expanded)
| Collapsed (stacked paper edge, default for > 50% viewport height) | Expanded (scrolled to bottom toggle) |

| ![Desktop light collapsed](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/chengyongru/7293a9f5be1a018d88bf4e70ea8baaea/raw/85b776005ee050ba4e081062a7177e7e952cbc43/desktop-light-collapsed.png) | ![Desktop light expanded](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/chengyongru/7293a9f5be1a018d88bf4e70ea8baaea/raw/85b776005ee050ba4e081062a7177e7e952cbc43/desktop-light-expanded.png) |

## Verification

prs.title: fix(chat): preserve routing for side-channel command replies
prs.body:
Resolves [NAN-476](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-476/修复-dream-与-pairing-命令截断-webui-流式回复丢失历史或脱线程)

## Why

Running `/dream`, `/dream-log`, `/dream-restore`, or `/pairing` while WebUI is streaming can erase the visible answer prefix. These replies also lose the context needed for WebUI history and for replies to stay in the originating Slack thread or Telegram topic.

## What changed

- Keep the request's reply routes and history generation on all four commands, including the background Dream result.
- Mark their WebUI replies as side-channel messages in both live delivery and history. Give the delayed Dream result its own WebUI identity so it can arrive after the command's `turn_end` without inheriting that turn's sequence or replacing a new answer.

## Verification

- Reproduced the metadata loss and the interrupted WebUI answer in regression tests before the fix.
- 48 focused Python tests and 274 WebUI tests passed, including a Dream result delivered and replayed after `turn_end`. WebUI build, typecheck, targeted lint and import boundary checks passed.
- Slack and Telegram route metadata is covered by automated regressions; no live workspace or bot was used.

prs.title: fix(webui): prevent sign-in autofill in channel credentials
prs.body:
## Why
Chrome can treat a channel token or password field as a sign-in field and fill it with the saved WebUI password. Saving then replaces the channel credential; Telegram can fail on its next start.

## What changed
Mark the shared channel form's secret inputs with `autocomplete="new-password"` so password managers can distinguish them from the WebUI sign-in field (`current-password`). Saving another setting still omits blank secrets, and users can still enter a replacement.

## Scope
No gateway or login changes. The fix uses the browser's credential semantics rather than comparing secrets from unrelated services. Password-manager extensions may apply their own rules.

## Verification
- The saved-channel autocomplete regression failed before the change and passed after it. Channel settings: 35 tests passed, including existing manual entry coverage and the new assertions that changing an IMAP host does not submit either mail password. The two focused sign-in tests also passed.
- Production WebUI build passed. In headless Chromium against an isolated gateway, both Email password fields rendered empty with `autocomplete="new-password"`. The desktop Chrome password-manager flow with an already-saved login password was not exercised.

Fixes #6732
Resolves [NAN-474](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-474/prevent-webui-sign-in-autofill-from-replacing-channel-credentials)

prs.title: fix(webui): gate focus indicators on keyboard navigation modality
prs.body:
## Problem

In WebUI, non-navigation keyboard events during or after pointer interactions — such as holding `Shift` while clicking "View changes" (`file-edit-diff-toggle`), pressing `Escape`, or pressing modifier shortcuts after clicking a button — caused browsers to widen `:focus-visible` and draw unexpected black focus outlines.

Two issues amplified this:
1. Browsers flip `:focus-visible` on any keyboard event (including modifier key repeats, `Escape`, and shortcuts), so previously pointer-focused controls suddenly lit up. The codebase had accumulated multiple per-component workarounds (`surfaceFocusProps`, `pointerFocus`, `hideEditorReturnFocus`) that only covered individual widgets.
2. Several native `<button>` elements (including the four diff action buttons in `FileEditRow.tsx`) lacked explicit `focus-visible:*` styles and fell back to the browser's raw UA `outline: auto`.

## Root-Cause Fix

- **Global focus modality owner (`webui/src/lib/focus-modality.ts`)**: tracks `html[data-focus-modality="pointer" | "keyboard"]` in capture phase across the app, gallery, and browser fixtures.
  - Pointer input (`pointerdown` / `mousedown` / `touchstart`, including `Shift+click`) sets `pointer` modality.
  - Explicit keyboard navigation and activation keys (`Tab`, `Shift+Tab`, arrows, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Enter`/`Space` on non-text controls, plus `Tab` and single-line `<input>` `Enter` submission) set `keyboard` modality.
  - Pure modifier keys, `Ctrl`/`Meta`/`Alt` shortcuts, and `Escape` in `pointer` modality stay quiet, while `Escape` during keyboard navigation keeps `keyboard` modality intact.
- **Unified CSS/Tailwind gating (`webui/tailwind.config.js`, `webui/src/globals.css`, and custom CSS files)**:
  - Gates `focus-visible`, `group-focus-visible`, `peer-focus-visible`, `has-focus-visible`, and hand-written `:focus-visible` rules on `:where(:root:not([data-focus-modality="pointer"]))` while exempting text-entry inputs (`textarea`, `[contenteditable]`, text-like `input`).
  - Adds a design-system `:focus-visible` fallback outline in `@layer base` and suppresses UA/base outlines on non-text-entry controls in `pointer` modality.
  - Adds explicit `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring` to the diff toggle/action buttons in `FileEditRow.tsx`.
- **Structural cleanup**: removes now-redundant local workarounds (`webui/src/lib/surface-focus.ts` and its 5 callers, `pointerFocus` in `LanguageSwitcher.tsx` and `ModelAPIControl.tsx`, and `hideEditorReturnFocus` in `ModelsSettings.tsx`).

## Verification

- `npm run lint` — passed (0 warnings)
- `npm run typecheck` & `npm run typecheck:browser` — passed
- `npm run build` — passed
- `vitest run src/tests/focus-modality.test.ts src/tests/sidebar-hover-css.test.ts` — passed
- Added unit tests in `webui/src/tests/focus-modality.test.ts` and a browser regression test in `webui/browser/file-diff.spec.ts` (to be executed in CI browser shards; local environment has no Chromium binary installed).

Resolves [NAN-475](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-475)

labels.description: Installer, updater, packaging, wheels, doctor

issues.body:
### Summary

Since Hermes switched to staged runtime venvs under `~/.hermes/installs/.../venv` (Python 3.14), a
`hermes update` rebuilds that venv with only the core dependencies. Native provider plugins (e.g.
`mnemosyne`) keep their *tools registered*, but their Python dependencies are gone. The failure is
completely silent: memory simply stops working on every profile.

### Observed behavior (v0.21.5+8673, git install, Linux, Python 3.14.7)

- After `hermes update` (201 commits pulled), all agent sessions report
  `{"status": "memory_unavailable", "reason": "Mnemosyne not initialized"}` — the tools exist, the
  provider can't import its core.
- `hermes plugins doctor` reports **OK** ("import, and registration passed") because its probe runs
  against the *old* 3.11 venv (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv`), not the staged runtime venv.
- Worse silent failure: plugin config readers that catch `ImportError` (e.g. mnemosyne's PyYAML-based
  `profile_isolation` check) fall back to defaults — profile-isolated banks were bypassed and new
  memories written to the wrong DB path. No log line anywhere points at the cause.
- The staged venv has **no pip**, so `mnemosyne-hermes install` cannot bootstrap itself into it.
- `hermes mnemosyne stats` (plugin CLI) errors `No module named 'mnemosyne'` for the same reason.

### Expected behavior

Either (a) plugin dependencies declared in plugin manifests get installed into the staged runtime
venv during `hermes update` / venv rebuild, or (b) the plugin system surfaces a loud, actionable
warning (doctor + gateway startup) when a provider's core module cannot be imported in the *runtime*
venv — and doctor's import probe must use the same interpreter the gateway actually uses.

### Workaround currently in production

External daily systemd timer that import-tests the staged venv, reinstalls plugin deps via
`uv pip install --python <staged-venv> mnemosyne-memory==3.11.1 mnemosyne-hermes==0.3.1 PyYAML fastembed sqlite-vec cryptography`,
and restarts gateways — plus a hook at the end of the local update script. Works, but shouldn't be
necessary.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a native provider plugin whose Python package lives in Hermes' venv (e.g. mnemosyne).
2. Run `hermes update` (pulls enough commits to rebuild the staged venv).
3. Ask the agent to call any tool of that provider → provider unavailable.
4. `hermes plugins doctor` → green, masking the failure.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.5+8673.g90a7ccc (2026.9.24), install method: git
- Linux 6.8.0-146-generic, Python 3.14.7 runtime venv (staged), legacy venv: Python 3.11.15
- Gateway: systemd (user) units, 6 profiles

issues.body:
## Bug Description

After an update that ended with a fleet restart, every CLI invocation keeps printing:

```
⚠ A previous `hermes update` pulled new code but did not restart running gateways.
  Gateways may still be serving pre-update modules (mixed sys.modules).
  Run `hermes update` or `hermes gateway restart`.
```

The warning is wrong: the gateway was restarted and its runtime status reports
`code_sha = <checkout HEAD>`, `code_version = 0.22.5`. It cannot be cleared by restarting, because the
host obligation (`~/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/host-update-restart-<install>.json`) records the
same gateway PID twice — once mapped, once as an unmapped stop — and
`_marker_only_restart_obsolete()` can never satisfy both entries.

Recorded inventory (verbatim, from the record this host kept armed after a successful restart):

```json
{"kind": "gateway", "profile": "default", "pid": 912, "supervisor": "launchd",
 "code_sha": "4d04303818b61bf3aa09278af48356315515965b", "code_version": "0.22.4",
 "restart_via": "launchd", "detail": {}}
{"kind": "gateway", "profile": null, "pid": 912, "stopped_unmapped": true}
{"kind": "gateway", "profile": "default", "pid": 8555, "supervisor": "launchd",
 "code_sha": "bf0203a794a07aac3ff764972ab9087baa4e4f4e", "code_version": "0.22.5",
 "restart_via": "launchd", "detail": {}}
```

Same PID (912) appears as an identified gateway and as `stopped_unmapped`. The record also carries a
`restarted` stamp for the expected SHA, which the readers do not consult.

## Steps to Reproduce

Deterministic, without needing a real update — the obligation is public API
(`hermes_cli/update_host_obligation.write_host_obligation`):

1. Have one launchd-supervised gateway, live, on the checkout HEAD (`hermes gateway status` → current).
2. Arm the obligation with an inventory that names that live gateway once mapped and once as
   `{"kind": "gateway", "profile": null, "pid": <same pid>, "stopped_unmapped": true}`
   (this is the shape `_record_owed_gateway_inventory` produces when the unmapped sweep stops a PID
   that the update plan already knew as a mapped profile gateway).
3. `hermes gateway restart -y` — the gateway comes back on HEAD, `gateway_state.json` shows the
   correct `code_sha`.
4. Every `hermes --version` / `hermes gateway status` / `hermes auth list` still prints the ⚠ block.
5. `_fleet_restart_obligation_armed()` stays `True` and `_marker_only_restart_obsolete()` stays `False`
   forever. Only `clear_host_obligation()` silences it.

Note: run the probe with `hermes-agent/venv/bin/python`. The launcher interpreter
(`~/.hermes/tools/python-<ver>/python3`, no `ruamel.yaml`) and `/usr/bin/python3` (too old) hit the
`try/except` in `_marker_only_restart_obsolete()` and return an *empty* fleet, which looks like a
second, unrelated failure while debugging.

## Expected Behavior

After the fleet is proven current on the pulled SHA, the obligation discharges and the warning stops —
even when the inventory contains an `stopped_unmapped` row for a PID that no longer exists (and even
more so when that PID is the same one an identified row already covers).

## Actual Behavior

The warning is permanent. The mapped entry is covered by the live gateway; the unmapped entry has no
identity to match, and the rule below refuses to let a live gateway be its successor because the
mapped entry already explains it — `covered - owed` is empty, so the function returns `False` on every
check:

`hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet.py:430` (v0.22.5)

```python
if owed and _UNMAPPED_GATEWAY in owed and not (_fleet_covered_gateways(
        [row for row in fleet if not row_is_external(row)]) or set()) - owed:
    # An unmapped stopped gateway has no identity to match, so only a local gateway that no
    # mapped owed one explains can be its successor; another checkout's gateway never is.
    return False
```

## Affected Component

- Other: update / fleet-restart bookkeeping (CLI startup warning)

## Environment

- OS: macOS 27.0.1 (Darwin 26A434), launchd-supervised gateway
- Hermes: v0.22.5, commit `bf0203a794a07aac3ff764972ab9087baa4e4f4e`, install method git
- Python: 3.14.9 (launcher) / 3.11.16 (`hermes-agent/venv`) — reproduces with the venv interpreter
- Single profile (`default`), one gateway, no serve/dashboard runtimes

## Root Cause Analysis

1. `hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet_verify.py:132 _record_owed_gateway_inventory()` builds the owed set as
   *mapped gateways from the update plan* + *one `stopped_unmapped` row per PID from
   `restart.stopped_unmapped_pids`*. There is no de-duplication: when the unmapped sweep in
   `update_cmd_fleet.py` stops a PID that the plan already knew as a mapped profile gateway (the
   `profile_processes` / `unrestartable_pids` path), the same physical process is owed twice.
2. `hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet.py:303 _marker_owed_gateways()` turns the mapped row into
   `("gateway", "default")` and the `stopped_unmapped` row into `_UNMAPPED_GATEWAY`.
3. `_marker_only_restart_obsolete()` (`hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet.py:354`) requires every owed
   identity to be covered by the live fleet, and additionally (line 430) requires that the live
   gateway covering the unmapped obligation is *not* one a mapped owed entry already explains. With a
   single gateway both conditions can never hold at once → fail-closed deadlock. The `restarted`
   stamp written by a successful restart is never read by this path.

## Proposed Fix

Either (or both) of these, both local to the bookkeeping:

1. **De-duplicate at write time** (`_record_owed_gateway_inventory`, `update_cmd_fleet_verify.py:132`):
   drop a `stopped_unmapped` row whose PID already appears in the mapped rows — the process is
   already named, so a second obligation adds nothing:

   ```python
   mapped_pids = {row["pid"] for row in rows if row.get("profile")}
   rows = [row for row in rows if row.get("profile") or row.get("pid") not in mapped_pids]
   ```

2. **Or discharge at read time** (`_marker_only_restart_obsolete`, `update_cmd_fleet.py:430`): treat a
   live gateway at HEAD as the successor of an unmapped row when the unmapped PID is one an owed
   mapped row already names (same PID), instead of requiring an unrelated local gateway.

The first is the cleaner fix: an unmapped row only carries information for a process nothing else
named.

## Workaround

Clear the record once its debt is provably paid — `expected_sha` equals checkout HEAD and every live
runtime is `current` on that SHA — via `hermes_cli.update_host_obligation.clear_host_obligation()`.
Back up the JSON first. A daily watchdog script that applies exactly that check and otherwise leaves
the obligation alone keeps the warning from accumulating.

issues.body:
**Repro**
From the hermes-agent tree:
```
python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/ -p my_plugin
```
instead of pytest loading the plugin, the run aborts with:
```
Profile 'my_plugin' does not exist. Create it with: hermes profile create my_plugin
...
INTERNALERROR> ...
```
The repo's CLI argparse consumes `-p` as `--profile` even in the pytest invocation path (and `pytest.main(..., plugins=[...])` direct call works fine).

**Impact**
Any custom pytest plugin/fixture module must bypass CLI parsing entirely; standard pytest workflows (`-p no:cacheprovider`, `-p xdist`) are unusable from the tree.

**Suggestion**
Namespace or disable the profile short flag when argv[0] is pytest, or don't install the CLI-level argparse for library test runs.

issues.title: web_server_lifecycle PORT_IN_USE sentinel os._exit(75) hard-kills pytest batches when a real service holds the port

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
**Repro**
With a real dashboard/gateway service listening on the expected port, run:
```
python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/ -q
```
Mid-batch, accumulated service threads/fixtures collide with the real port → `hermes_cli/web_server_lifecycle.py` (`PORT_IN_USE_EXIT_CODE = 75`) calls **`os._exit(75)`**, terminating the whole pytest process instantly (no summary, RC=75). Single-file runs pass; it is sequence-dependent.

**Impact**
The sentinel (designed for supervisor consumption) makes the module untestable in-service and self-destructs full test batches. We had to wrap `os._exit` in a conftest-level runner to convert it into a per-test failure.

**Suggestion**
Raise a typed exception (or call `sys.exit` only in the CLI entrypoint path) instead of `os._exit(75)` deep in the library layer, so tests can assert the code without killing the batch. Same for the gateway watchdog copy of the constant.

issues.title: Signal/process-lifecycle tests SIGTERM their own process group and kill the whole pytest run (RC=143, no summary)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P2

issues.body:
**Repro (batched run of tests/hermes_cli/)**
```
python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/ -q --tb=line
```
The run dies at a deterministic progress point with exit code **143 (SIGTERM)** and **no pytest summary**. Two separate full-suite runs died at the same 24% mark with identical early output.

**Diagnosis**
Certain `signal`/process-governance tests send SIGTERM to their **own process group** as part of the test scenario. Inside a single pytest process this delivers SIGTERM to the runner itself. We also found 19-hour-old orphaned test-fixture processes (`python -c "import signal, subprocess, sys, time; child=..."`) left behind by these tests.

**Impact**
Full-suite runs cannot complete; batch must be re-run as per-file isolated pytest invocations to survive.

**Expected**
Tests that exercise SIGTERM handling should target a child process only (e.g. `start_new_session=True` on the child), never the runner's process group, and should reap their fixtures in teardown.

issues.title: [Bug]: pm gc deletes an IN-USE install state whose recorded project-root is stale — active launcher breaks (data loss)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Symptom

`hermes pm gc` deletes install-state directories it classifies as orphans, but the orphan test (pm/install_states.py `_is_orphan`) only checks the recorded `inputs/.project-root` path and a retention window — it never checks whether the state is ACTIVELY IN USE. An install state whose recorded project-root has gone stale (e.g. it recorded a generation-local workspace path that a later generation rotation removed, or a path that a cleanup removed) is deleted even when:

- `/usr/local/bin/hermes` (or an equivalent launcher) points directly at its `environments/<id>/venv/bin/hermes`,
- processes are running from that venv,
- the state was used minutes earlier.

## Repro

1. Fresh pm-managed install; note `/usr/local/bin/hermes` → .../installs/<id>/environments/<gen>/venv/bin/hermes.
2. Cause the state's `inputs/.project-root` to reference a path that no longer exists (observed in production after an install-state generation rotation removed the recorded workspace path).
3. Run `hermes pm gc`.
4. The whole install state (venv, workspace, built products) is removed; `/usr/local/bin/hermes` becomes a dangling symlink; running services from that venv break.

Production log line: `gc: removed 0, kept 11; ... removed 1 install state dir(s) of deleted checkouts` — twice in a row, deleting two states including the live one.

## Expected

gc should treat a state as live if any of: a launcher/symlink resolves into it, a lease exists (the code already checks `_leased` for the removal step but the candidate listing/ordering still reaps states whose only fault is a stale root record), a running process holds an executable inside it. Stale-root states should be reported for manual review rather than deleted when they carry an active venv.

## Actual

Live install destroyed; recovery required from a sibling checkout. The message "of deleted checkouts" is misleading: the checkout was not deleted, only its recorded root path.

## Notes

Related (but distinct): #125537 (gc collects nothing due to install-key measurement), #129300 (Windows hardlink aborts collection), #138033 (stale stamped roots). This issue is the destructive case: the state IS collected, wrongly.

## Summary When a remote Desktop (macOS, SSH backend) reconnects to a host with many profiles, it starts one `hermes --profile

serve --isolated` for **every** profile within ~35 s, including profiles the user has not opened. On a box with 22 profiles that is 22 servers at 210-600 MB RSS each (~5.5 GB) plus their startup CPU, where a moment before the reconnect there was one. ## Observed (v0.23.3, Linux host, 2026-11-21) - 05:16 one `serve --isolated` alive; the gateway then sat in `update_paused` until 05:19:54. - 05:19:48-05:20:23: 22 `serve --isolated` processes, each a distinct `--profile` (one per profile under `~/.hermes/profiles` plus default), each with its own `--ssh-owner-nonce`, all from the same `SSH_CLIENT` (the Desktop), all reparented to pid 1. - No duplicates per profile, so this is fan-out, not a leak; but it is the largest memory consumer on the host after the gateway. ## Expected Backends start lazily, for the profile the user opens (and maybe the last-used one), and an idle backend retires after a timeout. A reconnect after a fence should not start more servers than were running before it.

issues.title: Dirty source checkout: any plugin-set change (e.g. a new profile) re-runs the full source-update tail and fences the gateway for 15-25 min

labels.name: type/perf
labels.description: Performance improvement or optimization

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/install-update
labels.description: Installer, updater, packaging, wheels, doctor

labels.name: area/profiles
labels.description: Multi-profile isolation, HERMES_HOME scoping

issues.body:
## Summary

On a self-updating source install whose checkout carries a local diff (`git status` dirty), any change to the
install-wide plugin dependency set makes the next launch run the **whole source-update tail**
(`hermes_cli/source_completion.py --finish-update`: product builds, launchers, maintenance) under the checkout
lock. That takes 13-25 min here. Meanwhile the gateway answers every new launch with `draining / update_paused`,
and every other launch prints `an update is still running`. Creating or deleting one profile is enough to trigger it.

## Observed (v0.23.3+118.g5b3cb30.dirty, Linux, 2026-11-21)

- Dependency environments rebuilt at 03:54, 04:07 and 04:31 (`installs/<key>/environments/*`). The workspace
  `pyproject.toml` files differ only by `plugin-deps/hermes-mobile-push-<hash>` / `plugin-sources/hindsight-<hash>`
  members: a profile (`tiertest`, born 04:23:27; `sephprobe`, born 04:30:50) entered or left the live-profile set.
  `dependency_homes()` (pm/plugins_state.py:124-146) unions every live profile, and `_member_key`
  (pm/workspace.py:342-350) hashes each home's resolved plugin path, so the stamp changes.
- `venv_is_current` turns False. `prepare_launch` -> `_finish_source_update(current=False)` ->
  `completed = _tree_matches_completed_stamp(root)` is False because the tree is dirty
  (venv_sync.py:367, `stamp.get("dirty") is not False` / `info.dirty`). So `_sync_source_dependencies(arm=True)`
  arms the tail, and the launch runs the full `--finish-update` (04:19 and 04:44 "Update complete!" from a cron
  wake launcher), holding the checkout lock the whole time.
- About 50 minutes of `update_paused`. Cron jobs and new `hermes chat` runs failed. The kanban dispatcher logged
  `ready queue non-empty ... 0 workers spawned`.

## Expected

A dependency re-sync on an unchanged commit should not re-run product builds. The tree is the same tree the last
tail built. Two possible fixes:
1. `write_source_stamp` records a digest of the dirty diff (`git diff HEAD` plus untracked paths), and
   `_tree_matches_completed_stamp` accepts a dirty tree whose digest matches. A local patch (for example, waiting on
   #157896) then stops costing a full tail on every dependency change.
2. Profile churn should not move the dependency set when a new profile enables plugins the union already has.
   Key members by plugin identity and content, not by each home's path, so N homes enabling the same plugin give
   one member.

Related: #145022 / #157896, the local patch that keeps this checkout dirty.

issues.title: check_runtime warns 'install out of sync' on a sealed Docker image: pnpm is never present, and the venv stamp ignores plugin members that runtime discovery adds

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/install-update
labels.description: Installer, updater, packaging, wheels, doctor

issues.body:
On v0.23.1 (image nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.23.1-desktop, sha256:385725287c20...), every CLI dispatch prints to stderr: '⚠ install out of sync (pnpm: not installed or outdated) — this docker-managed install must rebuild the artifact to fix'. Two causes, both in the sealed-runtime check (hermes_cli/venv_sync.check_runtime -> pm.activate):

1. pnpm: the runtime image deliberately leaves pnpm out (only build stages need it), yet pm.drift() reports it as 'not installed or outdated'. A sealed runtime cannot install it. The check should skip packages the sealed image does not ship.
2. venv: pm.build_env --record-selection records the venv stamp with plugin_dirs=[] (pm/build_env.py _record_selection), but the runtime check recomputes it with config-discovered plugin members (Venv.expected_stamp -> members_stamp(build_member_dirs(extras))). Any image that bakes a member plugin (for us: the pinned camofox plugin under /opt/hermes/plugins) or whose config enables a plugin with its own requirements (hermes_otel under HERMES_HOME/plugins) can never match, so the warning is permanent and nothing in a sealed image can fix it. Measured: stamp for the recorded 14 extras with plugin_dirs=[] equals the recorded value; with default discovery it does not.

Ask: on a sealed tree, compare only the core lock and extras (or record the stamp with the discovered members at build) and skip packages the image does not ship, so the warning means something. Today it is noise that hides real drift.

issues.title: [Bug]: opencode-go: glm-5.3 reasoning_effort never reaches the wire — model always runs the relay's default max tier

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Bug Description

`glm-5.3` via the **opencode-go** provider ignores every reasoning-effort preference: `/reasoning low|high|max`, `agent.reasoning_effort`, and per-model overrides never reach the wire, so the model always runs at the OpenCode Go relay's default tier — which is `max`-depth thinking.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.23.2 (local `ae2a81ccc00e`), Windows 10
- Provider `opencode-go`, model `glm-5.3` (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`)

## Root Cause

`plugins/model-providers/opencode-zen/__init__.py` — `OpenCodeGoProfile.build_api_kwargs_extras` dispatches per model family but only knows GLM-5.2 spellings: `_is_glm_5_2_model` matches `glm-5.2 / glm-5-2 / glm-5p2` (added in a6079dd350 on 2026-07-05 — 39 days **before** GLM-5.3's release on 2026-08-14). `glm-5.3` matches no branch and falls through to `return {}, {}` — no top-level `reasoning_effort` is emitted. The `extra_body.reasoning` fallback is also closed on this route: `_supports_reasoning_extra_body()` asks the profile's `reasoning_payload` hook, which `ProviderProfile` defaults to None and `OpenCodeGoProfile` does not override.

So the request leaves Hermes with **no reasoning field at all**, and the relay applies its default.

## Evidence — live probe of the Go relay (2026-11-21)

Probe: openai-python SDK against `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` — the same client stack the gateway uses (`x-opencode-session` header, attribution headers, proxy) — trivial prompt "17*23", `max_tokens=4096`, `temperature=1.0`, reading `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`:

| request | reasoning tokens | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| **no field** (what Hermes sends today) | 31 / 29 / 69 — **mean 43** over 3 runs | 200 |
| `reasoning_effort=max` | 40 / 31 / 79 — **mean 50** over 3 runs | 200 |
| `reasoning_effort=low` | 2 | 200 |
| `reasoning_effort=high` | 7 | 200 |
| `reasoning_effort=medium` | 7 | 200 |

Three facts follow:

1. The relay **accepts** `reasoning_effort` for glm-5.3 and the levels scale monotonically (2 → 7 → 26-79) — the knob works end-to-end; only Hermes's emission is missing.
2. No-field requests land in the same band as explicit `max` (mean 43 vs 50, overlapping ranges) — the silent default is the **max tier**, matching the note in #85890.
3. `medium` is accepted by the Go relay (unlike bigmodel PAYG, where it 400s with code 1210 per #140239) — endpoint vocabularies differ.

## Why this is a bug, not a design choice

- #85890 already stated the behavior in passing ("OpenCode Go … never sends `reasoning_effort` for 5.3, so `/reasoning low` does nothing and you stay on `max`") but its fix covered only the zai PAYG half; the opencode-go half stayed open in practice.
- The identical symptom on the zai route was reported as **#91789** and fixed the same day (30f9955a44) — that fix created `GLM53_EFFORTS` but wired it into the zai profile only.
- The a6079dd350 branch predates GLM-5.3's release, so the omission is a registration gap, not a decision; and f7d90c9410 explicitly classifies "drop left the server default = MORE thinking than asked" as the bug class it exists to remove.

## Expected Behavior

`glm-5.3` on opencode-go gets the same graded mapping the zai profile already has: efforts clamp to `GLM53_EFFORTS` (`xhigh`→`max`, floor `low`), a disable ask maps to `low` (5.3 rejects `thinking.type: disabled`), unset config keeps the server default.

## Related

- #49279 (open feature request: GLM-5.x reasoning for OpenCodeGo — no movement in 4 months)
- #85890 (closed; fixed the zai half only)
- #91789 (the zai-side twin, fixed same-day)
- #140239 (GLM53_EFFORTS still lists `medium`, which bigmodel PAYG rejects — separate endpoint, tracked there)

issues.title: [Bug]: ACP (gateway mode): session/cancel on a still-queued prompt drops its text

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/acp
labels.description: Agent Communication Protocol adapter

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

issues.body:
## Summary

When an ACP client cancels a prompt that is still queued behind a running turn and then sends a new prompt, the gateway-backed ACP adapter withdraws the queued prompt and never runs it, stores it as a message, or attaches it to the next prompt. The in-process ACP adapter keeps a cancelled prompt and merges it into the next one, so the two modes behave differently.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent 0.23.3, commit `caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029`
- `hermes acp` in gateway mode (`GatewayACPAgent`)
- ACP client: Orca 1.4.266
- Linux (Fedora, kernel 7.3)

## Reproduction (any ACP client)

1. Have a turn running in a session (e.g. one Hermes starts for a background-process completion).
2. While it runs, send `session/prompt` A. It is queued behind the running turn.
3. Before the running turn ends, send `session/cancel` for the session, then `session/prompt` B.

**Expected:** A's text is not lost. It either runs or is attached to B, as in the in-process adapter.

**Actual:** A returns `stopReason: "cancelled"` and B runs alone. A never reaches the transcript; its text remains only in `session_admissions` (`terminal`/`cancelled`, no generation).

Orca does this itself when it delivers an automatic message into a running turn: `session/cancel`, then the message as a new `session/prompt`.

## Cause

- `acp_adapter/gateway_server.py:448-457` `cancel()` → `:422-427` `_cancel_admission` → RPC `prompt.cancel`.
- `gateway/session_controls.py:962` → `gateway/session_authority.py:844` `cancel_or_claimed` → `:832` `cancel_queued` → `:859` `_commit_cancel`.
- `persistence/sqlite/authority/_admission_store.py:261-262`: a queued row gets `_CANCEL_QUEUED` (`persistence/sqlite/authority/_runtime.py:143`, `UPDATE … SET status='terminal',outcome='cancelled'`).
- `gateway/session_authority.py:878-891` `_settle_cancelled` publishes an empty completion. `acp_adapter/gateway_server.py:738` returns `cancelled`.
- `acp_adapter/gateway_server.py:679` sends the next prompt as `{'text': text}` with nothing carried over.

A started turn keeps its text: the user message is persisted at turn start (`agent/turn_context.py:1188`, called at `:1414`). Only a cancel that arrives while the prompt is still queued loses it.

## Contrast: in-process adapter

- `acp_adapter/server.py:704-705` saves `current_prompt_text` as `interrupted_prompt_text` on cancel.
- `acp_adapter/server.py:778-779` prepends it to the next non-slash prompt through `:241-242` (`"{interrupted}\n\nUser correction/guidance after interrupt: {next}"`). (docstring `:764-765`: "stop and send" clients).

## Suggested fix

In `GatewayACPAgent`, when `_cancel_admission` withdraws an admission that was still queued, keep its text per session. In `prompt()`, prepend it to the next non-slash prompt before building `submit` (`:679`), using the same format as `server.py:241-242`.

**Side effect:** a queued prompt the user cancels on purpose would also be re-attached to their next prompt. The in-process adapter already does this for a cancelled running prompt.

**Telling the cases apart:** the code offers no reliable signal. `cancel(self, session_id, **kwargs)` uses only the session id, and ACP `session/cancel` has no reason field. Untested options: a client hint in the cancel's `_meta`, or carrying the text over only if the next prompt follows the cancel within a short window.

## Inferred, not proven

- That the observed cancel came from the client's automatic delivery, not a manual stop. Hermes does not log `prompt.cancel`, and `session_admissions` has no timestamp column.
- The fix is neither implemented nor tested.

## Related

#55183 and #130405 concern queued prompts and cancel in the in-process adapter (`HermesACPAgent`); this report is about the gateway-backed adapter, where the queued prompt is withdrawn and its text is lost.

issues.title: Let file-based STT plugins opt into one retry after a rejected audio container

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: tool/tts
labels.description: Text-to-speech and transcription

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
**What we see (v0.23.3)**

A registered transcription plugin already gets the generic preparation in `transcribe_audio`: source validation, remote `.caf` conversion, the generic upload-size limit, compact re-encode and split/join for oversized files. What it cannot get is the **reactive** retry that the OpenAI-shaped path has. When the API rejects a container (a 400 with "unsupported / corrupted / invalid file", or the ambiguous 5xx from #81644), `_transcribe_openai` converts the clip to a 16 kHz mono M4A once and resends it. A plugin's `transcribe()` must return an envelope rather than raise, and nothing in the provider contract lets it ask core for that conversion. So a plugin either imports a private helper (`_transcode_audio_for_stt`) or ships its own ffmpeg handling.

Two smaller gaps, for completeness, and not the main ask:
- the pre-upload silence trim runs only for built-in cloud providers (`CLOUD_STT_PROVIDERS`), and it is best-effort;
- a plugin cannot declare its own byte or duration limit, so it inherits the generic default.

**Our case:** we run OpenRouter speech-to-text as a local patch inside the OpenAI-compatible path, using OpenRouter's JSON `input_audio` request form. On 2026-10-16, with `openai/gpt-4o-transcribe` through OpenRouter, the multipart form ignored our `language` and `prompt` fields; the JSON form with `provider.options.<vendor>.prompt` honoured them. We would like to move this to a plugin, as the project prefers, and the rejected-container retry is the step we would lose.

**Proposal (one backward-compatible opt-in):** a typed *result* rather than a new exception, so the "must not raise" contract stays. For example, a plugin returns `{"success": False, "retry_as": "converted_audio", ...}` (or a small documented dataclass), and core converts once per part, calls `transcribe()` again with the converted path, treats a second rejection as final, never retries authentication or billing errors, and cleans up its temporary files either way. Existing plugins are unaffected.

Would this shape fit the provider contract? We can send a PR with regression tests (old plugin unchanged; opting-in plugin rejected once and receiving one converted path; second rejection final; no retry on auth errors; temp files removed), against wherever the speech code lands after the open refactor in #156570.

issues.title: [Bug]: scratch prune never re-runs inside a long-lived gateway (once-per-process gate), so idle entries pile up

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: backend/local
labels.description: Local shell execution

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/profiles
labels.description: Multi-profile isolation, HERMES_HOME scoping

issues.body:
### Bug Description

The scratch dir (`<HERMES_HOME>/cache/scratch`, which `TMPDIR` points to) is only pruned when a process starts: `get_scratch_dir()` calls `_prune_scratch_dir_once()`, which runs at most once per process and is skipped if `.last_prune` is less than an hour old. A gateway runs cron jobs and sessions inside its own process, so after its first pass nothing prunes scratch again until the next restart. Entries far older than `SCRATCH_MAX_IDLE_HOURS` (24h) pile up until the disk fills.

I checked current `main` (`hermes_constants.py` / `hermes_constants_scratch_detach.py`, last changed in b12b263157 on 2026-10-26). The detached-child change makes each pass finish, but the trigger is still "once per process", so a long-lived gateway is still affected.

### Evidence (4 macOS gateway hosts, 2026-11-03)

In every case the last prune came right after the gateway started:

| Host | Gateway process start | `cache/scratch/.last_prune` | Scratch entries idle > 24h |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 2026-10-28 21:40 | 2026-10-28 22:25 | 389 of 446 entries, ~64 GB |
| B | 2026-10-30 16:57 | 2026-10-30 17:24 | 296 of 584 entries, ~18 GB |
| C | 2026-11-01 13:45 | 2026-11-01 13:56 | (small) |
| D (gateway restarted nightly ~04:11) | 2026-11-03 04:11 | 2026-11-03 ~04:10, daily | (small; prunes every day) |

`logs/scratch-prune.log` on hosts A and B has no entries after those dates. Host A's disk dropped to ~1 GB free, with scratch the biggest single contributor.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gateway continuously (launchd service) with cron jobs and agent sessions writing to `TMPDIR`.
2. Don't start any other `hermes` process on the host for more than 24 h.
3. Check `cache/scratch/.last_prune`: it still has the mtime from right after the gateway started, and `scratch-prune.log` has no new removals, while entries idle for days remain.

### Expected Behavior

Entries idle longer than `SCRATCH_MAX_IDLE_HOURS` get pruned roughly hourly while the gateway is running, as the docstring and the prompt hint ("entries idle for 24h are pruned") say.

### Actual Behavior

Pruning runs once per gateway lifetime. Hosts that never restart the gateway grow scratch without bound.

### Suggested fix

Have the gateway's cron ticker (or another timer in the long-lived process) call the existing hourly-gated path, e.g. `spawn_prune(scratch)` whenever `.last_prune` is older than `_SCRATCH_PRUNE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, instead of gating on `_scratch_pruned_once`. A `hermes scratch prune` CLI command would also let operators schedule it externally.

### Environment

- macOS 27.0.1 (Apple silicon), gateway run as a launchd login item
- Hermes commit bf0203a794 (2026-10-22) on the hosts; the trigger logic is unchanged on current `main`
- Affected components: Gateway, Agent Core (scratch dir)

### Related

- #134896 (named profiles never prune: `_scratch_pruned_once` spent on the default home), same once-per-process gate
- #132401 (closed), #144638 (closed)

issues.body:
## Ask

In the Hermes Desktop chat, allow **branching a conversation like git**: pick any earlier message, fork the conversation from that point into its own line, keep the original line untouched, and switch between lines later.

Typical flow:
- hover an earlier user prompt or assistant reply → "Branch from here"
- the current conversation is saved as-is (the trunk)
- a new conversation opens containing everything up to the fork point (at a **user** message: everything *before* it, ready to re-ask differently; at an **assistant** reply: including that reply, dropping what followed)
- both lines stay listed and reopenable; branches carry lineage (parent id/title + fork point) so the UI can badge them

## Prior art already in the ecosystem

- The agent's own session store already models this: `state.db` sessions carry `parent_session_id`, and `model_config` markers `_branched_from` / `_delegate_from` / `_reset_from` distinguish explicit branches from compression continuations (`hermes_state_common.py`). So the data model largely exists; this is about surfacing it in the Desktop chat UI.
- Community web UIs implement exactly this on top of the agent API: a `/branch` command + per-message fork action (`POST /api/session/branch` with `keep_count`, children marked `session_source='fork'`, sidebar badges for branch lineage). Same UX maps 1:1 to the Desktop chat.
- ChatGPT/Claude-style "edit message → alternate branch" is the familiar consumer-grade equivalent.

## Why it matters

Long agentic conversations accumulate wrong turns; today the only options are regenerate-last or start over. Copy-on-write branching keeps the good context and explores the alternative without losing either line.

prs.title: fix(gateway): refuse a compression-segment id terminally instead of retrying storage_unavailable
prs.body:
## Summary

A client that asks for a compression segment's id polls `storage_unavailable` forever. The receipt lives on the lineage root, so the lookup for the segment id can never succeed, yet the reason says "retry".

```diff
 owned_receipt(sid)
   local_receipt(db, sid)
-    missing -> storage_unavailable   (clients retry every few seconds)
+    missing -> sid is a non-root compression segment whose root has a receipt?
+                 yes -> not_found     (terminal, same as RESUME_GONE handling)
+                 no  -> storage_unavailable (unchanged)
```

Seen on a long-lived local conversation that had compressed three times: the gateway logged `receipt refused: storage_unavailable` in bursts of five every ~5 s, 12k+ lines in one afternoon. The row for the old segment exists in `sessions`; only the root has a `gateway.local_policy.v1` receipt.

Same symptom as #155582 / #153729 / #153739. #155602 covers the deleted-conversation half through the retirement fence and does not touch this case (the segment is not retired), so the two changes are independent.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `tests/gateway/test_local_segment_receipt_terminal.py` with the guard disabled: 2 failed, 2 passed (the two segment cases fail, the unknown-id control still passes).
  **After:** 4 passed. A segment id gives `not_found` through both `owned_receipt` and `restore_local_session`; an id with no row and no lineage still gives `storage_unavailable`.
- Adjacent files, run with the change: `test_local_session_recovery`, `test_local_session_lineage`, `test_session_local_route`, `test_local_authority_transitions`, `test_local_recovery_pre_profile_origin`, `test_session_local_reopen_on_turn`, `test_local_closed_retirement`, `test_local_control_compression_child`: 35 passed, 0 failed.
- One existing assertion changed: `test_a_segment_rewind_keeps_the_owner_busy_gate[segment]` accepted `{session_busy, storage_unavailable}`. A rewind by segment id is now refused with `not_found`, so I added it to the set. The test still checks that nothing was rewound.
- Not run: the full test suite. I ran only the files listed above.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** callers that address a compression segment by id. They now get a terminal `not_found` where they got a retryable `storage_unavailable`. A retry could never have succeeded, and `session.resume` on the root id is unchanged.
