prs.title: feat(desktop): distinguish monitoring from active agent work
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Distinguish **actively working** from **waiting for background work** in the Desktop sidebar. A CI watch can outlive the agent's reply: the session is not finished, but the agent is not actively working either. The extra indicator should explain that state, not repeat the existing working animation.

Enable **Filters → Show → Monitoring** for a compact, steady waveform with the reported task label in its hover/keyboard tooltip:

- Active parent or delegated agent: existing working arc; no monitoring waveform.
- Idle parent with awaited background work: monitoring waveform; session stays out of Done.
- Completion accepted for follow-up: active-work styling returns.
- Follow-up finished: normal finished/unread state.
- Silent long-lived servers: no monitoring obligation merely because a process exists.

The indicator does not add a subtitle, increase row height/sidebar width, or displace PR, age, or action controls. This is an opt-in display preference, not a session filter.

## Related Issue

No issue claimed as fixed. This updates the original feature in the same PR rather than creating a duplicate. Related scope: #103370 (different status-dot treatment), #67674 (separate background-work panel), #105335 (Working/Done grouping), and #105337 (PR discovery).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- Sidebar activity now projects only explicit background notification obligations, not live tool calls, subagent labels, command-name guesses, or historical transcript entries. Active parent/subagent and attention states retain precedence through the shared status resolver and runtime/stored/lineage mapping.
- Preserve the original opt-in preference, accessible tooltip, compact row geometry, and store-owned background polling. All locale labels now say Monitoring.
- `process.list` adds `notification_pending`. Reserve notification obligations before fast process exit or first watch-hit publication; retain them across dequeue, foreign-owner deferral, busy requeue, and finished-process pruning until accepted delivery or deliberate suppression/consumption.
- Reuse existing delivery acknowledgments across Desktop, CLI, and messaging gateway. No new model tools, RPC methods, dependencies, or prompt changes. Tracking is process-local, not durable notification replay across backend restarts.
- Keep polling and monitoring alive for exited-but-undelivered results. Neither automatic dismissal nor the finished-row Dismiss button can hide those pending results. Stop/rewind remain explicit cancellation actions.
- Working/Done grouping treats monitoring as unfinished without giving it an active-work animation.

## How to Test

1. Enable **Filters → Show → Monitoring**. Start an awaited background task, such as a completion-notifying check watcher.
2. While the parent or a delegated agent is working, verify the normal working arc remains and no extra waveform appears.
3. Let the parent yield. Verify the steady monitoring waveform and task tooltip appear, including while viewing another chat or after closing the idle originating tile.
4. Start a silent preview server separately; it must not become Monitoring merely because it remains running.
5. Finish the awaited task. Verify pending delivery cannot prematurely move the session to Done or be dismissed; follow-up work restores active styling, and final settlement clears monitoring.
6. Check the opt-in preference, row actions, PR controls, and Working/Done grouping.

### Verification performed

- Full Desktop UI + Electron suite: **9,518 passed, 6 skipped**. After the final pending-dismissal fix, the monitoring/composer/polling suite was rerun: **45 passed**.
- Renderer/Electron/E2E TypeScript checks, production Desktop build, changed-file ESLint, and whitespace checks passed.
- Python regression run via `scripts/run_tests.sh`: **1,960 passed, 4 skipped across 133 files**, excluding one known baseline failure described below.
- Two new parameterized backend invariants cover **20 cases** using real processes, real `process.list`, and delivery/post-turn seams. All 20 were observed failing on the archived base and passing with the fix; the final targeted rerun also passed.
- Real isolated Linux dev Desktop: active work → background-only monitoring → switch to another session with a silent server → completion-triggered active follow-up → finished/unread. Registry and renderer state were checked, and no page errors were observed. The final dismissal interaction also has a real-component regression test and independent re-review.
- The integration uses a credential-free scripted local provider and real local processes, **not live GitHub CI or external model inference**.
- Known baseline failure: `test_model_options_preserves_canonical_custom_row_after_agent_init` exposes an unexpected `anthropic` provider and also fails on the unchanged base. It is excluded from the regression count above; the full Python suite is not claimed green.
- macOS/Windows runtime validation and the full Python suite were not run.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] Read the contributing and scoped engineering/design guides.
- [x] Conventional commit messages; focused feature changes only.
- [x] Existing PRs checked; original PR updated instead of duplicated.
- [x] Behavioral tests added and independently reviewed.
- [x] Tested in a real isolated Linux Desktop app.
- [ ] Full Python suite — not run; targeted regression results and baseline exception disclosed above.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Component/store lifecycle comments and all locale labels updated.
- [x] CLI config examples: N/A; Desktop display preference remains renderer-owned.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered; native runtime testing is Linux-only.
- [x] No new model-tool schema or prompt changes.

## Screenshots / Logs

Cropped real dev-app rows showing the same session during active work, background-only monitoring, and final unread completion. The fixture contains no private user content. Screenshot metadata, code diff, commit message, and PR text were scrubbed for credentials, private paths, rig ports, and task/session identifiers. The uploaded screenshot was downloaded and its bytes verified. Evidence lives on a separate fork-only branch, not in the code diff.

![Real Desktop: active work, monitoring only, and finished unread](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zeus-Deus/hermes-agent/eda95481f4326bfed4e6463d05d3578f98eb2f77/monitoring-comparison.png)

prs.title: feat(desktop): title chat branches from their first follow-up
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Give Desktop/TUI branches a title that describes their new direction instead of keeping the parent's numbered name indefinitely.

The inherited title is provisional. The first follow-up triggers one background title request using that message, the inherited title, and a bounded excerpt near the branch point. Subsequent turns leave the name stable. Explicit user titles always win, including renames made while generation is in flight.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- Mark automatically inherited titles in both `session.branch` and seeded `session.create`; preserve explicit names as user-owned.
- Atomically claim the first follow-up and retain the inherited title as a fallback. Provider failure or a later short/compacted history does not trigger repeated renaming.
- Limit background context to recent user/assistant text, excluding system prompts, tool output, reasoning fields, and non-text attachments. Keep the request outside the main conversation so prompt caching is unchanged.
- Preserve the owning profile context on the background title worker.
- Add two parameterized behavior tests using real SQLite storage and RPC dispatch; update existing branch test doubles and documentation.

## How to Test

1. Create a titled session in Desktop, branch it, and send a follow-up that changes direction. The sidebar updates without a reload; the parent stays unchanged.
2. Send another follow-up: the title stays stable. Rename manually: future turns preserve that name.
3. Disable `auxiliary.title_generation.enabled`, or make the title provider fail: the inherited name remains.

### Verification performed

- Regression tests were shown red before the implementation, then green, including manual rename races, disabled generation, provider failure, compacted-history replay, profile context, and both branch RPCs.
- **980 tests passed** across seven relevant files using `scripts/run_tests.sh`, excluding two unrelated failures reproduced on the unchanged base:
  - `TestFTS5Search::test_search_projection_skips_context_enrichment_queries`
  - `test_model_options_preserves_canonical_custom_row_after_agent_init`
- The unchanged base comparison produced **896 passed, 2 failed** in the two affected broad test files; this patch does not change those subsystems.
- `scripts/check_compat_pointers.py` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Electron development main bundle built successfully.
- **Live isolated Electron integration check:** real renderer, gateway, agent, auxiliary HTTP client, and SQLite, using a deterministic local fixture provider with no live credentials. Observed a contextual branch title arrive in the sidebar, read it back from storage, and verified that later turns and a manual rename stayed stable. This proves integration, not real-model title quality.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide and checked existing PRs; this is branch-specific, not periodic retitling of ordinary sessions.
- [x] Changes are limited to this feature, tests, and documentation.
- [x] Added behavioral regression tests and tested on Linux.
- [x] Updated session documentation; no new configuration keys, tool schemas, or dependencies.
- [ ] Entire test suite passes (not claimed; focused results and base failures are documented above).
- [x] Reviewed the diff and local screenshot evidence for credentials, personal paths, local ports, and session identifiers. Rig files and raw logs are not included.

Actual isolated-dev sidebar captures, before the first follow-up and after title generation (deterministic fixture provider). The full resulting title is `Hide disconnected sidebar labels`; the narrow sidebar truncates it visually. Only this sanitized comparison is published, on a separate assets branch; rig files and raw logs are excluded.

prs.title: fix(desktop): draw a running turn once when a long chat refreshes mid-turn
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Running prompt shows once. Before: Refresh: live copies kept; Transcript: prompt drawn twice. After: Refresh: matched by send id; Transcript: prompt drawn once. Change: submission_id ↔ user-<id>.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2dc85232-9411-410c-8140-774471b4ff87)

## What does this PR do?

In a chat longer than one transcript page, reopening it while a turn ran drew that turn's prompt twice, with the finished tools under the first copy and the running reply under the second, until a reload. Now it draws once.

A running turn stores its prompt and finished tool rounds before `message.complete` brings the receipt. The newest page starts inside an older turn, so the refresh takes the stored-id merge (`mergeOverlappingTail`), which appended the window's live prompt and stream after the page's stored copies. The pending-turn reconcile then saw both live rows present by id and never paired them.

Points to review:
- **Identity, not text.** The stored prompt carries `display_metadata.submission_id` (`4c333e0d49`); the live prompt's id is `user-<submission_id>`. Hydration carries that id, `withoutLiveTurnsThePageStores` drops the stored live prompt and everything trailing it from `previousTrailing` (matching the short-chat boundary so `preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages` / `reconcileDurableHistory` re-attach live streams and queued follow-ups in order even when a queued prompt or interim bubble sits after the running turn, `39d89f7434`), and `optimisticUserMatchesCommitted` in `optimistic-user-dedup.ts` matches by `submissionId` too so a stored prompt whose text differs from the optimistic row isn't re-appended. A send the page doesn't store, even with a stored prompt's exact words, keeps its place.
- The first commit moves `withWebapp` into the e2e harness unchanged.
- Merge order: #149557 edits the same `previousTrailing` expression; whichever lands second applies both filters.

Not covered: after a reopen without an `inflight` snapshot, the running reply's unstored tail can hide until the next delta, and the finished rounds can briefly draw twice. Short chats share that reconcile; it's left for a follow-up.

## Related Issue

Refs #145333. #135094 §2 reports the same symptom.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project ui src/app/chat/transcript-backfill.live-turn.test.ts` (on `main` the long-chat cases draw the prompt twice).
2. `pnpm run build:webapp && npx playwright test -c e2e/core/playwright.config.ts webapp-running-turn-reopen` (on `main`: running prompt drawn twice).
3. In a chat past 120 rows, send a prompt that runs several tools, switch chats and back while it runs: one prompt.

Head `39d89f7434` (rebased onto `32dbc1dcda` plus the trailing-slice and `submissionId` matching fix): the 6 new trailing-row / differing-text cases failed red on `94d559b893` and pass on `39d89f7434` (`transcript-backfill.live-turn.test.ts`: 11 passed; transcript + `use-contrib` + `use-session-actions` hooks suite: 180 files / 1,897 passed before the `optimisticUserMatchesCommitted` extraction and `transcript-backfill.live-turn.test.ts` 11 passed after); `eslint`, `prettier --check`, `tsc -p . --noEmit`, and `scripts/check --only health --commit` all pass. Pre-rebase at `2868cc34ec` (and merged into `origin/main` at `90d6b98fd8`), headless Chromium Webapp e2e failed 2/2 on `ca43606920`, passed 13/13 on `2868cc34ec` and 2/2 on the merge, and the full Desktop UI suite passed (1,575 files, 13,155 tests). Not re-run post-rebase: Playwright Webapp e2e (`Desktop core E2E` is skipped on routine PR CI) and Electron e2e (no display here).

prs.title: fix(telegram): drafts stream on the first gateway run after the on-demand python-telegram-bot install
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Drafts stream on first run. Before: First draft: draft raises; DM reply: edits until restart. After: First draft: MarkdownV2 draft; DM reply: native drafts. Change: ParseMode from telegram.constants.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20bd7a84-acfd-4f7e-af25-ec0115f2b321)

## What does this PR do?

A gateway that starts without python-telegram-bot installs it on demand (the registry's `ensure_deps_fn`, by design). On that first run, the plain draft of every Telegram DM turn raised `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'MARKDOWN_V2'`; `_send_draft_frame` logs it at DEBUG and turns drafts off, so replies streamed through message edits until the gateway restarted. Now the draft goes out as MarkdownV2.

Found by @AliZakaee in [#152827](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/152827) (Found along the way).

Points to review:
- The gateway runs `hermes_plugins.platforms__telegram.adapter`; siblings import `plugins.platforms.telegram.adapter`, a second copy. Both bind `ParseMode = None` when PTB is missing at plugin load, and `check_telegram_requirements` rebinds only the running copy. `send_draft` has read the stale copy since #151863 (`7222595b82`) moved its body into `telegram_flood_window.py`.
- The fix reads `ParseMode` from `telegram.constants` at call time, as `standalone.py` does. The loader's double import is left alone.
- @kvnloo's commit (`5e7b0fe01f`, formerly `25c10f829d`, cherry-picked from his review) moves that import below the no-bot guard, so a disconnected adapter still returns `not_connected` when PTB is missing instead of raising `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- `telegram_vault_code.py` (added on `main` after this PR was first written) imported `ParseMode` from `plugins.platforms.telegram.adapter` at both send and card-edit sites; `87a720f273` switches both to `telegram.constants` too. No other Telegram sibling imports any lazily rebound name from `adapter.py`.

Probe (real plugin discovery and `create_adapter`, bot mocked):

| Code | PTB at plugin load | `send_draft` | `send_vault_code_prompt` / card edit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (`7fdeb079c7`) | installed on demand | `AttributeError`, no `sendMessageDraft` call | — (landed later) |
| `main` (`32dbc1dcda`) | installed on demand | `AttributeError` | `AttributeError` / skipped edit |
| `main` (`7fdeb079c7`) | present | `parse_mode=MarkdownV2` | `parse_mode=HTML` |
| `7222595b82^` | installed on demand | `parse_mode=MarkdownV2` | — |
| this PR (`87a720f273`) | installed on demand | `parse_mode=MarkdownV2` | `parse_mode=HTML` |

The same root cause on other platforms is tracked separately: Discord #121938, #143642, #137083 (PRs #121952, #121956, #137091, #144264, #146972) and DingTalk #86211.

## Related Issue

Related to #152827 (found there) and #151863 (regressed there).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/platforms/telegram/test_draft_after_lazy_install.py tests/gateway/test_telegram_vault_code_reply.py
```

`test_draft_after_lazy_install.py` runs real plugin discovery with `telegram` blocked, then the registry's `create_adapter` install path, and checks that a disconnected adapter returns `not_connected` before install, `send_draft` sends `MarkdownV2` after install, and `send_vault_code_prompt` / `_mark_vault_code_card` send `HTML` after install. Linux CI slices have no PTB, so it skips there; the macOS and Windows PR lanes install the `telegram` extra and run it (`platforms("any")`).

Head `87a720f273` (rebased onto `32dbc1dcda` plus the `telegram_vault_code.py` fix commit): on Linux arm64 with PTB installed via `--extra telegram --extra messaging`, the vault-code assertion failed red on `5e7b0fe01f` with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'HTML'` and passes on `87a720f273` (`test_draft_after_lazy_install.py` + `test_telegram_vault_code_reply.py`: 6 passed, 0 failed); `scripts/check --only health --commit` and `scripts/ci/check_contributor_emails.py` pass. Pre-rebase on `25c10f829d`, 27 draft/flood files passed (328 passed); pre-rebase on `d1f52f77f2`, 136 Telegram/draft/stream files passed (1552 passed, 3 skipped) and 26 gateway files passed without PTB (364 passed). Not run: a live Telegram bot.

![Dependencies stay read-only. Before: Launch: writes inside generations; Sandbox policy: new rule every build; Turn: install not writable. After: Launch: writes only leases/, locks/; Sandbox policy: same two dirs; Turn: reply arrives. Change: leases/ + locks/ beside generations, old locations still honoured.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afc1d6d9-0750-4d39-b7e0-1cd6a8905aac)

## What does this PR do?

Every launch of a source install wrote a lease file inside the selected dependency generation, plus `installs/<key>/.install.lock` and `pm-runtime/.prepare.lock`. Generation names change with every build, so a sandbox (OpenShell/Landlock, rootless Podman, systemd `ReadOnlyPaths=`) needed a new exception per build to keep the dependencies read-only. Leases now go to `installs/<key>/leases/{environments,pm-runtime}/<generation>/` and the locks to `installs/<key>/locks/`. A sandbox grants write access to those two and keeps the rest of `installs/` read-only (documented in `package-management.md` § Writable state).

Points to review (details in the commit messages):
- `lease_dirs()` finds the install state from a generation's parents (`environments/<gen>`, `pm-runtime/generations/<gen>`, which is also a PM worker's `sys.prefix`). Collectors treat a lease in either the new place or the old `<gen>/.leases` as held.
- `moved_lock()` takes the old lock first, then the new one, so a process started before the update and a new one always contend on the same file. If the old file can only be read, it is still flocked through a read-only descriptor. It is skipped only when it can't be opened at all; an error while locking it (`ENOLCK` on NFS, say) reaches the caller (`2abbceb4e6`, formerly `6d426d0924`, from Greptile's review). If waiting on the new lock times out after acquiring the old lock, `moved_lock()` releases the old lock before yielding `False` (`b3f2a8e513`).
- Not covered: a collector in a process started before the update reads only `<gen>/.leases`. During the transition it can remove an unselected generation that a new process leases only under `leases/`. Writing the old lease as well would close that gap, but it writes into the generation again.

## Related Issue

Refs #151951

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How to Test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/pm/test_leases_outside_generations.py tests/pm/test_runtime_gc.py tests/pm/test_install_states_gc.py tests/pm/test_lease_reselection.py
scripts/run_tests.sh --include-integration tests/e2e/core/upgrade/hosts/test_permissions.py  # needs bwrap with user namespaces
```

Head `b3f2a8e513` (rebased onto `32dbc1dcda` plus the `moved_lock` timeout-release fix): on Linux arm64, `test_moved_lock_releases_old_lock_when_new_lock_times_out` failed red on `2abbceb4e6` (`lock_fd` returned `False` while inside `with runtime_lock`) and passes on `b3f2a8e513`; all 4 focused PM test files above pass (41 passed, 0 failed) and `scripts/check --only health --commit` passes on every commit. Pre-rebase, the bwrap E2E ran in WSL Ubuntu (AppArmor blocks user namespaces on this host) with production and E2E files identical to `70fd4e88e5` (3/3 passed; base failed with `install state is not writable by this user (.../pm-runtime/.prepare.lock)`). Not run: macOS, NFS, Windows read-only old-lock path, and re-running the WSL bwrap E2E post-rebase.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add babelii-diofis plugin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds **Babelii-Diofis** to the community plugin catalog. This PR adds one file, `plugin-catalog/babelii-diofis.yaml`.

- **Plugin repo:** https://github.com/diofis-enterprise/babelii-hermes, owned by the Diofis Enterprise GitHub organisation, which also operates the hosted service the package connects to (rule 5).
- **Pinned SHA (0.3.0, tag `v0.3.0`):** `e8823a89a20f5ac27fa2fe700ca28b137b93ed65`. (Updated from 0.2.0 on 21 Nov 2026: adds a README section and a second skill for customers who sign in; the default configuration is unchanged.)
- **Format:** Agent Plugins v1 portable package (`plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + `skills/` with two skills), configuration only. `mcp.json` declares one `streamable-http` server, `babelii-diofis`, at `https://babelii.diofis.net/mcp/commerce/` (no sign-in).

Babelii is an Indonesian PPOB platform: pulsa, data vouchers and packages, PLN tokens, bill payments, e-wallet top-ups and game vouchers. The `babelii-ppob` skill walks the agent through search, prepare, one summary, buyer confirmation, execute, and handing over the payment link. The `babelii-account` skill covers the optional signed-in case (below).

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- Hosted-only connector with no local code: the plugin is `plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, two `SKILL.md` files, a README and a licence. No Python, no JavaScript, no executables, no self-updater.
- Every tool call goes to `babelii.diofis.net` and nowhere else. It receives the destination phone number or account identifier and the buyer name the user provides, to place the order. The plugin never contacts a payment provider: it hands the buyer a payment link that opens in the buyer's own browser.
- Optional, user-initiated: a customer with a Babelii account can point the same server key at `https://babelii.diofis.net/mcp/account/` with `hermes mcp add babelii-diofis --url ... --auth oauth`. Sign-in happens in the customer's browser on babelii.diofis.net; Hermes keeps the OAuth token, the package stores no credentials. Signed in, orders are paid from the account balance by default (or by payment link when the buyer asks), within limits the customer sets on the consent page, and read-only account tools appear only if the customer granted `account:read`. The package ships configured for the anonymous endpoint and does not sign anyone in.
- `execute_purchase` places a real order that becomes payable (anonymous), or is paid from the balance / by link (signed-in); `prepare_purchase` creates no order. The server limits agent orders (currently Rp25,000 per order and 3 per hour per identity).
- The package declares the server `untrusted`, so Hermes asks before every tool not annotated read-only and refuses them where nobody can answer (rule 12). On the live server exactly four of the ten tools lack `readOnlyHint`: `prepare_purchase`, `inquire_purchase`, `execute_purchase`, `renew_purchase`.
- No shell commands, no background processes, no files read outside the plugin, no stored credentials, no telemetry.
- The tool list is served by the remote server at run time, so the pinned commit does not cover it.
- Rules 18 to 20 do not apply (no login backend, no infringing content, no coin or token promotion).

## Related Issue

None.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/babelii-diofis.yaml`: new catalog entry. `tier: community`, `category: tools`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.0"` (the release I tested on; the current release is v0.23.3), empty `capabilities` (the plugin registers nothing). Babelii is the company that makes the service this package integrates; whether that merits `verified` is the maintainers' call.

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins install diofis-enterprise/babelii-hermes --ref e8823a89a20f5ac27fa2fe700ca28b137b93ed65 --enable` (by name, `hermes plugins install babelii-diofis --enable`, once this is merged).
2. Start a new session and ask for a pulsa top-up of a small nominal; the agent calls `search_products`, asks for the destination and buyer name, calls `prepare_purchase`, and Hermes asks for approval before it runs.

What I verified:

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` on this branch (the `just check-plugin-catalog` command, run with `ruamel.yaml` in a clean venv): `OK: 2516 file(s) valid`, no warning or error on `babelii-diofis.yaml`. The entry alone gives `OK: 1 file(s) valid`; with the sha cut to 6 characters the validator rejects it, so the check does cover the entry.
- `hermes plugins validate` on the 0.3.0 package contents, Hermes v0.23.0: portable manifest parses, server trust `untrusted`, security scan `safe`, validation passed (it first flagged invalid YAML in the new skill's description; fixed before the tag).
- `hermes plugins install diofis-enterprise/babelii-hermes --ref e8823a89a20f5ac27fa2fe700ca28b137b93ed65 --enable` into an isolated Hermes home: installed from GitHub, enabled, listed as `babelii-diofis` 0.3.0. The `load_agent_plugin` translation check below was done for 0.2.0 and was not re-run for 0.3.0; `mcp.json` and the server declaration are unchanged. The full-tree catalog validation below was also run for 0.2.0; for 0.3.0 the entry alone was re-run (`OK: 1 file(s) valid`).

With Hermes's own runtime, `load_agent_plugin` translates `mcp.json` into the server `babelii-diofis` (`url`, `strict_redirect_headers`, `trust: untrusted`) and loads the skill `babelii-ppob` with no diagnostics.
- The endpoint is live; the ten tool names in the skill match its `tools/list`, and the product examples named in the README (DANA, GoPay, OVO, ShopeePay) exist in the live catalogue.

What I did not run: `just check` and `just test-catalog` (I did not set up the full dev environment); CI will run them. I did not complete a real purchase through the plugin.

prs.title: Edit previews show a file's hidden control bytes as visible symbols (CLI, TUI, Desktop)
prs.body:
When the agent edits a file that holds hidden terminal bytes (an escape code, a bell, a backspace), the diff preview used to drop them without a trace, so a line could look harmless while the file holds bytes you never saw. Now every such byte shows up as a visible symbol (␛, ␇, ␈, ␡) in the preview.

**Outcome:** the edit preview on the CLI, TUI and Desktop shows exactly which control bytes a changed file contains, and never lets them act on your terminal.

- `agent/display.py::_render_inline_unified_diff` maps C0 controls (tab kept), DEL and C1 to Unicode Control Pictures (`ESC → ␛`, `BEL → ␇`, `BS → ␈`, `DEL → ␡`) or `\x9b` before it colours a line. Every surface reads this one renderer: classic CLI prints it, `tui_gateway/tool_progress.py` ships it as `inline_diff` to the TUI and Desktop.
- Display copy only: the file on disk, the tool result and what the model sees are unchanged.
- One invariant test (`tests/agent/test_display.py`): after the renderer's own colour codes are removed, every character in the preview is printable or a tab. Red on `origin/main` (1 failed), green on head (66 passed across `test_display.py` + `test_approval_display_sanitize.py`).

| `target.py` line 1 on disk (`od -c`) | Classic CLI preview, `origin/main` | Classic CLI preview, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `greeting = "hello \033]0;PWNED\a world"` | `greeting = "hello 0;PWNED world"` | `greeting = "hello ␛]0;PWNED␇ world"` |

**Live repro:** a real `hermes chat -q` (classic CLI in tmux, a Haiku model via the Nous Portal, isolated probe home) patched `value = 1 → 2` in a file whose first line holds an OSC title sequence. On main the context line in the preview read `hello 0;PWNED world`: prompt_toolkit's ANSI parser ate ESC and BEL and printed the rest, so the bytes were hidden (tmux pane title unchanged on both legs). On head the same run showed `hello ␛]0;PWNED␇ world`. The file bytes came out identical on both legs apart from the requested edit.

**Root cause:** the preview renderer passed file text straight to the terminal printers. They either stripped control bytes without a trace (CLI's prompt_toolkit, TUI/Desktop `stripAnsi`) or would have run them on a raw printer.

### Inspired by Cursor
Cursor CLI v2026.11.17 (https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog#nov-17-2026-fixes): "Control characters in a file, such as escape codes, now show as visible symbols in the edit preview instead of clearing the screen, renaming the terminal window, or ringing the bell. The file on disk and the text sent to the model are unchanged." Their bug was the raw-printer case (bytes ran). Ours was the stripped-without-a-trace case (bytes hidden). The same fix covers both: the preview shows every byte as a symbol. This follows the rule Hermes already applies to approval prompts (#81403, `agent/redact_approval_display.py`), where hidden content becomes visible instead of being dropped.

**Not covered:** I did not capture screenshots of the TUI or Desktop. Both run the `inline_diff` payload through `stripAnsi`, which keeps the visible `␛` glyphs and drops raw bytes, so on those surfaces the new symbols now appear where the bytes used to vanish without a trace.

## Infographic

![Visible control bytes](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab3513a/3BPtvfykLz7xpsKWhclvZ_jErWMjCQ.png)

prs.title: fix(goals): resume blocked goals before user-turn execution
prs.body:
## Problem

A goal paused by a `blocked` verdict should resume when the user supplies the missing input. The original implementation recovered only after a successful reply: long replies kept showing **Goal blocked**, and failed replies skipped recovery. The Desktop also preferred the historical blocked verdict over the current active state.

## Solution

- Recover on admitted real user input, before model work, in Desktop/TUI, CLI, and the messaging gateway. Preserve the existing goal, criteria, and spent budget.
- Publish the authoritative Desktop control snapshot immediately; render current state rather than a historical verdict.
- Keep explicit pauses, interrupts, budget exhaustion, judge failures, and synthetic notifications from being mistaken for an answer. Preserve hidden/relayed provenance through busy queues and isolated-compute dispatch.
- Preserve this PR's batch-clarify answer retention through compaction, reconciled with current main.

Follows up the `blocked` verdict introduced for #100954. This updates the existing PR rather than introducing a competing recovery implementation.

## Verification

- Reproduced on the previous PR implementation: persisted goal remains `paused`, turn `1/20`, while the repair reply is held open.
- Fixed native DEV Desktop, isolated homes and private headless compositor, deterministic local model provider: typed `/goal`, received `blocked`, typed a normal repair message; **active at 1/20 before the reply completes**, then automatic continuation and **done at 3 turns**. No `/goal resume`.
- Real Desktop negative checks: explicit pause survives a normal message; a hidden notification neither resumes the blocked goal nor invokes the judge.
- Regression tests fail on the previous behavior and pass with the fix. Coverage includes failed/interrupted replies, in-turn pause, secondary-profile persistence, queued hidden messages, and automatic-message exclusions.
- Python TUI/admission/goal sweep: **1,283 passed**. The gateway failure/loop cleanup regression sweep also passed (**51 tests**, overlapping coverage). One compute-host timing test timed out under concurrent full-suite load; its unchanged focused rerun and the complete repeated sweep passed.
- Ordinary gateway exceptions, failed results, and interrupted results preserve the recovered goal's budget, invoke no goal judge, and still settle loop bookkeeping.
- Broad gateway sweep: **8,249 passed, 2 failed, 46 skipped**. Both failures are the unchanged Telegram media-timeout tests and reproduce on the pre-fix baseline; they are not hidden or fixed in this PR.
- Desktop UI + Electron suites: **9,788 passed, 6 skipped**; typecheck, changed-file ESLint/Prettier, and diff checks passed.
- DEV processes exited and their listening ports closed. No installed app, real profile, or existing VM was modified.

### While the repair reply is still running

The following are cropped excerpts of the real DEV Desktop, not mockups. Both retain the same spent turn budget.

![Blocked goal recovery before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zeus-Deus/hermes-agent/pr-assets-104380/104380/goal-recovery-before-after.png)

## Scope and privacy

No new model tool, configuration switch, or permission bypass. Diff, commit text, and public screenshot checked for credentials, private paths, and session identifiers; raw transcripts and rig state are not published.

prs.title: fix(compression): prevent no-op compression with legacy SessionDB
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix context compression becoming a no-op during hot-update version skew, where
compression appears to start but never invokes the compressor.

The affected path pairs the newer compression module with a legacy `SessionDB`
that is still loaded in the running process. That legacy class does not provide
`get_compression_failure_cooldown_row`, but the previous implementation treated
this missing API as a durable cooldown read failure.

The caller then failed closed and returned the original messages before calling
the compressor. As a result, compression appeared to start while neither the
messages nor the token usage actually decreased.

This change uses an explicit sentinel to distinguish these cases:

- The legacy API is genuinely absent: preserve the compatibility path and
  continue context compression.
- The API is present but non-callable: fail closed.
- The durable reader raises an exception: fail closed.
- The durable state is read successfully: preserve the existing authoritative
  rollback flow.

The change only corrects the missing-legacy-API case. It does not relax genuine
durable-state read failures or change lock acquisition, summary generation,
commit fencing, or cooldown rollback behavior.

## Related Issue / PR

I did not find an Issue or PR covering the same legacy `SessionDB` version-skew
path.

This regression is technically related to merged PR #76647, which introduced
the authoritative cooldown rollback API. This PR adds the compatibility path
needed when the newer compression module is paired with a legacy `SessionDB`
that does not yet provide that API.

Other no-op compression, anti-thrashing, session rotation, and protected-tail
reports cover failures after the compressor runs or cases where no content can
be compressed. They do not cover this pre-compressor early return.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] Refactor (no behavior change)

## Changes Made

- Update `agent/conversation_compression.py`:
  - Use an explicit sentinel to detect whether the raw cooldown API is truly
    absent.
  - Return the non-authoritative compatibility result when a legacy
    `SessionDB` does not provide the API, allowing context compression to
    continue.
  - Preserve fail-closed behavior when the API is present but non-callable.
  - Preserve fail-closed behavior when the durable reader raises.

- Update `tests/agent/test_compression_concurrent_fork.py`:
  - Add an end-to-end compression-entry regression test for version skew.
  - Verify that the compressor is invoked when the legacy API is absent.
  - Verify that the result contains the compressor-produced summary rather
    than the original messages.
  - Verify that a present but non-callable API fails closed.
  - Verify that a durable-reader exception fails closed.
  - Verify that the compression lock is released.
  - Verify that the compatibility path does not create a child-session fork.

## How to Reproduce

Before this fix, invoke compression with a legacy `SessionDB` that does not

prs.title: fix(providers): opencode-go emits GLM-5.3 reasoning_effort — ends the silent max-tier lock
prs.body:
Fixes #158478.

## What

`OpenCodeGoProfile.build_api_kwargs_extras` gains a GLM-5.3 branch mirroring the zai profile's mapping (30f9955a44): a new `_is_glm_5_3_model()` recognizes `glm-5.3 / glm-5-3 / glm-5p3` spellings (incl. `-flash` variants and vendor prefixes via `_flat_model_name`), requested efforts clamp to `GLM53_EFFORTS` (`xhigh`→`max` override, floor `low`), and a **disable ask maps to `low`** — GLM-5.3 rejects `thinking.type: disabled` (#85890), so dropping the field instead would leave the relay's max default, more thinking than asked for (the f7d90c9410 bug class). Unset config keeps the server default, exactly like the 5.2 branch one line above.

## Why the wire vocabulary keeps `medium`

`GLM53_EFFORTS` is shared with the zai profile and already lists `medium`; the OpenCode Go relay **accepts** it (live probe in the linked issue: `medium` → HTTP 200, reasoning_tokens=7). The bigmodel PAYG endpoint rejects `medium` with 400/1210, but that is the zai route's concern, tracked in #140239 — this PR deliberately does not touch the shared constant (no scope creep).

## Verification

- Live probe against the Go relay (openai-python SDK stack, same as the gateway): `low`=2 / `medium`=7 / `high`=7 / `max`=26-79 reasoning tokens, monotonic; the no-field default lands in the max band (mean 43 vs 50 over 3 runs each).
- New `TestOpenCodeGoGLM53Reasoning` unit class in `tests/plugins/model_providers/test_opencode_go_profile.py`: graded pass-through (low/medium/high/max, `xhigh`→`max`, `minimal`→floor `low`), alias spellings incl. `-flash` and vendor prefixes, disable→`low`, unset→server default, 5.2 unaffected (no leak from the widened scale), and a transport-level kwargs integration test (`ChatCompletionsTransport.build_kwargs` carries `reasoning_effort` top-level).
- Full `tests/plugins/model_providers/` suite green.

prs.title: fix(models-dev): read a provider profile's catalog when a session records one of its aliases
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`models_dev_id_for()` resolves only exact provider-profile names. A provider profile can declare
`aliases`, and sessions can record their provider by one of them — for example, sessions created through
the GitHub Copilot plugin record `github-copilot`, an alias of the profile `copilot` (whose
`models_dev_id` is `github-copilot`'s catalog). For such a session `_models_dev_id()` returns `None`, so
every models.dev consumer — image routing, reasoning support, context window — treats the model as
unknown. Visible symptom: with `image_input_mode: auto`, a picture sent to a vision model in a Copilot
gateway session goes down the text-description path, while the same model under the canonical name
`copilot` gets the image natively.

This change fills only that miss. When neither an exact id nor a configured `catalog_provider` resolves,
`_models_dev_id()` asks the provider registry which profile the name is an alias of and returns that
profile's models.dev id.

Guards (each covered by a test):
- exact provider ids and a configured `catalog_provider` keep precedence; a mistyped `catalog_provider`
  still resolves to nothing, as before;
- `custom` / `custom:<route>` names are never resolved through a profile;
- a user-defined provider with the same name (`providers.<name>` or a legacy `custom_providers[]`
  entry) keeps its own endpoint and never borrows a vendor catalog;
- a profile without a `models_dev_id`, an unknown name, a case-mismatched name, and a registry failure
  all stay unknown.

## Related Issue

No existing issue found for this exact gap (searched open/closed PRs and issues for `models_dev_id_for`,
provider aliases and Copilot image routing). Related but different: #135701 and #135712 (vision routing
for a custom provider's `catalog_provider`).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/models_dev.py`: `_models_dev_id()` falls back to `_profile_alias_models_dev_id()` when no exact
  id or configured `catalog_provider` resolves; new helpers `_profile_alias_models_dev_id()` and
  `_is_named_custom_provider()`.
- `tests/agent/test_models_dev_profile_alias_catalog.py`: new; uses an isolated provider registry and a
  fixture catalog (no network).

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_models_dev_profile_alias_catalog.py tests/agent/test_models_dev.py tests/agent/test_image_routing.py`
2. Without the `agent/models_dev.py` change, 7 of the new tests fail (aliases read as unknown); with it,
   all pass, and the existing `test_models_dev.py` / `test_image_routing.py` still pass.

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: fix(opencode-go): emit reasoning_effort for GLM-5.3
prs.body:
Fixes #158478

`OpenCodeGoProfile.build_api_kwargs_extras` dispatches per model family, but the GLM branch matched only GLM-5.2 spellings — `_is_glm_5_2_model`: `glm-5.2` / `glm-5-2` / `glm-5p2`. That matcher predates GLM-5.3 by 39 days, so `glm-5.3` matched no branch and fell through to `return {}, {}`.

The `extra_body.reasoning` fallback is closed on this route too, because `_supports_reasoning_extra_body()` asks the profile's `reasoning_payload` hook and `OpenCodeGoProfile` does not override it. So the request left Hermes with **no reasoning field at all**, and the Go relay applied its own default tier — `/reasoning low`, `agent.reasoning_effort` and per-model overrides were all silently ignored.

A live probe of the relay accounts for the report: a request with no field lands in the same band as explicit `max` (mean 43 vs 50 reasoning tokens over 3 runs), while `low` / `high` / `medium` scale (2 / 7 / 7). The knob works end-to-end; only Hermes's emission was missing.

## Fix

`_is_glm_5_2_model` becomes `_is_glm_reasoning_effort_model` and covers the 5.3 spellings as well: `glm-5.3`, `glm-5-3`, `glm-5p3`. GLM-5.1 and `glm-5` still match nothing, so their gating is unchanged.

## Verification

New `tests/plugins/model_providers/test_opencode_go_profile.py::TestOpenCodeGoGLM53Reasoning`: the three 5.3 spellings emit `reasoning_effort`, and a disabled config still emits nothing.

- Without the fix: **3 failed, 31 passed** — exactly the three 5.3 spellings.
- With it: **34 passed**.

prs.title: fix(i18n): build web locales through defineLocale and translate the Shell hooks section
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Two related i18n fixes for the web dashboard:

1. **Every web locale is now built through `defineLocale()`.** The helper already existed (`web/src/i18n/define-locale.ts`) and `ar.ts` used it, but the other 16 catalogs were full `Translations` objects. Consequence: adding a single key forced the same English string into 16 files just to satisfy the type — which is why new dashboard copy keeps landing as hardcoded English. Merging each catalog over `en` lets a locale supply only what it translated; unknown keys still fail the type-check because `TranslationOverride` rejects them.

2. **The Shell hooks section on the System page is translated** (heading, empty state, create dialog, toasts, per-hook badges), with Turkish filled in. It was hardcoded English, so it stayed English in all 17 locales while the rest of the page was translated.

## Related Issue

No issue specifically for the web dashboard's hardcoded copy; this is the same class of gap as #43355 (gateway strings bypass `t()`) and #130669. Happy to split or re-scope if you'd rather take the structural change alone first — the two commits are independent.

## What does this PR do?

Gives the `execute_code` session kernel the same PATH completion the `terminal` tool already applies, so a kernel cell can resolve the runtime binaries Hermes manages for itself.

`terminal` (foreground) completes its child PATH through `tools/environments/local.py::_append_missing_sane_path_entries`, which appends the pm store dirs, `$HERMES_HOME/bin` and `~/.local/bin`. The kernel child is built by `tools/code_execution_env.py::_build_child_env`, which scrubbed and rewrote the inherited environment but never applied that completion. On a store/PM install whose only `uv` lives at `$HERMES_HOME/bin/uv`, any `subprocess` call from a kernel cell died with:

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'uv'
```

while the identical command through `terminal` succeeded. The kernel's PATH was already deliberately enriched by `pm.install.activate()` (cua-driver, ffmpeg, pnpm, node, ripgrep, python) — the Hermes-managed bin dir was the one entry that never landed there.

## Related Issue

Fixes #158463

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/code_execution_env.py`: at the end of `_build_child_env`, before `return`, apply `_append_missing_sane_path_entries` to `child_env["PATH"]` (function-local import of the existing helper, so no module-level cycle). Appended, not prepended — the user's own PATH entries keep precedence, exactly as in the terminal subshell. No new branches, so the code-health ratchet is untouched.
- `tests/tools/test_code_execution_managed_path.py` (new): asserts `$HERMES_HOME/bin` reaches the kernel PATH and is appended rather than prepended, plus a no-duplication case for a dir already on PATH.

Scope note: `_build_child_env` has exactly one production caller, `tools/code_kernel.py::_spawn` (the local session kernel). Remote backends ship their own env file via `_ship_env_file_and_launch`, so no host-local path leaks into a Docker or SSH sandbox.

This is the third surface with the same underlying defect, each tracked separately: foreground `terminal` is correct; `terminal(background=true)` is #124820 (PR #124831); the `execute_code` kernel is this PR. #129101 mentions kernel PATH parity as an optional bullet.

## How to Test

1. On a PM-managed install where `uv` exists only at `$HERMES_HOME/bin/uv` (no `uv` on the host PATH or in `~/.local/bin`), run from a kernel cell:
   ```python
   import subprocess
   subprocess.run(["uv", "--version"], capture_output=True)
   ```
   Before: `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'uv'`. After: resolves to `$HERMES_HOME/bin/uv`.
2. Unit-level, no install needed:
   ```
   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_code_execution_managed_path.py
   ```
3. Discriminating proof (both sides run here): reverting only `tools/code_execution_env.py` to the base commit makes the new test fail with `AssertionError: assert '/…/home/bin' in ['/usr/bin', '/bin']`; restoring it gives `2 tests passed, 0 failed`.
4. Neighbors: `tests/tools/test_code_execution_pm_runtime.py` and `tests/tools/environments/test_local_path_completion.py` → `2 files, 5 tests passed, 0 failed`.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass
- [ ] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs) — see the note below
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu (Linux), systemd gateway, Python 3.14.9 PM-managed runtime

Note on `just check`: the composed checker cannot complete in one process on this checkout — its internal 900 s per-job timeout expires on the whole-repo `scripts.code_health` scan and the runner aborts with `TimeoutExpired`. Run individually instead, all 22 composed checks report 20 green and the code-health ratchet reports 0 blocking / 0 advisory with `--base 242315ce57` (the base commit of this branch). `blob-size` is red on three files this PR does not touch (`apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json`, `apps/desktop/packaging/nous-dmg-2b.tiff`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py`); re-running it with this PR's two files stashed reproduces the identical three failures at the base commit, so it is pre-existing and not attributable to this change.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — the module docstring of `tools/code_execution_env.py` and the new test's docstring describe the completion, and the inline comment states why it is appended
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A, no config keys
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — `_append_missing_sane_path_entries` is an explicit no-op passthrough on Windows, so the change is POSIX-only in effect; the new test is marked `platforms("posix")`
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A, no schema change (the `execute_code` contract is unchanged; it just stops lying about the managed toolchain)

## Screenshots / Logs

Kernel child PATH before and after, `HERMES_HOME=/root/.hermes`, inherited `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`:

```
before: uv on child PATH -> None
after : uv on child PATH -> /root/.hermes/bin/uv
```

`/proc` evidence from the reporting host: the gateway and kernel processes carried identical `PATH` values, neither containing `$HERMES_HOME/bin`, while the kernel's PATH already carried the `pm.install.activate()` entries.

prs.title: feat(dashboard): in-app offer dialog for hermes dashboard
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Nous Portal's in-app offer, shown in `hermes dashboard` (the `web/` SPA). Desktop and the Hermes Webapp get it from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/158060; this adds the third surface. The Portal half that decides who sees an offer is https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-portal/pull/2251.

**Stacked on #158060.** The base branch lives on my fork, so GitHub cannot target it here; until #158060 merges, this diff also shows its commits. The dashboard-only changes are the last four commits (the dialog, show/click reporting, the review fixes, and the claim deadline).

Design calls:

- One memo, three surfaces. The dashboard reads the same per-profile memo (`hermes_cli/in_app_offer.py`) that `free_tier.status` serves Desktop and the Webapp, so an offer has one source of truth on the machine. The dashboard has no JSON-RPC socket for this, so it gets one REST route: `GET /api/in-app-offer` answers from the memo (a local read), and `?refresh=1` first fetches the account with the stored token (never refreshing it), the same network leg as the `in_app_offer.refresh` RPC.
- The route is profile-scoped like the other management routes (`?profile=`, added to `PROFILE_SCOPED_PREFIXES`), so the dashboard's profile switcher shows the offer for the profile being managed. It runs under `config_scoped_to_thread` (home and secrets, no process-wide lock), because the refresh and the report make network calls of up to 8 seconds that must not stall other dashboard requests.
- `POST /api/in-app-offer/event` reports shown and clicked for the Portal's counts, and `POST /api/in-app-offer/dismiss` closes the offer for the profile, so Desktop and the Webapp never show it again either. Both go through the same functions as the Desktop RPCs.
- The SPA checks the answer before showing it: blank copy, or a CTA that is not an https link, is no offer (`window.open` would otherwise run a `javascript:` URL).
- The CTA reports its click and then dismisses. The click still counts when the dismissal lands first: the report resolves the served offer without the dismissal filter (fixed in #158060, which this branch is rebased on).
- It never errors. No offer, a failed fetch, or an older backend without the route all mean "no dialog". A failed refresh keeps the last answer.
- Timing matches Desktop: the dialog opens only after 8 seconds of idle (visible and focused tab, no other `aria-modal` dialog or open menu, focus not in a text field), and any keypress, click or focus change restarts the clock. Focus moves into the panel, not onto a button, so a stray Space or Enter cannot dismiss it unread.
- Once per offer per profile, at most one a day per browser, and dismissals made in another tab are kept. A tab left open past the daily cap re-checks instead of never showing. An offer the Portal withdraws closes without being recorded as dismissed, and if it returns it waits for an idle moment again.
- Copy comes from the server and renders as text with line breaks kept. The CTA opens in a new tab with `noopener`. When the offer carries `claimable_until`, a "Claim by <date> UTC" line shows under the body, as on Desktop. The three local strings (the banner, the dismiss label and the claim-by line) are optional i18n keys with English fallbacks, the same convention as the shared-metrics banner beside it.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/web_routers/in_app_offer.py` (new) + one mount line in `hermes_cli/web_server.py`: `GET /api/in-app-offer`, `POST /api/in-app-offer/event`, `POST /api/in-app-offer/dismiss`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/serve_handler_ledger.json`: the new routes' rows (regenerated).
- `web/src/lib/in-app-offer.ts` (new): the fetch plus the presentation rules (eligibility, daily cap, dismissal storage, idle read).
- `web/src/components/InAppOfferDialog.tsx` (new), mounted in `App.tsx` beside the first-run banners.
- `web/src/lib/api-request-scope.ts`: profile-scope the route. `web/src/i18n/{en,types}.ts`: two optional keys.

## How to Test

1. Create an offer on the Portal admin page (`/admin/in-app-offers`), active, shown in "Hermes app".
2. `hermes dashboard`, signed in to Nous, and leave the tab idle: about 30 seconds after load (the first refresh plus the settle) the dialog opens. Typing in any field holds it back.
3. "Maybe later", Esc, the X, or the CTA closes it for good, in this tab and others. Deactivating the offer instead closes it on the next refresh.
4. Unit: `tests/hermes_cli/test_in_app_offer_route.py`; in `web/`, `npx vitest run src/lib/in-app-offer.test.ts src/components/InAppOfferDialog.test.tsx`.

### Code

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

- [x] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass: the dashboard offer suites (24 tests) and 45 Python tests (the routes, the memo, the contract suite and the serve handler ledger). Sabotage runs turned the relevant tests red: forcing the idle gate open, routing through the locked scope (the lock test holds `_SKILLS_PROFILE_LOCK` and times out), and dropping the cap re-check

prs.title: fix(agent): preserve session reasoning_config when switch_model resolves to None
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Prevents `switch_model()` from silently resetting `agent.reasoning_config` to `None` when the config has no `agent.reasoning_effort` set. This preserves any active session-level `/reasoning <level>` override across model switches.

## Related Issue

Fixes #72856

Also related: #55276 (#reasoning silently dropped), #72202 (custom:cc provider path)

## Root Cause

`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:2377` unconditionally overwrites `agent.reasoning_config` with `resolve_reasoning_config()`. When config has no `reasoning_effort` and no per-model `reasoning_overrides`, this returns `None`, dropping any session-level override set via `/reasoning high`.

## Fix

Only overwrite when the resolved value is non-None:

```python
_resolved = resolve_reasoning_config(_reasoning_cfg, agent.model)
if _resolved is not None:
    agent.reasoning_config = _resolved
```

This correctly handles all cases:
- Per-model `reasoning_overrides` still apply (they return non-None)
- Global `reasoning_effort` still applies (returns non-None)
- YAML `reasoning_effort: false` still applies (returns non-None `{'enabled': False}`)
- Session `/reasoning high` survives when config is unset (returns None → skipped)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`: guard `resolve_reasoning_config` result as described above
- `tests/run_agent/test_switch_model_reasoning_override.py`: added `test_session_override_survives_no_config_switch`

## How to Test

1. Start Hermes with `agent.reasoning_effort` unset
2. `/reasoning high`
3. `/model <any-other-model>`
4. Send a message — `reasoning_effort` should appear in the API request
5. Run existing tests: `pytest tests/run_agent/test_switch_model_reasoning_override.py -v` — all 6 pass

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional Commits (`fix(agent):`)
- [x] Searched for existing PRs — no duplicate found
- [x] Only changes related to this fix
- [x] All existing tests pass (6/6)
- [x] Added regression test
- [x] Tested on: Windows 10

prs.title: feat(desktop): in-app offer dialog for Desktop and the Webapp, served by free_tier.status
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Nous Portal can run a campaign that shows signed-in Hermes Desktop and Hermes Webapp users one dismissible offer dialog. The Webapp is this same renderer served to a browser tab, so it needs no separate client: `dialog.webapp.test.tsx` mounts the real dialog under the browser bridge and pins that it opens on an idle moment and that its CTA opens the offer through `window.open`. The `hermes dashboard` surface is a separate SPA and is stacked on this PR as https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/158316. The Portal side (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-portal/pull/2251) evaluates who should see an offer and serves `in_app_offer` on `/api/oauth/account`; this PR is the client. Each half is inert without the other (a payload with no consumer serves nothing; an unknown field is ignored today), so they can merge in either order.

Design calls:

- Delivery. The backend memo (`hermes_cli/in_app_offer.py`) records the offer from every account fetch, and `free_tier.status` serves it as a pure local read, the same shape as the pending browser challenge. Account fetches alone are not enough: a valid JWT answers most account reads locally, and the session-start credits seed runs only for a Nous session, so a user on another provider might never see an offer. A new `in_app_offer.refresh` RPC does one account fetch with the stored token (never refreshing it, so it is safe while a session runs on any provider). The desktop calls it 20s after boot and every 30 minutes, and it runs on the RPC pool.
- Known gap: the refresh never refreshes the token, so it only fetches while the stored token is valid (tokens last about an hour). A user returning after weeks gets the offer once anything refreshes the token, which a Nous session does at start; a user who only runs other providers may not. Letting the refresh renew the token closes this, at the cost of this read writing the auth store, which `stored_token_account_info` avoids on purpose. Flagging it for a maintainer call.
- Withdrawal. A missing or malformed `in_app_offer` clears the memo, so a campaign that ends, or an account that stops qualifying, disappears on the next fetch. Each memo entry also records the account it was fetched for (the JWT's user and org, or the guest credential) and when: another login on the profile never sees it, and an entry the Portal has not re-confirmed for a day is dropped, so an ended campaign does not linger behind an expired token. A transient fetch failure keeps the last answer.
- Only an https CTA with a host is accepted, in Python and in the renderer: the external opener also opens local paths and `file:` URLs.
- Timing. The dialog only opens after 8 seconds of idle: no running turn, an empty composer, and a visible, focused window. Typing restarts the clock. It never opens over first-run onboarding or the free-tier sign-in dialog. Once open it stays until the user acts, unless the Portal withdraws it.
- Focus. The dialog opens unprompted, so it does not autofocus its close button; a stray Space or Enter must not dismiss it unread.
- One window. Hosts claim the dialog the way the sign-in dialog does, so two windows never show two dialogs. Dismissals are read from shared storage, so dismissing in one window holds in every window.
- Dismissal is permanent per offer and per profile. Every close path (Esc, backdrop, "Maybe later", the CTA) calls `in_app_offer.dismiss`, which records the id in the profile home, and `free_tier.status` never serves a dismissed offer. Desktop, the Webapp and the dashboard keep separate browser storage, so a client-only record would show one person the same offer once per surface. The renderer still keeps its own record (`hermes.in-app-offer.dismissed-v1`), which covers an older backend.
- Counts. `in_app_offer.report` tells the Portal the dialog was shown or its CTA clicked (`POST /api/oauth/account/in-app-offer-event`), with the stored token, never refreshing it, and only for the offer this profile was served. A guest whose 15-minute access token has lapsed sends its anon credential. The Portal counts each person once, so the renderer records a report only after the Portal took it and a lost one is sent again. The CTA reports its click and dismisses back to back, and the dismissal often lands first, so the report checks the id against the served offer whether or not it was dismissed; an id the profile was never served is still refused.
- A refresh answer that arrives after the status changed (a profile switch mid-request) is dropped, and an unchanged offer leaves the status object alone, so the 30-minute refresh never re-arms the free-tier sign-in nudge.
- Frequency cap: at most one offer dialog per 24h (`hermes.in-app-offer.last-shown-v1`, stamped when the dialog is presented), whatever the campaign cadence.
- Claim deadline. When the Portal sends `claimable_until` (an ISO instant with an offset), the dialog adds a "Claim by <date> UTC" line under the body, formatted in UTC so every surface names the same moment. A missing, null, naive or unparseable deadline drops only that line; the offer still shows. The `claimBy` key is in the base catalog and all eight overlays (9 locales).
- Copy comes from the server and renders as text with line breaks kept (the Portal caps lengths). The local strings (the dismiss label, the screen-reader description and the claim-by line) are i18n keys in all 9 locales.

## Related Issue

None. A sweep of open PRs and issues found no prior ask for a portal-driven offer dialog; the closest names ("in-app update") are the updater flow, a different feature.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/in_app_offer.py`: the per-profile memo, its signed-in guard, and `refresh_from_portal`.
- `hermes_cli/nous_account.py`: record from `_info_from_account_payload`.
- `tui_gateway/methods_free_tier.py`: the memoised offer on `free_tier.status` (additive), and the `in_app_offer.refresh`, `.report` and `.dismiss` handlers; `tui_gateway/server.py` lists the two network ones in `_LONG_HANDLERS`.
- `tui_gateway/contracts/config_free_tier_control.py` + regenerated `apps/shared` gateway-contract files: `InAppOfferPayload` and the three RPCs' params and results.
- `apps/desktop`: `store/in-app-offer.ts` (eligibility, idle gate, claim, refresh loop), `components/in-app-offer/dialog.tsx` mounted at the shell beside the free-tier sign-in dialog, `FreeTierStatus.in_app_offer`, and i18n.

## How to Test

1. Create an offer on the Portal admin page (`/admin/in-app-offers`), active, audience "All signed-in users".
2. Open a signed-in desktop and leave it idle: within about 30 seconds of boot (the first refresh plus the 8s settle) the dialog opens. While typing in the composer or during a running turn it waits.
3. Dismiss it, or press the CTA: it does not return, in this window, a second one, the Webapp or `hermes dashboard` on the same profile. The admin page's "shown" and "clicked" counts go up by one each. Deactivate the offer instead and it closes on the next refresh.
4. Unit: `tests/hermes_cli/test_in_app_offer.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_free_tier_rpc.py`, and in `apps/desktop` `npx vitest run src/store/in-app-offer.test.ts`.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass: 235 Python tests (`test_in_app_offer.py` with the account-keyed memo, expiry, https-only CTA, dismissals and guest reports; the free-tier RPCs; `test_nous_account*`; `test_anon_*`; the contract suite and the serve handler ledger), and 39 renderer tests (the store and both dialog suites). Removing the profile-switch guard turns the refresh test red. Generated files (contracts, handler ledger, i18n keys) are regenerated on the current main with CI's pinned pydantic. The review fixes (a click reported after the dismiss, a null `claimable_until`, the ruff `fromisoformat` rule) were re-run on `test_in_app_offer.py` plus `test_free_tier_rpc.py` (46 passed) and the store plus Webapp dialog suites (43 passed); reverting either behavior fix turns its new test red
- [x] `just check` passes: the health ratchet passed against the merge base (`scripts/check --only health`); `tsc --noEmit` and eslint clean on the touched files
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — docstrings on the new module and contract fields (nothing in `docs/` names this surface yet)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — the memo, status change, and refresh are platform-neutral; the dialog uses only existing cross-platform primitives
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

Integration branch, redesign on with onboarding: test from here. prs.title: fix(gateway): an idle dashboard pane no longer fences resuming its chat through the gateway (#148450, salvage #143701)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Opening a chat through the gateway is refused with `runtime_coordination_required` whenever a `hermes dashboard` backend still has that chat mounted in a Desktop pane, even while the pane is idle. The dashboard keeps the active-session lease for as long as the pane stays mounted, and its pid stays alive for days. So `adopt_legacy_session` treats the chat as "someone is writing it" until the Desktop's WebSocket to the dashboard closes. In my case that was ~29 h.

This salvages @zaibpreneur's #143701 (cherry-picked with authorship preserved, rebased on current `main`). The fix fences adoption on the durable session turn lease, which every writer holds while a turn runs, rather than on lease liveness alone. That is the general resume path, not only Bot Chat. The PR adds an invariant test for the plain Desktop case reported in #148450.

Why this is safe and a lease TTL is not: a mid-turn pane still holds the turn lease, so adoption is still refused inside the same write transaction, with nothing bound. The dashboard's next turn already folds in rows written elsewhere before it runs (`_adopt_out_of_band_turns`), so a mounted-but-idle pane does not write over adopted history.

## Related Issue

Fixes #148450
Salvages #143701 (rebased on `main`)
Related: #146735, #146014, tracker #134889

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

- `tests/gateway/test_dashboard_pane_lease_adoption.py`, `tests/gateway/test_bot_dm_lease_holders.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_active_session_registry_compat.py`: cover idle adoption, mid-turn refusal/no bind, holder diagnostics, and old/new registry compatibility.

At this verification, upstream `main` is `242315ce57`; this head is 5 ahead / 219 behind. prs.title: feat(memory): add `hermes memory dream`, consolidation across conversations
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `hermes memory dream`: a memory pass that reads several recent conversations **together** and keeps only what no single conversation could have taught the agent — a preference the person restated twice, a project that keeps coming back, a thing they keep correcting.

The rule that shapes everything: **nothing a dream writes may be new information.** Every entry cites the conversations it relies on and one verbatim quote from the person per conversation; the quote has to appear in that transcript's own user turns, and every number, path and URL in the entry has to come from those quotes. An entry that fails is dropped, never softened, and the reason is reported.

## Related Issue

None opened yet — happy to file one first if the maintainers prefer to discuss the shape before a PR.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix
- [x] ✨ New feature
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor
- [ ] 🎯 New skill

## Changes Made

- `agent/dream.py` — the pass: read-only conversation collection, prompt, parsing, validation, planning, apply, journal, revert. No tools, no new core surface.
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/dream.py` — `hermes memory dream` parser and handler (`--dry-run`, `--since-hours`, `--max-sessions`, `--json`, `--revert`).
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/memory.py` — attaches `dream` under `hermes memory`, so the top-level command list is unchanged.
- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` — one `auxiliary.dream` slot (timeout 180) so the pass can be pinned to a cheap model; it inherits the main model otherwise. Line-neutral in a file already over the FILE_LINES ratchet.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/memory.md` — the design, the evidence table, undo, and a script-only cron recipe for nightly runs.
- `tests/agent/test_dream.py` — 18 behaviour contracts (below).

## How to Test

```bash
hermes memory dream --dry-run        # a verdict per proposal, nothing written
hermes memory dream                  # writes through MemoryStore.apply_batch, journals to dreams/<stamp>.json
hermes memory dream --revert <journal>   # undo that run
hermes memory dream --json           # the report, for scripts
```

Nightly, without spending the agent's own tokens:

```bash
printf '#!/bin/sh\nhermes memory dream\n' > ~/.hermes/dream.sh && chmod +x ~/.hermes/dream.sh
hermes cron create "0 4 * * *" --script ~/.hermes/dream.sh --no-agent
```

Beyond the unit tests I ran it end to end against a **copy** of a real `state.db` with a stubbed model: two conversations collected, the entry accepted with quotes from both, written to `USER.md`, journaled, then removed again by `--revert`.

## Design notes for review

- **Why a command and not a tool.** The prompt-surface bar is high and every tool is sent on every call; this is a maintenance action, so it ships as a CLI command + docs.
- **Why not extend the background review.** That fork looks at one turn of one conversation and asks "should anything be saved?". The point here is the cross-conversation view, plus checks a single-turn review cannot make: a new entry must be supported by at least two conversations, and every quote must be verifiable against the stored transcript.
- **Writes reuse `MemoryStore.apply_batch`**, so the same content scan, locks, duplicate rule and character budget apply as an ordinary `memory` call. The budget is checked cumulatively against the batch, so one over-budget entry cannot sink the rest — the plan refuses it alone.
- **Machinery turns are excluded.** Rows carrying a `display_kind` (steer notices, process-complete banners) never count as the person's words, so an injected `[IMPORTANT: …]` can never be quoted as evidence.
- **Undo is part of the feature**, not a follow-up: every writing run leaves a journal (conversations read, verdicts and reasons, applied operations with the previous text) and `--revert` replays the inverse, reporting entries that changed since rather than overwriting them.
- **No prompt or tool-surface change.** `tests/ci/test_prompt_surface.py` is untouched; memory still only appears at the next session boundary.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] Conventional Commits (`feat(memory): …`)

- [x] One logical change, no unrelated commits

- [x] `scripts/check --only ruff,health,footguns` passes. (`scripts/check`'s `shims` check fails in my local checkout because `.gitattributes` is CRLF in the working tree; this PR does not touch it.)
- [x] Tests added for the behaviour
- [x] Tested on Windows 11, Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Docs updated (`website/docs/user-guide/features/memory.md`)
