prs.title: feat(a2a): accept-then-poll client workflow and transient retry for a2a_call
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Requests A2A 1.0 immediate task acceptance and adds bounded client polling with transient read retries and task-ID-based resume. Once a peer returns a task ID, polling failures preserve it so callers can continue observing the accepted task without submitting another message.

## Related Issue

Not `Fixes`: this is a client-side robustness improvement to the A2A task lifecycle, not a fix for a single filed bug.

Related open work, stated plainly:
- #94880 and #91688 are **alternative implementations of non-blocking A2A tasks** and touch the same files. This branch is textually **conflicting** with both (`git merge-tree` reports conflicts in `adapter.py`/`protocol.py`/`tools.py`), so they are alternatives, not stacking PRs. Choosing between them is a maintainer call; this is the smaller, client-scoped one.
- #134286 (park long jobs past the reply window) is complementary in intent and also conflicts textually with this branch for the same reason.
- #156433 (tenant in `a2a_orchestrate` fan-out) merges cleanly with this branch.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/a2a/protocol.py`: new `return_immediately()` parser for the v1.0 `configuration.returnImmediately` flag (accepts the proto snake-case spelling and the v0.3 `blocking=false` equivalent; malformed truthy values do not silently opt in). `TaskStore.complete(..., force_terminal=...)` so `INPUT_REQUIRED` is terminal for the dispatch cycle but can still be overridden by cancel/hard timeout, and `TaskStore.watch()` returns immediately for it.
- `plugins/platforms/a2a/adapter.py`: inbound `returnImmediately` path returns the peer's real task id, plus a `_finalize_pending` settlement path that persists the reply once a turn result arrives, ignores late results for already-terminal tasks, and fails orphans via `fail_orphans`.
- `plugins/platforms/a2a/tools.py`: `_poll_task_until_terminal` (exponential backoff, retrying 408/425/429/500/502/503/504 without aborting), `_task_poll_error` preserving `task_id` in the error header for resume, `a2a_call(task_id=...)` to resume polling, `_persist_client_receipt` for idempotent client-side persistence of terminal replies, and `is_success()` in `a2a_orchestrate` so in-progress/polling states are not counted as completions in `best`/`first`.
- `gateway/platforms/event.py`: `merged_message_ids` records every message ID coalesced into one turn so each accepted ingress can settle its own lifecycle.
- Tests: `tests/plugins/test_a2a_client_polling.py`, `tests/plugins/test_a2a_task_lifecycle.py`, `tests/gateway/test_message_event_merge_ids.py` (all new) and `tests/plugins/test_a2a_plugin.py`.

## How to Test

1. `just test tests/plugins/test_a2a_client_polling.py tests/plugins/test_a2a_plugin.py tests/plugins/test_a2a_task_lifecycle.py tests/gateway/test_message_event_merge_ids.py` → 4 files, 133 passed, 0 failed.
2. Apply the four test files from this branch onto plain `main` **without** the source changes: 21 of 133 fail across all 4 files, so the suites exercise the new behavior rather than passing unconditionally.
3. `just check` → `scripts/check`: 22 checks, ok; code health 8 changed files vs `9f47677483d1`: 0 blocking, 0 advisory.
4. `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` clean.

Verified on exact head `b1b8c0e600b3f1f961cde3bbb3a3d040871ac72a` (parent `9f47677483d1`), 1 ahead / 219 behind current `main` `242315ce57`. `git merge-tree upstream/main p141947` is clean, so the distance is age, not conflict.

prs.title: Telegram voice notes and photos no longer time out on every retry after connections go stale (#156504, salvage #143866)
prs.body:
On Telegram, voice notes and photos were regularly lost with "could not be downloaded (Timed out)" and voice replies failed the same way, even though the network was fine: once a few of the gateway's kept-alive connections to Telegram went dead, each of the 3 retries picked up another dead one. Now the first such failure throws the whole set of connections away, so the next attempt opens a fresh one and goes through.

Fixes #156504

Salvaged from #143866 by @appstester0919 (classifier change, authorship kept), with the late-body-read case from @kvnloo's fork commit [`6a1ab9b682`](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/commit/6a1ab9b68200314848f0f253580d955d5b58f7fe) (Co-authored-by). Reported with excellent same-minute probe data by @mspservices.

## What changes (real sockets, local server whose 4 pooled keep-alive connections go silent)

`scratch probe: warm 4 keep-alive sockets, then each answers nothing; read timeout 1 s`

| request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ReadTimeout | ReadTimeout |
| 2 | ReadTimeout | **200** (fresh connection) |
| 3 | ReadTimeout | 200 |
| 4 | ReadTimeout | 200 |
| 5 | 200 (pool finally drained) | 200 |

The adapter retries `getFile`/`send_voice` 3 times, so on main all 3 land on dead sockets: exactly the reporter's "3/3 timed out while an independent client answers in 50 ms".

## Changes
- `PoolTimeout` joins `ConnectTimeout`/`ConnectError` as walk-on errors: the request never left, so trying the next Telegram IP is safe.
- `ReadTimeout`, `ReadError`, `RemoteProtocolError`, `WriteTimeout` (the request may already have reached Telegram) retire that path's pool generation and clear its sticky IP, then raise to the caller. **Changed from #143866:** that PR walked on and resent the request on the next IP in this case, which can post a `sendMessage` twice. Here nothing is resent inside the transport; the adapter's existing retry gets the fresh pool.
- The same retirement fires when the read dies in the body after the headers arrived (from @kvnloo: the transport's `except` has already returned by then), and on the primary-only route (proxy / custom `base_url`).
- Retirement uses main's `PoolGeneration.retire()`, so other requests still in flight on that generation are not cut off.

## Evidence
- Real-socket A/B above (`sockprobe.py`, main vs head, same harness).
- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_network.py`: 3 new cases (dead socket before headers, dead socket in body, pool timeout walks on) fail on main, all 26 pass on head.
- All Telegram gateway tests (`tests/gateway/test_telegram*.py`, 145 files): 1595 passed / 5 skipped.
- `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking.
- **Not covered:** the reporter's second finding (on a fresh connection `getFile` still sometimes exceeds the 20 s read timeout on their host) is a different, host-side cause; they are measuring with `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_READ_TIMEOUT`. Not tested against the live Telegram API from Windows.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab2bc49/ApKVMVtXJ5SnNEUvSK_0R_RiKYsXNR.png)

prs.title: fix(gateway): a failed stop no longer leaves the gateway running until SIGKILL
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the gateway hang in #158360. When a stop phase **raised** instead of hanging, `_stop_impl` disarmed its own thread watchdog on the way out (`finally: _watchdog_done.set()`). `_stop_release_runtime_state`, which sets `_shutdown_event`, never ran, so `wait_for_shutdown()` never returned. Every later `stop()` (a SIGTERM, another restart) re-awaited the failed `_stop_task` and re-raised. The process kept the host-gateway slot until SIGKILL, and on the restart path the failure was not logged at all.

Two commits, each with its own regression test:

1. **`fix(gateway): a stop that does not complete no longer disarms the shutdown watchdog`**
   - The watchdog is disarmed only when the teardown runs to completion (`shutdown_watchdog.disarm_after_teardown`).
   - A phase that raises is logged with its traceback right away, and a cancelled stop is logged as interrupted. The still-armed watchdog then forces the exit on its normal leash (stack dump, pid file and runtime lock released, `os._exit(1)`), exactly as it already does for a wedged phase.
   - Cancellation needs the same treatment: cancelling a task that awaits `_stop_task` tunnels into it, as the #12875 comments in `_stop_release_runtime_state` note.
   - This is suggestion 1 in the issue. It covers every phase, whatever raised.
2. **`fix(gateway): an ACP sweep that cannot import no longer aborts the stop`**
   - `settle_gateway_runtime` treats `end_idle_acp_sessions` as best-effort but imported it outside its `try`. The import now sits inside it (suggestion 5).
   - This is the import that raises the reported `ImportError` when v0.23.3's tree sits under a v0.23.2 process.
   - `hermes update` can leave a gateway in that state: one still doing live work when the pause wait runs out "keeps its pending restart and the update runs unpaused" (`hermes_cli/update_cmd_posix_pause.py`).

Why this approach:

- It reuses the existing forced-exit funnel rather than adding a second exit path.
- The leash and the exit code are unchanged, so in-flight turns keep the drain budget they had.
- No config and no env var.
- `run_shutdown.py`, already over the 2,000-line ratchet, gets two lines shorter.

Two consequences you may ask about:

- **Exit code 1, also during a requested restart.** A stop that fails is reported as a failure, as a wedged stop already is, not as a clean planned restart (75). The stock systemd unit is `Restart=always`, and launchd's `KeepAlive` respawns on any non-zero exit, so the gateway comes back either way.
- **The watchdog can now end the process after a failed stop.** It already does that after a wedged one, and every in-tree caller of `start_gateway()` hard-exits as soon as it returns (`gateway/run.py` main, `hermes gateway run`, `cli.py --gateway`). On the restart and SIGTERM paths nothing returned control to a caller before this change either: `wait_for_shutdown()` blocked forever.

Not done here are the issue's suggestions 2–4: continuing the remaining phases after a failure, making a second `stop()` force the exit, and a done-callback on `_restart_task`. With the watchdog armed, none of them is needed to get the process out. Happy to follow up if you want a faster exit than the leash.

## Related Issue

Fixes #158360

Overlapping open work, checked before writing this:

- **#108738** (for #108729) contains the same core change as commit 1 inside a larger post-teardown exit backstop: `_watchdog_done.set()` gated on a `teardown_complete` flag. Its description does not mention the raise path. The two agree on semantics: disarm only on completion, cancellation included. If #108738 lands first, commit 1 shrinks to the immediate error log and the tests, and I'll rebase.
- **#156799** changes the next line of the same loop (`await asyncio.to_thread(end_idle_acp_sessions, authority)`). That is a textual conflict with commit 2, not a semantic one.
- #145396 is the same call site with a slow sweep, not a raising one. This PR does not change it.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/shutdown_watchdog.py`: adds `disarm_after_teardown(done_event)`. It sets the done event only when the guarded body completes. An `Exception` is logged with its traceback and re-raised; a cancellation or other `BaseException` is logged as an interrupted stop and re-raised. Either way the watchdog stays armed.
- `gateway/run_shutdown.py`: `_stop_impl` uses it instead of `try/finally: _watchdog_done.set()`.
- `gateway/run_runtime.py`: `settle_gateway_runtime` imports `gateway.session_acp_lifecycle` inside the existing best-effort `try`. The docstring no longer says that raising "would disarm the watchdog".
- `tests/gateway/test_gateway_shutdown.py`: behaviour tests that run a real `stop()` in a disposable child process, following `test_refusal_stamp_reaches_disk_before_the_hard_exit`, so the watchdog's real `os._exit` can only end the child.
  - The watchdog `stop()` arms is started (0.2 s leash) only after the stop has unwound, so its expiry follows what the stop did on any runner.
  - A stop whose phase raises, and one cancelled midway, both end the child with exit code 1 and the watchdog's own firing diagnostic, and the raise is logged with its traceback. A completed stop disarms the watchdog: the child exits 0 and the watchdog never fires.
  - The child is outside pytest's fences, so it gets a seeded home, an empty managed-config dir, its own lock dir and no `.env` loading. It also bounds itself (60 s), because on a Windows venv the parent's timeout only reaches the launcher shim.
- `tests/gateway/test_run_runtime_hot_serve_cleanup.py`: `settle_gateway_runtime` completes, and still revokes tickets, when `gateway.session_acp_lifecycle` cannot be imported.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_gateway_shutdown.py tests/gateway/test_run_runtime_hot_serve_cleanup.py -k "watchdog or acp_sweep"`
   - On this branch: 4 passed, three repeats. Both files in full: 21 passed.
   - On `main` (a0097551b6): the three new regression cases fail and the completed-stop case passes.
2. Mutations of `disarm_after_teardown`:
   - Always disarm (`main`'s behaviour): the raise and cancel cases fail.
   - Disarm on cancellation: the cancel case fails.
   - Never disarm: the completed-stop case fails.
3. A real process with the real watchdog and `os._exit`, a throwaway `HERMES_HOME` and a 3 s leash. This uses the A/B script from the issue, which makes the ACP import raise:

   | tree | result |
   |---|---|
   | `main` a0097551b6 | stop raised; watchdog disarmed; `_shutdown_event` never set; **still alive at 10 s**, rc 0 |
   | commit 1 only | error **logged with traceback at once**; watchdog stayed armed and **fired at 3 s, rc 1** |
   | both commits | import failure logged and absorbed; **stop completed**, `_shutdown_event` set |
   | both commits, `hang` control | watchdog fired at 3 s, rc 1 (unchanged) |

4. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/` (2,126 files): 17,002 passed, 388 skipped, 1 failed.
   - The failure, `test_session_client_env.py::test_auto_started_gateway_does_not_inherit_client_behaviour_env`, fails the same way on `main` a0097551b6.
   - Stop-path tests outside `tests/gateway/` (`acp_adapter`, `agent`, `hermes_cli`, `tools`; 5 files): 52 passed, 2 failed. Both failures (`test_delegate_resumable.py`) fail the same way on `main` a0097551b6.
5. `scripts/check`: 22 checks ok; code health 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (see Related Issue)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [x] I've run the tests for the code I changed (`scripts/run_tests.sh`, what `just test` runs), and they pass
- [x] `scripts/check` passes (what `just check` runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 27.2.1 (arm64), Python 3.14.9 dev env (`pm.build_env --group dev --group test`)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation: docstring in `settle_gateway_runtime`. No user docs describe the stop watchdog's disarm.
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: the watchdog is a thread plus `os._exit`, the same on every platform, and nothing here is POSIX-specific. The child-process test uses `sys.executable`, UTF-8 I/O and a self-imposed deadline, so it is safe behind the Windows venv launcher.
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Commit 1 alone, real process, ACP import made to raise (trimmed):

```
Gateway stop failed; the shutdown watchdog stays armed to force the exit
Traceback (most recent call last):
    await settle_gateway_runtime(self, _effective_watchdog_leash(self) - ctx.elapsed(), GatewayRunner._shutdown_interrupt_reason(self))
    from gateway.session_acp_lifecycle import end_idle_acp_sessions
ModuleNotFoundError: import of gateway.session_acp_lifecycle halted; None in sys.modules
[  0.0s] watchdog disarmed=False  shutdown_event set=False
Gateway shutdown watchdog fired after 3s (pid=43558); dumping all thread stacks.
Shutdown watchdog fired after 3s — forcing process exit (asyncio drain path appears wedged; see …/logs/gateway-shutdown-watchdog.log)
rc=1
```

Known cosmetic limitation: the watchdog's own message still says the drain path "appears wedged". The error logged just before it says what actually failed.

---

*Prepared with [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent): it reproduced the hang, wrote the fix and the tests, and ran every check above. OpenAI Codex reviewed the branch over five rounds; all of its findings are addressed.*

prs.title: fix(bootstrap): helper imports must not fence running cron with install maintenance
prs.body:
## Summary

Prevent a standalone Python helper from acquiring automatic installer/source-update custody merely because it imports `hermes_bootstrap` directly from `__main__`.

**Operational impact / priority request:** please consider this a reliability bug, not a startup-speed optimization. On a running installation, a small repair/reporting helper entered `prepare_launch` after plugin inputs changed. Its output reported `completing source-update dependencies`; during that custody window an unrelated scheduled monitor was refused with:

```
GatewayUnavailableError: Gateway draining: update_paused
```

The cron did not ask for an update. This can make scheduled work fail while an operator is performing an unrelated task. Retrying cron or waiting longer does not remove the unintended maintenance trigger. We have observed repeated maintenance-related disruptions on the installation; this PR reproduces and fixes the specific direct-helper-import path rather than claiming to solve every draining/restart failure.

## Reproduction and change

A normal `python helper.py` or `python -c 'import hermes_bootstrap'` is not necessarily a Hermes product launch. Today both can call automatic completion and early dependency repair from the module body.

- Recognize the existing managed-launcher marker and actual source/product entry points, without matching command-line keywords.
- For helpers, skip `prepare_launch` and automatic `recover_if_needed`; still activate the committed runtime and retain interrupted-tree recovery, networking and scratch setup.
- Preserve product launches and explicit update behavior. A real update's lock is not bypassed, cron failures are not hidden, and no new configuration flag is introduced.
- Update disposable launcher fixtures to identify themselves as launchers; include the new bootstrap dependency in their source slices.

## Related work / why a separate PR

Related: #152045, #140045, closed #134221.

This is a narrower operational distinction, not a claim that the broader bootstrap import hazard is new. In #152045, `_ENTRY_POINT_MODULES` includes `__main__`, so an ordinary helper directly importing bootstrap is still classified as a launcher. That proposal also keeps `recover_if_needed` unconditional. Those two details leave this reproduction reachable. #140045 removes some indirect library triggers but not a helper's deliberate bootstrap import.

Happy to fold this direct-helper regression and maintenance boundary into the broader fix if maintainers prefer one combined landing. Please retain both negative helper cases and the positive launcher/update controls.

## Verification

Against upstream main `242315ce571cde721e717a544cf8ae6c343315cf` (also checked latest release `v0.23.3`; both retain unconditional launch preparation):

- Before production change: two isolated helper regressions fail, recording `prepare` and `repair` before activation.
- After: `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 1 tests/test_bootstrap_helper_no_install.py -q`: **4 passed** (two helper negatives and two managed-launcher positives).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_source_launcher_publication.py`: **29 passed, 11 skipped** on Linux.
- `tests/pm/test_source_update_launch.py`: **19 passed**, including real PM source-update/re-exec checks for script, module and command launches, failed-update degradation and explicit recovery behavior.
- `python scripts/check --only ruff,health --base origin/main`: **passed**, zero code-health findings.
- `git diff --cached --check`: passed. Changed-file/diff secret-pattern scan: zero matches; no configuration, credentials, account identifiers, runtime state or unrelated plugin edits included.

Tests used the canonical runner, one worker and an existing isolated test interpreter. The PR worktree was moved outside the production Hermes data root when the home-I/O guard correctly refused PM's parent-manifest metadata probe; the guard was not disabled. The full all-checks lint command exceeded bounded local execution time; **full lint/CI is not claimed green**. CI remains authoritative for that lane and for skipped host-specific cases.

## Scope

This does not suppress genuinely requested upgrades, remove update locks, change cron retry policy, or promise that every library import is side-effect free. Source repair/activation and their existing failure semantics are deliberately retained. The local production gateway was not restarted to validate the helper-import fix.

prs.title: Slack file downloads never send the bot token to Slack's API (port centaur#2164)
prs.body:
Before this change, a Slack event carrying a forged file link could make Hermes call any Slack API method with the bot's own token, because the download check looked only at the host and every Slack host also serves the API. Now a file link whose path leads to Slack's API is refused before anything is sent, while real file downloads (including Enterprise Grid's `files-origin.slack.com` redirects) work as before.

Port from paradigmxyz/centaur#2164 (and its api-rs twin #2298).

## What changes

- `SlackAdapter._is_slack_cdn_url` keeps its host allowlist and now also refuses a URL whose first path segment is `api` after the normalization Slack applies before routing (percent-decoding, `//` collapse, dot-segment resolution).
- The same check already runs on each redirect target, so a redirect into the API is refused too.
- One parametrized invariant test in `tests/gateway/test_slack_download_ssrf.py` (red on main for the 6 API shapes, green on head).

## Live repro (real adapter, real slack.com, fake token `xoxb-forged-probe-0000`)

`SlackAdapter._download_slack_file_bytes(url)` on each tree. `invalid_auth` JSON means Slack's Web API router received and checked the bearer token.

| forged `url_private` | main | head |
|---|---|---|
| `https://files-origin.slack.com/api/auth.test` | **token sent** → `{"ok":false,"error":"invalid_auth"}` | refused before network |
| `https://slack.com/api/auth.test` | **token sent** → `invalid_auth` | refused |
| `https://acme.slack.com/%61pi/auth.test` | **token sent** → `invalid_auth` | refused |
| `https://slack.com/files-pri/T1-F1/../../api/auth.test` | **token sent** → `invalid_auth` | refused |
| `https://files.slack.com//api/auth.test` | sent, Slack answered 400 | refused |
| `https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T0123-F0456/report.pdf` (real shape) | fetched (404 for the fake id, via the files-origin redirect) | fetched, same |

With a real token, that first row is a working `chat.postMessage`/`conversations.history`/`users.list` call made by whoever controls the file payload.

## Ours vs theirs

| | Centaur #2164/#2298 | Hermes (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Host allowlist | narrowed to `files.slack.com`, `files.slack-gov.com` | keeps `*.slack.com`, `*.slack-files.com` (Enterprise Grid needs `files-origin.slack.com`, c57458a97c6d; already DNS-pinned + SSRF-checked, 8e4b5d877431) |
| Web API reachable via file URL | closed by the host narrowing | closed by refusing the API path |
| Redirects | rely on fetch dropping Authorization off-origin | each hop re-checked (existing), now including the API path |

Root cause: the allowlist trusted the host, but the Slack hosts it trusts all route `/api/<method>` to the Web API.

Tests: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_slack_download_ssrf.py tests/gateway/test_slack_download_redirects.py tests/gateway/test_media_download_retry.py tests/gateway/test_slack.py`: 258 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped. `scripts/check --only health`: ok.

Not covered: `files.slack-gov.com` (GovSlack) is still not in the host allowlist. It was not there before either; adding it is a separate change.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add lumoauth 0.1.1 (LumoAuth Guard)
prs.body:
Adds **LumoAuth Guard** (`lumoauth`), submitted by LumoAuth, the owner of [lumoauth/hermes](https://github.com/lumoauth/hermes).

## What it does

LumoAuth Guard checks every tool call in `pre_tool_call`, outside the model, and allows it, asks a person, or blocks it. The rules are capabilities that the owner grants to the agent in LumoAuth, so a prompt injection cannot change them. Some rules hold whatever the owner grants: the agent can never read the Guard's key, change Hermes's settings, turn plugins off, run `hermes plugins` / `hermes config`, or read credential stores such as `~/.ssh` and `~/.aws`. It is published on PyPI as `lumoauth-hermes`, and documented at https://docs.lumoauth.dev/agents/personal-agents.

LumoAuth publishes this plugin for its own service. It is pinned to a release tag; the same version is on PyPI.

## Hermes surfaces

- Hooks: `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call`, `post_approval_response`, `post_api_request`, `on_session_start`. No tools, no middleware, no `requires_env`.
- `ctx.register_cli_command()` for `hermes lumoauth setup | status | doctor | lock | unlock | reset`, and the `/lumoauth` chat command.
- Hermes's own approval prompt (the `approve` directive) for calls that need a person.
- The `lumoauth-guard` skill.

`hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes at the pinned commit. The plugin's CI runs its tests inside a real Hermes every week, on `main` and on 0.21.6 (`requires_hermes: ">=0.21.6"`, declared in `plugin.yaml` too).

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Network calls**, only to the LumoAuth organization that the user enters during setup:
  - Agent tokens (`private_key_jwt` and DPoP).
  - The agent's capabilities, every 60 seconds.
  - One audit receipt per decision, with a SHA-256 digest of the arguments. The argument values never leave the machine.
  - Approval requests, when the user picks LumoAuth approvals (`approvals: auto` or `lumoauth`).
  - The number of model tokens that the agent uses, once a minute, which LumoAuth counts against the token budgets that the owner sets for the agent. `reportUsage: false` in the Guard's `config.json` turns it off.

  There is no other telemetry.
- **Reads outside its own data:**
  - It reads the arguments of every tool call, which is how it checks them. It resolves symbolic links in paths.
  - It reads Hermes's `config.yaml` (approval mode, hook timeout).
  - Setup adds `lumoauth` to `plugins.enabled` and raises `plugins.hook_callback_timeout` to 180, using Hermes's own config writer, and prints both changes. `--no-hermes-config` skips this.
- **Credentials:** the agent's own EC P-256 private key, in `~/.lumoauth/guard/hermes/agent-key.pem` (directory `0700`, file `0600`). The plugin never reads Hermes's `.env`, `auth.json` or any other credential store. It blocks the agent from reading them.
- **Background work:** one daemon thread in the Hermes process that refreshes capabilities and sends receipts. No subprocesses, no shell commands.
- **Security scan: caution.** The scan finds credential paths (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`, `~/.docker`) in `src/lumoauth_hermes/paths.py` and in the skill. These are the paths that the Guard blocks.

## Approvals (rule 12) and the private-import warning (rule 9)

The plugin never approves anything itself. When Hermes would approve without asking (`--yolo`, `/yolo`, `approvals.mode: off`, or an unattended context whose mode is `approve`), the Guard blocks the call instead, so that no call skips the person.

To know that, it reads `tools.approval` and `tools.approval_context`, and `hermes plugins validate` warns about these two imports. When they are missing or change, it falls back to `config.yaml` and `HERMES_YOLO_MODE`. We asked for a public function in https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/158457 and will switch to it.

## Limits that the README states

The Guard runs inside Hermes and is not a sandbox. The README recommends the Docker terminal backend and lists the calls that bypass the tool hook (subprocesses that `execute_code` scripts start, `!cmd` shell escapes, tools that other plugins run with `ctx.dispatch_tool`), and safe mode, which loads no plugins.

prs.title: fix(kanban): refuse a model pin the assignee profile does not run
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A Kanban task's per-task model/provider pin (`kanban create --model/--provider`, `kanban set-model`, the dashboard editor, the `kanban_create` tool) is now accepted only when it is justified by the assignee profile's own configuration: it must be that profile's own model on the profile's own provider, or a model declared in `model.approved_pins` (on the provider the entry declares — bare entries inherit the profile's provider). Anything else is refused at mint, naming the allowed value(s).

## Why

Today `create_task` and `set_model_override` accept any non-empty pair, and the pin travels with the claimed card into the worker's session policy. A pin built from an invented string therefore buys a whole worker run on the wrong route, or dies at startup:

- a duplicated provider prefix — `nous/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` alongside `--provider nous`;
- a retired dated snapshot that is still a real catalog entry, so an "is this a known model?" membership check passes it;
- a truncated id;
- a foreign model pinned to this profile's provider, or the profile's own model pinned to a foreign provider.

Each is a typo-shaped string that nothing cross-checks against what the profile actually runs. This PR judges the pin by PROVENANCE, not membership.

## Changes

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`
  - `_validate_model_override` gains a `target_profile` keyword and the provenance rule; a model whose leading path segment repeats the supplied provider is normalized onto the bare id, but only when that bare id is itself a value the profile runs — normalization can never widen the gate.
  - `create_task` validates against the canonicalized assignee; `set_model_override` validates against the card's own assignee (looked up by id; an unknown id still returns `False`).
  - New helpers `_profile_model_policy`, `_approved_pin`, `_approved_pin_match` read the profile's own `config.yaml` side-effect free (no merged defaults, no `HERMES_HOME` switch).
- `tests/plugins/test_kanban_model_override.py` — existing plumbing tests declare the profile's model first; new coverage for the refusal message, the invented-string shapes, approved pins (bare and mapping entries), an approved model on an unapproved provider, the fail-closed cases (no assignee, no declared default), both call sites, and the dashboard PATCH surface.

## Behaviour notes

- A card with no pin is unchanged.
- A card with no assignee profile, or whose profile declares no `model.default`, fails closed: nothing can justify a pin.
- The profile's own model cannot be re-pinned to a different provider: `model.default` runs on the profile's declared provider, and a mapping pin that re-points the default model elsewhere is refused (fail closed — change the profile's config instead).
- A pin cannot supply a provider to a profile whose config declares none: the pin is refused rather than resolving the default against a guessed backend.
- Clearing a pin, and unknown task ids, never need a policy.
- Existing rows are not re-validated; only new writes (create / set-model) are checked.

## Related

- #138458 / #138487 — the assignee profile being authoritative over the injections the dispatcher applies (opt-in, at spawn). This PR is the complementary write-time half: which override values can exist on a card at all. They compose; no conflict.
- #157714 — the skill-side analogue of this check (refuse at create what the assignee profile cannot load).
- #139302 (closed) — an opt-in pre-claim guard requiring that a model selection exists. This PR judges the selection's provenance at write time instead.
- #158166 refuses a card with no resolvable model before spawning; #144088 is its gateway-session counterpart. Same goal at a different layer (missing model vs unjustified pin); no file overlap.
- #128753 — fail closed for pinned worker runtimes; adjacent, but a different failure class (runtime fallback, not admission).

## How to test

```sh
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/test_kanban_model_override.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py -q
```

Manual: a profile declaring `model.default: deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` + `provider: nous`:

```sh
hermes kanban create "x" --assignee <that-profile> --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 --provider nous
# refused: names the allowed value and the approved-pins route
hermes kanban create "x" --assignee <that-profile> --model deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash --provider nous
# accepted
```

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`fix(kanban): …`)
- [x] Searched existing PRs — no duplicate (see Related)
- [x] PR contains only changes related to this fix (2 files, 1 commit)
- [x] Tests added and run locally (runner: `scripts/run_tests.sh`)
- [x] `ruff check` clean on the changed files
- [x] Tested on: Linux (CPython 3.11)

prs.title: Cron jobs run correctly on the DST fall-back night: hourly jobs fire in both 01:00 hours, fixed-time jobs once (salvage #128024 + #146444, inspired by Muse Code)
prs.body:
On the night clocks fall back, 01:00–01:59 happens twice. Today an hourly (or every-N-minutes) cron job goes quiet for the whole second pass, and a fixed-time job like `30 1 * * *` whose run ends in that second pass fires again the same night. Now hourly-style jobs keep their real cadence through both passes and fixed-time jobs fire once, like cronie.

Salvages @Froraut's #128024 (earliest fix for the wildcard half) and @Alexbob0's #146444 (the fixed-time half), with both authors' commits intact. Fixes #147553. Inspired by Muse Code 1.4.16 ("Scheduled prompts with an hourly or faster cadence now fire during both passes of the repeated hour when daylight saving time ends").

**Outcome:** across the fall-back night, every cron job fires exactly when cronie would.

## What changes (real scheduler cycle, America/New_York, 2026-11-01 00:00 EDT → 04:00 EST)

Driven through `create_job` → `get_due_jobs` → `claim_job_for_fire` → `mark_job_run` every real minute on a scratch job store (`sched_probe.py`, main tree vs this head):

| job | run length | `main` fires | this PR fires |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0 * * * *` | 1 min | 01:00 EDT, 02:00 EST, 03:00 EST (**second 01:00 skipped**) | 01:00 EDT, **01:00 EST**, 02:00 EST, 03:00 EST |
| `*/30 * * * *` | 1 min | …01:30 EDT, 02:00 EST… (**90-min gap**) | …01:30 EDT, **01:00 EST, 01:30 EST**, 02:00 EST… |
| `30 1 * * *` | 45 min | 01:30 EDT, **01:30 EST (twice)** | 01:30 EDT only |

Root cause: `compute_next_run` hands croniter the zone's naive wall clock, so from inside the first pass the second pass is "behind" the base and is never a candidate; and the existing strictly-after fold guard happily picks the second-pass copy of a fixed wall clock once a run ends there.

## Changes

- @Froraut (743c52c, b957311): scan the repeated span for a strictly-later second-pass (fold=1) occurrence when the job has `*` leading its minute or hour field (cronie's MIN_STAR/HR_STAR) or is `@hourly`.
- @Alexbob0 (a594164): fixed-time jobs only try fold=0 candidates (`jobs_time.repeated_hour_folds`), so a run ending in the second pass schedules tomorrow.
- Ours (b472ce9, from a Greptile P1): a fixed slot list in the repeated hour (`0,15,30,45 1 * * *` from 01:01 EST) fell through the two-candidate loop and returned a past 01:45 EDT. The loop now keeps advancing until a candidate is strictly later (bounded at 62).
- Ours (ff9542d): one `_runs_both_passes` rule instead of two copies, the second-pass scan moved next to it in `cron/jobs_time.py` (`cron/jobs.py` is past the file-lines ratchet); trimmed the fixed-time test file to its scheduler-cycle invariant.

## Verification

- Red on `origin/main` (swap of `cron/jobs.py` + `cron/jobs_time.py`): 4 failed / 8 passed in the two DST test files; green on head.
- Property sweep: 14 expressions × New York / Lord Howe (30-minute shift) / London × every minute of 6 h around each 2026 fall-back = 45,360 `compute_next_run` calls, 0 past results. The previous head failed it.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/`: all pass except `tests/cron/test_scheduled_occurrence.py` (3 failures), which fails the same way on `origin/main` in this worktree (`home_io_guard` FileNotFoundError on `effects.txt`). That's an environment issue, not this change; CI is the verdict.
- `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking. ruff (pinned 0.15.22) clean.
- Live: the scheduler-cycle A/B above (real job store, real due-scan/claim/mark path, no mocks of cron code; only the clock is stepped).

Not covered: a real gateway ticker across an actual DST transition (would need a wall-clock change on the host).

## Infographic

![The hour that happens twice](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab30956/2qYkW0NgtvYxzkja9xcZH_gRfWwjDd.png)

prs.title: feat(gateway): busy_result_mode carries mid-turn subagent and background-process results into the running turn
prs.body:
Fixes #136703

## What and why

When a background `delegate_task` child finishes while the parent is mid-turn, the session holds the result until the turn ends and then spends a separate model turn on it. This change adds an opt-in setting so the result can reach the turn that is already running:

```yaml
delegation:
  busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

With `steer`, the gateway's completion-delivery seam (`_deliver_completion_notification`) offers a claimed async-delegation completion to the session's running agent instead of admitting it as a new turn. Classic CLI runs its turns on the gateway (one-gateway runtime), so this one seam covers CLI, TUI and messaging sessions. `agent/background_results.py` appends them to the **next tool result just before that result is persisted**. This is the same mutable tail slot the iteration-budget and run-budget notices use, so:

- past context is never rewritten, and the prompt cache holds;
- the transcript matches what the model saw;
- the text is marked as background tool-channel evidence. It is deliberately **not** the `/steer` user-authority marker, because a child's output must not be given user authority.

If no later tool batch carries an offered result (the turn ends without another tool call, or is stopped), it goes back to the completion queue and arrives as the ordinary next turn, exactly as `queue` mode delivers it. Durable claims are acknowledged when the result is accepted, the same way the idle drain acknowledges them on enqueue.

Events owned by other sessions are returned to the completion queue untouched.

## Background-process completions

The same opt-in covers `terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` completions, under their own key next to `display.background_process_notifications`:

```yaml
display:
  background_process_busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

They go through the same seam and carrier, with a process-specific marker (`a background process you started finished…`). The settle contract differs because a process completion has no durable claim and belongs to its per-process watcher: requeuing it onto `completion_queue` would strand it. So the delivery call waits on the carry (`gateway/run_notifications_busy_result.py`). If a tool result carried it, the call returns True and no turn starts. If the turn ended without carrying it, the same call continues into the ordinary `_inject_watch_notification`, so watcher retries and fallback notices are unchanged. A cancelled delivery (shutdown) withdraws the offer, so the turn cannot carry what the watcher retries. A completion the agent already read with `process(wait/log)` (`is_completion_consumed`, checked for every process in a coalesced batch) is not shown again. Watch-pattern matches, heartbeats and API-server sessions keep queueing.

## Relation to #104434

#104434 (`result_delivery="inject"`) only injects into the **originating** parent turn and is chosen per call by the model. This PR covers the common case where the result arrives during a *later* turn, and is a user-level config default. The two are orthogonal.

## Scope

- Durable claims stay held while the result rides the turn: acknowledged once a tool result carried it (watcher tick), deferred and requeued at turn cleanup otherwise, so nothing is lost and no delivery attempt is spent. API-server sessions and per-task failure notices keep queueing. `gateway/run_busy.py` is untouched: other internal events still never steer.
- New config keys are in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, plus the dashboard selects, `cli-config.yaml.example` and the docs (delegation, tools, gateway internals). No env var. `config_defaults.py` is over its file cap, so both keys are offset by folding neighbouring comments.
- #140296 / #142319 change how the *queue* path coalesces completions; they are orthogonal (with `queue`, the default, nothing here runs).

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_background_results.py`: a real `run_conversation` loop. A result offered while the model is thinking appears on the tool result of the next request, never as a user row. It is red without the `tool_executor` hook.
- `tests/gateway/test_delegation_busy_result_steer.py`: a busy-session result rides the running turn's tool result and no new turn is admitted; an uncarried result is deferred and requeued as the next turn. Both red on `main`.
- `tests/gateway/test_process_busy_result_steer.py` (mode read from a real `config.yaml` through the gateway loader): a busy-session process completion rides the tool result and no turn is admitted; an uncarried one is admitted once as the next turn; one already read with `process(wait)` is not shown again. The carry test is red without the process commit: the completion is delivered at once as a new turn.

Run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`: the two new files plus `tests/gateway/test_completion_delivery.py`, `test_completion_owner_retry.py`, `test_async_delegation_session_binding.py` (all passed). Process part: 14 files incl. `test_background_process_notifications.py`, `test_gateway_shutdown.py`, `test_display_config.py`, `test_web_server.py` → 498 passed. `python scripts/check`: ok. Platform: Linux.

---

**Rebase note (2026-10-15):** rebased onto `main` @ `3dd9e4edfd` (2 commits, clean); `tests/agent/test_background_results.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_delegation_busy_result_mode.py` → 3 passed.






**Update (2026-10-17):** the first version hooked the classic CLI's turn monitor, which no longer runs since classic CLI turns moved onto the gateway; live probe confirmed results still queued. The steer path now lives at the gateway completion-delivery seam and the dead CLI hook is removed. Rebased onto `main` @ `e7e839a5f4`.
**Update (2026-10-24):** rebased onto `main` @ `dd5bc7ee13`; added the background-process completion path (last commit) and a `config_defaults.py` line offset.

prs.title: fix(cli): withdraw a prompt fenced behind a lost turn after submit, and say when it waits on a running turn
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Upstream now covers the main lost-turn path in the classic CLI: `_prepare_submit` refuses a prompt
when the session already holds an `unknown` admission, and `/discard <admission_id>` acknowledges it
(4e35169b2b, 342a55ebad). This PR was rebased onto that work and narrowed to the two cases it does
not cover. The `/discard` route, the pre-submit refusal and the related tests that this PR originally
carried were dropped in favour of upstream's.

1. **Fence lands after submit.** If the owner restarts while a prompt is being submitted, the
   pre-submit check passes, the prompt is admitted, and the restarted owner then fences the turn
   ahead of it as `unknown`. The new prompt sits `queued` behind it and the CLI waits for a
   `message.complete` that never comes (`Initializing agent...` with no end). `_pump` now watches
   the `pending` list from `session.info`; when its own admission is `queued` behind an `unknown`
   one, it withdraws the prompt with `prompt.cancel` and returns `failure_reason="unknown_execution"`
   with the same `/discard` recovery copy, instead of hanging.
2. **Queued behind another running turn.** When the prompt is queued behind an admission that is
   still running (for example an automation turn the restarted owner drains first), the CLI prints
   once that the message is queued and should not be resent. Previously it stayed silent, which is
   what led users to resend the same message into the queue.

Fail-closed is unchanged: nothing is replayed, and no turn is discarded without an explicit `/discard`.

## Related Issue

Refs #139532 (CLI + gateway paths; ACP is #139541)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: `_pump` returns `_BLOCKED` when this turn's admission is queued
  behind a lost turn (`_queued_behind_lost`); `run_conversation` withdraws it with `prompt.cancel`
  and returns the `/discard` recovery. `_running_ahead` drives the one-time "Queued: another turn is
  still running" notice.
- `agent/turn_failure_copy.py`, `agent/error_surface.py`: `unknown_execution` is a gateway-layer
  site failure code, so the CLI shows the recovery copy as written instead of classifying it as a
  provider failure.
- `gateway/session_authority.py`, `gateway/session_ingress.py`: the `Session … paused:
  unknown_execution` log warning names the exact operator command (`hermes [-p <profile>] sessions
  discard <id>`) instead of an unnamed operator.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore reasoning display after gateway reconnect
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Restore the classic CLI's reasoning display preference when its existing connection reconnects to the gateway.

The gateway's `live.show_reasoning` flag is intentionally session-scoped and in-memory. `GatewayAgent.reasoning_callback` sends it and caches the last `(session_id, enabled)` pair. After a gateway restart the CLI keeps that cache, but the new owner has no flag. `GatewayConnection._resubscribe` restores the subscription without restoring the preference. Replies still stream, but live reasoning no longer does; the CLI can subsequently render `last_reasoning` in its end-of-turn fallback box, below the streamed reply. Restarting the CLI masks the problem by sending the flag again.

Keep the preference in this viewer's per-session state and replay it after a successful resume, before the reconnected socket becomes ready. Use the asynchronous client already on that loop, not the blocking `connection.call`. Preserve explicit hidden preferences too; sessions without a preference are untouched. A restore failure follows the existing reconnect failure path, so no prompt is silently admitted before restoration. No prompt replay, persistent config write, transcript mutation, or new protocol/config field is introduced.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (classic CLI reconnect regression).
Related: #139470 restores the same live flag on ACP reattachment. This PR changes the classic CLI only; it does not duplicate ACP, Desktop, reasoning-effort persistence, or commentary routing work.

Searched open and closed/merged issues and PRs for the symptom, `show_reasoning`, reconnect/restart, and the cache symbol; checked the tracker body and comments. No existing classic CLI fix for this path was found.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: remember the callback-derived preference on the session's shared viewer state.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_connection.py`: restore that preference after resuming each retained session, before readiness/new requests. A refused resume is still skipped, with no config write for that session.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_reconnect.py`: exercise shown/hidden preferences, first-turn ordering, same-connection write deduplication, and independent preferences for multiple sessions. Update the existing lost-turn test for the added restore request.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_reasoning_reconnect_live.py`: use a real disposable gateway daemon and a loopback fake model, restart the daemon, and verify the same CLI connection/agent receives reasoning before answer deltas on its next turn.

## How to Test

Interactive reproduction:
1. Start a classic CLI session with streaming and `/reasoning show`.
2. Finish a turn, then restart its gateway while keeping the CLI open.
3. Ask another question in the same CLI. Expected: live reasoning still arrives before the reply, without restarting the CLI. On the base, the owner loses its flag and reasoning falls back to the end-of-turn box.

Automated validation on Linux, Python 3.14.7:
- Base: `0f3eac0b8f7ccef9c469c9e9469c5b08e538d8f4`.
- New regression cases on the unchanged base: **3 failed**, at missing reasoning callbacks / missing restore writes (not collection failures).

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep a session's subagents visible after its cached parent agent is rebuilt
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A session's delegated children disappear from `subagent.list` once the gateway rebuilds the cached agent for that route, while the children are still running. `subagent.tail`, steer and interrupt then report the child as unavailable, so the Ctrl+T monitor and the dock show an empty roster for work that is still in progress.

Root cause: `gateway/session_ancillary.py::subagent_records` ties a child to the session only through the parent agent object (`registry._is_descendant_of(record['agent'], parent)`). A child keeps a weakref to the agent that spawned it. After a cache rebuild, `authority.agent(ref)` returns the replacement agent, the old weakref no longer matches it, and the roster comes back empty. The lineage fallbacks don't cover this either, because they only list rows read-only.

The fix carries the gateway's own `LiveSession` record, which survives a parent rebuild but not a replaced conversation, and matches on that exact object:

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`: `wire()` binds the turn's `LiveSession` on the agent as `_canonical_session_owner` (added to `_TURN_ATTRS`, so `restore()` puts back the previous value).
- `tools/delegate_tool.py`: `_build_child_agent` copies it onto the child when it is built, because a detached child can register after the parent turn has unwired.
- `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`: `_register_child` stores that record as `owner_session_record`, and nested children inherit it.
- `gateway/session_ancillary.py`: `_owner_objects` passes the session's `LiveSession`, and `subagent_records` checks `record['owner_session_record'] is session_owner` before the existing parent and lineage matches.

This keeps the existing rule that an identical durable session id never transfers access to old objects. The match is object identity on `LiveSession`, so a different `LiveSession` that reuses the same id gets an empty roster. A child that carries no token is still invisible after the rebuild (`owned` in the fixture).

Overlap checked: #114420 carries owner authority across a background-thread hop, #116204 shares the roster across processes, and #135874 lists sibling sessions in `delegate_task(action=list)`. None of them covers a parent cache rebuild within the same process.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. The searches I ran are listed under Overlap checked above.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`, `gateway/session_ancillary.py`, `tools/delegate_tool.py`, `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`, as described above.
- `tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py` (new, 2 tests):
  - The roster and controls keep the owned child after a parent rebuild and after the parent is gone. A foreign token and an unstamped child stay hidden. Reusing the durable id with another `LiveSession` returns nothing.
  - A child registered after the parent unwired still records the session owner.
- `tests/gateway/fixtures/ancillary_reads_peer.py` (real gateway daemon probe used by `test_session_ancillary_reads.py`): adds a `rebound` child stamped with the session's `LiveSession` under an old parent. It is listed and tailable, and after `_agent_cache[route]` is replaced with a new generation it is still the only child listed. `owned` (no token) stays hidden, as before.

## How to Test

1. Plant only the test hunks on `main`: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py tests/gateway/test_session_ancillary_reads.py` gives 3 failed, including `assert [] == ['owned']` and `test_activity_snapshot_requires_current_owner_objects`.
2. Same command on this branch: 4 passed.
3. Related files (`tests/gateway/test_session_ancillary*.py`, `test_subagent*.py`, `test_local_viewer*.py`, `tests/tools/test_delegate*.py`, 51 files): 418 passed, 0 failed.
4. `python scripts/check`: 14 checks ok, 0 blocking health findings.

I've been running this change on a long-lived gateway since mid-October. Before it, a rebuilt parent left the CLI subagent monitor empty while its children kept running. With it, the children stay listed and steerable.

prs.title: fix(build): run build scripts' main() from a symlinked checkout
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Node build scripts under `scripts/build/` did nothing and exited 0 when the checkout was reached through a symlink. Node resolves symlinks in `import.meta.url` but not in `process.argv[1]`, so the main-module checks (`import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(resolve(argv[1])).href`) never matched and `main()` never ran. `hermes_cli.source_build` then printed "✓ Building the web UI" while `hermes_cli/web_dist` stayed missing.

This compares against the canonical (realpath) entry path instead. I kept the fix inline in each file rather than adding a new shared module, because these scripts ship in fixed file lists (`nix/*.nix`, `scripts/ci/desktop_build_cache.py`, the desktop side-by-side test) and a new import would have to be added to all of them.

## Related Issue

Fixes #157761

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/build/frontend-common.mjs`: `isMain()` (used by `web.mjs`, `tui.mjs`, `desktop.mjs`, `webapp.mjs`, `freshness.mjs`, `desktop-reuse.mjs`) compares against `canonical(path.resolve(argv[1]))`, reusing the file's existing `canonical()` helper.
- `scripts/build/node-deps.mjs`, `scripts/build/electron-runtime.mjs`, `scripts/build/python.mjs`: same check, `realpathSync` guarded by `existsSync` so a module imported from `node -e ... <arg>` (where `argv[1]` is an arbitrary arg) still just reports "not main" instead of throwing.
- `tests/scripts/test_build_main_symlink.py`: runs each entry point through a symlinked `scripts/build` dir and asserts `main()` actually ran (python.mjs writes a marker through `HERMES_PYTHON`; node-deps/electron-runtime fail with `--source is required`; `isMain` returns true through a symlink and false when imported from `-e`).
- `contributors/emails/victorgalloo@icloud.com`: contributor mapping (same file as in #157955/#157956).

Not touched: `apps/desktop/scripts/*` and `tests/install/e2e-assets/*` use the same pattern but aren't on the source-build path from the issue; happy to follow up if you want them aligned.

prs.title: feat(gateway): know which client sent each turn and which attached clients were recently used
prs.body:
## ELI5

Hermes could not tell which app you typed a message from, or whether you were still sitting at it. So a plugin that sends notifications to your phone had no way to stay quiet for a reply you were already looking at on your computer. Now each app can say what it is when it connects, Hermes remembers which app sent each message, and it keeps track of which connected apps you used recently. Nothing changes in what the model sees or in how any app behaves today; this only makes the information available to plugins.

## What does this PR do?

It adds three things to the gateway, all attribution only:

1. **A per-connection hello.** A client names itself once per connection on the existing `client.capabilities` call: `{name, version?, kind?}`. Known kinds are `desktop`, `webapp`, `tui` and `mobile`. An unknown kind is not an error: the name is kept and the kind is dropped, so a new kind never needs a server release. Desktop and the Webapp send it, in a call of its own, after their existing `server_requests` call. The version they send is the install's own; the hello waits at most one second for it and otherwise goes without.
2. **A turn stamp.** When an announced connection submits a turn, the session authority copies that label into the admission's committed `surface_v1.client`. `prompt.submit` gains no wire field, and a client-sent `client` param is still `invalid_params`.
3. **Presence.** Per connection and session, in memory, the gateway keeps the time of the user's last input. It is fed two ways:
   - input the gateway itself sees: submit, steer, interrupt, approval answers, and a person's accepted answer to a question, sudo, secret, vault or picker prompt;
   - a new `client.activity` call, in which a client reports how long ago the user last touched the device, for which sessions, and whether it can get the user's attention itself.

   A report is the connection's whole statement: sessions it does not list are dropped for that connection. `sessions: []` clears it, and `away: true` clears it at once (screen locked, computer suspended). A connection keeps at most 16 sessions per source.

Plugins read both through two new accessors, `hermes_cli.plugin_session.turn_client()` and `session_viewers()` (also `ctx.turn_client()` / `ctx.session_viewers()`).

**Why this shape**

- Identity is a self-declared label. No permission, toolset, approval, prompt text or telemetry reads it.
- **Nothing the model sees changes.** The system prompt, the tool list and every message are byte-identical with and without an announced client and with and without activity reports. A new test pins that, and a container run confirmed it on recorded provider request bodies (S15 below).
- **The stamp is not part of exact-retry identity.** An app updated between a send and its retry announces a new version; the retry is still the same request and returns the first row. Different text is still `admission_conflict`.
- **No hello means today's behavior.** An unannounced connection commits exactly the payload it committed before.
- **Profiles stay apart.** On a socket shared by several profiles, input counts only for the profile the request was for, and a report counts only where its session id names one attached session.
- **Accessors answer only for what the calling code is bound to.** `turn_client()` answers inside the turn it describes. `session_viewers()` answers for the session the calling context bound: a turn's, or the one a plugin's own slash command was typed in. In a delegated child, and where nothing is bound, they return `None` / `[]`. They never read the process environment.
- **Observing input cannot change a reply.** Recording presence never raises into the request it observed.

**The consumer.** The repo rejects accessors without one. The push-notification plugin for the Hermes mobile apps uses these two accessors to tell its relay when a reply's sender is at their computer, so a phone can skip that alert and alert again once they have walked away. That plugin change is built and was run against this branch (see "Container run").

**What a user sees**

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| CLI, TUI | None. They do not announce themselves in this PR |
| Desktop app | None visible. It sends one more `client.capabilities` call per connection |
| Webapp | None visible. Same extra call |
| Dashboard | None |
| The model | None: byte-identical requests |

## Related Issue

None.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

Eight commits (43 files, +2,094 / −54):

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `feat(gateway): let a client label carry a kind` | `gateway/session_client.py`: `kind` on the existing label, `CLIENT_KINDS`, unknown kinds dropped. Contract types updated |
| `feat(gateway): clients announce themselves once per connection` | `client.capabilities` takes `client`; stored on the WebSocket transport. A malformed label answers `4001` and keeps the earlier one |
| `feat(gateway): track which attached clients were recently used` | New `gateway/session_presence.py`; `client.activity`; `client_activity: true` in the `client.capabilities` reply; accepted server-request answers counted in `gateway/session_server_requests.py`; the serve handler ledger and its generated page list `client.activity` |
| `feat(gateway): advertise client identity and activity; Desktop and Webapp say hello` | `client-identity-v1` and `client-activity-v1` in `runtime.describe`; `apps/shared/src/json-rpc-channel.ts` sends the hello; `apps/desktop/src/lib/client-identity.ts` |
| `feat(gateway): stamp each turn with the client that submitted it` | `AuthorityConnection.submission` adds the label; `gateway/session_surface.py` commits and restores it; `surface_turn_client()` |
| `fix(persistence): keep the client stamp out of exact-retry identity` | `retry_input` beside `admission_fingerprint`, used wherever a session-input payload is fingerprinted |
| `feat(plugins): plugins can read the turn's client and who is attached to its session` | `hermes_cli/plugin_session.py`, `plugins_context.py`, `plugin_api.json`, `gateway/session_context.py` (`bound_session_env`), plugin docs |
| `test(gateway): provider requests are identical with and without an announced client` | The prompt-cache guard |

Docs: three existing pages are updated to stay accurate (`developer-guide/gateway-local-sessions.md`, `developer-guide/plugins/public-api.md`, `user-guide/features/plugins.md`). No new page.

**Mixed versions**

| Pairing | Result |
|---|---|
| Older client, this server | No hello, never stamped; today's behavior |
| This Desktop or Webapp, older server | The hello call is refused (`4000`) and ignored, the same way `desktop_local` already is. Row S0 below is this pairing with a scripted client |
| Session rows written before this change | No stamp key; their retry digests are unchanged (pinned by a test against a literal digest) |
| Managed worker | The stamp crosses the worker frame; `session_viewers()` is `[]` there |

## How to Test

1. The feature's test files (base `ff7c9b202872`):
   `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_serve_handler_ledger.py tests/gateway/test_session_client_identity.py tests/gateway/test_session_presence.py tests/tui_gateway/test_client_identity_hello.py tests/gateway/test_turn_client_stamp.py tests/gateway/test_turn_client_retry.py tests/gateway/test_turn_client_prompt_cache.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_session_client.py tests/gateway/test_surface_admission.py tests/gateway/test_managed_turn_contract.py tests/tui_gateway/test_interrupt_resume_request_path.py`
2. `python scripts/check`.
3. By hand: connect a WebSocket client, send `client.capabilities {"client": {"name": "my-client", "kind": "desktop"}}`, attach to a session, send `client.activity`, submit a prompt, and read `turn_client()` / `session_viewers()` from a plugin's `on_session_end` hook.

Local results on this head (`0215829b3e68`, Ubuntu 24.04):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| The eleven files above, at each of the eight commits in turn | Passed at every commit: 63, 70, 88, 88, 101, 107, 113 and 114 tests, 0 failed (a file runs from the commit that adds it) |
| 125 test files that touch the changed modules | 1,974 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped, 12 errors. All 12 errors are in `tests/tools/test_delegate_child_shell_state.py`, which errors the same way on the base on this machine (its guard refuses to run when the temp directory sits under the real Hermes home) |
| `scripts/check` | 22 checks ok |
| Code health against `ff7c9b202872` | 0 blocking, 0 advisory |
| `gen_gateway_contracts.py --check`, `gen_plugin_api_docs.py --check`, the serve handler ledger test | Up to date |
| `apps/shared`: typecheck, vitest | Pass; 223 tests in 23 files |
| `apps/desktop`: typecheck; `src/lib`, `src/api` and `src/app/gateway` tests | Pass; 2,649 tests in 288 files, including the 5 in `src/lib/client-identity.test.ts` |

What the new tests prove against the base: the behavior tests fail there on behavior. The presence and accessor test files fail there because the module or function they import is new. Some tests are controls that pass on both.

### Container run

A throwaway gateway in a container, built from this head (`0215829b3e68`), a scripted model that records every request body, the push plugin described above, a recorder standing in for the notification relay, and scripted WebSocket clients standing in for the apps. "Active" was set to 20 seconds, except the two rows marked 300. The right column is what the plugin posted for the reply of the turn in question.

| # | Situation | Plugin reported |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Desktop hello, activity reported, short turn | source `desktop`, active `true` |
| S3 | Webapp hello, page-input activity | source `desktop`, active `true` |
| S4 | Desktop turn that outlasts the threshold, no reports | active `false` |
| S4b | Desktop hello, never reports, short turn | active `true` (the submit itself is input) |
| S5 | `away: true` mid-turn | active `false` |
| S6 | Desktop disconnects before the turn ends | active `false` |
| S7 | One connection on sessions A and B, active on A; B finishes | B: active `false` |
| S8 | A phone submits while a Desktop is attached and active | source `ios`, active `false` |
| S9 | An unannounced client submits while a Desktop is active | today's label (`gui`), active `false` |
| S12 | Desktop active but says it cannot alert | active `false` |
| S14 | Same request id retried after reconnecting with another version | The retry returned the first admission; one turn ran; one push |
| S15 | The same two-turn conversation run twice: unannounced, then announced with reports | Each of the two provider request bodies is byte-identical between the runs, nothing masked |
| S16 | The client moves to session B four seconds before A's reply | A: active `false` |
| S17 | The client reports no session in view, without `away` | active `false` |
| S18 | Still active on the session, but can no longer alert | active `false` |
| S1 at 300 | As S1 with a five-minute threshold | active `true` |
| S4 at 300 | A 305-second turn with no reports | active `false` |
| S0 | The same plugin and clients on the base commit `ff7c9b202872` | today's label, no new fact; the hello is refused with `4000` and ignored |

All 18 rows passed, in one run. (A nineteenth row in that run covers a plugin-side switch and belongs to the plugin's own PR.)

**Companion changes**

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| Hermes Desktop and Webapp: report when the user is active | https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/158424 |
| Push plugin: label a reply with its sender and whether the user is active at a computer | https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-mobile/pull/126 |
| Apps: say which app is connecting | https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-mobile/pull/127 |
| Apps: Desktop Messages becomes Always / Only when I'm away / Never | https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-mobile/pull/128 |
| Relay: the per-device rule (patch attached to the issue) | https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-mobile-push-relay/issues/23 |

The plugin, app and relay changes live in private repositories.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass — results in the table above, including the one file that errors on the base too
- [x] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 (unit suites and the container run above)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A, no config keys
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — server-side Python with no platform-specific calls, plus one extra call in the shared client channel
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A, no tool changes

## Known gaps

- **The TUI and the classic CLI do not announce themselves.** Their turns are never stamped.
- **`clarify.lock` is not counted as input.** Its params name a request, not a session.
- **The stamp is stored; presence is not.** The label is written into the turn's admission row with the rest of `surface_v1`. Presence is per gateway process and in memory: it is empty after a restart until clients reconnect and act, and it is not available inside a managed worker. In each of those cases a consumer sees nobody present.
- **Rolling back with a stamped turn still queued.** A managed worker without this change refuses a stamped turn frame (`invalid_managed_worker_bootstrap`). Workers start from the owner's own checkout, so owner and worker normally match. The case that remains is the opt-in managed-worker mode rolled back to an older version while a stamped turn is still queued.
- **The Desktop hello can trail the first requests on a connection by up to a second.** On a window's first connection it waits that long for the app's version, so a prompt sent in that second can be admitted unstamped. An unstamped turn behaves as today. If the version read is slower than that (the hello came 13 to 15 seconds after a cold start in a Windows 11 VM before this limit existed), the first connection's hello carries no version; later connections of the window carry it once the read has finished. That is what the Windows 11 VM run showed with this limit in place: both cold launches said hello about a second after connecting, without a version, and both later connections of the same window carried it. In a macOS VM the cold-launch hello came 0.6 seconds after connecting and carried the version. Nothing reads the version today.
- **A client that never reports keeps only what the gateway saw.** Its submit counts as input, and nothing says whether it can alert.
- **An unknown key inside the label** is refused by the generic parameter check with `4000`; a bad value gets `4001`. Clients ignore either.
- **The retired-target retry path** uses the same digest helper but has no end-to-end test, because a submit to a deleted session is refused before it reaches the store.

## Screenshots / Logs

No UI change. The container-run table above is the log evidence.
