prs.title: feat(desktop): tell the backend when the user is active, so phone notifications can stay quiet
prs.body: ## ELI5 Hermes on your computer now tells the Hermes server when you are actually at the keyboard, so a plugin that notifies your phone can stay quiet while you are there and speak up once you have walked away. On Mac, Windows and Linux (X11) the desktop app uses the computer's own idle clock, so working in another app still counts as being there. In a browser, and on Linux under Wayland, it can only see typing and mouse movement inside the Hermes window. Nothing about notifications on the computer itself changes. ## What does this PR do? This is the client half of the server change in https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/158407, and it is stacked on that branch: **review only the last three commits** (listed under "Changes Made"). The other commits here belong to that PR and drop out of this diff once it merges. A report is a claim: "the user is at this computer, and this window can show them this conversation's reply." A false claim would silence a phone for a reply nobody sees. So the rule throughout is: report only on evidence, take a claim back the moment it stops being true, and say nothing when unsure. Silence is safe, because the server ages a report by itself. - **Main process (Electron).** Reads the OS idle clock (`powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime()`) on macOS, Windows and Linux under X11, and tracks lock, unlock, suspend and resume on every platform. It pushes a snapshot to the windows when the user comes back, every 45 seconds while they stay, and at once on lock or suspend. Nothing is pushed while the user is idle. Under Wayland there is no trustworthy clock, so it reports "no system source". - **Renderer (Desktop and Webapp).** One small reporter per window sends `client.activity` for the conversation on screen in the chat view. Evidence is the OS idle time when the main process has it (`basis: "system"`), otherwise pointer, key, wheel and touch input inside the document while it is visible (`basis: "page"`). Focus and visibility are never evidence by themselves. - **When it reports.** Only while the newest input is under a minute old: when the user becomes active, then at most every 45 seconds. Coming back is noticed at once when the first input is in the Hermes window, and within 15 seconds (the main process's check) when it is in another app. - **When it takes a claim back.** At once when the conversation on screen changes (the new list), when the window shows any page other than the chat, such as Settings (`sessions: []`), and when the window can no longer get the user's attention (`can_alert: false`). Screen lock or system sleep sends one `away: true`. - **"Can alert".** True when the conversation is on screen (a visible, focused window whose chat is the tab in front, not covered by another tab of its zone and not minimized), or when this app's own "Response ready" notification would fire for it if the turn ended now. A client that cannot get your attention itself never makes a phone go quiet. - **Only for backends that ask for it.** Nothing is sent unless the backend's `client.capabilities` reply carries `client_activity`. A refused report is swallowed. Nothing is ever created, resumed or dialed in order to report. - **Settings → Notifications.** One read-only row says what this window tells Hermes: which signal it uses (this computer, or this window only) and how long ago the last input was. On a backend without the feature it says phone notifications are not affected. **What a user sees** | Surface | Change | |---|---| | Desktop app | One new read-only row in Settings → Notifications. No change to when Desktop shows its own notifications | | Webapp | The same row. Presence there is "this window only" | | CLI, TUI, dashboard | None | | The model | None | Nothing is quieted by this PR alone. The reports are only data on the server until a plugin reads them. ## Related Issue None. ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made Three commits (35 files, +2,608 / −21, of which about 1,600 lines are tests): | Commit | What | |---|---| | `feat(desktop): main process knows when the user last touched the computer` | New `apps/desktop/electron/presence.ts`: guarded idle-clock reads, lock and suspend tracking, numbered snapshots pushed on `hermes:presence`, a fresh sample on `hermes:presence:get`. The preload and the Webapp bridge expose `presence.get()` / `onChange()` | | `feat(desktop): tell the backend when the user is active in a session` | `apps/shared/src/json-rpc-channel.ts` remembers `client_activity` per connection. New `apps/desktop/src/store/presence.ts` (evidence and the reporter) and `presence-view.ts` (which conversation is on screen and which connection owns it, the same way the composer decides). `usePresenceRoute` tells the reporter about a route move at once. The "would this notification fire" check is shared with the notification dispatch in `native-notifications.ts` | | `feat(desktop): show what this window tells Hermes about you being here` | One row in `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/notifications-settings.tsx`, listed in the settings manifest so search reaches it, with strings in all nine locales | Edits to existing files outside the new modules: - `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` is at its size cap and may only shrink, so the existing battery broadcast now uses the new send-to-every-window helper. Behavior is unchanged. - `apps/shared/src/json-rpc-gateway.ts` gains one getter so the renderer can read the `client_activity` flag. - `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/controller.tsx` mounts the three-line route hook; `use-gateway-boot.ts` starts the reporter. ## How to Test 1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project electron electron/presence.test.ts` 2. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project ui src/store/presence.test.ts src/store/presence-statement.test.ts src/store/presence-window.test.ts src/store/native-notifications-would-fire.test.ts src/app/hooks/use-presence-route.test.tsx src/app/settings/notifications-settings.phone-presence.test.tsx` 3. `cd apps/shared && npx vitest run src/json-rpc-channel.test.ts` 4. `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` in `apps/desktop`; `python scripts/check`. 5. By hand: open a conversation, then Settings → Notifications. The row shows "Last input N sec ago" and the number grows when you stop touching the computer. Local results on this head (`11794f98014f`, Ubuntu 24.04): | Check | Result | |---|---| | The eight test files above | 13 + 59 + 19 tests passed, 0 failed | | `apps/desktop` typecheck; `apps/shared` typecheck | Pass | | Whole `ui` test project | 1,664 files, 14,313 tests passed | | Whole `electron` test project | 4,331 passed, 7 failed (run one commit-fold earlier; the change since touches only three renderer files in `src/store`). The same 7 fail on the base branch on this machine (uninstall cleanup, a relocated-store check, a source launcher, two script tests); none touches this change | | `apps/shared` tests | 225 passed | | `pnpm lint` in `apps/desktop` | 0 errors | | `scripts/check`; code health against the stacked base | Pass; 0 blocking | | Each of the three commits by itself: typecheck, the presence tests, `apps/shared` | Pass at every commit | ### Live runs Each run used a throwaway gateway in a container (the server branch plus a phone-notification plugin that reads these reports), with a recorder in front of the gateway for the frames it received and a recorder standing in for the notification relay. "Push" is what the plugin posted for the finished reply: `true` means "the user is at a computer that can show this reply". Input was real: key presses and pointer moves through the VM console on Windows, real input events through the DevTools protocol in the browser. "Active" was 90 seconds unless noted. **On this head (`11794f98014f`), all three surfaces** | Situation | Windows 11 | macOS 27 | Webapp | |---|---|---|---| | Type a prompt, short turn | `true` | `true` | `true` | | Two minutes idle during a turn, then only move the pointer over Hermes (twice) | reported 0.23 and 0.24 s after the move; `true` | reported 0.13 to 0.28 s after; `true` | once, between turns after 155 s idle: reported 1 ms after; next turn `true` | | Same turn with no input at all | no report after the first minute; `false` | same; `false` | same; `false` | | A second conversation opened as a tab in front of the chat, pointer kept moving in Hermes (twice) | `can_alert: false` within 0.13 s; `false` | within 56 ms; `false` | at the click; `false` | | The chat's tab clicked back to the front | `can_alert: true` 23 ms later; `true` | 42 ms later; `true` | at the click; `true` | | Open Settings during a turn | `sessions: []` at the click; `false` | 47 ms after; `false` | at the click; `false` | | Lock the screen during a turn | `away: true` 0.16 s after; `false` | 0.24 s after; `false` | not applicable | The tables below are from earlier builds of this branch and were not rerun on this head. Since those builds two things changed, both in the reporter and both covered by the table above: a covered chat no longer counts as on screen, and a return to the Hermes window is reported at once. Rows marked † also predate the route hook (`usePresenceRoute`). **Windows 11 (VM), earlier builds, connected to the gateway as a remote gateway** | Situation | Frames the gateway received | Push | |---|---|---| | Type a prompt, short turn | report `basis: system`, `can_alert: true`, then the prompt | `true` | | 150 s turn, no input | reports at idle 14 s and 59 s, then none; Windows idle clock 108 s mid-turn | `false` † | | 120 s turn, typing in Notepad meanwhile, "Response ready" on (twice) | reports kept coming with `can_alert: true` and small idle times | `true` † | | Same with "Response ready" off | `can_alert: false` when Hermes lost focus, and in every report after | `false` † | | Turn in conversation A, switch to B and type | `sessions: []`, then `[B]` 68 ms later | A: `false` † | | 120 s turn, open Settings 4 s and 11 s after sending | `sessions: []` within 20 ms of the click | `false` | | 8 s turn, open Settings 1 s after sending (twice) | `sessions: []` at the click | `false` | | Settings and back to the chat during a 60 s turn (twice) | the session listed again 145 and 188 ms after returning | `true` | | Lock the screen (Win+L) during a 90 s turn | `away: true` 0.2 s after the lock | `false` † | | Gateway restarted while Desktop is open (twice) | Desktop reconnects by itself and says hello again | next turn `true` | | "Active" 300 s: 240 s turn / 330 s turn, no input | reports stop after a minute | `true` / `false` † | | Same Desktop against a gateway built from current `main` | the hello is refused and ignored, **no** `client.activity` frame at all, no error shown; the row says phone notifications are not affected | unchanged from today † | **macOS 27 (Tart VM on Apple silicon), the build before this head** | Situation | Frames the gateway received | Push | |---|---|---| | Type a prompt, short turn | report `basis: system`, `can_alert: true`, then the prompt | `true` | | 150 s turn, no input | one report at idle 26 s, then none; macOS idle clock 65 to 147 s mid-turn | `false` | | 120 s turn, typing in TextEdit meanwhile, "Response ready" on (twice) | reports every 45 s with `can_alert: true` and idle under 10 s | `true` | | Same with "Response ready" off | `can_alert: false` 16 ms after Cmd-Tab | `false` | | 120 s turn, open Settings and keep moving the pointer there | `sessions: []` 41 ms after the click | `false` | | 8 s turn, open Settings a second after sending | `sessions: []` 31 ms after the click | `false` | | Turn in A, switch to B and type | `sessions: []`, then `[B]` 19 ms later; later reports list only B | A: `false` | | Lock the screen (Ctrl-Cmd-Q) during a 90 s turn | `away: true` 0.28 s after the lock | `false` | | Gateway restarted while Desktop is open | Desktop reconnects by itself in 12 s and says hello again | next turn `true` | | Same Desktop against a gateway built from current `main` | hello refused and ignored, no `client.activity` frame, no error shown | unchanged from today | macOS asked for notification permission at the first finished reply; after "Allow", the "Hermes finished" banner showed (screenshot below). **Webapp (headless Chrome, fresh profile), earlier builds** | Situation | Frames the gateway received | Push | |---|---|---| | Type a prompt, short turn | report `basis: page`, `can_alert: true`, then the prompt | `true` | | 150 s turn, no input | one report at idle 17 s, then none | `false` † | | 120 s turn, then another tab in front (notification permission not granted) | `can_alert: false` 1 ms after the tab switch | `false` † | | 120 s turn, open Settings and keep moving the pointer there (twice) | `sessions: []` at the click | `false` | | 8 s turn, open Settings under a second after sending (twice) | `sessions: []` at the click | `false` | | Settings and back to the chat during a 60 s turn | the session listed again at the click | `true` | | Another in-app page (Capabilities, Scheduled jobs) during a 60 s turn | `sessions: []` at the click | `false` | | Turn in A, switch to B and type without sending | `sessions: []`, then `[B]`; later reports list only B | A: `false` † | | Same bundle against a gateway built from current `main` | hello refused and ignored, no `client.activity` frame, no error shown | unchanged from today † | The two "open Settings" rows are the reason for the route hook. On the previous build the Webapp reported leaving the chat only at its next 15 second check, because the router changes pages without a `hashchange` event; an 8 second turn finished inside that gap and was pushed `true` while Settings was on screen (seen twice). With the hook it is reported at the click. Not run live: Linux Desktop under X11 or Wayland. Those paths have unit tests only. **Companion changes** | Part | Where | |---|---| | Hermes server: which client sent a turn, and which attached clients were recently used | https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/158407 | | Push plugin: label a reply with its sender and whether the user is active at a computer | https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-mobile/pull/126 | | Apps: say which app is connecting | https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-mobile/pull/127 | | Apps: Desktop Messages becomes Always / Only when I'm away / Never | https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-mobile/pull/128 | | Relay: the per-device rule (patch attached to the issue) | https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-mobile-push-relay/issues/23 | The plugin, app and relay changes live in private repositories. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) — the commits before the last three are the server PR this is stacked on - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — these three commits change no Python; the Desktop and shared suites above ran locally, the rest is left to CI - [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs) - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 (unit tests, Webapp in headless Chrome), Windows 11 in a VM and macOS 27 in a VM (Desktop, live) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A, no user docs describe this yet; the settings row explains itself - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — the idle source is per platform, and Wayland falls back to in-window input - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Known gaps - **Wayland and browsers see only the Hermes window.** Working in another app there reads as away after a minute, so a phone is notified sooner than on macOS, Windows or X11. - **On native Desktop, "can alert" does not know the OS-level notification permission.** The renderer cannot read it, so it trusts the app's own notification setting. In the Windows run the OS put the "Hermes finished" notification in Notification Center (screenshot below); whether it also showed a banner was not determined. - **Only the main conversation is reported.** A conversation open in a second tab or a split tile is never reported, so it never quiets a phone: a reply there is pushed as it is today. - **After a reconnect the first report can take up to 15 seconds,** unless the user types first. - **macOS: a report sent in the same instant as a click or key press can carry the idle time from just before it** (seen in the VM while the user was already active: 6 to 21 seconds, where Windows reported about 0). The claim itself is right and the next periodic report corrects the number. - **Changing conversation sends two reports** (an empty list, then the new one, about 70 ms apart) instead of one. - **The settings row refreshes every 5 seconds,** not continuously. - **A minimized window was not tested.** Renderer timers are throttled there; the main process's pushes are meant to wake it. ## Screenshots / Logs **Webapp, Settings → Notifications** (same viewport and steps). With the added row the pane no longer fits and scrolls, so the "after" shot is scrolled to its end and its first two rows are off the top. | Before (`main`) | After | |---|---| | | | The new row, enlarged. On a backend with the feature: On a backend without it: **Windows Desktop** | The row (it reads "this computer": the OS idle clock) | On a gateway built from `main` | The app's own "Hermes finished" notification still arrives | |---|---|---| | | | | **macOS Desktop** | The row | The app's own notification while typing in another app | |---|---| | | | **A second conversation's tab in front of the chat** (the case that now reports `can_alert: false`) | Windows Desktop | Webapp | |---|---| | | | ## Infographic ![desktop-says-you-are-here](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab34b43/CFKWzeAd5wLmW5wU65bLv_Yijsyb5a.png)

prs.title: plugin-catalog: bump pit-crew to 0.2.1 (Hermes v0.23.2 compatibility)
prs.body:
SHA bump for the `pit-crew` entry: `91dec4414b60f7a90b5bdd561d336604b1cc630e` → `de3d51cf47ba8a1aced3060ac5af6ab530cfca1c` (0.2.0 → 0.2.1). Banner and screenshot URLs move to the new pin; images are unchanged.

Why: v0.23.2 moved `tools/send_message_tool.py` to `gateway/outbound/send.py` with no shim, and dropped `send_message action=list`. On the current pin, push alerts and `/car notify test` report "send_message is not available" on v0.23.2, and `/car notify list` can't list targets. Stored alerts (`/car alerts`, next-turn context) are unaffected.

Commit range: https://github.com/trevornk/pit-crew/compare/91dec4414b60f7a90b5bdd561d336604b1cc630e...de3d51cf47ba8a1aced3060ac5af6ab530cfca1c
- `watcher/delivery.py`: resolve `send_message_tool` from `gateway.outbound.send`, falling back to `tools.send_message_tool` (older Hermes still works; `requires_hermes` stays `>=0.23.0`).
- Target listing reads `gateway.channel_directory.format_directory_for_display` (read-only), falling back to the legacy `action=list`.
- Tests for both paths; CI now runs the real-Hermes steps (plugin load, approval pipeline, delivery, `hermes plugins validate`) against both v0.23.0 and v0.23.2, pinned by tag and verified commit. All 4 jobs pass at the new pin.

No capability changes: same tools, hooks, env.

issues.title: [Notice] Active Fork & Continued Maintenance: afjcjsbx/picoclaw
issues.body:
Hi everyone,

Since this repository currently appears to be unmaintained and there is still significant interest and demand from the community, I have decided to set up and actively maintain a fork to keep the project alive and moving forward:

 **Active Fork:** [https://github.com/afjcjsbx/picoclaw](https://github.com/afjcjsbx/picoclaw)

### For Contributors & Users:
* **Pull Requests & Issues:** If you have open PRs or unresolved issues here, please feel free to reopen or submit them on the new fork.
* **Maintenance:** I will be actively reviewing contributions, addressing bugs, and accepting new features.

Everyone is more than welcome to join, contribute, or leave feedback!

I hope this doesn't bother you,

Best

issues.title: Model identifier validation suggests lowercasing unknown provider prefixes, breaking case-sensitive upstream model IDs
issues.body:
## Summary

In the model edit sheet, entering a model identifier whose prefix is **not** a picoclaw provider but is an upstream model namespace (for example `ACME/gpt-4o-mini`, where the upstream API is case-sensitive) shows a warning:

> "ACME" should use "acme" — Fix

Clicking **Fix** rewrites the model to `acme/gpt-4o-mini`. With case-sensitive upstream routing this breaks a previously working configuration (401 / provider not found).

## Steps to reproduce

1. WebUI → Models → Edit (or Add) a model.
2. Provider = OpenAI, API Base = an OpenAI-compatible gateway, Model identifier = `ACME/gpt-4o-mini` (the prefix is an upstream namespace, not a picoclaw provider key).
3. The form shows the warning `"ACME" should use "acme"` with a Fix button.
4. Click Fix → the field becomes `acme/gpt-4o-mini`; saving it makes the upstream reject the request because its provider namespace is case-sensitive.

## Expected

- No "should use" suggestion unless the prefix actually maps to a known provider/alias in the provider catalog.
- When a Provider is selected and the field is documented as a full model ID (the field hint says a slash-containing value is kept as a full ID and not re-split), provider-prefix validation should be skipped.
- At minimum, do not offer a destructive one-click "fix" that lowercases an unknown prefix.

## Root cause (v0.3.1, git 2cf030d2)

- `web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts:26-28` — `normalizeProvider()` lowercases the input.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts:76-82` — `getCanonicalProviderKey()` returns `aliasMap[normalized] ?? normalized`; for an **unknown** prefix it falls back to the lowercased input instead of returning empty.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts:85-91` — the validator treats that fallback as a real alias and emits `models.validation.shouldUse` with `fix: ${alias}/${model}`.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/edit-model-sheet.tsx:268-269` — the Fix button applies `modelValidation.fix` to the input.

## Proposed patch

```diff
--- a/web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts
+++ b/web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts
@@ -79,7 +79,7 @@ export function getCanonicalProviderKey(
   const normalized = normalizeProvider(provider)
   if (!normalized) return ""
-  return getProviderAliasMap(backendOptions)[normalized] ?? normalized
+  return getProviderAliasMap(backendOptions)[normalized] ?? ""
 }

--- a/web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts
+++ b/web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts
@@ -64,6 +64,17 @@ export function validateModelField(
   const provider = trimmed.slice(0, slashIdx)
   const model = trimmed.slice(slashIdx + 1)
   if (!model) {
     return { level: "error", messageKey: "models.validation.emptyModel" }
   }
 
+  // When a provider is explicitly selected, a slash-containing identifier is
+  // documented as a full model ID for that provider (see modelIdHint) — do not
+  // re-interpret its first segment as a provider prefix.
+  if (selectedProvider) {
+    return {
+      level: "success",
+      messageKey: "models.validation.parsed",
+      messageParams: { provider: selectedProvider, model: trimmed },
+    }
+  }
+
   if (!knownProviderKeys.has(provider)) {
```

Add a regression test with an uppercase upstream namespace (e.g. `ACME/model`) and a lowercase provider alias in the catalog, asserting that no `shouldUse` warning is produced.

## Impact

One click can silently change a working model ID to a different, invalid one; the UI appears to be helping but breaks the configuration. This is more than a cosmetic warning.

## Environment

- picoclaw v0.3.1 (git 2cf030d2), Linux, WebUI

prs.title: build(deps): bump modernc.org/sqlite from 1.53.0 to 1.61.1
prs.body:
Bumps [modernc.org/sqlite](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite) from 1.53.0 to 1.61.1.
Release notes

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's releases.

v1.61.1

Signed provenance for this release: the two files below. VERIFYING.md in the repository says how to check them.

Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

Entries for v1.38.1 through v1.44.1 and for v1.49.1 were added on 2026-09-05, reconstructed from the git history and the merge requests they cite; they were missing at release time.

  • 2026-11-02 v1.61.2:

    • Limit now works on a connection handed out by a driver.Connector that wraps the ones NewConnector opens, provided the wrapper has an Unwrap() driver.Conn method; it used to fail with unexpected driverConn type. NewConnector now also says which optional interfaces such a wrapper must forward. Resolves [GitHub issue #11](modernc-org/sqlite#11), thanks Andres Morey (@​amorey)!

  • 2026-10-31 v1.61.1:

    • Prepared statements are no longer parsed and planned again on every execution. Since v1.61.0, SQLite 3.54 expired a cached statement that has a col = ? term in a join or an ORDER BY query whenever the driver cleared its bindings after a run, so a statement prepared with db.Prepare or tx.Prepare cost about twice what it did in v1.60.1. Integer bindings now stay in place between executions, so a parameter bound to 0 or 1 does not re-prepare it either. Resolves [GitLab issue #264](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/264). See [GitLab merge request #147](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/147), thanks Roman Khafizianov (@​requilence)!
    • Fix a panic reachable from SQL through a VFS made by vfs.New. It reported its files as writable, so with PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF a write reached a write method the VFS does not have and the process panicked, as did closing a WAL database shipped with its -wal file; with the journal on, the write failed with a misleading SQLITE_NOMEM. Such files are now read-only to SQLite, and every write fails with SQLITE_READONLY. See [GitLab merge request #145](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/145), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Fix a process abort reachable through a VFS made by vfs.New. SQLite's request to delete a journal, made when PRAGMA journal_mode leaves PERSIST or TRUNCATE and on the first read of a 0-byte database that has a -journal file next to it in the served file system, reached the transpiled xDelete, an unimplemented stub that aborted the process. It now fails with SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE, which SQLite tolerates, and nothing is deleted; the write methods the VFS lacked answer SQLITE_READONLY instead of being nil.
    • Tx.Commit now stops waiting for a lock once the context given to BeginTx is done, and Rows.Next and Rows.Close once the query's context is done, each returning the context's error; they used to wait the full busy_timeout when a reader's lock in rollback-journal mode blocked the COMMIT, or the commit of an autocommit INSERT ... RETURNING finished or closed after its first row. Only the wait watches the context; Rollback is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #263](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/263), thanks SirLouen!
    • The attest CI job now copies vendor.json into the provenance document from the tagged commit, not from the working tree make vendor-check has just stamped with its own Go release; the v1.61.0 job failed its own verification over that field, so v1.61.0 has no provenance document, see VERIFYING.md. Tooling only.
    • Add THREAT-MODEL.md, the threat model behind the scope in SECURITY.md: the connection string, the connection lifecycle, the page cache binding and the VFS bridge, one row per concern with its status and the commit that settled it. TestVFSReadEOF now also checks the short read on vfsRead itself. Documentation and tests only. See [GitLab merge request #146](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/146), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-10-21 v1.61.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.54.1, re-vendoring lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.2 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.7.0; sqlite-vec stays v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.79.0; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add _time_format=string_no_monotonic, opt-in: times are written in the default layout but without Go's monotonic clock reading, the m=+... suffix, so a scanned time matches its row again when bound in WHERE col = ?. The default is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #259](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/259). See [GitLab merge request #142](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/142), thanks 不插电 (@​r27153733)!
    • Each release tag now gets a signed provenance document, linked from its GitLab release; VERIFYING.md says what it proves and how to check one. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #141](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/141).
    • Add an opt-in SQLite authorizer per connection: AuthorizerRegisterer, reached through sql.Conn.Raw or installed on every pooled connection from RegisterConnectionHook; existing connections are unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #256](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/256). See [GitLab merge request #139](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/139), thanks Tedla Brandsema (@​TedlaBrandsema)!
    • Closing a connection now forgets the pre-update, commit and rollback hooks registered on it; their entries used to linger after Close.
    • With a shared cache, BeginTx now waits for a lock another connection holds instead of failing at once with SQLITE_LOCKED_SHAREDCACHE (262), as executing BEGIN IMMEDIATE did; Commit and Rollback wait likewise while another connection changes the schema. busy_timeout does not bound the wait; the call's context does. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • PrepareContext and BeginTx with a context that is already done now return the context's error, as ExecContext and QueryContext do. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • A context that is done before a statement starts running, for example while its arguments are being bound, now stops the statement within 1000 VM steps. SQLite discarded that interrupt, so a long statement ran to completion and only then returned the context's error. See [GitHub pull request #9](modernc-org/sqlite#9), thanks Chris Gianelloni (@​wolf31o2)!
    • A statement waiting for a lock under busy_timeout now stops waiting once its context is done, with the context's error, instead of sleeping on until the timeout; the wait's retry schedule and its bound are otherwise unchanged, and so is a call without a deadline. PrepareContext ended this way returns the context's error too, where it returned SQLITE_BUSY. Resolves [GitLab issue #262](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/262), thanks SirLouen!

  • 2026-09-29 v1.60.1:

    • Binding arguments to a statement is no longer quadratic in the number of its parameters, which made multi-row INSERTs with thousands of ? parameters slow. Resolves [GitHub issue #8](modernc-org/sqlite#8), thanks wencycool!

  • 2026-09-28 v1.60.0:

    • A fault while reading the memory-mapped -shm file of a WAL database no longer crashes the process. The statement fails with a disk I/O error, extended code SQLITE_IOERR_IN_PAGE (8714), and the connection stays usable, as in MSVC builds of SQLite. On by default on every platform and not switchable; lib.SehInject and lib.SehPending inject such a fault for tests. Resolves [GitLab issue #221](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/221), thanks Roman (@​requilence) for the report, and supersedes libsqlite3!4 and [GitHub pull request #7](modernc-org/sqlite#7), thanks hazyhaar for the two rounds, the ccgo finding and the Windows Server runs!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.6.0; SQLite stays 3.53.4 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. Go 1.26 is now required, and the pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.77.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Nine exported lib constants that never had a meaningful value are gone: INFINITY, MB_CUR_MAX, NAN, RESERVED_BYTE, SHARED_FIRST, SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT, SQLITE_CORRUPT_BKPT, SQLITE_DEFAULT_LOOKASIDE and SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT. The transpiler now evaluates object-like macros as C expressions, so other constants take their C value (lib.WALINDEX_PGSZ is 32768, not 0) and some appear; the full list is in libsqlite3's CHANGELOG under 2026-09-19.
    • make vendor now writes vendor.json, the modernc.org/libsqlite3 and modernc.org/libsqlite_vec commits and the Go toolchain lib/ and vec/ were vendored with, so git show vX.Y.Z:vendor.json says which revisions a release carries; the test suite fails when they no longer match. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #140](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/140).
    • vfs.FS.Close now refuses while a database opened through it is still open, returning an error that wraps the new vfs.ErrInUse and leaving the VFS registered. It used to free the VFS the open connection still called through, so the next query crashed the process or read through freed memory. Close the databases first, then the FS.
    • Fix handle reuse in modernc.org/sqlite/vfs on 32-bit targets: after 2^32 file opens in one process the handle counter wrapped and could overwrite a live entry, such as a file system registered at start-up, and crash. 64-bit targets were not affected.
    • The pluggable page cache now panics when a Cache breaks its contract by returning nil, or a different Page, from Fetch for a page SQLite still holds pinned. It used to free memory SQLite was still using, corrupting the database without an error. Only a Cache implementation with that bug is affected; modernc.org/sqlite/pcache is not.
    • Document three limits of the pluggable page cache on RegisterPageCache and Cache: it cannot be combined with modernc.org/sqlite/vec, PageCache.Create may be called concurrently, and under cache=shared a Cache is called from several goroutines. Documentation only.
    • Document in the package documentation that state set on a pooled connection is inherited by the next caller to borrow it, and that a connection reached through sql.Conn.Raw is not safe for concurrent use. Documentation only.
    • Add StrictPragmas, opt-in and off by default: once enabled, a connection whose _pragma DSN value holds more than one SQL statement fails to open with ErrMultiStatementPragma, before any DSN parameter is applied. A _pragma value runs as SQL text, so anything after a ; runs too. Recommended for any application whose DSN is not a compile-time constant.
    • Document SQLite's own URI query parameters on Driver.Open: mode, cache, immutable, nolock, psow and modeof, which have always worked in a DSN starting with file:, and the trap that a plain file name has its query stripped before SQLite sees it, so /path/to.db?mode=ro opens read-write. Resolves [GitLab issue #257](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/257). Documentation only.
    • Add SECURITY.md, the vulnerability reporting policy: three private channels, what is in scope, that only the latest release is supported, and how a confirmed report is disclosed, including an entry in the Go vulnerability database so govulncheck reports it. IRP.md, linked from it, is the maintainers' incident response plan. Documentation only.
    • Add CONTRIBUTING.md: where to send a merge request, which files are generated and must not be edited by hand, how to build and test across the 20 supported targets, and the AUTHORS/CONTRIBUTORS convention. Documentation only.
    • Ship LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.md, a transitively flattened inventory of every third-party component this module carries with all seventeen license texts in full, and a Software Bill of Materials, sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.6) and sbom.spdx.json (SPDX 2.3), explained in SBOM.md. Both cover what a module-graph tool cannot see: the transpiled SQLite and sqlite-vec C, and the upstreams modernc.org/libc carries, musl among them. Documentation only.

  • 2026-09-15 v1.59.0:

    • Bump the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.7 and re-vendor lib/ and vec/. The transpiled SQLite is unchanged, still 3.53.4. On the Linux targets the new libc replaces transpiled musl memcpy, memmove, memset, memcmp and strlen with native Go, cutting CPU time on query-heavy workloads by up to a third; see the new Performance section below. As always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does; see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Hand user-defined function and aggregate callbacks a pooled *FunctionContext instead of allocating a fresh one per call, removing the last driver-side allocation per invocation. Like the argument slice, it is valid only for the duration of the callback and must not be retained past its return. Updates [GitLab issue #226](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/226). See [GitLab merge request #137](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/137).
    • Add regression tests pinning the identity and the pooling of that context. See [GitLab merge request #138](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/138), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add a Performance section to the package documentation: measured CPU-time ratios of this driver against the same SQLite compiled from C, where the gap comes from, and the two consequences for applications — index the columns that ORDER BY, GROUP BY and WHERE use, and bound the database/sql pool with SetMaxOpenConns.

... (truncated)

Commits

  • e699042 conn.go, stmt.go, rows.go: unbind only the parameters that point into the dri...
  • 519e1d2 Merge branch 'clear-bindings-reprepare' into 'master'
  • 0afd2c8 stmt.go, reprepare_test.go, AUTHORS, CONTRIBUTORS: stop re-preparing cached s...
  • 683b727 vfs: implement xDelete and the write methods SQLite could still reach
  • 78c3b0c Merge branch 'threat-model' into 'master'
  • 56d8077 Merge branch 'vfs-readonly-open' into 'master'
  • 0ea9fb8 THREAT-MODEL.md: a row for the vfs.New write panic

issues.title: [bug] verify-agent-image fails when the old image pin can no longer be read

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

main `a4903adb3`, `.github/workflows/verify-agent-image.yml`, step "Size delta is plausible". Seen on https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4512 (run https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/actions/runs/44823655374).

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

The `verify` job failed on https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4512, the main to channels sync. The sync moved the `channels` pin in `agent-images.json` from the 10-21 image to main's 11-14 image. The new image passed every real check: both platforms, lock matches, hardened. Then the size step ran `docker buildx imagetools inspect --raw` on the old 10-21 digest and got nothing back. The Python one-liner crashed with `JSONDecodeError`, and that failed the job.

### What did you expect?

If the old image can't be read, the size step should skip its comparison and pass. It is a rough tripwire, and its own guard already skips the check when the old size is 0.

### How can we reproduce it?

Open a PR that changes a pin in `agent-images.json` whose old digest can no longer be read from the registry. For example, merge main into a branch whose pin is several image rebuilds old, as #4512 did.

### Relevant redacted logs

```
Size delta is plausible | json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
Size delta is plausible | ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

### Last version that worked

Not a regression. It only shows when the old image is gone, and the usual bump PRs (for example https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4500) compare against a recent image that still exists.

Fix idea: in `total()`, don't let a failed inspect crash. Add `|| true` after the `docker buildx imagetools inspect` call, and have the Python print 0 for empty input. `O=0` then skips the check through the existing `[ "$O" -gt 0 ]` guard.

issues.title: add_reaction: schema asks for shortcode names; handler passes verbatim, breaks WhatsApp + Discord

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## What's wrong

`container/agent-runner/src/mcp-tools/core.ts:230` documents the `emoji` parameter as `"Emoji name (e.g., thumbs_up, heart, check)"`, and the agent instructions at `core.instructions.md` reinforce "emoji is the shortcode name (e.g. `thumbs_up`, `heart`), not the raw character." The handler at `core.ts:255` then writes the value **verbatim** into the outbound JSON — no shortcode→unicode resolution anywhere.

Two dispatch paths consume it; one works by accident, the rest are broken:

- **`src/channels/whatsapp.ts:703-714`** passes the value to Baileys' `react.text`. Baileys expects unicode (e.g. `"👍"`); a literal `"thumbs_up"` ends up as the reaction text and either renders as the seven-character word (no emoji) or is rejected silently. The operator sees no reaction.
- **`src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts:381-384`** passes through to `adapter.addReaction(threadId, messageId, emoji)`. Each Chat SDK platform adapter then dispatches with no translation: Discord's REST reaction endpoint expects URL-encoded unicode, Telegram/Teams/GChat expect unicode, and only **Slack** actually expects the shortcode form.

Most plausible origin: a conflation of the Chat SDK's TypeScript `emoji` helper (`emoji.thumbs_up` resolves to the right per-platform form *at call time inside TS*) with the JSON wire form that lands at the MCP tool. The helper is compile-time sugar; the wire form is whatever literal string the agent emits, which never goes through `defaultEmojiResolver`.

## Repro

```
agent: add_reaction({ messageId: 42, emoji: "thumbs_up" })
→ outbound row: { operation: "reaction", messageId: "<platform_id>", emoji: "thumbs_up" }
→ WhatsApp adapter: sock.sendMessage(jid, { react: { text: "thumbs_up", key: { ... } } })
→ result: no reaction visible on the user's phone
```

Symptom: agent's logs show `add_reaction: #42 → thumbs_up`, `Message delivered` fires for the outbound row, but the reaction never renders. The agent then often follows up with text (`"reacted with 👍"`) trying to compensate, doubling the noise.

## Proposed fix (two parts)

### 1. Schema + instructions ask the agent for unicode

Raw emoji chars are correct on every supported channel except Slack. The agent shouldn't have to know which platform it's targeting.

```diff
- emoji: { type: 'string', description: 'Emoji name (e.g., thumbs_up, heart, check)' },
+ emoji: { type: 'string', description: 'Emoji character (e.g., "👍", "❤️", "✅"). Pass the actual emoji character — shortcodes like "thumbs_up" are sent to WhatsApp verbatim and do not render as reactions.' },
```

Mirror change in `core.instructions.md`:

```diff
- `emoji` is the shortcode name (e.g. `thumbs_up`, `heart`), not the raw character.
+ `emoji` must be the actual emoji character (e.g. `"👍"`, `"❤️"`), NOT a shortcode like `"thumbs_up"` — the handler passes the value verbatim to WhatsApp and shortcodes don't render as reactions.
```

### 2. Dispatch-side translation for Slack in the Chat SDK bridge

The Chat SDK already exports `defaultEmojiResolver` with `.fromGChat(unicode) → EmojiValue` and `.toSlack(name) → string`. Chain them in the bridge's reaction branch; everything else passes unicode through:

```diff
  if (content.operation === 'reaction' && content.messageId && content.emoji) {
-   await adapter.addReaction(tid, content.messageId as string, content.emoji as string);
+   const rawEmoji = content.emoji as string;
+   const platformEmoji =
+     adapter.name === 'slack'
+       ? defaultEmojiResolver.toSlack(defaultEmojiResolver.fromGChat(rawEmoji))
+       : rawEmoji;
+   await adapter.addReaction(tid, content.messageId as string, platformEmoji);
    return;
  }
```

WhatsApp adapter needs no change — it already passes through, which is correct for Baileys.

## Empirical verification

Tested against a shared-number WhatsApp install:

- Agent emitting `"👍"` → reaction visibly lands on the right message ✅
- Agent emitting `"thumbs_up"` (pre-fix behavior) → no reaction visible (matches symptom)
- `defaultEmojiResolver.fromGChat("👍")` → `EmojiValue{name:"thumbs_up"}`, then `.toSlack(…)` → `"+1"` (canonical input to Slack's `reactions.add`)

Sanity table from `defaultEmojiResolver`:

| Raw | Slack form |
|---|---|
| `👍` | `+1` |
| `❤️` | `heart` |
| `✅` | `white_check_mark` |
| `🎉` | `tada` |
| `👀` | `eyes` |
| `🤡` (unmapped) | `🤡` (pass-through) |

## Reference patches

Applied locally in a fork:
- Schema + instructions: `0de2a7d`
- Bridge dispatch-side conversion: `0fac791`

Happy to send a PR upstream if useful.

---

## Update: a second, related bug in the same code path (shared-number WhatsApp mode)

Discovered while smoke-testing the unicode-emoji fix on a shared-number install (`ASSISTANT_HAS_OWN_NUMBER` unset). The "Empirical verification" claim above — *"Agent emitting `👍` → reaction visibly lands"* — is only true on non-shared-number installs. In shared-number mode, even with unicode emoji, reactions to user-typed messages still silently fail.

### Root cause

Baileys identifies a reaction's target by the tuple `(remoteJid, id, fromMe)`. The host's reaction dispatch in `src/channels/whatsapp.ts:703-714` hardcodes `fromMe: false`:

```ts
key: { remoteJid: platformId, id: content.messageId as string, fromMe: false }
```

In shared-number mode the operator's phone-typed messages share the WhatsApp account with the bot's session (multi-device protocol). They land in `messages_in` as logical inbound rows but carry `fromMe=true` on the wire — the account *did* send them, just from a different linked device. WhatsApp resolves the target by `(remoteJid, id, fromMe)`, can't find a `fromMe=false` row with that id, and silently drops the reaction.

The same hardcode also breaks **bot-self-reactions** on any install — a bot reacting to one of its own previous messages needs `fromMe=true` on the target key, regardless of shared-number mode.

### Repro (shared-number mode)

```
agent: add_reaction({ messageId: <seq of an operator-from-phone message>, emoji: "👍" })
→ outbound row: { operation: "reaction", messageId: "<wa_id>", emoji: "👍" }
→ host: sock.sendMessage(jid, { react: { text: "👍", key: { ..., fromMe: false } } })
→ Baileys: returns sent.key.id (looks successful from the SDK's perspective)
→ result: no reaction visible on the phone
```

Send the same payload with `key.fromMe: true` and the reaction visibly lands.

### Empirical verification

On a shared-number install, injecting two reactions targeting the **identical** message id from the same chat:

| Payload | `key.fromMe` | Baileys return | Visible on phone |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{ emoji: "👍", target: <op-msg> }` | `false` (current behavior) | `sent.key.id` non-empty, `hasMessage=true` | ❌ no |
| `{ emoji: "🧪", target: <same op-msg> }` | `true` | `sent.key.id` non-empty, `hasMessage=true` | ✅ yes |
| `{ emoji: "🌈", target: <same op-msg> }` (with the fix's exact output shape) | `true` | same | ✅ yes |

Instrumented host log on dispatch (added during debugging):

```
reaction dispatch (TEMP-DIAG) platformId=...  targetMsgId=3A94... emoji=👍 targetFromMe=false
reaction dispatch result      sentKeyId=3EB0B3... hasMessage=true   ← Baileys accepts the send
(no reaction visible on phone)

reaction dispatch (TEMP-DIAG) platformId=...  targetMsgId=3A94... emoji=🧪 targetFromMe=true
reaction dispatch result      sentKeyId=3EB0DB... hasMessage=true
(🧪 visibly renders on phone)
```

Both sends look identical to the SDK; the difference is purely whether WhatsApp's server matches the target.

### Proposed fix

The container side knows whether a seq corresponds to a bot-sent or account-sent message — it can read `content.fromMe` from `messages_in` (the WhatsApp adapter at `whatsapp.ts:~631` already stores the wire-level `msg.key.fromMe` when constructing the inbound). Thread the value through to the host dispatch.

Container-side helper:

```ts
export function isSeqFromMe(seq: number): boolean | null {
  const inbound = getInboundDb();
  const inRow = inbound.prepare('SELECT content FROM messages_in WHERE seq = ?').get(seq) as
    | { content: string } | undefined;
  if (inRow) {
    try {
      const parsed = JSON.parse(inRow.content);
      return parsed?.fromMe === true;
    } catch { return false; }
  }
  const outRow = getOutboundDb().prepare('SELECT 1 AS x FROM messages_out WHERE seq = ?').get(seq);
  if (outRow) return true;
  return null;
}
```

In `add_reaction`:

```diff
+ const targetFromMe = isSeqFromMe(seq) ?? false;
  writeMessageOut({
    ...
-   content: JSON.stringify({ operation: 'reaction', messageId: platformId, emoji }),
+   content: JSON.stringify({ operation: 'reaction', messageId: platformId, emoji, targetFromMe }),
  });
```

Host dispatch:

```diff
+ const targetFromMe = content.targetFromMe === true;
  await sock.sendMessage(platformId, {
    react: {
      text: content.emoji as string,
-     key: { remoteJid: platformId, id: content.messageId as string, fromMe: false },
+     key: { remoteJid: platformId, id: content.messageId as string, fromMe: targetFromMe },
    },
  });
```

Chat SDK adapters (Discord/Slack/Telegram) don't use `fromMe` on their reaction APIs — the field passes through harmlessly for those channels, so this change is effectively WhatsApp-specific even though the plumbing is shared.

### Reference patches (in the fork)

- `targetFromMe` plumbing through outbound + host dispatch: `5b38df0`
- `isSeqFromMe` reading `content.fromMe` (not inferring from row location): `1120929`

Same offer applies — happy to bundle both fixes into a single PR upstream.

issues.title: Silent log loss + inbound message duplicate-insert errors after long uptime; no systemd unit installed

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
**Environment:**
- NanoClaw v2, commit 2d9375531b1e52574b6b61861c4153b26f2ae68a (2026-06-06), fork at libellebilai-collab/nanoclaw
- WSL2 Ubuntu on Windows, Docker Desktop (backend), Node v22.22.3
- Channel: Matrix (local homeserver on localhost:9007)

**Summary:**
Two separate issues found while debugging an unresponsive agent:

**1. Application logs silently stop being written, with no error.**
logs/nanoclaw.log and logs/nanoclaw.error.log have not been modified since 2026-06-23 21:07:54, per `stat`, even though the NanoClaw process has been running continuously/restarted many times since (confirmed via `ps`, current PID uptime since today 19:43). Inspecting the running process's file descriptors:

lrwx------+ 1 libelle libelle 64 Jul 17 19:43 /proc/<pid>/fd/1 -> 'socket:[934]'
lrwx------+ 1 libelle libelle 64 Jul 17 19:43 /proc/<pid>/fd/2 -> 'socket:[934]'

stdout/stderr are connected to a socket, not the log files — meaning however the process is currently being launched, it no longer inherits the shell redirect (>> logs/nanoclaw.log 2>&1) that produced the historical log content. Parent PID is 1 (init), i.e. the launching parent has already exited and the process was reparented. There is no nanoclaw.service systemd unit installed (systemctl --user status nanoclaw -> "Unit nanoclaw.service could not be found"), so the docs' service-management section doesn't apply to this install, and whatever is launching the process isn't documented/discoverable from inside the repo.

Impact: weeks of runtime produce zero log history. When something goes wrong (e.g. a scheduled job doesn't complete), there's no way to diagnose it after the fact from the file logs — only the session DBs (data/v2-sessions/.../inbound.db, outbound.db) retain ground truth.

Ask: NanoClaw should either (a) detect and warn on startup if stdout/stderr aren't going to a regular file/pipe it expects, or (b) document explicitly how the process is expected to be supervised (systemd unit template, or an explicit "don't rely on file logs unless you set X up" warning), so this failure mode is discoverable without hours of /proc spelunking.

**2. Duplicate inbound Matrix message causes a SQLite unique-constraint error during routing.**

ERROR Failed to route inbound message channelType="matrix" err={ type: "SqliteError", message: "UNIQUE constraint failed: messages_in.id" ...
  at insertMessage (dist/db/session-db.js:71:175)
  at writeSessionMessage (dist/session-manager.js:148:9)
  at deliverToAgent (dist/router.js:341:5)
  at routeInbound (dist/router.js:196:19)

Also seen with messages_in.seq as the failing constraint. This happened repeatedly (at least 5 times across ~2 hours) on 2026-06-23, always paired with a same-timestamp successful "Matrix message received" -> "Message routed" -> "Matrix message sent" sequence — suggesting the Matrix sync loop is delivering the same event twice (dedup happening too late, after an insert attempt) rather than the error being fatal. Worth confirming whether any inbound messages are silently dropped when this hits, since a dropped message would look identical to "the agent never replied" from the user's side (which is what triggered this whole investigation).

**Additional observation (context, not necessarily a bug):** around 2026-06-23 21:04-21:08 the process received clean SIGTERM and restarted roughly every 60-90 seconds, four times in a row, with no systemd unit present to explain the source of the signal. Not confirmed whether this was manual (terminal Ctrl+C repeated) or something else — flagging in case it correlates with reports of "the agent stopped responding."

issues.title: add_reaction / edit_message on inbound messages always fail: agent-group suffix not stripped from platform message id

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## Summary

`add_reaction` and `edit_message` **always fail for inbound messages**: the agent-group suffix is not stripped from the platform message id, so the platform is asked about an id it has never seen. On Slack every attempt comes back `message_not_found`, retries 3× and ends as `failed`. Observed on v2.1.21 — 19 out of 19 reaction attempts failed on one install.

The failure is silent from the user's point of view: normal replies are delivered fine, only the reaction/edit never appears.

## Root cause

The host makes the inbound row id unique per agent group by appending the group id — `src/router.ts`:

```js
return `${id}:${agentGroupId}`;
```

The runner then hands that composite id to the platform as if it were the bare platform id — `container/agent-runner/src/db/messages-out.ts`:

```ts
// Inbound messages: ID is already the platform message ID
const inRow = inbound.prepare('SELECT id FROM messages_in WHERE seq = ?').get(seq) as ...
if (inRow) return inRow.id;   // <-- still carries ":<agentGroupId>"
```

The comment states the opposite of what the row actually holds. From there it flows unchanged through `mcp-tools/core.ts` (`addReaction` → `content.messageId`) into `channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts`, which calls `adapter.addReaction(tid, content.messageId, emoji)`.

Outbound messages are unaffected: they resolve via `delivered.platform_message_id`, which is the real platform id.

## Reproduction

1. Have a user send a message to an agent on Slack.
2. Let the agent call `add_reaction` on that message (`messageId` = the inbound seq).
3. `messages_out` gets `{"operation":"reaction","messageId":"<ts>:<agentGroupId>","emoji":"eyes"}`, delivery fails 3× with `An API error occurred: message_not_found`.

Verified against the Slack API — same channel, same message, only the id differs:

| `timestamp` argument | `reactions.add` result |
|---|---|
| `1234567890.123456:ag-1111111111111-aaaaaa` | `ok: false`, `message_not_found` |
| `1234567890.123456` | `ok: true` |

## Suggested fix

Strip exactly the suffix the host appended. **Do not cut at the first `:`** — platform ids may legitimately contain colons (the doc comment's own Telegram example is `6037840640:42`). The runner already knows its group via `loadConfig().agentGroupId`:

```ts
export function stripAgentGroupSuffix(id: string, agentGroupId: string): string {
  if (!agentGroupId) return id;
  const suffix = `:${agentGroupId}`;
  return id.endsWith(suffix) ? id.slice(0, -suffix.length) : id;
}

// in getMessageIdBySeq:
if (inRow) return stripAgentGroupSuffix(inRow.id, loadConfig().agentGroupId);
```

Applied locally with 6 unit tests (bare Slack ts, UUID group id, Telegram `chatId:messageId`, id without suffix, empty group id, non-matching group id). Happy to open a PR if useful.

issues.title: Setup script silently deletes existing groups/*/CLAUDE.md without warning or backup

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## Summary

Running `bash nanoclaw.sh` on a freshly cloned repo silently deletes the agent configuration files in `groups/`, with no warning, no backup, and no log line indicating the deletion. Users who had spent time customizing their agent personality lose all of it on a re-run.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `git clone https://github.com/qwibitai/nanoclaw && cd nanoclaw`
2. (Optional) Modify `groups/global/CLAUDE.md` or `groups/main/CLAUDE.md` with custom instructions.
3. `bash nanoclaw.sh`
4. Setup fails partway through (in my case, Docker wasn't ready), but inspecting `git status` afterward shows:

```
deleted:    groups/global/CLAUDE.md
deleted:    groups/main/CLAUDE.md
```

The deleted files were 166 lines and 312 lines respectively — the default templates shipped with the repo.

## Expected behavior

Setup should either:
- Preserve existing `groups/*/CLAUDE.md` files (treat them as user data, not setup scaffolding), **or**
- Back them up before overwriting (`*.bak` or a timestamped copy), **or**
- Detect that they already exist and prompt the user before deleting.

At minimum, deletion should be logged to `logs/setup.log` so users can audit what happened.

## Actual behavior

Files are deleted silently. The setup log shows nothing about it. A user who didn't run `git status` afterward would have no idea their config was wiped.

## Impact

Anyone re-running setup (including after a Docker/dependency failure mid-setup) loses customizations to their agent's CLAUDE.md. This is the agent's "personality" config — losing it silently is a meaningful regression.

## Environment

- nanoclaw `v2.0.46` (commit `0e11eaf`)
- macOS 26.4.1
- Node 22.x, pnpm latest
- Setup failed at the Docker readiness check (`runtime_not_available`)

## Suggested fix

In whichever setup phase rewrites `groups/`, gate the write behind an existence check:

```bash
if [[ -f "groups/global/CLAUDE.md" ]]; then
  cp "groups/global/CLAUDE.md" "groups/global/CLAUDE.md.bak.$(date +%s)"
fi
```

Or simply skip overwriting if the user has local modifications (compare against the canonical template).

issues.title: groups/global/CLAUDE.md is unconditionally deleted on every startup — should be removed from the repo
issues.body:
## Summary

\`groups/global/CLAUDE.md\` is committed to the repo but is unconditionally removed by \`migrateGroupsToClaudeLocal()\` on every NanoClaw startup. This produces a permanent dirty working tree on any instance that pulls the repo and restarts the service.

## Reproduction

1. Fresh clone of \`main\`.
2. Build and start NanoClaw.
3. Observe \`groups/global/\` directory disappears.
4. \`git status\` reports \`D groups/global/CLAUDE.md\` indefinitely.

## Code reference

[\`src/claude-md-compose.ts\` lines 174–177](https://github.com/qwibitai/nanoclaw/blob/main/src/claude-md-compose.ts#L174-L177):

\`\`\`js
const globalDir = path.join(GROUPS_DIR, 'global');
if (fs.existsSync(globalDir)) {
  fs.rmSync(globalDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  actions.push('groups/global/ removed');
}
\`\`\`

The migration function comment explicitly states: *"delete \`groups/global/\` (content already in \`container/CLAUDE.md\`)"*.

## Why this is different from \`groups/main/CLAUDE.md\`

\`groups/main/CLAUDE.md\` plays a seed role for fresh installs (the loop at lines 151–172 renames \`CLAUDE.md\` → \`CLAUDE.local.md\` only if \`CLAUDE.local.md\` doesn't already exist), so it has a purpose in the repo. \`groups/global/\` is unconditionally removed regardless of state, so its presence in the repo serves no function.

## Suggested fix

Remove \`groups/global/CLAUDE.md\` from the repository. The universal agent base content lives in \`container/CLAUDE.md\` (mounted RO at \`/app/CLAUDE.md\` in the agent container).

Optionally, also drop the unconditional global-dir cleanup from \`migrateGroupsToClaudeLocal()\` once the repo is clean — but keeping it as a safety net for legacy installs is fine.

I can submit a PR if useful.

issues.title: create_agent MCP tool is ungated despite "admin-only" comment & description — any container can create agent groups
issues.body:
## Summary
`create_agent` is documented/described as admin-only, but it is exposed to **every** container and the host performs no role/admin check — so any agent container can create new agent groups.

## Version
upstream `main` @ d144721 (≈ v2.0.64); present since e83ffbc.

## Claim vs. reality
`container/agent-runner/src/mcp-tools/agents.ts`:
- L8-9 (comment): "create_agent is admin-only. Non-admin containers never see this tool (see mcp-tools/index.ts). The host re-checks permission on receive."
- L35 (tool description, shown to the agent): "…Admin-only. Fire-and-forget."

Neither holds:
1. **Registered unconditionally.** `registerTools([createAgent])` runs at module scope (`agents.ts:66`); the barrel imports it for its side effect with no gating (`mcp-tools/index.ts:11`). Every container's MCP server exposes `create_agent`.
2. **No host-side re-check.** `handleCreateAgent` (`src/modules/agent-to-agent/create-agent.ts`, dispatched from `src/delivery.ts` `handleSystemAction`) validates only source-group-exists, name-collision, and path-traversal — no role/admin/permission check.

## Impact
A container agent processes inbound messages (a prompt-injection surface). With `create_agent` ungated, an injected agent can spawn arbitrary agent groups with attacker-chosen `name` + `instructions` (the new group's CLAUDE.md) and wire destinations. Path traversal is guarded, but unauthorized agent-group creation enables namespace pollution / persistence / resource abuse — higher impact on shared/multi-user deployments.

## Suggested fix
- **Conditional registration**: don't register `create_agent` for non-admin containers (gate in `index.ts`/`agents.ts` on role/`cli_scope`), matching the "non-admin never see this tool" claim; and/or
- **Host re-check**: in `handleCreateAgent`, verify the source group is authorized before creating, matching the "host re-checks permission on receive" claim.

Then align the `agents.ts` comment + description with whichever gating ships.

issues.title: Emoji shortcode normalization: map Slack shortcodes to Unicode for add_reaction
issues.body:
## Problem
`add_reaction` accepts Slack-style shortcodes but only a subset work — the rest fail silently or with an error. Live testing across a Telegram group revealed that ~16 emoji work via shortcode, while ~57 more from Telegram's official reaction set only work when passed as literal Unicode characters. A further ~6 emoji fail entirely (not in Telegram's reaction whitelist).

## Findings (from live testing, Apr 26 2026)

**Works via Slack shortcode:** `thumbs_up` `thumbs_down` `heart` `fire` `100` `eyes` `thinking_face` `tada` `sob` `clap` `trophy` `pray` `ok_hand` `zap` `rage` `sleeping`

**Works via Unicode only:** 🤣 🤯 😍 😱 🤮 💩 🌚 🍌 🐳 🤡 💔 👻 🤩 😈 🤓 🍓 🍾 🦄 ❤️‍🔥 😁 👨‍💻 🙈 😇 🤝 🤗 🫡 💅 🗿 🎃 😨 ✍️ 🎄 🤪 💊 🆒 💘 🙉 😘 🙊 💋 🥱 🥴 🕊 🖕 🎅 ☃️

**Not supported at all:** ✅ 🚀 👁 🆘 🤦 🖤

## Proposed fix
Add a complete shortcode→Unicode mapping table covering all 73 Telegram-supported reactions. When `add_reaction` is called with a shortcode, normalize it to the Unicode character before hitting the Telegram API. This makes the full reaction set accessible without callers needing to know whether to use shortcode or Unicode.

## Acceptance
- All 73 supported Telegram reactions work regardless of whether shortcode or Unicode is passed
- Unsupported emoji return a clear error, not a silent no-op
- Unit test covering shortcode → Unicode normalization round-trip

issues.title: Outbound reactions/edits reuse the router's namespaced message id; Discord rejects them (400 50035). Actions-only cards rejected too.
issues.body:
## Summary

`src/router.ts` namespaces every inbound message id per agent as
`${platformMessageId}:${agentGroupId}` (`messageIdForAgent`) so a fanned-out message
cannot collide across session DBs. The agent sees that id and echoes it back in
`{"operation":"reaction","messageId":"…"}` and `{"operation":"edit","messageId":"…"}`.
`src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` passes `content.messageId` straight to
`adapter.addReaction` / `adapter.editMessage`, so Discord receives
`1555378824211075093:ag-c682606f-…` and answers:

```
Discord API error: 400 {"message": "Invalid Form Body", "code": 50035,
 "errors": {"message_id": {"_errors": [{"code": "NUMBER_TYPE_COERCE", …
```

The delivery retries three times within a second and is marked failed permanently.
Observed 5 lost reactions on one Discord channel on 2026-10-01 (NanoClaw 2.4.0).
`src/channels/whatsapp.ts` has the same shape in its native reaction path.

A second, independent rejection: `send_card` with only link-button actions (no
title/description) builds a Card with no text child; the Discord adapter emits an
embed with an empty description and Discord answers 400 `BASE_TYPE_REQUIRED` on
`embeds[0].description`. 2 lost cards the same day.

Edits were not observed failing: the host's own action handler passes the raw id.

## Repro

1. Wire a Discord channel to an agent; send any message.
2. Have the agent call `add_reaction` on it (the id it holds is the namespaced one).
3. `logs/nanoclaw.error.log`: "Message delivery failed permanently … NUMBER_TYPE_COERCE".
4. Have the agent `send_card` with `{actions:[{label,url}]}` and nothing else →
   "BASE_TYPE_REQUIRED" on `embeds.0.description`.

## Fix applied locally

- `stripAgentSuffix(id, agentGroupId)` and `outboundContentForPlatform(raw, content, agentGroupId)`
  in `src/platform-id.ts`; `delivery.ts` passes the stripped content to
  `deliveryAdapter.deliver` at the one chokepoint where `session.agent_group_id` is
  known, so every adapter (bridge and native) gets the bare id and no prefix
  convention is assumed.
- Card builder: when the card has neither title nor text body, set the Chat SDK
  `Card.subtitle` (Discord maps it to `embed.description`) from `fallbackText` or
  the first rendered button label, instead of shipping an empty embed.
- Tests: `src/platform-id.test.ts`, a delivery chokepoint case in
  `src/delivery.test.ts`, and card-shape cases in `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts`.

Happy to open a PR if the shape is acceptable; an alternative is to have the runner
expose the bare platform id to the agent and keep the namespaced id host-side only.

issues.title: WhatsApp attachments saved to data/attachments/ but not mounted into agent containers

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## Summary

Inbound WhatsApp attachments (images, video, audio, documents) are downloaded by the host adapter to `<project>/data/attachments/`, but no corresponding mount carries that directory into agent containers. The agent-runner formatter references attachments at `/workspace/<localPath>` (resolving to e.g. `/workspace/attachments/image-123.jpg`), but `/workspace/` is the per-session mount only — the shared `data/attachments/` dir is never mounted.

Result: agents receive messages with attachment metadata but cannot access the files. Image-based requests ("identify this artwork", "what does this say", etc.) silently fail — the agent reads the inbound row, the file path returns ENOENT, and the agent acks the message as completed without producing any reply.

## Repro

1. Have a WhatsApp channel wired to an agent group.
2. Send the agent an image-bearing message in WhatsApp.
3. Observe in `logs/nanoclaw.log`:
   - `Media downloaded type=image filename=image-...jpg`  (adapter wrote it)
   - `Message routed wake=true`                            (agent woken)
4. Observe inside the running container: `ls /workspace/attachments/` → `No such file or directory`.
5. Observe agent's `outbound.db`: no response message produced.
6. Observe `processing_ack` in outbound.db: message marked completed (sync'd back to `messages_in.status` by host-sweep).

## Where the gap is

- Adapter writes to `path.join(DATA_DIR, 'attachments')` — `src/channels/whatsapp.ts:322`
- Adapter records `localPath: 'attachments/<filename>'` — `src/channels/whatsapp.ts:326`
- Agent-runner resolves to `/workspace/${a.localPath}` — `container/agent-runner/src/formatter.ts:240`
- `src/container-runner.ts` `buildMounts()` mounts the session dir at `/workspace`, the group dir at `/workspace/agent`, the global dir at `/workspace/global`, etc. — **but not** `data/attachments/` at `/workspace/attachments/`.

## Proposed fix

One mount entry alongside the existing global / shared CLAUDE.md mounts:

```ts
const attachDir = path.join(DATA_DIR, 'attachments');
if (fs.existsSync(attachDir)) {
  mounts.push({ hostPath: attachDir, containerPath: '/workspace/attachments', readonly: true });
}
```

Read-only is appropriate — the host owns the directory; the agent should only consume from it.

Verified locally with this single change. Affected agent immediately picked up previously-stuck image messages on the next sweep tick.

## Scope

Today this only manifests with the WhatsApp adapter, since that's the only channel currently writing to `data/attachments/`. Any future inbound channel using the same write convention (Telegram, iMessage, Slack with file uploads, etc.) would inherit the bug as long as it follows the existing `localPath: 'attachments/<file>'` pattern.

## Recovery for stuck messages

Messages already in `processing_ack` as `completed` won't get reprocessed by just resetting `messages_in.status` — the host-sweep's `syncProcessingAcks` will flip them back. Need to delete the matching rows from `outbound.db.processing_ack` first, then reset `messages_in.status` to `pending`.

(Probably worth a separate small PR to surface this state more clearly — e.g. logging when an agent acks a message without producing any outbound, since "completed with zero output" is a strong signal of a silent failure mode.)

issues.title: [bug] ncl groups config add-mount cannot create read-write mounts.

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.10.0

### Host platform

macOS

### What happened?

In v2026.10.0, the handler (src/cli/resources/groups.ts) writes readonly: true when --ro is passed and omits the field otherwise. Mount security (src/modules/mount-security/index.ts:368) grants read-write only when mount.readonly === false, so CLI-created mounts are always read-only even when the allowlist root has allowReadWrite: true. docs/SECURITY.md:115 describes the intended behaviour.
Suggested fix: write readonly: false when --ro is absent, or add an explicit --rw flag.

### What did you expect?

Running ncl groups config add-mount without --ro, for a host path whose allowlist root has allowReadWrite: true, should produce a read-write mount inside the group’s containers.

That’s the behaviour docs/SECURITY.md:115 describes: read-write is granted when the mount requests it (readonly: false) and the matched root has allowReadWrite: true. The command’s help also implies it: --ro is presented as the opt-in for read-only, so leaving it out should mean read-write.

Instead the mount is always read-only.
- The handler in src/cli/resources/groups.ts (config add-mount) writes readonly: true when --ro or --readonly is passed. Otherwise it omits the field entirely.
- Mount security, at src/modules/mount-security/index.ts:368, grants read-write only when mount.readonly === false.
- An omitted field therefore always resolves to read-only.

The CLI has no way to create a read-write mount: --ro false is still truthy, and there’s no --rw flag.

### How can we reproduce it?

Environment: NanoClaw v2026.10.0 (release tag), macOS 27.0.1, Docker Desktop, OneCLI 1.42.0, a fresh install via bash nanoclaw.sh.

Create a host directory, for example /Users/<user>/testmount.
Allow it read-write:

> pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step mounts --force -- --json '{"allowedRoots":[{"path":"/Users/<user>/testmount","allowReadWrite":true,"description":"test"}],"blockedPatterns":[]}'

Confirm that ~/.config/nanoclaw/mount-allowlist.json shows "allowReadWrite": true.
3. Add the mount without --ro:

> ncl groups config add-mount --id <ag-id> --host /Users/<user>/testmount --container testmount

Inspect the stored config:

> ncl groups config get --id <ag-id> | grep -A5 additional_mounts

Observed: the entry contains hostPath and containerPath only, with no readonly key.
5. Run ncl groups restart --id <ag-id>.
6. Ask the agent to create a file under /workspace/extra/testmount/.

Observed: the write fails, and the agent reports that the mount is read-only. Nothing is logged as mount REJECTED: the mount is accepted, then silently forced read-only.

Suggested fix: in the config add-mount handler, write readonly: false when --ro/--readonly is absent. Alternatively, add an explicit --rw flag and document that the default is read-only. Either way, the CLI and SECURITY.md would then agree.

Workaround used: setting readonly: false on the existing mount entry through the /manage-mounts skill, then restarting the group.

`main` @ `ddf824e8c`

"Your agents, messages, files and keys never leave your machine." "Talk to your assistant with the trigger word (default: `@Andy`)". "spawns per-agent-group containers".

issues.title: [bug] Setup's image-source prompt says it records less than registry login sends
issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

main @ ddf824e8

### Host platform

Other

### What happened?

When the portal is disabled, `chooseImageSource()` in `setup/auto.ts` (L1455) tells the user:

> Fetching it means authenticating with NanoClaw: we record your email address and that you fetched an image, nothing else. Building sends nothing at all.

That says less than what is actually sent:

- **At sign-in**, `clientRecord()` in `setup/registry-login.ts` (~L448) sends `os`, `arch`, `nanoclaw_version` and a persistent `host_id`, along with the email.
- **On each image pull**, the image digest goes out with the Node and credential-helper versions.
- **"Building sends nothing at all"** ignores the setup diagnostics, which still go to PostHog unless `NANOCLAW_NO_DIAGNOSTICS=1` is set. It's true for NanoClaw's registry, but not in general.

The README's "Accounts and what leaves your machine" section, as rewritten in #4506, now lists these fields. So the README and setup's own consent text disagree, and the in-terminal text is the one users actually see when they decide.

### What did you expect?

The consent text at the moment of choice should be at least as complete as the README. Ideally it names the extra fields in short form, or points to the README section.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Run `bash nanoclaw.sh` on a checkout with a pinned agent image and the portal disabled (`portalEnabled()` false).
2. Reach the "Where should your assistant's sandbox image come from?" prompt.
3. Compare the text above it with `clientRecord()` in `setup/registry-login.ts` and with the README section.

### Suggested fix

Something like:

> Fetching it means signing in to NanoClaw: we record your email address, a random host id, your OS, CPU type and NanoClaw version, and each image pull — nothing about your agents. Building contacts no NanoClaw service (setup diagnostics aside; `NANOCLAW_NO_DIAGNOSTICS=1` turns those off).

Also worth checking that the portal path (`runImagePortal` → `beginPortal`) tells the user the same thing before sign-in.

Not channel-specific

Not provider-specific
