issues.title: [capability] Port Slack agent-to-agent rooms to the Mattermost channel

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New capability or improvement

labels.name: delivery/skill
labels.description: Delivered as a skill; independent of kind

labels.name: area/channels
labels.description: Primary subsystem: exactly one per triaged item

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
## What problem are you trying to solve?

The new Slack mode's flagship is agent teams in shared rooms (a human plus sibling bots in one group DM, `slack-a2a-rooms`). On Mattermost, agents cannot converse with each other at all: the channel's engagement defaults state "posts from other bot accounts never reach an agent, even when they mention it," and `create_room`/`add_to_room` exist only on Slack. Self-hosted Mattermost is the most likely channel for exactly these deployments.

## What should be possible?

A Mattermost user creates a "room" (group channel) holding a human and several agents; agents reply mention-gated, and only in allowlisted rooms are bot-authored messages admitted — under a consecutive-hop cap (default 6, reset by a human message), re-attributed as `mattermost:bot:<bot_id>`, with roster changes tracked via `channel_added`/`channel_removed` websocket events: the same loop-safety contract as Slack.

## What kind of skill is this?

Channel install (a skill on the `channels` branch, mirroring `slack-a2a-rooms`).

## Who benefits?

Self-hosted Mattermost deployments running multi-agent teams (the Slack-mode feature set) below ~50 users, where the server runs unlicensed Enterprise (Entry) or Team Edition.

## What have you tried?

Ran the Slack rooms feature on a live workspace. On Mattermost, group channels exist via the adapter's `openDM`/`G`-type support but carry no room semantics; `send_message` between sibling agents works host-side but is invisible in the channel. Related: #1379 (Mattermost channel integration, closed); A2A issues on other channels #2332, #2048, #4222.

## What would this change?

One companion skill + admission policy on the Mattermost channel (bot-inbound analogue of the Slack guard), room actions on the adapter surface, and a pinned channel file as the canvas substitute (Mattermost has no canvas API). No new runtime dependency; removal deletes the skill and restores the current bot-drop default.

## How could we test it?

Fresh checkout + `/add-mattermost` on a stock Mattermost 12.x server: create two agents without rooms, `create_room` with both, verify each answers only when mentioned, verify the 7th consecutive bot turn is dropped until a human speaks, then remove the skill and confirm bot posts are dropped again.

## Can you help maintain it?

- [x] I can help maintain this skill.

**Affected NanoClaw version or commit:** v2.3.0 (tested at beedba45, upstream/main)
**Host platform:** macOS

## What happened?

On the Mattermost channel, slash commands (`/clear`, `/compact`, `/cost`, admin commands) work only because the host command gate parses message text beginning with `/` (`src/command-gate.ts`, dispatched from `src/router.ts` before the container runs). The adapter never registers anything with the server (`src/channels/mattermost-adapter/` makes no `/api/v4/commands/custom` call), and nothing appears in System Console → Integrations → Slash Commands after `/add-mattermost`.

## What did you expect?

Typing `/` in the message input shows NanoClaw's commands in the autocomplete list (with hint/description like any registered integration), so they are discoverable — as on Slack, where slash commands are a first-class channel affordance.

## How can we reproduce it?

1. Clean checkout, `/add-mattermost` against a self-hosted server (Mattermost 12.x, unlicensed Enterprise/Entry).
2. Add the bot to a team and a group channel.
3. Focus the message input, type `/`.
4. Observe: built-ins only; no NanoClaw commands in the autocomplete.
5. Send `/clear` anyway — it executes (text-parsed), confirming the command is handled but unregistered.

**Suggested fix:** derive the command list from `command-gate` (single source of truth, shared with Slack) and idempotently upsert each gated command as a custom slash command with autocomplete enabled (hint + description) via `POST /api/v4/commands/custom`, dispatching on the existing webhook server; keep the text-parsed path for DMs (Mattermost slash commands do not fire in DMs) and guarantee single dispatch so a command never executes twice.

## Optional context

**OS version and CPU architecture:** macOS 26.6, arm64 (Apple Silicon)
**Install or update path:** Standard setup with nanoclaw.sh (Mattermost channel via `/add-mattermost`)

**Agent provider:** Not provider-specific

issues.title: [bug] WhatsApp: quoted replies reach the agent without the quoted message

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: priority/medium
labels.description: Maintainer-set

labels.name: area/channels
labels.description: Primary subsystem: exactly one per triaged item

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.11.0-rc.1 (6a108c72). Also checked `src/channels/whatsapp.ts` on the `channels` branch (53f63a31, 2026-11-15): same code, no reply handling.

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

When a user replies to (quotes) a specific message in WhatsApp, the agent only gets the new text. The quoted message is dropped. A reply like "this one is my favourite" arrives with nothing to refer to, so the agent has to ask which message the user meant.

### What did you expect?

The quoted message should reach the agent as context, as it does on Telegram. The agent-runner already renders `content.replyTo` as `<quoted_message from="…">…</quoted_message>` plus a `reply_to` attribute (`container/agent-runner/src/formatter.ts`, `formatReplyContext`, ~L269/L412). The Telegram adapter fills it through `extractReplyContext`.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Wire an agent to a WhatsApp chat through the native Baileys adapter.
2. Have the agent send two messages or images.
3. In WhatsApp, long-press one of them, tap Reply, and type "this one".
4. The agent's inbound `<message>` has no `<quoted_message>` and no `reply_to` attribute.

### Root cause

`src/channels/whatsapp.ts` builds `InboundMessage.content` with `text`, `sender`, `senderName`, `attachments`, and so on, but never sets `replyTo`. The adapter only reads `contextInfo.mentionedJid`. It never reads `contextInfo.quotedMessage`, `stanzaId` or `participant`.

### Suggested fix

Read `contextInfo` from `extendedTextMessage` / `imageMessage` / `videoMessage` / `documentMessage` (the same set already used for mentions) and map it like this:

- `stanzaId` → `replyTo.id`
- `participant`, resolved from LID to a phone JID the same way as the sender → `replyTo.sender`
- `quotedMessage.conversation`, `quotedMessage.extendedTextMessage.text`, or the media caption, with a placeholder such as `[image]` or `[sticker]` when there's no text → `replyTo.text`

issues.title: [bug] Slack (Socket Mode): messages sent while the host is suspended or disconnected are never processed, and nothing catches up on reconnect
issues.body:
**Affected version:** `2026.11.0-rc.2` (commit `69bbf734`, trunk plus the Slack channel installed from the `channels` branch)
**Host platform:** Linux (systemd user service, linger enabled)
**Channel:** Slack (Socket Mode, `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` set)

### What happened?
The host machine was suspended. A user then sent a reply in an existing DM thread with the agent. After resume the host was running again, and the agent container worked normally for messages sent later. The message sent during the gap was never processed.

- Slack has the message. I read it back with `conversations.replies`, and it's in the thread with the expected timestamp.
- The host log has no `Inbound DM received` entry for it. The log shows no inbound Slack messages between the previous evening and the first message after the restart, so the message never reached the router. This isn't a routing, wiring or `pending` queue problem.
- The user had to resend the question before the agent replied.
- After resume, the log and `nanoclaw.error.log` show repeated `SlackWebSocket: A pong wasn't received from the server before the timeout of 5000ms!` warnings, so the socket was in a stale state.

### Why it happens
Socket Mode only delivers events over a live WebSocket. Slack retries an unacknowledged envelope for a short time and then drops it. There is no durable queue to replay on reconnect, so anything sent while the socket was down is gone unless the adapter fetches it.

The Slack adapter (`src/channels/slack.ts` plus the Chat SDK bridge) has no catch-up step. I couldn't find one on adapter start, on socket reconnect, or in the host sweep:
- The "channel-timeline backfill" mentioned in `slack.ts` is context backfill for newly created sessions (`cross-session-context`). It doesn't ingest messages the host missed.
- The 60-second host sweep resyncs local session DBs only. It never asks Slack what it missed.

No doc or code states this is intended. `docs/architecture.md` ("Message Batching") covers messages that reached the host while the container was down, which works. The case where the host itself never received the message is not mentioned.

### What did you expect?
Messages sent to the agent while the host was down, suspended or disconnected should be processed once the host is back, or at least the behaviour should be documented. Laptops and desktops that sleep are a normal host for a personal assistant, and the user sees Slack accept the message with no sign that it was lost.

### How can we reproduce it?
1. Run NanoClaw with Slack in Socket Mode and an agent wired to a DM.
2. Suspend the host (or block the Slack WebSocket).
3. From Slack, send the agent a message, including a reply in an existing thread.
4. Resume the host and wait for the adapter to reconnect.
5. Observe that no inbound event is logged and the agent never responds. Resending works.

### Suggested direction
The adapter needs to ask Slack what it missed. There are two ways to do it, and they can be combined.

**Option A: lazy lookback when a message arrives (smaller change)**
When an inbound message arrives for a Slack chat:
1. Read the newest Slack message `ts` already recorded for that thread or channel.
2. For a thread reply, call `conversations.replies` for that thread since that `ts`.
3. For a top-level message, call `conversations.history` for the channel since that `ts`.
4. Add any missed human messages ahead of the new one, deduplicated by `ts`.

- **Cost:** one API call per inbound message, no startup burst, and no replay of old requests on its own. The missed messages arrive as earlier context in the same batch, and the agent decides whether they still matter. In the case above, the user's later message in the same thread would have pulled in the lost one.
- **Gap:** nothing is recovered until another message arrives. If the user sends one message and then waits, there is still no reply and no sign anything went wrong. If the stale socket also drops that nudge, it won't help.

**Option B: eager catch-up on start and reconnect (closes the gap)**
On adapter start and on each socket reconnect, run the same fetch for each wired Slack messaging group, without waiting for a new message.

- **Cost:** `conversations.history` can't show which threads have new replies. It filters by the parent message's timestamp, and in my case it returned nothing for the window while the thread had a new reply. So this needs one `conversations.replies` call per known thread. Every thread is its own session in `per-thread` mode, so the call count grows over time. It should be bounded to threads with a session active in the last N days, with a configurable maximum lookback age.
- **Benefit:** recovers messages even if the user never sends another one.

I'd suggest A as the baseline, since it's the smaller change and avoids acting unprompted on stale requests. B could follow as an opt-in for people who want silent loss fully closed.

### Related
- Telegram, WhatsApp and Signal appear to recover missed messages through their platforms (server-side queue or offline push). Dial documents a roughly 2-minute replay window. Slack has no equivalent, so the adapter would need to do this itself.
- Discord (gateway) looks like it has the same gap: no replay after a long disconnect and no catch-up in the adapter. I haven't verified this against a live bot, and this issue is only about Slack.
- Different from #3064 and #3728 (adapter fails to start or poll silently) and from #2995, #3058 and #4415 (outbound sends dropped while offline). I found no existing issue about missed inbound messages.

issues.title: test(cli): some src/cli tests cannot fail, or build their expected value from the code under test
issues.body:
Some tests under `src/cli` pass whatever the code does, so they would not catch a regression:

- **The expected value comes from the code itself.** The stdin limit test builds both its input and its expected error from `MAX_STDIN_JSON_BYTES`, so raising the limit still passes. The approvals status test builds its list from the same constant the column uses.
- **The result comes from the test's own mock.** Two `groups create` tests check a config row that the test's mock of `initGroupFilesystem` writes. The real path is already covered by the folder-reuse tests.
- **The assertion can't fail.** "normalizes dashed flags" expects `unknown flag --bogus-flag` with or without normalization. "global: does not auto-fill --id" runs on a resource that never gets `id` filled in any scope.
- **Duplicates.** A few tests repeat a check another test already makes, with less detail.

Proposed fix: rewrite these against literal behaviour (for example `64 * 1024`, or a group-scoped agent reading a wiring through real dispatch), and delete the copies. Each rewrite should fail when the behaviour it guards is broken. Tests only, plus dropping one unused `export` (`DROPPED_MESSAGE_REASONS`).

Done when: a draft PR that closes this issue keeps `src/cli` green and typecheck clean.

issues.title: [hardening] Agent image and CI: Bun 1.4.4 is inside an upstream advisory, fixed in 1.4.5

labels.name: kind/hardening
labels.description: Defense-in-depth improvement; not exploitable across a trust boundary

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Confirmation

- [x] I confirm that this is not an exploitable vulnerability and can be discussed in public.

### What should be safer?

The agent image and CI pin Bun 1.4.4. That version is inside a public upstream advisory published on 19 November 2026:

- [GHSA-p268-p2w7-qr8x](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/security/advisories/GHSA-p268-p2w7-qr8x) on `oven-sh/bun`, high severity: use-after-free in HTTP/3 header decoding in the bundled LSQUIC.
- Affected: `>= 1.3.14, < 1.4.5`. Fixed in Bun 1.4.5, released the same day.

Whether NanoClaw can reach the affected code is not established. A text search of `container/` finds no HTTP/3 or QUIC use in the agent runner, and the runner sends its traffic through an HTTP proxy, so it is probably not reachable. That was a search, not a test.

Proposed: move the pin to 1.4.5 in every place it is set:

- `container/Dockerfile` line 31 (`ARG BUN_VERSION`)
- `bun-version:` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (3 lines), `.github/workflows/registry-skills.yml` (7 lines) and `.github/workflows/release.yml` (1 line)

1.4.5 is one day old. It may be worth waiting a few days before merging the bump, as the repo does for npm packages with `minimumReleaseAge`.

Nothing follows this pin today: it is a Dockerfile `ARG`, which Dependabot does not read. That gap is tracked in #4493.

### How can we verify the concern?

`grep -rn "1\.4\.4" container/Dockerfile .github/workflows` lists the twelve lines. The advisory's range and fixed version are on the linked page.

After the bump: the image build already checks `bun --version` against the pin (`container/Dockerfile` line 83), and the CI jobs run the agent runner's tests on the new version.

Read from the repository and the upstream advisory; nothing was built or run.

### Affected version

main at 1a02784c (also v2026.11.0-rc.3)

### AI assistance

Yes. I verified it myself and can explain it

### AI assistance details

Claude Code compared the pins that no tool follows with upstream advisory lists and found this one.

### Related trust boundary

Supply chain

issues.title: Telegram: lines starting with #<number> are rendered as headings
issues.body:
**Bug:** an agent message with a line that starts with `#<digits>` (no space), e.g. `#467 is closed. ...`, arrives in Telegram as a large heading.

**Observed:** 2026-11-12, agent reply beginning `#467 is closed. I left a comment ...` rendered as a heading block (bold, enlarged); the rest of the message rendered normally. A mid-line reference such as `(#374)` is unaffected. Issue/PR references at the start of a line are very common in agent output ("#467 merged", "#12 is blocked").

**Cause (suspected):** Telegram's rich-text parsing now promotes lines starting with `#` to headings without requiring the space after the hashes that CommonMark requires for an ATX heading. Same behavior reported in another Telegram bridge: adolfousier/opencrabs#1257 (they fixed it by enforcing the space-after-hash rule in one shared predicate). I have not confirmed whether the promotion happens in Telegram itself or in `@chat-adapter/telegram`'s converter.

**Context:** after #3250 dropped `telegram-markdown-sanitize.ts`, there is no `transformOutboundText` hook on the Telegram channel, so nothing guards this case.

**Proposed fix:** in `src/channels/telegram.ts`, add a small `transformOutboundText` hook that escapes a leading `#` only when it is followed directly by a digit at the start of a line (`^#(?=\d)` to `\#`), skipping fenced code blocks. Narrow on purpose, so real headings (`# Title`, `## Title`) keep working. Needs a test that checks `#467 foo` is not a heading, `# Title` still is, and code fences are untouched. The exact escape form should be checked against the adapter's MarkdownV2 output.

**Why in the channel and not in prompts:** it applies to every agent group on Telegram, including new ones, and does not depend on the model remembering a rule.

Related: #3250, #2767, #2877.

prs.title: feat: add AgentMail email channel adapter
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-agentmail`: an email channel on an AgentMail-hosted inbox, so an agent gets its own address without touching the operator's domain MX records.

- **Adapter**: native (no Chat SDK bridge exists for AgentMail). One messaging group per correspondent (`agentmail:<address>`), same flattened model as Resend. Can originate threads (`messages.send`) and reply in-thread (`messages.reply`).
- **Modes**: cron-scheduled polling (default; no public endpoint) or webhook (Svix-verified, on the shared webhook server).
- **Sender allowlist**: optional `AGENTMAIL_INBOUND_ALLOW` (addresses and `@domain`s). Unlisted mail stays in the inbox and raises no approval card, so a public inbox doesn't flood the operator with spam cards.
- **Agent-facing text**: a header (from, subject, thread/message ids, attachments) plus AgentMail's `extracted_text` (quoted history stripped).
- **Restart safety**: poll cursor, recent ids, and reply targets persist to `data/agentmail-state.json`; resume is capped at 3 days back.
- **Channel defaults**: declared (`dm-only` mentions, `request_approval` for unknown senders).
- **Out of scope**: an agent-side mail tool (reading the inbox, attachments, cold sends with subjects). That will be a separate `/add-agentmail-tool` PR.

This PR was rebuilt as one commit on current `main` (the earlier history conflicted).

## Related work

No issue. #287 is an older AgentMail skill PR (Feb 2026, pre-v2 channel model); this one targets the current registry-branch / `ChannelDefaults` shape.

New /add-agentmail skill: give an agent its own email inbox via AgentMail (polling or webhook), with an optional inbound sender allowlist.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops `verify-agent-image` from failing when the image a pin replaces is no longer in the registry.

- **Problem**: the "Size delta is plausible" step reads the old and the new image to compare sizes. On https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4512 the old 10-21 image read back empty, the JSON parse crashed, and the job failed, although the new image passed every real check.

prs.title: Fix: strip agent-group suffix from inbound platform message id
prs.body:
Fixes #3153

## Type of Change
- [x] Fix - bug fix or security fix to source code

## Description

`getMessageIdBySeq()` in `container/agent-runner/src/db/messages-out.ts` returned inbound `messages_in.id` verbatim, claiming (per its own comment) it was already the platform message ID. It wasn't: the host namespaces inbound row ids per agent group by appending `:<agentGroupId>` (`src/router.ts` `messageIdForAgent`) so ids stay unique across per-agent session DBs.

That composite id flowed unchanged into `addReaction` / `editMessage` (via `mcp-tools/core.ts` → `channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts`), which real platforms reject — e.g. Slack returns `message_not_found` for every attempt.

### Fix

Added `stripAgentGroupSuffix(id, agentGroupId)` and applied it to the inbound branch of `getMessageIdBySeq()`, using the runner's own `loadConfig().agentGroupId`.

The suffix is stripped via an exact end-of-string match on `:<agentGroupId>`, **not** by splitting on the first or last colon. Platform ids can legitimately contain colons themselves — e.g. Telegram's `chatId:messageId` format (`6037840640:42`, referenced in this file's own doc comment) — so a naive colon-split would mis-parse those ids even before this fix's suffix is appended. Exact-suffix matching handles this correctly regardless of how many colons the underlying platform id contains, and safely no-ops when `agentGroupId` is empty or doesn't match.

Outbound messages are unaffected — they already resolve via `delivered.platform_message_id`, the real platform id written by the host after delivery.

## Test plan
- [x] Added `container/agent-runner/src/db/messages-out.test.ts` covering: bare Slack-style id, Telegram-style id containing its own colon, id without the suffix, id with a non-matching agent group suffix, and empty `agentGroupId`, plus two `getMessageIdBySeq` round-trip tests against an in-memory `messages_in` row.
- [x] `bun test` — 7/7 new tests pass; full `container/agent-runner` suite: 305 pass / 1 skip / 1 fail, the 1 failure (`poll-loop.test.ts` task-run timing test) reproduces identically on `main` without this change and passes in isolation — confirmed pre-existing/flaky, unrelated to this fix.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` — clean.

**What:** Removes the committed `groups/global/CLAUDE.md` from the repo (−166 lines).

**Tested:** `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm exec vitest run` pass; no source or test code reads `groups/global/CLAUDE.md` (the only reference to the path is the migration's delete).

prs.title: fix(router): a new thread does not wait for its siblings' mailboxes
prs.body:
## What

A new thread's first message no longer waits for its sibling sessions' mailboxes. The typing indicator shows before any context is gathered.

## Why

When a message opens a new per-thread session, the router seeds the session with the conversation's top-level talk before it writes the message: each hot sibling's root user message and its top-level agent posts (`backfillSession`). The backfill read those by opening up to eight sibling sessions whole. On a remote (S3) mailbox, a session that is not in the Host's memory is read whole, record by record, through one Host-wide pool of reads. So the message and the typing indicator waited for all eight.

Seen on a production Host, two and seven minutes after a Host restart, Slack DM:

| | "Session created" to "Message routed" |
|---|---|
| new thread 1 | 23.3 s |
| new thread 2 | 12.2 s |
| reply in an existing thread (no backfill) | 0.8 s |

Nothing else between those two lines takes time: wake context is held to 1.5 s and logged no slow warning, and the message write is one insert. The person saw nothing for that time; the reply came 60 s after the message.

## How

- **Record the talk where the Host sees it.** A small central table, `conversation_timeline` (migration 027), gets one row per top-level message:
  - the router records a new session's first message (same rules as the mailbox's `getConversationRoot`: a chat message on a real chat surface, never a Host-injected instruction);
  - delivery records each delivered top-level agent post (same rules as `getTopLevelOutbound`: no system, task-log or agent-to-agent rows, no thread or a thread id that names only the chat).
  Both writes are off the message's path and never throw.
- **Read it with one query.** The backfill reads the newest rows of the same hot siblings, with the same horizon (`ECHO_MAX_AGE_MS`), the same catch-up floor and the same limit (12). No sibling mailbox is opened. Labels, surfaces, row ids and the single write into the new session are unchanged.
- **Typing first.** The router starts the typing indicator in the wake branch before the backfill and wake context; the start after the write only refreshes it. It is a one-line helper call, so skills anchored on the wake branch's `startTypingRefresh(` block still match once.
- **Retention.** Rows older than the horizon are never read and are deleted when their conversation records its next row. A session's rows are deleted with the session (`deleteSession`, group delete, chat delete; no foreign key, like the host-coordination tables). Text is kept to 4000 characters, the most the backfill writes for a row.

No wait, timeout, retry, cache or setting is added.

## Limits, stated

- Talk from before this release is not in the table, so for up to three days (the backfill horizon) a new thread in an older conversation gets less of it. Slack chats with history reading on still get the platform's own timeline from the `channel-timeline` wake-context provider.
- A long-idle existing session still reads its own newest row to set its catch-up floor (one mailbox open of the session being woken, which a new thread never does).
- `getConversationRoot` and `getTopLevelOutbound` stay on the mailbox interface (the S3 mailbox in nanoco-recipes implements them); this PR no longer calls them.

## How it fits with other work

- nanoco-recipes#2432 (approved, not merged) stops the host sweep from opening idle sessions, which keeps the mailbox cache from churning. Its memo is in memory, so right after a Host restart every session is cold again; this PR removes the backfill's sibling reads altogether, cold or not.
- #4247 changes the same backfill (attachments on echo and backfill rows). Whichever merges second carries the other's change: here the rows come from the timeline, so attachment ids would be recorded with the row.
- The 18.6 s the same message also waited while its group's pod was replaced as stale is a separate fix.
- Governance's session delete keeps its own list of session tables: nanocoai/nanoco-recipes#2609 adds this table to it.

## Tests

Red first, each on `main` plus the new test:
- `backfill-timeline.test.ts`: two hot siblings whose mailbox opens never answer (a cold remote store), their root and post recorded. Red: the backfill is still waiting after 2 s. Green: both rows seeded, no sibling opened.
- `router-new-thread-wait.test.ts` (real `routeInbound`): the typing indicator starts while the backfill is still running (red: no typing until the backfill ends); a new thread's first message is recorded as the session's root (red: no row).
- `delivery-timeline.test.ts` (real `deliverToSessions`): a delivered top-level post is recorded, a reply in a thread is not (red: no row).
- `timeline.test.ts` (real central DB): what is and is not recorded, redelivery, text cap, horizon pruning, the read's order, floor and limit, deletion with the session.
- `backfill.test.ts`: the existing cases kept (hot set, labels, surfaces, floor, limit, horizon, row ids), now against the timeline read.

Local: `src` suite 2511 passed, 0 failed (201 files); typecheck and lint clean on the changed files. nanoco-recipes `check-recipe nanoco-k8s-nancy-v3` with this head pinned: compose (117 skills), install, typecheck and packaging ok. In that composed tree the related tests fail only where they fail on `main` too (no S3 endpoint for local tests).

Box proof: to follow in a comment.

prs.title: feat(release): let allowlisted maintainers approve their own stable publish
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets glifocat approve their own stable publish run. Anyone else still needs a second release reviewer.

- **Problem**: the `release` environment blocks self-review for everyone, so every stable publish waits on a second reviewer.
- **Check**: a new first step in the stable publish job, before checkout, reads the run's attempt and approval history. It fails if the dispatcher or re-runner approved the run (matched by account ID) and is not on `SELF_APPROVAL_ALLOWLIST` in `release.yml` (`glifocat`). It also fails on an API error, with no `release` approval, or when an app or bot started the run.
- **Verify**: expects `prevent_self_review=false` on `release`; the other environment checks stay. A new stable-only step fails unless main requires a team's approval for `.github/**` (a ruleset required-reviewers rule, nothing negated).
- **CODEOWNERS**: adds glifocat to the existing lines and gives `/.github/` (workflows, the allowlist, CODEOWNERS itself) the same owners. Ruleset 12836988 (protect-main) has `require_code_owner_review=false`, so CODEOWNERS only routes reviews; the team rule is what enforces them.
- **Later**: a comment marks where a signed-tag check (YubiKey) can go.
- **Out of scope**: pre-releases (unchanged), and the ruleset and environment changes themselves.

**After merge, in order:**
1. Wait until v2026.11.0 is published. Re-running a publish job from an older run uses that run's workflow, which has no check.
2. Ethan adds the required-reviewers rule to protect-main: a team approves `.github/**`, at least 1.
3. Ethan turns off "Prevent self-review" on `release`. Steps 2 and 3 are admin changes, logged in the repo change log. Until both are done, stable verify fails.
4. The next stable can be self-approved.

## Related work

No issue. This changes the maintainers' own release process, the release owner asked for it, and the full design is in this PR. Closed #3649 also proposed a `*` default owner, owners for the supply-chain files and dropping dead rules. None of that is folded in here.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/release.test.ts scripts/release-notes.test.ts` -> 114 passed. New tests run both steps' real scripts with a stubbed `gh`. A second reviewer and an allowlisted self-approval pass. Other self-approvals fail (dispatcher, re-runner, earlier attempt, renamed login), and so do app dispatchers, weak or missing team rules, and API errors.
- Removing any one of 10 conditions across the two checks makes a test fail.
- The API shapes were checked against real runs. Run against the live API today, the main-rule step fails as expected.
- `actionlint` 1.7.12 with shellcheck: clean, apart from the unknown `ubuntu-26.04` label it also reports on main.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

## Security and trust boundaries

Workflow change. For stable releases, the two-person rule moves from an admin-only environment setting into `release.yml`. Verify requires that a change to `.github/` needs a team's approval on `main`; ruleset bypass actors can still merge without review, as today. Adds `actions: read` to the publish job. The check runs before checkout, so no target code runs first.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-antigravity with its own payload
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-antigravity`, a provider skill that runs agent groups on Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`) and Gemini models, switchable per group with `ncl groups config update --provider antigravity`.
- **Problem**: there is no way to run a NanoClaw agent on Gemini through Google's own agent harness; OpenCode reaches Gemini models but not Antigravity's tools, planning and conversation store.
- **Fix**: a provider skill shaped like `/add-cursor`. All code and tests live in the skill's `payload/`; apply wires the five provider barrels and adds a pinned, sha512-checked `agy` 1.5.8 to the agent image. Auth is a Gemini API key held only by the credential gateway; the container sees a placeholder.
- **Out of scope**: Google-account (OAuth) sign-in, which Google's terms do not allow from a third-party harness; a generic manifest for native binaries (see "Core changes" below).

<details>
<summary>Core changes outside the skill, and why</summary>

agy is a native Go binary that is not published on npm, so `container/cli-tools.json` (npm only) cannot install it. The block has to run as root, before the setuid sweep and `USER node`, and is best placed above the often-bumped layers so a lockfile or Claude Code bump does not re-download 265 MB. No existing hook does that, so this PR adds one:

- `container/Dockerfile`: an empty `# >>> nanoclaw:provider-binaries` / `# <<< nanoclaw:provider-binaries` marker region just above `# ---- agent-runner deps`. With nothing installed it changes no layer.
- `docs/skill-directives.md`, `scripts/skill-directives.ts` (comment), `docs/skill-guidelines.md`, `docs/skills-model.md`: one line each naming the region as the native-binary path.
- `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts`: the scratch root gets a stub Dockerfile carrying the region, the same way it already stubs `cli-tools.json`.

Alternatives considered: a prose-only Dockerfile edit like `/add-mnemon` breaks setup's deterministic provider install (`setup/providers/install.ts` fails on any step it cannot apply); appending at end of file with `USER root`/`USER node` breaks on remove, which deletes by line and would also delete core's own `USER node`. A `json-merge` manifest for native binaries (url + sha512 per arch) would be cleaner long term but is a bigger core feature. I'm happy to split the marker into its own PR first, or to rework it into a manifest, if you prefer.

Other edits: the `registry-skills.yml` matrix entry, the provider list in `skill-descriptor.test.ts`, `.github/skill-pins/not-covered.json` (regenerated; `AGY_VERSION=1.5.8` now appears as a hand-checked binary pin), and README (Antigravity listed next to Codex, Cursor and OpenCode).
</details>

## Related work

No issue. It is a self-contained provider skill in the `/add-cursor` shape (#4107), so it can be reviewed directly; nothing changes for installs that don't apply it.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation
- `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm run skill-pins:check`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint` -> pass (lint: 0 errors)
- `pnpm test` -> pass: 345 files, 5082 tests
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts add-antigravity` -> pass: apply, host and container typecheck, payload tests (vitest 102, bun 87), provider-contract verifier (9/9), image build (agy 1.5.8 amd64, `cli.tar.gz: OK`), byte-exact remove, re-apply
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts --combined-providers` -> pass with codex, cursor and opencode (vitest 288 passed, bun 462 passed)
- **Live end-to-end on Linux x64** (Docker, Iron Proxy gateway, CLI channel, real Gemini key): two turns in one session; resume after `ncl groups restart` (new container, `--conversation` reused, earlier codeword recalled); the `conversations/` archive written with both exchanges; inside the container `ps` shows agy and no claude; the gateway saw only Google hosts (0 Anthropic requests); `REMOVE.md` restored the tree byte-exact and re-apply reproduced it. The real key was found nowhere in container env or filesystem, the image, logs, process args or the checkout. An earlier run of the same setup also covered file and shell tools, MCP `send_message`, `ask_user_question`, and a 12-case scripted eval against the live API.
- **arm64**:
  - (a) Native GitHub `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner ([run](https://github.com/kennethleungty/nanoclaw/actions/runs/44118483750)): apply/remove, image build, all tests (bun 759 pass), and agy reaching the Gemini API from the arm64 image.
  - (b) QEMU-emulated arm64 on x64: full NanoClaw chat behind the gateway (reply, resume, tools, MCP, `ask_user_question`).
  - (c) Both ran before the installer switched from `TARGETARCH` to `uname -m`, so the final 5-line block was rebuilt for arm64 under QEMU on the pinned base image: arm64 tarball selected, sha512 OK, `agy --version` 1.5.8 on aarch64 as `node`. A mismatched `AGY_VERSION` stops the build before any download.
- **Live on a real chat app, behind OneCLI**: a long-running downstream install (2026.10.0 core, OneCLI 1.42 gateway, Telegram channel, GCP e2-small x86_64). That core predates the Dockerfile region and the exchange archive (#4105), so both were backported first, plus the provider list in `skill-descriptor.test.ts`. The skill's own pre-flight check then passed and its directives applied cleanly (host build, runtime typecheck, payload tests, verifier 9/9, image build with agy 1.5.8). The key went in through `setup/index.ts --step provider-auth antigravity` at the masked prompt and landed in OneCLI as a project-scoped secret for `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` with `x-goog-api-key` injection. Then the group was switched with `ncl groups config update --provider antigravity`:
  - Messages sent from the Telegram mobile app were answered by agy. In the session container `agy … --model gemini-4-hydrogen-medium --conversation <id>` was running, and there were 0 `claude` processes.
  - The container env held only `GEMINI_API_KEY=nc-antigravity-placeholder`, and OneCLI logged only Google hosts (`generativelanguage`, `play`), with 0 Anthropic requests.
  - The conversation resumed across a model change and `ncl groups restart`, and one `conversations/` archive covered both turns.
  - `agy models` from inside the container, through the gateway, listed the slugs the key can use.
  - Replies arrived about 11 s after the Telegram message on `gemini-4-hydrogen-medium`, including a cold container start.
  - On current `main`, OneCLI also records the connection for the group's provider from `provider: 'antigravity'`, the same target shape as `/add-cursor`, asserted in `setup/providers/antigravity.test.ts`.
- **Apple Silicon** (`macOS arm64`, Darwin 27.2.0, Node v24.15.0, commit `009028b`):
  - Static and CI checks: `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm run skill-pins:check`, host and container `tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` (0 errors), and `registry-skills.yml` matrix discovery (`23/23`) -> pass.
  - Skill lifecycle and composition (host-side, no local Docker daemon): `scripts/test-registry-skills.ts add-antigravity` (pre-flight, 21 payload files, 5 barrels, `Dockerfile` `nanoclaw:provider-binaries` block, host/setup 101 pass, container 87 pass, `provider-contract-verifier` 9/9, byte-exact `REMOVE.md` restore and re-apply) and `--combined-providers` with codex, cursor and opencode (`update-skills` refresh, verifier 9/9, 287 host + 462 container pass) -> pass; both pinned `1.5.8` (`4602374149505024`) `amd64` and `arm64` tarballs verified `OK` with macOS `/sbin/sha512sum -c`. (Docker Desktop on Apple Silicon runs the same `linux/arm64` image validated on the native arm64 runner and QEMU runs above.)
  - Live agy 1.5.8 native integration on Darwin `arm64`: `antigravity.native.test.ts` (7/7 pass) against the signed macOS `arm64` agy 1.5.8 binary — two-turn stream-JSON session with `nanoclaw.md` memory rules and `x-goog-api-key: nc-antigravity-placeholder`, `--conversation` resume, unknown-conversation fallback notice, stdio MCP tool call across macOS `/var/folders -> /private/var/folders` symlink, turn abort, HTTP 400 auth classification, and queued follow-up respawn; plus `HTTPS_PROXY` + `SSL_CERT_FILE` TLS gateway check confirming `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` and `play.googleapis.com` carry only `nc-antigravity-placeholder` with zero secret leakage.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-antigravity skill: run agent groups on Google's Antigravity CLI (Gemini models) with a Gemini API key held by the credential gateway.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- **Credentials:** the Gemini key goes only to the credential gateway, through `getCredentialStore().connection()` with a `GatewayCredentialTarget` that sets `provider: 'antigravity'`. Containers get `GEMINI_API_KEY=nc-antigravity-placeholder`, which agy sends as `x-goog-api-key`; the gateway swaps it for the real key on the wire. The key is never in `.env`, container env, argv, mounts or logs. The live runs scanned for it and found it nowhere.
- **Supply chain:** one exact build (1.5.8, execution id 4602374149505024) downloaded from `storage.googleapis.com`, a sha512 pinned per architecture and checked with `sha512sum -c` before extraction, a `--version` check that fails the build, and auto-update forced off. The tarballs are byte-identical to the assets on Google's GitHub release.
- **Egress:** model domains are `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` and `play.googleapis.com` (agy telemetry, which 1.5.8 cannot turn off in API-key mode). Requests from antigravity groups pass without an approval card; with Iron Proxy, model domains are allowed install-wide (as for other providers).
- **Permissions:** agy runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and its terminal sandbox off (it needs user namespaces, which Docker's seccomp profile blocks), so the container is the boundary, as with the other providers. The image still ends as `node`, with no setuid binaries.
- **Prompt injection:** per-session instructions go in-band as a `<nanoclaw_system_context>` block in agy's first turn. Core's formatter escapes `<` in inbound text, so a chat message cannot forge that block.

## Skill delivery

- **Apply:** the pre-flight check refuses a core without the provider contracts, the credential-connection seam, the exchange archive or the Dockerfile region, and leaves no partial change. Apply then copies 21 payload files (host, container and setup provider code, their tests, and `container/install-antigravity.sh`). It appends one import to each of the five barrels (`src/providers`, `src/provider-contracts`, `container/agent-runner/src/providers`, `container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts`, `setup/providers`) and adds the 5-line Dockerfile block inside the region. It then rebuilds the image and host and runs the copied tests.
- **Remove:** `REMOVE.md` reverses each step; every appended line is unique to this skill. After removal the checkout is byte-identical to before (checked by `test-registry-skills.ts`).
- **Fresh clone:** `test-registry-skills.ts` applies the skill to a fresh clone, builds, tests, removes and re-applies it, alone and combined with codex, cursor and opencode.

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Fixes README claims that are false on `main`, in place, before 2026.11.0 ships.

- **Scope**: `README.md` only. Same headings, order, nav row and anchors. No positioning, translations or badge recount. One added block: #4460's readiness TIP.
- **What leaves your machine**: messages, files and API keys never go to us; diagnostics and portal/account data are a short list; the default image source (Claude only) needs the free account; answering no to the Echo prompt skips it.

- **Readiness prompt**: the `[!TIP]` prompt from #4460, word for word, before the Quick Start commands.

Rewrites `src/cli` tests that could not fail, so each one now breaks when the behaviour it names breaks.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops recurring tasks from growing a session's `inbound.db` by one full copy of the task payload per run.

- **Problem**: every re-arm copies the full content (prompt + script) into the next occurrence, and finished occurrences are never trimmed. Size grows as payload × runs, without bound. On a real install, one 21 KB prompt on a `*/10` cron reached 238 MB over 11k runs.
- **Fix**: inside the existing `armNextTask` transaction, the content of the series' older finished occurrences (`completed`/`failed`, recurrence already cleared, `seq` below the new occurrence) is replaced with `{"superseded":true}`.
- **Why rows stay**: `getTaskStats` (runs, failed runs, last run) and `trailingFailedRuns` (script-failure auto-pause) count rows by status. Deleting rows would change both; replacing only the payload changes neither.
- **Why nothing notices**: once a later occurrence exists, every content reader resolves to the newest row of the series: `getTask`, `listLiveTasks`, `findTaskBySeriesSlug`, `updateTask` (future rows only), and the re-arm itself (it reads the just-completed row before compacting). Retries only touch `pending`/`processing` rows. `sessions history` already renders task rows as empty text, because task content has no `text` field.
- **Existing installs**: a series' backlog is compacted on its next re-arm. No migration is needed.
- **Out of scope**: reclaiming file size. SQLite reuses the freed pages, so the file stops growing. `VACUUM` is left to the operator.

<details><summary>Only observable difference</summary>

`ncl tasks get <id>` with the row id of a *superseded* occurrence (not the series id) now shows an empty prompt. The series id and the live occurrence still show the full content.
</details>

## Related work

No existing issue. Searched open and closed issues and PRs for inbound.db growth, retention, prune and recurring tasks. #3289 / #3291 are about the pending backlog, not finished rows.

Open PRs in the same area, all compatible:
- #3696 and #3741 add fields to task content. They read them from the just-completed row at re-arm time, or from the live row at spawn. Neither row is compacted.
- #2915 and #3247 touch the pre-`armNextTask` recurrence path.
- #3594 is container-side.

Happy to rebase whichever lands second.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/mailbox/sqlite/arm-next-task.test.ts` -> 7 passed. 5 are new:
  - a payload is kept once per series, and every row, `getTaskStats` and `trailingFailedRuns` are unchanged;
  - a cancelled series keeps its payload;
  - a pre-existing backlog is compacted on the next re-arm;
  - other series and non-task rows are untouched;
  - when the insert fails, the compaction rolls back with the pair.
- Same file without the one-line call in `armNextTask` -> the two compaction tests fail. The three guard tests still pass, as intended.
- `pnpm run build` -> ok.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` -> 4242 passed, 1 skipped. The clean base had 4237 passed, 1 skipped, so the 5 new tests are the only change.
- Copy of the 238 MB production `inbound.db`, through `wrapSqliteInbound`:
  - stats identical before and after;
  - 203 MB of pages freed;
  - first re-arm 105 ms, which compacts 11k rows once;
  - steady-state re-arm 8 ms.
- Live install, same patch:
  - after the next sweep re-arm, all 11,072 finished rows of the series hold the marker;
  - the pending occurrence keeps its full 12 KB payload;
  - `ncl tasks get <series>` shows the full prompt and an unchanged `completed_runs`;
  - no new host errors.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Recurring tasks no longer grow the session database by one copy of the task prompt per run.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. Host-only write to the session's `inbound.db` (its single writer), inside an existing transaction.

## Summary

Moves the pinned Bun from 1.4.4 to 1.4.5 in the agent image and in CI.
- **Problem**: Bun 1.4.4 is inside upstream advisory [GHSA-p268-p2w7-qr8x](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/security/advisories/GHSA-p268-p2w7-qr8x) (high: use-after-free in HTTP/3 header decoding in the bundled LSQUIC; affected `>= 1.3.14, < 1.4.5`). A search of `container/` finds no HTTP/3 or QUIC use in the agent runner, so it is probably not reachable; this is a precaution.
- **Fix**: `ARG BUN_VERSION` in `container/Dockerfile` and every `bun-version:` line in `ci.yml`, `registry-skills.yml` and `release.yml` move to 1.4.5 (12 lines).
- **Out of scope**: nothing tracks this pin automatically; that is #4493. The `1.4.4` strings in `scripts/update/*.test.ts` are fixture values the tests write themselves and are left as they are.

## Related work

Closes #4496. Related: #4493.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Moves the pinned Iron Proxy from upstream v0.52.0 to v0.59.0.
- **Problem**: the pin was seven releases behind and nothing tracks it. The newer releases harden request and WebSocket handling and the destination deny list, and the pin sat inside the range of an upstream advisory for a feature NanoClaw does not enable.
- **Fix**: `iron-proxy-commit` moves to `c32e47d6` (v0.59.0). Upstream needs Go 1.27.3 since v0.54.0, so the build image, the `iron-front` job's `go-version` and the front proxy's `go.mod`/`go.sum` move with it. One front-proxy test changes: Go 1.27 closes the connection after a refused CONNECT, so the challenge test now accepts the retry on the same connection or a new one.
- **Out of scope**: no change to the front proxy's code or to the config NanoClaw writes for Iron. Base-image digests are #4490.

## Related work

Closes #4494. Related: #4493.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- Against upstream v0.59.0 in `golang:1.27.3-bookworm`, as the `iron-front` job runs it: `go test -mod=readonly -race -count=1 ./...` in `_front-proxy` -> ok; `gofmt -l .` -> clean; upstream's `go test ./cmd/iron-proxy ./internal/config ./internal/transform/grpc` -> ok; both binaries build with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
- The old test fails under Go 1.27.3 on the old Iron commit too, so the cause is Go's HTTP server, not Iron. curl 7.88 and git 2.39 against a stand-in for the front's 407 challenge: with Go 1.26.1 both retry on the same connection, with 1.27.3 both retry on a new one, and both send the identity either way.
- `conformance/credential-scope-cases.json` regenerated against v0.59.0 with the script in that folder: identical apart from the commit id.
- Read, not run: every key `ironProxyConfig` writes is unchanged upstream; `internal/controlplane`, `internal/management`, `proto/` and `gen/` have no differences between the two tags.
- `pnpm exec vitest run .claude/skills/add-iron-proxy/scripts scripts/skill-pins` -> 172 passed. `pnpm run skill-pins:check` -> clean.
- Not run: the full image build, a live install, managed mode with Iron Control, a browser behind the proxy, macOS.

releases.name: v2026.11.0
releases.body:
NanoClaw 2026.11.0 is the new stable release, so `/update-nanoclaw` on the default `stable` channel now offers it. 🦐 It covers everything since 2026.10.0 and was tested on the `beta` channel through nine pre-releases. Five changes you'll notice first:

- **Each agent gets only the keys you give it.** OneCLI moves to 1.45, where new agent groups get only their model key and other keys go to the groups you choose. OneCLI's database also gets its own password, which closes a critical security hole (see Security below). On OneCLI installs, both need a step from you. ([#4094](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094), [#4439](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4439))
- **Agents can create other agents from templates.** Ask for one in chat, or pick one from `ncl templates list` or the public library. ([#4112](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4112))
- **Cursor is an agent provider.** Run `/add-cursor`, or pick Cursor in setup, and your agents run on Cursor's Agent SDK. ([#4107](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4107))
- **Cards can show KPI fields, a table and charts.** Agents put them in `send_card` cards, and Slack draws them natively. ([#4292](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4292))
- **Newer models.** Locally built agent images run Claude Code 2.1.321 with Claude Haiku 5.5 and know Claude Fable 5.2. Codex groups signed in with ChatGPT can use GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. ([#4332](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4332), [#4446](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4446))

Eight changes need action from some installs, among them the OneCLI upgrade, the OneCLI database password, the webhook address and two new Google Chat settings, so check the section below before you update.

Thanks to everyone who ran the betas and told us what broke, and to the community contributors whose fixes are in this release: @shachartal, @carstenf, @topcoder1, @antonio-antuan, @witek, @refactornator, @patrick-hofmann, @musashinm, @NechuBM, @petrolette, @echarrod, @stefancgillberg, @bmultini and @OowhitecatoO.

### ⚠️ Before you update

- [BREAKING] **Chat SDK channels move to adapter 4.41.1, which fixes Telegram messages with links that were never delivered.** Affected: installs where `grep -o '"@chat-adapter/[a-z]*"' package.json` prints anything (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Teams, WhatsApp Cloud, GitHub, Linear). Fix: `/update-nanoclaw` refreshes installed channels; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one. Google Chat: @mentions in spaces now need `GOOGLE_CHAT_BOT_USER_ID=users/<id>` in `.env` (DMs work without it; without it the log says "Google Chat botUserId is not configured" at startup): once the app has replied to you in a DM, list that DM's messages with the Chat API (`spaces.messages.list`), copy the `sender.name` of a message whose sender `type` is `BOT`, and restart the service. Slack agent-to-agent rooms: a sibling bot now arrives as `slack:bot:U…` instead of `slack:bot:B…`, so approve each sibling bot once more. Check: each channel answers a test message. Rollback: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts rollback --id <transaction-id>` ([rolling back](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/operate/upgrading#rolling-back)).
  Thanks to @shachartal. ([#3570](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3570), [#3993](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3993))
- [BREAKING] **Iron Proxy installs that connected Codex with ChatGPT before this release must sign in to Codex again.** Detect, from the NanoClaw folder (works while the service is stopped): `f=data/session-materials/iron-control/codex.json; [ -f "$f" ] && grep -q '"mode":"chatgpt"' "$f" && ! grep -q '"accountId"' "$f" && echo affected`. Once running, an affected install's Codex agents answer only with the failure notice ("Sorry, something went wrong and I couldn't answer") and the agent container log shows `selected workspace missing from routing discovery`. Why: Codex 0.156 and later check the login's workspace id, and older Iron logins never recorded it. Fix: `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex`, then check that a Codex agent answers. OneCLI installs are affected only when the vault holds several ChatGPT logins or one without a recorded id; the host log then says "OneCLI login stand-in keeps its placeholder account id": delete the extra or stale login (`onecli secrets list`, then `onecli secrets delete --id <id>`), run the same command, and grant the new secret to each agent that had the old one, as `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` in your install describes. Rollback: return to the previous release.
  ([#4133](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4133))
- [BREAKING] **Forks and hand-made templates: the template code moved and `templates/` is now ignored by git.** Affected: fork code that imports `cloneRegistry`, `listTemplatesFromDir`, `copyTemplate` or `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` from `setup/templates.ts` (it stops compiling), forks that edit the `GROUP_SCOPE_RESOURCES` line or the stamper's `ensureContainerConfig` line, forks that point setup at their own template library, and anyone who keeps a hand-made template in `templates/`. Why: templates fetched by setup or by an agent are install state and must not block `/update-nanoclaw`, and setup now lists a library from its `index.json`. Fix: import `cloneRegistry` and `listTemplatesFromDir` from `src/templates/library.ts` and `await cloneRegistry()`; `copyTemplate` is gone, so call `ensureTemplateLocal`; a fork that changed `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` edits `LIBRARY_REPO` (`owner/repo`) and `LIBRARY_BRANCH` in `src/templates/library.ts` instead; re-anchor fork edits on the new lines; keep a new hand-made template in git with `git add -f templates/<ref>`; give your own library an `index.json` at its root in the same shape as `nanocoai/nanoclaw-templates` (`{ "schema": 1, "categories": { "<category>": [{ "ref": "<folder>", "name": "...", "description": "..." }] } }`). Check: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes and setup's library picker lists your templates ([building templates](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/templates/building)). Rollback: revert this release; fetched templates then show as untracked in `git status`, so delete them or `git add` the ones to keep.
  ([#4112](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4112))
- [BREAKING] **OneCLI installs: upgrade the gateway to 1.45.0 and the `onecli` CLI to 2.11.0, where agents get only the keys you grant them.** Detect: the gateway's `/api/health` reports a version older than 1.45.0, or `unknown` (Iron Proxy installs skip this). Why: OneCLI 1.44 replaced secret modes with per-agent grants, and 1.45 is the last version that converts existing installs, so do not skip past it. Fix: before restarting, follow `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` in your install ([the same guide on GitHub](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-onecli/payload/docs/onecli-upgrades.md)); it backs up the gateway database, stops if the conversion would delete your rules, and covers the CLI binary. If you use `/add-dial-tool`, run the guide's Dial check before you pull; it deletes the Dial key only when the upgrade could hand it to agents you kept away from Dial (see the Dial item below). Existing groups keep what the conversion gives them; new groups get only their model credential, and on a 1.42 gateway new groups still get every key until you upgrade. To give a group a tool, re-run that tool's skill (for example `/add-vercel`) and pick the group; with `/add-tavily-tool`, re-run its Phase 5 so paid-key upgrades attach the key. `/add-vercel`, `/add-tavily-tool` and `/add-dial-tool` refuse a gateway that is not 1.45. If your Claude key in OneCLI is not named `Anthropic` (or your Codex key `Codex` or `openai`), new groups get no key: run that provider's login again after upgrading (`pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step gateway-auth claude`, or `codex`). Check: `/api/health` reports 1.45.0 and a new agent group answers. Rollback: restore the database backup the guide takes.
  ([#4094](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094))
- [BREAKING] **OneCLI installs: give OneCLI's database its own password. `/update-nanoclaw` does not do this for you.** Detect: `[ -f ~/.onecli/docker-compose.yml ] && { ! grep -q '^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.' ~/.onecli/.env 2>/dev/null || grep -Eqx "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=[\"']?(onecli)?[\"']?[[:space:]]*" ~/.onecli/.env; } && echo affected`. Remote gateways and Iron Proxy installs are not affected. Why: OneCLI's database still used the fixed default password from OneCLI's compose file. Fix, from the NanoClaw folder: `pnpm exec tsx .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/postgres-password.ts`. It saves a random password in `~/.onecli/.env`, sets it on the database and restarts OneCLI once; your data stays. If it prints "Not changed", fix what it names (usually a setting to save in `~/.onecli/.env`) and run it again. Check: a second run prints "OneCLI's database already has its own password", and once the update has finished, an agent answers. Rollback: none needed; the previous release keeps working with the new password.
  ([#4439](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4439))
- [BREAKING] **The webhook server now listens on 127.0.0.1 by default.** Tunnels and reverse proxies on the same machine keep working. Affected: a proxy on another machine, or anything in Docker on Linux that calls back to the host, such as a Mattermost server; webhooks stop arriving, and the log shows `Webhook server started host="127.0.0.1"`. Fix: set `WEBHOOK_HOST=0.0.0.0` (or one interface's IP address; a name such as `localhost` stops the host at startup) in `.env` and restart. Check: a message on that channel gets an answer. Rollback: the same setting restores the old behavior.
  ([#4185](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4185))
- [BREAKING] **Google Chat installs need two new settings, or the channel does not start.** Google Chat now verifies that webhooks come from your Workspace add-on Chat app, using `GOOGLE_CHAT_ENDPOINT_URL` and `GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_NUMBER` (digits) in `.env`; `/update-nanoclaw` brings the new adapter but cannot ask for them. Detect: the log says "Google Chat needs GOOGLE_CHAT_ENDPOINT_URL and GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_NUMBER (digits) in .env to verify webhooks". Fix: re-run `/add-gchat`, which keeps your existing values and asks for the endpoint URL, the project number and the bot user id for @mentions in spaces, or set both values by hand and restart. The Chat app must be a Google Workspace add-on, and converting an app to one cannot be undone. Check: a test message gets an answer. Rollback: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts rollback --id <transaction-id>`.
  ([#4132](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4132), [#4100](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4100))
- [BREAKING] **Custom skills and forks: a card's response handler must say what the click did.** Affected: your own skill or fork code that registers a response handler for card clicks, or that calls `finalizeReject` with a reason. Detect: a response handler that returns `true` still compiles, but its card no longer changes and the host logs `legacy_true`; a `finalizeReject` call with a 4th string argument no longer compiles. Why: a card may show only what the host decided. Fix: return `'accepted'`, `'refused'`, `'closed'` or `'ignored'` (or `false` to pass the click on), and pass a reject reason as `finalizeReject(approval, session, userId, { reason })`. Check: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes and a clicked card changes. Rollback: return to the previous release; handlers that return `true` then redraw as before.
  ([#4168](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4168), [#4171](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4171))
- **`/add-dial-tool` users: run the upgrade guide's Dial check before upgrading OneCLI.** It reads only, and says `delete` only when the gateway has not converted yet (1.43 or older) and the upgrade could remove what keeps agents away from Dial, such as `Dial: blocked agents`, or when it cannot read all the rules that decide; a gateway already on 1.44 or later keeps its Dial key and its grants. When it says `delete`, the guide's `--delete` command removes the key; re-run `/add-dial-tool` after the upgrade, which gives the Dial key only to the agent groups you choose, and new groups get Dial only when you add them. NanoClaw's `ONECLI_PROJECT_ID` and the `onecli` CLI's project (`onecli config set project`, or `ONECLI_PROJECT`) must match or both be unset: when they differ, the re-run stops and writes nothing to OneCLI. An agent group name with a line break no longer changes which groups keep Dial. ([#4196](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4196), [#4095](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4095))
- **Update Node to its October 2026 security release.** Setup now requires Node 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 or newer and refuses the end-of-life 23 and 25; locally built agent images move to Node 22.23.5 (Node's November 2026 security release), pinned by digest, and hardened installs get it with a later image. NanoClaw keeps running on an older Node; re-running setup picks a Node that meets the minimum, and stops only when it finds none. After `/update-nanoclaw`, run `bash setup/install-node.sh`, then re-run `bash nanoclaw.sh` so the service uses the new Node. If Node comes from nvm, fnm, volta or asdf, update it there. ([#4183](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4183))
- **Egress lockdown now covers agents that were already running when it was turned on**: they restart on the locked network when the host restarts. If the lockdown network exists but is not internal (only a network made by hand, or a setting that points at an ordinary one), agents no longer start and the host log says "Refusing to spawn with open egress". Fix: list what is attached with `docker network inspect nanoclaw-egress`, detach it (`docker network disconnect nanoclaw-egress <container>`), then `docker network rm nanoclaw-egress`; the next agent start recreates it as internal. Iron Proxy installs name it `nanoclaw-egress-<slug>`, and `NANOCLAW_EGRESS_NETWORK` can set another name. ([#4160](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4160))
- **Locally built agent images move to Claude Code 2.1.321 and Agent SDK 0.3.321, where Claude Haiku 5.5 replaces Haiku 4.5.** They are the first pair that knows Claude Fable 5.2. On the Anthropic API, Claude Code's background requests and groups set to `haiku` move to Haiku 5.5, which costs a tenth of Haiku 4.5's price for prompts up to 100K tokens. Hardened installs keep Claude Code 2.1.280 and Haiku 4.5 until an image for this release is listed. ([#4332](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4332))
- **Hardened installs move to the image built from v2026.10.0.** A pull now takes the image listed in `agent-images.json` on `main` for the newest release in the install's history, so a new hardened image reaches installs without a new release. Until an image built from 2026.11.0 is listed, this release uses v2026.10.0's (Claude Code 2.1.280, newer than the old pinned build), and the pull's "agent-runner lock drift" warning is expected. `main` lists a newer build of that image, made on 2026-11-14, so `/update-nanoclaw` pulls it again. Run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step registry -- --refresh` to move onto it, and again once the 2026.11.0 image is listed ([hardened runtime](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/guides/echo-hardened-runtime)). ([#4139](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4139), [#4149](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4149))
- **Codex groups signed in with ChatGPT can use GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol.** `/add-codex` now pins `@openai/codex` 0.169.0; OpenAI refuses these models to Codex 0.165 and older on ChatGPT logins (API keys already worked). Groups with no model set start new threads on GPT-6.1 Sol with an API key and on GPT-6.2 Sol with a ChatGPT login; existing threads keep their model. To pick one, run `ncl groups config update --id <group-id> --model gpt-6.2-astra`, then `ncl groups restart --id <group-id>`. To stay on the 2026.10.0 default, use `--model gpt-6-astra`. ([#4446](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4446))

### ✨ New

- **Agents can create other agents from templates.** Ask in chat, or pick one from `ncl templates list` or the public library ([using templates](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/templates/using-templates)). ([#4112](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4112))
- **Cursor is an agent provider.** Run `/add-cursor` or pick Cursor in setup; it needs a locally built agent image ([providers](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/extend/providers)). ([#4107](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4107))
- **Setup waits for a slow first reply instead of failing**, and shows each stage with its time, so local models that take minutes to load pass setup. Setup without a terminal now stops waiting after 2 minutes instead of 30 seconds. ([#4108](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4108))
- **Agents on slow local models are no longer cut off mid-turn.** Raise `NANOCLAW_ABSOLUTE_CEILING_MS` or `NANOCLAW_CLAIM_STUCK_MS` in `.env`, then restart ([environment variables](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/reference/environment-variables)). ([#3646](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3646))
- **Cards can show KPI fields, a table and charts.** Slack draws them natively and Teams shows a chart as a table; where a channel can't show them, the agent sends the numbers as text. ([#4292](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4292))
- **Early test builds are now called betas** (`vX.Y.Z-beta.N`), and the last one or two before a release are release candidates. To get them, run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts set-channel --channel beta`; the default `stable` channel never gets either. ([#4313](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4313))

### 🔒 Security

- **`/add-resend` installs a Resend adapter with no known advisories.** The pin moves from 0.1.1 (4 moderate findings through `uuid`) to 0.3.0, and `/update-nanoclaw` moves existing email installs to it (after a manual merge, rerun `/add-resend`). The webhook now answers before the message is processed, so a message that fails is not retried, and replies are sent as HTML with a plain-text part that drops link targets. ([#4042](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4042))
- **Signal setup checks the signal-cli download's sha256** before installing it. ([#4093](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4093))
- **OneCLI setup keeps keys off the command line.** Setup now gives keys to the `onecli` CLI through a private temporary file or stdin, and hides them in error messages. If setup ever failed while saving your Anthropic key or OneCLI API key, rotate that key and delete the old files in `logs/setup-steps/` and `logs/setup.log`. ([#4187](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4187))
- **OneCLI's database gets its own password, so agent containers can no longer log in to it.** It used a fixed default password, so code in any agent container, including an agent steered by prompt injection, could log in and take control of OneCLI. Setup now gives a new install a random password; an existing install runs the one command under Before you update. `/add-onecli` also tells you when the database still accepts the default password after setup, and `~/.onecli` can no longer be mounted into an agent container. See [GHSA-j39m-796j-gjm3](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/security/advisories/GHSA-j39m-796j-gjm3). ([#4439](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4439), [#4471](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4471))
- **Dial setup no longer leaves the account token readable by other users on the machine** while it pins the default sender number. ([#4315](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4315))
- **Registry sign-in opens your browser only for a plain https link**, and says so when it starts no browser. On WSL without `wslview` or `xdg-open` it no longer tries `cmd.exe`; open the link it prints instead. ([#4316](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4316))
- **Text that task scripts and webhooks put in an agent's prompt can no longer pose as text NanoClaw wrote.** Script output, webhook bodies, task prompts and attachment types can no longer close the block they sit in. Thanks to @petrolette. ([#3717](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3717))
- **Locally built agent images move to Node 22.23.5, Node's November 2026 security release.** `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image. Setup's minimum Node stays the same. ([#4398](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4398))
- **Approval cards on Google Chat and Discord show request text as typed.** On Google Chat a card's own labels are bold, so a line of request text can't pose as one, and a line in an agent's message that starts like a label, such as `*Action:*`, stays as typed. On Discord, `*`, `_` and `~` in request text show as typed, so they can't turn code into links, mentions or spoilers. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-gchat` or `/add-discord`. ([#4356](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4356), [#4360](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4360))
- **Locally built agent images move to Bun 1.4.4, which no longer trusts the revoked eMudhra certificates.** `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image. ([#4193](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4193))
- **Locally built agent images clear every known High and Critical advisory that had a fix.** The image ships npm 11, pnpm 10.34.9, a fresh build of its Node base and updated agent-runner libraries. `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image. ([#4270](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4270))
- **Re-applying a template to an agent (restamp) can no longer be pointed outside its group folder.** It refuses, with an error, to write a context file or skill through a folder in the group folder that was swapped for a link, and checks template file names more strictly. On a Mac this needs the NanoClaw folder on an APFS or HFS+ disk (the usual Mac disk); on other disks these writes are refused. ([#4194](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4194))
- **Hardened how the host opens files in agent folders.**

### 🔧 For custom installations

- **Custom container code that reads `inbound.db`** through `openInboundDb()` or `getInboundDb()` (`mailbox/sqlite/connection.ts`) must use `readInbound((db) => ...)`: `openInboundDb()` is gone, and `getInboundDb()` now works only in tests. ([#4118](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4118))
- **Custom mailbox stores that create storage on first write**: a new thread or conversation now gets its earlier context there. The default SQLite store was not affected. ([#4347](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4347))
- **`CLAUDE.md` matches the code again.** Coding agents get the right session folder and image tag, and know a group's `CLAUDE.md` is rewritten on every start: standing instructions go in `instructions.prepend.md`. ([#4380](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4380))
- **`/add-codex` ships its provider inside the skill**, so installs and forks no longer need the providers branch; on an older core its instructions tell you to update core first. Codex archives pick up core's header fix (the thread-id line no longer renders as a heading). ([#4104](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4104))
- **Provider skills can archive exchanges through core.** Use `container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/exchange-archive.ts`; refreshing `/add-codex` deletes the old copy in `providers/exchange-archive.ts`, so a custom provider that imports it must switch. ([#4105](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4105))
- **Skills can add context when a message wakes an agent, without editing core.** Register a provider with `registerWakeContext` (`src/wake-context.ts`): blocks it returns within a shared 1.5-second budget are written before the waking message, as `<tag about="...">`, a later block rides with the next message, and a slash command gets none. Channel adapters gain an optional `readHistory` (the Chat SDK bridge has it), and the mailbox's outbound reads carry an optional `platformMessageId`. With nothing registered, routing works as before and the agent's prompt gains one line about the `about` attribute. ([#4435](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4435))
- **A gateway credential can target one exact path on a host.** The provider credential seam moves to version 2: a custom provider skill that requires exactly version 1 must accept 1 or later, a skill that sets `path` must require 2, and a custom gateway must declare `connectionPaths: true` to accept path-scoped credentials. ([#4106](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4106))
- **The agent image no longer installs `cron-parser`** or its `luxon` dependency (about 4.9 MB); scheduling still runs on the host. Custom container code that imported them must add them back. ([#4088](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4088))
- **Forks that pointed the `versions.json` agent-image pin at their own mirror** must move that reference to `NANOCLAW_AGENT_IMAGE_REF`, because the `agent-images.json` list now comes first. ([#4139](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4139))
- **Forks no longer run the agent-image refresh workflow**, which failed every 6 hours outside `nanocoai/nanoclaw`. ([#4157](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4157))
- **OpenCode: `OPENCODE_NATIVE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` and `OPENCODE_NATIVE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_COUNT` are gone**; they never took effect. ([#4172](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4172))
- **Forks: keep `@chat-adapter/discord` at 4.41.1.** A newer adapter needs a newer `chat` than core pins, so `pnpm run build` fails. If pnpm stops with `ERR_PNPM_UNUSED_PATCH`, run `pnpm add @chat-adapter/discord@4.41.1` or re-run `/add-discord`; to remove Discord, follow its `REMOVE.md`. `/add-discord`'s troubleshooting now gives the same fix, instead of keeping a newer adapter that doesn't build. ([#4404](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4404))

prs.title: fix(dsh): fork conversations at the selected message
prs.body:
## Summary

Fork native dsh conversations at the selected assistant event, including that event. Bind saved sequence numbers to their originating dsh session. When a selected release or inherited message has no position in the current native log, continue from the copied local prefix. - Reproduced later-turn context in a native fork and later summary content in a fork of a release-format conversation.

- Ran changed-file lint, targeted Vitest coverage, Electron compilation and a production renderer build.
