prs.title: fix(window): defer preload zoom to prevent dropped ready-to-show
prs.body:
## Problem

After PR #3106 (`39b62584`), calling `webFrame.setZoomFactor(1)` unconditionally at the top level of `src/main/preload.ts` triggered Electron #51972 (regression in Electron 40.x–43.x; we ship 43.5.0): setting zoom on a hidden (`show: false`) window before its first compositor paint permanently suppresses `ready-to-show`.

In QA Windows logs, this left the desktop companion floating orb (`Mascot`) invisible even with the toggle enabled (both on fresh install and upgrade, and after toggling OFF→ON), and also prevented `mainWindow` from auto-showing / creating the tray on launch because `did-finish-load` disarmed `showFallbackTimer`.

## Changes

- **Preload / IPC (`WindowIpcChannel.ApplyZoom`)**: Removed top-level `webFrame.setZoomFactor(1)` from `src/main/preload.ts` and replaced it with a `WindowIpcChannel.ApplyZoom` listener. Companion windows never receive zoom updates.
- **Windowing (`installMainWindowZoom`)**: Deferred initial per-window 100% zoom isolation on `mainWindow` until `ready-to-show` or `show`, and routed shortcut/wheel zoom steps and reload resets through `WindowIpcChannel.ApplyZoom` so zoom remains per-window isolated and non-persistent.
- **Windowing (Desktop Companion fallback)**: Added `onCompanionWindowReadyToShow` in `src/main/desktopCompanion/companionWindow.ts` (250ms `did-finish-load` fallback) and applied it to `Mascot`, `Result`, and `PermissionGuide`.
- **Windowing (`mainWindow` startup fallback)**: Added a 1.5s `did-finish-load` fallback in `src/main/main.ts` to complete initial show / tray / cron setup if `ready-to-show` is dropped, and fixed `showFallbackTimer` so `did-finish-load` no longer disarms it before startup completes.

## Verification

- Vitest (`preload.test.ts`, `mainWindowZoom.test.ts`, `companionWindow.test.ts`, `companionPermissionGuide.test.ts`, `desktopCompanionManager.test.ts`): 5 files, 243 tests passed.
- `npm run compile:electron`: passed (0 errors).
- `npx tsc`: passed (0 errors).

prs.title: fix(desktop-companion): keep orb docked across displays and Windows DPI
prs.body:
## Summary

- Start the desktop companion orb flush against the right edge of the work area by default and stop writing fallback/default coordinates back to storage during display changes.
- Persist docking metadata (`edge`, `yRatio`, `displayId`) under `desktop-companion.position.v2` so docked orbs stay flush to their edge and keep proportional height across monitor changes, display unplug/reconnect, and skin size switches.
- Track the active orb display in memory (`activeOrbDisplayId`) and listen for `display-added` events so undragged orbs stay anchored to their display and reconnected monitors restore their docked orb.
- Re-apply Windows orb window bounds after creation and before `ready-to-show` to guard against cross-DPI misplacement on secondary monitors.

## Electron-Specific Changes

- **Storage**: Bumped the orb position store key from `desktop-companion.position.v1` to `desktop-companion.position.v2` (`src/shared/desktopCompanion/constants.ts`) to store edge-docking and display metadata (`edge`, `yRatio`, `displayId`) without inheriting stale absolute coordinates.
- **Window management**: Added `screen` `display-added` handling (cleaned up on dispose), display-aware orb/panel anchoring, and Windows cross-DPI bounds re-application in `createCompanionWindow` and `DesktopCompanionManager.showOrb` (`src/main/desktopCompanion/companionWindow.ts`, `src/main/desktopCompanion/desktopCompanionManager.ts`).
- **IPC / Runtime / Preload**: No changes.

## Testing

- `npm test -- desktopCompanion` — 40 files, 614 tests passed (including new coverage for edge docking, monitor switching/reconnection, skin switches, undragged orb display anchoring, and Windows cross-DPI bounds re-application).
- `npm run compile:electron` — passed.
- `npx tsc` — passed.
- `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 --no-warn-ignored <changed files>` — passed.

prs.title: feat(cowork): restore subagent sessions on the dsh engine
prs.body:
## Summary

Restore the existing subagent panel on the dsh migration branch. Previously the parent could finish a delegated task and show the output files while the subagent panel stayed empty.

## Changes

- Associate delegated calls and results with dsh child session IDs. Keep the parent subscribed across an early yield so it can receive the children's results and finish its summary.
- Read each child's progress and history through its owning parent. Delegated tools inherit the bound Cowork context and retain the child's dsh permission restrictions.
- Import indexed legacy child transcripts at startup before the old engine directory is archived. Reuse cached messages and materialized child sessions so users can reopen an old parent and delegate new work alongside its existing children.

## Testing

- 87 focused Vitest tests passed. Electron and renderer TypeScript checks and changed-file ESLint passed.
- Verified on Windows by driving Electron with Playwright/CDP and the pinned dsh runtime. A deterministic local model endpoint exercised two and five parallel children, on-disk files, restart, asynchronous parent completion, and new delegations in an upgraded parent session.
- The Windows full suite reported 19 failures. Seventeen also failed on the base commit. The remaining two passed independently on this branch.

issues.title: [Bug]: exec tool `command` parameter says "shell command" but paired-node exec doesn't use a shell
issues.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported yet
- [x] I am using the latest version of Moltis

### What happened?

In the exec tool schema, the `command` parameter is described as a shell command (crates/tools/src/exec.rs:427):

```
"description": "The shell command to execute"
```

That is not true when the target is a paired node (not an SSH target). The gateway splits the string with `shell_words::split` (crates/gateway/src/node_exec.rs:68-74) and sends it as a `system.exec.v1` request with a program and arguments (`SystemExecRequest{program,args}`, crates/gateway/src/node_exec.rs:128-143). No shell is involved. The node also only runs programs on its allowlist (`resolve_allowed_program`, crates/node-host/src/runner.rs:600-628). Pipes, `&&`, `;`, redirects, globs and `$VAR` are therefore not interpreted. SSH targets still go through ssh and do get shell semantics (crates/gateway/src/node_exec.rs:217-274), so the two kinds of target behave differently.

The tool description (crates/tools/src/exec.rs:414-419) only says it runs a "structured process command on a remote node". It never says that shell syntax won't work.

Because of this, the model sends normal shell commands to a paired node, for example `cd repo && git status | head`. `cd` becomes the program. Since it is a shell builtin, it either does not resolve or is rejected with "program '...' is not allowed by this node". Even when the program is allowed, `&&` and `|` are passed as literal arguments. Every attempt is a wasted tool call, and the model can keep trying other shell variants without knowing why they fail.

### Expected behavior

The `command` description should say that paired-node execution is not done through a shell and that the program has to be on the node's allowlist. For example:

```
"description": "The shell command to execute. On a paired remote node (not SSH), it is not run through a shell: it is split into a program and arguments (shell-style quoting only), so pipes, redirects, `&&`, `;`, globs and variable expansion do not work, and the program must be allowed by that node."
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pair a remote node (not an SSH target) with the gateway.
2. In a chat session, ask the agent to run something on that node that it will likely write with shell syntax, for example checking git status in a subdirectory.
3. The agent calls exec with a command like `cd repo && git status | head`.
4. The command is split into program `cd` plus literal arguments `repo`, `&&`, `git`, ... and fails, either because the program can't be resolved or with "program '...' is not allowed by this node".

### Is this a regression?

I don't know

### Moltis version

8a12400dc1

### Component

Agent / LLM providers

### Install method

Built from source

### Operating system

Other

### Additional context

This doesn't depend on the OS. The issue is the text the model reads in crates/tools/src/exec.rs:425-428 and the paired-node exec path in crates/gateway/src/node_exec.rs. An empty command after splitting fails with "node command must not be empty" (crates/gateway/src/node_exec.rs:68-74).

prs.title: agents: add tools.agent_max_cost_usd per-run USD cap
prs.body:
## Problem

`tools.agent_max_iterations` (resolved in `crates/agents/src/runner/retry.rs`, `resolve_agent_max_iterations`) bounds how many provider calls an agent run makes, not what those calls cost. 25 iterations against a long context on a frontier model can cost far more than 25 against a small one. There is no dollar cap anywhere under `crates/` today, even though every provider response already carries a `Usage` with fresh input, cache reads, cache writes and output split out.

## Change

Adds an optional `tools.agent_max_cost_usd` (unset by default, so behavior is unchanged unless you set it):

- `RunCostGate` in `crates/agents/src/runner/helpers.rs` prices each request's reported `Usage` on the run's model and books it.
- Both `run_agent_loop_with_context_and_limits` (non-streaming) and `run_agent_loop_streaming_with_limits` (streaming) check the gate before each provider call, next to the existing `max_iterations` check, and record usage right after `usage_accumulator.record_request`.
- Once the cap is spent the next provider call is refused with `agent run exceeded cost budget (spent $X of $Y)`.
- It fails closed: if a cap is set and the model has no known price, the run is refused up front instead of running with a cap that books $0 for every call.
- `Usage.input_tokens` is documented as fresh input excluding cache reads and writes, so the four buckets map straight onto fresh input, cache read, cache write and output pricing. Cache reads are not billed at the full input rate.
- Config plumbing: schema field, `schema_map` entry, commented template line, and a semantic validation error when the value is not a positive finite number.

Example:

```toml
[tools]
agent_max_cost_usd = 2.0
```

## Why a dependency instead of a hand-rolled price table

Pricing needs a per-model table that covers cache read and cache write rates and stays current. `llm-budget` provides that plus the spend accounting. It is added with `default-features = false`, so it brings no async runtime. Cargo.lock gains 19 lines: `llm-budget 0.10.0` and `llm-prices 1.8.0` (a dated price table). Its other dependencies (serde, serde_json, thiserror 2) are already in the tree.

Disclosure: I'm Matthew Busel, and I maintain llm-budget. If you'd rather not take the dependency, all pricing goes through `RunCostGate::record`, so it can be swapped for an in-tree table without touching the loops.

## Known limitation

The gate prices usage on `provider.id()`. With a `ProviderChain` that falls back to a different model mid-run, usage is still priced at the primary model's rates. Happy to price per response model instead if you'd prefer that.

## Tests

`crates/agents/src/runner/tests/cost_gate.rs`:

- `no_cap_means_no_gate`: unset cap creates no gate, even for a model with no price.
- `gate_refuses_next_call_once_cap_is_spent`: gpt-4o with a $0.05 cap; one request of 10k input + 1k output books exactly $0.035 and the next call is allowed; a second identical request crosses the cap and the next call is refused, although the iteration cap would allow it.
- `cache_tokens_are_priced_separately_from_fresh_input`: 1M cache-read tokens cost more than $0 and less than the $2.50 full input rate.
- `unpriced_model_is_refused_instead_of_running_uncapped`
- `non_positive_cap_is_rejected`: 0 and NaN are rejected.

`cargo test -p moltis-agents cost_gate`

issues.title: [Bug]: config docs list only GET/PUT/DELETE /envs, so the QA/guidance agent suggests a PUT that deletes all other env vars
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

Commit 8598e47e63

## Description

The environment variables section of the config docs gives the API in one line:

website/public/docs/config.en.md:825
```
- **API** — `GET/PUT/DELETE /envs`
```

The router does more than this, and PUT and DELETE work differently from what a reader would guess:

- src/qwenpaw/app/routers/envs.py:114-131: `PUT /envs` replaces the whole stored set. Any key left out of the body is removed.
- The router also has `PATCH /envs`, which merges and keeps keys that are not in the body. The docs do not mention it.
- src/qwenpaw/app/routers/envs.py:80: `GET /envs/catalog` exists and is not documented.
- src/qwenpaw/app/routers/envs.py:134-154: `DELETE /envs/{key}` on a known setting returns 400 "Known variable must be reset". Known settings have to go through `POST /envs/{key}/reset`, which is not documented either.

The model reads this text. The QA agent (src/qwenpaw/agents/md_files/qa/en/AGENTS.md:23) and the guidance skill (src/qwenpaw/agents/skills/guidance-en/SKILL.md:71) both point it to these docs to answer configuration questions. When a user asks how to add a single variable over the API, the docs leave the agent only `PUT /envs`, so it suggests a PUT with just the new key. That deletes every other stored variable. When asked how to remove a known setting such as `QWENPAW_LLM_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, it suggests `DELETE /envs/QWENPAW_LLM_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, and that returns 400.

Suggested text for config.en.md:825:
```
- **API** — `GET /envs` lists stored variables; `PATCH /envs` merges and keeps omitted keys; `PUT /envs` replaces all stored variables (omitted keys are removed); `DELETE /envs/{key}` removes a custom variable; `POST /envs/{key}/reset` restores a known setting to its inherited/default value; `GET /envs/catalog` lists known settings with their effective value, source and editability.
```

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [x] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [x] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** commit 8598e47e63
- **OS:** not specific
- **Install method:** not specific
- **Python version (if applicable):** not specific

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Store two or more environment variables.
2. Ask the QA agent (or use the guidance skill) how to add one more environment variable through the API.
3. Follow its answer, which is `PUT /envs` with only the new key, then call `GET /envs`.
4. Ask how to remove a known setting such as `QWENPAW_LLM_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, then follow the suggested `DELETE /envs/QWENPAW_LLM_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT`.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** After step 3, only the new variable is left and the other stored variables are gone. Step 4 returns 400 "Known variable must be reset".
- **Expected:** The docs describe PATCH for merging, say that PUT replaces everything, and point to `POST /envs/{key}/reset` for known settings, so the agent suggests calls that work and keep existing variables.

## Logs / Screenshots

No logs. The relevant code is at src/qwenpaw/app/routers/envs.py:80, 114-131 and 134-154.

## Additional Notes

If the other language versions of config.md have the same API line, they need the same fix.

issues.body:
## Summary Markdown tables inside assistant messages are wider than the message bubble, are painted past the edge of the message list, and cannot be scrolled horizontally. The overflowing columns are effectively invisible, although the text can be selected. ## Environment - QwenPaw 2.3.0.post1, QwenPaw Desktop (Tauri webview) - Windows 10 Home 22H2 (build 19045), WebView2 / Chromium 126 - Viewport 1366 x 705 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Ask the agent for a response containing a markdown table with a few wide columns (a two-column table with a long first column is enough). 2. Look at the table in the rendered message. ## Expected The table either fits the bubble, or is horizontally scrollable inside it. ## Actual The table extends beyond the bubble and beyond the right edge of the message list. There is no horizontal scrollbar, and the columns that fall outside are not readable (but remain selectable/copyable). ## Measurements From the live DOM for one such table: | Element | Value | | --- | --- | | `` width | 1007 px | | `.qwenpaw-bubble-content-wrapper` width | 898 px (overflow 109 px) | | list right edge | 1299 px | | table right edge | **1377 px** | | list `clientWidth` / `scrollWidth` | 930 / 930 (no horizontal scroll available) | Ancestor chain of the table: ``` table .x-markdown.qwenpaw-markdown overflow-x: visible .HostBubbles-module__quoteResponse__ overflow-x: visible .qwenpaw-bubble-content-wrapper overflow-x: visible, 898 px wide .qwenpaw-bubble.qwenpaw-bubble-start overflow-x: visible .qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll overflow-x: auto, scrollWidth == clientWidth .qwenpaw-bubble-list-wrapper overflow-x: hidden ``` ## Root cause The Console stylesheet applies the overflow rule directly to the table: ```css [class*=bubble-assistant] .x-markdown table { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; } ``` `overflow-x: auto` has no effect on a `

## Suggested fix

Wrap rendered tables in a block-level scroll container, for example in the markdown component:

```jsx
…
``` ```css .qwenpaw-table-scroll { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; } ``` The same treatment is worth applying to wide standalone images and to `
` wrappers for consistency.

issues.title: Console: message list is not keyboard-focusable, so arrow/PageUp/PageDown never scroll the conversation
issues.body:
## Summary

In the Console chat view, the conversation cannot be scrolled with the keyboard. Arrow keys, PageUp/PageDown and Home/End do nothing, because the scroll container is not focusable and clicking inside a message never moves focus to it.

This makes the chat unusable on machines without a mouse wheel (laptops using a TrackPoint or keyboard-only navigation), where wheel events are not available as a fallback.

## Environment

- QwenPaw 2.3.0.post1, QwenPaw Desktop (Tauri webview)
- Windows 10 Home 22H2 (build 19045)
- WebView2 / Chromium 126, viewport 1366 x 705, devicePixelRatio 1
- Conversation with long history (scroll range ~6900-8000 px)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a conversation long enough to scroll.
2. Click inside the message text.
3. Press ArrowUp, ArrowDown, PageUp or PageDown.

## Expected

The conversation scrolls, or at minimum the list takes focus and then scrolls.

## Actual

Nothing scrolls. `document.activeElement` remains the composer input, so the keys are consumed by the chat input instead of the list.

## Root cause (measured)

The scrolling element is `.qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll` (the wrapper that Ant Design X's `Bubble.List` renders with `overflow:auto`, `flex-direction:column-reverse`, and a scrollTop range of `[-range, 0]`). It reports:

```
tabIndex: -1
```

so it can never receive focus, and clicking a message does not focus it.

Direct evidence from the running app, same conversation:

| Action | scrollTop |
| --- | --- |
| seed | -1500 |
| PageDown, list not focused | -1500 (no change) |
| set `tabIndex = 0` and `focus()` | -1500 |
| PageDown, focused | **-1059** (441 px page) |
| ArrowUp, focused | **-1099** (40 px line) |
| ArrowDown, focused | -1059 |

With focus the native keyboard scrolling works correctly, including the inverted (negative scrollTop) list. So the scroll maths are fine; only focusability is missing.

Wheel scrolling in the same build is unaffected: synthetic `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` wheel and a real `SendInput` `MOUSEEVENTF_WHEEL` both scroll the list normally.

## Suggested fix

Give the scroll container a tab stop and keep keyboard scrolling working:

```jsx
<div className="qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll ..." tabIndex={0}>
```

plus a `:focus-visible` outline so the focus is visible, and optionally a `keydown` handler on the message area (Arrow/PageUp/PageDown/Home/End) so the keys work even when focus is on the page body.

Related but separate: the scrollbar's page area works (a track click jumps 441 px), and the round chevron at the bottom-right of the list is `qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll-to-bottom`, not a scrollbar arrow, which is easy to mistake for one.

issues.title: WeChat channel: silent inbound polling death - error-ret loop has no logging or recovery, cursor never resets
issues.body:
**Environment**
- QwenPaw 2.3.0 (Desktop, Windows 10), official `qwenpaw_channel_wechat` plugin (`platform.py`).

**Symptom**
- Inbound WeChat messages silently stop arriving. The channel worker process stays alive, channel health reports healthy, and there are zero errors in the log. Outbound (e.g. cron sends) still works.
- The only effective recovery is rebuilding the worker (agent hot reload) with the same token — no QR re-scan needed. This proves the failure is in the worker's runtime polling state, not credentials/model/send path.

**Occurrences (local time, Asia/Shanghai)**
- 2026-11-14 13:14 -> 2026-11-15 18:43 (~29h silent window)
- 2026-11-15 20:24 -> 2026-11-16 00:56 (~4.5h silent window)
- Similar silent receive deaths also observed 2026-10-25/10-26.
- In each window: no inbound rows in history DB, no `consume` log lines, no worker stderr at all.

**Code analysis (`platform.py::_poll`)**
```python
data = await self._poll_client.getupdates(cursor)
...
if data.get("ret", -1) not in (0, -1) and not messages:
    await asyncio.sleep(3)
```
- When `getupdates` returns a non-zero `ret` (other than -1) with empty `msgs`, the loop just sleeps 3s and retries forever with the same cursor: no logging, no failure counter, no recovery.
- The exception path logs and backs off, but the error-ret path is completely silent — matching the observed zero-log dead windows.
- `cursor` is only updated from `get_updates_buf` and never reset; a stale cursor / half-dead long connection / server-side subscription lapse cannot be distinguished because `ret` is never logged.

**Related but different:** #4697 (poll thread crash during zero-downtime reload, v1.1.7, closed inactive). This report involves no reload, no exception and zero logs on current 2.3.0.

**Suggested fix**
1. Log abnormal `ret` codes (throttled, numeric only).
2. Track last successful poll; after sustained abnormal ret (e.g. 10 minutes), rebuild the poll client and reset the cursor.
3. Optionally refresh the poll client after a long inbound silence (e.g. 6h) to cover the "ret ok but empty forever" mode.
4. Expose polling freshness in channel health so external monitoring can detect silent death.

**Local mitigation**
A minimal patch implementing 1-3 has been applied locally and is under observation. Diff below; happy to turn it into a PR if useful.

```diff
--- original
+++ patched
@@ -170,2 +170,11 @@
         cursor, failures = "", 0
+        # Local poll-resilience patch (2026-11-16):
+        # log abnormal ret codes (numeric only, throttled) and rebuild the
+        # poll client when polling stays unhealthy, instead of looping
+        # silently forever on a stale cursor/connection.
+        last_ok = time.monotonic()
+        last_msg = time.monotonic()
+        last_rebuild = 0.0
+        last_ret_log = 0.0
+        logged_ret = None
         while not self._stopping:
@@ -174,2 +183,9 @@
                 failures = 0
+                ret = data.get("ret", -1)
+                now = time.monotonic()
+                if ret in (0, -1):
+                    last_ok = now
+                elif ret != logged_ret or now - last_ret_log >= 300:
+                    logger.warning("WeChat poll abnormal ret=%s", ret)
+                    logged_ret, last_ret_log = ret, now
                 if data.get("get_updates_buf") is not None:
@@ -177,2 +193,4 @@
                 messages = data.get("msgs") or []
+                if messages:
+                    last_msg = now
                 for message in messages:
@@ -184,3 +202,19 @@
                         logger.warning("WeChat inbound message failed")
-                if data.get("ret", -1) not in (0, -1) and not messages:
+                reason = ""
+                if now - last_ok > 600:
+                    reason = "abnormal_ret_10min"
+                elif now - last_msg > 21600 and now - last_rebuild > 21600:
+                    reason = "no_inbound_6h"
+                if reason and now - last_rebuild > 60:
+                    logger.warning(
+                        "WeChat poll recovery: rebuild client reason=%s",
+                        reason,
+                    )
+                    await self._rebuild_poll_client()
+                    cursor = ""
+                    last_ok = last_msg = time.monotonic()
+                    last_rebuild = time.monotonic()
+                    logged_ret = None
+                    continue
+                if ret not in (0, -1) and not messages:
                     await asyncio.sleep(3)
@@ -192,2 +226,14 @@
                 failures += 1
+
+    async def _rebuild_poll_client(self):
+        # Fresh HTTP client + cursor reset reproduces the empirically
+        # effective worker-rebuild recovery without touching login state.
+        old = self._poll_client
+        new = ILinkClient(old.bot_token, old.base_url)
+        await new.start()
+        self._poll_client = new
+        try:
+            await old.stop()
+        except Exception:
+            pass
 

```

issues.body:
## English summary

When an OpenAI-compatible gateway/relay fails mid-stream, the OpenAI SDK raises a **bare `openai.APIError`** (no `status_code`, no `response`) whose only status hint is plain text like:

```
status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)
```

`extract_status_code()` only recognizes the narrow `"Streaming response failed: [5xx]"` message format, so this error is classified as `unknown` by `classify_model_error()` → **neither same-model retry nor cross-model fallback fires**, and the whole turn/cron job dies. A genuine HTTP 502 from the same gateway WOULD be `transient` and fallback-eligible, so identical upstream failures behave inconsistently depending only on how the gateway wraps them.

Observed in production today: 3 scheduled agent jobs (07:30 / 08:00 / 09:30) all failed with no fallback, no message delivered. Reproduced against `classify_model_error` with the exact logged exceptions (see below).

Suggestion: extend `error_utils.extract_status_code()` to also recognize `status_code=5xx`-style patterns in gateway messages (keep it narrow, e.g. `\bstatus_code\s*=\s*([1-5]\d{2})\b`), or treat bare `openai.APIError` with a `5xx` in the message as transient. Related but distinct from #8092 (that one is about content-inspection text being misclassified as `bad_request`; this one is about status extraction missing a gateway message format).

## 环境 / Environment

- QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1（Docker `agentscope/qwenpaw:latest`），Debian 13 宿主机
- 模型走 OpenAI 兼容中转网关（relay），主模型 `deepseek-v4.1-flash`，已配置 `fallback_models`（zhipu-cn / glm-5.3-flash），`fallback_policy.enabled=true`

## 现象 / What happened

2026-10-30 早上三个 cron 任务（07:30 备份上云、08:00 早报、09:30 巡检）准点触发（日志有 `cron execute`），但全部失败，备用模型一次都没被尝试，飞书一条消息都没发出：

```
07:30:30 ERROR runtime: unhandled error ...: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'status_code=400, 请联系管理员处理！', 'type': 'upstream_error', 'code': 'bad_response_status_code'}}
08:00:12 ERROR runtime: unhandled error ...: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'status_code=400, 请联系管理员处理！', 'type': 'upstream_error', 'code': 'bad_response_status_code'}}
09:30:40 ERROR runtime: unhandled error ...: APIError('status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)')
```

## 复现 / Reproduction

用日志里的**原始异常形态**直接喂 `classify_model_error()`（QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1 自带实现）：

```python
import openai
from qwenpaw.providers.model_error_policy import classify_model_error

class FakeRequest: method='POST'; url='http://x/v1/chat/completions'; headers={}
class FakeResp:
    status_code = 400
    headers = {}
    request = FakeRequest()

# 形态 A：网关把上游故障包装成 HTTP 400 + type=upstream_error
e1 = openai.BadRequestError(
    message="Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'status_code=400, 请联系管理员处理！', 'type': 'upstream_error', 'code': 'bad_response_status_code'}}",
    response=FakeResp(), body=None)

# 形态 B：流中失败，SDK 抛裸 APIError，真实状态码只在消息文本里
e2 = openai.APIError(
    message='status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)',
    request=FakeRequest(), body=None)

print(classify_model_error(e1))  # kind=bad_request  retryable=False fallback_eligible=False
print(classify_model_error(e2))  # kind=unknown      retryable=False fallback_eligible=False
```

实测输出：

```
08:00  400 upstream_error: 分类=bad_request  可重试=False  会切备用=False
09:30  裸APIError 502: 分类=unknown  可重试=False  会切备用=False
```

## 期望 / Expected

- **形态 B（本 issue 核心）**：`status_code=502` 明明白白写在消息里，应被 `extract_status_code()` 提取出来并归类为 `transient` → 可重试、可切换备用模型。
- **形态 A（顺带讨论）**：`type=upstream_error` + `bad_response_status_code` 表明是网关上游故障而非请求本身问题，但被包装成 HTTP 400 后按现有设计判为 `bad_request`（不 fallback）。这个可以理解设计初衷（400 通常意味着请求有问题），但网关把 5xx 包装成 400 是常见行为，`upstream_error` 这个 type 是否值得加入 transient 判定，请作者权衡。

## 源码位置 / Source

- `qwenpaw/providers/model_error_policy.py`：`fallback_eligible = retryable or kind == "model_not_found"`，`unknown`/`bad_request` 均不在内
- `qwenpaw/providers/error_utils.py`：`_STREAMING_ERROR_STATUS_RE` 只匹配 `Streaming response failed: [5xx]` 这一种文本格式，注释里也写明"keep this fallback deliberately narrow"

同类参考：#8092（阿里网关审核文本被误分类为 bad_request，同属"网关非标准错误形态导致分类失真"家族）、#8124（已修：审核错误路由到 fallback）。

谢谢！

issues.title: Memory tag index never rebuilds: /memory/tags returns 503 "Memory tag index is unavailable" (tags are generated but unreadable)
issues.body:
**Environment**
- QwenPaw Desktop UI: v2.3.0b2; backend package `qwenpaw` PKG-INFO: 2.4; `reme_ai` 0.4.2.0; Windows 10 (AMD64).
- Config: `running.reme_light_memory_config.auto_memory_generate_tags = true` (set through `PUT /api/agents/{id}`, read-back verified; on-disk `agent.json` diff = exactly 2 lines).

**Observed**
1. After enabling the switch, auto-memory saves DO generate tags. The log shows `[FrontmatterUpdateStep] path=memory/... keys=['memory_tags']` on 2/2 post-enable cycles, and the note frontmatter contains `memory_tags:` with values.
2. But both read endpoints fail permanently:
   - `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/tags?page=1` -> HTTP 503 `{"detail":"Memory tag index is unavailable"}`
   - `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/tag-files?tag=<t>&page=1` -> HTTP 503, same detail
   - The Console file panel "tags" tab therefore stays empty.
3. `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/status` -> 200; `runtime.auto_memory = {enabled: true, interval: 5}`; worker idle; embedding_store / file_graph / file_store / keyword_index components all present.

**Root-cause evidence (from qwenpaw.log)**
- Tag index rebuild fails on historical file paths that contain backslashes: the log carries 159 index entries whose `path` field contains a backslash, and rebuild attempts since 2026-10-28 error out on them.
- There are 18 successful `Rebuilt tag index: files=0, tags=0` lines, all dated 2026-10-28; zero successes afterwards. So the failure predates enabling the switch (the toggle is not the cause).

**Expected**
After enabling `auto_memory_generate_tags` and at least one successful auto-memory save, `/memory/tags` should return 200 with the generated tags; the Console "tags" tab should list them; `memory_search` should accept a `tags` filter.

**Actual**
503 always; tags exist only inside note frontmatter; no error is surfaced in the UI (silent 503).

**Repro**
1. `PUT /api/agents/{id}` with `running.reme_light_memory_config.auto_memory_generate_tags=true`.
2. Wait for an auto-memory save (interval 5 min) or trigger one; confirm the note frontmatter gains `memory_tags`.
3. `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/tags?page=1` -> 503.

**Impact**
The feature is half-working: write path OK, read path dead. Users see an enabled toggle and an empty tags tab with no explanation.

**Suggested fix**
- Normalize stored paths (backslash -> forward slash) during tag-index rebuild, or skip/quarantine malformed path entries instead of aborting the whole rebuild.
- Surface the rebuild failure in `/memory/status` (e.g. `tag_index: {healthy: false, last_error}`) and in the Console tab instead of a bare 503.

prs.title: fix(runtime): reject chats until background startup completes (#8746)
prs.body:
## Description

During background startup, a chat submitted before the runtime is fully initialized was accepted (HTTP 200), but the agent was built against a half-projected workspace (`tools=1` in the logs) and the run hung before its first LLM call — no error, no timeout, no log. The stall was process-wide: every subsequent chat (new sessions, different models, Console and Feishu) was swallowed the same way until the process restarted. Fixes #8746.

This PR fixes the issue in four layers, so the user-visible failure mode is gone regardless of which internal wait was poisoned:

1. **Runtime readiness gate** — new `qwenpaw.utils.runtime_readiness`, a lifespan-bound, process-wide gate. The existing `startup_ready` only covers core agents; this gate is published only after the *entire* background startup (plugins, workspace projection, provider sync, skill pool) completes. Failures wake all waiters with a concrete reason. CLI/embedded callers that never run the lifespan are unaffected (inert gate).
2. **HTTP admission** — `POST /console/chat` (new sends, not reconnects) and `POST /console/chat/task` wait up to 5s for readiness (`QWENPAW_RUNTIME_READY_HTTP_TIMEOUT`) and then return **503 + `Retry-After: 5`** instead of admitting into a half-initialized runtime. Reconnects still attach to an existing stream as before.
3. **Single entry-point gate** — `AgentBuilder.build()` awaits runtime readiness (`QWENPAW_RUNTIME_READY_TIMEOUT`, default 180s), covering Console, all channels, cron and sub-agents in one shared point.
4. **No more silent stalls**:
   - `MultiAgentManager.get_agent()` no longer returns a workspace in the window between publication and the plugin `workspace_created` hooks (the half-projected toolkit behind the `tools=1` build).
   - Pre-model watchdog (`QWENPAW_AGENT_PRE_MODEL_TIMEOUT`, default 180s): if a built agent produces no non-heartbeat event before its first model call, the run ends with a visible `AGENT_PRE_MODEL_STALL` error and a task-stack dump. Heartbeats deliberately do **not** disarm it (they prove the transport is alive, not that the model call started).
   - Rate-limiter registry hardening: the module-level `asyncio.Lock` (which could become a no-wait process-wide wait if its lazily-created loop went stale) is replaced by a thread lock, and each limiter is bound to its event loop — cross-loop reuse now raises an immediate `RuntimeError` instead of deadlocking, and closed-loop limiters are replaced.

`/healthz` now additionally reports `runtime_ready` and `runtime_startup_error`, so monitoring can distinguish "core agents loaded" from "background startup finished".

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8746

**Security Considerations:** The task-stack dump logs only `file:line` and coroutine names — no prompt content, message bodies or credentials. The readiness gate does not touch authentication/channel-trust logic. New environment-variable reads reject non-numeric and negative values and fall back to defaults.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [x] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks (nothing was auto-fixed; the tree was clean afterwards)
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed) (3 new environment variables documented in config.en.md / config.zh.md)
- [x] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [x] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes (`No channel changes detected.` — the backend admission change touches no channel implementation)
- [x] Official channel changes are covered in `tests/unit/channels/test_<channel>.py` (startup, shutdown and message delivery) (N/A — no channel-specific code changed)
- [x] Shared host/process changes are covered in `test_channel_host.py` / `tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_process.py` (N/A — host/process internals untouched)
- [x] Console changes retain the built-in contract checks in `tests/contract/channels/` (`19 passed` — the Console chat SSE contract is unchanged)

## Testing

Four new unit test modules (23 tests) cover each layer:

- `tests/unit/app/test_runtime_readiness.py` — gate no-op (unbound), immediate ready, timeout reason, failure wakes waiters, late failure does not unset readiness, budget env override / invalid fallback, cross-loop wait raises, HTTP 503 mapping (status, `Retry-After` header, detail), `AgentBuilder` checks the gate first, live endpoint returns 503 before admission via `TestClient`.
- `tests/unit/app/test_multi_agent_publish_race.py` — fast path waits for provisioning; bounded timeout becomes `ConfigurationException`; startup owner does not deadlock on its own workspace; post-wait startup failure is visible.
- `tests/unit/providers/test_rate_limiter_loop_isolation.py` — cross-loop use raises instead of hanging; closed-loop limiter is replaced; same-loop reuse; `bind_loop` rejects a foreign loop.
- `tests/unit/runtime/test_pre_model_watchdog.py` — a stalling executor ends the run with a terminal failed response carrying `AGENT_PRE_MODEL_STALL`; a heartbeat-only stream does **not** disarm the watchdog.

Manual verification (repro script for reviewers):

```bash
qwenpaw serve &
sleep 2 && curl -i -X POST localhost:14711/api/console/chat \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"session_id":"s1","input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"hi"}]}]}'
# Before "Background startup completed": expect HTTP/1.1 503 + Retry-After: 5
# with detail containing "Runtime is not ready".
# After startup completes: 200 + normal SSE stream.
```

## Evidence

`pre-commit run --all-files` (the `actionlint` hook's tool installer is blocked by this sandbox's network, so it ran as `SKIP=actionlint pre-commit run --all-files`; every applicable hook passed, nothing was auto-fixed, and the tree stayed clean. This PR touches no GitHub Actions workflow files):

mypy......................................................................Passed
black.....................................................................Passed
flake8....................................................................Passed

```

Targeted test suites (venv, Python 3.11.6):

```bash
pytest tests/unit/app/test_runtime_readiness.py tests/unit/app/test_multi_agent_publish_race.py \
       tests/unit/providers/test_rate_limiter_loop_isolation.py tests/unit/runtime/test_pre_model_watchdog.py \
       tests/unit/app/routers/test_console_chat_task.py tests/unit/app/routers/test_console_chat_reconnect.py \
       tests/unit/app/routers/test_healthz.py -q
36 passed in 9.12s

pytest tests/unit/runtime tests/unit/providers -q
1658 passed, 2 warnings in 111.53s   # 2 warnings: pre-existing claude-sonnet-4-5 deprecation notices

pytest tests/contract/channels -q
19 passed in 1.07s

pytest tests/unit/app -q
2903 passed, 18 skipped, 3 deselected in 135.19s
# deselected = 3 failures proven PRE-EXISTING on a clean checkout (git stash -> same 3 fail -> stash pop):
#   - 2x test_config_router: src/qwenpaw/official_channels/index.json is a build artifact absent from this checkout
#   - 1x test_access_control: order-sensitive, passes when run in isolation
```

## Additional Notes

- Deliberate behavior choice worth highlighting: **channels/cron/sub-agents wait up to 180s for readiness instead of failing fast** (messages may be delayed but must not be lost), while the HTTP chat entry point fails fast with a 503 after 5s (holding a browser connection open through a 90s+ cold start is worse). Both budgets are configurable.
- `QWENPAW_AGENT_PRE_MODEL_TIMEOUT` defaults to 180s to match the channel-side wait budget, so a run waiting out startup is not misreported as stalled.
- The readiness gate lives in a standalone module rather than as an `app.state` field so non-HTTP entry points (channels, cron, sub-agents) can consult it without importing the FastAPI application.
- Follow-up work intentionally left out of this PR: a TaskTracker adaptive watchdog for already-stuck runs, and phase-level instrumentation for the 92s background startup itself.

prs.title: fix(approvals): deliver approval prompts to the chat channel that raised them
prs.body:
## Description

Approvals raised from a chat turn never reached that chat. The console showed its dialog, WeChat showed nothing, and after five minutes the request resolved to `TIMEOUT` while the tool silently did not run.

Reported before as #6695 and root-caused in #6819. `ApprovalService` only pushes a notification when the pending record carries a channel instance:

```python
if channel and channel != "console" and (
    (extra or {}).get("_channel_instance") or _is_spawn_child_approval(pending)
):
    asyncio.create_task(self._notify_channel(pending, channel_body))
```

`request.channel_instance` was attached in exactly one place — `BaseChannel._stream_with_tracker`, the console/SSE path. Chat channels run their turns through `BaseChannel._run_process_loop`, where it stayed `None`. #6833 fixed the *propagation* through `driver_gate`, but the value it copies was still empty, so the notification could never fire for a chat channel.

### Changes

1. **`_run_process_loop` attaches `request.channel_instance`**, mirroring the console path. This is the line that makes chat approvals reachable at all.
2. **Actionable bodies.** `format_approval_actions()` renders copy-paste commands with the short request id, and driver-policy approvals get the same header/actions block as ToolGuard ones instead of a bare `"Tool 'x' requires approval for call."` sentence.
3. **`no_merge` for approval notices.** `send_approval_notification()` marks its message `no_merge`; WeChat merges text for 30 s by default (`message_merge_enabled`, `message_merge_delay_ms=30000`), so prompts could flush after the approval had already expired.
4. **Expiry is reported.** `wait_for_approval()` pushes an `approval_timeout` notice when the window closes, so the user is told nothing ran instead of being left guessing.

### Behaviour notes

- Console is unchanged: `channel == "console"` still skips push notifications.
- Spawned-child routing keeps its existing channel-manager path.
- `message_type` is keyword-only with the previous default; existing channel subclasses inherit the base implementation unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduction: WeChat session, `Bash` approval. `qwenpaw.log` shows `Approval pending created ... session=wechat:o`, then `decision=timeout` twice (09:53:33 `driver:mcp:blender`, 09:59:20 `Bash`), while every successful approval came from `routers/approval.py` (the console API). `Control command` never appears — nothing ever reached the chat.
- With the fix the same pending carries `_channel_instance`, `_notify_channel()` runs, and the body includes `/approval approve <short id>`.
- `pytest tests/unit/app/approvals tests/unit/channels/test_wechat.py tests/unit/security/tool_guard` → 689 passed, 10 skipped.
- `pytest tests/unit` → 17101 passed, 163 skipped, 45 failed. The failures are pre-existing on this Windows host: 51 of the same files fail on a clean `origin/main` worktree (portability fingerprints, cli lifespan, docker provisioner, openai response provider, offloader retention).
- `black --line-length=79`, `flake8`, `mypy`, and `pylint` (10.00/10) are clean on the changed files.

## Related

- #6695 — same symptom, closed.
- #6819 — root-caused the missing notification.
- #6833 — propagated the routing fields, but not their source.
- #6728 / #6804 (unmerged) — Chinese approve/deny replies in WeChat; out of scope here.

## Not in this PR (design notes)

Ideas for follow-ups, deliberately not implemented here:

1. **Channel approval protocol.** Let `BaseChannel` own `send_approval_notification()` + `resolve_approval(action, request_id)`, with a default text implementation (numbered choices) that card channels (Feishu / QQ / Telegram / WeCom) override. WeChat would then only need short-reply parsing (`1/2`, `A/D`, 同意/拒绝 → `/approval …`), which is what #6728 / #6804 were aiming at.
2. **Non-blocking approvals.** `wait_for_approval()` currently parks the tool call — and the turn — for the whole timeout. Moving the wait to a background task and resuming on the decision would keep long chats responsive, but it changes the waiting model in `tool_adapter` / `driver_gate`, so it deserves its own discussion.
3. **Per-channel approval settings.** `approval: {enabled, timeout, default: deny|approve, notify_merge: false}`, so a WeChat-only deployment can decide how long to wait without a process-wide environment variable.

prs.title: feat(console): support runtime base-path deployment
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8714.

Related context only: #1853, #8177, and #8316. This PR does not reopen, comment on, or close those older issues or pull requests.

Add an optional `QWENPAW_BASE_PATH` runtime setting for serving the standard prebuilt Console and API below a reverse-proxy prefix such as `/app/qwenpaw/web`.

#8316 covers custom builds through `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME`. This PR covers the complementary runtime case: pip/uv/Docker users should not need to rebuild the Console or have a proxy rewrite minified JavaScript. Uvicorn `root_path` alone cannot solve the absolute URLs already present in that prebuilt output.

### What changed

- Add a validated base-path ASGI middleware using standard `root_path` semantics for HTTP, mounted static files, and WebSockets. The bare prefix redirects to a trailing slash; requests outside the prefix return 404.
- Inject only two explicit deployment values into `index.html`: its `<base href>` and a JSON-encoded runtime prefix. JavaScript and CSS response bodies are not rewritten.
- Build default Console entry and module URLs relative to the document base; resolve public assets, API calls, router/login navigation, and chunk-readiness probes against the same runtime prefix.
- Preserve the existing root and `/console` behavior when the setting is empty or `/`. Existing build-time `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME` and desktop behavior remain separate.
- Document runtime proxy configuration in English and Chinese. Proxies must preserve rather than strip the configured prefix.

The current login flow uses a Bearer token in `localStorage`, so no authentication-cookie path change is needed.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

### Components affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Console
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests

## Evidence

Backend regression coverage includes prefix boundaries, `root_path`-aware URL generation, HTTP and WebSocket mounting, HTML token replacement, byte-identical static assets, SPA deep links, static containment, response compression, authentication, agent routing, and voice routing:

```text
176 passed in 17.96s
5 passed in 0.22s (voice)
```

Console tests:

```text
Test Files  676 passed + 2 initially uncollected suites
Tests       8766 passed | 2 expected fail | 7 skipped

The two suites were rerun after adding the intentionally sparse-cloned plugins/harness sources:
Test Files  2 passed
Tests       28 passed
```

Build and formatting:

```text
npm run build
Initial bundle: 10.00 MiB raw, 2.58 MiB Brotli across 11 assets.

npm run format:check
All matched files use Prettier code style!
```

Real Chromium verification applied the review patch to a clean worktree, rebuilt it, and used isolated QwenPaw processes, temporary working directories, and a dedicated test account:

- Opened `/app/qwenpaw/web/login`, loaded the prefixed logo, and logged in through the real form.
- Opened Chat, then `/app/qwenpaw/web/settings/models`, and refreshed the deep link.
- Observed 463 same-origin responses and 306 JavaScript module responses.
- No URLs escaped the configured prefix; no asset request failures, request failures, or page errors occurred.
- The entry JavaScript response was byte-identical to the built file (1,041,361 bytes).
- A second control run with an empty base path logged in and refreshed `/settings/models` successfully with 463 same-origin responses and 306 JavaScript module responses.
- `vite preview` served the default root HTML without unresolved deployment placeholders and returned the entry JavaScript with HTTP 200.
- Both runs returned the same pre-existing standalone `DELETE /api/hub/pawapps/sessions` 405 during session cleanup; it is unrelated to this path change and was not hidden from the captured reports.

### Checklist

- [x] Relevant backend and Console tests pass.
- [x] Console production build and formatting pass.

prs.title: fix(console): stop the web_search config modal from saving untouched values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening `/tools` → `搜索网页 [配置]` wrote the configuration back to the server even though the user had touched nothing (#8836). The values it had just loaded from the API were indistinguishable from an edit, so the debounced auto-save fired once on open.

That write is not harmless: `handleSaveConfig` runs `saveToolConfig()` and then `loadTools()`, which refreshes the whole tool list. The list re-render can re-enter the same modal, load the same values, and save again — the reported "page keeps refreshing".

The same modal is the shared path for any tool whose config carries a password field, which is why the report names password components specifically.

## Evidence

Before — the user does nothing but open the modal (repro test, `onSave` is the spy):

```
[8836] fetches after open=1 afterWait=1 saves=1
```

`saves=1`: one write, zero user input.

After:

```
[8836] fetches after open=1 afterWait=1 saves=0
```

`fetches` staying at 1 also shows the fix does not add a request per open.

## Scope

Type: A (single-component fix)

- Compares the form against the values the server handed over and skips the write when they match. Both sides go through the same fingerprint, so `undefined` and `null` collapse: the backend reads an empty `api_key` as "delete the stored key", so a stray null must not look like a change.
- The snapshot is taken on the initial load only. Switching the provider is a genuine user edit, so the form must still differ from the open snapshot and get written — refreshing the snapshot there would silently drop the provider switch (the first draft of this patch did exactly that and the existing test caught it).

## Self-review

1. **User edits a field** → fingerprint differs → saved as before.
2. **User switches provider** → snapshot untouched → saved, and the provider-slot isolation tests still pass.
3. **Config arrives without a provider** → `anysearch` default is part of the snapshot, so opening still writes nothing.
4. **Config fetch fails** → snapshot stays `null`; the comparison is skipped and the existing retry/error path is unchanged.

## Test scope

- Target: `console/src/pages/Agent/Tools/WebSearchConfigModal.test.tsx` + `WebSearchConfigModal.autoSave.test.tsx` — 16 passed
- Neighbour: `console/src/pages/Agent/Tools` — 46 passed (7 files)
- Falsify: with the guard removed, both cases in `WebSearchConfigModal.autoSave.test.tsx` fail with `expected 1 to be +0` (`onSave` called once)
- `prettier --check` and `eslint` clean on both files

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep llama-server from outliving a crashed backend
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`llama-server.exe` survives QwenPaw dying (#8830). The plugin launches it with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and nothing else — no new process group, no job — so when the backend crashes or is force-killed, nothing tells the server to stop. The reporter's table shows four successive starts each leaving a healthy server behind on its own random port; the fifth start then finds no RAM commit left, the child dies inside `load_model`, and all the user sees is `llama.cpp server exited before becoming ready`.

`stop_server` covers the orderly path (SIGTERM, then kill, bounded). It never runs on a crash, and the reporter notes the `atexit` path does not run either. The same hole exists on POSIX: `start_new_session` puts the server in its own group, but the group signal is also sent by `stop_server`, which a `SIGKILL` of the provider skips.

**Fix: bind the server's lifetime to the provider, at the kernel level, on both platforms.**

- **Windows** — a job with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`. When the provider's last job handle goes away, on any exit path including `TerminateProcess`, the kernel terminates every member.
- **Linux** — `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` set in a `preexec_fn` that runs between fork and exec. `SIGKILL` of the parent makes the kernel deliver `SIGKILL` to the child.

No exit handler has to run in either case, which is the point: crash-path coverage by construction, not by cleanup code a crash skips.

macOS has no equivalent knob, so it keeps the existing behaviour (`start_new_session` + group signal on an orderly stop).

## Evidence

**Windows** — same `process_options()` arguments the plugin uses, then `taskkill /F /PID <parent>` without `/T`, exactly as a crash leaves it:

```
parent pid=10460 child pid=1448
child alive after parent was killed: True      <- orphan reproduced
```

with a kill-on-close job:

```
parent pid=10308 child pid=12188
child alive after parent was killed: False     <- fix verified
```

**Linux** — real kernel, Ubuntu 24.04 / kernel 6.8.0-138 / Python 3.12.3, run against the patched `io_helpers.py` (not a stand-in):

```
process_options keys: ['preexec_fn', 'start_new_session']
--- control (no hook) ---           child_alive_after_parent_sigkill=True
--- patched process_options() ---   child_alive_after_parent_sigkill=False
VERDICT: FIX HOLDS
```

**On the documented `preexec_fn` risk.** The Python docs warn that it is not safe with threads, because the child can deadlock before exec. That is a probability, not a certainty, so it was measured rather than assumed:

| shape | worst case | stalls |
|---|---|---|
| 8 / 32 / 96 hog threads, 400–800 forks each | 0.016s / 0.061s / 0.126s | 0 |
| 16 / 48 / 96 threads forking simultaneously, 30–40 rounds | ≤ 0.029s | 0 frozen |
| bare `os.fork()` without exec, 32 / 128 / 256 threads | ≤ 0.014s | 0 stuck |
| 64 threads, 180s soak | 0.015s over 38,244 forks | 0 |

About 150,000 fork/exec cycles in total: **the deadlock never reproduced**. It is not eliminated on principle — the window the docs describe is "another thread held a C-level lock at fork time", and only libraries that fail to register an `atfork` handler keep that window open. This hook calls `libc.so.6` and nothing else, which is why it held up.

The measurement also changed the implementation: with the lookup `LIBC.prctl(...)` inside the child, the 96-thread worst case was **0.126s** — 15× the control — against **0.016s** once the function pointer is taken in the parent. The code resolves `_PRCTL` at import and the child does exactly one call.

## Scope

Type: B (process lifecycle / failure handling)

- **This stops new orphans; it does not reclaim existing ones.** Servers left over from earlier crashes keep running — they need a restart or a manual kill. Reclaiming them means deciding which `llama-server.exe` on the machine is ours; separate change.
- **Adopting an already-running server** instead of spawning a fresh one is the other half of what the report describes. It needs a persisted port/pid contract and a handshake; out of scope.
- macOS: no `PDEATHSIG`, so nothing changes there.

## Self-review

1. **Job creation fails / prctl unavailable** — logged, server still starts, only the protection is missing. No start path throws.
2. **Repeated launches** — one job per backend, later servers join it; `assign` on the same process is idempotent.
3. **Two launches at once** — `assign` runs synchronously after the `to_thread(Popen)` await, on the event-loop thread, so two coroutines cannot both see an empty handle; `_server_transitioning` already serialises server switches.
4. **Test doubles without `_handle`** — skipped with a debug log instead of raising, so the existing fake-`Popen` tests keep working.
5. **Parent already dead before `prctl` runs** — the child checks `getppid() == 1` and leaves immediately, since `PDEATHSIG` would never fire.

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/plugins/local_model/unit/test_llamacpp_backend.py` — 100 passed, 2 skipped (the two Linux-only cases skip on Windows)
- Neighbour: `tests/plugins/local_model/unit` — 263 passed
- Wider: `tests/plugins` — 303 passed, 1 failed, 25 errors
  - The single failure (`test_provider.py::test_existing_provider_settings_and_path_survive_unload`) fails identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout, so it predates this change.
  - The 25 errors are `integration/` refusing to run without `pip install -r plugins/provider/local-llamacpp/requirements.txt`; environment, not code.
- Linux cases were additionally run on a real Ubuntu 24.04 host against the patched module (transcript above), not only through CI.
- Falsify: replacing `self._server_job.assign(process)` with `pass` → `test_setup_server_binds_the_process_to_its_job` fails
- `pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files: mypy, black, flake8, pylint all pass

prs.title: fix(sandbox): probe Landlock without requiring securityfs
prs.body:
## Description

`_probe_linux_landlock()` 在无法读取 `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` 时直接返回
`supported=False`。容器不挂载 securityfs，该文件因此通常不存在——即便宿主内核的
Landlock LSM 完全可用。

后果不只是能力报告错误。当 `security.sandbox_enabled=true` 时，
`ResourceGovernor.execution_sandbox_config()` 走 fail-closed，于是每次 Code Mode
的 `run_code` 都以如下错误失败：

```
Script failed: Sandbox is enabled but unavailable
```

在官方 `agentscope/qwenpaw:latest` 镜像（2.3.0）、WSL2 宿主内核 6.18 上复现，
此时内核通过 `landlock_create_ruleset` 系统调用报告 Landlock ABI v7：

| 步骤 | 容器内结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 第 1 步 — 内核 >= 5.13 | 通过（6.18） |
| 第 2 步 — 读取 `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` | `FileNotFoundError`，securityfs 未挂载 |
| 探测结论 | `supported=False`，`reason='Cannot read /sys/kernel/security/lsm'` |
| 系统调用探测（根本没执行到） | 本应返回 ABI v7 |

根因是第 2 步和第 3 步对"支持"的定义存在冲突。第 2 步只是读一个文件；第 3 步
才是真正决定能否创建 ruleset 的系统调用。第 2 步被当成了权威判据，导致权威检查
永远没有机会执行。

**修复方式：** 把 LSM 列表降级为尽力而为的旁证。

- 文件不可读 → 结论未定（securityfs 未挂载）。记 debug 日志，继续走系统调用探测。
- 文件可读但不含 `landlock` → 仍然是真正的"否"，仍返回 `supported=False`。不放松安全边界。
- 系统调用失败（如 `ENOSYS`）→ 仍返回 `supported=False`。

未知架构分支（没有硬编码系统调用号，例如 `riscv64`）此前仅凭"内核版本 + LSM 检查"
就假定支持。LSM 检查变成可选后该假定失去依据，因此现在只有 LSM 列表确实确认过
`landlock` 时才报告支持，否则返回 unsupported 并给出明确原因。这是有意的收紧，
在 `x86_64` / `aarch64` 上行为不变。

`_probe_linux_landlock()` returns `supported=False` whenever
`/sys/kernel/security/lsm` cannot be read. Containers do not mount
securityfs, so that file is routinely absent there even though the host
kernel exposes a fully working Landlock LSM.

The consequence is not just a wrong capability report. With
`security.sandbox_enabled=true`, `ResourceGovernor.execution_sandbox_config()`
fails closed, so every Code Mode `run_code` call dies with:

```
Script failed: Sandbox is enabled but unavailable
```

Reproduced on the official `agentscope/qwenpaw:latest` image (2.3.0) on a
WSL2 host kernel 6.18, where the kernel reports Landlock ABI v7 via the
`landlock_create_ruleset` syscall:

| Step | Result in the container |
| --- | --- |
| Step 1 — kernel >= 5.13 | passes (6.18) |
| Step 2 — read `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` | `FileNotFoundError` — securityfs not mounted |
| Probe outcome | `supported=False`, `reason='Cannot read /sys/kernel/security/lsm'` |
| Syscall probe (never reached) | would have returned ABI v7 |

The root cause is that steps 2 and 3 disagree about what "supported"
means. Step 2 reads a file; step 3 performs the syscall that actually
determines whether a ruleset can be created. Step 2 was treated as
authoritative, so the authoritative check never ran.

**Fix:** demote the LSM list to best-effort corroboration.

- Unreadable file → inconclusive (securityfs not mounted). Log at debug
  and fall through to the syscall probe.
- Readable file that omits `landlock` → still a genuine "no", still
  `supported=False`. No security regression.
- Syscall fails (e.g. `ENOSYS`) → still `supported=False`.

The unknown-architecture branch (no hardcoded syscall number, e.g.
`riscv64`) previously assumed support from "kernel version + LSM check"
alone. With the LSM check now optional that assumption would become
unfounded, so it only reports supported when the LSM list actually
confirmed `landlock`; otherwise it returns unsupported with a clear
reason. This is a deliberate tightening, not a behavior change on
`x86_64` / `aarch64`.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #5982, #6023

**Security Considerations:** 本改动让一条此前被阻断的执行路径变得可达，因此隔离性
是经过实际验证的而非假定（见 Evidence）。探测在未知架构上收紧，此前那里会高报支持。
不改任何配置默认值，`security.sandbox_enabled=false` 的关闭路径不受影响。

This change makes a previously-blocked execution path reachable, so the
isolation itself was verified rather than assumed — see Evidence. The
probe tightens on unknown architectures, which previously over-reported
support. No configuration defaults change, and the switch-off path
(`security.sandbox_enabled=false`) is untouched.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [ ] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [ ] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes
- [ ] Official channel changes are covered in `tests/unit/channels/test_<channel>.py` (startup, shutdown and message delivery)
- [ ] Shared host/process changes are covered in `test_channel_host.py` / `tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_process.py`
- [ ] Console changes retain the built-in contract checks in `tests/contract/channels/`

Not applicable — 本 PR 不涉及任何频道。

## Testing

针对探测函数的每个分支编写单元测试，并跑既有沙箱套件确认无回归：

```bash
pytest tests/unit/sandbox/ tests/integration/test_sandbox_module.py -q
```

新增文件 `tests/unit/sandbox/test_landlock_probe.py` 覆盖：

1. LSM 文件不可读 + 系统调用可用 → `supported=True`（本次容器回归场景）。
2. LSM 文件不可读 + `ENOSYS` → 仍为 `supported=False`。
3. 可读列表包含 `landlock` → 支持。
4. 可读列表不含 `landlock` → 仍为 `supported=False`（防止过度放行）。
5. 内核低于 5.13，以及 `os.uname()` 不可用/无法解析。
6. 未知架构，分别在有无 LSM 确认的情况下。

关于可移植性：测试整体替换 `os` 模块而非 patch `os.uname`，因为非 POSIX 宿主上
`os.uname` 不存在，`patch()` 会抛 `AttributeError`。因此该套件在 Windows 开发机
上也能运行。

Targeted unit tests for every branch of the probe, plus the existing
sandbox suites for regression:

```bash
pytest tests/unit/sandbox/ tests/integration/test_sandbox_module.py -q
```

The new file `tests/unit/sandbox/test_landlock_probe.py` covers:

1. Unreadable LSM list + working syscall → `supported=True` (the
   container regression).
2. Unreadable LSM list + `ENOSYS` → still `supported=False`.
3. Readable list containing `landlock` → supported.
4. Readable list without `landlock` → still `supported=False`
   (guards against over-permitting).
5. Kernel below 5.13, and unparsable/unavailable `os.uname()`.
6. Unknown architecture with and without LSM confirmation.

Note on portability: the tests swap the whole `os` module for a small
fake instead of patching `os.uname`, because `os.uname` does not exist on
non-POSIX hosts and `patch()` would raise `AttributeError` there. The
suite therefore also runs on a Windows development host.

## Evidence

> 说明：以下记录均在本地产生，镜像与宿主内核版本已在各块中注明。
> Note: the transcripts below were produced locally; the container image
> and host kernel are named in each block.

**1. 单元测试 + 集成测试 / Unit + integration tests**

```text
$ pytest tests/unit/sandbox/ tests/integration/test_sandbox_module.py -q
........................................................ssssssssssssssss [ 20%]
sssss................................................................... [ 41%]
.............s.........................s................................ [ 62%]
........................................................................ [ 83%]
...................................................s....                 [100%]
320 passed, 24 skipped in 0.83s
```

**2. Lint / 格式检查 / format gates**

```text
$ black --line-length=79 --check src/qwenpaw/sandbox/config.py \
      tests/unit/sandbox/test_landlock_probe.py
All done! 2 files would be left unchanged.

$ flake8 src/qwenpaw/sandbox/config.py tests/unit/sandbox/test_landlock_probe.py
(no output; exit 0)

$ pylint src/qwenpaw/sandbox/config.py
Your code has been rated at 10.00/10
```

`mypy` 对该文件未报告任何归属问题；运行中出现的
`import-not-found` 错误均来自裸 venv 里未安装的可选依赖
（`pydantic`、`agentscope`、`reme`），属既有噪声。

`mypy` on this file reports zero issues attributable to it; the run emits
pre-existing import-not-found errors from optional dependencies
(`pydantic`, `agentscope`, `reme`) that are not installed in a bare
venv.

**3. 官方镜像内的探测行为（securityfs 未挂载）**
**Probe behavior inside the official image (securityfs NOT mounted)**

同一镜像，仅替换 `qwenpaw/sandbox/config.py`：
Same image, swapping only `qwenpaw/sandbox/config.py`:

```text
# upstream 2.3.0
SandboxCapability(supported=False, mode=<SandboxMode.NONE: 'none'>,
  reason='Cannot read /sys/kernel/security/lsm', landlock_abi_version=0)

# with this PR
SandboxCapability(supported=True, mode=<SandboxMode.LANDLOCK: 'landlock'>,
  reason='Kernel 6.18, Landlock ABI v7', landlock_abi_version=7)
```

**4. 真实 agent 端到端运行（`qwenpaw task`，真实 Code Mode `run_code`）**
**End-to-end agent run (`qwenpaw task`, real Code Mode `run_code`)**

命令执行成功，且确实经由沙箱后端：
Command succeeds and is routed through the sandbox backend:

```text
INFO resource_governor.py:287 | governance decision: tool=RunCode
  action=sandbox_fallback source=sandbox sandbox=landlock reason=sandbox fallback

{
  "status": "success",
  "response": "fixed-branch-ok
Linux 03f366e91e5d 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 ... x86_64 GNU/Linux"
}
```

**5. 隔离仍然生效（最关键的一点）**
**Isolation still enforced (the part that matters most)**

要求 agent 向工作区外写入：
Asking the agent to write outside the workspace:

```text
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/etc/sandbox-escape-test.txt'
```

因此本修复并没有把"探测失败"变成"无沙箱裸跑"，而是变成"在一个可用的
Landlock 沙箱内运行"。
So the fix does not turn "probe fails" into "runs unsandboxed" — it
turns it into "runs inside a working Landlock sandbox".

## Additional Notes

- 这实际上是一个容器场景的回归，但探测改动与平台无关，同时消除了未知架构上
  一处潜在的高报。
- #5982 被以 "Fixed in #6054" 关闭，但那个 PR 只是新增了
  `security.sandbox_enabled` 开关并调整了 fallback 动作，并未改动 LSM 探测。
  开关默认关闭恰好掩盖了探测缺陷，直到用户打开沙箱。之后的 Code Mode
  （#8224）让探测结果变成 fail-closed 路径上的硬依赖，两者这才叠加成硬故障。
- 后续可选工作（不在本 PR 范围）：把 securityfs 挂进容器仍是有效的运维规避手段，
  且不受本改动影响。

- This is a container-only regression in practice, but the probe change
  is platform-independent and also removes a latent over-report on
  unknown architectures.
- #5982 was closed as "Fixed in #6054", but that PR added the
  `security.sandbox_enabled` switch and changed the fallback action; it
  did not touch the LSM probe. The default-off switch masked the probe
  bug until a user enabled the sandbox. Code Mode (`#8224`) later made
  the probe result load-bearing on a fail-closed path, which is how the
  two combined into a hard failure.

prs.body:
## Relationship

These three PRs form one feature, in merge order:

| Order | PR | Scope | Base / dependency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **#8649 (this PR)** | llama.cpp GPU + auto-update | `main`; merge first |
| 2 | #8647 | managed MLX + auto-update | stacked on #8649 |
| 3 | #8648 | Console engine/GPU/MLX UI + auto-update | depends on #8649 + #8647; merge last |

Relates to #8646.

This PR is self-contained: it does **not** add MLX and does not depend on the other two.

## Description

QwenPaw Local currently tells users that CPU is used by default, even though the shipped macOS runtime already includes Metal. This PR exposes the detected accelerator and lets users control GPU offload for llama.cpp.

It is rebased onto the plugin-owned local model manager introduced by #8499 (`plugins/provider/local-llamacpp/`): the accelerator probe, the GPU setting, the runtime auto-update loop and the management API all live in the plugin now, so the host `lifespan` no longer touches local-model state.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8646

**Security Considerations:** Auto-update adds outbound downloads from the existing QwenPaw runtime release endpoint and verifies the published checksum/manifest. No new inbound listeners or credentials are introduced.

## Summary

- Detect `Metal` / `CUDA` / `CPU` and the device name via `llama-server --list-devices`.
- Return `accelerator`, `device_name`, and runtime `version` from `GET /api/local-models/server`.
- Persist `gpu_acceleration`: `--gpu-layers auto` when enabled, `--gpu-layers 0` when disabled.
- Cache the accelerator and version, and invalidate both when the runtime is replaced.
- Add an `auto_update` setting (on by default) and a plugin-owned background loop that installs a newer llama.cpp runtime only when no local server is running. A running server defers the update, an in-flight download is left alone, and a missing runtime is never auto-installed.
- Expose `gpu_acceleration` and `auto_update` through `PUT /api/local-models/config`.
- Treat unsupported device backends (for example custom Vulkan builds) as CPU so the API/UI never claims an accelerator they cannot represent.
- Update the model docs and add backend/manager/API tests.

prs.title: fix(task_tracker): bound the run completion callback and always clean up
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes the **run-cleanup half** of #8173: a chat run whose completion callback hangs or is cancelled never releases its entry in `TaskTracker._runs`, so the run stays `running` forever.

### Root cause

`TaskTracker._producer` clears its `_runs` entry and pushes the end-of-stream sentinel at the end of a `finally` block, *after* awaiting the `on_finished` completion callback. Two paths meant that cleanup never completed:

1. **The callback hangs.** `on_finished` is `ChatManager.mark_chat_finished`, which persists a completion marker under a lock shared with ~24 other manager methods. Lock contention or a stalled repo suspends the producer task *inside its own `finally`*. The task is then not done **and** the entry is still registered, so every status reader reports `running` — workspace reload is blocked and inbound messages are dropped with HTTP 409.
2. **The producer is cancelled mid-callback.** `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so it escapes the `except Exception` guard and skips cleanup entirely, leaving subscriber streams without their sentinel.

### The fix

- Run the callback through `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(...))` bounded by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT`, so a hung callback is logged and given up on rather than holding the run open.
- Move the cleanup into a nested `finally` so it always runs.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8173

Deliberately *not* `Fixes` — see the scope note below.

### Scope — what this does **not** fix

This addresses the cleanup leak only. The other items from #8173 are **not** implemented here: the post-spawn connection health probe, the idle watchdog, `force` semantics on the reload/disable-enable paths, and in-channel hints for `/new` and `/stop` on backends that do not support them. Those are larger design questions and I would rather land the narrow fix first.

Note that the wedge is now **bounded** by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT` rather than eliminated: the run stays `running` while the callback runs, because `test_attach_or_start_reports_completion_before_becoming_idle` pins that ordering deliberately (it asserts `get_status == "running"` from inside the callback). Reordering the pop ahead of the callback would break that contract.

### What the new tests cover

New `tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py` (6 tests) covers a hung callback, a callback that raises, a callback that raises `TimeoutError`, a producer cancelled mid-callback, and `request_stop` against a slow callback. Waits are event-based rather than fixed sleeps.

Against unmodified source these fail on behavioural assertions (`run entry survived a hung completion callback`, etc.), not on import or attribute errors.

### Security Considerations

Not applicable — no change to channel auth, credentials, or config handling.

## Evidence

Verification is a real failure on unmodified source followed by the **same command** against the patched tree. Base is `5c56644a` (`main`), patch is `e2b7b8be`.

**1. Unmodified baseline — the new tests genuinely fail.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_hung_completion_callback_does_not_block_new_messages
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_completion_callback_timeout_is_logged_not_raised
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_cancellation_during_callback_still_clears_the_run
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_request_stop_with_a_slow_callback_does_not_wedge_the_run
4 failed, 1 passed in 8.32s
```

**2. Same command with the patch — all green.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
.......................                                                  [100%]
23 passed in 0.49s
```

**3. Full `tests/unit/app` with the patch — no regression.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app
3118 passed, 1 skipped, 12 warnings in 58.77s
```

One caveat worth stating plainly: the baseline run pins the module source with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at a pristine checkout. The venv's editable install points at the patched worktree, so simply `cd`-ing to the unmodified tree would still have imported the patched code and produced a false green — that happened on the first attempt and the baseline above is from the corrected invocation.

Lint: `black`, `flake8` and `mypy` are clean. `pylint`, run with the full argument list from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, scores **10.00/10 with zero findings on both the unmodified and the patched tree** — I have not pasted a terminal transcript for that one because I did not capture it to a file, and I would rather say so than manufacture the output.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## AI assistance

The root-cause analysis was verified by running probes against both the unmodified and patched trees rather than taken from the issue description — in particular, the issue's claim that `has_active_tasks()` stays true does **not** hold on the cancellation path (the producer task has already completed there, so every status reader reports idle). The path that does produce the reported symptoms is the hung callback.
