### Affected component plugins ### Severity S2 - degraded behavior ### Current behavior Each plugin store is built with `StoreLimitsBuilder::new().memory_size(spec.limits.max_memory_bytes).table_elements(spec.limits.max_table_elements).instances(spec.limits.max_instances)` (`crates/zeroclaw-plugins/src/component.rs:297-301`), with defaults of 256 MiB, 100,000 elements and 64 instances (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs:9957-9975`). Those three settings bound the size of one memory, the size of one table and the number of core instances. They do not bound how many memories or tables a store may hold, and wasmtime's `ResourceLimiter` fills those in with `DEFAULT_MEMORY_LIMIT = 10000` and `DEFAULT_TABLE_LIMIT = 10000` (`wasmtime-48.0.8/src/runtime/limits.rs:3-8`). `memory_size` is consulted per memory as it grows, so the effective ceiling on a store is the number of memories times 256 MiB. Multiple memories per module are reachable because the engine is configured as `Config::new()` with fuel metering and nothing else (`component.rs:710-711`), and wasmtime enables the multi-memory proposal by default (`wasmtime-48.0.8/src/config.rs:1206-1209`, "This is `true` by default"). A component whose core module declares, say, sixty-four memories and grows each to the limit commits sixteen gibibytes while every individual check passes; sixty-four instances each with a handful of memories reach the same place; and the table side allows 10,000 tables of 100,000 elements each. Fuel and the call timeout bound compute, but growing memory is cheap and the allocation lands before either intervenes. ### Expected behavior The builder also sets `.memories(n)` and `.tables(n)` with small values (one or two per instance is enough for current plugins), or the store carries a `ResourceLimiter` that budgets total committed bytes across all memories and tables so that `max_memory_mb` means what an operator reads it to mean. A test loads a component that declares two memories and asserts that the second cannot grow the store past the configured budget. ### Steps to reproduce ```bash # Build a component whose core module declares two memories and grows both to the maximum # (wat: (memory 0 4096) (memory 0 4096) with memory.grow calls on each), package it as a plugin, # install and invoke it; watch the daemon's RSS pass 2 x max_memory_mb with no limiter error. # Scale the memory count to see the ceiling move with it. ``` ### Impact The actor is a plugin the operator installed, so this is a supply-chain and robustness concern rather than a remote one: a malicious package from a registry, a compromised update of a trusted plugin, or an honest plugin with a runaway allocation takes the daemon down with it, and with it every channel and agent the daemon hosts. The likelihood is moderate; plugins are the project's extension mechanism and the registry is open. Nothing is disclosed; the loss is availability and the false assurance the memory limit gives when a plugin is reviewed. **Data flow** ```mermaid flowchart LR L["StoreLimitsBuilder:
memory_size 256 MiB (per memory)
table_elements 100k (per table)
instances 64"] --> S["store"] D["wasmtime defaults left in place:
memories 10000, tables 10000"] --> S F["engine Config::new():
multi-memory enabled by default"] --> P["plugin module declares N memories"] P --> S S --> R["committed = N x 256 MiB, up to the 10000-memory ceiling"] classDef bad fill:#fde2e2,stroke:#b00000,color:#000 class D,R bad ``` **Evidence:** static review of master `1c1cd118ac` and the vendored wasmtime 48.0.8 sources; not executed. ### Logs / stack traces _No response_ ### ZeroClaw version master `1c1cd118ac` (v0.8.7) ### Rust version 1.98.0 (CI toolchain) ### Operating system any ### Regression? Unknown ### Pre-flight checks - [ ] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release. - [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

issues.title: gateway: a failed session-state write leaves `running` until restart, and Stop can't clear it
issues.body:
### Problem

The gateway writes a session's turn state (`running`, `idle`, `error`) with the result discarded, in [`ws.rs`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/dfc70a2b49/crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/ws.rs#L2180) (lines 2180, 2591, 2772, 2814):

```rust
let _ = backend.set_session_state(session_key, "idle", None);
```

If the `idle` or `error` write fails (for example, SQLite stays busy past the connection's busy timeout), the row keeps `running` with the old turn ID. Nothing retries it and nothing logs it. The row stays `running` until the next start, when [`recover_abandoned_turns_at`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/dfc70a2b49/crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_sqlite.rs#L88) marks it `error`. The runtime's RPC path has the same pattern in [`rpc/dispatch.rs`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/dfc70a2b49/crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs#L7517) (lines 7517, 7550, 7610, 7622).

### Effect

`GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` keeps reporting `running`. Every client that reads it treats the session as busy: with #12376, the dashboard locks the composer and watches the turn, in every tab and on every device.

Stop can't fix it. [`session_abort`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/dfc70a2b49/crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/dashboard_core.rs#L1486) returns `no_active_response` when no turn is registered, and leaves the stored row as it is. #12376 works around this on the page: after Stop is refused, two more `running` answers for the same turn ID end the watch. Other clients still see `running`.

### Evidence

Found by reading the code at `dfc70a2b49`. I haven't seen a failed write in production, and I haven't reproduced one. The reasoning is the discarded `io::Result` plus an `UPDATE` that can fail under lock contention.

### Possible fixes

Either or both:

1. **Settle the row on refusal.** When an abort finds no registered turn and the stored state is still `running`, set it to `idle` (or `error`) before returning `no_active_response`.
2. **Stop discarding the write result.** At the very least log a failed state write, and retry it once for the terminal states (`idle`, `error`), because those are the ones that leave a session stuck.

Suggested by @JordanTheJet in the #12376 review.

issues.title: [Tracker]: Deslop pass: dead code, inert features, comment slop and extra docs

labels.name: dev
labels.description: Auto scope: dev/** changed.

labels.name: priority:p2
labels.description: Medium priority

labels.name: type:tracker
labels.description: Active parent coordination issue for release, RFC/design, implementation, cleanup, or audit.

issues.body:
### Tracker kind

cleanup / audit tracker

### Purpose

Coordinate one cleanup pass over ZeroClaw. It removes:

- code nothing reaches;
- features and config that cannot take effect;
- comments that restate or misdescribe code;
- Markdown, assets and scripts nothing uses.

The work lands as small PRs that can each be reviewed on its own.

The baseline is a read-only audit of `master` at `dfc70a2b49` on 2026-11-20. Each finding came with a search command that reproduces it, and a second pass reran that command and looked for uses the first pass missed. None of the 59 findings was refuted. 25 needed a correction to their scope or action, and the items below use the corrected versions.

### Scope and non-goals

**In scope:**

- delete never-compiled files, unused modules, functions and dependencies, and duplicated tests;
- retire config and API surfaces that cannot take effect, following the replacement-first rule (#6165) and `RETIRED_KEYS`;
- fix comments and docs that are stale, contradict the code, or narrate history;
- remove committed working notes, screenshots, unreferenced images and uncalled scripts.

**Out of scope:**

- Behavior changes inside cleanup PRs. A removal that changes what a user sees gets its own issue first.
- Panic, `unsafe` and `#[allow(dead_code)]` policy debt. #10118 owns it.
- The docs-restating-code audit. #8858 owns it. Comment fixes here link to it.
- Features that already have an accepted plan or an active PR. Those are linked below, not removed.

### Linked work

**Already landed or open:**

- #12580–#12589: first cleanup batch.
- #12611 and PR #12612: retire the local LLM response cache.
- #12521: retire the Lucid memory backend.

**Sub-tracks:**

- #10118: Rust anti-slop policy debt.
- #8858: drift surfaces in comments and docs.

**Owned elsewhere (link, do not refile):**

- #9328: Verifiable Intent has no production consumer.
- #8850 and draft #10557: the cron plugin outbox has no producer or consumer.
- #3767: OTP gating of tools and domains is not enforced.
- #9390, #9802 and #12491: the emergency stop only writes a state file.
- #12038 and #10781: context compression.
- #12477, #11585, #12500, #11589 and #12165: cost enforcement keys.
- #11224 and #10593: backup destination, compress and encrypt keys; the scheduled backup job.
- #12036: memory knob warnings.
- #11053: knowledge auto-capture keys.

**Planned batches, mechanical (no user-visible change):**

- [ ] Never-compiled files: 67 one-line `src/tools/*.rs` stubs, `runtime/platform/{wasm,traits}.rs` and `skills/symlink_tests.rs`, plus their stale labeler globs. Move the stray `firmware/zeroclaw-nucleo/.cargo/config.toml` into `firmware/nucleo/`.
- [ ] The root crate compiles 27 `src/` modules twice, once for the library and once for the binary. Delete the six that are dead in both, drop seven library declarations nothing imports, and drop the root copies of runtime and API tests.
- [ ] 27 tool-call parser tests are duplicated in `agent/loop_.rs`. Two same-named tests with different bodies need reconciling, not deleting.
- [ ] 25 unused dependency entries across 10 manifests, including the firmware lockfile.
- [ ] 33 `#[allow(unused_imports)]` that suppress nothing.
- [ ] Remove unreferenced code:
  - 13 public functions and one module with no reference;
  - unused `Agent` and channel-start constructor variants;
  - the command-audit API, which nothing constructs;
  - three unused `RuntimeAdapter` methods and `Channel::send_choice`;
  - 14 unused macOS permission bindings in the desktop app.

  Keep the TLS CSR seam until its owner confirms no external signer uses it.

**Planned batches, comment slop:**

- [ ] Stale references: 29 citations of a renamed "ABSOLUTE RULE" heading, dead file paths and symbols, and 22 half-sentences left by #8901's reference stripping.
- [ ] Change-history tombstones, planning labels nothing defines (EPIC, Task N, TODO(PR C)), and copy-pasted blocks. One stale note is copied 56 times.
- [ ] Comments that restate the next line: about 400 candidates, reviewed in per-crate batches.
- [ ] Doc comments that contradict the code they describe.
- [ ] `web/`: #8901's sweep and the comment gate never covered TypeScript, which still has 86 issue references. Sweep it, then extend the gate.
- [ ] 14 TODOs with no owner or issue. File the real ones and allow a full issue URL in the comment.

**Planned batches, docs and files:**

- [ ] 165 dashboard i18n keys nothing uses, about 4,760 lines across 31 locales.
- [ ] 3.2 MB of PR screenshots committed under `.pr-evidence/`, and 8.2 MB of unreferenced images in `docs/assets/`. Check the website for links to these files first.
- [ ] Notes from finished work: agent working files, two maintainer audit trails, and a stale copy of the CI workflow doc.
- [ ] A third-party `skill-creator` copy under `.claude/skills` (5,654 lines), never updated since import.
- [ ] Smaller dead files:
  - blog feeds and a sitemap the dashboard never serves;
  - the config for an inactive Gemini review bot;
  - duplicate VNC scripts;
  - a duplicate zerocode page.
- [ ] Broken or unused tooling:
  - the broken manual Telegram kit;
  - seven dev and test scripts nothing calls;
  - labeler, label-table and CODEOWNERS entries that match no file;
  - the skill catalog page, which is missing 3 of 11 skills.
- [ ] Book pages and the README still show the retired V2 `[agent.*]` and `[autonomy]` tables.
- [ ] Decide the Raspberry Pi deploy kit under `scripts/`: update it or fold it into the hardware guide. Its config predates V3 and sets pairing off, a public bind and full autonomy, and the script copies it over the Pi's config on every run. ZeroClaw itself keeps supporting the Pi; this is only about the deploy script.

**Planned retirements (issue first; each changes config or a public API):**

- [ ] `runtime_profiles.<alias>.eval`: the response scorer has no production caller.
- [ ] Memory pinning keys, `chunk_max_tokens`, `default_namespace` and `fts_early_return_score`: nothing reads them.
- [ ] `runtime.kind = "cloudflare"` is accepted but always fails.
- [ ] `cost.rates` for TTS, transcription and tools never prices anything. Retire it or wire it.
- [ ] The log-to-observer bridge is never bound, so some observer events and metrics never fire. Bind it or remove it.
- [ ] Five `HookHandler` events are never fired. Wire them or remove them; removal changes the API.
- [ ] SOP calendar and peripheral triggers have no event source. The SOP owner decides.

**Docs fix that can land now:**

- [ ] The security docs say OTP gates `shell` and `file_write`, but nothing enforces it. Correct `security/model.md`, `yolo.md` and `security-first.md`, and point to #3767, which owns enforcement.

### Routing evidence and next decision

The audit report holds the evidence for every item: the search command, its output, and the verifier's rerun.

Next decisions:

1. The batch order. Mechanical batches first, since they need no design call.
2. An owner for each retirement issue.
3. Answers from the owners of the "owned elsewhere" items: keep with a deadline, or retire.

Reason to stay open: it coordinates a multi-PR cleanup pass.
Next decision/revisit: batch order and retirement owners.
Visible owner, assignee, milestone, linked tracker, or review cadence: assignee JordanTheJet; sub-tracks #10118 and #8858.

### Close criteria

- Every planned batch is merged, or declined with a reason recorded here.
- The linked trackers are updated with what landed.
- A fresh audit of the then-current `master` finds no new items in the mechanical categories.

### Stale-exemption requested?

Yes - tracker itself is the active coordination surface

issues.title: [Feature]: browser tool has no file-upload action, blocking every form that requires attaching a file
issues.body:
### Summary

`BrowserTool`'s `BrowserAction` enum exposes open, snapshot, click, fill, type, get_text, get_title, get_url, screenshot, wait, press, hover, scroll, is_visible, find, close — but nothing that sets a local file on an `<input type="file">`. The `agent-browser` CLI it wraps does have `upload`, so the capability exists one layer down and is simply not surfaced.

### Impact

Any form that requires attaching a document is unfinishable. Concrete case: job applications via ATS (Spark Hire, Workday, Greenhouse, Lever). The resume control is a hidden file input inside a cross-origin iframe — clicking it yields `element is not visible`, and there is no `setInputFiles` equivalent to set it directly. The agent correctly stops and reports it cannot submit.

### Reproduction

1. `browser.automation_enabled = true`, default `backend = agent_browser`, `agent-browser` 0.43.0 installed.
2. Ask the agent to apply to a posting whose form has a resume upload.
3. It opens the page, snapshots, clicks the attach control → `element is not visible`. No action exists to attach a file.

### Proposed solution

Add a typed action rather than a passthrough:

- `Upload { selector: String, path: String }` → `agent-browser upload <selector> <path>`
- Validate `path` exactly like `screenshot`: resolve against the workspace, canonicalize the parent, reject symlinks and anything outside the workspace allowlist, reject runtime config files.
- Expose it in `parameters_schema` so models know it exists.
- Tests: in-workspace file accepted, outside-workspace rejected, symlink rejected, missing file errors clearly.

Optionally consider `Download` in the same pass, since it has the mirror-image problem and the same path-policy machinery.

### Environment

v0.9.0 (6c78ba5), Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, headless; Playwright Chromium 159; agent-browser 0.43.0; `browser.backend = agent_browser`.

issues.title: [Feature]: Retire the local LLM response cache

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Summary

Remove the local LLM response cache (`[memory] response_cache_*`, `zeroclaw-memory::ResponseCache`), which almost never serves a hit, and retire its four config keys with a migration notice.

### Problem statement

The response cache stores full LLM replies in `response_cache.db` and replays one when the same request comes back. On `master` (`dfc70a2b49`) it almost never gets a hit:

- It is off by default (`response_cache_enabled = false`).
- `Agent::response_cache_key_for_messages` skips the cache unless every one of these holds: temperature is exactly `0.0` (unset by default); the agent has no tools; no hooks, memory injection, native-thinking override or `[IMAGE:]` content; and the provider reports a stable request identity (one provider, no model fallbacks). An agent built from config gets the full tool registry, so ordinary agents never qualify.
- Every `Agent` turn path prefixes the user message with `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS TZ]` (`enrich_user_message`) before the key is computed. A hit therefore needs an identical transcript within the same second. #8320 reported this; #8323 pinned the clock in tests and left production unchanged.
- Channel messages run through `run_tool_call_loop`, which never reads the cache. Only `Agent::turn` and `turn_streamed` (CLI, ACP, RPC, gateway webhook) consult it.

It still has costs:

- a SQLite file that keeps prompts and replies at rest (#10091 and #10835 hardened its permissions);
- cache bypass checks on every `Agent` turn;
- `ModelProvider::has_stable_request_identity`, a provider probe whose only consumer is this cache key;
- steady fixes: #7704, #7779, #9675/#9720.

Provider-side prompt caching (Anthropic `cache_control`, Bedrock `cachePoint`, OpenAI automatic caching) already covers the repeated-prefix cost that matters in practice.

### Proposed solution

Retire it the way #12521 retires Lucid:

- Delete `crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/response_cache.rs`, `create_response_cache`, and the `response_cache.db` cases in the SQLite storage checks.
- Remove the cache field, builder method, key function, and hit/miss branches from `Agent` in `zeroclaw-runtime`.
- Remove `ObserverEvent::CacheHit` and `CacheMiss`, plus the `zeroclaw_cache_hits_total`, `zeroclaw_cache_misses_total` and `zeroclaw_cache_tokens_saved_total` Prometheus counters. Only this cache emits them.
- Remove `ModelProvider::has_stable_request_identity` and its wrapper implementations. `supports_exact_request_replay` stays, because `turn/provider_call.rs` uses it.
- Add the four `memory.response_cache_*` keys to `RETIRED_KEYS` at `retired_in: 4`, with one shared reason in every locale's `cli.ftl`. An existing config then loads with a `Removed` notice instead of the keys being silently ignored.
- Update the docs (`agents/filesystem.md`, `ops/overview.md`), config fixtures, and `scripts/rpi-config.toml`.

Existing `response_cache.db` files stay on disk. The docs will say they can be deleted.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Provider prompt caching (`cache_control`, `cache_ttl`, `cache_passthrough`) does not change.
- Bedrock and OpenRouter cache-placement fixes are separate.
- Existing `response_cache.db` files are not deleted automatically.

### Alternatives considered

- **Define a volatile-context policy (#8321) and keep the cache.** This adds design and code to a feature with no known users that duplicates provider prompt caching.
- **Strip the timestamp from the key.** The temperature-0 and no-tools gates remain, so ordinary agents still never qualify, and a cached reply to a time-sensitive prompt would be wrong.
- **Leave it.** This keeps the maintenance cost and an on-disk store of prompts for no measured benefit.

### Acceptance criteria

- Production code no longer contains `ResponseCache`, any `response_cache_*` config field, `ObserverEvent::CacheHit`/`CacheMiss`, or `has_stable_request_identity`.
- A config with any `memory.response_cache_*` key loads with a `Removed` migration notice, and the migration drops the key. Tests cover each key and a `ZEROCLAW_MEMORY__RESPONSE_CACHE_ENABLED` environment override.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the workspace tests pass.

### Architecture impact

- `zeroclaw-config`: schema fields, `RETIRED_KEYS`
- `zeroclaw-memory`: module, factory, SQLite storage checks
- `zeroclaw-runtime`: `Agent`, observability (log, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus), CLI locale strings
- `zeroclaw-api`: `ModelProvider::has_stable_request_identity`, `ObserverEvent` (already `#[non_exhaustive]`)
- `zeroclaw-providers`: model-pin, reliable, router and vision-override wrappers
- gateway tests, the runtime-composition consumer fixture, docs

### Risk and rollback

Behavior risk is low. The cache almost never served a hit, so replies and provider costs stay the same. The one realistic hit was an identical text-only request repeated within the same second, such as a duplicate webhook delivery; it would now reach the provider again.

Surface risk is medium. Four config keys, three Prometheus metric names, and the Rust API items listed in #12612 go away. A dashboard that graphs `zeroclaw_cache_hits_total` loses that series.

Rollback: revert the PR. The keys become ordinary fields again.

### Expected routing

Ordinary feature triage

### Next decision surface

Maintainers set the release level. FND-001 keeps removals out of patch releases; #9644 (Lucid) was retargeted to v0.9.1 as a retirement precedent. The v0.9.1 merge cutoff has passed, so this targets the next release.

When this lands, close #8321 as superseded. Open PR #12460 adds tests to the module this removes.

### Breaking change?

Yes

### Data hygiene checks

- [X] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [X] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

prs.title: feat(web): manage scoped HTTP credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an operator-managed, write-only WebUI catalog for local HTTP Basic, Bearer and X-API-Key credentials, bound to an exact HTTPS origin. Each alias starts denied and requires an explicit grant. Rotating the value on the same origin preserves the grant. Changing the origin clears it.

Operators use Settings → Secrets to register and grant a disposable credential, then supply its alias as the HTTP Request tool's credential argument. The existing network policy still applies. Credential changes through generic configuration writes are rejected and dedicated mutations are audited without secret values. The OpenAPI schema describes the dedicated endpoint.

## Dependencies and rollout

Merge #12402, then #12408, then #12490. SSH, TOTP, directory credentials and external vaults remain under RFC #12422. The previous integrated catalog is preserved on the fork and continues to be tested independently on Jarvis.

## Validation

Production WebUI build passed on the dependent Token slice. The backend compile identified a gateway-only dependency reference, fixed by moving URL validation into the config crate. Local Rust tests passed for operator-only, default-denied credentials and the write-only OpenAPI schema. The previous Jarvis deployment showed the broader catalog and is historical evidence.

Shared Security blockers are tracked in #12101 and #12505.

Lint and Installer Drift passed after synchronizing the canonical Fluent catalog. Workspace formatting was verified locally after the subsequent rustfmt-only fix. The new CI run remains authoritative for the published heads.


## Current review scope and security validation

Current scope is locally encrypted API keys and Basic credentials bound to one HTTPS origin, with an explicit default-denied HTTP grant. The current schema has no TOTP, SSH, directory destinations or external resolvers. Extended functionality is preserved in draft #12517, conditional on RFC #12422.

The quote-bearing credential and numeric JSON redaction findings are corrected in the current head. Four real-crate Linux regressions passed, covering literal quotes in text/HTML, escaped JSON strings and keys, numeric credential replacement and large integer preservation.


## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.

## Managed credential RPC placement

Depends on #12563, the separately reviewed bounded Core Team exception record for the generic-RPC credential write guard. The guard stays enabled; this feature does not approve its own placement. The record must land before this feature merges.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose ADR-016 exception for daemon-held OIDC refresh grants
prs.body:
> **Stacked:** Depends on #12608 (adjacent row in the same table). Until it merges this PR also shows `2855c46171`; review only `ed35854ead` and `5f6c8ee82f`.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds the `zeroclaw-runtime` exception row for the refresh-grant implementation that the ADR-017 amendment (#12496, approved) records. The existing #12317 OIDC row explicitly excludes "refresh-token storage", and #12496 now states that each implementing PR touching the auth-provider owner in the holding crate needs its own row first. Proposed ahead of the implementation, as ADR-016 requires and as the plugin-admission row did.
  - Scope names exact paths and limits: retaining the refresh token the existing device-grant and browser responses already return (`EnrolledToken::refresh_token`), a refresh request that omits `scope`, RFC 7009 revocation, never-sent vs unknown-outcome classification (`enrollment.rs`); a new `refresh_grant.rs` module *inside the existing auth-provider subsystem* for the pending grant (keyed by a hash of its paired access token) and the durable, `SecretStore`-sealed grant with version, single-flight, in-flight marker and uncertain state, registered in `auth_provider/mod.rs` limited to declaring the module and re-exporting its public types; a grant table in the existing ledger database so the claim commits in the same transaction as `record_issued`, plus deletion on revocation or unrenewed lapse (`cert_ledger.rs`); and a pre-auth refresh method admitted like `cert/renew`, sign-out, and grant deletion on provider removal/repoint (`rpc/{auth,dispatch,types}.rs`).
  - Explicit exclusions: no dashboard refresh or client-held refresh token, no OAuth flow beyond refresh and revocation, no change to introspection or `initialize`, no new subsystem. Encryption reuses `zeroclaw_config::secrets::SecretStore` (ADR-013) rather than adding crypto to runtime. Gateway hand-off, the Zerocode trigger, and `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` method names stay in their own crates.
- **Scope boundary:** Governance record only; no code. Does not cover #12497/#12498 (that's #12608).
- **Blast radius:** None at runtime. Gates the refresh implementation PRs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12608. Related #12496, Related #8289

### What this does, simply

The ADR now says how ZeroClaw will keep a laptop's sign-in alive across sleep: the daemon holds the identity provider's refresh token, and the device certificate lets Zerocode ask for a fresh access token. Most of that code has to touch sign-in code in a temporary "holding" crate, which needs a written, approved exception before anything lands there. This is that exception, drawn tightly around what the refresh work needs and nothing more, so the implementation can be reviewed against a fixed boundary.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Governance-table edit with no behavior.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Docs style covers the edited Markdown table.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

prs.title: feat(web): enable browser voice for OIDC sessions
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch: `master`. Depends on #12269.
- Enable browser dictation and narration for an OIDC dashboard operator without a paired-device token.
- Store voice choices in the current browser profile under the verified principal ID. The paired-device API remains the source of truth for paired browsers.
- Clear capture and narration state when the signed-in principal changes. Use the existing global silence setting and dashboard permission checks.

### What this does, simply

An OIDC operator with Chat and Config access can enable the microphone and speaker in **Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio**. Each account in the browser has its own opt-in choices.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested? Yes.
- Interface: `web`, dashboard chat and voice settings.
- Setup: HTTPS dashboard with an OIDC operator and an unpaired browser profile.
- Sign in, open **Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio**, enable dictation and reading, and choose a voice. Open chat, dictate, pause for the configured interval, and listen to the reply. Change to a different OIDC account in the same browser and verify its initial settings.
- After: controls work without pairing, the transcript is sent once and another account starts with its own preferences.
- On the parent PR: the voice preferences require a paired-device record.

### How I tested

- Focused component suite: 33 passed. The OIDC test exercises settings, fake recognition and playback in an unpaired session, denies stale capture after switching accounts, and checks that no paired-device route was called.
- CI relied on: Web Permission Tests and CI Required Gate. The voice suite was run directly, as shown below. 
- Coverage gap: the new deployment smoke test did not exercise real speech input or audio output. The localized preview is covered by the voice suite.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New capabilities? Yes. Voice controls are available in an existing chat session. Browser audio permissions and gateway permissions still apply. Account-scoped storage holds only voice choices.
- New external network calls? No. The existing recognition mode remains an explicit user choice.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. At runtime, browser storage associates preferences with the SHA-256 digest of the verified account ID, which is a persistent pseudonymous identifier. The raw account ID and session credentials are excluded from the new storage key.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced or changed? No. Dictation continues through the ordinary composer.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback

- Revert this PR and rebuild the dashboard assets.
- Feature flags or config toggles: none added.
- Observable failure symptoms: missing controls for an opted-in OIDC account, or settings shared across accounts.

### Live OIDC acceptance

An operator tested an unpaired browser against a deployed dashboard using Keycloak. Dictation, single send after the configured silence, and audible narration worked before and after closing the window and signing in again. The test identified an English preview for a Portuguese narrator. The follow-up selects sample text and utterance language from the narrator locale. The automated suite verifies a Portuguese sample with an English WebUI and verifies that the saved automatic-reading default is restored for the same principal. The chat-local long press remains scoped to the conversation.


## Scope boundary and blast radius

Depends on #12269. Head `3930bb832` incorporates #12269 at `d6cdf58ec`. The OIDC-specific diff still covers the same six files. All 35 voice tests and the production WebUI build passed locally on the aligned head. Merge #12269 first. The OIDC branch applies only when the session has Chat and Config access. The paired-device persistence path continues through its existing API. In an authorized browser profile, an existing preference for the same OIDC account is migrated to the digest key.

## Current interface evidence

Captured production components from PR head `25431a005` in headed Chrome with a synthetic OIDC session, preferences and conversation. The settings view shows that the paired-device picker is absent. The chat view shows the microphone and speaker. The fixture also verified that localStorage uses a SHA-256 key.

![OIDC browser voice settings without device pairing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/c2eef22421000bc322ad71e45bbdf6b668f29243/.pr-evidence/voice-oidc-settings-25431a005.png)

![OIDC chat microphone and speaker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/c2eef22421000bc322ad71e45bbdf6b668f29243/.pr-evidence/voice-oidc-chat-25431a005.png)

## Test output and live smoke test

```text
npm run test:voice
✔ OIDC voice settings enable chat controls without pairing and isolate accounts
ℹ tests 35
ℹ pass 35
ℹ fail 0
```

The OIDC test also checks that a Chat-only principal sees no controls and cannot write preferences. The integrated Jarvis WebUI build `66086f10f` passed `npm run build` and was deployed as static assets. In a fresh, unpaired Chrome profile, Keycloak sign-in reached the voice settings. Both toggles persisted after reload, the chat showed the microphone and speaker, and the browser stored a digest key. No microphone capture or playback was attempted during this smoke test.

The shared Security findings are tracked in #12505 (chrono and chrono-tz) and #12101 (zip 9.0.5). This voice PR does not alter the workspace dependency graph or advisory policy.

prs.title: docs(adr): propose daemon-held OIDC refresh and Okta/Entra ID support in ADR-017
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Amends proposed ADR-017 with a decision for **device-session continuity**: the daemon holds the IdP refresh token as a sealed *refresh grant* keyed by provider alias + ledger `device_id`; a pre-auth RPC authorized by the device's mTLS certificate (admitted like `cert/renew`) refreshes it, verifies the new access token through the same `oidc.<alias>` provider and same `sub`, and returns only the access token for an ordinary `initialize`. Today a Zerocode session cannot outlive one access token: the gateway discards the refresh token and Zerocode replays the login-time token on every reconnect, so sleep/resume past `exp` ends in `-32010`.
  - Adds a decision for **Okta and Entra ID** (required for v1.0). Neither issues RFC 9068 tokens: Okta access tokens have no `typ` and use `cid`; Entra uses `typ: JWT`, `uti` instead of `jti`, and has no introspection endpoint. The amendment keeps token-purpose separation by requiring audience ≠ every configured client_id when `typ: at+jwt` is absent (an ID token's `aud` is always its client), and admits vendor claim spellings only as named, tested compatibility rules (precedent: the Keycloak `azp` rule). Device-grant scopes become per-provider so Entra can request the API scope that sets the audience.
  - Adds matching acceptance gates (sleep/wake + rotation/revocation tests; real-tenant Okta and Entra verification), consequences (daemon now holds long-lived IdP secrets; partially deployment-side audience invariant; Entra revocation bounded by token lifetime + refresh interval), and standards/vendor references. Updates the ADR index gate summary.
- **Scope boundary:** Docs only. No code, config schema, or behavior changes. Browser dashboard stays refresh-free. Existing docs describing current behavior (`zerocode/remote.md` "no refresh-token cache") are left alone until the implementation lands.
- **Blast radius:** None at runtime. Constrains future work in `auth_provider/oidc.rs`, `auth_provider/enrollment.rs`, `cert_ledger.rs`, RPC dispatch pre-auth methods, and Zerocode's connection/auth path.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8289

### What this does, simply

Signing in to ZeroClaw from Zerocode through an identity provider currently lasts only as long as one access token, often minutes to an hour. If your laptop sleeps longer than that, the session can't resume and you have to restart and sign in again, even though your identity provider would happily keep you signed in. This records the plan to fix that: the daemon keeps the provider's refresh token (never your laptop), and your device certificate lets Zerocode quietly ask the daemon for a fresh token.

It also records how ZeroClaw will accept Okta and Entra ID tokens. Their access tokens are shaped differently from what the verifier accepts today, so Entra cannot sign in at all and Okta only works through introspection. The plan accepts their formats without weakening the check that stops an ID token being used as an access token.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Docs-only ADR amendment with no behavior change.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Docs style and link checks cover the two changed Markdown files.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The links gate runs lychee offline, so the 8 new external links (RFC Editor, OpenID, Microsoft Learn, Okta developer docs) are excluded rather than fetched. The Entra and Okta pages were fetched manually while drafting.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base upstream/master HEAD) scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Linting: 2 file(s)
Summary: 0 error(s)

$ BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base upstream/master HEAD) scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
Collected 9 added link(s) from 2 docs file(s).
Checked 1 local docs link target(s).
👻 Excluded.........8
🚫 Errors...........0
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Checked each technical claim against source: `api_oidc.rs` drops refresh tokens (test `rt-never-relayed`); `apps/zerocode/src/main.rs` snapshots `WssRoute.auth_token` at startup and replays it on reconnect; `rpc/dispatch.rs` `handle_initialize` re-authenticates a live connection and enforces same-principal on bound connections; `oidc.rs` requires `typ: at+jwt`, `jti`, and `client_id`/`azp` in JWKS mode; `enrollment.rs` hard-codes `scope=openid` for the device grant; `cert_ledger.rs` keys rows by fingerprint with a stable `device_id`. Token formats were checked against the Microsoft Entra access-token claims reference and Okta's OIDC overview. Not verified: behavior against real Okta or Entra tenants (now an acceptance gate).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (docs only). The *decision* records a future change: the daemon will retain IdP refresh tokens, sealed through the ADR-013 key source, deleted on every refusal path, revoked at the IdP on sign-out, and never released to clients. Containment is certificate revocation plus IdP session revocation.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

prs.title: feat(web): add paired-device voice settings and chat controls
prs.body:
### How I tested

Validated at `d8900473b3`.

- `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib voice`: 6 passed, 0 failed. Includes the reproducer with a pending SQLite writer, concurrent token revocation, and an unrelated bearer check. Existing revocation and cookie authorization checks still pass.
- Equivalent Windows invocation of `npm run test:voice` with the same Jiti environment and entry point: 39 passed, 0 failed. Includes a direct stale-utterance ownership regression and the updated polling assertions.
- git diff --check: clean.
- [Required Web Permission Tests](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44872294096/job/136749348894): generated contract typecheck and the new voice test step both passed.

The token-set hold begins after SQLite admits the transaction. The authorization callback runs before taking the short bearer hold, and cookie-only writes do not hold the token set. The voice suite is added to the required Web Permission Tests job. Narration walks the Markdown AST without importing the React server renderer. Visible dictation polling is now 30 seconds, with the pre-send recheck retained. The unrelated navigation translation change was removed.

The new head has not been tested with a real microphone or audible playback. The historical Chrome and Edge evidence remains below. A standalone web build was not completed on this checkout because the generated gateway contract was absent.

<details>
<summary>Historical PR description and evidence</summary>

## Summary

- **Base branch:** master.
- Add opt-in browser dictation and narration in agent chat, with paired-device voice preferences and a localized guide under Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio.
- Save microphone, recognition mode, language, voice, speed and automatic narration on the authenticated paired-device record, not browser storage. Operators can select another paired device's record without changing the current browser's identity.
- Add one global `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs` setting in that same voice screen: default 15 seconds, accepted range 0–300, with 0 disabling automatic submission. It applies to every device/conversation and uses the existing authenticated configuration property API.
- Speak rendered Markdown text rather than hidden delimiters; omit only a trailing crab signature. Preserve meaningful literal code punctuation. Formatting-only replies do not block the continuous reading queue.
- **Scope boundary:** browser speech APIs, paired-device preferences, one gateway configuration field and normal chat submission. No server STT/TTS backend, microphone-audio upload endpoint, new identity or external service is added.
- **Blast radius:** web Config/chat, existing device-registry migration, gateway configuration and same-origin microphone Permissions Policy.
- **Linked issues:** none.

### What this does, simply

A paired browser can enable microphone and speaker controls next to the composer. Recognition starts only when the user clicks the microphone and grants browser permission. Local recognition is the default and never falls back online automatically; browser-service recognition is an explicit choice.

Dictation appends final recognized text to the draft. After the global silence interval, capture stops and final results are accepted before the normal send path is invoked once. Empty captures, hidden/cancelled chats, disconnected/busy sessions and stale conversation requests do not auto-send. A browser ending recognition early still honors the remaining silence interval. Local slash commands remain for manual submission. Set the global value to 0 for manual sending only.

The speaker reads a reply once, stops it, or enables continuous reading through a hold/Shift+Enter gesture. Automatic reading skips restored history and consumes unreadable formatting/signature-only replies so later responses can play. Changing the speech text never changes the displayed/stored response.

<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Historical validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at 9a9f6a1be. Combined voice controls with scoped chat while retaining operator-only image uploads. Voice submission honors the existing canSend/first-conversation path. A regression drives the actual voice callback through a restricted account's first WebSocket conversation, verifies exactly one message after session_start, and verifies that file uploads remain unavailable. Canonical API generation, the auth suite, all 31 voice tests, and the production build passed. Five gateway voice authorization tests also passed, including revocation during a write. This update was validated locally; earlier installed-browser evidence below describes its recorded revisions.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces:** web Config and agent chat; authenticated gateway configuration/device APIs.
- **Preconditions:** HTTPS or localhost, a paired browser, browser/OS speech support; select a locally available voice to test playback.
- **Steps:**
  1. Open Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio. Enable dictation/narration, select language/voice and try the sample.
  2. Change global silence to 15, dictate and pause: verify exactly one send after the interval. Test 0 (manual only), another value, empty capture, manual stop, conversation switch and hidden chat. Confirm the same value appears on another paired device.
  3. Read a response with headings, emphasis, lists, a link and a horizontal rule. Formatting must not be spoken; code such as `apt-get --yes` must retain literal punctuation. A final crab signature is silent, but a crab in the body remains content.
  4. Enable continuous reading; place `---` or a signature-only reply before another readable answer. The latter must play. Restored history and trim notices remain silent.
  5. Reload settings and switch the device selector: per-device choices remain isolated, while the silence timeout stays global. Revoke a technical device and confirm its voice API refuses access. No voice preference storage key is added to browser storage.
  6. Try unavailable local recognition: no online fallback. Browser-service mode and online voices remain explicit choices.
- **Expected after:** documented opt-in controls, durable per-device voice choices, one adjustable global silence deadline and readable narration.
- **Before on master:** these browser speech controls and preference APIs are absent.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- **Earlier layout revision:** 61aeff4bb (global silence, narration fixes and responsive settings/toolbar spacing); the corresponding integrated candidate uses the same feature changes.
- **Latest checks actually run:** 24 voice tests passed; configuration default/range test passed; canonical `cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- gen-api` passed; integrated TypeScript check and production WebUI build passed. The checks exercise the actual component speech-submission callback, global property save, zero-disable, final-results ordering, activity resets, empty/hidden/cancelled capture, early recognition end, signature filtering and continuous queue progress.
- **Historical baseline checks:** gateway paired-device tests (14), security-header tests (5), auth/session/UI tests and format/diff checks passed at earlier documented revisions. These are not reattributed to the new head.
- **CI status:** current head includes master 755bc9a4e. Its SQLite exception was approved and merged by maintainers in #12321; this PR does not introduce its own exception. The functional/layout source and installed bundle remain unchanged by that policy-only merge. Current-head CI is authoritative. The independent PR's shared SQLite advisory remains tracked by #12320; the checkout-only #12322 bridge was removed here after its registry-publication limitation was found. No advisory ignore was added. The preceding head's 32-bit check failed during runner `apt install` timeouts, before checking this code.
- **Coverage limits:** component tests simulate speech APIs. Actual microphone hardware, audible OS voice output, language pack downloads and browser-provider network behavior require device testing. New browser validation/deployment results will be reported separately, not inferred from unit tests.
- **Installed-browser validation:** synthetic microphone transcript, actual WebSocket/model completion, exactly one automatic send after **15,131 ms**, technical conversation deleted, global field verified at 15 in Browser Voice and Audio; a nondefault16-second value was saved, verified on disk/after reload, then restored to 15. Actual microphone hardware/audio playback are not claimed.
- **Responsive layout follow-up at 61aeff4bb:** label above the numeric input (8px gap), separate help and save row (16px gap), and nonshrinking 40px microphone/speaker buttons. Verified the installed UI at 1280px and 390px wide; both controls remain visible. The layout-only static update preserved configuration and binary and did not restart the daemon.

![Historical desktop voice settings before global controls/themed dropdowns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-desktop.png)

![Historical mobile layout before the global controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-mobile.png)

- **Earlier functional-field evidence (before the spacing follow-up):** cropped from the installed UI matching the feature changes at 3f70b1efc; the evidence branch adds only this image, without changing the reviewed feature head.

![Global browser voice silence setting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6423d16e3db0b77a369c815b7839f81bbe79d357/.pr-evidence/web-voice-global-silence-live.png)

- **Visual evidence provenance:** the following captures were originally recorded at 6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae and retained at the evidence revision below. They show the prior device selector, guide and controls; they do not show the newly added global field.

![Paired-device selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-devices-other-desktop.png)

![Settings and usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-desktop.png)

[Mobile chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-chat-mobile.png) · [Portuguese guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-pt.png)

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **Permissions:** same-origin microphone/on-device recognition is permitted; microphone and narration default disabled per device. Browser consent and user initiation are still required. Global silence defaults to 15 only after dictation is explicitly started.
- **External calls:** optional browser language-pack downloads, explicitly selected online recognition/voices; no microphone audio reaches the gateway.
- **Credentials:** own-device routes resolve the existing paired bearer under the live pairing guard; other-device management uses existing operator authorization. Global timeout reads/writes use the existing config property API and its authorization/validation. No credential is returned or logged by this feature.
- **Personal data in fixtures/docs:** none; synthetic content only.
- **Model-visible text:** recognized text follows the existing user draft/send path; no approval bypass or additional execution capability.

## Compatibility (required)

- **HTTP/config:** existing paired records receive disabled voice defaults; the new global field defaults to 15 when absent. Its range is validated on configuration writes/load. Rust struct-literal callers may need the new field or `..Default::default()`.
- **Config surface:** `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs`; existing device preference routes remain per-device. No new environment variable or transport endpoint.
- **Toolchain floor:** unchanged.
- **Upgrade:** build matching gateway/WebUI, enable desired device controls and adjust the global interval in Browser Voice and Audio. Cookie-only sessions without a paired-device identity cannot edit device preferences.

## Rollback

- Disable automatic sending by setting global silence to 0; microphone/narration/continuous reading can be disabled independently in the voice screen.
- For binary rollback, restore a verified prior binary; remove the new configuration key if rolling back to a version rejecting unknown fields. The nullable device-preference column can remain. Preserve state and credentials rather than blindly restoring an old database after accepted work.
- Observable failures: Config save/load errors, browser capture/playback errors or preference-API refusals. Global-setting load failure disables automatic submission rather than guessing a deadline.

### Localization

The existing voice guide/device strings retain their ten-language translations and English fallback. The six new global-setting strings are provided in English and Portuguese; other locales use the existing English fallback.


<!-- followup-20261110-b:start -->
## Additional review follow-up
Continuous reading now checks readiness, listening and speaking before parsing a queued Markdown answer. Added a regression demonstrating no repeated DOM conversion while the parent rerenders during playback; it fails before the fix and passes after. All 32 voice tests pass; the integrated WebUI production build passes.

Local evidence above is from the integrated candidate. Fresh hosted CI will run on the published branch commit; maintainer architecture/merge decisions remain unchanged.
<!-- followup-20261110-b:end -->

## Authenticated browser evidence

A paired Windows operator completed the real spoken-input, single automatic send and audible-reply check in Chrome and Edge on integrated revision `77c0b647d`. The [operator acceptance](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6880263250) and [screenshots](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6880323951) are available. The settings capture shows local dictation selected. The operator did not record browser build numbers or the recognition mode used for each recorded round trip.


## Earlier mobile interface and playback ownership (historical)

The screenshot below renders the production `BrowserVoiceSettings` component and stylesheet from PR commit `610484335` in a headed Chrome viewport at 390 CSS pixels. Device, voice and API data are synthetic. The image shows the reading-voice selector and the speech-speed row. Historical head `1f331f278` changes only the navigation wording in the book relative to the capture.

![Mobile Browser Voice and Audio settings with a reading voice and speech speed control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/850c9a854fb577686c5d6448914df6658ffb8278/.pr-evidence/web-voice-settings-mobile-610484335.png)

For the earlier evidence, integrated build `77c0b647d` used the paired voice changes through `bf0093778`, whose themed-dropdown patch has the same stable patch ID as integrated commit `ec761ae6f`. That build predates `2a70a0f90` and `fec38c9b9`. The older image above is historical. This update removes the nine stale captures from the PR branch and stores the new capture on a separate evidence ref.

```text
npm run test:voice
✔ stopping one pane does not cancel playback owned by another pane
✔ manual playback in a second pane shows the playback busy message
ℹ tests 34
ℹ pass 34
ℹ fail 0
```

The headed browser also opened the authenticated settings route on Jarvis and confirmed it remained accessible after reload. The screenshot is from the isolated PR fixture. The production check verified navigation and rendering.

The shared Security findings are tracked in #12505 (chrono and chrono-tz) and #12101 (zip 9.0.5). This voice PR does not alter the workspace dependency graph or advisory policy.



## Earlier evidence follow-up at 21dec7b (2026-11-18)

Head 21dec7b incorporates master bec292f. The actual production settings component was rendered in headed Chrome at 390 x 844 and 1280 x 1000 with synthetic device/API/voice data. The current mobile reading-voice selector and speed row are visible. At that historical head, 34 voice tests passed. Historical build provenance, screenshots and coverage limits: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6978640606 . These screenshots are kept on a separate evidence branch. Real hardware acceptance from the historical integrated build is not reattributed to the current head.



## Current source follow-up (2026-11-18)

The refreshed source includes master 3773cae2d7 (#12552). The shared page capture/playback owners prevent cross-pane echo. They also allow the same pane to switch its cancelled narration to dictation even when the browser reports stale speaking/pending flags. The base component suite passes 38 tests; the separate OIDC extension passes 39. Exact published heads and test tails are recorded in the follow-up comment. Hosted CI must still validate the refreshed revisions.

prs.title: feat(web): provision catalog credentials in external cloud vaults
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch: `master`. Depends on #12481. Related #12422 and #12373.
- Provide operator-only create and rotate for 1Password Connect, Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, and Google Secret Manager.
- Reuse the external reference form and provider-scoped editable defaults. Retain explicit linking, blank preservation on replacement, and catalog-only deletion.
- Use verified HTTPS, per-operation write authorization, and configured vault or name scope. Store only encrypted references. Existing read adapters still use their own identity.

### What this does, simply

An operator can provision a value from the same Secrets form regardless of which configured vault holds it. Azure and 1Password check for a name collision before creating. Their APIs provide no atomic conditional create by name, so configure a dedicated single-writer namespace. Google may create a resource before its first version fails. The UI directs the operator to check, link, and replace in that case.

## Testing

### How you can test

Enable one provider with a disposable prefix according to the WebUI guide. Use a scoped test identity. Add a synthetic value, verify the reference, replace it and confirm it advances, then delete the catalog alias. A blank replacement preserves the external value. Repeat with an existing name to see the conflict.

### How I tested

Added mock HTTP tests for all four providers. Tests cover expected request bodies, routes, AWS signing headers, scope validation, collision handling, 1Password IDs, and Google's partial-create recovery. `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib cloud_vault_write::tests` passed all five tests. The integrated WebUI passed TypeScript build and Vite production bundling. Real accounts are not available in this environment.

## Security and privacy

- New capability and external calls: yes, opt-in operator-only writes to a configured scope via verified HTTPS. Redirects and proxy environment routing are disabled.
- Secrets: transient write authority and value. Neither is included in catalog responses, audit output or persistent configuration.
- Personal data and untrusted model inputs: none added. Provider responses are never forwarded to the model.

## Compatibility and rollback

Remove the writer prefix to disable writes while preserving existing references. Reverting the code restores link-only behavior for these four providers. No migration is required. To remove an external resource, manage it in the vault.


### Integrated smoke test

The Linux release built with XMPP enabled. A disposable OpenBao KV v2 instance over verified TLS and an isolated gateway passed create, path denial, collision, versioned replacement, blank preservation, deletion of the alias and catalog-response redaction through the shared mutation route. After deployment to the Jarvis lab, the gateway, WebUI, OIDC and XMPP were healthy and the SSH helper remained Rust. The four cloud writers remain opt-in and unconfigured in that environment.

### Review and dependencies update

The branch inherits the catalog and manifest-validation corrections from #12408 and #12402 through the OpenBao work in #12481. The four cloud adapters are covered by mocked provider HTTP tests. The real OpenBao smoke test covers the shared mutation route. Live provider validation remains open for contributors with access.

### OpenBao managed authentication and live validation

The OpenBao form uses the server's configured identity and never asks the operator for a vault write token. It preserves the editable reference suggested from the mount, prefix, alias and field. Add writes the value through the gateway. Link existing saves only the reference and performs no vault write. The server can use the existing OpenBao Agent token sink from BAO_TOKEN_PATH or a dedicated ZEROCLAW_OPENBAO_WRITE_TOKEN_FILE.

Validated on the integrated Jarvis build 0504477e9. The operator confirmed a real WebUI save without a token field after the OpenBao policy was scoped to the configured credential prefix. A synthetic OpenBao API test with the Jarvis identity verified create, read and rotation; the fixture was removed. Validation here covers OpenBao. The other cloud providers retain their own authorization flows.


## RFC scope and deployment status

Depends on #12517. Approval and merge are conditional on acceptance of RFC #12422. This remains a draft. The OpenBao implementation is in actual operational use on our company's Jarvis production server for live testing, with existing secrets and skills. Provider-specific claims retain their documented test coverage. We will adapt these features as the RFC evolves.


## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.

## Managed credential RPC placement

Depends on #12563, the separately reviewed bounded Core Team exception record for the generic-RPC credential write guard. The guard stays enabled; this feature does not approve its own placement. The record must land before this feature merges.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch** `master`
- **What changed and why**
  - A fresh SQLite installation can lack a typed storage alias. Both banners then displayed `Memory: none` while SQLite was in use.
  - During channel startup, the banner now reads the name from the agent's initialized memory handle. The CLI selects the enabled runtime agent and uses the same memory routing rule as the constructor to report its backend without opening a store.
  - Markdown and disabled agents use their local backend. SQL, Qdrant and Lucid agents use the install-wide backend. The auto-save field continues to show the install-wide setting used by the channel runtime.
- **Scope boundary** Memory backend reporting in `zeroclaw status` and the channel startup banner, plus their regression coverage.
- **Blast radius** The memory constructor and reporting code share a private routing decision. The five CLI cases and the initialized-store test cover its behavior.
- **Linked issues and prior work** Closes #9896. Supersedes #9898.
- **Labels** Pending the PR labeler and maintainer intake.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The component regression launches the real `zeroclaw status` command with temporary installation directories.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change** Pull-request CI is pending. The local component test exercises the linked CLI and Fluent output. A memory unit test builds actual agent stores for local Markdown, disabled memory and a shared SQLite alias.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any** The local tests ran on macOS with Rust 1.98.0. Hosted platform validation is pending.
- **Commands run and tail output**

  ```text
  cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0

  cargo +1.98.0 test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-memory --lib configured_memory_backend_matches_the_opened_agent_store
  test tests::configured_memory_backend_matches_the_opened_agent_store ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed

  cargo +1.98.0 test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features agent-runtime --test component status_memory_cli
  test component::status_memory_cli::status_reports_the_runtime_agents_backend_and_configured_auto_save ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed

  cargo +1.98.0 build --locked --offline -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features agent-runtime,channel-filesystem --bin zeroclaw
  exit 0
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Restoring `src/main.rs` from base commit `cda933e6b9` made the component test fail on the first fixture. It read `none (auto-save: on)` where it expected `sqlite (auto-save: on)`. Restoring the candidate source byte for byte made all five cases pass again. The stock v0.9.0 binary also reproduced the bare SQLite case. I started a real filesystem channel in a temporary install with a Markdown agent over global SQLite, observed the channel banner, and verified a clean shutdown after SIGINT.
- **Visual interface evidence** Exact plain-text output.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path** Signed head `6706aa3e23`, tree `eb629c1765`, English locale, `zeroclaw --config-dir <temporary directory> status` and `zeroclaw --config-dir <temporary directory> channel start`. The checked-in regression is `tests/component/status_memory_cli.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence** These are the memory lines from standalone CLI runs with the default configuration and with a Markdown agent and auto-save disabled.

  ```text
  🧠 Memory:         sqlite (auto-save: on)
  🧠 Memory:         markdown (auto-save: off)
  ```

  Channel startup with the Markdown agent produced the following lines.

  ```text
    🤖 Model:    test-model (agent: worker)
    🧠 Memory:   markdown (auto-save: off)
    📡 Channels: filesystem.local
    🤖 Agents:   worker
  ```

- **Action or changed state and observed result** The component test also covers explicit bare SQLite, an agent selecting disabled memory, and a runtime agent that differs from the ACP default.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why** Validation focused on the changed CLI and memory-store paths. The full workspace suite is delegated to CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- Risk and mitigation for affirmative answers are inapplicable.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? The existing human-readable memory line now reports the selected backend correctly. Its format, flags and configuration fields are preserved.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps for existing users are unnecessary.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command** `git revert 6706aa3e23` on a review branch, or revert the merge commit after integration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms** A status line identifying a different backend from the configured runtime agent or its initialized memory handle.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- **Superseded PR and author** #9898 by @ArmanAvanesyan.
- **Scope carried forward** The earlier PR identified both display paths and the bare SQLite and unmaterialized-alias regressions. This revision uses the initialized channel handle and reproduces the current constructor's precedence in CLI status, including an ACP default that differs from the runtime agent.
- **Human co-author trailer added** Yes.

prs.title: fix(ci): bind removed PR files to the merge-base in the risk report
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The PR Risk Report fails closed on every PR that deletes a file: `PR file evidence is not bound to the captured head SHA`. A removed file has no content at head, so GitHub reports its `contents_url`/`blob_url`/`raw_url` at the **merge-base** of the PR base and head, but `validate_files` required every file to be bound to head.
  - Removed files are now required to be bound to the merge-base; every other status stays bound to the captured head SHA, unchanged.
  - The merge-base is resolved with `GET compare/{base}...{head}?per_page=1` and fails closed unless the response's `base_commit` is the captured base SHA. It is fetched only when the PR file list contains a removal, so PRs without deletions make no extra API call.
  - The PR `base.sha` cannot stand in for the merge-base: once `master` moves past the fork point they differ (live examples: #12589 and #12586 report removed files at merge-base `dfe8ab35`, while `base.sha` is `ad4c1f6c`).
- **Scope boundary:** Only the file-evidence SHA binding changes. Classification, the policy file, the workflow, labels, and the report schema are untouched. Not addressed here: the 9530 test-only proof reads base-side source at `base_sha` rather than the merge-base, which could compare against the wrong pre-image on a PR behind `master`; that is a separate concern.
- **Blast radius:** The report-only `PR Risk Report` workflow (`pr-risk-labeler.yml`), which loads this script from the trusted ref. No mutations, labels, or other workflows are affected.
- **Linked issue(s):** None. Observed failing on #12443 (run 44688227863), #12521, #12589, and #12586.

### What this does, simply

Every PR gets an automated "risk report" that looks at which files changed. As a safety measure, it checks that the file list GitHub gave it really belongs to the exact commit being evaluated. But when a PR deletes a file, GitHub points that file at the older commit where it still existed, not at the PR's latest commit, so the safety check rejected it and the whole job failed. Any PR that deleted even one file got a red check.

This change tells the check where deleted files are supposed to point: the commit where the PR branched off `master`. It asks GitHub for that commit and verifies deleted files against it. Everything else is checked exactly as strictly as before, and anything that doesn't line up still fails the job.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. The fix only takes effect after merge (the workflow fetches the script from the trusted ref), so an A/B run of the script against a live PR that deletes files is the most direct check.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** CI workflow script (`scripts/github/pr_risk_label.py`); no `surface`/`channel` runtime interface.
- **Setup / preconditions:** `gh` authenticated with read access to `zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw`; `export GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)`.
- **Steps to run:**
  ```sh
  git show upstream/master:scripts/github/pr_risk_label.py > target/old.py
  for s in target/old.py scripts/github/pr_risk_label.py; do
    python3 "$s" --repository zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw --pr-number 12443 \
      --policy .github/risk-labeler.yml --summary target/summary.md; echo "exit=$?"
  done
  ```
- **Expected on this branch (after):** exit 0 with a report (`"proposed_risk": "risk:medium"`, `"mutations_attempted": false`).
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** exit 1 with `{"error": "PR file evidence is not bound to the captured head SHA", ...}`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Validate GitHub helper scripts` (`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/github -p '*_test.py'`) runs `pr_risk_label_test.py`, which now covers the removed-file binding.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The `PR Risk Report` job on this PR runs the script from `master`, not this branch, so it does not exercise the fix. The live A/B runs below cover that gap.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```text
  $ python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/github -p '*_test.py'
  OK
  $ python3 -m unittest scripts.github.pr_risk_label_test
  Ran 43 tests in 0.073s

  OK
  ```
  New tests: removed file bound to the merge-base in a mixed PR and in a removal-only PR; merge-base not resolved when no file is removed; removed file bound to head, base, or an unrelated SHA fails closed; removed file with no resolved merge-base fails closed; a non-removed file bound to the merge-base fails closed; `get_merge_base` builds the expected compare path and fails closed on a malformed response, missing `merge_base_commit`, invalid SHA, or a `base_commit` that is not the captured base. The existing `test_9530_negative_statuses_and_mixed_files_propose_high` built its `removed` case with a head-bound URL that GitHub never produces; it now uses a merge-base-bound fixture and reproduced the CI error before the fix.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Ran the `master` script and this branch's script read-only against live PRs:

  | PR | Shape | `master` | this branch |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | #12443 | deletes 2 files | exit 1, head-SHA error | exit 0, `risk:medium` |
  | #12589 | deletes files; `base.sha` ≠ merge-base | exit 1, head-SHA error | exit 0, `risk:medium` |
  | #12521 | deletes files | exit 1, head-SHA error | exit 0, `risk:medium` |
  | #12599 | no deletions (regression) | n/a | exit 0, `risk:medium` |

  Not verified: GitHub Enterprise API origins (the compare request goes through the same validated `request` path as the existing calls).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `681800347c`, `scripts/github/pr_risk_label.py` CLI, output quoted above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See table above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo fmt`/`clippy`/`test` skipped: no Rust changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The compare endpoint is covered by the workflow's existing `contents: read`.
- New external network calls? Yes. One extra read-only `GET` to the same GitHub API origin.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The new call is `GET compare/{base}...{head}` on the configured API origin through the existing read-only, origin-validated `GitHubAPI.request`. Both SHAs come from `parse_pr_metadata` (validated 40-hex), the response must echo the captured base SHA, and the returned merge-base is validated as a SHA. Binding stays fail-closed: removed files must match the resolved merge-base exactly, and removed-file evidence without a resolved merge-base is rejected. The existing post-evaluation re-read of head/base still rejects a PR that moves mid-run, and the merge-base is a pure function of those two SHAs.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 681800347c`. The workflow picks up the reverted script from the trusted ref on its next run.

## Summary



- **Base branch:** `master`

- **What changed and why:** Match cached HTTP clients to their owning Tokio runtime, so a client whose dispatcher ended cannot be reused by a later runtime. Preserve one existing cache entry per service/timeout profile and the current proxy-generation invalidation.

- **Scope boundary:** No global test serialization, disabled HTTP pooling, new proxy authority, or provider retry policy.

- **Blast radius:** Shared runtime proxy HTTP client builders, including provider calls.

- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12236 and #12238. This addresses the production cache ownership rather than disabling pooling only in tests.



### What this does, simply



A cached client could outlive the runtime that owned its connection tasks. A later request then failed with “dispatch task is gone”. Cache lookup now checks the current runtime identity, and clients built without a current runtime are not cached. Ordinary calls on one runtime still reuse their client.



## Testing (required)



### How you can test (when useful)



- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; the regression starts a real local HTTP server and performs requests from two successive runtimes.



### How I tested



- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Fresh CI requested; pending.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Full workspace and platform CI pending; no live provider credentials used.
