prs.title: feat(memory)!: retire the local LLM response cache
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The local LLM response cache almost never served a reply, so it is removed. A hit needed all of these: temperature exactly `0.0`; an agent with no tools; no hooks, memory injection, native-thinking override or images; and a single provider with no fallbacks. Every `Agent` turn also stamps the user message with the time to the second (`[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]`) before the key is computed, so even a qualifying turn hit only when the same conversation arrived within the same second. Channel turns run through `run_tool_call_loop`, which never read the cache.
  - The code that existed only to guard it goes too:
    - `ModelProvider::has_stable_request_identity` and its wrapper implementations;
    - the provider context-truncation flag (`take_last_provider_context_truncation`), whose only reader was the cache write guard;
    - `ObserverEvent::CacheHit` and `CacheMiss`, plus the three Prometheus counters fed by them.
  - The four `memory.response_cache_*` keys are retired through `RETIRED_KEYS` with a shared reason in every CLI locale. A config that still has them loads with a `Removed` notice and the next save drops them, instead of the keys being silently ignored.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Provider prompt caching does not change: Anthropic `cache_control` and `cache_ttl`, compatible-provider `cache_passthrough`, Bedrock `cachePoint`, OpenRouter markers.
  - `VisionOverrideProvider::factory_leaf` still wraps every factory-built provider. With the identity mark gone, that wrapper is a pass-through when no `vision` override is set. Going back to wrapping only when `vision` is set is left for a follow-up.
  - Existing `response_cache.db` files are not deleted. `V2_MEMORY_DATA_NAMES` still lists the file so the V2 → V3 directory migration keeps moving it.
- **Blast radius:**
  - **Agent turn paths:** both `Agent::turn` and `turn_streamed` lose a branch that ran a skip check every turn and never fired in ordinary use.
  - **Config load and migration:** configs that set `[memory] response_cache_*`.
  - **Prometheus scrapes:** `zeroclaw_cache_hits_total`, `zeroclaw_cache_misses_total` and `zeroclaw_cache_tokens_saved_total` disappear.
  - **Rust API consumers:**
    - `AgentBuilder::response_cache`;
    - `zeroclaw_memory::{ResponseCache, create_response_cache}`;
    - `ModelProvider::has_stable_request_identity`;
    - `ObserverEvent::CacheHit` and `CacheMiss` (the enum is already `#[non_exhaustive]`);
    - `zeroclaw_providers::reliable::take_last_provider_context_truncation`.
- **Linked issue(s):**
  - Closes #12611.
  - Related #8321: its cache-policy question has no subject once this lands.
  - Related #12460: open; it adds tests for the module this deletes.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw could save a model's reply on disk and hand it back when exactly the same request came in again. In practice, almost nothing qualified. Ordinary agents have tools, the setting was off by default, and every message carries the current time to the second, so two requests matched only if they arrived within the same second.

The feature still cost something. It added a check to every turn, kept a file of prompts and replies on disk, and needed several pieces of supporting code in the provider layer. It also had its own share of bug fixes.

This PR removes the feature and its supporting code. If your config still sets the old keys, ZeroClaw tells you they were removed and carries on. Provider-side prompt caching, which is where repeated prompts actually save money, is unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`, for the config retirement notice; the rest is a removal covered by tests.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a scratch config directory with a current (`schema_version = 4`) config whose `[memory]` table sets `response_cache_enabled = true`.
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw --config-dir <dir> config migrate`, then `zeroclaw --config-dir <dir> config get memory.response_cache_enabled`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `migrate` prints `warning: dropped retired config key `memory.response_cache_enabled` …: the local LLM response cache was removed; provider prompt caching still applies` and removes the key from the file; `config get` reports `Unknown property`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the keys are ordinary schema fields, so `migrate` keeps them and `config get` prints the stored value.

### How I tested

All Rust and docs gates ran on dev-box (Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0), inside a throwaway `HOME` with a private network namespace for the test runs.

**At `446612a351` (this head):**

```text
cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check                        -> clean
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
                                                          -> Finished, 0 warnings
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib              -> test result: ok. 1998 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
```

**At `f5f2881f7a`:** the docs gates, plus the clippy command above, also clean. That commit differs from this head only by one test in `migration.rs`.

```text
DOCS_FILES=<the 2 changed pages> BASE_SHA=dfc70a2b49 scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  -> No prose em-dashes in changed docs files. Linting: 2 file(s). Summary: 0 error(s)
scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  -> Collected 1 added link(s) from 2 docs file(s). Checked 1 local docs link target(s).
```

**At `5412d514ab`:** this head minus the two new `zeroclaw-config` tests (+43 lines, test-only).

```text
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --all-targets --no-default-features --features "$(xtask cli-only feature set)" -- -D warnings
                                                          -> Finished, 0 warnings
cargo test --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
  -> 142 test binaries: 20544 passed; 4 failed; 47 ignored
```

None of the four failures comes from this branch. Each was rerun alone, and the two that still failed were also run on `master` `dfc70a2b49`:

- `zeroclaw-providers` `openai::…::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` passes alone on both this branch and `master`. It fails on both whenever it shares a process with `openai::tests::responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config`, which leaks the runtime proxy into it. Open PR #11907 fixes that.
- `zeroclaw-providers` `openai::tests::responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config` passes alone. It failed only under parallel interference.

prs.title: test(providers): hold the runtime proxy guard in the tool-round wire fixture
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` fails intermittently in full `zeroclaw-providers` runs. The cause is shared state, not timing. `responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config` and `codex_responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_after_construction` point the process-wide runtime proxy at a throwaway server for `model_provider.openai`. They serialise on `RuntimeProxyTestGuard`; the tool-round fixture (`wire_body`) did not take that guard. When it overlapped one of them, its OpenAI clients were built through the proxy, and its request went to the proxy fixture instead of its own server.
  - That gives three failure modes, all of which I've seen locally:
    - a decode error, when the proxy answers with its own JSON
    - "Connection refused", once the proxy test has stopped its server
    - the fixture's 5 s timeout, when a stream never sees its final event
  - `wire_body` now holds the guard for its lifetime.
- **Scope boundary:** test-only. No production code changes. I didn't audit other fixtures for the same pattern.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-providers` tests only. The tool-round test now waits for a running proxy test instead of overlapping it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11467 (added the test)

### What this does, simply

Two tests temporarily switch on a global HTTP proxy for the OpenAI provider, and they take a shared lock so nothing else is affected while they do. One newer test didn't take that lock. When it happened to run at the same moment, its requests went through the other test's fake proxy, and it failed for reasons that had nothing to do with what it checks. It now takes the lock too.

prs.title: feat(oidc): accept untyped access tokens and declared claim names for JWKS
prs.body:
> **Stacked:** Depends on #12497 and on the ADR-016 exception in #12608. Until #12497 merges this PR also shows its commit (`140e9e594f`); review `fd2bb3da4c` and `26b2d63d68`.
>
> **Update (`26b2d63d68`):** after review on #12496 and #12498, a token accepted through the `require_at_jwt = false` waiver must carry exactly the configured audience. An ID token's `aud` may list audiences beyond its client (OIDC Core §2), so a nonce-free ID token with `aud: [client, api]` previously passed. Typed tokens are unchanged.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Okta and Entra ID are required for v1.0 (#12496), and the JWKS verifier refused both. Okta access tokens have no header `typ` and name the client in `cid`. Entra ID tokens have `typ: JWT`, use `uti` instead of `jti`, and name the client only in `azp`, including for service principals. Entra has no introspection endpoint to fall back to.
  - **Untyped tokens, without weakening token purpose.** `require_at_jwt = false` (previously rejected for `jwks`) now admits a header with no `typ` or `typ: JWT` only when `audience` is an API identifier that no client signs in as: not `client_id`, not in `interactive_clients`/`service_clients`/`allowed_authorized_parties`/`service_profile_map`, and not a client of another `[oidc.*]` entry for the same issuer. Every ID token's `aud` is the client it was issued to (OIDC Core), so an ID token cannot carry that audience. Config validation enforces this; the verifier re-checks the entry's own clients through the same `OidcConfig::audience_shared_with_a_client` so a provider built from unvalidated config is still safe. Other header types (`logout+jwt`, `dpop+jwt`, ...), `nonce`, and non-access purpose markers are still refused.
  - **Declared claim names instead of vendor detection.** `client_id_claim` (default `client_id`) and `token_id_claim` (default `jti`). Chosen over built-in fallbacks (`cid`/`uti`) because `azp` means different things on Keycloak (stamped on user tokens of service clients) and Entra (the client of every token): only an operator declaration can safely let `azp` prove a *service* client, and fallbacks would grow into a per-IdP mapping table. A declared client claim has no `azp` fallback and must agree with any present `client_id` or `azp`. Both are JWKS-only and refused for introspection (RFC 7662 answers use `client_id`).
  - Removes the now-unread `Claims.jti` field; the token id is read from the declared claim.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to introspection, typed (`at+jwt`) tokens with default claim names, the resolver, or refresh. Okta and Entra are NOT added to "Tested providers": they still need real-tenant verification (an acceptance gate in #12496).
- **Blast radius:** JWKS bearer verification for every surface (RPC/WSS, gateway, dashboard). With defaults the accepted set is unchanged; the new behavior is reachable only by setting `require_at_jwt = false` or the new claim keys.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12497, Depends on #12608. Related #8289, Related #12496

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw checks that a sign-in token is really an *access* token meant for it, and not an *ID token* (which only proves someone logged in to some app). It did this by requiring a "this is an access token" label that Okta and Microsoft Entra ID don't put on their tokens, so neither could sign in. This adds a second, equally strict way to tell them apart, based on who the token is addressed to: ZeroClaw's own API identifier, which no app ever logs in as, so an ID token can never be addressed to it. It also lets the operator say which field a provider uses for the app's name and the token's ID, rather than ZeroClaw guessing per vendor. Existing setups behave exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Verification is covered with signed tokens against a mock JWKS issuer; real Okta/Entra tenants are a tracked gate in #12496.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust lint/test jobs cover `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-runtime` (verifier) and `zeroclaw-gateway` (consumer). Docs style covers `identity-providers.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No real Okta or Entra tenant in CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (CI-pinned toolchain `1.98.0`, on `fd2bb3da4c`)

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output, exit 0)

$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 19s

$ cargo +1.98.0 check --workspace --all-targets
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 17s

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-config
test result: ok. 1999 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
(integration targets: 106, 9, 8, 5, 1, 1 passed)

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::auth_provider
test result: ok. 139 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6083 filtered out

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib oidc
test result: ok. 49 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 867 filtered out

$ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/identity-providers.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Tests were written first. Config tests failed to compile (missing fields); of the 9 new verifier tests, the 4 asserting newly accepted shapes failed on behavior before the implementation, while the 5 refusal tests already passed, confirming nothing previously refused was relied on. New verifier coverage: untyped refused while typing is required; `typ: JWT` and no-`typ` accepted once waived with a separate audience; other header types, an untyped ID token (`aud` = client), and `nonce` still refused when waived; the verifier refuses untyped tokens without separation even if config validation was skipped; Okta `cid` names the client and is refused when undeclared; declared claim contradicted by `client_id` refused; declared claim has no `azp` fallback; Entra service token (`typ: JWT`, `azp`, `uti`) resolves to a service principal only when `azp` is declared, and is refused with defaults; token id read from the declared claim only. New config coverage: defaults, separation against `client_id` (empty and equal), each client list, a same-issuer sibling entry (and not a different-issuer one), TOML round-trip with an Okta shape, claim-name format, JWKS-only. Not verified: real Okta/Entra tokens.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `fd2bb3da4c`
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `cargo test --workspace` skipped: changes are confined to `OidcConfig` and the OIDC provider; affected crates were tested and the workspace type-checked.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (synthetic ids, `example.com`/`example.okta.com`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: This changes which bearer tokens authenticate. Risk: an ID token accepted as an access token. Mitigation: opt-in only (`require_at_jwt = false`); accepted only when the audience is provably not any configured client of that issuer, enforced at config load and re-checked in the verifier from one shared definition; non-access header types, `nonce`, and payload purpose markers remain refused; tests mint an untyped ID token and assert refusal. Residual (documented, and recorded in #12496): the IdP must never sign anyone in *as* the API registration itself, which ZeroClaw cannot observe. `azp` proves a service client only when the operator declares it as the client claim; the Keycloak default (azp never proves a service) is unchanged.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (defaults unchanged; `require_at_jwt = false` was previously a validation error for `jwks`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: `[oidc.<alias>] client_id_claim`, `token_id_claim`; `require_at_jwt = false` newly permitted for `jwks` under the audience-separation rule.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: None required. Okta: `require_at_jwt = false`, `client_id_claim = "cid"`, `audience` = the authorization server's audience. Entra ID: v2.0 tokens (`accessTokenAcceptedVersion = 2`), `require_at_jwt = false`, `client_id_claim = "azp"`, `token_id_claim = "uti"`, `audience` = the API app's client ID (a separate registration from the signing-in client), plus scopes from #12497.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert fd2bb3da4c`. Per-deployment, set `require_at_jwt = true` and remove `client_id_claim`/`token_id_claim` to return to exact prior verification without a code change.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[oidc.<alias>] require_at_jwt` (opt-in), `client_id_claim`, `token_id_claim`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** After a revert, entries with `require_at_jwt = false` fail config validation ("require_at_jwt must be true"), so affected deployments surface the problem at load rather than silently. Mis-configuration shows as `-32010` / "OIDC authentication refused" for Okta/Entra users.

prs.title: fix(mcp): send the text alone when structuredContent is the FastMCP result wrapper
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - #10397 sends only the text of a `tools/call` result when `structuredContent` copies it, but it recognises a copy only when the text parses as JSON equal to `structuredContent`.
  - The MCP Python SDK's FastMCP wraps the return value of a tool whose return type is not an object as `structuredContent: {"result": <value>}`. Every `-> str` tool on such a server therefore still sends the pretty-printed envelope, with its payload twice.
  - `all_text_content` now also accepts that single-field wrapper, when its value is the joined text (a string return) or the value the text serializes (any other return). The check moves into a small helper, `structured_copy_of_text`.
- **Scope boundary:** only what counts as a lossless copy changes. The rest of the compaction rules from #10397 are unchanged: plain text blocks only, known envelope keys only, `isError` false. A wrapper with a second field, a different value, or a key other than `result` still keeps the full envelope. Binary and resource handling are untouched.
- **Blast radius:** `format_mcp_tool_result_for_model` in `zeroclaw-tools`, the one place an MCP result becomes model-facing text (`mcp_tool.rs`). Results from string-returning FastMCP tools get shorter. Every other result is byte-identical to master.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12604. Related #10394, #10397.

### What this does, simply

When an MCP tool answers, ZeroClaw hands the answer to the model. Many tool servers send the same answer twice: once as text, and once as a structured copy. Since #10397, ZeroClaw drops the copy when it is identical to the text, so the model reads the answer once.

Servers built with the official Python SDK package the copy of a plain-text answer differently: they put it inside a `{"result": ...}` wrapper. ZeroClaw did not recognise that wrapper as a copy, so for those tools the model read every answer twice, plus the JSON wrapping around it.

This PR recognises the wrapper when it holds exactly the same answer. Anything that carries more than the text is still sent in full.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the unit tests build the exact SDK result shapes, and the change is a pure function of the result JSON.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` and `Lint` cover `zeroclaw-tools`; the new unit tests run in the default suite.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output** (on `19a9dd37be`, master `dfc70a2b49`):
  ```
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  # exit 0
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- embedded_resource     # test result: ok. 49 passed; 0 failed
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings # exit 0
  RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-tools  # exit 0
  scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/embedded_resource.rs  # passed
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - With master's comparison restored and the new tests kept, `mcp_intake_wrapped_string_result_sends_the_text_alone` and `mcp_intake_wrapped_value_result_sends_the_text_alone` fail, and `mcp_intake_wrapper_that_differs_from_the_text_keeps_the_envelope` passes. So the tests pin the gap, not the existing behaviour.
  - The wrap rule matches the SDK: `mcp/server/fastmcp/utilities/func_metadata.py` (`mcp>=1.10`) wraps primitive and generic return types in a model with a single `result` field.
  - On a real FastMCP server with 18 string-returning tools, 444 of 444 stored results held their text twice. Not verified: the separate `fastmcp` 2.x package. The check reads only the result's values, not the tool's output schema, so any server that wraps the same way is covered.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace test suite. Only `zeroclaw-tools` changed, and CI runs the rest.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The model sees the same tool text, once instead of twice. The compaction remains exact-equality only, so nothing the server sent beyond that text is dropped.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes

prs.title: fix(web): show a detached chat turn and load its answer when it ends
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - When a dashboard chat socket closes mid-turn and reopens while the turn is still running, the page reloads the transcript once, before the turn is stored, and nothing reloads it again: the answer stays missing until a page reload or a conversation switch (#12107).
  - Hydration now asks `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` before it loads the stored transcript (asked after it, a turn ending between the two reads would leave its answer unloaded). While the turn is `running` there, the page shows it as running (before the composer unlocks, so it does not offer to send into it) and asks again every 2 s. Once the state leaves `running`, it loads the transcript once more. The gateway sets `idle` or `error` only after it has persisted the turn (`ws.rs`), so that load has the answer, or the stored outcome of a failed turn.
  - The watch ends without a reload on the next hydration, a conversation switch or clear, a model switch (a clear or model switch also stops one that has not started yet, while the first check or the transcript load is still out), unmount, and when its socket closes (the reopen reloads and asks again). A check still in flight when the watch ends is ignored. A failed check, including the 404 of a gateway without session persistence, reads as "not running": the page keeps today's single load and never retries in a loop. So does a check without an answer within 10 s (`STATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`): each check has its own deadline, and the page stops awaiting it at the deadline or when the watch ends, so a stuck request can neither keep the composer locked nor keep the turn shown as running. A daemon restarted mid-turn settles the abandoned turn to `error` (`recover_abandoned_session_turns`), which also ends the watch.
  - Because the check runs after any hydration, a page loaded while its conversation's turn runs (a reload, or a return from another conversation) also shows the turn and loads the answer when it ends.
  - A stored `running` state can outlive its turn: the gateway ignores errors on its state writes (`let _ = backend.set_session_state(...)` in `ws.rs`), so a failed `idle` write leaves `running` until the next restart. A page watching such a turn would stay locked, and Stop did nothing, because the abort route's `no_active_response` answer was discarded. Stop now reads that answer. The gateway also gives it in the moment between a turn's end (its cancel token removed) and its `idle` write, so the answer alone does not end the watch: two state checks that both start after it must still read the same turn id `running` (a check already out when Stop was refused does not count). Then the watch ends like a finished turn, with one reload, and later loads on this page do not lock on that turn id again. A different turn, or one without a turn id, is never treated as stale. This assumes the gateway's tail from token removal to the `idle` write takes well under one poll interval (2 s); it is a transcript write and a state write.
- **Scope boundary:** Web dashboard only (`web/src`); no gateway or API change: the state route already exists. A turn streaming on the page's own socket is not watched. A conversation switch still does not abort a detached turn (it aborts a live one, as before); Stop aborts a watched turn through the existing abort route, and the watch then loads the outcome. Accounts whose chat goes through the core (one conversation per socket) are unchanged: there is nothing to reload. No partial-answer replay while the turn runs; the answer appears when it is stored. Not covered, as possible follow-ups: an "outcome unknown" notice or tool-card settling across a reload; a deadline on the transcript load itself (`GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`, unchanged here and signal-less on master); a turn that another client starts in the same conversation, which this page does not see live at any time (a dashboard socket receives turn frames only for its own prompts; the multi-viewer direction is #9002 and #11185), so a turn started while the transcript loads is shown at the next load, as one started just after it would be; and the known limit pinned in `chatHydration.logic.test.ts` (#11571), where a prompt another client committed with identical text hides the same prompt in flight here: transcript rows carry no turn id, so that needs a server change. A stale `running` state is handled per page: a reload, another tab or another device locks again until Stop is pressed there too; settling such a row on the server (for example in the abort route when no turn is registered) is a separate gateway change.
- **Blast radius:** `AgentContext` hydration, the socket close handler, and Stop's handling of the abort answer. One extra `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` per transcript load (a gateway without session persistence answers it with 404), plus one every 2 s only while a detached turn runs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12107. Related #9002 (the wider reconnect contract), #11571 (keeps the in-flight prompt on reload), #11965 (introduced the reload on reopen), #11185 (server-side session-owned turns for RPC clients; no dashboard change).

### What this does, simply

The gateway keeps working on a chat turn after the browser loses its connection, but it saves the turn only when it finishes. If the browser reconnected before that, it fetched the conversation too early, got no answer, and never looked again, so the chat sat idle with the answer missing. Now the browser asks the gateway whether the turn is still running, shows it as running if so, and fetches the conversation again as soon as the gateway reports it finished. It stops asking when the turn ends, when the user moves on, or when anything goes wrong, so it cannot loop. If the gateway's record wrongly says a turn is still running, pressing Stop now unlocks the chat after two checks instead of leaving it stuck.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Session persistence on (the default) and a turn that runs at least ~20 s (for example a shell tool running `sleep 20`).
- **Steps to run:** Send the turn. While it runs, drop the connection briefly (devtools offline for a few seconds, or restart a proxy in front of the gateway) so the socket closes and reopens. Wait for the turn to finish. Separately: reload the page while a turn runs.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** After the reopen (or reload) the turn shows as running and the composer stays locked; when the turn finishes, the answer appears on its own and the composer unlocks. The prompt appears once.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** After the reopen the page stops showing the turn; the answer does not appear until the page is reloaded or the conversation switched.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the web test jobs run `test:contexts`, which includes `sessionLifecycle.test.ts`, where the new tests live next to the existing reopen test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI has no browser test; the network-drop behaviour is covered by the manual browser check below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (on this head, Node with the generated API files from an xtask web build)
  - `npm run typecheck`: clean
  - `npm run test:contexts`: `ℹ pass 159` / `ℹ fail 0` (`sessionLifecycle.test.ts`: 91 pass, 28 new)
  - `npm test`: 174 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:auth`: 247 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:navigation`: 9 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:permissions`: 34 pass, 0 fail
  - `git diff --check`, `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` on the changed files: clean
- **Rebased 2026-11-17 onto master `cda933e6b` (head `263acc119`), then server-side onto `1c8f2b59b` on 2026-11-19 (head `f84cfd0d9`, all three commits patch-identical by `git range-diff`) for the advisory fix in #12516.** Two conflicts with master, both in tests: the `/api/config/list` mock in `sessionLifecycle.test.ts` (kept master's `configListEntries` and this PR's abort route), and the runtime mock in master's new `contextMeter.dom.test.ts` (#12074), which lacked this PR's `getState`; it now answers `idle`, folded into the first commit so every commit type-checks. The second commit is unchanged (`git range-diff`). On this head: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` 180 pass; `npm run test:auth` 250 pass; `npm run test:contexts` 169 pass; `npm run test:permissions` 34 pass; `npm run test:navigation` 9 pass; 0 fail in all; `git diff --check` and `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` clean. The browser and gateway results below are from before this rebase.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The new tests fail against master's `AgentContext.tsx` (same tests, master's production file): the reopen, page-load, Stop, switch and close scenarios fail at the first "shows the turn as running" assertion.
  - Reverting each guard one at a time (live-turn guard; switch keeps a detached turn; close, clear, model switch and unmount end the watch; the abort checks after the wait and after the last check; a failed check reads as not running; the reload when the turn ends; the per-check deadline, the race that stops awaiting a stuck request, the cancellation of a check when the watch ends; a hydration's pending check registered, and cancelled by clear and by model switch; no watch once cancelled before the load) fails at least one test each: 17 of 17.
  - Stale state (third commit): the tests for Stop on a turn the gateway is not running (unlock after two checks, no re-lock on the same turn id, re-lock on a new one), a check already out when Stop is refused, and a turn without an id fail against the previous head `44618fc9d` or the commit's first draft; a refusal followed by another running turn, Stop accepted, and Stop just as a turn ends (its answer still loads) pin the unchanged paths.
  - The tests also assert the prompt shows exactly once while the turn runs and after the answer loads, and that the page never re-sends it.
  - A turn that ends while the transcript loads (the test's gateway flips to `idle` when the snapshot is read) still gets its answer loaded; this fails with the state asked after the load.
  - A state check that never answers: hydration finishes at the deadline with the single load (no watch), and a stuck check during the watch ends it with one reload; the stuck request's signal is aborted in both, and on a conversation switch.
  - **Browser check against a real gateway with a real network drop** (added 2026-11-15; headless Chromium, isolated `zeroclaw gateway` built from this PR's first two commits, patch-id identical, plus unrelated carried changes). A fake OpenAI-compatible model streams a fixed answer over 20 s; a TCP proxy between browser and gateway drops every connection, with no close frames, and refuses new ones for a set time. Each trial opens `/agent/<alias>`, sends a message, cuts the network once the model's first words are on screen, then waits for the complete answer without any reload or navigation. Control: the same tree with this PR's two commits reverted and nothing else.

    | Network outage | Without this PR | With this PR |
    |---|---|---|

prs.title: fix(cron): persist --agent reassignment on cron update
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `zeroclaw cron update <id> --agent <alias>` validated the alias and printed success, but never stored the new owner (#12228). The CLI now reassigns jobs through a dedicated operator-only entry point (`update_shell_job_with_approval_reassigning` → `update_job_reassigning_owner`).
  - Reassignment is deliberately **not** a `CronJobPatch` field. That struct is deserialized from model input by the agent-facing `cron_update` tool, so an owner field there would let an agent move its own job into another agent's execution context. `cron_update` now rejects a patch that names `agent_alias` (or `agent`) instead of silently dropping it.
  - Unrelated updates (gateway edits, pause/resume, scoped tool updates) bind `NULL` for the owner, and the `UPDATE` keeps the row's current alias via `COALESCE`. This runs inside master's existing `IMMEDIATE` transaction, so a stale caller copy can never restore a previous owner.
  - Naming the current owner is a no-op for ownership, so the required `--agent` no longer breaks same-owner edits to declarative jobs. Actually transferring a declarative job is still refused because its owner comes from `[agents.<alias>].cron_jobs`.
  - The new errors use Fluent keys (`cli-cron-owner-empty`, `cli-cron-owner-declarative`, `cli-cron-update-owner-forbidden`) in all five runtime catalogues.
- **Scope boundary:** Gateway `PATCH /api/cron/:id` and RPC updates keep treating `agent` as the shell risk-profile alias only; they cannot reassign. No change to declarative sync or the agent rename cascade.
- **Blast radius:** Cron store update path, the `cron_update` tool's patch parsing, and the `zeroclaw cron update` CLI.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12228

### What this does, simply

Every scheduled job belongs to one agent, and that agent's tools, memory and policy are what the job runs with. The CLI let an operator name a different agent on `cron update`, said it worked, and then silently kept the old owner. This PR makes the CLI actually move the job, but only the CLI. Agents editing their own jobs through the `cron_update` tool still can't hand them to another agent, and ordinary edits keep whatever owner the row already has. Jobs defined in `config.toml` keep getting their owner from config.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The CLI, tool and store paths are each covered by focused tests at the real entry point (listed below).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Lint`, `Format`, `Test` (runs the `zeroclaw-runtime` cron/tool tests and the root CLI cron tests).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for this surface.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (macOS arm64, on head `ae8f1491c28f5bd58ac9a49327850744de50ab24`)

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- cron:: tools::cron_ i18n::
test tools::cron_update::tests::rejects_owner_change_and_keeps_stored_owner ... ok
test cron::store::tests::update_job_reassigning_owner_persists_new_owner ... ok
test cron::store::tests::update_job_reassigning_owner_rejects_empty_alias ... ok
test cron::store::tests::unrelated_patch_keeps_current_owner ... ok
test cron::store::tests::update_job_reassigning_owner_rejects_declarative_transfer ... ok
test cron::store::tests::update_job_reassigning_owner_allows_same_owner_declarative_edit ... ok
test result: ok. 354 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5803 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Traced every `CronJobPatch` consumer (CLI, gateway, RPC, `cron_update`) to confirm only the CLI can reach `update_job_reassigning_owner`. Not run: a live daemon.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no rendered-interface change).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `ae8f1491c`, `cli` and the `cron_update` tool, via the tests named below.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:**
  - `cron_update` with `patch.agent_alias` (object and stringified JSON) → rejected with the localized `cli-cron-update-owner-forbidden` message; owner and name unchanged (`rejects_owner_change_and_keeps_stored_owner`).
  - Operator reassignment persists (`update_job_reassigning_owner_persists_new_owner`, `cli_update_agent_reassigns_imperative_job`); an empty alias is refused (`update_job_reassigning_owner_rejects_empty_alias`).
  - An unrelated patch from a stale copy keeps the newer stored owner (`unrelated_patch_keeps_current_owner`).
  - Declarative jobs: same-owner edits succeed and transfers are refused, both in the store and through the real CLI path (`update_job_reassigning_owner_allows_same_owner_declarative_edit`, `update_job_reassigning_owner_rejects_declarative_transfer`, `cli_update_same_owner_edits_declarative_job`, `cli_update_rejects_declarative_owner_transfer`).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test`; the focused crates cover the changed paths and CI runs the rest.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: `cron_update` now returns one new localized error when model input tries to set `agent_alias`. The field has no effect on the store; ownership changes are reachable only from the operator CLI.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. `cron update --agent` now reassigns imperative jobs to the named agent (it was documented as doing so but did not).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Upgrade steps: none; existing jobs keep their owners until an operator runs `cron update --agent`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

prs.title: fix(security): accept a mid-argument @ in the PowerShell command grammar
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `split_powershell_pipeline_syntax` returned `None` for any unquoted `@`, so an allowlisted command with an email address argument (`himalaya message compose --to user@example.com ...`) was refused as "Command not allowed by security policy" before the risk gate ran (#12005).
  - PowerShell only starts splatting (`@args`), an array subexpression (`@(...)`), a hashtable (`@{...}`) or a here-string at `@` where a token starts: at the start of an argument, after a `-Name:` parameter, or after a `,` array separator. Inside a bare argument it is literal text.
  - The grammar now accepts `@` inside a bare argument and keeps rejecting it in those three token-start positions. `@(`, `@{` and `@"` inside an argument are still rejected by the `(`/`{` arms and the mixed-quoting check.
  - After review: outside quotes the grammar now fails closed on any whitespace other than space and tab (U+00A0, U+0085, U+1680, U+2000–U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, vertical tab, form feed) and on the typographic quotes U+2018–U+201E, because PowerShell ends or starts a token there and the grammar would otherwise disagree on where a token starts. `@` also stays rejected in any token that contains `$`, since `$a.b@HOME` splats after the member read.
- **Scope boundary:** only the `@` arm of the bounded PowerShell grammar. No change to the POSIX or cmd.exe dialects, the allowlist, the risk classifier, or the trusted wildcard opt-out.
- **Blast radius:** PowerShell commands that contain a mid-argument `@` now reach the allowlist and risk gates like any other command, and simple ones also get the UTF-8 setup prelude (`powershell_command_supports_statement_prelude` uses the same grammar).
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12005

### What this does, simply

On Windows the shell tool checks PowerShell commands with a small, strict grammar and refuses anything it does not understand. It treated every `@` as PowerShell syntax, so any command with an email address or a `user@host` argument was refused with a message about the allowlist, even when the command was allowlisted. PowerShell itself only gives `@` a special meaning at the start of a word (and right after `-Name:` or `,`), so this change accepts it in the middle of a word and still refuses it in those positions.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: the change is a pure grammar decision covered by unit tests at the `SecurityPolicy` boundary.

### How I tested

I checked PowerShell's own tokenizer (Windows PowerShell 5.1, `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseInput`) for where `@` starts a new token:

| Input | PowerShell tokens |
|---|---|
| `Write-Output user@example.com` | `Generic<user@example.com>` |
| `Write-Output --to=@x` | `Generic<--to=@x>` |
| `Write-Output -InputObject:@x` | `Parameter<-InputObject:>` `SplattedVariable<@x>` |
| `Write-Output a,@b` | `Identifier<a>` `Comma<,>` `SplattedVariable<@b>` |
| `Write-Output @x` | `SplattedVariable<@x>` |

New tests in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs`:

- `powershell_grammar_accepts_at_sign_inside_a_bare_argument`: mid-argument `@` is accepted; `@` at token start, after `-Name:`, after `,`, and `@(`, `@{`, `@"` are still rejected.
- `validate_treats_powershell_email_argument_like_any_other_argument`: through `validate_command_execution_for_shell`, the command with `--to user@example.com` gets the same result as the same command without it, with and without approval.

Before the fix (fix lines reverted, tests kept):

```text
test policy::tests::powershell_grammar_accepts_at_sign_inside_a_bare_argument ... FAILED
test policy::tests::validate_treats_powershell_email_argument_like_any_other_argument ... FAILED
a mid-argument `@` is literal text: himalaya message compose --to user@example.com --body test
assertion `left == right` failed: approved=false
  left: Err("Command not allowed by security policy: himalaya message compose --to user@example.com --body test")
 right: Err("Command requires explicit approval (approved=true): high-risk operation")
```

After the fix:

```text
test policy::tests::powershell_grammar_accepts_at_sign_inside_a_bare_argument ... ok
test policy::tests::validate_treats_powershell_email_argument_like_any_other_argument ... ok
test policy::tests::validate_blocks_powershell_splat_after_unicode_whitespace ... ok
```

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and lint jobs cover `zeroclaw-config`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for this change; the grammar is pure string handling and runs on every platform.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on Windows 11 (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu): `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib` gave `1943 passed; 1 failed`. The one failure, `platform::native::tests::powershell_full_scripts_execute_with_native_semantics`, fails the same way on unmodified `master` on this machine: its console code page is 932, so PowerShell writes the test's non-ASCII output in that code page and `String::from_utf8` fails. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean. `cargo clippy` reports no warnings in `policy.rs`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The PowerShell tokenizer table above. I did not run a live agent with himalaya.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `N/A`
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `N/A`
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `N/A`
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace test run; only `zeroclaw-config` changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`; tests use `example.com` addresses)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: none are `Yes`. This relaxes the bounded PowerShell grammar in one place: an unquoted `@` is accepted inside a bare argument (`user@example.com`), and stays rejected wherever PowerShell starts a token: at the start of an argument or command, after `-Name:`, after `,`, and in any token that contains `$`. To keep the grammar's token boundaries the same as PowerShell's, it now fails closed on every whitespace character other than space and tab and on the typographic quotes U+2018–U+201E outside quotes; the backtick, `(`, `{`, `;`, `&`, redirection, `--%`, mixed-quoting, variable, provider-path, allowlist and risk-gate checks are unchanged.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>`. No feature flags or config. If it misbehaves, a PowerShell command with `@` would get a different allowlist or risk result than expected.

prs.title: feat(runtime): run a subagent on an operator-declared model route
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
- `spawn_subagent` takes an optional `model_hint` naming a `[[model_routes]]` entry. The child runs on that route's provider and model; its identity, workspace, security policy and memory allowlist are inherited from the parent exactly as before. Before this, a subagent always ran on its parent's model, so a parent on an expensive high-reasoning model had no way to run broad, mechanical subtasks (a scope inventory, a simplification pass) more cheaply. `delegate` changes the model, but it also changes the agent, and with it the workspace and the policy, which is exactly what a subtask over the parent's own files cannot give up.
- The hint resolves through the existing provider and model overrides that `agent::run` already accepts and `spawn_subagent` passed as `None`, so every option the route's provider owns applies, including `chat_template_kwargs` and `temperature`. A lower-effort alias of the same local model therefore works as a route, which is the motivating case.
- The choice is bounded by the operator's route list, never free-form. A child can read everything its parent can, so a free-form provider argument would let the model send that workspace to any configured provider, including one set up for a different agent. The parameter appears in the schema only when routes exist and the parent’s configured risk profile admits `model_switch` without requiring approval, as an `enum` of exactly the declared hints, and an undeclared hint is refused before any spawn work rather than falling back to the parent's model, so a typo cannot silently run the subtask on the expensive model.
- The child's `temperature` now comes from the provider that serves the run: a routed child takes its route's, not its parent's.
- An enforced SOP step scope also limits the choice. When the active step, headless or live, excludes `model_switch`, a routed spawn is refused and `model_hint` is not offered, even if the agent's profile allows switching. A step that cannot switch models directly cannot reach another provider through a child either.
- Live nested SOP steps now publish their step scope on the task, as headless steps already did. Tools that start child runs (`spawn_subagent`, `delegate`) read the boundary there. Before this, children started inside a live step did not inherit that step's tool scope at all.

- **Scope boundary:** No change to `delegate`, to how `[[model_routes]]` are declared or validated, to `hint:` model routing for an agent's own requests, or to anything a subagent inherits other than its model and, inside a live SOP step, that step's tool scope. No new config key. Without a `model_hint` argument, `spawn_subagent` behaves exactly as on `master`.

- **Blast radius:** `spawn_subagent`, plus the live nested SOP step driver in `agent/turn/mod.rs`, which now runs the step's loop under the same task-local step scope the headless driver uses (`sop::executor::headless_step_scope` became `pub(crate)` for this). Child runs started inside a live step now inherit its scope and its fail-closed approval handling. The `spawn_subagent` schema gains one optional property, and only for configurations with at least one `[[model_routes]]` entry whose parent profile admits `model_switch` without requiring approval; configurations without routes see an unchanged schema. One docs page, `docs/book/src/agents/delegation.md`.

- **Linked issue(s):** None

The current diff spans ten files, +860/-27: `spawn_subagent.rs`, the live step driver in `agent/turn/mod.rs`, a visibility change in `sop/executor.rs`, a test extension in `agent/loop_.rs`, five refusal keys in each of five locale catalogs, and the delegation docs page.

### What this does, simply

When an agent hands a piece of work to a helper (a "subagent"), the helper is a copy of the same agent: same files, same permissions, same model. That last part is the problem this fixes. If you run your main agent on a slow, thorough reasoning setting, every helper runs on it too, even for chores like listing which files changed, where the extra thinking buys nothing and fills up the helper's memory faster.

This lets the agent ask for a helper on a different model, but only on one the operator has already listed in the config under `[[model_routes]]`. The helper still works in the same place with the same permissions; only the model changes. If the operator has listed no routes, nothing changes at all. If the agent asks for a route that is not listed, the request is refused instead of quietly falling back to the expensive model.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (any surface that runs an agent turn with `spawn_subagent` available; the behavior is in the tool, not the surface).
- **Setup / preconditions:** An agent whose risk profile allows `spawn_subagent` and `model_switch`, with `model_switch` auto-approved (or Full autonomy) and with no matching `always_ask` entry, and two configured provider aliases, ideally the same model at different reasoning effort so the difference is visible in the provider's logs. Declare one route to the second alias:

  ```toml
  [[model_routes]]
  hint = "light"
  model_provider = "custom.my-model-low"
  model = "my-model"
  ```

- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to spawn a subagent with `model_hint: "light"` for a trivial task, then again with `model_hint: "missing"`, then with no hint. Watch which provider alias receives each child's requests, in the provider's logs or zeroclaw's `llm_request` events.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The `light` child's requests go to `custom.my-model-low` with that alias's options. The `missing` call returns a failed tool result naming the configured hints (`configured hints: light`), and no child run starts. The unhinted child runs on the parent's alias. Removing the `[[model_routes]]` table removes `model_hint` from the tool's schema.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `model_hint` is not part of the schema and is ignored if sent anyway: every child runs on the parent's alias, including the `missing` case, which raises no error.

### How I tested

- **Integration validation at `da479969b1b4`:** I merged master `d9ea409acc2` and resolved the SOP test conflict, preserving the seven-case matrix and the scope probe. On this exact integrated tree, formatting passed, `run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope` passed all seven internal cases, and all 27 `tools::spawn_subagent` tests passed. Hosted CI results are tracked on this revision; the earlier author results below remain historical evidence.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The workspace `Test` job runs `zeroclaw-runtime`'s lib tests with no feature flags, and `spawn_subagent` is not feature-gated (`pub mod spawn_subagent;` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs`), so all 27 tests in the module, and the live-step scope test in `agent::loop_`, run in required CI. `Lint` covers the code and `Docs Style` the docs page.
- **Earlier CI evidence at `7a6328f94`:** CI for `7a6328f94` had not finished when this body was updated. On the previous head `bb7f3bc31a7c`, the [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38475227504/job/115564154389) passed the profile-authorization, schema-hiding, denied-route zero-request and authorized-route provider-options regressions. Security fails on the base lockfile's `ruzstd` advisory, which is unchanged by this PR and fixed separately in #11715.
- **Step-scope regressions on `7a6328f94` (run locally):**
  - `a_step_that_denies_model_switch_cannot_route_a_child` runs the real tool inside an enforced step that denies `model_switch` and permits spawning. The agent's profile allows and auto-approves switching. The routed call is refused with the localized not-permitted message, and the alternate recording provider receives no request. The schema omits `model_hint`. An unhinted spawn in the same step still completes on the parent's provider.
  - `run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope` now also runs a probe tool inside a live nested step. It checks that the step scope, including the `model_switch` exclusion, is visible to tools there.
  - Both tests fail with their fix removed: the first with the step check disabled in `route_authorization`, the second with the live driver change reverted.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No real-provider smoke is recorded for this head.
- **Earlier author-run validation:** The commands and outputs below were recorded for `980eafe27` and are retained as historical evidence.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```sh
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  # (no output; clean)

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::spawn_subagent
  test tools::spawn_subagent::tests::a_declared_hint_resolves_to_its_route ... ok
  test tools::spawn_subagent::tests::an_undeclared_hint_is_refused_and_names_the_valid_ones ... ok
  test tools::spawn_subagent::tests::an_undeclared_hint_is_refused_before_spawning ... ok
  test tools::spawn_subagent::tests::no_model_hint_keeps_the_parent_model ... ok
  test tools::spawn_subagent::tests::the_schema_offers_model_hint_only_when_routes_exist ... ok
  test result: ok. 21 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5542 filtered out

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
  test result: ok. 5555 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  $ bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)

  $ bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  No added links detected in changed docs lines.
  ```

  On `7a6328f94`:

  ```sh
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  # (no output; clean)

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
  test result: ok. 5561 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  ```

The five new tests have teeth: with the resolver forced to ignore the hint (`return Ok(None)`), three of them fail (`a_declared_hint_resolves_to_its_route`, `an_undeclared_hint_is_refused_and_names_the_valid_ones`, `an_undeclared_hint_is_refused_before_spawning`); the other two pin the no-hint and schema behavior, which that change does not affect.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That the hint reaches the child's provider resolution: `agent::run` resolves `provider_override` through `options_for_provider_ref` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/loop_.rs`), which applies every option the named alias owns, so a route to a lower-effort alias carries that alias's `chat_template_kwargs`. Not verified: a live run against a real provider on this exact head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`. No rendered interface changes; the change is a tool parameter and its behavior.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `980eafe27`, on top of `e654b4b73`; `N/A` for visual evidence.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `N/A`
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `N/A` for visual evidence; functional results are recorded above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace clippy with `-D warnings` does not complete on the toolchain I have locally (rustc 1.99.0), because lints new in that release fire in code this PR does not touch (`needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `zeroclaw-providers`, `assert_is_empty` in the root crate). With those two allowed, the workspace run with `--features ci-all` reports nothing in `spawn_subagent.rs`. The `Lint` job on the pinned toolchain is the authoritative check.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **`Yes`**
- New external network calls? `No`. A routed child calls the route's configured provider, which the operator already declared; no new endpoint is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`. The route's provider resolves its own credentials through the existing path.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`. Fixtures use `custom.light` / `light-model`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:

**The capability:** the model can now choose, per subagent, which of the operator's declared routes serves it, and that child can read everything its parent can. So a route's provider can now receive the parent's workspace content through a subagent at the model's choice.

**Why that is bounded:** the choice is limited to operator-declared `[[model_routes]]`; the schema enumerates those hints and rejects undeclared values before spawning. The parent’s configured risk profile must admit `model_switch` and allow it without an approval prompt. ReadOnly, exclusions, restrictive allowlists and `always_ask` refuse routed spawning. An enforced SOP step scope that excludes `model_switch` refuses it too, on both the headless and the live step paths. Unhinted spawning keeps the existing behavior.

**Step scopes:** an earlier head checked only the configured risk profile, so a step that denied `model_switch` while allowing `spawn_subagent` could still choose a route. The route check now also reads the active step scope. Live nested steps now publish that scope, so the check, and child-run scope inheritance, cover both execution paths.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`. Configurations without `[[model_routes]]` see an unchanged schema and behavior. With routes, `spawn_subagent` without `model_hint` behaves exactly as on `master`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`. No new key; the existing `[[model_routes]]` table is reused.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- Behavior change inside live SOP steps: a child run started by `spawn_subagent` or `delegate` in a live nested step now inherits the step's tool scope. Like a child of a headless step, it uses non-interactive approval, so its `always_ask` tools are denied instead of running unprompted.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash-commit-sha>` after the PR is squash-merged. Operationally, removing the `[[model_routes]]` entries removes the parameter, and a risk profile that excludes `spawn_subagent` disables the tool entirely.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None dedicated; the presence of `[[model_routes]]` and configured model-switch permission without required approval enable the parameter.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a `spawn_subagent` tool result failing with `unknown model_hint` names a hint the model invented or the operator removed. A child running on an unexpected provider shows in its `llm_request` events under the child's `subagent-<uuid>` tracing scope, with the route's `model_provider` and `model`.

prs.title: feat(runtime): show a foreground delegate's tool calls in the parent turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A foreground agentic delegate ran its tool loop with an inert observer, so while it worked the parent turn, the RPC stream and ZeroCode showed nothing until the child answered. A long delegate looked the same whether it was working, looping or stuck.
  - Each tool execution in a turn that streams events now scopes the turn's event sender and the call id (`agent/tool_execution.rs`, next to #11298's cancellation scope). A foreground agentic delegate gives its child loop an observer (`tools/delegate_activity.rs`) that turns each child tool start and finish into one new live turn event, `TurnEvent::DelegateActivity` in `zeroclaw-api`: the tool name, a secret-redacted argument summary (`approval::summarize_args`), and a 400-character output preview of the already-scrubbed result. Parallel workers carry the scope across their spawn. A delegate inside the child reports one level deeper (`depth`) against the same parent call.
  - The observer sends with `try_send`, so a full parent channel drops activity instead of slowing the child or the parent turn.
  - RPC forwards it as a `delegate_activity` `session/update` (`rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs`). ZeroCode shows a child-call count and the running tool under the delegate card, and the call list when the card is expanded.
  - A tool's own `approved` input is left out of child summaries: under a successful call, `approved: false` read as a refusal.
  - While the delegate's turn runs, its card's Response line now says "Waiting for response" instead of "Result not recorded". The card only says that for a call this pane saw start in the running turn; restored history and calls a finished or cancelled turn left without a result keep the neutral wording from #11446.
- **Scope boundary:** no persistence: the event isn't written to the turn checkpoint or session history, so restored sessions look as before. Background delegates don't forward (their turn may be gone; #11292's `check_result` progress covers them). The child's text, reasoning, usage and approvals aren't forwarded. No config key and no opt-in. Other channels (ACP server, gateway WS, chat channels) ignore the new variant through their existing fall-through arms.
- **Blast radius:** the tool-execution scope wraps every tool's `execute` when the turn streams events, but only the delegate tool reads it. Foreground agentic delegates now run with a forwarding observer instead of the no-op one. RPC clients get a new `session/update` type; older ZeroCode builds ignore it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #10531 (its observer-forwarding piece; #11292 shipped the first piece). Related #8763 (live half of the ZeroCode subagent view), #11446 (the neutral wording kept for restored cards). Holding-crate exception row: #11697 (merged).

### What this does, simply

When one agent hands work to a helper agent and waits for the answer, you used to see nothing until the helper was done. Now the waiting card in ZeroCode shows how many tools the helper has used and which one it's running right now, and expanding the card lists each of them. Only the tool names and a short, secret-stripped summary of each call are shown, never the helper's full inputs or outputs. Nothing is saved; reopening the session shows the card as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: I ran it live in the experiment build; the tests below drive the delegate path end to end with a scripted provider.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Chat with an agent that has an agentic delegate target.

### How I tested

```bash
zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::delegate agent::tool_execution rpc::dispatch::tests::delegate rpc::types
zc-cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" zc-cargo doc -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <changed files>
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Test and Parallel Runtime Test run the new runtime and ZeroCode tests; Lint covers clippy, rustdoc and comment hygiene; Docs Style covers the `rpc-socket.md` addition.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no test drives a real daemon and ZeroCode together; the RPC mapping and the ZeroCode handler are tested on each side of the wire.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Latest local run on `9f3090ee37` (the head `db3d91e2f9` since then only removes TestBackend evidence tests): fmt and clippy clean; `zeroclaw-runtime` + `zerocode` suites 7916 passed, 3 failed: `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and two `relay::local_dial_tests` tests, which fail on master on the same machine. CI Required Gate green on `db3d91e2f9`. @tidux's points are fixed in `563ed8555` (id-less results paired by arguments), `c6fb85a71` (reused child ids, neutral unfinished rows) and `035aa48f4` (checkpoint-exclusion test, `output_preview` documented in `rpc-socket.md`). Earlier run: clippy clean (exit 0). Runtime filter: `318 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`. ZeroCode: `1459 passed; 1 failed` — the failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which also fails on master on the machine I ran it on. Rustdoc exit 0, fmt clean, hygiene gate passed, docs gate `0 error(s)`.
- New tests:
  - `foreground_agentic_delegate_reports_child_tool_calls_to_the_parent_turn`: a scripted agentic child calls `echo_tool`; the parent sink gets exactly one start and one finish with the parent call id, agent, child call id, a summary and an `echo:` preview.
  - `background_delegate_does_not_report_to_the_parent_turn`: same child with a progress sink (the background shape) runs its tool and sends nothing to the parent.
  - `tools_see_the_parent_event_sink_only_in_a_streaming_turn`: the scope is visible inside `execute` with the call id, absent without an event sender, and gone afterwards.
  - `delegate_activity::tests`: secret argument redacted, preview bounded, id-less calls get one id shared by start and finish, a full parent channel drops instead of blocking.
  - `delegate_activity_notification_is_flat_and_round_trips` (RPC), `parses_delegate_activity_update` and `delegate_card_shows_child_activity_while_running_and_keeps_it_after` (ZeroCode).
  - `subagent_card_says_waiting_only_while_its_turn_runs`: a live delegate card says "Waiting for response"; after its turn settles without a result it says "Result not recorded". The existing `subagent_card_restored_missing_result_does_not_claim_live_work` passes unchanged.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Swapping the forwarder back to the no-op observer makes the foreground test fail and leaves the background one passing; forcing the card's waiting flag off makes the waiting test fail. Both restored afterwards. Live run in the experiment build ([branch](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d), dogfood base `0341618f9d69`): a foreground delegate to another agent running four slow read-only tool calls; the parent's card counted the calls, showed the running one, said "Waiting for response" until the child answered, and kept the list afterwards.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Screenshot`: real macOS Terminal.app captures of the current head `db3d91e2f9`, at https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Tests: `9f3090ee37` (above) and CI on `db3d91e2f9`. Interface: ZeroCode TUI, debug build of `db3d91e2f9` (daemon and ZeroCode from the same build), captured in https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777. Earlier captures from experiment build [20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) are in 6232092560.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777 (current head `db3d91e2f9`; earlier: 6232092560)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** asked the agent to delegate in the foreground to a helper agent that runs several slow tool calls. While it runs, the card shows the call count, the running tool and "Waiting for response"; expanded, it lists each call with its redacted summary; after the helper answers, the list stays and the result replaces the waiting line.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `zeroclaw-runtime` suite; I ran the delegate, tool-execution and RPC-type filters, which hold every test touching the changed code.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots of the current head `db3d91e2f9`: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777 (the delegate is running with live child-call counts, and the card expands to the child call list). Earlier captures from the experiment build: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6232092560.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Child arguments go through the same redacting summarizer as approval prompts, and the output preview comes from the result the loop has already credential-scrubbed. Tested with an `api_key` argument.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The activity goes to the client only; it never enters a model request. ZeroCode renders it through the existing terminal-safe text path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The `session/update` type is additive; older clients fall through their unknown-type arms.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, `git revert <squash-commit>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a delegate card without a child-call line while its child runs tools, or child calls shown under the wrong card.
