prs.title: feat(zerocode): configure and select canonical provider models
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.
- **What changed and why:** Use the canonical registry RPC editor and exact model references in Zerocode configuration, Quickstart and chat selection; retain masked edit baselines, add text navigation and update independent Fluent catalogs.
- **Scope boundary:** Backend and protocol contracts are provided by the parent. Web dashboard changes are a separate child.
- **Blast radius:** TUI onboarding, configuration save/reload, model selection and validation feedback.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 10; current head `dc57422998`. Depends on #12450.

### What this does, simply

The terminal setup and configuration screens need to edit the same connections and models that the backend resolves. This change switches Zerocode to exact registry keys and adds connection/model editing, replacing the old provider-profile workflow. The exact-head ZeroCode edit/save/reopen workflow has been verified with the matching daemon and synthetic data; the reopened registry shows the persisted model and masked credential.

## Testing (required)


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the interactive workflow below supplements the passing required CI gate.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Requested surface: `tui`, exercised interactively at `ed8b169bef` with the matching daemon; English locale, 80 columns × 24 rows in the authorized PTY. The subsequent `dc57422998` follow-up is isolated to the Web cost-rate route and does not change the TUI implementation or daemon binary.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this head with its parent commits. Use the isolated V5 configuration under `target/z`, containing synthetic connection/model key `openai.evidence_fresh` and a masked synthetic credential. Build ZeroCode and its matching daemon together.
- **Steps to run:** Run `cargo build --offline --locked -p zeroclaw -p zerocode --bins`; launch `target/debug/zerocode --config-dir target/z`. Open Config → Provider registry → providers.registry, inspect the dotted model key and revision, press Ctrl+S, and reopen. Then open Quickstart → Model and Chat → `/model-provider`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The TUI reads and writes V5 registry documents, preserves complete model names and reports edit failures without discarding the draft.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The TUI edits provider-family tables and derives selections by splitting profile references.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The latest full CI run [44757836809](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44757836809) passed all code, format, lint, test, parallel-runtime, platform, Web and build jobs. Its only required failure is Security: `wasmtime-wasi` 48.0.9, RUSTSEC-2026-0587 (published November 19, 2026), which is outside this PR's dependency changes and requires an upstream dependency update. The actual terminal interaction is covered separately by the exact-surface evidence below. The report-only risk workflow remains outside this PR's gating scope because it rejects an inherited removed-file entry in the cumulative stack (the same failure is present on #12450).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No duplicate local full test/clippy matrix was run; the required CI gate is the validation source for that matrix. The focused manual run covers registry editing, Ctrl+S persistence, reopening, dotted keys, credential masking, Quickstart selection and chat model-provider selection.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0, no formatting diff. `git diff --check`: exit 0, no whitespace errors. `cargo build --offline --locked -p zeroclaw -p zerocode --bins`: exit 0, both binaries built in this worktree's `target` directory.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Ran the actual ZeroCode registry edit/save/reopen sequence against the matching local daemon. The editor displayed the dotted key `openai.evidence_fresh`, the persisted registry revision, and `No pending edits`; Ctrl+S returned `Saved "providers"`. Quickstart's model picker and Chat's `/model-provider` picker both displayed and accepted the same literal dotted key. The synthetic credential remained masked and no provider inference request was made.
- **Visual interface evidence:** The exact-output transcript from the Rust/TUI head is recorded in `target/quickstart-evidence/ed8b-ui-transcript.txt` during the authorized PTY run. It includes the current registry revision/footer, Quickstart selection and Chat selection. The transcript contains no secret value; the UI was exercised directly against the matching daemon. The Web-only route fix after that capture cannot affect this TUI surface.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Rust/TUI behavior `ed8b169bef1d3784d6f31107e9d873b52d52ac14`; final PR head `dc57422998`; `tui`, 80×24 PTY, November 20, 2026. The evidence is a local review artifact and does not change the implementation diff.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Registry editor showed the literal dotted model key and revision, Ctrl+S returned `Saved "providers"`, and reopening showed `No pending edits`. Quickstart showed `[✓] Model openai.evidence_fresh`; Chat showed `Select configured model / openai.evidence_fresh` and then `model_provider switched to openai.evidence_fresh`. Result: PASS.
- **Follow-up fixes at `8a42b79179` plus master merge `ed8b169bef` and Web route fix `dc57422998`:** Provider setup documentation places credentials and endpoints on the referenced connection, including regional `extra.endpoint`. Registry refresh preparation skips unrelated sessions before taking their turn guards, includes an immediately observable transient tool selection, and falls back to the ordered lock-in path whenever that selection is busy; scope errors are converted to RPC errors. Cost-only TTS/transcription type pickers use `cost.rates.providers.*` templates, including the canonical `custom` slot, with its regression fixture running inside Tokio. The current head also includes the latest master dependency/security fixes, and Web cost-rate provider clicks now navigate directly to the canonical rate-sheet route instead of the legacy selector.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate local full test/clippy matrix was run; the existing required CI covers it. A local build and focused real TUI interaction were performed to fill the reviewer-identified evidence gap.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No additional permissions.
- New external network calls? No additional provider endpoints; existing backend RPC remains the transport.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes; editors preserve masked connection fields through the backend registry-edit contract.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No additional model-visible input path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A masked value must never overwrite a real credential. The editor carries the backend edit baseline and uses the same validated persistence path; the real edit/save/reopen check confirmed the stored credential is preserved and the reopened editor remains masked.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Requires the parent V5 backend and its registry-edit RPC contract.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; terminal onboarding and editors use connections and exact model keys.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Merge dependencies first, migrate existing configuration to V5, and rebuild Zerocode against the matching backend. Old profile editing is not retained in the new UI.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this client layer together with dependent UI layers; retain the matching server and V5 config or restore the V4 backup for a full downgrade.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added for staging the stack.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** CI compile errors, configuration load failures, or changed provider behavior in the layer-specific regression tests.

Stack integration: this repository grants this author read-only access. These fork PRs therefore target `master` and have cumulative diffs. Review the incremental layer against its declared parent; merge parents first and refresh each child before merging. Original #9809 is closed; this stacked PR remains the Zerocode layer.

Incremental review: [declared parent to this layer](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/compare/6fe2985212728254b90d9b807a9040b5db92095d...dc57422998).





### Latest head validation (2026-11-20)

- Current head: `dc57422998`; declared parent: `6fe2985212728254b90d9b807a9040b5db92095d` (#12450); merged latest `origin/master` (`dfc70a2b49`).
- Rebuilt from the corrected registry parent; this diff contains only Zerocode configuration, Quickstart, chat selection, text navigation and the related Codex documentation correction.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` passed for the changed Zerocode files.
- `RUSTC_WRAPPER= CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target cargo build --offline --locked -p zeroclaw -p zerocode --bins` passed locally after disabling the unavailable sccache wrapper.
- The ASR endpoint review finding is fixed in #12450's provider boundary and is not duplicated here.
- Full workspace CI and the exact-surface interactive evidence remain the validation source for this client layer. The inherited report-only risk-script failure is documented above; non-PR dependency-security changes are supplied by the merged master commits. The Web-only follow-up is covered by the Web permission/contract CI jobs.

prs.title: fix(providers): send configured extra_headers on Anthropic requests
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Native Anthropic configuration already accepts `extra_headers`, but its factory dropped them. Forward the existing runtime options into `AnthropicBuilder` so gateways receive their configured headers on buffered and streaming requests.
  - Validate header names and values once, skip invalid entries with a warning that omits values, and mark valid values sensitive. Install them as client defaults. Headers the provider actually sets on a request take precedence over those defaults.
  - Build a dedicated buffered client when headers are present, propagate construction failures without a headerless fallback, and apply the existing host/port redirect restriction to both header-bearing clients. Retain the allowed redirect, denied destination, hostname-only, and construction-failure controls.
  - Preserve master's endpoint-based single-tool-round support while forwarding headers. Extend existing tests to cover both credential modes, capability selection with extra headers, and streaming-test isolation from runtime proxy changes.
- **Scope boundary:** Only `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/anthropic.rs` and its factory wiring/tests change. No new config key, auth-selection rule, request-body format, shared redirect-policy implementation, other provider behavior, dependency, or CI change. No decoupled redirect repair is included. The draft remains held for the outstanding credential-boundary review described in the [latest maintainer review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11541#pullrequestreview-5520939876).
- **Blast radius:** Native Anthropic entries with valid configured extra headers now transmit them. Buffered requests with no valid extra headers retain the shared cached client. Streaming requests retain the existing timeout and proxy behavior. Request wrappers introduced on master retain their tool-round controls.
- **Linked issue(s):** No linked issue. Related #11544 for subsequent Anthropic streaming header/timeout integration; this PR does not implement that PR's timeout change.

### What this does, simply

Some model gateways require a custom authentication header. ZeroClaw already lets users configure those headers, but the native Anthropic provider ignored them, so those gateways could reject requests with 401 responses. This change sends the configured headers on Anthropic requests, including streaming requests.

The provider's own header wins when it sets the same header on the request. API-key requests set `x-api-key`; setup-token requests set `Authorization`. A configured header for the other authentication mode is still sent. A provider-generated `anthropic-beta` replaces a configured default rather than merging it. Invalid configured entries are skipped with a warning. The remaining credential-boundary review must be completed before this draft can proceed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` - existing loopback wire tests exercise header delivery and redirect behavior; refreshed exact-revision execution is still required before relying on them.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** N/A - no rendered `web`, `tui`, or `cli` state changes; the affected boundary is Anthropic provider HTTP traffic.
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A - no additional manual setup is requested; automated fixtures use synthetic credentials and loopback endpoints.
- **Steps to run:** N/A - use the focused automated validation recorded below rather than a credentialed manual gateway test.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Configured valid headers reach native Anthropic requests; request-set credentials win collisions; disallowed host/port redirect targets receive no request; buffered client-build failures send no fallback request.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The native Anthropic factory ignores configured extra headers, so a gateway requiring one receives no such header.

### How I tested

The existing suite covers buffered and streaming header delivery, factory forwarding, invalid entries and sensitive values, allowed same-host redirects, denied different-port redirects, denied different-host/same-port redirects, and buffered/thinking-stream client-build failures with zero receiving requests. The refreshed tests also cover setup-token `Authorization` precedence and official/custom endpoint capability selection while extra headers are configured.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI Required Gate, Format, Lint, Test and platform checks](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37699203609) passed for published head 745f0add9d42579215d54b944b9867971d91c787. These are historical evidence for the earlier provider code, not validation of the refreshed merge or latest test edits. The [maintainer's earlier review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11541#pullrequestreview-5475206102) records the test job's 19,366 passed / 39 skipped result on its merge snapshot.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Fresh CI runs on the pushed head `94d90cc15`. The local fmt, Clippy and provider tests below cover the merge and the test edits. No live gateway retry on this revision.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on the master merge `9af933d21` and on head `94d90cc15`, Mac mini, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`, `--test-threads=2`:

  ```text
  # 9af933d21 (merge only)
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                              ok
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings          ok
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers   lib 1987 passed; 1 failed; 4 ignored; integration tests ok
    failure: openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults
    (connection refused; passes on rerun here and on clean master; not touched by this PR)
  # 94d90cc15 (head)
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                              ok
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings          ok
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers anthropic                              210 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers factory                                128 passed; 0 failed (+7 integration)
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source review traced factory forwarding, all buffered-client callers, streaming/thinking error handling, credential precedence, and composition with master's single-tool-round changes. Direct Rust formatting and whitespace checks passed. No live gateway retry was performed for the refreshed revision. Earlier live-body reports of mutation tests and a mixed local build reaching a gateway are historical author reports, not exact-revision evidence for this refresh.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` - no rendered user-interface state or presentation changes. Real screenshots and recordings supplied for this refresh: none. None are required for this transport-only change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Local runs cover merge `9af933d21` and head `94d90cc15` (provider HTTP traffic, no rendered interface). Historical public CI covers `745f0add9d`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** No screenshots apply (no interface change). Command output is above. No live-gateway capture is claimed.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The provider tests send synthetic configured headers through the real provider clients and check the received headers, or zero requests at denied redirect targets. All pass on `94d90cc15`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full `-p zeroclaw-providers` suite ran on the merge. On the head only the `anthropic` and `factory` filters ran, because the head commit changes only those tests. No live gateway retry.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No - existing Anthropic calls now carry configured headers; no new endpoint or operation is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No - test credentials are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Operator-configured headers may contain credentials and now leave the machine on native Anthropic requests. Values are marked sensitive, invalid-entry warnings omit values, and request-set authentication headers override matching configured defaults. Existing host/port redirect restrictions and loopback controls remain on both header-bearing clients. Those controls do not constitute clearance of the outstanding credential-boundary review; no broader security guarantee is claimed. Buffered construction errors propagate without a headerless fallback. Streaming's pre-existing invalid-proxy behavior remains a separate follow-up.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes - entries without valid extra headers retain existing behavior; explicitly configured headers now take effect as intended.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No - `extra_headers` already exists.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A - no schema or toolchain migration. Operators who configured previously ignored Anthropic headers should review them before upgrading because they will now be transmitted.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, `git revert <squash-commit>` restores the prior native Anthropic behavior of ignoring configured extra headers. Reverting does not revoke credentials already transmitted.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added. Removing `extra_headers` disables the new header-bearing path for that entry, but a gateway requiring those headers may reject requests.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Gateway 401/403 responses, Anthropic client-construction errors, or failures after redirects. A 403 alone does not establish successful gateway authentication. Investigate without logging credential values.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A - no Supersedes

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A - no Supersedes.
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A - no superseded work.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? (`Yes/No`) No
- If `No`, why (inspiration-only, no direct code/design carry-over): N/A - no superseded contributor work incorporated.

---

**Labels** live in the GitHub label UI, not in the body. The PR path labeler owns path/scope labels from `.github/labeler.yml`, and the PR size labeler owns canonical `size:*` labels. Maintainers and reviewers with label permissions still set `risk:*` and any missing manual labels via the sidebar. Contributors without label permission can note obvious label mismatches in a comment. Canonical colon-scoped labels use no-space spelling; during migration, copy exact live label spelling from the GitHub UI.

**Do not add bot/AI attribution footers** such as `Co-authored-by: Claude ...`
or `Created with Claude Code` to the PR body or commit-message tail. Human
co-author trailers are appropriate only for incorporated contributor work under
the supersede-attribution section and privacy contract.

**Privacy contract** (`docs/book/src/contributing/privacy.md`) is a merge gate. Never commit real identities, secrets, personal emails, or PII in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs.

prs.title: feat(providers): adopt the canonical V5 registry and runtime model bindings
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.
- **What changed and why:** Activate canonical registry admission and backend consumers, promote V4 configuration to V5, materialize complete models for routing/fallback/switching, and wire secret-safe registry editing. Registry types, native protocols, chat transport and reflection are prepared in #12454, #12455, #12456 and #12457.
- **Scope boundary:** V5 admission, persistence/editor wiring, canonical model construction and backend consumer/lifecycle cutover. Activation and affected consumers remain together so no intermediate revision clears profiles that active consumers still read. Zerocode and Web follow separately.
- **Blast radius:** Config persistence and secret handling; provider construction; agent/session lifecycle; memory, speech and decision consumers; channel/gateway/RPC dispatch.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 9; reference implementation `320aa43a62`. Depends on #12457.

### What this does, simply

The preceding layers prepare independent registry types, native capability protocols, chat transport and generic reflection. This layer activates those components: V4 input is promoted at the V5 admission boundary, backend consumers resolve exact model references, and routing, fallback and switching build complete target bindings. Configuration activation and dependent consumers stay together to avoid a partially switched runtime. This remaining cutover is still large; the preparatory layers make their own architectural boundaries independently reviewable.

## Testing (required)


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the migration or interactive workflow below supplements passing current-head CI.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Requested surface: `cli`. Not exercised interactively at this revision; CI covers the compiled CLI surface.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this head with its parent commits; use the repository toolchain and existing test fixtures.
- **Steps to run:** Run workspace Quality Gate, migration and registry edit tests, provider protocol tests, runtime route/switch/fallback/refresh tests and feature-matrix checks; exercise `zeroclaw config migrate` with a V4 backup.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** V4 configuration becomes V5 connections/models; internal consumers resolve exact model keys; switching/fallback materializes all target configuration and a failed update preserves the previous binding.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Master stores provider-owned profiles and consumer-specific capability settings, and has no canonical decoupled registry.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Earlier green runs are historical only. Current-head workspace Quality Gate 44723952832 passed after restoring the required RPC contract; the separate PR-risk reporter is report-only and failed head-bound evidence capture without mutations.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The separate PR-risk reporter failed its head-bound evidence capture. Live CLI/migration verification remains pending; The added migration and embedding identity regressions cover the old-configuration restrictions identified in review. Original #9809 CI does not validate intermediate stack revisions.
- **Commands run and tail output:** At `41a53d6b2f`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed locally; Quality Gate 44723952832 passed the full workspace matrix. Expanded config unit suite passed 2,085 tests, including the final fallback and timeout regressions. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check` and the changed-line docs quality gate passed. Existing Rust-toolchain deprecation/unused-dependency warnings were not changed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Addressed previous-head split dependency errors (retained embedding factory, complete timeout helpers, deferred dispatch-dependent sampling, and secret-test trait import). The registry and provider libraries compile on the cleaned head. Compared the integrated provider and UI trees byte-for-byte with the saved pre-split snapshot. Preserved the frozen V4 fixture. Corrected previous-head CI failures caused by unnecessary TOML rewriting; the existing comment-preservation and atomic-save assertions remain intact. Inspected ownership, imports and the incremental diff against the declared parent. Runtime/network behavior remains delegated to CI.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact-head PTY evidence is recorded in `target/quickstart-evidence/exact-head-evidence.txt`: fresh creation completed with canonical connection/model output, and an existing configured provider was offered through “Use existing”.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `6fe2985212728254b90d9b807a9040b5db92095d`; source formatting plus GitHub Quality Gate.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** No screenshot was generated in this CI-focused pass; exact-head CLI capture is retained as a manual reviewer step.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The current-head Quality Gate passed. The registry-edit RPC remains the runtime control-plane entry because OIDC/authority recheck paths and the generated RPC contract consume it; the canonical editor implementation remains in zeroclaw-config and the gateway delegates to it.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Cargo build/test/clippy were intentionally skipped at the author’s request to use GitHub CI instead of repeated heavy local compilation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes; existing capability selection is represented in the new registry. Existing admission boundaries remain in force.
- New external network calls? Yes; native capability adapters use the selected connection and protocol. No additional allowlist bypass is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes; connection credentials and sensitive headers use the existing encrypted persistence and masked edit contracts.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes; shared extraction policy is selected per materialized model.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Migration, registry editing and provider selection cross configuration trust boundaries. Preserve ciphertext, use masked compare-and-swap edits, validate references before installation, and keep the previous binding when construction fails. Provider output remains subject to runtime tool admission.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Older files are converted at the migration boundary; the new internal API and persisted V5 shape replace profile-owned construction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; connections, models, presets, fallback references and configuration editing use the V5 shape.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Back up the existing configuration and run `zeroclaw config migrate`. Inspect the resulting connections/models and exact model references. V1-V3 first migrate through the frozen V4 step, then V4-to-V5. Install the dependent clients before the complete interactive rollout; restore the V4 backup for a V4 downgrade.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert merged children before this layer. Restore the pre-upgrade V4 backup when returning to a V4 binary; retain memory identity checks and never downgrade by editing only the version number.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added for staging the stack.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** CI compile errors, configuration load failures, or changed provider behavior in the layer-specific regression tests.

Stack integration: this repository grants this author read-only access. These fork PRs therefore target `master` and have cumulative diffs. Review the incremental layer against its declared parent; merge parents first and refresh each child before merging. Original #9809 remains the reference PR and is not superseded or closed.

Incremental review: [declared parent to this layer](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/compare/46c5c37bb1...ef3e4d88e0).



### Review fixes (2026-11-17)

- Preserve V4 primary selection and non-strict text tools; strict policy follows named models, routes and fallback targets, with conflicting agent policies refused. Materialize fallback connections even when a canonical model shadows legacy input.
- Preserve non-streaming versus streaming timeout semantics with `api.stream_request_timeout_secs`; keep Grok subprocess deadlines bounded.
- Reject registry saves when disk edits diverge, compare stored references without resolving external secrets, and avoid blocking chat sessions for speech-only edits.
- Compare legacy embedding identity against the actual endpoint digest, and normalize image recovery using the served fallback model policy.
- Follow-up native Azure/Bedrock/Gemini timeout wiring is in #12455 and propagated to descendants. Follow-up `96a2d022fd` regenerates only the V5 fixture and fixes the recovery test setup and Clippy condition; `3e7455f7f0` fixes strict Clippy fixture initialization. Placement exception and fresh head-bound Quickstart evidence remain review items; this update does not claim maintainer approval.





### Latest head validation (2026-11-20)

- Current head: `ef3e4d88e0`; declared parent: `46c5c37bb1`.
- The branch was rebuilt from the clean reflection parent; downstream ZeroCode and Web changes are not included.
- Registry model defaults preserve unset reasoning extraction (`None`) outside the documented MiniMax/Groq defaults, so think-only responses are normalized and explicit `false` remains an opt-out.
- Registry edits reject deleting the configured vision model, in addition to the existing embedding reference guard.
- `cargo check --offline -p zeroclaw-config --lib` and `cargo check --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --lib` passed with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=`.
- GitHub CI is the source of truth for the full workspace and feature matrix; baseline dependency-security findings remain outside this PR's scope. The runtime RPC is the control-plane transport entry; registry mutation authority remains the shared zeroclaw-config editor consumed by runtime and gateway.


This backend cutover layer supersedes #9809; the original PR remains the historical reference only.

prs.title: fix(providers): preserve attribution during stream construction
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  Provider streams can emit records or capture parser-task context before their returned stream is polled. The dispatch wrappers entered the model span only during polling, so construction-time records could lose the effective model.
- Enter the existing model span while owned and borrowed dispatch invoke stream_chat_with_tool_round_policy.
- Reuse canonical provider attribution and the existing polling scope.
- Check construction-time and chunk-time records for owned and borrowed dispatch, with Batch and Single policies reaching the provider unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** Structured stream construction attribution. No terminal, retry, fallback, accounting, request payload or log-schema changes.
- **Blast radius:** Records emitted during provider stream construction, and spawned work that captures that current span, receive the same provider/model context already used during polling. Shared dispatch serves runtime, routing and reliable-provider paths.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9447 for adjacent terminal/recovery work; this attribution fix has no dependency or superseding relationship.

### What this does, simply

Some providers start parser work as soon as a stream is created. Its logs should identify the same provider and model as later stream chunks; this change keeps that existing context active during construction too.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: automated boundary tests exercise this change without external credentials or a user-interface walkthrough.

prs.title: feat(memory): order recalled memories with an external rerank endpoint
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - New `rerank_strategy = "external"` for the memory recall stage. After the existing deterministic preparation, the head of the eligible candidate pool goes to an operator-configured `/v1/rerank` endpoint, and the returned order decides the final selection. On the deployment measured in #12022, this raised the share of useful injected memories from 47% to 66–68%, where no `min_relevance_score` value could.
  - **Placement**, as agreed on #8891:
    1. `rerank::run` keeps its exact behaviour for `none` and `mmr`. Its preparation (pool cap, blend, eligibility, duplicate collapse, sort) is shared.
    2. `prepare_for_external` adds the relevance floor, so `min_relevance_score` applies **before** the call and candidates under it are never sent.
    3. The endpoint orders the first `max_candidates` of that pool.
    4. `apply_external_order` and `finish` reorder and trim to the recall limit.
    5. The renderer keeps that order.

    The reranker's scores are never written into `score`, so the renderer's floor check stays a no-op for entries that already passed it.
  - **Failure behaviour.** A timeout, transport error, non-2xx status, unparseable or wrongly shaped reply, out-of-range index, or repeated index all yield exactly the block the `none` strategy renders. One `WARN` record carries the reason, the status, the candidate count and the elapsed time, and never memory text. A successful call leaves a `DEBUG` record with the count and elapsed time.
  - **Before anything is sent.** Candidates come only from the existing recall path: the `ScannedMemory` recall-boundary scan from #8984 (which wraps every factory-built memory, under `[memory.policy] threat_scan`, on by default), identity and session scoping, the renderer's eligibility predicate, then the floor. The client (`zeroclaw-memory::rerank_external`) is built from config in the injection assembler and takes no part in storage-backend construction. It goes through the network guard below, and dials directly rather than through the runtime proxy.
  - **Network guard.** The endpoint goes through the shared guard in `zeroclaw_infra::net_guard`, the one `http_request` uses.
    - **At config load:** a cloud metadata or link-local literal is refused always. A private, loopback or local host (`127.0.0.1`, `192.168.x.x`, `localhost`, `.local`) is refused unless `allow_private_endpoint = true`.
    - **On every call:** the host is resolved once, under the guard's normalized spelling, and the answer goes through `ResolvedDestination::new`. That refuses metadata in both modes, private addresses without the opt-in, and a mixed public/private answer. The request URL is rewritten to that spelling (a trailing dot dropped), and the client dials only those addresses, with redirects off and no proxy (a proxy would resolve the host again). A refusal keeps the local order, with the reason `refused`.
    - **Not covered:** network-specific NAT64 prefixes (`security.nat64_prefixes`) aren't passed; the well-known `64:ff9b::/96` form is still decoded.
  - **Config**, all new and off by default:

    ```toml
    [memory]
    rerank_enabled  = true
    rerank_strategy = "external"

    [memory.external_rerank]
    endpoint       = "http://127.0.0.1:8098"   # /v1/rerank is appended to a bare origin
    model          = ""                        # optional, passed through
    timeout_ms     = 1500                      # 1..=60000
    max_candidates = 16                        # 1..=256, clamped to the candidate pool
    allow_private_endpoint = true              # needed for loopback, LAN and .local hosts
    ```

    Validation requires an http(s) endpoint with a host whenever the strategy is `external`, applies the host check above, and checks both bounds. The section's doc comment and the memory lifecycle page state that the recall query and the candidate memory text are sent to the endpoint.
  - **Stale validation warning, separate commit.** `validate_memory_semantics` still reported `rerank_enabled` and `rerank_threshold` as having "no effect", from before #8895 wired the stage in. Operators enabling the stage were told it does nothing. Those two warnings are removed, and the tests now pin the opposite.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No reranker inside ZeroClaw, and no model download.
  - No change to storage backends, consolidation, retrieval mode, or the `none` / `mmr` output; the default-off golden output is untouched.
  - No reranking outside memory injection.
  - No API-key field yet; local endpoints don't need one. A hosted endpoint would want one through the secrets store, as a follow-up.
- **Blast radius:**
  - `zeroclaw-memory`: the `rerank` split (crate-private `prepare_for_external`, `apply_external_order` and `finish`, plus `RerankStrategy::External`), and the new `rerank_external` module: the client and `ExternalRerankSettings::rerank_pool`, which runs the whole external step, its fallback and its log records. The crate gains a dependency on `zeroclaw-infra` for the guard, and tokio's `net` feature for name resolution.
  - `zeroclaw-config`: `MemoryExternalRerankConfig`, its validation (the host check included), and the stale warning.
  - `zeroclaw-runtime`, wiring only: `MemoryInjectConfig` carries the endpoint settings, so it is now `Clone` rather than `Copy` (two call sites clone it), and `render_memory_context` calls `rerank_pool` when the strategy is `external`. This needs a holding-crate exception, proposed in #12037; this PR should merge after it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12022. Related #8891, Related #8895, Related #8984. Depends on #12037 (the runtime exception row).

### What this does, simply

Before each turn, the assistant picks a few remembered notes to show the model. Today it picks them by a score that turns out not to separate useful notes from useless ones. With this option on, a small local ranking model reads the message and the candidate notes together and puts them in order, and the assistant keeps the best few. If that service is down or answers oddly, nothing changes from today.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional. The tests use a mock HTTP server for every reply and failure shape.
- **Setup:**
  - `llama-server -m bge-reranker-v2-m3-Q8_0.gguf --reranking --port 8098`;
  - the `[memory]` block above;
  - a few memories on related and unrelated topics.
- **Steps:** Ask something that matches one memory better than its blended score says. Then stop the server and ask again.
- **Expected:** With the server up, the better match leads the `[Memory context]` block. With it down, the block is exactly what it is without the option, and one warning names the reason.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on the three crates, and clippy.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the end-to-end latency numbers below come from a local server, not CI.
- **Commands run and tail output** (at `fd5b969a65`; memory crate re-run after the trailing-dot fix, the rest at `3e9c2d04d3`):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                     ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-memory --lib                                             ok. 577 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib                                             ok. 1821 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings   ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-config                            ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                         passed
```

  The `zeroclaw-runtime` lib tests (`memory_inject`, against a mock server) passed at the previous head, 38 of 38. At this head their only change is the fixture's `allow_private_endpoint` and one assertion; they compile under clippy above and run in CI.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The new tests cover:
  - **`rerank`:** the external strategy runs as `none` inside `run`; `finish(prepare_for_external(..))` equals the `none` output entry for entry, scores included; the floor and eligibility apply before anything is sent; the order reorders the sent head and keeps the tail; unranked head entries follow the ranked ones; scores are untouched; the trim follows the order.
  - **`rerank_external`:** URL building, query strings included; a chunked reply with no length that runs past the 1 MiB cap is refused; replies ordered by score whatever their own order; partial replies; ties; out-of-range and repeated indices; six malformed shapes; character-safe clipping.
  - **`memory_inject`, against a mock server:**
    - the endpoint's order decides the selection;
    - only eligible candidates above the floor are sent, and no Conversation entry or autosave key is among them;
    - `max_candidates` bounds the request;
    - each failure (timeout, 500, malformed body, wrong shape, out-of-range index, duplicate index, closed port) renders the local block byte for byte;
    - the external strategy with no endpoint renders the local block;
    - `from_memory_config` builds settings only for the enabled external stage.
  - **The guard:**
    - in config, metadata and link-local literals are refused with or without the opt-in; each private form (IPv4, `[::1]`, `localhost`, RFC 1918, `.local`) is refused without it and accepted with it; a public host needs no opt-in;
    - on the call, metadata literals are refused before anything is sent; a private address without the opt-in is `refused` (a closed loopback port, so a request past the guard would be `transport`); a 307 to `169.254.169.254` is reported as a status, not followed; a trailing-dot host (`localhost.`) reaches the checked address and is sent as `Host: localhost`.
  - **Config:** defaults, TOML parsing, endpoint and bound validation, and that other strategies leave the section unchecked.

- **Added turn latency at pool 16.** The external step adds one HTTP round trip; the rest of the stage is in-process and unchanged. I timed 200 calls shaped exactly like the client's, against `llama-server --reranking` with `bge-reranker-v2-m3` Q8_0, on synthetic note-length text (80–700 characters per candidate, 20–300 per query). With the default 1,500 ms timeout, none of these calls would have fallen back.

  | Hardware | Candidates | p50 | p95 | max |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Ryzen 5 9600X, CPU only, 8 threads (llama.cpp b11857) | 16 | 614 ms | 726 ms | 784 ms |
  | Ryzen 5 9600X, CPU only, 8 threads | 8 | 304 ms | 368 ms | 421 ms |
  | RX 9070, Vulkan (llama.cpp b11327) | 16 | 97 ms | 110 ms | 146 ms |

  On the evaluation's real memories, which are longer, the same model took a 1.4 s median and a 3.0 s p90 on the CPU with b11327 (#12022). So on a CPU-only host, an operator with long memories should raise `timeout_ms` or lower `max_candidates`; on any GPU the default holds.

  Human-checked sample of the evaluation's judgements, which Nillth asked for on #8891: [on #12022](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12022#issuecomment-7037257310). The judge never called a useless memory useful, but it is stricter than a human, and more so on hybrid's picks. Read with the human labels, keyword + bge-reranker-v2-m3 is at least as good as hosted-embedding hybrid on that deployment (about 82% against 78% estimated useful, within noise), rather than clearly better.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? Yes, opt-in only. With the strategy on, the recall query and the text of up to `max_candidates` candidate memories go to the configured endpoint each turn. Off by default; the docs say what is sent. Candidates pass the #8984 recall scan, scoping, eligibility and floor first. The endpoint passes the shared network guard: never a metadata address, and a private one only with `allow_private_endpoint`.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new model-visible text. The endpoint returns only an order, which the reply validation bounds to the candidates already selected for injection.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Defaults unchanged; `none` and `mmr` outputs unchanged. One API change: `MemoryInjectConfig` is no longer `Copy`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: `rerank_strategy = "external"` and `[memory.external_rerank]`, including `allow_private_endpoint`. Also, `rerank_enabled` and `rerank_threshold` are no longer reported as inert.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** set `rerank_strategy` back to `none`, or `git revert <sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `rerank_strategy = "external"`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a `memory external rerank failed; kept the local order` warning with a `reason` (`timeout`, `transport`, `status`, `malformed`, `invalid_index`, `refused`). A config that names a private endpoint without `allow_private_endpoint` fails validation and says which key to set.

prs.title: fix(mcp-builder): support mcp>=2 streamable_http_client import and custom headers
prs.body:
Fixes #1668

### Problem
In `mcp>=2.0.0`, `streamablehttp_client` was renamed to `streamable_http_client`, and custom HTTP headers are configured via `create_mcp_http_client` / `http_client` rather than as a direct kwarg to `streamable_http_client`.

Because `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/connections.py` unconditionally imported `streamablehttp_client` at module scope, importing `connections` or running `evaluation.py` fails on startup when installing `requirements.txt` (which specifies `mcp>=1.1.0` without an upper bound):

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../scripts/evaluation.py", line 19, in <module>
    from connections import create_connection
  File ".../scripts/connections.py", line 10, in <module>
    from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client
ImportError: cannot import name 'streamablehttp_client' from 'mcp.client.streamable_http'
```

### Solution
1. **Compatible import:** In `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/connections.py`, import `streamable_http_client` and `create_mcp_http_client` with fallback to `streamablehttp_client as streamable_http_client` for `mcp<2.0.0`.
2. **Context configuration:** In `MCPConnectionHTTP._create_context()`:
   - When `create_mcp_http_client` is available, create `http_client` with custom headers and pass to `streamable_http_client(url=self.url, http_client=http_client)`.
   - On `mcp<2.0.0`, pass `headers=self.headers` directly.
3. **Regression tests:** Added `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/test_connections.py` testing import resolution, stdio/sse/http transport factories, context manager creation, and validation error cases.

### Verification
- Ran `pytest skills/mcp-builder/scripts/test_connections.py -v`: all 5 tests passed.
- Verified `python skills/mcp-builder/scripts/evaluation.py --help` under `mcp 2.1.1` and Python 3.14: cleanly displays full usage and exits 0.
- Verified compilation with `python -m py_compile`.

prs.title: fix(skill-creator): isolate trigger evals and handle Windows and runtime failures
prs.body:
## Problem

Trigger evaluation can report false misses or invalid scores: per-worker command probes compete, select() on subprocess pipes fails on Windows, and unrelated tools stop the scan. Runtime failures also become non-triggers, incorrectly passing negative examples and misleading optimization.

Fixes #556.

## What changes

- Install one real candidate skill at `<temporary project>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, preserving its production name and candidate description. Parallel workers share it; concurrent runs use distinct UUID-based roots.
- Leave caller files untouched. The legacy `project_root` argument remains accepted but is no longer used.
- Reject same-name personal skill collisions, including those under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- Resolve the Claude executable, including Windows npm shims. Read stdout/stderr with portable threads instead of select(). Close stdin and cap probes at eight turns.
- Keep scanning after Bash/Glob and other orientation tools. Match exact Skill names or skill-entrypoint Read paths, including Windows separators.
- Stop the probe process tree during cleanup: `taskkill /T /F` on Windows; a separate session/process group on POSIX.
- Treat error results, timeouts, truncated output and worker failures as invalid evaluations. Abort the batch instead of assigning zero trigger rates. Cancel pending work where possible; active workers finish their bounded cleanup.
- Preserve successful evaluation JSON. Initial optimization failures propagate; later failures preserve completed iterations. Empty and partial reports render correctly.
- Write candidate artifacts as UTF-8.

## Validation

Latest revision: Windows, Python 3.14.

```sh
# From skills/skill-creator
python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
uvx ruff check scripts/run_eval.py scripts/tests/test_eval_failures.py scripts/tests/test_stream_probe.py
git diff --check
```

- **21/21 tests pass.** Coverage includes artifact isolation, exact matching, late triggers, configuration collisions, invalid batch rejection, cleanup and partial-result recovery.
- A real Windows .cmd wrapper launches a Python child; the regression verifies that the child cannot continue after timeout. This test requires process-termination permissions and was run outside the restricted sandbox.
- Ruff passes for the files changed in the latest revision. Whitespace checks pass.
- Tests make no model calls and need no credentials. Instructions and limitations are in `scripts/tests/README.md`.

## Scope and limitations

The temporary project excludes caller-project files and configuration. Queries requiring local fixtures need those fixtures made available separately. Personal and managed Claude configuration is not fully isolated.

The original investigation included live routing experiments on Claude Code 2.1.149. Those historical observations are not a claim about every current version. This revision has not rerun live model evaluation or POSIX integration. The candidate uses the standard skill layout independently of legacy command behavior.

Related work: #794, #996, #1027, #1755 and #1757. This PR combines a real-skill artifact with portable stream handling, full-turn detection and explicit failure semantics.

In `skills/webapp-testing/scripts/with_server.py`, server commands were spawned using `subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True)` to support `cd <dir> && <command>` chains. Passing unsanitized user/agent command strings into a system shell introduces command injection risks (CWE-78).

prs.body:
## What changed
`skills/docx/scripts/accept_changes.py` now returns an Error when `soffice` times out instead of reporting success, and only claims success after checking that the output DOCX no longer carries revision marks (`w:ins` / `w:del` / `w:moveFrom` / `w:moveTo`) in `word/*.xml` parts.

## Why
Defect 1 in #1770: `soffice` operates in place on a copy and the macro stores/closes the document itself, so a timeout leaves the output in an unknown state (possibly untouched, possibly partly processed) while the caller was told "Successfully accepted all tracked changes". `__main__` keys on `"Error" in message`, so the process also exited 0.

## How verified
LibreOffice is not installed in this environment, so the fix is verified with mocked `subprocess.run` plus real DOCX fixtures:
- Timeout (`subprocess.TimeoutExpired`): returns an Error mentioning the timeout, never "Successfully".
- `returncode == 0` but the output still contains `<w:ins>`: returns "tracked changes remain in output document".
- `returncode == 0` with a clean output DOCX: still reports success.
- `_docx_still_has_tracked_changes`: True for each revision marker (`w:ins`, `w:del`, `w:moveFrom`, `w:moveTo`) and for a non-zip file, False for a clean DOCX.
- `python -m py_compile` clean; no new third-party imports (`zipfile` is stdlib).

The macro-setup path (`_setup_libreoffice_macro`) is untouched.

### Summary
Adds `proofcore-contract-auditor`, an Agent Skill for Web3 developers that performs automated static analysis of Solidity and Rust smart contracts and anchors cryptographic audit proofs onto the public TON Blockchain using ProofCore's zero-storage Merkle protocol.

### What this skill does
- **Security Audit:** Scans `.sol` and `.rs` files for common vulnerabilities (reentrancy, overflow, access control).
- **Data Boundary Isolation:** Explicitly isolates untrusted contract source code as passive data to prevent indirect prompt injection.
- **Cryptographic Notarization:** Generates an immutable SHA-256 Merkle root of the audit report and anchors it on-chain without storing proprietary contract code on remote servers.
- **Safe Execution & Fallback:** Binds natively to `mcp__proofcore__seal_content` if an MCP server is configured, with a safe file-based Python fallback (`scripts/anchor.py`) that prevents shell command injection.

### Verification & Testing
- Validated against the `agentskills.io` standard format.
- Tested locally with Claude Code CLI.
- No root or elevated privileges required.

prs.body:
﻿Fixes #2013

### Summary

In `skills/xlsx/scripts/recalc.py`, `external_links_at_risk` previously only inspected workbook-level `defined_names` with direct regex matches against `EXTERNAL_REF_RE`. This caused false negatives where formulas referenced external links indirectly via:
1. Worksheet-scoped defined names (`localSheetId`).
2. Workbook or worksheet-level aliases that point to other defined names (e.g., `AliasAmount -> ExternalAmount -> '[1]Sheet1'!$A$1`).
3. Case differences in defined names referenced inside formulas.

As a result, workbooks with missing external caches could pass the pre-recalculation safeguard when `force=False`.

### Changes

- Replaced the direct global defined name check with `_resolve_external_names(ws)`:
  - Collects both workbook-level and worksheet-scoped defined names (with worksheet-scoped names appropriately shadowing workbook names).
  - Traverses name-to-name alias dependencies with cycle detection.
  - Matches names case-insensitively using `re.IGNORECASE`.
- Verified against the reproduction matrix (`direct`, `alias`, `local`, `ordinary`):
  - `direct`: flagged
  - `alias`: flagged
  - `local`: flagged
  - `ordinary`: unflagged

prs.title: fix(skill-creator): support direct execution of package_skill.py and update usage paths
prs.body:
### Problem
Running \package_skill.py\ directly as a standalone script (e.g., \python skills/skill-creator/scripts/package_skill.py <skill-path>\) fails with \ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts.quick_validate'\. Additionally, the docstrings and CLI help messages contain outdated references to \utils/package_skill.py\ and \skills/public/...\.

### Root Cause
When executed directly as a script, Python places the script's immediate directory (\skills/skill-creator/scripts\) at \sys.path[0]\, preventing the top-level \scripts\ package from being resolved.

### Solution
1. Add the parent \skill-creator\ directory to \sys.path\ if not already present, allowing \ rom scripts.quick_validate import validate_skill\ to resolve under both direct script execution and module execution (\python -m scripts.package_skill\).
2. Update the docstring and CLI help usage examples to reference current repository paths (\scripts/package_skill.py\ and \skills/brand-guidelines\).

### Verification
- Direct execution from workspace root: \python skills/skill-creator/scripts/package_skill.py skills/brand-guidelines\
- Direct execution from \skills/skill-creator\: \python scripts/package_skill.py ../brand-guidelines\
- Module execution from \skills/skill-creator\: \python -m scripts.package_skill ../brand-guidelines\
- Verified CLI usage message when called without arguments.

### Risk
Low. The change is limited to \package_skill.py\ and preserves the existing \scripts.quick_validate\ import. Direct and module execution were both verified successfully.

prs.title: Add document-typography skill: typographic quality control for generated documents
prs.body:
Prevents common typographic problems in AI-generated documents: orphan word wrap (1-6 words spilling onto the next line), widow paragraphs (section headers stranded at page bottom), and numbering misalignment.

These issues affect every document Claude generates. Users rarely ask for good typography, but they notice when it's bad.

**How it works**

The skill introduces a render-check-fix cycle: generate the document, convert to PDF, render pages as images, visually inspect, fix and regenerate. It also includes the M-count method — count how many capital M's (the widest character) fit on one line. Any real text will always be narrower, eliminating orphan wrap entirely.

**Included scripts**
- `measure_m_count.py` — Safe character limit per line using font metrics
- `check_orphans.py` — Reports lines at risk of orphan wrap
- `check_layout.sh` — One-command docx → PDF → page images
- `measure_line_width.py` — Visual line-width calibration

**Origin**

This skill emerged from iterative human-AI collaboration between [@PGTBoos](https://github.com/PGTBoos) and Claude. The user kept pointing out what the AI couldn't see (orphan words, widow paragraphs, layout balance) until the patterns were systematic enough to codify into a reusable skill. The M-count formula was the user's insight. The user actively wants to make LLMs more human-like, and sees this contribution as a help for both AI and humans writing skills.

- [x] SKILL.md with valid YAML frontmatter
- [x] Scripts are self-contained
- [x] Complements existing docx/pptx/pdf skills
- [x] Tested on real document generation

prs.title: Improve frontend-design skill clarity and actionability
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR revises the frontend-design skill to improve clarity, actionability, and internal coherence. The goal was to ensure every instruction is something Claude can actually follow within a single conversation, and that the skill's guidance is specific enough to steer behavior without being prescriptive.

## Background

I've been exploring Anthropic's open-source ecosystem after building a [GUI for Bloom](https://www.justinwetch.com/blog/anthropicbloom) and [proposing new behaviors](https://www.justinwetch.com/blog/10behaviorsbloom) for it. Looking through the Skills repo, the frontend-design skill caught my attention. Reading through it, I noticed a few places where the instructions, while well-intentioned, weren't quite actionable from the model's perspective.

For example, the original skill said "NEVER converge on common choices (Space Grotesk, for example) across generations" and "No design should be the same." The intent is clear: avoid repetitive patterns. But Claude can't see its other generations. Each conversation is isolated. These instructions are impossible to follow because they reference information the model doesn't have access to.

This got me thinking about what I call "model theory of mind": reasoning about what the model can actually know and how it processes instructions. A prompt can sound good to humans but be confusing or non-actionable for the model. I wrote up my thinking in more detail [here](https://www.justinwetch.com/blog/scaffold).

## Key Changes

**Coherence fixes:**
- Removed instructions assuming cross-session awareness ("never converge across generations," "no design should be the same")
- Resolved internal contradictions ("pick an extreme" conflicted with "the key is intentionality, not intensity")

**Clarity improvements:**
- Replaced vague adjectives ("beautiful, unique, interesting") with concrete guidance
- Rewrote the Typography section to focus on actionable instructions rather than aesthetic judgments
- Added specific palette directions to Color guidance (bold/saturated, moody/restrained, high-contrast/minimal)

**Structural additions:**
- Added INSTEAD block to pair positive instructions with existing NEVER guidance
- Expanded aesthetic direction list (added dark/moody, lo-fi/zine, handcrafted/artisanal)
- Expanded spatial composition guidance (z-depth, full-bleed, dramatic scale jumps)
- Unified imperative voice throughout

## Validation

I built an evaluation system to test whether the changes actually improved outputs. The setup:

- 50 representative prompts covering different design contexts (landing pages, dashboards, portfolios, menus, band pages, etc.)
- Each prompt executed twice via API: once with original skill, once with revised skill
- Puppeteer captures full-page screenshots of both outputs
- Claude Opus 4.5 judges blind (screenshots anonymized as A/B) on five criteria: Prompt Adherence, Aesthetic Fit, Visual Polish, UX & Usability, Creative Distinction

Results across the Claude 4.5 model family: Haiku showed the strongest improvement (8-2), followed by Sonnet (7-3), then Opus (6-4). Across all three tiers, the revised skill won 21 of 28 decisive comparisons (75% win rate, p = 0.006).

Interestingly, the revised skill helped smaller models more than larger ones. My hypothesis is that Opus can compensate for ambiguous instructions, while Haiku benefits more from explicit guidance.

## More Detail

For a full walkthrough of the approach, reasoning, and specific edits: [Teaching Claude to Design Better: Improving Anthropic's Frontend Design Skill](https://www.justinwetch.com/blog/improvingclaudefrontend)

Happy to discuss any of the changes or adjust based on feedback.

prs.title: fix(pdf): handle missing checkbox checked/unchecked values without KeyError
prs.body:
Fixes #1819

## Problem
In `skills/pdf/scripts/fill_fillable_fields.py`, `validation_error_for_field_value()` assumes every checkbox dict contains `checked_value` and `unchecked_value` keys:
```python
if field_type == "checkbox":
    checked_val = field_info["checked_value"]
    unchecked_val = field_info["unchecked_value"]
```
However, in `skills/pdf/scripts/extract_form_field_info.py:27-34`, those keys are emitted only when `len(states) == 2`. For checkboxes with multi-state / tri-state appearances, those keys are absent. When attempting to fill such a form, `fill_fillable_fields.py` raises an unhandled `KeyError: 'checked_value'`, aborting the entire form fill and discarding all other fields.

## Fix
Use `.get("checked_value")` and `.get("unchecked_value")`. When either key is missing (such as multi-state checkboxes where specific boolean states cannot be cleanly partitioned by the extractor), allow the field value to pass through rather than crashing.

## Validation
- Tested with multi-state / tri-state checkbox definitions lacking `checked_value`. Confirmed it no longer throws `KeyError`.
- Confirmed standard 2-state checkboxes still validate values and report format errors properly.
- Validated with `quick_validate.py` on `skills/pdf` (`Skill is valid!`).

prs.body:
# Add harness SDD suite: spec-driven development, dispatch discipline, adversarial review

Three process skills extracted from [harness](https://github.com/jordimarsal/harness) (MIT), a multi-agent Spec Driven Development harness battle-tested on real projects (an Astro portfolio site, a Kafka telemetry pipeline, a Java/Spring Boot status API).

## What's in the suite

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `spec-driven-development` | EARS-formatted requirements, 3-file specs (`requirements.md`/`design.md`/`tasks.md`), human approval gates, and **objective** requirement-to-test traceability via a mechanical checker (`check_traceability.py`: every `R<n>` must map to a real, existing test — file stem, Python function, or JS/TS test title). Exit 0/1/2, JSON protocol. |
| `agent-dispatch-discipline` | The subagent orchestration protocol: one dispatch = one batch (2–4 tasks, never 5+), minimal dispatch anatomy, on-disk evidence checks after every batch (a chat claim is not evidence), the "Nothing was written" re-dispatch opener, fresh-session restarts at ~70% context. |
| `adversarial-review-gauntlet` | Sequential adversarial review G1 correctness → G2 adversarial → G3 maintainability → G4 evidence, with a mechanical G1 gate script (`gauntlet.sh`, same protocol/exit codes as the checker, which ships vendored so the skill is self-contained). A G1 REJECT stops everything. |

## Why here

They are pure process skills (no API keys, no machine-specific paths, no binaries): exactly the "reusable workflow" category — they teach any agent a strict, verifiable way to run feature work, and they compose (the gauntlet delegates G1 to the traceability checker).

## Validation done

- Each `SKILL.md` < 500 lines; frontmatter `name`/`description` per the repo template and the [agentskills spec](https://agentskills.io/specification).
- The gauntlet zip/copy runs its G1 gate to `PASS` standalone against a fixture repo; checker tested against frozen PASS/FAIL fixtures (traceability gaps, unchecked tasks, vacuous-PASS guards).
- Full suite tests in the source repo: 49 checks green.

prs.title: Escape closing script tags in embedded JSON
prs.body:
## Summary

Escape `<` characters in the embedded JSON before inserting the serialized data into the generated HTML page.

## Motivation

If user-controlled content contains `</script>`, the browser can interpret it as the end of the inline script element. This can break the generated page and create a potential script-injection issue in standalone HTML output.

## Change

Updated `generate_review.py` to replace `<` with the JSON escape sequence `\u003c` in the serialized embedded data.

## Testing

Ran a focused manual check with a payload containing `</script><script>window.pwned=1</script>`. The generated embedded-data snippet contained no literal closing-script tag, and the escaped payload was present.

The full project test suite has not been run.

prs.title: fix(slack-gif-creator): account for text bounds when centering
prs.body:
## Problem

`draw_text(..., centered=True)` subtracts half the width and height returned by Pillow, but ignores the bounding box left/top offsets. The captions therefore sit away from their requested center. On Pillow 12.3.0, a `gyp` caption requested at (64, 64) has an ink center at y=68; `Hello\nSlack` has an ink center at y=66.

## Change

Subtract the bounding-box origin as well as half its dimensions. Keep the existing integer rounding and non-centered drawing path unchanged. Document centered single-line and multiline captions, and add two rendering regressions. The tests compare against a centered crop of the native text layout, preserving whitespace inside the font bounds rather than assuming every font has identical ink margins.

## Verification

- Both final regression tests fail on unchanged upstream `dbd4588` with Pillow 12.3.0.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` from `skills/slack-gif-creator` passes both tests with Pillow 12.3.0 and the minimum supported Pillow 10.0.0.
- Actual three-frame 128x128 GIF generated through `GIFBuilder.save` and reopened with Pillow: three frames, correct dimensions. Rendered PNG inspected. Corrected ink center y=64 for both example captions.
- Exercised on Python 3.12.15, NumPy 2.5.4, imageio 2.38.1. No changes to palette optimization, timing, frame ownership, or font selection.

This is independent of the existing gradient, ndarray-normalization, frame-snapshot, and GIF-timing contributions.

prs.title: Add blast-radius skill
prs.body:
## What

`blast-radius` — a checklist for the moment before a bulk or destructive write:
archiving users, revoking access, deleting rows, mailing a batch.

It covers the gap between a query being right about *rows* and a bulk operation being
right about *the world*. The core move is to classify every affected row into
**act / exclude / unknown** before touching any of them, where *unknown is never act*,
then check the act bucket for people the rule was never meant to catch.

## Why

Every example in the skill is a real near-miss from running an internal platform, not an
invented scenario:

- "Archive everyone with no account on our chat platform" would have archived the
  **research director** and a physician hired three weeks earlier. That signal measured
  *never joined*, not *left* — of 505 active members, exactly one had ever left.
- "Revoke the 98 stale permission grants" would have cut off the **service account** and
  the team leads. Classified, only 18 were genuinely stale.
- One batch email would have gone to someone who already held an offer, **rotating their
  token and invalidating the accept link already in their inbox** — their status field
  said otherwise.
- "78 of 80 file weekly reports, so they're working" — 3,037 of 3,392 reports were
  auto-generated drafts.

None of these were caught by being careful. They were caught by splitting a count into
named rows before trusting it.

## Contents

```
skills/blast-radius/
  SKILL.md                    instructions (113 lines)
  LICENSE.txt                 Apache-2.0
  scripts/blast-radius.sh     optional PreToolUse hook
```

`scripts/blast-radius.sh` is opt-in and does nothing on its own — hooks load from
settings, not from the skill folder, so SKILL.md carries the `settings.json` wiring. It
exists because of the trigger problem: a skill about not trusting a query only helps if
it loads, and the agent that would blindly run the query is the one that will not think
to load it. An unfiltered write returns `permissionDecision: "ask"`; a filtered bulk
write returns the checklist as `additionalContext`; read-only commands and anything
already flagged `--dry-run` stay silent. It fails open — missing `jq`, unrecognised
input or any error exits `0` silently.

The skill is useful without it; drop the script if you would rather `skills/` stay
instructions-only.

## Notes

- Layout matches the per-skill convention in `skills/` — SKILL.md + LICENSE.txt, with
  aux files under `scripts/` as eight other skills do.
- `python3 skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py skills/blast-radius` → valid.
- Hook smoke battery: 19/19, covering unbounded writes, filtered bulk writes, read-only
  fast paths, multiple leading `VAR=value` assignments, `#` inside string literals,
  malformed input and output shape.
- Also published standalone at https://github.com/kishormorol/blast-radius

Happy to rename, trim, or restructure to fit house style.
